reviews.comment: Took the class Fall '16, which was also Allen's first semester teaching. Definitely cares about student success in the class and will be totally available during her office hours and via email. Sadly, the material for 311 is incredibly dry/boring/hard, and this bleeds into lectures. I'd recommend a more experienced prof, but not a bad last resort.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking Levant: Colonialism and Coexistence with Professor Agbaria. He was very knowledgeable and motivated students to take an active role in learning about power relations, imperialism, colonialism, and coloniality of power. His office hours were quite generative and productive; one can tell he is passionate about his expertise.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wanted to enjoy this class. Unfortunately the mostly engaging lectures were overshadowed by absolute incompetence in course structure, communication & grading. I swear I saw a tumbleweed roll through the canvas page. He won't provide a rubric or tell you what's being graded (I asked). Don't take this class if you care about GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Posts no slides, lectures are disorganized, and he rushes through material while going on random tangents. Don't trust the grade distribution, he gave me the WRONG FINAL GRADE and ignored my emails. If I didn't track him down and catch him by PURE LUCK, I would've left this class with a wrecked GPA because he mixes up people's grades. Absurd prof.

I genuinely hated this class. The professor acts like a loud cartoon character but can't stay on topic or deliver a coherent lecture. He constantly tries to sneak in and push his political views and derails class with hour-long rants if you ask questions, then rushes through the rest and we cant even take notes. Total mess of a course.

I'm a STEM major used to tough classes, but this is the only one I didn't get an A in. I gave 100%, yet the professor made success impossible—no slides on Canvas, no exam reviews, ignored emails. It felt like he was actively working against us. Horrible experience. Worst class I've ever taken.

He secretly grades participation but won't tell you unless you pry in office hours. He's mixed up grades before, so your final grade is likely wrong. Most students didn't bother checking since he ignores emails and hides in his office. The worst part? Leaving with a wrecked GPA because of his careless mistakes. And you probably wouldn't even tell.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Absolutely does not care about students succeeding. The final is worth 35% of your grade and he DOESN'T GIVE AN EXAM REVIEW. Lectures make zero sense, and he constantly mixes up names and the spelling. Randomly changes grade weighting without announcing it, and lies about difficulty for each assignment. Awful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Syllabus and office hours are useless, he can and will change up the class format on a whim. Cannot properly do math, so chances are your grade will be misleading. No coherency at all during lectures, if you're not already strong in the subject, you're gonna do terrible. How UT allows these professors to teach is beyond me.

AVOID. While he held office hours, he lied about pretty much anything he said regarding the course format. My grade was up in the air until the final week of the class so that was a bummer too. Sure he was nice but did not teach properly. His lectures were all over the place and for a history class there was no chronological order.

He was the worst professor I ever had. He changed the rubric on the tests with no clear direction on anything on paper. Avoid at all costs if trying to find a good government class as the GOV366T label for this class is misleading due to this class being solely a history class. He is terrible with technology and does not respond to emails.

Terrible professor due to his constant rants during the lectures which causes him to rush his lectures. He constantly changes the class format and rubrics verbally and does not post lecture slides or a final review despite rushing. Office hours do not help at all as he constantly changes what he says so cannot trust office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at UT. "Lectures" are unorganized and rushed slideshows with dense slides that aren't even shared. No Canvas use. Expectations for writing assignments are unclear. Grades rely heavily on the exam and final (no final review guide either). Avoid unless you have prior knowledge on the topic or grad-level writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is nice and willing to help answer some questions, but wow, his class is extremely unorganized. He posts nothing but the readings on canvas. He goes very fast during lectures and doesnt post the lecture slides on canvas. Doesnt do reviews for the midterm/final. You wont really know your grade until after the semester is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting class, with more unstructured lectures, but engaging, focusing on broader historical patterns and concepts as well as trying to draw out their current relevance. While he listens to his students, his assessment organisation wasn't great - our midterm format was changed a few times without notice.

Agbaria is an amazing lecturer and clearly cares about the students and course material. Course has 3 (mini) essays, midterm + final, and all of them are graded pretty generously. I learned more in this class than in any other history course at UT. Only downside is he doesn't post slides or record lectures.

Professor Agbaria is one of the best professors in the Middle Eastern studies department, and he's incredibly passionate about what he teaches. He is very well knowledged on everything about the Middle East, specifically Israel-Palestine, and he does a great job of interacting with his students on the subjects.

Nice guy, but extremely unorganized class. Lectures were all over the place. Tons and tons of reading. If you don't know a good amount about israel prior to taking this class DO NOT TAKE IT, you will struggle even with going to office hours and putting in a lot of extra work. No rubrics for some reason. Refuses to give prep for tests.

Agbaria is a new teacher and does not know how to run a classroom. He does not believe in study guides for exams. Lecture notes are not provided. He does not use canvas and not a single grade was ever posted. Lectures are extremely unproductive and most of class time was spent bickering with students. Absolutely do NOT recommend taking his class.

Dr. Agbaria is a very characteristic and passionate professor. He has all of the best intentions, but falls short of what is expected in a teacher. His doesn't use Canvas (not a single grade nor assignment posted all semester). His grading criteria is very unclear with no rubrics whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor super passionate about the subject matter. He made me want to go to lectures. The writing assignments were largely graded on completion, and if you put effort into the class, you will make an A. Highly recommend this incredible man!

I took MES 301L, not 343, but it wouldn't let me change the course code. Dr Agbaria was a professor whose class I looked forward to attending, and I don't enjoy early classes. His lectures were clear with what will appear on the exams, just make sure you attend class daily and do the readings. He's funny and I felt comfortable asking him questions.

Dr. Agbaria is genuine, funny, and knowledgable. I learned a lot about the Arab-Israeli conflict from both sides. The class could be more organized, and tests were worded slightly confusingly, but he is understanding and more than willing to adjust. Lecture attendance is important for papers and exams. Overall, very rewarding class.

Amazing and engaging lectures. Clearly an expert on the topic. Truly cares about students, however it was too easy to succeed. I loved the content but wasn't meaningfully tested on it, so I did not grasp itwell. His lecture style works best in smaller class sizes. First prof I would ever say needed to give more assignments to reinforce the content.

Avramov is one of the greats! Engaging lectures, fascinating material, really genuine guy. My only critique is that the class allows students to succeed without learning the material. Ex- tests are online, hw only covers part of the reading. Bc of this, his class ended up on the back-burner. I wish he demanded more, bc I know I had more to give!

Professor Avramov is super awesome, the lectures are very engaging and this class is super relevant to current events. Discussions are lively and students are super welcomed to share their opinions. Would hundred percent recommend for everyone to take it - one of my favorite classes and professors here at UT!
Amazing Professor, keeps the class interested regardless of topic and always explains things thoroughly and well. Accepts questions and encourages students to be ambitious/ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I like Prof. Avramov a lot and I think what he teaches is extremely important BUT -I am kind of disappointed in him.He is so incredibly careful to stay away from even mentioning certain political topics in class. Everyone can clearly see that what he says applies to what is happening in the real world but he is too afraid to discuss it meaningfully

Dr. Avramov is one of the best professors I have taken at this school. This class is interesting at times but can often be boring and he kept everyone engaged. There is a lot of reading but quizzes and tests are open note/book so you don't have to do it all the time, but it helps. Other assignments are short discussion posts. Take this class!

Dr. Avramov is definitely one of the best professors at UT!! He is the most caring and passionate professor I've had. Cares more about the students actually learning than the grades. There were three exams and two discussions a month based on readings. However, he is pretty lenient and doesn't want to add stress to his students. Take his class

He was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He is so passionate about these topics that he is teaching which makes it so enjoyable to go to class and learn. Even though it is a big lecture class, he makes an effort to get to know all of his students. Great experience. I am taking another one of his classes next semester.

Professor Avramov is very caring about his students and takes that into account by not giving heavy loads of work, only what is needed to be successful in the course. As long as you take notes during lecture you will have all of the answers for the exams, which are open note. Very funny dude and makes tough info to get fun to learn

Dr. Avramov is literally the BEST professor I've had at UT!! He is super smart and knowledgeable, and cares about his students immensely! His lectures are superb and he really tries to keep you engaged throughout! You have to read a bunch, but it's super worth it! Dr. A is a true master in his field, so if you can you should absolutely take him!!!!

Dr. Avramov was my favorite professor I had during my time at UT. He is an amazing lecturer who is clearly a master of his subject. He is kind and takes the time to know his students. He is engaging and interesting. Do yourself a favor and take one of his amazing courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This Political Manifestos class. Both professors are really good and fun. However, there is a tremendous amount of reading and you are expected to read all of it. Can you make if you skim through? Yeah, not too bad. After the first precis scare is over, class is easy. Friday lectures are the most important, they guide you through the assignments.

Lectures are fascinating, you can truly tell Professor Avramov really cares about what he is teaching and making sure students understand the concepts. He gives great feedback on writing assignments making it really easy to increase your grades on them throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Avramov is an outstanding teacher. Very knowledgeable & engaging, he knows how to keep students interested and promote participation. Tackling the soviet security apparatus in the space of a semester is a mammoth task, but I feel I have gained genuine insights which have fed my curiosity on specific subject areas. Could not recommend enough.

If you're not sure how to do a Precis, then you will definitely learn how to in this class. If you don't let the Precis freak you out, then you should be fine along with the rest of the coursework. He does love to cold call and the lectures can be a tad boring, but the information is pretty interesting. He clearly loves what he teaches!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Heavy reading courseload. Excellent excellent professor. He cares and wants you to understand the Russian Security environment. Take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. A! He is an awesome professor and genuinely loves educating his students about Russia, Eastern Euro, security, etc. Classes are very reading heavy and exams are not for the faint of heart-- you MUST study! If you try in class and you speak up, he will like you a lot. He expects students to put in effort but never wants them to stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avi Blitz is an outstanding teacher. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and you can really tell he cares about his students. Homework is graded fairly, and quizzes are given every other week. As long as you show up to class, participate, and do homework, you will get an A. If you are genuinely interested in learning Hebrew, take this class!!

Avi is the best Hebrew teacher I've ever had. He knows everything there about the culture and language and presents in an engaging and meaningful way. As long as you come to class and participate, you will get a good grade. Take this class if it's open you won't regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: HES SO NICE!!! One of the best profs at UT!! If you want to take Hebrew take it with Avi. Hes so so kind and cares about his students

TAKE AVI!!! I absolutely loved his class. He crafted slideshows just for us and according to the topics that WE wanted to learn about. He's so kind and funny and cares so much for his students' success.

Avi is an absolute GEM of a professor. His classroom feels like home. He's so kind and welcoming, and he TAILORS THE CLASS MATERIAL TO THE CLASS based on our interests in subject material. He's also accessible out of class at Schulchan Ivrit or by email. He will improve your Hebrew drastically, and you'll have fun learning!

Dr. Blitz is one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. He will go out of his way to help you, and he cares tremendously for his students. Loved the atmosphere of his class. I am shocked to see that others claim to have not liked his class: I have a feeling they weren't expecting Hebrew to be so difficult. Take him, you'll learn so much!

I would definitely not recommend. This professor demonstrates a lack of care for his students and total apathy about the subject im interested in. A very poor experience I give 0 as a score if I coyld
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he grades really tough on homeworks (i got a lot of 60s) and there's hw everyday + weekly quizzes. good at teaching, supportive but sometimes unsympathetic (or has too high expectations of how easily we can retain words). accessible through groupme or text, not email. class discussions sometimes became anti-Palestine which was uncomfortable
Doesn't answer emails, disorganized, and does everything last minute.

This man is NOT accessible outside of class, doesn't answer emails, and isn't clear in his lectures. He rambles about easy concepts and speeds through the difficult stuff. His exams are only 3 q's. If you take this class DON'T FORGET THE QUEST HW he won't mention it in class or put it on Canvas. The material itself seems easy, he makes it hard.

DO NOT TAKE if no experience in calc. 2 exams, 3 questions each all purely based on bad lectures. notes and lectures not posted, does not respond to emails, must rely on your own notes to study. discussion and HW not what is related to exams. there are better calc teachers. avoid or get ready to get a C for getting 1 question on the exam wrong.

LITERALLY THE GOAT! Didn't show up to class for a whole month or two but still end up with an A. The exam is basically what is covered during exam review session, and final is not cumulative. 3 quizzes drops, 2-4 HW drops. THIS IS FOR M 427L.

Horrible teaching style, boring lectures, and unclear grading. Grades everything last minute so you don't know your actual standing until the end of the semester. Class time with the TA every other day gets you nowhere-- it's all busy work with a group you're randomly assigned to and nobody pulls any weight.

Macedo requires you to solve the questions in his own way which can be really annoying for tests. I struggled with Calculus and did not find the lectures that helpful. Most people generally get good grades but the instruction was not great.

Dr. Katie Bradford is one of the most caring and loving professors I've had while at UT. She would always print out the assignments for us, so that we knew exactly what to do for the next class. She brought in donuts one day as a sign of appreciation for us. She really cares and is really like a mom for you in the class.

Neurotic. So much busy work throughout the semester, 1000 extra worksheets worth 0 points, incredibly tough grader for no reason. Incredibly suspicious of AI and assigns extra work for the entire class if she suspects one student possibly used AI. Spent almost no class time on the huge "semester long" project until the last 2 weeks of the semester.

I love Bradford so much. She is such a pleasant professor who has a true passion for teaching. Her lectures were easily comprehensible and engaging. She fostered such a fantastic community within the course. Yes, there is a lot of reading, but the content was genuinely interesting and assignments were easy!

Learned so much from this conflict res course! There's lots of homework and multiple things due at similar times, which can be overwhelming, but it's all pretty doable stuff. Dr. B was a bright energetic spirit, and she genuinely cared about us. Loved the groups projects; be prepared to talk to lots of people!!

I really enjoyed this course! Dr. Bradford's lectures were engaging and made me excited to come to class. While there was more work than a typical communications course, I genuinely enjoyed the assignments. She made an effort to connect with students, which I appreciated, and the group projects were positive thanks to great teammates.

Dr. Bradford is by far one of my favorite professors. She wants you to succeed, teaches in a variety of ways, has engaging lectures, and takes feedback seriously. The class itself is fascinating and has practical applications in everyday life. Since taking this class, I have handled conflicts much better in both my personal and professional lives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Bradford is definitely one of my favorite professors. She is genuine, insightful, and extremely understanding. The structure of this class tied in with her teaching style allowed me to truly understand the course material. After coming out of this class, I walked out with many new lessons that I can apply to my life now and forever.

I took her web-based communicating with stuff course & it was not a blow off class. You will actually have to read the books and study the lectures if you want to do good on the exams. The exams are majority of your grade and can be quite difficult.

Professor Bradford has the most pleasurable and most important course that I've ever taken at UT. Her interviewing class will prepare you for any life situation beyond college. Participation is heavy In this course, almost every lecture we break off into smaller groups for interviewing exercises. I'm an introvert so it was tough to get used to.

I LOVED Dr. Bradford. She is a great professor who answers emails quickly and genuinely cares about her students. The class ended up being one of the most helpful classes I have ever taken at UT. It really prepares you for the real world. Some of the projects were time consuming, but she walks you though them step by step. I highly recommend.

I absolutely LOVE Dr Bradford!!! She was so personable, extroverted and made class fun.  There were multiple projects but she fully prepared you for each of them and gave ample time.  Probably one of the most important classes I've taken thus far at UT... it prepared me so much for the real world.  PLEASE take her class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradford is one of my favorite professors at UT!! This class provides the opportunity to network with and interview professionals in a field that interests you. Dr. Bardford gives fantastic feedback and is more than willing to help you in any way she can. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Really great professor. Dr Bradford found the perfect balance between not having tons of work versus actually learning and comprehending. I always looked forward to class every day, what a fantastic professor

I didn't understand how much I would be actually interviewing in this class despite the name. Ill be honest and say that if you get any sort of social anxiety I wouldn't take this class, several instances of having to present to the class and/ or interview professionals. Just be wary and read the syllabus before hand.

Dr. Bradford is a gem! CMS316L is useful material that is applicable to any area of life. She teaches real world skills and allows students firsthand experience in interviewing and networking. Her grading is very clear and fair and the textbook readings are the only useful ones I've had at UT. Gives students all material to succeed and cares!

Bradford is an amazing professor. She clearly cares so much about her students and her class is super interesting no matter what your major is. It's a great real-life experience. This class is project-based and all 3 of them are super useful and I'm very happy I took this class and got to create a relationship with Professor Bradford.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved this class and Dr. Bradford! She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There are a few main projects that make up most of your grade but I really enjoyed all of them. This class will definitely prepare you for the professional world (networking, interviewing, being interviewed, professional communication, etc.)

Dr. Bradford is such a gem. Grades consist of reading comprehension checks, 4 big projects, 2 exams, and participation. Project are broken down into steps and she details exactly what she expects. Fair grader and always gives feedback. Very receptive and inviting of questions. You'll get a lot of hands-on experience w/ networking and interviewing!

Dr. Bradford is a very sweet professor. CMS 316L is most projects, but if you follow the rubric you should get a good grade. Also, this class's test was super easy as she even gives you a study guide. Read the textbook throughout the semester and for the exam and you should be fine.

This class is a project-based class, but all of the projects are extremely helpful no matter what major you're in. You learn about networking, interviewing (both as R/E), and how you learn how to ask questions the right way. Dr. Bradford is also an amazing professor and she gives you plenty of time to complete each assignment. 10/10 bc helpful&ez
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

The "flipped lecture" is just code for "I am not going to teach you anything and you are going to work out of a workbook most of the time and also have quizzes at the beginning of every class."
i love you straumanis but this class was really hard :(

Straumanis is a nice guy but holy this class almost feels anti-learning and I might learn better from recorded lectures. You will be teaching yourself and if you have questions 9/10 times you're gonna get hit with a "what do you think". If you want to learn and have a good time, take someone else.

Do NOT take this class if you don't absolutely excel in teaching yourself, asking questions, or learning in a group, because that is what you will be doing. If you have to work on the worksheets at home, good luck knowing if you're doing anything right. He's got his heart in the right place, but this class is made for a very certain type of person.

reviews.comment: You'll learn if you put in the hours
I really really struggled with the flipped class format. This class really took so much of my time. Near the end he gave a pity party for himself that made me hate him more. Worst ochem professor.

Had Straumanis for both ochem 1& 2. Hes amazing! His class has a bad rep because ochem is tough. the way he structures his class really emphasizes LEARNING and applying over memorizing. If you put in the work, you WILL leave with an A as his exams are curved TWO LETTER GRADES!!!  Ochem 2 w straumanis was my favorite class at UT. hes phenomonal :)

I think Dr.Straumanis is a decent person but if you are looking to learn ochem and have a easier time, take someone else. I walked away with not much ochem knowledge and still a A because of his insane curves. He doesnt teach at all so you have to teach yourself everything and when you ask him a question he hits you with "What do you think".

The hate is so forced for Dr. Straumanis!!! O-chem is so difficult for any professor, but Straumy tries his very best to make the content digestible. I think inquiry-based learning is a great way to get a grasp on the subject, you just really need to set aside the time for it and never (EVER) brain-dump.

His class is more work, but you will have a deeper understanding of ochem. Treat his daily quizzes as diagnostics. His massive exam curves (30+ points) ensure A's to students who know even just some of the content. The biggest challenge in this course is finding a competent LA. Learned a lot of chemistry without once stressing about this course.

I really didn't like the way he did flipped classroom, having us work out of his pink book during the course time and only giving a brief lecture at the start of each class. His grading scale is incredibly lenient, but that means I got a decent grade in the course without learning much ochem...
The “trauma” in Straumanis should have been enough of a warning. The class would have been ok if he actually taught. Review lectures didn't go into the depth that his tests demand.

O-Chem II was much easier after having him for O-Chem I. While he's very nice and engaging, he's really nothing more than a warm body in the class. However, he cares enough to ensure every student excels and can get an A. Insane curves make up for teaching yourself everything. So many LAs and OH/WS to get help from! Good guy? Yes. Professor? Iffy.
Straum probably cares about his students but his flipped classroom approach only works for

there's a ton of resources and extra credit to succeed in his class. but it's also flipped classroom which means if you don't want to teach yourself ochem, plz don't take him. textbook answer keys, OH, and ed discussion will be your best friend in this class. also there's daily quizzes. ngl tho straummy was pretty iconic, in a traumatizing way.
Most horrendous professor ever, does not teach anything, leaves students that do not know much more confused

reviews.comment: I hate this dude. Praying that I don't have to retake it with this guy. Hardest class I've ever taken and the only class I've ever failed. I literally hate Straummy Mommy.
Dr. Straumanis does a lot to help you get an A. As long as you put in the work and don't get behind you will succeed in his class
Lowkey my fav, but hardest class at UT

Flipped classroom, meaning lots of work outside of the actual classroom. Classes consist of a quiz, him lecturing for 10 minutes, and then hundreds of people all talking in an echoey room after that, making it not a good learning environment. He gives super generous curves, so if you know what you're doing you can get like a 120% overall grade lol
Dr. Straumanis will do a lot to help you get an A, all you need to do is put in the work.

Hated this class. He wastes time when he should be lecturing and was incredibly condescending. Daily quizzes got exhausting and having to teach myself everything using his textbook was a massive waste of time. His book is full of typos and errors and feels super jumpy, making it hard to follow. He's also super sneaky about how he curves. Weird.

One of the most polarizing profs at UT, but if you buy into his method, you'll learn Ochem better than with anyone else and be ready for the MCAT! It's most effective for Ochem 1, but still your best bet for 2. It's a shame he has to pander with grade inflation for approval just because his method so dividing, but most appreciate the boost.

I'm not exaggerating when I say that the stress of his class caused severe physical illness. Took 320M with him- difficult but manageable. He ineffectually organizes both courses differently from every other prof, 320N is too dense to properly teach his way. He passes ppl through w his curves and you don't learn much. Will cost your soul

I love Straumanis! He's genuine, fun to talk to, and treats students like humans. Yes, his class is hard: its organic chemistry lol. His tests are fair, and if you work at it and try to understand, you will 100% pass. TAKE HIM!

Sweet and smart professor, not a good teacher. You will become Benjamin Franklin with the way you have to teach yourself.  He does offer lots of ways to make up for bad grades. He has had to curve every exam as well as the final. He has an assignment due before every class, quizzes every class, and in Instapoll in class.

reviews.comment: I just love this man 🥹

SUCH a rewarding class. Ochem is tough, and the flipped classroom takes some getting used to, but Dr. S is definitely onto something with his learning approach. If you make an effort to keep up with the material and take the time to do all CAs/exercises, you'll do fine. Would 1000% take this class again!!!
Nothing new to say here, but Dr. Straumanis is really good. Class is highkey grade inflated and I think being hot is a selection criterion for being an LA.

Straummy gets a bad rep (b/c ochem is HARD) but genuinely cares. Although I'm not pre-med, it was nice that he emphasized MCAT-related topics. Exam- and daily quiz-heavy, but with lots of EC (he replaced both midterm grades w/ the final if helpful). Do the workbook problems and study for quizzes (will really help your avg)—you'll be totally fine.

I was very scared coming into this class because of the horror stories I heard, but this class ended up being one of my favorite classes here at UT. I have learned so much, and it made me like science again bc before this I felt like I was just memorizing things. If you want to learn, TAKE THIS CLASS. Work hard, study hard, and you will be fine!

This is the first class in college where you actually have to learn how to problem solve and not just memorize random things to get an A. It radically changed the way I view learning for the better and for that, I am grateful. I understand why some people dislike this teaching style but i wouldn't be so harsh on him. He's doing the hard owrk

If you want to actually learn ochem, take Straumanis. The class is extremely difficult, but you WILL know ochem better than most of your peers in the end. 2 exams and a final that are heavily weighted, but curved (extremely). If you do CAs, exercises, and ask LAs questions, you will get an A in the course. Took him for org I and II w/ an A in both.

reviews.comment: Dropped Iverson for this man. Best decision ever.

Straumanis the goat I don't care. He genuinely wants to help you succeed by challenging you, and the flipped class actually forces you to stay on top of your work. And he gives a massive curve on his midterms! Ochem 2 is a breeze to me because of him.

Dr. Straumanis is one of the best professors I have had since being at UT. He genuinely cares for his students and gives them SOOOOO MANY opportunities to get an A in this course. As long as you study and keep up with your assignments, you should get an A. He and his LA's are amazing and make learning ochem so much better and less stressful.

He genuinely cares so much for his students and wants them to succeed. The only way to learn ochem is by practicing and the class is structured around that! It's better than wasting time hearing lecture then spending even more time on your own practicing. Stay on top of CAs and exercises and you are guaranteed to get an A with how much he curves

He is the only professor that I've seen go to such great lengths for every students. You can't fail with him as your professor because he makes so many accommodations and wants everyone to succeed. he cares so deeply about all of his students and totally changed my way of thinking. forever grateful i was in his class for 2 semesters and have nothing but great things to say about him. his style of teaching made me not afraid to ask questions and i feel so much more prepared for my future tough classes.

he cares about everyone. incredible professor and group of TAs always there to help you. so much extra credit. if you apply yourself, you will make an A. he responds to emails despite having upwards of 700 students. do not listen to the bad reviews. made me love organic

I could write an essay on having Straumanis for orgo1 and 2. Genuinely the best professor I've ever had and have never gained so much knowledge on a subject than I have in this class. helped me 🍇 my midterms and ace them!

Lots of hate for him in the past but honestly hes solid. Lots of extra credit, if you try even a little you will likely end up with A and a solid understnding of ochem2. Flipped classroom annoying but honestly his workbook and LAs are quite effective in teaching and understanding the content. Recommend wholeheartedly.
great taste in LAs
LORD of the Alkoxides! Dr. Straumommy really cares about his children! Gigachad LA's. W people fr! You will fall in love with all of them ;)

THE STRAUMANIS SLANDER MUST BE STOPPED! OChem is painful, but no pain no gain right? also the amount of extra credit he gives out is actually nuts.

reviews.comment: I love Straumanis! He genuinely cares about his students. Concepts may be challenging at first, but he provides lots of resources (past quizzes/exams, extra practice problems) to ensure we learn them. If you are self-motivated and keep up with the CAs and quizzes, you will gain a strong understanding of ochem and get an A (or 100+) in the course.
Great professor. Flipped classroom is the best way to learn things like this.
He is so kind and makes many adjustments to the course for the success of students. If students struggle in this class, they probably have a hard time with the flipped classroom model.

Boy oh boy where do I even begin. Dr. Straumanis. honey, my pookie bear. I have loved you ever since I first laid eyes on you. The way you drive into the paint and strike fear into your enemies eyes. Your silky smooth touch around the rim, and that gorgeous jumpshot. I would do anything for you. I wish it were possible to freeze time

Straumanis is one of the best professors I've had at UT. He provides adequate course material to learn the content, the pacing of the course is good, and there are many extra credit opportunities. I wish I had taken him for Ochem 1. If you can, take Straumanis!

People are WAY too dramatic about this class being "awful" and "impossible". The truth is: the people who say that do not put in effort consistently. This class is manageable. Quizzes are not unfair, they keep you accountable for your work. Every exam is curved 20-30 points. This class is hard because OChem is just hard, Straumanis isn't the issue.
meow meow meow meowmeowmeowmeow meow meow. meow meowmemwom meow, meow meow meow. MREOW

I know that Straumanis gets a bad rap in general, and I'm not sure if he changed recently but he is genuinely the most understanding professor I will ever have at UT Austin. He is so easy to approach and rewards real effort with the extra credit near the semester. If you do the basic CTQ and some of the exercise an A is easier than any other prof.
Really HOT LAs, makes it hard to pay attention in class, otherwise would def recommend. Throatmanus

I transferred from Callmann second semester and now I wish I took him last semester. His quizzes can be annoying to study for all the time, but it made that week of the exam so much easier &less stressful. Allows you to understand the nitty gritty stuff that week. I would suggest every freshman take him. Genuinely!

He's goated, I actually learned alot.

Where do I start? DO NOT take this professor. He gives too much extra credit. It is way too easy to learn in his class and ask questions, and this is shown by the exams. I can't believe I have never gotten less than a 100 on his exam, and it's terrible. STAY AWAY. Additionally, his aura is way too much for me to fathom.
My glorious ochem monarch Straumommy is the ultimate aura farmer. No one comes close, not even sung jin woo or gojo.

Everyone hates on Straumanis but he is really not bad. Flipped classroom sucks, ochem sucks, but he tries to get as many people as possible A's. He does a multiplier curve so you will always be curved up. He also changed the entire grading structure last semester so an A was a 90. His LA system is great and there is always someone there to help you

Straumommy changed me. He made me explore ochem in a way I didn't know was possible. He was an inspiration—my group and I craved every drop of his knowledge juice. The classroom was flipped, but only because if he taught, we'd master ochem 1 and 2 in weeks.

Straumommy was like my second mother. So caring and cares about our learning. Straumommy backs up the class structure with research. Did you guys know that students who take 320M with Straumommy go on to do better in other professors who teach 320N than those who did not have Straumommy?Straumommy makes his class structure data driven!

I could not recommend him enough, truly one of the best professors I've had. He truly cares about his students success & it shows. Quizzes are annoying but they're SO helpful and he gives a ton of extra credit. Exams were difficult but o-chem is hard anywhere. Go to class, ask questions, keep up with material, you have an A.

unique teaching style that is hard to acclimate to.make friends in this class and make plans to study outside of class and you'll pass.definitely attend work session(office hours) its how I passed each quiz.the la's and ta's are your friends and are so willing to help,befriend them and ask a lot of questions.i suggest doing activity the day before

For ochem, this class was not that bad. He changes the grading criteria to better your grade, and there are extra credit opportunities. I wish I would have studied more everyday, as there is a lot of memorization. Come to class for the quizzes, but afterwards you basically do whatever you want.

No lectures, learn through CAs & exercises. Deeply understand content because topics build upon one another. DON'T get behind. Quizzes each class are annoying, but help you keep up w/ content. Ask the TAs any questions you have in class. Exams are hard, but there's TONS of curve. He is very approachable & truly wants you to succeed. Def recommend.

Dr. Straumanis' flipped classroom is a very difficult but effective way at learning ochem. I did not particularly like it, but his 20% curve on each test and final was clutch. This class requires A LOT of out of the classroom time and focus. Do not take him if you do not love chemistry. The flipped classroom can be an extreme pain.

He makes the tests quite difficult but there is an immense curve on everything. He made me really enjoy learning during class because it was a lot of group work instead of lecture (this is a controversial opinion but my attention span isn't that long so it was beneficial to me). The quizzes helped a lot. Go to work sessions.

If you don't mesh well with flipped classrooms don't take this class. Get in a good group, treat every quiz like a test, and stay on top of work. The curve at the end is very nice but there is little to no instruction done in class. Go to the learning sessions at least once a week and you'll be fine.

survivable, saved by extra credit. study a lot and do as much practice as possible. for transformations, dont bother w all the diff flashcards, only for memorizing what changes between steps. use other professors summaries and notes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you take him, just know that you're going to teach yourself everything. This worked fine for me, but I know people who did not have a great time. He curves a ton because the averages are horrible. There are daily quizzes, but you get used to them pretty quickly because they are not super high stakes. Big tip: study the exams from previous years!

I love this man. If you want lots of good practice and you want to actually KNOW how things work in ochem, he is amazing. He was super lenient this semester on grades, dropping the cut off, having three options to get an A, and insane curves. One thing: you can't slack off in this class. Every class matters!

Straumanis isn't a bad professor at all, but the course is almost entirely self-learning. Exam 1 was okay, but the 2nd one was pure evil. Exam 2 & the final were curved 30+ points bc most people fail. If you're pre-med and want to understand ochem deeply for the MCAT, this class is great for that! If you're not pre-med and lazy like me, AVOID him.

While guided inquiry style learning is more work, it helps you develop a solid conceptual understanding of ochem. Treat the daily quizzes as diagnostics. Exams can be tough but are curved 20-30 points each. Figure out how you learn best, and this class can be very rewarding. He cares about the class and makes it very possible to do well.

As a professor he can't explain to save his life. But he gives a bunch of extra credit. Midterms 1&2 were fine, and he posts past tests. The final was mentally scarring. We had no idea what we were going into and basically everyone failed. If you need someone to explain the concepts to you DO NOT TAKE HIM. If you can self study you're set.

The class is hard, but Straumanis really cares about his students. The class is flipped and there are learning activities before each lecture, daily quizzes in class, along with 2 exams and a final. They are difficult, but everything is curved A LOT, and there are plenty of office hours with TAs/LAs to get help. Not as scary as people made it seem.

If you are taking other difficult courses at the same time it is hard to keep up with the content. Take Straumanis if this will be your hardest class in the semester because I do think the flipped classroom does help you really understand organic chemistry. TAs were very helpful also but quizzes were very annoying and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He didn't really teach the class, lots of youtube and workbook teaching you, but heavily curves and adds bonus points so I was never stressed about my grades, added 20 points to each test and 40 points on the second test...don't know if that reflects poorly on his teaching but he adds a large buffer, just be better than average.

Straumanis was grades-wise one of the most accommodating professors I've had. The exams were tough, but daily quizzes helped catch mistakes. LOTS of bonus points, drops, and great LAs. I enjoy learning from practice problems so I liked the class and content stuck, but I wish he had summary lectures during class instead of just in work sessions.

i think flipped classroom is effective when done properly; straumanis does not do that. if you don't have time to go to work sessions or other office hours, you won't learn anything. he does give a lot of extra credit, however, i don't think it compensates for his lack of teaching in class. daily quizzes are annoying and so are the tests

Excellent professor who really cares about his students. Do all exercises and study well for each quiz and you'll do fine. There's a lot of extra credit opportunities and curves heavily on exams. He took the best of our midterms and lowered the grading scale to give everyone higher letter grades. Tons of TA's and work sessions if you need help!

There is a lot of hate about Straumanis and his class. But what is not discussed is how many resources he gives and how helpful his team is. Ochem is an insanely hard class and even harder to teach yourself. He changed grades for an A to be a 90 and was VERY generous with extra credit. He tries to give you an A and if you try you will be okay.

This class was hard but not as bad as I expected. If you are someone who learns best through practical application and independent learning, then you will enjoy this class. If you prefer learning through lectures and step-by-step explanations, then you may struggle a bit. My best advice would be to analyze your mistakes and ask lots of questions!

reviews.comment: He's alright, not the best but no the worst. I'm 50/50 on the flipped classroom. I just wish he lectured more in class instead of just sending us to work on the textbook straight away. His exams are curved. I never really asked straummy questions because I've heard he's condescending, but the LA's are the best. Going to work sessions kinda saved me

For next semester he should consider curving the quiz avg grade. In class he told us to treat them as diagnostic and that they won't affect our grade, but they brought my grade down a letter bc it weighs the same as an exam. The quizzes are 5 minutes long and at start of class, and if ur like me you don't fully get the lesson until after class :(

reviews.comment: Though the exams are very difficult, he gives you an incredibly fair shot of succeeding in his class with the amount of extra credit he gives. You can also tell he cares about his students by the resources he provides and the talks he gives. If you put in enough effort, you should be totally fine in the class.

Though flipped classroom is unpopular, I think it works for more people than you'd expect. A huge percent of his As come from grade inflation, but if you put in the work and go to work sessions, you'll be fine. Ask questions literally every single time you're confused; otherwise, you won't build the foundation required to succeed in the class.

Trying to understand the content from a textbook riddled with errors, and relying on the help of group members and LAs who are in the same boat as you doesn't help. People "do well" because the curves are insane, and the grades are over inflated. Definitely an experience!

I went into this class scared because of his rate my professor. Though I'm not too fond of flipped classrooms (I prefer lecture-style teaching), I admit that this teaching method helped me learn ochem thoroughly. He is a nice person and he is passionate about ochem. I'm actually glad I ended up with Straumanis for ochem, he's not bad at all.

I don't think I've ever wished more ill will on a professor than I have with this guy. Most fake and disingenuous prof I've ever had. Acts like he cares whilst also dismissing student concerns, coming across as two faced

Doesn't really lecture that often. Lots of TAs and other people to help you, plus he makes people form groups. Heavy curves (like 20ish points)

Not my fav but tbh he's not that bad. Curve is very generous. He doesn't really lecture in the traditional way so be ready to learn in a group and ask TAs (or him) questions. Book has some errors but nothing too bad. don't expect it to be easy and then blame the prof if you can't get an A like everyone does here. If 1 gets an A all can get an A.

why sigmaunis is awesome:
curves his tests a lot

leaves his old crusty wife for a younger baddie

rides his bike to class (healthy)

I was really scared about ochem but this class made it seem not so bad! You have to be proactive about your learning and HAVE to attend work sessions and ask questions. Exams have loads of bonus points and he curves generously. Dr. S is not the most approachable to ask questions but his TAs and LAs are super helpful and never judge.

This class is honestly not too bad if you're willing to put in the work. Do something for ochem everyday so its repetitive and you think about it frequently. Pay attention to the quizzes, especially the bonus. If you go to study sessions the LAs can give helpful tips that can come in handy. Do what he tells you and ochem can be approachable.

This class is tough but A LOT OF resources were given for students to succeed. 90 and above is an A. ECs built into exams and bonus questions on quizzes. If you can't study on your own and would prefer for the prof to explain step by step, this class is not for you. Las and Tas are helpful! Would recommend :)

Prepare to spend lots of time on this class. Quizzes every class, self-taught content via worksheets, etc. Even though it is hard, it is very do-able to do well with all the resources he provides (practice quizzes/exams, several weekly work sessions, recorded lectures, and EdDiscussion). He also gives LOTS of extra credit.

reviews.comment: All I know is he invented curved arrows. Yipee. After experiencing so many profs at UT I realized that you don't have to make a class hard, or berate your students, which is something that he does. He is not with the times and roasts you for no reason. When there are other amazing ochem profs I have no idea why you would take him.
Probably the most condescending and out of touch professor I have ever had. Actively takes digs at other professors who are much more qualified to be here at UT than he is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Highly recommend! His flipped classroom isn't as bad as it seems. He obviously wants everyone to get an A but also LEARN chemistry. He has SO MANY RESOURCES for studying. It starts off easy but picks up rapidly in the middle so be prepared. Its a really difficult class but theres lots of opportunity to raise your grade EVEN if you fall behind.

I'm sure staumanis isn't anyone's first choice so here's my advice if you're stuck with him. prepare to spend around 5 hours a week. go to a work session before every quiz. figure out how to learn by yourself. if you can spend a lot of time on this class you should be fine. i wouldn't recommend taking him with other difficult classes though.

Ochem is really hard, and this class is no exception. Straumanis doesn't spoon feed you answers, which I appreciate, and when you do understand things, you understand them well. However, he gives you very little to start out with, and relies on an army of TAs, some of whom don't seem to know much more than I do. Curve goes crazy.

Ochem is an inherently hard class, but Straummy's course is a million times better than that of Hsu or other profs. Ochem is still hair-tearingly difficult, you actually have a fighting chance here where other profs have slaughterhouses; Straumanis has lots of EC, bonus opportunities, and doable exams (on which he will boost your grade by 20 pts).

his class was a lot better than I had expected, his curves are so insane! he gives many opportunities to get an A in his course even if you start the semester off poorly. his work sessions are super helpful and a great way to ask questions. i enjoyed his class!

Straumanis' curves are some of the craziest in UT Ochem. If you're used to teaching/reviewing by yourself, you'll probably be fine in this class. Quiz during beginning of each lecture (not worth alot) and preactivities of the next unit due before the lecture (not worth alot). Each exam/final curved 20%.

Despite all of the bad reviews he gets, I can confidently say Straumanis is the best choice for ochem1. Ochem is objectively difficult, but putting in adequate time and effort will easily earn you an A. Insane curves on the tests (+30 on mine) and you only need a 90 to get an A. If you don't stay on top of the content you won't do well. Take him!!!

Straumanis cares about his students and gives them countless methods to succeed in his class. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The structure of his class did not work for me. Workbook was full of errors and not even the TAs knew what was going on. He doesn't explain anything, so be prepared to literally teach yourself the entirety of ochem 1. The only reason he's getting a 2 is bc he curves everyone up from failing. If you need ochem past this course, take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Claims to have lots of bonus/ec but it won't matter bc you'll fail anyway. His curves are generous, but you'll still end up barely passing. Tries to be inspirational instead of answering the question and will gaslight the class after exams and tell you that you have "chosen a challenging path" when he's the one making it impossible to get an A.

Every positive review is going to say that ochem is a hard class in general. We obviously know that coming into it but having a professor who will tell you to learn material basically on your own, provide no accurate practice problems, and give unreasonable exams that are worth over 70% of your final grade certainly doesn't make it any easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Keyword: GUIDED OChem class. Flipped classroom with quizzes every class period (except exam days) with bonus points on every one. Very generous with bonus points and partial credit on exams. Don't let that fool you: this class can be difficult and will eat up your time. Dr Straumanis is apart of the sassy man apocalypse so beware of that.

I would be cautious of all the poor reviews that Straumanis gets on RMP. Ochem is not easy and a lot of people blame ochem professors on their performance. Straumanis very clearly cares about his students. Anyone that pays attention in class or attends his work sessions should see that. However, it's true that a flipped class isn't for everyone

If you're not pre-med TAKE ANYONE ELSE. He seems to care about the pre-med students, but that's it. The few interactions I've had with him have been awful. He expects you to just know everything. The curve on exams is generous but be prepared to study so hard and get a raw score of 50. I think he's like a good guy, but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Straumanis cares about all of his students and if you listen to his guidance and how you should approach the class, this means being open-minded to his teaching style, you will succeed. His POGIL-esque learning style puts the power in the students' hands. Finished the class with a 110%, and so did a lot of other people I know. Curves are generous.

This class is heavy on self-teaching but when you go to him with a question he will answer it well. He gives a crazy amount of extra credit and if you put in effort you will get the grade you want. I'm pretty sure he gave the class a 30 point curve on midterm 2.
Grades tough and tends to lose his bike.
Too hard. Failed :(

I studied so much for his midterms. Failed both. Waiting on the final to try and bump up my grade. The daily quizzes suck. Don't do it if you're taking other hard courses at the same time, as you have to put in a lot more time since he doesn't lecture. He'll say he has his "summary lectures" but those honestly don't help, bro assumes you got it.

You don't know what you don't know. But he expects you to know what you don't know. He seems to care about your success, this class structure was not helpful at all. Even if you complete all the worksheets, he says "you're not getting the full picture", and proceeds to not even tell you what you're missing. Extremely stressful, take someone else.

Would not recommend. Interesting teaching approach however daily quizzes and impossible exams make this class miserable. No lecture as he believes you teach yourself with his book but his book is filled with errors. Be prepared to study a lot and still not succeed. Exam 2 was unbelievably difficult.

Teaches via flipped classroom, which was helpful for me due to working with my group and studying with them as well. Quizzes every class sucks, but prevents procrastination and you can earn up to 120/100 points (same for tests), so plenty of extra points can be earned. Test 2 was pretty difficult, but he added a curve, so not too bad.

He was very much aware of how stressed his students were and didn't really seem to care. Daily quizzes were super annoying and didn't help you prepare for the midterms at all. He basically never lectured and the midterms were completely different to all of the practice he gave out. Take someone else if you can.
His class is such a demotivator. sad way to make students feel.

Not to sugarcoat anything, but despite the trauma and stressful atmosphere that this man has needlessly imposed on us students, there may be some merit to his teaching approach because I physically felt my pre-frontal cortex developing this semester, likely as a survival instinct for this class. That being said, save yourself the agony.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bro doesnt even write his own tests.

Even though I study so much for the exam and feel prepared, the exams are extremely difficult. I learn a lot in the class it self through the reverse classroom, but the exams do not give me a chance to show what I know. This class requires a lot of effort and time to study and complete the activities.

TBH: The first test was very fair, but the second test not so much as people seemed confused about what content was covered. His quizzes are the root of a lot of stress, so if you can't take daily quizzes well consider that. He emphasizes self-study, and it works for some and not for others in a very polarizing fashion. Good luck if u take him
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This man is so terrible I can't even put into words. He does not teach at all and you will probably fail if you don't spend your life on YouTube trying to learn. It's like he expects you to wake up knowing the information without ANY guidance!! I don't know how you are supposed to make up your own chemistry but that's basically how the class works.

If you want to teach yourself everything then take this class. His tests are nothing like the practice exams or what the workbook is like. He is so annoying, all he does is give inspirational speeches after giving us the most ridiculous tests. Quiz everyday so be prepared. He wrote the workbook himself and class time is basically work on your own.

If you want to be left rethinking your entire career and traumatized by exams and quizzes then take straumanis! His exams are 100 X harder than the practice exams he gives us and does not represent the material we learned in class. He does not even teach! His classroom is literally just a place to work on his workbook the entire time.

Ochem is expected to be hard and it is way harder if it is self taught. The prof doesn't teach at all. If you are ok with doing worksheets every class and then being quizzed on it by the next class, then this class if for you! the workload of this class is not doable at all when you're balancing other science classes. I do not recommend.

I get that its OCHEM, but he made it harder than it needed to be. He's nice but his lecture videos and the guided textbook aren't very helpful. Practice tests are significantly easier than the real test. It's also difficult to work in a giant sweaty auditorium with 500 people talking over each other. Quizzes are fast but keep you accountable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is a nice person, but not a good professor. The 1st half of the semester we had 5 mins to take a quiz at the start of class- it then changed to 7 mins. He doesn't lecture, you just work on activities during class that don't highlight important concepts. It just felt like he didn't care about his students' success.

Mr. Straumanis is nice, but his class is too difficult. In class, we work through a worksheet with our group and take a quiz on the material the next class. The quizzes are too hard and are in total worth as much as a test grade. I really lack the support I need to understand material this challenging when sitting in a 1000 student lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly he is a pretty good professor. His class is hard but he likes what he does and tries to be pretty accommodating. Grading seems very harsh at first but gets a little nicer through the semester. Quizzes every lecture and 70.5 % of the grade is from tests/final so make sure to do the work between classes.

This class is great if you enjoy teaching yourself. I wasn't able to attend the work sessions because of other commitments that took place at the exact same time, so I'm not sure if they were helpful, but if you have a hard time in chemistry this is not the professor to take. You can expect quizzes at the start of each class, and no lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was awesome! Failed a test? ITS HIS FAULT FOR NOT PREPARING YOU! Bombed a quiz? YOURE ONLY MISSING ONE KEY CONCEPT!  GOOD LUCKING FIGURING OUT WHICH CONCEPT THAT IS! This class is amazing if you love hanging out with your friends and failing tests TOGETHER! OH, AND DONT WORRY ABOUT ANY OF THOSE NASTY LITTLE EXAM CURVES. HE DOESNT USE EM!

Two words: F.U STRAUMANIS! This class was insanely hard, no help from the professor and quizzes were 5 minutes in length while it took this wannabe marine biologist 20 to explain the whole thing. No reviews for exams and you sure bet the exams were hard! Lots of fun to fail every test!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't teach!!!! He uses POGILS. Just wait for another professor. He only has 2 midterms and they are hard. When asked how to improve, he will not offer opportunities, he will just say get better. DONT TAKE

I haven't finished the course yet, and I'm not even doing that bad, however he is HORRIBLE. Literally just gives inspiration ted talks every class, is extremely boring, and his textbook/answer keys are CONSTANTLY riddled with mistakes. He provides almost no helpful resources. His textbook he wrote also sucks. His philosophy on teaching is so poor.

Was a pretty hard class, I felt it was fair throughout the semester, just quite inconsistent. It's clear that students do worse overall than he expects so there's a lot of rearrangement in the class to accommodate for that. Final was absurdly hard and quite different than exams through the semester. No dropped exams.
I love prof RG! She's super well-read and her lectures are interesting. Grade is determined by your TA though, so be aware.

Class has a lot of reading and writing (which is the point of all UGS classes).
Professor R.G. is an amazing lecturer who deeply cares for her students and for the topics she teaches.

i never went to lecture, just do the instapolls for attendance, discussions were mandatory and boring but if you show up to all its automatic 100 for attendance. 100 word responses for every reading which were interesting for the most part. stay on top of the work bc it is really easy to forget about this class. 2 easy essays and easy asf project.

Dr. RG's lectures are pretty good and she covers a lot of topic. For assignments, we're required to read a lot for hw, you'll have two writing assignments, and you have to write 100 words per prompt for the travelogues (Part I and II); but is there's no midterm or final. Overall, an easy class to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor RG was great. You can tell she's really passionate about her subject and the lectures were always interesting and engaging. There's no midterm or final, only 100-word entries for each reading, one paper, and final project. The readings often felt really heavy. Overall great class, if you keep up with everything it's an easy A.

Dr. RG is super knowledgeable and passionate. The class is extremely reading-heavy, but the passages are often interesting and relevant to the course, obvi. The lectures are an hour and a half long, which can be grueling, but Dr. RG's visuals/audio examples can wake you up. Overall, she's super compassionate and truly loves what she does!

Dr. RG's lectures are very interesting/engaging & she covers a lot of interesting topics! The one thing that I'd note is that we're required to read a lot for hw & you'll have to write two large papers (1 has 13 prompts and the other has 10) & you have to write 100 words per prompt (1000-1300 words total). The plus side is there's no midterm/final!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took professor RG for my UGS class. One of the best lecturers (if not the single best) I have ever attended. While you do have to read a ton in her class, it is definitely worth it.

Such an interesting human! And their voice while speaking is so soothing. The examples that are shown and discussed in class are so intriguing and unique. I honestly think about them quite often and want to find them again to fully watch the movies.

Absolutely incredible professor to have. It's a very fun class, though make time for doing a lot of reading, or at least looking at summaries to keep up on the material. Reach out to the TAs or Dr. RG themself if you have any questions, they're always happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In UGS 303 Modernity and the Art of Uncanny the TA will either make or break you in this class. My TA was Thomas Rushin and my FIG peers could agree he was a very strict grader and extremely blunt. Dr. Richmond-Garza, however, was very sweet and understanding. Each lecture there are graded instapolls to answer but no tests or quizzes. SCARY MOVIES!

Dr. Richmond-Garza was an amazing lecturer who taught in an engaging way and seemed to actually be passionate about her class. If you show up to lectures and discussions, participate, and actually try on her assignments, you should get an A. She is a very solid pick if you're looking to get a UGS.

Easy class but the few assignments take a lot of time, every point is a point towards your grade, make sure to do all the instapolls, I never went and only did 50% and lost out on an A due to attendance. Also the teacher and material is pretty cool but as a stem major I didn't really have time to read the extensive catalog. Harder than average UGS.

Not a hard UGS, but more work than other UGSs. LOTS of reading (just skim), weekly reading entries, and a few papers/projects. Project/paper expectations are not clear, so talk with your TA to make sure you got everything (TAs grade everything). Lectures were chill (mostly opinion-based instapolls).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you liked AP Lit in High School you'll like this class. It really is oriented over reading a decent amount of books, and 3 assignments, and as long as you try your best on them, you'll pass the class with an A most likely. Make sure to go to the discussion section and build a good relationship with TA's, since they're the graders after all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Easiest UGS ever

Dr. Richmond Garza made this course feel anything but required or chore-like. It's a fairly easy UGS with plenty of readings but you'll be fine with just sparknotes. The course content was enjoyable, interesting, and all of the above!

would recommend for ugs. workload isnt too bad, mainly readings and a couple written assignments. 30% of your grade comes from the video project, which can be time consuming. your grade depends on your TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. RG's lectures are engaging, and you can tell she's passionate about the material. The workload is heavy, but using resources like unstuck AI for study prep can really help. The TA makes a big difference, so choose wisely.
Lots of reading but the books are good.

Great class. Only 4 assignments and attendance. Lectures were kinda interesting. My TA was very sweet and tried their best to make discussions engaging. Don't summarize for assignments in this class, always include every thought you have regarding the reading, even if it's silly. Analysis is really important to get full credit.

Excluding the attendance grade, there were only 4 assignments. At the start of the semester that intimidated me, but trust that as long as you put effort into each assignment (as well as turn them in on time) you'll be okay! Discussion sections were terribly boring, but that's entirely on the TA. Definitely recommend Dr. RG for World Literature!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love her so much. Extremely passionate about the material. No quizzes or tests, just small writing assignments and a video project. Readings are interesting, and you can skim them and still do well. Discussion sections are fun, you just talk about the reading and your opinions. Highly recommend for english/literature requirement!

This class was super easy, but you have to get good grades on everything because there is only like 7 assignments. Attendance is a really big part of the grade and discussion is mandatory. She is super nice and interesting to listen to. Readings can sometimes get confusing but stay on top of everything and you will pass the course.

Dr. RG is such a sweetheart! Her office hours are always so helpful when it comes to discussing readings, developing arguments for the assignments, or just chatting in general. Her grading is clear but it depends on your TA. My TA (Hamna) is amazing and she is very helpful! but again, the experience you get out of this class depends on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment:
RG as a professor is great. But if you have Mustafa as your TA I would suggest dropping the class immediately. He will not show up to office hours and will try to fail you.

If you receive anything less 100 on the first assignment, drop the class bc the TA will grade worse on the next assignment.

For World Lit, the lectures felt kind of boring and redundant to me. Lots of high level reading that can be hard to keep up with but if you can get through it the class is pretty interesting. I enjoyed discussion sections too and I didn't find the grading too harsh but it depends on your TA.

Dr. RG is awesome, and her lectures were very interesting! You can tell she loves what she does and cares deeply for her students. There is quite a bit of reading, but skimming is your best friend (as Dr. RG suggests). Grading depends on your TA; I had Hamna and she was great. If you're needing to take a fun and easy UGS, this one is a hidden gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were incredibly engaging, some of the best I have ever heard. She has an uncanny (...) ability to command the room with her voice. I suspect many of the lower scores come from students who simply do not like work in general, since the reading, while not light, is given with the instruction to SKIM.

Class is VERY reading/writing heavy and incredibly boring lectures. That said, half your grade comes from Instapolls so it's not hard to do fine if you want a B or C. Essay grading is very subjective and getting an A is entirely dependent on your TA (they grade all your assignments). Had to use my first Q-drop. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Showing up to class and participating in Instapolls is half our grade. This is ideal because this formula gives some leeway on actual assignments. The assignments themselves are very straightforward. Although there is a clear grading criteria, due to the nature of the course the instructions can be quite vague. TA can make or break your experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To say the least, I am so glad I didn't take my AP Lit exam in high school, because if I did I wouldn't have had to take Dr. RG's class now. This is one of those professors you don't want to miss taking if you have the opportunity. She's so kind and understanding and you'll even look forward to her incredibly entertaining lectures.

The timing of the assignments wasn't great; once I had gotten feedback, it was too late to change anything and it had already brought my grade down. There's a lot of reading in this class, but it's worth doing to keep up with the lectures and discussion sections. Overall, if I had to take English again, I would probably try another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is someone that cares a lot about her work. Her classes were interesting and you could tell she had a passion for what she was doing. My only complaint is that the assignments were at times very broad and unclear and the TA was not very helpful.

Dr. RG is an excellent professor, you can tell she is very knowledgeable and passionate in her teaching. I will say there is a lot of reading to do before the class and for discussion, however, the readings are quite interesting and you can skim read. The lectures are really interesting and lovely to listen to. This has been my favorite class!

Dr. RG is well-renowned at UT. I may not be majoring in something Literature related, but Modernity has connections to all disciplines! Your TA seems to make this class a hit or miss since they grade everything. Readings can be a lot sometimes, and you're graded on a few assignments. If you enjoy the class, consider he E316L class in the spring!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is super sweet, but the amount of readings we were given was insane. If you skim it you will be fine and the TA is in control of your grading. Overall, a lot of work but an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures looked like a mess - old pop songs, cartoon movies, and pics from the internet mixed with some boring liberal dogmas. I would say if you read three articles from Wikipedia instead of listening to all this barely systematized mixture of mass media stuff - you wont waste your 40 minutes of life.

This class was very fun to take for a UGS and Professor RG was very knowledgeable about all the topics. The work was manageable and not too much if you stay on top of it. The TA grades most things and all TA's are different in how they grade. Professor RG was very understanding of any personal issue that interfered with your assigned work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is very knowledgeable and her lectures are really interesting. I wish I could have taken a smaller class with her so that I could have had a closer relationship with her. She and the TA's grade promptly, and her criteria are very clear. Participation is important, so if you're not there in person you need to at least do the Instapolls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, I really liked Dr. RG and the class was enjoyable. However, the course felt more like a literature class and the readings could be excessive. I had friends taking other UGS classes with significantly less work, but this one gives a GC flag. Just make sure to tryhard the assignments and ask for feedback if needed.

Professor RG is really kind and passionate. I took notes on the lectures at first, but then realized you won't need them. Interesting readings, but I never read 100% of all of them. Just do the polls during class, try-hard your essays, email your TA for feedback, and you'll be fine. My TA, Lindsay, was super nice and graded pretty nicely.

dr rg was very flexible on the grading criteria, even allowing our final essay to be optional/counted only if it helped your grade. her lectures are very interesting, but there is a LOT to read in a short time, so its easy to fall behind and miss out on the full experience. this class was tough but i encourage you to reach out to your ta for help!

Took class in Fall 2020 Dr. RG is great, the course is super interesting, and has everything you need on her website. Participation is key (especially during discussion sections). Grading from teaching assistants and rubrics on assignments are fair for the course. Best to pay attention, especially during dicussions Class is mainly for first-years
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class content was kinda niche and seemingly irrelevant at times but the professor was truly passionate about her class. I'm sure there are people who really enjoyed the entire class. Taking the Art of Uncanny was a great choice for me as I received credit for a core flag in addition to the normal UGS requirement.
