If you are good at writing, definitely take this class. Even if you are not, it is a doable humanities course if you put in effort - get to know your TA and ask them for help. Professor Richmond-Garza is very sweet and accomodating, lectures are interesting. Lots of reading but interesting texts.

Dr. RG is one of the most caring professors I have ever taken. This respect extends into the TA's as well. My TA provided good feedback to my writing and analysis (s/o to Vanessa). The class is reading heavy, but if you don't read the texts it is easy to catch up! The class is spread out among a few different assignments, which I liked.

Literally the coolest professor I've taken! However, this class has a loooot more readings compared to other UGS courses, but the material is super interesting. Professor is so sweet and caring, but your grade is dependent on your TA, but as long as you read the material, you have an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is a fantastic woman. Passionate, incredibly interesting, and flexible. The class felt more like an English class than a UGS. You will need to read. The material is exciting, however. All assignments are graded by TAs, but you can also contact her about concerns. I would take her again.

Dr. RG herself is nice. However, her UGS class is graded almost entirely by her TA's. Your grade really depends on who your TA is. She also assigns excessive reading for a UGS course which is supposed to be a class to transition to college. Unless you are a Liberal Arts major or an artsy person, I would not recommend her UGS course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE CLASS!!! I took this class because Dr. RG had good ratings and the class itself sounded interesting. BOY was I wrong! The TA's are absolute garbage, none of them know how to grade properly. Grades are SO UNCLEAR. So much reading especially for a UGS. The teacher is nice but I have nothing good to say about the class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Beautiful human being. Her lectures are so engaging and relevant to the course's content. Very organized, and always available to you when you have any questions or concerns.

Professor RG was super kind and passionate about class, she chose really interesting texts and wove things together well so it was interesting. Your grade is heavily dependent on your TA, and many aren't clear on instructions. Lots of reading, and if it's online, be ready to write for each reading. I would recommend, but probably just in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is great, the course is super interesting, and has everything you need clearly on her website. Grading is fair given the amount of time you have to do assignments + available rewrite options. Its really not as much work as other reviews indicate, however the class is mainly first years who may not be used to university yet.

I've spent more time on this class alone than my three engineering classes combined and that's saying something. I'm no expert in math or physics but the amount of time and effort for just this introductory UT course is insanely high. Extremely poor communication regarding assignment requirements and poorly structured class in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For a lower division UGS class, this was more work than all three of my upper division classes combined. She lacks any sort of communication, and her only redeeming quality is that she is kind, but not kind enough to extend due dates. Get ready to read and write a lot.
Dr. RG is an AMAZING professor. She is so articulate and gives her students a great insight on her analysis of international texts. Your grade is HEAVILY dependent on who your TA is.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Richmond-Garza is a brilliant professor who makes her students really want to read. You have to work for an A, and the grading on exams were particularly hard. All the readings are accessible on her website so you won't have to buy any books. She makes lectures fun, but you need to go to class to get what will be on the exams.

Dr. RG is super empathetic and caring, her lectures and TopHat are very interesting. She is SO accommodating during the COVID-19 crisis. You need to mention your opinion, as well as other analyses of the texts in the journals and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is my favorite professor at UT so far! She's awesome and her lectures made me enjoy books/texts that I never would have liked without this class. You need to show up to class for test info & tophat, but her lectures are so fun and interesting that you'll want to be there anyway. I would take every single course she teaches if I could!

Dr. Richmond-Garza is such a great teacher and person, but her UGS is way too much reading for my tastes. Most UGSs are considered blow offs but hers had a decent amount of reading (one story of chunk of a novel before every class), and had supplemental writings to do with every reading. No final per say, but there was a final video project.

I LOVE Dr. RG!!!!!! Wonderful and extremely interesting class, only choose for UGS if you're a reader, writer, and lover of the arts. Beware, your grade is heavily dependent on chemistry with your randomly assigned TA, I got lucky and had a great one! The TA can make or break the course so if you aren't willing to gamble I'd suggest something else!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A lot of students find her classes genuinely interesting and end up taking away a lot from her classes. Just be prepared for deadlines to sneak up on you and lecture to be generally disconnected from the reading and assignments. The very few assignments there are count tremendously towards your final grade, so be careful.

Professor Richmond-Garza is so passionate about the coursework she teaches in this class and it really shows. Lectures were always interesting and you never really had to do anything but show up for them. There weren't many assignments and as long as you make an effort and consult with your TA you'll definitely pass. Loved this class!

Used Top Hat for attendance and easy in-class questions. Her lectures are very interesting and eccentric. You won't be graded over reading but you should try to read to participate well in the discussion group class. She graded most of my writing in the class and she seemed a pretty kind grader. She was really nice and explained assignments well.

I enjoyed going to lecture, I had a really good TA that really cared about my progress with writing essays. If you read, you will be okay. All you need to know is how to right clear arguments and make connections to the "real world".
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is a good professor but does not properly prepare you for her exams. She uses far too much time going around the stories plot and background than actually talking about it. Once she showed us a movie clip of 007 that had no relation to the story??? Heavily controlled by TAs so youll be lucky to get a good one. Never on the same page as TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: RGs a good lecturer. But the assigned TA made this the worst course Ive ever taken. Showing an extreme inability to convey the grading criteria or to help connect our concerns to the professor, sordid behavior, just not enough characters to truly do them justice. Also an attendance policy thats oddly strict, wouldnt recommend for any non-majors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great choice. Her lectures are very insightful and make you look at the texts in a unique way. Graded by 3 tests, a reading journal, and attendance. For me, the tests were pretty difficult. If you want an A, you're probably going to have to work for it by going into office hours and studying a lot! Also TA grades all your stuff so get to know them!

She is amazing!! Take her for your English credit! I really enjoyed her class, it was my favorite from the semester. The readings are pretty good and the discussion group TA should help you understand the texts a lot more. Pay attention bc the lectures and discussion groups will srsly pay off so much bc that will help you do great on exams.

I LOVE Dr. RG!!! I took this to complete my core and ended up an English major by the end of the semester. Not to mention she has SOLID TA's. I had an issue with my attendance bc there IS a policy, but after going to her office hours and working it out, everything was fine. She's clever and empathetic, and super approachable - she's just goth!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. RG is an amazing professor. She loves what's she's teaching so much, and it really shows. My issue with my time in her class was with my TA. The grading criteria was consistently changing AFTER assignments were already turned in, and nobody felt like they fully understood what was expected of us even after asking for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grading criteria can be a bit unclear, otherwise great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really loved her class and the lectures that she gave were so interesting. She really cares about literature and sharing that passion with other people. Her class does involve a lot of reading, but that's to be expected of a lit course. The course isn't easy, but as long as you attend lecture and take good notes, it will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took this class just for an English credit but ended up really loving it. The lectures&stories we read are really interesting. Although a few can be a bit tricky to understand, Professor RG explains them v clear in lecture. You do have to read for each class but readings arent too long. Lectures are dynamic & include movie clips, art, music, etc
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof RG is pretty dope!Her UGS is actually a crazy amount of work though, and the grading is very strict. The TAs usually follow the grading to the T so make sure you go to office hours and ask them to proofread your essays. Make sure you show up and do the tophat cause even if you have a attendance code it tracks your location and knows.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's awesome. Her lectures are entertaining and engaging, I enjoyed them throughly. You will learn alot of interesting things. The assignments are not hard, but there is only about five so they weight alot. They are graded by the TAs, so I recommend going to office hours if necessary. Overall, I really enjoyed this class and an A is achieveable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's great. Participation is online through typing one word of what you think about a movie clip. Her lectures are funny and she's incredibly nice and respectful before showing disturbing movie clips. Your TA in the class matters. There's only a handful of grades, and they're not weighted much, so every point counts. Can get by without reading
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Richmond-Garza is a great, intelligent professor, but the TA you get for this class really matters. The TA I had graded extremely tough for a UGS course, which is detrimental in a class with few grades. The lectures were interesting but didn't seem super relevant to the coursework.

They changed syllabus this semester, so apparently, they are still trying to figure out a way to manage this class. I'd suggest you take this class if you are interested in literature and movies. Got a 92% in the end, but still got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bradshaw is monotone, and it is difficult to stay engaged in his class. I had him at 8am so that makes it harder, but he talks so slowly it feels like we could have gotten through the entire semester's content in a month. That being said, the tests are just memorization of the slides, and it is easy to get a good grade.

Class is different than accountings I am used to, no math at all, like English for accountants. Tests are very memorization-heavy, but he's a nice guy. No busy work, which is nice. Start memorizing content for the tests a week in advance and pay attention in class (try to)
Easy tests and grading, not engaging or exciting to listen to but also it's 8am...
M&A Class - He skips a lot of content during lectures but his guest speakers are top notch. Be ready to study a lot before exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does NOT care about you learning the material. You will have to study slideshows 40-70+ slides long per chapter but maybe talks about 2-10 of those in class. He fully skips chapters when guest speakers come. The material is interesting he just doesn't teach it or gives long winded explanations. Be ready to stress for tests.

Takes an interesting topic and makes you dislike it. Almost 80% of classes are guest speakers, which may sound great, until exam time, when you realize he has taught nothing. Very lecture-heavy with little class participation. Exams are all written and make you teach the textbook to yourself.

good luck yall boys, if you're reading this and youre in his class, its too late for you. every test will absolutely push the limits of the human mind. every case is a arduous process. the roughest part, though, is having to sit through his class without sleeping. He doesnt respond to any questions or hands raised, and is a yapatronic. runaway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs I have ever had. I had my hand raised for 14 minutes straight and never got called on. He proceeded to ask "Any questions" while my hand was up. And then said "ok good no questions lets proceed." It has happened 5 times in 3 classes. He just reads the slides then closes his eyes or stares down and then paces back and forth.

Lectures are long but meaningful—he's passionate about fraud and wants students to truly understand it. Cases are fair, and he's always willing to talk through them. He teaches for comprehension, not just the test. If you stay engaged, you'll learn a lot.

I have taken multiple courses with this professor and he manages to make the most interesting classes such as fraud analysis sound super boring. 15 minutes will feel like the longest hour of your class. Not only does he only stare at his feet and outside the window while teaching, but he offers no help or additional learning opportunies.

He insists on testing us all the materials although some of them weren't covered in class. Offers no help prior the exam, no review session, no practice questions. His condensed slides for exams are almost 350 pages + extra readings. If you want to spend more time in class with the guest speakers, then don't put that much of a weight on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a very nice or accommodating professor. I would recommend taking a teacher who actually cares about the students

He is a good teacher, but this class is too much of a headache. He teaches with jpgs of handwritten practice problems with glare. You just end up teaching yourself through the textbook homework problems. Exams are very similar to in-class "problems." The written/essay questions are graded very hard. Disappointing because puts forth zero effort.

Pretty disappointing class; could be taught in a much more engaging manner. Cases and exams are graded stringently with incredibly specific rubrics, but there seems to be a big curve. A lot of guest speakers, but most of them don't have much to say. Bradshaw himself is fine and very smart, so I feel like he's capable of much more.

Nothing special. Simple class. The tests are based off entirely from the slides. Only pain is having through wake up at 8am to hear him lecture. He sprinkles some of the "homework" problems on the tests so make sure to review for free points. Overall, a good class because you don't have to worry about it until test week.
My man is so boring. Like he's nice but I'm telling you, everyone in my class at 8AM as I'm writing this has no desire to be here.

Prof. Bradshaw is pretty good. He's a very smart guy and his lectures are really interesting when you can stay awake through them. Textbook is a drag. Syllabus goes on a lot about participation in class but he doesn't really give any opportunities to do so. Huge curve, yet he's the easiest professor to take for audit. Solid choice.

Pretty average prof, work load is average, exams are short answer, no textbook purchase. Could have been a more interesting class, but he is so monotone it makes it hard to pay attention and enjoy the subject.
He is hilarious and you really get to know him! Classes are simple and lots of interactive discussions!
Took for Power of Words UGS. Such a fun class and insanely easy. Professor does tend to go on random tangents/talk about nothing. Very little work and it is hard not to get an A.

I literally love this guy. He is so kind and he is very accessible if you miss a quiz or a test. He is extremely knowledgeable and receives questions well. He also does review sessions and goes over your exam 1:1 with you which is reallllyyy useful. The class itself is straightforward and the exams are just like the review.

Joy of French truly was joyful. He cares about the content he is teaching, and it is fun to learn about French curse words, common sayings, and other aspects of the language that typical classes do not teach you. He is passionate and understanding, so this is the 3rd class I have taken with him because he's simply the best. I highly recommend him!

Dr. Birdsong has been my favorite French professor at UT. He is so kind towards each student and genuinely wants you to succeed in this class. This class also greatly improved my pronunciation, and I will truly miss having him as a professor next semester.

Great class to really learn about pronunciation. He's engaging and fun. Writing recommendation letters for multiple people in class. Cares about your individual progress. He gives practice tests and quizzes. Homework isn't too bad but to do well you want to do it. I definitely recommend him for any french class.
Dr. Birdsong is very caring and passionate about French. There are two tests, homework assignments each week, and a handful of quizzes. There is a final project at the end that is not hard.

Professor Birdsong has been my favorite french teacher in the six years I've been learning french. He's very sweet and cares so much about the material he teaches. He goes out of his way to relate to his students and makes accommodations if you don't understand or might not be able to attend lecture.

Birdsong is a very enthusiastic & fun teacher- gets you excited about what he's teaching. He was not originally supposed to teach 317C, so he did not create the material and tests. Prepared us well w/ handouts, practice quizzes, & told us where to find the study material. Pretty generous with grading. Attendance points are self grading after class
Professor treated me with such disrespect that I had to drop the class. If you have disabilities, I do not recommend taking this professor. I suggest taking another upper division French class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UT by far. I have learned the most in his class and he genuinely cares. Don't let him scare you off. He is knowledgable and caring, and has the coolest experiences in his research. His humility is astounding. Class is not easy, but it is so rewarding and prepares you for grad school type work. Could not recommend more.

Everything based off 3 tests, and test wording can lowkey be confusing. Had to study a ridiclous amount for the tests just to not even get a 100, I had nothing else to do tho. If your course is alr loaded take a diff one. He's really funny.

The course material is super interesting, and Barany is such a fun lecturer. The class is pretty seminar-based, but it isn't intimidating at all. You are graded by very few things; however, I think he's a pretty fair grader. He's also super approachable and funny, so I never felt too afraid to ask for help. Take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took GOV365G Military in Politics with Barany. The class was fun and Prof Barany is genuinely passionate about the topic and discussing it with students. Pay attention in class, review lecture slides and do the readings! There are pop quizzes that are pass or fail so make sure you read. He's really one of UT's gems so take advantage!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super easy, 3 tests, you don't have to study or go to class, they are all common sense if you look at powerpoints for like one hour
I loved this prof, not many grades just 3 tests and that's it, very understanding and funny. 100% would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barany is an amazing professor, the class is pretty reading heavy but the readings are always interesting. He is a tough grader but as a professor he is incredibly helpful, understanding and funny.

Barany seems intimidating but was actually very funny and approachable. Lectures covered all the material in the reading I didn't read any of the book and managed to do well. Exam is lecture heavy but the TA had reviews telling you exactly what to study. 3 exams were easy but it was stressful since they are all that your grade comprises of w no EC

Professor Barany is very laid-back. He was not super enthusiastic about this course, but still gave entertaining lectures. If you actually do the suggested readings, you will be reading maybe fifty pages a week, although, you can definitely get away with not doing them. Three exams make up your grade, but all were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class isn't that difficult, but I severely underestimated how much attention I'd have to pay. The exams are pretty specific so you do need to pay a lot of attention in class and your grade is dependent almost exclusively on exams. I'd strongly recommend taking the virtual version of this course, as it's a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm a CS student and in all the complex math and coding courses I've taken this is the lowest grade in a class I've gotten, he's very textbook heavy and the lectures are a little dry, the exams test you on quotes/little things from the book so if you didn't read the chapters and you don't have good memory you'll lose 15% of ur grade per exam

I did not have a good experience in this course. I did all of the course assignments, everything he asked, including weekly papers, hundreds of pages of reading every week, and the final paper just as he wanted- and I still received a B, with absolutely no explanation as to why. He grades tough and arbitrarily. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Three exams are 90% of grade. Lectures are funny, but only somewhat helpful for exams. Be sure to review slides and book.

Tests are worth 90% of your grade and if you get a bad grade on one of them, you're screwed. This guy does a fantastic job of saying a lot of stuff without even getting to the main point. Just rambles off-topic at times and will put random things that he talks about in class on tests that you cannot find in the PowerPoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really like professor Barany as a person, but this class is literally graded on 4 things: 3 midterms and a book report. The midterms are entirely created and graded by the TA's, so the questions are often confusingly worded and graded pretty harshly. There is also a ton of reading to do. I didn't hate the class, but I wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barany was eh, OK. Not sure if it was just my hate for GOV but I hated this class. Very unorganized and no one communicated anything!! Especially the TAs Thomas and Avery the worst TAs ever!!! This class is a joke. Took it during the COVID-19 pandemic and the TAs were still very tough graders. There are only 3 exams and one paper, so watch the pps

Tests really arent that hard. I didnt attend class after the 2nd wk of school but if you just study the PPTs youre solid. Barany and the TAs dont seem to care at all about this class so if you have something important to discuss, just go to office hours. They probably wont reply to your emails. And dont bother getting the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barany was a good professor and the course material was really interesting. However, the tests were graded unnecessarily hard by the TAs for a core class and averages were low. Your grade is only 3 tests and a paper, so you have to do really well on each to get a good grade. I learned a lot, but I would look for an easier prof for GOV credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a total nightmare. Tests were 80% of the grade and were worded ambiguously to the point they were almost incoherent. TAs are helpful in office hours but then grade impossibly difficult on tests (class average on an exam worth 30% was a 79 in a lower division, core class!) Books have nothing to do with the lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Barany was super cool. He might be a spy. His tests were ok, just don't blow them off - you do actually have to study. Also, you'll have to do quite a bit of reading for a government class...

Dr. Barany is probably my favourite professor I've had at UT. His classes were very interesting, and he keeps you engaged with his wit and humour. Lectures aren't mandatory, but you miss a lot if you skip. Tests are relatively easy, and the TAs host a review session before each one. This class should be an fun, easy A with some minimal effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Tests were based on lectures, readings from books (which were actually very interesting) and films. Lectures aren't mandatory, but if you want to receive a good grade you need to attend them. He's very funny and the tests are easy as they are made by the TAs who have a review session before every test and go over the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He posts all the PPTs online, there's 3 tests, and a paper. The TA's grade everything so I think it just depends on who you have. Our TAs were really nice and funny. Tests are written with the goal for students to do well, however they do put a few random questions on their to make sure people don't get a 100. Paper was only 6-8 pages, very easy.

The lectures are interesting and the content of the class itself, including the readings, are pretty cool. Dr. Barany is funny. That being said, his TAs are a total nightmare. They grade extremely inconsistently. They make the exams easy except for four-five random questions that absolutely do not test your knowledge about the class. Rude too.

Professor Barany is hilarious!! This is his first semester teaching Politics of Poverty (as Gov312L), and it was awesome and intriguing. He posts all the PPTs online, there's 3 tests, and a paper. While the class was super easy, it was clear he enjoyed teaching the class a lot. I loved him/this class so much that I'd definitely take more w/ him!

His gov 312 class is incredibly easy. He just lectures each class & uses power points. You can honestly never go to class and just read the PowerPoint for the test & you will still pass. He only has 4 grades. 3 tests & 1 six page paper. The tests are incredibly easy. The books he chooses for class are also enjoyable. He has a great personality!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Zoltan was a good and funny professor. But my cold war class tests were unnecessarily hard and confusing for a government class. The TA did literally everything except teaching and she wasn't nice at all. Don't take this class if you are not a government student or if you don't want multiple choice questions were like 3 options are alike

Dr. Barany's class was undoubtedly one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken, but his dry sense of humor, extreme intelligence, and willingness to help entirely make up for it.  I would take another class with him, without hesitation

Loved this course.  The readings were interesting, class discussions stimulating, and Dr. Barany was always helpful and available to students.  This is what I thought graduate school was supposed to be like!  You should definitely take a course with Zoltan.  You won't be disappointed.

Extremely smart and pretty funny guy. However, he hates teaching in general and hates students in particular. I was very interested in the topic and learned an incredible amount, but he made no attempt to hide his disdain for teaching, which was disappointing.

Very difficult tests on a hard subject matter.  Excellent professor with limitless knowledge on the subject matter, one of the tops in the govt. dept.  Is willing to help you outside of the classroom.
I thought he was funny.  It is better if you are interested in European government/politics.  Do the reading and prepare for the essay!
He's funny
*sigh*

He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. The class is very useful, and he is willing to answer any questions after class or over email. A few short assignments every week or so, you just have to show up to class once a week and participate.

Professor McKinney's class was incredibly straightforward, well taught, and was always a great person to talk to. Very knowledgeable and passionate lectures. No tests, a couple projects/assignments, mandatory attendance (as part of grade), plenty of extra credit opportunities. Overall, great class and great professor.

Brett was a very caring guy and he's definitely the type to genuinely care about his students. I've learned a lot on this class and I would say I developed some professional skills as well. It can be a bit work heavy since you only meet once a week but overall very easy.

Brett really wants to help everyone in the class, and teaches the course in a way that your resume writing and communication skills really improve by the time you are done. I didn't like the course because there was so much work, and had to do extra credit events to keep my grade up, but nothing against Brett. Very well spoken and great guy.

He is very engaging even at 8 am classes. A lot of homework but all is useful for your career-building process! Gets you familiar with facilities around campus and career coaches. So much extra credit is offered by participating in McCombs events, which can replace your lack of attendance if needed. Easy A!
Loved this guy. 8am class and he made it engaging. So much busy work though. Like some of it was helpful but some of it was just pointless. Lots of extra credit. TA does all the grading.

This class is extremely easy and to some extent the content is a bit go-figure for some but helpful if you dont have much of a business background already. Just make sure to submit all the work on time and you will be fine. There were required attendance checks so show up but theres so much extra credit if you miss a few times.

Take this class!! As a transfer, he explains the basics of everything business-cover letters, resume, networking, interview, etc. As long as you do the assignments and go to class, easy A. TA is very nice when grading. Has EC too if you miss class.

The professor was so engaging and very fun! This class is super easy and helpful for interview tips and preparation, and it is a good foundation for business. There is a lot of extra credit even if you might not need it, but attendance is required. Very easy class, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was nice and seemed to want to help in the classroom, however she is incredibly disorganized and at several points pushed back due dates from the ones listed on the syllabus without announcing it. she took over 2 months to grade our 10 point multiple choice quiz and almost never replied to emails and if she did it took over 2/3 days.

Professor Collins is nice, but it's the grading that really gets you, especially the quizzes. Lectures are super fast (messy notes, hardly any examples), and on your 13 quizzes (60% of your grade), there's only 5-8 questions. Get one wrong and you're cooked— once there were 25 points to a single question. Super picky about anything you write, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Collins was incredibly sweet. She would pause for questions and created a folder for practice problems. She would also post the notes from each lecture with examples, however they might be difficult to understand if you did not attend class. She wanted to remember everyone's name + leave feeling confident in their understanding of statistics.

Dr. Collins was very nice, but beware she is very unorganized. She often times forgot to upload quizzes/homework, and she sometimes responded to emails up to weeks after I sent them. Not a great lecturer either, she rushes through material and doesn't give many chances to practice with examples. I wouldn't recommend taking her if you can avoid it.
she was really sweet and explained concepts really well imo!! seemed like she genuinely wanted to make sure everyone understood the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor was very caring and always willing to explain things. Her Canvas is disorganized and difficult to navigate but it's not that bad once you're used to it. Only downside was that she posts the weekly quizzes Friday morning and makes them due Sunday by 10 pm. So if you have a busy weekend you're sorta cooked.
Lectures were unnecessary confusing sometimes but overall very useful topics. Lecture quality wasn't the best, as it was hard to stay engaged. Exams and homeworks weren't too bad.

Dr Collins stats class is one many CS majors will take. Weekly homework is doable. Lecture slides help a lot with exams, and practice problems are similar. You get a cheat sheet for formulas/notes. The class is fully online except for exams, offering flexibility. Exams are generously graded with partial credit and usually include a bonus question.

Dr. Collins was a really good professor. This class is pretty similar to AP Statistics but even if you didn't take it, it is still super easy to get an A as long as you do the homework and additional practices. However, her posted notes are SO messy sometimes I can't even read what she's writing in class. Make sure to have a friend to get notes!

Dr. Collins is a very nice lady, but I felt like her teaching was very rushed and disorganized. The content itself was easy but I felt I had to just teach myself the majority of it. She flies through her examples and does not upload her lectures online which made learning with her unnecessarily difficult. If you can take someone else you should.

Course isn't necessarily hard but I feel like she manages to make it more complicated than it is. Lectures are long with a lot of talking and disorganized manner of teaching. No time to retain information, she solves problems very fast during class while everyone else is confused. I wish she'd slow down as well as record the lectures.

Super easy content, yet hard class. She's nice but soo hard to get in touch with. The quizzes (tests) are very easy to fail or barely pass and have a super short time limit. They're so picky about the homeworks and labs and I disputed so many of my grades. Her teaching was fine but I hated her late policy, assignments always end up taking longer

PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF. Dr. Collins is really sweet, don't get me wrong there. But she is SOOO disorganized and she isn't accessible outside of class. This was my first (and hopefully only) class at UT that broke me, and its not bc of the content but bc she doesn't explain and the "quizzes" (they are really tests) are so time crunched.

She is very caring and makes getting a good grade pretty easy. However, the class is unorganized (exam 1 grades are still not updated at the end of semester). Lectures are frustratingly inconsistent compared to how simple most of the content is. A step down in terms of quality from Scott, Parikh, Chatterjee but at least your grade will be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A relatively easy class with generous grading schemes. She's very caring and tries her best to help out any student. A lot of reviews say she's inaccessible, but it isn't that bad - she will answer your concerns during class and OH. Sure, the content could be slightly unorganized, but she posts lecture slides + worksheets, which are enough prep!

Nice professor and the material is pretty easy. However, she rarely answers emails or ed discussion, you have to go to office hours to reach her. The class is pretty disorganized and it was clear that the professor didn't have mastery of the material. For example, she would borrow questions from colleagues without understanding the answers to them.

She's sweet but super unorganized due to which our exams were online instead of in-person. Just do the worksheets and hws and you'll be fine for the exams (basically repeats of these questions). The lectures were quite boring and explained things in a more convoluted manner than they needed to - only 10% of the class showed up towards the end
Unbelievably unorganized

Dr. Collins was disorganized: had to push back the test (forgot to book exam room), not posting zoom lectures, and sometimes forgetting to post homework (she did extend the due date). She is a very caring prof and is relaxed on grading,the self-proclaimed "Queen of Partial Credit." Lots of lectures but she walks through the material quite well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was very disorganized this semester, but if you attended office hours and asked questions during lecture it is easy to keep up. I appreciated how she was open to any questions and willing to change deadlines according to student request. Exams and homeworks were relatively easy.
why does she lecture so fast bro... free A tho

Easy but most frustrating class I've ever taken. Professor/TAs completely inaccessible. I sent multiple emails and heard back 3 months later. 2 tests all FRQ are reasonably easy, w/ tons of partial credit. However, lectures are so sporadic and all over the place, w/ slides that are confusingly written. So disorganized, but your grade will be fine.

Professor Collins is good. Lectures were online, not mandatory, but useful; she gives all of her notes in PowerPoints on Canvas. There were 2 exams which are representative of the content but easy if you study a decent amount. Other half of grade is hw. No cumulative final. Only complaint is that she was unbelievably inaccessible outside of class.

Felt like the class was too large or Dr. Collins was too busy as she was not that accessible and often posted homework late. HW was usually pretty quick and 50% of grade so that's nice. Lectures can sometimes be fast or boring but are good if you stay focused and ask questions. Lots of partial credit on tests. Hard to get help from prof or TAs.

Though class was online, content was capable of being learned. On many occasions I started slipping behind because of CERTAIN 429 LABS, but was able to catch up because of the super helpful slides and zoom lectures Professor Collins records. Exams have tons of partial credit; class average even for the worst exam was in the 80s.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I want to be nicer since she doesn't usually teach regular biostats, but she was VERY disorganized. She's knowledgeable in stats but overcomplicates lectures. The TAs are strict on grading for HWs. The class project is easy and for exams, you can make a cheat sheet. I've never taken a stats class before and I never want to again. She's nice though.

Great professor. If I had gone to office hours more my grade would be a lot better than it is now ngl. Collins is very strict with grading the homework but as long as you take detailed notes in class and work all the in class practice problems you can make above a 90 on every last one of them. The research project was tiring but enjoyable.

50% HW and 50% exams is not terrible, and she is very generous with partial credit on exams. However, her lectures feel discombobulated, and she goes fast through problems that I dont even know what I dont know. She seems to not answer to emails or even answer on the question forum we use. Her TAs for this spring were also not helpful

I had Professor Collins for SDS 321 on Zoom for the Spring 2023 semester. First things first, Professor Collins is very knowledgeable, but the biggest caveat is she is not accessible. As someone who is not technically and mathematically gifted, I found it difficult. I felt pretty unsupported while taking this class.

She did not make the curriculum and taught off a pre-made one. In class I understood everything, but then homework could be pretty difficult, and labs every week were kind of annoying. Overall it isn't too bad, but it is just so boring.

Very accommodating and caring. Grade is 50% HW, 25% Exam 1, 25% Exam 2, but there is a lot of partial credit on the exams so do not worry. Sometimes bad with deadlines/waits until the last minute to post things, but she adjusts due dates to compensate. She will help you if you ask for it. Definitely recommend for stats.

Prof Collins was a great stats teacher. Her lectures were recorded which was great for me and her teaching style made it easy to learn. Grade was 50% homework 50% exams. One midterm and one final, she is very generous with partial credit and drops one homework.

Dr. Collins is very caring and an okay lecturer. Due to her sometimes length explanations though, she does have pacing issues and often rushes to finish covering content for exams as students bombard her with questions; she is just too nice not to push questions to office hours (which are limited). Very accommodating and receptive, however.

i took stats in high school (and hated it) but dr. collins made me enjoy stats. she gives engaging examples and helps you understand the concepts (rather than having you memorize formulas & plug numbers into it). however, there was too much work for us to do, and too much for her and the TAs to grade. took a while for grades to be posted

I did not enjoy this class with Dr. Collins. I felt that the entire semester was very hectic in the sense that even she never really knew what was going on, or what she was going to cover that day. She was not super accessible outside of class, and ultimately wasn't much help even when she was. The T.A. for this class was amazing though.

Great professor and really cares about you learning stats. The homework was pretty easy and was a great resource to help prepare for exams. Plenty of practice worksheets and exam reviews were also posted. Found the class really easy and only one small wk per week. Had a couple hiccups adjusting to exams from quizzes, but otherwise a great choice!

GREAT professor, but she decided to switch her course structure this semester to in-person exams and the whole semester has been really hectic. She's very last minute. We used Ed but she never answered any of the questions until weeks later, exam reviews were posted the day before the exam, and she was unclear about the content of the exams.
It's a difficult class, but Sarah Collins does pretty good to get students through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A really great professor that does whatever she can for students. Lectures are not super convoluted, grading scheme is straightforward. Overall, the course is a great experience to learn instead of stress about grades. Even if there were things I didn't understand, Dr. Collins never hesitated to health in class / office hours.

Dr. Collins gives very refined lectures, and is very conscious of her language use when it comes to making sure no one is offended. She is precise in describing things. Very accessible outside of class in office hours and email, and seems to really care about students. One thing that I wish was better is her response speed on Piazza.

Wonderful introduction to stats at UT. Extremely caring and understanding, clear and concise lecture style, and grading system distributes effort across quizzes/homework instead of big tests. Highly recommend
Professor Collins is one of the most caring professors I've had. She is easy to talk to and ask questions to. Her classes aren't mandatory but everything is based on the lectures.
Dr. Collins truly cares about all of her students and puts in her best effort. She's pretty good at teaching and the homework and quizzes aren't too bad.

Dr. Collins is a super accommodating, caring, and relatable prof. She drops a HW and quiz, no exams, and the quizzes are open-note. Most of the HW can be found online to check your work. Very low-stress class and I highly recommend her if you need to take 321. My only critique would be I wish she and the TA were more active on Piazza.
Dropped one HW and one Quiz. Very relatable, really cares about her students. Course felt very fair and never made my life too difficult or frustrating. Absolutely recommend this professor.
Super nice and compassionate. Her lectures didn't really click though.

She's really nice and and explains things thoroughly when asked questions. I liked that she was actually proficient with technology (unlike some of the other math professors), so taking notes was a lot better than other classes. The twice a month quizzes and weekly HWs made the class less stressful than 3 midterms. Really caring prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher, clearly very caring about students and actively seeks to help. Generous with extra credit, and was accomodating even during the pandemic. The first third of the class is review if you have prior experience with stats in high school. Homework weekly (easy), independent project (relatively easy), 3 tests (1 dropped/replaced), no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Collins is one of the best professors I have taken at UT. The class doesn't require the use of books. Because of the whole pandemic situation, she provided some accommodations so that the class doesn't get overwhelmed. I did not have AP Stats experience, so aside from lectures, I watched YouTube vids and her PPTs to cover the material.

Dr. Collins is so nice. She scheduled a special office hours for our class when she realized many of us were unable to make it. Her lectures are good, and you get extra credit for participation. I had some trouble with the latter half, but I hadn't taken AP stats. If you ever need help, her office hours are great.

She's super nice and really cares about her students. Lectures are clear and straightforward, and they are always posted online for reference. She also encourages questions and clarifications. If you have taken AP Statistics in high school, this class covers a lot of the same material. Also gives extra credit for attendance (pre-Corona).

Dr. Collins is the best! I know stats can be challenging sometimes but she breaks it down and doesn't move on until everyone understands. She responds to emails very quickly and encourages you to ask questions. She knows just about everyone's name and truly cares about her students. If you want an easy stats credit take her class!!

Dr. Collins is a gem of a person. She truly cares about her students and is extremely helpful during office hours. She provides tons of material to study with so you don't need the textbook, and often gives points back on exams if you explain your reasoning in office hours. Workload isn't too heavy, and do go to her review sessions before tests.

Professor Collins was awesome! She gives lots of opportunities to end the class with an A. Her tests and projects are graded fairly and she is available outside of class if you need help. Definitely go to class and you'll be fine, textbook isn't necessary. Would definitely take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is a great professor. She knows how to explain the concepts really well so that all students have a clear understanding of what they are learning. You have to attend class, read the textbook (even though it's optional) and do practice problems in order to get an A but it is absolutely doable. I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is passionate about stats, and that makes her lectures easier to understand. However, if you're not a math person (like me) you're definitely going to have to work to make sure that you have a solid grasp on the concepts required for each test. Collins is a wonderful professor, but you'll have to work for the A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite profs! She explains the concepts more than doing example problems, but it was easy to understand & she makes herself available during office hours/email if you need help; she is really open to questions. She uploads review problems before exams, and the online hw wasn't too difficult (you get 2 attempts). Project was pretty easy.

Prof Collins is super nice and very understanding. This course is not too difficult if you show up and pay attention. There is one project that is worked on though out the year but is fairly easy, and it accounts for 25% of the final grade. Test are pretty simple too. Prof Collins always makes sure that everyone understands all class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors so far! Very understanding and caring! If you go into office hours regularly, she'll talk you through mistakes and even give you some points back on test/assignments if you can talk through where you went wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: If I didn't go to class I would have failed the class. She works with you to make sure you understands and classes are really helpful especially if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Most of my class was made up of communications majors, but Professor Collins told us on day one that she would work hard with us so that we could leave the class with an appreciation for statistics. While I don't necessarily like stats now, I definitely am more confident in my ability to learn math than before. Very helpful, and a very kind person.

Professor Collins is super nice and really wants you to do well in this class. She provides may extra credit opportunities in the form of 'upgrades' which place you in a new grade cutoff bracket if you complete them all. She always replied promptly and in detail to my queries over email and always gave ample time for questions in class.
She wont answer your emails until days later! She tends to over explain stuff but if you just watch her rather than listen you will be fine. I am bad at math but did fairly well in her class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She spends a lot of time explaining the math and the concepts behind it rather than just showing you with examples. Overall, the class is not easy but she really cares about helping her students. Making a good grade is definitely doable if you work hard. The projects are very time consuming but the TA is pretty nice with grades.

I took SDS306 Statistics in Market Analysis in the spring of 2016 and it was by far the easiest math related class I've had at UT.   The professor presented the info in a way that made sense and didn't overcomplicate the simple subject matter.  She is very up front and open about grading and what is required to get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The material for the most part isn't bad, but Collins is disorganized, has messy handwriting, and presents unclear lectures. Collins often skims over important material, doesn't hand back quizzes, and is very behind on Canvas and her own deadlines. Her instructions on assignments are also incredibly vague. I regret taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Collins is super caring of her students, if you go to her office hours she will really help you out. It is by far the easiest math perquisite class you could take for CH301. The HW is easy, just skim the chapters before lectures and the class will be a lot easier for you. Extra credit is a life saver. KNOW HOW TO USE EXCEL, YOU WILL NEED IT

Her lectures are long, and I always felt like there were holes in my notes because there were things she wasn't too clear about. She loves when students ask questions, but I honestly did not know what to even ask. The reading confused me. Math was never my strong suit, and her teaching didn't help me at all. Her TA wasn't really helpful either.

Collins' lectures are very long and unclear. She would come to class and start working on an example without saying what statistical test we are learning today.  She also talks very quietly. You also need to know excel. You need to self study for this class for sure and it's a lot more work than it should be, honestly. (I got an A, btw)

I struggled with her class throughout the semester. The book was difficult to understand. There are two separate TA's, one that grades (that you never meet) and one that you can ask questions and talk with. Her lectures were long and mostly unhelpful. Lastly, her tests were usually too long to complete.

Doctor Collins knows her math. Her lectures a long, but she takes her time to explain new concepts and work through problems. I think the most difficult thing was learning how to do all of the calculations by hand. You're only allowed to use a simple 4 function calculator, so doing these long problems was tedious.

Dr. Collins is a really sweet lady! She made me enjoy statistics, and her primary goal is to do just that: inspire a love of statistics in her students. She's very understanding, super helpful in office hours, made stats not too hard. Never had to read the textbook. Some homework, but manageable. Would take her classes again.

Her lectures are somewhat frustrating. She spends a lot of time talking about concepts and not much time explaining how to do the actual math. Also, there's A LOT of work. There are quizzes, homework assignments, an Excel quiz, portfolio projects, exams, a final, and a final project...

Do the upgrades! She offers upgrades to get a better grade (essentially you can get an A with the grade points needed for an A-), so do not skip them! Very helpful in office hours, and tries to get to know the students. The lectures are 90 minutes, but clear-cut on how to do the steps in problems. Great lecturer, very helpful in office hours!

BY FAR, the best professor at UT. He is literally so chill. Go to cyphers, trust me. I was able to build a really personal, mentor-mentee type thing with him by doing that and dude, he gave advice on everything from finance to relationship stuff. Absolutely chill, talks a lot, but it's honestly a good thing. Just don't slack.

I'd say the class is easy to pass, and you can miss some lectures and still do well. The TA this semester was overwhelming and sometimes bothersome, though clearly passionate about the class. The walk can be long, especially if you live off campus, which made it less convenient. Overall, I disliked the class itself but the teacher is engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Carson is hands down THE BEST professor at UT. 100% recommend this class to everyone, especially if you're into hip hop. He also hosts a cypher that lets you get hands-on experience with what you learn in class. Definitely recommend signing up for that too. Dr. Carson is very chill, and I felt very comfortable talking to him about everything.

So easy and such a fun class to learn (it's the history of hiphop). I recommend taking the cipher class as the discussion section because it's so fun learning how to rap. Harder to fail than pass (literally a pass or fail class).

pass or fail class, get 70% or fail (it's impossible to fail tho). don't even need to show up if you don't want. just do the final project (1-2 hours) at the end of the sem to makeup for it tho. he is a funny & passionate professor but at the end of the day you just need the vapa credit, so TAKE THIS CLASS for a free A.
Incredible professor. I highly look up to him for his confidence, conversational and fun lectures, anecdotes on his life. I would love to take more classes with him if possible.

Super easy class basically gives you an A for passing the course. Has multiple weekly readings due before class but they take like 30 minutes tops to complete right before class starts. Do go to sections and participate in them as they care about that. Overall, super easy VAPA recommend for everyone.

Most enjoyable summer class I've taken. Lectures were very engaging and fun while not being too long either. Graded by instapolls (don't have to get them right), weekly discussions that are completion, and weekly open note quizzes. An easy A for the VAPA credit and a great professor. Definitely take this class if you need the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took as an async summer class while working full time. super chill! lectures were actually pretty fun, and no exams. make sure you do your work on time, staying ahead on assignments def made my life easier.

If you're looking for an easy and fun class to fulfill your VAPA credit, I'd recommend Dr. Carson's class. He was a wonderful presenter, interesting to listen to, and readily available whenever I needed him. There are a lot of assignments, but they're easy to do. I recommend getting ahead of the work so it's even easier.

He was a very passionate professor and his lectures were very engaging. You only needed a 70 average on all assignments + participation to pass this course. It may be tempting to skip class, but you will learn a lot by going to every class. If you have space in your schedule, you should take this class. It is a very low stress class which is nice.

An absolutely incredible class. Dr. Carson is clearly passionate about what he teaches, which in turn makes the lectures fascinating. There are multiple weekly reading guides, weekly assignments, and unit quizzes - however if you pay attention in class, they are very manageable.  IF YOU GET THE OPPORTUNITY, TAKE THIS COURSE!

Dr. Carson's lectures were always so fun. He structures the class to where it's impossible to not get an A. Take this class if you want an easy + fun VAPA, there was quite a bit of busy work but it was more or less completion. No midterms/finals, just quizzes that were pretty easy tbh as long as you went to lecture and took notes. Go to cypher!! :)

Dr. Carson is super nice. He is super passionate so, during lecture he may go on weird tangents. Particpation matters but as long as you talk during discussion sections, you should be good.

It is a super interesting class. It is nearly impossible not to get an A.

loved this class. all assignments were basically completion. the quizzes were a little hard tbh but if you use chat gpt you'll be fine. he's super nice and the class is easy as hell. even if you fail all the quizzes you can do the optional final project to make up for it. he's super funny too - if you need an easy VAPA, take him

Loved the class! He's super cool but swears he has a southern accent, lol. Anyway, definitely take the class. You learn a lot about Hip Hop and its roots. If provided the option of a cypher session, do it- they're super fun. Take advantage of the class. Unfortunately, I doubt it'll exist in the near future...

Very interesting class about hip hop history. Prof wore different shoes to every lecture. Nearly impossible not to get an A. Engaging lectures. If offered take the cypher discussion option, you won't regret it
Super easy and interesting class. Carson does seem to have a bit of an ego problem though. Cool shoes too!

Loved this class and Dr. Carson! The course was fully asynchronous and solely graded on participation, weekly discussions, and weekly quizzes. Super easy to get an A as long as you watch all lectures, answer the instapolls, and take good notes. Dr. Carson is engaging and great at simplifying/explaining music to beginners so it's an easy VAPA credit

You have to try to fail in order to fail. He is a very interesting speaker, so  given that most VAPAs are pretty awful/unnecessarily difficult, this is a very good class to learn about an interesting topic, especially compared to the other overzealous VAPA professors trying to prove that their class is indeed relevant.

Took this fall 23'. By far the best and easiest of the music history courses, in terms of material, structure, and lecturer. Dr. Carson is very engaging, and the course isn't set up nearly as terribly has history 1 (and to a lesser extent 2). If you're in 1 or 2 right now, don't worry, it gets better.

be mindful of how much you choose to miss class. while i personally dont think you need to attend every lecture to pass the quizzes; you can't completely ditch because of the 70% threshold. Pretty engaging lecturer and very funny

Music of African Americans is a hip-hop history class. It is extremely interesting whether you are a hip-hop fan or not. I cannot emphasize enough how easy this class is. You just have to participate/show up and essentially have to get 70% in the class to get credit for an A. Carson is funny and his lectures are engaging because he is passionate.

Really cool guy. I think the slightly higher difficulty rating comes from earlier semesters where his grading was different. If this is the only review you read: you only need a 70 to get an A. A nice class to take in-tandem with other more difficult classes since there is not a huge emphasis on grades.
Amazing lecturer and very enjoyable and easy class. Participation is mandatory to do well in class.

Prof Carson is an amazing lecturer, and is genuinely a hilarious guy. He makes it to where its super easy to get an A (extremely lenient grading rubric), where all you need to do is do the quizzes, the readings, and attendance and its a free A. He makes his lectures super interesting, so you actually want to come to class. Totally recommend!!!

The grading criteria is clear, and gives you a generous amount of assignments, lectures, videos, and even quizzes you can miss. Do your work, make it to most classes, participate in class, and you'll get an A as long as all of those are met. The only possible grade he gives other than an A is failing, and this is from the syllabus itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just get above a 70% in 4 parts (attendance, reading guides, assignments, and quizzes), and you have an A in the course, its that simple. At max spent only 20 minutes on this class per week. Dr. Carson commitment, passion, and engagement for this class made me love going to class, and I would 100% recommend this VAPPA. Lots of fun pop culture.
Pretty solid. Lectures were enjoyable and if you paid attention then assignments were really easy. Would definitely recommend

material isnt hard but u have to pay attention and show up. he is super funny and actually passionate abt what he teaches (and the class is actually really interesting imo). grading scale is super easy (u need like a 70% on quizzes, participation, and hw to get an A). just show up and its an easy A. also his shoe game is fire !!

Honestly, this is one of the most interesting classes I've taken here at UT. If you actually do the work and put the time in, you won't be worried at all about what your grade will be at the end of the semester. There is a good amount of reading so just keep that in mind though. Participation is needed to pass as well.

Participation is key. This is an all or nothing class- you get an F or A+. Carson makes the criteria for an A+ very clear, and it's not too difficult to achieve. Participation is a decent part of that criteria, make sure Carson and the TA know your face, talk at least once a week. Also take some notes, he covers a lot of different songs.

Very Straightforward class, if you literally show up to 70% of lectures and discussion and pay attention you will easily get an A in this lass. Dr. Carson was one of the most entertaining professors that I have had at UT, does and amazing job keeping you engaged, very funny.

Carson is very strict about his grading procedures, but if you do all the work, the class is an easy A. He makes it seem very hard, but as long as you earn 70% in 4 categories: quizzes, participation, assignments, reading guides, you will get an A. It is quite hard to find the grades, though. His class is not difficult as long as you do the work.

Lenient grading system that is basically pass fail (70% gets you an A). Def pay attention in lecture to do well on the quizzes. Participation is essential. At times, there was confusion between the prof and TA on participation grading criteria which was stressful, but overall interesting class, good prof & TA, and not too much effort for a VAPA.

Very fun and engaging lectures, the grading system is very lenient and organized. The class is not a burden on your time, just engage to some degree in the material. TA was awesome, very understanding and will fight for you if you are showing effort.

I really enjoyed Dr. Carson's class - lectures super were engaging, and the content was interesting. There are 1-2 readings per week in addition to 1 discussion post, so it wasn't too time intensive. However, it's really important to show up to class and take detailed notes to pass the quizzes.

a lot of assignments in this class, I took it as a summer course. The quizzes are hard as most of it comes from random stuff he mentions in lectures. However, you only need a 70% to get full credit. Total of 5 assignments per week; one quiz, 3 reading guides, and a unit weekly assignment. Class wasn't horrible but prof was rude at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Carson is the worst professor at UT. He expects too much and he is so proud of his doctorates degree in music. The whole thing is a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: love the energy and spirit definitely my favorite class ;) just make sure to take notes and you learn a bunch of new aspects to music which is fun

Dr. Carson's exams are very specific to lectures so copy everything he says. His tests are open note and he gives you the entire weekend to take it. His lectures are very engaging both over zoom and in person and the content of the class is very interesting even if you don't know much about hip hop. Take this class for VAPA!!! Easy A.

Professors lectures were never on time, always ended late. 
The quizzes were very specific with questions likely only mentioned once in lecture. Lectures also tended to deviate from the topic.
Good extra credit opportunities. 
Offered zoom or in person lectures.

This is one of the best instructors at UT. Excellent class and not too hard to get an A. Surprised by a lot of these reviews. Maybe some people expected easier based on this being an AFR class(Im an AFR minor so no offense intended), but show up, turn your assignments in on time, participate a little, and youll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course and the assignments are easy with the exception of exams. Even with the lectures recorded, there were quite a few questions that he quite literally never gave a (clear) answer to. Trust me, I rewatched during the open-note exam. He also has a bit of a superiority complex at times and thinks his class is away more important than it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Carson makes you read so many papers and do reading guides for each one. You spend so much time doing those reading guides and they don't raise your grade at all. Your grade is solely determined by quizzes, which are super detailed and unfair for the 50% they take up. This class feels like you are working a full-time job unpaid,
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You probably won't fall asleep during lectures, I'll give him that. HOWEVER, I constantly feel that he doesn't understand the amount of work he gives to his students, and the inflexibility of his class, especially for an online class. If you want to take this for an easy A I suggest you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: doesn't care for the majority of the students. Doesn't explain the lectures effectively and expects you to know it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was highly unorganized and there was no communication really of what we needed to know. Quizzes were based entirely on lectures and his own words. It was really difficult to take notes. He drags you on the entire year making the class hard but then at the end, most people got an A.

Professor Carson is very infuriating. From a very disorganized class with last minute, long assignments he expects you to complete, to berating and mocking students for assignment mistakes that he made, he is a very uncompromising professor who is unwilling to be even slightly accomodating to his students.

He was a great professor with absolute GEMS of TAs on board. Lectures are interesting and easy to comprehend. I took this class online, so I'm not sure how it is in person, but there were tons of reading guides to do. Thankfully, the reading was fairly interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are extremely fun and if you are a fan of hip hop music you will enjoy them a lot. However, this is by far the most unorganized course I have ever taken in my life. Assignments are posted less than 24 hours before they are due, he REFUSES to post lecture slides, and quizzes are entirely based upon small details he briefly mentions.

This class is so interesting - I recommend the class for the content. However, Professor Carson was not always accommodating - he didn't share lecture recordings (including when students had wifi issues) and his quizzes were over small details. The assignment were graded quite late, making the class very stressful. I'd think twice before taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Carson is very knowledgeable about musicology and does a great job breaking everything down for students to digest easily. However, he is heavily opinionated and does not set up room or a safe space for disagreement. Instead, he assumes everyone agrees with him and berates the other side of an issue. Regardless, he is very flexible and helpful.

Carson is a great *lecturer* -- his lectures are interesting and his personality is great. The course itself, however, is pretty bad - if you're looking for sudden homework assignments assigned the NIGHT before the due date, late grades, and overly difficult quizzes, take this class (difficulty still is OK). Way too much effort for a VAPA class.

Don't take this professor. He causes unnecessary stress and is snarky and rude. The quizzes are super hard, and there are long readings and reading guides due before every single lecture. He is funny at times and if you really enjoy hip hop go for it, but I came expecting a fun, interesting vapa and left with a bad grade and a bunch of stress.

Not worth your time. The quizzes are unreasonably difficult and looking at my quiz scores (Bs or Cs) would cause my anxiety levels to spike. The professor is not reassuring and is very sarcastic when students ask genuine questions. Students are expected to meet deadlines but our assignments are graded MONTHS later. Came to learn, left with anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Carson's class is engaging and fun, however, it's far from an easy A as many might expect. The quizzes are absolutely brutal, often testing trivia mentioned very briefly in lecture. More importantly, subjective questions are graded as if they had objective answers, often involving extremely arbitrary concepts (flow, layering, rupture).

Taking this class was the highlight of 2020. Dr. Carson is a great lecturer and the class is very straightforward. There are a total of 5 quizzes which are all totally doable as long as you take some solid notes or are a great listener. Extra credit can literally boost your grade by 5 percentage points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Carson is AWESOME. He is really interested in the material & he easily keeps the class engaged. 5 quizzes (take good notes in class & you will be golden), some weekly readings (interesting & aren't too dense) & a final decoding a hip-hop song. If I could, I would take this class again 100%. Nicest professor & Andy was an awesome TA as well!

Passionate professor, very understanding of the grind of college-life, knows this is a blow-off VAPA for most people and doesn't mind. Lectures are not posted tho, so you must go to class and take good notes or the quizzes will kill you. However, if you are white and/or conservative, you won't always like his political opinions he offers somedays
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Passionate professor who understands what it is like being a student and very understanding that his class is a blow-off VAPA for most students. Extra credit opportunities too My only complaint is he gave personal political opinions a few too many times, so if you are white and/or lean conservative, you will be a little uncomfortable at points.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the class grade setup: 5 Unit Quizzes, Reading Guides over articles assigned weekly (just do them and you'll get a 100) , polls in-class, and a Song Project. Pretty simple class. Just take good notes and you'll pass the online unit quizzes because they are open note. He's pretty funny and cool professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: An outstanding professor. This was my favorite class at UT so far. Every lecture is entertaining and interesting. Dr. Carson is very funny and knowledgeable of hip-hop. Online quizzes, reading guides, and other assignments are simple. A really good choice for a VAPA.

Dr. Carson is hands-down the most fun and consistently engaging professor I have had at UT, and I don't see myself having another class as enjoyable anytime soon. I looked forward to every class. He is super relatable and funny and has a really cool personality. I love hip hop, but I feel the class would be a blast even if I didn't. SO FUN!!
This class so chill. Really gave me a different perspective on hip-hop and made me appreciate it a lot more. Easy A, just do the readings and go to lecture (not mandatory) or go over lecture notes.

5 online quizzes, easy to ace if you take good notes. Show up to class because he doesn't post notes online. Reading guides for completion grades over readings. Super interesting and funny professor, really knows his info and will inspire you to look deeper into hip hop. Get ready to listen to examples of hip hop throughout the ages!

Lectures are always phenomenal and get you really thinking about the socioeconomic factors that played in to hip hop and its tropes. He addressed a wide variety of topics, and always in a very open, energetic and engaging manner. Through this class i got a better ear for hip hop, now that i can look deeper into sampling and the lyrics.

Dr. Carson is a great lecturer. He is extremely excited about the material he is teaching and he makes you excited. He offers so much extra credit you can get well over a 100 in the class. He has unit quizzes based on lectures and a small reading component.

Dr. Carson's class is my favorite I've taken in college. His lectures are funny and engaging. Occasional readings on essays provided through Canvas (no textbook). A midterm, two assignments, four quizzes, and a final project. He gave us one extra credit assignment. Easy to do well if you put in a reasonable amount of effort and go to class often.
