Gave a huge curve on a test, giving many people well over a 100. One midterm and one final, not multiple choice but not difficult if you study. Hilarious lectures that can be off topic sometimes but interesting. Readings about once a week from the textbook with a reading guide. Doesn't take attendance but most of the test info is learned in class.
Taught myself everything. Don't take
His lectures are really pointless, tests are difficult, and he does not teach in class you have to teach yourselves outside of the class. he made me get GPA factory bc he taught so bad.
Lectures are not engaging and are confusing. Exams are tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very nice and kind professor - but the class is SO boring and monotonous and he isn't really great at getting the content across to students especially when it comes to teaching how to use R for our statistical methods. you have to pretty much self-teach everything and hope for the best despite the fact the tests aren't super easy or super hard.

This class is not engaging and is organized poorly. Lectures are mostly discussion and vague which isn't very effective for learning and retaining information. I have to teach myself everything. When I asked for help, he laughed in my face.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring, making an already dry subject even more unbearable. His project grading was quite arbitrary, and he honestly struggles to communicate to his students. BHP will probably  replace him, so hopefully future students have a better experience with the class.

The class was easy as the homeworks, midterm, and final (written by chatGPT) were very easy. He was brought in as a last min replacement and I think he tried his best, but he is a very unengaging lecturer imo. His grading is also very ambiguous and he screwed a lot of ppl on the project. Overall easy class and you can do well with minimal effort

The professor was a last-minute addition and new to this specific course. While the homework and exams were manageable, the reading workload was extremely heavy. I think most of the class just didn't read them and it was fine. The group project felt a bit rushed due to the timing, but the professor was understanding and fair with the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she doesnt teach in class and you have to self learn, and the lectures are pointless and wont curve till the end

She clearly cares a lot about her students and the subject but a lot of the lectures are not very interesting and pretty confusing. You cannot pass this class if you don't understand the material!!! I had to re-teach myself most of the stuff. She's very strict but kind, I liked her a lot but she's not for everyone.

I am taking M302 and it is possible the worst decision I could have made. After most of the class failing the first exam, she refused to take accountability. She does not teach well and the worksheets given are basically pointless (even though they are supposed to help with the homeworks). The exams have stuff on there that the practice exams dont.

If you see that everyone is giving bad reviews and theres a couple 5 stars with A+'s understand that these are the outliers. DO NOT LISTEN TO THEM. Save time and do ACC do not try with UT. They do not care I promise.

Cabrera didn't have control over test curves or know what was on the tests so I give her that, but she was just not good at teaching. I would not recommend Cabrera unless you're prepared to do every single homework problem (theres lots of homework) and more practice problems because that, and my goated TA Justin Le was what saved my life.

M408L is a coordinated class, curves test difficulty etc isn't up to the professor, which nearly all of the bad reviews are complaining about. She is kind, wants students to succeed, and advocated for us to get the final to replace 2 exams rather than one. Her lectures are fast I found them useful to understand the content before going deeper alone
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Acts like its a chore to help students when they don't understand a concept. Treats her students with no respect at all and gets a lot of her own work wrong. Do not take this class unless you really want to struggle and teach yourself for the whole semester. Also very obvious she has favorites, clear to see in person and through the 5 stars here.

Very nice and helpful professor. She gets a bad rep because the class she teaches is hard and class structure is not under her, but up to the math department. Overall, office hours are very helpful, and she will try her best to negotiate with MA dept. to help students. Lectures can be hard to follow sometimes but she is more than willing to help.
Useless lectures that are hard to follow. Better to teach yourself. About half of the original class dropped

Dr. Cabrera is such an amazing professor. She is so passionate about mathematics. Exams are modified homework. Definitely not an easy A because of the nature of the material. Don't let spoiled high school children discourage you. I love her and love her class!

She overcomplicates everything and goes extremely fast all the time. This ended up being a self-taught course but even then the exams were extremely hard and count for majority of your final grade so even missing some questions already drops your grade by a lot. No extra credit, no drops nothing.

Exams are pretty hard. You have to REALLY master the material to get >80 (B-). Exam mean did not get past 65% in all 3 midterms. The worst part is that exams are the majority of your grade. HW doesn't contribute much. Office hours and classes left me more confused so I relied on YT and Sanger Learning Center. Get ready to obliterate your GPA.

Calc is a hard class, but her lectures and office hours are helpful! She explains better than some module lectures, and if you go to office hours, she explains the concept. But you have to actually do work, she doesn't spill the answer, but guides you. The class has a coordinator, so it's not up to prof. cynthia to decide if there's curve. Go to OH

Even with tutoring, office hours, and tons of studying, the class still didn't click. The course design is just not effective. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone unless you're already very strong in the material and able to self-teach the entire semester.

Cabrera is such a sweet woman. I understand she is not the greatest teacher, but she is so caring. Yes, her class was time consuming, but if you put in the work it is not that bad. I had to teach myself most everything, but if you actually show up to class it is not that bad.

I have taken calculus before, but I have no idea how her exams are this difficult. Even if you miss a few questions your grade is gone. Even if she curves at the end, most people will end up with Bs and Cs. I highly suggest you dont take this class.

reviews.comment: This course caused more stress than any class I've taken. I spent hours studying every day and still barely understood what was going on.
The workload was overwhelming and didn't seem to contribute to actually learning the material. Just busywork on top of confusion.
There was no transparency in grading, no feedback on mistakes, and no real way to understand how to improve. Extremely frustrating.
The exams felt disconnected from what was covered in lecture. Even when I thought I understood the material, the tests were completely different.

reviews.comment: Start making deals with the devil or sell your soul because thats your only hope in passing this class and this comes from a straight A student who had to pass fail this class.

Cabrera is genuinely caring and sweet, but she cannot teach calculus to save her life. She seems like a math major who never wanted to teach but ended up teaching due to a lack of opportunity (I assure you it isn't for the money, instructors make terrible money)
I would strongly recommend taking calculus with someone else.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. She does not care about her students, half of them have to Q-drop the course/stop showing up. Her class is a joke. She doesn't know how to teach, so expect to teach it all on your own. You can study all day everyday and still not pass. DO. NOT. TAKE. HER. for your mental health.

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to follow and she overcomplicates everything and goes extremely quickly. Need to learn the material on your own and exam formats are terrible. Don't take this class for your mental health. You will study everyday of the semester just to fail. You don't even know what you are studying for. She doesn't do anything in class. I don't know how she sleeps at night knowing she taught nothing to her students. Goes to show the UT Math department is a joke.

Her lectures are basically pointless to attend, its pretty much a self-study class. The average grade in our class on tests was never above a 55%. Zero curve was given, only the chance for the final to replace an exam if the final was a better score(which isn't guaranteed because usually the final has a lower average than the normal midterms lol).

reviews.comment: Her bad reviews are getting down and thats why she's UP to a 2 but you will struggle so much in this class and study so much just to get a horrible grade in the end the homework, learning modules, and discussions will carry your grade but each tests are still 54 percent not including the final the tests are nothing like what she teaches in class.
Homework feels simple, but the exams are like a different class. She tests the smallest details that were never covered. You'll walk out confused and wondering if she even reviewed her own material.
No curve, no extra credit, no flexibility. You can study nonstop and still fail because of how bad her exams are. She makes learning stressful instead of rewarding. Worst experience ever.
She doesn't explain topics well, skips steps, and assumes everyone already knows everything. The tests are random and way harder than any homework or review. Complete waste of time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She replaces your lowest test grade with the final, but I would assume the final is even worse. It's not a safety net it's a trap. Tests make up most of your grade, so one mistake and you're done for.

She changes homework dates constantly, so you'll miss deadlines unless you check every hour. Tests are brutal and don't match what's taught. Easily one of the most disorganized classes I've ever taken.

She doesn't teach or care about student success. The lectures are useless, reviews don't match the tests, and the exams are way harder than anything practiced. No curve or help take someone else if you want to survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the worse professor you can ever take she does not do a good job teaching, and her exam review material is nothing like the test I genuinely think she enjoys seeing us struggle there are no curves or extra credit given you will struggle in this class and it will mess up you GPA

DONT TAKE HER CLASS I have never taken exams so hard there is no way you can pass them the material she teaches and the homework are such a big gap from the tests unless she curves grades at the end you won't pass with a good grade or barely will

She does not teach or provide material that is helpful to study for tests yes there is practice problems but those are either you get it of not there is not work to help you understand it and sometimes the explanation on learning modules are wrong too so you won't understand correctly this is a difficult class and tests will kill you.

I am a straight A student and I have never struggled so much in a course she is not a good professor at all you have to self teach and it is so hard you can do the learning modules easily but its still a lot of work though but her tests are so much harder and the homework are horrendous too just avoid this class unless you want to ruing your GPA.

Just don't take the class for your own good test are so difficult and will have you stressing and she doesn't curve is she at least curves you overall grade at the end you would have a change this class is a GPA tanker and you will regret taking her she does not teach at all her TA's are still somewhat helpful and lowkey better at teaching than her

This class is horrible and so difficult for no reason you can study all you want for literally weeks in advance and you will still fail you can do all the homework and still fail you can go to class go to discussions and office hours and you will still fail there is not passing this class she doesn't give extra credit or curves on tests

She's absolutely horrible do not take her this class makes me want to end it all she does not teach so much work and the tests are insanely hard you have to self teach yourself and you will fail these test do not take her avoid at all costs

The quality of this class is terrible… 1. She's terrible at explaining so you end up learning on your own. 2. Exams are all MCQ for long questions meaning the likelihood of mistakes are high yet you don't get partial credit. 3. Averages are low on exams yet there's no curve. I transferred here and I was stunned at how bad calc classes are here.

Professor Cabrera clearly cares about the class and subject, but isn't very good at conveying the topics. I attended every lecture and I simply learning nothing. I relied on outside material and used the class mostly for the occasional practice problems. She's a very nice, sweet, and passionate professor, just not incredibly effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for M408D RMP doesn't have that option.Genuinely, the worst professor I have ever had. The way the class is organized is ridiculous, the discussions were not worth going to, and the final was far harder than the midterms. Only 3 eight-question midterms with no partial or extra credit. Horrible lecturer. Doesn't care about students' success.

I like Cabrera; she's dedicated to teaching and available for office hours. Tests and assignments are multiple choice. You teach yourself the lesson before class, but she explains it well. She often says "you following" which gets annoying but ensure understanding. She's nice but slow to respond to emails, so CC the TA for quicker replies.

She literally does not care. She never responded to emails, all tests were like 15 MCQs and all exams were about 90% of our final grade. Class averages were approx 60% on every exam yet she didn't change anything or give any extra credit. Only her curve (which wasn't guaranteed) saved us in the end. She's a menace.

reviews.comment: She's incredibly sweet and you can tell she loves her job. However, she's not a good teacher. About 1/5 or of her students actually go to lectures because they're unhelpful, she's a confusing lecturer. Time is spent super inefficiently. If you reach out to her personally, she'll try her best but you'll have better luck self-teaching in this class.

****For 408D ****

Just not a class you want to be in. 3 learning modules, a homework assignment and a packet due every week, only worth 15% of total grade. Just an insane amount of time spent on something that is worth nothing. Discussion were not collaborative at all. Also you were very limited to the questions that you can ask the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good person bad teacher. Doesn't record lectures and accent PMO. Homework nothing like test be ready to self study bc the hw and learning modules suck. No extra credit and no curve.

Professor Cabrera was not the best lecturer (although she clearly puts in a lot of effort). The positive of this class was that the exams were quite easy if you can do the homework questions without much difficulty.

She is sometimes hard to understand and sometimes makes the problems harder than they need to be. If you watch the videos on quest and take notes on then you will be fine. May need to watch YouTube videos on certain concepts when it gets harder at the end.

She cares but she sucks at teaching. The amount of homework for this course was also way too much. Tests were also very inconsistent in difficulty meaning some only needed an hour or two of studying were others needed weeks of prep to get even a C. Would NOT take again

Cabrera is the sweetest woman, but she can NOT teach! She constantly got problems wrong in class and gave no curve even when test averages were failing; the only redeeming quality is that the final replaced a test grade (then changed to two test grades). I only passed this class by having previous knowledge of the topic. AVOID IF YOU CAN!!

Don't get me wrong, Professor Cabrera is a very sweet woman- but I could not learn from her. I attended office hours and TA office hours; if you did not have a specific question, then it was of no help. I would be stuck on whole concepts and wasn't given the opportunity to understand them with her or the TAs.

Professor Cabrera is incredibly caring and engaging. The coarse is standardized and easy to follow if you keep up with the learning modules. She was always checking in with students and relieved our stress before exams. I would highly recommend taking her classes!

She was very kind but often makes mistakes during lectures that make it hard to understand new concepts that you're learning for the first time. I stopped going to lectures and really struggled with this class because it seemed like I had to teach myself the material.

The class is lecture heavy except the professor is not a good lecturer at all. She is super nice but it sucks that her teaching is more often confusing and not helpful. Stopped going to lectures halfway through the semester and only used notes from my senior year in highschool.

Mrs. Cabrera was a chill teacher who is very passionate about teaching. However, the class itself is pretty challenging because of the tests and homework (she does not have any control over them). The tests were very similar to the reviews so make sure to go over those. The discussion classes are skippable.

Most of the course structure/ exams is set by the department. She leaves a LOT of class time after teaching material for practice sets (similar to hw/ exams) where you can ask as many questions as you want. Also she's the only professor I had this semester that actually tried to connect with students.

I think Dr. Cabrera did the best she could with what she was given but the class seemed like you were set up to fail unless you did really good in precal/calculus in high school. Dr. Cabrera was super caring and wanted to make sure we understood the content but some things were not explained very well. Not a horrible choice for calculus.

By far the most caring professor I've had this semester! She will explain things 5 times if needed and will stay after class to help you. Very reasonable with her grading criteria (reevaluated letter grade cutoffs after seeing final scores). There is a lot of homework but it's honestly for the best because the extra practice is much needed!!

Very sweet professor, horrible at teaching. As someone who had no previous experience with calculus, her teaching style made everything seem more complicated. ChatGPT and Youtube were the only things that pulled me through. Averages on exams were low and the final is ur saving grace. If you can take this class with someone else, do it.

Professor Cabrera is a kind and caring person that holds a great understanding of mathematical concepts. More than 50% of your grade is three midterms, which are often quite difficult/tricky. While her lectures can be useful at times, it is best to teach yourself outside concepts for the best test results. Taking her isn't peak, but not too bad.

She is super sweet, but her lectures are confusing and unhelpful. Attendance is not mandatory and honestly not advised. The class is essentially self-taught and your grade will depend on the exams and the final.

Professor is very kind but does not teach well. I had to learn everything on my own and had a very difficult time understanding. Spent hours studying and was not able to do good. Final is mandatory and it is the only way you can save your grade which did not work for me.

If you do not need to take this class, just don't. She is a super sweet person, but can not teach. You have to learn everything yourself. As someone who took calc before it was hard to follow her teaching. I just watched my old hs teacher's videos to learn.

If you can, take this credit in CC, she makes everything overcomplicated. Practically had to learn everything through youtube. Exam are majority of class so if you mess up, theres only the final to help you.

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher but since I had already taken calculus before the class was easy do not recommend to anyone trying to get a good grade there is no extra credit and your fate is sealed after the first two exams.

She is a very kind and caring professor, but horrible at teaching. She can not explain concepts well at all. I made a great grade in this class, but I had to teach myself everything. Averages for exams were in the 60-70 range. Don't take her unless you are going to put the time in to teach yourself. Our TA wasn't helpful at all either.

By far the best professor I have ever had, she was attentive and willing to explain something 3 times if it was needed to grasp a concept. Fairly lecture heavy but the homework assignments are fairly easy as long as you pay attention in class and stay on topic.

She is a sweet professor.That is the only positive quality of her teaching style. The "discussions" are a waste of time and the content we work on in those classes is meaningless compared to what we learn.On our second test of the year, there were about 4 questions that we had never seen before and the average grade was a 58 FOR THE WHOLE CLASS.

She is a lovely person who cares about her work, however, she is not a good professor. She overcomplicates simple concepts and underexplains the more difficult ones. Exams are weighted heavily making the other assignments seem unimportant even when they take a lot of time. I would recommend avoiding her and taking calculus with another professor.

Just horrible at teaching, nice person and passionate at math, but she makes so many little mistakes while teaching it makes someone who already took calculus worse at calculus. Would not recommend. If you get this teacher I would recommend self teaching and tutors. Good luck.

Professor Cabrera is obviously very passionate about teaching. But she consistently gets practice problems wrong and explains concepts in overly complex ways. If you can do well with this teacher that means you already took calculus or you completely learned the course on your own time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Getting in contact with her is very hard. She overcomplicates subjects, and her lectures are very hard to understand. Many of the assignments you do seem unrelated to what you are learning. In addition, on the tests, there is a lot of material that you will feel like you never learned. Take calculus with someone else.

He is really good at teaching and provides plenty of resources to study with. I had him for statics and solids and liked him for both. The tests can be difficult, so prepare in advance. He takes "cheating" on attendance very seriously. There are weekly quizzes with two drops and 4 exams with scaled weighting.

I struggled a lot in Statics, but Landis' grading scale really helped. A C was around a 65, so even low exam scores counted. The class isn't easy, but many still got A's and B's. He provides lots of past exams and quizzes. He seemed grumpy a lot times due to cheating scandals in our class and sending attendance codes.., but overall he's fair.

Take Landis! His class is very well organized & he provides all the material you need to succeed. dont take early semester warnings lightly-- falsely filling the attendance form is -5 pts off overall grade. exams are fair, study at least 4 most recent past exams and you'll be set. but expect to put a little more effort in for exam 3. quizzes are ez

Landis makes this class so approachable. Do the optional homework! The course is manageable until after exam 2, then you need to lock in. Landis provides great resources. Take ownership and stay engaged in lectures for an achievable A. Content is challenging, but Landis breaks it down well.

THE GOATTT. As someone who barely passed eng physics 1, I learned so much from this class and did surprisingly well despite being worried. Loved this class so much I signed up for his solids class next semester, and super excited. The material is difficult sometimes, but he provides an ABUNDANCE of HWs, past quizzes, and past exams.

He is a great teacher and organized in the notes he takes. Provides more than enough resources to help you be successful. The attendance and quiz policy is pretty forgiving. The tests are difficult, but that's just how statics is.

By far the best engineering professor at UT in my opinion. Very organized lectures, always guide students to fully understand the materials. Course contents are incredibly accessible outside of class; Past Exams, Quizzes, and Notes. 5 Weeks, 4 Midterms, 1 Final, 5% Attendance grade. Time challenging, but do a ton of practices, you will get the A.

Professor Landis is a awesome professor. His class is very clearly laid out and there is a clear path to get an A in his class. He does problems that are very useful to quizzes and tests. Never did the HW once. Couple times throughout the semester he would pause the recording and tell the people in person insight on the test.

Had for statics and solids and highly recommend. 4 midterms, weighted 30/25/15/10% depending on how well you did on them. Weekly quizzes. Has lots of resources (past exams and quizzes) - definitely do them to do well!

Landis is THE solids professor to take. His lectures are really easy to follow and teach you everything you need to know for tests/quizzes. He's also incredibly resourceful and organized: you have access to all material types from previous years. Super friendly and one of my fav professors so far!

Dynamics is hard, so you will need to practice alot. But Dr. Landis provides alot of material to help you do so.

Overall, great professor and learned alot.

Dr. Landis is a very good teacher in my opinion. He talks about theory first usually and then gets into example problems.

Provides previous years materials, which is great for quiz and exam preparations.

Grading is mostly made up from exams, but practice a-lot and it will be worth it.

Attendance is not mandatory, but go to class!

Very "Solid" professor, who gives great lectures with logical sense. Every lecture is recorded, tons of previous exams/quizzes with explaination videos. Does a high(30%) to low(10%) performance grading for exams, drop 2 lowest of the weekly quizzes. Make sure to look for details from the current lecture notes and practice a lot, you will get an A!

His lectures were a little disorganized but still helpful. He overall provides a very good foundation for statics for the EIT exam. I went out of this class feeling very knowledgeable about statics. His office hours were not that helpful as he acted irritated at every OH i went to but his class was structured very fairly and difficulty was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Always plays music before class. The class is hard, but as long as you attend lectures, do the optional homework, and do all the tests and quizzes from the previous years (they go back to like 2007), you should be ok. Your grade will be from only quizzes, midterms, and the final. But he does give partial credit on all.

started at basics so dont be worried if you barely passed physics 1. lectures are recorded but def attend in person, learned better that way. study very hard for the quizzes and exams, it kind of builds up if you don't. lots of partial credit on the exams (final answer almost doesn't matter), based on the methods. weekly quizzes are like hw

Dr. Landis provide students with a solid foundation to further success in other EM courses such as solid mechanics. Being said, his course is not gonna be an easy one. Homeworks are practice only, no grades. Weekly quizzes are 20% of the total. And 3 midterms are 15-25% depending on the performance. He does curve at the end of course by endeavor.

Great lecturer. Statics is a tricky class for most, but Landis is good at breaking down hard concepts and making them easy to understand. He gives you access to all his past exams and quizzes, as well as tons of HW problems which makes studying easy. HW isn't graded, instead grade comes from exams, a final and weekly quizzes. Don't expect a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy horrible teacher. Does the easiest examples possible gives tests with the weirdest setups. Atleast other horrible teachers recognise that and give curves to balance that out but so far no curves and doesn't look like any curves will be added for the final or the total grade. Again awful teacher but good personality. 24 Fall

Great professor who explains hard concepts in a way that makes them easier to comprehend. Solids is hard, but he has extra videos and past tests that rly help. He records all his lectures too. No final, just 4 midterms weighted based on your performance, making it a pretty easy A. HW can be hard but they're not graded. Overall would def recommend
Organized notes from professor; no textbook; lots of past exams and quizzes to use as resources; weekly quizzes; recorded lectures; overall great professor just the content is a bit hard at times
Great lecturer and very helpful during office hours. Midterms and weekly quizzes are okay as long as you do the homework.

Top tier professor at UT. His lectures can seem daunting at first, but if you closely pay attention to them, they are extremely helpful for practice. Provides more than enough resources for test prep, like optional homework and past midterms on Canvas. Grades exams pretty leniently too.

Great lecturer and cares about teaching his students properly (constantly asks for feedback during lectures). Homework is very helpful for weekly quizzes. Make sure you do well on all assignments because only the weekly quizzes, midterms, and the final count for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Optional homework, but will help prepare you for weekly quizzes. He gives you past quizzes and exams and all the material you may need. Very organized. He's a funny guy but has a bit of a sassy attitude sometimes. Comes in clutch with the final grade adjustments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His lectures were in depth but easy to understand. His past tests he has on canvas help you prepare for the exams.
lectures are really good; homework is optional but really helpful; lots of resources from past years quizzes, exam, and homework
Dr. Landis is an amazing lecturer! He breaks down the content in a way that is clear and easy to understand! There are weekly quizzes, however they reflect the material in class and on the homework.

Landis is genuinely one of the best engineering professors at UT! He explains Solids in a way that makes it extremely easy to understand, and his tests feel fair. There are weekly quizzes based on assigned (but ungraded) homework. Overall, Landis is the Solids professor to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Landis eats as a solids professor. He's very clear in his lectures and expectations regarding what we need to know for exams. I did find that he did a lot of deriving of the equations and such which can be nice, but it was mostly lost on me, and I only felt confident after we did practice problems. Just do the past exams and hw & you'll do good
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely important. It isn't the type of class you can get by with youtube ad such. He has a specific way of explaining and asking for things in problems that you wouldn't be able to solve unless you watch his lectures. Past exams are your bff for exams. Quizzes are the hw (15%). 3 exams, 15, 20, 25. final 25%. solid choice for prof.

Class material might be difficult, but his lectures are detailed and all recorded. All exams from previous years are provided as well. Textbook is optional. He works hard to make sure his students are successful. One of my favorite professors I've had during my time at UT.

Put in the work and you will do well. Dr. Landis is a decent professor but the course material is the type where you have to learn it for yourself to pass the exams. Use the resources and past course material to help you study and prepare for the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Landis can come of as a bit rude at times, I liked his teaching style and his overall sense of humor. He spent a ton of time at the beginning of the year on the fundamentals of the course, and this made the rest of the course fairly easy. He is one of the harder professors though, and some of his exam/quiz questions were difficult.

Dr. Landis can come across as rude often times, but in reality he is a very good professor who cares a lot about the understanding of his student. If you cannot make it to lecture, DEFINITELY watch his lectures online. I found his videos especially helpful for the exams and utilize the past exams, because he tends to make the exams similar.

I never give a 1 for difficulty, but this was THE easiest class I have taken so far in college. The concepts are all the same throughout the course, whether it be 2D or 3D. I honestly don't get how people struggle in this class. Chad is very clear in his lectures. Lectures go a little slow, but that's good for working ahead. Do HWs and you're set!

Dr. Chad Landis is a really good teacher if you're already a statics expert. He assumes that everyone knows statics already, and does a terrible job explaining concepts. The lectures are a waste of time, with most of the time dedicated to examples of concepts we never learned. This class (professor and TAs) degraded me and made me lose brain cells.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a good professor that knows what he's doing and is willing to answer questions during class. But go to him in office hours, and he makes you feel stupid. Very condescending. Yes, he does give you his past exams but that only means his tests are challenging; you better know the material. thankfully, no surprise questions on exams.

Landis is the goat. He truly explains concepts and then does examples to further cement them in your brain. If someone says this class was hard, then they're dumb or lying. This class becomes insanely predictable when it comes to what's on the tests and quizzes. Go to class to get 'hints.'
really cool
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's sad this is a required course for many, and even sadder that Landis is supposed to be one of the better professors. Statics is difficult and Landis somehow makes it way harder. In addition, there is no mc, only free response on quizzes and tests so if you're not prepared, you can't even guess, you're just screwed. He's very condescending too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never been strong in physics, however after taking statics with Professor Landis everything has clicked! He primarily taught by going through examples, which I found extremely helpful. As long as you work through the homework's and practice tests properly the class is relatively straight forward.

I did really well in this class because it was very straight forward. I went to class, studied for weekly quizzes, practiced for tests. If people say this class was hard, it's because they didn't go to class. He's a caring prof and a good lecturer. Content is pretty easy, but the problem solving can be tricky. I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Landis is easily one of the best professors I've had. While Statics is by no means an easy A, Dr. Landis makes the course material accessible to those who may have struggled with similar subjects in Physics I. He provides all of his past exams and quizzes and lets you know what's expected on tests. Really generous with partial credit. 10/10

Chad lives up to his name as he made me understand physics for the first time in my life. This glorious man provides so many resources and study materials and he sets you up to succeed in his class. Statics is a hard subject, but Chad is very good at lecturing and explaining. You can succeed in his class if you learn how to use the study materials.

Second time through Solids (Q drop) and I can definitively say Dr. Landis is the best. His lectures are very thorough, and he makes sure everyone knows what's going on. Homework is optional but not really if you want to do well. The tests are much harder than the quizzes but not unbearable, just make sure to do the homework.
rough experience

Landis is a great prof. Statics requires work, but Landis gives you YEARS worth of old tests with detailed solutions. If you spend the time to work the problems, you'll do great. There's really only seven concepts in this class, but they take work. On the exams, the name of the game is PARTIAL CREDIT. He is generous on test grading.

Statics can be a difficult class if you don't keep up with the content. Homework is only for extra practice so your whole grade depends on quizzes and exams. Prof Landis does multiple example problems in each lecture and highly encourages students to participate and be confident in their analysis. Do old exams to excel in class.

Dr. Landis provides you with a lot of resources including past exams and textbook problems. If you keep practicing the past exams you'll do great the upcoming exams as they are structured the same way. Lectures are pretty useful but he goes pretty fast so I'd recommend redoing the lecture problems on your own time as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are no surprises from Dr. Landis. If you take notes and do your practice problems, you'll do great. For Statics, Dr. Landis provides plenty of example problems and all the tests from past years. Lectures are very easy to understand and Dr. Landis will always answer questions for confused students. Easy reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Landis is a great teacher and explains concepts pretty well. The problem is the structure of this class. It is really tailored towards people who enjoy self-learning physics. Homework is 0% of your grade and the entire grade is based off of tests and quizzes which means it is up to you to generate your own motivation to study this tough content.

The class itself was very boring, if you don't pay attention, you will fail. Has 2 midterms and one final for a 4 week- summer class. Is a terrible grader, and isn't sympathetic as a teacher even if you're going through mental issues that hinder your learning. Do as many practice problems as you can.

Landis was a solid choice for Dynamics. This was his second time teaching it at UT but he makes ALL his old tests from previous universities available. Homework is optional, but you should really do it if you want to do well on exams. PS: This is engineering; dynamics is not easy. Take some reviews on here with a grain of salt :)

Landis is a phenomenal professor. Provides access to his old exams and is all about learning through solving problems instead of talking about theory for the entire lecture then saying, "Good luck." Also records his lectures so if you need to go back to understand something you can. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Chad Landis is a great option for statics. Yes the class is hard, but Landis is an outstanding lecturer who really cares about the success of his students. He explains materials, does review for every exam, solves practice exam problems for the class. He gives you all the resources to succeed. Only con, The TA sessions are useless and 2 hours.

Chad the Dad is a cool guy. Yeah, it was hard waking up at 9 am sometimes but I learned a lot during lecture. He pretty much just goes over past problems he has created and they are all on Canvas. Def do the homework to grasp the concepts. TA sessions sucked but they are very lenient with grading midterms.

I hated statics with Landis. He was a boring lecturer at 9am, and mostly did practice problems instead of teaching material. The TAs were hopeless, and the discussion sections were material-based but extremely boring. The quizzes were relatively straightforward, but if you weren't on top of the material, you'd get a bad grade. DO THE HW to learn!!
Definitely have to work for the grade in this class, but Landis is a great lecturer and is always open to questions. Definitely practice all the past exams he posts and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Explains all of the material very well, and ensures that he has every exam he's ever given out available far ahead of time. Some exam questions were taken directly from his past exams. Weekly quizzes given out during discussion sections, taken directly from weekly homeworks. Lectures move quickly but he explains everything in great detail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chad is such a dad. He is a great lecturer and posts all of his past tests to Canvas so it is really easy to study for the exams. He is very receptive to questions and clearly loves teaching, so this class was enjoyable.

Amazing. His lectures are very organized: explains the basics of the topics then does several examples. If you do the homeworks and practice exams he gives you, the exams are easy. He often uses past exam questions so if you don't have time to do every one, at least look at his solutions for each one so if it's on the test you will have seen it.

Great Professor. He seems to genuinely want everyone on the same page, and cares for his students. Was struggling but he helped me out and recognized that I was really trying. Easy to pay attention to, really entertaining, clear and funny.

Chad Landis? More like DAD Landis. This guy was awesome. The material was presented in an interesting and engaging manner, making it a pleasure to show up to class everyday. Tests are fair and pertain to what you learn in class. Homework is optional, but helps you with quizzes and further understanding. I HIGHLY recommend my dad.

Dr. Landis is an awesome professor. He's a nice guy, has a sense of humor, and definitely knows what he's talking about. I had him for both Statics (E M 306) and Solids (E M 319). Only downside is that he doesn't do +/- for grades. I would've ended up with a B+, but was bumped to a B since he doesn't round up. Also has really good taste in music.

Landis is a wonderful professor! His lectures explain difficult concepts in a crystal-clear way. He posts his notes and past exams online and is very helpful during office hours. His grading is generous, and you won't be significantly penalized for careless errors. The class is by no means trivial, but he's the best professor you can take.

Makes you learn in class, easy to concentrate/take notes with his immersive style of teaching. He's there for you and makes a point about it. The tests may be hard but they are fair. All his resources are posted online for you to use. My only complaint is that the homework and weekly quizzes are easy and don't prepare you for tests.

To be fair I went into this class thinking it would be an easy A and rarely studied, HOWEVER compared to the practice problems you do in class and TA sessions the tests are WAY more complex. However Dr. Landis is quick to respond to emails and his tendency to cover all aspects well is a real treat.

Great professor! Sometimes gets a little lost in the algebra, but who wouldn't? Tests are doable, if you prepared for them. Weekly quizzes, except for test weeks, and drops 2 of them. HW is optional. Gives students access to his old tests and finals with the solutions. Great guy.

Landis is an awesome dude. Super funny, and an extremely good teacher who obviously has a lot of experience.  He doesn't throw curve balls, and his tests are very straight forward, but the material progressively gets more difficult.  The first test is insanely easy, GET 100% ON IT.  They get harder and harder, and the third test is pretty hard.

Dr. Landis is a smart guy. His lectures have a lighthearted, comfortable air about them. Exams are just about the right difficulty for engineers. Helpful; HW problem solutions are posted from the get-go. His explanations are clear, and his example problems are usually pretty well thought out and fairly representative of exam questions. Recommended.

He is a knowledgeable guy, however, his TA's as well as him all have a smug atmosphere about them. It makes a large class even more intimidating especially when the people who are supposed to help you out are so condescending when you don't quite understand a topic. I would suggest a different professor for this class.
Lots of real-life examples discussed in class

This is surely the most difficult course I've ever taken at UT. He likes challenging students, so be ready. He does unannounced pop quizzes any time during the lecture so you actually have to pay a lot of attention. This was a very hard class but also very practical. the only class in which I've seen how things actually work in reality.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take this class if you want to learn valuable and applied things. This is not an easy class so dont expect easy exams and homework. But it is all worth it because the class is one of the very few in the program that is based on actual engineering examples of application. Be prepared to be challenged.

Overall great instructor and very well organized course with lots and lots of practical examples. Very good solution sets. Subject matter is hard but it is what we expect in a professional setting. The instructor organizes a field trip. Highly recommended

Hes a great professor that really wants the entire class to engage and learn. Exams are hard, but if you understand the material you will be fine! Go to office hours, he is even better explaining one-on-one. He is accesible after class, super funny in lectures and tries his best to be as resourceful as possible to optimize students learning!
Wow, one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. You learn so much from this professor, but he is an all around great person. This class kicked my ass, but is extremely relevant to our major.

This professor really cares about teaching. He has a binder full of practical examples that he uses to teach. He writes summaries for each lecture. Exams are aligned with homework. Great TAs. Excellent solution sets. Field trip included.

Great instructor and very well organized. He teaches practical knowledge and designs the homework and exams to be complementary. Nice person. Very helpful. Optional field trip and visit to core facilities. Cares about students.
Excellent professor

Any comment regarding something outside of his agenda will get you a roasting in class. He does not have structure in his lectures so if you miss a day good luck. The grading is really subjective and people will get points with the same range and procedure as you but you might get zero. Super smart guy, but horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you challenge him and ask for more clarification he gets mad at you and calls you lawyer. Very unprofessional! There is no book and you are forced to purchase his lecture notes. These notes are awefully unorganized! The grading criteria is not clear. Over 10 of his grad students grade different papers and grading is very subjective.
Excellent instructor!!
Best class
EXCELLENT
The class is really hard. I regret taking it anyway.
Just at the time you think nothing can go wrong, take his class.
this professor is one of the nicest professor I have ever had. he cracks some jokes every once in a while, he grades quickly and on time. great hair and jawline
Such a lovely course. I loved his Politics and Science Fiction class, the readings were phenomenal and he really cared. Take this UGS! It's so much better than any other.
Absolute Stud
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The subject of the class was fascinating to me, but I thought the book was not always clear and the quizzes and exams had ambiguous questions. I also think the professor could gain from improving his lectures by paying attention to the flow of his speech for a more natural and smooth delivery: get meditation/massage to create relaxed recordings.

Professor Chapman is a very standard professor. His class on global governance consisted of reading a module, watching a lecture, taking a quiz. Then three exams were based on the modules, lectures, and quizzes. This is going to sound obvious, but it is especially true in this class. Do the modules and the readings and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely fun, required to read very interesting science-fiction books and write papers on it. A little demanding but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take this course, Global Governance.  It was engaging and challenging. Professor Chapman is the best.

The most engaging professor I've had. Took him for sci fi and pol, but he genuinely wanted to open a discourse with his students regarding real-world conflicts. He was excellent at guiding discussion, provided meaningful feedback on papers, and responded to emails fast. Always eager to help out his students. Thought-provoking class

Sci-fi and Politics class. He was a very good professor, but discussions could get quite chaotic, readings weren't always well spaced-out, and he graded essays pretty tough as the semester went on. All that said, he was really helpful in showing us the resources at UT and his class and lectures were really helpful and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy, not so great professor. He didn't seem to have prepared anything for lectures and the material was just really dense. He didn't explain it very well and we had to present on some pretty heavy articles. Two tests that were open note and I never read the textbook because the chapters were super long. I just used it for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chapman is very knowledgeable and passionate about his classes. There is a lot of reading (nearly a full book every week or two), and if you don't keep up with your work then you may fall behind. The lectures were always interesting and collaborative. He's a very generous grader and genuinely wants to see you succeed and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, if youre even mildly interested in the subject youll do great. Hes super helpful and a generous grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Hes a great professor and a very generous grader. You learn a lot from his class, especially if youre into politics.
I had Dr. Chapman for my UGS. Extremely nice guy, cracks some good jokes, leads a discussion well. Highly recommend him to others.

Great teacher. If you're interested in how institutions (i.e. UN, World Bank, IMF etc.) interact on global issues this is very interesting. I really liked the section on international finance. There is a paper you have to write in the class but it can be on any topic of your choosing. Not a very hard class at all, but very enjoyable. Nice guy!
The course was Global Governance. The tests were multiple choice.  If you do the study guide and know the voc. from the book, you will do well.

Prof. Chapman made this upper division government class worthwhile. He was very interested in the subject matter and related it well to his students. Although attendance isn't necessary, he will learn everyone's names. He is always available for office hours. This course has a lot of readings from the textbook and outside articles.
Lecture heavy and get ready, they are monotonous. She's so intellectually dry that I had trouble not falling asleep during her courses.

As long as you keep up with the work, it's an easy A. If you miss a few tho, it's hard ot get back up on your feet. There was like 2-3 assignments a week and then tests every 4 weeks. Overall great experience for a summer class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took this course online over the summer and was extremely easy. Not much homework and very few quizzes which is all your grade is accumulated with.
The average of every assignment was failing or close and her feedback was terrible
Easiest government credit. You watch lecture videos from O'Brien. Exams are so straightforward. Never used the textbook.

I've had Dr. Caudill for gen chem 1 & 2, and to be honest, she's not as bad as everyone is saying. You can tell she definitely cares for us as students and wants to see us succeed. There are quizzes every lecture, but so many of them are dropped and their weight is so low that I've never personally felt stressed about them. Lectures are meh.

idk why her rating is so low, but caudill works closely with other chem professors like laude to provide students with as MANY resources as possible. With all the resources, self-studying is probably best for this class

If i'm being honest, a lot of the bad reviews here are extreme exaggerations. While I did not find gen chem overly difficult, I can say the class can be challenging at times. However, the fault does not lie with Caudill. Sure she goes on tangents occasionally, but she is kind and provides numerous resources that help prepare for the class.

There are quizzes every class day except for exam day and the day after exams, and they are not easy and only some get dropped. A lot of the learning is done outside of class, her lectures are not helpful The ta's are amazing and explain things very well. she gives a lot of extra credit, but i wouldnt take this class if you cant teach urself well.

With all of the materials she gives you it's super easy to self study the class. Lowkey just study a little for the quizzes (every class period) then brain rot the rest of the class. Then a week before the test lock in use the study notes and you'll be fine. My lowest midterm was a 96 on acids and bases.

I don't usually rate my professors, but I have to give other students a warning. Her lectures are pointless; she drags on about topics and makes concepts overly confusing. She also talks a lot about herself, which doesn't give time for material. The only redeeming part of her course was the TAs. As far as I could tell, they did all of the work.
Hard content and lots of quizzes

I suggest avoiding Professor Caudill's section. Lectures often lack structure because she spends significant time on personal tangents, which leads to rushing through the actual material at the end of the hour. Her teaching style can feel disorganized and unnecessarily complex. Be prepared for a quiz during every class session. TAs are great.

This class is easy; most students achieve their target grade. Online department materials are great, and needed, as lectures can be slow and often focus on personal anecdotes or redundant topics. Attendance mandatory for daily quizzes, but there are retakes and extra credit. While the professor's style is often frustrating, the TAs are fantastic!
Lots of quizzes

Her teaching style isn't effective for most students. She confusingly explains concepts. She goes off topic frequently, spending a lot of time talking about her personal life instead of focusing on chemistry. She goes through slides without providing clear explanations or taking meaningful notes. Because of this, I had to teach myself the material.

I don't recommend Professor Caudill; she frequently goes off topic, goes on random tangents about her week, taking up time out of class instead of lecturing, forcing her to rush content at the end. Very unorganized, indirectly passive-aggressive, and overcomplicates the material. She stops class when she hears people whispering. Quiz every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Caudill's class does not feel super organized. Her lectures are generally very scattered. Her lectures do not dive very deep into the content and focus more on teaching specific question types for the exam. The class focuses more on passing the test than actually learning chemistry.

Her teaching style could be better, but all the resources you need to do well are available on Canvas. There's a decent amount of extra credit, but there's also a lot of homework. There's a quiz every class though. Overall lot of stuff to pad your grade, and prof is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures add very little to what you learn in learning modules, really just focus on the provided modules and question types and you will do fine.
Her lectures are completely pointless and serve no benefit. She also gets extremely upset when people leave even when classes are subsequent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not important to doing well in the class. Often times she does not add much info from what is on her slides. She is really great at helping one on one in office hours and you should definitely take advantage of that if you are struggling in the class

Don't like the way she talks, lectures are her straight up reading the slides, is always complaining about someone whispering but no one is whispering?? She doesn't teach at all so your basically teaching yourself. When she asked the class on their opinion about something, she completely disregarded it and ended up doing her own thing.

Professor Caudill is the most unlikeable chemistry professor. Her voice tells you she doesn't want to be there. I found the lectures to be disengaging and hard to follow. The exam proctoring and academic integrity process was handled unfairly in my case, but the dean cleared me. She does NOT want the best for you. Do NOT take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took her for CH301 and got an A in that. She is very caring and tries, but the actual lecture is a waste of time. You have to self-study for her exams. The class is test-heavy, with 4 midterms at 20%, you can replace two. The in-class quizzes for 302 were harder. I would say to avoid this professor if you care about learning from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is generous with quiz drops and extra credit, and she practically gives you the exam questions ahead of time with "question types" which are also what the daily quizzes are based upon. Many students leave the lecture after the quiz because she doesn't have enough additional information in lecture compared to online learning resources.

She cares about her students, but the lectures are not useful. Prepare to study on your own, especially if u didn't take AP Chem in high school. The organization of the class gives you study materials, so use them and go to office hours.

Dr. Caudill is a very nice person; however, she is not a good professor. Her lectures weren't helpful, and I learned more from the TAs and the review notes than I did from her. She constantly talked during the quizzes and would always review the material with us after we took them. You will do fine in the class as long as you put in work.

This class is easy to succeed in due to the online resources made by the other teachers, but her lectures are boring and not very helpful. She loses focus easily, yells at people for talking, and gets held up on basic concepts while breezing over the more complicated topics. Overall okay, but not the top chem professor.

Dr. Caudill is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. While lectures are not that engaging, she does cover the content and also does demos which are super cool. The class itself is not difficult at all. She gives you all the resources needed with practice exams, question types for quizzes and exams, and tons of extra credit.

Dr. Caudill is very kind. Sometimes her vibe might not be as energetic but she is genuine and has an appreciation for academia. Content is explained in QT slides. She tells you what content will be specifically on the quizzes, provides example questions. Correlates questions to tests, quizzes, EC available, fast email response.  around 3 hr/week hw

Dr. Caudill would often spend the entire class lecturing over basic material leaving the hard content to be self taught. When people talked or left class early she would stop the entire class for several minutes which would cause her to almost never get through the entire slide show. Overall, study the question types and you'll be fine.

Dr. Caudill was such an amazing professor! I really don't think I'll find a professor better than her at UT. She made lecture so fun, it was the only class I could actually get up for. The chem course is super organized, and there are plenty of resources to help you succeed. Don't take her if you're not going to attend lecture.

Caudill is nice but probably the most difficult gen chem teacher to get an A in because of the quizzes every single day. U have to go to every single class and she gets mad if u leave after the quiz. However, there is no homework which is nice, but the quizzes can drag your grade down if u dont study before every single class

lecture is inexplicably boring and caudill is not a good lecturer. attendance mandatory because of in-class quizzes every class. chem is relatively easy due to the gen chem department setup as a whole. caudill's course is much harder than others because you'll have to self teach to succeed. kind lady, but very short tempered and passive aggressive.

Dr. Caudill is a very nice and caring person, but for most lectures, she reads off slides. For me, it seemed like a waste of time, and the lecture would be very boring. There are a lot of resources and help offered by the gen chem department. Attendance is counted by quizzes at the beginning/end of almost all lectures.

Caudill is not a great lecturer. She is very easily distracted and takes being absent from her class personally. The CH301 structure is the only thing holding her class together; without it, the class would genuinely be impossible. Overall, this class is not hard to pass if you put in the effort, but don't expect to learn the material in lecture.

Lectures tended to be very boring as you learn material before the class using online learning modules. Isn't a great lecturer. 5 question quizzes at beginning of class. Only good thing was the vast amount of review content for tests, but this is made by the other professors and not specific to her.

Lectures droned on, would not begin teaching classwork until 30-45 minutes into class and would spend first half of class talking about anything other than subject matter. Changed whole week schedule after getting hungover at ACL. Consistently returned test scores well after other sections/professors. Find any other professor to take Gen Chem with.

boring lecture, quizzes every class but they were easy and there's a list of quiz topics posted, class format across all chem is easy and made the tests easy to study for, tests were light n the practice tests each unit were very similar, ec was so easy n brought my grade up like 6 points

In my expirence with Professor Caudill, the overall class is easy and the learning modules provided by Dr. Laude provide all the critical content needed. For as much as she tries, Professor Caudill is a poor lecturer and she assigns quizzes at the beginning of each class. She can often be tempermental, once scolding a TA for helping a student.

Genuinely the most boring lecturer ever. Would always spend the beginning 15 minutes of class talking about the same useless things and never finished a lecture. There were also quizzes at the beginning of every class, and these quizzes were harder than most other professors. Prepare to teach yourself all the content to get through this course.

The structure of the class makes it really easy to pass. She has good online resources but her lectures are a little meh. The only thing is that there are quizzes every day. They aren't hard, and they don't weigh too heavy but can be annoying. You have to be in class to take them but you can leave after.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This teacher does not teach. In addition to not teaching, she somehow manages to blame the students for her lack of ability to teach. She gets distracted so easily in lecture and ends up wasting a good portion of lecture time asking students to be quiet even if they were whispering. She once yelled at her TA for helping a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The test and quiz material is very clear. Dr. Caudill does not teach very directly in class, so be prepared to do lots of self learning. If you work hard, you will do well. Also, the TAs are actually really helpful, so ask them questions and go to their office hours.

Dr. Caudill is a very sweet and caring professor. She clearly wants you to do well in Chemistry. Daily quiz's which are stressful at time but the drops and clear question types covered made it bearable. Lectures can get boring and I felt like I had to self teach a lot of it but she keeps this class very organized and clear. Would take again.

Dr. Caudill is a sweet human being; she is caring and kind. However, most of her lectures don't tend to cover all that we are learning. I came in with a very weak chemistry background and had to study very hard to even make a C+. The additional resources are very helpful, and you will have to do a bit of studying outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Some how my previous rating on here disappeared. Somewhat sketchy, but I will not allow my voice to be silenced, and I will exercise my first amendment right. She is monotone and boring. The only saving grace of this class is the review notes and organization of the class, but all other chem professors use it too, so it is somewhat irrelevant.

Dr. Caudill is a very kind and caring professor. I have definitely experienced worst professors. She gives 10 minute quizzes each class and some don't like it but it personally helped me stay on top of the material. While she isn't the best lecturer, she does much better in her office hours. She is very kind and actually listens to your concerns.

This professor doesn't really teach. She does the lectures and reads off the slides, but the lectures are only like the biggest and most basic concepts of the unit that you need to learn. She talks extremely slow and never gets through all the material in class. Be prepared to do most of your learning yourself.
Not the best instructor, but she is a smart teacher.

She seems like a nice person but she is so easily irritated. Every time students leave class early she tries to make everyone feel bad. Her lectures are pretty solid and all the material is easy. Just do the learning modules and you'll do good.

Really caring professor but a really bad lecturer. There is a quiz every single class day so attendance is basically mandatory, although a few drops are available. Very easy to doze off in her class because of how boring it is. Not a terrible option but not the best, I would recommend other chem professors.

Dr. Caudill is not the best lecturer. This class is easy to manage due to all of the online resources, but be prepared to teach yourself everything. She is a kind professor, but I do not recommend taking her if you want to get something out of lecture. But overall, the class is super easy if you put in the work

I hadn't taken chem since sophomore year of hs and thought this course was very straightforward. Caudill's lectures were slower, sometimes leading to her classes being behind other prof's classes, but it was because she provides lots of examples and practice during lectures to ensure understanding. Exams are easy as long as you do practice problems

This is the only professor that made me truly feel very disregarded when asking a question the answer was already no. We have a quiz EVERY SINGLE CLASS DAY. She always has something to complain about. Definitely go to TA's for help they are pretty helpful. She doesn't answer emails as much as she always says to email her cause she "wants to know".
she is really not good at teaching freshman. too much work for beginners. she should be a senior year professor

Honestly her lectures are sooo boring, i never learn from them. i spend a lot of time studying for this class outside of class time, just because in her lectures shes very vague and drags out unnecessary material. Luckily you get two redo exams and some quizzes are dropped, but study for the quizzes using the quiz schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's very nice and caring and you can tell she wants her students to succeed. There are extra credit opportunities and she drops quizzes and hws so a couple low scores won't effect your grade. There is a quiz every single class and the 4 exams so attendance is mandatory even though the lectures itself are recorded and posted online.
get ready to teach urself in this course dude. im so bad at chem
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures tend to drag and her monotone voice makes it extremely difficult to focus. Resources provided are ones all chem professors provide so. I will say she does drop multiple quizzes however it does not make up for the content being difficult to understand (which I think is very). Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her voice is so boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Being completely honest, if you don't have any interest in chemistry and don't understand chemistry you will probably struggle in this class. She doesn't really teach she reads off the slides and you'll most likely have to teach yourself. I personally walked out of there rethinking my major that I really am interested in.

Caudill was a nice professor, and you can see that she wants everyone to succeed. There are many opportunities given to raise your grade. Her lectures are a drag and she just reads off the slides. You will have to put more effort in understanding the course material yourself. Go to office hours and constantly look at her review notes to succeed.

Teaching wasn't great and I had to learn everything on my own (mistakes in lecture slides too). Wasn't clear on what'll be tested in the weekly quizzes. Wasn't very helpful in office hours and directed students to her TAs for help. If you take her, prepare to learn on your own (Use review notes & practice questions/exams).
The overall class is fine, but only because all gen chem profs came together to make the classes uniform. Otherwise, Caudill is a boring lecturer and a s

Lectures were mid and she barely answered any questions during them. It felt more like a flipped classroom and self teach using all of the review notes. Her review notes are the bible and should be ur priority. She offers 3% EC on your overall grade and offers 2 test retakes though, so if you don't get the grade you want it's literally all on you.

Despite her efforts, Dr. Caudill is not a great teaching professor. She reads from slides and doesn't explain thoroughly, often using valuable lecture time to review redundant examples and waste time. All gen chem courses are standardized, so all material is the same--that being said, you will have to teach yourself everything. Class is pretty easy

People overreact—she's not a terrible professor at all. Gen Chem 2 is easier with all the resources she provides, including helpful ones from other professors. Office hours are GREAT, and extra credit is easy. I didn't take AP Chem and still got a 99 both semesters. Only downside: lecture pace can be too slow or fast which I don't like.
Horrible lecturer, makes class not worth going to. However, the resources she provided carried me throughout the semester. Only take this class if you are comfortable self-studying.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anyone saying negative things were probably talking, so she had to babysit instead of being able to do her job. Dr. Caudill teaches HOW to think about chem, not just WHAT to know for exams.  IMO that's the best quality you can ask for in a professor.  She's extremely approachable and knows chemistry like the back of her hand. Excellent professor.

was averaging Cs and Bs on exams until I stopped attending class and taught myself instead. Shes not horrible but lectures are so redundant and you will learn nothing unless you did prior reading or the learning modules before. quizzes are harder than in ch301
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took Caudill for both 301 and 302, and honestly the class isn't bad. She isn't a great lecturer but the course is structured so self-studying is very doable. She offers 3% of extra credit. The quizzes were definitely MUCH harder than 301 so be prepared to study for those.

Don't take under any circumstances. She knows the material, but does not know how to teach. She jumps from slide to slide and has in class quizzes every week. These quizzes go over the same material learned from that same day. She uses other professors materials to "try" and "teach." SHE DOES NOT DROP EXAMS ANYMORE. Expect to do 6+ hours every week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Fairly decent class! Lots of comprehension is done outside of the classroom but everything for the semester is laid out in Canvas in a way that is easy to follow. Properly prepare for the weekly quizzes! Good semester.

Had Caudill for both CH301 and 302. Although her quizzes seem to be more difficult that of other chem professors, it is not too bad, given quiz drops + extra credit. Yes, she is quirky, pointing noisy ppl out. But she is actually very funny and caring, you just have to get used to her format. Study from her review notes, they are extremely helpful!

very monotone voice and tbh a bad lecturer but the class isn't bad at all. i took her for chem 1 and 2 and i would just sit in lecture and go over the review notes and teach myself. the review notes are all you need to succeed. lecture was BORING but shes nice i suppose

Take Caudill. Yes, she's annoying, calls kids out, nitpicks noise, but she explains chem well. Gen Chem is standardized now, so prof doesn't matter much. She gives 3% extra credit, making an A = 90% if you do it all. She really cares about students, you'll see in office hours. So, if you want an easy A and solid understanding, take her.

Caudill was an extremely boring lecturer and very monotoned. She constantly stopped class to point out someone being late and if people were talking in a 400 person lecture hall. This would then cause us to not get through all the material on the exam and we were then left to teach it ourselves. If you look at Laude review notes you will be fine.

Dr. Caudill gets a lot of unnecessary hate imo. Chem 2 is just a tough class. She really tried to make things more fun (toy dinosaurs, ice cream) this semester, and really listened to feedback (dropped another quiz when our grades were rough). In office hours she obviously knows what she's doing and really cares about student success
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I also took her for CH301 and got an A. Anybody that doesn't like her is crazy- she literally gives you every SINGLE question type (25) for the exams, and a page of review notes for every type of question. Lectures are useless/irrelevant though. quizzes every week. 4 exams worth 80% of final grade, but you can redo two of them for your final exam.

Dr. Caudill is the best chemistry professor I've had at UT. I took Dr. Anderson, Dr. Laude, Dr. Hollenback, but nothing compares to Dr. Caudill's excellent teaching style. She is the sweetest and always there for her students. Now I am a junior about to be done with organic chemistry and still remember the days I had her as my chemistry professor.

Anyone complaining about this class is being overly critical. She is very clear on grading criteria and gives you a TON of resources outside of class. If you work hard, study the learning objectives, and do the assignments, you'll do great. Lectures can be a little boring at times, but she's very nice and genuine if you actually talk to her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took 301 not knowing anything from high school since freshman year chem. She gives 2 retakes and 301 is pretty easy up until the final test on Thermo, but even then I got a 84 so you should be okay. Lectures are boring and if you understand the Learning Modules and Question Types, theres no need to go to Lecture. Caudhill is just a Mid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: all chem classes are structured the same but she is so boring and doesn't teach the same tricks that other professors do. You'll pass but take someone else tbh
