Had Dr. Caudill for CH301 and 302. She is quite nice and wants to make class fun, but her lectures are slow, and she mostly reads off of slides, which are lots of questions that she pauses class for you to work out on your own. Using Dr. Laude's online lectures and review notes to learn and practice is much more efficient.

Dr. Caudill is very organized and encouraging, but her lectures can be a bit tedious and slow. If you're struggling with chemistry, I would recommend taking her class since she walks through the content step-by-step, but if you're used to a faster-paced environment, getting through this class may be a bit frustrating.

She's nice but not a good lecturer since they are super boring and not engaging. However, this is an easy class so your grade will be fine. She does provide a lot of extra credit and lets you retake 2 tests at end of sem. Also, she always tweaks about hearing students whisper when I or any of my other friends never hear any whispering??

Caudill is pretty concise but relies on Laude's lectures. If you did well on AP chem, Caudill is a pretty solid choice. However, if you need a professor that writes down their thought processes when working out a problem, she is not too great at that unfortunately. Overall, her class is quite manageable with lots of resources available.
Very passive aggressive and lectures are all-over, but doing good is doable if you put effort.
She was fine in CH301 but she did not know what was going on in CH302.

She was okay at first. Towards the end of fall, she got frustrated over small things: students discussing lectures and asking TAs for help. She even called a student rude for being late, despite 2/3 dorm power outages where some couldn't even shower. Instead of using a lockdown browser, she spent a whole class lecturing about cheating and lateness.

Lectures are not engaging whatsoever. She singles people out for showing up late stating "they are disrupting the class" rather than being understanding life happens and at least they showed up. She often complains when people are talking though it is her TA's actually being helpful. She is quite rude to her own TA's who offer more help than her.

She always skips over lecture slides and sometimes rushes towards the end of class to get through everything, making it difficult to understand what's happening. I don't even think she covers everything in the learning modules. In CH302, it becomes much more complicated with this teaching style.

I wouldn't take this professor at all. She made me dislike chemistry, and when I went to office hours, she wouldn't help there, either. She would skip through her slides and get very upset if she heard one person speaking. I would never hear anything. If you like teaching yourself, take this class.

Going to her lectures can seem like a big waste of time since she just goes through the slides found online and reads them or highlights the important information. She kind of doesn't teach in class and the slides don't have all the information but the notes she posts are really helpful to do well in the test.

Lectures are not engaging, she just reads from slides and jumps around. She is constantly referring students to other professors' resources instead of being helpful. Any helpful content used to self-teach isn't even created by her so it's widespread among the chemistry department. Her only useful resource is her review office hour before exams.

had her for 301 and 302 currently - hoped she would improve? she isnt a first year teacher so i dont know why she teaches like it? info is read straight from slides that have numerous errors. no hw/reviews are her own material. chem is standardized curriculum at UT but it doesnt mean shes a good teacher. study on your own and youll be fine
Insanely mid professor. She is extremely boring and is always going off about people whispering when no one is whispering. Gen Chem at UT is just not good and not taught well.

Overall good professor. Lectures can get a bit boring, she skips over stuff sometimes. She does provide a great exam prep resource with review materials which is super helpful. Honestly I learned more through those than actually going to class. I'd try to get Laude if you can but Caudill is totally ok if you can't.

Her lectures seem to be unorganized and just jumps around from slide to slide sometimes skipping multiple slides. Did I mention she teaches with slides like come on this is UT. Her classes are more meant for review rather than learning, she obviously knows the material, she just doesn't know how to teach it.

She's super nice. Her lectures don't help much, she doesn't explain concepts the best. But she gives a lot of resources to help students learn. Practice tests, review notes, practice problems, everything. She also offers 2 replacement exams out of the 4 you take. She also offers extra credit for your overall grade.

The only reason this class was easy was because of the fixed curriculum. She isn't an awful individual, but her lectures were very unhelpful; the only reason I did well was putting in work outside class. Her practices had numerous errors, and the TA's were no help either, couldn't give answers that made sense. Put in the work, you'll do fine

CH301 is an easy class based on learning modules by Laude and 4 unit tests worth 80% where they literally give you what every question is going to be on. Caudill as a lecturer, however, was basically useless and made the material more confusing and convoluted during her lectures. She is also constantly complaining about whispering when no one is???
Her Lectures brush by topics, often verbatim to the slides. The only way to learn is the modules which are typoed and rely on Dr. Laude.

Dr. Caudill is a professor who cares about her students and the subject material. She provides endless extra credit opportunities, making the class pretty much a breeze. However, she gets caught up during lectures and often will skim through VERY important information. Do not whisper in class until you want to be yelled at. I mean it.

Dr. Caudill definitely cared about the class. She is very passionate about the subject, often diving too deep into parts of the lecture. Because of this, she frequently left crucial quiz information until the last 20-30 seconds of class.

80% of your grade is by tests (however this is currently standard across all CH301 teachers). Caudill provides a lot of helpful resources however she is not the best lecturer. It is easy to lose focus and she seems only repeat the easy content and never really teaches the confusing stuff. Lots of self studying but it was do able.

Professor Caudill definitely cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. She gives an absurd amount of extra credit, lets you retake up to two exams, and drops your 3 lowest quiz grades. If you pay attention, easiest A ever. Definitely use the review notes to prepare for exams because questions are sometimes taken directly from it.

Dr. Caudill's lectures for CH 301 were okay, but I didn't find them particularly helpful in understanding the material. However, the study materials she provided were excellent. The review notes for each unit were incredibly helpful, especially when preparing for quizzes and exams.

I personally found Dr. Caudill's lectures very useless and boring. Weekly quizzes on Wednesday. I dropped the class because I genuinely could not handle Caudill even though I took AP Chem in high school. Laude's lectures on Canvas modules were more helpful than Caudill's lectures. Take Laude if you can.

Professor Caudill's class was great. We were provided learning modules before every class and in lecture she expanded on the topics. Our LM's had 3 retakes alongside being able to retake 2 exams at the end of the semester with no final. We were provided test reviews, practice problems, and external means of learning. Overall amazing class.

I think Dr. Caudill was a solid professor overall. Her lectures were pretty boring, but she gave plenty of material to help on the exams such as practice exams, question types, etc. If you put in the work (practice questions!!!), pay attention to lecture/learning modules, and try to learn the material conceptually, you'll do great!
She's really bad at teaching but the notes she gives are enough to get an A in the class. Its 80% test grades so you have to make sure you do well on them. You can also retake two of them.

The professor is very easy to reach out to, the course is structured well and lectures are okay but not great I stopped going as the semester went on. Lots of extra credit but the learning modules are the best part, she makes the material easy to approach and I learned most of it independently. Tests are straightforward, easier than practice.

As a professor, she is a 4, but the amount of extra credit pushed her to a 5. You needed less than a 90% to score an A if you did all of it! She was really good at lecturing and gave amazing canvas modules that meant even if you did not go to the lectures you would still retain information. Test questions are worded weirdly, but they're not hard.

Dr. Caudill cares a lot about her students. I felt her lectures varied in quality, but the resources she provided made up for it. I really enjoyed her clear grading criteria, and she did her best to provide extra credit wherever possible. I would recommend her to anyone for CH301!

Dr. Caudill made me love chemistry. Though she did jump around during lecture, the materials she posted made self-learning easy. The structure of the class & assignments is very clear in the syllabus & online materials. She posts review slides before every exam which makes getting an A doable. Lots of extra credit & offers 2 replacement exams.

Overall this class was not difficult. All tests are MCQ and the content covered is very clear, so you will know what to study. Caudill's lectures can oftentimes be boring or repetitive, but all the information you need is somewhere on canvas if you get confused. Plus, EC added ~3% to everyone's final grade so if you're a bad MCQ test-taker, its ok.

Lectures were usually unhelpful and unorganized. Practice tests and review notes were super helpful to study for quizzes and tests! Learning modules were also usually not a great resource. Does instapoll (attendance) in class, and has in-class quizzes. Also drops the lowest grades and gives extra credit. Lots of self-learning, but totally doable!

Lectures are pretty boring and weirdly paced, but her canvas page is great. Use review notes, question types, practice exam, and learning modules to study. 4 tests, 25 MCQs each, exactly like the question types. Tons of extra credit, lots of drops, can retake up to 2 exams. Do a little legwork outside of class and it's an easy A. No complaints.

I liked Caudill. Her lectures do tend to drone on a bit, but you can really just learn the material from the learning modules and other resources she provides. I plan on taking her for CH302 as well. She is not as bad as the other reviews say. I would recommend if you want an easy, low maintenance class.

I did not learn much from lectures, but her learning resources on Canvas were very helpful and clear. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are instapolls every lecture and a quiz weekly. Doing all the practice makes you ready for the exams. Replacement exams are available during finals weeks. Study with the unit resources and you'll be fine.

Very structured class with 25 question types per exam. Offers 30 pts (3%) worth of extra credit, and two optional replacement exams instead of a final. I found Dr. Caudill's lectures to be informative, but it honestly depends on your learning style. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are Instapolls occasionally.

There are plenty of extracurricular opportunities. The question types for the exams are released as soon as the unit starts. The professor and TA are easily accessible online. Plenty of study resources that prepare you for exams. Easy class but I kept tuning out the lectures lol
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caudill was a decent professor as she tended to struggle with time on lectures that led to her being behind and for quizzes to happen over material we covered that day. However, the class is still very easy as the review notes and QT will give you everything you need to know for quizzes and tests as well as there being exam retakes and a lot of EC!

Caudill is an okay professor, there are definitely other profs that can teach and better engage with students. She teaches slow and goes thru some topics detailed and others super fast. Definitely a lot of self teaching required (at least for me) but she gives resources to help with that. For exams, just milk the practice exam as much as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good teacher at heart but cannot explain the concepts during the lecture her lectures didnt help at all. Just do the practice tests and read the review notes she has on canvas.

unless you have a recent background in chemistry, take literally anyone else for ch301. caudill seems like a good person, but this woman cannot teach. lectures are useless, which sucks because attendance was mandatory. everything i learned in this class was either learned from the TAs or learned by myself. only + is the extra credit she gives out.
Honestly a really manageable class. Just spam the practice tests before the midterms and actually do the learning modules and you will be fine.

actual horrible professor, her voice is the worst thing known to man, and I would rather have my ears cut off than to listen to her again. She is horrible at lecturing so the whole semester I taught myself, and although the canvas page is very helpful you have to put in a lot of time as not really much is learned in lectures.

She is not the best, but also not the worst. Take notes and really learn the material from canvas assignments. That the only way you will get the material bc she is not that great at lectures. Exams are not horrible if you really go over review slides. WATCH THE EXAM WALK THROUGH VIDEO. Seriously, they are helpful in knowing what will show up.

Lectures were helpful, the question types made me prepared for every exam and quiz, and daily Instapolls were annoying but made sure I came to class. There's ample credit and retake opportunities to cover up a bad day or unit if you have one. Caudill is obviously knowledgable and wants to help! I didn't take AP Chem and was perfectly fine

If you do the learning modules ahead of time, you'll understand her lectures. Exams are very easy to do well on, she gives you 25 slides that you can memorize and get a perfect grade. If you study a few hours for the exam and learn the material along the way this is an extremely easy A. Also she's pretty

She expects you to already "know" a lot of the material from high school. She has a very dull tone and is relatively new to teaching. Her lecture slides are all over the place. I had to teach myself the whole semester. If you want to pass the tests, get ready to study.

The class was meh. Her as a person was meh. Everything was meh. Mostly self-taught because depending on her to teach is like expecting your Tinder date to not be a bad person. Sometimes I'd rather be waterboarded than look at the time during her class because it was actual torture.

Lectures aren't organized well and everything is very rushed. But, she gives us a lot of resources to do well on exams, and the canvas is very organized. If you haven't taken chem since high school you'll be just fine, just put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Caudill was not a great lecturer, often referencing other instructors rather than going in-depth herself. However, she sets clear question types for the exam, so you always know what to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures were useless, but she records them so watch in x2 speed later. Course is mostly self-taught, but she provides lots of resources to learn the content. There were many easy bonus opportunities and the tests were exactly like practice material. The class is an easy A if you put in the work. Attendance is mandatory and taken on Instapoll.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor just used other professors' materials to teach. I felt like I had to teach myself everything outside of class because she made things more confusing than they needed to be. Her tests are honestly straightforward, but her lecture quality is awful. The lectures were never engaging!!! TAKE LAUDE INSTEADDDDDD

Professor Caudill is SO PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE. If one person whispers in a lecture hall of 500 she will literally lose her mind and completely stop the lecture. She takes forever to go over slides and she's just directly reading off of them and writing on them in illegible hand writing. This class is basically self taught.

Professor Caudill wants her students to succeed, but her lectures aren't very good and are often boring. Her grading allows mistakes, including two replacement tests and some quizzes getting dropped. Overall decent, but nothing more than that.

Overall a pretty decent teacher, a lot of the lectures are kind of pointless because a lot of the learning takes place outside of the classroom. If you do the learning modules and look at the exam review materials you should be fine. Tests are also 80% percent of the grade but there are a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Caudill wants the best for her students, however, the way she doest this is questionable. Attendance is mandatory via instapolls and her lectures were the most useless thing of the entire course. Do the learning modules and the all the practice problems given through the exam prep modules and you will do fine even with no AP chem experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: withdrew from class because Caudill is probably one of the worst professors out there. even though she seems nice, she doesn't really know how to teach. she just goes over the slides and scribbles on them. no one knew what was going on in this class. basically a self taught course. take with another teacher or at community college.

Dr. Caudill is an overall good professor. She is very organized and provides lots of helpful resources. Her lectures can be relatively dull at times, though. Before each midterm, there is a practice test that is nearly identical to the actual test, and the required learning modules are helpful and easy grade boosters. I would take her for CH301!

Dr. Caudill is a good professor, but the lectures got SOOO dull. The concepts aren't hard to understand, but she often overexplains the simple concepts and then rushes through the difficult material in the last 5 minutes. If you know how to study, this class isn't hard to get an A in and the canvas provides SO many materials and makes it easier.

This class was fairly easy, especially as someone who took AP chemistry. But her lectures are SO. DULL. She overexplains easy concepts while brushing over hard stuff; I found it much easier to teach myself than to listen in lectures. If you study the review notes and do the practice exams you'll be fine, but you will dread coming to class.

Her class isn't that bad but there are probably better chemistry professors you can take. Sometimes I get lost and she assumes you learned a lot during high school. Even with AP Chem knowledge, her lectures sometimes make no sense. But that being said it is not a hard class to get an A in if you actually study and lock in.

Lecture and slides were useless, but it honestly doesn't matter as long as you do the learning modules. The gen chem department gives out lots testing resources--utilize them and you will be fine. Quizzes every week over what you JUST learned in that day's lecture which was unfair because she would rush through topics at the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class grades are very structured. 4 tests (each 20%, can retake 2 at end of semester), 9 quizzes (3 dropped), instapolls (2ish%). I feel no need to go to class bc I basically study the night before using the question types and REVIEW NOTES (emphasis on using review notes). Tests are pretty easy especially if u can do prac exam well.

Caudill isn't the best lecturer in the world, and she isn't great with time (she speeds through the last 20ish slides at the end of every lecture), but she's a nice person and provides plenty of resources to succeed in the class. Review notes, practice exams, etc. are more than enough to prepare for exams. Overall, getting an A is very doable.

Emily Caudill's teaching style is just lectures, so attendance is mandatory. In order to pass the exams and quizzes, you must study and pay attention at all times during class time. She also gives lots of extra credit opportunities. Emily Caudill is a great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Format of general chem classes are great and provide lots of resources, including review notes, homework directly tied to course content, and office hours (some even recorded). Caudill is a decent lecturer but tends to skip around, so review outside of class is necessary.  exam heavy but lots of opportunities for extra credit (2 replacement exams)

She is a terrible lecturer. I have already taken a chem class very similar to this one and she still manages to confuse me with her nonsense. Overall easy to get an A but you should try to get another professor.

She's ok. The attendance is mandatory through Instapolls, but the lectures themselves are useless. I took AP Chem, so maybe this stuff was really easy for me, but I didn't feel the need to show up to her lectures at all. Just go over the slides by yourself and wait for the polls. Her lectures overexplain easy concepts, you really don't need to go.

This class was so much easier than AP chem and the tests were 25 MC and were pulled from the same test bank as the other chem teachers. Caudill might be schizophrenic though because she keeps complaining about whispering and she's not that great of a lecturer. But, the tests and quizzes are easy. Easy A if you understand the general concepts

i took ch301 last year and i feel like the restructuring by the chem dpt made it super easy to follow this year. around 10 HWs per unit, practice exams, lots of TA office hours / practice question sessions. caudill's teaching style is straightforward, although i do think she skips around a little. will retake for ch302
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Format of class was completely restructured, giving us a clear understanding of what we needed to know for quizzes and exams. So easy, I have absolutely no notes about content or learning it. However, beware that Caudill tends to act like a kindergarden teacher a lot (shushing students for 10 min of lecture). Will take for CH 302, great choice!
Attendance only mandatory to do Instapoll questions. Slides were very unorganized.

Professor Caudill's class was one of the best I've ever taken. She made me love gen chem, and I had never taken chemistry before - never in middle/high school. Getting an A was not super easy, but anyone can do it. It's also very hard to fail this class.

Lectures tend to be rushed so I didn't find them to be that necessary to succeed. Professor Caudill is kind and wants her students to have the best grade possible. As long as you practice with the take home questions, past exams and the practice exams on the orange course book, it is an easy A. I found the tests to be easier than the practice.

Dr. Caudill was a great professor.\ I loved her lectures, and even though they were not mandatory she would have questions here and there for participation points. Her exams had a high weight on the overall grade but were questions similar to what she went over.

About half of class time was covering new content and the other half was going through examples with us to make sure we knew what to do. As long as you do the LEs (before class), the HWs, and pay attention in class you should do well on the tests and get a good grade.

Easy and organized with clear grading. Pointless lectures but attendance required for random quizzes/polls. 3 attempts allowed on HW/LEs even after answers posted for easy 100%. Study for 4 exams with 2 optional makeup exams. Lots of practice problems required. HW clumped before exams annoying. Overall straightforward if you put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly idk why Caudill gets a bad rep lol. I know alot of people say her lectures don't make sense BUT, to be frank a lot of talking over was done during her lectures. Rewatching them alone and doing the practice problems on the slides help A BUNCH!!!! Cannot stress that enough. Really easy to fall behind so make sure to try to keep up.

Kinda disorganized lecturer but the online work (factored into overall grade) of "learning exercises" and HW's  are helpful. So many resources to prepare for the tests, so nothing is unreasonable. Lots of TA/SI sessions available. The actual lectures weren't crazy engaging but the canvas structure/grading breakdown is helpful. Form a study group.

Not the best lecturer, but also not the worst. Content can be difficult at first, especially if you have limited prior chem experience. Lot's of assignments that I found only necessary to do because they were part of the grade. Tests were definitely doable, and were most reflective of the lecture slides. You will have to do a lot of work.
It's test-heavy 800 out of 1000 points on all 4 exams and her lecture slides are not organized if you want to download them to take notes it doesn't match with what she has on the screen.

Attendance is mandatory because there is Instapolls, but the grade in Canvas stays at 100% for Instapoll whether you do them or not. Her class is easy, if you read the LE's thouroughly. All the answers are online, but since the tests are just the LE's worded differenly, you would most likly fail since you cheated on the LE's. Good class, good prof.

slides were so unorganized, if you were to download it from canvas it will not match with what shes showing during lecture. its hard to pay attention to her, so many hw/quizzes due before class, doesnt drop exams or retest, had to drop the class because it was mentally draining trying to teach myself the material. take her or not, just be mindful

CH301 is hard but Caudill tries to help you get the best grade possible. Her final is the opportunity to retake your two lowest tests, which is really helpful. She is also offering a lot of extra credit. The class is hard and you need to teach yourself a lot. Only complaint is that her slides dont match the lecture a lot, but its fine.

tries to do a flipped classroom + teach 4 different topics and trying to do multiple practice problems for each topic during a single 90 min lecture. at some point, i only took notes for the LE's and just passively participated in lecture, it made the class much easier. she wants to do a good job at teaching, but is very disconnected from the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I struggled a lot with chem in high school, but Caudill set up 301 in a way that I really was able to grasp it. There's a bit of self-teaching you have to do, and definitely plan to study for tests, but for a college chemistry class its' not scary at all. She gives lots of opportunities to practice material, I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not good. Do not take

This professor was very nice but not very helpful. The whole teaching team was clearly unqualified and would constantly lecture with the wrong information and solve many problems backwards. was overall very difficult and felt like a waste of time and money. you will be teaching yourself and unlearning all the wrong answers they give you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super caring and she really does her best to make sure everyone does well in her class. Exam questions are basically the same as in-class practice problems so if you pay attention you'll be fine.

In completely honestly, if you attend all lectures and complete the homework/ practice on your own you will do more than fine. Lectures and slides cover all material and she gives more than enough practice over every topic. Awards up to 2 EC points your final total grade. An A is very doable.

Chem 302 is a very interesting class, her lectures are recorded so you could always go back to rewatch the videos and those helped me so much, there are also many chances for extra credit. 
Prof. Caudill genuinely loves chemistry, and if you work hard, attend lectures, and don't fall behind you should get an A.

Though I thought this class was difficult and had a heavy workload, Professor Caudill did her best to give us the highest grade she could with extra credit, our final exam format (retake our two lowest exam grades), and overall performance. She was very caring and wanted to see us all succeed, and is also very passionate about chem.

She is genuinely an amazing professor. Obviously the class is hard because it is chem, but if you put even the slightest bit of effort you can easily get a B. She gives so many extra credit opportunities, she drops lowest test, and lets u retake 2 of the lowest which is the final. If you're a pre-med, dont blow off the class and you can get an A.

She was a really good professor, if you put in the work for this class and do practice problems you'll be fine. She is new to teaching so things may seem disorganized and you might need to review outside of class but overall the the class was not bad. The review problems are similar to exam questions and homework questions are harder than exam.

I can't speak for those who haven't taken chem before. However, if you took AP chem in high school, trust me, you'll find that this class is way easier. I saw reviews saying Caudill is a bad lecturer, but I honestly can't complain about her teaching. Take notes on LEs before class, do practice problems in class, and go to office hours if needed.

Lectures are disorganized and rushed. Caudill assumes students already know the concepts and does not explain problems well. You have to teach yourself to be able to do the homework and pass the exams. Decent amount of extra credit. Amount of work per week is obscene and requires too much effort for how superfluous the assignments are.

you'll have to teach yourself, as her lectures are disorganized and it feels as though she assumes you know concepts already. caudill is very caring though and takes into account what students say about exams. personally, would not take caudill again, but then again, she is new to UT.

Caudill is incredible. She tries her best to go through as many practice problems which hinders the time she has to teach but her going over how to do problems in class is very helpful for the exam. Go to her office hours she will hint at topics and questions to really understand for the exam.

This class was ridiculously easy. She is new to UT, so she changed her entire grading format mid-semester to make it easier. She gives an insane amount of extra credit and a huge curve on every exam. Her test and quiz averages were low, but I never struggled or had to go to office hours. You DO have to teach yourself, she doesn't lecture well.

Like the other ratings said: make sure to do well on the LEs and HWs because you get 3 attempts on them. She also gives out extra credit so make sure to do them no matter what. There are no make-up exams so if you miss an exam because you are sick, you'll just get a 0. It sounds bad but she lets you drop 1 lowest exam grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's very chill. There are learning exercises for each unit and you'll learn everything there, make sure to do those before the lecture so you'll have an idea of what's going on. There are 3 homework for each unit, and the exams usually have questions from the hw so make sure to do them well. Her TAs are god-tiers so reach out whenever you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nothing is really spectacular, but what can you say about a class with 500 students. Lots of online assignments, all fairly simple. Her lectures are easyish to follow with personalized notes. Tests aren't too bad. iClicker participation checks almost every class. She is just a solid choice if you need to take 302.

caudill is a pretty decent professor. she does take the time to listen to her students and will actually alter the exams (not often though!) to help get the best grade they can. lots of homework and learning exercises that are due before class but close right before the exam and you get 3 attempts on them to get a 100. overall, decent professor.
Easy class, if you're struggling in it maybe reconsider your major. You don't have to take the final if you get an A. Gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit/test help.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So much homework with the actual homework and LE's its nice you have 3 attempts but they are worth so little and take so much time to do ): I wish they would be worth more since we have to put so much effort into them. There is also 4 exams which makes studying hard because you dont have a lot of time esp with all the homework
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Caudill's is approachable and clear throughout lectures. Same as the other profs (trio), as long as you do the course pack problems you will be just fine. Chemistry is just a subject you have to put the work in for, but she is a good professor. I have Dr. B for 302 and actually prefer Dr. Caudill's more laid-back teaching style.

She gets a bad rep for no reason lol. I took her class, participated in lectures, and did what I was supposed to do with no particular excess studying. I made an A+. I'm taking Anderson this semester and I actually prefer Caudil''s teaching style as the lectures are more organized. I would definitely recommend it.

A good teacher. Passionate about chemistry and tries her best to teach it. Lectures mandatory with iclicker. No tests were curved, but they were pretty easy. Canvas page problems were helpful! Get ready to pay about $60-80 for TI-30 (can't use ti-84), iclicker subscription, and course packet.

Professor Caudill is a very good professor who makes the content as easy to learn as possible. She team teaches with three other professors making it easy to get help. The way the class is structured with these teachers is very straightforward and makes it as easy as possible to succeed with difficult content.

Dr Caudill was very rushed in her lectures and we rarely got through all the content planned for that day. I did appreciate all the extra credit that was available. The orange book was more helpful than the lectures so use that as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think students mistook her lecturing as the cause for poor grades when in reality the material is just difficult. If you study all the material they hand out and do a bunch of practice problems, an A is definitely possible. Enjoyed her lecturing style although she rushed at the end of class. Do good on the first 2 exams and you will have an A
Her lectures are always rushed mainly in the last ten minutes of class. She tries to cover too much content in one lecture. The orange book is helpful for practice.

Not the best professor. Lectures were honestly kinda boring. 
Exams were hard-hitting.
STUDY. STUDY. STUDY.
The practice problems are your best friend. Do the practice exams, questions, worksheets, and you'll do well.
TAs are friendly and always available through email.
Tests are hard and weigh a lot. 
Opportunity for lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were very disorganized and rushed. The orange textbook helps a lot. The unit exams and final account for most of your grade, but one unit exam is dropped. This class was overall pretty difficult and I had a very hard time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring, however, her exam reviews ARE SO HELPFUL. Her day of the exam reviews pinpoint ideas that are exactly on the tests which in my opinion gives her a bit of an edge over the trio. She is really sweet but her lectures are rushed and a bit unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't love her teaching style. Seemed like she rushed through a lot of material and the monotone way of teaching class often put me to sleep. I still pulled through pretty decently, just stay on top of your classwork and you should be fine. Would recommend one of the other teachers of this course instead, but she isn't terrible.

Dr. Caudill is kind and caring but, as a new professor, her class is structured somewhat poorly. I would often leave lecture feeling more confused. I definitely recommend purchasing the orange course pack because I did not and I definitely suffered for that choice. Lectures are fast and often hard to follow, but Dr. Caudill is nice.

Dr. Caudill is a great person and cares for her students. Her lectures are rushed but I think it's because of how much content there is. You definitely have to put in time outside of class to do well. Look over lecture slides, do the orange workbook, and use extra canvas materials to do well on tests, which count for most of your grade.

Caudill is a new professor, so it's going to take a second for her to figure out pacing and how to teach. She is genuinely kind and caring, and she makes sure you know what you're supposed to know for the exam. As long as you go to office hours (which I know the people that left bad reviews didn't do) and do the orange course pack, you'll do well.

Dr. Caudill is a very nice person but her lectures are often rushed as she tries to cover too much content in one day. I recommend getting the course packs if you want to follow the slides as they are. Tests aren't difficult, but there will be questions that will cover ideas presented only once or twice, so be prepared for all content.

For an intro professor, Dr. Caudill is pretty good. She is a little shy and is learning pacing in her classes (like one day shell do 3 topics and the next is 1, etc.) but she knows her stuff. Sometimes, her lecturing is annoying because she has expectations, but she really does care. Lots of canvas HW, but nothing too hard. Examsfair and STUDY!

She excepts you to know all the content before coming to class. She speeds through the lectures and yet is always behind the other professors. Her class is very boring, and she does not help if you have any questions. Her office hours were not helpful either. The only helpful thing is the orange coursebook and other professors' office hours.

Dr. Caudill is a decent proffesor. Her lectures are pretty dull, but she uses the same material as Anderson, Biberdorf, and Sparks so its easy to work with other students. Tests are medium difficulty and there isn't a ton of homework outside of class.

Caudill speeds through lectures and laughs at students whenever they vocally express that they are confused.  She expects you to know everything when you come to class. I usually leave lectures feeling more confused. One good thing is the orange course pack as it has lots of questions to help prepare you for tests.

Dr. Caudill is a decent lecturer, but sometimes rushes topics in order to catch up if behind schedule. However, since she's part of the teaching team, you get access to Drs. Anderson/Sparks/Biberdorf's office hours. Not hard to get an A as they provide ample resources. 85% of grade is dependent on midterms/final, but lowest midterm gets dropped.

Not that great of a teacher, she expects the class to know everything with little explanation, and she just laughs when the class audibly says we're lost. I learn more from the gchem website than her, but she's not horrible either. Very meh imo, try to take anyone else in the big 4. kinda boring, but 301 is a p ez class so its not hard to do well

Most recent addition to the 'Big 3', and def the weakest. Piggybacking off their structure/content. Her lecture style grates on students bc her narrative pretends  everyone's always 100% prepared and understands everything, so she's unable to respond even when it's obvious she lost the class. Go w/ a prof w/ more experience if possible. Buff arms.

1st class he said that TTH lecture was optional, and Fri discussion wasn't. Then 1/3 through the semester he did class grades and quizzes TTH. It was so much work for UGS. Locked our grade so you couldn't see how you were doing, and didnt allow devices, claiming he would "get us out of class early for trade off" and we never got out early since.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was decent enough, though I feel the grading criteria is somewhat unclear. Once, I received a B on one of my assignments for “appearing to be stressed”. Additionally, Professor Dempster rarely got back to me when I asked for feedback. The course is simple enough, however, if you're in need of a UGS, I wouldn't take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Could not recommend more. Work can be pretty intensive, but stay on top of it, and you're in for an incredible experience.

His lectures are engaging, and he incorporates many interesting activities. However, he couldn't understand my paper, and the A threshold is 95, not 93. Ultimately, due to my final paper, I received an A- with a final grade of 94.7.

This class was amazing! Coming in, I thought I knew what creativity was, but this class allowed me to reflect on and challenge my views. Prof Dempster taught us through a lot of fun activities, from scavenger hunts to movement labs. There are 10-minute talks that require you to give a presentation during your lab section, but they're not too hard.

such a good professor. cancelled friday lectures for the last two months of class. easy readings and fun labs. great professor literally nothing bad to say. the creative notebooks are fun and easy to do and count as a big portion of the grade- he also encourages students to work on them during class. super interesting and engaging. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
It was fun class to take for UGS. A lot of the class is your creativity journal, just stay on top of it and you'll have a good time. Really enjoyed the feedback on my journal :)
Very interesting class that's structured in a way to keep you engaged in each section. Professor Dempster is an incredibly smart and knowledgeable teacher. Would take it again.

If you genuinely care and try, you'll do great. Prof. Dempster is a true inspiration and simply a genuine human being. It may seem like a lot in the beginning but it ends up being not bad at all. He gives you so much opportunity to do things you love that his class actually becomes fun. I would recommend his Being Creative class to anyone.

Prof Dempster is one of the greatest people I'll ever meet. TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He is so intelligent and it was so insightful listening to him talk. Main assignment is a creativity notebook that is easy, then a presentation (also easy). He is INCREDIBLE and as a STEM person I was scared to take this class, but I wish I could have more time now.

It was his first time teaching this year so we were his guinea pigs. Not bad overall, one of my favorite professors. He seemed to genuinely care about his students and the opinions of others. He is very generous, he bought us pizza multiple times, cookies, and provided us with "creativity notebooks" along with drawing utensils. Def would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very unwelcoming environment makes it intolerable. Easy class subject matter with SO many busy work assignments. Lecture is required but not relevant to the assignments. Did not learn anything. Disappointed at best.
Spoke down to us and gave us too much busy work. learned nothing. Uses AI to grade everything so he throws work at us like we are machines and talks about nothing in lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Relatively easy A if you don't procrastinate on larger assignments, all lectures are recorded but there will be in class assignments that are not noted beforehand so you prob need to show up to class. the small individual grades accumulate to effect your grade in the end even if it doesn't seem like it matters at the time.

He's an alright professor. Makes odd comments about current society standards at times. The course itself is built willy-nilly. Don't believe the "love him!" if you can think critically. Do work hard and be on his good side, he teaches 3+ required BME courses. Also grades preferentially, so make a good impression.

TLDR: ok class, ok professor.

Much more interesting than 303L, but it's also much more work and can be overwhelming at times. Your grade is going to depend on your group, so prioritize forming relationships with them. 

Dr. Dan is fair and provides very clear expectations and instructions. If you show up and don't procrastinate, this class is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dan is knowledgeable in the subject, but his demeanor made the class feel unwelcoming. His choice of language was sometimes inappropriate, for example, he used the R word slur while referring to a machine, which made the classroom environment uncomfortable.
I always do fine in his classes but why is he so darn sassy and condescending. Likeeee theres no need for the power trip when simply communicating.

Be on time with your work and don't procrastinate. Upperclassmen describe him as like a bad professor, but as a freshman he is literally the goat. Your lab TA is directly responsible for your grade so make sure you have a positive relationship with him.

Not understanding, not accommodating, his labs are unnecessary difficult and time consuming due to his own poorly written instructions, and he is extremely condescending and will publicly shame your work to later classes. He doesn't contribute to UT at all so I don't understand the power trip he has.

Somewhat unaccommodating professor and uninvolved TAs, which can make class unpleasant but can be avoided with proper planning. Good preview to BME,concepts taught in the class are important and interesting especially the research essay and projects were fun and interesting. Do not blow off work and make a good impression and the class will go well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had way too much work for a 2 credit hour course. The projects in lab take so much time outside of class, and there are so many assignments to keep track of. The content is pretty interesting, and the grading is lenient, but there are so many unnecessary assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Dan is a cool dude. Show up to every lecture and don't procrastinate on the larger assignments, and this should be a relatively easy A. Lab groups are random, so that'll definitely play a role in your experience in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are not representative of the weekly lab so you basically learn everything yourself but they are still mandatory due to the pop-quizzes. Labs are super boring and require a lot of work for 2 credit hours. Dr. Dan is also not that accommodating in my personal experience.

I love Dan, but his labs are absurd. Very little amount of direction especially for ECG project. Biggest piece of advice - find an upperclassman who can mentor you when you are stuck. He's incredibly understanding when conflicts arise, CONTACT BEFOREHAND when you miss class or assignments will be a 0. Easily approachable, solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I rated Dr. Dan 5/5 for BME303L. Complete switch of rating. This class was hard, like, really hard. I spend more time on this class than ochem, which says a lot. Rubrics are unclear, and TA's are often trying as hard as they can but still unhelpful. Too much work for a 2 credit hour course.

Super friendly, caring guy. Class was very easy but had a lot of busy work. The research papers can be difficult if you have zero experience, and the 3-week coding unit was very fast paced. Lab took up a lot of time and was pretty boring. Overall extremely easy A as long as you put effort into assignments and turn everything in on time.

Pros: genuinely cares about his students, his whole job is teaching (he does zero research), not too difficult but not too easy

Cons: can be boring, most lectures are intuitive and you don't learn anything groundbreaking, in-class assignments

Advice: you will have him for your entire academic journey, so be sure to make a good impression

no tests, just projects, papers, and some easy quizzes. good intro BME class, a bit boring imo. a lot of busy work i feel like, but an A is very doable. fun professor, he really cares abt his students (esp since you will probs have him for a few more classes)

This class was easy to succeed in & Dr. Dan is chill. About 3 big assignments, but most of it is done in lecture. 2 big papers, but grading isn't harsh (depending on TA). Lectures were sometimes boring. Lab was interesting, but very low-stress. Lots of small assignments for points. Make sure to do the professional development assignments early.
He was a great professor, did some occasional pop quizzes but they are easy if you go to lecture. He is a funny and caring guy, and he also explains topics well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class. Great guy.

Average. Research paper assignment is tedious but doable. Excel & MATLAB assignments are fast-paced, but office hours are helpful. Quizzes require a little practice. Attending lectures isn't needed at the end of the semester but try attending all before it. If you genuinely try, getting an A is straightforward even if you're not good at STEM.




.

214L is definitely a step up from 303L. This class has three lab projects: CAD flow simulation, ECG instrumentation, and machine learning. I thought everything we learned was super valid, but machine learning was definitely the most interesting. ECG was challenging but doable. Lectures were interesting, but there are pop quizzes, so go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is an easy class if you have a reliable team during lab. Dr. Dan does not do a lot of explanations during lecture which makes some assignments difficult to follow, he also grades strictly and takes off points for the smallest things, so just be careful because they will add up. He is also very accessible for office hours, so meet with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He does not communicate well with his TAs and LAs that are grading assignments. If you don't do things how he perfectly likes it, you'll be heavily penalized. Lectures don't teach you much, for MATLAB and Excel you just copy his code and he expects you to complete assignments on your own. With all lab assignments, you'll be teaching yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really candid about his experience in engineering. Open to discussing BME and its potential avenues in office hours. Excel based lectures will be hard for first time excel users, and the research paper is intense. But, if you manage your time you will be fine. The problem I had with the class was the lab TA, not Dr. Dan.

This is a step up from 303L, and the class is a lot more interesting. The main projects were based on CAD and then constructing a working ECG. Dan is really kind and is always available after class to help with any issues. The most difficult part of the class was machine learning, so make sure to stay on top of that or you'll definitely face issues

Dr. Dan is great! He was always ready to teach us. The only thing is that he would assign a lot of busy work to do. This class is a GPA booster for sure! I ended with a 97 average and didn't attend all of the lectures.

Dr. Dan objectively is a great guy and super inspirational. His class is easily a GPA boost so long as you don't fall behind on the HUNDREDS of busy work assignments that he randomly assigns. He has little sympathy for late assignments if you don't communicate with him beforehand. Stay on top of lab work, and attend lectures for the Quizziz grades!

Dr. Dan is amazing and cares a lot about his students. I would strongly recommend starting assignments when they're assigned since it's very easy to fall behind on deadlines. There's just a lot of assignments going on at the same exact time, which is the only bad part about this class. Also, the class may seem useless sometimes :D
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dan deserves 5/5. If you want to go into biomedical engineering, you should be up for a challenge. Luckily for you, this class will not be a stressful challenge. If you put in a reasonable amount of effort, you should easily get an A. For the large lab reports, I do not suggest procrastinating. They take time, so put in the effort beforehand.

Dr. Dans BME 303L was an amazing intro to biomedical engineering. Hes the type of professor that really cares about students and truly enjoys his job. I 100% recommend him because he gives feedback, teaches important skills like Arduino, MATLAB, Excel, etc. His labs are also very interesting. Theres no reason to not get an A if you try!

Most people like him, but for me, his grading criteria was very confusing. Points were taken off for really small things and your grade realllly depended on your TA (especially the one grading some of your lab reports). I felt like in class he went too fast over the things that mattered and spent too much time on things that didn't.

Dr. Dan was an amazing intro to BME professor. His labs were interesting and his lectures introduced important skills for engineering such as Excel and MATLAB. He was always accessible outside of class for extra help and responded to emails really quickly. His class is an easy A as long as you show up and try.

Dr. Dan is simply the greatest. For an Intro class professor, he is warm, inviting, and detailed. You learn Excel, Matlab, and basic BME handiwork skills like breadboards and spectroscopy. The class rigor is manageable and he gives easy participation grades. A word of caution: don't underestimate the quizzes. Take his practice quizzes to prepare.

He is an alright professor, but he is very vague regarding assignments. The lab section was always difficult because everyone had a different interpretation of what the assignment will be. His lectures are easy at first, but then he begins to go extremely fast, especially with excel and matlab.

This course could literally be described in one word: fine. It had a pretty solid amount of work, and prepare to get close to your TA rather than Dr. Dan. Most of his grading is pretty fair though. If you put in a solid amount of work, youll get a solid grade.

Dr Dan is a lot of fun and makes class enjoyable without making the class too easy. I felt that almost every day I learned something valuable and applicable for our careers. He gives good lectures and teaches in a way that allows most people to understand the material. Labs are mandatory but he gives us more than enough resources to succeed

Dr. Puperi was one of my favorite professors last semester. He really wants us to participate. He is very passionate and he wants you to put in effort. You will be successful in this class if you put in effort to participate and avoid procrastinating. Many of the assignments are project based so procrastination will keep you up all night.
BEST BME professor so far :), would take again if I was staying in BME program as an undergrad :((( you will enjoy his lectures and assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: If you're taking this class, change your mindset from trying to get a good grade to actually wanting to learn. He gives you a great look into what BME is, very kind, and truly wants you to learn. You have a few lab reports, quizzes for excel/matlab, but also several easy assignments. The good grade comes as a bonus if you are eager to learn more.

I LOVE Dr. Dan! He is so approachable and caring to talk to. You can tell that he genuinely wants all his students to succeed and cares about making sure that we have a good introduction to engineering industry and design. You're required to take him no matter what, but be excited that you will!

Dr. Dan is a great professor, and a great person. I respect him a lot and his expectations for us as students and as adults. My only complaint is that some material was confusing or not clearly explained in lecture, which made some labs hard to follow. He gets frustration from slackers and cheaters, but I like that he holds everyone accountable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Dan is the most approachable professor at UT Austin. He cares about his students and wants you to learn from his class. We invited him to play volleyball with us, and not only did he come, but he's really good. Overall, a super awesome, charismatic, and genuine professor.

Dr. Dan is an excellent lecturer in the BME department. He spends a lot of time making sure all the content is relevant and there is no busy work. I generally felt the work I did was useful. I do wish he graded some of the writing assignments versus the TAs. I have enjoyed all my classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dan was great for intro to BME! His class made me excited for the rest of my degree. He did a good job of balancing being strict, yet also being generous and caring to students. Definitely enjoyed this class and learned a lot!
Dr. Puperi is a compassionate professor. If you just show up to class and do your work, you WILL get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It's a lab so get ready to work with people. Generally easy but if you don't have a coding background is extremely difficult to keep up. Homework is easy.

Dr. Dan is a really nice and relaxed professor. Work and labs are relatively easy, just make sure to show up to lecture to get the information necessary. Also don't plagarize/share work because he WILL call you out and report you. Overall a very enjoyablee professor for a first year engineering class.
Dr. Dan is a wonderful person who really cares about his students. You need to be present in lecture unless you enjoy making your life unnecessarily hard learning random information on your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dan is an awesome guy with an a great engineering background. He's very personal, knowledgeable, and easy to access outside of class. The course is designed to give you a BROAD exposure to biomedical engineering, so expect quite a few different lab projects. But every assignment has a clear grading rubric. It's a pretty easy A.
Dr. Dan is probably a BME's favorite professor. He's super nice and his class(s) he teaches are genuinely fun. Probably one of the few professors that seems like a human.

A very fun an easy intro to the BME curriculum. Interesting prof, used to work at NASA. Nothing bad about him, a little confusing at times, but nothing major. Very nice in office hours and very flexible with grades. Makes intro lab a very fun time!

Dr. Dan is an alright professor. I had him my first semester of sophomore year (his first semester) and he tried to make the best of what he could. I tried cutting him some slack for it was his first time teaching, but he was just so unclear about directions and expectations. From what I have heard from newer students though, he has improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Dan really cares about teaching and making the class interesting. He has really good discussions in lecture and the labs are usually fun and engaging. One of my  favorite classes at UT; made me more interested in the BME curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I had him for his first semester as a lecturer, and I think he did pretty well. There wasn't a final, and all of the assignments were fairly straightforward. The labs were fun, and what we learned during lecture was useful information.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The entire point of her lectures is Context for the analysis that you will do over the readings, which felt redundant.  I think more perspective would be appreciated. We do a lot of readings that basically offer the same ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was not expecting these reviews to be so harsh. I took E323U with her so ignore the course tag (it wasn't an option). Dr. C was great! I learned a lot, I enjoyed listening to her lectures. Kind of seems like people were mostly upset about playing roulette with TAs, which isn't her fault. She is definitely not evil. Idk what y'all are on lmao
When you take this professor, it's not the class you registered for.  It's mental gymnastics 101.  Save yourself the chronic headaches and don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to do lot of group projects but she's very lenient. Super helpful if you have any questions. Class just consists of lots of research but if it's a topic you enjoy it can be lots of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this course for the MAS credit, but I enjoyed this class! She is very personable and picked great stories to read for Latina/o culture. Instead of writing essays, we made Zines for every cycle. She also gave good feedback to people who were getting adjusted to her class system. She also set up professor and student norms as boundaries.

Terrible course, a terrible professor, and I had the worst TA. Don't take this course and don't stay in the course if your TA makes you redo multiple assignments. This class is taught by people who don't want to admit that their entire profession is a joke and will be even more useless in a couple of years, and they're taking it out on the students

I had a quite positive experience (I liked her class so much that I picked up an English minor). The readings for the class could be a bit uncommon but I enjoyed them because they offered different perspectives. Stay on top of everything, and if you have a problem with TA's grading I would suggest reaching out to Dr. C. She is very kind & helpful.

Never watched online lecture videos because they were quite boring, and the assignments were very straightforward, so there was no need. Grade in class heavily depends on your TA. Mine was very chill, and I never had to resubmit an assignment (make sure you read the instructions in their entirety).

Now that flags are gone DO NOT take this class here. It is entirely self paced other than discussion but they grade super strict. The lectures are SO SO boring and the discussions are super awkward. I HATED this class. Also, the readings are all super long and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has nothing to do with her (she's nice TBH), but rather the TA. Some are OK but mine was PICKY even though they would grade very late. Which can screw you over at the end of the semester. If you go to discussion prepare for the most awkward 50 mins ever since no one talks. Now that flags are gone, make life easier: take the class at CC.

I was surprised to see such a low score for someone who has quickly become a favorite professor of mine. She is a kind, fascinating, and understanding professor. Her class focused mainly on reading and class discussions. If you love to read, I highly recommend this class!

Oddest grade system I've had, but you get the hang of it (ish). You determine your own grade. Lectures unnecessarily long, readings lengthy. Just keep up with it. For reading journals, just follow the "tips to success". Grades depend on TA most of the time :( Dr. C's personality is all about her culture lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I put hilarious because it is just laughable. The class was absolute dog water. The TA "Jefferey Nguyen" is a 24 yr old child on a power trip. Do not take this class under any circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Please don't be scared by the reviews. Although this class can be a bit overwhelming at first, the workload is incredibly manageable if you stay on top of it, and there truly isn't that much. The grading requirements are clear, and this class will only be a bit difficult if you despise writing, but other than that, I promise you it is quite easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof CdeBaca's E316M can be a mixed bag. While the course content is engaging, the workload and grading system can be tricky. Staying on top of assignments is key. Utilizing unstuckstudy alongside the course materials can be a game-changer for managing the workload.

To the other rater that claimed CdeBaca is evil; I couldn't have said it better myself. The course itself is laughably easy, you only have to do a few assignments for a good grade. God forbid you face any personal struggles during semester though; don't expect a shred of compassion or understanding. Only rude emails and a holier than thou attitude!

Super chill because you just need to do whatever assignments you want then the points get added up. There is a lot of reading to do so it might be hard to juggle with other classes. I kind of got screwed over because everything said I had gotten an A, but it went in the system as a B+ and there wasn't anybody for me to reach out to for help to fix.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof C's class is chill if you're on top of it. Texts are relevant, lectures drag. Assignments clear; 4 points for A. TAs make it or break it- some ppl had to resubmit for credit, I didn't. Stay on track for easy A. Love/hate course, needs self-motivation. Cultural awareness great. Don't wait until the last week to do most of your work (like me)!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't do it. Click another english class or take it as ACC or another community college. The whole class seemed like an ego project to prove a point. Professor seemed nice until you realize that she said, "Nothing you turn in will be an instant A and you won't get an A if you don't go to my office hours". Very very dependent on the TA you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class at UT. The expectations of an entry level course are outrageous. There are over 6 weekly assignments that take 2-3 hours each. That is almost 18 hours per week just in assignments. Recorded lectures  take quite awhile, on top of reading. 4 Finals/midterms. Grading system is you need 4 points to get an A but hard to even get .20 points.

Do NOT believe others when they say she is caring or kind. She is not nice at all!! I had some serious personal struggles during this course, and she had no compassion in the slightest. Dr. Cdebaca is evil. 

As for the class, the workload was alright. The rubric was confusing though, and did not match up with the assignment instructions. :/

I took this class over the summer to fulfill my core credit. It only required about 12-16 hours per week, so very doable. Dr.C picked exciting texts to read, and the assignments truly helped me understand not only the texts but also the American social climate. Dr. C was extremely accessible through email; I would recommend this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer so I would assume my experience would be different than it would during a full semester. There are a lot of readings and the reading journals take a while but it's pretty easy to skim through the course. The grading system is different than over any course that I've seen, basically just need 3.85 points to get a A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The material was outdated, poorly organized. Assignments were unnecessary challenging, leading to confusion and frustration. Feedback on assignments was minimal and unhelpful, providing no guidance for improvement. Overall, I would strongly advise against taking this class unless you enjoy feeling confused, frustrated, and unproductive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I have ever taken. The professor was extremely unclear with her rubric and especially her lecture videos. I got the feeling that she just wanted to flaunt how intelligent she is. American Literature but feels more like world history and feels even more dry than that. Stay clear if you don't care for pretentious professors.

Easiest class I've taken. You complete any combo of assignments you want and only have to earn 4 pts to get an A (attendance can count as 1 pt). I did 1 assignment a week and was done by Spring Break. A manageable class as long as you stay on top of work. Just make sure to follow the rubrics and you will be fine. Everything is graded by your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do yourself the absolute largest favor and do not take this course with her. The class is dependent on TA's and papers either "meet standard" or don't. Grades come out late and the questions required for each essay are overcomplicated, so you get no credit for writing a 4 page essay. The grading scale is confusing+ not well explained so you're lost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just need to get 4 points to earn an A. You are allowed to mix and match what assignments you choose and attending discussion is not mandatory but worth 1 point. Assignments were all easy and an A is very achievable as long as you don't wait until the last minute. The professor and TA were also super approachable and kind.

Ts make or break the class if you want to do this class at the last minute. My TA graded assignments super fast and was on top of things, so getting all the points needed for an A was easy. I would recommend finishing the class a month before the last class day, which is more than doable and if you do its an EASY A.

Lazy grader and doesn't fully read over submitted papers. For example, we were allowed resubmissions, professor failed to grade the resubmission and regraded the first submission, telling me once more to refer to her notes...I do not recommend any of her courses, she is just too much to deal with. Save yourself the stress and find someone else.

I really enjoyed the course, especially the selected readings. This class is entirely dependent on TA's, so your experience may vary. If you are a good writer, this will breeze by. I took this course with 5 other STEM classes and barely felt any strain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment:
Get past the first few weeks of theory n you'll be fine
Researching at the Benson Center and Harry Ransom Center was novel. Beware;both places close at 5pm+closed weekends. 
Biweekly group presentations. 
Dr. C was generous with extensions + gives good feedback. Ask for her help on your final Oxford bibliography. 
Paredes rules, Faulkner drools.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Online lectures & discussion section with TA. You get to choose what four things you want to complete to get an A. There are no due dates, so time management is huge. If you manage your time and don't get lazy it's fine. Lots of reading and all the assignments are essays. Not bad and you can finish early as long as you stay on top of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Never hated a course more. Horrible professor, we don't see her, all we see is the TA and all the TA does is waste our time while the ACTUAL course vids/work is online. Kept saying be specific, but never gave an example of what she meant. The deadline for all assignments is the last day of school, but DON'T WAIT the grading speed is horrid
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Straight forward class with clear expectations. This is by par one of the most simplest English courses at UT Austin and the hardest part is just getting starting. The readings are doable and as long as your people skills are good, TA discussions are great. Overall not a hard class, just not a class people want to take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Majority of negative reviews are either shocked that one has to read for a Lit. class, had a bad TA (unfortunate but NOT Dr. C), didn't manage time, or didn't read the syllabus/go to office hours. Dr. C is GENUINELY caring and considerate. Even in the midst of serious adversity, she is accommodating and interested in nurturing relationships.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: literally don't listen to these reviews. she's the sweetest person. any negative comments are from those who did not communicate with her. she lets you turn in assignments as many times as possible to get a 100 on it, you just need to listen to her feedback.

She always forgets to post whats due before class until the day before, grades terribly, gives very unclear instructions, and makes writing and class dreadul. Don't take her. I hope she sees this because she needs a wake up call

Assignments can be done whenever you want so I finished the class in about a week (summer '23). You can re-attempt any assignment you didn't get a 100 on. The lectures were useless and I never watched them. Your grade 100% depends on your TA, I was lucky enough to get one who graded pretty easy so I never had to re-do an assignment. Overall easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Heavy on the readings. Although the class isn't impossible, it's an unnecessary amount of stress. Videos were helpful for context and could be sped up. It is important to read all of the information on the Canvas page and assignment instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She posts so many readings and her lectures are hours long (and pointless). After module 2 I didn't bother watching the lectures. The majority of the work in this class are the reading journals, which have vague prompts and take hours to write. Self paced class, so don't fall too far behind the suggested due dates. It's a lot of effort to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class consumed the final weeks of my summer. Everything revolved around painstakingly writing reading "journals" for this class. The lectures were incredibly slow and hard to follow. So much reading for such a short amount of time. While I got an A (i think), this was a laborious A to achieve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class isn't too terrible, but I don't know if I would take it again. You can speed up her lectures, and you get unlimited attempts on assignments. However, the readings were a lot, especially some units that had more than five readings. Wasn't my favorite, but if you do all of the assignments, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible class. I cannot stand how she focuses so much on historical and literary contexts and expects us to incorporate that into our writing. Fortunately you just need to complete every module to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is so annoying. The assignments consist of reading journals, which at first seem chill, but eventually escalate into you writing 1500+ words per journal. There are also so many readings and they take forever to do. She posts hours of  useless lectures on top of that. Grading system is awfully slow.

This class is unnecessarily difficult; the lectures and readings are long. When grading the reading journals the feedback given is vague and the TAs usually just quote the prompt with no real explanation. TA is different for every assignment so no real connection formed. This was more time-consuming and more work than my summer stem classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class unless you have a lot of time to devote specifically to it. It can be very easy to fall behind bc of the grading system. I worked incredibly hard & was still stressed throughout the course. If writing isn't your thing, take this at a CC. I would take this prof again for an in-person class bc prof & TA's were fair to me.
