reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: easy A but annoying class setup. You had to get perfect scores on the homework to access the next module, but the TAs graded weirdly so it's easy to get behind. I often had to wait days for grades and I would have to submit the next assignments late.

The structure of the class with grading was frustrating. Professor expected students to complete entire modules within two to three days, these modules often took me five hours to complete. It took over two days to get my grade back to move onto the next module. This caused me to already be behind because of the slow grading turnaround.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! She was the worst instructor I've ever taken and would not recommend anyone to take her classes in the future if you don't want to suffer an extremely illogical grading policy. It doesn't worth the time and money at all. I regret to just not take it in community college.

Do NOT take this in the summer if you want an easy class. Grading is SLOW and can be picky. Lots of reading and writing. But, if you do exactly what they ask for and ask for help via email or office hours, it is possible to get the grade you want. Last words: don't rush submitting assignments because resubmitting is a pain.

Don't take this prof in Summer. Absolute horrendous TAs who use an arbitrary grading structure to hold students back. The "self-paced" structure is not true if you have to wait DAYS to go from one module to the next; add in the fact that you might get a horrible TA to grade your work, meaning they halt your progression further. Don't take it.

Do NOT take this class. The class format is incredibly stupid because although it is asynchronous, you can't move forward until the previous module has been graded. TA's are nit-picky and unclear in their instructions. I highly highly advise against taking this class.
The class was okay. I think that it required a lot of time but as long as you submit the module by the preferred due date, then receiving an A is very possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was entirely completion-based, and all assignments were pass/fail. You couldn't move on to the next module until you had passed all assignments in the previous one. Grading took 1-2 days, but given that they were multipage essays, I thought that this was a reasonable turnaround. As long as you don't procrastinate, you'll get an A.

I just want to say that the low reviews are spot on.DON'T take this class if you do many other things over the summer!The lectures and readings for the 9 modules are unnecessarily long and you have to get a PERFECT to move on to the next assignment because all of them are LOCKED!The TAs are harsh and inconsiderate with grading. Take something else!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hated this class so much, if you hate writing/literature, don't even take this class, it'll make you hate it 10 times more. Pointless readings with objectives that aren't well explained, assignments declined for rubrics that don't really tell you what to do anyways. Just really unenjoyable.

Imma give yall a no bs review. Didn't watch all the lectures, read everything, no TA/Prof OH.

Good: all online, readings are mostly interesting, grading is pretty lenient (especially on resubmit), concepts and assignments are pretty easy

Bad: The grading system forces you to stay on track. Assignment grading turnaround is slow. CRIT is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is reasonable if you complete all assignments on time. 9 modules that take 4-5ish hours each, but it takes 2 days to grade which means you do less work than you'd expect. However, it's stressful if you fall behind or have to get an assignment regraded. As long as you don't fall behind this class is a completion grade.

The course structure is unreasonable.  The professor does not care to teach you the entire course.  You have to score perfect in each module before you can move forward.  You will not finish the course because a module could take 2 weeks to grade, make corrections, and regrade.T  Take another course that is worth your time and money.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SUMMER! It was very frustrating, especially for students who also have other commitments, like other classes or jobs, which the professor called out in a very passive-aggressive tone. The grading was very slow and it took longer than the advertised 1-2 days, and many times, the assignments would have to be redone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've never left bad reviews on RMP, but this was the most demotivating class I've taken at UT. I spent several hours working on reading journals and annotating readings. But my journals were sent back anyways. Feedback mostly nitpicked my answers' organization into their "CRIT" style rather than correcting content of responses themselves. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer, which was a lot more complicated than it should've been. The TAs take a long time to grade journals, leading to you falling behind, especially if you need them to regrade them. Readings and lectures are very lengthy, so if you are taking this class with any other classes or jobs, expect to have a heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The structure of this course, as a summer class, is rigorous to the point where it's stress-inducing. Very lengthy journals. Grading takes a very long time (>2 days). You can try to stay ahead & turn assignments in early, but the stressful part is if you pass to "unlock" the next module, and if you don't, expect another 2 days after you resubmit.

Do not take this professor under any circumstance. She does not clearly communicate the timing and goals required for the class and when asked to make reasonable adjustments to rectify issues, she immediately hid behind "you signed an agreement." A lot of people in the class are getting way worse grades they otherwise would because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You have to wait 4 days to move on to the next module because your TA takes forever to grade your assignment and if you make any errors or your TA is moody you're on that module for a week. Time flies in a half-summer session class. Feedback should not take 3+ days, especially if you need it to advance.

This is class is a joke. The grading, the set up of the class, and how long it takes to grade the assignments. I'm taking this class right now. ITS HORRIBLE!!! The teacher locks each module until you get a perfect score on all the assignments in the module before. The TA's are a joke and take three days to grade one assignment. so ducking stupid.

Structure is incredibly difficult and for no reason at all. You level up your grade as you move forward with the modules but the next module will remain locked until the TA grades your previous one (and they take ages to grade it). WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TAKING IT IN THE SUMMER unless you want to ruin your gpa over an English class.

Took during summer, tons of tedious work. Grade comprised of 8 modules and 1 essay/project. In each module, there are 3-6 long readings, one reading journal assignment, and a discussion post (post 2 questions & 1 reply). All work is completion-based, but they do check for quality before letting you move to next module. Its really excessive work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very unnecessarily time consuming course, lectures are incredibly boring
I never met Professor Cdebaca-Cruz, but my TA was great. You only meet once a week, and everything is self-paced each week. Easy A!
Tough grader and get ready to read multiple books. She is very sweet and easy to talk to but her grading is tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is based on how many modules you complete. Each module is extremely time consuming since you have to annotate multiple pieces of literature, watch hours worth of lectures, and then complete a writing assignment. The grading criteria was very unclear and my TA made it more difficult then it needed to be. Also, didn't learn a single thing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: look I had an amazing TA so my experience was not that bad, so it just depend on your ta. work was easy but it is a lottery on who you get. You never see the professor besides the recorded lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this course for the HUM credit. The course grade is based on 10 essays/writing assignments(ik that doesn't seem like much), but the grading criteria are random based on the TA that you get (most of the TAs are really harder graders). The assignments are based on a lot of reading assignments. This course is an extreme waste of time.

This course seems to be a hit-or-miss, as your experience depends heavily on the TA you get. Unfortunately, I had a subpar TA and barely got an A. The professor's lectures were incredibly monotonous. I would not recommend it for the HUM credit. Take pinto instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is completion based. Finish all nine modules? Cool you get an A. Finish just 5? That's fine you still pass. It is key to complete the modules by the suggested due date, otherwise, you get stuck in a hole that you keep trying to dig out of. My TA was kind and on time with her grading so I can't attest to other reviews about TAs.

Extremely easy class. Self-paced and no deadlines until the end (I did almost the entire course in the last week of classes). However, modules are only unlocked once your TA grades the last one, so you need to plan around that. Journals are graded very easily and you basically just write whatever you want to pass. Grade is based on completion.
She makes her lower-division writing class feel like an upper-division writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A few hours of pre-recorded lectures each week & 9 Journal assignments due. Grade is completely dependent on TA. If they don't grade on time, you can't even move on to the next assignment. Pretty time-consuming course and didn't even really learn. Avg class that's frustrating at times due to the poor quality of learning and time-consuming nature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is definitely dependent on your TA's. If you do each module for each week - you'll finish with an A. It is COMPLETELY up to you though. You have to use your time wisely because this course is asynchronous. You have journals due each week and thats it. No tests. No quizzes. Just do readings and follow the prompts and you'll do great!

Your entire experience will be based on your TA. Such a waste of tuition money just watching prerecorded lectures when this credit can easily be obtained at a community college or by taking a credit-by-exam. TA never responds to emails and both TA and professor were very unaccommodating. Not worth all the time, stress, and lack of guidance

Take British/World Lit instead. depending on the TA, it takes forever to complete modules bc they are so picky when it comes to grading. The lectures weren't very engaging and there was A LOT of reading. Keep in mind its hard to stay on track bc this is a self paced course. Just take something else if you need this for the core curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would highly suggest finding a different class for this unless you're a really strong writer. I think there were FAR too many readings for each journal and the journal questions could be really confusing even after watching the lectures. It's so easy to get behind and was really overwhelming when I didn't understand a journal prompt.

The TA Jenny is a horrible grader. It takes weeks to complete a module because she grades so insanely hard and you have to get a perfect 100% before moving onto the next module. She makes critiques on writing when your writing literally has what she says is missing. The class is just terribly structured as well and professor/TA sucks. STAY AWAY!

I didn't have much direct contact with Dr. CdeBaca-Cruz, but the texts she assigned changed my way to see American history. I learned so much and ended up buying some of the books. Her grading criteria is fair (completion rather than numerical grades). Great class to take over Summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Definitely take this class over the summer. The workload was definitely manageable and I still learned a lot. The grading criteria is interesting but you have two do-overs if you miss an assignment so you can still stay on track for your grade goal. Dr. C really does care about the students in her classes!

Took her english class online this summer and the grading rubric is weird. There are specifics you do to get an A, B, C, etc. It's actually pretty doable to get an A - the way your journals get graded is all on your TA. Mine was dope and super understanding so I did fine her name was Megha I think
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. C was very informative in her lectures and the material she covered was always interesting. However, would not recommend taking this course in the summer if you really don't have a lot of time to dedicate to it. There were a lot of assignments per week and tons of reading. Great professor, but grading relies solely on TA's. Follow journal tips!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class at all. The grading system is heavily dependent on your TA, which makes it difficult to succeed for many. It's def possible to scrap by without doing all the readings and watching all the lectures but the extra stress that this brings for the journals might not be worth it. Try taking with a diff prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want an A you need to follow the grading criteria given at the beginning of the class. There is a lot of reading but they help with all of the assignments (journals, lecture instapolls, annotations). Some reviews say that your grade heavily depends on your TA so be weary. Jaya was a great TA who gave solid advice and returned grades quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Journals are graded as either complete or incomplete,If you want to get an A follow the journal tips provided in the first week of class . Actually take the time to invest in her lectures as they help with your thinking process and make the journal questions much easier.Personally my TA Jumi Kim was amazing and provided awesome feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor CdeBaca-Cruz does an amazing job lecturing and going over the texts thoroughly which helps you interpret them better. There's lots of readings - if you follow her calendar guide to balance out your time management you will exceed in this class! She provides tips on her syllabus for what you need to do based on your ideal letter grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a fantastic lecturer; however, your success in the class is based almost entirely on which TA you get, and some of them are literal spawns of satan. To the person on here who said "people are bitter because they aren't doing well" - you're only saying that because you got the easiest TA -_- (also shaming other ppl is never a cute look
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most prevalent issue in this class is the TA's. Professor C's lectures are informative, but your grade lies entirely in the hands of either an incredibly lenient TA or one of the most ambiguous/strict TA's you'll have in a class. You can literally write a masterpiece essay for a journal prompt that has a few questions and receive no credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof CdeBaca and her TAs have been great for this E316M summer course. Just a reminder-- most people who leave reviews on RMP are bitter because they aren't doing well. Prof and TAs are lenient and helpful. You just have to want an A and put in the time/effort to get there. Very chill course-- definitely recommend it for a summer class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every assignment is either a complete or incomplete and if you get an incomplete on just two of the weekly assignments you automatically get a B. These weekly assignments are also graded super harshly - if you miss a single thing or don't do it well enough you automatically get an incomplete on it. Try and take this course with another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the WORST class I have ever taken. The grading system is so stupid that if you miss even one minor assignment, your grade drops from an A directly to a B. The weekly journals are also graded ridiculously hard. Save your grade and avoid this Professor and course at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would say that this class can be an easy A if you have a lenient TA. If you have a TA that is not so lenient, you can kiss your A goodbye. The journals are either "complete" or "incomplete" and the rest of the grading is weird. It's very possible to get an A though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has as a very WEIRD grading system. There is only Complete or incomplete for assignments, so even if you get one thing wrong on a journal instead of getting say an 80 you are given an incomplete. A few more of these mistakes and you grade can drop from an A to a D in instant.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had the WEIRDEST way of grading. You could do perfect all semester but if you mess up on the last project you get a B or C. Discussions were mandatory and painfully boring. Overall easy class, you don't need to read everything. Grade is slightly dependent on who your TA is but if you put in a little effort you'll easily get an A.

Dr. C was fine. The class had a ton of readings, and most of them were kind of hard to follow at times. Her lectures were very drawn out and not as engaging as one would hope for. Weekly required discussion sections with our TA's did help a lot though in terms of understanding what was going on.

Absolutely take American Lit with Dr. CdeBaca-Cruz. The course itself is pretty easy, with a few readings per week and a reading journal at the end of the week. One or two essays throughout the semester, but you work on them and the reading journals during discussion groups. Even though this class is "American" literature, the readings are diverse.

Readings assigned each week with "Reading Journals" asking about the readings at the end of the week. Major grades from Midterm exam and Final Project. Discussion sections were meh. Didn't pay much attention in class, but if you paid attention, this is an easy A. CdeBaca is a good teacher and very responsive with comments and emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: 2-3 readings assigned each week. "reading journals" asking about the readings at the end of the week. I honestly did not read the stories and just used summaries. No other assignments, only one easy final project at the end that took me about a week. Discussions every week which kinda sucked. Easy A tho. U can tell she is passionate abt the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I can't express enough how much I loved this class! Professor CdeBaca is awesome and really cares about her students' learning. I usually am not an english person but this course was so engaging and transformational for me. Prof CdeBaca is so sweet and understanding, and even omitted some texts that put too much of a workload on us.

Professor CdeBaca is so sweet! She is probably the most understanding and accommodating teacher I've had this semester, which I appreciate. Lots of required readings for this class. Online, it wasn't very engaging, but the TA's make discussion pretty interesting! She's very intelligent and passionate about literature. Overall, a great person & prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: As an engineering major, this wasn't a dreadful class like other ratings. I was easily able to manage the weekly writings (200-300) words and the midterm and final project. There are a lot of readings, but they ALL aren't mandatory, you can read the some of it and make it through, which the majority do. The class mainly teaches you how to analyze
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. CdeBaca is a nice lady and is clearly very knowledgeable in her field, however, if you're like me and hate history, this course is basically another history class. This is probably what the class entails and it is not her fault that she must teach this, but she is not engaging at all. Any free time you have will go to reading for her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a good teacher, but the readings she gives will take up most of your free time. However, when it comes to grading assignments, the TA's come in, and oh boy, have fun trying to decipher the meaning behind your grade because you can put the same effort into two assignments and get entirely different grades. The rubrics are also a complete joke

Dr. C is a very nice woman however, she gives extremely long readings. You can expect about 2-3 long readings every night. Comprehension is impossible and her lectures are given through a live stream for Spring '21 so we can only ask questions through chat which aren't always answered. She goes into depth about the topics VERY early on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took him for Plan II philosophy. The entire class was graded on 3 tests (25% for each midterm and 50% for the final) and it was really hard to follow along with his lectures. Does not give makeup tests for any reason no matter how far in advance you contact him. If you're taking Plan II philosophy, take literally anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unbelievably impolite and disrespectful. Two essays constitute the entire grade and you won't receive your grade back in the first essay until after the deadline to drop a class. You'll have no idea of your standing. He simply wants your essay to regurgitate his exact opinion stated in class. Otherwise, he'll refuse to even grade it.

I took Deigh for Plan II Philosophy, and it was boring. I definitely think it's possible to get an A in his class if you work hard, but he's not a very engaging lecturer. However, he does explain well!

Lectures for an hour and a half with no slides or handouts. Very boring, which makes it incredibly hard to pay attention. Even if you write your papers using verbatim notes, he'll say you misunderstood the prompt. Submitted grades extremely late to the point where I was forced to use my OTE drop to save my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kinda boring lectures, it is the end of the semester and I still don't even really know who he is despite showing up everyday. But Deigh is very helpful during office hours, also a fair grader who will explain if you lose points or need help. I finally figured out what I was supposed to learn from Dr. Deigh, don't be a  snob and you will too.

His lectures are long and boring without any supplements or presentation materials to help learning. His class structure makes A's impossible, especially considering how tedious it is to pay attention in lectures. Thank goodness my TA understood outlined the main points of our many, many readings. Don't take unless absolutely necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a very tough grader. "Enjoys the sound of his own voice" is an understatement for his lectures. Grader your papers very very very late. Therefore, knowing your grade is quite a mystery. If you're thinking whether to take his class or not, just don't. Save yourself from stressing out about your grades and boring lectures.

Standard 3 long essays for the grade. He kind of repeats himself a lot and can stay off topic of the readings for that lecture which can be slightly annoying because the essays are about the readings. Don't take him if you can't sit through an hour of straight listening to a philosophy professor talking. Very kind and interested in students' input.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are not too compelling, but if you're truly interested in Philosophy you'll be able to keep up. The essays are long and time-intensive; prompts alone are about a paragraph. Most of class participation is just showing up, he does almost all the talking. He cares a lot about the students and material, so he's always available during OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is the easiest class you will take at UT. No exams or projects. 45% of your grade is from quizzes at the end of every class. One Instapoll at the end of each class (completion grades). There are 7 hw assignments, but they are multiple-choice Canvas assignments, around 20 q each. TAs are very sweet. Lots of EC (you won't need it).

Probably the easiest class I have ever taken. There were about 7 assignments in total for the entire semester. Lots of EC opportunities even if you don't need it. Def take if you need a science credit.
don is a sweetie pie would recommend for an easy science credit

Couldn't have asked for a better astronomy credit class. Professor Winget is super sweet. You can tell he loved teaching his class. No test and honestly that made my experience learning about astronomy so much better. Take if you want an easy A and love having a great professor.

Awesome guy. His class was super easy so I never really talked to him, but even though the topic was outside of my major he did get my attention a lot. Super passionate and you can tell he really cares. Loves engagement during class and always super willing to answer questions. Instapolls for attendance and quizzes + homework, no exams.

Professor Winget was amazing! His class was easy and offered a low-stress environment to learn about astronomy. It honestly helped me learn better, as I wasn't having to worry about cramming information. No tests, just weekly assignments and quizzes. His lectures are fun and will have you engaged. One of my favorite classes!
This class was super easy. There were 5 question quizzes after each class, but they were easy and have 2 attempts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures that are easy to follow! I learned more in this course than in other astronomy classes. Don is hilarious and a great professor. Not a heavy workload.

Don is hilarious but often goes off topic. He uses powerpoints to teach most of the time. There are no exams, just a ton of quizzes that get harder towards the end. No required book either! Theres also an extra credit assignment that can boost your grade. Overall a funny professor who understands his class is an INTRO to astronomy course.

I looked forward to Dr. Winget's lectures. They weren't always directly on the subject matter, but he was certainly entertaining for the most part. I did struggle a bit with the exams, but as long as you do attend the lectures and take notes on what he deems important, you should be fine for tests. Attend the review sessions put on by the TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didn't go to class once because the lectures confused me, just studied the slides online, and wound up with a B-. I did the extra credit project and it brought me all the way up to an A. It's a little hard to get high scores on the quizzes (there are 7, all multiple choice, 25 questions), but don't be intimidated. He wants you to do well.

Don is one of the easier choices for an Intro Astronomy class. No trig or anything crazy. He's engaging in lecture and actually cares about getting his students to understand. If you're struggling, he is definitely a professor who will help rather than slam the door in your face. Just try and you'll be fine.

Dr. Don Winget is a very accomplished astronomer and a great lecturer. He makes Astronomy interesting and really engages with students. He does not have tests but there are 8 quizzes, 1 every other week which are all multiple choice and not difficult. You don't need a book at all. He is responsive and will help you if you have questions.

Loved the professor but as for the class just do not take it. TAs grade horribly. Spent weeks working on the final project that was meant to help our grades and they graded mine horribly, brought my grade down. Ruined my GPA. Don't take this class if you heard it was easy.

The professor is sweet, he truly seems passionate about Astronomy. However, the quizzes in this class are the difficulty. There will be material in the quizzes that was very briefly discussed in class and that are puzzling to a non STEM major.

I came into this class thinking it would be an easy A and therefore I did not study that much for the quizzes. I did well for the first few quizzes and after that my grades just tapered off. He drops your two lowest grades and there's extra credit! Don is hilarious though and he's always cracking jokes to keep people awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don is a great professor. He is very passionate about astronomy and cares about his students. He can go off track in lectures sometimes but he makes sure to get the material across. If you like low stakes testing, this is the class for you. Also, DO THE PROJECT. It will replace two of your lowest quiz grades with the 2 that they already drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, makes class fun as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don rocks! If you're not super into astronomy, his lecture can get a little boring but he tells a lot of jokes and tries to tell stories to help you better remember the material. He really cares about making the course doable for the students and the quizzes definitely aren't hard if you take notes in class. Go to class and do the extra-credit!!

Winget was fun, but did go off on tangents. Lectures get boring often if astronomy or physics isn't your thing. You definitely need to understand the concepts to do well on tests. However, the project helps your grade A LOT. I had a B- up until the end of the semester and I got a really good grade on my project and I ended up getting an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don was an awesome professor who actually cared about his students. His class is structured differently than most classes I've had at UT as he does 8 exams, 1 every 2 weeks, but he drops your two lowest scores and will drop your next two lowest scores and replace them with an optional project grade if you want.

Don Winget is a cool guy with a really easy system of grading. This is by far the easiest science class I've ever taken. He can sometimes go off on tangents, but it doesn't really detract much from the class. He has really interesting stories and he's hilarious. If you're going to take a science, take this one.

Don is a fantastic professor. His lectures were consistently interesting and entertaining. You can tell he loves being an astrophysicist and a lecturer. His homework is very easy, and the exams are very similar to the practice tests he gives. If you have to take a science class, take his.

Don was a good professor and deserves his own late night comedy show. However, his lectures seemed to drag on forever and I found myself zoning out a lot. I am interested in astronomy, but this class couldn't hold my attention because of the content. I recommend Don as a professor, but this class just wasn't for me.

Don is one of my favorite professors at UT! The class was always thoroughly entertaining, and his jokes made learning about astronomy extremely easy. The first test was somewhat difficult, but once you've encountered the testing style, the following tests are a lot easier. I don't think his "tangents" are disruptive whatsoever.
Tests are tricky! Nalin and Sarafina are bad TA's! Easy B but Difficult A.

Winget's a good professor, but this won't be an easy class if you find yourself unable to become interested in astronomy. Tests can be pretty tricky. This is still not a difficult class to pass: there are four exams and no final. The lowest score is dropped automatically, and he lets you do an optional project to drop another. Overall fair course.
not a tough class, multiple choice tests but can sometimes be tricky or particular

Really really interesting lecturer- you cannot pass the class if you don't show up for lectures. 90% of test questions are based on lectures, but he's really helpful and gives you review material before tests.

Don is a really cool professor. Anyone who says this isn't an easy A didn't work hard enough. His tests are all multiple choice, he drops the lowest, and you can make up the second lowest with a project. He doesn't use the +- system, so I got an A even with a 90.8. Would recommend this to any non-science major.

Although didn't get an A in this course, it was really refreshing to have such a passionate professor. His tests can be tricky at times but he encourages you to ask for help and provides review sessions the day before every test. Not to mention that he also provides practice exams so you know what to cover. He's very approachable and kind. Do it!

Don is a great professor. Although I found his lectures to be slightly on the dry side, they were tolerable unlike a lot of science professors. 4 tests, 3 HWs, and an observing assignment are what make up the grade. There is an optional project that is super easy that can drop a test grade. Don clearly cares about his students and astronomy.

I had no prior interest in Astronomy, and now I am absolutely fascinated by it thanks to Don.  He is an awesome teacher who gives his students plenty of opportunities to get an A.  Reviews are very similar to the tests, and the homeworks are graded very fairly.  You do have to put in effort, but it is worth it.  Favorite professorclass this fall.

Completely agree that Don frequently goes off topic. He always has a side remark on everything he has to say, and most is not relevant at all. It was humorous at first, but when he goes off  95% of the time, it becomes harder to follow what his main point is. If there's one thing I learned from this class, that would be Don dislikes politicians.

So I took this class based on word of mouth and reviews, it was SUPPOSED to be an easy A. Don't believe that for one second. If you're taking an average to heavy course load this class will be a nightmare. Winget is funny and nice but goes off on tangents and is not incredibly clear. If you don't have time for astro physics don't take this class.

Don is great! He is clearly passionate about astronomy, but he realizes that not all of his students want to pursue it as a career. On the first day of class he told us that his goal is to make us love astronomy and pursue it as a hobby. Overall he seems like a great guy and has a nice sense of humor.

GREAT professor! He is so funny and always making jokes. He makes astronomy so interesting through his passion. He gives you plenty of opportunities to succeed. Even even holds 2 hour review sessions the night before the test. If you have to take astronomy, take him.

Great prof. He's very helpful and his tests are pretty easy. This class is an easy A if you go to class most of the time and review the practice exams and the notes. The stuff toward the end of the class gets harder and more boring, so pay attention at the beginning and do well on the first tests so you dont have to take the last one.

He was alright... I guess. Really boring lecturer he kind of just reads of slides. The essays are super easy basically just completion grades. His exams are kinda hard, you are expected to remember a lot of things that are very inconsequential, which is fine, they are just hard to remember because his lectures are so boring.

Professor Leal is very accommodating and kind, but his lectures can get lengthy or tangential. Not super heavy reading load, but keep up with notes as exams can get detailed; make sure you understand concepts and key events/figures. 10 short response essays (33%), 2 Exams (66%). Attendance optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The majority of the grade is made up of two pretty easy exams --- you just have to make sure to read all the slides super carefully and take detailed notes from them. I attended probably less than 50% of the lectures, but I still did fine when I dedicatedly studied for the 5 days before the two exams. Attend his pre-exam review sessions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exams are based off of tiny details in the lectures that don't seem to be that big of deal, therefore get missed when studying seemingly more important things. the lectures are so boring

Attend the lectures - the class is 10 essays and then 2 tests and although the essays are easy 100s the tests are graded based on more stuff from the lecture. This is includes random fun facts on the test that he gives that really is not substantial information so if you forget these fun facts on the test you are cooked.
He's nice! Lectures are interesting but I attended about 50% of the time. He clearly cares about the subjects he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Leal was a fantastic professor, he always made his lectures interesting with all of his jokes and he genuinely cares about government. The exams are very easy if you bring the double sided notecard to them, and the reflection essays are loosely graded, you can basically write whatever and still get a 100.

This man is a GEM and definitely the best option for GOV310L. Exams are multiple-choice and oddly specific to his lecture slides, but he allows you to use a double-sided notecard so use that to your advantage. He's very wholesome and makes a lot of squirrel jokes.

Dr.Leal is a phenomenal educator, he is approachable & caring. Lecture heavy but very interesting & easy to follow. He also likes the ut turtles & squirrels. Holds lots of review sessions before exams. He is also very passionate about the course material. If you need a gov credit and can, take his class.

Dr. Leal is a funny squirrel obsessed professor that I would recommend to anyone trying to find a GOV 310L credit. His tests are lengthy but easy to answer with clearly wrong answers to help eliminate options. He has a textbook listed but I have not used it once in class so buy it only if you want to.

Professor Leal is a great professor and you will get a lot out of the class if you show up to most of his lectures and glance at the textbook. The course is graded on a few completion essays which are easy and tests that are challenging but not impossible, and he gives a generous curve. Not an easy A, but a great class if you are interested in gov.

Leal is a sweet guy but not a classroom manager. Tends to get distracted and is a slow grader. Will forget about important dates and assignments coming. That said, incredibly knowledgeable and helpful. Readings aren't really necessary, come to class and you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a super easy class. Lecture isn't mandatory, but I'd recommend going as much as you can. Leal posts the ppts but you can fall behind quickly. Grades were based on 10 2-page essays (graded easily) and 3 exams. Professor Leal is super sweet and very approachable. He loves squirrels and constantly brings them up in class. He's great!

He loves squirrels, but besides that, Prof Leal is test heavy, on paper, 100 questions. Attendance is not mandatory. TA Cheyenne is more helpful than Prof Leal. Prof Leal will not help you with your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laid-back professor who emphasizes the discrepancies between textbook and reality in implementation, goes on tangents about his own experience in government and gets behind on schedule. Never once opened the textbook. Summarize the tangents for writing assignments, remember what he says about each bullet point on the slide and you're golden.

The class is graded on three 100 question tests (25% each) and 10 short reflection essays (other 25%). Since it was graded on so little you need to make sure to study for each exam to get an A. The reflection essays are easy As, just annoying to do. There is no final exam and professor leal is very kind and you can tell he cares about his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: You will have to write 10-2 page papers on various chapters of the textbook over the course of the semester. He's cool about letting you turn them in late, and while his lectures aren't very exciting, he does a good job of covering the topics thoroughly. The tests can be difficult because they draw so much from the textbook, which is pretty dense.

Professor Leal is a great guy. He loves squirrels too (mentions them at least 5 times a week). His class was difficult in my opinion. His tests were around 75 questions and you had little time to complete them. The final essay was easy, but the tests really lowered my grade. If you struggle with fast-paced tests I wouldn't recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Leal is super nice. There is no homework, just 3 tests and a paper. There are 100 questions in 75 minutes with lots of short answers. The questions can be super random and challenging. He is nice though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very passionate which makes the lectures enjoyable. I personally have little interest in government, but he did a great job maximizing my interest. I honestly believe this class might not be as difficult as I made it on my self. The key is that basically everything is on his PowerPoints. When you take your tests, have them open.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His exams are so packed full of stuff that you have to race through the exam to get everything done on time, leaving you to turn in a steaming pile of garbage. exams consisted of 20 term identifications and an essay. Boring material, boring guy, wouldn't touch this class again.
IVY league professor, eh? Save your effort and time. Choose a different professor.

Dr. David Leal is a knowledgeable guy; however, he has high expectations and principles that he doesn't follow himself. This morning my class got our grades back from our written exam. There are no comments or points explaining where the most points were lost. We are less than two weeks shy of our next exam and he wants improvement with no feedba
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Okay, I took David Leals Immigration class. Almost the worst decision of my life. His TA graded too hard. I didnt like that he covered so much info FULLY covered slides of info. Trying to even just take notes was too much. He does post the slides before hand online. Let me just say this, Ive never got less than a A+ NEVER. I got a D- in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Leal is a really sweet guy who is genuinely passionate about the field and wants everyone to succeed. I highly recommend him and this class!

A truly caring professor. He wants his students to succeed and will help if you have any concerns or questions. Make sure you use the textbooks for exams and that you use the powerpoints... if you do, you'll get an A. He's a really kind man and is extremely passionate about teaching.
Tests were hard but if you come to class you will be fine. His lecture slides come almost straight from the book so theres no need to read if you go to class.

Great professor. While sometimes the lectures could get boring, his humor and passion for the material made it worth attending. He always held review sessions before the exam and made sure to answer any questions anyone had during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: I didn't go to class but I studied well for the tests by reading the textbook side by side with his powerpoint slides . If you put in decent time and effort doing that you should get an A. There is also one writing assignment that is somewhat lengthy but not hard. Overall, his class was very doable and he is a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: In order to make an A I just read the textbook and new important parts. His tests were extremely lengthy I'm talking hundreds of multiple choice questions but they were all multiple choice and he often puts funny answers you know are wrong, so the class is very doable. He makes a lot of jokes about squirrels and he was a nice guy. Just read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: avoid this class if possible, unless you really like squirrels.

Not much work outside of class, just readings. If you want to know everything about congress or plan on working in congress, this class will teach you more than even imaginable about procedure and political science. Professor Leal is very, very knowledgeable on the subject given his experience working for a senator. I can't recommend him enough.

Professor Leal has a unique personality that I haven't seen elsewhere during my time at UT. He is genuinely curious about congressional procedure and political science. He has been, by far, the most politically neutral professor I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: The class was mediocre at best. In class, I was annoyed by how he said one thing, while his Powerpoint slides said another. The final exam was a 300 MC question combo of the final third of the class and a comprehensive review. The textbooks were too boring and dense to read. Curves were good though. Looking back, I should've tested out or done ACC.

Dr. Leal is a really sweet guy who is super passionate about government. The class has one midterm, one final, and two writing assignments that are relatively easy. The tests were hard in my opinion, just make sure you take good notes in class and read the textbook from the beginning, he does however usually give generous curves.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not very responsive to communication outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's definitely not an easy class and you have to work hard. Many kids don't do well because they except the teacher to feed them everything. I've recieved A's on the exams without the generous curves he gives out so it's possible. The lectures can come off as boring but I respect him as a teacher as he is extremely knowledgable and articulate.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Your grade relies on only three tests (and a paper that is only 5% of your grade and is easy to get a 100) and you better get ready to know every single detail about us gov because some of the questions get pretty involved. The final is cumulative and made me a broken woman. But he is knowledgeable and nice! Why does he love squirrels so much?
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: US Congress. His exams are so packed full of stuff that you have to race through the exam to get everything done on time, leaving you to turn in a steaming pile of garbage. exams consisted of 15 term identifications, an essay, and 10 multiple choice questions. Boring material, boring guy, wouldn't touch this class again.

He only has tests as grades which include random questions he never mentions in class or is talked about in the textbook. There is three tests and one writing assignment which is only 5% of your grade. I read the entire textbook and showed up to all the lectures. Impossible to get an A in this class. Lectures are pointless and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Leal was a great professor and I was happy to take him during my last semester at UT (Spring 2017) grade consisted of 3 exams and 1 paper. The exams came straight from the powerpoints and the paper was over a book of our choosing. Exams were easy if you out 2 days of studying in and the paper was short and an easy A. I rarely attended lecture.

Really nice and interesting prof. I appreciated that he encouraged discussion in class, made it more engaging. Exams are easy if you read through the chapters and attend class, generous curves (first exam was curved by 10 points!). Can be a lot of reading if you fall behind. An approachable guy, great speaker; class is pretty clear-cut, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Beware of the squirrels. But seriously good government teacher. I respect him a lot. Teaches government in an unbiased manner.

Professor Leal is VERY knowledgable. However, he spends way too much time on a single slide, and we often found ourselves 2 weeks behind where we should be in the curriculum. Have to read out of 2 books AS WELL AS an online book (but that's free). His lectures get pretty boring and lots of people fall asleep during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Leal is an amazing lecturer who knows just about everything there is to know about government. HIs class is based off of three tests and a very small research paper. You will have to read but the reading is not hard to understand. 90% of test questions come from his lecture so take good notes and an A should be no problem.

Leal is a great professor who passionately cares about his job! Definitely need to attend class because most of his test questions come from the lefture! Take this class if you want a great professor and a high grade!
Prof Leal is a great guy who is really passionate about government. Great class to take and although many don't go to class after the first day, it really helps and he's a pretty funny guy!

Great class! Prof Leal is very quirky and tries to keep the class upbeat. The midterms are very straightforward and actually test your knowledge of the material. The one con is that there are three books that are essential, but as long as you skim that material for general ideas, it's not that big a deal.

Profesor Leal loves government and you can definitely tell. At times he gets too stuck on a subject or slide (but really its because he just knows so much he doesn't know how to stop). He cracks jokes and gives examples throughout class. Get ready to study a lot for tests though because they are the only grades he gives (and one writing assignment)

I found the lectures to be a waste of time, they're just pretty much over the material in the assigned chapters of the book. The tests are all multiple choice, and again, just straight forward and over the material from the book and other readings. You have to do the readings to be able to pass the tests. Pretty easy and straight forward class!

Dr. Leal is very fair and will describe the test at length before examination, usually giving you 2-4 possible prompts for the essay section. If you come to class and look over PowerPoints before the tests, you are good. Latino Politics was not the most interesting class I've had at UT, but I'd be happy  to take any course with Dr. Leal again.

All multiple choice tests that were for the most part straight forward. It's a necessity that you read and study the textbook to get a good grade on tests. Leal isn't very clear on what exactly he'll be testing on in class and tends to go off on rants. His TAs hold review sessions before tests. Only two short essays that the TA grade easily.

Had him for my UGS class and contrary to popular belief, this class is NOT an easy A. I thought all UGS classes were GPA boosters, but his is one of the hardest. The material isn't hard, but he's a tough grader. Very nice guy and extremely knowledgeable. Take a class with him, just not this one.

I took latino politics with him. Great teacher and great guy. Class has a midterm, paper, and a final. The course is not easy but if you go to every class, pay attention, and take good notes you will do fine. Works mostly off of powerpoints and discusses them. This is where most of the test comes from. No need for the books.

very simple, straightforward format. 1 problem set a week, 3 tests total with cheat sheets. Challenging class but basically impossible to fail given the grading scheme, allowing you to focus on the content rather than the grade. Would def take her again over other profs

Moshkovitz is a great lecturer with a lot of experience in the field. She was accessible and always willing to answer questions. Weekly homeworks are usually not too difficult (1-2 questions each). Exams are not too difficult but have a strict time limit. All problems are graded on an A-B-C-F scale. TA discussion section is helpful.

Very solid algorithms class. Lectures require careful attention to follow fully. Homework and exams are very fair. They can be tough (given the course). Shafik was an excellent TA. Moshkovitz explains things well, but be sure to phrase your question clearly so she understands how to best answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Algorithms is an inherently difficult course by idea, but her lectures make it much more fun and approachable (great lecturer tbh, except writes 1 like i). I think she delivered the content very well. Psets helps with content understanding. Exam is difficult (by nature) but very fair. (provides textbook but lecture is sufficient)

Tests are very hard but she curves. If Shafiq is still the TA, I highly recommend taking with Moshkovitz, he knows what he's doing + his homeworks aren't bad. Her lectures can be difficult to follow but she's great at answering questions and organizing notes on the board. I think the majority of reviews here are exaggerating, she's a solid choice.

Her lectures are extremely unclear, writes in hieroglyphics. Better off watching YouTube videos (Abdul Bari). She skips steps, doesn't always prove things but expects us to be able to prove them, and grading on HW and exams is very subjective and harsh. Take Fraij, THIS IS NOT WORTH, everyone else is lying. I'd take OS over this class any day.

Exams were an extreme time crunch and quite stressful. Lectures felt a bit unstructured - it was tough to take notes a lot of the time, as there wasn't much of a category to what she taught (and it was difficult to tell what was necessary information vs. something she found interesting). Not bad overall, just mid.

The tests need you to be pretty creative to do well. The lectures were good IMO, but the discussion sections were very disorganized. The homeworks help you study for the tests, and she gives a huge curve at the end. It is very possible to succeed in this class, and I think she explains things well.

Very unstructured class, lectures are not recorded, lecture notes are very minimal, doesn't really explain how to understand proofs, but rather just tells you how to do a specific proof. It would be helpful if she taught the fundamentals of proofs. Discussions are meaningless since the TA covers things that aren't even on the test. Take fraij

Explained content very well in class. Zoom notes were very pretty (especially illustrations) and were conveniently uploaded to Canvas. HWs and exams were very challenging and required a lot of creativity.

Moshkovitz, above all, is a very caring person. She offered to personally help students during SNOVID, enjoys teaching the class, and encouraged student participation to make the class as interactive as possible. Not only that, but her lectures are fantastic. The only source of stress is the unclear grade cutoffs, but I found it very forgiving.

I was horrified of this class initially but professor Moshkovitz is really caring and a great lecturer. Discussion sections were quite helpful as well. Do the problem sets (though they tend to be difficult and take a long time), read the textbook, and do LOTS of practice problems, and you will be fine for the 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Moshkovitz was a great lecturer and I got a ton out of going to class (and discussion session). Tests are reasonable and there's a lot of support in terms of office hours/Piazza that makes the homework very doable. Prof Moshkovitz is very passionate about algorithms and complexity and was always very approachable if I had extra questions.

Knows her stuff but difficult to follow if you are an average person. Lectures are heavy/bland. Writes on board only, no in-class slides/online notes. Exams are harder than hw because you get a cheat sheet, but curved accordingly. You'll probably learn more than w/another prof but you really have to work for it &still possibly end w/ a low score.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're graded a 0, 1, 2, or 3 on each assignment/exam, so grades aren't really clear. They said at the beginning of the semester that a 1 could be a C- depending on where everyone falls. You'll need to attend lectures and discussion sections for good notes. She allows cheat sheets on all her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's an AMAZING professor who's extremely talented and caring. She teaches the material clearly and is very fair with grading. I was so nervous for this class initially, but I thoroughly enjoyed her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Having come into the course expecting one of the hardest experiences of my undergraduate career, It was a breath of fresh air to have Dr. Moshkovitz make the material approachable and lectures engaging. Pay attention in class, ask questions, start early on problem sets, and spend time understanding the algorithms at hand and it's an easy A.

The class is very hard, but that's determined by the material and other profs are not any different. However the professor is aware of that and is really generous on the grading. HW are super hard but shout out to the amazing TAs! Tests are again, also difficult but you can bring one page of notes with you. Overall not a bad class

Honestly - the best professor I have ever had at UT. Professor Q is so kind and really is passionate about what he teaches. The material is interesting too, just be sure to keep up with the readings and GO TO CLASS! Would take another course with him again. 10/10.

Professor Q is the best. Attendance is not technically mandatory but participation is a chunk of your grade, so make sure you stay on top of that. Honestly, I would just go as much as you can. He is a great lecturer and the tests are easier if you're in class. I highly recommend this class and any you can take with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've ever had at UT. The material could be seen as boring, but his engaging lectures and passion for the subject make it very interesting. Attendance is not a grade, but participation is, so I'd recommend going as much as possible. The tests aren't bad, just keep up with readings.

Nice and very passionate prof, interesting course. If your name isn't easy to pronounce you have to fight to participate cause you won't get called on. People in the front row get more priority. Be prepared for people to ask obvious questions/repeat wrong answers just for participation point. Constantly falling behind in lecture/getting off topic.

Business law sounds like it would be boring, but he makes it exciting and shows how useful it is for everyday life. He makes lectures engaging, interesting, and memorable. As a CS major, this class felt like a breath of fresh air. Definitely one of my favorite professors at UT. Just make sure to keep up with the readings and participate in class.

Prof Q is one of the best. You will want to show up to class b/c his lectures are so great, but be ready to raise your hand and participate for a grade. I didn't find exams too difficult, he will try to trick you but everything tested is taught in lecture. This class will make an impact on your life!

He truly cares about your learning. Attendance is not mandatory, but participation (speaking- he keeps track) is graded, so you should show up. His lectures are fun anyway, and his teaching style is easy to understand. He is also very funny and keeps his students very engaged. Just make sure you are doing work for his class or he will call you out.

Genuinely the best lecturer I have ever had, even for a class that didn't require attendance I found myself wanting to go hear him speak. If you knew me you would know how shocking that really is. Would highly recommend to anyone, he made what I thought was going to be a boring class for my minor into one of my most memorable courses ever

AWESOME lecturer, so knowledgeable, teaches so well, super inspiring and down to earth/real with you, useful content. Hardest part about him is his quizzes and test questions, he makes things tricky and traps you but also everything he tests about has been lectured over. Take him and you will appreciate how much you change + grow.

This was hands down the best class I've ever taken at UT. He gives 100% every single class and you can genuinely feel how much he cares about teaching and his students. I looked forward to every class because he made everything engaging and meaningful. If you get the chance to take him, DO IT. Easily the BEST professor at UT!

AMAZING. Resources readily available, TA's communicative, assignments clear and professor brought a warmth, passion, and enthusiasm that kept the room full every lecture in a non mandatory attendance class. This class made me remember what it was like to love learning. Best class I've ever taken, can't say enough good things about Prof Q.

I love this man; he is an incredible lecturer and an extremely caring, intelligent professor. I can't say enough good things about him, frankly. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Professor Quintanilla, DO IT! I promise you will never be bored in class, and you will always have a caring professor to rely on.

I am so sad I will be graduating and will not be able to take his course again. He's kind, caring, knows every student and will check up on you even after you are done with his course. Engages everyone and genuinely made me question if I wanted to go to law school because of how interesting this class was. Last day of class had everyone in tears.

Professor Quintanilla was incredibly kind, wise, and passionate. If I could re-take his course every semester I would. And the only thing I mourn about graduating is to not be able to retake his course again.

I looked forward to class everyday. Prof Q lectures in such an engaging and conversational way that even the most dry law facts become memorable. At first I was scared about the participation requirement but there were so many opportunities to answer questions. And he made it a point to remember students' names despite teaching hundreds a sem.

prof q is so goated. he truly cares about his students & it was one of my favorite classes. lectures were insanely engaging that it's pretty much impossible to be bored in class. we could use the textbook and our notes on exams & participation is part of your grade, but prof q made it pretty easy to get all your points. he also has the best TAs.

Professor Quintanilla was one of the best professors I have ever had at UT. His teaching style is incredibly engaging, and he offers patience to every one of his students when they make the effort. He connects concepts to the real world rather than teaching law and ethics in a sterilized environment. Read before class + participation is encouraged!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Quintanilla is personable, and an amazing lecturer. He makes concepts easy to understand and remember. I just wish grading was focused more on the material than participation in class and exams with questions about specific things from class. Make sure to read the articles that the TAs send out. Overall, a fantastic professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: only take this class if you're a good test taker. the exams are written in a confusing way so you can fail.

If you think law might ever be applicable to you, you have to take this class. This may be the best UT professor. The professor is amazing. Be aware that he is pushy to have participation in class, but the questions are low stakes and easy to follow. Class preparation can require some reading from a mandatory McCombs textbook which is not cheap.

This was the best class I've taken at UT because of the absolute passion Quintanilla has for the course. It makes you want to show up to lectures. Reading isn't bad as it's mostly learning about vocab concepts and learning how to apply them. If you have a chance to take any of his classes you will not regret it. Truly a role model.

Prof Q is amazing, and my favorite prof so far. He's super caring, very funny, and makes things genuinely interesting to learn. Everyone loved it, would take it again. Exams are a little hard, I attended almost every lecture and read and still never got above a 90. But still a great class!

By far the best professor I've had at UT the past 3 years. Please take this class for your business minor! Lectures are very entertaining, engaging, and he makes a point to get you to think critically. He's an avid hater of TikTok though :)

Professor Q is one of the best professors I've had, he is so amazing and really is passionate about what he does! The class is him having a conversation with you the whole time, as long as you take notes he will give you everything you need for the exams. Group projects are graded by the TA and are very easy. Participation is super easy as well!!!

This is the BEST class I've ever taken at UT. Prof Quintanilla teaches material in the most passionate, well-thought-out, relatable way - it's truly inspired. He does require class participation (has us pull out name cards at the beginning of each class), but believe me when I tell you it's never intimidating, and has kept me consistently engaged!

MUST TAKE! Best teacher in my entire life. Didn't know anything about law and still got an A. Stay up on readings to do good on tests. Tests are open note!! Go to the lecture, as that is where most test questions come from. Every lecture was so fun and entertaining. Truly UT's best professor!!

The BEST professor at UT. If you come to class and skim the textbook you'll be fine. Exams can be a little hard for some, but I found them incredibly straightforward since I never skipped class and did all of the readings. Genuinely my favorite professor EVER. He's an amazing lecturer.

THE BEST PROFESSOR! He keeps all students engaged and expects students to understand concepts (which he makes easy if you come to class) rather than memorize terms. I wish all my professors were like him, I definitely recommend him!

Professor Q's class was very insightful and helpful for the future. I definitely recommend taking him if you need a business credit (like for the advertising degree) like I did. He really brought the material down to a level that an average person could understand and made it engaging. Professor Q's passion for Business Law helped me actually learn

Prof. Q is of the best professors I have had at McCombs. He made the classes fun and made an effort to get to know each and every student in the class despite it being online. Pay attention to lectures and you will be golden for the exams.
Interesting lectures that keep you engaged. Not a difficult class but you need to pay attention and study in order to do well.

Prof Q is actually amazing. Caring, kind, and super good at holding the room and maintaining attention of the class. Wants to know your name! You MUST go to class to be successful on the exams, cannot stress enough. He has been my favorite professor at UT.

One of the best professors I have taken at UT!!! Prof Q is very charismatic and knows how to grab class attention. Attendance is not required, nor are the readings, but both are very helpful for Exams. The exam format is multiple choice, 3 exams, the first two noncumulative, and the last one is a term exam, so it is cumulative. Awesome guy

Lectures are everything. You don't have to read as long as you attend the lectures (I would still do it cause it helps on tests). Tests are open notes and mostly based on the lectures. He is genuinely so funny and has the best scenarios for class. Definitely my favorite professor and class at UT. He makes a hard class simpler! Take him!!!!!

This class ought to be required for all UT students - very important material, you'll thank yourself for learning it. Prof Q himself is an engaging and animated lecturer, I can't imagine anyone better to teach such an important class. Passionate, fair, funny, and sharp as a whip.

Prof Q is awesome!!! Business law/ethics is a tough, detail heavy subject that can be boring at times, but prof Q made this class quite enjoyable. There is not an insane amount of homework, just a few papers and like two group projects. Lectures were always interesting and enjoyable. Just go to class and you will do fine!! Highly reccomend.

He was so sweet & funny. To people who claim he likes to "trick" his students... if you came to class he literally said he would trick us on the test so whose fault is that? He does cold call but the class is fun so you won't be embarrassed or scared to answer. The tests do have specific lecture content, but they're easy. Textbook is super easy too

This class was my favorite class. He does cold call, but he makes it so fun that you end up wanting to participate. And this is coming from someone who never raises their hand. The tests are easy if you go to class, and his textbook is the modified version compared to the other LEB professor's textbooks. Open note and book tests.

Hilarious professor with incredibly engaging lectures that I not only actively listened to, but genuinely enjoyed going to. Highly recommend that you go to all the lectures, as the test questions typically have stuff ripped from lectures (e.g. "The conclusion that we determined in class regarding the means principle of the Trolley Problem was...")

by far my favorite professor at UT!! amazing and entertaining lectures, he genuinely really cares about students and loves teaching. tests are very lecture-based, so while attendance isn't req. you should definitely still go to class + bc of the mandatory participation (which is not bad, hes nice even if ur wrong) i would def recommend!
This guy is the MAN. Best professor I've had at UT by far. Take him.

Prof. Q is a gem! Genuinely such an inspiring man with a clear passion for doing the right thing and helping people learn. Lectures are a lot of fun and very interesting - even some of the more dry subjects are enjoyable because of him. Tests are completely manageable, just study in advance, read the textbook, and you'll be good!

Professor Q is an amazing lecturer. His lectures were engaging, and he prioritized communicating important and useful concepts. Tests were lecture-heavy, so attend class and be attentive. Not too many assignments but good amount of quality writing needed.

I MADE AN ACCOUNT JUST TO RATE PROF Q 5/5!! I'm not even joking when I say this is the greatest teacher I have had in my time being in school. I will probably tell my kids just how good he was. His "lectures" are incredible the way he gives hypotheticals. And will literally spend class time telling us how much we matter to him. Hands-down the best!

Best professor ever. I enjoy his classes and often think about everything i learned in it. I wish every professor was like this. He sends encouraging messages and is just a wonderful example of a great person overall. TAKE IT! best business minor for sure!

Best business minor class hands down. Interesting content and clearly passionate about the subject. You learn a lot just by showing up and participating, don't even need to put in that much effort to retain information. Tests are super easy if you pay attention. Really fun class and really charismatic guy. He has a great personality

I LOVE PROFESSOR QUINTANILLA. HE'S THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UT AND SIMPLY DESERVES THE BEST IN THIS WORLD. He is truly so passionate about teaching and it shows. He is inspiring and respected. He loves his students and business law, the best professor ever.

This prof is AMAZING!!! He is such a wonderful lecturer and everyone comes to class even though you only need to talk a handful of times for your participation grade. I have never loved a class more. 10/10.

Lectures frequently go off topic and on random tangents which wouldn't necessarily be a problem but he likes to trick students who don't attend class regularly and add questions on exams from class unrelated to the course. He usually spends half of class time yelling at students for not paying attention and class often feels like a waste of time.

He is a terrific lecturer and teaches a very compelling class. I would give him 5/5, but was not given my participation points (10% of your grade). Said you only had to participate 3 times to get full credit; I participated 6 times and only got a 7/10. Take notes on the class and book for open note exams; it helps a lot to merge them w the slides.

Amazing professor and although I ended with a C (all on me I was lazy this semester until the final) as long as you go to class, read and participate, and look over the exam reviews you're golden. Prof Q uses real examples instead of just reading off slides and cares so much about his students. Highly recommend!

One of my favorite professors at UT. I learned so much in his class and truly enjoyed lectures and what we were learning about. Will call on you in class but usually the answer is on the board or if you don't know he's super chill about it. Gives cool uncle vibes.

This class is awesome and the prof really emphasizes attending class because he discusses test material which can't be found in the text. Also, participation is a big part of his class but he's not rude if you don't know the answer to his question. The exams are hard if you don't study. Read the book, go to class, take notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Q has become one of my favorite professors at UT. His lectures are engaging! I learned alot. He is also such a nice, caring person. If you show up and listen, you will do great on the exams!

Prof. Q was the best professor I had at  UT, and I am a junior. He genuinely cares about each of his students and teaches topics that are important to our future. Attend class and be ready to talk. The lectures are truly interesting,  and it helps to go to do well on the exams. A few group projects but nothing major. Read and attend class.

I didn't do the best in this class ( to my standards) but I respect Professor Q a whole heck of a lot. He was a great professor when I had him and I learned a lot. It is evident in his teaching style that he truly cares about his students. For my business minors/ people going into law, if you have a chance to take him... highly recommend it.
Best professor I had at UT! Lectures are super engaging and exams are easy if you pay attention and take notes during class.

Professor Quintanilla's lectures were always so engaging and very easy to keep up with. Textbook was also an easy read and directly related to lectures. The assignments are easy, and exams (even our final) was online and all open note. Only thing I didn't like was the participation grade, but it's not too bad if you keep up with your readings.

Professor Q was very passionate about teaching and truly wants you to succeed. Lectures were actually fun to attend because he uses stories and example to explain concepts and he is genuinely a funny person. Participation is a good chunk of the grade so you will be expected to speak up occasionally but it makes the class a better experience.

This has been by far my favorite class. Prof. Q is an amazing lecturer and I really enjoyed going to class. It is very important to go to class and participate to get points.
