reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, but gave insanely hard tests. The class average for one of the tests was in the 50s.  He gives 4 exams with one drop and a final.  One of the TAs said that he was the hardest M408D teacher and that his tests were unnecessarily hard, and I have to agree. Great lecturer, but his crazy tests make it not worth it. Dont take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Staron is a great teacher, the tests aren't too hard, but they are unforgiving, so be careful. You will learn s great deal with Staron
Staron is an amazing professor. His lectures are worth going to and he provides many practice problems. Out of all the calculus professors, he is definitely one of the best.

I enjoyed having Staron as a professor, he's a nice guy, and his lectures went smoothly. Sometimes the tests were a bit tricky, and since they are mostly multiple choice you have to be careful. Overall, I think I learned a lot in the class.
Great professor. Tests are't too bad, but it's mostly multiple choice so be careful not to make silly mistakes. Still a challenging course, but Staron made it really enjoyable.
He is one of the few good profs in the math department. Totally recommend him. Very clear lectures. Good exams.

Prof. Staron is so good! He will put his lecture notes online if you miss class. If you're in class he writes the notes with you as class goes on, working all concepts and ideas out with practice problem. He's really good at explaining things and breaking them down and if you're ever confused, he's really chill in office hours. Plus he's hot too.

He's kind of rude in that he doesn't really seem to care much about his students, but he's open to questions and he's super clear. Also, his tests are just like his homework so do the homework. Overall, I worked my butt off and got an A, and it is very doable for most students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His class always had the highest average for midterms because he was definitely the best professor that semester.

His lectures were extremely disorganized and he was very unhelpful in office hours. The exams themselves were not difficult but he took off tons of points and strongly prioritized computational accuracy over actually learning the material. He is ok but I STRONGLY disliked his teaching style

Best math teacher/professor I've ever had! Really explains everything well and he writes what he says down as he goes and then posts the lecture notes online. Still should go to the actual class though, because things are explained better and he is great at answering questions. I would HIGHLY recommend this professor.

Tests were pretty easy, straight from homework or examples. Quizzes were honestly harder than tests. Couldn't really follow him sometimes but his TA was really good. He might be one of the professors you either love or hate because most people who said the class was easy tended to also go to a GE or office hours all the time.
Stellar, spectacular, extraordinary, fabulous, astounding, extravagant, super, wonderful, amazing, excellent, superb, suave, genius, brilliant, astute, clean, orderly, beautiful human being.

Staron is a great professor when it comes to teaching the material; However, it is hard to make an A. There is no room for error, no leniency, and no curve even if the test average is failing. He also makes countless mistakes on exam questions and doesn't correct them until half way through the exam, costing you time. Great professor, hard exams.

Staron is a great lecturer with clear lectures. I was fortunate to have a good TA who supplemented his lectures with tricky practice problems. The tests make you think a lot and are comparatively hard. Not an easy A class at all. Staron is very helpful during office hours and is open to all questions.

Lectures were great! He is very clear and organized for all of his notes and gives examples in class for students to work through. Homework is pretty standard Quest. Tests were pretty difficult though, in my opinion. The short answer sections on the test didn't have any partial credit which I hated. Textbook is used only at your discretion.

Dr. Staron is an AMAZING professor. He explains things very clearly. Weekly homework. Attendance is not mandatory but if you skip any, you'll definitely receive a bad grade. The only bad part is that his tests contain a lot of questions that are not straight-forward. It's more about truly knowing the subject than remembering formulas.

Dr. Staron is a stand-up guy! He's usually pretty friendly (unless you try to prove him wrong in class, don't do that, just trust the guy... he's the one with the doctorate). He's helpful during his office hours but get there early, it's usually packed! Tests are straight from Quest so just study homeworks and you'll be fine.

Staron is very enthusiastic about math, and knows what he is talking about. However, he seems to care very little about how his students are doing in the class.  - A lot of first year students ended up dropping the class or struggled through the rest - I did well on homework and studied for tests, still did not do well. - Very strict grading.
Pretty terrible professor. Thinks he's funny with sarcasm too.

Doesn't really care about the success of students in his class. Went to every discussion section, every class and took time to complete every homework and still barely passed. Makes the tests ridiculously hard and 9 times out of 10 doesn't give partial credit for problems.

Great professor; just a really really hard class. Hardest part is probably the grading distribution so that 90% of your grade is exams. Good guy willing to help; homework isn't bad. Expect to study a lot for exams.

Staron was honestly amazing at his job. He was extremely clear, knew how to explain things very well, and would always allow some time to ask questions about homework (btw expect a lot of it but it's necessary to pass) I think  overall he does a good job at providing all the resources needed to be successful. He is also very cute and sassy.

Nice guy, but doesn't always seem to have your best interests in mind. Although he's somewhat clear during lecture it sometimes seems like he doesn't care about your personal success and teaching is more a job to him than a passion. He'll run through examples during lecture but he goes pretty fast so keep up on the material.

Dr. Staron was not only fun and entertaining during lectures, but astoundingly clear in his explanations of all of the material. At the beginning of each class, he willingly helps with homework questions, and then clearly lays out the material to be covered in the lecture. Exams aren't exactly easy, but he more than prepares you!

I really enjoyed Staron as a professor. In classes, I would get lost a lot, but if you go to his office hours he clears EVERYTHING up. Don't be afraid to ask questions. Exams are tough, definitely redo homework and some problems from the book to make sure you got everything covered. Go to the TA sections!! They give you hints for tests.
He was super nice and really helpful in office hours. It's still  a calculus class though, so its going to be hard  and there's a lot of homework.

Professor Staron is incredibly awesome. Besides the fact that he is young, funny and interesting, he really knows his stuff. His examples are clear and he is happy to answer questions. He posts answers to quizzes and tests right after class, so it's really easy to study for his tests. He's extremely approachable. Very easy on the eyes.
Very very smart and clear. Tests aren't that bad at all!

Dr. Staron is an incredible math teacher. His notes are very easy to follow and he does a great job at explaining why and how things work the way they do. Tests and homeworks were not hard at all. As stated before, Staron is a great teacher and you can do very well in this class without ever having seen sequences/series/multivariable before hand.
This guy's awesome. Very clear and understandable lectures and just all around great dude.

Well organized. Available for help in office hours. His thorough knowledge makes the concepts interesting and applicable. He is young and has a sense of humor, which works well for college courses. The best math professor I have ever had. He convinced me to switch my major to mathematics.
Best math teacher I've ever had. He explains everything crazily understandably and offers as much help as you could need. Plus, he's nice on the eyes.

His lectures completely prepare you for the homeworks, and the exams are multiple choice questions that are variations of the preceding homework problems. As long as you attend lectures & put a good amount of effort into the homework, you'll get A's on the exams. He's very good at explaining concepts. I got an A w/out ever attending TA periods.

She is a very nice person, but I found it frustrating that she talked like we were children and over simplified math terms so much. Not the best preparation for intense calculus courses, but if this is the only math you have to take then you're good. Not much homework and you get cheat sheets on the exams

She is super sweet and understanding. Lectures are not mandatory but they aren't recorded and its hard to get notes. All test are easy because study guides are direct. Many resources and extra credit. 2/3 weekly assignments. Definitely can get an A if you study and do the work.

Just one of the nicest people ever, super fun and easy math class that is good for education/UTeach. Tests were easy, projects were fun. Awesome professor, and very good teacher too. Material was easy, but she is a great explainer of things. GOAT level professor, can't recommend enough

Pam is the best, truly makes math enjoyable and cares about what she's teaching! The hardest part about this course is exam time management in my opinion, but go to discussion sections, pay attention in class and get help when you need it, you will never be shamed by Pam or her teaching team!
Pam is the best! She allows a cheat sheet on exams, and her TAs are amazing too. A 10/10 class for precalculus.

Pam is an amazing professor!!! If you ever get the chance to take her class do it! She is inspirational, kind, caring, and makes sure everyone is understanding the content. She is also very approachable and accessible! Her TA's are also amazing. Can't stress how amazing she is!

I loved Pam, she is sweet,kind,& smart. She truly loves teaching, and you can tell. Attendance is not required (but you should definitely go because it helps a lot!). She builds in no-class days before and after holidays. Her office hours (along with the TA) are helpful. No matter how much math you have going in,she'll make sure you understand.

If you ever have the chance to take Pam as your professor, please do!!!! I just completed my first semester at the UT Austin, and she was without a doubt my favorite professor of the entire semester. Pam is so energetic, and she teaches the material in a way that helps you understand no matter what your math background is. She is the absolute best!

GENEUINELY THE BEST PROFESSOR!!!!!! Her lectures are engaging, and her explanations are clear and concise. The TAs are super helpful, the homeworks were easy, and she allows cheat sheets for her exams.

My GOAT. She gives you test reviews for the midterms and the final that match the test exactly and you get a one page cheat sheet (front and back). Attendance isn't required but the daily homeworks match what she does in class so it's best if you go. TAs are very helpful and reachable. Easiest class ever if you listen in lecture and put the work in

Here's the thing, Pam is incredibly sweet, funny, and always at your disposition, but I feel like explaining wise both her and my TA's could have done a little better. Solid 9/10 course, since office hours and discussions remediate that issue. I would take this again, but moving forwards in maths I would stay away from this prof.

I took Pam's Pre-Cal class during the fall semester of 2025. She was honestly amazing, but I also have to give credit to her amazing TAs. To pass this class is simple: attend lectures, ask questions, and attend both office hours and TA sessions when needed—no harsh grading system.

I had Pam for pre-cal in my first semester, and she was one of the best teachers I have had. She is so funny and creates an inclusive learning environment that encourages questions. She always has opportunities outside of class to meet with her if you need extra help. What is on the exams is clearly communicated by word or the Canvas reviews.

Pam is great! She allows cheat sheets on the midterms and your final, and graciously gives a review for each one as well. Lectures were never dull and I never felt discouraged in her class, truly a kind and passionate soul!
Pam is great! Only 2 midterms and she is so, so kind to allow a cheat sheet (for the final as well) and reviews before each one. Truly a kind soul.
This professor is genuinely the GOAT.

Pam is the BESTTTTTT. I took this class in order to prepare myself for calculus for the upcoming semester. She is honestly one of the sweetest professors and she's always ready to help. Her TA's are AMAZINGGGGGGG as well. Definitely take her!!

Attendance does matter in this class, aside from that, Pam gives you everything you need to succeed. She's super caring and tries to make math fun. She cares a lot about her students and is everything you should want in a teacher.

AMAZING, AMAZING, AMAZING. She's a wonderful instructor and her TA's are really good! Attendance isn't mandatory, but you have to be there to excel in the class. Her and her TA's make sure you learn the material and they are all easily accessible outside of class. 10/10 would recommend her as a professor.

Pam was such a great professor for a subject I was worried about. She is so nice, wants you to succeed so bad, and it showed with every interaction we had. 3 exams, but she basically tells you exactly what questions are on them, and allows for a double-sided cheat sheet. You will not find a better math teacher at this university so take her please.
Absolutely incredible professor. Not only is she funny and kind, but she knows her stuff and explains possibly difficult concepts in a really accessible and thoughtful way. I really enjoyed it.

Pam is the best professor ive ever had!! So good at explaining concepts and making sure you are understanding throughout the lecture. She is also very caring and wants you to succeed. Offers a one page front and back cheat sheet on every test. This course you are not allowed to use a calculator.

Pam is super supportive of her students and cares about their education. She explains mathematic concepts very clearly and uses fun activities to engage students. She is also hilarious and loves to throw jokes and stories into her lectures. Definitely recommend her!

Pam lectures so well and makes concepts so easy to understand. She is always happy to help you out with the material if you need and really cares about her students. Definitely recommend taking a class with her!
Professor Elias is such an amazing instructor, she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is really funny and engaging, and truly tries to strengthen benchmark math skills.

Pam is a great professor. She explains things very well and is more than willing to help, her goal is for every student to do well. She also helps you prepare for the test and make the concepts seem super easy.

Best professor I've ever had. Super kind- she genuinely cares about her students and wants us all to succeed. She is who I aspire to be studying education. Take any class with Pam!! You won't regret it

Professor Elias is absolutely hilarious and lectures extremely well. While the concepts can be challenging to wrap your mind around, she explains it so well that the class feels very easy. Her tests might seem difficult, but she prepares you very well, so there is no reason to worry. Totally would take this class again!
Really easy lab. Work was pretty much all group, but easy to do. The TA is super nice and Dr. K is very understanding if you have any issues. The lectures can be boring but overall not too bad.

New lab thoughtfully designed, not just busywork. Feels like you're contributing to real scientific research. Not too much work 1 credit. Wet lab meets 3 hours per week, but often get out at least an hour early. Midterm is tough with no multiple choice. You need to really know and explain concepts. Final is not harder than the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved her! She genuinely wants everyone to succeed and makes it a goal to not work outside of class since it is only a 1 hour credit course. This is a very easy A as long as you go to all the labs and understand the purpose of each lab. There are midterm and final lab practicals but they are fairly easy with an extra credit question.

she's WONDERFUL. this whole class is just writing one mini-systematic review on a nutrition topic of your choice. she guides you, assignment by assignment, and then you're all done about a month before finals. 10/10 i learned so much and wasn't even that stressed out about it. she's great, take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: final + midterm are doable, but she makes them seem so much easier than they were. other than that, there's one in-person lecture per week plus the lab, which is TA-based. you learn a lot for sure, and they make sure you're never doing too much work outside of class. overall worth it for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Klingbeil is a wonderful professor! Her lectures are very clear and concise with plenty of pictures to help students understand the material. She was also very kind in answering all of my questions. The quizzes and tests are a bit tricky, but at least they were open note. Projects and extra credit helped my grade :) 100% would take her again.

Dr. Klingbeil is AMAZING. She explains things SO WELL, is very clear and concise in her explanations, and is quite passionate too! Ask questions after class if you need, she will answer them well. Quizzes & tests were a bit more difficult but do-able because they were open note. Projects are fun! Overall great professor, would 100% take again.
Very easy class, all material was accessible outside of the class and all the tests and quizzes were open notes

most stressful class genuinely
i cried because of this class
a nightmare.
Don't want to be too harsh because I don't think she is all there. But she shouldn't be a professor anywhere to be completely honest

My previous review and many similar reviews were deleted. I'll try to keep this one without any commentary to avoid deletion. Fong reported me a few days before university closed in fall 2025 for a single programming assignment. I hired a lawyer and defeated her claims. I received an A in the class.

The in-class lectures are less than 30 minutes, and we are assigned difficult programming assignments that require a much deeper understanding of the content. The mass reporting makes the class extremely stressful. Take any other professor available.
reports everyone

Ton of work. Inconsistent syllabus and unnecessarily strict grading. Dr. Fong can be helpful during class but only if you come in already with a decent understanding of the material, and her lectures are very surface level. Mandatory $100 textbook unfortunately ends up being the most useful resource. Very stressful class, avoid this professor.

reviews.comment: There is a disconnect between the instructor's PhD specialization in CS Education and the technical nature of CS 429. The instructor lacks deep knowledge of the subject matter. The course would be better served by an instructor with a background in this discipline. The instructor should use their strength in CS Education within entry-level courses.
In-class lectures would be helpful
lectures are not helpful (lectures for 15-30min, then the rest you just do practice questions), required $99 zybook which are not helpful either

Well-structured class, reasonable workload, and fair exams. However, Dr Fong is the most exasperating professor I have ever had. Her grading is picky to a fault and she is not understanding at all. Truly feels like she goes out of her way to make her class as annoying as possible. $100 mandatory textbook btw.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: cheating reports aside, she's not a good professor. i self taught for EVERYTHING in this course - her lectures are around 20 minutes long and then you have to answer questions that are 10x harder than the practice for attendance. coding assignments have nothing to do with the class lectures. you're better off with ANYONE else, not worth the risk.

Prof. Fong did not lecture in class so we had to learn entirely before showing up. The programming assignments did not reflect inclass activities or textbook readings and were incredibly difficult. Exams were the same style as the mock, so studying was easier. She is quick to reply on Ed, but overall was very unhelpful in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take this course. I am paying tuition PLUS another $100 to teach MYSELF this entire course? Her lectures are bad. She doesn't teach you how to code and expects you to just figure it out with a BASIC idea of the concept. The coding assignments are difficult and lectures don't prepare you for them at all.

Mock exams match real tests, but lectures don't prepare you for the material. This isn't a true flipped class with structured online instruction so class can be used for practice. Instead, there were only introductory readings, so most of the material had to be self-taught. Programming assignments were extremely difficult with almost no guidance.

Very straight-forward class. Content is, for the most part, not difficult to grasp. Homeworks are a bit harder, but only take a few hours. Professor Fong is receptive to feedback and has your best interests in mind (as long as you don't cheat :P). The TAs were very helpful for in-class assignments, so definitely take advantage of that time.

Her lectures were below average in quality, so you have to rely on the textbook a LOT. She seems nice, and her mock exams are very like the actual exam, but if you rely on just her slides it sucks. Hard class in general

Guys... this class was extremely straight forward. Not many professors give a mock exam that is EXACTLY like the midterm exams. So, I really appreciate that directness. Just don't cheat. If you do cheat, be more slick and you can't get mad at the prof for doing her job and reporting people who cheat... She's a great professor and I recommend her.

DO NOT TAKE HER. absolutely horrible teaching and outside of the classroom spends more time reporting students over a mere homework assignment. Even if you drop the course she will still find you for "cheating" or having similar code to half the class for something that contained very common code. by far the worst prof ever encountered.

I've never felt so hateful in my 20 years as I have since Fong. Her lectures are useless, the workload is absurdly difficult for the single resource she requires. Her "flipped classroom" is pointless when everyone is equally confused and can't help each other. She uses free time to file reports instead of reflecting on why we need to work together.

reviews.comment: Repeatedly crossed Guad without looking in hopes of being hit by a car otw to her class. She reports everyone for some unknown reason, regardless of the fact that half the coding assignments require a specific direction to follow (i got reported). Lectures are unhelpful and self-learned everything through the readings.

reviews.comment: This teaching style is extremely inefficient. Students are forced to teach themselves because lectures provide almost no guidance. Class time is wasted on coding tasks that far exceed the allotted time, assignments don't reinforce concepts, and exams fail to measure real understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Students didn't receive an email or were contacted at all to explain themselves they were just automatically reported for having similar code structure/logic to other students The thing is the class is textbook heavy and the textbook code examples needed for assignments are the same. So how are student being blamed for following the textbook code.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor likes to give student anxiety by reporting them on their HOMEWORK assignment

This professor reports people on their homework assignments (ridiciously hard). Her lectures are boring and most of the time she just lets the notebooks do the teaching for her. She also doesn't follow her own syllabus.

professor is chill but reports often, honestly for the best to teach ppl to actually code, be sure to pay attention to 303e bc u will not pass if u dont know how to do the difficult assignments , other than that the class is ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Not a really good professor. She reports everyone for some reason.

Understanding and engaging with lecture depends on keeping up with the pre-class reading. The programming assignments are manageable, and office hours are genuinely helpful. She did report AI misuse, but it was specifically disallowed for programming assignments on the syllabus. She's very caring and funny!

Professor Fong has a flipped classroom with a textbook you teach yourself from, and then x2 a week, problem-solving sessions where she briefly touches on the material. The programming assignments are very difficult, TAs are somewhat helpful. Exams are easy. The reporting thing is cruel, considering there was no warning, but understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most people complaining because they probably got flagged. She has good lectures, summarizes the key aspects of the readings, and her daily assignments are really fine if you do the readings/lectures. Tests are also super light. The prog. assignments are bad because they are a huge step up from lessons, but expected for a medium-level CS course.

Aside from the reporting everyone thing here are some genuine critiques (I got reported). If you take this class be ready to learn pretty much entirely on your own. During class she lectures for 5 minutes and then lets you work on usually a needlessly hard in class coding assignment. Only good thing about her is the exams. Pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR EVER. take this class if you want to grow grey hair.
If you actually want to learn, DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She lectures for ten minutes and makes you do the in-class activity that is ridiculously hard and is nothing like what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Exams don't relate at all to the assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: horrible professor, lectures doesn't help with understanding materials, had to do self studying, also horrible cutoff and no curve.

So interesting to listen to, lectures are extremely eye opening and really get you thinking, make sure to do the readings before the TA discussion sections because that's where participation comes from, course is slightly unorganized because the lectures sometimes don't relate to the readings at all

saying he "victim blamed" is totally out of context, he genuinely cares for his students and was inspired to share safety tips after the events on 6th street, not saying that they would've prevented the attack

good professor, way too much reading for a ugs but interesting stuff (you have to go to discussion sections but lectures are irrelevant)

Fine subject matter, but gave an 80 minute lecture victim blaming the innocent students killed after the shooting at Buford's on 6th. Made me and many others uncomfortable as he told us we shouldn't even be out at the bars past 2am, as if its students fault for having fun. Also made fun and mocked his experience coming across drunk students out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He clearly cares about his students. He is very grounded and shares his knowledge by connecting course material to realworld events in a thoughtful and respectful way. He did cancel class fairly often, which I did not mind since I would just check Canvas beforehand. I benefited a lot from this class, and it pushed me to make more connections.Easy A

This professor refused to let students use laptops during class and then somehow expected us to know if he randomly cancelled class at 2 AM. When he was obviously going through the lectures too quickly, he mocked students who used their phones to take pics of important information. 0 self-awareness about his own teaching style. Would not recommend.

Amazing lecturer although lectures aren't required (there are “surprise quizzes” somedays but you honestly know in advance if there's a quiz next lecture). TAs were super nice and helpful. Did have readings, but they were honestly interesting and not super hard to get through. Easy to get a good grade in the class!

Dr. Foster is hands down one of the best lecturers at this uni. He is so knowledgeable and truly cares that his students learn. The conversations in this class were eye opening and helped all of us grow ideas off each other. Loved this class so much! Would 100% recommend to anyone interested or hasn't had the pleasure of meeting dr foster

this was such an easy UGS. I never went to the lectures, but you do need to go to the group discussions sessions because that work is what's graded. The TAs were easy graders and teach the material, and the papers were typically group papers. They gave a study guide for the final and it was the same questions that were the prompts on the test.

Dr. Foster's lectures are so very interesting and as an engineering student they really prompted me to think much differently than I am used to. The class is graded almost entirely based on the semester-long research paper from the discussion section, and it isn't a lot of work. It was just super cool to listen to this guy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
THIS godforsaken class was miserable. The grading criteria are unclear and often change from class to class depending on if Dr. Foster feels so inclined to explain the work in class. The lectures have nothing to do with the coursework and the is only BRIEFLY discussed during sessions with the TA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster was absolutely my favorite professor! His lectures were informative and enticing, he is very interactive, and he gets you interested in the topic out of sheer passion. The course is not work heavy. There is a semester long research paper that is not that bad, as the TA's walk you through it and you have the whole semester to work on it.

Dr. Foster was passionate about what he was teaching us, but he also understood that we have a lot of work in other classes so he didn't burden us with a lot of assignments or exams. We had 2 writing quizzes but as long as you tried you got a 100. There's a research paper but the TA's walk you through everything and are extremely supportive.

I had Dr. Foster for US Public Education UGS303, and he was fantastic. Very passionate about his subject which makes him very enjoyable to listen to. Lectures are interesting and work is easy. A few research papers which took a bit of time but weren't difficult and were graded easy. TA's were amazing, really care about their students.

Good lecturer and guest speakers. This class was easy and a great introduction to writing a paper. The term paper(most of grade) is done in parts and is very easy if you do stuff early. Grading was very light. Only bad part was lack of communication/mismatch on dates. It's very go-with-the-flow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is a great choice of professor if you are taking a UGS as an incoming freshman. His class is straightforward, with the clear goal at the beginning of the class to be working towards a final paper. Though his class does teach the ins and outs of long thesis writing, the lectures are truly insightful, fun, and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Take his UGS. He is such an engaging professor, and the workload is super light. The only big assignment was a 5-7 page research paper, but you build on it the whole semester. I really enjoyed his class, and the TAs were very helpful. Interesting class and great professor :)

Dr. Foster is an extremely passionate and thought-provoking lecturer! His class is super interesting and the workload isn't too bad for a flag. The class consists of a quiz, group assignment, and the research paper that you write throughout the semester with the help of the TAs. Highly recommend for a UGS that's different from your other classes!

Loveable and very knowledgeable guy. I loved the class, and the workload wasn't too bad, especially for a flag. I thought it was very fun, and some of our discussions were genuinely entertaining! A great break from my other classes, would recommend

- The entire semester is just working on one research paper
- His lectures are amazing, he's very thought-provoking + will ask the class/students for insight on the topic we're going over
- Take his class!! It will open your eyes to so many things
- Started taking random attendance when people didn't show up later in the semester 
- Super hilarious

Dr. Foster is an awesome person. I loved going to class to hear him talk about random stuff. The class is very easy. He is a bit disorganized and will often cancel class/delay assignments. We ended up only having one quiz, one group assignment, and the term paper. I wouldn't say I retained a lot but the class was very fun, interesting, and easy.

Dr. Foster is passionate about the subject and lectures were interesting. We were supposed to have 3 pop quizzes but only had 1 and he warned us before so we knew to read. The paper will take a bit of time, but was graded easily. The readings were pretty long though and I stopped doing them. Highly recommend for a fun/pretty easy UGS credit.

Dr. Foster's lectures were incredible, I learned a lot from him and the readings he assigned. He wasn't very organized and didn't do a great job communicating with the TA, but got everything resolved by the end of the semester. He's very easy to communicate with and willing to grant extensions as needed. Definitely ask him for help if you need it!

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Foster is an excellent professor. I am just not too strong in liberal arts courses, so I did not enjoy the class as much. I still ended up with an A because Dr. Foster provides clear instructions, and it is super easy to communicate with him through office hours.

Class is in discussion format. The course is meaningful for anyone, regardless of major. Professor Foster is laid back and an easy grader. The TA grades harder but your overall grade will be good. The course's only drawback was Foster's disorganization. Take this UGS!!

Homework was always reading, some was very interesting. This class makes you think and Foster is a very intelligent and charismatic guy. The only issue with him is he is quite disorganized. The TA grades hard, Foster grades easy. This class is super fulfilling
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took the Education and Black America course and I have to say it was amazing. The discussions we had in this course brought to my attention many things that are important in this political climate. Easily one of the most interesting classes I ever have taken. The only bad thing I have to say is that Dr. Foster is kinda unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My TA really made this class for me. It is easy to tell Dr. Foster is a really good professor but the lectures were not outstanding (probably because it was a freshman class). However, he is funny and I learned a lot through the readings in this class. There is a ten page final paper. Everything in my experience was graded very generously.

Took him for Public Policy Education in US. Class was pretty interesting, but very disorganized. Lean on your TAs as they always have the best up to date information. You don't have to read the readings if you don't want to. Just one major essay made up the grade, but you work on it throughout the semester with checkpoints, so not too bad.

Took class for my UGS and it was way too much work. I had the most work in that class and when I asked friends who took another UGS class they said it was an abnormal amount for a class that isnt going toward my major or core. Hes very friendly and good lectures, but it came to a point when I wasnt learning anything and was way too stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't learn anything from his class. Felt like the course wasn't actually about U.S. education. Only coursework was 8page research paper, but the TAs were very helpful. Stressed out for the class for no reason, but foster was very unpredictable and unorganized. second "quiz" ended up not even happening and he gave us all 100s

anyone that says Dr. Foster is not an amazing professor is frankly, looney. He provides the best for all. If you want a truly groundbreaking class on education in the United States, or you need a relatively easy UGS, you get both. He genuinely cares about the class and his students, this is THE UGS.

The class content didn't really interest me, but it turned out alright. There are a lot of readings; do them, and you'll be fine. Quizzes are actually essay tests, but the professor/TAs help you prepare. There is a 6-8pg position paper but you write it in chunks. Professor is super nice. Only problem was that this class was very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher, had no real quizzes or readings. Our only "quiz" was showing to class on a random day. Major grade is a research paper that is graded in chunks. Very engaging conversation and dialogue! Only downside to the class is you never really know what you're going to do that class day. Moves a lot of deadlines and readings around.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is a great lecturer; however, his class is rather unorganized. If you are willing to read and self study, you will receive at least a B. Overall, this course was very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is an engaging lecturer and a very cool person. However, his UGS class is extremely disorganized and disappointing.  It seemed like Dr. Foster didn't really put any real effort into teaching this freshman class. Instead of teaching us the course material, Dr. Foster spent his time in class facilitating political discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While this UGS was all over the place in terms of its topics, and I felt the "quizzes" were more like tests that were a bit harder for the time constraint, I felt like the class was fair and the TA and Prof both took the class lightly enough for us not to feel stressed, but serious enough to have engaging discussions. Good Overall, reading is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's full of really cool ideas and loves to share them, but that comes at the cost of the class having a focused direction. I honestly can't tell you what we have learned in the class because he goes on so many tangents for entire class periods. There's a lot of reading involved and the "quizzes" are really just tests in disguise (essay heavy).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very unorganized  class, it's up to you to self study. Goes off topic too much. Other than that its doable if you self study. Also he makes it seem his opinion is the only and correct opinion. But cool class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took him for 2 classes and received A's in both. All of his tests are free response and as long as you can justify your answer with support you're almost guaranteed an A or B. He also gives quizzes that he gives the answers to just to boost your grade and reward you for actually coming to class.
Easy pass if you're  willing to think outside the box a little.
The content/material of this class was amazing. Dr. Foster  is a very amazing and inspiring professor however, this was the most disorganized class I ever took.

Took this class because I saw that Dr. Foster had a 75% A rate. So glad I took this class, way more than an easy A. Dr. Foster is one of the best professors I've ever had. I was never bored in class. Readings are shorts and actual books, no textbooks needed. Tests are easy, just do the (short) readings and go to class as much as you can.

Promise and Peril is not difficult. Three pop quizzes throughout the semster and one six page paper. The class is not hard if you go to lectures and read the books and articles. If you don't read, you won't do well. Dr. Foster is very nice and passionate about the subject of education so his lectures are very interesting.

Attendance wasn't necessarily mandatory, but he had pop quizzes that helped him with attendance. Two papers, one was 3 pages, the other was 6+. Your grade really depends on your TA, but mine was pretty great. He has interesting stories and can get off topic when students ask questions. I didn't use the "required" textbook once.
Very Unorganized. Powerpoints were not done well.  However, if you do the work, you can get an easy A.  My TA was great! We had good discussions too.

His class wasn't difficult at all. There were unannounced quizzes, so you had to attend class. His grades were based off raw points. The quizzes were focused on the main idea. Just look over his previous powerpoints. There were readings, but not necessary besides like one. There were 2 papers and a test. Lectures were interesting!

Foster is a cool guy with interesting stories. Not an easy UGS class. Lots of info and pre-class readings. All quizzes are pop quizzes. 2 papers (my TA gave terrible feedback for the 1st -- didn't know how to succeed on the 2nd). Test & quizzes are 95% short answer

Dr. Foster's Public Edu class is interesting, but if you are looking for an easy UGS then this isnt your best bet. I enjoyed listening to his lectures & learned a lot, but the midterm & work load is a bit more than I expected from a UGS. Lots of reading & writing. The TA's are not all on the same page, so each discussion learns something different.

This class was my easy A!  The class didn't follow what the title led it to be but Dr. Foster is a good lecturer.  He does use big words but his grades consisted of 3-4 papers and only one test, the midterm.

Took US Public Education for my UGS course with Dr. Foster, thinking it'd be an interesting class about different systems of public education in the United States. Boy, was I wrong. Readings have little or nothing to do with public education- just about how it sucks to be a minority/poor.  3-4 papers, and tests are all short answers.

Professor Pederson is a great storyteller, and her lectures are super engaging. She also has a very dry humor that is super funny. The only grades in the class are attendance and three exams. Sometimes the questions can be tricky, but it's open note, and if you don't overthink it it's totally doable.

Fran is the goat and she is my queen. Love her so much her lectures are fascinating and she draws you in with excellent storytelling that compel me to attend the 8am. She has a real passion for the material and has major ball knowledge, I wish she could teach every class I have.

Prof. Pedersen is the most passionate lecturer I have ever had. She cares about the topic and about the students. Your grade is based on 3 exams. I did poorly on the first, and aced the other two and made a B-. If you aren't good at taking tests, take someone else. She adds some curve to each test grade.

LOVEEEE the professor and wish i could blame my grade on her however i just flopped. sucks how your overall grade is only determined by the 3 exams. however, study well for those and you'll be alright, i literally just had to much faith in myself that it was "common sense". prof keeps lecture entertaining, textbook not needed, lots of irl sidenotes
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Pedersen is incredibly engaging. One of the best teachers hands down . However, her course is graded by only a few things (3 exams), so you must perform well on all 3. Midterm 1 is the hardest , midterm 2 and final are not that bad.  Side notes are really important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mrs. Pedersen is without a doubt an exceptional professor and I really enjoyed her class. Her lectures are engaging and tests are open note. However, the only grade in the class is 3 tests, 2 are 15 questions and the final is 20. I loved her but if you're grade conscious I would look elsewhere (Quintanilla I heard is also great).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 10/10, she is honestly amazing. So kind, smart, and funny. I understand being only graded by 3 tests is scary, but the lack of homework allows you to both enjoy and learn the material in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at UT. Cares about the students and is an amazing lecturer. The grade is based only on 3 tests, but as long as you attend class and pay attention, she will prepare you well.

I LOVE FRAN. She has such clear learning objectives, that every student HAS to succeed. Her tests are hard, but so fair. If the majority of the class misses a question, she removes it. She held office hours on weekends, yapped with us after class, and wrote half of our class letters of rec. Take her class- you won't regret it. Effort=A

Loved Pedersen's course! Amazing lecturer! She is so enthusiastic about Law and Ethics and makes an early class so lively. You're only graded on tests, but if you attend every class you should be fine bc they're open note. Attend office hours! Her office hours were so underutilized but she clarifies so many things there it's definitely worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pedersen is the best professor in McCombs hands down. You must come to every single class, and if you listen, you will do well on the exams. She says to buy the textbook but I did not and ended with an A+. Enjoy this class, she is awesome!!!

Prof. Pedersen is HILARIOUS, and incredibly engaging. You will not miss your phone at all (tech. is banned in her classroom). However, as shown by my grade, her course is graded by only a few things (3 exams), so you must perform well on all 3 (I didn't). Exams are open-note excluding tech., and the textbook is helpful as supplemental material.

*LEB 320F* I will start by saying that I had registered for Prof. Quintanilla and about 1 month before school started UT switched professors on me. I am SO GLAD that this switch happened because Prof. Pedersen was one of the best professors I have had at UT. She is so inspirational, an amazing lecturer, and tells funny anecdotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: *FOR LEB320F* Dr. Pedersen is a real-deal litigator and the best lecturer I've had in college. I learned SO much about the law, and her storytelling goes great with the content. I will say that she is strict, and the average is based on 3 exams; no make-up exams are allowed. Take this class if you are interested in law, not for an easy A. Love her.
Don't take her class

I adore Dr. Pedersen, she is the best LEB professor!! I had her 8 am spring 24 and enjoyed every lecture. She is hilarious and makes complex law concepts easily digestible. The class is heavily weighted on 3 exams (so that's a bit rough), no homework, and attendance is not required. Pedersen has made me so interested in law and the best professor.

Such a great lecturer!

Also, people will tell you that LEB323 is reading-heavy. This class is not! Pedersen's class outline and the notes she has you write are very detailed and all you really need for this class. Textbook is available but not required.

Class is graded on just 3 exams. Make sure to study the outline and how it applies to cases!

She's a very knowledgeable professor and delivers material really well and clearly but class can be boring because its just lecture the entire time. The tests are tricky and each word in the question can change the response and the entire class is based on 3 tests. No homework or work in between classes though which can be nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was prob my favorite course I've taken at UT. Pedersen's lectures were so interesting and it was worth attending every single one (also kinda vital to doing well on the tests). Tests require a lot of critical thinking, which I actually thought was fun, and they're open note. She also cares SO MUCH about every student and is a fair prof

Professor Pedersen knows her stuff, but the exams are very difficult. If you miss class you are screwed, because her tests correlate to her lectures. Your whole grade depends on 3 exams (55 questions total) and if you are not a great test taker who knows how to apply your notes to hypotheticals, then you will have a difficult time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved listening to Pedersen's lectures. She's really funny, and explains law concepts in a way that is very easy to understand. You get the most out of the class from listening to her give examples in class, so attendance is very important. Your entire grade is also dependent on 3 exams, which can be a bit tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: while pedersen is a nice prof who knows her stuff, i absolutely hate the way the class is structured. no technology allowed, have to take notes on paper only, entire class grade comes from 45 questions, shes very not understanding of students missing class

Only complaint with the class is your entire course grade is from a total of 55 exam questions. As you can tell, getting even a few questions wrong in this course will severely harm your grade. However, Pedersen is a great lecturer, and is extremely good at teaching material and explaining concepts. The class is tough, but Pedersen is a great prof

She is sweet. She gives good notes too. Tests are tricky, but you will be okay if you read carefully. The class is only based on tests, so you really have to do good on them. Pay attention in lecture and review notes carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Pedersen in Fall 2021. I loved this class. Professor Pedersen is an amazing lecturer, her class is interesting, she is very good at effectively explaining concepts and she is very kind. The only grades in the class are 3 exam, so it is important not to skip class. I highly recommend Professor Pedersen!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Pederson during Fall 2020, so the classes were online due to COVID. She was not very accommodating given a literal pandemic and would frequently interrupt class to chastise students she thought were distracted (talking to someone, etc.) Content is fine, but did not find her to be a welcoming professor.

Pedersen is a brilliant prof, definitely an expert in her field. Her lectures were phenomenal and she literally hands you the information on the test. Book is unnecessary. She will call you out in front of the class, so look professional. She handles all her OH as she has no TA, really says something about her expertise. Read tests carefully!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Like others have said, listen to the lectures and you'll do fine, don't buy the book. I got to have her for Fall 2020 and she was a Karen about the smallest details. Would stop the presentations and call students out for not having the camera on, looking distracted, or even smiling, really happened, Get a real prof who isn't triggered all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is brutally boring, however she does try and liven it up a little bit. The class is based entirely on tests. She's a very good teacher and explains the material very thoroughly. You have to read the questions very carefully, I did not which is why my grade suffered in this class. Overall she is a great professor though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pedersen is super knowledgable about this material. The class is ridiculously boring but as long as you go to lecture, you'll do fine on her tests. The textbook is unnecessary (don't waste your money on it). You have to go to class; attendance is 10% of your grade. She's a little bit dramatic and kind of over the top but overall a good prof.
Probably the most boring class I've taken at UT. Her class isn't that difficult though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Pedersen is a great professor. She is very interesting and full of passion in class. However, the material is tough and she gives side notes that help you in the open-note tests. You will learn a lot by taking this class, but just be prepared to study hard to earn the grade.

I took this class at 8 AM, but Pedersen really made the experience enjoyable. She is very knowledgeable on the subject and tries her best to explain things clearly. Tests are open note, but they are not a piece of cake. Nonetheless, if you go to class, take good notes, and study a small amount before the test, you should be fine! Awesome class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pedersen is a great prof- really easy to listen to listen to and her course outline is super informative. However, she is NOT easy. Do not trust the 70% A's grade scale on MyEdu. The class average is an 85, about 25-30% get A's. This class has definitely changed and gotten more difficult over the years. Expect very tricky tests.

Professor Pedersen is absolutely amazing. She explains things very well in class and she wants you to ask her questions. Her exams are open book, but that doesn't mean you can study at the last minute. She gives "side notes" during the lectures that don't appear in the book, so don't miss class. She also gives out points based on attendance.

This teacher is extremely easy, but super helpful!  All her tests are open book and open note, but I was surprised I learned so much from her class.  This is definitely one of the best business law professors at UT.

Not really a good nor bad professor; her lectures weren't great, but all of the slides are provided and they're really all you need to study for the tests. The exams are pretty easy, and the group projects and excel assignments aren't very time consuming. It's not very difficult to get an A in this class as long as you do the work.

She just doesn't make it enjoyable to learn and her lectures aren't the easiest to follow. She's very snarky and will absolutely snap at you for not knowing the answer to a question. Be ready to hear her brag about being an Apple engineer once or twice a class. Take her if you have to. You're going to be fine but you won't enjoy it.

I don't get the hate for this professor, I found her to be absolutely fine. She was a good lecturer, well organized, and gave clear expectations. Outside of class, you mostly interact with her TAs. Easy assignments and a few group projects. Open note, open book, open internet tests. Reading is required though!
Lectures are fire on mute

Super easy class but man is she a passive aggressive person. For someone who teaches about computers, she really doesn't know how to use one. When instapoll didn't work/glitched, she would passively aggressively and very rudely blame it on the student/student's internet. She also assigns a lot of group work which sucks to do as it's an online class

Her updated syllabus says tests are online but on first day she says they are in person- if you cant get the syllabus correct you are simply being disingenuous to all students who based their enrollment decision on the content of the syllabus.

Ghini ensures students understand the material. She ensures to read questions and comments. The class felt like common sense at first, but then the first exam came up. She makes her exams to test critical thinking using class concepts. She provided extra credit opportunities. 2 Group projects, and weekly excel homeworks very doable.

Attendance is mandatory through instapolls, but you get about 5 days you can miss so not too bad at all. The exams were long and tricky, if you don't really learn the excel they will be difficult, there are also quizzes every two weeks, online, but not enough time. The lectures tried to be engaging but felt short sometimes.

55% of the grade is based on tests. Attendance is mandatory (she does 4-5 instapolls each class). The tests are online and the excel homework can be time consuming but not too difficult. She is a kind and caring professor, she just takes a LONG time to grade stuff. Group projects are also graded difficult and not "give me" grades.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love love love. She is the most caring professor I have ever had. Easy A. Tests and quizzes are open note, open AI, open everything. 8 homeworks and they are easy, 1 drop. 3 projects, also easy. You have to be actively trying to fail to get anything below an A-. I would take all her classes if I could. You can tell she loves teaching and the topic.

Dr. Liz's RMP is misleading. She really cares about the content, and the textbook, assignments, and lectures are coherent and well-integrated. At times, she can come off as condescending, but she truly just wants people to participate and understand the content, and she means well.

I have no idea how her RMP is so low. This class rocks for what it is. Prof. Ghini is so sweet and really wants every student to succeed. Tests are open note, open internet. 

Not sure why she is getting so much hate, I maybe spend >5 hours a week on this class and have a 100%.

I was worried about her RMP rating, but the class was super easy. You have to have a good understanding of the material for the test and study the week before, but the tests are open AI and book. Try to raise your hand in class or she will get a little frustrated. Learning Excel is so useful! I would 100% take again. I learned lots about technology
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very kind, and makes sure to answer all questions. The group projects in an online course are annoying but straightforward. Excel homework allows multiple attempts with specific feedback, quizzes are timed 15 min, tests are long but there's only 2. Mostly open resource, no lockdown browser. Instapolls in every class.
She never releases the grade

I recommend going to every class. I found the exams to be pretty tough, but if you read the book, you should be fine. Overall, it's a great class with a dedicated teacher. (Also, don't be afraid to ask for help; other comments here say she's mean, but I found her to be easy to talk to.)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Miss. Moliski was a caring and compassionate teacher overall in my experience. On the excel homework we had, we only get 5 tries but when I showed up to office hours, she gave me 5 more tries just so I could get the perfect score! She always had office hours available and the assignments we had were easy and doable. Overall, excellent teacher!
got a 53 on exam and ended with a B so huge curve. lectures are useless. probably the most bs mccombs class ive taken and one of the worst profs. but at least it was online so...

Dr. Moliski creates her tests to trick students. She says she doesn't but all the answer choices will have the "good" answer and then the "better" answer. Her lectures were extremely boring, and the textbook was extremely long and tedious. She will test you on random things you read. She does not prepare you well for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was not bad and is doable. There are only 2 exams so they are weighted quite a bit and the true/false ones are tricky. Hardest part about group projects was getting group members to respond to you. She is also very rude for no reason and will yell at you. She has an attitude when you ask questions in office hours or through email.

This class isn't too difficult if you study and compile your notes (ctrl+f is your friend). I didn't love the professor because she would occasionally make rude comments about students, not necessarily to their faces but still frustrating. We had a handful of group projects but they weren't too bad and were graded pretty fairly.

lowkey skimmed the textbook but took good notes and passed. she's a little snappy if no one answers. take notes bc u can use them on exams. 2 group projects and 7 quizzes that are 5 questions each done in class. she lectures well but the class is kinda boring. excel part was useful though and the excel HW is also easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was a great professor for this class. Instapoll is only 3% of your grade, and there was extra credit for the class. The exams are easy if you go over the material and practice Excel, and she drops 2 quizzes and one Excel homework. This class was super chill, and she was a great lecturer. I definitely recommend taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, the class is not that hard, if you keep up with reading and do excel homework you will do fine. Dr. Liz is not the friendliest, she will call you out for not engaging in class, be condescending in emails, and brag about herself only. The hardest part of this class was showing up, lectures are boring and she doesn't make them any better.

Lectures are pretty good. Got to learn a couple of cool things that are applicable in terms of business and excel. She flexes a lot about working at Apple and investment banking. Tests are decent - some confusing wording but overall not bad. Excel projects are very useful. Definitely not as bad as people make her out to be. I would recommend.

Class of doom and despair. She will mention at least once per lecture that she's worked at Apple. She will yell at you if you ask questions, and yell at you if you don't. Group projects are so bad. Overall not that hard. Hardest part is sitting through the lecture, and acting like you want to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: she expects you to already know what she's talking about. if you don't already know about tech, good luck. very fast paced and passive aggressive with questions. 2 tests worth 55% of your grade is insane. also expects you to just know excel and follow her within 1 second
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I know Liz has terrible ratings on here but I really don't see why. This class was super straightforward especially after watching lectures and reading/skimming the book. If you put in the effort you will do fine.
She's awesome. Very very smart woman and she is super flexible and understanding with her students.

Honestly super easy class. There are 5 instapolls every class, but she posts the slides before class so you have the questions. Excel projects are super easy and she encourages AI usage to learn how to use excel. Two group projects which were annoying but easy. Exams aren't difficult if you pay attention in class.

Not sure why her reviews are negative, she is a great professor who knows what she is talking about. There are no midterms or finals, just 3 tests that are not cumulative. 2 group projects that are very easy, easy excel work with many attempts, lowest quiz grade is dropped. To make it all better: extra credit at the end. Highly recommend!

This is the easiest of the business minor classes. You'll get out what you put into it. Try and you'll get an A, don't and you won't get an A. Tests are open note and quizzes/projects are easy if you try. While the content itself is boring, the lecture slides do a good job of outlining what's important for the test. The Excel stuff is useful too.

She was kinda impatient with people. After seeing her answer questions from my classmates during times when we were working on a project, I never dared to raise my hand. She is a decent lecturer but this class made me not want to pursue MIS anymore.

This professor does not adequately teach the material. The material that she does teach in class is never actually included in her AI-generated tests. If you have to take MIS301, and she's the only option, take it next year instead.

Based on past reviews this class has clearly got better. Not too difficult but SO boring and SO disorganised. Canvas page is a mess and you're basically working around her to post assignments last minute so you can never plan your schedule ahead. Online lectures take so long as she's always checking the chat!

I think Dr. Liz is misunderstood. She cares deeply for her classes and is always willing to make changes for her students. She doesn't repeat herself sometimes bc she really won't tolerate questions she already answered, but lowkey fair. They truly hate to see a computer-savvy woman in STEM.
The class is manageable if you stay on top of the readings and assignments. Lectures can be dry, but unstuck ai was a lifesaver for exam prep. Overall, a decent course.

The exam and quiz questions are NEVER straightforward, and the content is hard to understand, especially as a class taken by many non-business majors. The professor said she was satisfied with the midterm average being a B, which is nuts. This has been the most challenging class I've taken so far, take something else.

Not the worst professor to exist, but definitely doesn't make the content more digestible or enjoyable to learn. Pretty straight forward class in terms of layout but in general the questions aren't clear. If there's a problem with the instapoll during class it's overlooked and considered a drop but they should be used for absences/fault of our own.

Very confusing class. She says one thing in class and the syllabus says another thing. She does not acknowledge when she's wrong in class and will blame students. There are definitely other business classes you can take instead of this one. Excel HW's are easy. Quizzes and reviews get more difficult as the class goes on.
Quizzes and tests are designed to trick you. Even if you fully understand the content, you will likely get a 70 or 80 on an exam just because of how she words them.
No comment …

If you can find another course — take. It. The class of great content and overall very easy but the professors presence is extremely stressful. She is a master at excel and will not hesitate to make you feel stupid.
If you're taking this you better be brilliant and not sensitive. She makes me cry just about every interaction

All I have to say is don't take this course if you can find another. She is extremely rude to students when they have a problem especially technical stuff. It seems she is too busy to be a kind person. She makes it very clear that she's the smartest in the room. Not a good way to encourage learning in my opinion!

Super rude both in person and in emails. If you come to her with an issue, she will just make you repeat everything you've already tried and then act like you're brainless one. Any solution she does give will be one that completely misunderstands the problem. Textbook readings are too long and mostly useless. At least the class was really easy.

I contribute most of my learning to the lecture slides and textbook. The lectures were straightforward, and she cared for the students' learning. I did really well in all of the assignments, projects, etc. However the grade is test heavy, and the tests have uncovered questions. In the one time I've talked to her, she was passive agressive and rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: As long as you stay on track with the readings, quizzes and Excel assignments, you'll get a decent grade.  Lectures are about interesting topics, but prof teaches them in a boring way.  Textbook readings are long, relatively unnecessary.  Exams were mostly fair and not proctored, so no issues on that end.  Go to office hours for Excel help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: honestly i feel like this class is what you put into it, i am in the 9 week course so its more fast paced but still able to pass. although everything is open note, i still struggled lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Okay... Alright......

She was a very good professor who actually listened to student feedback and made changes to her course accordingly. There's a lot of content, but tests are all open note and internet so it's honestly not difficult. Weekly quizzes but they're only 6% of your whole grade. Harder of the business minor classes for sure, but not bad at all.

Moliski is boring during lectures and somewhat unorganized. She seems busy af and comes off as passive aggressive/not super friendly at times. Read the textbook and you'll get a A on the exams. Class is honestly really easy, so professor didn't matter too much. Slightly pay attention for instapolls during lecture (she drops 20 tho)

Moliski is sometimes very nice and understanding but also very passive aggressive. Regardless, the lectures are not very important and everything tested on is within the textbooks. There are many assignments, however they are all very easy.

I found the class hard largely because the content is hard to understand and goes super in depth with technology.  She will not teach Excel, so pay attention to the trainings. The few times I interacted with her she was not very kind, although I think she is good at lectures and the InstaPolls make you focus in class. Make sure to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's great! Genuinely cares about her students and is very accommodating toward people's circumstances. The workload is a little heavy, but it's mostly busy work and not hard at all. Tons of drops too! Overall, this is a very easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class is structured extremely well, she cares about what she's talking about and is interested to hear from different perspectives. The assignments are very easy and won't take long at all. Consists of reading reviews, excel trainings and projects, instapolls, and 3 group projects. There are 2 exams but as long as you go to the lectures, EASY A

Very kind and caring professor, being an online class with so many students she really did try to reach everyone and not make it overwhelming. Also sends reminders for due dates since sometimes all the assignments can be confusing. Overall, she has more patience than any professor I've had and tried to give as much credit as possible.

I do not see why people say this class is hard, as long as you know how to use computers its a fairly easy A. The professor has been kind in most interactions in class however, she tends to go off topic often and somethings talks about things that do not pertain towards the lesson. Overall she's decent and the class was pretty easy.
Completely incompetent in everything she does

Worst lecturer ever, but even worse person.  I am a disability student and she straight up didn't give me any accommodations and after, shamed me for not being able to keep up with the class due to my disability. rude, unhelpful and exercises her privilege to shame others. save yourself some emotional distress. don't take her class.

Do not take Liz Moliski. She yelled at me during office hours over Zoom. Personally, I understand that screen sharing takes a bit of patience due to the delay; however, her reaction towards me was extremely unnecessary. The material wasn't too bad, but it was extremely textbook heavy, and the tests were difficult. Choose another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is absolutely the best professor I've had at UT. She is incredibly caring and its clear that she wants the best for her students and prioritizes being accommodating and responsive with the chat. Her lectures are well structured and move at a great pace with weekly quizzes at the beginning of the week and instapolls throughout every lecture.

Shout to the ta nick, he fr the only reason a lot of us passed. the prof is hard to get in contact with and doesnt help with answering questions. She is a little stuck up and not the most organized. tests were insanely hard, but ta holds test reviews; go to those. be prepared to do a bunch of work for atmost a B+/A-, she aims to give few A's.

This class is online but does require attendance along with in person exams. 2 exams are worth 25% each and requires self studying to be successful. Overall, the class wasn't too bad and the work besides test prep was pretty light. People don't like the class because of the test weight but also dont study for them on their own. Review the textbook!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't like her as a person, she seemed kind of entitled, however the class itself was informational and I didn't find it too hard to make an A. Just need to make sure you don't get behind on anything

She is a snarky professor who, at times, does genuinely care about your learning but is also not hesitant to question your intelligence. Very easy to get a B in the class with the curve, but if you are seeking an A, expect to work for it. I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you don't need it, lots of time and stress for an intro-level course

Be prepared for a rigorous academic journey. This class is challenging, with an abundance of work and numerous projects to navigate. While it demands a lot of time and dedication, it's a testament to the depth and breadth of the subject matter. Despite the workload, Moliski is a good professor.

This class was difficult but the content was very interesting and usable (especially the Excel portion). If you want to do well in the class you need to put in a lot of work. Reading is heavy. There are reading quizzes and content quizzes every week along with homework assignments. Be ready to put in the time and effort for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was hard for no reason. She made the tests super hard so no one could get an A. Her lectures were way too fast and she always contradicted herself. The TA was the only good thing of the class as he explained things a lot better than the professor. Problem was he was not the most available. Take this at CC or w a different professor.

I went into this class so excited to learn more about Excel because I had used it all of high school. I was so disappointed by the professor and her ways of teaching. Oh, wait... she basically does not teach you anything. She is unclear about what she is doing when she is saying things. She is also so insanely inconsiderate. DON'T RECOMMEND!!!!

I felt so cheated on the exams, especially with the Excel questions. They are unlike what is asked of us on the HW and assignments. I think Liz is nice, but I dislike how she touts that this is not meant to be a hard class, while also saying she doesn't give out many As. There's an annoying amount of HW and reading/review quizzes due every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ive never met a professor who is hell bent on giving as few amount of A's as she is. This class is disorganized and honestly makes no sense. You learn excel and random mis topics. The tests and quizzes are SUPER difficult, and her lectures are way too fast. Go to the ta for help, he is the polar opposite of the prof and only reason im passing tbh.

Alright all. I want you to imagine getting tortured in fire. This is what this class is. Not only does Liz proudly announce that not a lot of students get A's, but she makes the exams extremely random, the quizzes and homework so frustrating and lengthy, and its almost like smashing your pinky toe into a wall 400 times. Take the class, you'll see
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, the content is not difficult, the professor is. The lectures are pretty awful, the exams are completely random and up in the air. The homework is frustrating, you'll see if you take the class :). At first, this class will seem organized, but it is so thrown together. This class feels like if Michael Scott ran a class, hilarious, but bad.

She is extremely inconsiderate and really just a terrible professor. She acts like she teaches everything but really just teaches the easiest parts of each excel unit/tech chapter. I couldnt tell you a single thing she taught me but the excel textbook was good. Dont take this professor.
