If you keep up with the readings, you'll do fine on the assignments and two exams.
Professor Farmer was a great and engaging lecturer and I felt that she really cared about what she taught. The class was fair but just make sure to do the readings as they're covered on tests.

Dr. Farmer is, hands down, the most dedicated and inspirational professor I've ever had. The class can be challenging (need to pay attention to long lectures, read the textbook & books, and there are a few assignments), but her passion for the content and for teaching was AMAZING. I'd take any class she teaches 10 times out of 10.

Dr. Farmer is a joy to have as a professor. Her lectures were interesting and engaging, and she often offered "labs" (activities in class) that were very helpful! If you respect her she will respect you, and she truly cares about her students. She's very passionate, honest, and fair, and you will do well in this class if you put in the effort.

Dr. Farmer is, by far, the best professor I've ever had at UT. She's incredibly passionate about the course content, & her lectures are so engaging and detailed. There are readings, but they're reasonably short, & the textbook chapters are reviewed in lectures. She's your fav professor's fav professor, & as long as you go to class, you're golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Farmer! She is so knowledgeable about everything she discusses in class and goes into a ton of detail so you could get away with not reading. 2 tests and some easy participation grades, she does take attendance through instapoll and will affect your grade if you don't show up, but honestly she's so engaging its worth going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer, and it wasn't too difficult. We had quizzes every week, but if you read the textbook it's easy. She's a pretty generous grader and gives a lot of critique/feedback for future reference. You can tell she genuinely wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Farmer is the best professor I've had at UT. She is very passionate about her lectures making them extremely engaging. Your grade in her UGS is dependent on the TA and how difficult of a grader they are. I learned so much in this class because of her teaching and I looked forward to attending lectures every T/TH.
The teacher is so engaging and amazing at lecturing. She only has two exams and some cute random assignments in class for random attendance grades. She is amazing, don't be scared.

Joy on earth. I would recommend professor Farmer to anyone interested in learning about Black History. Although there is a lot of reading, it is useful for class content. Her lectures were very engaging and thoughtfully communicated. I wish I could take another one of her classes!!

1000/10 would recommend! Dr. Farmer is absolutely amazing and this class absolutely changed my understanding of history. She is funny and her lectures are extremely engaging! She is really passionate and cares a lot about the content of the course. LOVE LOVE LOVE this class, one of my favorites at the university. Take this class if you can!

Dr. Farmer was amazing! She's very engaging and makes the lectures super interesting. Only two major grades, a midterm and a final. Exams are over textbook readings and lecture. They're not terribly hard but you do need to review everything ahead of time. She also starts the class by catching us up on pop culture :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grading criteria is very vague. Mixes around with attendance and participation grades (which was a whopping 25%). Hardly know where the grades come from as there was no clearly stated method to assess these and clearly that high of a percentage can make or break a grade. Content-wise a great class to take but ask yourself if it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was such an informational class and I highly recommend this class to anyone wanting to finish off their history requirement. Dr. Farmer is phenomenal and is very passionate about black women's history which makes her lectures engaging. Get ready to read for every class, but the workload is not excessive. Assessments are not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Farmer is amazing. She is really nice and funny, and always open to talk at her office hours. Attendance is not mandatory, but its a good idea to show up to class because there are a few assignments for participation grades. Also her lectures are just awesome, so you should go anyway. There are a few readings, about two a week, but its not bad.

I took AFR315I (African American Women's History), but idk how to add the class.
Dr. Farmer's class is extremely eye-opening and will change how you perceive America. The class is also relatively easy, with assigned readings, 2 quizzes, 2 exams, and a simple final project. She wants students to succeed. Also very entertaining! Wonderful experience

Wow wow wow. What a class. I took this just for the US History credit, but it ended up changing the way I think about US History. I highly recommend her class for anyone who needs a history credit or just wants a different perception of American history.

Loved Dr. Farmer! She makes class and lectures fun, and you can tell she cares about the topic and her students. Lectures are usually class or small group discussions. Class was weekly media analysis, one doc and one visual analysis, and then an end of semester research paper. She allows you to correct the doc & visual analysis for a higher grade.
Best teacher ever! I loved this class and would chose to take it again every time!
She was very engaging and made sure you know the content. She sets you up for success in outside class assignments and exams. Overall, she was a caring, understanding, and personable professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Finley is the best professor out there! Her classes are so engaging and she cares if her students do well. there's extra credit for first test, DO IT! She really is there for you with every question you have. She's newer so that's why there are not many reviews but she's amazing and you should take her without doubt.

Prof Finley really cares about her students and values learning over grades. The course material is difficult, but she does a good job on explaining and is always willing to meet outside of class time. TAKE HER! She is the best.
Hard class, but Professor Finley did a good job of explaining the course material, and all reading are given to you without having to buy a textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Finley is probably one of the best professors I've taken at UT. She is super approachable, caring and wants to help her students learn. She is also really smart. GO TO OFFICE HOURS trust me it'll help. Make sure to come to class bc that is important. Her lectures can be long but as long as you come to class and take notes, you'll be good.

Professor Finley is very caring and genuinely wants her students to learn as much as they can. She definitely appreciates participation in class and during office hours so try to do that as much as you can and you should be fine. For tests, use the unit notes to study and make sure you understand the mechanics of all of the concepts.

Professor Finley was great! This was her first semester teaching and her sections did better than others. She really cares that students understand what's going on and takes a lot of time out of her day to help you. I would def take her again and there was a curve.

Reviewing for BCMS. First semester is a lot of work, but he is flexible with due dates so it's manageable. Heavy emphasis on conversation, and by end of first year you will be speaking Croatian. He's responsive and available outside class time for support if you are proactive in communicating.

I cannot speak to the experience of Frane's Russian class (it didn't give me another option on here but I'm taking is BCMS classes). The first year was also a huge volume of work, but by the end of the year we basically spoke BCMS- he was incredibly flexible with deadlines and understanding of how much work he assigned was actually possible.

(Spring 2025, Online course) He is great as a person, but the workload is heavy. Daily modules and it's recommended by him you study 4-6 hours per module...Theres 2 speaking tests and 9 “major” tests that are formatted like the modules/assignments. I'm not going to lie it's a big decision to take this class. Unless you're passionate, be prepared.

Loved Frane as a person, but not a professor. Not only does he expect an insane amount of work out of you considering it is a 4 credit hour course, but ontop of that TA grades extremely harshly and acts as if we already speak the language when this is a first year introductory language course.

I was doing 5 to 6 hours a week for his course. Most of the time, things were poorly explained and I felt poorly supported. I have hope that the rest of the Russian department at UT is better, but for now, I do not recommend online Russian 1 with this professor unless you want to be up late every night teaching yourself Russian.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. he barely speaks english and you wont be able to understand a thing he says. he doesnt know how to lecture and doesnt know how to answer questions. the lecture slides are going to confuse you more than help you and even if you try to learn the content through youtube/khan academy, it wont be the same on tests at all.
Dont take this class.

This class sucks don't take it the midterm averages are in the 40s. Frank cant lecture or answer questions at all. If you took AP stats you will have a slight leg up at the start but still I would take another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE Frank aka Yuanke Yan his lectures are all over the place he cant speak English well enough to get past the first row. The course is graded relative to the class around you top 30% get an A is the only good thing about the class even though the test Avg is 40. Dont Take him if you want to leave the class with any knowledge in eco stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam grading is ranking based. It doesnt matter if the mean is super low in exams, the top 50% of the class gets an A- regardless of what grade you got, as long as its above 40%. Beyond that, he is good at lecturing, although his accent is not great. He also takes what other people want into heavy consideration.

PLEASE AVOID IF YOU CAN. RUN.  Frank Yan is first off EXTREMELY hard to understand (not sure if he has linguistic issues). He always tells us in lecture that what we are learning is intuitive, when the MEAN for exam 2 was a 40. I am having mental health issues due to this class because it is honestly so stressful.

kahoots for attendance, 3 midterms and an optional final. wayne is a fun guy, the TA review sessions led by nathan help A LOT. the others meh. just do the practice questions before tests and you'll be fine. OA are chill u should go. exams are a little hard but some questions are pulled from IQ and kahoots. show up and listen you'll do well.

I loved Wayne's class--he was a super funny teacher and actually made me look forward it despite it being at 8am. It's really easy to get an A if you just go to class, and you get easily get extra credit points from the kahoots. Would highly highly recommend the dude is a great guy

I absolutely loved Prof Geerling! He made economics so interesting to the point that I contemplated taking macro with him even though I already had credit for it. He's so helpful, and if you pay attention, attend class, and do the multiple practice problems he provides you, it's easy to succeed! People call him the goat for a reason

Professor Geerling was easily my favorite professor I have ever had at UT. His Evolution of Economic Thought Class was extremely engaging and very applicable to the real world. TAs can be very tough graders, but he will help you out in any way possible. Wayne was engaging and made every lecture interesting. I cannot recommend him enough.
Tests were tough but he provides you with all the materials to succeed if you want to. Interesting lectures and a very nice guy. Would take again.

Class was okay. Attendance is very important since you have in-class kahoots and google forms that play a big role into your grade. Exams can be difficult if you don't study, and it is only FRQ, so you do have to be knowledgeable of the subject. Reviews are exactly like the exams (same questions), its just a lot of content to remember.

Literally the GOAT. Amazing reviews for a reason. The lectures are incredibly easy to understand, and he is very easy to reach through emails. The TAs are amazing as well. He tries his hardest to make his lectures fun and enjoyable for everyone. Lots of pop culture references tied into econ. Highly recommend.

Prof. Wayne is genuinely the GOAT. His classes are fun, and the material is fascinating for anyone studying economics. The open-ended exams are challenging at first, but he provides an overwhelming amount of preparation material. I highly recommend attending office hours—he also gives excellent career advice.

This class was incredible. The lectures are engaging and prepare you well for the exams. There is also a large safety net to ensure you get a good grade. Your lowest exam grade can be replaced by the final, three assignment grades can be dropped, and extra credit is available for attendance past the required amount.

lectures are very interactive and make the 8 am worth it. syllabus is clear and reiterated throughout the semester. exams aren't the easiest, but study guides are very clear on how/what to study. rewatch lecture as he pulls questions from it! light homework/reading per week. participation points given every lecture

i have never taken econ before this class nor did i ever get above a 90 on an exam and i got an A-. lots of cushion if you do poorly on exams. exams are slightly difficult but if you study well enough u will be fine. i really love geerling, he really cares about his students and i highly reccomend taking him over grooms or other intro teachers.

Wayne is a great professor and very respected at UT. He gives detailed study guides with exact questions and answers that will appear on the exams. The grading is somewhat strict as you need to cover the specific key points to get full credit (fully free-response exams). However, if you study enough you can easily ace the exams.

He has a great attitude and enjoys to be interactive with students. Attendance is pretty much mandatory up until earning all Kahoot points, which is relatively easy. There is a book for this course; however, all you need are the lecture slides and some YouTube videos, though the book can help out.  Its a great class and he's an awesome lad!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Lectures were engaging and fun because he would take student volunteers for live demonstrations that fit the lesson, even giving rewards to participants. Regardless of it being an 8 am, he's good at keeping attention because he integrates Kahoots/media references relating to economics. I'm taking him again next semester for macro.

Professor Geerling is my favorite professor so far. He is very caring, has interesting and engaging lectures, and often tells you what is going to be on the exam. He offers extra credit through daily Kahoots, so be sure to attend. The exams are somewhat easy; I would just recommend rewatching his lectures that he posts to Canvas and taking notes.

GREAT PROFESSOR. Class was always interactive. Studying was easy due to how much help was provided. Grading criteria is clear and it is very easy to get an A in the course if you put in the effort. Take him!

wayne is genuinely the only teacher that has ever made economics make sense to me. he is funny and engaging and trust me even thought its an 8am its worth it if you want the A. take econ with him he's actually the best

My favorite lecturer at UT.
Cares deeply about his students' success, has clear-cut grading, which allows for a generous amount of in-class points and extra credits. Exams are clear, no trick questions. His study guides give you the tools to succeed.

Geerling is genuinely my favorite professor I've had so far. He cares for his students a lot, and don't listen to the other reviews - his tests are not that hard if you just study for them and show up. The guy literally gives away like a third of the questions during the lectures. Anyways, I can't wait to have him again for macro.

If you are an Econ major, this is the best professor you will ever have. He is really cool; class is not hard as long as you study. I got 82 and 60 on my first two exams and still managed to get an A. The lectures are great and give you almost all you need for the exams and there are kahoots in every class that can get you extra credit.

This man was my GOAT. I wouldn't recommend that you take 304L with anyone but him. The exams were so easy, the IQs are super easy, there's plenty of room for extra credit if you do the class Kahoots, and the class is final optional. Dr. Wayne is also very engaging and easy to listen to; the Australian accent makes things stick better! GOATED.

Dr. Geerling is a truly great professor. He is hilarious, intelligent, and down-to-earth. ECO 330T can be difficult due to the nature of the exams being completely writing based, however he provides an abundance of material that makes the exams manageable if you utilize them.

Great professor. He's eccentric for sure. He provides all the resources necessary to make an A in this class, it's just up to you if you want to put the effort to prepare and study for the midterms. Really interesting class :)!

Honestly, he's one of the best teachers I have ever had at UT Austin; he's such a nice guy and makes himself available to all his students. Exams are really easy if you read your textbook. If you do find yourself struggling, his office hours are great.
The professor is great. His exam reviews are really helpful!
10/10 professor. i couldn't recommend him more. i can really appreciate a professor that is consistent and actively works in his students favor. best econ prof ever!

His lectures are pretty entertaining, follow them because there is always kahoot(s) that follow. lots of room to get full credit on attendance and extra credit that can boost up to 2% more on your final grade. MANY study guides on each unit given DO THEM because they help a lot. Textbook given was one I actually enjoyed reading

Not a hard class at all, only thing I would say is make sure you make friends who can send you the kahoot code for in class points some days he would do none and others do 3 in one class. But very nice professor, gives out lots of prizes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best Econ professor at UT…actually explains concepts and genuinely cares for students and their learning. Please take him he is an amazing professor

Geerling was passionate about Macro and teaching it. As someone who is an Econ major, I cannot complain about his commitment to student success, even if he was strict come exam time, though in fairness, they were not particularly hard. In-class Kahoots were an easy way to get extra credit and bump my grade up. Props for making the final optional.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly such a respectable professor, the only difficult thing was trying to ge around his accent (but easy nonetheless). Read textbook, look at Kahoot, and do your assignments and it's so easy. He may add some niche questions from lectures that aren't listed anywhere. In the end, do the practice questions for each unit and it's a breeze.

Geerling is a very interesting professor, creating interesting lectures with real world and pop culture examples. Going to class is important specifically because Kahoot points are part of your grade. Three exams with an optional final that can replace your lowest grade and he has helpful practices. I struggled with micro and this class was easier.

Ngl I have never gotten anything lower than a A- in any class here at UT but this one. Tests are kinda confusing but it could be worse. Just work hard in the class and you'll end up with a grade you can't complain about. He is kinda rude tho lol

If you attend class (daily Kahoot for points) and engage with the textbook and practice material, this class is very easy. Wayne wants his students to succeed and has long office hours to support that. His lectures are knowledgable and they're recorded so you can access them after. There's three exams and the extra credit is easy if you're in class

we know this diva! his class structure is like grooms', and its #lit - optional final if u take all 3 exams, inquizitives every week, kahoots in class for participation and extra credit. hes a sweetie pie and i love his accent lol take him if u can!

Wayne is rude to students and has zero empathy when it comes to students being confused or asking questions. He is not flexible and he often makes snappy comments to students. When briefly rushing through an explanation he claims concepts are easy. The class grading system isn't extremely difficult but I was not a fan of him or the class.
The class is really easy, extra credit is easy to attain, and the exams are far easier than the other econ professors. Lectures are engaging and useful/helpful.
Wayne is hilarious and very engaging; he keeps class fun!!

Geerling is such a great professor!! All he wants is for his students to succeed. His lectures are really engaging, for an 8am class it was really fun. Daily kahoots(count for attendance). If you go to class and pay attention I am sure you would do great on the tests.

I wasn't a huge fan of this class. Lectures kind of felt all over the place and hard to follow, even though the subject matter wasn't extremely complicated. I think his teaching style made the class seem harder than it was - at least, to me. A lot of people seem to like him, though.

such an awesome professor to have. attendance isn't mandatory and lectures are recorded. he has daily kahoots that contribute to your grade (uses a point system). as long as you inquire about the topics you are unsure of, he will is more than happy to answer and explain further.

Professor Geerling is a good professor & teaches the material well enough but gets impatient with students & their questions so dont expect him to elaborate more than he has to. The class itself is not hard as long as you put in time to learn & understand the topics. Exams are the hardest part so dont let homework & attendance keep you from an A+

Not a good choice for STEM majors looking for a social science class, leave this for the Business people because this class is way too hard for an intro class. The entire class is weighted on 3 exams, but he makes up for it by being an amazing and really funny lecturer that there are graded Kahoots in every class. His office hours are great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is heavily dependent on the three exams and they're not easy. Final exam (optional) replaces your lowest score though! Also, the class isn't really notebook and pen friendly, lol. However this was probably something out of his control. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed his lectures, even at 8am. Extremely caring guy, too.

Professor Geerling is an incredibly engaging lecturer, and his class is highly relevant to today's world. He offers 2% extra credit for Kahoots and TPS, which can boost your grade a few points. Tests are challenging, but he drops lots of hints about what will be on them during lectures. Overall, a really good experience.

This is my second class with professor Geerling and he is amazing and really makes every class engaging and entertaining. My only complaint with this class was that he made the class too difficult this year. He said that last year too many kids got A's so he made the grading harsher. I thought that was unnecessary but I would still recommend him.

Great professor with engaging lectures and genuine care for students. That does not mean this class is an easy A. Most of your grade is made up of tests, and you likely will not succeed if you skip lectures and don't engage with the material. But, the lectures are very fun and professor ge does a great job at making it interactive

Felt cared for even in a lecture of 500 people. Took this at 8 AM and still enjoyed the class. Has an extra credit system that basically automatically gives you 2 additional points on your final grade. The homework is easy and helpful, but tests pretty much make up your entire grade. Would definitely take his class again!!

Professor Geerling is an outstanding lecturer and the best economics professor I've had at UT. His ECO330T class has been the most impactful course of my college career. If you are truly passionate about economics, I highly recommend taking it. While the class is challenging, it is engaging and deeply relevant to understanding today's world.

He is great. Anyone who says he is not did not care enough to learn or take advantage of the opportunities he gave. It is a 3 exam class with a final that is optional to replace lowest. Tests are super hard and harshly graded even if you know all the material. Office hours were the most important but he wont teach this class no more so dont worry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Geerling made the lectures very entertaining and fun for an 8AM class, and definitely made the class very enjoyable. Exams are not too difficult if you do homework and practice problems.

If you don't mind the 8 am wakeup, Professor Geerling is the way to go. His lectures are engaging and interactive. He provides sample exams and review topics for every single chapter exams cover which is the perfect way to ensure a good test grade plus we do daily kahoots in class that can give you up to 2% of a grade boost. Super fair class!

Great professor! Go to every lecture to get the Kahoot extra credit. His review sheets help. He prepares you for the tests but they are kinda hard. Micro is not a blowoff class, but it also won't be the hardest class. Do your work and ask him questions and you'll get an A or A-
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to read the textbook for his class. He makes the lectures very entertaining and knows what he is talking about. His tests are kind of difficult, but if you study the Kahoots, lecture notes, and read the textbooks you will get an A. His office hours really help. He wants his students to do good in the class. Take him for micro.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor for microeconomics!! His lectures are super engaging and are the only things you need to do well on the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory but participation is part of your grade and he has in-class extra credit opportunities. Show up, pay attention, and do the practice questions and there's no way you don't get an A! (Optional Final)

Besides the lectures being at 8am, they were actually engaging and fun. That being said, do NOT take this class lightly if you're taking it for a minor like I did. Class averages were C's for each exam. Geerling is funny and gives up to 2% extra credit through Kahoots which was nice but make sure you really pay attention during lectures to do well.

Wayne is a solid professor and is pretty good at lecturing, but his tests were made to be too hard and the grading criteria is somewhat confusing. I don't think worry too much about his reviews for 330T though since he says he's not going to teach this class in the future (maybe the reviews and semester surveys were really bad?).
He is a fair grader and a good professor. The class can be difficult, but it's doable so you have to work hard. He cares a lot about his students and wants to help them succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
First off, many of these reviews look like they were written by the same person and are not reflective of most students.

Secondly, Yes this class was hard. Hard but worth it. Dr. Geerling gives his all. He devotes so much of his time to helping students, but you have to put your part in as well. LOVED the class no matter what grade I get.
Professor Geerling was an excellent and engaging lecturer, and was very engaging, though the 8:00 am is a tough time slot. Overall, I learned a lot in his class, and found it really enjoyable.

His Micro class with Mateer was alright, but 330T was complete hell on earth. Exams are graded on complete minutiae for vague questions. Imagine studying 20+ hours and doing all course materials and not getting even a decent grade

His tests are insanely difficult as they are graded very harshly. They are all 4 written essays and he offers no leniency. I have read the book, attended all lectures, do active recall and still do bad. He previously curved but said he won't to make his grade distribution more accurate. Avoid this class.

Prof Geerling is a nice guy and a good lecturer, however, this class is awful. A large portion of your grade is based on the midterms, which are literally 4 essays you write over 4 different economists in 90 minutes. Even with studying all of the content I struggled on them. 41% of people failed the first exam and only 13.5% got an A/A-. Stay away.

Professor Geerling cares a lot about his students. His office hours consist of 6 hours weekly and he's very helpful and open to all types of questions, no matter the difficulty. His lectures are fun and use pop culture examples and little stage activities to drill in the point. 3 exams + optional final, kahoots, and easy weekly MCQ homework.

Sometimes he can go a little fast in the lectures, but he is very understanding and responsive via email outside of class. Best method for studying for exams is to read the chapters, do the IQs, and then take the practice exams he gives you. Overall, very enjoyable class and he gives you many opportunities to achieve an A+ in his course!
0/10 Hated this course. Professors were overly conservative.
Harsh dude with difficult tests
good lecturer but tests are way too hard
makes an easy class too hard also his tests are way too confusing and grades pretty harshly

Good prof, hilarious and informative at the same time. Lectures are fun with interesting activities from time to time, content seems rushed sometimes. Attendance is graded through kahoot quizzes every class, so don't skip. Test difficulty depends on your level of preparation.

Absolutely horrible test grading policies that are set up to allow you to fail even if you know the content. He is a good lecturer and overall the class is fine, but it's nearly impossible to get As on exams because of the scale. Does not take feedback well and is going to screw over my GPA.
makes what's supposed to be an okay class way too hard
AVOID. I HATE HIM

He gets stuff wrong on his kahoots and refused to change it when told and acts annoyed when you get proof. He's very stubborn and close-minded. Even when the majority of the class misses a question (for kahoot or TPS), he refuses to change when it's mainly because he words the questions really bad so it sounds like it's asking the opposite.

Horrible professor with confusing test grading. He wants the class to be harder since apparently he made the course too easy his first year. He makes you to write the tests his way and won't take anything else and he grades really harshly. He said he wants the grade distribution to be like an upper division econ class when it's just an elective.
Awful vibes all around.

This dude blows. I actually think he teaches well but that's not the problem. His tests are very heavy and hard for no reason. He had more people fail the first Exam than get A on it. That really all I need to say. Don't think the teaching is a problem it's his exam grading honestly would just avoid this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are way too hard for no reason. Even with correct material rarely you'll get full credit. Averages are low Cs the professor claims it's good he purposely wants grades low. TAs said class is not cured as of now. Overall don't take, really hard to improve your grade even if you know the material setup against the students no leniency on exams.

This class is terrible ignore the good reviews from macro. The test in this class are just outrageous. You can know everything study hours in advance still fail the exams. He grades off how you write it and gives no leniency on anything. He claims a low C is a good average class is not curved. Overall class is just bad the way he grades exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wayne is awesome, but this class is not an easy A. I have found lectures pretty interesting, for the most part, but the short-answer exams are kind of tough. No homework. In class Kahoots and think-pair-share. Overall, I have enjoyed the course, but found it harder than expected.

This class is not as enjoyable at micro or macro, but that has to do with the content not professor. Basically a history class for economics, so if you aren't good at history it might be harder than you think. Literally no homework, tests are kind of hard though. Overall interesting, but definitely not a free A.

Wayne is a very nice professor and the class is entertaining- I would not suggest taking him unless you are prepared to go fast. He would often interrupt lectures with activities that were super fun, but then rush and not fully explain the material which caused me to have to figure it out for myself after class.

Overall a good class but he comes off a bit harsh sometimes towards his students. I attend class not because I love his lectures, but more so because I fear missing the constant quizzes and assignments both due during class and at 8pm afterwards. He gives good lectures on interesting content, but I can't say I love his approach.
He is literally one of the greatest professors I have had. He is incredibly entertaining and very knowledgeable. Definitely take Wayne Geerling if you have the opportunity.

He could have made this course so much more difficult than it needs to be, but he clearly cares about teaching and does not seem interested in failing people for no reason. If you study and actually listen to the lectures, then this class will be a breeze. It's not a terribly exciting course, but he makes it as good as it can get.

prof geerling is one of the best profs at UT, he genuinely cares about his students and their understanding of the content, and is always available after class. participation is a big portion of the grade, and is done through kahoots and super easy to get extra credit from, 3 exams and an optional final, no papers! loved his course

Geerling held amazing lectures and was very engaged, a big plus because he is Australian. Most of your grade will be determined by the tests. There is a textbook that is recommended to help study and complete some assignments.

He is an amazing professor. Would 100% recommend. The best part about this class is that the final is optional. If you score well on the three exams this class has, you can easily get an A without taking the final. Also, Geerling is very funny and the lectures are enjoyable (even at 8 am).

Wayne is one of the most caring and funny profs I've had. I read the textbook and took notes for every chapter which helped a ton with exams -- lectures are straight from the book. Exams were straightforward if you read. Take him if you can!

Geerling is a great guy, but only an okay professor. He gets upset sometimes if too many questions are asked about things that he thinks are easy. He's very interesting though. His tests are lowkey way harder than they should be, I got C+'s on test 1 and 2, but he makes exam 3 pretty easy and I got 92. Homework is super easy, good luck on tests tho

If you have the chance to take Wayne for this course, do it. Similar to macro at UT your grade is composed of Kahoots (attendance), weekly inquisitives, 3 exams, and an optional final. I didn't attend for the last month and still got all participation points bc threshold is so low. Wayne is very funny, easy to reach, and cares about his students.

Macro with Wayne was great. His lectures are engaging and the grading criteria are extremely simple. There are 3 exams, with the second being the most difficult. Minimal work outside of lectures and as long as you show up and stay engaged/put in effort, the material is pretty easy. There are extra credit opportunities. I loved this class!

The variety of teaching methods, the humour, videos, presentations, kahoots in class, and grading style is all EXTREMELY effective and made this class genuinely fun to learn the material. Not only did I enjoy it, but I felt that I learned a lot from this course. It is clear this professor puts in a lot of effort into the class :) t

I'm sad I won't be able to take this class again he's a really good professor. HWs aren't bad at all and in-class Kahoot's are a big part of your grade so make sure to do them. Test are definitely manageable if you study well. You still get 3 skips per exam. Final is optional or can replace worst midterm grade.
Exactly like micro, he is a good teacher and class is engaging. Tests are hard if you haven't been paying attention in class, but easy if you have. Overall great class, not too homework heavy.
He's a yapper bro
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Him and Dirk are an insanely funny duo, and the class was extremely easy. As long as you did the readings with inquisitive, you were set for an A. They made my morning amazing like every Tuesday and Thursday because of how hilarious they are.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams aren't very difficult; I study each one in the morning and still manage to get an A- in the afternoon. If you're a hardworking student, I bet you'll earn an A in the class. Additionally, the final exam replaces the lowest of the previous exams. Prof Geerling is the most hilarious prof in UT ngl.

Wayne Geerling is an amazing Micro professor. IQ assignments are super easy and helpful for studying for exams. The in class participation grade is based on Kahoots and Google Forms on the information in the lectures, so attendance is mandatory until you have all of those points. Interesting lectures made for the fact that the class was online.

Took online ECO304K with Dirk and Wayne. Lectures super interesting and kept me engaged. Workload was light; weekly IQ assignment that took about 20-30 minutes a week. Very straightforward and fair exams; if you do the kahoots, TPS, and IQ assignments you're good. Offers extra credit for having over the maximum participation.

Super fun, easy to understand lectures with demonstrations and questionably-related clips. Attendance points can be easily met by going to 75% of lectures. Pay attention to questions solved in class, kahoot questions, and inquisitive questions for the 3 tests. Inquisitives are weekly assignments and you can keep going until you get a 100 on each

Wayne & Dirk's online web-based microeconomics was an amazing class, especially for non-math majors. They're hilarious in class and offer so many opportunities for in-class and extra credit points. Exams can be hard  if you don't study, but you would have to go out of your way in order to fail the class.
Him and Dirk Mateer co-taught this class and they were great together. It was probably the most fun I've had in an online class.

Attendance is mandatory because it counts as your grade. Homeworks are Inquizitives, Kahoots are during the lectures, and tests are based on Inquizitives, Kahoots, and lectures. Reading the textbook is helpful before lectures, and extra credit is offered based on participation. LECTURES are AMAZING! So creative and engaging, you will love it!
Great professor for the online Introduction to Microeconomics 304K! He is very engaging and hilarious during the lectures, making it an entertaining class!

Wayne is a super nice and caring professor. He actively encourages and invites students to come to his office hours. Sometimes he doesn't explain things thoroughly enough and students without previous knowledge are left confused (especially true when talking about US gov/econ, bc he is Australian). Imo, the latest textbook is a waste of money.

Grading system was clear and straightforward. Large lecture class but Professor wants to get to know you and encourages you coming to his office hours. Professor was really caring and tried to make lectures interesting. If you didn't struggle with Micro then this class should be about the same difficulty.

The professor was quite good with his lectures and explanation of new concepts. Sometimes the lectures can be boring, but it was mostly because of the material and not the professor. Tests were very doable with 3 skips and extra credit is also given for participation in Kahoot. He was also caring and accessible after class.

Cool funny and enthusiastic dude. Lectures can feel fast paced but there's just a lot of info to get through, I took textbook notes before each class so class Kahoots were easy and I didn't have to stress about keeping up in lectures. Structure is exact same as eco304k w Mateer (IQs, textbook, Kahoots, demos w prizes, skips) just with frqs on tests

Geerling is awesome! Very accessible with office hours. Not the kind of guy you won't be able to find outside of class. Very straightforward about the class, exams, and expectations. Lectures were interesting even at 8am. Overall 10/10 professor!

Really fun professor, good teaching style. The exams aren't easy so study hard. Attendance isn't technically mandatory but in-class kahoots make up a decent chunk of your grade so go to class. An A is very achievable, especially as you have the chance to get 2% extra credit with the kahoots. Great professor overall, would recommend his class.

Wayne is a great lecturer and provides a ton of study resources. If you study, the tests are easy. The final is optional if you take all 3 exams. Go to every class: there are attendance questions that can also serve as extra credit. The only work outside of the class is homework every week. You'll definitely need to read the textbook to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Read the textbook, go to class, and rewatch lectures before the exams to do well on the exams. There are many opportunities for extra credit so go to class and farm kahoot points. People who complained about his accent and teaching style are just haters.

Geerling is a really mediocre teacher. His lectures are really bare bones and don't prepare you for the exams nearly enough (which is a problem when exams are 70% of your grade) and he doesn't really make an effort to help you learn. The only way you'll be successful in this class is by studying straight from the textbook. Wouldn't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While some may say Wayne spoke too fast in lecture, I believe he was an effective lecturer and provided lecture slides with blanks to fill in so you did not have to copy everything down. Also, the textbook for the class is amazing. Reading the textbook is key to doing well in the class. Majority of grade is based upon three tests w optional final.

He goes fast in his lectures (Australian doesn't help), and you have to go back and re-watch them later before the exams (or read through slides before getting to class). There's three midterms and an optional final, but tests are difficult. Reading the textbook and using the study materials he gives are helpful, but the frq can be graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Geerling is amazing. His course is hard but that's just bc its macro. he has office hours twice a week that are so helpful and it helped me end with an A. his tests are hard but going to lectures, doing the kahoots, and reading the textbook is super helpful. he goes a bit fast in class but lectures are recorded.

He goes by SO fast in class is barely impossible to pay attention and write at the same time, (good thing he records his lectures) so be ready to re-watch his lectures recordings after class. That said his lectures were interesting but def you needed to put in extra work for his tests which were hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Majority of the grade is from the 3 exams, but if you look over the given study guide and textbook/notes, you should do fine. Weekly chapter quizzes that are easy if you actually read the chapter. Daily in class Kahoot games totaling 19% of your grade, so make sure to attend class in order to get full credit. Really great class, would recommend.
He was a good lecturer and the class is not too difficult if you study and pay attention, but he is very Australian.
Great professor. Interactive lectures with 3 important tests. Final is optional if you do well on the first three midterms.

Great professor! Really engaging. Read the textbook and make good notes before you attend lectures. Attend Office Hours, they are really fun, and he is willing to answer questions about how the topics he teaches can be applied to the real world. Complete the test reviews and study the Kahoots from previous lectures and you'll likely to receive an A

Pretty good professor for an intro class. Exams aren't hard necessarily, only annoying thing is how picky he is on free response questions. Not much leeway, but the majority of the exam, the multiple choice is pretty easy anyways.

One of my favorite professors ever. His lectures are so interesting and he does kahoots with prizes everyday for attendance. He's so organized and gives you ample study material for the exams. His lectures are basically verbatim from the textbook so that is also good study material. He's so kind, helpful, and down to earth.

Prof. Geerling is a great lecturer. He is very knowledgeable on the topic and clearly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Going to class is not necessary, but Kahoots are a main part of your grade. The only thing I did not like, is he works very hard to e ahead which sometimes feels like lectures are rushed.

Wayne is such a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about many topics. He's a really cool guy and accessible after lecture. However, exams are quite difficult, but there's a chance to take an optional final to replace a low exam and there's extra credit to increase your grade.
I enjoyed Prof. Geerling's class. He is hilarious and makes lectures engaging. The course overall isn't challenging if you read the textbook and pay attention in class.

Great professor and personality, Prof. Geerling really cares about his students. Attendance is not required but necessary to succeed in this course. Get ready to read the textbook as well. As long as you show up to class, read the textbook, and study for exams, this class is built for you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to go to class to complete Kahoot! points which can get annoying. Exams are difficult if you don't pay attention in class. Great guy.
Wayne is a great guy. Great personality. Really need to go to class or you will struggle on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is the literally the sweetest soul ever!!! No quiz no exams and the work load is little to none tbh.

a very interesting course at face value but lectures were long and attendance is mandatory unfortunately. class is graded off of mostly writing assignments so beware of that. TA did all of my grading. super sweet though and would recommend for an easy A (if you're a decent writer lol)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulbas is so unbelievably kind, and her class is a guaranteed A as long as you put in the work! She has no tests or quizzes, and her grade is entirely based on the reading responses/final paper, attendance, and resilience training, which are all basically participation grades. She also offers a lot of EC and makes the lectures so interesting!

Professor Gulbas was one of the best professors I have had! She is very understanding and inclusive. Attendance is mandatory BUT she also gives you a few days of unexcused absences. There are two required readings but they are both interesting. The memoir we read was very impactful to me. I loved lectures and I loved my discussion section!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really amazing professor. Cared a lot about her students and showed interest in the subject. Subject topic was presented with care with sensitive topics. Lot's of extra credit. Easy grader. The discussion sections were wonderful with great TA's. Good for psych students or anyone interested in psychology.

If you have to take it as a UGS its okay but lectures are hard to pay attention to and overall information is not that interesting. Discussions with TA's was better and the group projects are fun. Overall, its easy to get an A but not that interesting to take as a subject matter.

She's very friendly, but we only learned about Women and Madness during the beginning but then stopped learning about it by the end. Classes were unorganized, and it turned into her resiliency in the classroom program, which is not what I signed up for. There's a lot of reading and writing with NO writing flag. A lot of work, but it is doable.

Dr.Gulbas was an incredibly kind professor; you could tell she cared deeply about what she taught, but this class had a lot of work for a UGS and some disorganization. Attendance is mandatory, but class time doesn't feel very efficient or necessary, so get ready to spend hours reading and watching her lectures outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: way too much work for a UGS class and class is very unorganized and stressful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was definitely fun, but this class wasn't the most freshman friendly. There was a lot of homework to do that she only changed the number requirement halfway through the semester after a bunch of complaints. There is a group project that isn't too bad but is graded based off your TAs. Only take if you REALLY need a UGS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Like other reviews said, this class has heavy coursework for a UGS. However, Dr. G is very flexible to what works for the class and will accomodate to what the class finds more doable. There are two books: 1 for the weekly assignments and 1 for the final paper. Most of the class is graded by the TAs.

best professor to have for your first semester of college. she makes everyone feel welcomed and she actually understands the stressful workload students have. by the middle of the semester, she gave us several assignment freebies. the TAs were amazing as well and gave great feedback. im not a writing person, but this class was writing heavy!!

Dr. Gulbas is nice, but this course has a heavy workload. There are 2 weekly participation responses tied to our readings, a group project, a 1-page reflection, and an 8-page final paper. Attendance is required with only 3 allowed absences. Grades depend on TA (except the final paper) but they're really lenient, plus there is extra credit.

She was a nice and caring professor. Kind of a joke of a class though. There was too much busy work for a UGS and an unnecessary 8 page paper at the end of the semester. But it will be graded with leniency. Would recommend taking this class for an easy A!

Dr. Gulbas is really great and the class is interesting, although, for a UGS, her class was A LOT. There's 2 books to read, a group project, an 8pg essay (with multiple mandatory drafts), weekly lecture videos on top of class lecture, weekly discussion responses (with required book citations), and mandatory discussion section (on Friday).

Taking one of Professor Gulbas' courses is one of the best decisions you can make. She truly cares for her student's mental health. Course consists of 3 lecture videos a week and 15 responses (full semester) , reading 2 books outside of class and an 8 page simple essay that she walks you through during the semester.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVE DR. GULBAS! Her lectures are super interesting and engaging! You will definitely learn so many cool things about women and mental health. While the Dr. Gulbas is awesome, the workload for the class can get overwhelming. However, it is all manageable if you keep track of everything. Dr. Gulbas is super reasonable and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Gulbas this past semester! She provided a clear and thorough syllabus with instructions for all major assignments. She was also extremely understanding and accommodating. She puts student well-being first, which is why I enjoyed learning in her class so much. However, the readings tend to be lengthy, so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Gulbas was the best professor ever! She is an understanding, knowledgeable, and enthusiastic professor. Keeping up with the readings is pretty necessary for the class, but they were so interesting and enlightening. I would recommend this UGS to anyone even if you don't think you're interested in psychology/psychiatry.

Professor Gulbus was amazing! Very accommodating to students. I took Women & Madness. You need the textbooks for discussions and Willow Weep for Me to write the paper. An overall easy class if you do the work. Attendance is a big part of the class, so if you know you can't attend the class, let her know in advance if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulbas is amazing. She genuinely cares for her students and implements practices throughout the semester to support their mental health. Not only do you gain knowledge about the history of mental health, but you also learn how to care for yourself and others. Wonderful course.
Dr. Gulbas is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. She is very understanding and genuinely wants her students to succeed. I loved her UGS Women and Madness.

Such a sweet professor who is clearly passionate about what she teaches. She really cares about her students and their mental health, and this can be seen when she sets aside time for us to do mental wellness practices. Big assignments are a video presentation and a final paper (which is broken into many parts over the semester so it's manageable).

By far my favorite professor at UT. This is such an amazing course to take your first year. I wish more professors were as caring as Dr. G. She puts an emphasis on the mental health of her students which a lot of professors could care less about. One of our assignments was a self-care log which was life-changing for a first-year college student !!

Dr. G is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so caring, accommodating, and understanding towards her students. She genuinely cares about her student's mental health. The required books were sometimes difficult to read, so ask questions. The big analysis paper was broken up into parts, so it was never overwhelming. HIGHLY recommend.

Dr. G is the most caring and passionate educator I have ever gotten to be taught by. Not only in her class did I learn about psychological history through women but also how to better care for my mental health. She always included us in deciding about assignment deadlines and how to better help our workload. I would have her as my professor forever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Literally the sweetest, kindest, caring professor I have EVER had. I would take any class she offered. She cares so much about her students and their mental health, and often canceled/postponed upcoming assignments or classes if we were stressed! Love her so so much she deserves everything good in the world. <3

Taking Women and Madness with Dr. Gulbas for my UGS was one of the best decisions I could've made. Dr. Gulbas cares deeply about her students and will accommodate to the class's needs. There are easy participation responses due before class each week, a group project, 2 test (midterm and final) and a memoir essay - sounds like a lot but doable!

One of the most caring and engaging professors at UT. She reduced the workload partway through the year to help reduce stress. I strongly recommend taking her UGS, especially if you're interested in psychology.

I wish she was my mommy. I love her. I would take every single class she teaches for the rest of her teaching career if I could. I think Dr. Gulbas should be president of the United States. Sometimes when I think about her I start shaking and crying because I love her so much.

Dr. Gulbas is truly the most caring and loving person I've ever encountered. The coursework isnt always a breeze but she will be there for you every step of the way. It is so apparent Dr. Gulbas is very passionate about her work and really wants the best for each and every one of her students. Also, the course content is so so interesting!!

Dr. Gulbas is an ANGEL. Not only does she care about her students, but the course material is very straightforward & interesting as well! She literally got my whole class "sleep kits" to help us with our sleep health, and accommodated the deadlines to what we as students needed. Very amazing, kind, funny person. You will not regret taking her class

Dr. is truly wonderful. She cares for her students more than anyone I know and is passionate about what she teaches. The class has a heavy emphasis on self-care and she does her best to make sure that this class is never causing you stress. This is a wonderful UGS course! Plus, my discussion group TA, Micaela Williams, was also so kind and helpful!

Dr. G is one of the best professors at UT! definitely take her class if you have the chance. She creates an extremely welcoming environment where it is very easy to participate and give your opinion. She is the nicest and most compassionate professor ever and she really cares about the success and well-being of all of her students.

Wow, I would take Dr. G a million times over if possible. She is the most compassionate, caring professor I have ever had the pleasure to learn from. The class definitely requires work but I learned so much. Definitely take her class if you get the chance!

Dr. Gulbas is my favorite UT professor so far!! She is seriously the sweetest person ever and I would take any class that she offered. She is so understanding and would ask everyone how they were doing before class. She even cancelled our final because people said they were stressed. The class has a decent amount of reading, but it's an easy A.
Dr. Gulbas is the sweetest professor that I have ever had at UT. She is so caring and kind and does everything she can to make sure you understand and enjoy the material.

I took this class online and I LOVED Dr. Gulbas so much. Shes so understanding.  talk to her if you have any issues. She is so amazing! Def a lot of reading, but I really never did it and have a 99 in the class. Pay attention to the lecture videos if you dont get the reading. A good amount of writing but she is so understanding so dont worry
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulbas is an amazing professor. There are 2 textbooks that you need. Weekly reading homework questions that are easy. One Midterm and one final, you get to take both home, and the final is optional. One group project that is pretty easy. Do Also do the extra credit, which there is a lot of it!

Dr. Gulbas is a wonderful lecturer and you can really tell she loves the subject. She is always willing to help and answer any questions you have! The readings can be a lot, but do NOT skip them they are so helpful when the test comes around. There was an eight page paper over a book, but Dr. Gulbas and the TA will help you work through it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulbas was such an amazing professor! Her lectures are super interesting and I love how interactive she was with the class. Its not hard to get an A if you do your work. There was only 3 exams including the final, one 8 page paper, and a ton of super easy reading responses. I highly recommend this class you will not regret it!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulbas is such a sweet professor, her lectures are always interesting and I never have trouble paying attention. She made me feel so welcomed in my first class at UT. I will say, there is a lot of reading and writing, and it may feel overwhelming at times, but I promise if you take things one step at a time you will get through it with an A.

Yu is an enthusiastic lecturer, and his lectures are worth attending. He answers questions in class an during office hours, and is very caring. The workload is very manageable, and his exams aren't bad.

I highly recommend on taking this course with Professor Yu. He explains concepts clearly, encourages questions, and cares about his students' learning. The office hours are also really helpful and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu was a great professor. He can be confusing and/or boring at times but he is very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. Class is very test heavy, so be prepared. Would def take again.
Professor Yu is an excellent lecturer. His teaching style is clear and easy to understand, and he is always open to questions. I learned a lot during his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very good, excellent teacher

This course covers a variety of modern topics: solar cells, piezoelectrics, nanogenerators, and batteries, as well as nanotechnology. The professor is highly knowledgeable in these fields. The overall difficulty is moderate, and a certain amount of time is needed to digest the content and gain valuable insights in those topics.

Awesome prof!! HW every other week, realitvely easy. One exam, carbon copy of old exams from prior semesters. Final is a group project + individual paper, also very easy. 25 min presentation + 10 page paper, but honestly didn't feel like much work. 10/10 recommend for easy, interesting CGE. Unique concepts & he knows what he's talking about!

Great professor, very kind and has good class structure. Is responsive to questions, and while his tests are memorization heavy, they are not bad at all. He knows his stuff too, and I was glad to have taken his class.

Dr. Yu is an excellent Professor and lecturer. For every important point in the  slides he will make a clear explanation to help students better understand. He is also very nice and pretty patient to answer the questions we raised. I do learn a lot and have a great time in his class.

Professor Yu is a great guy-- he cares a ton about his students and wants them to not just succeed in his class but also have a greater understanding of the subjects needed to successfully perform in the real world. Tests are very memorization-heavy, but nonetheless doable. He is flexible and is readily available to help students in need.
Pretty easy grader. If you don't understand something go to office hours. Not a whole lot of work, but a ton of memorization prior to exams. The exam reviews in lecture are essential

Dr. Yu is highly versed in the field of nanotechnology which makes learning from him very encouraging. His classes always challenged my knowledge and motivated me to further explore the magic behind science. Dr. Yu is also very caring and wants you to succeed if you share your goals with him.

Professor Yu is amazing. You can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you don't understand something from a lecture, go into OH! I was so nervous about materials eng. but I ended up loving his class so much! Also, he doesn't try to kill your grade but rather cares more about your overall understanding of concepts.

The lecture is really amazing and inspirational. Prof. Yu is a nice guy, with great patience and profound knowledge. You will learn a lot after taking this course. Strongly recommend this course to the students who have interests in nanotechnology.

Prof. Yu's class covers varieties of nanotechnologies and nanomaterials in energy fields, which is a very good introduction class for learning about these fields. In each section Prof. Yu would introduce the key principle of each technology and the state-of-art works. It's real worthy to have taken this class. Strongly recommended.
Prof. Yu is very responsible for the lecture and tries to incorporate more fascinating and useful nanotechnology information/news.
Dope lecturing! You can learn a lot from Professor Yus class. Also its a great chance to get familiar with energy-related research fields.

A conceptually difficult course but the Prof made it easy to understand. Straightforward exam questions if you follow the lectures and do the homework. Very helpful Prof if you are willing to know his door.

Dr. Yu is my favorite professor thus far. He is amazing, and his lectures are clear and organized. Dr. Yu prepares almost every lesson so well, and it is very hard to fall behind. By the way, he is also an emerging and outstanding materials scientist.
Prof. Yu is patient and encouraging. You can learn a lot about advanced research in materials science from this class.

Prof. Yu is a great lecturer and professor. You can learn a lot in his class. He provides clear and detailed explanations for every points in his lecture notes, and always extends the knowledge points we learn in his class to the most state-of-the-art research.

Interesting lectures. Puts a lot of effort into helping out students. He has an accent, but its easy to understand. He only started teaching this course in 2012, by he's very highly educated. Take his class before word gets out that he is one of the best profs on campus
Good lecturer, nice guy, clear expectations.

I love Dr. Smith. He's a really chill guy who is passionate about what he does. Loved hearing about his life and the things he does are so cool. This class made me interested in religious studies. take if you like history. Will miss Dr. Smith.

Hes so chill but clearly very smart. His lectures are interning and he's really funny. He had a good amount of readings but no other homework. Everyone loved him, def take his class, he's not a harsh grader.
Great professor. Super funny and approachable
Overall, super easy UGS, and the professor is so nice. The only thing is that attendance is mandatory and a part of your grade, but other than that, one of the easier UGs for sure.

Loved the class, there is a lot of reading recommended, but even if you don't read anything, you'll still be able to succeed cause of the great TA. Incredibly chill guy, super aproachable in his office hours. The only negative is that he grades really slowly, but I would say he grades leniently and most of your grade comes from completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his Religion and Medicine in the Ancient Mediterranean World course, and it was great. My degree has nothing to do with religion and this has singlehandedly been the best course I have taken. Professor was amazing, it shows that he deeply cares about this subject. He's very considerate with the workload and understands educational struggles.

I took his Religion and Medicine in the Ancient World last semester, SUPER GUD. His UGS is slept on anyone considering taking one should def sign up. Took Professor Gulizio's Intro to Ancient Greece. Lecture attendance was optional - highly recommend attending. Content was pretty interesting. Was pretty easy to get good grades in the class w/open note online quizzes & identification assignments. DO NOT use AI. Professor Gulizio was great, passionate, & made herself available for students.
this class is super easy to do well in even if you don't watch every lecture. def don't use chatGPT on simple assignments bc she reported a bunch of students this semester for that a lot.
Great professor, great lectures.

I love Dr. Gulizio so much! She's so sweet, kind, and funny. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should totally show up to her lectures as they are very interesting. Work is minimal, no final exam, just a project that can be creative, and weekly open note quizzes. Highly encourage taking her class for your VAPA credit.
Great teaching style & very approachable.

Her lectures are entertaining, and you can tell she enjoys the subject matter. There are no exams, just online quizzes, identification assignments and annotation assignments, all very easy. This class is not hard to pass, and you will actually learn stuff if you attend the lectures. She is also funny and sweet and will help you out if you need it.

Very easy class since there are no exams. Instead, there are quizzes every week but they are short & easy. If you do take this class, be very careful with AI as the prof actually checks and WILL write a referral if she catches you. Attendance isn't required, so make your own choices whether you want to block out the time or not- but I personally found her lectures so interesting to listen to! This class gives you all the material for its open-note quizzes and has a final project instead of an exam which you can be creative with, so it's easy and fun. 10/10 VAPA!!
Nice prof; my class was huge, and attendance was not taken. Lectures were all online and quizzes were easy, pretty much identical to notes and lecture content.

Joann is the best Latin professor at UT. If you ever have a choice, always choose her. She's a good teacher imo and most importantly she cares about you and your grades, which is important for a teacher of subject so challenging.
Joann is nice and cares about students including their grades.

Professor Gulizio is one of my favorite professors, I took her classical mythology class for my VAPA and it was not super hard, just some quizzes and papers/projects, also annotations on readings. She is such a good lecturer and just super cool and funny, would highly recommend.

I took Greek Architecture for my minor and LOVED Prof. Gulizio! She is very sweet, gives engaging lectures, and is clearly passionate about her work. She is always willing to work with students so that they can do well in the class, and her class is very nicely structured. Highly recommend taking her class if you can!
Amazing! Caring, sweet, great professor.

Professor Gulizio was very passionate about Greek mythology. She made it a very enjoyable class with relatively easy work. If you pay attention to her lectures and read her assigned readings, you should get an A+. Easy VAPA, would 100% recommend.

Dr. Gulizio is a cool gal who is passionate about mythology and truly loves the subject. Class has a set structure based on quizzes, discussions, short write-ups, and a final project. Weekly quizzes are all in the PowerPoints and lecture is honestly optional if you know how to research and write something up quickly. S-tier VAPA and cool subject!

As someone who was taking her class with little Roman-knowledge, she was a great professor! She cares for your mental health. She is very passionate about her lectures and loves to talk to students. One project & lots on discussions/short essays. NO tests. I highly suggest the class to someone who is looking for a easy class with a nice teacher.

reviews.comment: She is incredibly charismatic and fun. I did not find this class interesting and struggled to pay attention in lectures but all the info needed for homework is posted on Canvas. Dr. Gulizio is great option for any VAPA. I took her mythology class and loved it. Assignments were simple and doable with no test. Just make sure you take good notes weekly for the quiz. It was nice to be able to do a project as a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Gulizio is an amazing professor. I took this class to fulfill a VAPA requirement but became genuinely interested in Roman archaeology because of her. There is a fair amount of weekly work but it is manageable. There are no tests but there is a final project which you have the choice of doing an essay project or a creative project.

Lots of extra credit, some assignments w/ no timer, 3/4 essays, all answers in the slideshows, was very engaging. I stopped going to class after the first month, but didn't struggle just have to check for deadlines. No penalties for late assignments (NOT the writing assignments) as long as you get it in before she grades. Highly recommend!

Weekly online hw assignment (best of 2 tries), weekly quiz (open note), weekly extra credit quiz (open note), 3-5 image IDs / discussion boards graded p easily, final essay project just start it early and get it out of the way. Very fair grading, teacher is accessible via email, don't have to go to lecture because all slides are posted. TAKE HER!!

Overall she was awesome! Easy weekly assignments and open note quizzes. Super caring and considerate of you having other classes and things going on. Willing to change almost every due date if needed. Definitely cares about every student! An easy and enjoyable VAPA and GC flag!!

Gulizio is a great prof and very passionate about mythology. Even if you don't like mythology, this is still a very easy VAPA + GC flag class to take. Open notes/readings, online quizzes, and perusall annotations each week with an occasional writing assignment and a final project/essay instead of a final. No exams and not required to attend class.

reviews.comment: Professor Gulizio is so passionate about what she teaches which makes it a very enjoyable class. All Quizzes are open note, and there are extra credit quizzes offered weekly. The final is a project which was super fun and relatively easy to do. Very caring and understanding when it comes to extensions and deadlines.

Dr. Gulizio is such an amazing professor and I would definitely take her class again. She is very caring and if you need help with anything she is always open to help. Its an easy A and a great choice for a VAPA. There are no tests and easy online assignments each week. There are weekly quizzes that are open note and no final exam, just a project.

Dr. Gulizio is extremely caring and obviously very passionate about the subject matter. She is willing to go over any material if needed and made lectures very interactive and informative in a fun way. All textbooks were provided by her as pdfs on canvas so it saved me a lot of money. Even her TA added a whole level to the class that made it fun.

reviews.comment: Professor Gulizio is absolutely amazing!!! I am an engineering major that took this class as a VAPA and a GC flag. Attendance isn't necessary and this course is an easy A as long as you do the work. However, I genuinely wanted to go to this class every TTH, it got me up in the morning. She's inspired me to study abroad in Rome. So good!!

Take Roman Archeology with Professor Gulizio. She is so sweet and it is super easy. No tests, a weekly assignment that takes like 20 minutes. Weekly open note quizzes and extra credit quizzes, will take 20 mins combined. Occasional longer writing assignments (easy). No attendance/tests so I went to like half of the lectures and got an A easily.

The work was manageable, with weekly quizzes and persuall annotations. There was no final exam, just a final project, and occasional writing assignments that were not difficult at all. She would extend deadlines if needed and overall she was just an amazing professor. strongly recommend

Dr. Gulizio is AMAZING. This has been one of my favorite classes at UT, and I'm a 3rd year. The content is super interesting and the homework is so easy yet still very engaging.
