reviews.comment: Just got out of my bio midterm 2 after studying for 8 hours straight. Was warmly welcome to a midterm that did not follow any of the learning outcomes and with questions that didn't include any of the information from the textbook. Dr. Fritz cancels lectures at will and responds sarcastically to several questions asked in class. You've been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz was an amazing biology teacher. Lectures were engaging, discussions were worthwhile to attend, and tests were easy. As long as you keep up with reading, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I don't know why Fritz gets so much hate. As long as you go to class and can read questions on the test, there's no reason that you can't make an A. She is pretty obvious about what's important based on lecture, and she bases her tests on the Testable Skills that she gives you. It's not a hard class especially with an AP BIO background.

Dr. Fritz is very knowledgeable about biology and it's evident. I did not like the way she structured her tests at all. She always gave us "testable skills" to study before the exam, but when the exam came around, only a few of those testable skills would be on there. Tests are MC and short answer. Very tricky wording and sometimes confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very surface level; as a student who had taken AP bio (& got a 4), they didn't get me thinking and I didn't find them valuable at all. Be prepared to self-teach a lot of the content in prep for the exams. If anything, look to your TA for help. The grading weights are in your favor, though, so take advantage of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was my pleasure to study under Dr. Fritz. Her lectures were incredibly thought provoking and in order to succeed in this class we had to develop a deeper understanding of the material. I HIGHLY recommend her classes for any pre-med or science majors because she is hands down one of the most intelligent people Ive ever encountered. GO TO CLASS!

Great caring professor. Really wants you to learn processes rather than memorize material. Go to EVERYTHING including office hours. Do the homework before class, go to discussion and hands-on, and do all of the quizzes. Those are easy points to earn. I dropped out of UT 19 yrs ago and this was my first class back so if I can do it, YOU can too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great professor. Shes a great lecturer and really helps you understand biology and the concepts, not just memorize stuff. The tests can be tough because of that - its not rote memorization, but application. If you want an A, you have to really study! Her lectures slides actually follow exactly what she tests on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content isn't bad, and she knows what she is talking about, but the questions on the exams are always worded really vaguely or in a weird way so that you need to ask for clarification to even know what she is asking.

She's an okay teacher, not too memorable. Be prepared to shell out 50 bucks for that mandatory iclicker piece of garbage. This class is boring, but good thing is that it's kinda easy. If you pay even a little attention in class, the exams will be a breeze and they are curved a lot too. You can get above a 100 on every exam so take advantage of that

Very detail-oriented exams, she'll find something mentioned once in the textbook and put 5 questions about it on the test. You can petition to get credit back on the short answer portion of an exam, but she won't give it to you. If possible, take the class with Dr. Buskirk.

I had taken AP bio in hs so granted, a lot of the material was easier for me to grasp. But she prints out her powerpoints and gives them as handouts, which is very useful. The short answer can be a little convoluted at times, so make sure you ask questions during discussion sessions (which are extra credit if you go to enough) to understand content
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to teach yourself the entire course, Fritz is the one for you. Also set aside around $200 for the materials needed. This is technically a flipped classroom except you barely learn in class. Most lectures consists of "talking to your neighbor" about diagrams and "movies" that she puts up in class. Fritz is sassy and annoying.

If you are on a budget then do not take this class, she charges you 75$ for a pearson account in order to complete your homework and you have to buy one of those 40$ iclickers for her class. The other bio teachers dont make you buy either of those things... She is not too nice either.
horrible. have had her for maybe three classes and i just know she's an absolute mess. doesn't cover anything in lectures but the HW and readings are so long. also textbook is super expensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, this class was difficult. However, an A IS ATTAINABLE if you put in the work. Go to her office hours, ask questions, pay close attention during lecture, and study days in advance for her exams. DON'T MEMORIZE, you won't do well. You absolutely have to understand the information and apply it to other situations. Don't give up! :)

I love Dr. Fritz. She is passionate about what she does and knowledgable, as well. The class is an easy A (I didn't take AP bio either), the textbook goes in too much depth, but you'll get an A if you understand what's in it. Listen in lecture she always repeats things that will show up on the test (usually word for word how she says it).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: study powerpoint slides in depth and discussion activites come up very often in the free response. Textbook is a waste of time because that's what I studied and I never did well. Understand general applications of the topics because her tests are more of a general understanding and it can trip you up if you only study specifics.

A midterm was so disorganized that some questions had several correct answers and other questions had no correct answer at all. As an apology of sorts, Dr. Fritz created the opportunity for more points on the next exam. This class is not necessarily difficult, but in an attempt to create rigorous exams, Dr. Fritz ends up playing herself and you.

- Study lectures and testable skills (prov. by her), masteringbio, quizzes in this order. DON'T STUDY THE TEXTBOOK UNTIL AFTER EVERYTHING ELSE! Test material comes from lectures and even off the cuff statements she makes. - She has some very edgy humor which I appreciate - It's not harder than APBio just covers slightly dif. material more in depth

Not going to lie, Fritz's tests can be really tricky, but her teaching style really enforces deep, conceptual learning of the material. If you're looking for an easy A, she is definitely not the professor for you. The key is listening to what concepts she puts an emphasis on during lecture and really knowing the testable skills back and forth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is genuinely a great person, but her class is extremely difficult. In order to attain a high grade, you must study for at least a week or more in advance. Her course is centralized by her exams, which are unnecessarily difficult. It would be beneficial to go into her class with some background in biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are a complete waste of time and do next to nothing to prepare you for the exams. She is not a good lecturer yet requires her students to attend them for credit. The tests are either made to be confusing intentionally or perhaps they are a reflection of the lack of care and effort that this professor puts into her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take her. The TAs and discussions are more helpful than the professor and lectures. She would spend a lot of time covering irrelevant topics that arent tested. The tests are tricky and worded in ways meant to confuse you. I took AP Bio, got As and passed the AP exam but still found her class difficult. Attendance is mandatory

I believe this class to be for people who STRONGLY retained the information from AP Bio in high school. Her lectures are broad, but her exam covers specific details on application, and questions that were very vague on what to answer. You pretty much teach yourself reading the textbook, and learn how to pass tests rather content. Pro: TAs are good

Challenging, but great and caring professor. Exams focused on information covered in lecture slides. Don't worry too much about extra information covered in homework or assigned readings.. Weekly quizzes are a VERY good indicator of the information that you will be tested on. As long as you pay attention and put forth the effort, you'll be fine.

I got a 6 on IB biology, and SUFFERED in this class. I thought I was going to fail it for MOST of the semester. It is do-able, if it's ALL. YOU. DO. You can know everything you're supposed to and still fail, because it's more about how to take an exam than what you've learned. She makes inappropriate jokes in class, and is overall unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tests are MC and FRQ and can get specific at times. However, her lectures stress test-related material and she provides several avenues for getting more help. Weekly HW assignments and discussion sections are useful (discussions are EC). An A is definitely attainable with effort. Overall, she's a great lecturer and a pleasantly sarcastic person!

Main advice -- go to office hours. She will give you tips and advice on how to do well on not only her tests, but future tests in other classes. Everything you are tested on is fair and has appeared on her lecture slides or during discussion. Plus, the final is fairly easy and has extra credit on it! Also, not a boring lecturer. Great professor.

I came into the class with no background of biology (except from my freshman year of high school taught by the football coach) and I managed to do well in the class. She definitely makes you work for it, but it is very doable. Pay attention in lecture and GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! She's a hard professor, but definitely cares and wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fritz is a good lecturer and overall really nice professor so it's really hard to dislike her. Nonetheless her exams are extremely hard and detailed. You MUST MUST MUST put in a lot of work and practice in order to do well. If you don't have a strong background in Biology (like I didn't) choose another professor.

DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU DIDN'T DO AP BIO IN HS. She was a great professor and I learned a lot from her, but the test questions are VERY detailed/analytical and she grades it very particularly, so if you don't already have a strong background in biology, it's near impossible to get an A.

BIOLOGY WILL BE 38482 X MORE DIFFICULT THAN HS NO MATTER THE TEACHER!! Fritz is known to be a harder bio teacher but she's amazing. Tests count for 80% of the grade. To do well on the tests, USE THE SWBATS AND KNOW THEM BACK AND FORTH! You have to put in the effort if you want to do well but that's college for you!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: HER CLASS IS HARD IF YOU DO NOT HAVE A STRONG BACKGROUND IN BIOLOGY. BUT OVERALL FRITZ IS A GREAT PERSON AND A GREAT PROFESSOR

reviews.comment: This professor tailors her class to people who have a background in biology. Tests are so extremely detailed and half the information she never even covered. reviews.comment: Difficult class. Biology is MY subject and I ended up with a terrible grade. She does not give A- and As are very hard to get. Also, good luck if youre right on the edge of an A! She lacks all empathy for students in need of assistance. Take an easier bio professor. You dont learn any more from having a hard teacher like Fritz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is a decent professor. She's definitely not the best professor I've had but she taught the material well and made it easy to digest. Her tests and the final were fairly difficult but she didn't give too much homework and the at home quizzes were very easy. She also made chapter study guides which helped a lot in learning the test material

Professor Fritz is an amazing woman and teacher, she cares about students and if you are a science major I really recommend you take her class, it might hurt your GPA, but what your going to learn from her class is priceless. She is really dedicated and motivated, she was a great inspiration to me. (Im not a science major and I loved her class)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very animated so class was never too boring. I understand why people think the tests are difficult: very specific, but if you put in the time it isn't bad at all. I only read the textbook for clarity on some topics. Do the study guides and study with a friend, practice past exams. Homework is easy but not helpful. Go to discussion for extra credit

Personally loved her. Every single bio class involves a LOT of reading and memorization, so dont hate a prof for that. Had a roommate in another prof at the same time and Fritz had easier tests. She's pretty funny, answers questions patiently. The homework is graded SUPER easily, barely any points taken off if you get something wrong.
tests are challenging but she gives her students plenty of opportunities to learn outside class. attendance is not mandatory but necessary for success!

The Unsalty Honest Truth::: Her class is tailored towards students who are already familiar with Biology. Her lectures and study guides are easy to understand, however, the tests are very detailed and tricky. Thankfully, I figured this out early on and decided to drop before my GPA did. Please do not take a chance and risk being given an L.

reviews.comment: Overall a great professor. Loved the course material, and it was well organized. She also kept lectures interesting with jokes and such.

reviews.comment: take this at your own risk, it was the hardest class i have ever had to take. i truly believe that i studied my very best and i studied everything. the exam questions either go into too much detail or are too broad for you to piece information together in your brain. i would try my best to get another professor

3 exams later & I still never understood how or what to study for her exams. I think Fritz is a super nice person, but her exams will kill you no matter how hard you study. An A is possible, but majority make B's & below. After 2014, she had to make her exams harder, & you can't find any old exams online ANYWHERE. hope yall have a better experience

reviews.comment: Great professor! She provides copies of her slides and the readings she covers in the textbook. Read those chapters/sections in the textbook and you should do fine on the test as a lot of her questions are straight from the book. Not a hard class if you put the effort in

If you aren't willing to put in time outside of class, you WILL fail. I never made less than a B on any test but I really had to work for it. READ THE TEXTBOOK, do the study guides, and you'll do fine. If you want to understand the material it its entirety, take Fritz. She's hardcore but very knowledgable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lots of salty students on here... final was easy if you prepared well and she offers extra credit. Solid biology professor. Lots of students dont know what hard work is I guess.

I've seen some harsh reviews about Dr. Fritz; she is honestly a wonderful lady who brings a lot of energy to her lectures. She cares about the well being of her students! The tests (3+final) are hard; you have to work hard for your grades. Weekly quizzes and daily hw can help your grade. I didn't always use the textbook, but it's a good supplement.

Dr. Fritz is a fantastic professor. Her lectures are interesting and she is very funny. She does give hard tests, but if you put forth the effort to understand the material, you will be fine. An A is most definitely attainable as long as you are willing to work for it.

reviews.comment: I don't recommend taking her if you don't have a strong biology background. Her lectures are too broad and general compared to her tests.

Lectures are easy to understand. however the tests are much harder than she portrays. It is important to take the time and study regularly. Keep up with the lectures and material because you will be learning new and testable material up until the class day before the exam. She also makes a lot of awkward sex and alcohol jokes.

reviews.comment: Even though I heard a lot of bad things about her, she is one of the best professors I've had so far. Her study guides list out what she wants to know from the textbook, and her lectures cover everything else. Just take good notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've heard a lot of bad things about Dr. Fritz, but she is a great lecturer and makes sure her students understand the information very precisely. The study guides and lecture notes help a lot. If you're pre-med, she is probably the best professor, but be ready to study hard because this is definitely a weed out course.

She is by far one of the best professors i've ever had. Her teaching style is pretty simple. First exposure readings, second exposure homework, third exposure in lecture. People who are complaining about the grades they are receiving simply didn't put in the hours or the effort mindfully. She is fantastic and inspirational! Would take again.

This class is more tailored towards students with strong bio backgrounds, even though she says otherwise. She claims that her lectures and study guides are the key to doing well, but her lectures are too broad and the guides are too detailed for the test. Loves having tricky MC's on her tests, which weigh more in comparison than the simple SAQ's.
DO NOT TAKE FRITZ FOR BIO311C. Lectures are all over the place and the exams are unnecessarily confusing. I had to drop and take someone else
Maybe went to lecture 3 times the whole semester. Exams are based on the textbook. As long as you do her reviews, you can get a solid A in the course.

Tests are so unnecessarily difficult, and the workload is insanely high. Lectures are often confusing, and she treats students like high-schoolers. reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! If you have to take bio take a different prof. She isn't a good teacher and her test are impossible. I have studied more for this class than I have for any other class and I have not passed a test yet. I don't recommend.

reviews.comment: Professor Fritz is a really nice person but has a hard time really explaining in depth the material we learn in class. reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Worst class I've taken at this campus. Tests are ten times more in depth than what she teaches or tells you to learn about. reviews.comment: She changed the test this semester and they are nearly impossible even with reading the book and doing the study guides. I do not recommend having her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Treats students like they're in high school by calling on them for problems and berating them for being on their laptop/phone. Tests often go beyond what is talked about in class and frequently have trick questions. Makes you buy iClicker knock off app and Pearson online program which felt like a waste of money but was required in order to get an A

I really enjoyed this class. Fritz tries to keep things interesting. Definitely a fast paced course and you will have to read ALOT but if you are prepared to buckle down and work hard an A is completely achievable. Lecture can be overwhelming but the test are straight forward. I would totally take this prof again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a professor she was kind, funny, and knew what she was talking about. To pass the class you NEED to read the chapters, since the test questions are taken verbatim from the text. Study question sheets were helpful but not necessary, since all of the answers were found in the book. There was plenty of time to get everything done for her class.

Dr. Fritz is amazing!!! If you are pre-med, TAKE HER!!! Her class really forces you to actually LEARN the material. Tests are not THAT challenging--do the study guides (emphasis on this!!!), pay attention in class, read the book, and go to discussion. Commit to the class and you will get an A for sure!

Dr. Fritz is probably the most amazing prof I've had here so far. I love her sense of humor and her determination to really teach her students everything the class has to offer. I thought I had a C+ in the class but she bumped it up to a B! I'm waiting to take her for 311D because she's just that good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is ridiculously hard. You need to read all the chapters, know all the study guides, and know all the details or else you wont do well. the lectures alone are not helpful, you need to do a lot of outside work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty diffult because you have to actually read all the chapters from the textbook and do the study guides that go with them and make sure you know all the details. The lectures do not go in enough detail to prepare you for the test, and her tests are really tough. I wouldn't recommend taking her unless you already know a lot about biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: My school hired this botany professor from UT Austin to teach at American Embassy School in New Delhi. So much homework and teacher wont teach anything. Get a tutor for sure if you want to do well on IB exam
Fun lectures and gives a lot of extra credit. Tests are extremely confusing. Attendance is taken through clicker points.

Great class, when I showed up. If you miss class often, expect 70s on the tests, because she takes about 30% of her tests from in-class anecdotes.  Great lectures, occasional ham-fisted weed joke here and there (420 was the best class yet). I would recommend her if you are passionate about the subject, or you plan on continuing Bio.

Tests aren't really THAT hard you just need to cram study and read the textbook and her lecture slides which she posts before the tests. It's not a blow off class, but her point system allows attendance to make up for her hard class. For me it was a pretty easy A, and I hate bio. Lectures are pretty entertaining too.

Her lectures are very broad and the tests are difficult. With the discussion sections and the homework and clicker questions its not impossible to a decent grade (B)but I would not say this was an easy class.

Fr. Fritz is a wonderful woman, but her exams are difficult. You have to go through the powerpoints and pay attention to the "Learning Objectives." She loves to talk about the material, so don't be afraid to ask questions and go to her review sessions. She also takes attendance in class through clickers.

Okay, so Fritz is an awesome PERSON but not so awesome when it comes to running the class. Her lectures weren't so bad, and 20 percent of the class is just clicking and turning in homework. However her exams were extremely difficult in comparison to everything we discussed in class. So if you do take her, prepare for extremely tough exams.

test questions don't only come from her powerpoints, even though she said they do. class out of 500 points, which is nice because i didn't pass a single test but ended up acing the final and getting a B in the class.

although it was a hard class, its not hard to get an A. If you read and look over powerpoints, especially the part where is says "what to know", you should be fine. She is hilarious and I loved going to class!

Dr. Fritz' lectures were very fun and easy to follow, but her tests were extremely difficult. It required applying the basic principles to an extreme. With that though there are quizzes once per week, clicker questions every day, extra credit for attending discussion, and a heavily curved final. It is extremely possible to make an A in this class.
People with no prior knowledge of biology, be warned. This class is not for you. You had to go to class for clicker questions. Her tests were hard in comparison to what she taught.

Dr. Fritz was one of those professors I was never able to fully understand. Her lectures did not consist of core content that showed up on her exams. Her class objectives and expectations remained ambiguous no matter how many times I reached out to her during office hours. I did not learn a lot from flipped classroom setting & would not recommend.

Fritz is a great professor and very entertaining. Took this class because of good reviews and high distribution of A's and B's. However, half way through the semester, Fritz announced she would be making the test more difficult due to instructions of the dept. Tests were random, scattered info and were unlike topics and material covered in class.

Dr. Fritz is the worst bio professor i've ever had. Test material is completely random and not covered in class or discussion for the most part. Reading is helpful but only to an extent. She's a nice person, but not an easy A, or B for that matter.

Professor Fritz is good at explaining basic biology concepts in a way anyone can understand. She has a sense of humor too, and occasionally works funny videos and comments into her lectures. I really enjoyed taking this class - it's pretty easy to get an A as long as you pay attention and do all the assignments. Recommended!

She is super sweet and makes the class really entertaining! You need to always be there because there are clicker questions. Homework is once a week but extremely easy. Tests are not bad if you look over notes the day before. You can zone out in lecture with no problems. Quizzes are online and you just need to pass them. I also just love her.

Dr. Fritz's class was one of the most difficult classes I have taken. The material isn't too hard to grasp as long as you read the book. However, her tests are made to make sure you know everything about that subject. Her questions are very easy to get tricked on. She offered a lot of extra credit/hw points so this is what saved my grade.

I enjoyed Dr. Fritz as a person, but as a professor, she was a little all over the place. Her tests are a lot harder than you'd expect since her class is so laid back. Reading the book is VERY helpful, but VERY boring.  Overall, the class was just okay. She really is nice though, so office hours can really be helpful.

Such a nice person. She is incredibly funny and her lectures are quite interesting, not to mention she deeply cares about her students. The only setback is the difficulty of her exams. Some of the free response can be VERY difficult, along with her MC. Reading is definitely a must for her, and understanding the applications of the reading.

Dr. Fritz is funny. She has great energy so her lectures are enjoyable. You will probably have to read from the book, because she tries to use lectures for additional material rather than to review what the book gives you. This class is really easy if you have a strong background in science.
She's a good teacher but she's not an easy a. Definitely possible as long as you study and pay attention!
So nice and really helpful. I didn't open my book once and got an A just from going to a majority of the lectures and discussions. Posts ppts online which helps to study. Great teacher!

Dr. Fritz is enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and personable! She encourages questions, presents funny videos, and holds informal coffee groups to get to know you better. Her lectures are really helpful in prepping for the upcoming tests, which aren't too hard if you feel like you really understand the concept. The grading is fair and simple.

Fritz is a really nice professor and her lectures are very clear and helpful. BUT her test are soo hard! I failed 3 of her exams even though I understood the powerpoints. In order to pass w/an A, you MUST attend office hrs and read the textbook over and over again. MEMORIZE EVERYTHING! Memorization is the key in being successful in her class.

Extremely helpful, one of the few professors I have met that is so willing to help her students. College biology is not easy, but she adds humor to her lectures to make them less painfult to sit through. Her knowledge of the subject makes up for the fact that her T.A. is a tad clueless about most of it.

Dr. Fritz was very helpful during my semester and even had an open discussion on Tuesday mornings, allowing students to meet with her informally to discuss biology.  Her tests are hard and very specific, but reading the book will help. This is not a blow off class but a good grade is possible. You will learn a lot.

Dr. Fritz is very interested in her students. She encourages class discussion and tries to make material relevant. She knows her stuff and is an educator more than a researcher, which makes her great for introductory Biology.

Not sure whether it was me not understanding the class at all, or whether she was horrible at explaining. I had to study an extra lot to barely make a C in her tests. As someone else said, it didn't feel like bio. for non-majors.

Go to class to get attendance points. Her tests are HARD and require application of the material. Make sure you take advantage of the prep u questions (come with textbook), because she uses questions off that on her tests. She loves to be tricky with test questions so read carefully. It really did not seem like a non science major class.
ATTEND EVERY SINGLE LECTURE. don't blow off the quizzes in discussion, and prepare to be thoroughly confused about the short answer sections. i hated this class

One of the worst teachers i have had my college career.  I regret taking her class.  She tries to be funny and interesting but is quite the opposite of that.  Her tests are vague and ridiculous, essay and short answer format with some multiple choice.  I hate her class....stay away from her, far away!

Dr. Fritz is a nice lady, but don't let her fool you. Her tests are hard. Made up of a free response section worth about 25 points and multiple choice worth 60. Free response questions are difficult, you have to apply what you know to a sometimes strange question. Put forth A LOT of study time, and I mean a lot. Read the book and the powerpoints.

She's a good, fun teacher and very helpful but this course isn't easy. You need to know all the material and then be able to APPLY it. Read the book throughly. Pay close attention to pictures from powerpoint slides and book and understand whats happening in them. Tests are wordy and very big on application instead of straight memorization.
bottom line, she's a fun teacher. not a hard class at all. she does A LOT to help you out. she can teach you and make you laugh at the same time. take this class. its an easy B (at least).

Awesome teacher, she is entertaining and doesn't drift too much. Office hours are a students friend, she will help you with ANYTHING you need, go to them! Don't be nervous, she is super cool! Much of the exam is free response and fill in the blank, but as long as you have a basic understanding of the material, you will ace it :) extra credit given
Love the class, love Dr Fritz! I'm an Liberal Arts major, so Bio has never been my thing, but she's adorable and funny and very helpful!

OMG Ms. Fritz is the best teacher at UT period. I hate bio but, I LOVED her class. She made it super funny and in the end I'm walking away with a lot of Bio Knowledge. My exam avg is a very very low C but, I did everything else and I'm getting an A!! Best Teacher Ever!
Read the book, go to lectures, and study. You'll be fine. She's a great teacher especially for intro bio kids.

I really enjoyed her class...but if you want a good grade there is no doubt you will have to study/read. Attendance is very important as what she goes over during lectures is basically the outline of what you should study. Shes very clear and humorous so the class isnt dry. Going to her during office hours also really helps.

Professor Fritz is a funny, energetic professor that tries to keep information interesting.  Her tests are somewhat difficult, consisting of many short-answer problems and in-depth diagrams.  However, she does give extra credit, and there are easy homeworks and slightly harder quizzes to buffer your overall grade.

lectures are really easy and quick. exams are hard though. you must know the material. even though she says her exams area lecture based, you have to read the book to do well. she's energetic and tried to keep lectures fun, despite the subject matter.

Dr. Gnagy is a good guy, don't get me wrong, but his lectures are very boring, and he rambles about the same thing every day. Most people skip, myself included. Study the slides before one of your 50-question tests. There are 3 total. If you do poorly on one of them, it may be difficult to raise your grade, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Ironically, my hardest class is an elective. Pre-lecture and lecture slides are crucial for the Challenges and daily assignments (DO them). Lectures can be in Challenges, but only present in 1-2 questions, you can skip lol.

Recommend uploading the pre-lecture, lecture slides, and the study guide into a study resource for practice tests/ review
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were very engaging, and he always amped up the class by playing fun music before every class. I spent a lot of time writing notes on the lecture slides ahead of time. Make use of the study guides for the exams and actually study, then you should get an A. I am almost tempted to take the golf course with him because he was so much fun.
Stay on-top of deadlines, because he gives little to no reprieve. Make use of the study guides because lectures will not be covered on the test.
Shoutout Doc! Great teacher and extremely approachable. Golf class was a great stress reliever during my last semester. Just show up and do the stuff and you'll make an A. Easy peasy!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Goated golf teacher, I still 3-putt but I feel better about it. He's very personable and will give you pointers if you ask. Most days you'll be at Belmont Hall but sometimes you'll have to go 15 minutes off campus to Hancock Golf or Butler Pitch and Putt.

Dr. Gnagy always brought great energy in class. He was always happy to be in class with us, which motivates you to want to come and engage. His tests are based on the pre-lecture slides. Those pre-lecture slides can get lengthy but if you study those, you will do just fine on the exams. No use of technology in class helps you focus too!

He is an ok teacher but he rambles so much. To the point where he will be talking about one thing, talk for 30 minutes when he could have summaried the concept in like 1 sentance. He does review zooms that aren't really that helpful because he rambles. Overall ok professer just talkes a lot about random things.

An amazing guy overall, tests were 50 questions each (3 total). There isn't a textbook but each day before class DO THE LECTURE NOTES. Some things on the lecture notes won't be read in class. Funny presentations with his own drawings and transitions. A good person once you get to know him. Awesome music played before class (mainly rock and 80-90's)

Dr. Gnagy is a very quirky guy who makes a lot of awkward jokes. Going to lecture was a waste of time and it feels like he talks about the same topics everyday. This class is mostly common sense and all you need to do is study the pre-lecture slides and you'll be fine.

I just don't think Dr. Gnagy is a good public speaker if I'm being honest. After every lecture I'd feel like it was a huge waste of my time with him just rambling on and on. If you're taking this class, just study the pre-lecture slides. There's really no need to attend lecture as it's just a waste of time.

No technology. Had to take hand written notes. Lectures are interesting and he gives more in depth examples but a lot of material is covered in pre-lec slides. Tests were kind of hard because it's heavily knowledge-based.

Genuinely an awful lecturer. He does bring energy and it's appreciated. However, he rambles often, mumbles sometimes, and is overall very disorganized when trying to make his point! Definitions are on pre-lecture slides, but even then, it's still very disorganized and around 30-40 slides each. Avoid this course if you can!

Dr. Gnagy is like a motivational speaker so the lectures are mostly entertaining but some days it is annoying. He provides opportunities for easy points and if you study off of the study guides the exams are fine. There are no phones or electronics allowed and he is serious about that but it makes you stay better engaged in the lectures.

Dr. Gnagy was a very kind and respected professor by my peers. He taught a lot of us life lessons that can be used for many other classes and skills to use in our daily lives, with that being said related to being an educator I felt he lacked an understanding of the students learning. Not having test reviews, poor communication on test content etc.

As someone who couldn't care less about psychology but is an athlete, I ended up really enjoying this class. No tech. The tests seem scary but are super easy if you go to class and take notes. 3 tests, 1 group project, and 2x20 day super easy homework assignments with loads of extra credit. Will pretty much only talk about golf but a cool guy.

Decent professor, lectures could've been better but I understand why he'd want to present different material from the pre-lec slides. Only three tests so if you read slides you'll be fine. Loads of extra credit opportunity to help if you don't do too hot on the tests. Overall, an okay course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor rambles on the entire lecture about philosophy like a pseudo-intellectual and takes forever to get to the point. There is a ton of different psychology terms to know. I would walk out of the lecture feeling like I wasted time that would've been better spent just studying his pre-lecture slides and taking notes. Lecture diff then tests

Non-major, took this class as an elective, as his ratings were high. The primary issue was the professor's tendency to delve into rambling monologues about life and philosophy. Exams are bizarre & unrelated to the lectures. More concerned with discussing the meaning of life than coursework. Wouldn't take this class unless it's required.

One of the few classes I've ever taken that actually changed my outlook on things in my life. The class was very straightforward and the lectures were interesting enough. Only rule is no technology, so notes need to be handwritten. 3 tests that are multiple-choice, 1 extremely easy group project, and essentially no homework

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS CLASS!! This class taught me self-efficacy, self-confidence, to learn to take responsibility, give myself some self-care, and sooo much more that I will take with me throughout my entire college and personal life. Professor Gnagy ALWAYS showed up with so much energy and smiles which transferred to the class!

Professor Gnagy gave a ton of extra credit opportunities and was very approachable. If you study pre-lecture slides for the Challenges you will do very well. The daily assignments were super easy points- you just can't forget to do them. Lecture isn't mandatory, but there are a few examples taken strictly from class within the Challenges.

Not a bad professor. His lectures can be hit or miss, but for the most part, are good. To be honest, the class is very easy, you just need to study the pre-lecture slides pretty well and you'll ace the challenges. Don't forget to do the daily gratitude and what went well assignments, as they really boost your grade.

He is a great teacher. Classes tend to be upbeat and interesting. Homework takes 30 seconds to do and gives extra credit for every HW you turn in. There is no attendance, but lectures are very important. Just take notes, make flashcards when you can, enjoy the lesson, and learn. Test are challenging, but certainly not impossible

I took this class my first semester of college and I really enjoyed it. Tests can be difficult but almost all the information can be found in the pre-lecture slides. There will be a few test questions asking about specific examples he went over in class, so it is important to go. He also curved every test and there were extra credit opportunities.

Overall the subject is super interesting however lectures can be kind of shallow compared to prefecture slides. Test are hard, they mainly go over the prefecture slides so make sure you take notes on those. Overall the class was fun and there are two opportunities for extra credit just make sure you remember to do it!
Lectures are pretty bad and very boring

The lectures were very easy to understand, and could be pretty inspiring with advice on improving your own life. You could easily show up to the lecture to get all the information in a pretty entertaining way, or simply read the pre-lecture slides and be prepared for the tests.

Fun! You spend most days at BEL but have to go to actual golf courses in austin(transportation not provided, bus accessible tho). "Final" is a test about golf terms/rules so study those throughout semester. He helps you learn how to properly swing and play the game. Very chill and easy-going. Talk to him and he will get to personally know you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are 3 exams & group proj. For COVID he canceled the proj. The 2 extra credit assignments are easy but DONT FORGET TO SUBMIT EVERYDAY. His exams were heavily dependent on the pre-lecture slides on canvas. Lectures are okay but its very shallow info compared to pre-lecture. I would print those slides and take notes on them. He is kind/energetic
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly I got nothing out of the class, and the professor wasnt very understanding or helpful with questions or concerns during the covid period

Gnagy is really energetic, but wants what's best for his students. Pay attention to lectures, review all the slides that he posts, show up (not mandatory), be active, and do all the little assignments, because he usually gives extra credit on all of them, and those alone will really help your grade out.

Fairly easy class. Just study the 'pre-lecture' slides and do the daily homework/extra credit assignments and you'll be fine. Everything seems very unorganized and he lectures like a super nervous teenager that isn't 100% sure about what he's teaching so I would not bother showing up to class as long as you check Canvas.

Very basic teacher. He was honestly very annoying to listen to and he talks a lot more than he needs to. But he also posts the important stuff you actually need to know in "pre-lecture" slides. So missing class won't hurt you too bad but it is helpful to hear some of the examples he gives. Bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures in the style of an empty TED talk -- lots of pictures and inspirational messages but in the end boring and not very content heavy. Takes more than a week to grade scantron exams. Pretty easy A with little need for attendance, but grades unnecessarily hard on the group project and you have to know the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class wasn't hard at all. I went to probably half of the lectures and still got A's on the tests. As long as you look over the lecture and pre-lecture slides to study for the tests you will be fine. His lectures are interesting, but not necessary. He also gives curves on tests if needed and has built in extra credit on the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was fine -- mostly cheesy powerpoints. Felt very much like a spiritual class minus the religious aspects.

Gilmore is very well versed on the text (more than any professor I've ever seen). He's very witty, smart, and his essay prompts are daunting and challenging, but sitll very doable if you put the work into it. I'd go to his office hours a few times and try to participate and get on his good side also.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very harsh grader. I asked how I could improve my first essay, and I used his feedback on the second one. He somehow gave me a worse grade, vaguely saying I didn't “master” the text. Not to mention he is one of those teachers who does participation points. Absolutely would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The other reviews saying that he's "intolerant of new ideas" made me laugh. Gilmore is very tolerant of other ideas; they just have to have evidence to support them. He gives fantastic feedback, so if he's never told you that you have a good idea, that's probably a skill issue. Not an easy A but a very achievable and rewarding one!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: (GOV355M) Excellent lecturer. Very well versed in political philosophy and good at teaching students how to analyze the text beyond what is obvious/apparent. He is a tough grader, but gives excellent feedback. I am a better writer for having taken this course. Read the text, participate, and go to office hours to get the most out of this class.

This class made me switch majors because it was so bad. He is incredibly intolerant of other ideas besides his own and punishes you for it, grades SO HARD for no reason and his feedback isn't good either, rambles and doesn't know how to clearly present ideas. One of the worst classes I've taken here and I would never take anything from him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took this class my first semester at UT. He claimed it was an upper division course (it was not) and that he'd grade us accordingly. His lectures were impossible to follow as he wrote everything on the chalkboard (what century is this), and his grading was so unfair. No matter the level of effort I put into my writing he'd give me a bad grade.
Nathaniel Gilmore is one of the worst professors I've ever had.  Unfair grading, favoritism, and very intolerant of ideas different from his own.  Do not take this class; it is a waste of time.

Lectures moved at a pace that was too fast.  He was intolerant of ideas that were different from his own and would mark you down if your own interpretation differed at all from his own.  


Communication and public speaking skills need a lot of work, as he often spoke more to the board facing away from the classroom than to the classroom.

Horrible lecturer. For being a philosophical class he has a right and wrong answer for everything. For one of the essays he told me my opinion was wrong and that therefore I didn't read ANY of the material. I have never had such a petty and closed minded professor. like How on earth did i write a 7 page essay if I didn't read any of the material??
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gilmore is an amazing lecturer and very knowledgeable. You should make sure to do at least some of the readings before class and participate meaningfully. The two papers for this class are challenging and you will do best if you spend time thinking deeply about the different authors. Attend class, make good notes, and attend office hours!

This class is very challenging but absolutely worth it. This is a class all gov majors should take because you get so much out of it. Professor Gilmore is extremely knowledgeable and articulate. Show up to class well-read and ready to participate.

The CTI department has some good professor but Prof. Gilmore was by far the worst professor I have ever seen. For a philosophy class, he has right and wrong answers and if you are someone who disagrees with him, be prepared for a B- or lower. He cannot teach and is not open to listening to students and is closed off to only his own views.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gilmore was a good lecturer and cared about what he was teaching, but this was not an easy class. Be prepared to read A LOT. The readings were very long. The only grades are 2 essays (30%/40%) and participation. He is a very tough grader. I had never gotten a B on a paper until this class. Not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gilmore is very down to earth and very honest. This is not an easy class, he grades his essays harshly but gives useful feedback. I really enjoyed the class discussions and felt like my opinion mattered. If you want to become a better writer or enjoy thinking for yourself then take this class with prof. Gilmore.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved classics of soc/pol thought. the class was heavy on reading, but completely worth it. gilmore is truly brilliant -- every thing he says is incredibly thoughtful. he might be the hardest grader I've ever had, but unlike any professor I've previously had, his class really made me grow. i do not regret taking this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Gilmore's lecture style. His enthusiasm is contagious, and I truly feel like he cared about our learning. In order to get anything of out his class, expect to spend a couple of hours a week learning and preparing for lectures. Overall, his class on social and political thought was a 10/10.
An incredibly incredibly smart man. Dedicated to learning and helping you succeed in the class. Lecture heavy and definitely a hard grader but if you show effort he will help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the course (classics of social and political thought) he claimed that it was an upper division course, however it was indeed not an upper division course. His class made me feel stupid, and he graded incredibly hard. Unless you actually care about the content, I would not recommend taking his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Of all my professors, Gilmore is likely the smartest. He really knows what hes talking about in regards to foundational texts, so much so that his vernacular could have been written by Thomas Hobbes himself. Only 2 papers plus participation, but lots of reading. Highly recommend this course for lower division gov requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Absolute WORST.She would directly target students to make them feel less than. She made us take a bathroom break in the middle of class to stop disruptions, even though the break caused more disruptions. Do not take her for this course
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overall, I would not recommend this class. Dr.Garcia was nice and cared about students, but expectations for assignments and exams were often unclear, and the grading was really tough. Despite attending and participating in every class, I still struggled to understand how work was evaluated. Clearer rubrics and grading guidance would help.

The class content is fairly easy and gives some extra credit.  Attendance is not mandatory, but there are pop quizzes and in-class assignments that are graded (you can't do them if you missed class). No make-ups for any assignment. Implemented a restroom policy because it is a "disruption" when people get up.

Doesn't post slides before class, making it very difficult to take notes! There are 1-2 readings that you need to do before every class, and there are 5 pop quizzes on them. Half of the class is think-pair-share. Little structure and no concrete understanding of crucial topics that need to be taught, and not talked about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I just put the previous rating and I meant to give her 5 stars! LOL shes great

Dr. Garcia is actually amazing. She was one of my first professors at UT, and she made the class so engaging and helpful! Not to mention, she was very funny. She cares a lot about her students and actually puts effort into making sure you understand the concepts. Take her!

GOAT, she wants u to succeed. be prepared to write/study and ur good. Quizzes are random, be there for attendence (though not mandatory). Recommend using NoteBook LM or Quizzify to study as its content heavy. Feedback is specific, use it to improve and exams depend a lot on slides. Overall, great professor, would take again :)
I had Dr. Gonzalez for the TIP-Scholars-in-FRI seminar, and he's the best!!! Always brought us HEB cookies and all the selected readings were interesting :)
He's super funny, chill, and understanding/flexible. His feedback is helpful, and you can definitely learn a lot from him.
Honestly, I loved Tony so much. He was one of the best professors I had my freshman year and was super understanding if you had to miss lab or had any issues. I would highly recommend his class!
Tony is THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!

Definitely my favorite professor at UT. He doesn't really do grades, just turn things in on time and you'll do fine. Also flexible with deadlines! Understands that people have other time commitments and doesn't expect you to come to lab more than 1-2 hours a week. Super chill dude, I recommend any class he teaches. I'd say more but character limit-

Tony is the best professor I have met at UT, he genuinely cares for his students and is always available when you need him. Show up to lab and lecture and you will get an A. Try to become his friend, he is awesome to talk to!!!

Dedicated to his work and cares about the student. Go to lab when you have time and he would rather you try and fail than not try at all. Also, it's a writing flag class, but is not as difficult. I took him for FRI and ARI.

Took her for a different class than what is listed here Her definition of understanding you is to retake the class later instead of adjusting her way of teaching, grading, or assignments. Everything in this class was a time crunch. Been encouraging people to put certain reviews on here

I don't understand why she's been getting so many negative reviews as of late when she was at a near 5 star score when I registered for her class for the spring semester. Her lectures can be a bit boring and long, but overall, the class was really simple and easy, with the tests being pretty easy if you attend lecture. Plus, 90 and above is an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Have her for a separate class. Man if you're gonna complain about being a professor then why are you a professor?
I wish she cared about teaching. She was intentionally vague assignments, and her feedback was often minimal and not constructive.

very sweet and understanding. cares more about participation than anything. Lots of reading but minimal graded assignments. Very accommodating with extensions. 90 and above is an A, and gives a reflection assignment at the end to boost your grade.
I had her for a different class. I wish she would actually care about her job. It seems though she's more concerned with being woke and politically correct. Sad
Yall need to read her other RMP for Austin community college
Had her at ACC and now here. No, just no. Literally not sure what she wants from us even after taking in 110% of her feedback. Such a stickler.
She always moved around her office hours so if was impossible to get help all the while she graded wayyyyy tooo strict. She also showed up late to her own class bruh
*sighs* (in depression)

Im guessing (could be wrong) that she has tenure because she literally does not care about anything. So many arbitrary rules. She doesn't respond to emails on weekends (fine), needs two business days to respond (okay), then doesn't respond. But she said she "saw it though". She also changes her office hours all the time so you can really attend it.
She goes on a tangent alot which wastes class times about the most random topics too, kid you not she talked about her and her husband's favorite types of "drinks" and how they like to "drink"

Something that I know it's not really talked about enough is her accent, which makes it difficult to understand what she's saying. She attempts to speak in Spanish, which is kind of ironic because this is an English class.
There's easier ones for sure

took her last semester- DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE. Grades aren't put in until the last week of classes, doesn't respond to any emails whatsoever, zero expectations are set for the course so not only will you have no idea what to do, you will be punished for it, literally only gives out B's. Literally worst class you can take, save yourself!!!
5 foot 3 and an attitude. That's all imma say about her

Currently in her class, she has this evil smug looking face. Had to ask her a question at the end of class. She pretended not to see me waiting. I ended up waiting almost 15 minutes after class to ask a simple question because she does not respond to emails.
I had her in one of her past English classes. She was great. She doesn't smile anymore. She's seems to have lost her spark and interest
She was verbally rude outside class and made me cry after I talked with her about why I was getting the grades that I was
rubrics seem fair but unfortunately she is not

Love this class! In comparison to other World Lit classes this one has minimal long reads, and she is very understanding to students. She allows absence makeups and essay redos, definitely gives students the benefits of the doubt. All of our essays were graded either 85, 90, or 95 so not a big variety. And an A is 90 +!
Hugo ego and expects students to write like her

What makes me mad is how she doesn't really seem to care about what she does. She doesn't care to give full attendance points to anyone even if they show up all the time to class and is extremely slow to grade things to the point where we got stuff pushed back and had cramped deadlines. She always whined about stuff such as her leg, job, or family.
