reviews.comment: I regret taking this class. She acts nice and all but man she is extremely rude when you try to speak one-on-one and does not respond to emails very well. Did not improve as a writer in this class

Lectures were all over the place and not very helpful. The assignments and readings were fascinating, but her instructions were super unclear. Her feedback was confusing, but she offered plenty of revision opportunities. I liked that she offered office hours to make up for absences!

required to take it
i shouldn't have
Do not be misguided by her false cloak of kindness, it's a red herring

She literally does whatever she feels like. (not to your benefit) If she doesn't feel like teaching, she won't. If she doesn't fee like grading, she won't. If she feels like bringing you down in office hours, she will. Not sure where all these good reviews cam from. I looked at them & thought she was going to be a good professor but I was mistaken.

Her hair is dyed blue for a reason, she sucks. She sucks at responding to emails, sucks at grading stuff on time, and sucks at giving feedback. She took 4 months to grade assignment until the last week of class. She's so political and isn't even a good teacher in the slightest. Who hired her?

She was super unhelpful in office hours, rants on useless stuff in class, grades harsh (btw no one makes above 95 on assignments in her class-in her own words) and talks about innapropaite stuff in class such as her and her husband's alcoholic habits. Even after attending EVERY SINGLE class she took attendance points off because it'll be above a 95
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: In no way was this a "liberal humanities class" like the other reviews are saying. Just because an author dyes her hair and cuts it short doesn't mean her work should be thrown out. The class itself is really easy, and the lectures are honestly not that important. I went for the extra credit, but there is only 20 minutes of teaching per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take unless you are politically liberal. I was super excited to cover Beowulf, until I realized it was feminist Beowulf (author has affinity for the word daddy and the F word). Listened to drag queen recitation in class. Prof read short story about 16 year old lesbians s*xual awakening in class. Super weird all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have nothing good to say. Her lectures are useless. She spends more time giving the facade of being jolly than she does coming up with quality assignments. All supposedly analytical writing assignments actually require us to support one of her biased views, and she rarely provides quality feedback. Professors like her give humanities a bad name.

Really nice class. Professor definitely expands the scope of world literature beyond the European canon and incorporates independent texts such as film projects. There is no A-, so it's pretty easy to get an A overall, even though she caps essays at 95.
this class was just too boring as a stem major, easy otherwise, but you have to read the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Highly recommend this class and professor. The material was interesting to read and as long as you did the readings the class was an easy A. Best part of the class was that we watched two films that were pretty entertaining. There's also bonus points on the midterms for attending the lectures and doing the Instapoll questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I rarely attended class and got an A+ in this course. That being said, this class was an adjustment. The old English was hard to read and comprehend, but the longer I engaged in the material, the easier it got. There were also 1-2 assignments due every single week, so this course was quite manageable with everything being open note and online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A cutoff is 90, which is huge. Didn't read a single text all semester, and got an A. Going to lecture isn't required, but gets a decent amount of extra credit on exams. I was dreading humanities, but I feel like I got out of this awful requirement with Dr. Garcia's class. If you hate reading but need a Lit credit, I promise this is the best one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course involved quite a bit of reading, but it really isn't too bad. As long as you attend discussions and review the lecture slides, you'll do just fine in the class.

Professor Garcia is very sweet and understanding. She assigns a lot of group projects and a few writing assignments, but nothing too difficult. She's pretty good with grading and gives ample extra credit opportunities. Overall, she's a very caring professor and I would definitely take her class again.

LOVE Garcia! She's so passionate about this class which really shows through in lectures. Her class is so fun and allows us to explore course themes in a more relaxed way. She only grades between a 85-95 but if you show more effort (go to office hours) she will help you improve your essays and get a better grade. Readings are really interesting!

Prof Garcia is a very laid back professor. This class had two units and the assignments were the same in each unit they just covered dif things. The tests were open note and pretty simple and straightforward. Attendance isn't required but you get extra credit if you attend class. Such an easy class, I would DEF recommend!!

Super easy class. I got away with not reading most of the stories for class, even though I felt like the texts were interesting. Exams/quizzes are open note and you can find most answers online. No essays and any writing assignments were really simple. The TAs grade all of your work, but my TA was sweet + didn't grade harshly, so I had no problem

Pretty easy, straightforward course. Some books were more difficult than others, but thankfully no essays, just two open-note tests and ~6 open-note short quizzes in total. Lecs were a liiittle boring, but the info is great for tests/quizzes. only mandatory attendance was the 1x/w discussion sections with TA, which were easy (depends on TA, ig)

Easy class with clear rubric. No written papers just 2 unit tests worth 40% of grade. Attendance for lecture is not mandatory (but extra credit is given if you go), but discussion is mandatory. Grading depends on TA, but usually work is simple and straightforward.

simple for a brit lit class. i like professor garcia, but the lectures felt like a waste for me. just know enough about the readings and follow the rubrics for all the assignments. grading is really fair and expectations are clear. discussion is mandatory but lecture is not
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia was great to take for Brit Lit. There was not any papers and only 2 exams based off of the readings and lecture material. The class was also hybrid, so you only had to go to mandatory discussion once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia was great to take for Brit Lit. There was not any papers and only 2 exams based off of the readings and lecture material. The class was also hybrid, so you only had to go to mandatory discussion once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class exceeded my expectations! Grading is super fair and although there is a lot of readings they are engaging. Attendence isn't neccesarily mandatory but it helps a lot to show up! Be careful when it comes to tests, there's only two and they're 40% of your grade!

The best decision I made was taking Brit Lit with Garcia. She picks the best readings (sometimes they're long but it's manageable). The grading is seriously so easy as long as you give it some thought. I have a 102 in the class right now. Dr. Garcia is so caring and interesting and I love listening to her lectures. I recommend her 100%.
Attendance is mandatory although showing up really boosts your grade. Didn't read a single text all semester and got an A. The grading scale for A is 90-100 which is nice.

What makes this class so special is Dr. Garcia's way of teaching. The readings she gives are genuinely interesting and not long at all compared to most Plan II teachers. Dr. Garcia deserves the world and nothing less. If anyone has the opportunity to take Dr. Garcia they should. Follow the rubrics and you'll get an AQ.

I loved Dr. Garcia's class! I was nervous about taking my first honors world literature class at UT. She's super welcoming and does her best to engage her students. She's very available to her students. I also love how she focused on more modern novels from different countries rather than starting with ancient literature. I miss being in her class!

I made and A in this class without doing any of the readings. If you go to lecture and discussion, and read summaries you can slide by. Super easy, but discussions are mandatory. They suck if your TA sucks, like mine did, but Garcia is very patient and understanding with extensions and grading criteria. She also extends deadlines sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia's class is easy enough and she is a nice lady. I will say, all this class talks about is feminism. Every reading she picks, she ties back to feminism. And many of the interpretations of text are eisegetical.

Such a sweet person and gave great lectures! I loved the class topic and it was clear she did too--she always seemed so excited for class and was so informative. Very accommodating with Zoom and accessible in office hours. Only complaints are grade scale (capped grades at 95) and slow response to emails. Amazing professor otherwise!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia is an amazing professor who takes the extra step to engage with her students, even though this is difficult through Zoom classes, through discussion of our readings, which were almost always really interesting. She was also very accomodating during COVID and the freeze and genuinely cares about her students' wellbeings.

Dr. Garcia is an amazing professor. I've taken two of her classes now, and I've loved them both. She truly cares about her students and she's a great lecturer with interesting topics to teach. As long as you demonstrate interest in what you write about, it's an easy A. I really recommend taking a class with her!

Loved Professor Garcia! The assignments and readings were always interesting, our class discussions were engaging, and she gave great feedback on our writing assignments. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it!

If you don't put off the readings, this class should be an easy A. Dr Garcia is a good lecturer, and her tests and assignments are straightforward. Poll points are taken in class, but you can miss up to 3 days without consequence. The TAs do most of the grading, and they give good advice and feedback. I highly recommend Dr Garcia.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the UT Austin's best professors, Dr. Garcia's Literature Courses are very good, she provides good feedback, is accessible outside class, very good and helpful TAs, good sense of humor, amazing lectures, and provides opportunities for group discussion projects. Altogether, Dr. Patricia Garcia is a great professor, and is highly recommended!

NOT an easy A! She is a really nice professor, but the material isn't very engaging. You have to read the assigned material or you will not do well on the exams or quizzes. She uses Squarecap in class and the questions weren't always easy so make sure you pay attention in lecture! Participation matters in discussion, all in all it was BORING.

Very good and interesting English class. Left leaning but thats a given. Still an awesome and super nice prof. Best English class I have probably ever taken. Made an A+. Supposed to be three tests and three short papers. Covid changed the class format but first test and first two papers were very straightforward, clear, and graded fairly. Cool TAs.

British Literature are two scary words. With professor Garcia, Brit lit is actually interesting. There is more text to cover than with American literature (since Brit history starts from the 10th century not 17th), which means that the details required for you to know per text is not much. Go to her lectures and turn in your work, A, no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Garcia has been one of my favorite professors at UT. She really cares about what she's teaching and the class discussions are always nice to have. She handled the switch to online classes very well and I will miss having her as a professor.
Professor Garcia is great! Her lectures are super informative and detailed and she is genuinely a nice person. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'd have to TRY to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia really makes British literature more relatable and interesting to read. Lectures were very interesting and she broke down readings to really convey the meanings/relationships. Great professor, go to class and read and youll be fine

Professor Garcia is amazing. She has such a wonderful insight on topics regarding gender, sexuality, race, and class. All the readings are interesting. Graded on 3 essays, a group presentation, and discussion posts. Really enjoyable class .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is so much potential for this class to be much more interesting, but it was only okay. Assignments, quizzes, and exams were easy enough- about on par with other English classes. Not too much work. Avoid if you don't want to act. Overall the class and prof were just average.
The class is pretty easy as long as you go to class and pay attention to what she says you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: TAKE DR. GARCIA!!! This was probably the easiest English course I have taken in my entire college career, and I'm a senior. If you read the plays, you'll get 100 on quizzes. 3 exams all easy if you literally just know the plot. She is very caring and understanding, and the class is amazing. Take her if you can, automatic A+.

Garcia's lectures are quite interesting and in depth and hit the main points that are on the frequent quizzes. Exams (4) consist of objective, short answer, and an essay question. There were 2 standalone extra credit opportunities and another on a close reading installment (4 CRITs total, 16%). We also went to the HRC for to see original books.

Everyone should take this class. No tech, no AI. You have to use your brain, you must think critically, and you cannot choose to not read, as the class operates in a Socratic format, so you will get cold called. The class is hard, but if you work hard it should be manageable. Prioritize your readings; it is really not an option to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Textbook is a band. You will be graded on three things. Make friends early. Love or hate him, he's an incredible lecturer, and I highly recommend taking him IF you are well-practiced in upper-division coursework. I was not, and my grade reflected that, so you've been warned.

Professor Perry's course was a transformative journey through constitutional law, akin to time travel to a bygone era of profound intelligence. His lectures challenged beliefs, offering life-saving legal insights. Despite the intense workload, his passion for law made learning immensely rewarding, marking him as a favorite among students. Take him.

Professor Perry is one of the most respected professors at UT. If you are interested in law school, I would highly recommend him. He teaches his class the Socratic way, the same as a law school. He may initially seem intimidating, but he is a cool and nice guy. 
Advice: This course is reading-heavy, so PLEASE READ the casebook!

I was in one of his early (first?) classes at WashU. I took his ConLaw class and loved it. We loved the content and his teaching style.  Discussions were lively and as noted if you say anything silly he will use the Socratic method to make you realize your mistake, why you made it, and how to think to avoid a similar mistake down the line.

I cannot fit enough characters into this review to describe how wonderful Perry is. With that said, do not take this course if you aren't willing to put in the work. It is difficult because the content is very vast, but it's interesting and made me realize that I love con law. Keep up with the reading and go to office hours if you are confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Perry is easily the best professor I've ever had. Be prepared to read and study *a lot*. I really recommend finding a study group as early as possible because the cases can be difficult to understand and theres a group moot court for 25% of your grade. Actually read and understand each case because he will grill you at random.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to go to law school, take Perry! He treats it like a law school class and cold calls students so make sure you do the reading. He assigns a lot of reading, especially towards the end of the semester. The only grades are the midterm, final, and a moot court. If you're deciding between this class and civ lib, take civ lib!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Perry's class is a great introduction to law school. He's a bit tough on students, especially when he randomly chooses to grill you, but he has a great sense of humor. Everything he does is to prepare you for law so he doesn't put up with weak answers or excuses. Be prepared to read around a dozen cases a week, and be prepared to be interrogated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're planning on going to law school, take this course. It is essentially a first-year law course, albeit slightly easier. Perry is an expert in his field, and will therefore tolerate no tomfoolery. In spite of this fact, he truly cares about his students and wants them to learn. He WILL push you to do your best, but you will want his approval

I had Perry for both Constitutional Interpretation and Civil Liberties. If you want to go to law school, you *have* to take his class. He's a hardass (be ready to be cold called!), but if you put in the effort you'll be rewarded. I still use the notes I took in his class to supplement my current law school readings.

Perry's a great professor if you buy into his teaching style. Know the facts of the case before you come to class, decide whether you agree with how cases were decided and come up with justifications for your opinion. If you don't like talking in class, don't register. He has some frustrating habits and there's a lot of reading, but it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Perry is a (self-described) tough professor, his classes take the form of "discussion" where he will randomly call on students to grill them about their understanding of the readings. The tests are very difficult even if you study hard, simply because of the format. Treat this course as if it's a 6-hour course when planning out your semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor I have had at UT. Not even close. If you want to learn about the constitution, there is nobody better. The class is challenging and the reading is heavy, but it is worth it. Dr. Perry is a master of constitutional interpretation. Cannot recommend him or his courses enough. Wish I could take one of his classes again.

I've taken both his Con Interp and his Civil Liberties class. His method of teaching is a little intimidating at first, but it is very engaging. Since he also teaches at UT Law, I believe his classes are very good for preparing for law school. He mentions that he teaches his UT classes similar to his UT Law classes. Best Professor I've had ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Perry is my favorite professor I've had at UT. Even with class being online, every session was engaging, and his passion for Constitutional law shines through every day. There is a ton of reading and you really need to stay on top of it, as he teaches with the Socratic method and you'll get cold called during class.

Although this was the most difficult class I've taken it is also the class I've leanred the most from. If you want to go to law school I highly recommend this class. You have to read before every class and know the material like the back of your hand. You grow to love him, and you want to do well so you don't disappoint him.
If you take one government professor during your time at UT, make sure it's Perry.
It's quite a challenging class but Perry is a gem of a professor. Amazing man through and through. You won't regret taking him.

Absolutely brilliant man. Perry is witty, funny, and uses the Socratic method to discuss cases in class - no boring lectures. Will challenge you intellectually and give you a new appreciation for our Constitution. It's definitely a hard class, but one of those classes where you learn so much that you end up appreciating the rigor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very lecture and test heavy. Two tests the entire semester plus one moot court project. Perry is super witty and very engaging. He's provocative and will put you on the spot if you can't defend one of your views. I've learned a great deal in this class not only about constitutional law but about my own views and how to back them up. Awesome class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: gREAT PROF.

Constitutional Interpretation with Perry was one of the harder but most enjoyable classes I have taken at UT. In the beginning, he seems fairly mean, but as the semester progresses you will learn to love his sense of humor. He does call on students randomly so you have to do the HW every night. There is also only 3 grades the whole semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Perry is brilliant when it comes to SCOTUS and has a great sense of humor. However, he calls on you at random. He grades on only 3 assignments- a moot court and a midterm and comprehensive final. He is a very tough grader. A's are not handed out easily. There is also a very large amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: TA was always willing to adjust if students spoke up about what they needed. Overall, a helpful and knowledgeable TA who genuinely wants students to succeed.

Grading was fair and mostly consistent, though sometimes I wanted MORE verbal feedback during office than I got from the scripts and could've been a bit more detailed to help improve on future assignments. Yahaya was also approachable outside of class, which made it easier to get help when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had this TA for US History and overall the experience was pretty solid. reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Halidu is exceptionally gifted and very caring. He takes him time to explain confusing terms and concepts clearly to us during the class and in the weekly sessions we attend. I have benefitted immensely from his and guidance. Thank you!
A great TA
Such an amazing TA ! He makes learning seem easier for us. I was not so user to group activities but I have cone to love doing them in his class. He is such a naturally gifted teacher!

Attended his session and it was absolutely fantastic. He is great at doing what he does and seems very knowledgeable of the content and subject. He is a cool guy who genuinely wants his students to succeed in this course. He seems to be highly motivated too and you could see how he carries his messages across.

Incredibly intelligent and knowledgeable TA & SI Leader. His Canvas updates keep us on track, and he goes far beyond what a TA normally does-- providing extra sessions, notes, and exam guides. Grateful to have Halidu this year-- thank you for all your effort!

Fantastic TA & SI Leader! Always smart, patient, and approachable. Makes US History engaging and is available both in and out of class. Halidu truly appreciates students' learning. Thank you for your hard work and support—it really makes a difference!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good sessions. He basically led discussions with an exam review which ended with all questions coming in the quizzes. He is simply a joy to listen to!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such an organized, and supportive TA who creates a positive learning environment that makes challenging material feel manageable. Truly an outstanding SI Leader and a huge reason I did well in this class during our just ended quiz. I have huge respect for this man. Thank you Mr. Halidu. I recommend going to his sessions if you want to do well.

This SI Leader is absolutely exceptional. He explains concepts clearly, breaks down difficult material in a way that actually makes sense, and always makes sure everyone is comfortable asking questions. You can tell he genuinely cares about student success and puts real effort into every session. His teaching style is engaging, organized, and 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An awesome facilitator !

He was not my TA but did far more for us in the class than even my TA whom I have not had the chance to interact with since Mr.Halidu seems to be the one always there for us in terms of  course explanations, announcements and giving exam guidelines. His presence in the class basically made us forget who our TA's were. Go for the SI. Super helpful

If I have to, I will take his class again. Such an amazing experience in his sessions and an awesome personality he has. He is great at doing what he does and you could clearly see the passion he has for the job. Great Guy!

I enjoyed his sessions. He gave me lengthy comments in my initial drafts which helped me to refine my points for the final exams. He is very accessible outside of the SI too. A very highly rated TA you should know if you want to improve your writing skills.

I enjoyed Mr. Halidu's class as he genuinely cares for all his students as evidenced by the record numbers always waiting to see him during his office hours, after lectures and especially on Thursdays after his regular weekly SI class. He went over and beyond to make our work easier in the class. Thank you and best wishes for the future.

The class is definitely challenging, but the Instructor is great and leads really meaningful discussions. He  proofread all my essay drafts before submissions, held office hours, offered comments and suggested areas of improvements. I got an A+ in the end. I was in his Intro to Africa class too. Worth taking again if he has another class next year.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy A if you take his regular SI Sessions seriously. Most of the students who attended the weekly discussions got A both in the midterm and final exams. Join the class if you have difficulties in writing. He basically taught us what to do to get the A's. Easy class.

A demanding course, yet Halidu's teaching style in the SI makes it highly rewarding through meaningful group discussions and pair-works. We completed extensive reading, do the inquizitive tests and are expected to contribute during the weekly SI Halidu facilitates, though it was optional. As a US History course, he managed the class extremely well.

He was very meticulous about my essays when he asked to read and comment on my initial drafts before the midterm and final exams which he did tremendously well. I adhered by his clear instructions and couldn't be too pleased and grateful. I would give him 5/5 stars. Such a caring Instructor !

Yahaya was very enthusiastic in this class and kept us engaged always. We were always eager to meet and looking forward to his weekly sessions. I wish him the very best for the future. He is just an amazing person to be around with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Facilitator he was !
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: But for Mr. Halidu's intervention and the regular SI Sessions he held every Thursday, this would have been extremely difficult for some of us in the class. I appreciate the support and practice questions he took us through for the final exams. Thank you.

Nothing much actually but Halidu was a great TA for this course. He carried himself too well throughout the Fall semester in class with constant reminders and periodic announcements over Canvas. He reached out to all students via emails and was also quick to respond to queries and gave clarifications on all assignments to keep us engaged!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A great Professor and friend of all. He made the class his own and was very passionate about what he teaches. You could see the dedication and commitment. He goes beyond what other Professors do and engaged with students. Very accessible to us.
A very difficult US History course but, Halidu made it easier. Could have been worst for many of us without his SI lessons.

reviews.comment: Mr. Halidu made this course easier than it would have been for most of us. reviews.comment: Nothing really but, just to appreciate Mr. Halidu for the wonderful work and efforts he put into making this class worthy and interesting. We had great engagements during his weekly Thursday SI sessions.
He was awesome for us all in the US history course. Caring and very accessible.

A very great guy and an even excellent SI leader and course facilitator. He was hardworking and made everything possible to ensure we understood the assignments, prompts and midterms requirements. He prepared us effectively for the main exams. Thank you Yahaya. I hope you become a Professor!

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his SI sessions this semester and would be looking forward to taking more of his courses next year. He is well versed and knowledgeable in what he teaches. A great Professor in the making!

reviews.comment: This is the second time I am taking Halidu's TA class. I was in one of his Trad Africa class last Spring and he was engaged with us throughout. reviews.comment: He held SI sessions which students found vital. He was engaged both in explaining class content and during exam preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Emailing updates on class announcements.
The most helpful thing is that TA always provided clear explanations for my homework questions.

Yahaya Halidu was clear in his expectations as well as explaining how to write the essay. His passion and encouragement helped me study and engage with the material more. Going to his SI courses were very helpful. Helped me better understand the content for future essays.
THANK YOU for the SI sessions and helping us prepare for what were otherwise the worst and most stressful parts of this course. Amazing personality and passion for teaching and history.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Yahaya is an excellent T.A. that makes learning interesting. He is well informed on everything he discusses and keeps the energy moving when teaching his S.I. sessions. His form of teaching is unique (something I've never experienced from any other professor) but highly effective in getting his points across in a highly comprehensible manner.

The TA sent many notifications of relevant learning events and others that were very helpful in reminding me of good opportunities.Leading Supplemental Instruction to all students (not just his own) gave me the chance to review and learn topics I would otherwise

reviews.comment: Great lectures. All notes are posted to canvas. HW is essentially a completion grade. Weekly quizzes in class aren't hard and lowest 2 dropped. Asinine exam grading policy. Questions were not difficult but very harshly graded with minimal partial credit. One exam had no calculators allowed. Final grade cutoffs are very generous (40 = C-)
I don't usually write reviews, but Hall really knows how to abstract really complex ideas to be digestible. This class is very effort = reward, no tricks. Plus Hall is just fun to listen to.

Homeworks were completion grades, but grading on test was extremely harsh, taking off many points even for just simple arithmetic errors. The cutoffs for letter grades were adjusted to account for this, but it's not super clear what cutoffs were used in the end. Lectures and notes are also not that clear, would recommend just reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is a very nice professor, but his lectures were disorganized. He also relied heavily on the TA, who did not seem to care much about this class. His exams are also graded quite harshly, but they are much easier compared to other professors. He also sometimes did not cover some homework topics in class until the last day which was not fun.

Overall, glad I took 313 with him, but lectures felt disengaging, so I started to skip and learn on my own. Homeworks are p hard, and sometimes he doesn't cover  concepts you need to know for the hws until the day it's due. Exams weren't bad and quizzes were p easy. My raw score was my final grade, so I don't think he curves at the end

Great person and lectures, but exams are graded very harshly. A simple arithmetic mistake changes a score by often times more than 10 points. Problems can feel a little vague but make sure to master the HW. If you can consistently make no errors when solving problems, you'll be safe from the ridiculous partial credit rubric used on exams.

Dr. Hall explained the concepts clearly during lectures and walked through examples well, and he clearly cared about our learning. The homework did take some time, but it was super useful for preparing for exams. Exams were based on our homework, and I felt that the problems were fair and not super challenging. Overall, I really enjoyed his course.

This semester (F24) is Professor Hall's first time teaching emag, and given the circumstances, I think he did a pretty good job. Lectures are incredibly dense, but Hall does a good job at making it as easily understood as possible. Only gripe is there are at times few examples to work off of, but this is usually fixed by office hours.

Professor Hall has to be one of the best ECE professors at UT.  313 is a tough class but I can confidently say that the work you put into the class perfectly translates to the grade you get. Homeworks are crucial since he uses homework-like questions on the exams, so go to OH for a better understanding of the concepts. Overall great class!

Dr. Hall is the professor you want to have for a course like this. His lectures are worth their weight in gold, they take the dense book chapters and dumb them down. 
Exam grading emphasizes precision. Go to OH to do the homework. Get good with complex numbers, transform tables, and conceptual understanding of applications (sampling, filters).

One of the best professors out there. I initially had no interest in this kind of course but Hall does great at explaining concepts and providing a lot of examples. His hw grading isn't tough and his tests are very similar to the hw. He cares a lot about understanding the material and gives extensions or drops hw questions to give more time

A class that I did not enjoy, as it is reflected in my grade. But Professor Hall is a very lovely professor and easily explains the concepts. He always stops for questions and is not afraid to get a little challenging and testy with the students. Homework isn't that difficult. Lectures and textbooks are critical to the class. Exams are a challenge.

reviews.comment: Best engineering professor I have had so far. He does a very good job explaining the material and is also a cool person. He makes sure you will be very prepared for the exams and doesnt throw any trick questions out. Very good experience in this class.

Very personable, clear, articulate prof. Homework plenty but helpful for exams which make up most of your grade. Good jokes and stories, respected and experienced dude. I enjoyed hearing about his research on acoustics. Go to OFFICE HOURS for homework help.
Great guy. Always made things interesting even when we got into more difficult material
Awesome professor

I really enjoy her teaching style as it is a balance between lecture and discussion. The readings are required but you can usually skim them to get full points. She is very passionate and makes the content engaging.

Nice lady, but the amount of reading assigned is crazy. A 20-40 page paper every other day— and you really need to read them to participate. Participation is 20% of the grade, class is entirely discussion based. She focuses way too much on statistical methods used in research for an intro level mandatory class. Ryan is honestly the best professor I have had at UT. Ryan was one of my favorite professors I've had at UT! He is so understanding and is a very engaging lecturer. I thoroughly enjoyed this class even though I thought I wouldn't like physics. PLEASE TAKE HIM!! I was very hesitant on taking him due to him not having a RMP at first. But taking him SAVED my GPA. I had friends fighting for their life taking marder. His lectures are fun and he's nice, which is why people like him. His teaching is not that great.. tells you to UNDERSTAND but really just MEMORIZE.. at the end of ochem 2, he started saying memorize as well. His exams are hard.. make sure you're not taking other challenging classes!

I was worried about this class, but Iverson made this class not only easy but so interesting. I looked forward to every lecture because of how he explains everything. Exams are fair and he offers many resources to do well.

Amazingly kind professor. As a chemical engineering major, I almost wanted to switch to medicine. He not only teaches the content you need to know, but includes valuable life lessons within the coursework. One of my favorite professors in the university. Very rewarding class if you put in the work!

The best prof. I had. SO many resources and his lectures are amazing (don't skip). Tests are fair if you know your stuff. I had an A in the class the whole semester but the final got me and dropped my grade unfortunately. Go to problem solving office hours to ask TAs HW questions to get 100s on all HWs. I wish he offered a real curve on tests

no other ochem prof can be better than him. offers old exams so you know exactly what will be on the exam, and sooo many resources. he truly wants his students to do well and is so caring and forgiving. content is still hard but he makes it manageable and digestable. TAKE HIM, no other prof is as good as him.

Having Iverson for Ochem 1 and 2 was an absolute privilege. Outstanding lectures, tons of resources to help (previous tests), and a fair amount of content that didn't feel overwhelming. My Goat I love you Dr. Iverson
One of the best professors I have ever had.

I could talk all day about how much I love Dr. Iverson. He cares for all his students, not only as students but as people. He makes Ochem easy and provides so many resources for students to do well. I would take him for every subject if he taught them. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it. He really is changing peoples lives.
Ochem is hard anyways, but he makes it as easy as he can

i love brent. brent is the kindest, most caring, and brilliant professor i have ever had. not only does he truly care for his students as chemists, he cares for them as people (cue: run for the water plug). if you get the chance, you should take him. getting to experience a professor who is truly passionate is once in a lifetime! dr. iverson = king

Amazing professor! He's great at teaching, and he makes things as easy to understand as possible. He as a lot of resources to help if you struggle. There are several office ours throughout the week, all are recorded (as well as lectures).

Professor Iverson made me absolutely love organic chemistry. I didn't do too well in basic chem 1 & 2 so I was nervous coming into Ochem. He is genuinely the most caring and engaging lecturer. If you have the chance to take him, do it!!

BESTTTT Ochem professor could not ask for someone to explain better. Has a plethora of resources and is genuinely committed to ochem. Also brings in inspirational people and cares about health just as much as learning! Def not an easy A but if you put in the time its achievable.
BEST OCHEM PROFESSORRR

Keep grades off for the semester, as they are not accurate. For reference, I had a 40% most of the semester but still ended with an A. Keep up with content/practice heavily to succeed.

I had Prof. Iverson for both ochem 1 and 2, and he's one of the best professors I've had. You can tell he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed, and he made ochem understandable and a bit enjoyable. He also stressed the importance of physical health, especially running.

Geniunely the best professor I've had at UT. For reference, I got a C in OCHEM I, and I thought OCHEM 2 would be worse; however, Iverson's commitment to explaining things in lecture and office hours, plus the numerous practice exams he gives (I did all of them before every test), made the class so doable and amazing. I would 1000% retake him.

If you're not good at learning on your own you def gotta pay attention in class, ochem did NOT come naturally to me so it took a lot of extra practice outside of class and homework, practice practice practice it's all about recognition.

Actually the GOAT. Had him for both semesters (320M and 320N) and got As in both. 
Seemed more manageable compared to Ochem 1 since I was used to the material.
Do everything he says, hammer the old exams, and you should be fine. This class is not an easy A - it is a sacrifice for sure- but your effort will pay off

BEST PROFESSOR EVERRR!! For reference, I got a B- in ochem 1 w/ Straumanis. Very glad I was able to change profs! He really cares about his students. I won't lie, his homeworks were lengthy at times, but they did have problems that pertained to the midterms.

Dr. Iverson is by far one of the best lecturers I've had at UT (definitely the goat of Ochem!) Dr. Iverson is by far the best professor I've had at UT. His lectures are super engaging and he explains ochem in a way that makes sense and also shows how ochem is important to our lives and our careers. He is super sweet and does care about his students. Ochem II did have a steep learning curve esp if you come from an easier ochem I professor like Callmann. I didn't do great on the first two midterms however he gives you the opportunity to replace final with a midterm so though midway through semester I thought I'd get a B, I ended up with an A

One of the few professors who really, REALLY cares about his students. He wants you to succeed in life not just in his class. Only thing I did not love was that the TA's were not active at all on EdDiscussion, but that's not his fault.

While lectures are a bit yap-full (sorry), Dr. Iverson explains difficult concepts in ways that make Ochem easy to understand. Recorded lectures are great, as I did the class completely on my own time (do at your own risk). The course is test-heavy, but worthwhile. He is extremely accommodating to students' needs and genuinely cares about teaching.
I'm begging you guys if you can take him please do it best decision in my life woke up everyday thanking god I had him. If you are a hard working student and not lazy you guaranteed an A.

the goat of ochem. took 320m and 320n with him, his grading policies are graded off only 3 things but is extremely understanding with one exam drop and your final can replace a test. ochem2 is harder than 1

I took his OChem class back in Fall 2019, and not only was he the best professor I had for my STEM classes, he was my favorite professor at UT hands down. He's incredibly patient and compassionate with his students, and his lectures are very informative and engaging. Take him if you can!

Iverson is easily the BEST professor I have here at UT. By the end of the semester, I have a really strong grasp of OChem and genuinely enjoy the material. That being said, he is definitely not easy as some say. His class requires a lot of work and effort, and the tests can get REALLY difficult and unforgiving if you don't study well for it.

He makes me find ochem interesting. Class is test heavy but duh, do the old exams they help so much, and learn your mechanisms. He'll say it's not memorization and it's all about critical thinking but tbh it's a mix of both, do whatever works better for you. Overall loved him and 10/10 would take again.

Absolutely incredible. Some of the best lectures I've had at UT so far and he actually makes a class that seems daunting interesting and fun. You do have to work hard to succeed in this class, but as long as you put the work in & take his advice on how to approach the class & study, you should be able to do well.
You won't regret it.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've ever met at UT. I went to his office hours every week because he actually made ochem fun. He told us so many inspirational stories, and mentions that there is no stupid question to ask. I highly recommend taking him!
This man is him
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the best. caring professor, engaging, interesting lectures, EXTREMELY patient - answers everyone's questions and encourages any/all questions to be asked. best professor i've ever had

Genuinely the BEST class I've taken at UT. I cannot even explain how good of a professor Dr. Iverson is. I was genuinely so sad in the last lecture at the end of the semester. If you can take him, I definitely recommend having him as a professor.

Honestly best science class I have ever taken!! I would have never imagined saying that for O Chem 2 but Iverson seriously made it that good. He made lectures so entertaining and truly taught why orgo is so important for our world. Tests are very similar to HW and past tests, so just work hard and practice and you should be fine.
He seriously is the best professor at UT. If I would have tried a little harder and didn't have so much going on this semester, an A would have been easily attainable.

He is a phenomenal professor at UT. Take him for O chem, you will not regret it! He is very passionate and attentive to the needs of his students. Make sure to go to his Office hours, do the HW (and redo them), and do the previous exams! His tests are fair to what he teaches, and he has clear expectations of what he will be testing on.

ochem2 is def much harder than 1 but iverson made it way better. the way he explains things is so good but ngl had to rewatch some lectures bc i didn't get it the 1st time. previous tests for practice and redoing the hws helped prepare for the tests.

truly the goat. hes been in the game for 30+ yrs so he truly knows what hes about. it says a lot that ive taken chem 1, 2, and ochem 1 here at UT and this has been my first A in a chem course. his website is a treasure trove. take practice exams, listen to his advice on the hw, and give yourself time to truly understand the material and youre solid

Very easy and doable class. Sometimes, I wished it was more to the point. Professor often goes on tangents to make the class easier (dumbs it down to the max so if you struggle w/ chem take him), which is not the best for ADHD students, however he makes good connections to pharma and chem-bio concepts. Overall, nice guy and nice TAs, so I recommend

Absolutely loved him. He kept the whole class engaged through his witty comments and analogies. He taught in a way that made you understand and learn the material rather than memorizing. Homework +
 quizzes, but quizzes were due the next day and were easy. Exams were a bit tricky but just practice the released exams + hmwk! Made synthesis easy!

My favorite professor so far! His lectures are engaging and fun, and he cares about your academic and personal well-being. He fosters a great learning environment and provides ample resources to do well. Office hours are very helpful and he is very approachable. Exams were not bad at all if you studied. Dr. Iverson is seriously a national treasure!

IM HIS BIGGEST FAN. Hands down the best professor, he truly cares about students, he is the BEST lecturer, content can get difficult but he truly explains things so well and is super approachable. He fosters the best learning environment, the tests are not hard and they a lotttttt like the homeworks. Go to office hours!!!! Iverson is awesome

The best professor I've ever taken. His lectures are amazing and he really cares about the content he teaches. He loves to promote health and exercising and it's really helped me overall outside of class too. Course has so many resources so if you're lost, you definitely have a chance to get back on track. Exams are very predictable and easy.

Amazing, amazing professor, take him if you can!! Orgo 1 & 2 are so fun with him, you don't even feel like you're in class. He tells lots of fun stories to help remember concepts and holds lots of review sessions. Practice exams are very helpful in preparing for exams. I didn't need to take CH 328N and I took it anyway because he's that good.
Iverson makes this class so enjoyable! Learning the content requires some effort, but the midterms and final are very doable.

I took Dr. Iverson for both OChem 1 and 2. There is no person better suited to teach this class. Lectures are clear, he provides a multitude of resources for practice, and has some sort of office hours almost daily. He makes OChem a manageable class. There's a reason why so many people like him, he's the best professor I've had while at UT.
Dr. Iverson is one of the BEST Professors around!! I came in thinking I wouldn't like ochem, but Dr. Iverson made me love it!!

Could not ask for a better professor. I was lucky enough to have him for CH320M and CH320N and it was an awesome experience. He really gives you all of the tools to succeed. Best way to study is to do old exams and re-do the homeworks. If you struggle with a concept then use the textbook but aside from that I didn't need it.

I LOVED DR. IVERSON!! I had Dr. Shabbir for CH320M and I thought I hated ochem, but Dr. Iverson made me love it!! He is very accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about his students' success. His exams were all very challenging, but very fair. Although he is not an easy A like everyone says, if you work hard you can earn an A.

The GOAT. Iverson is the golden standard for incredible lectures at UT. He goes above and beyond to maximize the learning experience, using effective strategies to make his lectures as helpful as possible. His genuine passion for the subject shines through, and he will do everything that he can to make sure you thrive in his course.

Having Dr. Iverson for O chem II truly was a gift. His lectures are engaging and if you pay attention, and take good notes, you will do very well in his class. Treat the practice problems like exams, and always take full length practice exams when studying. He truly cares about his students, and treats them like people.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is the gem of UT. He restored my faith in professors for he is someone who ACTUALLY cares about his students. Having him as an Ochem professor is the greatest gift anyone could get in their academic career.

I thought he wouldn't live up to the hype, but oml this man is frickin amazing. If you can take him, DO IT, I feel so honored to have taken his class fr. Tests are very fair, but they are worth a lot, and ochem is not easy content so make sure to study! He gives tons of practice hw and exams, so do those and your set.

Dr.Iverson made me believe that professors are genuinely good people again. He is the sweetest ever and genuinely cares about people and made the hardest subject in the world possible to understand. He is so fun and makes lectures actually interesting. If you have the luck of getting him, hold on tight!

Dr. Iverson is easily one of UT's best professors. He loves teaching and shows up with a smile every day. It's ochem, so the material isn't easy, but he works really hard to help you understand it. His exams are difficult but nothing on them is a surprise. If you can, Iverson is a must-take professor.

Dr. Iverson comes to class everyday in a suit, and hosts surf-themed office hours evenings in a Hawaiian shirt. His years of expertise never dulled his enthusiasm for teaching, and even as an expert he never gets frustrated as he congratulates us with "good question" every time we ask. Thank you Dr. Iverson, for supporting us in and out of class.

This man is everythingggg. I loved Ochem because of him. I heard the worst things about this class, but Iverson made it possible to do well. He really cares and enjoys teaching. Pay attention to what he emphasizes. Make sure to understand the HOMEWORKS, do PRACTICE EXAMS, and take advantage of the help they offer. Ochem is hard, but it's possible

Dr. Iverson is amazing and the best professor I've had. It is evident that he genuinely cares for his students. Overall, ochem was hard for me, but he presented the material in a fun and straightforward manner. He is receptive to student feedback, and there are many opportunities to get help. Also his TAs (especially Qifan) are the absolute best.
Hands down best professor EVER! Lectures were inspiring and Dr. Iverson truly provides you with everything you need and more to earn an A! Also, go to office hours!!

Iverson was born to teach. He makes ochem extremely approachable but also recognizes what a hard class it is. You MUST go to lectures and sometimes even rewatch them a few times. He gives so many resources to practice and has great TAs. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS! YOU CAN DO WELL IN OCHEM!! He is a great lecturer and his test averages are pretty high.

Dr. Iverson is THE Organic Chemistry prof. He is amazing, him and his TAs have office hours everyday of the week to ensure you understand the material. He records everything, all the time so you don't need to worry about missing anything. There are tons of practice he gives so there's no reason for you to be lost. 10/10 if you can get him, do it.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING !! His classes are always the first ones to fill up - and his amazing lectures explains that a lot. He truly cares about his students and makes ochem a breeze. He is promoted now so he doesn't teach ochem anymore, but if he comes back definitely try to sign up !

Amazing professor! Just make sure to study your mechanisms and read the book. Practice problems are essential!! Also, make sure you take and do well on as many practice exams as you can!! Have a great time. He is truly amazing and cares about you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I have ever had in my life. If you have the chance to take this class, take it immediately. He is kind and listens to his students and somehow packages Ochem into an interesting format (which is not any easy thing to do). Please take this course, he is amazing

All I have to say is that Iverson was the best professor I have ever had, and he is an OChem prof. His TAs are also amazing, and he gives so many opportunities to talk to him and learn. Please take him

He makes Ochem so fun and interesting to learn. He is also very very passionate about the subject so he will tell a lot of interesting stories or facts during class. He loves and cares about his students too!
Literally the best professor at UT!

Don't buy the textbook. Iverson is a great professor with fair, but difficult, tests. Do not get behind no matter what you do and take advantage of all of the resources available! The final is worth a lot and no matter what, he'll make you take a test at the exact day/time it's set for (maybe with a time extension) or use it as your drop.

Loved him. I took him during the corona semester of Fall 2020. OChem is tough, but he makes it doable. Don't need the textbook but it helps. Make sure to do old. practice tests as those resemble the real thing and look at the rules of the day resources. Do physical synthesis practice problems before Exam 3 and final. Rewatch lectures before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've ever had. He takes a personal interest in your success and he was also very accommodating with the pandemic. His lectures are absolutely incredible and always engaging. That said, it is ochem. You will have to work really hard for the grade you want, but Dr. Iverson does his best to help you out.
Best professor I've ever had. Makes learning fun. Class is hard but he makes it doable. Take if you can. 10/10

You are LUCKY if you have the chance to take him. I was so scared to take Ochem bc I'm an average student and I loved his class and he is hands down my fav prof. He is super accessible outside class despite corona. He goes above and beyond to help you learn and keep you interested in lecture. He also provides a ton helpful materials and practices.

By far the best professor at UT!! Dr. Iverson cares so much about his students and it really shows. OCHEM is hard no matter what but he does all that he can to make it as fun as possible. Daily quizzes, weekly HW, 3 midterms, and a final. He provides so many resources for his students and is honestly so funny and makes his lectures interesting.

Dr. Iverson is by far the most amazing professor I've had at UT period. Not to mention that Organic is already super difficult, Dr. Iverson makes it a class that is definitely doable while inspiring you to push yourself in other ways. He genuinely cares about his students and I can feel his support even through the Covid Pandemic. 10/10 professor

Simply put, I never thought I would like ochem as much as I did! Dr. Iverson is extremely kind, approachable, and encouraging. I've never had a professor work so hard for his students He always stayed late for all of his reviews to answer everyone's questions and understands most students are pre-med and accommodates to that! I love Brent :)

Fall 2018.3 curved midterms with a drop, one final, homework and quizzes which are weighted lower. Be prepared to read the textbook, practice the material off the notes packets, and do the homework if you want guaranteed success. At least 6-8 hours of work per week on this class. However, excellent Ochem foundation and Dr. Iverson is very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great professor! Such an honor to listen to Dr. Iverson. He is so smart and cares about the well-being of his students. He records all lectures no instapoll, but he makes going to class fun. Ochem is a hard subject that you have to work to understand, but Dr. Iverson makes the class interesting. Tests are difficult but not impossible.

Iverson is an incredible professor. He makes learning organic chemistry fun! I would try your hardest to get him. Graded primarily on tests the cover literally everything you were taught but you get one drop.

Everything people have written here about Dr. Iverson is true - he is the most inspirational, wholesome, funny, caring, and whatever positive adjective you want to insert professor you'll have. Organic chemistry isn't easy, but you'll learn a lot more than chemistry in his class. Register quick if you want him though, his class fills up fast!

The hype is 100% true! Iverson is the best professor I've ever had. Engaging lectures, clear explanations, and tons of resources (old tests, hws, and mechanism sheets). Don't think I would have loved/understood ochem nearly as much if it wasnt for him. Just wish he also taught ochem 2! (tip: dont buy the molecular model kit he recommends)

Prof Iverson was amazing. He did everything he could to help us do well in Ochem. There was a lot of resources that he gave, and a lot of office hours, problem solving sessions, and past exams posted for us to do. Iverson is amazing, but Ochem was hard in itself. A lot of work was put in this class to get an A, but it's definitely doable.

Believe the hype-- Dr. Iverson is an awesome professor! However, it is very important to note that while he is a stellar teacher, ochem is an inevitably difficult class. This class is conceptually hard to understand, and it does require a lot of work to do well. You learn so much that it makes up for it, though! Love this class!

Unpopular opinion: Iverson is overrated. He seems like a great person and genuinely cares about the students, but he overwhelms students with too many resources and things to do. It's excessive. Lots of deviations in lecture to irrelevant topics. Tests are long (3hours) and late at night. Overall, just an average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: best professor I have ever had at this school. he really cares about you understanding the material and gives you an abundance of resources on his website to pass the class. smartest man on this campus

He explains the concepts really well, has visuals for everything, and uploads every lecture online. The tests are difficult but this is ochem so idk what you expect. He does his best to help you tho! His website has tons of online resources - past exams, recorded lectures and office hours, etc. - and he drops the lowest exam score. 10/10 professor!

Iverson was a great professor! He genuinely cared about his students and his method of teaching really worked for me. Probably the best professor I've ever had at UT. Take him for ochem 1, if you can! I wish he taught ochem 2 the following semester
The best professor I have ever had. That is all I have to say.

MUST TAKE HIS CLASS! You'll not only acquire more than enough knowledge to tackle subsequent UT courses (& MCAT) but he also imbues his class w/ wholesome lessons in life. In brief, Dr. Iverson is a prof who enjoys pointing out how smoothly he segues from one topic to the next, providing his class with "time capsules," & advocating to run run run!

He was a really awesome OCH1 professor. Really cared about the material as well as the general well being of his students. The course was challenging, but you really will learn in his classroom. Thanks Dr. Iverson

Whenever someone asked me who I had for organic chemistry and I said Iverson, they gasped like I'd said I had a literal angel. Iverson is the greatest and you're super lucky if you manage to get ochem with him. Go to office hours! They're so helpful! Pretty much everything on his website is, it's a goldmine. He records every lecture as well

All the comments are right. Man's a legend. Teaches from handwritten notes. Short quizzes every class based on textbook readings. Homework is really helpful. A great professor, but ochem is tricky naturally.

Iverson is AMAZING. People always look forward to his lectures- he knows how to explain the same topic in a million different ways so every kind of student will understand. He works tirelessly to make sure every student has the opportunity to do extremely well in his class, and the head TA (Chris) is great too. You will love this class!!!!

If you are between Iverson and Shabbir, but Shabbir fits better in your schedule, then change your entire schedule, switch your major if you have to so that you can fit this man's class in your schedule. People always talk about how great Iverson is, AND IT IS TRUE! This man is truly extraterrestrial.

Believe all the hype that has already been posted here. If you see Iversons name pop up on the registration site and youre due to take organic chemistry, then you need to move your schedule around in order to take his class. After two semesters of inorganic hell, Dr. Iversons teaching got me to fall in love with chemistry all over again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is without a doubt the best professor that I have had here at UT. He is funny and will bring in speakers. He is a huge believer in running and will give extra credit if the class does a fun run. records and posts all his lectures online. Its still Ochem so be prepared to work but with Dr. I you'll be ok. Truly an amazing professor
Great lecturer, really cares about his students. You will come out of this class really understanding the material. He provides with tons of resources in order to succeed in his class

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He records his lectures, but I highly recommend going to class because the vibes he gives off are great and he's an amazing lecturer. He has old exams posted which help a lot when it comes to studying for exams. His tests are a challenge, but definitely doable. He is the best ochem professor.

If you are going to take organic chemistry, you HAVE to take it with Dr. Iverson. He's such an inspirational lecturer who will go the extra mile to make sure you understand all the concepts that he teaches. His lectures are entertaining and kept me engaged throughout the course. He makes you work for the grade, but it is all worth it in the end.

O-chem is not an easy subject to make enjoyable and he did it. BEST professor ever! So funny and so knowledgeable! 3 exams and 1 gets dropped + final exam. He also gives homework packets that are optional, but they are extra credit on the exams if you complete them, so I would do them! He also has SO many opportunities for help outside class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Iverson is one of the best professors i've ever had. He cares soooo much. you can really tell that he wants you to do well in his class. has office hours almost everyday. subject material is very difficult but that's to be expected. overall, i love this man and if you have the chance to take him, it'd be a huge mistake not to!!!!!

Best professor ever, by far. He makes the subject as interesting as he possibly can and office hours are available basically everyday with live online office hours. Everything is recorded in case you had trouble understanding something. Take him. I wish he could've taken him for first semester of organic.

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! Dr. Iverson is such an amazing person, his lectures are always entertaining and he is genuinely passionate about his job. Ochem is a really hard subject but he makes sure you really learn it. I absolutely loved him. He created his own website with lots of helpful resources! I definitely recommend him! He's the best!!

Iverson truly loves teaching and his job, and it definitely shows in the way he runs his class. There are 3 exams, and 1 is dropped, plus a final. The homework counts as EC, so do them! Go to class if you can, it really helps. Also study with friends, it'll make life a lot easier. Use old finals he gives you to study and you'll do great!

He is the first professor I've met who loves his job. 3 exams (1 dropped) and a final. The homework are extra credit so do them!!! Look over the rules of the day (T/F & fill in the blank come from those). Go to the Problem Solving sessions. And study with friends! For the final & (exams), study the past finals & (exams) & corresponding hws.

I actually didn't finish his class. I had to drop it due to non-academic health reasons, but HE was the professor that made me love science, especially biochemistry, all over again. I'm going to do the research I want to do now because he's inspired me so much, but in the end his class wasn't required anymore. Take him. You won't regret it. GOAT.

Dr. Iverson is the BEST professor I've ever had. I absolutely loved going to lectures and I he made me like organic chemistry even though I sucked at it. He's great and if you just keep trying you will understand it if you just keep doing what he tells you.  It took me a long time to understand the material but his class is so worth it.  TAKE IT.

If you have the opportunity to take Dr. Iverson's class, do it. Don't even question it. Just take his class, you'll learn so much & have a great time. He genuinely cares about you and gives you all the resources you need to be successful at Ochem.

I don't have enough space on here to say all the amazing things this professor is, but this is definitely going to be the class I miss once I graduate. I didn't just laugh all the time in his class, but I definitely learned more than I ever expected to learn in an organic chemistry class. Bless UT for this amazing person.

Dr. Iverson is hands down my favorite professor so far! His lectures are so interesting and his exams are very representative of the homework he assigns. He gives 3 exams (the lowest of the 3 exams is dropped) and a final. He gave me a newfound appreciation for O Chem!! Seriously, take him!!! He is as great as everyone says he is!!!

Dr. Iverson is absolutely phenomenal. Take his class!! Ochem 2 can be hard at times but he makes so much effort to break and down and easy to understand. He literally gives you so many resources to succeed. On top of that, he genuinely cares about each and every one of his students and tries super hard to make lectures entertaining! Love him!

Dr. Iverson is hands down one of my favorite professors I've had so far. He cares a lot about his students and provides so many opportunities for you to get help to understand the material. I went to all of his office hours and thought they were very helpful. His lectures are funny, and his homework is very similar to how tests are formatted.

I liked having Iverson for ochem 2. His lectures are always clear and entertaining. You won't even have to crack open the book if you pay attention in class. However, he does seem to spend a significant amount of time discussing topics unrelated to ochem, and at a certain point in the semester I found myself thinking "really, more fish??"
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Respected by students--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Iverson was great but everyone overrates him. He provides countless resources to succeed and do well in the class, however theres so much that at times it makes the material more confusing. His lectures are amazing, but at times a waste of time and annoying. His test seemed harder then all the previous practice exams he posted. Overall great!

He is too hyped up. Many undergrads will defend his teaching style because it is relatively easy to reproduce answers on a test rather than actually understand the organic chemistry that is going on. He is great for premeds that are looking for an relatively easy A in orgo2. lots of supplemental help as well. Overall, nothing special.

Unpopular opinion: Iverson is overrated.  He talks about running, fish, and plays his trumpet.  Everything is always a "time capsule." He has dad humor and is the definition of doing the most. But, he's not a bad teacher, is super passionate about organic chemistry, and provides you with excessive amount of supplemental help.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He truly wants you to do well in his class. Ochem 2 is not an easy class, but he made it my favorite. If you go over class notes and his old exams that he posts, you will do fine on the tests. Love him!
Great teacher. Would take his class again.

Dr. Iverson is the best! He taught organic chemistry very well and he is able to make it doable and deliver it well! He's very clear, provides excellent foundations and fundamental basics for you so that you can combat complex problems. Provide old tests that you can practice and encourage you to ask questions and participate. Lectures clear + good

If you have to take Ochem, take this professor. I  have never been more satisfied with a class. Iverson's interest in his students is unmatched by any professor I have taken thus far. That is not say this class was an easy A. He uploads practice tests from 2006 and on which helped tremendously. I went from a C+ first semester to an A. Take Iverson!

Dr. Iverson made ochem II very interesting. The rumors are true, he is one of the best professors on all of campus. I didn't do so great in ochem I but I participated way more and "caught the wave." (You'll know what that means). He posts his old exams, which are great practice. Going over notes and going to problem solving help a lot!
Dr. Iverson, if you read this. You made me love a class I once used to hate. I was having anxiety over Ochem, but you changed that. Thank you for being there for your students, thank you for caring.

It isn't often you come across an individual, let alone a professor, as genuine and inspirational as Dr. Iverson. He's the image of what every educator should strive for. Only downside to taking his class is that he'll set a the bar high for what a professor should be, and you'll be disappointed with just about any other professor down the road.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor you will ever take. This class is hard, but he will make you love organic chemistry. Hands down the most amazing man you will ever meet. I will really miss this class.
The best professor I have ever had. One of the nicest people you will ever meet!
The most AMAZING Professor I have ever gotten.  He's so great that I don't think i'll ever meet another professor or anyone else like him again.

He turned a difficult course into my favorite class of the semester. He is very patience and approachable. He'll do whatever it takes to get a student to understand the material. He makes his lectures clear and concise. Go to class and do the his hw and ochem will be easy.

By far THE best professor I've ever had. He really knows the material and teaches extremely well. Very clear on all the assignments. DO THE WEEKLY HOMEWORKS AND THE BOOK PROBLEMS! This will almost guarantee you a high grade!
Had him for CH310M and N. By far, without a doubt, THE best instructor I have ever had in my life. There's a reason the entire university knows his name.

Dr. Iverson makes the class entertaining and material relevant. He provides past tests, which are great practice. Organic chemistry can be challenging, but if you keep up with the material and practice a lot, you'll do well.

GREAT PROF!!! He rele knows how to teach and he gives u all the tools u need to do well in his class. He presents the material rele well and really cares that his students understand it. He knows that ochem is hard and tries to make it as simple as possible. I took 310M n am taking 310N w/ him and both have been my favorite classes each semester!

Iverson is a god! I've always hated Chemistry but he makes it interesting. He's fun and keeps you engaged. There's no way you can fall asleep. Plus he tells us stories & sings for us. And he's very inspiring. Tests are straight forward. Go to class, keep up with your work, and getting an A in the class won't be hard. SOOO glad I took him!!
He is so amazing take him if possible. O Chem is hard but he makes it fun!
Amazing! O Chem is awesome because of Dr. Iverson. I actually look forward to my MWF classes because of this class!
Best Teacher ever!!!

If you have the chance to take Organic Chemistry with Dr. Iverson, take it!! He really makes it easy, believe it or not, to understand. The exams are fair and his class is just plain interesting. He takes this class above and beyond any learning experience you have ever had!
He sings for us on the last class day!

Iverson is an absolutely amazing professor. You have to take his class if you get the chance. Ochem is difficult, but the homeworks and TA recitation sessions really help clarify the material. Tests are very fair, and if you've done the homeworks and put forth some effort, you'll do great!
iverson is easily the best teacher i've ever had.  i came away actually enjoying the subject.
BRENT IVERSON IS A BEAUTIFUL MAN!!!  ORGANIC CHEMISTRY IS NOTHING WITHOUT BRENT IVERSON!!!
he'll actually teach you organic chemistry, he made me love it!!! and the underwater slides he shows you are awesome...
He's maybe one of the best teachers at UT- Austin.  Makes Orgo understandable.
The class is very small (20 ish people) and there is readings every week. You do have random pop quizes but you have the opportunity to make up points if you miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Like other comments, he does care about attendance, which he manages by having pop quizzez but does offer enough pop quizzes over the semester to receive full credit if you miss any. He is honestly a very nice teacher and cares about what he is teaching. Overall, a really nice teacher who cares about literacy and tries his best to show it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was okay but if you're not into film at all it might be a lot to take his class... def not just an easy english class I would just take the big one. You have to show up to every class because there are pop quizzes over the readings that are sometimes NOT fair. But you have a grade negotiation at the end which is nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hard homeworks with no feedback
