Iyer is the worst professor I ever had in my four years here!!!!!!!! His homework's are extremely long, he does not explain anything or give good feedback to do better on other assignments.

Gives vague instructions and grades far too harshly for such little guidance. Even when you reach out for help/clarification, he either tells you to figure it out on your own or talks to you like you should already know the answer. He spends far too much time talking about things we already know and not enough on things actually affecting grades

Dr.Iyer gives extremely hard homework that is barely covered in lecture, he spends 75 minutes talking about pure nonsense, that is due in 3 days after he opens it. Whole class asked for ,ore time and he wouldn't give it. He doesn't answer questions and his questions on the homework's don't make sense half the time. Take any other professor! RIH

Dr. Iyer is a great choice if you're needing to take genetics. You can tell that he actually cares about his students and is knowledgeable about the content he's teaching. On most days during lecture there was a QOTD which you turn in, an instapoll, and random zoom polls which counted only towards participation. Relatively easy to do for credit.
absolutely goated
She's the best; she helped me survive waves. Would 100% take again.
Great Professor, Finally understand Maxwell's equations, and found the last digit of Pi!
Neat prof
Great person with very energetic personality and very intelligent!
Dr. Zhang is an amazing professor and really cares about students and wants everyone to succeed

Dr. Molineux has been my favorite professor at UT!! The class is really intimidating at first (graded only on FRQ exams, a presentation, and some in-class participation points) but prof is super sweet and knowledgeable. Lectures are very dense with important details, so utilize his office hours+textbook as much as you can! Logic > pure memorization

He is a sweet guy but is so educated that I fear there is a gap of knowledge that he has a hard time bridging with his undergraduate students. His tests are some of the hardest I have ever taken, but he curves a lot. Pretty inaccessible and not very technologically savvy. His lectures were very boring and he talks so quiet its hard to hear him.

Dr. Molineux is so kind. However, his tests were very difficult (all FR). I was able to be successful on exams by re-watching his lectures/taking detailed notes/understanding the logic behind the points he was making. Write everything you know during exams. He also grades participation and he will remember whether/how many times you've spoken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Molineux is a nice guy in person and he really just wants his students to get something out of the class. That being said, his lectures are sometimes hard to follow and at times the class feels like a survey course. His exam setup is really nice as it allows for you to drop questions you have no hope of answering. Grades are curved immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nicest man ever but mumbles often in lecture so sit close or rewatch lectures. He expects very specific answers on tests but will curve at the end of the semester. This is a very challenging class and while most don't, I found textbook very helpful in clarifying details he expects us to already know. Study at least a week in advance for tests

Dr. Molineux is nice, but he tends to mumble during lecture so unless you sit towards the front you can't really hear him. His tests are all free response, but you get to pick which 8/10 you answer. However, he wants very specific answers, so the class average on the tests was always low (but he curves the whole class at the end so you're fine).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Review below sums it up, but note: *Would highly recommend studying at least 5-7 days in advance to be successful. *Know the power-points cold, he can ask you over any slide. Memorization and reproduction of key ideas and concepts in power-points slides is the best way to study for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His tests were difficult, but he curves at the end of the semester so everyone ended up doing fine. The class is graded just be 3 in class exams, all free response. For us they consisted of 10 questions and you had to pick 8 to answer. Overall I don't think the class is bad at all.
the goat. please never stop lecturing... *takes socks off*
irving dai is the goat

Super nice professor but not the best at explaining. If you took BC Calc in high school and did well, class will be sooo easy. Does not fully explain concepts in class and will have to learn at TA sessions. Exams are exactly like weekly quizzes and he allows a notecard to write anything for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. Often times proves all concepts in his lectures, which can be irritating for students with AP credit who couldn't get out of the course. Gives plenty of in-class examples. Textbook not mandatory. Quizzes & HW are harder than tests, but final was harder than all midterms.

Dr. Dai explained things really clearly, mainly from a mathematical proof perspective, which I liked but may not be the best for others. He allowed us to use a notecard on all tests, which was really nice, and the quizzes are fine as long as you look at the practice quiz. My only complaint is that he sometimes explains too quickly.

Nice professor w/ clear grading criteria and material! Lectures not recorded, but references heavily from textbook. HW is very time consuming but quizzes + tests way easier. Tests are 75% of grade but just redo quizzes/do practice midterm q's and you'll be fine.

Overall great professor. His explanations can be a bit hard to follow through at times but he makes a good job at trying to help you understand. The homeworks are a bit hard at times but they prepare you for the quizzes and exams.

Dai was overall a caring and intelligent professor. The exams are structured based on the quizzes, although it was a little harder. No practice exams only reviews that are harder than the exam. 2 midterms and 1 final. TA was goated tho, shoutout to Nathan. Just be a little "clever" and you can do well in this class.

He overcomplicates a lot of things and goes into irrelevant detail about it. Obviously good if you love calculus but for the sake of doing good on exams and quizzes it's just easier to learn the steps to do it through youtube and homeworks as opposed to trying to understand the minuscule details about how something relates to something not covered.

Very good professor! Gave extra credit, uploaded his notes online, and explained most concepts in detail. The tests are 75% of the grade but the questions he gives are pretty easy and also allows a notecard for each test.
Genius of a guy, could answer any question you'd have, and he explained stuff intuitively. Tests were fair and predictable. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Homework is significantly more difficult than the weekly quizzes and tests, but as long as you studied for them you'll be fine. Can get up to an extra .25 added to your grade from extra credit at the start of the semester. Professor Dai is really nice and patient, and he seems really passionate about math.

By far my favorite professor at this school. His lectures are quite interesting, and they cover what you need to know for the homeworks/exams. He teaches based on the textbook, so you can always refer to that if you are confused. He wants his students to succeed, and he seems like a very genuine guy.

Pretty cool material, and his lectures are good. Homework and exams are very reasonable. He posts lectures notes for all lectures which are very descriptive. Take care to not miss too many classes, its kinda hard to catch up. Complex projective plane my beloved.

Awesome professor. He really knows his material, and he seems very passionate about it as well. He explains concepts in a very intuitive manner, so his lectures can actually be quite interesting! On top of that, he is extremely nice, and he does truly care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework heavy, but very resourceful and helpful when help is needed. Clearly goes over what will be on exam and lectures are interesting and fun!

He is clearly knowledgeable and manages to make his lectures really fun to listen to. His weekly homework can be quite time-consuming, but is graded lightly. The material is not particularly difficult but requires practice. His exams are comparable to the homework and not anything crazy. A very pleasant experience, especially for mathematics!

The lectures themselves sometimes felt kinda useless. Most of my learning was from the textbook as Professor Irving does take his lecture and homework problems from it. His grading is pretty easy when it comes to homework and his tests are pretty simple as long as you studied for it.
Amazing and funny lecturer! Genuinely cares about his students understanding the material and clarifies important concepts from the textbook.
why did i take this class? first time a teacher has made me cry.
It's hilarious this guy is still allowed to teach. Avoid at all costs. Even his graduate students are afraid of him
do not take his course under any circumstances. awful human in a position of power.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: cruel professor with an appetite for public humiliation of his students and TAs-

Wow, well I should really have listened to all the warnings and rumors. He is an awful professor, rude and a gotcha artist. He has made several cry. He clearly loves flexing on his students - he clearly knows a lot, but just doesn't teach it and he gives the feeling that he is too good to teach. way too much work for so little pay off.

Prof talks at you rather than teaches, and uses complex terminology; hard to follow. Presentations are huge component of grade. Often made discouraging remarks or rudely corrected students during presentations. Literally did not know my grade until he submitted it to the registrar; did not know if i'd have C or A the whole sem. Curve saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Finkelstein is a really smart guy, no doubt about that. He knows what he's talking about. Except, he does not teach the material. Rather, he just says it. Lots of primary article presentations are more like stresses rather than learning points. Try to take someone else, especially if a pre-med who cares for their grade

Though I did learn a lot, there is too much work for too little reward in this class. I had to work harder in this class than any other class I took at UT. Quizzes were difficult and had class avgs of about 60. There was a lack of transparency about final grade cutoffs. He told us an 85-87 would likely be an A, but I got an 89 and received an A-.

I greatly learned a lot from Dr. Finkelstein's course, he is very knowledgeable in the course subject and shows that he really wants us to learn the material. You do have to put in the work for the course and have make sure to read your articles and go beyond to make sure you fully know your machine. He is a very caring and wishes our success.

He was very accommodating and nice throughout all the trouble we faced during this semester: pandemic, winter storm, other personal situations, etc. The majority of your grade comes from group presentations where you work with your group to explain an article. He does post grades very late, but he's an overall good guy and an excellent lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A difficult class for sure. The quizzes are pretty detailed but the majority of the grade was based on group presentations of research articles. As long as you put in the work and thoroughly understand what you are presenting, you'll be fine. Asks hard questions so be prepared. Nice guy, seemed to care about the topics he was teaching about
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: His course was crazy hard, and a large majority of the grade is on our article presentations. But I learned so much from this class and he was so accommodating and knowledgable! Be prepared to stay on top of things but if you do, you'll do fine!! He did grade everything really late though which sucked, but he gave lots of EC and curved:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Be ready to ready to read the article assigned to you. He will be able to tell if you didn't and give you hard questions so its on you. He did grade late but plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think I am doing well but I have no way of knowing because he hasn't graded a single thing that wasn't auto-graded for him by canvas (the quizzes). We just turned in our final presentation and the very first one in the first month of the semester hasn't been graded. Too lazy to even come up with quiz questions makes you write them. Doesn't care!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst prof at UT. Grades mostly based on quizes and presentations with tough Q&As where he would thrive off of roasting you. He seemed very uninterested in the class until he had the chance to rip you to shreds with questions. That's the only thing he seemed to enjoy. The quizzes were fine and based on lectures. Try taking another prof, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell his research is more important to him than teaching. The class is poorly organized and he gives you little time to do projects. You don't know any of your grades until the last day of class. He makes you feel stupid even though you're in undergrad and he has a literal PhD. Doesn't respond to emails either :)

Avoid this man. You have group projects where you focus on a research article he assigns you. The project itself is not too bad but he does not care about you or your well being. Publicly insulted my groups project and was very rude. You can tell during lecture that he does not care to teach he is a researcher before a professor and it's obvious

The worst Biochem class & professor I've ever taken. Smart guy, but terrible at teaching. Hardly anything from the lectures or office hours are actually on the exams. You study so much material to get tested on none of it. Test averages were in the 60s, yet he barely curves; a 66 to 69 is a C. What a joke. Oh, & he's not caring at all whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super unhelpful and very condescending. I would take any other professor but him. Before the 3rd exam, half of the entire class q dropped because everyone was failing. Only 8 questions on the exam and no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Everything (including some exams) is collaborative, essays are not bad, and the content is very manageable. If you can look at definitions/theorems and apply them, you can do the proofs in this class. He's a nice guy but particular about notation and formalities. Be respectful and you'll be fine. Probably the easiest class in the department.

Exams are just like the homework's given! Learn the process on the questions and you'll do fine on the exams. He has these silly jokes once in a while that really made this otherwise mundane class enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: office hours were really helpful, exams were based on hw problems, overall course was well-organized

Lectures are useless, but TA sections are GREAT. I didn't go to any lectures beyond the first week of class.

Prof gives a study guide before every exam, and the problems on the exam will typically be drawn straight from the study guide.

GOAT! Tests are identical to assigned study problems (or similar methods to solve). 6 quizzes, 2 dropped. GO TO DISCUSSION!! HELPS A LOT FOR PREPARING FOR TESTS AND QUIZZES. No graded homework, but they were useful as practice for exams. 

I personally didn't think he was the best lecturer, but he makes the class easy if you put in a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he's actually the goat
Tells you exactly what problems will be on the exam before you take it, and him and his TA grade super leniently on tests and quizzes. Two drops on the quizzes as well.

Gives you almost, if not the exact questions that will be on the midterm. Midterms are five questions and he gives you 12 to study, which is extremely manageable. TA was fantastic and explained solutions very clearly. Lecture is a little theory heavy, but solutions to every homework are posted in a timely manner. Take him if you want an A.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER NO LIKE GENUINELY!!! he literally tells you what you need to study for the midterm. He gives out 12 questions to study for the midterms and pick 5 of them. The TA is Awesome as well. Goes over content slowly and answers all the questions.

class is not an easy A but it is obtainable if you do not make mistakes, miss readings, homework, or presentations. You will have to teach yourself a lot .You will have to treat this class as a regular required class so be wary with how many other classes you are taking. He does offer extra credit opportunities and you will learn a lot in the end.

He is a nice guy, but a terrible professor. He doesn't actually teach anything in the class and instead you have to rely on other people and the dense textbook. The homeworks are basically free 100s and the tests are easy, so it's not hard to get a good grade, but the class itself is boring and you don't learn much

Very good alternative if you don't get Professor Meth. Tests are taken straight from the homework, and two quizzes are dropped. If you get over a 90 on all three midterms you get to skip the final. Lectures may be boring at times, but he does his best to be accessible outside of lecture times. Very helpful if you attend office hours.

A lot of textbook readings, but super easy exams and quizzes. Homework is optional, and he takes the exam word for word from HW problems. Lectures were fine and TA was good. If you have a brain you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: my GOAT. exams were straight from the hwk, and he posts keys for each hwk so you always know which ones you did correctly/incorrectly. quizzes were a pain but that's dependent on the TA and not necessarily him. you do get 2 drop quizzes though and as long as u show up to discussion at least once before the quiz u should be fine
LOVED HIS CLASS! he was super nice and tests were super similar to homework, which don't have due dates and purely for learning and practice. he's great!
Quizzes are a bit difficult but exams are VERY similiar to HW and quizzes. Lectures don't really make sense but just review HWs to prepare for quizzes and you should be fine.
Classes are proof heavy but it's manageable, and the grading is forgiving. You will learn a lot, and the concepts are interesting if you enjoy math!

Very chill class that reshapes how you think of geometry. Sometimes lectures would be pretty insightful, but most of the time we would prove homework problems as groups and present them to the class. I thought the problems were pretty fun, and the latter content was also pretty interesting. Easy exams.

Exams are either directly from the HWs or very similar with a few numbers switched around. Super friendly and approachable professor and really cares for his students. Quizzes are a bit difficult, but exams are pretty easy. Lectures didn't really make sense (in my opinion) but the textbook is a bit helpful if you are needing to review topics.

The tests aren't bad at all. He teaches pretty clearly. If you aren't comfortable with proofs, you'll get a lot of experience. The class is a flipped classroom, which allows you to work with your classmates on proofs if you get stuck. He relies on the textbook a lot and can be dry sometimes. Don't expect him to lecture much.
Really really hard to NOT get an A. Just don't accidentally miss the learning modules and absurdly long homework assignments.

Even if you're bad at math, his Calc class is an easy A. Very thorough with his explanation of course material, and each exam (including the final) is heavily curved in addition to them already being very easy. Was easy to get help outside of class, as he holds office hours/homework help almost every day either online or in-person. Take Dr. Osborn!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you don't want to spent time learning the content outside of class, don't take this class! It's a flipped-classrooms style. But, the tests are relatively easy since they are very similar to the review. Homeworks are very hard but he does review sessions. Didn't learn a lot in this class, but that difficult to get an A.
he's just the goat. tests are very easy and curved insanely generously. the homework is harder but he will do a monday zoom session and go on as long as until there are no more questions

Ozzy is the underrated goat of 408D. The homework and quizzes and are a little challenging but he has very helpful office hours and posts them afterwards. He has test review the lecture before class that is pretty much the test and you only need an 8/10 to get a 100, so overall a very reasonable class and course structure. Would HIGHLY recommend.

Everything is taught through quest video lectures. This class is easy to get a good grade in but I didn't learn the content very well. The tests are easy because they are just like the reviews and you only need 8/10 to get a 100. There are weekly hws. Dr. Osborn can be pretty funny and unintentionally roasts people.

Dr. Osborn does a great job at making this class manageable. HW problems are done in class in groups, and he encourages us to share your work with your peers. Grades hindered on HW, an essay, and in-class presentations (you need to do 2). He's also pretty funny! The only downside is he's kind of a slow grader, and the textbook is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: class is fast paced, but osborn is excellent at explaining and breaking down a problem. be afraid to ask a question if you havent been paying full attention/talking during class bc he will roast tf out of you. i had a 5 in ap calc AB and did pretty well in class. tests and all assignments are very easy if you pay attention in class or ask for help.

flip style class, learning modules at home, questions answered in lectures. HWs can be challenging, but office hours are super helpful. quizzes done on your own time, difficult but discussion sections will help immensely. exams Quest based, but also have a review day, which will prepare you well. had not taken BC in hs, but found the class easy.

Dr. Osborn is very reasonable with his assignments and tests. The Homework and QR will be more difficult but Dr. Osborn and the TA are accommodating. He holds online Zoom meetings and in-person hours to help all of his students.

John Osborn is the best professor of all time, do not be worried about his class too much, if you want to learn Calculus he will provide you with all the resources but his tests are also very reasonable.

Took him for M408C and M408D with the knowledge from AP Calc BC. This class is easy if you've already taken calculus. Classroom style is flipped so most of the learning will be outside of class. He is passive sometimes but he's an introvert. Would def recommend!

This class was a breeze as I took AP Calc B before M408D. Dr. Osborn's runs a flipped classroom and is extremely patient when resolving doubts during lecture. He has an extremely generous grading policy, with exams in MCQ format with 80% correctness required for a 'curved' 100, and 2-4 drops for the QRs, HWs etc. Would def recommend for an easy A.

Learned everything through Quest modules which was a lot of work and took hours to complete. ~3 modules, 1 HW, 1 QR per week. 3 tests (10 mcq) and the final (20 mcq) were straight from Quest and you only need to score 80% raw to make a 100. Gives a formula chart (except for test 1). Love my TA. Ended with a 100 and never went to class.

John Michael Osborn. He tells you he's an introvert but he's funny and a good choice if you want a simple calc 2. You aren't going to be directly taught by him, because Quest is very integrated in this course. Quizzes and tests were straightforward and he grades very forgivingly. Class isn't mandatory but helpful for reviewing tough questions.
You don't actually learn anything in class, it's all self taught. However the exams are easy and he helps review all the tough concepts before them.

Another one of UT's amazing math professors, cannot recommend him more for Discrete! Was very caring about student's personal needs, very accessible in office hours and zoom, good lecturer, and great teaching style similar to a flipped classroom in which students read and prepare solutions to select problems at home to be presented in class.

You were expected to doing a learning module for each topic before class. Then you would go to class and do incredibly easy problems with him. Homeworks and QRs were once a week, but they were unnecessarily hard. Midterms were just like the study guide but with different numbers. Final was really really hard. Would not recommend.

I stopped going to lectures after the first exam and my grades magically went up. Discussions are useless with super hard and super useless QR assignments. Osborn talks really softly so you have to sit near the front if you want to hear. LMs were helpful and lectures were not. Can teach this class to yourself better. Don't recommend this guy.

Although this was a flipped classroom (pre-lecture learning modules with all the content), Dr. Osborn is an amazing lecturer and thoroughly helps explain content, even if you didn't comprehend it before. He provides reviews which are almost identical to the exams and his grading is very forgiving. Discussions are useful, pending you have a good TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Osborn gives plenty of practice problems during lectures and explains in detail. His grading system is tedious but he gives reviews that are similar to the exam/replaces the lowest exam with the final. His homework sessions are very useful and he is overall caring for his students. I didn't take BC so it took some effort but was worth it 100%!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Is an average calc professor, his lectures are just reading off slides. Do his HW to practice for his midterms (which are all multiple choice and lil difficult without previous calc knowledge) go to office hours and that's where his caring side shines. Also he doesnt do well in big classrooms and will email you at 3am sometimes. Call him Ozzy.

His attitude can get derailed sometimes in terms of patience. However, he is caring/understanding to those who show effort. Osborn does lecture relatively quiet, so the room has to be quiet. 8 MCQ Exams only downside. Gives IDENTICAL practice problems w/ answers prior to exams though. Lecture and discussions not required to succeed but helpful.

Can be abrasive at times but it is obvious he truly wants his students to learn. The homeworks were challenging, but they were good preparation for the (easier) exams. Fair grading scale and vey structured class which I appreciated. Difficult class but he is willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very structured class: if you go to class and study you will get an A. He gives you all the materials you need to succeed and is rather passionate in seeing you succeed. However, the class is decently hard so you do have to work succeed, but the path is very clear. Nice guy too

He is a great professor when it comes to explaining concepts to you. He makes it super easy to understand and truly wants students to learn the material. The class is straightforward, and you will get an A if you look over the test review and do the homework.

He makes an effort to help people understand the homework with homework help zooms. The exam format is very stressful with minimal questions and no partial credit. He can also be very condescending. You will learn the material by watching around a 5-minute video in Quest and he will do a few practice questions during the actual class.

Provided test reviews that reflected the test concepts exactly. Although I wouldn't say he was the best lecturer, he tries extremely hard to provide resources for his students. He had this zoom hw help session that almost reached 3 hrs multiple times. Graded on hw, tests, and LMs. Really easy to make an A if you utilize the stuff he gives out.

Dr Osborn was great. He cares about out learnings and explains questions throughly.
The midterms are based on homework and learning module questions.
Final exam are also based on the extraction of questions from midterms.
The homework and learning modules are done by quest, thus they are multiple choices rather than free response questions.

I wasn't a fan of the exam structure since there were only 8 questions per exam. However, the questions were just like the learning modules and hw + Dr. Osborn was very clear with what material to review. He also had hw help sessions that would last nearly 3 hours which shoes how far he will go to help a student. Overall, very caring professor.

He is a knowledgeable professor, yet sometimes aggressive. Since I had a strong background, participating in his class was easy A for me, yet I was observing other students having difficulties. Downsides of him was that he is sometimes aggressive on Canvas, and a bit introvert, meaning that you have to push yourself towards him to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very good professor. Just do your homework and do REVIEW TESTS!!! and you should get an A.

Dr. Osborn cares about students, especially if you ask for help. But he sent a few passive aggressive canvas messages and lectured us for doing badly on an exam once. I would NOT take M333L if you haven't taken discrete math or another proofs class yet! There's not a lot of instruction on just how to do a proof and he expects you to read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Osborn doesn't really teach, true. This is a college class- he isn't supposed to hold your hand. He assigned us readings and we reviewed them in class. The homeworks and tests were completely fair..He was always available outside of class. Those who give a bad rating just didn't come to his office hours nor bother talking to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Never took calc in HS. I was nervous when I got to this class. But Dr. Osborn knows his stuff. He dedicates hours of time HW help sessions that are super helpful. You need to take advantage of every resource and be diligent to succeed. He can come off as condescending and seems to get irritated easily, but I think he's genuinely nice, just awkward.

Professor almost always seemed confused or unsure about his own lecture, seemed like he was often re-teaching him self along the way. Going into lecture he expected you to have mastered the topic already and work through problems "harder than would ever be on a test" which led to much confusion on the topic because of the difficulty of the problem.

Please take him, he is really sweet, and cares about his students. If you need help he will help you!! If you have personal things going on he is understanding and wants to help. He tries to simplify things and never makes you feel stupid for asking questions. Flexible class, if you go and or watch the lecture you will do well!

This is your calculus guy, especially if you're a business major with no intention of a math career. Took him for this course and calc 2. Teaches in a way that makes complex ideas way easier to understand.

He is so nice. Really cares for his students to succeed. I personally loathe Calculus, but he made it a lot easier to understand. Had him during COVID and he really supported us well even with the online format.
the class is so easy, and the professor teaches very well.

Dr. Osborn is very nice and very considerate. However, he lectures very quietly and the homework are exponentially harder than the ones taught in the learning modules. The way he explains the concepts are also unintuitive. However, I think the main problem with the class is because it is a flipped class and all lecturing is done through videos.
Very sweet prof, has many opportunities outside of class to receive help. Genuinely seems like he wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: LOVE HIM! sweetest. man alive. I loved his class even though I'm not a math p person at all. highly recommend him!

Teaching a calculus class to business majors who dont wanna learn is hard, and I fully recognize that! Dr. Osborn IS better than other professors in the department because hes on the students side. He even helps us with homework (which he is only allowed to do a little bit). It seems like he could be doing a better job, but Im grateful for my C+!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very kind prof. The class is a flipped classroom. Most learning is via learning modules online (which seem low quality y-tube vids). It is not his fault that the course is structured the way it is. (there's a course coordinator) He does have many OHs . He cares as long as u make an effort. However, he can be a bit hard to understand.

Prof. Osborn has been the most understanding and kind Professor I've had this year. As an athlete, I have had to reschedule exams and such and he has been without a doubt the most understanding of my circumstances. He is clear and thorough and encourages students in his lectures to ask questions (so please ask questions!).

Okay I will be the odd person out to say that this is the best math teacher I've ever had, If you're someone who isn't great at math and needs guidance, osborn is really helpful. He's never come across condescending in my opinion, I think email tends to hide emotion too. Class is based off modules, so if you're taking good notes you should pass.

The majority of class time is spent awkwardly attempting to solve problems in break out groups (where no one talks most of the time). It is frustrating because he then solves the problems afterwards, but we have already spent most of our time being confused rather than starting with the proofs and a foundational understanding.

He would email and send announcements late in the evenings and over holiday breaks stating corrections for concepts he had never explained to us. We would come to class and he would not teach us anything - when asked for clarification he would not provide it because he did not know the content himself. Impolite and has a weird superiority complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very nice prof, but I feel like class could have been organized better. Class time consisted of putting us in breakout rooms to discuss handouts/homework/material from textbook by ourselves, so the class didn't have a lot of guidance. Gave us plenty of time on exams in order to reduce stress. Sometimes, criteria for proofs didn't seem very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Seemed to mean well at first but went on to send very rude, discouraging, and intimidating emails concerning our intelligence and integrity. Never lectured and sent us to 50 minute breakout rooms to make sense of material never presented to us. Proof classes are not a prereq so a majority of the class had no idea what was going on with no help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of homework because the entirety of the content is homework. You get sent to breakout rooms daily to decipher the textbook and work on homework together, but he does not know the content nor does he teach it. He also uses passive aggression and intimidation tactics against students, and his email content and schedule is wildly unprofessional

This is Dr. Osborn's first-semester "teaching". He doesn't have clear grading criteria and students are always confused. Moreover, he does not teach in class and expects you to discuss homework with your classmates in breakout rooms, for a PROOFS course. Furthermore, he uses intimidation tactics on students in his rude, passive-aggressive emails. F
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Osborn gives discussion based lectures where he doesnt actually teach anything and he doesnt set his expectations for writing proper proofs, which should be expected from an intro to proofs course, and the worst thing is that he has been frequently rude to his students in emails, which is highly unprofessional and has stressed out students.

Professor never taught, it pretty much felt self taught. He gives a synopsis of todays topic then just send us to breakout rooms. When we asked for help he never had solutions ready. He admitted the content was not his work and that he had not read chapters. Also very rudely addressed us. Emails excessively at every hour of days, nights, holidays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes super specific about what your grade will look like. Theres a good amount of work, but its not hard. I had it MWF lecture and then TTH was discussion session. The lecture wasn't mandatory, but there were Learning Modules before class and Quizzes on TTH. But the TA is helpful and will give u the answer. Great class and Dr. Osborn is amazing.

Took both 319k and 445l. Tough professor, tough labs, tough exams. Lots of work. Valvano is willing to bend over backwards to pass his students. He has office hours every weekday and picks excellent TA's. Lectures are scattered but very helpful. 445l is more structured than 319k. Heavy emphasis on debugging, hirerability, and maintaining your job.

valvano is a really funny person and an absolutely horrendous lecturer which is a bit unfortunate cause the class is actually very interesting, but you're able to learn most of the material from labs and practice exams. if it were a harder course he would've been worse but the class structure makes his class just alright
Great professor maybe not the best lecturer tho

This class has an unusually high fail/drop rate compared to other professors. Labs are long and unclear, checkouts are harsh, and exams are exceptionally hard and don't match the material taught. The professor and TAs provide little support, making it feel like they want students to fail. If possible, take this course with a different professor.

He is extremely scatterbrained, but that can make class funny sometimes. Honestly all of your learning will come from the labs and the TAs help tremendously. His tests aren't terrible, but the second test is just coding and is one of those tests where you either get a 0 or a 100. Overall solid professor, but lectures are not super beneficial.
Free Cookies, I love you valvano please love me too

After Patt, I was terrified of what might happen in Valvano's class since people compare the two so much. Valvano is 10x better than Patt. He treats students with respects, and has great TA's! This class will be fun if you go in with the right mindset. You will for sure make lots of friends if you attend the labs. Go to Valvano's office hours!

He's pretty scatterbrained and unorganized at times, but he's good at teaching. ECE319K itself is standardized so the professor will not matter as much regardless. He's entertaining and roasts some kids (including myself) during lectures.

My favorite professor here at UT. You might think he's scary at first, but he is so caring and wants you to pass. Go to OH and ask questions! He will do a stellar job at showing you what you're confused about. I sometimes went to just chill and work honestly. :) He's also really funny. TAs are amazing too. Start the labs early and you'll be fine.

Honestly, I didn't go to many lectures during the year, you learn the most through just reading the textbook and through the labs. The office hours were super helpful and I loved the textbook! The TAs were great and so nice so definitely take advantage of OHs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were hard to sit through but his office hours are more useful if you wanna learn. Go to office hours/start early & utilize the textbook for labs. TAs are wonderful and helpful. Bro would set up zoom late at night just to help with students so he's pretty crazy but super caring for that, he is very considerate when it comes to his students.

The best professor I've had so far. If you ever struggle, there are an abundance of office hours to go to for help and I've seen him stay late multiple times to help. The textbook is well written and a godsend in labs. His lectures can deviate from the slides a bit but they get the point across effectively. Find a good partner and practice coding.

Embedded Lab is inherently more difficult due to the number of lab assignments, but Dr. Valvano doesn't make it harder than it needs to be. Projects are straightforward but lengthy, and TAs will help a lot. You'll learn a lot about embedded programming. Find a good group and make sure everyone is on top of deadlines. Some labs have extra credit.

Valvano's lectures are not amazing, he often skips through the powerpoint or start writing stuff down on paper that won't get posted, so be ready to self study or take lots of notes. Otherwise the class is very lab heavy, if you put effort in all labs you won't fail. Valvano is also very accessible outside of class and is happy to discuss topics.

Honestly such a great Professor with great TAs. If I wouldn't have utilized office hours, I don't think I would have been as successful. At times, lectures were confusing, so I'd advise keeping up with the textbook, which is where most lab checkout and quiz questions come from. Lab 10 is super fun!

Really underrated prof. Yeah, sometimes mid-lecture you might go "what???" due to him skipping around, but he CARES and just go to OH for clarification(tons of OH and very helpful).  Some labs take longggg time but the TAs are awesome and chill. Try to get a good partner. You get to have fun and learn a lot with him, so what else can you ask for!

Super fun prof. He engages the class and cares about his students. The textbook that he wrote for this class is fantastic and I highly recommend it! If you put in the effort for this class you will get the grades you want. 2 midterms are fairly straightforward coding. Final is cumulative, but covers material from the labs and quizzes.
Good lecturer, knows material better than anyone, easy to follow along course

He's a bad lecturer since he gets off task easily, doesn't explain concepts clearly, and assumes that students read the textbook before each class. In reality, work hard on the labs (and use TA office hours) and use old exams to study for the midterms/final

He's really smart and a professor who's easy to approach. His lectures can be a bit hard to follow but the textbook he wrote was AMAZING, has everything you need. For labs and exam preps, go to office hours, they are actually very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did really well on all the labs, they will carry your grade. I got hit really hard by the tests and the final was pretty hard. (it dropped my grade from a B to a C.) This class was affected by corona really heavily, they did their best to accomodate but it felt like all hours of my day became absorbed by the assignments. Valvano is messy, but nic
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I've heard many stories on how Valvano was a poor choice for lectures. This sadly is true. While brilliant, he gets easily sidetracked and is quite scatterbrained. However, the value lies in his office hours, as he is a great resource for 1 on 1 learning and truly cares about his students. While the content is easy, the labs do get time consuming

His lecture suck but he has a mind blowing amount of material to learn from. He´s got online lectures with interactive tools, the book, docs with summaries and questions form every lab and TA´s are pretty good. I would try to take it with another professor because he is a little bit intimidating when u go to his office and the others are very good

His lectures aren't great, but if you've been keeping up with the textbook material and read the lecture slides beforehand, it's pretty clear he knows his stuff. The course is standardized, so if you really hate him that much, you can go to another professor's lecture and learn the same thing. Taking notes in class is a struggle.

It can be quite confusing to tell when you're supposed to be taking notes, so just record everything on audio and pay attention. Lab assignments are time consuming, so start on time and READ THE CHAPTER. On Lab 10, if you are doing 3D, start 4 weeks before and use Raycasting. Spent 80+ hours on 3D and got a 60 because matrix projection is hard af.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Valvano is a bit scattered during lecture, but this means you'll learn about some random stuff in addition to the topics. Such as how a smoke detector works. He is fantastic in office hours and the labs are very thorough so you will learn the material well.

He is very scatterbrained and disorganized, and his lectures reflect this. It was extremely hard for me to follow his lecture style, and so the labs and tests were pretty difficult for me. That being said, he's really great one on one and going to his office hours helped. I probably wouldn't take again, but I have a lot of respect for him.
Knows his stuff and is very helpful, but might be hard to follow if you don't pay close attention. Scatter-brained, but helpful. Class is standardized so grading is fair.

Knows his stuff but a bit disorganized/hard to follow in his lectures, although he does provide all the materials you need to succeed anyways. The class is very transparent in what is expected of you. Cares a lot about his student's learning and success.

His lectures are very hard to follow, and he doesn't have any organization when giving notes. He goes off on many tangents but does manage to give some information each lecture. His lectures do help when it comes to labs. You can always opt to go to another professor's lectures (standardized class). His curve at the end was very generous.

EE 319K is the worst class I have ever taken. The labs are unworldly time consuming and difficult, and lab check-out is very stressful and the TA's ask you ridiculous, irrelevant questions. Absolutely HATED this class. Valvano is really unorganized and so is the class. If you're like me and need structure, you won't get it from this class.

Labs are very time consuming and frustrating, the second exam is an assembly program which you have to write, and debug on the fly in an hour. Worth 25%.. Either it works, or it doesn't.. Needless to say, it ruined my chance at A. 319K is just a weed out class you have to go through and there's no way around it. Start on the labs EARLY!!

The only real gripe I have with this guy is that he is EXTREMELY disorganized. One look at his office will tell you everything you'll ever need to know about him. Do NOT rely on him to make announcements about things or help you meaningfully, he can probably clarify some stuff but you might just end up the butt of a bad joke.
Dr. Valvano is the best professor I had at the University of Texas.  His class is very difficult, but you learn a great deal.  We need more professors and more classes like his.
Good teaching. Great guy. Need more professors like him.

Had such a good semester in Stoney's class! The projects in intro are material based and help you gain a confidence with the different mediums and applying them to sculpture. We had a presentation project where we had to research two artists and present them to the class, super easy and very educational. Overall, I would recommend him to everyone!

For sure a character; for intro he has great projects that lets you learn a lot of mediums. Lots of demos. Read through an insufferable book on modern sculpture and had group discussion. Does not post anything on canvas but you can text him any questions, anytime. Hilarious and caring. Donuts for crit, and random weird snacks occasionally

Had him for Degree Track Perspc Studio. Class is sculpture based b/c he's that kind of artist. Lots of readings for HW, discussions about readings in class, must get a different sculpture library book every week, site visits are often, a single group project/presentation, watched videos often. Easy A if you show up and participate. He's so funny!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Classes with Stoney are an experience. His lessons are relaxed and unpredictable, but he still manages to keep you on your toes by scattering gems of knowledge between every silly comment. You will absolutely come out of this a better artist.

I have him for 2 classes and he's already one my favorite teachers I have ever had. He's funny, lenient, and human. He's not a jerk by any means. I respect him and I've learned a lot from him and he has finally helped me understand things about art that I've been trying to figure out for years. I plan on taking a 3rd class by him.

Really lets you to do your thing/explore/contemplate.  I enjoyed his reading assignments as well as other book recommendations. The course included 2 small projects and one final project. You won't feel rushed to get something done unless you slack out. Overall, awesome intro class. Would recommend for art majors and non-art majors!

His projects involve lots of experimentation. He wants you to learn through your mistakes, and will often leave you to your own devices. He will grade you on the time and thought you put into your work, and you'll find his class to be casually cerebral.
idk. he is good, needs to give more help or direction sometimes. or confirmation that were in the right direction.

Synonyms for quirky is a place to start, I guess. Eccentric, interesting, funny, talks about things that don't always seem relevant. But in the grand scheme of life maybe everything is relevant. At times he seems condescending. Hard to know if I'm reading him right. I almost wish he expected/asked/demanded more of students. He might be surprised.

I learned absolutely nothing. You really will not be getting your money's worth here. If you care about learning, do not take this class with this professor. If you want an easy A, go for it, but you'll be bored to death.

He will waste your time and money. You won't learn anything about Crime Fiction. He's a pleasant, intelligent man, but puts no effort into teaching. He will waste a lot of class time talking about John Milton. If you're looking for an easy "A," then you won't mind. I had hoped to learn.

chill and interesting class. attendance isn't mandatory, but DO ATTEND bc the exams are just things he talks about during class. pretty easy class, just pay attention during lectures and take notes. i suggest having a few friends on a shared note doc so you can catch up when you miss stuff (his powerpoints don't help).

If this means anything, I made an account just for this professor. Rumrich is genuinely AMAZING. He's super funny and always means well. He made a class that I felt iffy about into something I enjoy. Very smart man; his intelligence glows. Def will be taking another class of his. Great class!

best professor i have ever had. prof rumrich is a master at his craft, is well-knowledgeable, and encouraging to his students. his lectures feel like a conversation, and as long as you do the readings they are easy to follow. SHOW UP TO CLASS!! and ask questions!! i can't stress enough how awesome this guy is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you need a UGS I 1000000% recommend this class. It was so much fun! There are 4 or 5 quizzes the entire semester but as long as you pay attention and take notes in class, you genuinely don't even need to study. There were 3 other assignments in the entire year that were so easy and graded really lightly. Rumrich is the best prof ever fr.

Tell me why this class was harder than my STEM courses? Professor is pretty boring and half the class isn't even about the Beatles; we studied Fraud in "fun easy UGS." TA grades pretty aggressively for small minute details and don't even get me started on the tests. Almost no content related to the course on tests. Do not take this class for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Rumrich's Meet The Beatles course. He's a great professor, has interesting lectures and you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, but I think it's best to take this class only if you're genuinely interested in the subject. There was only 1 essay, 1 short presentation, and 4 quizzes (1 dropped) so make sure you do well on these!

I absolutely loved Dr. Rumrich! You can tell he's really passionate about everything he talks about and he's so nice to talk to after class. I already knew a lot about The Beatles so I might be biased, but to pass the quizzes I highly suggest taking good notes. Questions range on pretty much anything he mentions. (also, laugh at his jokes y'all).

Each lecture was random facts, and some topics just seem complete unrelated to the class. The class was about the Beatles, and we spent 2 weeks on slave trade. Then the quiz comes around, and most questions are about topics he probably spent less than a minute on. Don't take it if you aren't interested in the history of music.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He says anything he says will be on the Exam, so you have to transcribe everything. He grades roughly on research papers and the quizzes are questions about fun facts. Where would I ever use fun facts? "It was the easiest". It was not. This class is difficult for no reason. The last quiz we took, the highest grade someone got was 88. Do not take.

I loved this class so much, however, if you miss class and don't have a good study group you will not do well on exams. His lecture slides do not cover much information on the test and sometimes test questions can be obsure and very specific. Other than that the class is great and would recommend it to anyone.

I took his "Meet the Beatles" UGS. Absolutely loved it. Loved Dr. Rumrich. My TA, Stephen Santoyo, was amazing. I had a lot of previous knowledge on The Beatles, though. 2 short essays that you read in front of your discussion group. 2 tests (i got a 96% both times) and a final (i got a 90%). Would take this class 100x over again.
He has a tendency to ramble during lecture, and his tests can include anything he's said. Other than that, he's a really funny guy who enjoys teaching and makes his class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the Beatles class, His tests are strictly what he says in class. You have to attend lectures to succeed. There isn't much to study but you have to pay attention, even if he does ramble too much. He is passionate about what he talks about, you can tell. But he does give more opinions in a lot of his lectures, not that it mattered much to me.

I took his Beatles class, and I found it to be very interesting, I learned a lot about the Beatles I would not have otherwise known. The tests are easy, and all based off of his lectures. However, he does ramble on a bit in his lectures, which makes it difficult to determine which is just extraneous info and which is going to be on the test.

This class was pretty interesting even though I did not know anything about the Beatles. There are 3 tests covering the lectures. Attendance is not mandatory but the tests are based on lecture material so it's best to not skip class. There are two written assignments and presentations that are very easy.

I took his Meet the Beatles class and it was an easy and entertaining UGS. He does talk a lot about the Beatles and the 60s, so if that's not something you're interested I would not recommend it. Tests are multiple choice and are taken from the lectures, doesn't require a lot of studying to do well.

Goes on about a lot of things that don't matter. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures but is graded for discussions. You also don't get any attendance skips for discussions, they all affect your grade. Weekly quizzes over specifics from lecture. Overall class was okay, easy A.

In terms of workload, there are three writing assignments in total & a multiple-choice quiz at the end of every week in discussions. Overall, lectures were manageable and weekly workload as well. There are a few lengthy readings. Moreover, the class itself is ok (content is somewhat focused on the Beatles). Your TA determines most of your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class hoping to learn more about The Beatles and that is not what I got. Lectures are not mandatory and the prof often talks about things that seem unimportant. The class consists of 6 writing assignments so if you are not the best at writing I do not recommend for a UGS credit . Other than that it is a fairly easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his Beatles course as a Beatles superfan, so I'm biased. However, this class was more of a research/writing course that used the Beatles as a vessel to teach those skills. So, it could be helpful for anyone. His lectures and assignments focus on big ideas rather than detail-memorization, which I appreciate. This class was meaningful and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures. He's very engaging and knows everything about what he teaches-- even how to relate poetic form to the Spongebob theme song. Class was also cool because we got to take a field trip to the HRC. He does seem disorganized at times, but by the end of the class we all learned what his system was and it worked out well. Do the reading!

This UGS was INCREDIBLE. I looked forward to going to class to hear his lectures, which were both interesting and hilarious. No quizzes or tests; all assignments are written. Lots of feedback on each writing assignments by the TAs, who are equally as respectful and lovely to talk to. Even if you know nothing about The Beatles, TAKE THIS UGS!
I got a 99 as my ending grade. I loved this class, but I love reading and literature so take my review with a grain of salt

Professor Rumrich is a really cool professor, and for a literature class there wasn't too much homework, which I really appreciated. The only thing is that the lectures don't always feel very organized and it can be hard to know how to prepare for the exams (which are essay formats).

The professor himself is great. I took his Meet the Beatles class and had very little interaction with Rumrich himself. His TA Dan on the other hand is the worst!!! If you choose to take this class pray that you get the girl TA... because if you get the boy TA you are in for a real nightmare grade wise. He grades unnecessarily hard for no reason..
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable on his subject and very passionate about it. I really felt like I learned a lot. The only grades were participation, quizzes, and an optional final. He made sure that anyone who read and tried to participate did well. He really wanted us to read, understand, and enjoy the works. Spectular, loved him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's so boring. Every lecture is monotone and he goes off on weird tangents that have nothing to do with what we're learning. His quizzes are detail-heavy so read carefully and then accept that you'll never get an A on one
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Rumrich is my favorite professor so far at UT. Right off the bat you can tell how knowledgable & chill this guy is. TBH wish he was my grandpa or something bc he's just clearly such a cool & interesting dude. I took his Detective Fiction class and loved his lectures, he's really invested in everything he teaches, funny teacher & a great guy!

I had Rumrich for Detective Fiction and really enjoyed the class. He didn't ever overwhelm you with reading, only assigning a couple of chapters a week. We wrote four papers over the semester which weren't bad at all. He loves to talk and discuss, and he genuinely is interested in "younger" people's opinions. Very nice and interesting man!

Plan II World Lit, he expects you to do reading. There is a quiz on reading weekly and essays are assigned periodically throughout semester. Enjoyed the detective fiction we read, he is clearly intelligent and has some good points to make.

Took his 2 semester class freshman year, and at first all we read was Milton (he is a Milton scholar), but I learned throughout my time with him how interested he is in all literature, and he has been one of my favorite teachers. I never actually read, but you have to have an idea of what is going on. He is absolutely great and so funny. No tests.

I personally hate Milton and did not realize it until I took the class. If you like Paradise Lost, want to read religious texts, and want are willing to dedicate a lot of time to one class, then take it. If not, DON'T TAKE IT. I ended up dropping. I personally feel that it's a lot of work.
Great professor!  I have never enjoyed a literature course so much.

Milton. John Rumrich really helps you get to know Milton as more than just a dead poet/writer. His class is tough though. You have to do the readings otherwise you will fail his quizzes. Sparknotes doesn't cover it. We also had to memorize and recited 80 lines total of Milton's poetry. He's tough but knowledgeable and challenging. Interesting class

Rumrich is my favorite professor that I've ever had. He's smart, funny, and interesting. He makes classes do journals/quizzes to make sure they're on top of things, so it's a bit harder than most 'write a paper at the end' classes. The plus side is, you really learn and absorb the texts. Also, he has superhuman powers of recitation. It's uncanny.

Mr. Jay is very caring and you can tell he loves calc. Explains concepts well, and I personally thought his lectures were very helpful. He does spend a lot of time on warmups, but they're often relevant + help you learn how to do different problems. Office hours were also very accessible to me! Tests were not bad at all; gives back a lot of points.

The professor can be difficult to contact. The professor will spend 30+ minutes on the warm-up and skim through the content covered on the test. There are no extra-credit opportunities. Test reviews can be long and don't reflect the test. Be ready to learn on your own if you take this class, and be an expert in algebra and trig.

This professor is nice and sounds passionate about the subject, but he spent forever on the warmup problems and barely any time on content that I found mattered. Homeworks took hours to accomplish and the discussions barely helped for exams. Practice problems will be your best friend to survive this class.

Jay is decent, but the math department truly is awful. The lectures are fine, but he typically solves halfway and then you have to wait and ask later for help. The practice exams do not help, they are old exams and don't match at all. Several Homeworks a week that require office hours since the questions aren't answered in Lecture.

Half the lectures were useless and it was a lot of self study and homework. The TA discussions were weirdly hard and not very helpful but that might be up to the TA. He's a nice guy but not great at teaching. Sanger saved me a lot this semester. Also tests make up like +60% in your grade.

Professor is a very kind man. However, his lectures are very disorganized. He spends more than 30 minutes on warmups which are sometimes helpful. TA isn't much help either, often gets many things wrong and is just as lost as the students sometimes. Exams make up most of your grade so be ready for that. Be ready to study and to have a hard time.

Lectures are fast and can get confusing the way he explains things, but we had learning modules in my class so we could learn outside of the lectures. Very nice guy though, willing to explain any concepts after class or in office hours. Tests not super hard but not super easy.

Grading took forever, majority of lecture spent catching up on previous lectures, so much hw - difficult to manage on top of the amt of studying for unnecessarily hard exams and quizzes, TA (ballet slippers, black toenails, outfit repeater) was zero help; instead of questions we could be tested on, spent time trying to explain phd math concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This ninja is so bad. Ignore the glazers in the section they lowkey busted ifywim for him. Got an A but had to grind so hard. Very nice guy but can teach and is abs garbage at p much everything to else. DONT take him 408d is supposed to be a blow off for ap bc 5ers but ts was NOT.

jay is a very caring professor. 2 learning modules, quest, and written hw due per week. personally, i found lecture to be useful (esp. warmups). exams weren't bad, and he posted lengthy review sets that were really helpful in studying. definitely doable if you put in the effort- go to office hours and review old homeworks. would take him again!

He truly did care, but just was super unorganized. Homework heavy, four assignments due a week. He gave reviews to tests, but no answers. Lectures weren't helpful in my opinion. If anything go to discussion!!!! Kris, the TA was amazing!! Tests were pretty straightforward, actually do the homework and do the reviews and you'll be fine.

Took in Fall '24: Prof Whitehead is a really nice guy, but this class was super disorganized, answer keys didn't exist for hw outside of quest, super weird/conceptual questions on tests.
