Prof Kaur is clearly passionate. She takes 2-3 weeks to respond to emails. Lots of extra credit, but for good reason. Tests are hard, the practice tests are nothing like them. Extremely passive aggressive and demeaning at times. She is the reason I no longer want to do cs. Took every chance to blame me for not being able to succeed in coding!

She's a very engaging lecturer. I think my main gripes with the class are just about the inflexibility in grading policy, as you can put in a lot of work and be rewarded pretty minimally. The assignments will take you hours to complete. The exams are very difficult, so STUDY. Weed out classes are meant to be hard so work hard and do your best!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've never coded prior to this class, and Professor Kaur taught a great first-coder class! There are so many opportunities for extra credit, and there are TA office hours for help on the assignments literally every single day from like 9am-5pm. The assignments can be difficult but as long as you attend lecture/watch lecture videos, you'll be ok!

Very receptive to questions and asks students for feedback (and you get extra credit for giving feedback). The lectures are really nice and I was able to actually learn from them. Assignments can be challenging but there are so many resources for help + extra credit. Exams reflect what was learned in class and there is a curve.

Beginner friendly but the pace does pick up in this class even though she teaches basics. Is really good about listening to student feedback. Talks very fast so if you don't understand something you have to ask in that moment or it's hard to catch up. Homeworks and exams are pretty on par with what is lectured on, slightly more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kaur is my favorite professor at UT. She is an amazing lecturer and very accessible to get help. As someone who entered her class in Spring 2024 with no coding experience, she broke down the material in a clear format for beginners. Homework assignments get difficult later on in the semester. Tests are challenging.

The content itself was not hard however, the format of the exams was on paper which made it annoying and difficult. The practice exams did not reflect the real exams' difficulty. Much of the stuff we learn in class is useless. Grading on homework was annoying I would get points off for things that didn't matter like an extra comment.

So many opportunities for extra credit from assignments, attendance, and feedback surveys. Gradescope for HW sucks, but there's so many TA's and office hours and that saved my life so many times! Kaur is a fantastic and engaging lecturer. Tests are kinda hard tho. Wish I went to office hours sooner. 10/10 would take a again!
Gave no feedback on the final and curved grades last minute. She is a nice person but the practice exams do not match the exams.

Prof Kaur is awesome! She really cares about her students, and she'll give you all the resources you need to succeed. Grades are weekly coding assignments (moderately difficult), 2 midterms, and 1 final. Lots of extra credit--take advantage!! Midterms are tricky, so study lecture slides, extra problems, and practice tests. An A is totally doable!

Prof Kaur was a very engaging lecturer and helps you wet your feet in python coding. She gives lots of opportunities outside of class for help and to better understand the content showing she cares a lot about student success. Office hours with her are great. Only complaint is that the practice exams never matched the difficulty of the real exams.

Prof Kaur is such a GOOD teacher. She is so patient and caring. There are lots of small opportunities for extra credit so TAKE ADVANTAGE- it adds up! The assignments are doable and easy if you go to office hours. Learn about style early and revisit throughout the semester so you can collect easy points. The exams aren't too bad. Best intro cs class

People have mixed opinions about Kaur. Honestly, she is not bad at all. She is a great lecturer and very willing to help during office hours. The homeworks will get tough as you go on, so make sure to utilize the TA office hours. She is very knowledgeable about what she is teaching, so if you are interesting is learning CS, you should take her!

Honestly one of the best lecturers I've had at UT as she's very thorough with explanations and resources. There's plenty of extra credit if you do stuff like turning in assignments on time and even going to lecture. A few assignments took way too long and gradescope is annoying asf, but there's so many TA office hours and you def should go, 10/10

If you already have CS experience, Kaur is an awesome prof! HWs will be super easy and exams are sometimes a bit sneaky, but overall fair and well written. If you haven't coded before though, this class will be pretty tough. Lots of extra credit opportunities and the TAs give really good feedback on HWs.

Good person, pretty bad professor. The main issue with this class is that the difficulty level of the exams is not at all similar to the material she teaches. She scratches the surface of all the core concepts however will test you on the most niche uses of these concepts. I would avoid taking this class with her at all costs.

She is a nice person but the difference between the lecture material and practice test in comparison to the test is laughable. The class and concepts are not that hard she just does a poor job of preparing people who have not coded before for the exams.
Content is hard and she's not the easiest to listen to, but it's doable and she provides all the resources needed to get a decent grade. Homework's can be time consuming, but they are doable.

Great person, but awful professor. Her lectures are filled with content, but she jumps around constantly from topic to topic. Assignments are extremely helpful and so are OH, but does not prepare you for the exams. You will be learning content up till the last day before the exam, and it will definitely be tested on.

She expects you to have no experience in coding. However, students in the class are either have experience already, or no experience at all. So no-experience ppl don't do as well on exams, but the ppl with experience will cancel that out. Therefore, the exam averages are normal so she doesn't really care and think everyone is doing fine.

Great professor for learning basic computer science, very thorough, and clearly goes through all the material in class. Plus there are tons of office hours and added learning sessions. She is very funny, and gives and receives feedback very frequently in service to improving the course experience.

Coming from a person who had 0 coding experience before...Professor Kaur is GOATED. She would not let you use any programming knowledge outside from her class which I think it's fair and indeed works very well with me so I only need to review what she taught. Exams are a little rough, but if you actually understand the material, you will be fine.

The exams are tough so be prepared to study! Utilize the practice exams she gives you and she also allows you to have a cheat sheet on the exams! Write good notes on your cheat sheet + do the practice exams to get an A. I entered this class with no coding experience and found the assignments difficult yet rewarding.

DOES NOT CURVE INDIVIDUAL EXAMS and will only CONSIDER curving final grade!! If you don't have any prior knowledge in python, I would strongly advise against taking her class or you WILL be struggling for your life. There is a huge disparity in difficulty between her exams and the actual material she teaches in class.

I took Amrita her first year of teaching. She does a pretty good job at teaching you the basics and the majority of the assignment were fun and easy! The only thing is that the homework difficulty changes extremely quickly and her practice exams sucked to take without anyone there to warn me.

But she's pretty chill and friendly overall.

Great class and professor if you had no previous experience with python, there's assignments every week which are time consuming but not very hard, coding challenges were easy, and midterm and final were in pencil and paper but she allowed 1 and 2 cheat sheets so they weren't very hard

She was nice and really understanding if anyone needed things like extensions. Good at explaining concepts and the homework each week was very doable. Her office hours were super short and a lot of people were cheating so I kept on losing points for the same reason each week but never changed it because the grades were released so late.

awesome class. would take again with prof. kaur in a heartbeat. super easy to reach her if u have questions over the homeworks or coding challenges. really wants you to do well and will do anything in her power to help. the course can be a little challenging if its ur first coding class but not too bad. cant recommend her enough.

TAKE AMRITA FOR 303!! She is so caring and lectures are amazing - extremely detailed and breaks problems/concepts down step by step. The class is difficult, yes, but any CS class will be. I came in with 0 coding knowledge and got an A in the class even after bombing the midterm (your final grade can replace the midterm if higher).

Amrita is a kind, knowledgable professor. Class is based on HW (easy but time consuming), coding challenges (completion grade), and tests (hard). VERY generous with extra credit/deadlines (automatic +2 ish points for meeting deadlines). Hard tests but doable if you study. I have 4+ years of coding experience, so the class was relatively easy.

Professor Kaur herself is nice, but the assignments are hard (and get harder, especially in the middle) if you don't have any coding experience. She also accuses students of cheating quite often for similarities to ChatGPT or other students assignments.

Don't take this class with Kaur if you have prior Python experience. This is "her" intro class, so you're not allowed to use prior knowledge for the assignments, CC, and exams. I took an intro programming class at UT, and was told it was cheating if I used stuff I learned from that class. Know an easy way to do something? Nope, I didn't teach it.
She allows students to use ChatGPT for their homework. She then goes on to accuse the class of using ChatGPT. I've never felt more accused of something I never did.

Professor Kaur takes student feedback every week. This is good, because she listens to her students. The assignments for her class are terrible, but shouldn't be a problem. Coding Challenges are a thing, so attendance is mandatory. She leaves a lot of stuff out of her syllabus. I.e. she will deduct points for anything.

She's right of out grad school, so she's still pretty new to the whole professor thing. I didn't like her at all. Her assignments will teach you the basics, but they won't show you any real application. Class is super slow placed. Lectures are boring. She does take student feedback well.

Professor Kaur was an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about the material and her students. 

Pace of the class is pretty slow. Exams do get you thinking. Coding challenges are fun. Homeworks are annoying (they require exact output), but relatively easy.

I only fell asleep in class once, so her lectures aren't that bad.

She's very kind!
Amrita is a great professor that truly cares about her students. I learned a ton in this class and feel like every assignment had a purpose. Highly recommend!

I took CS 303E with her and she's GREAT! A few things: I think she messed up w the whole going slow w easy things at first and then fast w hard things by the end. Also, homeworks DO get progressively harder so you cannot let go in the middle of the semester bc u feel like u are doing good. I already knew a bit of python and by the end I was a mess.

Not too difficult, engaging, relevant discussions, multiple case studies that can be done before class ends. There are guest speakers towards the end of the semester, which are also interesting, and grading isn't too tough. There's room for open-minded discussion.

Ethics was a great class! I enjoyed the balance between lectures and group work. Lectures were engaging, and group work days were chill but interesting to dissect with peers. The topics we discuss are relevant to the modern world while still acknowledging the history of ethics in advertising. Overall, loved it!

One of my favorite professors at UT. She uses classes for one lecture a week and one workday. Her class is actually interesting and she is so chill. Attendance is mandatory though. Only the tests are lowk hard so pay attention and study.
Law and Ethics is a pretty useless class in which she is underutilized. I did feel like there was a lack of connection between her and the TA regarding grading and rubric strictness.

Almost the entirety of assignments were done in class with an assigned group for the semester. The first few were graded tougher, but you get the hang of them. General rule of thumb: the more we wrote, the better grade we got. The lecture content was pretty common sense, but the tests were based entirely upon it -- not the readings.

Professor Pounders was amazing! Her lectures were so interesting and I loved her format with lectures on tuesdays and group work on thursdays. The only reason this class was difficult is because it covered hard topics. There's two exams, two papers, and a bunch of case study daily grades. I recommend taking Pounders for 353.

Law and Ethics: Kate was AWESOME. Responsive to emails, always provided feedback on campaign critiques, cared about the class, and gave interesting and attention-retaining lectures. The only thing annoying was our TA, who was very dismissive and graded way too hard, but Pounders was happy to hear you out and evaluate the grade herself.

I thought this class was ok. There is another section for the same course with Ciszek which I think is the better option (no tests). There is little to no homework in her course, but our TA graded our in-class campaign critiques pretty harshly. 2 tests that combined are worth 40% of your grade. Study hard for exams because they are worded weird.

Dr.Pounders is a very good professor The only setback about this class was that it was online, so a lot of things would get lost in translation. Also, her tests were a bit difficult, I found that no matter how hard you watched her lectures or textbook I would always do bad on exams. Other than that, loved the class, very helpful for future classes

Doctor Pounders was always very clear in her lectures about what content she expected students to know for the exams. The thing I didn't like about the course was the fact that I couldn't speed up lectures, so in moments where I felt the course was slow, I just had to sit through it. Overall though it was a great course with a great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I took this class as an elective and it was super easy. Short quiz and discussion post due once a week on Sunday and three tests that were very straightforward as long as you understood the content at all. Video lectures were pretty boring but the content was interesting. I definitely recommend taking this as a filler class.

She was AMAZING. Highly recommend her for this course. The class set up allows you to really learn and apply course materials to the world around you. Has discussion posts due every week, but they are fun to do. The exams are most of the grade, but they are pretty simple and straightforward, just really study lecture and book.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Being a first year college student I found this course hard to adjust to I ended the semester with an 89.9 and Dr. Pounders would not let me complete any extra credit which was a little frustrating. The part that made me most angry wasn't her not allowing me the extra .1. points, but she did not respond to my email and I was forced to follow-up.

This class was asyncronous. Each week you were required to complete about 2 lecture videos (45 minutes total MAX), a discussion post, and a 10 question timed quiz. Dr. Pounders is passionate about her field and a great professor. This was my favorite class all semester and I would take it again. Easy A and you don't really have to study!

weekly lectures/quizzes/discussion posts that are self-paced. very easy if you dont procrastinate. professor is very caring and passionate about the subject + gives opportunities to ask questions and gives feedback

Pounders is very knowledgeable in her field. Despite this though, her lectures were very unengaging. The textbook is required but I don't think it's necessary since the exams are lecture based. She does provide a study guide for her exams. She was so hard to reach outside of class for absolutely no reason.

Kate was really knowledgeable in what she teaches and therefore her lectures were really interesting and easy to understand. The class is fairly work heavy but its never overwhelming and its all organized super well
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Pounders was a great professor. She gives good examples that are relevant and help you better understand and relate to the topic. I definitely think reading the textbook is essential to get an A, but the info is super interesting in my opinion so it wasn't bad.

Dr. Pounders was a great teacher. Her Psychology of Advertising class was extremely interesting. As long as you follow the rubric for assignments you should do pretty well. The tests and quizzes should be pretty easy if you are familiar with the material.

She has the most concise lectures. They're long but for the amount of material, it's swift. She reuses the same example for everything, it can be repetitive, but the important ones stick. Write down everything and you'll be solid. Live review for exams were hell. Just do the study guide on your own. TA's were hit or miss but I really enjoyed mine.

A weekly discussion board, quiz, and lecture series that you could complete at any time during that week. Lectures were clear and concise. No group work or presentations necessary. Reviews were thorough and helpful. Textbook is helpful but not necessary. As long as you do the assignments, the class is an easy A. Dr Pounders was also super sweet.

Amazing professor, she's so sweet and you can tell she is truly passionate about what she is teaching and cares for her students. Easy class with like 3 exams but you can easily pass them with the study guides she gives out. There's a quiz and discussion post weekly due at the same time every week so it's easy to keep track of.

I really liked Dr. Pounders, she was very kind and straight forward. The tests weren't awful and the assignments were easy. Participation definitely can make or break your grade, as with attendance. She'll definitely do the attendance check the one day you're not there. Very cool, very nice, and very knowledgeable.
Dr. Pounders was very kind and obviously knowledgeable about advertising. I really enjoyed this class -- which was completely outside of my normal studies.

I love Kate. If you have the chance to take her for any class, do it. She is so kind and really knows what she is talking about. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There are no tests in this class, only quizzes, a few papers, and a group project. She is very accessible to her students. Also, she has a really cute dog.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Pounders is great! Her lectures are really interesting. She goes through a lot of info in the lectures, so sometimes it was hard to keep up with notes cause it goes fast, but not that bad. Overall just a kind person and you can tell how passionate she is about her work. Extra credit opportunities and weekly quizzes w/ info from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pounders truly cares about her students' well being and she is extremely knowledgeable in her field. As long as you attend lectures (instapolls and in-class activities are assigned), skim the book, and participate, you'll easily get an A. The class is really interesting for ADV majors and non-majors alike! 11/10 would recommend :)

Pounders is GREAT! I would highly recommend her for ADV353, the class is pretty straight forward and she cares a lot about her students. The TAs and her grade well and fairly, its very obtainable to get an A. Although she doesn't take attendance, she goes over examples that can appear on the quizzes. There is a team debate and research paper
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class. She is so funny and her class is so interesting. The papers were so easy and took me about 30 minutes to do they would be like a page single spaced. Her tests were kind of hard but if you read the textbook you're fine. She has random attendance checks and sometimes in class group activities. Cancels class a lot

Kate is very understanding and willing to meet outside of class to discuss material or even why/how stuff was graded. She, like a lot of other professors, says she cares about your mental health but she actually means it and her class/ grading methods reflect that. The course is very paper heavy but it's not an absurd amount of work.

Dr. Pounders is an OK professor. The class is semi-interesting and lectures are pretty long. She was very unorganized and canceled class a lot of times an hour before it started. I didn't read the textbook and I got an A. Just study her lectures and you will for sure do great. Easy class, just annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Liked this class, but wasn't my favorite. You definitely don't need the textbook at all, and there are lots of in-class participation assignments. Make sure to check deadlines for the papers and debates, but overall I felt like the class was fair and reasonable.

This is one of my favorite classes at UT. Kate is amazing and her lectures are engaging and interesting. Shes also very nice and understanding, especially if you talk to her. This isnt my major, but I loved the class and wish I could take her again. Highly recommend.

As a student with disabilities, Dr. Pounders was not understanding at all. I had to miss class a few times due to my disability, and she did not offer a way to make up missed in class activities despite having SSD accommodations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting class, despite not being directly part of my major. Kate is a wonderful person who works hard to make the content from the text clear/understandable. Honestly the complaints about her canceling class are idiotic; they were related to TRAGIC family losses, and Kate was professional and pushed back due dates for student's success anyway.

Professor Pounders is an amazing lecturer. Everything in this class is interesting and keeps you on edge. Showing up to class is not mandatory but a lot of the material on tests comes from lecture and she sometimes gives extra credit for showing up. She is so nice and will help a lot if you go to office hours!
Professor Pounders' lectures are really great, but this class also requires a lot of work out of class. I didn't mind the work too much personally because the course material is really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kate was an amazing professor. Her lectures aren't mandatory but she takes notice of who is there and who participates. Plus, her lectures are really interesting. Overall, she is one of my favorite professors I've had so far at UT.
Dr. Pounders was amazing and her lectures are amazing! Clearly cares about the content and her students. Highly recommend.
Dr. Pounders is amazing! I cant recommend either if her classes more. She cares, is knowledgeable, and relatable. Amazing prof.
I got nothing but love and respect for Pounders! Go over the powerpoints she provides along with the terms of the chapter and you should get easy A's!

Profesor Pounders is a very respectable woman and truly knows her stuff. Her class is enjoyable, and I learned a lot. However, it is very easy to get an A the 3 tests by simply going the day of the review and filling in information you need to know with friends. If you have friends willing to give you notes, you dont have to read or go to class.

Kate is an incredible prof. It breaks my heart that I cant take more of her classes because they fill up so fast. She is extremely inelegant and very passionate about her students success and what she lectures on. You have to study for the tests and pay attention to lecture but they are 45 min. Shell always  help you. Quizes are all on quizlet.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is great, its really easy if you attend every class. She makes a study guide at the end of each section which, if you study, is your free ticket to an A on every test. She cancels class frequently (Sometimes the morning-of) which is annoying if its the 8AM class and you don't check your phone b4 heading to class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 1. attend every lecture or say goodbye to your participation grade 2. seize every opportunity to get extra credit

I loved this prof and class! Your grade consists of 3 out of class writing assignments, random in class activities for participation, 10 question timed online quizzes for each chapter, 3 exams and an optional final (if you didn't miss any of the 3 exams). Cancelled class a few times but there's nothing on the exam that we didn't go over in class.

I loved Dr. Pounders and this class! She doesn't require attendance, however if you come to class and take notes you should do well on the tests! Not much homework, just reading the textbook to fill in gaps from lectures. It is definitely beneficial to get to know her in office hours! I really loved this class and would definitely take her again!

Dr. Pounders was a wonderful professor. She made a large class engaging and the content was interesting. Exams are straightforward but coming to class helps. She definitely cares about her students. Highly recommend.

Dr. Pounders is a good professor, class was easy, the exams were over stuff she went over in class so you don't really need the book except for the quizzes online. she comes off as rude but i think you have to go to office hours to get to know her (i didnt), canceled class a lot (maybe 4-5 times this semester) TAs kinda sucked

Dr. Pounders is super sweet and cares about her students a lot. The course is not too difficult, 3 test plus optional final, some easy projects, and some in class work. Test were not too hard just lots of memorization. Definitely a worth while class to take and a great prof to get to know. Only negative thing was that she canceled class often.

Pounders was great. Super knowledgeable, funny, and accepting. Six (pretty straightforward) quizzes and your lowest is dropped. You dont need the textbook at all. Lots of in-class participation assignments.

Dr. Pounders is, so far, my favorite professor at UT. The material is actually very interesting and lectures are entertaining to listen to. She provides a lot of cool examples of ads so that the class can understand the content more. She did cancel class a few times, but I wouldn't call that a downfall. Textbook is necessary for online quizzes.

Love her! Fair grader, would give points back on questions that weren't covered in lectures or missed by a lot of students. She cares about what she is teaching and does it well because she's so relatable. The class allows you to learn a lot of material and as long as you study and go to lectures an A is very achievable! Definitely take her!

cancelled class sooo many times, a lot of times right before it was supposed to start which was so frustrating because it was a 9 am so i kept getting out of bed for nothing. alright professor, don't bother reading the textbook because exams are based on the lectures and she skips stuff in the book and talks about stuff not in the book.

Professor Pounders is an outstanding professor. If you go to class you will have a better understanding of the definitions and concepts talked about in the book. In her exams she likes to use ads she shows in lecture so thats another reason to attend class. Overall I enjoyed taking this class during my first semester at UT.

Great professor - you can tell she really cares and is educated about the ethics in her field. Most of the work was reading a lot from the textbook/lectures. Online comments were fine. The final paper took a while since there were some length requirements. If you do the readings and articulate your ideas well, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: KATE IS AMAZING. Participate in her class and she makes sure to learn your name. Really cares about her students, I believe its genuine but sometimes it can come off a little fake. Her lectures are interesting. She does not test you on anything you do not learn in class. Even spends the day before a test reviewing you. AWESOME professor.

Dr. Pounders is undoubtably the best teacher I have had so far. In short, it is because of her endearing efforts to be both inclusive and daring. Inclusive, because all the group work, class discussions, and anything calling upon social aptitude was, in a sense, easy to partake in, yet daring, as the upward bounds for effort were nowhere in sight.

Very organized and clear about assignment and layout of class. Enjoyed having Professor Pounders. She cares about her job and her students. Would definitely take again. You do have to work for your grade though.

Grades consisted of bi-weekly quizzes, a debate, 2 research papers, and some random in-class assignments. The quizzes come straight from the PowerPoints. Dr. Pounders is very kind and genuinely cares about her students. I would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved this class and this professor! There's a weekly online quiz based on textbook readings/ lectures. The nice thing about this class is that she never tests over anything that she hasn't lectured about. That being said, it's important to to take good notes during class. She gives really great reviews before the tests which are immensely helpful.

I never really tried to find her outside of class because the online quizzes were pretty easy. She gives out random in class assignments so be in class every day or you'll regret it. She also didn't grade in a timely manner, took weeks to get back a single page essay grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pounders is really sweet, and her class is pretty easy. There are in-class activities each week and four at-home assignments, but tests are very easy and lecture-based. The textbook is good to read for more depth, but her lectures are basically the highlights you need to know. Come on review days; she literally tells you everything on the test.

I loved taking this class and I hope to take another one of Pounders' classes in the future. The class is an easy A and while attendance is not mandatory, there are weekly in-class activities that do count toward your grade so you won't want to miss those. There are only three tests and the course material is very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Pounders definitely cares about her field. Class was cancelled multiple times due to things outside of her control (car accidents, family matters, etc.), but she remained enthusiastic & we didn't fall behind. A typical week contained daily lectures, commercial watching, readings, & a Friday quiz. Very chill, yet rigorous & enjoyable.

Pretty disorganized and most assignments felt unnecessary and like busy work. Upside is that she cares a lot about students and tries to be as engaging as possible. No final, just debates+quizzes. Her heart is in the right place, her coursework just needs to be revised.

10/10 recommend taking Kate P!! She is such a kind woman, she really wants students to enjoy her lectures and participate. She covers many interesting topics and gives you reviews for the quizzes, and there are NO tests. There is a group project but she gives clear instructions and she isn't hard on her students. She is definitely 1 of my fav profs

Dr. Pounders is a great professor! She took an innovative approach to teaching the ethics class with debates. No tests and quizzes are doable. She cares about her students and the class is not hard if you pay attention and do the work. Highly recommend.

Dr. Pounders is amazing. I took her ADV 353 Advertising Law and Ethics class. I maintained an A the whole semester. Not an "easy A," you have to do a group project debate, some critiques, quizzes, and participation activities but nothing is harder than average. Really prepares you for all quizzes, answers all questions, understanding, SO NICE.

Dr. Pounders is easy to reach & wants to help. No tests in class; 7 quizzes, group debates +2 critiques & in-class work. The material is straight forward. A few slides with examples are left out online so attendance is helpful, especially because of group work in class. She is a great teacher and cares enough about her students to learn their names

I don't know why there's so much negative feedback. Prolly silly undergrads who expect to show up 25% of the time, and Facebook the little time they are actually in class...I had Grad-level Consumer Behavior. Some longish reading assignments, but nothing dreadful. She can be a bit slow to respond via email, but visit her office, and she's great.

No tests, just a debate and quizzes. She tries to make the class interesting and I think she does a good job. I really dont get why people complain. Literally just showing up to class and breathing will give you a passing grade. Some projects were a bit unclear, but she is always willing to explain more in depth if you are confused.

Grad-level consumer behavior class. The course structure was interesting, and the content was great. There were a lot of readings, but it helped. She's pretty lenient on rules for papers; she cares more about quality than length.

It was my worst class by far. Murphy's tests were easier than her quizzes, because you were getting grades for what you know. In Pounders' class doesn't matter if you study or not. She's confusing as hell. She should take some class at ACC to get better with computers, because boy... she's damn slow with anything what has buttons. Take Drumwright.

Pounders is as hot as she is confusing! She makes no sense. Changes the rules of assignments 2 days before the due date, constantly updates the schedule. This class is a nightmare. She's very disorganized. Forget to get any response from her. She isn't helpful at all.

People have a lot of negative things to say about her and I always thought most of them were uncalled for.  There were times when she had an off-putting attitude, but the students in my class were also very disrespectful to her sometimes. I thought it was an easy A if you showed up and paid attention.

I had 4.0. I had, because after taking Dr. Pounders' class I don't have any more. Dr. Pounders' quizzes are very confusing. Questions are stated unclearly and her teaching style is hard to follow by her students. She makes it harder than it should be. Additionally, she doesn't respond to emails very well, if at all.

Even though her many assignments were not particularly the "hardest", you better get ready to read cause either wise you'll find yourself losing points for not being "thoughtful" enough or "specific" enough in your writing responses. You may read a lot of comments that she is very nice but she is very self-center and has zero original thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Latimer is super kind and genuinely cares about each student. She always opens up discussions with insightful feedback and makes the classroom feel like a safe space. I have learned a lot in this class and it was very a cool structure. There are a lot of readings and the assignments definitely pile on at the end of the year, but still chill.

Literally my favorite prof this semester. Discussion-based lectures. 12 modules, 1 assignment and knowledge check per mod, and 4 quizzes (over 3 mods each). Was witty and funny while covering info which kept me engaged. Need 10 participation points which are assigned at random to lecture days. TAKE HER CLASS!

Dr. Latimer can be strict about some things but ultimately an easy class. There's 1 assignment and quiz per unit that you do outside of class, and all were pretty easy. You only need 10 attendance points so you really don't have to show up much. Lots of good topics covered! If you take her class she brings in therapy dogs so I 100% recommend lol!

Ms. Latimer has taught me so much. She is so kind and cares deeply about each person. I personally have never liked to raise my hand in class, but she makes her classroom so comfortable that I enjoy speaking in her class now. All of her information is useful for the real world. Overall, she is wonderful professor!

Dr. L genuinely cares about students well being and gives out great information. She also is very clear about grading and how/who to contact. You have to attend a majority of classes, but other than that you can skip and still understand as long as you look over the slides and do the work. We often had great class discussions, and she is funny.
Such an awesome professor. So sweet, and really cares about her students. TAKE HER!

TA's grading the course often do not elaborate as to why they gave you the grade they did. Assignment instructions often not very clear. Must have 10 participation points throughout the semester as "attendance". Lectures are heavy on material.

Dr. Latimer's class was so entertaining! She goes in-depth on many very interesting topics and provides new insight into a variety of things as well as providing the opportunity for guest speakers to share new perspectives. You only have to get 10 participation grades but I recommend going to all the lectures!

Dr. Latimer is such a great professor! She makes lectures very fun and engaging and allows a lot of extra credit for those who attend lectures. She's also super approachable and enjoys to hear student input. I loved the course topics and how she presents tough topics in a lighthearted and open manner. Definitely recommend a class with her!
not a hard class, weekly assignments, pretty easy.

Dr. Latimer is the absolute best. I was required to take 2 HED core classes with her and intentionally choose to take two more electives with her. She is so caring and understanding! She will make sure you learn the content and yes, she requires you put in effort, but essays and tests are straightforward and based on lectures.
SO much extra credit, such entertaining lectures, just overall amazing professor. Would take this class over and over again if I could

I took HED 335 with Dr. Latimer and she has been my favorite professor. I went into this class not looking forward to the topic or the writing flag. Her lectures are fun and the discussions in her class are interesting. She makes a point to memorize names and truly cares for students. 3 papers but she/TA provide good feedback before it is due.

I think the ratings speak for themselves. Dr. Latimer is absolutely amazing. She makes it a point to memorize faces and names and truly cares about you and your safety. The course itself is good; the topics can be overwhelming if you're unfamiliar with them, but she simplifies and makes them very digestible. Fair grading policies and no tests!

PLEASE TAKE THIS CLASS. Super easy A, interesting class discussions, Dr. Latimer is awesome too. And even if you don't care in the slightest about the topic, anyone with a prefrontal cortex can get an A in this class with just a bit of effort.

Dr. Latimer was such a wonderful professor! She made this class really straightforward. Put in the work and you'll get a good grade tbh. The weekly quizzes were pretty simple, and group assignments weren't bad either. I appreciate how it is clearly laid out what you need to do in this class. TAKE HER!!

Professor Latimer has been one of my favorite professors I have taken. Lectures are pretty easy to understand and everything can be found on the slides. There are weekly quizzes but they are open note. The weekly group assignments are not bad if you show up to class and pay attention. No final, just a final paper.

She is the best! One of the best professors I have had and I am taking another course by her next semester. She is very clear on what needs to be done, by when, and how. She is caring and you can tell she is passionate about her classes and what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Latimer isthe bes t professor I've taken. You can tell she is really passionate about what she teaches. Grades consist of knowledge checks, assignments, and quizzes. As long as you do them and pay attention, you'll pass. You won't suffer if you miss class and all of the assignments are super easy. I cannot recommend her enough, she is so great!

what a gem. she turns what could be a boring subject into something fun and interesting. she teaches health in a holistic way, and invites in guest speakers (and therapy dogs!) i always looked forward to her class. even the homework assignments are fun

An amazing professor, she really knows what she's doing. Even though there were like 100 students in the class, she really makes an effort to get to know people. Her lectures are really interesting and the tests are simple enough if you read the lecture slides. Homework is usually easy but you need to read the articles in the modules. I recommend!

This class is textbook heavy and you need to have done the readings in order to participate. The exams that she called "quizzes" were no less than 40 questions and repetitive and wordy. She offers extra credit but won't work with you on grades, I needed less than half a point to make a grade and she was not willing to budge and was passive about it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Latimer is an excellent professor and is extremely caring. For each module, you only need to read a few articles and respond to a discussion and there's occasionally a quiz at the end of the module.

Professor Latimer is very sweet and gives great lectures. She builds great relationships with her students. Quite a bit of discussion posts but all are very easy. Few other assignments here and there which are also easy. Definitely recommend.

Best class ever! Super easy A and Dr. Latimer is one of the kindest professors I've ever had. Fill out her study guides and look over them a couple of times before the exams for an A. Show up to class because she pretty much gives a point of extra credit every other day, which really boosts your grade. I literally ended up with a 99 at the end
I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! One of the best I've had. She is so interesting to listen to and she gives so much extra credit. I loved going to class and the tests were not hard if you pay attention!

She posts a study guide a week before the test. If you fill it out and study it then you're good for the test. The required textbook totally wasn't necessary (you only need it like 2-3 times anyways). I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures and didn't really need to take notes. Plus you'll get so many extra credit pts just by attending class.

Dr. Latimer is one of the most dynamic professors at UT. I loved her because she made the lectures actually interesting. There are 4 multiple choice tests that are very straightforward, and 2 essays that I finished the night before. She gives out way too much extra credit, that I could've skipped one of the essays and still get an A in the class
You are supposed to get a textbook, but I wouldn't because I never even looked at my textbook the whole semester. If you come to class and read the lecture slides before tests you will for sure pass.

tests are easy. attendance isn't mandatory but she gives out a lot of extra credit if you show up and she points out specific things that'll be on the tests. there are only two short papers; one research, one personal. readings are useful but not really necessary, only like one or two questions on tests come from the readings.

Dr. Latimer is by far my favorite professor Ive had! Her lectures are interesting and she encourages participation. She gives out extra credit just for showing up to class and has some todo outside. Her test are multiple choice and I never studied until the night before. She assigns readings but I never did them and did fine on the test.

hands down best professor I have ever had. she loves to hear what we have to say & she encourages participation in class. lectures are entertaining & while she doesn't require attendance, its helpful when taking exams. she occasionally gives credit if you come. easy course; 2 papers & 4 MC exams. if you love health, and children, take this class!!

She is the best!!!!! If you show up to class, you get extra credit. She gives so many outside extra credit opportunities on top of that. Tests are straight forward from the lecture power points. 4 tests total. She is a tough grader on papers, but there are only 2 papers total. In all, she is amazing & she keeps her lectures fun & interesting.

Dr. Latimer is the best. She's very open minded and has interesting discussions with her students in class. Awesome guest speakers. She gave extra credit which was awesome because we got to go to a yoga studio all semester for free. She also gives extra credit for just coming to class. She'll tell you exactly what is on the test during lecture!!!
She makes this class way harder than it needs to be. She is also incredibly rude to her students and treats them like children.

She's willing to help and gives study guides for her tests. It's best to have your class create a google doc and study that way. It's not imperative to keep up with the readings from the textbook but if you don't go to class you'll be lost until the times of the test. She's friendly and fun. We had two short papers but one of them took me six hours

I'm going to lock in and learn every physics principle, concept, thoroughly study every idea Albert Einstein had on relativity so that I can grow up, invent a time-machine to time travel back and not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Wickedly smart, and it's to her downfall. She's too qualified to teach this class. Doesn't teach very well, most lectures are just her writing over her own notes. She doesn't know how to teach people that are unfamiliar with the material. The tests were also next to impossible to complete in the allotted time.

Linda does not teach. She genuinely just writes over printed notes making them completely illegible. I pulled up to class but never bothered to take out my notebook because attempting to take notes is useless. If you ask her questions, she will proceed to answer a different question that you didn't ask. The only saving grace is the online midterms.

Very kind and extremely intelligent - too qualified to be teaching freshman physics honestly. I ended up mostly having to teach myself from the notes and Quest assignments, but her office hours are helpful too.

She is a wonderfully kind human. Lectures are kind of useless but mandatory, however you can zoom them. Homework's are long but doable, tests and quizzes are on quest. The worst part about this class is the TA. If you end up with Peter,  he judges you instead of helping you, and makes the mandatory discussion miserable. Hand to God I hope he quits.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were useless but participation is required. In my opinion, you would be better off skipping the lectures and self-teaching yourself from the posted notes. Exams are very rushed with not much time given for each problem. Homework was ~20 questions a week and only loosely based on the lecture notes.

Dr. Reichl as a person is wonderful and very sweet, but she can not teach. The only reason this class was doable was because of high school physics experience, so if you don't have any, please don't take her. Lectures go way too fast and she reads off of notes, not the best at explaining concepts during class. Tests are online but are fast paced

Avoid taking Reichl. She is a nice professor and there is no doubt that she is very knowledgeable, but when it comes to teaching its a different story. She condenses the textbook into "notes" which only consist of formulas and example problems and does not teach the class. Tests are online but she also gives you little time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you've never taken physics do not take this class. I wish someone would have told me so I could save my GPA a little bit. She is a nice teacher but I did not learn anything in class. Quizess were 50 min for 10 questions that took 10 min each.

She seems like a wonderful person but just simply doesn't teach. She makes an effort to explain but all she really does is read the textbook in class and suddenly expects her students to solve challenging questions. If you are taking this class, prepare to make a subscription on chegg for a full semester because that's all you got.

Professor Reichl is a great person but I did not like her teaching style. She mostly just read off PowerPoints and did not do too many example problems. If you have no previous physics knowledge then this class will be very hard. She also is not very tech-savvy so having the class fully online this semester made it even more difficult.
Great professor and very clear lecture notes. Stressed a lot but made it through.

Dr. Reichl is super knowledgeable and caring. This class does have a faster pace and covers a broader range of topics toward the end. Lectures are hard to follow along but the slides are great to read. Reading those before doing homework in Quest would make life much easier. It requires effort but is still doable.

Do not take this class. Prof Reichl has many admirable qualities such as her genius intellect but teaching is not one of them. She reads off the textbook and good luck if you can process what she says. Everything is unclear, there is no syllabus, and assignments are much different than the textbook she reads off of. Again, genius person, bad Prof.

I'm taking this class online because of covid. If you took AP physics and remember that, this class should work as a nice refresher. However, she simply reads from the textbook. Don't expect her to work any problems. Don't expect her to read the chat. DON'T TAKE IF YOU DIDNT TAKE AP PHYSICS IN HIGH SCHOOL OR IF ITS ONLINE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Reichl is NOT good at teaching. For her online class, all she did was read off of her PDFs during lectures. She didn't really explain physics concepts but instead just gave us formulas. I didn't really learn anything in her class, but at least we got to use notes on tests since they were online. Discussion sections were a waste of time as well.

Don't take this class, or actually try to avoid physics at UT in general if possible. If Peter is the TA, also do not take this class! Maybe she is a better professor in person but online just read notes with pre-worked examples. Added a test to the syllabus after the ice storm and final exam is worth large portion of grade, avoid at ALL costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Reichl is very accomplished in physics, but when teaching, it's mediocre at best. Unless you are already REALLY comfortable in physics, you will be struggling to understand anything the whole semester because the pacing is lightning speed. Granted, physics at Ut is already difficult as it is, so Reichl isn't the worst if you learn on your own.

Professor Reichl is a sweet lady, but she is past her years of teaching. Linda read incoherent lecture notes word for word that she had written down, and many times got herself confused. This is the worst class I have taken at UT, and avoid her at all costs.

She's kind, passionate and knowledgable. The material moves quickly, and so do her lectures. The discussion sessions (graded) are very useful for filling in holes. The twice-a-week HW and tests (one drop, mandatory final) are difficult but standard across all 303K sections/professors. Not sure how the curve works or how much it helps. 0% textbook

Very top notch professor, the material is really hard for physics but I feel she does a great job doing her best and she always tries to bump the curve as much as she can. Sometimes her class can be dreadfully long spent on homework problems rather than the actual material.25 percent of the grade comes from HW, discussion attendance and attendance

Really great lectures and is extremely knowledgeable. Gives some extra credit, but there are lots of test study materials which is helpful. Course is extremely organized and it is difficult to forget deadlines because she gives tons of reminders

Professor Mitchell is a wonderful professor! I had her for CH301 and CH302 because I loved her teaching style and class format. Yes, there are daily quizzes, but I found them to be more beneficial for ingesting material one quiz at a time; for me, I'd rather have more quizzes with fewer topics than fewer quizzes with more topics. Take her for chem!

her course is so organized! quizzes are daily so attendance is mandatory. i personally found her canvas course more helpful than lectures. she has a lot of opportunities to reach her outside of class and a lot of resources to study for tests. provides enough extra credit to bump you up a letter grade. i struggle w chem but 301 wasn't so bad!

A great professor who gives so many resources to succeed. She gives lots of extra credit, her lectures are amazing, and has plenty of study resources. Daily quizzes in class which are surprisingly helpful and helped me from procrastinating for tests. The learning modules and review notes are the only things I used to study.

She's a very great lecturer. I had her for CH301 and am taking her for chem 2 as well now. The actual content can be a lot but if you put in the work, an A is well within reach. Just show up to lectures, do the extra credit, and study a few days before midterms and you'll do well. She's very reasonable and has a very clear grading criteria.
Good professor so easy but some people are silly and fail the exams so as long as you show up to classes youll get a 100 on each midterm and then not even have a final unless if you are a brick
dr. mitchell is so sweet and accessible, and she has great lectures and clear format for class. i went to her office hours, and she is just as kind and helpful as she is in lecture.

Every class was a lecture then a quiz over the material from the prior lecture. There is a lot of extra credit offered and extra studying material for exams. She teaches pretty well and her lectures are engaging.

I love Mitchell so much; she is the best and so passionate about her subject. Very test-heavy (4 exams worth 80%), but Chemistry is standardized, so you know exactly what is going to be on the test and what you need to know, and instead of a final, you can retake up to 2 exams.

Very clear lectures, offers a lot of resources to help, spends time thoughtfully answering questions, and very time-efficient with the material. Put in minimal work and it should be a very easy course.

Truly caring professor and the structure of the class is beyond amazing. If you don't like quizzes, maybe reconsider, but some get dropped and I felt they were very helpful for checking comprehension throughout the unit! Just do the learning modules and halfway study for the quizzes (unit study guides were lifesavers) and you'll be fine.

Mitchell's class is organized and she responds to emails very quickly. The class has exam retakes but I wouldn't depend on them. I had to retake two tests in two hours and only miss two questions for an A at the end. The retake policy can enable procrastination. The quizzes really matter in the end by making the difference between an A- and B+.

Take Dr. Mitchell! Her lectures are easy to follow, and she provides practice exams that closely match the real ones. She offers plenty of extra credit and a wide variety of study materials that reflect actual quiz/test questions. There is a quiz every class, but it's manageable if you keep up with studying. She is very kind and supportive.

If you are not great with quizzes (one every class), her course might not be for you. However, there are many extra credit opportunities available and lots of studying resources. She seems nice as well. However, she has incorrectly solved some problems on lectures and has incorrect answers on quizzes, putting her course credibility in question.

My favorite Professor so far! She was an amazing lecturer. Best thing about her course was that it was so easy to understand what the exams and quizzes would be over, and she gave out excellent study materials. Your success in this course depends on if you put in the effort to do well, but she doesn't make it difficult or tedious to do so. 10/10

if u are scared about gen chem, dont be!! Professor Mitchell is literally the best. The exams are exactly like the practice ones that she provides you can also RETAKE exams if you did bad on them during finals week (which means there isnt a final!!). SHES SO SO SO GOOD HIGHLY RECCOMEND! so much extra credit too (ended the class with a 101%)

Dr. Mitchell is an amazing professor; I absolutely recommend for gen chem! Her lectures are very clear and she provides follow-along notes with practice problems. Offers a ton of extra credit throughout the semester and has SO many resources for exam prep. I was scared to take chemistry before coming here but I'm so glad I had her as my professor.

I love Dr. Mitchell :) She explains everything in detail during the lecture and is very caring during office hours. Also, the class felt personalized even though there were over 500 people in this class, and even though there was a quiz each class, it made me feel more prepared when the test came around compared to other classes!

Great lectures! Professor Mitchell is also easy to get to know! She always takes the time to motivate students about their grade. There is an abundance of extra credit available at all times. She begins every class by playing music. She gives quizzes every class, which tend to be pretty easy if you study lecture notes. 100% the best gen chem class.

She's the best professor I've ever had. It's obvious that she genuinely cares for her students and makes sure that they're following along during lecture. She outlines every type of question that you could see on the exam so that you're not blindsided. Homework is very manageable. Quizzes every class, but they truly help you prepare for exams.

I love Dr. Mitchell!! She is a fantastic lecturer, and she explains everything so clearly. She teaches you exactly what will be on the exams. 5-question quizzes taken in class every day, lowest few are dropped. Practice exams are very similar to the real exams. Up to 3% extra credit offered. Taking her for 302 next sem, genuinely enjoyed her class.

Was super scared going in for chem but explains everything well with good pacing. Discusses resources and dates at the beginning of class knowing the class is mainly freshman. Learning modules and quizzes every class but drops some and there's a variety of extra credit opportunities. Also you can retake 2 exams up to 100%.

There's two lectures a week and a short quiz each lecture. Study guides in this class help you with literally everything. Extra credit opportunities everywhere, and you can re-take 2 midterms at the end of the semester. Very helpful and kind professor.

Dr. Mitchell's genchem1 is lecture-heavy but she explains concepts well and opens the floor to questions very often. Pop quizzes are frequent, but as long as you do the review before and understand the concept through doing examples, you'll be okay, same goes for exams. Practice x3. She's such a caring person as well and an all around great person.

Professor Mitchell is a great lecturer and very communicative from the beginning about what to expect from her course. There are two quizzes a week over what was covered in the previous lecture, and four exams which make up most of your grade. Plenty of extra credit opportunities and the ability to retake two exams make it very easy to succeed.

Excellent at explaining topics clearly and clarifies confusing points. Course is 80% exams, so prepare for those! There was a 10 min quiz at the end of almost every lecture (2 per week). Lots of extra credit. Ed discussion board, very organized and extensive canvas resources, and Sage AI tutor bot help with studying A LOT.

Professor Mitchell is an amazing lecturer and explains the topics very well. After each lecture, there is a quiz on the last lecture's topics. She does drop a few quizzez and gives multiple extra credits. The class is very test-heavy, but it can be easily passed with the materials she gives us. I highly recommend her, and she is very approachable.

Amazing professor. In class demonstrations are so fun, speaks slowly and clearly and has super easy-to-follow lectures. She always gives opportunities to ask questions (even dumb ones) and answers them with comprehensive answers. The QT and practice questions on Canvas help a lot. There's little room for mistakes to get an A, no curve, some EC.
loved mitchell. we had quizzes every class but the topics were well taught so they weren't too hard. Im taking her again next semester

Professor Mitchell is a great lecturer and class is clearly structured. She has interesting demos during most classes and clearly cares a lot for her students, providing frequent reminders of upcoming events indirectly/directly relevant to class so students are informed. The exams and quizzes are easy, with dropped quizzes and retakes on exams

I love Professor Mitchell!! Lectures were always clear and full of useful information. She offers generous extra credit opportunities & so many resources to prepare for exams. There are quizzes at the end of each class covering material from the previous lecture, but she drops some of them. The class is definitely easy if you've taken ap chem!

Dr. Mitchell is a wonderful professor. Her lectures are concise and greatly help in understanding the content we need to know. At the end of every lecture, there is a quiz testing content and allowing you to learn the content over time making you more prepared for the test. There is EC and you can access lecture videos from home.

Mitchell is an amazing professor. Her lectures are very straightforward with many practice problems that you work together that correlate directly with the exam. She offers lots of extra credit/recources and is the sweetest.

Genuinely no complaints about this professor. Super kind and the lectures were easy to follow. Additionally, the coursework was very strategically laid out and it was hard not to learn from her. She's the one!

Class is structured the exact same as CH301 with 4 exams and hw on ALEKS but the material is definitely a lot more complicated so don't take it too lightly in the beginning. Mitchell had good lectures even though I never went usually and just self learned the material with the learning modules. Definitely better than most chemistry professors here.

Genuinely an amazing professor. Dr. Mitchell is a great lecturer and very accessible. She's approachable as well and always kind when answering questions. I wish I could take her for every Chemistry class ever.
provides a lot of resources to succeed in class and genuinely wants everyone to do their best
I took her for CH301 and CH302 and she organizes these classes very well. She provides lots of resources for studying. She is very approachable. I recommend.

I love Dr Mitchell! I took her both semesters and she made chem so light. Lots of extra credit is given and many resources prepare you for success on midterms such as comprehensive review notes, learning modules, and practice exams. I also liked how she did notes in class it really helped me retain and learn the information needed for the exams.

I had mitchell for gen 1 + 2, and I love her teaching method. Her lectures are follow along notes as she does them herself to ensure students are paying attention to the material as well. She has lots of extra credits. The quizzes are a little fast paced but easy if you understand the topic and she drops 3. Lots of practice on canvas for exams.

I wouldn't take her class if you are trying to get a A and learn more about chemistry. You will come away learning surface level material, from lecture and weekly quizzes, then be tested on very niche question types during exams. Often nothing like practice exams, though the review questions are somewhat helpful. Laude all the way, trust me

While she's a alright teacher, I would really recommend against taking her. She really speeds through her lectures, and make sure to study every single thing literally, as she will put emphasis on other topics and question types during lecture and homework, and half of the 25 questions are on topics we barley covered. No review lectures either.

Mitchell was wonderful! Got an A in CH301 & A- in CH302. Tests are pretty easy, 25 question MC. 2 retakes. Good amount of extra credit. She offers a lot of practice materials & she's very kind and helpful in office hours. You'll leave her class feeling like you have a good understanding of gen chem.

loooove dr mitchell. the class is essentially ap chemistry but she has such a clear passion for the subject i didnt even care. had her at 8 am and still managed to pay attention to the lectures. the best part of this class is the learning objectives she provides for each exam that go over exactly what you need to know. makes studying way easier

I LOVE DR. MITCHELL. took 301 in fall '24. the structure of this class was so organized. she's a great lecturer. 4 exams, can retake up to 2, no final. lots of resources and practice exams/problems were great for prepping for tests. LOOK @ STUDY GUIDES. great class & great prof, would recommend!

Mitchell is so sweet and has very comforting calm energy, which was great since I took her 8:00am. She really cares for her students and is so cute. She covers basically everything you need to know in lecture, but it is def your job to study the question types thoroughly to make sure you know absolutely everything.

easy class. they bail u out since u can retake 2 of the 4 midterms for up to a 100. i took her for ch 301 and 302; never had to retake one. had a 100 n a 99 in a class for ch 301 and 302, respectively. extremely easy. if u don't get an a, i don't know what to tell u: u have every chance in the world to get one.

I had Dr. Mitchell for CH301 as well and I loved her lecture style since she didn't speed through any material and frequently asked for questions. Had a good experience in this class despite not taking AP chem in HS, never felt like I was far behind. Take advantage of all the study modules, practice exams, and extra credit!

Mitchell is such a sweet professor, and she makes CH302 so easy to learn! The only thing is that the quizzes can get a little difficult as they are made by the chem department not her, so the lectures don't fully match up with them. However, she still drops three of them and offers lots of extra credit, so its worth it. Study the QT for tests!

I had Mitchell for 301 and 302 for her first year at UT. She's definitely a good lecturer and can be very thorough. She offers many opportunities for questions during class and answers them very well. I would recommend using this to your advantage and asking all the questions that you can. Definitely should take her!

Dr. Mitchell is great! Ch 302 is objectively somewhat difficult, but she does a great job explaining and is very open to questions. Tests are very fair and if you study and look at the review notes/ practice test, you'll do fine! She's very sweet and even gave us ice cream the last day of class! Would definitely recommend :)

After a horrible fall semester with a different professor, Dr. Mitchell was a breath of fresh air. Her lectures are excellent and genuinely interesting at times. This course is the same as all other genchem classes: graded mostly by exams, but questions are very reasonable and you can retake them at the end of the semester. Overall great professor!

Professor Mitchell was really good at explaining topics! All of CH301 and CH302 are the same format so you'll likely get the same experience with every professor. Make sure to review the review notes, practice exam, and lectures and you'll be totally okay for the class (I did not take AP Chem).

Your grade is 80% exams, but you can retake any 2 of them for a final and replace your grade with the higher score. The exams are really not that hard either. Pay attention in lecture, review HW before quizzes, and understand the review notes. Easy A if you put in the effort.

Dr. Mitchell is an amazing professor with lots of knowledge about chemistry! Her tests were average and you can retake up to two at the end of the year to boost your grade. I got to know her really well in office hours and by asking questions during and after class, which helped me have a good relationship with her and end with a great grade.

Great teacher, almost as good if not better than Laude with her lectures (very visual and she draws out lots of diagrams to explain the processes). Tests are fair, and you can redo two of them even if you mess up at the end of the semester. She's very nice, I liked her homemade ice cream she gave out at the end of the year. Test are 80% of average.
I took Dr. Mitchell for both 301 and 302! She is awesome and I love her lecture style. The class is very organized and manageable.

She's the best, took her for 301 and 302. Only lectures (Instapolls but once you hit 30 it doesn't matter), quizzes (weighted so little they don't effect you and she drops some), and Exams which are weighted heavy. So easy to get a 100 on the exam if you just look at her review notes. Out of all 8 exams for 301 and 302, I got a 100 on 7 of them.
if you want to actually learn take laude and get a easy A, and also only morning classes and TAs are useless

Took Mitchell for both CH301 and CH302 and she's goated. To get an A+ ur gonna have to study a bit outside of class but she lectures really well and she hosts office hours which are really helpful. HIGHLY recommend taking her!

I decided to take Mitchell for CH302 and she was great! She is a bit fast paced when it comes to lecturing but she is sweet and always makes sure to address any questions the class has. There is two replacement exams instead of a final and she gives up to 30 extra credit points. She also gave us ice cream as an end of the year reward!

For CH302. Literally the best professor in the entire gen chem department. Once you answer 30 instapoll questions then you literally dont even have to show up anymore. Homework is on ALEKS and its a hit or miss. Weekly quizzes are aight. Not flipped
Clear grading scheme, good lectures, opportunity to retake 2 out of 4 exams instead of a final (exams are weighted at 80%). Had her for both CH301 and CH302, nothing negative to say, she was awesome!

This review is for CHEM302. 
She's great at explaining stuff, and she provides a lot of review material for exams. She doesn't give you PowerPoints to write on because it isn't as effective for learning, but it's helpful, at least for me. Exams are easy if you study.

I have had mitchell for 301 and 302. She prepares us for the tests a week before the test so we have time to study by taking the practice exams and practice questions that she uploads. I have never talked to her but i love her and she is a smart icon. I never needed to go to the review sessions because she taught so well in lecture.

She is amazing and a very good teacher. constantly stops and asks if we have questions. I dont feel nervous to go speak to her and she is very available to her students even though it is around a 200-300 lecture. she is a queen

During the Lecture, she writes all notes on the screen relating to what's relevant to the quizzes and tests which is very generous. She has all of the important notes listed on Canvas so you can study, as well as many practice questions and tests. The test is 80% of your grade, but she provides plenty of study material. She also records lectures.

She is very good at explaining the concepts and she writes out the notes during class so she doesn't move too fast. She is also very clear about what is expected from students and there isn't anything unnecessary in her class. The homework and lectures are all very helpful. I highly recommend taking CH301 and CH302 with her.

I loved Professor Mitchell! Her lectures were easy to follow, and she wrote her notes alongside the students, so the class went at an easy pace. Attendance isn't mandatory because she posts them, but I would def still go because you'll pay more attention. Look at the review one pagers and do the practice tests and you'll do fine.

I'm taking CH302 now with another professor and definitely took Mitchell for granted. Mitchell is a great teacher and explains every little detail well. She truly knows how to teach chemistry unlike my professor now.

Mitchell's is amazing! Her lectures were concise + recorded in case of absence. There are also lots of resources for quizzes and tests! However, I'm in CH302 now and she's started using the homework platform, ALEKS. It's TERRIBLE- doesn't help with learning and will count answers wrong if there's no decimal point/incorrect capitalization of units.

Any issues or complaints you would have would mostly be up to the class itself and not the professor. I didn't really remember any chemistry from high school, but I was able to do well. The lectures are fast paced, but great. With the practice exams on canvas, you can definitely do well on exams.

Since Chem 301 is standardized for all courses, it really shouldn't be different if you have different professors, but I really think that if you can you should take Dr Mitchell's class. Her lectures are really helpful and genuinely make you learn so much. As someone who had no background in chem I honestly think she's the best prof to learn from.

Dr. Mitchell is the best general chemistry professor that you can take. She is an amazing lecturer while giving lots of extra credit. Make sure to study all of the topic review slides in Canvas as the quizzes and tests are based around the examples!
Test heavy, but that's how all chem classes are. You aren't required to do learning modules like other courses, and you are allowed a calculator. Overall a simple but good class.

Four exams makeup 80% of your grade. You can retake two of those exams. Her lectures are very interesting but fast paced, but the online lecture captures are extremely useful if you miss anything. The instapolls are a pain if you're not at the lecture. just make some friends there, and you should be fine

Decent professor; was kind of hard to get to know her personally. Exam criteria was clear enough, and you have the ability to redo up to 2 exams with the new CH301 program. Lectures are recorded, so do recognize that is an option if you are unable to attend all lectures. Take notes as given and don't be afraid to do supplemental material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you did well in a HS chem class, Mitchell is the easiest. All info covered in lecture, no HW learning modules like other profs. 10-20 qs weekly HWs, practice tests similar to real, quizzes are 4-5 qs, attendance through InstaPoll - need 30 points, 1-3 given per class.  Extra cred opportunities at end. Lots of review/office hours if you need it

Dr. Mitchell gives STEM baddie, she's a good lecturer and very transparent when it comes to due dates and preparing for what exactly will be on exams. You have the opportunity to retake 2 exams for full credit, and she gives a generous amount of extra credit and dropped classes. UT did their big one by hiring her, looking forward to CH302 with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mitchell had great lectures with frequent poll questions as well as making sure that all questions were answered before moving on to different topics. The class itself was very test heavy with exams being worth 80% and hw+ weekly quizzes+ extra things 20%, but before every test (25 mcq for 1hr 15 min) there was a review session. rlly great!

The instructor checks for understanding throughout the lecture with poll questions, which counts for attendance. There are so many practice questions available for studying for the exams. You do have to teach yourself a bit, but office hours are super helpful; utilize them! Overall, the instructor is super approachable and helpful.

Fast paced lectures where most learned is done outside of class by reteaching the material to yourself. Though I do respect Dr. Mitchell, this class is very demanding on you being able to understand the material straight away. Especially when in a 500 person class! Still learned a bunch! However it is a very different teaching style!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was supposed to have Professor Biberdorf and was initially disappointed when she left, however, having Dr. Mitchell as my teacher was one of the best things to happen this semester. She truly understands what it's like to be a freshman and for everything to be difficult. She provides an immense amount of extra practice and extra credit.
Super engaging lectures; it's chemistry it's hard but Dr. Mitchell is super kind and helpful. Highly recommend! Taking her again for 302

Dr. Mitchell was the best professor I had my first semester! She is knowledgeable and teaches the subjects well for us to remember and learn.
