His lectures were completely insightful and though provoking. I am lucky that I was in a program that made it mandatory to be placed in his class. Best class to take while entering college.
Very smart - Hilarious - Laid back - Outgoing

This class is interesting to attend every day and he's a great professor, truly inspiring and really likes to get to know his students. The books  in the class are very interesting as well and exams are based on it. The tests are free response and there's always an essay question. Attending class is never mandatory.  Easy history class!!

Dr. Moore is an inspiring lecturer. He discusses issues that are sensitive and keep the class engaged. All the books he assigned were great reads. The tests were based off the books and some lecture material but because the books were so easy to read, the tests were also easy. Even if you don't have the class, stop to listen to one of his lectures!

Dr. Moore was absolutely amazing! I have never had a professor as passionate as he was towards what he was teaching. There was a lot of variety in the topics he spoke about. The tests cover the assigned books. If you skim the books, you will be just fine. Super easy exams.
Love the lecture but it is not connected to the way the class is graded. Dr. Moore and the TA's seem to be on a different page so it was sometimes confusing.

I honestly think if you take this UGS303 class...  you will learn so much! I loved his lectures but it's really your TA that you have to discuss your grades with. So more than the professor, your TA makes a bigger difference. Dr, Moore is so knowledgeable and makes his classes "real" because we discuss about topics that are eye-opening!

Dr. Moore was an amazing lecturer. You could tell that he seriously cared about the success of each student in a 500+ person class. There was a lot of reading, but it was spaced out far enough that it wasn't too bad. 1 quiz, 3 essay tests, and 1 project made up the grades. I would HIGHLY recommend Dr. Moore.

Race in the Age of Obama one great class. His novel selections, along with his lectures are so current; it keeps many of today's students interested. This is definitely a great class; I would not stop talking about the issues brought up in class. Tests were pretty easy, and the writing assignments weren't tough either.

Dr. Moore's class is an amazing choice for so many reasons. Not only does he discuss controversial issues that are not often looked at. He also discusses other issues that can help incoming freshman look at themselves from a different perspective and help them look at their future and how they can make themselves successful. He is a great lecturer.
Amazing. I loved the way he would show different points of view according to a certain issue. Also, the readings were good and the class is nowhere near boring

Dr. Moore is great he helps you understand different point of views in different topics. He is always engaged and the books we read for his class are not boring at all, they are very interesting. His tests are also easy. You can get an easy A in this course!

Dr. Moore's Race in the Age of Obama was one of my favorite courses. The reading was all very good. The lectures were even better. He truly is passionate about the subject he teaches and loves to challenge student views. Expect to laugh and be open-minded!

Probably the easiest A you'll have at UT. Very interesting, engaging and eye opening lectures, and all tests were easy and over a combination of the book you're reading and his lectures. Basically, show up and have a good understanding of the books and you'll do great.

This guy is raw and real in his lectures. He might come off a little irrational but what he says is true, and makes you change your perception. Honestly, you can get by reading the books on sparknotes, but the books assigned are usually good.

Interesting lectures but the course was extremely disorganized- no textbooks or powerpoints and Dr. Moore posted little to none on Canvas. All exams are free response/essay and can be quite difficult unless you know the material from the assigned reading and lectures extremely well. Dr. Moore is a quite liberal professor, lectures are verypolitical

Dr. Moore is one of the most inspiring professors I will probably ever have in my collegiate career. His lectures are thought-provoking and influential. However, he is very disorganized when it comes to testing and assignments; he said it himself that he doesn't want to be "tied down by a syllabus". He's also very difficult to contact via email.

I took both his UGS303 and Black Power Movement course. Easily the most interesting professor I've had. While attendance isn't mandatory, I don't see why you would want to skip his lectures. He encourages people to debate with him and opens many eyes to issues that we may not always think about. Just take notes and read the books for an easy A.

The class itself wasn't hard. Test were easy and based off of the books and his lectures. I didn't like how the lectures were almost never relevant to the book or the subject of the class. I didn't like how he presented his opinions as if they were facts, but other than that he was O.K.

Dr. Moore is literally one of my favorite professors of my collegiate career. I actually look forward to all of his classes, and have never missed one. I even get upset when he cancels class. My friends who aren't even in his class come to our lectures just to hear him speak. He's very opinionated so don't be sensitive but he's also VERY inspiring.
I took the Race in the Age of Obama. It's an easy class to take as an elective. He's a really good speaker. Through this class I leaned a lot about myself and other people.

Dr. Moore is perhaps one of my best professors because he presents his ideas on controversial topics in such a way that once you take his class, your eyes are opened and you see things in a much different way than before. 3 tests, 1 projectassignment worth 20%, and the tests were free response, and easy. Attendance is not required, but go anyway!
He is by far the most amazing professor and easily connects with his students

Dr. Moore's lectures in the Black Power Movement class are funny, thought-provoking, and changed the way I view many issues surrounding race. However, a major problem with this class was a lack of organization. Moore rarely returns emails, doesn't provide clear instructions, and generally gives little attention to student's concerns.

Dr. Moore's class is very powerful. Very low workload. Lectures are great, once you see how he is you wont want to miss them. He cancels class a few times in the semester. This isn't your typical class. This class will prepare you for the real world in ways other courses will not. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Dr. Moore is the type of professor that wants you to be globally competitive, he is here for you and wants you not to be afraid of either success or failure. If you participate in his lectures all the time, you're in for some good debates. He is very critical because he wants us to be ready for what's out there in the real world. He creates leaders

Dr. Moore is incredible. Great lectures and great fun. However, I feel awful about being a middle-class male every time I walk out of there. But he admits, if you walk out of there thinking, he knows he's doing his job correctly.

I could say hands down my favorite course and professor at UT. He is very funny and interesting lectures. Does assign novels but always interesting to read. Highly recommend to take his course before graduating.

Always very captivating. This class taught me things about life I NEEDED to know. There was a lot of novel reading but all the books were pretty interesting. He did make a lot of sports references - beware.
Dr. Moore is absolutely the best professor at UT. Very funny, intelligent and engaging. He encourages student to think outside the box and share their ideas and opinions. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Dr.Moore's class was absolutely AMAZING ( Fall 2013)! We had 3 tests (all essay based) and 4 short writing assignments,. I got an A in his calss.He is really kind and cares about students.He told us once that if we didn't have somewhere to go for Thanksgiving that the doors to his home where open.

One of the best professors at UT hands down (and definitely my favorite). He's much more interested in critical thinking and learning rather than bubbling in answers. He's engaging and honest. I wish he taught more classes so I could take one each semester.
Black Power Movement with Dr. Moore was extremely engaging, fun, and you can take a lot away from his class. Tests are essay and multiple choice but they change each year. Go to lecture and STUDY
He is amazing, there is absolutely no way you can fail this class. He makes class fun so you actually want to attend, it's not like your being forced to go.

He's a great professor! Every class session seemed to go so fast because it was that much fun. He talked about life, and various things that a lot of college students need to hear. I'd recommend this class to everybody! There were 2 tests, 1 group project, and a few papers, but the class is still a great class.

One the most enjoyable professors to listen to. Easy class, even if  you haven't read the books. You can totally B.S. your way to an A, but the material is interesting so most people typically don't. He's very funny and opinionated. Encourages class discussion of major issues. Take this class!

Took him for the Obama class. Absolutely great professor. Has his own opinions, but encourages the class to voice their own. I NEVER read the books, but managed to get A's on all tests. Go to class, not because you have to, but because it's fun!

AMAZING CLASS AND PROFESSOR! TAKE THIS CLASS. read & take notes and you will get an A plus no doubt. Funny professor. His lectures are not mandatory but they are so good and interesting, you will want to come anyways. He is actually a pastor, so he knows how to keep students engaged. Easiest A you will ever get at UT. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This is the UGS 303 The Race in the Age of Obama. Just read the books get notes from class and you will get an A. Easy as hell class with a funny ass professor. Sometimes he goes overboard, but I don't care, I just took care of this dumb UGS credit
He is a great professor, and can inspire you even if you have no background in music or Jazz.

This class is genuinely interesting, and Sailors makes it even better just because of his passion for the subject. The class is extremely easy if you pay even a tiny bit of attention, most of your grade is made up of the Cerego portion, which is like Duolingo for Jazz.
Dr Sailors is a very awesome professor. I took this class for my VAPA but I would absolutely take him again. He is very passionate about Jazz and it shows through his lectures.

Honestly ended up finding the content very interesting, despite not really enjoying jazz prior to taking this class. Now, I really can appreciate jazz whenever I hear it! The lectures are great and interesting, and the Cerego sets are totally manageable as long as you don't start late. Really easy class that I really enjoyed.

Girl. Just take this class. You don't need to love jazz, but it's definitely an easy class. That said, it does come with work but it's nothing that should be giving you a headache. Only thing that may be bothersome to some people is to actually go out to a concert. I went to the free UT Jazz Combo nights at Mozarts and loved it.
Superrr chill guy. He wants to see his students do well and that's evident with how simple the class is. Easy A for sure.
Great professor, would definitely recommend taking jazz appreciation as a VAPA. You will earn an A if you keep up with the class (less than an hour a day).

It was a pretty easy class over all. The worst part was the closed note in-class-quizzes by far, but you could find what to study beforehand in a review he posts. Besides that you need to attend 2 jazz concerts outside of class and write a small paper for both. There is a final exam, but you can finish in the allotted time. Take it for sure!

Great music, way too much content. The summer online edition of this course tries to fit 9 jazz eras into 5 weeks. The required videos started feeling like complete noise after a point. Ridiculous emphasis on memorization. You need to know tons of artist and song names for weekly closed-note quizzes and final exam. Too much time spent on fusion.

Cerego is a bit annoying but easy to complete. Lectures are 15- 30-ish minutes have 6-8 instapolls and there's like 6 per module and 4 modules per week. great guy, DO CEREGO AND LISTENING QUIZZES. Those will TANK your grade if you forget. Easy class jsut keep up
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is straightforward but the communication was frustrating at times. Having to attend and write papers on two jazz concerts was cumbersome, and it didn't help that they didn't list any on-campus options despite there being some. I found lectures to be long, rambly, and boring, but because of instapolls they are essentially mandatory.

Dr. Sailors was a great professor and made jazz fun and exciting. The part of going to concerts for a grade and writing about them was fun. Make sure you show up to every class for your instapolls there's a lot (100, graded for 90). Overall the class was very enjoyable.

easy VAPA. one quiz a week and all the answers can be found in the lectures. most of the grade is cerego and as long as you do it you you're fine. attend two jazz concerts and write a 500 word paper but its so easy.

The class is easy as can be; however, Sailors and the TA both have this off putting ego that I could never get behind, always answering questions snarkily. Youre also required to go two jazz concert which you must attend in person and get autographs from the performers as proof. This totally defeated the purpose of an online class and was annoying.

Super easy VAPA if you just do the work. About 1, 5 question quiz a week and all the answers can be found word for word in the previous lecture. Majority of your grade comes from Cerego Homework which is so easy as long as you just do it. You are required to go to two jazz concerts a semester and write a 500 word paper but its graded super easy.
Super chill class and easy to manage if you have other demanding classes. It was also really fun. An easy A

The easiest class ever to take for your VAPA, quizzes and final exam wasn't bad at all, two writing assignments that require you to attend jazz shows in-person that aren't graded too harshly, lecture attendance is mandatory because of Instapolls, but you get 10 drops, make sure to start Cerego ASAP to get the highest grade possible.

Easy choice for a VAPA! The class is well-organized with online practice sets, weekly quizzes, 2 writing assignments, and a final. It introduces various jazz styles, and it's rewarding to recognize facts during the required jazz concert and once the class has ended. Stay on top of the Cerego sets to succeed!
You do the work and you get a very good grade, simple as that.
Its a chill class until you have an unfortunate situation and the professor doesn't care about what you went through (even with proper documentation) as the deadline is of more significance anyways.
What more can you ask for? Minimal work + guaranteed A + VAPA + Cultural Diversity
Teaching style is very boring. He just tends to play a lot of music during classes and expects analysis. Also, do not expect any mercy for unforseen circumstances as a deadline is a deadline.

Professor Sailors has a very structured class. Do not get behind in Cerego because you will not be able to catch back up due to mandatory breaks the site makes you take. The essays are graded fairly and the events you attend are super fun. Overall, a great VAPA and really easy to get an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a light class. The class is a good experience, introducing different types of jazz and some of the historic context. You won't retain most of the information from this class, but it might just change your perspective and give you some good info to recognize when you hear it again

Good choice for a VAPA as everyone would agree! Classwork consists of 1 cumulative final, weekly quizzes and online practice questions, and 2 writing assignments where you must attend a jazz concert in person. The difficulty is not high for any of these. Very interesting and fun class!
Very easy VAPA credit. There are a few times you have to attend a concert and write a paper. Most of your grade will be from online flashcards, instapolls, and in class quizzes.

This is THE vapa class to take at UT. Super easy class with instapolls, quizzes, memory flashcards activities, final exam, and concert write-ups which was 100% manageable with a tough schedule. Very passionate professor for a game-changing class at UT
easiest class I've taken. Just make sure to start your Cerego sets early because there is a mandatory day break (sometimes multiple days) every so many questions.
Great class to take for a VAPA, not a lot of work if you stay on top of it early.

BEST VAPA! This class was very easy and chill. Just make sure to actually do the Cerego everyday. Lectures were really interesting and it was nice having the class online. A couple of written assignments but they are easy to do.

Easiest class at UT. I never paid attention to a single lecture and I have a 100 in the class. Throughout the sem u have to attend 2 concerts and write essays about them, but the essays can be written in 30 minutes. Commit  like 3 minutes to Cerego a day and you're gucci --don't fall behind on it!

Love Dr. Sailors and I liked his assignments on watching concerts. The essays are so easy and MAX 500 words. Super easy to do the music learning if you just do them every night for 10 minutes and easy easy A of a class.
Take him. Super easy VAPA and CD Flag. Honestly kinda interesting too. Guaranteed A just do your Cerago on time.

This class is so easy and fun. TAKE FOR VAPA. You'll get to listen to a lot of amazing music, go to fun concerts, and even be able to recognize Jazz forms and eras. The lectures will have him playing music at the same time and you get to watch videos and listen to music for this. If you want a chill GPA boost take this class.

TAKE THIS CLASS FOR YOUR VAPA!!! Very easy and light workload! The class is online and you have to log on to complete "instapolls" for participation but it is fun to hear Dr. Sailors play music during class and the lectures are interesting!

I took this class thinking it would be an easy A (which it was) but I left with far more. Dr. Sailors' passion for jazz is reflected in his hands-on assignments that ask you to attend jazz shows (or watch a streamed show!). Overall it helped me rediscover my love for live music, and discover a new genre that has so much to offer.
Super engaging, easy A if you just pay attention and show up to lectures. Take this as your VAPA if you can

cerego sets worth majority of ur grade. DONT WAIT TILL LAST MINUTE BECAUSE THERE ARE REQUIRED BREAKS IN BETWEEN THAT COULD LAST ABOUT 3 DAYS BEFORE U CAN CONTINUE THE LESSON. weekly in class quizzes 5 questions each, you can literally find all the questions on quizlet. 2 papers 500 words (grading based on TAs). Attendance mandatory with instapolls
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: EASY A+ CLASS. All the answers for quizzes and tests were on quizlet. You have to join the video stream 2 times a week because there are instapolls that you have to click on (they are graded on participation so just click whatever answer it doesn't matter). It's cool to vibe out and listen to Sailors play the trumpet and sing. I recommend.

Chill and knowledgeable guy. Info in lectures can feel like a lot and scrambled. Grade is mainly based on pre-paced Cerego flashcards that you have to start early and do consistently to get full credit- can seem like a lot at first but you get the hang of it and it's basically completion. Easy VAPA credit and get to learn cool things

Very easy class, but definitely has a bit of work. Cerego sets (which are like flashcards) will take hours to complete, and almost weekly closed-note quizzes to study. Attendance mandatory (instapolls). Two easy writing assignments and 1 easy final, so overall, would highly recommend it! Just be prepared to spend a few hours per week on this class.
Professor Sailors is a great man. He understands that most taking this course are a Jazz fan and he teaches the material to that crowd. This class is an easy A as long as you show up.

Very talented and it was neat to see jazz performances during class! As a bio major, absolutely loved the class and the way is was structured. Dr. Sailors wants his students to learn and do well. Online class is mandatory for instapolls. GREAT music class to take - loved it!!

This class was pretty interesting. There's not much studying if you know the basics from lecture. There's a short quiz during class almost every week, so attendance is important (instapolls too). There's a few writing assignments, but they're straight forward. I would highly highly recommend this class for those who need their VAPA credit.

Must attend class because there are installs throughout it which are graded. There are a couple of essays throughout which are straightforward and easy. Majority of the grading is Cerego which you must purchase (cheap) and it's easy to complete and do. Super easy class and you are lucky to get it.

Very easy class for a VAPA. Quizzes once a week over information given during the lectures can be pretty specific, definitely helps to pay attention. The two essays and final exam were extremely easy and graded easy as well. Dr. Sailors is passionate about his teaching, so even the long online lectures are enjoyable to watch.

Professor Sailors is amazing! It is clear he loves talking about jazz and teaching it. Grading consists of Cerego sets, which you should never start near the due date, writing assignments, attendance, in-class quizzes, and final exam. He provides all the resources needed to succeed in this class. Should take this if VAPA credit is needed!
Very easy class. Need to attend online lectures for attendance but that is about it.

Jazz Appreciation is relatively easy, but if you get behind on your assignments you are screwed in the class. There are 5 big assignments that are worth half of your grade, so make sure to finish those well in advance of the deadline.

reviews.comment: McDonald and Moser were great government professors! They are good friends and you can tell they care about gov. The only grades are textbook responses (super short), lecture quizzes (5 questions), and 3 exams. The exams are just like the review and the lecture questions come straight from the recorded lectures or google. Definitely recommend

extremely lecture heavy with lots of work. the tests covers a lot of content and answer choices are intentionally designed the trick you, so pay attention. took up more of my time than the classes that pertain to my actual major, way too time consuming for no reason.

Online course with pre-recorded videos. Lecture is ok(but will make you think from their perspective on Global issues), McDonald has anger issues. You will use his book in class,  his main objective is $$ and making sure the youth don't have the freedom of free thinking. EXTREMELY one-sided on global issues BE CAREFUL. I DO NOT SUGGEST TAKING
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were two asynchronous lessons per week, and the grade consisted of quizzes on those sections and the tests. Overall, it was very test-heavy, but there was a curve for all of the tests. The content wasn't very difficult, but the lack of filler grades might hurt if you don't study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The online course for international relations was not difficult, but be aware of the strict deadlines and copious amounts of homework received. Finding a rhythm with this course took a few weeks, but it was not difficult overall. Be sure to watch all lectures and read the textbook, as they ARE on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the first B i've made so far in college, which was a hard pill to swallow because it was also the class I put the most time & effort in. I felt like I understood all of the material but the tests just screwed me over every time. Maybe Gov just isn't my strong suite but the exam questions were designed to confuse you. Super disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of lectures, and short (easy) quizzes after each unit. The lectures were interesting, but there were a lot of them. The three tests were multiple choice and curved a lot, so not too bad. There is no writing in this class, which makes it relatively easy.

Not an amazing class, professors were nothing sensational, sometimes sounded scripted in the online videos. Tests were really specific but straight off the slides and needed a day or two of memorizing but overall wasn't too difficult once you knew what to expect from the test.

CAREFUL WITH TEXTBOOK - I think a lot of people got confused and grade suffered bc nobody knew what was going on (myself included). The tests are tricky. Lots of A,B,C, "A & B are correct", "all of the above". Overall, easy A but will need some effort. Study bits and pieces 3 days before exam then it's a relatively easy A. Content is interesting!

I didn't realize there were textbook assignments until late in the semester (I joined the class late), and as a result my grade suffered significantly. Otherwise, I'm sure this class would be an easy A. Just keep up with all the different parts- lectures, quizzes, tests, and textbook assignments. Nothing is too hard, it's just a lot of moving parts

Not only are the tests for this class worth a large chunk of your grade, but they're also worded in a way designed to trick you and basically depend only on memorization. If it wasn't for the curves I'd be screwed. Both professors were good, but I'm rating them this low specifically because of the awful testing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was all memorization for me. Only take it if you are a good self-studier and you can memorize details. I disliked the tests with the A, B, C, A&B, All are correct choices. I took notes in unit 1 and only watched the videos for 2 and 3 and finished with a 96. They add curves- it was 8 pts for unit 1, 15 points for 2, and 10 points for 3

On the tests, there are usually 5 answer choices, 3 of which are answer choices while the final two are something like "both A and B" or "both a, b, c are incorrect". They are poorly worded and something I have never seen before. The weekly quizzes are easy, but they do not help for test preparation at all. DO NOT recommend...
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was one of the most difficult courses I have taken at UT. I studied extremely hard for each test, watched every lecture and took notes, filled out each exam review and went over it with a TA. STILL failed nearly every test. Do not take this course. It is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McDonald and Moser co teach GOV 312L. I enjoy government, but the lectures can get quite dry. Two untimed and easy quizzes due every week, Tests are fair with some weirdly worded questions, but they also give a curve after every test (8-15ish points) Two opportunities for small extra credit during the semester. Not as bad as some say it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class. For the tests, just watch the videos and fill out the study guides and you will get an A. However, Professor Moser and McDonald are very biased on their In the News segments and get very offensive at times. They promote U.S. propaganda and conveniently stop talking about war crimes and civilian casualties for certain topics.

Honestly such an annoying class. So much homework and exams are more difficult than they need to be. Take another class if you can for the gov credit. The class average for exams has been 50%. I think that's all you need to know. If you wanna succeed you need to set aside a lot of time to take detailed notes bc they are essential, hard but doable

Took online summer class, assignments due every weeknight and 3 exams. If you watch the lectures each night, take notes, and skim through the readings you'll be okay. I studied for all the exams, got a 103 on the first but 88s on the last 2. Definitely got harder. Doable, but you need to have a little time set aside for it. Very fast paced.

I took GOV312L online and was terrified by the other reviews I saw on here, but DO NOT FEAR! Truly, this class is not bad at all if you keep up with the lectures and readings. If you take good, detailed notes and fill out the review sheets, you will 100% be set for the tests. Super knowledgable professors and the class is very well-run/organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor McDonald over the summer, which I've heard is different than during the school year, and he was amazing. Along with Professor Moser, the two of them are hilarious and are great lecturers. I went into it thinking I would hate government, but I enjoyed the content very much. Lots of reading, but the grading is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took it during the summer semester. 3 multiple-choice exams (25% each) are very specific, content heavy, and proctored. Homework: lecture quizzes(12.5%) and textbook modules(12.5%). Even if u do all your homework perfectly, but exams are around 80\100, u won't get an A. Recommend taking it as a summer online class to fill core requirements.

Would wholeheartedly recommend McDonald's International Security course. Not the easiest A in the world, but his lectures are absolutely fantastic, and I learned so much from his teaching. Only gripe I had with the class was its size, which was large for an upper-division. If you're interested in war or security studies, definitely take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures and readings were boring. The tests were extremely detailed and meant to trick you which is annoying (they test test-taking skills rather than knowledge of content but oh well) but as long as you do the review you'll be fine. There's also usually a 10-point curve on each of the tests so definitely doable. Pretty easy besides the tests.
He actually cares about his students' grades and gives fair curves on exams. The workload is decent.

I took this as a summer class, so the pace was faster. However, lectures were not engaging (fully scripted), and there was a lot of homework. Tests were confusing because of their format (they were multiple choice though). Take notes on lectures and memorize ALL of the information because tests are very specific. It was an OK class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took McDonald and Shaw's GOV 310L Summer course and really liked it. Lectures are usually interesting but long. Most of the grade is made up of 3 exams, but they're not cumulative, online, unproctored, multiple choice coming from a test bank thats been used for years, so pretty easy to do well.

Very lenient. HW is very manageable (2 modules a week each with a quiz (no time limit, each module take less than 1 hr if u fast forward). The lecture vids and module questions cover everything you need to take notes on and you don't need to read the textbook (even though they say it's required). Idk y so many negative reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to read more on the GOV312L online course I would recommend looking at Prof Moser's RMP since he leads the course. McDonald co-heads the lectures and honestly is a big reason I was able to understand most of the course content. McDonald is a good lecturer and many times he clarified topics that I didn't understand the first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I truly did enjoy Moser's & McDonald's GOV312L course, they are both intelligent individuals who work off of each other well. With that being said, this was probably the hardest course I've taken to date. I feel like I was getting a good understanding of the content, but the tests are worded to make you second guess yourself. It is also proctored.

This class was very hard for me. I'm interested in gov, but these exams are surely meant to trick you. There are 2 quizzes a week and a discussion every other week that are way easier than the actual exams. They do curve exams a lot, but my GPA and I truly suffered anyway. I would recommend my past self to take another gov312L class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The weekly quizzes were super easy and same with the INNs although those took an hour sometimes. The tests were also easy as long as you watch his lectures (on 2x speed), take notes, and use your notes to fill out the study guide because the questions are basically applying the study guide.

Some of these reviews are very dramatic; Mcdonald is a good, passionate professor and he was very kind and understanding of students during the winter storm. The tests can be a bit difficult, but if you literally just study a little & watch the lectures, you will do fine. They curve well, and it is by no means impossible to do well in the course.
Super boring class, tests were really hard and super specific. The lectures dragged and dragged, not interesting at all.

I thought I wouldn't be interested in foreign policy at all, but Professor Mcdonald's passion regarding the subject was so moving that I almost felt obligated to listen. Even learning about the complex relationships in the Middle East seemed fun with his lectures shared with Moses.

I enjoyed McDonald's class. The material was so interesting since current events were incorporated into the lectures. The two quizzes each week are not difficult and they drop your 5 lowest quizzes. There are 3 exams in the semester. Many students struggled with the wording but there is a curve. With the curve, I never got below a 90 on an exam.

You don't need to read the textbook. Just make sure you can answer all of the questions on the study guide and you'll do fine. Also, the curves are ridiculously high so don't stress about the exams. The quizzes are open-note so you can find the answers in the powerpoint for the most part.
Awful class, awful Professor, dont take.

Literally the worst Professor ever. His tests are the worst and are purposely meant to trick you instead of test you for comprehension of the material. His lectures are awful and all over the place. If someone tells you not to take this class its for a reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was not as bad as I thought it would be, but it could have been much better. Quizzes are very simple, but Tests are extremely hard. Those tests are purposely meant to trick you. McDonald is a nice professor, but his explanations for concepts are way too complicated that he just leaves you confused. Just do the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of work: lots of lectures, readings, and weekly quizzes. The lectures were boring (watch them in 2x speed) but absolutely necessary to get a good grade. It is hard to keep track of the 2x/wk quizzes. Test questions are very hard and set up in a confusing way. If you don't have time/don't apply yourself you will do poorly.

All you need to do to pass the tets is complete the study guide that he gives you. He gave us all generous extra credit this semester because of the snow storm so he obviously cares about his students.

Take extremely detailed notes over the lectures & immediately fill out the questions on the study guide (given at the start of each unit). I didnt do 95% of the readings, they usually talk about them in lecture. Just fill out the study guide & a day before the exam read over it. I got a 102 in this class w/ extra credit. Not hard if you study smart
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from this class! All of the content was pre-recorded, and a lot was taken from prior semesters, so the flow wasn't always great. But overall it's a good course. The exams are a pretty tricky multiple choice, but there's a nice curve.

Hardest part of this class is probably the exams bc of the format but there is usually a decent curve on it. You will be fine if you study and read the questions carefully. I didn't use the textbook and it worked out. The lectures are broken down into manageable modules; 2x speed is the way to go. Set reminders for the quizzes. You've got this!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. McDonald is fine but the class is very work heavy. There are lots of readings per week and weekly quizzes which are fine. The exams are where things are quite difficult. The questions asked are quite tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In this class you will have weekly quizzes, and 3 exams throughout. If you like government and self-pace, then the course is fine. The exams are kinda hard since they ask for very specific things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: We have a couple of quizzes every week based on the lectures and then tests every few weeks. The quizzes are pretty easy, the tests are fairly hard in my opinion. The lectures are fine, but not engaging, and don't really help prepare you for the tests. I also don't like using Proctorio for exams. He is always available to answer questions though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams in this class were nothing like the quizzes. They were unnecessarily difficult and the answer choices were basically (A, B, C, A and B, All of the above) so it was pretty hard to say the least. 2-3 quizzes a week that don't really help with exams. Unless you love government, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class's exams were way harder than they needed to be for a core class. The modules were easy, it's fine, but they don't really provide you with any study materials for exams. The exams had like "A and B" and "A, B, and C" options that made it confusing and just harder than it needed to be. Idk, easy lectures, tough exams.

The class was okay... There were weekly quizzes due every Wednesday and Friday that really put a buffer on your grade. But the 4 exams were tough. The multiple-choice questions were all five answer choices and the exams were proctored.

Exams are extremely hard, even if you study a lot. Grades are curved, which helps a bit, but the stress and anxiety this class gave me+others, it's hard to measure. (Hard) exams+(easy) quizzes compose the majority of your grade. There's A LOT of assigned readings, and they're necessary to do well/okay on the exams... Student study groups helped...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was completely online. The quizzes are really easy. The exams are kinda difficult though and make up a large portion of your grade. The final paper is super easy.

Took Moser/McDonald's GOV 312L class. Quizzes are extremely easy, and the final paper is graded very generously. The tests aren't too bad as long as you spend the night before going through all the lectures. If you study well enough, you can easily get over a 100+ in this class. Good professors.
Test were made for you to fail. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty boring, but I enjoyed the INNs (current news segments) we had every other week. Tests were very easy, as were quizzes, and they try to give everyone a 100 on the final paper as long as you follow the instructions. Always available on piazza/ via email and the TAs were pretty nice. Easy class to take for credit.

Lectures get boring so I watch them at 2x speed. The quizzes and final paper were extremely easy. Make sure to stay on track of the quizzes yourself (I missed several because there was no reminder.) The tests are a bit harder but there is a generous curve. Make use of the study guide.
Easiest A ever. McDonald is a great speaker. 100% take this class.

The class is structured in a way that make it easy to get an A. The quizzes are easy but the tests are a bit challenging (curves help A LOT). The online lectures can be boring and long, however, this isn't too bad of a class. Also you don't really need to do the assigned readings.

Mcdonald and Moser are good lecturers but this class is very lecture heavy and tests are hard because of the answer choices. It will be like A, B, C, or A and B, or ABC, so it makes it hard to narrow it down to one. There are quizzes at the end of every module that are pretty easy. Just don't fall behind because it can be a lot to catch up on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McDonald was pretty good. The lectures could definitely get boring and took a lot of time to get to the point. As far as government classes go, this was one where I do feel like I learned a lot. However, it was all over foreign policy which I was disappointed about. I was excited to learn more about Congress and our US government.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: an online course that requires you to watch lecture videos and then take a fairly easy open note quiz after. However, lectures are extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. The test questions are designed horribly- questions like is the answer a, b, c, a and b, or all. Overall, not too hard to get a good grade but its def not the best class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Self-paced, easy and fun class if you like government, pretty easy but boring class if you don't. Pretty much all grades from tests which aren't too difficult (still gotta study a bit tho)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online 1st Semester Summer 2020. Overall it was easy. There's a lot of videos to watch but they weren't too bad. The quizzes after each lecture are easy but the exams are a bit harder. Take detailed notes and be sure to take note of examples given in the textbook and lectures. Do your work and you should be able to get an A or B.
He is not a good lecturer. His lectures can be hard to follow because he takes so much time to make a point and often explains concepts in a convoluted way.

The online class consisted of pre-recorded lectures followed by 5 question quizzes on the content (easy). Graded by quizzes, 3 midterms (in person), and every 2 weeks watching a longer video and paragraph response is required. Recommend 100%- completing the assignments and studying for exams will get you an A.
He's fine. Basically what you expect for government. I thought class load was very manageable.
Government isn't personally my favorite subject, but this class is totally doable. Just be sure to study throughout the semester and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The weekly quizzes are extremely easy. Tests weren't too hard after studying the day before. Make sure you stay on top of the weekly modules. The test material is directly from the lectures and just a little bit from the readings. The class is organized well and I learned a lot about government.

Lectures are SCRIPTED and use vocabulary that is literally frustrating to hear. Lectures are supposed to be fluid and human, not robotic and text like, especially in an online class. Moser does a decent job of talking like a real person but anytime McDonald comes on my ears just want to cry. Other than that very interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is super hard to concentrate on and kind of slow--as in literally so slow that it makes me want to fall asleep sometimes(and you can't speed up the videos???? would've made it so much easier). The tests are nothing like the quizzes they give at all; they're very very hard. I would not at all recommend this class to anyone.

It's a relatively easy class but it requires a lot of work. KEEP UP with the readings, listen to ALL the lectures, do well on quizzes, and DO NOT MESS UP ON DISCUSSION WRITINGS. You have two and each one is graded out of 2, so if you even slightly mess up, you have a 75% or 50% for your discussion writing avg. Tests are lecture/reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are very comprehensive and can include any detail covered in the lectures. All the quizzes are straight forward and the writing assignments are over current day events with a clear grading criteria. Only studying the day before the test using the collaborative review managed to pass each test with a B+ or A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to read a lot in order to pass the test. The tests are super hard. You have to take a quiz every week and you have tons and tons of readings!!! Personally I would have take a government that is not online!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class. Mos/McD were knowledgeable and cared about the topic. They wanted us to do well. If you get behind on the modules, expect a lot of stress before tests. Tests are also curved (5-10 pts) so an A is really doable. The downside was that lectures were scripted and hard to follow. Expect to pause and rewatch everything.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class. It was very interesting and McDonald loves what he does. You have to read and watch videos a lot but it is worth it. He is accessible and wants to help you. You have to watch class because there are quizzes. It keeps you up with current events. DO THE STUDY GUIDE!!!!! I got a C on the test when I did not do it and As when I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pat is a great professor and takes the time to make sure the students know the material; he explains it in a way that is easy to grasp. Came in not liking government and came out really interested in the way the US handles foreign policy. The only downside would be the amount of pre-lecture modules there were (they got to be a lot at some points).

Moser and McDonald were very fun and very boring to listen to. Their exams are straight forward but they're the type to actually throw trick questions in there. 3 exams but one slip up will HURT your grade more than it seems. Their lectures are long and you will take hours just on one module taking notes. TAKE NOTES!!! quizzes are fairly simple.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow this class was amazing! I learned so much about foreign policy and current events. This class is quite a lot of reading and work but seriously what you learn is so relevant!! You have to have the discipline to log in on class days and pay attention, but I thought it was really nice to just stay at home and do class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While the lectures can be on the longer side, the material and tests are straightforward. It can be easy to fall significantly behind. Besides their constant need to justify American imperialism throughout history, McDonald and Moser generally do a good job teaching the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the easier options for GOV312L. Made an A with lots of wiggle room. Online discussions/quizzes boost your grade. Tests are in person. Lots of outside videos/reading but not all are necessary. Just have a general idea of each article (can get from videos or PPT instead of reading). Do the review, skim the outside material and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McDonald is a good professor. Watching him and Moser interact was always funny. Course material can be a bit difficult to understand and goes pretty fast at times. I always had a relatively hard time on the test, as they seemed a little hard for an intro course like this. Lots of outside the class modules and readings. Overall, I enjoyed the course

This class had a lot of work outside of class, especially for a 3 hour class. However, if you watch the lectures and video clips/homework, it's easy to get an A. You do need to study for a day or two before tests, but if you do they aren't bad plus there's usually a curve. Quizzes during lecture were really easy, and you really don't need to read.
Lot's of modules to complete outside of class. The workload can become overwhelming if you don't keep up with it. As long as you keep up with the modules, you'll pass.

Lots of pre-class module readings, definitely have to rely on some sort of group review session on google doc for tests. Besides that though McDonald is a hilarious and chill professor that loves football and has amazing chemistry with Prof Moser who co-teaches this class.

READ THE MODULES - I thought that I came in with substantial knowledge about foreign policy and I was lax on keeping up/going in depth for the modules. Study the modules, go to McDonald's office hours and talk about the module info - he is so helpful. For the exams, make sure you know the review and DO IT YOURSELF, don't rely on the google doc
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The modules you have to watch does appear to be a bit excessive, but definitely doable. Just take the questions from the powerpoints and answer them (answers are in the modules) and bam you have notes that will aide you well. Tests are designed to be tricky, but at least there's a curve.

The amount of videos assigned every week is too much for a 3 credit hour class. However, as long as you watch the videos, do the reviews, and put some thought into the essay you'll be fine. Very interesting content, open-note quizzes, tests require effort but are generously curved, and you don't have to do the reading to get an A. Would take again.

Maybe it's just me but this class was really hard I definitely wish I would've taken it at a community college. The quizzes are either really tricky or pretty easy. The tests are super trick question based and was really hard in my opinion. Definitely watch the modules and do the readings. The professors are nice and entertaining though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work for this class between the learning modules and assigned readings. The tests also have a lot of material on them. Besides how tough the class was, McDonald was a good professor. The live class was always very interesting and the material discussed was always relevant to current issues in some way.

I took GOV 312 (online) with him and Moser and it's a pretty easy A. Both of them are very clear and the study guide basically covers all of the test so make sure to study them! I don't understand the negative reviews of them because the class is pretty easy. Don't sleep on the essay though, it's graded pretty hard.

Lectures are sooo horrible because they literally read a teleprompter and stutter and struggle with their own words. It's hard to learn because of this. My eyes glaze over. Class/quiz is online only ONCE a week but there's a lot of videos you have to watch outside of class. Required readings are long but you don't actually need to read them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. McD is so cool! Moser was good too. He answered all of my questions in Office Hours with an excellent attitude. He explains himself well, and is just an all-round friendly guy. The pop quizzes are easy, and if you use your Study Guides, you'll make an A. The class requires effort, and you must do your h/w as told and do the SGs, you'll do well

Prof. McDonald is great. He takes his job seriously, is fair, patient, and clear. He doesn't run away from tough questions by students and does his best to provide a well-rounded response. He would probably repeat/rephrase an explanation fifty times if he had to for you to understand.

Prof. McDonald is hilarious, but teaches the material in an effective matter and can be serious when need be. Short and simple: He's a good teacher. GOV 312L was an easy class, as long as you spent about 4 hrsweek doing the readings.

It's the standard government jargon associated with governmental foreign policy that can be found within this class. Take the readings seriously and make sure to go to office hours from time  to time just to cement your knowledge. I will admit that a 1.5 hr lecture is really hard to remained focused on at times, especially online. Not too bad.

Wonderful professor. Very clear and precise. Very helpful in office hours. Made subject extremely engaging. We spent half the course playing Statecraft with class divided into 12 teams, and it was a very rewarding experience. Take him if you want to learn.

moser and macdonald's lessons are not interesting, and the exams have pretty much nothing to do with the material. the exams are also wordy and confusing, with answers like a, b, c, both a and b, both b and c, all of the above, none of the above. unnecessarily complicated for a for-credit course.

I am an avid studier, and I spent about 2-3 hours a day for this class, and in my opinion this FOR CREDIT class should not be this difficult. Tests are worded weirdly and the way in which this class is talked feels like an insult. Phrases such as "obvious right and wrong answer" made me feel ashamed for asking for help. Chose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So good I wished I could take this class twice.

Him and Professor McDonald make an amazing pair and do an amazing job explaining the material/topics covered in class, they offer in person options for anyone in need of accommodations, they're very easy to talk to/get a hold of, and overall their class is very easy. I wish that they could provide more exam review options/feedback for how to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The reading is a lot and the lecture videos are hard. I recommend going to office hours as he is very accessible outside of class. The exams are easy to study for but make sure to understand how everything connects together.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests made up most of the grade. And they were not easy, but doable.

I think him and professor mcD do a very good job at explaining concepts that are extremely important to know. This is not a blow off class and if you actually take the time to learn and understand, it is very interesting. I used to hate government but they changed my mind
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst lectures ever. Reads a literal essay as the lecture videos, so the dialogue is extremely overcomplicated and hard to follow especially because the poorly made slides with too much information on them do not match what he is saying. It is impossible to take notes. The teaching ideology is off.

The better professor and makes the lectures more easy to understand, easier to reach. Textbook assignments are long and boring and a waste of time but crucial to grade. Exams are so specific and hard and late at night. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not worth the stress please since I didn't have the brain to, take it over the summer with community college or find an alternative.

Interesting class and the lectures are entertaining. If you center your notes around the test reviews it's very easy to get an A. Tests can be a bit tricky but they tell you that the wrong answers will be obviously wrong which makes it easy to narrow it down to the right one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are tough!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tons of textbook readings and long lectures, tests are impossible to get a perfect score or a gauge of how you did even after you finished it. the answer choices are kind of unfair, demented because its a,b,c, a&b, a&b&c so you are bound to miss questions. the 3 tests make up 75% of your grade (25% each). ruined my 4.0 :(

The lectures are a little boring and honestly the slides are enough to get an A if you don't put everything off until the day before the test. The tests are a little tricky but the content is so easy that it doesn't matter. Moser's and McDonald's dynamic is pretty cute and is the highlight of the lectures and INN@UT segments (which I adore btw).
you can lowk skip the videos and do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I hated this class so much. It's all online, and if you genuinely try to do the class, don't expect a good grade. The only way people get a good grade in this class is by cheating. Tests are over things he mentioned maybe once in an hour and a half long video. Take this class somewhere else!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was a good, caring professor. He tried to make lectures interesting, this just isn't my favorite topic. Easy A if you do the work, I started studying day of. The tests sometimes have curveball questions and video lectures are SUPER long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Though the content is very easy, the tests are not structured nicely and make the class a lot more difficult than it actually is. The class is very exam heavy and though extra credit is provided, it doesn't impact your grade too much. The lecture videos were often time-consuming and didn't help much. This class brought down my 4.0 :(

Professors are nice and clearly passionate about their work. Both of them respond to emails fast. Content is genuinely interesting if you're interested in actually learning but extremely time consuming. Do not take if you just want to get credit out of the way. No reason to make a gen ed class this hard. Got an A in my ECE classes but not in gov.

This course took up a LOT of my homework time. There were a lot of textbooks and outside readings, long lecture videos, and all of this prep took a lot of time. Tests were pretty difficult for me. Lectures were sometimes interesting, sometimes not.

Awesome and caring professor who cares about his student's success. The class itself however is way more time consuming than it needs to be, the topics are interesting and the professor does a great job at keeping it interesting and applicable to the current day, but can be stressful for students with already difficult or committed schedules.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Obviously since this is an online class consider your workload to also include the time it takes to attend a regular class. The review sheets were very helpful - use it to take notes. Just a forewarning that the textbook, which you are required to buy to do assignments, costs $100. MCQ is structured weirdly but the wrong answers were very wrong.

Best online class I've taken. Lectures are easy to follow and quizzes were good to check for understanding afterwards. Textbook readings are graded but its the same info as lecture so you can easily skip through and answer the questions.

Though Moser and McDonald were nice, take this class in-person. The workload is heavy for a core class and tests (which are WAY more difficult than daily quizzes) are in the format "A, B, C, A and B, All of the above" and they will intentionally make one answer choice confusing. If you do decide to take it, email Moser to opt in for the paper exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took him and McDonald because the other professor had no seats, but I advise you to wait for a different semester rather than take Moser. Most of the class is based on video lectures and a required textbook, but it is a substantial time commitment, at least an hour or 2. Your grade is based mostly on 3 midterms, but he does a little extra credit.

Prof Moser is great, but overall the class is very time consuming. Multiple quizzes and textbook assignments per week, and tests are worth a LOT (25% each). Extra credit is offered but only applied to lecture quizzes (your 4 lowest are also dropped), which don't impact your average very much. Set reminders for assignments - very easy to miss stuff.

Professor Moser was great, but the class is just hard. Lots of work every week. Was spending the same amount of time on this class as I was on Clinical Pharmacology. 4-ish extra credit opportunities. 3 major exams. Textbook required. 2 textbook quizzes per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are a majority of the grade, and the test questions are worded in a way that is meant to trick you making the class much more difficult than it needs to be.

-Three tests, each are 25% of your final grade
-Material isn't terribly difficult but does require studying to work out
-I found the professors to be interesting and the material to be fun, although this isn't universal
-My strategy was to do the modules/videos, go back and do the review sheet, and then watch the lectures again afterwards
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super simple course, easy to follow, and light course load. Lectures are engaging, and typically are shorter than a normal class. Highly recommend for a gov credit.

Exams could be tricky, but they give you a review sheet to do that covers everything on the exams. Do the readings, watch the lectures, and do the review sheet!! It helps narrow down what you realllyyy need to know!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you just want a GOV credit , i don't recommend. each week you have 2 modules , for each module there is the lectures to watch, a quiz, and a textbook reading that's due tuesday and friday. The exam are kind of tricky

One of the most time consuming classes Ive had despite being fully online. Lots of homework that are weighted so low that they barely matter in your final grade (but essential for studying to do decent on exams). 3 exams worth 75% of grade. If you are not a good test-taker, this is not a good class. Homework due every Tuesday and Friday.
His lectures were very entertaining; however, he likes to add a lot of information to topics not listed in the slides, so watching lectures is very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, it wasn't that bad if you're a procrastinator. Although I didn't enjoy the INN@UT being posted last minute. Tons of lecture videos and quizzes due every Tuesday and Friday, on top of Textbook work. Its not "hard" but it is busy work.

Do not take this class for a Gov credit! Honestly was really disappointed with how the assignments aren't weighed as much into your grade despite having so many chapter readings, and quizzes. Since the Tests weigh so much into your  grade.Extra Credit is given although it doesn't really factor into your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class structure was clear and the pacing honestly wasn't too bad compared to other summer classes. Material is pretty boring, but daily reading assignments and 5 questions quizzes only take 1-2 hours and he gives a slight curve to every test. Never actually watched lecture videos you can just get the information from the slides pdf and the book.

never been a big fan of history but actually really enjoyed the content of this class. workload was fine, I worked full time while taking it. make sure u stay on track, or even better get ahead. no essays thankfully! you do have to study for exams, but they give review sheets.

readings, lectures, and quizzes due nightly mon-fri. Content's easy, but the pace is brutal. Pro tip: SKIP THE LECTURE VIDEOS—they're long (about 1-2 hrs a day), boring, and mostly irrelevant. Just read the slides, they cover everything you need and save tons of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of weekly assignments, which can get stressful during a busy semester. The class covers easy to understand content, so the tests aren't bad. The prof. curves exams and provides extra credit too- so grades really shouldn't be a worry if you have the time to commit to the class. Moser is also easy to contact, if you need accommodations.
Lectures were clear and informative, if a bit long, and the structure of the class helped my learning and made it easy to do well in.

So ironic how my hardest class as an engineering major was this god forsaken summer class. Exams were extremely difficult because of how the answer choices were worded. There was so much reading to do. Just not a pleasant experience at all.


Just take this class at a community college.
The tests were SO difficult for no reason. There is so much content as well! There is no need for this class to be the same rigor as my major classes.

GOV 312L is one of the most time consuming classes I have taken in my life. I am a straight A student, never made a B, and never struggled in school. This class has been the most work I have ever done. I have over 300 pages of notes, 600+ flashcards, and hours upon hours of studying - all to BARELY make an A in the class. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOV 312L with Moser and McDonald was one of the most interesting gov classes I've taken. Get ready to read and watch the lectures + take notes, but quite frankly, the content is very useful and relevant and the profs are super chill. They grade fairly and give big curves as well. Highly recommend if you like learning!

GOV312L was very doable. Don't be like me and watch 7 hours worth of videos the day of the test, and you'll do fine. Even with last minute studying, I got an 86 on that test so it IS possible. Lectures 1.5x speed are your best friend. Tests can be difficult at times, but not impossible if you watched the videos. Overall: funny dudes, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There was lots of homework involved with this course, but it was pretty manageable to keep up with. Tests were kind of difficult but there's enough other grades to help balance it out and a couple opportunities for extra credit at the end of the semester with the course eval. Overall, not too bad.

Moser was a great professor, lectures were extremely interesting and I learned a ton from this course. However, the tests are very poorly written and do not accurately test your knowledge, and I believe there was cheating going on which brings down the curve and screws over the people who actually studied. Overall great course but tests were bad.

A semi-interesting class for those who are somewhat interested in current events and news. The lectures and textbook work were sometime a bore, but as long as you study the powerpoints and the review sheets you will do fine. It's all online, so unless you don't know how to use canvas and Pearson you won't find many problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: BARELY GOT AN A & I rewatched every lecture, read every chapter in the book, & filled out every single review sheet. This was such a huge waste of my time & it is very obvious Moser is reading off a script. I hated his awkward pauses it made me physically cringe. DO NOT TAKE unless you love government & already know everything about foreign policy.
I understand that this was an online course, but I still found it too difficult to reach Dr. Moser. When I did, I never got any helpful responses. I wish I had just cheated like everyone else.

After going through the entire GOV312L class, I couldn't tell you who is Moser and who is McDonald. But the class content was actually very interesting and informative. If you don't watch the lectures, the tests will be difficult. But if you actually watch the lectures, take notes, and do the review, you will do fine.

Tests can be very tricky make sure you study by doing review sheets. probably should watch every video and take some notes but at the end of the day not entirely worth it. Lots of work though each week. 2 assignments every Tuesday and Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were great and covered effectively all of the material, but for most of the class we still had to complete long textbook readings twice a week. The class had 3 exams where they record your video, audio, and screen so that you can't cheat. The exams are pretty easy though and they typically curve them to keep the average in the mid 80s.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly, you are graded by so little outside of the exams which hurts the grade a lot even if exams are worth so less because you have very little practice for the exams which are insanely tough. Viewing the amazing lectures is a must. Overall, the hard exams were a huge hindrance to this course as they did not reflect course material properly.

GOV 312L made me rethink my life choices. I took this class to fulfill a core requirement and I wish I could go back in time and just take it at a community college. I am a horrible test taker with pretty bad test anxiety, so the exam's were extremely difficult for me. Professors r very nice, just really hard for no reason.

He and Pat Mcdonald's course here at UT isn't bad, I didn't have to study too hard to do well on exams. Just yap on the textbook questions and it's a free hundred. Quizzes are straight from lectures or powerpoints, so just go over those and you'll have an easy A.

The class is taught by two professors and is entirely online. There are a 4-5 assignments a week including 1-2 textbook assignments where you have to read a chapter and answer questions. Quizzes based on module videos. At the end of the day the class is mostly graded on 3 exams worth 25% of your grade each and use honorlock so get ready to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams for this class are really hard. Unless you're prelaw/have an interest in government I would not recommend him for your core. It's a lot of reading and lecture videos. That being said, I loved the content discussed in this class and Dr. Mosers cracks funny jokes every now and then

honestly just a very content heavy class and it's not worth taking for a gov core requirement when other easier professors and classes exist. If needed just take at community college. exams are difficult and you will need to spend a lot of time on the lengthy reviews, readings, and lecture modules to do well. Also exams are proctored w/ honor lock

This class is taught by both Dr. McDonald and Dr. Moser. Their online lectures were lengthy for each module and their tests grabbed content from the lectures, readings, and textbook. The curves are pretty large that if you put in effort, you should be able to walk out with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is structured with lectures and textbook assignments, but the exams can be tricky. Staying on top of the material is key. Unstuck study was a lifesaver for prep - highly recommend using it alongside the lectures and readings.

Not too difficult if you actually read the textbook and look over the slides. Quite a big work load so what you end up with is dependent on how motivated you are to put in the work over the summer. Tests asks very specific questions so READ THE TEXTBOOK. Take at a CC if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I never liked government classes until I had Moser, the reading and the lectures were interesting, and didn't feel that hard to listen to or even read. I actually enjoyed the reading as long as you are ahead from the reading this will be a rather easy class. I took this class as my summer first term class and it was a good class to open to.

Really quite an easy class. Useful information, but if you watch the news regularly and keep up to date with current events and international politics and policies it can get a little stale. Finished most of the work for this online asynchronous class in 2-3 days. Just study the day before the exam.

I actually really liked this class! I'm usually not very into government and history classes but this one was well-paced and it focused on the Bush administration onwards and used a lot of real-world examples so it felt very relevant. Prof. Moser and Prof McDonald are a good pair. Keep up with the lectures and you'll be fine.

I thought this class was really good considering it was an online government class. He taught this with Prof. Macdonald, and they did a really good job with explaining expectations, organizing material, and explaining the material. I thought Moser was also so funny which is a bonus. There are textbook readings and assignments, as well as 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In conjunction with McDonald, this class was not hard to get an A in; however, do not let the exams get ahead of you though because a bad grade on those could potentially give you a lot of stress. There was also a lot of homework, ranging from textbook assignments and lecture quizzes. The lectures are fun and informative. Look at the slides.
Taken with McDonald. Class was super structured and had a low workload. McDonald was definitely the better prof as he would communicate with the students more.

Profs are really nice and have very enjoyable lectures. Readings are not super important (they go over in the lectures), but watch ALL the lectures, and do the reviews (extensively) before the tests. Very generous curves. This isn't a blow off class, but put in the work and you'll do fine.

Had him and prof. Pat McDonald online and they made a great impression. They put together amazing material and I learned A LOT. Does require a decent amount of effort/studying if you want to do well on the exams. Generous with quiz drops/test curve and did well even after missing multiple quizzes, turning in assignments late, and ok exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you need to take Gov 312L do not take this class, exams were multiple choice but made to trick you. You have to do so many readings and watch so many lecture videos. My first B in college, really do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is way too lecture-heavy. The lectures, on top of the textbook assignments, had me spending more time on this class than on my major-specific courses. The tests are nothing like the quizzes and require great memory and specific content knowledge. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's an online course so it really comes down to you to determine how well you do. I enjoyed the freedom of the pre-recorded lectures and the 50 question, 3 exams were very manageable if you did the review sheets. You should want to do them though because the exam formats can be very difficult (Usually 5 multiple choice answer options per quesiton)

Professer Moser and McDonald were both great! They are really funny and have a great dynamic. The only grades are the textbook reading responses (They are super short only 120 characters), lecture quizzes, and 3 exams. The lecture quizzes are really easy if you pay attention or google the question. The exams are exactly like the review.

The tests were very detailed and were based primarily on the lectures as well as a little bit of the textbook. Very time-consuming class but overall not too bad. There were also generous curves on the tests which helped a lot.

Lots of lectures, and short (easy) quizzes after each unit. The lectures were interesting, but there were a lot of them. The three tests were multiple choice and curved a lot, so not too bad. There is no writing in this class, which makes it relatively easy.

Not an amazing class, professors were nothing sensational, sometimes sounded scripted in the online videos. Tests were really specific but straight off the slides and needed a day or two of memorizing but overall wasn't too difficult once you knew what to expect from the test.

The tests are a big chunk of your grade and are mostly memorization based, but the curve helps boost your grade. The content was clear and pretty easy to understand, you just need to stay on top of all the assigned reading and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Actually watch the modules to get an understanding of course content. Textbook doesn't help much. Fill out the study guides with as much detail as possible to prepare for the test.
