The tests are 75% of your grade so don't skip out on studying. There's a lot of content in this course so make sure you stay on top of your work but overall pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took online summer class, assignments due every weeknight and 3 exams. If you watch the lectures each night, take notes, and skim through the readings you'll be okay. I studied for all the exams, got a 103 on the first but 88s on the last 2. Definitely got harder. Doable, but you need to have a little time set aside for it. Very fast paced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took it during the summer semester. 3 multiple-choice exams (25% each) are very specific, content heavy, and proctored. Homework: lecture quizzes(12.5%) and textbook modules(12.5%). Even if u do all your homework perfectly, but exams are around 80\100, u won't get an A. Recommend taking it as a summer online class to fill core requirements.

Interesting class, topical. I read all of the assigned readings (pdfs given) for the first half and it helped with solidifying the history. I read slow so it took about two hours each reading (2x a week) and 1 hour each accompanying lecture. After history did not read and could still understand. x3 speed everything b4 exam helped so much. 1 essay
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have taken two of Prof. Moser's classes and loved them both. I learned a lot from his Russian Politics course this semester. Take his online courses, bump the lectures up to 2x speed, and you'll never spend more than an hour or 2 per week on this class. Module quizzes are easy, essay is easy, and exams are easy if you do the exam reviews.

I have taken 2 classes with Moser while at UT and have loved both of them!! The tests use proctorio, so if you're looking for an easy A it's not for you. He provides a detailed test review, so if you watch the lectures and take good notes before hand you'll do great!

Exams are very specific, content heavy, and you can't guess on them due to the structure of the MC, so study hard. Missed the mark just barely for an A because I underestimated the first exam. However, Moser ignited my passion for government and I became a gov major because of his class. He is a wonderful lecturer and overall the course is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures and readings were boring. The tests were extremely detailed and meant to trick you which is annoying (they test test-taking skills rather than knowledge of content but oh well) but as long as you do the review you'll be fine. There's also usually a 10-point curve on each of the tests so definitely doable. Pretty easy besides the tests.

I took this as a summer class, so it was probably faster paced. However, the lectures were very not engaging (reading off a script type thing), and there was a ton of homework. There were both lecture quizzes and textbook modules. The tests are pretty confusing sometimes because of their format (although it is multiple choice). It was an OK class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you make Quizlets to study for the test you will do fine. Watch all the lectures because the test asks detailed questions. Also, do the textbook readings.

I never do these but I need to go out of my way to say how horrible this class was. It was far more difficult than it needed to be and the instruction style was lazy and boring. Stay far away and take this class elsewhere. The instructors seemed like nice enough guys, but idk what was going on there.. Unfortunate because I felt passionate otherwise

As a government major I enjoyed the course, but as others said the format of the tests made them harder. The curves were usually around 11 points so you could make over a 100 on a test and pad your grade a bit. Focus more on memorizing the lecture slides and do the study guides. The essay was pretty easy and only 10% of the grade.

Take this class at ACC if you want a good grade and aren't a good test taker. I got lucky and barely got a 93 which is the cut-off for an A. Quizzes are easy, but even if you understand the subject very well, the tests are difficult because of their format (A,B,C, A&B, all of the above, none of the above). Only graded on tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very hard class, read the book or you may not do well on the tests. tests and quizzes are the only grade plus a short essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests were challenging because answer choices would be A,B,AB,C, or All/None. Class is asynch and not overwhelming at all. Each test is curved by 10-13 points. Cutoff for an A is a 92.5. The important thing to remember is to consistently study your notes from the lectures. Tests are not cumulative. If you're consistent an A is not hard to get.

I really enjoyed the class, I found it very relevant to what was going on today and it's information that I can actually use in my day to day life. The workload is not too heavy but the tests are pretty difficult, especially compared to the quizzes, so you do have to study for them a lot. But it's pretty easy to understand, just a lot to memorize.
Your grade heavily relays on a final essay and you either get a 100 or 75 or fail. It made no sense and is not really a way you should grade essays

This class was well organized and interesting. If you actually pay attention to the lectures you will be completely fine in the class. I did not read a single thing for the class, and still got an A.They provide study guides that are exactly what needs to be known for the exam. It is overall a fair class. Not too easy, not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny professor but some of the reading can be sleep inducing. Tests are difficult but, he gives a very good curve. Quizzes and essay are very easy so as long as you keep up with that and do okay on the tests you will be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting to me, and Moser and his colleague, McDonald, are highly passionate and knowledgeable. There is so much content for this course, but it is doable. Easy quizzes based on the lectures. The tests were pretty difficult, but with a generous curve, it is possible to get a high A on the tests and in the course. Not bad!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of lecture material. Two easy quizzes are due a week. One easy essay. Three tests that were very hard for me to pass- even with a curve.

The lecture videos can be hard to get through at times, but if you actually watch them, the tests will be pretty easy. There was three tests that dictated the majority of your grade and they all had a large curve. Overall a straightforward class that if you put a little time into learning the content it should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture material covers everything you need for an A, I never read the textbook. Some test questions are from the text and not mentioned in lecture, but there's a 10+ curve so it's fine. Easy and interesting class as long as you ACTUALLY PAY ATTENTION TO THE LECTURES and watch on time! Pretty easily achievable A unless you procrastinate.

I've heard a lot of people say this class is hard but it really isn't all too bad. If you've taken AP Gov/ Econ, this class reminds me a lot of that. Although there are two quizzes every week (sometimes three) they're not hard but the tests are tricky. A+ is achievable if you put in the time to fill out the review guide.

This class was the easiest college course (including CC courses) I have ever taken. Two 5 questions quizzes directly from the short lecture videos. The tests are directly from the study guide he gives, so do that and you'll be fine (and he curves every test). One short essay 500 words max over content covered in lecture.
Landmind class, weekly quizzes are easy, exams are designed to trip you up, dont take if youre on any GPA based scholarships.

Moser and McDonald are two of the funniest Professors at UT. They work great together and as a result the class was very enjoyable. Tests are HARD you have to study a lot if you want a good grade. I literally never studied and barely made it out alive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Moser's class to fulfil my UGS requirement and there are daily readings and daily attendance quizzes, but participating in these aspects of class really prepare you for the 3 unit papers and 2 midterms. Although heavy on reading (some weekly readings may be 20-30 pages), Professor Moser covers the reading material well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quizzes were not too difficult, even if you didn't do the assigned readings, as long as you went through the videos and powerpoint that went over the reading. Tests were fairly difficult, but all three of them were curved quite a bit since they were difficult for everyone.

A lot of people dislike this class, it was one of my favorites. 3 tests all 22.5% of the grade, not gonna lie fairly difficult. there are quizzes every class, that why I said attendance was mandatory, if you miss class, you miss the quiz. Him and Mcdonald were always entertaining in lecture. You have to watch the modules before class tho!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As long as you watch all pre-lecture videos and take notes, all assessments will be super easy. Also, the exam reviews were really helpful. A study group could be useful here. Although textbook reading is assigned every week, I found that they were unnecessary for quizzes and tests. Curves on tests were about 5-10 points. Overall, great choice.

Prof. Mosers lectures and interesting and content specific. The class grade is heavily dependent on the tests which can be tricky so content knowledge is key. Overall, Moser is accessible and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Moser and McDonald are a good duo, but those tests will mess with your head. Make sure you do the reviews, re-watch lectures, watch their analyses of the readings, and try to remember the quiz questions. Tests were T, F, or AOTB, which was difficult for me because I over think a lot so dont second guess your answers! Pretty good class, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got A's on all of the exams without the textbook (except the 1st exam bc free trial). Just copy the ppt notes for every module and fill them out as you watch the recorded/live lectures (watch all of them!). The quizzes and discussions are pretty easy, just make sure you're there. They provide good study guides, fill them out with your notes!

I truly did enjoy Moser's & McDonald's GOV312L course, they are both intelligent individuals who work off of each other well. With that being said, this was probably the hardest course I've taken to date. I feel like I was getting a good understanding of the content, but the tests are worded to make you second guess yourself. It is also proctored.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly him and moser are great and very smart, but the way the class is set up is set up for a core class. The tests are extremely tricky even if you study the problem is there is so much information to memorize, I hate classes that are based on memorization of terms etc because you try to memorize and then boom you forget it all after each exam.

This class was very hard for me. I'm interested in gov, but these exams are surely meant to trick you. There are 2 quizzes a week and a discussion every other week that are way easier than the actual exams. They do curve exams a lot, but my GPA and I truly suffered anyway. I would recommend my past self to take another gov312L class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: great professor

Class structured like a live news show and Professors Moser and McDonald(co-teach) made it a blast. We watched lecture videos(can be long) before each stream and had a quiz(5 questions, super ez) at the end of each stream. Tests were also pretty ez(+7.5 pt curve) just had to work on the study guide. No need to read txtbook if u watched lectures.

Awesome class with him and McDonald. Quizzes and tests are not very difficult at all as long as you pay attention in lectures. Their lectures are fun and interesting. They also let you get easy credit with easy weekly quizzes. Take them if you can!

Him and McDonald are cynical. They are awful professors who do not care about their students. Their exams are meant to trick you, not test your comprehension of the material. Listen to everyone who tells you to avoid this class, theyre doing it for a reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Moser/McDonald's GOV 312L class. Quizzes are extremely easy, and the final paper is graded very generously. The tests aren't too bad as long as you spend the night before going through all the lectures. If you study well enough, you can easily get over a 100+ in this class. Good professors.
The test were made for you to fail. I am a usual straight A student and this was the HARDEST call I have taken in my entire life . AVOID BY ALL MEANS.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Your grade mostly depends on 3 tests, which are very difficult but they are curved like 7 points. My best advice: make your own study guide by answering the questions at the beginning of the lectures/slide on a doc a week or two b4 the test! There's one easy essay at the end and easy quizzes that are worth 25%. Not an easy A but still attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes are 5 questions at the end of every module and are an easy 5/5. The 3 exams are in no way like the quizzes. You MUST complete the review Moser gives out and study thoroughly in advance. Questions are extremely tricky (Ex: A, AB, BC, ABC, none) and require immense knowledge of the material. Fairly easy A if you study well for the exams.

Class was pretty easy. Did not study much for any of the tests and got As on all of them (there is a pretty generous curve). Felt like I learned a lot, but the lectures can be a bit long and boring as well as repetitive. The INNs were interesting though, and the interactions between him and McDonald were entertaining. Enjoyed the class overall.

Lectures get boring so I watch them at 2x speed. Textbook is provided for free. The quizzes and final paper were extremely easy. The tests are a bit harder but there is a generous curve. Make use of the study guide.
Easiest A of my college career. Moser is a Socialist but that's about it.

The class is structured in a way that make it easy to get an A. The quizzes are easy but the tests are a bit challenging (curves help A LOT). The online lectures can be boring and long, however, this isn't too bad of a class. Also you don't really need to do the assigned readings. I learned so much about foreign policy!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Moser and Mcdonald are very knowledgeable about government but their class is hard due to the lectures being very long and the tests are hard to narrow down answer choices because it's like A, B, C, or A and B, or ABC. Create a GroupMe so you can chat with other students, that was super helpful to me. There are quizzes at the end of every module.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer, immediately following GOV 310 L with a good professor duo. Coming from that forgiving course format, this was unbearable. The exams were very riddle-ish. Exams were proctored, which was super annoying, and he bored me to tears. Unless you're already super interested in foreign policy, I do not recommend Dr. Moser.

Good class, I absolutely despise government but it was a good class, I learned a lot. It's online so beware of deadlines and actually watch the lectures and take notes on it because they are actually helpful. If you do the work you can pass, if you study and review and such you can get an A.

Don't listen to what anyone else says about the difficulty. The workload was extremely doable, I even thought it was very easy class. Professor was caring enough to provide massive accommodations for students during the corona pandemic and made adjustments to the online course, despite having a million people enrolled in the class. Funny guy too.

This class is very straight forward. I don't consider myself good at government, but it was totally manageable. I would recommend studying throughout the year so you don't get behind and you'll do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Doing the study guide the profs send out by yourself AND thoroughly is the key to making an A. I typed notes during lecture to use on the biweekly quizzes and typed study guides to prepare for exams. Have a good understanding of the main points of each reading, which you can get from skimming. Profs were great - lectures were interesting and clear!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a good class to take for the gov credit. You really have to pay attention to all of the lecture material and you have to at least skim the readings, even though they summarize them in lecture. Make sure to study for the midterm exams because they are very memorization based and the answer choices are tricky. Still very possible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The test is just lecture memorization. You actually spend very little time in the class since you don't go to an actual lecture. I recommend opening the weekly quizzes in another tab while watching the lecture to get answers when they're said. The class was interesting to me but I understand gov isn't everyone's cup of tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Provided you read all the assigned reading and watch all of the lectures, you'll probably be fine. Definitely a more tiring course than it is particularly difficult. Moser and McDonald were very understanding during the the transition to remote learning. They do want to see you succeed. And no final! 10/10

Modules can be a bit dull and there are readings with them that can also be boring and sometimes really long. Requires lots of time commitment so dont take this class as a quick and easy a. Exams can be tricky but definitely do the review sheets they help so much. Very knowledgeable prof. Small curve on exams usually. Overall, pretty solid

One of the most tedious classes ever. It's not necessarily hard, it's just so tedious with quizzes due at every module (2 modules per week). Lectures are usually shorter than an in-person lecture, but still feels long. Tests are definitely something to study for - don't blow them off because there's a lot of material you'll need to know.

This class is heavily online-based. The tests are very detailed. It'll be like "both a and b" or "a, c, and b" type questions. The exams aren't THAT bad, but it's a LOT of memorizing. DO THE STUDY GUIDES! Don't just memorize everything from it, try to understand the material by rewatching the lectures at a faster speed. Not too bad, though.

This class was a lot of work and I can see how someone could fail it, but it is 100% possible to make an A without a ridiculous amount of effort. Just do NOT underestimate his exams. The quizzes will prepare you. The tests are very specific, but as long as you read, listen to the lectures he records online, and take good notes you will be fine.

Moser knows his stuff and the online format of this class lets you go at your own pace. You HAVE to study for the tests though because they aren't easy. Listen to the lectures, take notes, read the powerpoint, and do the study guide and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very good online course that actually kept me pretty interested. Time-consuming though. Easiest way to do it is to just go through the powerpoints and study a lot for the tests since those hurt me the most.

An enjoyable class that you can take more or less at your own pace, 2 short quizzes per week (5 questions) based on lectures. Very easy 1-page writing assignments. Tests are not a joke, but easy to get the hang of once used to them. Err on the side of caution, overstudy for the first test: watch every lecture (1.5x speed helps) & use study guide.

It's an online class which is nice since you can pace things according to your own schedule. This class is very low time commitment for a fairly easy A as long as you review the powerpoints and actually actively watch the lectures (instead of looking at your phone like some people do).

Watching the lectures made for easy quizzes and were helpful when it came to the tests. The tests were hard, but if you do the study guide on your own, it really does help. The 2 short answer essays were also easy as long as you watched the module. People try to avoid watching the lectures but they're actually important for this class.

It's a very interesting class and everything outside of the three tests are fairly easy. However, the tests are pretty darn hard. They're full of tricky wording and vague answer choices. His lectures were mostly good and his relationship with Prof. MacDonald was pretty funny. Overall, a solid class. I definitely learned a lot.

The class is fine; lots of Modules and lecture videos to watch. However, I really don't like his tests at all. They're literally designed to trick you into picking the wrong answer. Depending on who you are, studying/cramming for the exams is a lot. You'll study and still get a B. Use Quizlet for the quizzes and read the group review Google Doc tho

The tests definitely require at least a little bit of studying. Moser is an interesting lecturer. The readings are completely unnecessary to do well in this class. Just watch the lecture videos and pay attention and you're set. The two writing assignments are easy.

I took the online GOV class and had a pretty good experience. The module quizzes are really easy, the short answer papers are also pretty easy, but the tests are moderately hard. However, as long as you listen to the lectures and do the study guides Moser provides, you will at least get an A-. Moser is an amazing professor, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you have a decent knowledge of government and current events, this class is easy. He gives a review for all 3 tests where the last 2 reviews covered almost every idea he included on the test. No final. 2-3 modules due each week with easy quiz. 2 short essays (<500 words) on current events. Studied day before each test and never fell below B.

Awesome professor and lectures are very informative and easy to follow. Quizzes twice a week are easy (drops 4) but video lectures are very long. Three exams (no final) are very detailed and difficult (A, B, C, A&B, A&B&C format) but doable if you keep up with two modules a week. Two papers are ridiculously easy. Highly recommend for GOV credit
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3 exams no final with biweekly quizzes. Lectures get long so definitely get a video speed controller. The only hard thing about this class is you have to know a lot of information and the exams are tricky. However, the exams were always curved so if you put in the work you can expect a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved the lectures and listened to them like podcasts. Biweekly quizzes were ridiculously easy but exams really messed up my grade. You have to know the material inside and out and the readings are extremely important. Definitely recommend

i really enjoyed professor mosers lecture videos with professor mcdonald; their bantering takes the edge off of memorizing information i was not interested in. the workload is not bad, with a quiz due every tuesday and thursday and the occasional writing assignment on current news. the tests are tricky with multiple right answers :(
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Moser is very amusing, which makes his lectures pretty engaging, but the class itself consists of a lot of reading and lecture materials (too much, in my opinion). If you can, I would advise taking this class at a community college, because the credit is not worth the dense readings and tricky tests.
a King.

This class is by far the worst class I've taken. The online lectures are unbelievably painful and long, going over the material quickly. For the tests, you have to know everything from the modules. I do my work and get great grades on the quizzes. I study super hard for the tests and still fail bc of how poorly the questions are worded. Don't do it
He is such a nice professor and wants his students to succeed. He is passionate about the material and lectures are very clear. Workload in class is heavy with quizzes and fast past lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you pay attention to what's going on in the news, it is relatively easy to understand the concepts. Always found the lectures to be interesting. 2 professors were funny and knowledgable. Try to listen and make sense of the materials rather than memorize everything. The tests were tricky with the choices of a&b,a&c,b&c,all of the above, but fair.

GOV312L online is probably the best way to take GOV at UT. The tests are very tricky with some answers having 5 options with one saying Both B and C. The big difficulty of this class is the immense amount of material. I received a B because I missed one little part of the writing assignment even though it was implied. Moser is great to listen to.

Moser is the best GOV professor I have had to date. He truly cares about the material and is very considerate with students. One of the more comical professors in lecture as well. I would definitely take a class with him again. I learned a great deal.
gave me a .5/1 on something because I didn't specify something even though it was clearly stated and implied. Had a 96 until the last week of class and then ended up with an 88.
tests are tricky its rlly mean and hurts my feelings. but he does curve. tests are just worth a lot of ur grade so it sucks and i was .17% away from an A lol
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is entertaining, and you will learn a fair bit about the world around you, however, the tests won't reflect that, his tests are a mess like they are multiple choice but they are all over the place. Know the details, cram for two full days before the test.

Took online class. Online quiz every week. Be careful of two 500-word online essays (12.5% of final grade) on current events. Follow essay rules and google on essay prompt to understand well. Three exams taken in assigned room. Exams are curved. Some extra credit. Read and memorize well, you will get A+.

I was told that GOV 312L at UT was difficult, but this class wasn't really that bad. Although the modules were really extensive and way too detailed some times, if you do the study guides before the exams you should be fine. The exams are pretty straightforward and more memorization than application.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Moser is a good professor and is very knowledgable. However, I genuinely disliked this class as Dr. Moser and Dr. McDonald expect a lot from you, including taking extensive notes on long lecture videos, doing long readings and knowing every detail from every module for the test. NOT an easy A. You really have to put in a lot of work to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stay on top of the weekly modules and do the test reviews and you will do fine in this class. The tests are curved, and an A isnt too hard to get. Also, definitely get the plugin that controls video speed bc the lectures are a bit odd.
a very rough class. hard to pay attention to but if you did, it was easy to pass the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class. Mos/McD were knowledgeable and cared about the topic. They wanted us to do well. If you get behind on the modules, expect a lot of stress before tests. Tests are also curved (5-10 pts) so an A is really doable. The downside was that lectures were scripted and hard to follow. Expect to pause and rewatch everything.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For gov 312L, Moser is a good choice. If you do all the modules and the readings, the tests are not bad at all. Gives study guides before exams which are helpful. Gives quizzes every lecture but they are easy if you have done the module. Overall easy if you are willing to do the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class. It requires a lot of reading and watching videos, but the class is interesting and Moser loves what he does. He is very helpful and accessible. To be successful on the tests, DO THE STUDY GUIDE. IT IS SO HELPFUL. I got an A on the tests I did the study guide and a C on the one that I didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The way Moser and Mcdonald interact with each other is hilarious and make the lectures fun to watch. I learned a lot in this class and I'm glad I took it. The pre-lecture modules got to be much at times, and also the tests are pretty tricky. So make sure to go over the modules for the tests.

Didnt have to buy textbook cuz they provided it. Do need to read a lot. If u actually work on ur review sheet for the tests ull be fine. They give curves for every test based on average grade. Highest curve I got was 9 points (brought my test grade to 96.5). Tests are all 40 MCs. Quizzes every class at p much the same time (end of lecture).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Online class, you have to do so much work on your own. Ex. Read 25 pages, watch 1 hr of lecture and read powerpoints twice a week. Test are extremely hard and specific. I studied alot and only made a B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you watch the modules and study for the tests, this class is an easy A. The study guides are extremely helpful. The professors are also great and convey information ver well.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The tests in this course are way too hard for an introductory course. Requires hours of studying for an incredibly tricky test (they do give you a study guide, but it's usually about 15 pages long and takes forever to get through). The tests are usually true/false along with questions like: A, B, C, A and B, B and C, all or none of the above.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Inking gov 312L is pretty easy.. not sure why the reviews are so bad. Just watch lecture, easy quiz every lecture, and do the study guides and youll get an A. no final! just 3 tests

Robert Moser is an excellent professor. Gov 312 as a class is very challenging and you MUST listen to the hour and a half long lectures every Tuesday. They are clear and organized and everything on the review sheet falls on the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Moser is great. He lectures very clearly and does not reflect a biased opinion. The course is structured well for being as large as it is. The exams are all multiple choice and can be tricky if you dont prepare well. I learned a great deal in this course. Do the modules ahead of time and you'll be fine.

Good professor. Tries hard to teach the concepts without letting political views get in the way. The course can go a little fast at times and I always had a relatively hard time on the test. There are lots of outside of class modules to watch. Moser and McDonald interacting with each other was always funny though. Only one real lecture a week.

This class had a lot of work outside of class, especially for a 3 hour class. However, if you watch the lectures and video clips/homework, it's easy to get an A. You do need to study for a day or two before tests, but if you do they aren't bad plus there's usually a curve. Quizzes during lecture were really easy, and you really don't need to read.

He is an average professor. I know it is quite difficult to be non-bias and teach government, but they were so focused on not trying to be biased that they spent little time actually teaching the material. Not a very focused curriculum and felt that the tests were way to tricky for an introduction government course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was not a hard class but you really have to keep up with the readings and modules and take good notes to study for the tests. Grades are only daily quizzes, discussions, and 3 tests. The quizzes are easy but only 5 questions so if you miss one you're already knocked down to an 80. Tests have tricky questions but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class isn't that hard. It does require a fair amount of work between readings and watching the modules. However, if you pay attention to the modules you can skim the readings and be fine. Should be an easy A if you know about government, and should be manageable if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really easy class, just use common sense and pay attention during the modules. Tests are relatively simple. Don't understand the negative reviews.

I think that the people that leave bad reviews are those who have failed this class; I don't think that they're accurate ratings of the class. It was a pretty easy A. The class is flipped but as long as you actually watch and take notes over the modules you'll be fine. Also a study guide for the tests; do and memorize these and you'll get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Online lectures were good, and tests were a little more difficult than one might anticipate but nothing to worry about. Information was effectively covered, and from online quizzes & tests, it's an easy A. The biggest issue was the essay, which made up a good portion of the grade, had unclarified instructions, & grading partial to his views.

He stumbles over his words sometimes, but he's a genuinely good guy who wants his students to pass. He's not the clearest in lectures, but he's a lot better than some other professors I've dealt with. He teaches my class along with Patrick McDonald, who is better with his words, but they make a great team for teaching.

Class setup is great; Moser's awful. He's a bad speaker and cannot talk. Watching him speak's SO frustrating and I don't learn anything from him (luckily I'm good at this subject). His speech though is terrible; his speaking volume fluctuates wildly and he shakes his hand in front of his face. Uncomfortable and irritating lecturer. My frnds agree.

Even as someone intrigued by the class content, Moser's inability to effectively lecture deeply hinders the course experiece. He reads long, disengaging scripts, chokes on his words, has weird cadences and mannerisms that distract and disengage. Yes, the scripts need improvement (or to be thrown out) but Moser does not help the issue in any way.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was really easy, and the lectures were very entertaining. No textbook is required and you read journal entries instead. 3 Exams, all multiple choice. After extra credit, I had a 102 in the class.

Dry professors but interesting content. Tests can be confusing if you do not have detailed knowledge on the subjects. There is a quiz after each online lecture which are fairly simple. Some extra credit given. Take advantage of the material you are given way before the test date; knowing the videos and readings are key to doing well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Moser is an alright professor, sometimes the modules can be very dry and he stumbles on his words often. The class really wasn't that bad; as long as you keep up with the module videos and read the class google docs before a test, you will be fine. The people saying this is the hardest class they have taken haven't taken a STEM course at UT.

Good prof. Live lectures once a week with a 5 question quiz for credit (15% of grade). The rest of the grade is 3 exams (which are in person - heads up). You're responsible for keeping up with weekly modules, which consist of weekly lecture videos and sometimes readings. Workload seems like a lot but it's manageable if you stay on top of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class wasn't that bad. If you want an A, you will have to stick to the schedule that they recommend for you. The professors are really dry and the class can get very boring at the end, but if you just do the review and watch the modules by the dates they give you, you should get an A.

This is class is the hardest class I have ever taken. If you want to risk getting a B, go for it. The exams are extremely hard. There are three exams and about 12 in-class quizzes. Each exam counts for 25-30% of your grade. Quizzes are 15%. The test answers are extremely confusing. No matter how hard I studied, I couldn't get an A on a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Save your GPA and take this class at a community college. This is a core credit, but if you're not a government major/have no interest in it, this class is incredibly difficult. If this is you, the tests are unnecessarily difficult and you have to put in an insane amount of effort just to pass the class
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Make no mistake, this class requires a lot of work and the tests are difficult. However, intense reviews before tests can get you the A. I really enjoyed listening to Moser's views on foreign policy and I would definitely recommend him.
The class overall isn't too bad but the test are ridiculous. The questions they ask are poorly worded and i'm just happy to have gotten this class over with.

For people who said this class is easy, its not. I am a hard working student and this was my hardest class. The modules are very time consuming and they talk too fast. The tests basically try to trick you on every questions. I studied a week in advance for every test, thought I did good and only got a B (including curve). Moser is cool though.

Cool professor. His class is not hard. The worst part is the two hour binge watch of all the lectures the night before the live class, which is when he has an easy 5 question quiz. If you study the Google Doc review (on the class Facebook page) the day before exams and you pay attention to politics, you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class isn't bad if you have a general understanding of current news and politics and government. I did half the material and managed a B, but it is a lot of material and videos to watch. Essay takes a good 10 hours of work time. Take it if you are a good student and/or someone that coasts through classes but understands the news.

The ethics essay is graded hard-ish, so make sure you do well on the exams. The exams are all MC and very detail-oriented. You don't have to do the readings, which are really long, but it was a really informative class overall

Took him in an online class. There is a lot of outside work to be done for this class between the learning modules and the assigned readings. Tough class overall, but he made it enjoyable and interesting.

Moser literally reads off a teleprompter for all of the required lecture videos, but stutters on every other word. He is a bad lecturer and is unclear in both his slides and module videos. Overall, the class is a lot of work but not too bad. The professor, on the other hand is pretty god awful. Exams have poor word choice and bad grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The course work for this class is pretty heavy. I do not recommend this class to anyone who is not interested in government. The online course is more like a flipped classroom, you watch lecture videos on your own to learn the material. You only meet once a week for live lecture. Exams are extremely detailed so pay close attention to EVERYTHING!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Took the online class. Moser teaches it with one other professor, McDonald, and they're pretty funny together. The class actually only has live lecture once a week, but there are quite a few videos you have to watch. No homework besides that. I never do the readings and I do just fine, since they discuss them in the videos they have you watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are sooo horrible because they literally read a teleprompter and stutter and struggle with their own words. It's hard to learn because of this. My eyes glaze over. Class/quiz is online only ONCE a week but there's a lot of videos you have to watch outside of class. Required readings are long but you don't actually need to read them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: hard exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Drop if you have to. You're better off taking government at community college. Prepare to read. I spent hours each day doing the readings. You won't pass without doing the readings. Do not repeat mistakes other students have made. Biggest regret I've made.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Grades tough. If you do not put specifically what they want you to put then you might as well pencil yourself in as a B. Tests are way harder than they should be. TAs grade like you have to quote the textbook. Would not recommend. Should have taken community college Gov.

Moser and his partner in crime McDonald are really great guys, but this class is hard. I got an A- after working harder than I have for any other class. A good choice for government at UT, but maybe take it during a light semester. Don't double it up with math for example. Online format is nice, but it requires self regulation and discipline.

Moser was awesome. It's true that there are pop quizzes, but they are pretty easy. I'm pretty bad at the liberal arts, and I made a 100 on every single quiz. Do your reading, watch the modules, take notes on the modules and on online lectures, and USE YOUR STUDY GUIDE FOR EXAMS. They're long, but if you know all questions, it's a guaranteed A.

Compared to other online classes I have taken at UT, this class definitely required an excessive amount of work. Tests are hard and over specific concepts, they usually curve though. A lot of homework in the form of "quizzes". Lectures are usually short and end early which is nice; both Moser and Mcdonald are interesting to listen to.

Prof. Moser is funny, I end up laughing at a bunch of the stuff he says and it makes his lectures/explanations a lot more engaging and relatable. He makes concepts very clear and I would definitely take him again.

Great class! Was more difficult than 310L, but was so informative and explains FP in a way that is helpful for people who come in without knowing anything. Him and Roberts are very funny together! Pre-Class modules can be time consuming, and the test review is really long, but it is extremely comprehensive. If you can do the review you'll be fine!

Moser is an amazing professor. He really knows his stuff, is very clear, thoroughly enjoys teaching, and makes it interesting. My only complaint is the difficulty level of this course. The homework is ridiculously long and no matter how hard I study I can't seem to get a good test grade. You will learn a TON but not worth the GPA drop.

Very basic foreign policy class. Extremely well informed with actual experience and a passion for teaching. 10/10 would recommend. I gave Helpfulness a 3 because I never needed or asked for it but from what I hear it is available.

I've never really enjoyed government, but this class made learning about politics and foreign policy extremely enjoyable. The structure of the course allows the amount of work you put into the class to be reflected in your final grade. The lectures were interesting and funny. Great and insightful professor and I recommend this class highly to all.

I LOVED THIS CLASS. I cannot stress enough how amazing this class has been for me. It's made me really understand politics. Moser incorporates current events in the lectures which has made me exponentially more knowledgable on these situations. This class will really interest anyone with an open mind and of any major. I wish I could take it again!!

I LOVED THIS CLASS. It's extremely interesting and makes current events palatable. Office hours are great to answer questions. You have to watch the lectures but notes are optional. Moser and McDonald are a hilarious team  and taught me to love the news. They incorporate current events which makes the class useful regardless what major you are.

His teaching is pretty straight-forward and you get what earned for your grade. Take notes, do the reviews, skim through the readings- you should get an A. I made the mistake of not listening to lectures and just letting my laptop play the video while I laid down. I survived by doing reviews the day before the tests. 3 exams, all multiple choice.

Dr. Moser is funny, kind, interesting, and fair. Really the ideal teacher. Along with Prof. McDonald, he would insert jokes into what would otherwise be dull lectures. The class is an easy A if you spend about 4 hours reading each week. In fact, I made a 100+ on each of the tests.

Along with  McDonald, Moser is a pretty interesting guy that is very fascinated about foreign policy, especially Russia and Putin. Although he is sometimes overshadowed by McDonald, he sticks some really helpful information from time to time. it can be hard to pay attention to a 1.5 hr long lecture on a screen; it will take discipline.

Worst decision I ever made. I am a hard working student and this was lowest class grade I have ever received. The lectures are long and he talks so fast. For the exams, there is a review, but it's EVERYTHING that was in lectures, so you are expected to know everything from an entire semester, for 40 multiple choice questions. DO NOT TAKE!

His online GOV 312L class is pretty awesome. I didn't pay attention sometimes, but for the most part his lectures are interesting, he includes current events and talks about debatable issues and we get to see where we are on the spectrum compared to the rest of the class. 2 tests and 1 paper. Pretty easy overall. Just go over the powerpoints.

If people were passing the class, they were cheating. Me and my friend failed the class and we did our work! The questions on the tests were freakishly detailed. Just take this credit at a community college.
He's among the best lecturers I've ever had. However, his tests are not very good measures of knowledge acquired, and his general grading policies are confusing and (often) very upsetting.
He's one of the best professors in the department. Definitely take as many of his classes as you can.

Professor Moser is a great professor and he teaches outstandingly, his only pitfall is his awful choice of TAs, as they are the ones who grade the essays, it's hard for them not to have the greatest impact on your grades.

outstanding professor..as mentioned, expertly presents somewhat boring material in a very precise, clear manner.  Tests are half mult choice/half take home essay.  Final is a take home essay.  Awesome guy, very knowledgable
Awesome -very clear, straightforward. Makes a difficult subject easy to understand. Go to lectures for a good grade!
Great prof.  Very helpful and clear.  Made an otherwise boring class very interesting.

Very nice, funny, and approachable. In class lectures were kind of difficult to follow because they weren't very organized. Not much given to help you study for exams but only a few assignments the whole semester was nice to have

This was the first coding class I took and I'm really glad it was with Dr. Tisato. His lessons were clear and easy to follow. If you haven't taken coding before, it's hard at the beginning, but don't worry, you will get it eventually. Be patient. And don't worry, he will curve. Great professor. He's relaxed and has a good sense of humor.

I took him for the coding class and I did not enjoy it at all. Tisato himself was completely adorable - so funny and kind and patient. Unfortunately, that did not make the content any more understandable. His teaching is not clear and the class is very difficult, especially if you have no previous coding experience.

Very easy lab BUT only if you have a good TA. My TA Alberto was the best and only reason why I got a good grade. The research reports are a waste of time and add nothing to the course, but the actual lab itself is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Mind-numbingly tedious for intro lab. Grading is SO nitpicky. Don't expect a 100 on anything. Quizzes + prelab are fine. Extra credit saved my A. So few points for what feels like days of work per assignment. Cannot wait for this class to be over. Did not like my TA but had subs who were much more chill let us out early, played music, etc
Insane amount of work for a 2 hour lab credit. Unless you really like microbiology or bacteria this class will be more tedious and stressful than it should be.

sooo ta dependent you NEED a good one, youll never see Dr. Maas. the prelabs can be long but are supa easy. the actual labs are pretty fun and the quizzes arent that bad. the worst part are the research reports which can take a lot of time to write esp if u arent passionate abt it. just hope u get a good lab groub and a good ta and its an easy A

Lowkenuily, this class is very TA dependent (my TA is rlly good) so reviews vary. The pop quizzes are easy if you do the pre-labs. Not too much work just weekly research reports and a poster at the end. Very accessible, I once had a good conversation to Dr. Maas about my interests after undergrad. I don't like how the textbook is required $$.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, you will hardly ever see Dr. Maas unless you go to her office hours- this class is 100% TA dependent. I lucked out and got the best TA (shout out Sawyer), but I had friends who did not get as lucky. The grading rubric is clear and you can extra credit, but you can only miss 10 points the whole semester to get an A. Fun class though!
Lots of busy work (at least 40Q prelabs and post lab writeup every week).

The overall course is easy, just too much work for 2 credit hours. The prelabs are really long. The tests and the lab practical are pretty easy except for the last test which was unreasonably difficult considering the rest of the course, but it was given an ungodly curve so it worked out in the end. Just hope for a good TA, aka Kate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The research project was so interesting, but the workload was unnecessary and unreasonable. Pre-labs are long and exhausting and weekly reflections are graded arbitrarily. The final poster project also depends highly on your groupmates. On the bright side, an A is achievable if you keep up with the work.
exams were graded harshly and some of those questions are super specific, a lot of prelabs and research reports that are graded harshly and only have 1 drop, doing tooooo much for a lab course

Maas doesn't do anything except write the tests (which are random and do not prioritize what you learn in the class). Maegan was my TA and she was great but Maas' friend and was so unprofessional but nice. Most chill class ever but does not live up to UT standards. So much busy work in class but easy and chill overall.

You will only see Dr. Maas twice, the class is ran by TAs. I got Ally, who was simply the best. Your experience in the semester will be decided by your lab group. The content itself (the Tiny Earth Project) is actually really interesting, but it is quite a bit of work for a lab. Expect to spend an hour or two outside of class every week.

I will not tolerate Marco slander!! He is fantastic and very knowledgeable. I found this lab very enjoyable overall; we always had interesting work, and the semester project was engaging. The midterm and final/midterm were a bit ridiculous in terms of their content and specificity. Aside from that, it is very achievable to earn a high grade.
The class itself was not hard, but it was because marco was a great TA and helped us improve a lot! Some TAs make it very hard tho, but the class also lowk has a lot of busy work

I actually really liked this class. The pre-labs are pretty long, especially the quizzes. But if you actually read them, you'll do well in this class. The exams are more about understanding the material, there is no need to memorize the quizzes. Just be prepared for a good amount of work for a 2-hour credit class.

Way too much busy work! The exams were also terrible. Why are there two exams, a poster, and a lab practical? Mass was incompetent in preparing us for the exams, and the questions were open-ended and subjective, which the TAs are required to grade. However, I will not tolerate Marco slander; he was the saving grace TA of this horrible class.

Maas will make you hate bio lab. Tests are ridiculous unless you've been studying pre labs word for word, hours of busy work, and small amounts of points taken off for like every assignment that add up quickly and will drop your grade. TA was okay and my group was chill, but for an INTRO lab course this is ridiculous and a terrible experience.

Relatively easy lab, 1 low stakes pre-lab quiz before class, lab photos and report due at the end of each week, 2 tests (one mid semester and one at the end), and a lab poster summarizing work throughout the semester. Dr. Maas was very kind and helpful. My TA Marco was very genuine and helpful, but I know some TAs were more difficult than others.
Rubrics do not reward understanding of material but rather how closely your short answer response mirrors hers. Her answers are not even especially good. Far below standard for UT.

There is soooooo much busy work for this 2 hour INTRO lab. I spend more time on this class than I do for genetics and ochem. That is not ok. She also will blow up your canvas email for so many unnecessary reasons. Way way way too much work for this kind of class.

I spent more time on this class than on Ochem. Way too much work for a lab and extremely strict. If a question asks your age you better explain the day you were born, why you were born, where, when, go ahead and include why your parents met too. I lost so so many points for not including random things that weren't even asked for. Never left on time

You need to attend every lab and if you miss one there is no makeup available. If you miss more than one then it starts impacting your grade heavily. She also has a lot of policies that seem unreasonable such as only having up to 24 hours to discuss an assignment grade even if it's a mistake on her part.
Worst class I've had at UT. Lots of pointless work and so many messages on canvas. For a 2 hr credit intro lab the busy work is crazy

Heavily, heavily dependent on your TA. Unfortunately, you can't know if you have a good or bad TA until you're a few weeks into the semester, past the drop deadline. We had limited interaction with Dr. Maas (which is just a reflection of how the course is set up... she can't teach ~700 students at once). She was caring when I went to her OH.

Didn't see the professor once, depends on who you get for a TA, semester long group project so also pray for good teammates. Not too much work and you never do busy work in lab, always actually doing something.

Although I had a fantastic TA, the course structure is not good. It made me realize I never want to go into a lab ever again, as I would dread bio lab every week. The assignments are easy but lengthy (when you add up the time spent for only 2 credit hours) + a pointless final. Def not the end of the world if you have to take this though

I felt that I did more work for this class than a 2 hour lab should be. It was often frustrating when points would get taken off of assignments for no good reason other than just not wanting to give out 100s.

I love bio but this lab is disorganized, inconsistent, and frustrating. Grading criteria is nitpicky, yet there is practically no communication about what is expected. So, you end up constantly trying to guess what she wants. I also felt like the emphasis on ethics was an irritating waste of time. (Not what I paid for in a lab course, UT!)

This class is an insane amount of work for a 2 hour credit. The weekly lab reports are NOT helpful and neither are the ethics discussions. Your experience depends on your TA, but be prepared to put in time outside of class. Dr. Maas herself is extremely unhelpful and not approachable. I'd recommend taking another upper division bio lab if you can.

Dr. Maas is really nice, but your experience is based on your TAs. Im not the smartest cookie, and this was the easiest class I have ever taken. Even if your TA grades harsh, Lab reports are like 8 two-sentence questions...it's not that deep lol. People just complain, take the class and you'll do great. I spent MAYBE 2 hrs a week on it outside lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: "Pre-labs, weekly lab reports, biweekly lab photos assignment, weekly Perusall assignment, Group Research Project, Research presentations, Lab Practical, AND a Final Exam" retweet. Dr Maas is always nice, but if your TA sucks.. RIP you (and my 4.0)

Only saw Dr. Maas a few times but she seems sweet and is great with communicating through Canvas messages. The difficulty of this course is dependent upon your TAs (shoutout to Sawyer and Chandan for being awesome!!) and if you happen to get a good group, but it is a very fun and interesting lab!

If you can take this lab online. ITS SUCH A GAMBLE. my TA was awful, he never believed on giving 100s for ANY assignment - was incredibly picky on assignments, while other TAs graded much easier. We never left lab early even when it was just looking at posters - many other labs left within 30 mins at times. You either get lucky or you dont.

Pre-labs, weekly lab reports, biweekly lab photos assignment, weekly Perusall assignment, Group Research Project, Research presentations, Lab Practical, AND a Final Exam...for an intro bio lab course. The course is not hard and the labs are pretty fun, but all this for 2 credit hours is inconceivable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She exudes bitterness, as if she regrets every decision that led her here, and she seems intent on dragging everyone else down with her. UT students deserve far better than this miserable excuse for a professor. She should be fired immediately.

This professor is, without a doubt, the worst I have ever encountered. I have always loved biology, yet she single-handedly made me despise it. She is an absolutely atrocious educator—she explains nothing, offloads all responsibilities onto her TAs (who, frankly, do her entire job for her), and is completely unapproachable.

This class is HEAVILY dependent on your TA. I was lucky to have a great TA (thanks Avery!) that really wanted students to do well. The TAs decide the quiz questions, grade the lab reports, basically run the lab. Remember to do pre-labs and perusalls. Dr. Maas wants EVERYONE to participate the final group project which sucks when your group slacks

The professor is not even the one teaching the class. It is the lead TAs. Your grade is pretty much based on who your lead TA is. Mine was awful but my friend had a wonderful TA. You also take three quizzes but she makes you study like 100 questions and only 5-7 questions will be asked. Reports were graded harshly from my lead TA as well.

The professor is not involved at all, and the course is run by the TA. If you get a bad TA, it can be difficult to do good in the course. As long as you stay on top of the extensive workload, and learn the grading style of your TA you should get an A.

the professor has 0 to do with the class 
 it's all TA led, allyson was the best TA ever !! however i heard having a bad TA can completely mess up your experience. the class was graded basically as participation and if you show up and do everything you will get a good grade, she sends a ton of emails so it's impossible to miss deadlines
Horrible TA and she doesn't care. She'll send a bunch of messages/announcements but won't respond to emails.

Not involved at all. Does not respond to her emails but emails you a TON. Does not care about her students if anything happens to them. Her attendance and deadlines are very harsh and if you email her even if something horrible happened to you she does not respond and you have a 0 for the assignment. TA's can't change your grades either ugh.

I thought the Perusall component was not useless. Harshness of attendance especially with someone with accommodations, was not accommodating at all... Dr. Maas never responds to her emails and even after asking my TA to reach out to her multiple times she did not respond to me. My TA was lovely. Dr. Maas was not involved at all. Entirely TA led.

The professor was rarely available, but the TAs, especially mine, made labs engaging. Weekly reports, photos, and Pursuall assignments kept the workload steady and manageable. Quizzes were challenging, yet manageable with Quizlet prep. Overall it's easy to recieve and A in this class if you just do the work.

The lab is engaging, with weekly prelab and reports that are quick to complete. Rarely see the professor, but the TAs make the experience fun. Loved using unstuck ai and ChatGPT for study prep - really helpful!

The curriculum was restructured, so only looked at reviews 2023 and beyond. There was a pre lab every week which was the only thing I would complain about bc sometimes they were a little time consuming. Overall though, great lab experience. I learned a lot and had fun. Just study ALL the prelab questions for final (they'll release answers at end)

only met her once! sweet lady but not involved in the class. you are with your RA's the whole time for the lab. super easy and group project was easy. loved making friends with my lab mates. weekly ethics post, prelab, and lab reflections (took a lot of time to complete) final exam is a big % of your grade but it is all pre lab questions so easy:)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I LOVED THIS LAB!!!!! I was so lucky and had an amazing group. The lab itself is fun and you get to do a lot of hands on stuff with the end goal of making a poster. My group ended up getting full points of the poster and it was so rewarding. loveddddd this lab! loved my TA and LA!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You'll most likely never see the professor but so it depends on TA for your lab. Fun lab experience but the one thing is pre-lab takes forever to do and there is a final exam which is pre-lab questions. Overall a great intro bio lab.

This class was great, and I think the recent curriculum update made the class more fun and engaging! I never had to worry about this class, as the work most weeks consisted of a prelab over the weekend (1-2 hrs), Perusall assignment, and lab report (1 hr). I saw Dr. Maas periodically, but mostly engaged with my LI and TA. Highly recommend!!!

The new curriculum has made this class so much more bearable. You never really interact with Dr. Maas, so everything is really TA dependent. That being said, there is not a lot of work per week, but definitely not a class you can ignore. If your TA is chill, you will pretty much always leave lab 30-45 minutes early.

This class is a giant waste of time and is not organized as an intro course should be. You must pay for access to course materials on top of tuition, and the pre-labs are worthless piles of garbage. She also floods your email with spam and the grading criteria is terrible. Designed to waste your time and frustrate you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The new lab structure was fun and engaging. Requires weekly pre labs, and post lab assignments but they were never too demanding. Email notifications were frequent though, but helpful I guess if you can't stay on top of your work. Final poster at the end with lab mates, so it also depends on your TA and people you work with. Overall fun!

The restructured lab is engaging, with weekly tests contributing to a bigger end goal. Pre-lab assignments and reports are short (totaling two hours of work max per week). Perusall ethics discussions, though somewhat tedious, are informative and not difficult. Labs, scheduled for two hours, typically finish in one. Overall, it's a fun, easy class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was structured horrendously. Who makes students spend hours on pre-lab material in order to be prepared for insanely detailed pre-lab quizzes? The labs themselves were more or less fine, but then the post-lab quizzes were again another issue. Terribly written and designed to fail students, even if they do understand the actual material.

Lab was really fun but you don't ever see Dr Maas. It's all about who your LI is (shoutout Ryan you were great). Low-stress class with little work each week and no lab report. Your lab group will make or break the class for you since you have to work with them every day and do the project with them. Dr Maas sent an excessive amount of emails lol

You really never see Dr. Maas, it's all about your LI and TA. The grade is based on a weekly prelab, lab notebook photos, progress report, weekly ethics assignments, and the final poster. They all seemed like completions grades, so just show up and you'll get an A. Super fun class and way more interesting than a typical intro-lab course.

I took BIO 206L after they switched the curriculum and it was an easy, interesting, fun lab. One weekly online prelab, lab photo submission, and some ethics assignment due at the end of the week. If you can get a good LI, this lab is genuinely so much fun and not a stressor at all. I highly recommend Sawyer Stubbs, she was awesome!!

its a lab so mainly TA interaction; revamping the curriculum was truly the right choice. such a manageable and interesting lab, the final grade is a poster presentation on your semester research. shout out to allyson, best LI ever ever and if you get a good lab group this will be such a vibe. assignments are super manageable, completion grades.

low-maintenance class. one prelab/week online, two labs in-person. the new curriculum is interesting! we did antibiotic research based on soil samples, which is really relevant right now. we submitted research updates/photos once/week and some ethics assignments which sucked a little. end of semester final is a poster presenting our research.

New curriculum compared to previous semesters you research antibiotic production in soil samples with your group Super fun and easy Nothing is graded harshly at all, there's just prelabs which barely take any time, weekly reports that's just a summary of what you did in lab and peer reviews End of semester you present group's online poster free 100
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The bio lab curriculum is new this semester so do not read into reviews for past semesters. Really interesting, no lectures, research over bacteria found in soil you collect with your group, several cool assays, final poster project that you do with your lab group over bacteria, learn many basic lab skills, ethics assignments sprinkled in.

Maas is obsessed with academic integrity, and she will accuse you of cheating if she gets the chance. She is unapproachable and will not communicate with you. The best way to do well in this lab is to go to TA's office hours. Hope you get a good TA or this lab's going to be torture

Her lectures weren't really helpful in my opinion, but she gives Instapoll questions at the end for credit so I suggest going. The quizzes were graded harshly with no clear rubric and they make up a huge chunk of your grade. There is also a lab practical on which you aren't given much information on. The class should not have been this difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I showed up to all the lectures and classes but I found the class really hard. You may find yourself struggling if you're like me with no previous lab experience. The structure was horrible which is probably why it's being changed to be more free lab. Kuang Hu (TA) is rude and does not care about your learning. He should not be a TA. Awful.

Overall, had a decent time in this class. Her lectures were fine if kinda oddly mixed with ethical concepts. Learned a lot of basic lab skills I found interesting, hopefully, ones I can use in future classes/jobs. My group personally had a good TA, but that is a very deciding factor in your grade for better or worse. Go for the class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst + hardest class Ive taken at uni!!!
If she actually cared about our success she would make the class easier to do well in/curve like other professors. Not worth all the time and effort at all.

Good teacher. Has one lecture a week to go over the lab and all the information you will need for it. There are two quizzes over the lab itself so make sure to take detailed lab notes. The TA sets the tone for the lab itself, but all lab activities are the same.

I truly did enjoy my time doing the labs and learning the biological aspects behind them. What killed me were the very picky quizzes+unprepared and undetailed lab report expectations. TAs were amazing however everything ran outside of the lab itself and was pretty subpar. If you miss one ethics assignment, your grade is down a letter. Be prepared.

This course was not that bad. I generally enjoyed the labs and the LRQs were not as time consuming for me as chem lab. It can be easy to lose points, especially the "select all that apply" questions, but you can refer to the lab manual/lecture slides for most of it. The lab practical is not bad either if you participate in lab & attend the mock.

lab report grades based on tas. maas makes you buy brand new $80 lab manual/each sem so you cant buy used for cheaper. grading criteria unclear, no type of rubric provided yet expected to follow a specific template that we are never given. lectures were mandatory (instapolls) and unhelpful. i never referred back to her lectures slides for any info

Attendance is mandatory since she has Instapoll. The concept exam is straightforward if you pay attention to the material she gives each week. The practical was a lot for the short amount of time she gives but the TA is really kind about grading and works with you if you participate in labs. The ethics paper took the most time so start early.
She makes lab much more difficult than it has to be. If you want to succeed, go to your TA's office hours every week because the assignments are graded harshly.

Basically entirely TA based. If you get a good one then you have a good shot of getting a good grade in the class. Mine was amazing. Maas structures the class in an annoying way with participation instapolls and select all that apply LRQs. Concept exam was a bit random. Honestly do FRI or ARI if you can but if not then buckle up.

Labs are all annoying but this one wasn't hard to do good in. Sometimes I would skip lecture and just do the instapoll questions on my own when it was time for them. Some of the lab report questions were hard (like the select all ones) but if you ask your TA they'll probably point you in the right direction and most are answered in the lab manual.
The lab is fun, that is the only good thing about this class. Other than that this class is simply a waste of time with none of the stuff that I will remember in my college career.

very difficult class. lab reports are exceedingly vague yet harshly graded. lots of "select all that apply" questions with at least a dozen extremely specific answer choices. concept exam has a lot of questions over arbitrary facts that were never emphasized. dr. maas just makes the intro bio lab course much more difficult than it should be.

My TA was awesome for this class so for that reason I didn't think the lab was too bad; however, Dr. Maas designs the labs to take the full time so if you have a 6-10 pm lab expect to be there until 9:30. The concept exam was pretty difficult and the LRQs had a ton of vague select all that apply questions not to mention the $80 lab manual...

Dr. Maas is very nice but there is a lot of busy work in this class. You are required to write a summary of all labs and read ethics articles for discussions during lab. The LRQs have true/false sections with topics we never talked about in class. Concept exam is mostly ethics based. We should have had more lab time to prep for the lab practical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was the most confusing class I have taken at UT. Instructions are unclear, there's not enough information to do well, and your TA makes or breaks your grade. You will likely spend the entire 4 hours in lab and it'll feel like busy work. The lectures are not that helpful but are required. Overall the course could be taught a lot better

The labs itself are okay, but for the most part, you WILL stay the full 4 hrs. Maas and TAs grade off an arbitrary rubric as there's none given, and very little instructions are provided. BEFRIEND YOUR TA, and go to their OH if you want to do good on the LRQs.  Use an old manual and save money, the instructions aren't changed. She j wants money.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
- Purposely does not share information regarding quizzes, or tests
- Lectures are very evidently more focused on passing time
- Some "Learning Instructors" forces students to stay for 4 hours during labs even if you are done
- Forces students to buy her own book for $80 which we NEVER really use
- Reads of lecture slides, and can't answer questions

The labs themselves aren't difficult, it's the LRQs that will really bring down your grade. The LIs and Professor Maas grade assignments very harshly, with little to no instructions for each LRQ. Poorly taught class.
This is my last semester at UT and this class was the most tedious and hardest graded. The lab reports need more detailed instructions.

Maas by herself isn't terrible, except that she extorts her students. She writes a lab manual that barely changes each year, and makes every student purchase it, so she can profit. The worst part? Ryan the TA. He grades so harshly, takes off random points, and is overall a degrading and righteous person. This class is the worst I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Maas is very passionate and knowledgeable about the field, but the course difficulty is skewed because of the grading system. The labs are actually fun, but make sure you understand the lab materials thoroughly. Also, be friends with your LI, it will only help you. Do what she expects you to do, and you will get what you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Depending on your LI is how your grade is determined as they all grade differently. On top of this, you can only go to your LI's office hours with that being once/wk. How things are graded can also be unforgiving as everything is make or break, especially the LRQs. One thing I learned though is you can receive answers from the LIs for the LRQS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Every LRQ counts, and your grade sadly depends on whichever LI you get. Dr. Maas's lectures prepare you for the lab but barely cover ethics which doesn't help you on the awful ethics exam at the end of the semester. The labs are fun, but the preparation and homework take up too much time for a 2 credit hour class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Maas isn't too bad, but do not take the LRQs lightly. Email your LI about every graph, because they want to help you and you won't be given clear grading criteria.
