I got mostly Cs on my LRQs and I regret not asking for feedback. Overall, the lab is interesting and fun but be sure to communicate with your LI as often as possible.

Do FRI or wait until 226L. Dr. Maas is nice, but you're going to have to ask for help for every single assignment in order to get the grade you want. The ethics exam dropped my grade so much bc of actual server issues and nothing was done. My LI was very kind and helped me through a lot. Knowing what I know now, I wouldn't bother taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is simply the head of the class, it all depends on your LI. I had a great one, but she wasn't the one making the rules, Maas was. Focused more on ethics than actual lab which was very weird and doesn't really care about the students. Also, for a 2 hr credit, this class requires at least about 8 hrs in total so 0/10 would never recommend!

Dr. Maas is nice but the class is overall bad. So much work when you're only quizzed on super specific and random details. Spent hours and hours on this class and never knew how to properly prepare. Feedback was not useful/not provided. Content shouldn't have been difficult but structure of class made things way harder than it needed to be.

Professor Maas was, at least for me, very unorganized? I'm unsure if this is the right word, so for clarification: nothing expected of me is clear. I never knew what to study to prepare for labs/quizzes, and the lab review questions were to test my understanding after a lab, but no feedback was given nor was I corrected.

This is an EXTREMELY difficult class if you have Ryan as your TA. I went to every office hour and went to every class, and it was still so difficult. The ethics exam was so hard, and we have never had to deal with those types of questions before. Dr. Maas focused on insignificant details on the ethics exam rather than the holistic concepts.
The LRQs are structured to be confusing and tricky to understand. She seems more focused on making you memorize tiny details than actually learn about biology or ethics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grade is LRQs. LRQ MC questions are very semantic, and the FRQs are vague. Even if you have a "good" TA, and conceptually understand everything, and go to office hours to clear up some confusions, you will struggle to make more than an 85 on these LRQs. Your grade in this class does not depend on your understanding, but these terribly created LRQs.

For being a 2 hour class, this was A LOT of work. LRQs are worded ambiguously sometimes and warmup quizzes cover very obscure content from the ethics readings or the lecture and lab manual. However, as long as you are dedicated, can follow lab procedures, and know what you're doing an A is not hard to get.

The quizzes and LRQs are made to make you lose points since the questions are focused on minor details of the lab or things that were not taught. It's not worth it to spend hours on homework and lab prep to get bad grades on everything. Before our final, 30% of our class had an A or A- and class average was an 85. Grades are on a point based system

Although your experience in this class is mostly determined by your LI, Dr. Maas still does a great job organizing the class. If you put in the time to take notes for quizzes, put effort into the LRQs, and attend office hours for help, it's a guaranteed A. She has super cool labs and ethics topics- you will learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Maas was great as a Lab professor. Her lectures aren't mandatory but I found that they helped a lot. Your grade really depends on your LI, so its really up to chance unfortunately.

I didn't attend first 2 labs, or many of the in-person lectures. Even still, I found myself liking the class. She's a nice person, not a lot of contact with her though, most contact is with LI. LI matters lots, recommend getting a good rapport with them. (won't change grades but will make labs easier) LRQs suck but good notes can go far in labs.

Dr. Maas herself wasn't involved in much of the course at all. The LI's are the ones instructing as well as grading, so who you end up with is pretty much how your semester will go. There's an unnecessary amount of time needed for taking notes and the labs are largely busy work. The ethics half is interesting, but not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pretty straight forward class, that being said though a lot of assignments are unnecessary in their own way. Ethics heavy, although some topics are interesting it's essentially just busy work to pile onto students and can take away from important lab info. TA's grade unnecessarily harsh and demand perfection... very nit picky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Your grade in the class itself is heavily going to depend on which LI you have. Experiments are boring and the quizzes are meant to bring your grade down. You almost never see the actual professor and to make it worse, she loves to try to gaslight individuals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Maas class is taught by the TAs. My TA, Ryan, was a very good choice. He was very knowledgeable, caring, and accessible outside of class. However, the class itself was time-consuming, lots of HW, and the grading was a bit harsh (for all the lab sections Ive heard). If you work hard and study a lot for the practical, you will likely do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Depends on LI. No grading criteria. Some LI only take off whole points while others take 0.25. Very easy class don't need much brain, a lot of stupid work.

This class really depends on your LI, and unless you attend the optional lectures you won't even see the prof. A lot of reading and note taking is required before each class. I felt like I learned a lot with this class, but it definitely requires a lot of work if you don't want to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Everything concerning your grade is determined by the TA which sucks but there are opportunities to challenge grades, if you feel mistreated in anyway make use of them. Some of the TAs can be very nitpicky so pay attention to all the details. Lab practical was very stressful but they were relatively generous when grading it.

This class isn't as bad as some people say. I've taken other lab courses and this one was so much easier. The labs are long and annoying but everything is straight forward. The quizzes can be a tricky but I still managed an A after bombing a few of them. Final is hit or miss. Overall- as long as you get a decent TA- it isn't that bad.

Everything in this lab depends on your TA and how they grade. Assignment wise, there are no lab reports, just a few LRQs due every week. The labs themselves are very doable with detailed instructions. We had to pay $70 for the lab manual, which is pretty steep. The lab practical exam was horrible and hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took the class and did well. Initially I was about to drop the class because I was nervous about the grading and quizzes. However I managed to assuage those fears really quickly after trying super hard for the first two LRQs. I did spend 4-6 hours outside of class to do do each LRQ and take notes for quizzes. A lot of work for a 2 hour class though

Ridiculous quizzes and LRQs with the most freestyle grading I've EVER seen. The quizzes are literally so random, they'll have you studying for 2+ hrs to make sure you've written everything down. I've even heard one of the other TA take off points because a student finished lab early. God FORBID students are efficient in time management.

Worst class ever. Had to complete quizzes that focused on the smallest details of the exercise, and LRQs were a pain to complete without any clear directions of what the TA wanted to see. TAs were super hard graders and nitpicky. Ridiculous final lab practical. Ridiculous class

Made an account just to describe the clownery. The most ludicrous grading I've ever encountered. She will take points off for not including things that were never asked for, and I've been told multiple times that I didn't include something when I clearly did. Not many points total so each one counts. CH204L and FRI are way more reasonable.

I was excited for this course going into it, but looking back at the semester it was pretty disappointing. I felt that I was learning less about biology lab experiments and more about the small grading details on the assignments and quizzes in this class. Even if you understand the material and put in effort you can perform badly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AWFUL. Worst class ever. Your grade is based on these stupid LRQs that they are SO picky about. They have NO rubric so your grade is absolute BS. RUN FROM THIS CLASS. DO NOT TAKE IT. The lab practical was hard, the class runs for 4 hours and is not worth it for TWO credits... Take FRI. Trust me. This class is HORRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is awful and a sad excuse for a bio lab. LRQs are graded extremely randomly and the lab instructor takes of 10 points from lab write ups for every little thing they can (keep in mind the stuff they take off for is never mentioned in the instructions and questions). The lab takes all 4 hours everytime. Terrible professor and terrible LIs

Does not give a rubric for LRQs so you always lose points. 5 hours of lecture/lab per week for only 2 hours of credit. Warmup quizzes are random and sporadic in what they ask. Spend more time on ethics than actually learning biology or lab techniques. UT should really find someone better to teach this intro lab. Many complaints from peers too.

Absolutely horrible. This is an INTRO lab - I should not be having to spend 6 hours a week on this class. I did NOT sign up for a course on ethics - I signed up for a biology lab. This INTRO lab takes more time than upper-division courses. Useless memorization and super picky grading even when students answer the questions to satisfaction.

Dr. Maas is a great professor and choice. Took her during Summer 2021. LRQ's each week, the TAs offer great help (Sawyer is amazing!). UGLA give feedback, especially when you email questions. Labs once a week, no lab quizzes. Concept exam at the end was very straightforward from labs. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: People are giving her a hard time here, but tbh her class was pretty okay. You will lose a few points here and there on LRQS. Good thing is the Ethics and Home Activities are graded p chill, so do your very best on that. Don't miss any extra credit. The final concept exam was very doable if you went through all the lecture notes before the test
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Biggest complaint I have against the class is that they never release your LRQ answers after you submit them. They take a million years to grade off of some arbitrary rubric and then you receive useless feedback that says "2. -0.6" that provides no insight into what you did wrong. Also sat in breakout rooms doing nothing for 30 min. multiple times

Grade depends on your LI (I recommend Ryan - he taught Tuesday morning this year). Asking questions if you dont understand something will save your grade. Do well on the case studies and home activities because theyre worth a big portion of your grade. Concept exam should be easy if you have a rudimentary understanding of bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy intro course. Class online was insanely easy. Mass is whatever the TA and Li do all the work. Take this class for an easy A. The bad reviews are just from salty people that did not show up to class and want to complain.

Professor Maas is extremely friendly, BUT I don't think her assessments are an accurate representation of what you learn, considering she teaches the absolute bare minimum (even less than a high school class). It depends on whether you get a good LI or UGLA because they're hard graders. I don't think the class is fair, to be completely honest.

Don't panic, the reviews look bad but you can power through this class. If you get Sawyer (LI) and Dahnie (UGLA) they are really cool. Lectures don't help much bc the info was too general compared to the LRQs. Make sure to triple-check your work and participate in the discussions. The concept exam wasn't bad but keep an eye on the clock. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hardest intro class to exist. It depends on your TA so good luck, because they grade everything HARD. Concept exam was so difficult, she was lying when she said it was easy. Never had a class that cares about ethics and participation as much as she does, TAs will take off points if you don't participate ENOUGH in discussion (which is ridiculous)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: you can't avoid this class but if you can, run for your life. worst class i have ever taken. everything is graded by the TAs, they grade ridiculously hard and take off points for every small thing (you don't even know what you get wrong), spent way too much time in this class for only 2 hours of credit, concept exam was insanely hard for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I swear she told us that the concept exam is going to be easy. IT IS NOT. IT WAS SO DIFFICULT AND I CAN'T EVEN COMPLETE IT ON TIME. I think I might drop from an A- to a B- or even C. The amount of work in this class is a lot and very unreasonable. The second home activity took forever for me to complete. The LRQ questions are also very very hard.

After that concept exam, I think I might drop from an A to B+ Bc that was D.I.F.F.I.C.U.L.T. Youre very crunched on time for the concept exam that consisted of matching. Also 4 hour class that could end at 10 pm most of the time which was so unnecessary. They tend to drag the class by talking abt things or wanting everybody to finish together

Professor Maas herself, is very caring. There were multiple times when she would extend deadlines which helped a lot. HOWEVER, the TA's grading LRQ's were HARSH. The concept exam was EXTREMELY DIFFICULT. If you dedicate a lot of time, you can still get an A. I just don't think a intro course should be this hard.
The concept exam was something DIFFERENNTTT. It was so hard so good luck with that. This class is much harder than it needs to be tbh.

people are making Dr. Maas seem like she is he worst teacher ever which isn't true. yeah, lab quizzes are kind of ridiculous, but that's when emailing your TA comes in handy (I'm serious they answer any question you ask them). Communicating with the TA is what made me get through this class and also going through Dr. Maas's lecture slides.

Dr. Maas refuses to release old questions for study, doesn't let us go back to check our answers on tests, and is quite possibly the most nitpicky professor I have ever had. Her lectures do not prepare you at all for any of the quizzes/exams. If you have an option between Dr. Maas and literally anyone else, don't take her.

I hate this class with a passion. The lab questions got exponentially more difficult with select all of the correct answers out of a list of 8-10 choices. You also have to write paragraphs on ethical issues weekly. On top of that, she assigns two ethical studies and two home activities. The workload for this class is unreasonable.

This Professor acts like they do no care about students. Plus makes TAs do all of the grading where grades are unfair and often wrong. She is the worst about responding to emails, one time she shared her screen and have over 1000 emails unread. Oh and she changed a huge lab 3 days before it was due. Not Cool.

Maas refuses to accommodate students online, has vague grading criteria that is extremely nitpicky, and her lectures don't even apply to the too-specific questions on LRQs. Much harder than this class needs to beshe takes herself WAY too seriously. If you don't have to take this classdon't do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Labs were pretty simple but we had 3 Home Activity labs which were really tedious, but thankfully that was made up for by the assignments being graded more or less easy. If you've done well in any biology class and can understand ethics then you shouldn't worry about your grade.

It's like she WANTS you to fail. We never got any of our weekly quizzes back, so we never got to study what we got wrong or point out mistakes on the quiz (there are MANY). The final exam is ridiculous. Most people didn't finish. She doesn't teach at all but the weekly quizzes are insanely tricky. Also Jacob the LI is so rude and condescending.

The LRQs were extremely difficult and we weren't even able to see what we got wrong on them. They said the LRQs were hard because we didn't have lab reports, but, honestly, I would prefer lab reports over those. The lectures were also extremely unhelpful since they were often just treated like office hours. I didn't learn anything in this class.

It's a tough lab, but I hear it's easier online than it was in-person so I recommend taking it online if you can. The lab questions were hard, mostly bc there were lots of multiple-answer questions which Canvas grades weirdly. You might get a TA that's a harsh grader which sucks. EC for doing the instapolls during class whether it's right or wrong!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The LRQs are really confusing. Your LI graded the LRQs and home activities and an UGLA graded the ethics case studies. The UGLAs were lenient graders but my LI was a really tough grader and would take off points for not doing something that wasn't even required for the assignment. Not an easy A, but doable even without the 10 extra credit points.

Dr. Maas was actually very accommodating considering the circumstances and kept us well-informed. The workload wasnt too bad as some labs are tedious, but some UGLAs do grade the case studies harshly. Overall, interesting virtual labs, lectures and case studies! Study the PowerPoints before LRQs!

hated this class with my whole heart, never had UGLAs grade so hard, never seen a teacher not accommodate students for class being online (this is a lab course). if you have to take this class your going to have to study and annoy the TA so you can actually get information you need on the LRQ because you don' learn anything from the lab.

I never hated a class more, for a lab class its too hard, the UGLA grade hard and there isn't enough leniency or accommodation for the lab being online. I have never gotten anything below an A-, including this semester EXCEPT this class. The lab is super broad and you dont learn as much BUT the LRQ is specific and over stuff we didnt learn in lab.

I had to take this class online, which is not an ideal option for a lab class. That being said, the weekly lectures are super broad compared to the lab quizzes due every week. The UGLAs grade very toughly and there are no drops with anything whatsoever. Not an accomodating professor and does not care about student feedback. Avoid if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: would give her a 0 if i could. Doesn't care about her students and didn't accommodate for the issues that came with online classes

I don't know why people are saying Professor Maas is nice. She's not. Really, she's quite awful and rude. The TAs are tough but nice. The reason this class is horrible is that Maas does not care. I scored in the 99th percentile of the MCAT, and I've taken dozens of "killer" classes. This class is a joke, and Maas takes herself too seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is at best "doable," but could be better executed after going online. The online simulations were not great and not worth paying almost $100 for -- when someone else in your group would share screens. Quizzes are TOO vague, and not a big fan. No drops, lectures are not helpful for quizzes, and everyone is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can't believe THIS is the class that ruined my 4.0 streak. Absolutely hated it, the margin of error is SO SMALL and the TA graded my assignments SO harshly :)))

I don't know why her reviews are so bad. I found her to be funny and engaging. She also takes student feedback very seriously and makes changes accordingly (like getting rid of the "select the correct answers" questions on the concept exam!). Beware of harsh TAs-- they grade the home activities which are a good chunk of your grade.

Dr. Maas is a sweet person, but her lectures don't help at all for her lab quizzes. She loves using "mark all the right answer" type of questions, and besides the questions being vague, a lot of the answers (especially for determining ethical/scientific issues the papers we have to read talk about) are subjective and never clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Let me tell you about my terrible experience. I think having covid would've been more pleasant than this class. You miss one weekly lab review question quiz or do badly? You get a zero with no makeups or drops. Her questions are so ambiguous and convoluted that the entire class argued against it but naw Dr. Maas will crushed all 300 of us.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm sorry, I know you have to take this class. She forces you to buy her expensive book and her quizzes are the worst. You need to stay on top of the work and make sure you make smart friends. The TAs are cool but I could never get over how much she makes you pay for just her class. Good luck.

She is lovely. LIs are good but are NOT consistent graders & don't show you how to properly do things considering its an intro course. You have to figure it out on your own a lot even when you attend TA office hours for help. Her lectures are average but don't help much with the weekly quizzes. I used bio textbook a lot. Extra credit helped

LI Sawyer was great, easy to talk to, and reasonable. However, they decided to switch around LI's when grading assignments at some points during the semester and Ryan graded one of my assignments and took off points for random things that weren't required in the rubric. Lowest grade I got the whole semester. Switch sections if you get him as a LI.

Lectures are useless, she doesn't go over anything that will help you with lab or assignments. She also took 2 weeks to respond to my email asking why I got points off an assignment and gave no more than 5-word answers that didn't answer anything. My LI Krishna and UGLA were great, but I'd give Maas a 0 if I could.
Dr. Maas is nice and understanding, but your grade depends on the LIs you get, and most of them are horrible. If you have Ryan or Sarah, RUN AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a solid professor who is clearly explains all the necessary material to the students prior to labs. Your grade in this class, however, is determined primarily by your Lab Instructor (LI), so you're in for a very bad experience if you get a bad LI. The cool labs in this class will not only help you learn bio content but also lab techniques.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most of the class is graded by the TA other than the final test. Lab assignments are not as tedious as CH204 but I thought CH204 was more fun to go to. Most of the time, labs take up the whole time so don't expect to get out early all the time. As long as you take good notes, you will do fine in the lab quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pay attention in labs and definitely go over lab notes and procedures. Her lectures are mainly an overview of the topics of each week and just ask questions so she can explain everything. She's chill, and the labs are time consuming and make sure you follow every procedure in the lab manual. Ask questions during lab time, so your LI can help.

Honestly people need to chill on Dr. Maas. She's the best and just super nice and cool, but you won't really be with her very much; it all depends on your Lab Instructor. I got super lucky with mine (I would tell you her name but she's leaving) so honestly take all of these reviews with a grain of salt. The lab is interesting and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The switch to online due to coronavirus has us doing weekly worksheets instead of having to take the concept exam and the lab practical. Overall, it has made this class WAYY more time consuming and boring. If you get Sarah M. drop and find another TA because she grades way harder than she needs to.

I liked bio lab WAY more than chem lab. The lab instructors were a lot more chill and in my opinion, these labs are a lot more interesting. However, more than half of your grade is dependent on how well you do on the lab practical and concept exam. The concept exam was unnecessarily hard and brought me down from an A to a B+ at the very end.

I didn't really interact much with Maas but when I did she was very nice & understanding. I had Ryan as a TA and all I have to say is if you get him, switch immediately. He gives the hardest quizzes (confirmed by Maas) and won't let you leave lab early. Overall, if you put in the time and participate you'll do fine on the exam and practical
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: UHHHHHH the concept exam is absolute bs. The practical is very stupid. The grading in the class is too non-forgiving - it is all based on your exam and practical which I do not believe is a fair evaluation of how one does in the lab. Ethics is so stupid too - her exam was an unfair evaluation of what we learned in lab this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall I felt that the class was okay, nothing too hard but still got to work for it. The only problem I experienced was going to take the concept exam and starting 10 minutes late and then them running out of scantrons. The part that was even more upsetting was that the test had to be turned in at the 50 min. mark when we really only had 40 min
She is very clear on everything you need to do and know for class. Although it is mostly the TA/LA I interacted with, Dr. Maas was quick to answer emails and very helpful at all times.

If you get Ryan as your TA, rip. He doesn't let you leave early AT ALL. Everyone could be done but you'll still sit there until 12:30 waiting for a b s o l u t e l y n o t h i n g. Martha is fine, lectures are boring, she says she's all about ethics and then ends up killing like 10,000 crickets each semester. Quizzes can be hard, take good notes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One Lab Practical and one final exam make up your whole grade. At the end of the semester, you really don't know where your grade will fall at all. Everyone is right, your grades do depend fully on your Lab Instructor. Labs were long and I had done of all of them in AP Bio. Overall not a fun class but doable.

Prof is very dull, won't bump even if you're 1/250 points away from the next letter grade. Grading can be ambiguous, especially with the group ethics presentation. I'd say that your grade can be very dependent on your TA, and don't be fooled by the people who say this is an "easy A," because they most likely got lucky with their TA.

The syllabus had different due dates for lab reports which were not posted in canvas. I followed those due dates but they were an hour different than what she wanted (not posted on canvas) so I got a zero for my lab report which brought me to a B in the class. Very condescending when I asked for sympathy. Other students had similar experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maas is terrible. Thats it. Its a shame that every science major has to deal with her. She doesnt care about students and wants to see you unhappy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was much easier than chem lab, but so much harder to make an A in. The quizzes are often on unimportant details of the lab, so take thorough notes.

Maas is the most condescending full of it professor I have ever had to deal with. One of my lab mates emailed her asking about grades and her response was what I believe to be as just false. Absolutely ridiculous that this stupid intro class is so hard to get an A in. Absolute waste of time and effort, sucks that its required for all sciences.

I came into Dr. Maas's class with good reviews. She's passionate about her field in biology and is not bad to listen to in lecture. However, I couldn't help but feel like she didn't encourage her students to really get into biology. I felt like the whole class was her telling us "just do this" and not a lo of actual learning went on.

Martha was fine. She doesn't really teach well nor does she grade a majority of the work. I would really suggest checking out if your TA is good. Mine straight up told me she had to grade harder because she was giving out too many As. I tried emailing Martha, and she was zero help. They definitely don't care about their students.

This lab wasn't horrible - I didn't find myself devoting a ton of time to it. The labs are fairly easy, but can be long and boring. Dr. Maas seems like a nice, reasonable lady, but the grading does make it very hard to get an A. The course did have an ethics flag, and at times, it felt like we were juggling a lot of unrelated assignments.

Dr. Maas's lab is pretty easy, just be sure to attend every lab. Missing two brings down the maximum grade you can get down to an 80. Any more than that and you fail. She's pretty heavy on ethics, including ethics reports, which are pretty easy. Lab reports are pretty short too.

ONLY A 20 POINT MARGIN TO MAKE AN A IN THIS CLASS. 20 points, the whole semester. If you miss one question on every weekly quiz (5 questions, 2 points per question, 10 quizzes) there goes your A. Be prepared for them, know all info from lab manual, lab lectures, and ethical readings. 2 exams, 3 lab reports, 3 ethics reports. This lab sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Maas is an okay lecturer, but your experience in the class is really dependent on the TA you receive. Your grade in the class is dependent on lab reports, weekly quizzes, the final exam, and a lab practical. Study hard for the weekly quizzes, and when the final comes you will already know everything there is to know.

She has changed the class: 5 data reports, weekly lab quizzes, and one final exam. Data reports are easy and guidelines are clear. Lab quizzes can be specific so take detailed notes while doing experiments. Final exam and lab practical can be stressful: MOVE FAST on practical as time flies. Overall, she is picky about grading but class is alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: With the class revamp you now have weekly quizzes you can use your notebook on. Being said, there is now only one final exam that is cumulative. Data reports are manageable as long as you have a good TA. The weekly lecture has clicker questions for credit - go because it does make up a chunk of your grade. Grading is reasonable and outlined clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I found this to be easier than chem lab. During lecture she explained what would happen during lab and then you would just go and do it on your lab day. At the end, your grade will either be extremely boosted or drop a ton based on your attendance, if you remembered to score your lab partners, and performance. The tests were like 60% difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not as bad as I expected. Lab reports were annoying. Most labs took up the full 4 hours. Exams were actually pretty easy- all MC and straightforward. The practical exam was an awful experience, this needs to be changed. Some labs are interesting, most are just meh. Overall an okay class, just the practical exam ruined it for me.

She's a pretty fun lecturer, the biggest issue is that the class covers such a wide scope of biology in such a short amount of time. There's no clear transition in curriculum between labs, so this class felt like a hodgepodge of too many fields of biology. Lab reports were monotonous, but grading overall in the course is relatively lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My least favorite class at UT by FAR. I found organic chemistry easier than this class because she was so unclear on what we needed to know for exams. Rather than covering larger important concepts, we needed to know the length of a nematode and specific crayfish parts. She seems to really enjoy power and exercising it over students.

Like most intro labs, a lot of wasting time writing lab reports that only slightly effect your grade. Very strict on her policies, so make sure you follow all the rules. Go to lecture, lecture attendance is basically weighted as heavy as an exam. If you get a good LI and group of students in your class, the lab session can be fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Biology lab is the most useless class you could take. Dr. Maas uses this class in a way to make herself feel more important than she is. The material you are supposed to learn is very simple and is already learned in class, and Maas makes the tests and analyses very convoluted. I loved my LI, but this class killed any love for lab I had before.

Since it's a lab, your experience is highly dependent on the TA. Nonetheless, I did not enjoy the professor. Her lectures are random and boring. You don't really know what to expect for the tests and some of the questions are ridiculously specific. This class was unnecessarily difficult considering how the concepts covered were not advanced.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests were straight forward. Your lab analysis grades depend on your TA. You NEED the course pack for class and tests. Participation matters greatly, you need to be there at the beginning of each class. There is a lot of work, and it's crammed especially during the summer, but it's manageable. She is very interested in Bio so it's not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class can be super stressful. There is 2 exams and a practical. No final! Also, there is lab prep hw, lab analysis, lecture questions, and peer review for every lab (12). Some labs are boring such as the plant one. Cool labs were the chick embryo and the crayfish one. Exams are hard because each exam are over 6 labs. But they're fair!

An absolutely amazing prof! She cares about her students deeply. Her lectures are VERY clear and engaging. Her exams are fair, no tricks. Lab reports are time-consuming but they are not difficult. Grades for lab reports highly depend on your TA, so that is out of your hand. The most difficult part was the lab practical which was extremely hard! :(
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of bio lab. Of 12 lab reports, my lowest grade was an 85, but I found the 3 exams to be more of a challenge. I found lecture unhelpful, but had a great TA who always explained things in much more detail than Maas did in lecture. So like any lab, your grade is predisposed by whichever TA you end up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are useful but not necessary. Your grade depends on two tests and lab reports, which is not bad but needs effort. Okay, but not the best. Average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Maas was great. BioLab was my favorite lab and you honestly should get an A if you have a decent TA. Dr. Maas was funny, interested in what she was teaching, and worked to see students succeed. She knows what's up though, so don't expect to cheat off course hero etc

Marty is a sweetheart! She's always available and gives interesting lectures. Your grade does depend heavily on your TA. Her exams are completely fair though. She gives obvious hints for her "tricky" questions- pay attention to the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not as bad as I thought, however the course has organizational issues and artificial difficulty. On the week of exam 1, there's lab that has hardest part of 206L, causing one to fall behind. On top of that, many of the questions on the exams are specific memorization questions which makes the exams trickier than it has to be.  Be on your guard.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is not as bad as everyone makes it seem. Just study and always understand what's going on in lab/lecture and you'll be fine.

She is one of those professors that thinks her class is the most important thing in the world. Talks horribly about Chem lab and the professors that teach it. Her lectures are pointless and you are forced to go- she could easily make them online lectures but for some reason she doesn't. Your lab experience is completely dependent on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've done research for three years, aced every biology class I've taken here, and sincerely love science and biology. Despite all of that this class seriously made me consider dropping my BIO major, picking up BCH instead. Boring, tedious, and none of the material is even close to real science. Essentially a high school class.
A large percentage of your grade is at the discretion of your TA, which isn't always great. Labs aren't very clear, but they're not hard either. Doable class as long as you study and go to lecture.

Worst class I ever taken in my life. Does not respond to emails. Tests questions could literally be one sentence off a 60-70 slide PPT. Grades are depended basically upon on your TALI. Two 35 Multiple Choice Tests, rest is Pre-Lab, Lab Analysis, iClicker questions each week, and one lab report that was literally 15+ pages for me. Take at own risk.

This course was definitely restructured to be more realistic for first-time lab-ers. Not a bad class at all now. Only 2 exams so study. Majority of grade is lecture pointspre-lab MCQ hwlab analyses due every week and the practical which is totally dependent on how well u paid attention thruout the classin open-lab the week before. Mainly effort.
Terrible test questions, heavy homework load; avoid this teacher if able.
horrible lectures

Dr. Maas is a wonderful lady, and she says that she will never put something on the test that she can't do herself, so don't expect a lot of difficult math. There are lots of sources available for help. The real kicker is the TA you get, and you have no way of knowing who you will have.

There are two tests which go over the labs which you have completed.  Definitely fair questions that test your understanding of the labs.  She treats the students as though they know nothing about biology during her lectures which can be a good thing sometimes and a bad thing at other times.
Just... don't. Seriously. If there's any other option, go with them instead.
this class is awful and Dr. Maas doesn't know what she's doing. People can study all night and still bomb tests cause they're so badly worded. Stay away if you can.

Nice lady, but you're most likely not going to get an A in this class, but you can pull a B. Homework quizzes are HARD and a nice chunk of your grade. Tests are meh, averages fall in the high 70's. To succeed, you HAVE to read the textbook (I use Campbell, 9th), even though she insists you don't. Attendance is counted through clickers.
Pretty easy to get a B, nearly impossible to get an A. Homework quizzes are hard and dock you a lot of point for anything wrong. Tests are super specific and hard to get an A on.

Dr. Maas is flat out incompetent.  The class isn't hard, she is just not a  good professor and is not very knowledgeable. The exams are poorly worded and oddly specific every once in a while, but the main complaint is her inability to teach.  Probably the worst professor I've had at UT in terms of being knowledgeable and organized.

She talks like a mommy. Class is pretty easy, but she gives frequent quizzes to try to control your life and force you not to procrastinate on the material. Frequently writes incoherent quiz/test/homework questions. Fairly easy course though, and she's nice enough.
Very mediocre. Claims she doesn't use the textbook but she definitely tests out of it. Lectures are very simple, tests are more difficult. Not the worst or best teacher

This professor is wonderful. All you need to do is pay attention during class, take good notes and you will be able to pass her class. The tests are questions drawn from lectures and they are never impossible. Her lectures are simple and straight to the point and she will make sure she takes her time until everyone understands the material.

Dr. Maas is a nice lady but she should not be a professor. Her lectures are all off random power points. She tries to keep the class interesting with "case studies" but they are usually not helpful and she makes you "do them with the people around you". Unless you memorize the textbook you will probably end up with a C  or B.

Great teacher! But you have to go to office hours to do well. UT has a course transformation project with BIO 311C, few liked it.  Tests are extremely difficult, but if you copy her notes verbatim (I'd recommend bringing a computer to copy notes faster) you should at least make a B. Most that got an A were gifted or literally spent weekends studyin

Horrible teacher. DO NOT TAKE HER!! Her lectures are a joke. She goes through power points that do not help with her tests, you ask her questions and her main response is I'm not sure, I'll have to look it up. She teaches by asking the class questions, yet doesn't repeat the answers once they are said so you can actually know what is being said.

Lectures are a joke. "Ask your partner" is her catchphrase b/c she is too lazy to teach material herself- even her pp's are the product of others. Study from pp's or modules for exams, but frankly you are screwed b/c of her awful wording. Short answers are primarily graded on the inclusion of specific words, not understanding of concepts.  Bad prof

I thought Dr. Maas was awesome! She was really nice and every time before exams she would go over the important things to study which made it a lot easier to make a good grade on the test. The multiple choice on the tests require students to really understand the material, because a lot of the questions are HARD.

she's a very nice lady, very soft spoken. At times she does not know how to explain something so she will ask you to look it up either online or in the book. Her tests come mostly from her powerpoints online. The course is not easy, but if you study hard, you can pass.

she's unorganized. we're always behind. her test questions are awfully worded. i think she's a nice person, but her teaching methods aren't up to par. biology is not a tough subject, but she does not do a good job of presenting the info. it's not a bad class, but it's not that great either -_-

Professor Smith teaches a very easy class. As long as you sort of pay attention in lecture, you'll get an A. Readings are insightful if you actually care about the content. Their lectures often stray away from the ideas being discussed and end up addressing the thoughts and objections of a single imaginary strawman.

Nicole was a great professor, very insightful. Good lectures, the readings are pretty long though. Should be said, there is a no electronic policy in class, but honestly it made me pay more attention.

Prof Smith is nice but spends a lot of lectures rambling off-topic instead of better explaining some complex concepts. They are a very easy grader if you get everything done and put in a little effort. No electronics unless you have accommodations, they went on multiple rants about this because people would do it anyway. Pretty simple intro class

This class is pretty easy. Grades come from mostly in class assignments so there isn't much work outside of class except readings. Attendance is required but she isn't super strict but doesn't like when your on your phone in class.

Dr. Smith was a really enjoyable professor. Her course was not graded by many assignments, which felt pretty intimidating, but overall, she was pretty forgiving with grades. She lectured each class and was great at separating personal beliefs from the content. Overall, you get what you put into it, so if you do the readings, it's worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing at explaining such hard concepts. Very passionate about teaching each subject matter, which helps. Does not offer their own perspective of each philosophical concept and allows us to make our own determination and defend our perspectives. Dr. Smith offers a safe environment to learn and grow.

Dr. Smith is the best professor I have had the pleasure of learning from. They are really good at explaining complex concepts more simply and covering all of the ethical considerations of a concept. I am so glad I took PHL 304 as my first philosophy course because it set me up really well for my other ethics courses. Best. Professor. Ever.

Look at the end of the day this teacher is relatively chill. The problem is the attendance policy - she gets mad if you are on your laptops because she hates electronics for some reason and then will say to the class "you are free to leave" but the problem is grades your attendance AT THE END OF CLASS so you can not REALLY leave.

Class itself was quite boring with her turning a lot of things quite political on either side. TA small group was the highlight of the class though. Easy class overall, but definitely not my favorite. You'll get an A, but it won't be that fun imo.

great professor interesting lectures although it is a bit harder to get an A in their class (95 and above) my TA was a little weird but ultimately great class and made you think a lot about different perspectives and moral philosophies. just be prepped for the two writing assignments and your good. very little assignments so keep that in mind.

Great professor for an introductory philosophy course. While the content was very easy to politicize, Prof Smith (though obviously trying greatly not to incorporate her own political views) approached it in a neutral way that allowed for students with opposing views to communicate and succeed. Certainly recommend if looking to get into philosophy.

not the best lecturer she doesn't really know how to explain her thoughts. honestly didn't learn much as it was not engaging she's really nice and accommodating not a big course load at all but I was not interested with her teaching style
Doesn't allow laptops in class, but otherwise is super chill. Got back to emails quickly and was a pretty fair and easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: slow paced and not very engaging lectures. easy to get a good grade but I didnt gain much from the class. my small group was fun but I know the other TA was frustrating for people.

A caring prof but is lowkey carried by her course topic. The topics are very  
current making engagement easy and natural however her lectures are very cyclical. She more often than not sounds like she is struggling to express what she is trying to say and doesn't word her writing coherently. I did however love both my discussion section and my TA.

Nicole is caring. Her lectures are not as bad as others say here, and her PowerPoints are awesome. Essays were graded a bit tough by the TA. So don't blow this class off. In my class, unit 1 over animal rights was good enlightening material, but unit 2 was a whole waste of time imo. Nicole is left wing, which can make sharing opposing ideas hard.

I think it's safe to say Professor Smith puts very low effort into class formulation, with everything seeming to occur last minute. The class itself is easy, but the lectures are so incredibly boring even as a philosophy major. I would just avoid classes with her altogether.

Smith was a caring professor. I sometimes struggled to stay engaged because it is a relatively slow-paced class, but to do well on the essays, try to take good notes and do the reading if you want the A. As long as you keep up, the rest of the course is extremely manageable. I would definitely recommend this for a low workload ethics flag.

I took two courses with Dr.Smith and just registered to take another course with them. There are assigned readings but she will go over all of them in class. Your grades are determined by a couple in in-class quizzes (very simple) and in-class essays. Overall, an amazing professor.
Great class. Professor was very caring and tried her best to help. Had in class responses that were graded for attendance credit. Sometimes lectures dragged on a little later than needed or expected.

Dr. Smith was very nice and explained the class through lecture and discussion primarily. The class is low-pressure, but you still learn; I especially found the video about primates eating rotting meat interesting (you'll understand later). Grades are mostly participation, make sure to show up to lecture and discussion and to learn teminolgies.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is one of my favorites in the entire philosophy department. They are very understanding to extenuating circumstances and super supportive. Their lectures are interactive and relatively easy to follow given some of the complex material. They are able to explain concepts in a relevant way and apply them to day-to-day life.

Extremely helpful and understanding professor. Readings were "assigned" every week but were covered during lectures. In-class essays were structured as short answer questions in order to take the stress away. Quizzes could be taken multiple times and were reviewed in class. Grades were arranged so that it was impossible to not get a good grade.

My first philosophy class and absolutely amazing experience for anyone curious about philosophy. Two readings a week but not heavy, also not mandatory since they cover them in slides. Super manageable class and completely changed my view on race and gender. Always making sure they bring in different students' perspectives on the topic. Take them!

She was great! As long as you show up to class or watch the recorded lectures you will learn all you need to to get a good grade. It was also a very eye opening experience and taught me new ways to look at social problems and how we can solve them.

Nicole is a great professor. Material was interesting/thought-provoking, and though you could tell Nicole had certain opinions on topics, they never dismissed other people's thoughts and opinions. The readings weren't that necessary b/c Nicole's lectures covered everything, and I feel like I was adequately prepared for the 2 tests and 3 quizzes.

I really liked Nicole's lecture style. She brought to light many interesting topics that I had never even considered and I felt that the lectures were engaging and thorough. Her TA gave me a near failing exam grade but Nicole allowed me to defend my writing in office hours and remedied the situation in a way that was just and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was a pretty low-stress class. The professor was always very kind and had a lot of passion for the topics she'd teach us. Essays were very straightforward and weren't harshly graded at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nicole is a great professor who discusses a variety of well selected topics. The readings compliment the course and Nicole breaks them down. In-class participation quizzes, two in-class essays, with some discussion posts towards end of semester. I only wish there were more assignments to help prep for essays/have more weighted grade opportunities.

CMP was an easy class, you don't have to do the readings because she explains the concepts in lecture well enough. Her lectures may get a little boring but maybe bc they were online. She is really caring and professional, she will consider your opinion if it differs from hers. All the grades come from in-class assignments. Cant recommend it enough.

Professor Smith is a facet to the UT philosophy department. Teaching philosophy is sometimes difficult because of the trickiness of translating one's expertise to students. Nicole does this flawlessly with a humble, clear approach. Philosophy professors are known to ramble, and this is not the characterization I'd make of her. She encourages studen

Pretty easy class, grades were made up of essays, attendance, quizzes, and essay-tests. Didn't read anything that was assigned, because the TA went over it so in depth in discussion sections. Did not enjoy the lecture style, Nicole rarely spoke about important topics that we were covering or read about, went on many awkward tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Everyone on here who complained about Nicole's lecture style missed exactly what makes her a phenomenal professor. Philosophy professors can typically come off as condescending, but Nicole is the complete opposite. There is a lot of intention with how she responds to students (timidity). She regards peoples' beliefs SO charitably. Take this prof!

Nice and caring professor who loves talking about philosophy. She assigns really interest readings for environmental ethics. You get a few papers throughout the semester but they're straightforward and one of them gets dropped at the end. Attendance taken for a grade. Two in class essay exams neither are comprehensive and she prepares you for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I rated "level of difficulty" in her class a "4" b/c one of the TA's was brutal. Other than that, this was a solid course & I learned some interesting stuff & Nicole is a definite asset to UT faculty, imo. We need more professors like her! A+

Professor Smith was just alright for me. The information itself was incredibly interesting, and we focused on a lot social issues that I think are important. I found myself counting down the minutes until her lectures were over; she's a very monotone speaker, and she almost comes across as though she's unsure of what she's saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, Nicole is kind, caring, knowledgable, and clearly passionate. She grades fairly and is especially approachable and a joy to talk to! She clearly cares about students and their learning, for example, she doesn't require textbooks (in my experience) in order to keep the courses affordable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was really interesting and I definitely recommend it! Workload wasn't bad, exams (in class essays) were pretty simple, grading was fair, and there was sort of a lot of reading but it was all pretty fun to read in my opinion. Nicole is very sweet and funny and I loved hearing her talk about all of the topics we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Smith loves her craft, and does an excellent job of presenting it to her students.

If you want a caring professor with strong morals and a true passion for learning then I highly recommend Nicole. She is so kind and easy to talk to while remaining extremely professional. Her focus on inclusivity seems to ensure that all students feel welcome and comfortable. As long as you read and go to class you should be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith did a great job of presenting confusing material. I felt like I was totally lost the first half of the class but made a high A on the midterm. After the midterm the foundation she laid paid off for the issues we discussed in the second half. Go to class, take good notes, read and visit her in office hours (even just once).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At first I thought we were going to focus on social justice in health issues, but these topics didn't come until much later. The course moves very fast with a lot of readings that for the most part are skippable, but be sure to focus on the readings assigned for short assignments because they show up on the test. Show up for SquareCap and record.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: At first I thought she was a 20 something-year-old straight out of college but apparently, she's in her 40's which really shocked me. It's a challenging class but if you ask her enough questions and pay attention, you should do just fine. Every week there's one-page essays over reading. There's 2 in class essays over the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Smith did a decent job of teaching the material needed to succeed on exams and homework assignments. The weekly assignments seem daunting at first, but they are really manageable if you skim the textbook and look at the lecture slides online. Absences add up fast, but as long as you're mindful of that, the class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Smtih was fantastic. She is extremely knowledgeable and kept the lectures interesting even when the material was dull. No tests, just two in-class essays and no final. If you show up, do the reading, and keep track of the assignments, the course is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Smith enjoyed talking about the philosophy material we covered during lecture, but included too many personal issues in her tangents. I was often confused if the material was relevant to the philosopher we were discussing or not. Approachable, but will not answer you if you have questions on grades. I don't recommend this course.

The class was okay, but I would not take Dr. Smith again. She was a dull lecturer and offered no information that couldn't be found in the textbook. Often during lectures it felt like she went off on tangents, so eventually I stopped bothering to take notes and just showed up for the attendance grade. Read the book and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith, while intellectual, is not a phenomenal lecturer; she knows the basics of her information, but she comes across as incredibly timid - almost as if she is afraid of speaking. Really great class though - fosters debate and individual thinking. Tests/essays are graded fairly, and it is an easy yet interesting A if you show up. Take her.

Health and Justice is a new class and therefore there were some kinks to be worked out, but the topics are interesting, tough, and relevant. The professor became more personable as the semester went on, and office hours helped with that even more. Very good about listening to and welcoming all perspectives. Reading, writing, and discussion heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith's Contemporary Moral Problems class is one of the best classes I've ever taken. Incredibly interesting lectures, and the tests are not difficult at all if you pay attention and take notes in class. Dr. Smith is super nice and cares about her students as well. Would recommend this class to anyone!
He's there to help; the class content can be confusing. If you pay attention to class, he does a good job of explaining the theories. Go to office hours if you are confused!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is nice and means well but his teaching style is so ineffective. You end up having to teach yourself everything because he just lectures on and on about theory and doesn't do actual problems during class that reflect what's on the actual exam. This makes lectures annoying and a waste of time. He has a cool Australian accent tho

He is a really good professor who knows what he's teaching. Lecture and content heavy class - so make sure you attend + take good notes. Exam heavy, but as long as you do the practice exams and problems, you should be fine. Attend his OH for the problem sets for help - they're difficult. Overall chill guy.
Solid prof. Study the practice exams and you'll be fine.

His lectures are very boring, and it becomes your job to sit through it and filter what is actually important. Spoiler alert: it's not very much. This guy will spend 90% of the time deriving things that don't matter and aren't tested and maybe 10% of the time talking about how things are actually used to answer questions. Good luck yall

Woodhams has the unique ability of turning a simple and intuitive concept into something utterly unintelligible. He loves to teach by using variables and keeping things "theoretical" instead of just using real numbers or examples to explain things like a regular human being. If you enjoy vague math concepts, he's the guy. If not, stay away from him
Although this class was hard content wise, he broke down content that was easy to understand! The problem sets and exams were graded very fairly as well. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is extremely disorganized and so difficult, and Professor Woodhams just expects students to understand the calculus that he does even though he skips multiple steps at a time. When I would go to office hours he would act like I was stupid for asking a question. Would not recommend this professor at all.

I like him, but I hate the FIN321k course and how it is taught. He is a nice person and definitely super smart, but I am unsure why this is even a required course for the MPA program. The practice sets aren't too bad; everyone did about the same on the midterm, and the final is cumulative, so we will see how it turns out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never responds to students. Terribly difficult class and he tends to go through the lecture way too quickly.

Despite FIN 321K being really tough, Prof. Snashall-Woodhams is great. His lectures are very clear and he provides so much additional practice. He never responds to e-mails and the class is terribly disorganized, though. Problem sets are graded tough months late and he doesn't tell you what you did wrong or give you solutions. I'd still recommend.
Never prepared, no lectures, just random spiels, talks about his divorce in class, certainly no expert on his field, rude to students. Genuinely don't know how this guy is a professor.

I had Nik for CMS 367 and it was purely a class I'd go to to talk. Discussions on readings, personal experiences, etc. You just needed to talk at least once a week for credit. He's pretty chill if your open minded and participate you'll do fine.

Idk what the reviews here are on about, they're one of the best professors I've ever had. They made Quantitative Research Methods fun. The class is based mostly on lectures that feel like casual conversations. Assignments are short with very clear directions. There is plenty of opportunities for extra credit on their exams. Nik is SO chill

Honestly they were really chill and this class changed my perspective on how arbitrary gender is. They say there's required readings but I feel that they're not really required. This class is definitely not a lecture and is entirely discussion based. One paper and one presentation about whatever you want, no exams. Can get kind of boring at times.

unorganized class. expects us to write a research paper on research he conducted years ago and doesn't know how to perform the research. counts students absent when they're 5 minutes late when attendance is mandatory/for a grade. expects students to get notes from other students since lectures are not posted. mumbles a lot and goes on tangents.
class isn't very organized and not very accommodating if you are sick because the slides wont be posted. overall the class isn't hard at all but it isn't enjoyable.
Just avoid him if you can.
This guy wouldn't be able to teach prime Einstein to tie his shoes.

Professor Reyes seems nice, but struggles with expert bias and explains concepts poorly, making lectures hard to follow. The class is quiz and test-heavy with little review material, and the few questions make it easy to get low grades. There's also little communication with TAs, so support feels limited. I'd avoid if possible.

Lectures are all over the place and there is little effort into them, Nicky is clearly passionate about math but it doesn't translate well in a teaching environment. To make matters even worse there is close to zero resources for self instruction outside of class, which would be okay if the lectures were great but they are abysmal. 0/10 course.

Had some of the best reviews for a calc prof but his switch from online exams to in person broke this class. Quizzes are two questions completely free response and weighted almost identically to the midterms. They are super difficult and they are NOT curved. I finished 408C with a 98 and am struggling to do well on his quizzes.
Quizzes are nasty, and the TAs in discussion don't teach properly, so it's harder to succeed on the quizzes. Quizzes are now like 20% of our grade, comparable to midterms. Midterms are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, even better lecturer! If I could give anyone advice about this class it would be to really study for the final as it took me by complete surprise and ruined my A. Otherwise, the midterms and HW are very straightforward and honestly you prob can get by just reading the textbook imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not bad, just do the homework and your gonna be fine. tests are really easy

The professor described the quiz on proofs of reductions as “easy,” many students who don't work with this material found it quite challenging. The topic was not clearly explained during the TA discussion, which made the quiz harder to prepare. I would not be surprised if the scores were curved. lectures are sporadic and are not clear.
He is genuinely the most sporadic lecturer I have ever had. Goes WAY to fast. Would not recommend.

I understand calculus 2 to be hard, but reyes provides little to no support whatsoever. Lectures are hard to read, discussion sections are even harder to read. Stuff talked in class is really hard to follow.

Overall, this course feels disorganized and unsupportive. The combination of weak lectures, ineffective discussion sections, and heavily weighted quizzes makes it far more stressful than it needs to be.

The structure of this course has declined significantly compared to previous semesters. The shift to in-person exams combined with very challenging quizzes has made the class much harder, but the quality of instruction has not improved to match those changes.

TA discussion sections do not provide much help. They are disorganized and often fail to review or reinforce key material. Instead of clarifying difficult topics, they frequently leave students more confused and uncertain about expectations.

This class feels poorly designed and unnecessarily stressful. Quizzes make up 28% of the final grade, yet there is very little transparency or preparation for them. The quizzes are extremely difficult and often cover material in ways that are not clearly explained in lecture. Many students still feel unprepared.

Between the sudden shift to in-person exams, poorly aligned lectures, ineffective discussion sections, and high-stakes quizzes, the course feels unnecessarily stressful and poorly coordinated. Overall, this class is not well designed to support student learning, and I would not recommend it.

The TA discussion sections do not help compensate for this. They are poorly organized and often unproductive, with little meaningful review of relevant material. Instead of clarifying difficult concepts, these sections frequently add confusion and do not reflect what is actually tested.

Lecture quality has declined significantly. Explanations are rushed, examples are limited, and there is a noticeable disconnect between what is taught in class and what appears on quizzes and exams. Studying often feels like guesswork rather than a structured process.

This course has been extremely frustrating from start to finish. One of the biggest issues is the heavy reliance on quizzes, which make up 28% of the final grade. These quizzes are very difficult and often test material in ways that are not clearly covered in lecture. There is little guidance on what to expect.

With major grading weight placed on quizzes and exams, the lack of clear instruction becomes even more problematic. Overall, this course feels poorly structured and much less student-friendly than it was previously.

The lectures themselves are disorganized and rushed. Important concepts are skimmed over, while examples rarely match what appears on homework or exams. This disconnect makes studying inefficient and frustrating.

This semester felt like a step backward in almost every way. Last semester, exams were online and the course structure made sense around that format. This time, exams were moved to in-person, but lectures and course organization did not adapt accordingly. The result was a class that felt much harder

The lack of alignment across lectures, assignments, quizzes, and exams makes studying unnecessarily difficult. You're left guessing what content will actually be emphasized, which adds stress rather than reinforcing learning.

Lecture quality has also dropped noticeably. Explanations are rushed and often unclear, and many examples covered in class do not reflect what appears on homework or exams. It frequently feels like you're attending lecture just to keep up, not to actually understand the material.

This class feels completely inconsistent compared to last semester. Previously, exams were online and the course structure reflected that format. This semester, exams were suddenly moved to fully in-person, which felt like a major shift without adequate adjustment in teaching or preparation. Expectations changed, but the support did not.

Lectures themselves feel rushed and disorganized. Topics jump around without clear structure, and it's easy to leave class unsure of what the main points were or how they connect to what you're expected to know. This has made understanding the material far harder than it should be.

I had high hopes for this class, but overall it was one of the most frustrating academic experiences I've had. The transition from online to fully in-person came halfway through the year with no clear explanation or advance warning. That change made planning around other classes and responsibilities much more difficult.

The lectures have steadily become less effective over time. Concepts are often presented quickly and without sufficient explanation, and the material covered in class does not consistently reflect the homework or exams. This lack of coordination makes it hard to know what to focus on and significantly impacts learning.

Worse still, he made quizzes worth 28% of the grade, and there are four of them. That's ridiculous for a math course where lecture explanations are already falling flat. The increase in weight makes quizzes borderline make-or-break, and it feels arbitrary rather than tied to meaningful learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm honestly disappointed with how this class has been run this semester. Reyes used to be a decent instructor, but the course has taken a nosedive — and it's clear from how things are structured now that student learning is no longer a priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Reyes used to be good, but now he has been reduced to really not-so-great lectures, insane quizzes, and I am waiting to see how the tests are.

Exams are no longer online, which I am fine with, but come on, he now makes quizzes worth 28%, and you take 4. What is this?

Reyes style of teaching, syllabus, and just general vibes from him have changed. Maybe something having to do with new math department guidelines as he mentioned on our first day. The main issues are homework not correlating to lectures, discussions being overly hard, and just in general no synchronization between the many parts of the course.

The UT math department has become very weird. Reyes completely changed his teaching approach, often resulting in very poor lectures and low-quality discussion sections. Unfortunate for a 'university of the first class'
Reyes is the chosen one, do practice problems and you'll get an A. That's literally it.

He's a very approachable person and I liked his class a lot; he had a lot of cool insights and clearly understands what he's talking about. The homeworks were always applicable to what he lectured about and were honestly super helpful, and he was very straightforward about what you need to know on tests.

He is what many people would describe as the typical math professor. He is a very nice person in general as well and allows students to call him "Nicky" (not a professor who will get mad for not calling them "Dr."). There is a homework that was due every Wednesday for my TTH section that had around 13-25 questions. Exams are not too challenging.
Awesome professor! Nice grading system and interesting lectures, would definitely recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was probably one of the best calculus classes I have ever taken. The online tests are similar to the quest hw. the in class tests are discussion problems. just pay attention and its a guaranteed A.

3 exams - lowest dropped; mandatory final but all exams are take-home, from the homework, and you have ample time to complete them. Dr.Reyes is clearly very knowledgeable and it was very interesting to hear his lectures, however attendance isn't necessary and all information can be obtained through some YouTube videos. An A is an 89. Take for an A!

This class was super easy and everything was online except for a small portion of the tests, but he would show you how to do the problems in discussion the week before. Nicky is really good at math and will explain anything over and over again, but he can be a bit awkward. Classes are a bit boring but they can be fun if you love math.

THE GOAT! Very easy and a good lecturer. He helps you on exams by going over very similar problems right before and letting you take notes and use said notes . You'll genuinely learn the course content.

Dr. Reyes is the best professor you can take if you want an easy A in calc. Midterms and the final were all online and based on the homework questions so if you study those you'll be fine. 89% is an A and in class quizzes are based on discussion problems but are only worth 8%. Really great guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you didn't previously understand calc, you won't understand it with him. Reyes was very chill, passionate, and happy to help. Entire class other than in class midterms (8%) was graded online so you can make an A in his class. Don't forget about online assignments and make sure to use your learning modules if you struggle with math like I do.

if you're looking for a chill professor, reyes is that guy. i fw calculus tho so i went to all the lectures, discussions, and midterms anyways. the ta/kris is also chill af too, i recommend going to her if you're stuck on any problem. besides the final, there's 1 drop for everything. all the tests recycle the quest hws, so keep that in mind.
It really cant get any easier, just take him

Lol if you want an easy A, take Reyes. However, you will eventually be too lazy to learn the material so just a warning on that! He legit shows you the exam before you take it when you do the in person portion but changes the numbers. Online portion is easy.

His class was really easy. Homework is all on quest and exams are 20% in person, 80% online. The online portion of the exams are a little difficult, but they're basically questions from the homework. He usually went off on tangents during his lectures, but besides that he taught alright.

This class was super easy, and Reyes is fantastic! He's nice, laid-back, and hilarious. However, his lectures/videos often go way beyond what you need to know for the course.
