Lectures are long and the material is extremely boring. Would have had a better experience in the class if my TA didn't grade so harshly on the papers and group project with basically no feedback at all. Besides that there are weekly open note quizzes and quizzes in the book over every chapter that take way too long. A drag to go through overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A pretty easy online class to get that the Second Credit if you took APUSH and need to get 1 last US History course. The entire class grade is basically 2 essays and a massive group project that aren't bad if you ask your TA for help and don't try to do it the night before. Lectures were incredibly boring but worth some EC points.

The class and lectures were organized really well, which made it much less stressful, even with essays and a group project. She's a really good lecturer and kept me engaged, despite the class being online and faster-paced. She's a great option for summer classes and makes history more interesting and enjoyable!

loved Ozanne plan to take her again for 315K lectures not mandatory and consisted of 5 question weekly quizzes, textbook work, and 2 writing assignments and 2 group projects. all of which were very easy and recorded lectures if you do miss class. extra credit in class offered at random times. she also brought us candy on halloween.

Not a great lecturer, often would just play videos or go on a tangent about niche topics. Very inaccessible outside of class. TA's grade harshly, inaccurately, and give unhelpful feedback. I had a TA remove 10 points from a major grade because they didn't read the rubric correctly. Professor doesn't help with grade disputes. Would not take again.
This professor is the best; she is very kind and caring. Only went to lecture for the first week. No tests!

EASIEST HISTORY CLASS YOU CAN EVER ASK FOR. There are 2 group projects and 2 essays but they are doable and graded quite easily (probably depend on TAs). Outside of that, there are just open note take home quizzes and attendances are never mandatory but she will give you extra credits quite often if you go to classes. TAKE HER 1000%!

The class has optional attendance and no tests so a great class to take. the group projects and 2 essays can be graded pretty harshly depending on who your TA is. Recommend going to class a lot for the extra credit points. she surprises you with extra credit randomly and it will help your grade.

She was great. Her lectures were engaging although no one showed up because they were optional. Sometimes, if you show up you get extra credit. 25% of the class is homework and lecture quizzes which are really easy (multiple attempts) and a free 100%. Two essays - you get extra credit if turned in on time.

Lectures are engaging. Course is very organized. Lot of essays and are graded hard. You get random extra credit points just for showing up to class, and also if you submit an assignment on time. Professor is understanding and flexible, very kind as well. Just make sure to start early on assignments as they assigned weeks before they are due.

such a good prof! So sweet, and the class is easy. a blow off class imo, the essays and projects do require some effort, but other than that, super easy. The group project was most annoying, it has 2 parts, and I just don't like group projects because people don't do their part on time, but you get to pick your members easy class, would recommend

Dr. Ozanne is very nice, I think what made me dislike this class a bit was the other people in it. It was a small class, I felt like they never stayed focused and Dr. Ozanne wasn't always the best at keeping us all on track; she wasn't firm enough. The class was interesting and not too hard it was more a problem with the students than the prof.

genuinely SUCH a good prof, i took her for both HIS 315L and 315K and she makes history super entertaining! class is usually just a handful of students (attendence isnt mandatory) and honestly i wish i went more often than i did. she also posts weekly pics of her cats! super easy too, a harsh TA could screw you, but just talk to the prof
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is really kind but history is pretty boring to me. Thankfully class is not mandatory to attend. There are two group projects and two essays that make up most of your grade. The TA I had graded especially difficult compared to the other ones but there was many extra credit opportunities to make up for it.

Professor Ozanne's HIS315K is a laidback yet engaging class. With no exams and optional attendance, the weekly assignments and group projects are manageable, especially with the help of tools like Unstuck ai for study prep. The TAs can be tough graders, but overall this is an easy A if you put in the work.

Dr. Ozanne is one of my favorite history professors I've taken during my tenure at UT. Does a fantastic job at fostering a productive learning environment for everyone, takes her job seriously, has insightful lectures, and is super engaging. The work is not terrible if you're decent at writing, work hard, pay attention to lectures, and read.
Entertaining lecturer and the actual assignments were very easy.

Wonderful prof! You can clearly tell she is passionate about teaching history! Lecture quizzes and Inquizitives are easy 100s as long as you pay attention in class. The bulk of your grade is based on 2 essays and 2 group projects, which are also pretty easy as long as you put the effort into it. She also randomly gives EC if you show up to class.
Content wasn't too difficult, but there was a decent amount of work with weekly assignments. Essays were too harshly graded in my opinion.

She was great, i loved talking to her. her lectures were well made and interesting. On Thursdays, we had discussion days based on the assigned readings and discussion posts. There is a fair amount of reading, but the passages were manageable. There is a major grade from a 2 part group project and major paper, so avoid this if you dislike that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Doesn't get much better. Professor is great and class is composed of two essays and group projects, as well as weekly lecture quizzes and inquizitive assignments. Attendance not required and honestly not necessary to do well. Great class and professor to take for history requirement.

Essays and projects are super straightforward + inquisitive and weekly quizzes. So lots of grades, but pretty easy material and her lectures are very coherent and interesting. Attendance is not mandatory but lecture is super chill so I would recommend going bc she does extra credit for those who go to class on Friday.

Professor Ozanne has to be one of the best professors I've had at UT. Her lectures show you just how educated she is in the subject that she teaches! She is so sweet and gives leniency when you genuinely need it. I took HIS315K and HIS315L with her. Would definitely recommend!!

Took this class online over the summer. Graded on chapter + weekly reading quizzes (have 2 buy textbook for), 2 essays and 2 group projects. group project seems daunting but is really easy actually. This class is super easy if you keep up with the pace. Gave me really good insight into American history. Really interesting and I like her lectures!

Simply just so easy. So much extra credit if you actually show up to class. Essays and projects (project especially) can be graded somewhat hard so just make sure to get feedback on those before submitting and actually contribute. She's so nice and I hate the fact that she had to ask students not to speak on her appearance in course evaluations :/

Dr. Ozanne herself is fantastic! However, getting a tough TA (like I did) makes it a lot more challenging. The course itself is easy and not time-consuming; however, just make sure to rewrite essay #1 and collaborate with your group for the project, and you should be fine! Easy class!

I didn't attend/watch a single lecture and still got an A. If you're well versed with history this class is a breeze. There is a group project that makes up most of your grade, as long as you collaborate and use the feedback from the TAs you're good. There was an opportunity to rewrite essay 1 for a higher grade based on TA feedback which was nice.

Professor Ozanne's lectures are easy to follow and are accessible online. The weekly workload is relatively easy and does not consume much time. The major assignments are not too difficult but the grading is fairly dependent on your TA. Overall an easy class unless your assigned TA is particularly bad.

I love Dr. Ozanne! She does her best to make lectures interesting and weekly assignments are easy. The TA's are a little more tedious with grading essays and group projects, but an A is very attainable. She offers several in-person extra credits, so I would recommend attending class. Highly recommend!
the content itself isnt hard and attendance isnt mandatory, but the grading on group projects and essays is harsh. There is extra credit, but its only in person
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ozanne is absolutely hilarious I love her sense of humor. Pretty low maintenance class, though the 2 essays and 2 group projects took a lot of energy to do and were graded harshly by the TAs. Random extra cred opportunities for attending class, which added like 6 points to my letter grade. Optional attendance. Weekly hw takes like 15 mins.

If you want an easy A/low maintenance class for history, take prof Ozanne! NO EXAMS! Attendance not mandatory, but sometimes offers extra credit for it. Weekly textbook assignments are quizletable, and weekly online quizzes are pretty much common sense. There are 2 essays (TAs enjoy giving low grades, but you can rewrite one) and 2 group projects.

Great professor, attendance not mandatory. Most of grade comes from 2 essays and 2 group projects. "doesn't believe in giving 100s". Your project and essay grades really depend on your TA, but there are lots of small assignments throughout the semester that help supplement grades + extra credit.

Dr. Ozanne's class is fairly straightforward and an easy way to get history credit. Class is not mandatory, but if you do she often gives extra credit opportunities for those that are in class. For the first essay, you get the chance to rewrite it using your TA's feedback.

Never went to class after the first week. Her assignments are all inquizitives and lecture quizzes, which are really easy. The group projects are a little confusing but they're doable. The essays are graded hard though. She has random extra credit instapolls in her classes if you do show up. Overall, I think she was a great professor.

Professor Ozanne is a very likeable person. Caring and very clear on what needs to be done to earn a good grade. Humorous. No tests. Weekly easy quizzes. Two essays. Two (randomly assigned) group projects. Fair in assessing group members for the projects. Highly recommend taking this course for US History credit. Not hard to get an A.

Taking this class was one of the highlights of my semester. I loved the way Prof. Ozanne teaches and engages. Her lectures are easy to follow along and she is very funny. There is a lot of homework but it is manageable. There are no tests but the group projects were killer. Without the projects, this class would be a 10/10.

Took HIS 345J. Impossible to do all of the assigned reading, I stopped trying after the first week and did fine. Surprisingly hard grader but not impossible. Group project at the end of class. Snooze lectures. Good weekly assignments and projects/papers. Lots of things graded so if you try you'll do well.

Dr. Ozanne is an entertaining lecturer and provides the nuance of difficult topics. I found that taking notes during lecture (including primary source discussions) made the two unit essays (in which you only use lectures/textbook/provided primary sources) and the group projects (I got a good group, no issues) really easy. Highly recommend!

Her lectures are good and she is nice. The workload is fair and the essays are doable. They are just graded unnecessarily hard and nit-picky. The group projects themselves aren't difficult but group projects in college are just naturally frustrating and since attendance isn't mandatory expect half your group to not know whats happening.

Dr. O is really nice and I enjoyed her class. Found her class pretty easy, but wouldn't recommend if writing isn't your strong suit. 2 writing based group projects + 2 papers make up 75% of your grade, but TAs aren't tough on the projects and you get a full rewrite on the 1st paper. Would recommend for an easy history credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you have a good background in US history the class is a breeze. If you don't it will be like any other class, you just have to take notes and you'll be fine. Dr. Ozanne cares about students doing well so just ask her any questions. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, but weekly InQuizitives and open-note Lecture Quizzes were easy. I did the former in 1 day and never did an InQuizitive ever again. Essays harshly graded, but professor and TA feedback helpful in getting the grade you desired. You should be allowed to pick group members, as they were often dysfunctional otherwise and hurt you.

The only thing I didn't like about this class was the group projects. For a class this big, group projects are dysfunctional. The papers are graded harshly, but there is a rewrite option, so there's that. The lectures are engaging and there are lecture quizzes every week. The quizzes are open notes and basically there to boost your grade

So chill. Her lectures are boring but not even gonna lie I stopped going like three weeks into the semester. You have weekly lecture quizzes and an inquizitive that are 5 questions and the easiest thing ever. Two papers, two group projects. Papers are only 5-7 paragraphs. The first paper you get to rewrite. Take this class for easy history credit!

If you are looking for an easy HISL, I would highly recommend. Most assignments are Inquizitives and lecture quizzes. There is no final, only 2 essays (graded pretty tough) and 2 timeline projects (also kinda graded tough). Lectures are recorded so you do not need to show up. Prof is very sweet and makes the lectures as interesting as she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An inquisitive assignment is due every Sunday over the textbook chapter. You have to get a 1500 smart score over 20+ questions to get a 100 on it, unfortunately. 2 unit essays and 2 group projects over the semester which is most of your grade. No exams! Lectures are available online and recorded and transcribed so attendance is not mandatory!

If you don't like inquizitive, don't take this class. An inquizitive is due every Sunday where you have to answer 20+ questions and get a smart score of 1500 to get a 100 on the assignment. 2 unit essays over the semester and 2 group projects are the main grades. No test! Lectures are recorded and transcribed online so attendance is not mandatory!

Took it during the summer semester. 2 unit essays and 2 Group Projects, using the ClioVis timeline.Homework: 5 reading quizzes and 14 InQuizitives. Grading depends on your TA. Extra credit is available. Have to purchase a subscription for projects. Recommend taking it as a summer online class to fill core requirements. Easy A.

Attended during summer session, the professor herself taught the course very well. TAs were harsh graders and barely gave feedback for improvement. Group projects based on everyone's work, if one person lacks everyone is penalized. Essays were simple. Extra credit is available. Have to purchase a subscription for projects. Best to take another HIS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is funny. The only stressful thing is the group projects and trying to get into contact with your groupmates and the two essays. This is not a stressful class. If you do the work and care a little, then you will definitely get the A you want (which is why you are most likely reading this and debating whether to take this class or not).

one of my favorite professors. There were 2 essays and 1 group project throughout the semester. The group project is easy but annoying fi you get bad group members. Her grading is very easy and clear. Should have no issue getting an A. Also had amazing TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE HER!!! Her classes are really easy and fun. No midterms or finals just 2 essays and group projects. Essays have clear rubrics so if you understand the material it should be no problem. Quizzes and homework are take-home and should be easy 100. Group projects are fun. VERY EASY A PROF FOR HISTORY!!!!!!

Extremely easy class; never went to lectures, lecture quizzes and Inquizitive homework is super fast and easy to get 100%. First essay is revisable and they tell you exactly what to fix, only essays and group projects for major grades (no exams). She also gives a little bit of extra credit and communicates everything via Canvas.

There are weekly lecture quizzes (easy and with 2 attempts) and inquizzitives. The bulk of your grade is determined by a 2-part group project and 2 essays. You can rewrite the first one for a better grade but the TAs grade pretty tough so good luck. Dr. Ozanne herself is chill and great--try to go to office hours for essay/project help in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ozanne is really chill, and her lectures are interesting enough. The entire class pretty much is dependent on your 2 essays and 2 group projects which are TA graded. If you get a decent TA then this class is SUPER easy, but if you get a harsh one the essays can be a real pain. I'd recommend Ozanne overall if you need the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are about as interesting as you can make history lectures. TAs grade everything so I imagine if you don't get a good TA it might be bad but not sure as I had a good TA. Graded on 2 essays, 2 group projects, and then very easy homework
harsh grading on issues outside of my control. may have only been the TA but I would not take her class again. other courses fill the history core requirement better.

Dr. Ozanne is probably the best professor to take 320W with. She's incredibly smart, accommodating, and the content is interesting. She's funny, easy to reach and willing to help out, and just wants us to enjoy the class. There's lots of participation assignments, and she can be a tough but fair grader. Overall she's just awesome, highly recommend!

The lectures were boring and didn't really help. You should be fine without her lectures if you have a general knowledge of US history. There were no tests but two papers and two group projects that were not too difficult.

I took this class to fulfill a history requirement, and I was very happy with Professor Ozanne. The class has no exams, so your grade is made up of group projects, an essay, and small reading quizzes. If you do your work, you can easily get an A. The essay was graded a little hard, but you get a chance to rewrite it for a better grade.

Dr. Ozanne is amazing! The workload was very manageable and assigments were really easy. Heavily weighted assignments like the essays and timeline projects were dependent on the TA you got, but im pretty sure most of them are really chill. If you need a GenEd history credit, TAKE OZANNE!!

It's a pretty easy A. very clear on what you're graded on. No tests just projects, quizzes, and essays. I stopped showing up after the first week of class and still managed to do pretty well, just make sure you talk to your TA and ask for help on essays& projects to do well! Cool professor though, and really passionate about what she teaches!

Attendance not mandatory and you can choose to join on zoom. It is a content heavy course though so keeping up with it can be difficult at times. You're graded on 2 essays (you get a chance to rewrite the 1st one), 2 group projects, and weekly quizzes. Professor is really nice and doesn't make the lectures boring. Not a difficult A.

Dr. Ozanne was a very chill and nice professor. Attendance was never mandatory, and we had the option to log in via zoom or to just watch the recordings later. Easy lecture quiz each week, 2 timeline assignments that barely take any time, and 2 4-page papers with interesting prompts. Definitely take this class for a history credit

Most of my learning was from the textbook (not required). Lectures are vague and focused on the social/political history of America rather than an equal distribution of social/pol/military/foreign (ex. 1 lecture on WWI, II, Vietnam, but like 4 on social life in 1920s. Yes, important, but annoying that she has to leave other important things out).

Professor Ozanne is one of the best professors I've had here. Her lectures were recorded which was super helpful. She has weekly quizzes that are not hard at all since they are on the lecture slides. Group projects were fairly simple as long as you had a good group and the two essays weren't too bad. I really recommend this professor.

I didn't attend Ozanne's lectures because all her information was found on her slideshows in her modules. There are lecture quizzes and inquisitive homework due every week that is fairly simple. A majority of your grade is based on the two essays and group projects you will have to complete, the essays be graded fairly toughly depending on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is amazing. Her lectures are so organized and logical. Tests and exams are so logical and clear as well. She is the best professor in history. NGL!

Ozanne is excellent and the workload is light with two base assignments a week. You don't even need to go to lecture, but it helps with the two essays and group projects. TA may be harsh graders, but you can simply work to improve with the many opportunities. Take it.

Dr. Ozanne seemed to truly care about her students and even gives time to breathe and relax during class! Attendance wasn't mandatory which was great; however, the grading on papers was pretty harsh as they do not believe in a "perfect paper" and the group projects were pretty annoying but not difficult. Definitely good for a history class at UT!

Loved Professor Ozanne!
1-Allowed to attend: Zoom or in-person (hybrid)
2-Untimed lecture quizzes and essays
3-Attendance isn't mandatory
4-Two group projects (timelines) that are somewhat similar to essays - you'll be fine in these
5-Grades consist of weekly lecture quizzes (easy if you take notes/attend) & Inquisitives, 2 essays, 2 group projects
attendance never mandatory, informative lectures, in person and zoom lectures
If you can get any history class with her do it.

I stopped watching lectures after spring break because they were boring and unhelpful. The class was really easy it just depends on how your TA feels when grading your essays/projects. I got points marked off because I didn't introduce Abraham Lincoln "in case the reader was unfamiliar". Stupid class just pray your TA doesn't decide to fail you.

Other than a few nitpicky things on the 3 papers that required for the class. Generally the homework, lectures, and projects were not that difficult to manage on top of the rest of a full course schedule. While I do feel I was lucky to have fellow group members willing to do work for the group timelines, Professor Ozanne is a great option for HIS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She genuinely cares that you are learning as long as you are in contact with her. If you ask any questions, she is more than willing to research on her own time to help you with any confusing material. There were no tests this year and the major grades were 3 essays and 2 group projects. She also jokes around and tries to empathize with students.

Class is pretty easy, it's 3 essays and weekly quizzes, the weekly quizzes are a breeze. The essays aren't that hard if you actually listen to the feedback given to you after the first essay, got around a 68 on the first essay but finished with an A in the class.
took it in the summer- super easy A

I had such a good time in Dr. Ozanne's class. She was always engaging in the lectures and made the content interesting for us. The class had quite a bit of reading but the quizzes were very forgiving and achievable. My only qualm with the class was that my TA graded super harshly but other than that a great professor and enjoyable class.

The weekly online lecture quizzes and inquisitives are easy 100s. The essays require research and citations and are graded meticulously. TAs do all of the grading so it also kind of depends on your TA. There are 3 Unit essays which are around 4 pages double spaced in length with footnotes and use of primary sources, and there are 2 group projects
Dr Ozanne is great, would totally recommend. Grading is clear and lectures are pretty engaging. Everything is open book and she cares and is available outside of class to help.

Dr. Ozanne was one of my favorite professors, as she truly cares for the students and their grades. The most important assignments are graded by your TA, so it depends on them, but if you have a problem, she will look at your work. The weekly assignments are not challenging at all, and her lectures are interesting.

Lectures can be a bit boring. A lot is covered in the semester so there is not a lot of time spent on each topic, but overall this is a good introductory class to U.S. history. There is a lot of extra credit opportunity and NO TESTS. There are three unit papers worth about 3/5 of the grade combined, but Ozanne and the TA's give excellent feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Ozanne is very kind and understanding. Her HIS 320W class has a very interesting curriculum, which led to good discussions despite it being a small class. She allows for plenty of room for improvement and gives good feedback on assignments.

I really like Dr. Ozanne as a professor, while history is not my favorite she made it bareable. You get two assignments a week that are easy hundreds. However the majority of your grade comes from two group projects and 3 essays. The TA's are harsh graders and this can cause your grade to drop. If youre good at writing essays I would suggest this.
Ozanne is a great professor - doesn't believe in tests so you have open quizzes once a week, 3 unit essays and two group projects- super easy bc everything is open note

Wow! What an AWESOME professor - she is incredible! I really hate history and she made me LOVE this class. I had dropped the two previous classes I was taking for core history credit before this one because I couldn't stand the professors. I was starting to lose hope until I found this class. Seriously, take her! Only negative was group projects.

Easy class for history credit. Quizzes are open note/canvas and have no time limit so no need to read textbook or watch lectures. The majority of the grade is 3 essays (no tests). ATTEND SI SESSIONS FOR ESSAYS. TA's give extensive feedback on essays, so pay attention and implement suggestions on future essays.

Good choice, very rudimentary history so the class itself is not hard. This period of US history is super interesting, I feel like there is a way to make it even more engaging and go into more depth. Overall not a bad experience.

Honestly, I found this course really boring, but that's just because I don't like history. Dr. Ozanne was very nice and the 3 essays/2 group projects were graded pretty nicely. Lecture/textbook quizzes were easy 100s. The lectures had some fun content and Dr. Ozanne was always enthusiastic. But if you can CLEP and don't like history, do it.

solid choice for a history class, if you're looking for an easy class for credit, this class is definitely the way to go. requires work and effort for an a so don't fall behind, three total essays and two group projects count heavily toward the final grade (the lecture quizzes are straightforward as long as you watch the lectures)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I really liked this class. The group projects were frustrating as only 5 of 50 points were individual grading, so people who didn't contribute much would get basically the same grade. Lectures were interesting enough and lecture quizzes were super straightforward. I genuinely enjoyed the textbook reading and the associated quiz program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Ozanne was a great lecturer. I had her during COVID, and her lectures were some of the few I could actually watch the whole way through without getting distracted. The lectures were only 2 hr/week, the group assignments were actually pretty fun, and the essays were not too difficult (and the last one is optional). No exams!

I took this course asynchronously, but her format of the course was amazing and super easy to understand. She was also super informative and obviously enjoys teaching. She really cares about what she teaches and her students. It's not difficult to make an A and basically hard to fail, would definitely recommend.

Dr. Ozanne is awesome! Each week you do a quiz on InQuizitive, watch 2 lecture videos, and do a 5 question quiz with 2 attempts. There are 3 group projects which are timelines you make on ClioVis and they are pretty simple. There are 3 essays and she drops your lowest one so you can skip the last one if you did well on the first 2

She called my friend and I out ALL THE TIME in a huge lecture hall for "talking" when we were discussing lecture material in class. She has the ears of a hawk and it seemed like she was *trying* to embarrass me/others in front of the class. It took away from my learning. But true, her lectures were good if you don't discuss in class with friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ozanne is so awesome. She makes me laugh and she is really encouraging and understanding. The essays are fairly clear-cut and the group projects aren't bad either if you have a good group! There are easy quizzes and no exams at all! I highly recommend Dr. Ozanne, especially if you would rather write than take an exam.

Your grade is all up to your TA not the prof. However, her lectures are great, her cat is cute, and the workload is more than manageable. 3 essays and 3 group timelines. every week you watch a lecture and answer a few questions, doesnt get simpler. just hope your TA isnt a strict grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous, so every week there was a lecture quiz and textbook quiz, and they were super easy. There are normally two recorded lectures a week that are 45 minutes long. The other half of the class is made up of three group projects and two papers. These are simple as long as you dont procrastinate! I really enjoyed this class!!!

3 group projects per unit, 3 unit papers (topics to choose from given ahead of time), uses InQuizitive software for weekly quizzes, fun & easy software but reserve 1-2hrs to complete it (lets you keep trying til you hit 100), 1-2 lectures weekly then a 5 question lecture quiz with 2 attempts untimed, sweet professor, easy enough if you keep up

Professor Ozanne did a fantastic job for an online-based course. Her lectures are a little long sometimes but she literally gives you all the information you need. Group projects are not dreadful and essays are graded fairly (if you know what you are writing about). Super nice and funny.

3 exams that are timed essays and two papers that analyze a primary source already discussed in class. TAs grade a little harder than expected for an intro class (and during a pandemic). But she is fun and nice, has good lectures, and gives extra credit that can only be received if you show up. otherwise attendance isnt mandatory (lectures online)

I loved Dr. Ozanne! She's fun, passionate and always makes class engaging. Class consists of 3 essay exams, 2 primary source papers and 3 online quizzes with no final. Also offers extra credit randomly like 5 times throughout the semester for going to class. Don't need the textbook at all. Grades rely mostly on TA, but some are tougher than others.

Dr. Ozanne is funny, approachable, and caring. You get 3 midterms, 2 online quizzes, 2 primary source responses, and no finals. Extra credit opportunities that appear randomly are given, as well. However, grades all depend on your TA, and her TAs are tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Rachel Ozanne is lovely! You can tell how passionate she is about history and how much she cares about her students' learning. There were only 2 papers and 3-4 exams that were all in essay form. She allows grade disputes with the TA's, so it's flexible! She's quirky and laid-back, but knows her stuff! Would definitely recommend for your core credit

Lectures were very entertaining and gave an excellent overview of the material covered. The class was structured very well, 3 essay tests and two papers with good prompts. Kept me very engaged and interested in learning history.

Heres the deal, Professor Ozanne is very kind and although the subject itself is boring, you are graded by very few assignments. Your grade is basically luck based-some TA's much easier than others which can be extremely unfair. My last name starts with an A so I got the toughest grader. The TA determines your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great lectures, though didn't feel I learned a ton having already taken APUSH. Exams and papers aren't bad but grading can be nitpicky and depends on the TA a lot, quizzes are easy. She makes the class interesting and she's super caring, so I loved going to class even though it's not all that necessary. Don't bother with the textbook

Dr. Ozanne is not only caring, passionate about history, and engaging in her lecture style, but is one of the most genuinely friendly people I've ever met. There is no way you'll regret taking her for a history credit. I never even purchased the textbook and still made an A  you just need evidence/quotes and more than anything a strong argument.

She's fabulous. Lectures are always fun, and informative. Tests are all in-class essays. Exam topics will be given a week before the exam date. Her sense of humor is amazing, she'll throw some jokes so you don't get bored just listening to her. Class discussions are helpful to not fall asleep if you hate history. Read the textbook and go to class

Great professor. Grade heavily relies on TAs. Tests are all essays which sounds scarier than it is. She is entertaining and provides extra points for attendance. Must work to get the grade in this class and put in time to meet with TAs/professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Ozanne!! Her class is really lecture heavy, but she does a good job of keeping them engaging. There's reading assigned every week, but she lectures over the same material so you're honestly fine if you don't read. Then there's 2 primary source document papers and 3 exams (no final). Take her class!!

Dr Ozanne is very nice and friendly. The best way to succeed is going to class and taking detailed notes on all of her lectures, she gives good info that is not in the textbook. The days leading up to an exam are a lot of work and she expects you to know a lot of detail, but as long as you study a lot it is fine.

We had 3 in-class exams which were essays - she gave us 4 essay questions a week before and picked one on test day. We also had 2 papers that were submitted online. Dr. Ozanne was sweet and made little jokes during lecture that I enjoyed. I wasn't a fan of the class during exams but if you prepare ahead of time you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great and entertaining professor. Your grade pretty much depends on 2 things: the 3 in class essay exams and the 2 primary source responses. Attendance isn't required but she gives extra credit points sometimes for being there and lecture is very important for exam prep soooo... go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There's 3 midterm papers, 2 papers turned in online, and 3 really easy multiple choice online quizzes. If you attend lectures (there's extra credit for going) and read the 3-4 pgs of assigned readings each class, you won't need to read the textbook. The grading is done by the TAs, so you don't know what to expect, but write well and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is a good choice to fulfill the HIS315K credit. Ozanne's lectures are very interesting, and she is genuinely interested in her students and making sure lectures are engaging. There are 2 papers to write outside of class, and 3 in class exams (all essays). Though the class is lecture/writing heavy, it is an interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ozanne is a kind professor who made lectures moderately entertaining. Tests are entirely essay based with 4 prompts given approx. a week in advance. She will pick one of these and then require an in class essay. The issue with this is they expect a ridiculous amount of detail in only an hour. The paper assignments had terrible feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Ozanne was a great professor and lecturer! 3 In-class Essays: 4 possible prompts given a week in advance 3 Outside-of-class Quizzes: Super easy as long as you take notes from class and the textbook 2 Outside-of-class Papers: Choose a document to analyze from a list, pretty easy (as long as you have a clear thesis and topic sentences!) No Final!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ozanne was a great professor! The class is lecture heavy, but the lectures are generally pretty interesting. There are 3 online quizzes, 2 papers, and 3 in-class essays throughout the semester. Though the class does take some work, it is a fairly easy course.

Dr. Ozanne is a good lecturer and delivers a surprising amount of information in one hour. The course is not hard, but you do have put in a lot of work. Her "exams" are 1 hour in class essays where she randomly picks from 1 of 4 prompts that she releases a weak prior. I'm an engineering major, so the course was good but I dreaded working on it.

Ozanne is a great person! I personally dislike US history, but it wasn't super terrible. If you read the textbook or go to lectures you'll be fine, but try both! The tests are essay based which sucks but you can prepare easily and they're only an hour- make sure you can write a thesis. She's funny also the lectured based style isn't for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took her class as a freshman and definitely recommend it unless you hate doing essays! Our exams were all in class essays but it wasnt anything over the top. I definitely recommend taking her class!

Professor Ozanne's class is powerpoint heavy and lots of reading. You have to read a book and write an essay on it. Lots of reading from articles. Grading is a bit tough because it's all essay. TA mainly does the grading. She will give you a list of questions for exam prep and on exam day she'll pick one. Do prep, pass class. No prep, fail class.

Ozanne is a really sweet, charismatic and funny professor. The TA was a pretty tough grader, but she did curve the class slightly to compensate for that. You can tell that she cares about her students and your education, and though you will have to put effort into the class, it is worth it.

Dr. Ozanne gives long lectures that last from the first minute to the last. Her lectures were useful as you can use the information on the essay so you won't have to read. There are 3 midterms that are bluebook essay type. However, she expects perfection on the essay and getting A is very tough. She gives 5 extra credits out of 360 for attendance.

Took this course in person. Lectures weren't all mandatory but there were pop quizzes ( heavy at the end of the semester). All lectures were recorded. 10 pop quizzes but only 6 are graded. Lectures are kind of boring but there is a lot of resources for help. Test are all different ( free response, multiple choice, T or F). One group project.
Great professor who cares about her students, but if you know basically anything about health, society, and sociology this class is pretty boring. Easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Loved this class! The lectures weren't always engaging but often very interesting. The content was easy to grasp and the tests were easy. You get a cheat sheet for 2/4 exams and 1 exam gets dropped. Attendance measured by group quizzes graded on participation. Only thing that was unenjoyable was the group project.

Professor O is so passionate about her subject and is a very clear communicator. There are random pop quizzes, but you get a 100 for writing your name down, so they're more for attendance. My only issue was a group project worth 10% of your grade, where you are assigned a random group (and only given Canvas to find them in a class of 300+).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring prof, easy lectures to follow but also really engaging. I didn't take many notes for this class besides guest lecturers. Also provides a ton of extra credit opportunities.

Will have occasional pop quizzes throughout the semester, so you should probably show up often. Assigns a good amount of reading but you could get by without reading it and taking good notes during lectures. Exams are mostly lecture content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing prof + TAs. Super interesting topics, a lot of it is pretty obvious/common sense topics being taught so it's not crazy hard. The free response exams are graded a little harshly and getting even a few half-points off can kind of tank your grade. Very charismatic teacher & had amazing guest speakers. Love her.
She's nice and class is interesting. Lots of discussion posts but there's like 6 drops I think. Cheat sheet on exams full page front and back handwritten.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Osbakken was AMAZING. Super knowledgeable and topics apply to many people. Not and HS major but I loved this class. Tests were easy as long as you did the review, she also allowed a cheat sheet. As long as you pay attention you'll get a good grade.

I love Osbakken she is so mom and cares a lot about her students. You have to pay attention to every little detail about the slides for the exams EVERY detail. For the final exam I had to buy a book out of pocket but it was actually good and I never read yayy. She will NOT curve your 89.999 also do your very best on the group project nothing lazy.

I really enjoyed Dr. Osbakken's lectures. You get a front and back note sheet for every exam. However, they can be a little challenging if you don't take notes and don't do the readings. The discussions are very easy.
Nice lady but can be condescending and a bit passive aggressive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 4 exams but the lowest gets dropped. Lectures are boring sometimes. Allows cheat sheet on exams that are front and back. Easy discussion posts. There is a group project towards the end of the semester. She's chill, take this class it's interesting

Dr. Osbakken was awesome. Her lectures could be a little long at times but the topic was super interesting. The grading was super fair and the tests are not difficult as long as you use the resources she gives you (an entire page of notes for each test).

She is very passionate about her teachings. She has guest lectures every other week to wrap up the material covered. Her lectures are engaging and easy to follow. The tests are relatively easy, she allows one cheat sheet. Overall, I recommend her!

This was an interesting class and Dr O was able to teach the material very well. The slideshows are often very dense but just retaining the key concepts is whats important. A few tests but theres a cheat sheet, would recommend.

Dr. Osbakken is single-handedly the best professor I've had. She's incredibly caring, insightful, and has enriched my academic experience in more ways than one. She will teach you to look at issues from multiple perspectives and to strive to understand the systems of society in a more holistic way. I couldn't speak highly enough of Dr. Osbakken!

Osbakken is great professor! Her lecture slides are very content heavy but as long as you take notes and do the readings you should be fine. she does also do a good amount of extra credit and drops a test. You also get one paper front and back as a cheat sheet for every test. Great class for any pre health student and very relevant to real world
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor O is a great lecturer and truly cares about what she teaches. There is a group project and 4 tests along with an essay at the end of the semester but if you go to class, take notes, and stay attentive you should easily do well!

Other students grade your work for your weekly essays. Let me repeat, other students can determine your grade. If you want the TA to grade your work, Dr. O says the TA will grade 1000x harder. I think a professor, or at least a TA, should be responsible for dolling out grades, not other 19-year-olds.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor O is an amazing speaker and lecturer. Some of the slides are a bit dense, but she walks you through it effortlessly. All tests are open note and we had a group project which was pretty fun! I enjoyed and learned so much in this class!

Professor O's lectures were great. She is extremely well-spoken, caring, and educated. She isn't afraid to talk about controversial subjects, but she is open and fair to all students. Your grade is made up of short essays and quizzes. Make sure to take good notes, because she rarely posts the slides from the lectures.

Dr. O was a great professor and SO kind. Her TAs are awesome and there are so many helpful resources for this class. There was a lot of writing involved, as well as three heavy weighted quizzes. This being said, the course material was current and interesting and I highly recommend it!
I honestly loved Professor O so much she was one of the kindest women ever. The class is very easy to understand and connect ideas together.

I found the lectures boring, but I would suggest going either ways. Professor was super accommodating, tests were open-note and notes were provided per lecture (it is because of this that I didn't tank tests). Still the topics are interesting and it would benefit you to go to office hours and participate. Group project is doable but no slacking.

I love Dr O! We covered a lot of material, but the pace wasn't too fast. There are 3-4 essays graded by peers, which I hated because it's easy for retaliatory low grading to happen. Tests are relatively easy if you pay attention, and are open note. AWESOME professor -- 10/10 recommend. She loves participation, so maybe don't t take if you/re shy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was not easy it takes a lot of time through readings, discussion posts, and essays. However it is doable with the right mindset and determination. Attendance is optional the professor is extremely understanding. I would not recommend this class if you're not majoring in medical related, this class asked for too much time and work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Super compassionate and understanding professor, one of the best I've taken at UT. Lectures do cover a lot of information but exams were open notes (so take good notes!). Essay assignments were graded by other students, so easy A's. Discussion prompts were short, but lots of reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a very mind-opening class. The information is so important, especially if you plan on going into the medical field. There is a LOT of reading and the open-note quizzes were IMO pretty hard. 3 tests. 3 short essays. 1 long essay. 1 group project. 10 discussion posts. Some extra credit. It's easy to skip but don't!! Take notes and participate

Took Dr. O's Cancerland course - Best class I've taken! Rlly inspirational & completely changes the way you view healthcare! Majority of the class was discussion-based w/ guest speakers - 3 papers & 2 presentations. All pretty straightforward! You need to have a connection to cancer or compelling reason to join the course, for discussion purposes.

As many students at UT know, Dr. Osbakken is the best. She is incredibly well respected and you are lucky to get into her class. The H&S seminar was at times challenging. There is a big group project that moves fast. Dr. O can be a tough grader, but as long as you show up and participate you will succeed.

Dr. Osbakken's class was one of my favorites this semester. The course was a bit reading-heavy, but overall it was pretty manageable. Make sure you take good notes because sometimes the tests can be a little tricky, but overall the course was not too difficult. Fantastic class!
Very good class and professor. I have learned a lot from this course without having to struggle much. Easy class for the A. Great information taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Osbakken is a good lecturer. Essays are graded by peers and then you have to give them a feedback score. If a peer does not agree with the score you give them, they can give you a low feedback score and the TAs will not change your grade. Exams are tricky and the exam grades are posted after 2weeks. Nice professor, poor grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is an interesting course with an AMAZING professor. She truly wants you to succeed and wants to hear your opinions. Technically reading heavy but as long as you understand the main points, I don't find the reading necessary. 4 SHORT peer-graded essays, 3 open note quizzes, 10 disc posts (can drop 2), one group project. She is so kind.. TAKE!!!

Dr. O was a great professor and gave many opportunities to talk about the readings we were assigned. The only issue I have is that your essays are based on what your peers grade you. There is a pressure not to grade them perfectly even if you felt they did amazing. You have to make sure to grade them off of things even if you are not 100% certain.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors ever. Her class is very interesting and being in a pandemic she made sure her students were adjusting okay to everything. Weekly readings but nothing too hard and an essay every two weeks but from the material you learn in class and the readings they aren't hard to overcome. I would recommend this class to everyone!

I think everyone needs to take this class if possible because the things we learned are beyond useful. Although Dr. O is awesome this class is extremely hard to keep up with. There are a ton of things due each week and her quizzes are super tricky. My biggest advice is to stay on top of everything especially since the readings each week are long.

This ranks in one of my favorite classes I've taken the past 2.5 years. The material is so important and useful for today's problems. Professor O and her TAs are AMAZING, they are all very caring. There are weekly discussion posts, 7 essays, and 3 quizzes. Make sure to do well on the quizzes because that's why I got a B! but great class!

I highly recommended this class not only for the professor but also the course content. I find the material Dr.O includes is extremely important for people to learn, and I bet you will change your mind on a lot of issues. The essays are straightforward, and the tests are doable if you have completed the readings and have general grasp on concepts

All the other posts explain her class accurately however it is important to know that her tests are worded awfully. Every question is "select which one is false" or along those lines and all the choices are so similar. That part isn't that bad but it gets worse when there is actually more than one answer. No extra credit provided yet either :((((((
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading assignments! I didn't read them until before the 4 tests & still am doing well. Lecture attendance isn't req. and is recorded- must watch to do well on tests. Interesting material-some is common sense. Essays are graded by peers but this DOESN'T mean the essay grades are easy A's!! study for the tests and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lovely professor, would definitely take another class by her. She does assign an unbearable amount of readings but as long as you attend class you should be able to write a solid essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hands down, the best class I have taken in college. Dr. Osbakken is amazing, the exams are long and my TA graded harshly, but the class is worth it. She is always available to talk to students, the readings were never boring, and if you go to the TA's study review sessions you will do well on the exams. The papers aren't worth much of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor I've taken at UT! Truly cares about the success of her students and will do everything she can to make sure you make the most out of your learning experience with her. Very engaging- her persona fuels a self-motivation to do your best. Class environment was very inclusive. I'll never forget Stephanie.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Osbakken was a great lecturer, I learned a lot from her class. Her class is a little workload heavy, with lots of readings (2-3 per each class) that are covered on the exams. It is doable to get an A as long as you attend class and study a few days before the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stephanie is very nice and cares about the material, but makes the class much harder than it needs to be. The tests focus on what information comes from which author, instead of just the information. The A, B, C, A/B, A/C, all of the above format for the tests makes it difficult as well. I would avoid if possible.

Dr. Osbakken helped me facilitate strong social capital at UT. She urged me to visit professors and build relationships on my road to graduate school. Her Health and Society class was both inspirational and engaging. Great lectures and lots of new and thought-provoking information. Definitely take this class!

She's wonderful- she's an engaging lecturer who really cares about both her subject material and her students and is really such a proponent for their success. Her tests are a little weird because she asks if multiple answers are correct are not, but the information is definitely relayed in class and in your readings.

Enlightening lessons that are clear and easily comprehensible. Participation comes in the form of in-class activities that are random. Work isn't bad and you should really talk to your TA if you want to do well on the weekly reading reports bc they're the ones grading it. Don't sweat the class. It's not hard.

Dr. Osbakken is an amazing professor. She was always well prepared and confident during her lectures and is ready and willing to meet with her students. She's very direct and if you go to class and pay attention (and read the materials) then her tests are really fair. I honestly can't stress how amazing of a professor she is. Take her classes!!

For the year I was in, it was almost impossible to get a 100 on the reading responses. People in my study group said the TAs gave little and vague feedback. Definitely do the readings and attend the lectures. The exams sometimes have specific statistical questions and can be difficult, but an A is doable. The study guides are dense, but helpful

Osbakken is an amazing professor. You can tell she cares about what she does. You have reading responses every other week and a lot of readings outside of class. Her tests are very tricky like A, B, C, A and B, A and C, All of the above etc.. However the class is worth it and is very interesting. Would recommend.

This class took work. It is very lecture heavy so even though attendance isn't mandatory, I would go. Exams weren't easy but they were fair. She is great to those who do the work and ask for help. But she will never raise your grade if you have been slacking off and missing class. This is an intro class so it sets up your foundation.

Dr. Osbakken was great! This class is an easy A ONLY if you show up to class & pay attention. I didn't do all of the readings (and trust me there are a lot) however if you read the lectures slides and do the study guide before each test and you will be fine. The topic opened my eyes to healthcare system in the US & around the world. Amazing Class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite teacher at UT so far! I got an A soley through attending every class and taking great notes, doing all the hw assignments and following directions, skimmed the readings and taking notes on them, and for the test looking over reading notes and powerpoint. No homework besides to read. Easy class if you put in a little effort. Amazing lady!!!

This class was amazing. Topics were very interesting, fun, and relevant. 5 short essays on certain assigned articles (easy 100). A lot of assigned reading but honestly except for the essay ones, i didn't do them because she summarizes them in class anyways but i did take great notes and didn't skip a class. Made 85+ on all 3 exams (30 all MC).
Great class, learned a lot, got 85+ on all tests and essays, slacked off on participation so I got a B, should have been a solid A
You must do the readings (keep up with it) and attend lecture. Overall the class isn't too difficult, but you have to keep up with the work. Be sure to ask questions and attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor made it clear from day one that if you became buddy/buddy with her she would help you out but idk how that exactly worked for out for most people. The one essay and final really messed up a lot of kids grades. Overall the material is pretty interesting, but there is a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, super helpful, didn't do the readings that she required, but showed up to each class, and she was super interesting and engaging. Definitely speak up and go to office hours, she's super open to questions, and she's pretty funny too. Tests are pretty doable without doing the readings. Do the study guides and pay attention!

Dr. Osbakken is a wonderful professor. My advice is to sit in the front, speak up in class, and go to office hours. She makes it clear that she will help you grade-wise if you participate in class. The midterms are very straight forward and mostly common sense. While there is a lot of reading, she mostly asks for main ideas of articles.

She was so helpful and really got me interested in the topic. She's very lenient when it comes to grading, and she's extremely empathetic. Attendance is mandatory, but you won't regret going. She does assign A LOT of reading so be prepared.

DO NOT take Pryor if you have public speaking anxiety. Spoke to him about my anxiety disorder so that he could better help me improve, berated me in front of the whole class for no reason and made me cry. Truly enjoys picking on the quieter students, even when you show up to every class and put effort into assignments. Would never take again.

Easy going
Human focused
Textbook does not matter
Easy grading

DP tells a lot of stories and loves to make people laugh. He truly is a sweet old man and wants you to be friends with your class. A lot of people ended with an A-, but you can get an A if you go to office hours every time. All the TAs grade harshly without much reasoning. Don't be afraid of the A-; take Pryor's class and you'll learn something.

Great guy, hilarious, and he actually connects with the students. By the end of the semester, he makes sure you know the rest of your class, too.
Embrace the A-. There's basically no leeway to get an A, and the TA's grading is ridiculously harsh. So you'll almost definitely end with an A-, but it's a fun class, and Pryor is a really good professor.

Pryor is a great person, but beware that presentations will never be 100 and will always be in the 90-96 range if you did well, which can eat up the 60 points you are allowed to lose to get an A. The TA grades really harshly and will take off for the same writing error multiple times, so make sure to check the guidelines.

Although, he is a tough grader on group presentations, Pryor is a nice and understanding professor. The grade you get is almost entirely dependent on your TAs. Double check writing guidelines to not lose points. Presentation grading is subjective, but is not hard to get an A if you put some effort. I didn't like the random 50 mcq tests at all.
Doesn't care about students and very harsh.

I really liked Dr. P. He was a classic teacher who taught with notes and his incredible memory. His TAs grade extremely harshly but talking to them in-person really helps. Dr. P was very understanding of peoples situations and was more than a fair teacher. He's such a genuinely and kind professor who actually wants you to succeed.
Amazing 324 prof. So funny and passionate about the subject he teaches. Hard to get an A but absolutely worth taking

Pryor is funny and well-spoken, but he is a tough grader especially on group presentations. The 'exams' are some 50 MCQs for which you have to memorize 8 chapters each so not fun. Little room for error in this course, but he creates a very inclusive environment and encourages everyone to participate. Talk to your TA often and they grade you well.

He's the best professor I've ever had at UT!! There are lots of speeches in this class and I usually get super nervous giving speeches, but the environment the professor created made it feel comfortable and supportive. He also gives thoughtful and constructive feedback. TAs are the ones grading the written assignments, and they grade pretty tough.

He has been the most amazing professor I've ever had in my college experience here at UT. We started off rough since he can sometimes be harsh with critiques but if you talk with him and show that you care he will help you out. An amazing person and human being! I wish I could take his class again. Love DP!!

Literally the best prof ever! He gives very valuable feedback on presentations and has a good sense of humor as well. Though assignments don't have a clear rubric, you can dispute your grade with him.
Such a dawg. Take him.

Dr. P is a great and caring professor. He allows 3 un-excused absences before it affects your grade. If you speak with him, he is more than flexible. TA grades almost all work, so per his advice become besties with ur TA. Helps you grow as a person, very understanding.

Professor Pryor is the BEST!! BA 324 is overall a bad class, but Pryor really makes the most of it, even when you have him at 8 am (just like me). He doesn't allow phones, but that doesn't even make a difference because you're actually engaged with him. He cares a lot about his students and wants them all to succeed. TAKE HIM!!!

Dr. Pryor is a fantastic professor who genuinely cares about his students. The only problem is that grading with written assignments is never clear. If you don't go to TA office hours every time, don't expect to get an A. Grading in general is so much harder than the other BA324H sections. That being said, class was always a good time.

If you are between Dr.P and any other professor I highly suggest taking Dr.P, even if it is an 8am (like mine). He is one of if not the best professor I've had during my 4 years at UT. He really enjoys speaking to his students and building classroom connection. Tests are easy if you take notes (Open book). Everyone needs to meet Dr.P- the best @ UT

Professor Dyer is great, however the TAs really bring this class down. Grading extremely harshly and are only available once a week for an hour, so assignment criteria is extremely unclear. Tests are tough but not worth much. Would recommend anyone take Pryor if not for the TAs, speeches & presentations are enjoyable due to him.

This class has some of the worst grading I have ever experienced. Unclear assignments with no real rubric. The writing assignments were extremely subjective. The speeches weren't difficult. The workload wasn't heavy, but the assignments were graded way too harshly.

One of my favorite professors I have ever taken at UT and McCombs. He is really understanding and wants you to succeed. Show up to class, go to office hours. He is really smart and makes his lectures as enjoyable as possible even at 8am. Tests were open note if I remember correctly, go to class and the class is easy!

Pryor for MAN is very diff from BA! The class is just discussion over very basic topics but I think this is changing moving forward so beware ig lol. Not tech savvy at all and if you ask him about grading criteria (or anything he doesn't have an easy answer for) you won't get an answer and will likely be graded unfairly and very subjectively.

I was pretty nervous taking this course as I heard bad things about the class, but Prof. Pryor is great!! Yes, there is a lot of public speaking and presenting but he makes you feel very comfortable and doesn't criticize you too harshly. He genuinely cares about his students and as long as you communicate your needs he will be of great help.

Pryor is a great person and values quality over quantity. He lectures with no visuals which can be boring at times but the content is very simple and there are not many assignments. Assignments are very open-ended. The group project is simple but standardized and the tests were very simple. His class was enjoyable if students participate.

Pryor was a great MAN professor. However he will call you out for not participating / being attentive in class. Exams are all open note / open textbook. Didn't take any notes in class and still was able to do well on exams, also his lectures are interesting

If you are the type A McCombs student who needs clear direction don't take this class. If you can handle a bit of ambigious instruction, changing deadlines, and watching the occasional film in class then take him. He really encourages discussion and challenges McCombs sterotypes. If you want something low stakes and enjoyable I would recommend.

This class is honestly super frustrating because getting an A can just be up to luck. Also, all the writing assignments save the capstone are graded by the TA. This can also be very frustrating bc in order to fit a distribution, you will get points off for random subjective things like "too cliche" or "Pryor doesn't like this".

Professor Pryor is probably one of my favorite professors. Extremely funny and provides helpful feedback. TA does grade extremely hard, but if you attend office hours and ask questions about the assignments, you will get high grades. Pryor is an amazing professor, but you have to work hard to get an A. Attend office hours and ask questions!

The class helps improve business writing skills, but grading is tough. Meet with your TA's before every assignment to get feedback and guidelines about your writing. In terms of presentation skills, personally, I didn't gain too much besides learning how to work with new groups often.

Professor Pryor is a fun professor. The class helps a lot with business writing and presentation skills. However the problem lies in the grading, which is very harsh. Go to the TA before every writing assignment to know where you can fix a paper to maximize your score. The exams are very tough and don't make much sense at times
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fun class where you get to present and learn about your classmates. Problem is, DP only gives out 95s and below and you need above a 94 to get an A. Go to the TA office hours for every writing assignment or you will lose tons of points. Pryor actively encourages other teachers to grade more harshly. Textbook exams are tough and require heavy study.

The only great thing about the class is being forced to present, and that's the primary way of learning. He never teaches in class, so you're expected to learn off feedback on assignments. TAs grading assignments are almost all awful, and assignments from the textbook are even worse. Listening to other people's stories is interesting though.

Caring guy, wanted all of us to grow. Sometimes grading criteria was unclear. He doesn't give 100s. I think I liked the class because it was a chance to hear other people's stories rather than anything he said.

Pryor is an extremely down to earth guy who knows what he's talking about. As long as you're comfortable having conversations, you'll do good in this class. The only thing to worry about is how awful the TA's may be, they give unreasonably low grades on written assignments.

Listen. RMP says Prilipko is an easier A (admittedly true) but I managed to get an A w/ Pryor and it was 100x more rewarding. He is SO out of pocket in the funniest way, will truly push you to grow, and overall is hands down the best prof I've ever had. Don't let these reviews scare you away from what will end up being your favorite class ever.

Dr. Pryor is the best professor I've had at McCombs. He challenges students to take risks which is refreshing compared to the norm at McCombs. An A is attainable if you go to TA office hours and have them read your writing (multiple times). There are a lot of presentations. Learn from the feedback he gives your peers and you'll be golden.

Dr. Pryor likes to come off as ambiguous. He values humor creativity and makes a point to let you know he doesn't care about your grades. Nor will they be curved. You need to go to TA office hours to understand how the TA will grade written assignments. Written assighnments are strictly graded; quizzes are easy. Speak clearly and be humorous!

Dr. Pryor is kind and he genuinely wants to see your speaking improve. I seemed to get the same ballpark grade on every speaking assignment, and it seemed kind of arbitrary. Definitely get to know Pryor during class and office hours. That said, much of the grade depends on written assignments graded by the TA so attend their office hours too.
Take another professor unless you want to do more work for a lower grade. Class is very subjective, and grade is dependent on the ta

Dr. Pryor is a genuine person who wants to see you become a better speaker and presenter. You need to work with the TAs a LOT in this class if you want a good grade because they grade all the writing assignments. Build a real relationship with Pryor during office hours so he actually remembers who you are. Work hard, speak well, and you'll be fine.

Dr. Pryor makes very inappropriate comments, made a comment about eating disorders to student and made the class uncomfortable. cannot time manage well so had to do a presentation during finals week that should have been done in class and it took 3 hours for me to go. Didn't even give me feedback on it. I think he literally only gives between 85-90

Pryor is funny and nice, but grading was pretty hard. Had to go to office hours to make sure I wouldn't get points off for obscure things. Presentations were also unpredictable in terms of what he was looking for in our speaking. Exams/textbook quizzes were open note and super easy though despite not reading the textbook.

The grading of writing assignments felt subjective but not too unfair. Go to the TAs for feedback on your writing a day or 2 before submitting it. My advice- learn to communicate openly everything with your groups well and early bc the capstone group project is a huge chunk of the grade. Apart from the capstone, the workload is easy. Pryor is funny
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pryor is a nice professor and he can be hilarious if you can catch his jokes. He is so nice and tells some really great stories as well. Keep in mind this class is tough to do well in. If you go to the TA frequently to fix your writing, get a good capstone group, turn in everything, and go to class you can do well. Overall, I loved this class!

Pryor is great and has a good sense of humor. Most written assignments are very straightforward and easy to complete! His grading criteria for oral assignments are a bit vague, but it is not too difficult to do well in this class. The capstone project is a massive group commitment, but it is actually enjoyable.

Pryor is a solid choice for the BA324 class. It can be rather difficult to get an A in his class but don't be discouraged, very few people do, so getting an A- is great. Talk and get to know him he is a great person to talk to in office hours; be sure to use the textbook for the writing assignments; class is group-work heavy with projects too!

Dan is an absolute gem. He is funny and has an excellent personality. However, the criteria for assignments if very vague. Can be good or bad depending on your creativity level. Lectures do not offer much, you do all your learning through assignments. Group work HEAVY. My only suggestion is be creative and talk with him. Not a difficult class.

I didn't learn much from lectures, mainly from assignments. Everything except the capstone is essentially busy work. Really hard to not get an A. The TA is rather not helpful and grades a little hard so make sure you go to textbook for how to construct the written assignments because the professor doesn't tell you that in class. Lots of group work.

His grading criteria was definitely difficult to grasp and I think his humor is sometimes questionable, but the assignments and group projects are actually pretty fun. Made some new friends in this class because it's so group project heavy! Not terribly difficult to get an A.

Dr. Pryor is such a nice man! I didnt think his BA324 class was difficult, plus is he super funny and caring. The only thing is that he is very old school and does things a lot differently than other professors would. Definitely take this class with him!

The assignments are actually graded by the TA's which always find some small detail to take off points for. Expect a B+. Compared to other professors Pryor doesn't lecture much, and his assignments have a lot more leniency to them.

BA324 is known for being a hard class at UT, but taking it with Pryor made it so much fun. I looked forward to going to this class because Pryor encouraged us to speak and be outgoing. You will have to work hard for an A and there are a lot of group/partner assignments so get ready to make new friends. Take Pryor - he's pretty amazing!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: BA324 is hard in general with lots of presentation and writing assignments. Pryor would be there for people who were scared to talk in front of others. He helped me to get better in my public speaking and I sucked haha. I took him 2 years ago and I still visit him to chill and talk! One of my favorite professor at UT!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Pryor is a great professor. He gives great advice on presentation skills and professional development. That being said, you definitely have to put the work in to get an A. Papers are graded tough by the TA, and presentations must be polished. You will learn to work with teams in this class. He stresses creativity and humor which is awesome.

Truly one of the best professors that I've had at UT. His class is not even close to as difficult as other professor's classes. While you're going to have to work to get an A- or even possibly an A, it is definitely not impossible as long as you work consistently in the class, go to office hours, and just get to know him. Definitely, recommend.

My favorite professor yet. He is very kind and genuine. He cares about his students, gives excellent feedback, and is very entertaining. Take Dan so you at least enjoy not getting an A (McCombs curves BA324 to a B-). I don't like that my grade is heavily dependent on how my group members perform, but that's life.

BA324 itself is hard. Be ready to write, present, and work with a partner and teams. This class helped me to overcome talking front of people at least a little bit. Pryor genuinely cares about his students (I took him a year ago and I still go talk to him). The grading criteria are not straightforward but I just dealt with it.

Dr. Pryor is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. His class is not easy by any means, but his teaching makes the course actually feel fun. He is also very understanding to students' specific situations, and if you have a genuine reason for missing class or turning in an assignment late he'll work with you. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND.
