reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Loved Dan, but his TA wasn't the best. She was super sassy, and she constantly conflicted with Dan. She failed to remember that she was a student, too. She spoke to us like she was our professor. Lastly, if you get a 89.99 in this class, they won't curve you.

If you don't care much about your grade, he's fine. Fun class, but if you want any sort of A, good luck. Grades are based on random stuff, you will never understand why someone got 5 points higher or lower than you. There's little to no instruction on anything and points are taken off randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: BA324 is one of the hardest/most time-intensive classes you'll take as a business major at UT. Pryor helps lessen the blow by being a caring man, a nicer grader, and a fun person to be around. I loved this class/my section with him. Remember that every point counts in this class and to ask the TA about everything because they usually know best!!!

BA324 is hard no matter who you take, but Pryor makes the class a bit more entertaining. Your grade is heavily based on your TA as well, and I got unlucky with a TA that grades extremely hard. Pryor can also be pretty vague on directions for assignments, so always clarify with him or the TA if you have any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: 324 is a rough class regardless of who you take it with. Pryor is a likable guy who seems genuinely interested in your growth as a speaker over the semester. If you don't understand an assignment don't be afraid to ask for help. Tough grader but be sure to ask for feedback after presentations and improve on them. I'd recommend him.

Pryor is a great guy (a bit obtuse, but nice nonetheless). This class is stacked with group projects and presentations, but that's true of any 324 class. He genuinely cares about you learning in the class, and he gives great feedback on your presentations. Grades are mainly determined by TA, and you'll more than likely get a B/B+ in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Grades are based a good bit on your TA, but Pryor still has a good 30-40% of your grade. Me and others feel like you could be better than most the class but still get worse grades than others. If he likes you you'll be fine, but if not, like in my case, good luck. And he doesn't round 89.93 to an A-.

Pryor is a cool guy. He doesn't give great directions, and the TA's give poor/no feedback, but he is totally interested in watching your presentation skills improve. He's pretty good about giving you a hand if you mess something up. Your grade is 80% determined by the grader you get on hw, so an A is a bit of a long shot if you get a bitter one.

Gives absolutely no direction when it comes to assignments. Pretty nice guy who is willing to work with you when it comes to grades. Easy to miss ridiculous things on assignments because of no direction. Tough class with a lot of work. Don't be afraid to speak in front of people.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: An easy class that satisfies the core writing requirement (previously writing flag, idk what they're calling it these days). Weekly assignments that can be finished quickly. She is a very understanding and accommodating professor, but lectures were quite boring and the class is not very interesting.

Avoid taking this class if you can. The majority of lectures devolve into her chatting with a few students about her politics. Constantly tries to push her own agenda, and asks loaded questions on canvas. Doesn't seem to have a very strong background in computer science and most issues discussed are generic tech issues. Lenient on late submissions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is very easy but not particularly interesting. Take if you want a simple upper div CS class.
Just take her. She's very understanding of deadlines and flexible to your needs. Just go to her classes and you're fine.

I took HDF 306 with Professor Quimby. She was very accommodating during my time in this course when it came to online vs. in-person attendance and sick days. While the concepts were certainly important, they could have been explained in 1/5th of the time. Easy class -- prepare for two simple essays total, and weekly discussions posts. You got this!

Dr. Quimby is so so kind and understanding. Lectures are interesting and she is always ready to help her students. Workload is not heavy. I would take her over and over again. Wednesdays are office hours instead of class. Take Quimby for any HDF classes.

I have nothing bad to say about Dr.Quimby! Her lectures are extremely engaging and the assignments to be completed weekly hardly feel like work and only take 30 mins to 1 hr to complete. It's important to actively participate to make the most out of this class but Dr.Quimby will never make you feel silly for speaking your mind.

Took her for HDF340. While her lectures are politically charged, she encouraged open discussion and was very honest with her own experiences. She constantly stressed the importance of mental health days and rest. We had to do a discussion post, presentation, and occasional paper per week, very low effort class but the information was invaluable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the class was easy, we often talked about her political views rather than the course content. She was a very nice woman, but I didn't feel that class was the right place to be so politically charged.
Would recommend! She's really sweet and caring and is mostly concerned with professional development. She keeps it real to allow us to develop professional skills.

Dr. Quimby has been one of the best professors I've ever had at UT. She is GREAT, and she makes this class so interesting. There's a lot of discussion posts and activities but I did not mind it at all... She is very engaging with her students, and I really appreciate her education and open-mindedness about the issues in the world today.
Go to class. She is amazing. You won't regret taking her class. She's super sweet and funny!

Quigley is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. He keeps the class fun and light while lecturing on the core pillars of journalism. Will try to take more classes with him before I graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Quigley is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable in the field of journalism, as he spent many years working as an editor and a few years as a reporter. His approach to the class is very hands-on, having groups go through the reporting process step by step. Overall, it was a fun class, and if you want to be a reporter, it will be useful!
Quigley is a great professor, and this podcasting class was definitely one of my favorites.

Quigley is an amazing professor and a gem of UT. Assignments are really straightforward as long as you follow the rubric. He also invited alumni like Pulitzer winners and reporters to give unique Q&As. There is an overarching group project with a low-stakes presentation at the end, but it's easily manageable unless you're stuck with an awful group.

Had Quigley for 301F and it was a great experience! The whole class is basically step-by-step instructions of the journalistic process with a short, low-stakes presentation at the end. He also gets some very interesting and accomplished people to give guest lectures. Overall, Quigley wants the best for his students and creates a solid foundation.

For his first time teaching 301, Professor Quigley did amazing. The homework and group projects were easy to complete and content was well taught and easy to understand, especially if you have a journalism background. Quigley is funny and kind and wants the best for his students. Choose your group wisely, you'll be working with them all semester.
Everyone should take this class if they want to be a better journalist.

You can tell he really loves his job and especially journalism. There are two big projects but they are fun to do. There were multiple guest speakers which were pretty boring. There are multiple opportunities to get a good grade. Just go to class and do your work and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was already a fan of Quigley, but I really enjoyed having him again in Editing Techniques. Attendance is a big one in this class, so make sure you are willing to go or else your grade will get docked. Highly recommend taking Quigley in a smaller class setting you can get to know him better. He really is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It was an easy class with fun projects that were actually pretty helpful. It helps you improve at video and audio. However, the lectures were boring and hard to pay attention to and he doesn't allow people to take notes on computers/ ipads/ tech. Otherwise, pretty chill.

Professor Quigley was a great lecturer and gives great feedback. He really cares about student success and you can tell is very passionate about what he teaches. If you do good work, you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved this class! It was required for me, but it was genuinely so enjoyable. The class had one group assignment, and two major assignments for digital media. The TAs graded everything but he also looked over most things. The class is ~100 people but even so, he makes a point to meet with every person.

I love Robert. This is the second class I have taken with him, but this class was more close-knit as the class size was fairly small which made me nervous at first, but he is truly one of the kindest people out there. The course was very organized and he always took in our workload into consideration. 10/10 would take again.

love love love quigley! really made me excited to major in journalism and was very inspiring! he has so much advice and experience throughout his lectures that made them super interesting. also had lots of guest speakers that offered great information as well. only two major projects that are pretty fun to do imo.
You spend more time with the TAs in lab than with Quigley himself, but he's supper approachable and willing to help, as well as the TA!

Professor Quigley is so inspiring! In a sea full of professors nodding to how journalism is no longer a viable career, Quigley gave me inspiration and new excitement for my career in journalism. His lectures are interesting and practical and there weren't many assignments for the class. I've taken another class of his and I'm really enjoying it.

I loved Professor Quigley! He's clearly super passionate about journalism, wants to connect with students and wants his students to do well. Majority of grade is an audio and video project, and they're pretty easy as long as you don't procrastinate!

Professor Quigley is one of the best professors at UT. He truly cares so much about his students and their success out of college. There are two major projects, small easy assignments, and an easy final. Everything is graded by your TA. Super easy class if you pay attention and have some type of interest in journalism.
The best professor I have had at UT so far. He is so nice and approachable. on top of that the lecture content is interesting and an easy A if you come to class.

Best professor for freshman journalism classes. Entertaining lectures, but make sure to take notes for finals based on them. Most of your grades will come from your projects, which may be tough to learn, but time management went a long way. Aside from that, just a few assignments here and there. Quigley is very supportive; I highly recommend it!!!

I loved taking this class. I learned so many new things. Attendance is graded, I missed one class and it brought down my grade. There are two main projects, a video an audio project. If you follow what he says in lecture and look at the rubric then you are good to go. Easy A. He truly cares about his students and it shows.

Your grade depends on weekly discussion posts over a few podcast episodes. Overall the class was pretty easy and entertaining. Quigley is a knowledgeable journalism professional who tries to make the class entertaining while taking the course material seriously. I recommend it to those interested in journalism, true crime, or just a fun elective!

Quigley's a really nice guy & the class had very few assignments - it's really just focused on 1 video project and 1 audio project with a few random, easy assignments throughout. The lectures are not extremely valuable. You would be fine missing every class except for that attendance is graded. Overall, you only meet for the labs 5-6 times. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind, engaging, truly an advocate for his students and wants the best for them! He actively wants to know his students, and will still stop me to say hi when he runs into me around Moody! I took 301F and then immediately took true crime podcasting! Would recommend Quigley any day of the week!
He's one of the most kind and genuine Professor's out there. I would recommend anybody to take his course!
The BEST Professor EVER!

Quigley is my favorite professor EVER! He is so inspirational, and as someone who had zero journalistic experience coming in, he is reassuring and gives amazing career and learning opportunities. This course will change your life. You must try on your two projects, and don't be afraid to ask for help. I learned more than I could have ever imagined.

I love Professor Quigley. He makes class fun and interesting. Graded on a couple main projects that he provides lots of help with. Attendance is not required but the final exam is based on what is said in lecture.

10/10 one of the best professors in Moody. He is so knowledge and teaches his class in a very interactive manner. Most of this class is project-based which is tedious but rewarding. You learn how to use new mediums and become a better journalist. Get to know Quigley outside of class, he's truly a great person to learn from.

One of the best profs in Moody. He's approachable, an inspiring lecturer and so genuine: he actually tried to learn students' names. He gave a lot of insight about the industry and had great guest lectures. My advice: go to class/lab, ask questions, don't procrastinate projects. Reach out to Quig or your TA if you're struggling--they want to help.

Quigley is the best!! Even though his class was online bc of the pandemic, Quigley made the class so much fun and enjoyable. It is mostly project-based with plenty of time to complete them and your TA is always super helpful and resourceful. I really want to take another class with him and in person!! He's such a delight and loves what he does.
Amazing professor. Definitely best professor so far at UT. Lots of projects, but as long as you complete the requirements and try, you will get an A.

Professor Quigley was great, his lectures really helped you understand journalism in order to prepare you for future classes and your career. You had to put effort in the two projects he gives out, but if you just try your best you will do fine.

Professor Quigley is by far one of the best Journalism professors at UT. His course is fairly easy and he gives multiple opportunities for you to receive extra credit to raise your grade. He has experience in the field which made class more interesting. Lots of guest lectures which I found helpful.
Loved this class!!! Quigley rocks. He makes lectures engaging and really enjoyable even on zoom. Great class and great professor! TA matters though.

Whatever class you take with Prof. Quigley, I guarantee you'll enjoy it! His classes are super interesting and he often brings cool guest speakers to interact with us. Grade is composed by attendance and a few projects (video+audio+writing+some extra credit) - but don't freak out, it's all VERY doable! TAs are INCREDIBLE! I loved this class!
The best professor at UT Austin. Period.

I enjoyed J336F SO MUCH! It was so interesting and fun. Some of the projects require a lot of work and effort but they are so interesting and fun and are worth the hard work. Professor Quigley has made this class so interesting and he teaches it so well. I feel very informed and equipped with skills for my career after taking this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Quigley was immensely understanding and helpful during the transition to online learning. His focus was on students still interacting with each other and making sure you're still learning something. Great prof/course to end UT with.

Quigley is a great professor, but the more minute aspects of the class really just depend on your TA. The lectures are good, but if you're someone who keeps up with the issues in journalism, they're pretty much common sense. The class is pretty easy, but of course, you have to put in a lot of effort into the projects.

This class was a lot of fun and you definitely learn about a lot of new media. Quigley keeps the lectures interesting and lively. You'll have to actually try on the projects to make a good grade, but also a lot of it is based on who your TA is.

i LOVE quigley. he loves to help students and he really encourages them to have fun while learning. he doesn't expect perfection, he just wants to see you trying. I got a lot out of his class & not just as a journalism major. I always looked forward to his class & i'll definitely try to take more in the future

Quigley is so passionate about what he teaches and he really knows how to keep me engaged throughout lecture. It definitely wasn't my favorite class bc it was more digital based, but he made it not feel like a chore. Attendance is mandatory and you do have to try on your projects because my TA (Jordon) graded pretty hard. Overall really great

This course is required for my major and I honestly enjoyed it. I did have a really good TA (Chenyan). The grades are pretty much 4 quizzes (super easy but you have to ready), 1 test (stupid easy), 4 assignments (1 is a partner assignment), and 2 mandatory events (boring but easy 100). I started out with a 40% on a quiz but ended with an A.
Quigley's J301 class is mandatory for the journalism program, but he honestly made me fall in love with my major a million times over. I left this class so excited to tackle the reporting class.

I loved Social Media Journalism so much!!! Im not a journalism major, so I took this course for the flags. Quigley really makes sure you know how to improve upon your communication. Aside from the Tweets and Snaps, the quizzes are easy. His class made me figure out how to make my potential business shine.
Prof. Quigley has a gift for teaching. He's very down to earth in terms of workload and grading. I had an excellent experience in his class.

This class was such a blast. Even though it was online, it was very interactive and straightforward. All the quizzes are put up at the beginning of the semester so you can do them all in a few days if you wanted, or not. Quigley is THE man, and I can't recommend a class from him enough. Very up to date on media, approachable, and helpful. Love him

Quigley is an easygoing, genuine kind of guy. He enjoys talking with students and encourages big ideas. Overall, J302 took minimal effort but you learn so much through the small projects scattered throughout the semester. 10/10, would take again.

There's minimal reading which is all posted to canvas for free. He's very funny and personable. Genuinely cares about students and their future. There are a couple big projects but they weigh very little so it's more about the learning experience than it is about failing you. I would take him again without a doubt. One of the best professors at UT
Not many words needed rather that Quigley is the BEST professor at UT Austin.

I loved going to this class. Quigley and RB are wonderful. They are passionate and they know what they're talking about. I only had a problem with the group work because sometimes my partners would be flaky. Overall, I loved this class, it opens up a lot of perspectives in the field.

I loved taking Digital Storytelling! Quigley was always so funny, and he inspired me to look to different options for myself after I graduate. He opened up a whole new world of journalism for me. The class itself was easy, just make sure to go to labs. The TA's are flexible if you have an honest reason though.

Quigley knows his stuff! I had him for Digital Storytelling Basics, and he's very clear on instructions, and is very approachable when asking questions. A lot of the grades in the class are dependent on if you showed up to your lab days, however.  Show up and pay attention in class and labs, and you'll be fine! I really enjoyed this class!! 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lecture are clear and he talks about his anecdotes as examples for class. He is also nice to talk to and patient to explain concepts for students. Love him! Would def take this class again.

If you are ready to learn beyond the text of social media journalism, take this class! Get ready to work virtually as a social media journalist on the course's different accounts. I had a blast.  It is easy to get an A if you put the effort and heart into the work. I am not even a journalism major and this class was greatly beneficial.

Lectures are quick & interesting. No homework. 1 group project. 2 tests. No final! Need to read assigned reading (all articles) & go to class to do good on tests (which aren't hard if you do that). Loved this class & Quigley! Knows his stuff!
You can get an A in here pretty easily, but you have to do the work.  It's an interesting class, and I learned a lot.

Quigley taught this fully-online social media journalism class (J336). It was probably the easiest class I've ever taken at UT. You just have to tweet and use other social media platforms (Tumblr, etc.) to talk about news. There's an essay at the end (super easy). That's about it. Kind of impossible to NOT get an A in this class.

I found Lili's lectures very inspiring. It really highlighted how essential wireless is during the age of AI. The breadth of topics she covers went well beyond what I expected. Thanks to her engaging teaching, I've developed strong interest in wireless.
Lili is a fantastic professor. She is very knowledgeable, and her lectures are thought-provoking. I learned a lot from her. She is genuinely caring toward her students.

Professor Qiu was accommodating and willing to adjust her teaching to class feedback, but there was still way too much material covered. The tests were unfairly difficult, and as a result, the final grades were curved. I didn't end up learning much since none of it sunk in because of the rapid pace.

Worst professor I had in UT by far. People would regularly fail quizzes and homework. Test was insane with most people failing it. She didn't curve. Instead she gave a make up exam that was harder than the actual exam. She would go through 100 slides in one day or two if you were lucky. She was a nice person though, but the class itself was hard.

Prof Qui is a very very knowledgable person who knows a ton about networks. However, this means that she skims over a ton of material (80+ slides) every class and expects students to understand it. The lectures are dry and the tests were unexpectedly hard. She gives a ton of extra credit though. You learn a LOT in the class but its hard work!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hard exam, tough grading. Lectures is so boring that 90% class is not listening at all, people attend class just for the quiz. If you want to learn something don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible lectures, just read over 100+ slide every class and barley explain anything.

Qiu is a kind professor but the class is somewhat hard mainly because of her tests. She put hard problems that you never seen in HW or other places on tests so be prepared for that (still within the material though). Unlike other professors she tells you when you'll get a quiz to make you study. No textbook but lots of stuff in slides to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Personally I think the prof is very generous. Like someone said she will reschedule a few lectures that she can't attend, but attendance is never mandatory so it's your choice. Also, she ended up starting the test that person mentioned at 9am instead of 8:45 and extended the test for a total of extra 75 min! I justcan't complain more about the prof

Decent professor but bad with logistics; she tends to reschedule any lectures she can't make, and she will make you come early/stay later on test days. I didn't appreciate that she made the Final start at 8:45AM instead of the normal class time (9:30AM). There's a lot of material but she gives you tons of cheat sheets for the exams. Not too bad.

Qiu is a great professor. Her accent is definitely there, but not enough to detract from understanding (unless perhaps if you sit at the far back). Furthermore, she genuinely takes an interest in the class, promotes class discussion and participation, and makes sense of the material. She's an excellent professor.
Very thick accent
No Comments
You might never meet the actual professor so your grade depends on the TA's and LA's. The presentation is easy but we have a final exam for excel now??
she doesn't do anything the TA does everything. So disorganized and she doesn't care. Worse lab at UT
This is a very boring lab that is mostly dependent on the TA

i mean you'll live... probably the most annoying and boring class ever but there's no way you'll fail chem lab lmfao. just do not sign up for an 8:30 or a 4-6 it'll be the bane of ur existence (arguably it might be no matter when you have it!)

Chem Lab felt like the longest two hours of my life every week. its not hard at all just so boring and tedious it felt like i was losing braincells but its required for so many science majors so... sorry just be ready for the worst 2 hours ever.

the class is run by TAs, but i had great TAs (caroline for dry lab and hanlin for wet lab) and my lab group was great. the class was very easy and gives you very good, basic lab skills. any time i emailed dr. sotelo via canvas messages, she responded very quickly and was very helpful and caring. the makeup labs are also very accessible. easy a+

The professor communicates through weekly announcements and office hours. The lab experience involves working closely with wet and dry lab TAs. My TAs provided clear feedback on assignments. Pod group dynamics can influence the overall experience.

Echoing others: your experience depends on what TA's and group you get. On the whole however, dry labs were super boring while wet labs were quite fun. Always opportunities to resubmit, so there is no reason you can't get an A in the class. Definitely a learning curve with all the documents you have to submit during Dry lab, but you'll get it quick
Never saw the Prof. I had great TAs, Cristobal and Claire and also a great table group which made the class breezy. The TAS did a great job walking us through the dry and wet labs.

You will never see Dr. Sotelo. The class is just the TAs running it, you have 1 for dry and 1 for wet lab. Both of were very fair in grading. They were Nicolas D'Annunzio and Rinnish, very glad that they were alright.

Class is run by TAs, so you just have to hope you get a good one. My dry lab and wet lab TAs constantly contradicted each other and made the class way harder than it needed to be, also it's all group work, so you need to hope you get a good group. You get one redo on every assignment, so it should be an easy 100, but it felt like a waste of time.

Never met her before, so lab is ran completely by TAs. Dry lab was annoying the way that you had to sit around and listen to info being read off of slides, but wet lab was great for me. Your experience really depends on the TA you get.

We never actually met Dr. Sotelo; everything is run by the TAs and your lab experience completely depends on what TA and lab pod you get. The work isn't hard and you get the chance to fix any worksheet mistakes for full credit. Lab makeup is a pain so attendance is basically required
I don't know who the professor it, but TA's grade the whole class. If you have good TA's then the class is good. Dry lab gets annoying, but it was fun overall. I loved my TA's

I don't even know who the "professor" was but I do know that chem lab is annoying af. Dry lab is confusing but you'll make it through, wet lab as well. I think it's pretty TA and pod dependant which sucks. You'll be fine just stay on task, theres little outside of class work, just communicate with your pod and ask the TA's questions.

Experience dependent on TA for dry and wet lab. Guaranteed A if you turn in work, you get feedback and then can resubmit for new grade. Most work is done by group so I got stuck with more than my share but it still wasn't much work. Final project is individually graded group assignment and basically participation grade if you meet requirements.

Lab ran completely by the TA, so your experience in the class will differ from others. I liked my TA, but he was a tough grader. The good thing is that you can resubmit the lab worksheets for a regrade up to a 100, so definitely take the feedback and improve. Easy A, but turn in your work EARLY and be on top of everything.

Lwk this class really depends on your TAs, never met the professor. This class was very boring, but an easy A+. The TAs that I got this year were chill. I came late to wet lab one time and they said I could just say I was sick to get an excuse redo the lab.
so boring but an easy A, shout out prith!

Easy A+ no matter what TA you get you just have to do the worksheets which take max 30 mins. My TA had a thickest accent and made lab very hectic at times. You have outside class time to finish worksheets and the TA's are lenient. Guarantied A+ as long as you do some work.
Attendance is required and you are randomly put in a pod that you will work with for the entire semester. Really easy A as long as you do your work and show up on time.
never actually met the professor. ur grade was entirely based on the ta, and while mine was chill, some of my friends had horrible experiences. the actual labs were pretty mid.
Extremely easy lab run entirely by TAs, can resubmit all assignments for full credit.

You never interact with the professor, and your success in the class is completely dependent on who your TA is. In general, the dry lab portions serve as a really boring setup towards wet lab, which can be more interesting as it covers what you're currently learning in CH301. Overall easy if you get your work done, but can be a boring two hours.

Absolute easiest lab to ever exist, but beware of Erich. He is a TA that oversees the other TA. Since Dr. Sotelo doesn't know how to make decisions herself, she actually asks Erich what to do if you go up to her. She also walked into class and started saying she didn't even like her own TA in the back. Very unprofessional behavior.

Very TA dependent. Grading criteria can be all or nothing, but you can resubmit worksheets once in the week after submission. Also depends on how proactive your pod group is. Not too difficult, but a lot of work. Attendance is also mandatory, esp on lab days!
Extremely easy to get an A, because all assignments can be resubmitted for full credit. Barely any time commitment outside of the lab. However, your enjoyment is completely TA-dependent.

Class entirely run by TAs. While yes everyone is right you just kinda have to pray you get good TAs/LAs and pod members it's also really hard not to get an A in this class. Resubmissions and makeups are given out like candy. Dry lab can be a snoozefest but it's a very easy course so don't worry :)

Never actually met her, the labs are run by TAs. For dry lab, Maddie is the best. She's very excited and you can tell she cares. If you get Muhammad for wet lab, GOOD LUCK. He grades harshly and late and is poor at explaining. Lab is easy and thank god you can resubmit. Hopefully your lab partners aren't dummies because you're stuck with them.

entirely TA led so hope that you get good ones!
very easy; if you mess up a lab report, you can resubmit for full credit. the lab reports are also pretty easy. class itself moves quickly, but you don't have to worry about much homework or anything. just hope that you get a good group/TA!

This class is completely led by TAs and LAs (shout out tyler and zachary). Literally easiest class ever, you just do assignments and one paper at the end of the semester. You can also redo all the assignments up to an A. Attendance is mandatory so choose a time where you will actually show up on time.
Labs are led by TA's. Probably will never meet Sotelo. You are also placed into a random pod, but as long as you guys work together it should be fine.
The professor is not present, the class is run solely by TAs. The class is incredibly boring and the grading system is weird however it is not difficult to do well in the class.

How this class goes depends on your TA, but you can't choose so it's pure luck. Overall, the class is boring and feels like it lasts an eternity but not hard. It all comes down to your TA or pod members but you can't chose either. So how it goes is 50/50.

I hoped I would get insanely injured, just so I had a chance not to show up to this lab. Professor is fine it was just the TAs. My TA was honestly so lost and would tell us to do something, but later would yell at us for doing the thing she told us to do. TA and coordinator just contradict each other's words and left students confused most times.
Literally easiest class you will take, it's difficult to not get an A. All just worksheets, Excel, and one final project. Overall boring, but as long as your group does your work, you'll get an A.

Chemistry lab is better than it used to be (1 4-hour lab each week rather than 2 separate courses). It's pretty easy but can be frustrating, sometimes the experiment instructions conflict with what the TA says. A lot of the dry labs felt like busywork. If you get a good group you'll do fine

Lab is completely run by the TAs so your experience will depend on that not Dr. Sotelo. 104M is split into dry and wet lab and were two hours long (felt like atleast three). They try to cram too much into the two hour dry/wet lab period every week.

Easy to get an A. Lab is run by the TAs. TA in 104M was a saint. TA in 104N was also good. Enjoyment depends on your lab partners. 104M was torture but 104N was great. Overall, it's boring (duh), but it's not the worst. Meet once a week, stay on top of your quizzes/assignments and you're fine.

Grade purely depends on TA. Sotelo isn't even there. I'm rating this higher that I would purely because I had great TAs and decent groups. If you get someone that's a bad labmate, just report it and don't put up with it. It's your grade, do what you must.

Really depends on your pod members and TA but I have lucked out for both. My TA was so chill and let us out an hour early like every time. If you do the work you will get a 100 in the class because they are only allowed to give you a 100, 50 or 0 on the assignment. And if you don't get a 100 you can retry one time

This lab depends on the TA and LA you get. My dry lab TA was okay, but the LAs were sweet and approachable. My wet lab TA was super sweet and very forgiving. She also made the experiments easy to complete and did some experiments herself so the lab could end early.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really just based on your TA, but the TAs all seem chill. You also get two attempts on every assignment in case you make a mistake the first time. This is an easy A, just show up to everything and turn all the assignments in.
You'll get an A as long as you show up to everything and do all the work. Mostly based on your TA, but most of them seem to be really nice.
It all depends on your TA
TAs are not helpful in dry lab and very frustrating

The class is run by TAs, and thankfully, my TA was awesome. It's very hard to actually get in touch with her and often times, there were miscommunications. It all felt very removed. She was the only prof running labs for sp25, so of course I had to take her again, but if I could've chosen otherwise, I would've.
No prof just TA's. Wet and dry labs were pretty easy this is def a GPA booster. Please be best friends with your group members I was so scared of them but guess who got a better grade ayee
The lab reports can be a real grind, but with the help of unstuck AI and a good TA, you'll be just fine. Try to get a partner you work well with - it makes all the difference.

You will never meet Dr. Sotelo as the class is TA led. Thankfully my TA was really easy on grading and my group was not that bad. If this isn't the case for you though the class will be a huge pain. Dry labs were simple and straight copy paste and the wet labs were fun to do. Group paper at the end was also graded easily.

I loved the CH104M/N design. No long lab reports or practicals, all work is essentially done during the dry/wet lab classes. You are grouped with 3 other students and assigned a TA for wet lab who essentially does all your grading. If you get a good group, this class will be no stress at all. Final paper at the end of the semester b/n the 4 ppl.

This class is run by the TAs. My dry lab TA was rude and condescending and ruined the class for most students. Dry lab is fast paced and just overall stressful but wet lab was fun depending on your TA. The way the canvas is organized is almost enraging and so confusing. A lot of easy but busy busy work.

Class is lead by TAs so unless you directly reach out to her or one of the TAs reach out to her about a concern, you'll almost never meet her. My TA happened to be an extremly sweet woman who was lenient on grading, but your class grade mainly depends on if you have good Lab Partners and a nice TA. If your lab partners are slacking, do report.

It all depends on who your TA is and if you get lucky with a good lab group. Dry Labs are so easy (just copying straight from the screen), but wet labs were my least favorite part of the week (specifically because of my TA who was such a picky grader). It's a required class that you should get an A for completing everything, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dry labs were stressful and Wet lab was fun. Dry labs were run with a video playing with overelaborate instructions and not enough time. Wet lab was fun and always look difficult at first but always ends up not being hard. Beginning the class was hard as navigating th canvas pages was difficult, but you'll get used to it. All TA ran.

The classes are split between "dry" labs and "wet" labs. Dry labs are annoying because you have to submit 3+ worksheets during the class and follow a million instructions at a quick pace. Besides that, there's barely any HW -- If you have good lab partners, you should be able to finish everything during class. Also, you can resubmit assignments.

It's a pretty straightforward class. If you do your part in lab, you should be fine. Just pray you get good lab partners. If you have any issues with your lab partners, make sure to tell a TA, that way it won't hurt your grade. Also, if you get half credit on something, you're allowed one resubmission for full credit.
it all depends on your TA and lab partners. the work itself isn't hard and you can resubmit for a better grade

Your experience depends on your TA's and your lab group. The dry labs are often confusing and move fast, but the actual work isn't that hard. The wet labs are very clear. The group paper at the end of the semester is a lot of work but in my experience wasn't graded harshly at all. There are resubmissions for regrading, and attendance is mandatory.

VERY dependent on which TA you get & the lab group you randomly get placed in. Some TA's are strict & plain rude (happened to me & I reported it & he straightened up) & some don't even care & give you answers to the post-lab & give 100's on everything. Really depends on your luck. If your group is making you do all the work too, report that.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your experience in this class is entirely dependent on your TAs and your lab group! Some of the Dry Lab lectures went way too quickly. There are many opportunities to redo your assignments and the worksheets are fairly easy and should be submitted during lab. As long as you show up and finish your work, you should be able to get an A!

I loved what they did with the Gen Chem labs this semester. Most of the work is done within the span of the lab itself, so there's not much to do outside of class. There are a total of 6 labs, all of which were very interesting to explore in Wet Lab. Most labs coincide with units in CH301. I had a lot of fun in this class!

This course is heavily TA-oriented and you will only see the professor through pre-recorded videos. Labs were pretty easy and easily graded, you got re-dos on assignments to get full credit. You pretty much have to luck out and hope you get a good TA and lab group.

literally never saw the professor more than twice throughout the semester. this class was entirely TA-led, luckily both my dry and wet lab TAs were awesome and easy graders; you are able to redo assignments and resubmit for full credit. there is a final paper at end of semester, but it is a group effort, so it really wasn't stressful at all.
Completely TA led. Grading is harsh but there are lots of opportunities to correct what you have done. Pray that you have a good TA
The course was very disorganized, which is expected since it is newer. To succeed you need to have a good TA and a good lab group.

i took her fall lab and I registered for her again for spring 25 because I loved everything. i never actually saw her in person which is interesting, it's all TA-led. if you make 1 mistake its a 50% but you can always redo it and get a 100%, super easy. you need to talk to the dry/wet lab TAs and ask them to check over your pre/post lab worksheet

This class is ludicrously easy. Everything is pass/fail and you can resubmit every assignment for full credit if you miss it the first time. You'll have in-class worksheets for every dry/wet lab, but otherwise the only thing you'll have to work on outside of class might be your end of semester scientific paper. Entirely TA led/run.

It might just have been a TA thing, but the lab write ups were graded exceptionally harshly. I lost points for misspelling the TA's last name. Class is fun, but the work is time consuming. Good choice if you have to take the lab otherwise don't.

Yeah, you'll probably get an A...but is it worth it? NO. This class took up SO much of my time, lab reports are 15+ pages long. It's ridiculous for a general chemistry lab. You'll learn a lot, but the amount of work is extremely unnecessary. In the end, you'll do fine if you work hard and pay attention. It'll make you question your sanity, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I never met Dr. Sotelo, but I was blessed to have a great TA (Imon), and your chem lab experience depends almost entirely on your TA. Get to know your TA, and make sure you like your lab partner as you'll be working with them a lot. Start as soon as you can on lab reports. Not hard, just genuinely such a time consuming course. Very doable though.

Didn't see the prof once all sem but duh it's a TA led lab. I loved my TA (Sridhar Markand), he's hilarious and helpful. Do not procrastinate on the labs it will come back to bite you and make sure to put good effort into the lab reports. If you can, choose your partner carefully as they will decide whether or not you leave lab at 7 or 8:30.

Idc about Sotelo, literally never saw her. Your lab experience is dependent entirely on your TA and thank god mine was awesome (my goat, Yang, he rocks!!). this class had so much useless busy work tho (prelab flow chart, quiz, assignment). lab reports are time consuming. this class is def a grind, so just pray you get a good TA.

Didn't speak/hear from the professor all semester, which led to this rating of them. The assignments before lab were tedious and time consuming, about 1.5 hours. The lab reports after lab took even longer. This class had so much "busy" work that it made it not fun and made my lab class count the days until it was over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor is laughable, did absolutely nothing for the class. Was out for maternity leave and didn't affect class whatsoever. Only have to attend 8/10 labs, practicle is easy depending on which lab you get, which is random. Difficulty of lab reports depends solely on your TA, mine was amazing and super helpful, but heard others graded very hard.
Your grade depends a lot on if your TA is a nice grader! Mine was really good so it made the papers less annoying, but they were still very long. The experiments are easy though.

when I saw this class is TA dependent, BELIEVE MEEE. I took so much time on the lab reports each week and saw the light come back to my life after this course was over. I was lucky enough to have a great TA who wasn't that harsh a grader, but had friends who didn't. Either way, it just took so much time. Not worth all that work for a gen chem lab.
I imagine, like most labs, it depends largely on your TA. There are 10 labs and you can drop 2, but the reports are very time-consuming. Still, if you put in the work, it's a straightforward A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had an amazing TA for Gen Chem lab, so my experience in this lab was great. Everything depends on your TA. I never saw the professor even once. The lab reports are tedious and take up a lot of time, so try to get in the habit of starting them early. Practical and lab overall were easy. As long as you stay on top of your work, it's an easy A.

You only interact with your TA which range from very easy to very difficult graders. Lab reports are tedious and take hours but labs are relatively easy. Online pre-lab quizzes are graded strictly and the lab practical at the end of the semester is the only real difficult assignment requiring memorization of all the labs. Overall an easy A!

the lab is not as hard as it seems. just a lot of busy work that is so tedious that they nitpick about. however, they drop two lab reports, two in-lab performance points, two pre-lab quizzes and two pre-lab assignments. plenty of extra credit options provided. this course is getting revamped, so it may be different in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very organized and you'll learn relevant lab techniques. Get to know your TA and labmates to get through experiments. Grades are TA dependent, but there is a mechanism in place that ensures that grade distributions are consistent. The main con is the sheer volume of work (prelabs, quizzes, reports), but this may be mitigated as 204 splits in two.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Was reviewing 204 but remembered it's being split into two classes, so I'm just going to try giving some general chem lab advice. Start your lab reports early, they're not difficult per se but they take FOREVER. Use your drops well, skip strategically! This class is tedious but can still be fun; to that end, get to know your lab partner and TA!!

Your grade in this class completely depends on your TA. I know some TAs were very lenient in their grading and some were extremely tough. You will spend around 5-10 hours a week on this class so prepare wisely. Pre lab assignments, and lab reports take a huge chunk of time.

TA dependent, mine took off points for the smallest things. LRs will take you hours to finish & prelab assignments were so time consuming. Rules in lab are very strict, some experiments will take you the entire 4 hrs, and overall an annoying class bc of all the busy work.

Your grade largely depends on your TA, but my TA wanted to be nice and Dr. Sotelo said their averages were too high and to take off more points. The rules in lab are also very strict so make sure you don't accidentally have your ankles showing one day or you may have to put on foot coverings. The lab reports take a long time so don't put them off
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: dont take chem lab unless u have to for ur major. too much unnecessary work for GEN CHEM LAB. talked to my other friends at diff colleges none do this much work for GEN CHEM LAB so tedious. ur TA makes ur grade so if u have a bad TA idk what to tell u I had Ovie who was harsh grader at first but then chilled out love her sm, hated this class sm

Your grade is determined by your TA, as you never see Dr. Potelo. Luckily, I had Ovie who was so accessible (would answer my emails at 3 am) and nice! The lab reports do take a lot of time and I wouldn't choose the monday lab (you'll prob spend the weekend working on the report if you procrastinate). Just ask your TA for help and it's an easy A.

lots of drops and boosts so an A is def doable. my ta was very lax but there were plenty of resources made accessible to help you. however, this class is insanely time consuming and nit-picky for no reason.

Chem lab isn't hard but it's time consuming. It's best if you have a helpful and accessible TA. You only have to go to the very first lecture and that's it for the whole semester. Lab practical was easy and not a large part of your grade. Lots of pre lab stuff but just read through the lab manual and lecture slides beforehand and you'll be fine.

Class was very time consuming but if you put in the work you can get an A. My TA was very accessible in and outside of class. Lab practical was extremely easy and a grade booster. Definetly depends on the TA but you can ask them question for lab reports. Start lab reports at least 3 days before or you will fall behind.

The class's experiments are relatively easy to do, but the lab reports take a lot of time during the week. However, the class is pretty standard and very affected by whoever your TA is. Mine was fair and pretty nice, but I did struggle in this class to get everything right. My advice is to follow the posted guidelines to the T for the best score.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor herself was rarely in lab but was very kind during office hours. My TA was amazing and so helpful during lab. The lab reports are not too bad but try not to procrastinate!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Sotelo structured the class to be a lot of work but consistent and manageable. There are two drops for every assignment so it's possible to get the grade you want. Honestly though your TA does all the grading and instruction so the experience you have in lab is up to them. The structure overall is a lot of work but not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class really depends on your TA. I think I talked to Sotelo once throughout the semester. My TA was great which made the course easier, but I've heard of people who had terrible TAs and didn't do well.

I only saw Dr. Sotelo two times the whole semester. You will spend all of your time in and out of class with your TA. The TA that you have definitely determines your grade and enjoyment of the course. I had Changhyun as my TA and he was the BEST. Lab time is fun, but the post-lab reports are extensive and sometimes difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class had a lot of work for the Lab Reports and Pre-Lab assignments, but it was very rewarding in the end. Grade drops in each category and extra credit on lab reports made this class very manageable despite the amount of work. Some lab reports were math heavy, but it helped if you went to TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I saw the prof maybe once. ALL TA-based. The labs/pre-lab stuff isn't too difficult, but the lab reports are graded *very* specifically and the grading criteria is not made known unless you travel to office hours, where 10+ students are all trying to ask questions to 1 TA. Points off for stupid things. Somewhat easy A tho just time consuming.
All grading is completed by the TA you're assigned. I had a TA who taught well and graded decently easily so I recommend this course simply because that was my experience.

Easy A, go to your TAs office hrs and ask for help on your lab report cuz you get get stupid points taken off. Lots of bonus points given. Lab practical is mandatory but easy (only worth 3% so it doesn't matter). Labs are easy, reports can be time consuming but you have a whole week to do it and can drop two (hint: just skip titrations).

Amazing class depending on your TA, saw professor once so this review 100% reflects the TA lol. If you get Xinyi wu she is a nice grader, very understanding and has amazing earrings. The labs never really took 4 hours unless you messed up. DO NOT DO LAB REPORTS DAY OF. Lab reports take about 2 days generally, there are plenty of drops :)

My TA was kinda picky but I still managed to do well. The experiments were easy-ish and I got to leave early most of the time. You don't have to go to the lectures bc they're now during the actual lab time so that was nice. There's some EC and they drop low grades so its not hard to get an A, just takes a lot of time (especially the reports).

bad rap for no reason--lab reports fairly easy as long as you have a general understanding of ch301 concepts. grading depends on your TA, but mine was easy on us and accessible. Only saw dr. sotelo twice throughout the semester. lab reports are easy but prepare to spend 4-6 hrs a week on this class

This class is excellent if you get a good TA! There is a lot of work but it is manageable if you don't procrastinate. Schedule the class so that the day before isn't too busy because you'll be writing your lab reports the night before. Use your extensions but it's a fun and exciting class if you put in a few hours a week! The practical is easy too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I only saw her on the only lab lecture and never again. The class is so incredibly easy as long as you do eight out of the ten labs and spend time on the assignments. The prelab, quizzes, and lab reports will take up a TON of time but they are not hard. I loved my TA and she was very friendly, responsive to canvas messages, and super fair on grades

Your experience in CH 204 depends on your TA. I saw Dr. Sotelo twice during my semester. My experience was not very good because my TA was a stricter grader. Laboratory experiments were very tedious and each one related to a general chemistry concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had the best TA, so it was easy to ask questions or advice on lab reports. There's a prelab, quiz, and lab report due every week, w/ 2 drops in every category. Grade was mainly from reports, but you have a clear outline of how to write the reports, so they're just time consuming. Your grade is really just based on your TA.

CH204 grade is dictated by your TA. Pre-lab procedure, quiz, and last lab report due weekly. It isn't hard work but it is tedious. Expect to spend a good amount of time on this class. Grades are mostly straight forward. They release tips for reports, so use them and you'll do fine. Lots of drops and lots of extra credit. Ended with a high A.
Class is dependent on TA. There is a lab report and pre-lab every week which can be overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work, and you need to put in effort. It also depends on your TA and their grading. I showed up to every lab and turned in every assignment, BUT you do get 2 drops for lab reports, pre-labs, and quizzes, which is really nice. Sotelo does communicate weekly and sends out information. It was satisfying to complete this class.

mostly graded by TA; go to TA office hours for help; sotelo is caring about absences just reach out 2-3 weeks in advance. keep on top of lab reports. hardest is the third lab, so get ready to drop that one. kinetics and first lab report are easy. overall pretty easy class as long as you show up on time and are on top of it.

Overall, chem lab was not bad. The labs themselves were average, but the reports are quite lengthy. There is a LOT of homework and busy work to do. But, making an A is achievable. Just make sure to get to lab on time and take a few days to do the reports and you will be fine. There is really only one professor for this class, but a lot of TA's.

Professor Sotelo had no direct affect on any aspect of the course. Everything is fully dependent on the TA: taught by the TA, graded by the TA, etc. The pre-lab is unnecessary and time consuming, but the labs themselves were easy to follow and interesting to participate in. The reports are long, so give yourself plenty of time to do them.

This class depends on your TA, but I really liked this class because the assignments are more time consuming than difficult. If you work timely and use the drops and extensions that are given, it's really easy. Try to have the lab on a day you're not busy during because you'll be doing your assignment either the day before or the day of.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is very manageable once you get the hang of the weekly requirements. If you plan to do the same assignment on the same day every week, it isn't overwhelming. Grade is mostly made of pre-lab quizzes and lab reports. You get two drops for every assignment as well. Grade is also totally based on the TA you get, as they grade everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is completely TA dependent. You have little interaction with the Sotelo as everything in the course is given, taught, and graded by your TA. The pre-labs and lab reports can take a long time to complete, but you get used to it. Be sure to have/make good lab partners that you work well with cause you can all struggle together.

It all depends on what TA you have and how they grade the lab reports. Going to the TA office hours are super beneficial and are very helpful if and when you have questions regarding the labs and the lab reports.

took chem 204. Terrible class with no organization or guidance, grade depends on TA which is so unfair, some of my friends wrote terrible reports and got full credit, but i had a strict TA so i got points decked off for minor things. very unfair and hw heavy class. wish i did not have to take it.

100% depends on your TA. Unfortunately, that's how this class is, but I can say most of my friends had good TA's, so this class wasn't hard. Try your best to get a 100 on the safety quizzes and prelab quizzes bc this is the easiest part of the class. Go to office hours for your TA if possible because honestly they are looking for different things.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your experience will mostly depend on the TA you get. Mine was very nice and graded fairly, so my experience was pretty good. Lab reports were long but the experiments in the lab were pretty short most days (leaving class 1-2 hours early).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CH 204 was an easy lab class depending on the TA. My TA wasn't great, but Dr. Sotelo was always available by email and she is very approachable before/after lectures. I was able to resolve many issues with my TA with Dr. Sotelo. She is very supportive of her students and is very open to TA feedback, so make sure to speak up.

Dr. Sotelo's class was okay. Students didn't really get to interact with her, as all of the grading was based on your TA. It was a lot of work, the lab reports were not difficult but took a ton of time to do. All the labs were relatively short (except the titration labs), and you could leave as soon as you were done. There is an extension policy.

Everything was based on the TA, and luckily, mine graded pretty easily and was always available for questions. The workload is extremely heavy with a prelab, quiz, procedure, and a report due every week. The reports themselves aren't hard but take several hours. Lab itself only takes 2-2.5 hours tops since they're not that difficult.

You never see Dr. Sotelo but you really don't need to. The class is as easy as your TA makes it. It's quite a bit of work with weekly assignments but even people with tough TA's did just fine after figuring out what they were looking for. Go to office hours when doing your reports. It helps.

The class is a drag, but not as bad as I was expecting. Try to gauge the expectations for reports/assignments as early as possible, and befriend your lab partner. Almost no one attends pre-lab lecture as the semester goes on--you don't need it for the pre-lab quiz (just Sotelo's lecture slides).

I never once interacted with Dr. Sotelo and you don't have to. This class 100% depends on your TA, but even if you get a TA that grades harshly, an A in the class should still be pretty easy. The labs are easy, but the reports definitely take a long time if you wanna get a good grade on them, so be ready to spend a lot of time working on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You won't ever Dr. Sotelo, the class is run by TA's so it is HIGHLY TA dependent on your experience. The labs last 1.5-2 hours each and a lengthy report is given to follow them up. The reports are not bad you just need to manage your time well to complete them. A pre-lab assignment and quiz are due each week before lab but those are quick and easy
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pre-lab lectures were not very helpful (imo). Grade is entirely dependent upon your TA. CH 204 is not hard, but it is tedious and time-consuming. It should be a relatively easy A as long as you put in the work. Probably interacted with Sotelo once so I wouldn't worry about the reviews here. Just befriend your TA, work hard, and you'll be fine!

Sotelo was only around for the lectures. Your grade depends on the TA and how strict they grade the lab reports, which I spent around 5 hrs on every week. Be prepared to put lots of time into this class because you can't just bs the prelabs, quizzes, and reports. Would definitely not recommend taking other labs with this course.

It is extremely unfortunate that professor sotelo is the only one who teaches CH204. This class is really dependent on your TA. You will most likely never really meet Dr. Sotelo, however if you do attend a meeting with her she is extremely rude, unhelpful and very impolite towards students.

I did not did well in the class but Dr. Sotelo gave me a lot opportunities to improve as we move in the semester. Always contact her to discuss your case she handle a very large class and it is hard for her to take care of everything.

I had a very difficult time in the semester but Dr. Sotelo was pretty helpful and offered extra office hours to help me to catch up with lab reports. TAs was not that good but if you attend to her office hours you will get anything you need for success in the class
Dr. Sotelo is very understable person. She takes care of TAs and students and try to do her best to fit avery student concern.

Professor Sotelo is not an understanding person never interacts with students. The entire class is TA-based, I dropped the class because my TA was awful and when I took it the next semester I got an amazing TA, so I feel like it's not really a fair class. The workload is overwhelming, but manageable, unless you are also enrolled in another lab

Since this course is lab based you don't interact with the professor(Sotelo), but rather your TA, who is also responsible for grading everything. The little interaction I did have with her wasn't very positive and she was not an understanding professor. I almost had to come to class despite being very sick and she almost didn't let me makeup a lab.

To be honest I never ever saw this professor. Grading depends on your TA so you have to hope you get a good one. It's not that bad but its a LOT of work. There are lots of little points that the TAs can take off for. Was not my favorite class but it was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gen chem lab was okay. Most of the labs were pretty basic and boring. Lots of work for a 2 hour course (pre lab assignment, pre lab quiz, write procedure, lab writeup). Grade / experience is completely determined by your TA, so good luck. Overall not too bad. If you put in the effort you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: The amount of tedious work in this class is excessive & patronizing, and it didn't even line up properly with CH302's subject material to make the lab as meaningful as possible. (The TA does literally all the work/is the only person you see.) The professor is also unforgiving with deadlines to an absurd degree. Love the subject, just not her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: sotelo had vids where she just spoke over a ppt for each lab, so i cant say much about her. the class was hybrid and i enjoyed the in person labs a lot. my ta gabriella was the Real hero! i woke up late twice (9am labs) but she still let me come in and then even made my solutions for me so i wouldnt fall too behind. youd be lucky to have her.

I can definitely see why people are upset as this class did have a pretty heavy workload. Definitely worked hours on a lab write up before. But I went to office hours and had a very fair TA so I had a good experience in this class as long as I put in the work. Also learned a lot and the copper experiment was cool

This class isn't as horrible as the reviews make it out to be. It is a heavy workload, though. Every week a lab report, pre-lab, and lab quiz are due. Just be sure to stay on top of things. TA's do grade everything, and they can be tough graders. However, just follow the rubric for reports and you'll do just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: havent seen her all year, ta's did everything. all ta dependent. you can get a b- if you try pretty hard, an A- is nearly impossible. the lab reports are really tough and average was under a 50, everything else is a free 100. you get 2 drops so you can get a passing grade easily and a b- if you tryhard.

This class was awful. Saw the teacher maybe once and she was very rude. The amount of work was ridiculous. UT labs are the worst, and she did not make it any better. I ended up switching to pass/fail because I didn't want to spend 5 hours on lab reports anymore. I still ended up with a 91 so if you put in the work you can get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class had an excessive workload given it was only 2 credit hours. The lab reports take many hours to write, so start early. The quizzes are easy though, so they will help your grade. I had no contact with Sotelo herself, only one zoom meeting. The only instructor you will see is the TA for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: This lab isn't as bad as people make it seem, but it's so. much. work. for only 2 credit hours. Grading is all based on your TA, and they vary in their preferences greatly. Some are a lot tougher than others. Worksheets take forever and don't bother watching her lectures, they're impossible to understand. The pre-labs and quizzes are easy, though.

Grade based on TA. Class was so much work considering it's only a 2 credit hr course. I no doubt spent more time on work in this class compared to my other classes. 1 lab a week and the pre/post lab took 4hrs plus every time. The in person experiments weren't bad, it's just the work for the labs that is so unnecessarily long.

Grading depends on your TA. Work load is insane for a 2 credit hour course. The actual chemistry part is easy, but with the amount of writing and formatting can result in loss of points for tiny errors, which is ridiculous. I feel like they should focus on us understanding the chemistry rather than cramming a bunch of experiments in 1 lab session.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class in spring 2021 as a hybrid. Class is only worth 2 hours of credit but more time consuming than my 3 hour classes. If it weren't for the winter storm and 2 COVID lab drops, I would not have had an A. Save drops till end. Video lectures are hard to understand, don't waste your time watching them if you took CH 301/302, use slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really easy class. One lab per week and workload was about 6 hours per week. Its definitely not as bad as these reviews are. Just show up to lab and do all the work. Dont watch recorded lectures theyre useless
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible horrible class. Worst class I took by a mile (I hated this class more than Ochem as a pre-med). So much work for no reason. It's the same content as CH 302 but just with a ton of busywork mixed in. I got a good TA but just a horrible class that consumes at least 6 extra hours a week. I would say don't take the class but it's required sooo
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I recommend not to have a job when taking 17 hours with a lab because the reports and assignments take time. If you have a job, please take 14 or 15 hours because labs will drain you, and I want you learn the content because it's not that bad. Labs are straight forward if you review everything before. My lab instructor is very kind so it depends.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 100% depends on the TA you get. Her recorded lectures weren't worthwhile - just read the posted slides to prepare for the quizzes. There's a lot of work, but it isn't that hard, just very time consuming. With covid, it's a hybrid class where half of the labs are online and half are in person (no option to do fully online or in person).

I felt like this class was really tedious. You've heard this 1000 times - it all depends on your TA. 50% of ur grade is an easy A, and the other 50% is a bit more challenging. If you want to be smooth in lab, watch lecture + read lab manual. There are A LOT of available OH, so take advantage of those!! Some TAs are good, others are terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TA's grade everything. In order to get an A in chem labs- put your heart and soul into studying for the lab quizzes and finish the lab report couple days before it is due watch lectures (which are opt) to get hints about the questions on the quiz questions. Dr. Sotelo is really good clarifying questions in her office hours !!!
Make sure to attend lab either online or in person otherwise you will not pass the lab class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Make sure to attend to her classes she work in a lot of examples that will be similar in the exam.

She only is the coordinator but takes care of students and concerns either about the reports of any thing that is grade by the TA. she is very good explaining concepts I loved to attend to her office hours because make things much more clear.

Shes so hard to understand. And theres so many lab reports. Take the prelab assignments seriously. Youll only know what you got on the first one around 3 weeks in and only THEN can you check what you did wrong the previous times and fix it. If you dont read your TAs comments and fix your mistakes, youll make low grades all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: if I could give zero as my rating I would. Hands down the worst class I have taken at UT. The workload is just ALOT. The lab reports take an incredibly long time, to do and your entire grade is dependent on your TA. So if you have a harsh TA It won't be good. Also, the professor is not involved and is rude towards the students.

Literally the worst class. I've never hated anything more in my life. The lab reports take an insane amount of time and she doesn't even teach. I would rather be in Ochem than this class, and that should say something.
Very thick accent. Very inflexible is not understanding. Tedious busy work. Guess what though, shes the only professor so get ready to deal with it

She mumbles to herself and trails off and jumps around from thought to thought. She does not even bother to look if we have questions. She honestly may be the worst professor I have ever had and I have been in school for 6 years now. Good god how is she still teaching.

I would recommend choosing another professor. She is hard to understand and lectures are not helpful. The way she explains things is also not good. Go ahead and save yourself. This is genuine advice. I took her for sum ch302 and she only taught one week. Im writting this on day 2.

Non-mandatory lectures are once a week and are supposed to help you on the quiz, but I didn't really go. Quizzes can really help you in the end so TAKE THEM SERIOUSLY. Your grade depends on your TA... hope you get an understanding one. Overall though lab reports are time consuming and tedious, so go to office hours.

Dr. Sotelo was alright considering I only ever saw her once a week at lecture, but her accent is extremely difficult to get over. Your grade is really dependent on your TA, so hope for the best. Writing lab reports takes forever and the rubric can really bump your grade down if you miss multiple small details. The transition online was a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Paola's not very understanding at all. Extremely strict and I couldn't understand any of her lectures. The quizzes were extremely specific and difficult-- basically memorize the longgg prelabs and her lecture ppts if you want to pass the quizzes. If you get a bad TA, you're screwed. The lab reports also took hours to finish and were difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: CH204 was doable. The lectures prior to the lab are non-mandatory and frankly not useful. The labs took two to three hours to complete, and the lab reports are extremely time-consuming. Make sure to study for and take the pre-lab quizzes seriously! They can make or break your grade at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was almost completely based off of the lab reports, each of which took me about 3-6 hours out of class per week. The professor has a very thick accent which isn't understandable, but thankfully lectures aren't mandatory or necessary. Depending on your TA, it could be an easy A or nearly impossible to do well. Be prepared to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Okay so Sotelo herself isn't that great, shes really rough & strict about plagiarism(get ready for a lot of TurnItIn). Luckily, shes the lab manager and not actually doing your grading, she only does weekly lectures that are little help. Really it all depends on your TA so don't get too overwhelmed by her low RMP. Make sure to read your lab manual!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 100% based on your TA. If you get a bad one you are screwed. Some TAs are tough and others are amazing, Sotelo really doesnt do much with students, she offers office hours and offers to regrade assignments but threatens to lower your score since she is a harsh grader. her lectures were boring and you couldnt hear her anyway. labs were not too long
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Sotelo has strong accent and I can't understand her. Lab reports need a lot of work every week. Scores are based on TA. My TA is very kind so I think this class is good. Go to your TA's office hour and you will be fine!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sotelo was unfortunately the worst professor I had thus far at UT. She seems to be very rude to her students and often comes in the lab lectures and calls out the students for the slightest things in a very rude manner. I was she was more approachable. Her chem lab is hard and her TA are hard graders. Lab reports take days to finish and are tedious

Only chem lab prof available. I never went to lecture because i couldnt understand her but attendance to weekly lab is obvi mandatory. Grading depends on TA. Lab report every week that takes a few hours to complete but other than that I liked the class. Weekly quizzes are easy as long as you look at PowerPoint and read manual.

She mostly lectures. Grades depend mostly on TA, but if you go to office hours, she may be more lenient. Since it was chem lab, as long as you regurgitate the Gchem site in your own words, you should be fine. Write literally everything in the lab down for that easy A.
