reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really easy CS Honors class for grades, and while he covers important info, he doesn't seem to care about teaching so the class feels like a drag sometimes. TA Ziyi is the goat though, he's most of the reason the grades are so good cause Prof. Liu just comes in, lectures exactly till the class cutoff time, and then is the first one out of class.
For ML2-H, he is extremely knowledgeable and has good lectures and homeworks. It is also almost impossible not to get an A.
Took ML2 Hon and was a great class. HW and exams were directly related to course content and were similar to practice problems. Lectures were good as well.
Super easy class if you need a tech elective. Class was just basic HTML/CSS. Does take attendance on random days but gives lots of extra credit to make up for it. Great guy.

The professor is an extremely harsh grader, often deducting points without clear justification, making the midterm feel unfair. Although the final is worth 30%, the exams are excessively difficult and ignore students' balancing multiple finals. Despite claims of supporting student success, the grading and exams add stress rather than help learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quoc is genuinely a good and caring professor but the class itself is very hard with the final being the hardest exam by far.

Nguyen is honestly the sweetest professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and treats us like his own kids. From the very first day, you can tell how much respect everyone has for him. Even though the class is tough, he explains things so clearly and makes sure we really understand. He's definitely one of my favorite professors ever
Very hard class. Go to classes, take notes, solve questions.

Dr Nguyen is truly a once in a lifetime professor who genuinely cares about his students. If he thinks you are putting in ample effort, he will be flexible about your test grades and will give points back where he can. Exams are exactly like lecture examples and homeworks and are open notes. Show up to lecture and pay attention and you'll be fine.

The content is not fun, but he genuinely cares about his student's learning so overall it's not horrible. Don't skip class and follow along with his examples. The first midterm is definitely the easiest so try your best on that one.

We love Doc Quoc. He is literally the kindest, most caring professor at UT Austin. He spends lecture after lecture asking students what they need from him to succeed in the class; wanting nothing more than for students to understand the material. He gives completion homework grades, tells you the exam topics, and is very generous with grading.

Dr. Nguyen is an alright professor who knows his stuff about transport phenomena but his tests and homework are nothing like what he talks about in class. Although he tries to explain things thoroughly, it still does not make sense a lot of the time and the final exam is the hardest exam in the class.
Run
Fun Recpectful Loving Funny Smart Kind
Great professor who cares for his students. He knows his stuff very well and is always glad to help others.
He grades very haphazardly,and the course material is not very useful.
Great Professor. His class is relatively difficult and his tests are very hard. He curves at the of the semester so that everyone passes with an A or B usually.

Dr. Que was overall a very nice and caring professor, and you could tell she wanted her students to succeed but because it was her first time teaching the class you could tell there was a little bit of a learning curve for her. Not having taken AP Chemistry in high school, I found the material more difficult due to her lecture style and long tests.

Good professor with the best intentions. Just felt like the ability to actually teach the content was lacking, if you supplement your time or already took AP Chem, you will be fine. 3 midterms and a final project, the tests were long but graded fairly and with partial credit. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

This was her first year teaching the class, which was evident. Lectures mostly consisted of reading from an extremely long PowerPoint, and exams often didn't align with lecture material. Although the grade scale were curved at the end, the course was unnecessarily frustrating and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hard exams, but there's plenty of extra credit/exam retake opportunities; literally, you could retake any/all of the three exams for full credit. However, the lectures are extremely redundant, as she just reads off of the slides. Overall, she definitely cares for the students, but her expertise in the subject isn't super obvious.

Dr. Que is a kind person and cares a lot about her students. Her lectures can sometimes be hard to follow, but if you have a prior background in chemistry (like AP chem in high school) you'll be fine as long as you study outside of class. There are many many office hours opportunities and her and the TAs are all super willing to help you succeed.

For future folks taking her CH301C class: 1) Read and take notes on the textbook *while* doing pre-lecture HW, 2) There's also weekly chapter HW, 3) Exams are long and concept-heavy, lots of but partial credit is given, 4) Good amount of extra cred. opp, such as going to office hours (Que & TAs are helpful), 5) No final, just a chill group project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She's not a great lecturer and can be very disorganized, but she's kind and very willing to answer any questions you have. Very willing to accommodate your schedule for office hours and changed grading system for difficulty. Tests are very hard, even with having taken AP chem, online homework is clunky and unclear.
Dr. Que is a great professor and mentor. Prof dev is a free pass if you show up. I wish all of my chem upper divisions were like this one.

Dont show to lectures because she repeats word for word whats on the slides and still manage to stumble on her words, and then rewrite whats already on the slide with her apple pen. Spends time talking about the element of the day when she still have 75+ slides to lecture about. Creates long exams the night before giving them. Dont take her class.

This course is extremely challenging beyond all means. Exams are long, high-weight, and not curved, although majority performs poorly. Lectures often involve reading slides and can feel disorganized with frequent errors. It's her first time teaching gen chem, and she's currently the only instructor, so dropping may be necessary for some students.

Dr. Que is a wonderful professor. Her lectures are decent, but reading the textbook is required to fully understand the material. A basic background in chemistry is assumed, but additional reading is provided. She gives 100+ problems to prepare for exams which mimic the real exam almost exactly. Exams are challenging, but not overly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Que is the worst professor I had. First time teaching gen chem and it shows. Exams are long, heavy weight, no curve, rushed. Lectures are reading slides, messy work, and disorganized explanations that confuse instead of help. She makes mistakes and relies on students to correct her. If you lacked strong high school chem, this class is a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Que is talented in her work and is very nice; however, this does not translate to her skills as a teacher. Her lectures are hard to follow, and at times she will skip certain skills, as it may take too long to teach, or be stuck on information that won't be on the exam. No curve, her exams WILL be long. You will NEED DC Chem or AP Chem to live.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's nice, but the lectures are super hard to follow. she doesn't like to explain her work when "teaching" her lectures. If you didn't take AP/dual chem in high school, you'll be lost. For one of the exams, she made it too long and despite most of us not finishing, she didn't give us a curve despite acknowledging that the test was too long.

Can't even solve her own questions, even relying on students to help her. When she make mistakes (pretty often), she just smiles through it and laughs it off. Embarrassing for her honestly. Lectures are essentially pointless because she just reads off of the slides without ever explaining anything. Might as well be a biology major and take Laude.

Dr. Que is extremely hard to follow in lectures. She doesn't completely work out problems and expects us to follow unfinished messy work. She jumps from topic to topic with confusing explanations, does not simplify any concepts. Tests are too long, which she acknowledges but does not change. Can only understand material by teaching yourself.

Que is very nice and wants her students to do well. The final is optional if you do well on the first 3 exams since 1 of 4 exams is dropped. TA office hours were extremely helpful and exams were tough but not impossible.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She knows her stuff and answers every question you want her to. She is fun and engaged during lecture which kept me interested for the whole hour and a half. Multiple attempts on HW and the tests are fair. Lots of extra credit opportunities. She cares about our success! Would take again in a heartbeat.

This class was so difficult in the lectures were incredibly hard to understand. She uses um like its a buzzword and then she pauses for 15 seconds before figuring out what to say, which annoys me every time. 5 tests for this class on saturday and one on halloween. Umm no thanks. Im a chemical engineer and this class use to be easier by what I heard

Dr. Que was so unorganized and the notes during class were very hard to comprehend. We used TopHat which was not user friendly and also very unorganized. The tests were ok, but it's hard to study unless you have other resources other than the PowerPoints, notes and practice problems that she provides. Labs graded harshly too.

i hated every second of this class and im a chem major. she uses tophat which is very unorganized and not user friendly, she expects us to know various things about chemistry without a good explanation, she reads off slides, takes unorganized notes, is bad at speaking,when she doesn't know how to answer a questions she makes a joke out of it. help.

Que's super nice and tries her best to make the class doable. However, she can a bit disorganized and confusing. I felt super lost during the entire semester but once we covered all the material things started to connect after I went over all her tophat lectures in 1 sitting. The labs are chill and short but reports were pretty hard.

Lab reports were awful and requried 8+ hrs/wk of work. She gave past exams, but she made the more recent exams so much more difficult that they were basically useless. Went back on her word multiple times (e.g. "You won't need this for the exam ever", but it showed up on the final). She made this class harder than pchem or ochem were.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend enough. She provides SO MANY resources (past exams/practice probs/in-class lecture notes) plus the PDF of the textbook+textbook solutions (don't waste your money) to ensure her students succeed. Tests are lengthy, but she usually gives make up quizzes to earn points back. Seriously one of the best chem profs I've ever had.

I personally enjoyed her class. Very nice woman and tries very hard to present the material in a way that is easy for students to understand. She has not taught very much but she cares very much for her students. She also put a large curve on the class which personally I didn't even think was necessary as it was not hard to make a raw A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I guess I should cut her some slack because she's only been teaching for 2 semesters, but the way she structures her class is pretty terrible. She'd make us do groupwork for most of the class then attempt to cover all the material in the last 15 minutes of class. Exams were pretty hard, lab portion my TA graded pretty strictly, wouldn't recommend.

Dr. Que's class was terrifying. She is a great person, however it was her first semester teaching ever. It felt like she was never prepared for lecture. The test outline she gave before hand was basically what was on the test, however the test were still difficult. I ended up with a B with the curve, actually had like a C-

Quigley is absolutely my all time favorite professor at UT. She is one of the most kind and understanding professors here. If you have the chance to take reporting words with her you ABSOLUTELY need to. It not only has made a difference in my experience in taking the class, but she also has made a difference in my college experience as a whole.
Professor Quigley is great. She gives great feedback and really cares about student's success. If you go to her office hours, you will get an easy A. One of my favorite professors at UT.
EQ is amazing. My writing improved so much because her feedback is so detailed. She is also a cool person overall. Labs are fun. Take her if you can!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Quigley was one of the best professors I ever had. She truly cares so much about her students and helps them with everything to succeed in journalism. She was always avaliable to help. Participation is also a huge part of this class.
Probably my favorite professor at the j school!

chose professor Quigley as your reporting words teacher. She's my favorite professor at UT by far and truly wants you to succeed. She's chill and laid back but also pushes you to be the best. She's someone you can go to for more than just class and understands reporting words is difficult so she's awesome

Professor Quigley is the kindest, most helpful professor I have ever had. She is super communicative and sends out weekly emails saying what's happening in class that week and lab with her is always enjoyable. She wants you to do well in the class and will go over your stories before they are due so you know what to fix. Cannot recommend enough.

if you get quigley for reporting words you have a guardian angel looking out for you fr. she gives incredible feedback and is super accessible. she emailedwith me at 10pm helping me with a cover letter for a job
go to her office hours. she goes line by line through your story making sure it's exactly the way she wants it before she grades it.

Quigley is an angel, and you will be extremely lucky if you have her. She cares so much about her students and is always ready and willing to help you with anything you need. My writing skills improved drastically after taking this class, and I credit much of that to Quigley. She tells you exactly what she expects and truly wants you to succeed.

Quigely is my favorite professor by far. Reporting words can be challenging and time consuming, but she will help you through it. If you show up and listen and ask for help you'll do fine. Super personable and you tell she cares a ton
I love Quigley, she is so awesome. This class will kick ur butt if you don't keep up with it.

Quigley is the most helpful and available professor I have ever had. She offers constructive criticism on every writing piece you send her and is just cool asf. This class is hard, but you learn a lot with the help of your lab professor. Definetly recommend taking her lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Quigley is such a valuable professor to have. She really cares about student growth and success. She goes out of her way to give honest feedback and clear writing expectations.

I really loved Professor Quigley! She is so understanding and accessible and super helpful. She won't go super easy on grading news stories but she will help you out during every step of the process! Labs are a great time to get to know her and other students in the class, and she is really funny and down-to-earth.

Quigley is amazing!! There are four profs who co-teach this class, but Quigley is by far the best one. She's incredibly helpful and always happy to answer any questions you might have. She also makes sure to properly prepare you for all the tests and quizzes. Her journalistic background makes her a great editor for a class where you have to write.

Dr. Huang is a nice guy. You go through a lot of material and a bunch of math derivations in lecture. But, projects were not too hard w/ a bunch of extra credit. Exams were pretty hard but graded leniently. I think this was his first semester teaching generative visual computing, but it was pretty good.

Topics are very dense, both for good and bad. Concepts often feel somewhat overwhelming, but you will doubtlessly learn a great deal about a great deal. Exams are very rough, but graded leniently. Assignments are moderately rough, but have plenty of extra credit. Brush up on your math and be prepared for slow lectures.

Covers difficult concepts, some of which are not explained in depth. Exams are very challenging but graded leniently. Assignments are challenging, but you get 12 slip days, extra credit opportunities, and they're not graded too harshly either. Uses MATLAB which is not ideal, but u have the option for python for later assignments iirc.

Class was graded off of 6 projects and 2 exams (tons of EC tho). Exams were difficult (mostly theory that was covered in slides) but graded very leniently. Projects (choice of matlab or python) were time consuming but covered really cool topics. Lectures that didn't involve linear algebra were pretty good, but the ones that did were a struggle.

His lectures aren't the best, and he throws a bunch of formulas on the slides and expects us to understand them. Projects are interesting but difficult, but he does give lots of time to complete them. Exams are very difficult, but they are graded leniently. There is also lots of extra credit. It is easy to get an A, but lots of work is required.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can be dry sometimes but if the class is interactive and asks questions he gives great responses and tries to explain things better. Exams are difficult and comprehensive but not graded tough, and assignments are very difficult as well but we are given ample time to do them and 12 Slip days to use throughout the semester. Decent prof

The grade distros lie. People drop the class, also there's extra credit/lenient. The workload isn't bad (2 weeks/project) 5 projects total. But he slaps formulas onto slides and doesn't explain them well. Lots of self research to understand the linear algebra/calculus. This class is good if u r interested in CV research and want to know what's new.

The lectures are great! Generally speaking computer vision is math heavy and requires lots of reading, but he managed to cover most of the important topics without much of background requirements. There were lots of extensions that were based on his own research, but those were never tested. Tons of extra credit, homework was manageable.

Very dry lecturer. Did not provide a syllabus and never gave out a clear grading scheme. Tons of generous extra credit (A total of 24 extra points towards our final grade). Thought a lot of complex topics were trivial and did not explain them correctly. Often brushed over topics necessary to complete assignments. Hard tests but graded generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The lectures are taught extremely slowly and are difficult to follow, I skipped most classes to study the slides which were generally more informative. He can be condescending at times, expecting the students to know information he hasn't taught. The projects are easy enough, but in Matlab and time consuming. Tests are also easy.

I stopped going to lecture after a couple of weeks because they were utterly painful. He gave completely false information about something in lecture and, after class, condescendingly argued that it was correct with absolutely no basis (though corrected himself the next day apparently). He touched on OpenGL for only a day. 100% regret taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Rutledge for RHE306, and she was amazing. I loved her. She creates an open and learning space for her students and is easily accessible. Her class has back-to-back essays, 5-7 pages, and uses around 3-5 resources, so essays are doable and easy to write! If you put in effort, she'll put in effort on you. I would take her again!

Professor Rutledge is a wonderful and caring professor. Her lectures are engaging, and she creates a comfortable environment for everyone. She is also very accessible outside of class for any questions. I would take this class again!

I had Dr. Rutledge for RHE 306. She is an amazing teacher who really cares about her students. She is very passionate about the material she teaches and is adamant about helping her students absorb it. If you put effort into this class, Dr. Rutledge will put effort back into you. I highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Rutledge for RHE 360. She is a tough grader but a great professor. She cares about her students and wants them to get the best out of the class. She is approachable and caring. I would recommend her class if you are up for putting in the work!

I had Professor Rutledge for Rhetoric of Inclusion. She was passionate about the subject and genuinely cares about her students' success. The lectures were engaging and clear, and she was always available to help outside of class. I learned so much, and I would definitely take another class with her. Highly recommend!

Professor Rutledge is amazing! I took RHE 306 and I learned so much in her class. She creates a fantastic learning environment where everyone feels comfortable sharing their ideas. Her feedback is really helpful, and she makes writing and critical thinking fun and engaging. Highly recommend her class!

I took her RHE 306 class, and I honestly feel like I am leaving this class without having learned anything. Her rubrics were difficult to understand and her 'lectures' were just her reading off of slides but not necessarily helping you understand what she's trying to teach.She comes off as very passive and gets annoyed when you ask her for help.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Grades very hard (especially if you don't try to become her friend) rubrics and instructions make no sense. She will get mad at you if you dispute a grade with, basically irritated you challenged her very large ego. Stay away please, terrible professor.

I took her RHE309K class this semester. For a rough draft on a paper, she had the class average at a 50% and added the criteria for a rough draft after it was due and graded. Her rubrics are horribly constructed so students are bound to get bad grades. Blows my mind that teachers like this actually chose this as their profession.

Professora Rutledge will make you work, but she is really approachable in my opinion and genuinely wants you to learn Portuguese. There is a lot of homework assignments, but she just checks for completion. Tests are extremely difficult, so you definitely have to study hard (like any language class), but they aren't too heavy on your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this course, especially if you actually care about graphic design. It is easy to get an A, but the lectures are not productive. Professor Rao spends each lecture giving "feedback," but he often gets sidetracked, and the feedback is rarely constructive. You don't get any lessons on programs or software.

He offers subjective feedback to everyone in class based on his own opinions, but it can sometimes be helpful. He is a very qualified creative, but extremely disorganized as a professor. Assignment instructions and overall organization of the course changed too frequently. I got an A, but this class could be unnecessarily stressful.

Professor Rao is a really nice guy! He is a little all over the place sometimes, but that's just how creatives are sometimes. He's really smart and wants to help you succeed in the creative industry! Make sure you take his constructive feedback and use them to improve your work, he really appreciates that.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rao is a fun, kind, and knowledgeable professor! He's always got great ideas for improvement. Loved this class. Attendance is technically mandatory but not necessary - he spends 95% of class critiquing projects that aren't yours. Really easy and fun assignments as long as you've got a good group!

Perfect balance of easiness and wanting to rip your hair out. If you're stuck with a dormant group, good luck. BUT Rao is a very approachable person and is always down to help you with campaigns. The class overall really helps you develop your creative muscles. Attendance is required but lectures are just going over all the groups work.

AMAZING for improving your advertising creative skills! The class is basically a combo of short individual projects and group projects that last a couple of weeks. You'll get feedback each class. Grading is really easy, but the class is very valuable.

The best professor I have ever had!! He truly has so much knowledge, experience, and feedback to share. The projects are exciting and engaging and allow you to meet so many new people.  I am leaving this course as a more creative and critical thinker, and I will carry knowledge from this course throughout my professional career.

My second time taking Rao. He is awesome. This class is heavy on the assignments and is 100% assignments based, no exams/lectures. He goes through work in class and gives you tips on how to fix it. He will not be teaching you how to do the actual Adobe stuff, so be prepared to teach yourself. However, is an easy A as long as you do the work!

Took this class thinking I would learn how to use Adobe, but I've been pretty disappointed. We have cool assignments, but he just tells us what he wants to see, without explaining how to get there. In class he just goes through everyone's submissions. I took this so I wouldn't have to learn outside of class, which is exactly what I've had to do.

Rao gives you incredible feedback on all projects and has so much experience. My only critique is that he was sometimes really bad about emailing back and uploading our Google Drives to submit our work which was annoying. Just be open and ready to expanding your creative mind! Awesome course, inspired me to apply and get into Creative.

An amazing professor who cares about the success of his students. Be prepared for your work to be displayed and critiqued publicly, but it's all helpful in the end. Projects are engaging and fun, and taught me how to challenge my creativity!

This review is for ADV 447- AD Seminar.
This is my 2nd time taking Rao's class. He is amazing and the best professor you'll have at UT. If you have the opportunity to take his class, just do it. You will not regret it. He has changed my view of the Advertising field so much, and he's just a cool guy.

Such a good foundational creative class! Rao gives his students so much room to be imaginative and explore what it means to create advertisement campaigns. Most major grades are group projects. However, will say, the class is only as fun as you make it. Students tend to have a quiet attitude - like yall please just talk and be collaborative!!!

Oh my god my favorite class I've taken yet. Rao is an amazing professor. His class is super interesting and teaches you so much abt the industry. The best part: no exams, quizzes, or real assignments. The entire course is made up of group projects where you create your own ads. We also have a super fun "idea journal" that shows ur creativity. DO IT

Best professor I have had at UT. I wish it could have been in person. Lectures were so cool and the professor is actually so cool. Really cool guest speakers. He is a tough grader, but is willing to hear you out. Go to office hours to get to know him.

Ro is amazing! I learned a lot. Make sure each paper you do has some personal aspect in it. The paper doesn't have to written; it can be a drawing, presentation, video, etc. Just be creative! If you don't really know the topic for the week, you may want to attend lecture and take notes for a good understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rao gave really interesting lectures and his class was always fun. The work consisted of 6 "papers," about the topic he lectured on that week. The paper could really be anything like a powerpoint, video, or art piece, as long as it was creative. There was one group project for the final, but it was fun and you could choose the topic.

I get that if you're very into creative, you will love him. Assignments are a lot about burning your brain to get ideas. Lectures are mandatory, mostly watching ad examples or having guests. Yet, if you are not as creative (like me), you can feel stressed having to come up with so many things and worrying if the idea gets you good grades.
Ro is one of the most unique professors ever. He teaches from some kind of secret art studio, is brutally honest (in the best way) and will spark your creativity.
Amazing professor. Passionate.
Professor Rao was absolutely awesome. He was so passionate about the topic and the semester was just an incredible journey through aesthetic movements and subcultures in the U.S.

Ro is amazing! I took Portfolio 1 with him and he was there for me every step of the way. He responds to emails almost immediately, even if its 2am. He is inspirational, motivational, and all-around an amazing person. You are very very lucky if you get to take a class with him, savor every moment!!
Ro is not only a great professor, but he's also a fantastic mentor. He was probably the most inspirational, caring, and impactful professor I've ever had.

Great class if you need a Moody elective. Go to class for attendance. 60% of the grade is based on 6 "papers." I recommend writing them, but make sure you make your paper as personal as possible or you will fail, and double-check grammar or they will take points off. If you put in the work and go to office hours it should be an easy A.

Prof is Rao is an interesting guy. His personality takes over his lectures, making them entertaining and educational. ADV316 was therefore really easy and the group project a the end was really fun. He's super chill and willing to help you out!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ro is the BEST professor. His class is what you make out of it. He really cares about creative work and I felt like P1 with him was like a mini history class of classic iconic ads. He showed us so many cool things that were before our times and I really appreciated that. If you go to office hours he will help you tremendously:) He's fun to talk to!

Theres a few one page papers that have really flexible topics which is cool! As well as one group project at the end with a lot of freedom on topic and medium of presentation. Each lecture was on a different unique topic of creativity in American culture from skateboarding, to MTV, to Dia de los Muertos. I was super engaged in all lectures!

LOVE this class and rao so much!! i had him for creativity and american culture and he is so passionate about each lecture and makes it so interesting and he really just wants you to learn so there are some short 1 page papers & a group project at the end, but if ur creative and passionate u will easily pass

Easiest class! Rao is the chillest professor you'll ever meet. 6 one page papers, a few canvas discussion boards, and one final group project. Easy A if you've listened to lectures. He is so flexible, and will even let you do something else in place of an assignment if you're feeling creative. Such a cool, funny, and easy class. 100% take again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Rao is an excellent professor, he has a great sense of humor and really allows students to be creative with their work. He is great and suggests everyone get out of their comfort zone when creating, I can say I was so intrigued by some of the things we hit on in this class that I took time outside of the course requirements to do further research.

take this class! she's so sweet. the class was easy, as long as you do the homework that doesn't take long and isn't very difficult. I will say that my class was tiny so we all got more individualized feedback on how to improve, so it might be harder to manage all the random cold calls she does in a larger class. my spanish improved so much

Profesora Ramirez can definitely be the kind of professor not many people are used to having, but personally, I enjoyed the challenge. As long as you do the homework and actively participate in class you will definitely pass. Take advantage of her office hours as she provides valuable feedback and is also an easy person to connect with.

Contrary to some reviews on here, I found her to be an amazing professor that really cares about her students and helped me improve my Spanish. Yes, it can be intimidating to be cold called but I am by no means a great Spanish speaker and I never found it to be as bad as everyone says, it actually helped me improve. Advice: always do your homework.
save yourself.
very sweet lady, terrible teacher. she will not reply to your emails, make her expectations clear for assignments, or grade your work consistently.

She can be intimidating especially if you're not strong in proficiency but if you WANT to learn the language this class is perfect for immersing yourself. Theres a lot of homework, but its necessary if you want to learn. The class is hard but she's an easy grader. I only recommend this class if you want to learn Spanish dont take for just credit.

One word. RUN. Profesora Ramirez is a mess. Inconsistent grading, murky expectations, and relentless cold-calling leave you feeling degraded 3x times a week. Learning? Not her concern. Trouble outside of class? Who cares. Email replies? Nonexistent. If you love constant mistakes on exams, plus feelings of inferiority, this class is for you!

Profesora Ramirez conducts this class entirely in Spanish, and calls on people to respond as she walks you through the topic of the day. Most of the difficulty of the course comes from the pacing, which she does not have much control of - UT Spanish in general is just way too fast paced. Overall, she's a decent professor

The usual brutal pace of summer classes, but this professor makes it ten times worse. Expects you to talk about complicated concepts on the spot, will interrupt you when you pause to think about what you say, and will call you out in class given the chance. She is near impossible to get a hold of through email. Made me want to drop the class.

Overall, super easy class that only involved discussion and conversation practice. She seemed to be very caring however would take forever to respond to other students emails and would take the entire semester to finish grading assignments. Grades are based off of weekly handouts and two written/oral exams and as long as you attend you'll do fine.

I think Prof. Ramirez is an excellent professor, who doesn't have the hang on virtual teaching. It felt like I had to teach myself the majority of the material, and that we didn't really get anything done in class. There was a plethora of issues with canvas, for which she got frustrated with us. Grading was all over the place, and I felt, unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid taking her. Extremely unorganized, not clear about due dates and expectations, and will not speak to you unless in Spanish so things get very confusing if youre not fluent. Everyone in this class is on a different page and always confused. AVOID!

Professor Ramirez grades very tough and inconsistently. She grades only from her point of view, and never answers questions properly. She has vague to no directions and does not know how to work her Canvas page at all. This was not an enjoyable class; it requires so much guessing from the student's side. I didn't learn much at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Profesora Ramirez is a sweet lady but is unorganized and makes a lot of grading errors. Her lessons aren't very helpful and found myself having to teach myself most of the criteria(book and youtube). I learned more from subs when she was gone. The group projects do help boost your grade as she isn't as tough on grading those. Quizzes every week.

Sra. Ramirez goes above and beyond for her students. If you go to her to tell her your concerns about this class, or honestly even life, she will do her all to help you. If you are not perfectly fluent she will remember that when grading and give you helpful notes to improve. She sees the effort you put into her class so make sure you participate.

Pra. Ramirez was one of my favorite professors despite having an extremely difficult class. She is a very sweet and funny lady. Make sure you participate in class, and do all the homework. Sometimes has unclear guidelines and doesn't always follow the syllabus. Tests can be difficult. However, I can definitely say I learned A LOT in this class.
I didn't learn anything in this class, I had to learn everything on my own. Profesora Ramirez is not clear on what she expects and her grading is hard and not consistent.

Profesora Ramirez is a great teacher. You get what you put into the class. Participation matters and she makes you interact with other students. In turn, this makes speaking Spanish more comfortable. She is a bit stubborn with the grading but is not too bad. I would not recommend this class if you do not speak Spanish well or have never written it.

Profesora Ramirez is my all-time fave. I have learned more spanish in the past semester than i have in my whole life. Grading is FAIR and reasonable. She speaks clearly and MOST IMPORTANTLY she provides a friendly and safe atmosphere to make mistakes with your peers. Native speakers and non-native speakers both should take this class.

It's her way or the high-way. It doesn't matter if you're a good writer, you have to write exactly how she wants it (hint: she doesn't understand what a thesis is). She also gives 0 feedback. She never tells you what she wants then you go to her office hours and all she says is "this wasn't what I wanted." Doesn't help you improve before next paper

The homework isn't bad (and she doesn't collect it). And she doesn't lecture in class, you just go over the homework with partners. The biggest problem is her clarity. She never announces projects, she just emails you about it and says there are docs up online (all super confusing). No help in office hours. Not even she knows what she wants.

She is a good teacher. If you haven't taken any previous Spanish classes, don't think this is an easy A. You have to study and prepare for the quizzes and the timed writings. Overall good teacher, but don't underestimate this class especially if you are a native!

Took her and did pretty well. Compositions are very short (a page usually). There are 3 test, one of them being the final which is ALL multiple choice. Super nice lady once you talk to her outside of class. She is crazy busy (teaching like 6 or 7 classes) so she doesn't grade too harshly. She hates tardiness and she is a bit disorganized. She is ok

I didn't really like this guy. His lectures are pretty boring, and he is a really weird grader. He often has taken points off and I really don't get why, not clear feedback. To put it into perspective how my class probably felt, I showed for a lecture for the first time in like 3 weeks and maybe 10/45 people were actually present.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dense and all he does is read off his slides. He's allergic to his inbox. He's a very particular grader and his feedback is sparse. He's not very clear as to what you should focus on when exams come around. Get ready to memorize the IPA buddy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind of an obnoxious grader. Took off points for really little things. Besides that, he was okay. He was always available for office hours.

Mr Myers was pretty knowledgeable but sometimes condescending when you ask him questions or said something. Hed make a face which sometimes made you feel dumb, but I dont think he meant it? He was also an impossible grader with insane expectations for us...and everyone else felt the same way too but he i dont think he cared...
nevermind, disregard my last rating. he is allowing us a chance to turn in some of our assignments again. i guess i underestimated his kindness. overall great professor!
good lecturer but way too harsh of a grader…probably the harshest professor i’ve had.

Absolute beast of a professor. He takes complex topics and breaks it down so everyone can understand, and he teaches you exactly what you need know, so as long as you attend lecture, you won't need to consult many external resources. You will know the ins and outs of the IPA, speech acoustics, and speech perception after this class.

His lectures are pretty clear, full of references for you to read up on for interesting topics. He likes to teach at ungodly times, eight in the morning, so consider that. What you'll struggle with will probably be sound recognition for transcriptions. COVID-19 took our last test away, so I can't say anything about the rest of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best linguistics professors I've taken. I'm a little bummed I didn't have the opportunity to take him for LIN344K! Overall, it's an easy class if you show up. Most of those disgruntled with their grades are those who slept in. Dr. Myers is a fantastic lecturer and learned a massive amount with him.

I enjoyed class with Myers. Homework every week and only two exams (final was second exam). He's a total dad (you'll see) and a quirky guy. Lectures were a little boring some days but he surprised us with his humor every now and then. Fair grader; if help is needed, willing to meet up outside of class. Come to class, do the work, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very straightforward. Weekly homework is a huge part of your grade, but it's pretty easy stuff and Myers is very willing to help. Tests are just like the homework. Decent lecturer (throws in the odd joke) and the lectures were available online to review. Go to class, do the homework, and you'll pass with no problem.
Very, very, very straightforward. Go to class, do the homework, and you'll do great. He's a great professor.
No Comments

I love love love Dr. Schwartz ! Took his UGS on circadian rhythms and honestly learned so much. He is such an amazing professor and also a very caring person. Attending lectures is crucial as his slideshows have nothing but pictures, but lectures are interesting and short.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is interesting, fun, and helpful. A great upper-div course.

Dr. Schwartz is wonderful! He learns all of his students names and tries to stay involved with their lives. Lecture heavy class that isn't recorded, so definitely attend. Very fun though. Also a good resource for a recommendation if you form a good relationship with him!!!

Dr. Schwartz is a really chill prof, he learns everyone's names and makes an effort to get along with students. This class is an easy A but not a blowoff, you have to attend lectures and study in order to do well on the exams. Most of your grade goes to 3 exams so there's little room for error there, but there was no final. Definitely recommend!

3 easy exams, 5 short < 1 page papers, no final. Need to attend class (not required) to understand the lecture power points, but those are where he gets all of his exam questions from. Funny, always eager to answer questions asked in class, and takes time to individually learn every student's name. Highly highly recommend for any neuro major!

Awesome man. Power points are hard to decipher unless you attend and pay attention. Cares for students and class isn't too hard. Accomplished in his field. Truly a gem of a professor. Goes out of his way to accommodate his students.

He is a great person but his lectures are kind of confusing/boring. We wrote 9 papers 70% <1 page, 30% longer. There were 2 quizzes and the final is a 5-minute oral presentation. He's nitpicky on grammar and the quizzes are also very detailed so make sure to actually pay attention/take notes. Interesting class got a 93 but you have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice teacher, a lot of papers, confusing content if you don't have a background in science or circadian rhythm etc. Only recommend if you want to pursue a major related to sleep cycles and circadian rhythms.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwartz taught this class for the first time fall 2018, and it was a very interesting class to me. Most of the students expect an emphasis on sleep or basic lifestyle choices. That isn't just what this class is!! You will learn a LOT about circadian biology. If that is interesting to you, this class is a must. I apply what I learned every day.
Professor Wilt was awesome! Every assignment criteria is very clear, and his lectures were great. He has a lot of cool experiences and tells fun stories to connect the course concepts.

Wilt is the best. He is very knowledgable. I took his class at 8 am and never struggled to stay awake. He is super engaging and his stories helped me learn the material. Exams can be weird and sometimes hard but you will be fine.

Prof. Wilt genuinely cares about his students and is the only professor I'd recommend taking an 8 AM for! He offers plenty of extra credit to help students succeed. Exams come straight from the textbook, so studying is important, but lectures are engaging with lots of stories and real-life examples.

Prof Wilt is so caring and understanding! Gave us exam answers and extra credit. Presentation was easy, but there are a lot of papers that are also easy but time-consuming. Lectures were interesting but exam questions were straight from the textbook!

Professor Randolph is funny, caring, and easygoing. He has pretty strict policies to make sure people engage with the class, but is very nice and understanding. Best prof you could take for MAN by far. reviews.comment: Professor Wilt was great for BA324, can't recommend more. Assignments are graded tough, as is the case for every BA324 professor. However, he offers more opportunities than most and is far more lenient in my opinion. Take him!

Dr. Wilt is extremely caring and approachable. He has tons of stories from his career and frequently references them throughout his lectures. Highly, highly recommend taking him for BA 324 or MAN 336 (I took him for BA 324). One of the most highly regarded professors at McCombs.

Dr. Wilt is a caring and knowledgeable professor. He is always ready to help and genuinely understanding in tough situations. His lectures are engaging and informative, and as long as you thoroughly read the textbook, the class should be manageable! I highly recommend him!

Dr. Wilt is an amazing professor and easily one of the best at McCombs. He genuinely cares about his students' success, and his engaging lectures make you want to attend class. Put in the effort, stay on task, and you'll do great. If you're reading this, take it as your sign to take his class!

Wilt is phenomenal. His lectures are entertaining and he is very passionate about helping students learn. Most of the lectures include his personal stories about working in the industry. Professor Wilt is very knowledgeable and truly cares about his students. He takes content from the book and provide personal anecdotes to help us understand. I will gladly take him again. LOVED this professor. I will be taking him for MAN 336 as well! Cares so much about his students and gives such good career advice. If you are looking for a professor that you can talk to about internship, career, interview, graduate advice TAKE HIM!! Very Great Professor! Really understands the in and outs management with all his experience.

Dr. Wilt is by far one of the best professors I have ever had - I took an 8am for this class just so that I could have him as the professor. great professor, makes learning about what is otherwise not the most engaging topic fun and informative

Just not what I was expecting because lectures were more of him telling stories than the class material that would be tested on the exams. This results in you HAVING to read the book to do good and the lectures kinda feeling like a waste of time.

Professor Wilt gave very engaging lectures and gave good feedback. The class is 2 exams (very textbook heavy), 2 written assignments, group project, and discussion posts. Take Dr. Wilt if you can! He is the best professor I have had thus far. He is super funny and made lectures entertaining. This is best professor I've had. He's really caring and wants his students to success. His lectures are interesting, engaging and fun. The negotiation practices are helpful and fun to do.

The best professor. Easy going, listens to student suggestion and feedback, and is a great lecturer. I loved this class and feel like I am better because of it, which certainly can't be said for all classes.

Although I was required to take this particular course to satisfy one of my degree requirements, Professor Wilt was by far one of the most engaging and informative professors I've ever had the privilege of interacting with during my time at McCombs.

Dr. Wilt is well-educated in the areas of management and negotiation, and is great at keeping the classroom not only focused and organized, but also excited and entertained with his lecture content and negotiation exercises.
Great Professor, really enjoyed the class, it was very interactive and easy to follow. Lots of fun group negotiations.

Wilt is great! With recruiting, I was scared about interviews and timing. He's amazing, not done with the course yet, but would 1000% take it again. He's very caring and understanding if you need extensions or anything. Engaging and knowledgeable, mandatory attendance, but you just sit there and listen to his anecdotes. Offers Ec and is def the best MAN336 prof to take

Great professor, very kind and funny. His lectures were great, no need for note taking. Class was based on discussion posts, two papers, two exams, and a group project. Offered extra credit. Def recommend taking him.

Dr.Wilt gives some of the most interesting lectures. The class consists of few assignments. Discussion posts, two papers, two exams, and a group project. Overall, an easy class to manage. Definitely recommend taking him.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was definitely hard considering I am not a classics major. If you do end up taking this class, be aware his lecture slides have no words and you have to write down everything he says because you will have to describe the pictures from the slides on the midterm/final. It is possible to get an A, but it is not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pretty interesting class overall, Taylor is super nice and helpful during office hours. Really pay attention to the lectures and the PowerPoint pictures and you'll be fine. I would miss about one class a week, hardly read the extra reading assignments and Aced the class. Term paper can make your grade, so be sure to do well and go to office hours.

Would STRONGLY advise to run in the opposite direction if this man is your instructor. EXTREMELY tough grader. Doesn't specify he wants from you and then rips your grade to shreds. He's very quiet and only presents boring lectures. Lots of tests. No mercy shown. God forbid you don't know absolutely everything. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS

Originally I wasn't supposed to have Dr. Taylor as a professor for this course, and I regret not dropping it when I realized he had been switched to the class. He's friendly enough, but his lectures are hard not to sleep through, and his grading is ridiculous (and on few things). Especially if you are a STEM major I do not suggest him as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Respected professor that knows his stuff, but his lectures are so quiet and boring. Really drags it out. For an intro class, its very difficult to keep up and get a good grade. Expects you to read the entire textbook, and extra articles assigned per week and attend all classes. 3 difficult tests, 5 quizzes, 2 outside writing assignments.

Prof. Taylor focuses extensively on material culture, not emperors/events. If you are more of a history person than an archaeology person, this class is not for you. There is about 100 pages of hard reading each week: archaic primary sources and dry research papers. Tests/quizzes were easy but the mandatory reading quizzes each week were a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pretty easy overall. Exams are easier than the quizzes which are more specific. Study the powerpoints and this class is a breeze. The textbook is a bit boring but just read the sections that the powerpoints describe.

Wow great professor! Easy quizzes and tests, just study the helpful powerpoints. Soft spoken but he is a nice guy and curves up huge. Posts textbook online too so you don't have to buy. Essays aren't easy but not worth much.

Super smart professor who demands excellence from his students. Every class consists of a powerpoint with about 40 slides of pictures--NO text. He lectures at great length about each picture, and expects you to know it and intuit what will be on the tests. No study guide. You will learn a LOT. Great class overall. You will get your money's worth.

I never had trouble with staying awake in class, until I took his. I thought the class would be interesting and you would really learn about culture, but not at all. He clearly knows his stuff and is passionate about it, but it was made boring to those he taught. Lots of work and you need to come to class. Grade mostly comes from essays!
The topic is interesting but made bored by professor. Lack clarity on guidelines for papers. Heavy workload! Great leturing monotonous voice which can get you into sleep 10 mins after he begins.

REALLY smart man, ex-Harvard prof. Very soft-spoken in real life but an incredibly merciless grader. Class quality depends on where your interests lie, can be boring for some. Do what he asks on your papers and you will be fine. Really liked him as a person.

This class is the most pointless class. It is over possibly the most useless field of study imaginable. Its like they took a subject that was already boring, and took out all the exciting parts. He expects expert navigation of the library system which is impossible.

He is a really nice man and you can tell he enjoys what he is teaching. He posts his PowerPoints which is helpful. You have to attend extra lectures. Others thought the class was boring but I really enjoyed it and I think it's a great class with not too much work and a great professor.

Extremely knowledgeable professor. Has traveled all over Italy and more so he knows his stuff well. However, unless you're a classics buff or an archaeology major or something similar, this class will probably be really boring and pretty difficult for you. Exams are tough.
Great professor! Midterm really hard! But fun!!!

He makes a noticeable amount of mistakes (especially in the morning section), but he is nice. Personally, I found his lectures confusing (just ask the UGCA's for help w/ instapoll), so I just self-studied everything. Attendance is required in discussion (free points) not in class. EC is up to 30 pts, lots of drops & resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TULEY IS AMAZING! He is a great lecturer and provides many outside resources for extra help. he also provides lots of extra credit and is overall just an amazing professor.Not much homework either

this semester's setup felt less organized. Graded instapolls for attendance and weekly quizzes. Lectures felt inconsistent and missed some key fundamentals, so they weren't very helpful. I'd rely more on student hub resources and use lectures as practice. Overall, I wish the setup hadn't changed.

Personally, i got nothing from tuley's lecture. His handwriting is really bad and everything i used for exams was purely from the review notes which is generalized across all chem professors. You'll be ok no matter who you have for chem 1 or 2 but for me i self studied the entire course and if anything tuleys lecture just confused me more

He's an overall good professor and does care about his students knowing the material, but the class does get difficult in acids and bases. This is a unit that is in general already hard, but he's not the best at breaking down so self study a LOTTT before this exam. Prepare well for weekly quizzes. He offers lots of extra credit and 2 retakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: so many resources, extra credit is easy to get and max 30pts. gives everything needed to do well on exams. ngl acid and bases will cook you alive (im not kidding) but if you study you'll pass (all of our grades dropped by a letter). quizzes in class right after exam, must self study (his only downfall). GO TO OFFICE HOURS

Dr. Tuley is a really caring and genuine guy. This class was difficult but you have the opportunity to earn up to 30 points of extra credit and retake two of the exams as your optional final. I went to office hours once a week and felt much more confident on the material afterward. He'll basically do the hw with you which sets you up for quizzes.

Best professor I had. Be aware of weekly quizzes but as long as you know what you are doing should be fine. He drops 3 and there is no final in the class so 4 exams total, but you can make up 2. Practice is key in this class and attending lectures and ESPICALLYY office hours help. I missed having a A plus buy 3 points aka less than one question.

I was not a star student and should've gotten a C- for not studying, but I showed up for every class and did the instapol and weekly quizzes which made the difference. He quite literally hand feeds you everything you need to get an A in this class and as long as you use it you'll be fine. Or be like me and just show up (but actually pay attention.)

I had a hard time with this class. Prof. Tuley was a sweetheart and made the class enjoyable. If you're willing to actually to study—even though I did—you should be fine, but wow, I could only FULLY understand maybe one week of course content. I Q dropped this class.

Tuley gave a lot of resources you could use to study for quizzes and exams, if you want to get a good grade in his class you should definitely study the Question Types for each unit. My only cavoite for his class is the quizzes, they're simple enough but if you don't have foundational understanding, you will overthink the questions sometimes.

Dr. Tuley was an amazing professor! He offers a lot of EC, resources, and office hours. Most people do not realize that no matter the course/prof., A LOT of studying is required if you want to end the course with an A. Any science course will demand you actually put time into the class!! He is very approachable and flexible with any conflicts.

Dr. Tuley has an excellent way of teaching, a good sense of humor, and offers a wide variety of resources. As a non-chemistry/natural sciences major, I still felt I managed to grasp a basic yet fundamental understanding of chemistry while also being able to keep up with the material. Note: Practice with home works and you will be fine on the exams.

He's a good professor, a little funny, and he really cares. I personally thought his lectures were a little confusing because he did make a noticeable amount of mistakes. So 99% of my learning was self studying with CSS. If you put in the work, you can definitely get an A in the class. EC is up to 30 pts, lots of drops and resources.
Good professor. He really does care,provides resources, and gives a lot of EC. Idk what the other review is talking about because we definetly have a lot of resources lol.

Avoid this class! I took chemistry 301N, expecting this class to be a great science to take but this was not the case. His lectures weren't helpful towards learning the content and I ended up having to teach myself. This class is provided with hardly any resources compared to other chemistry classes. Very test heavy, lots of students struggled.

Going to class is mandatory since lectures include instapolls, and there are weekly quizzes on Wednesdays. He is a clear speaker with notes, and weekly homework assignments have unlimited attempts. Additionally, he offers multiple ways to earn extra credit! Tests and quizzes are manageable as long as you put in work to pay attention in class.

Really cares about his students. 4 exams that cover each unit and very doable. defintely some challenging concepts, but it is gen chem at the end of the day. Gives weekly quizzes that are low stakes, but can help you asses your learning. Easiest way to do well is to go to his office hour.

Took this as a non-science major expecting it to be manageable because of the great reviews, but it was much harder than expected. Weekly tests meant nonstop studying, yet most students struggled to earn above a B-. Content feels unadjusted from the regular course, and emails rarely get responses. Avoid for 301N unless required.

ok i only got a bad grade bc i didnt lock in. theres so many resources for this class and its literally just discipline bc tuley IS a good prof. pay attention in lectures and DO YOUR LEARNING MODULES. do practice tests and go to office hours. theres a bunch of extra credit opportunities. so many ppl fail chem 1 so he literally WANTS u to pass

His CH 301N class for non-science majors isn't easy, but he gives you many chances to boost your grade with up to 2 exam redos, extra credit (go to office hours, they're super helpful!!), and homework/participation. 

He's got a killer sense of humor and his lectures are fun and real-world applicable. Take this class if you need a science credit!

His class is super chill & he's really funny. I would mention that he does tend to skim through topics and talk about it kinda vaguely. Most of your learning needed to pass the class and test is based off of the resources in canvas, not his lectures. quiz every week, tests are a little hard but with use of resources its easy. tons of extra credit.
As long as you do your HW and ask for help, you will pass. He is very understanding and wants everyone to pass his class. I recommend studying the HW questions for the quizzes and exams.

Dr. Tuley is nice and cares about the students. His class is not as easy as people say if you have almost no previous chem knowledge, but it's not as hard as other professors. He offers extra credit by attending his office hours or CSS which is generous.

Very interesting lectures and an all-around great professor who really cares for his students. Took CH301 with him in the summer, and it was a very easy class. Despite the short-semester schedule (6 wks), I did not feel overwhelmed, and I felt like the class was very manageable. I can only imagine that the class would be easier in the fall/spring.

Best professor at UT so far. He makes chemistry accessible to all. Highly recommend his office hours to get advice for quizzes and exams. He offers so many resources from himself and the chem dept. He is funny, caring, and devoted to his students. Studying lectures, quizzes, learning modules, and practice problems/exams are all necessary.

Very chill prof who was passionate about chem and teaching. Gen chem was pretty easy as long as you knew how to do all the practice problems and question types, and Tuley gave out a lot of extra credit for going to office hours.He taught through practice problems done on paper on a doc camera, and lectures were recorded. Weekly quizzes/discussion

Not that hard if you actually put effort in. Dr. Tuley is very nice, and office hours are helpful. Extra credit is generous, so do as much as you can. Make sure to pay attention in lecture and do the homework because it can be easy to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is not that difficult, and it can be interesting if you pay attention and put effort into the class. There are many resources provided to help learn and review for exams, which are very easy if you do them. Dr. Tuley explains concepts well in lecture and is very friendly. This class is very easy to do well in if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Tuley for CH301 and CH302 and absolutely loved it! Tuley is the goat and as long as you take notes and take a look at the review notes(a god send) you'll probably get an A. CH302 was for sure harder with the toughest unit being Acids and Bases but remember just lock in. Tuley is actually funny and gets us.

Dr. Tuley is the best professor ever. He is caring, considerate, and amazing at what he does!! Stay on top of the weekly quizzes, study on time for exams, and go to office hours. He is seriously the best!!

Had Tuley for both CH 301/302, provides a lot of extra credit! Weekly quiz abt what you've learned (only 5 questions). He also allows a scientific calculator on the exams. To do well in his course make sure you do the practice exam and practice question types. Sometimes it's difficult to understand ex problems but he's happy to explain it again.

The BEST chemistry professor. He's so good that everyone from my class last semester took him again this semester. Great lecturer and lots of opportunities to raise your grade. He cares that you're learning, and it shows. If I could take him for every chemistry course for the rest of my life, I would, and this isn't even exaggerating.
Great professor, great guy, and great class.  I would honestly argue that earning an A was too easy.

He provides many opportunities to get an A in his class - extra credit, practice problems, extra readings, detailed study guides for exams, and two replacement exams. He is very kind and approachable as well.
The homework is helpful but can take some time to do. He posts a Review PowerPoint of the unit which is convenient and super useful for tests.

Dr.Tuley was one of the best chemistry professors I had. He is very passionate about chemistry, and he is willing to get to know you and help you. He gives four midterms, and you are able to take replacement exams if you did not do well on some. He also has a very generous drop grading and gives extra credit. I really recommend taking him!!

Prof.Tuley is amazing and if you can take him def do. He offers a lot of extra credit, and drops a a lot of assignments. He is great at explaining content and is very kind to his students. He offers a lot of resources to make sure you are able to succeed in his class. There are 4 exams, no final, and you can retake 2 exams for a higher grade.

Dr. Tuley is great! He makes chemistry easy to understand and is very accessible outside of class. Even if you cannot attend office hours, he will make an effort to meet up with you if you communicate your needs. I am taking him again for CH302 and strongly believe his teaching will help me do good again.

I hate chemistry, but Professor Tuley did such a great job of explaining complicated concepts and offered many resources. He's super friendly and helpful, and his lectures are sooo good. Genuinely just does an amazing job on all fronts.

Dr. Tuley is the absolute best! If you have the opportunity to take his class, do it!! He is by far my favorite professor, and I thoroughly enjoyed going to his class. The exams are very easy if you pay attention and do well on the practice exams.
He is the goat 🐐. Very nice and funny man. Just attend lectures, discussions, and office hours and do your study guides ahead of time and you'll be fine.

easy class, Dr. Tuley is very caring for his students and won't leave you behind so long as you put effort in. 4 midterms that are all relatively easy, practice exams, a detailed review, and many practice questions, and an optional final you can use to help your grade as much as possible. You have many options to succeed, put in work to see results
It is an easy class to pass; the professor provides every available resource.

Dr. Tuley was a great professor! His syllabus and grading system were very generous; many extra points/extra credit given, & drops for attendance/discussion. Lectures are recorded, & quizzes were based off the previous week's discussion & exams weren't bad at all since there are study guides and practice questions.

Dr. Tuley is amazing he made the class so fun and easy to understand. He's very caring toward his students and really does his best to make sure his students succeed in class. Really was a kind, understanding, and respectful professor! Also offers several opportunities for extra credits. Best professor I've had this semester.

I believe Tuley is a very funny and approachable professor who cares about his students. He is thorough and makes sure to get difficult concepts across clearly. His office hours also help alot if you want extra help on muddy concepts. I recommend Tuley for CH301 and I plan on taking him for 302 as well. One of the best professors I've had!

Dr. Tuley is awesome! He explains the material clearly, making even complex topics easy to understand. He is supportive and always willing to help, ensuring that every student feels confident and prepared. He is approachable and creates a positive learning environment, and genuinely cares about his students' success. Highly recommend his class!

Taking the time to write a review as I don't usually do this but Dr.Tuley truly deserves one. He is one of the only professors who (truly) notifies, emails, and offers many resources to make sure you pass the class with a good grade. The learning modules are well-made and explain the concepts in a digestible way while cracking a few jokes!

Professor LeFlouria was wonderful, and the class is fairly easy and informative. Prof LeFlouria does take a bit to get back with you on grading which can make it difficult to understand what she wants from you, but is overall helpful and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor, make sure you show up to class would have gotten an A if i went to class more. Easy class overall, just do the work.

The African American Women's History course was very easy and often pretty interesting. The class is just teacher lead insights that is sometimes about the assigned readings. Just do the assignments and show up and easy A.

Professor LeFlouria is amazing! I've taken both of her HIS365g courses and she has been wonderful both times! She approaches the topic she teaches in such a way where she's able to help explain both the gravity of the situation and make sure that she isn't overwhelming us at the same time. She really cares for her students!

She is a kind and inspiring professor, I talked to her a couple of times after class and she was always ready to answer my questions. You don't have to participate if you don't want to but it sure helps. Overall this was my favorite class this semester and I believe I learned a lot from it. Would 100% Recommend

Professor LeFlouria is great, she's really fun and sweet and clearly knows so much about the topic. This class is not hard at all, I have gotten a 100 on every assignment so far, but I do feel like I'm learning a lot. She teaches about things I would never have learned about in other history classes. Would definitely recommend.

The class is discussion-based so be prepared to participate and make sure to do the weekly readings. Other than that, just one presentation and one (relatively short) research term paper/end-of-semester project. You'll learn a lot about parts of US history that aren't taught elsewhere and gain hands-on research skills. Excellent professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good professor and she cares for her students. Classroom is flipped (attend lecture twice a week for an 1hr). She emphasizes understanding/learning, theres a lot of extra credit around 2.5%?, a lot of instapolls (she counts attendance too). First exam is usually the most rough in her class, 1st exam (56%), 2nd exam (90%), 3rd exam (71%).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love her, she's so fun and lit, tests are kinda hard but she gives a lot of extra credit and drops 2 units on the final. 10/10 goat

I was kind of scared at first because of the RMP reviews but she was honestly the best bio professor I could have asked for. She's so caring and she genuinely wants her students to succeed. Her exams are doable if you study but I wish there were more resources to study for them. Her class is flipped so take note before you register.

Ecology is an easier subject, but she's not the best at explaining things. You can usually get it on your own. She does talk down to students some, stating things are 'obvious' or 'easy' when they're not that way to everyone. Lots of your grade is decided by group projects. They're not the worst, but they're not fun either.

Dont listen to bad reviews. This is a flipped classroom so a lot of the content is self-taught but I was used to that from my BIO311C class I took with another instructor. Literally just put in the hard work and pay attention and study and this class is a breeze. TAs were super helpful. Dr. Thijs is very nice and attentive to her students.

Very organized and fair if you put in effort. Flipped class where class is spent on Instapolls (free points) where she goes over every answer. Lots of small assignments and exams are similar to practice questions. Dr. Thijs is a great professor who cares about her students. Highly recommend both the class and her as a professor.

Professor Tjhis was an OK professor. Her class was pretty rough, not much Extra credit and her course was pretty much self thought. She won't give out A's like candy, you have to really work for it. Instapolls were only there to reinforce the content you were supposed to study in the assignments. Test wording is not it.

This is a flipped class, so most of the material is covered in your own time (though you could use the class time on Monday too), but otherwise, it's not too bad at all.  There are plenty of resources and the Instapolls test your understanding pretty well.  Just pay attention to the Panoptos.

This classroom is flipped but attendance is still mandatory. We only did instapolls in class and they were nothing like the test. One TA is helpful but I wouldn't have gotten an A without doing bio before this class.

The class is pretty easy and straightforward, do all the assignments and understand the content and you'll do well on the tests. It is a flipped classroom, which was not ideal imo but still worked out in the end. The hardest part was the Pearson homeworks, which were just plain out unreasonable at some points, but overall very easy.

Dr. Thijs is awesome! It is super easy to succeed in her class if you actually put in the effort. She has a ton of extra credit opportunities too. The format is a flipped class, so you complete the lecture portion asynchronously. Exams are not bad at all- a lot of the material comes straight from the practice problems she posts.

Flip schedule class, so we had Monday off to watch the recordings/learn the content. Wednesdays and Fridays were in class lecture. The exams are a mix of multiple choice and short answer questions, but it's not unreasonably hard so long as you study. There are extra credit opportunities too. Dr. Thijs is wonderful and truly cares for her students.

To start it is a flipped classroom with a pre-recorded lecture that you watch on your own time Monday, then regular in person lecture Wednesday and Friday. I loved Dr. Thijs! Previously I took this course w/ a different professor and q-dropped bc of his demeanor, but Dr. Thijs is the sweetest. She looks out for her students and makes sure they pass

She's an amazing professor. Her class might seem hard at first because it's a flipped classroom and is your responsibility to watch the videos. There's also a lot of homework but if you do it, it will be very easy to study for the exam. People say lectures are useless because you only answer instapoll questions but they're good practice for exams.

Like many other people say, this is a flipped classroom. I think it was a good flipped classroom though, because the activities done in class does help engage with the material. The instapolls, apply and extends, and homework assigned helps with making sure you learn and apply the material. Tests are fairly easy to study for (no surprises).

Flipped obviously. It's done in a way where you watch a lecture video on Sunday, practice it in lecture, and do homework/discussion over it later in the week. Overall pretty easy, although the tests have been challenging for some people I know. Lots of extra credit too, so don't be too bummed about a bad grade.

As you've probably read from all the other reviews, the class is flipped. Dr. Thijs does come off as condescending which leads to usually few people raising their hands but she's ok.
