The hw was the main source of practice for the exams which I didn't like at all. I'm not good at physics AT ALL. All you need to do is REDO HW, go to ALOT of office hours, watch yt vids, & pray.
He's honestly not that bad of a professor. I enjoyed his lectures and found the assignments he posted very helpful. He could do better by being more open to questions when talking one on one.

Physics is already a challenging subject, but a good professor can make it feel exciting and approachable. Unfortunately, this class did the opposite. I left feeling more confused than when I started due to his attitude when teaching one on one.
IF YOU WANT ANYTHING HIGHER THAN A B-, SAVE YOURSELF AND YOUR TIME AND DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF.

I 100% would not recommend this class nor professor. I am a junior with a 4.0, and I got a B in this class. This class is already extremely hard and Dr. Perera honestly seems like he tries to make it harder. The homework is the only thing you can use to study, but  expect to teach most of this class to yourself. He also does not believe in curving.

Never actually met the guy since the only thing that matters is your TA. The labs itself aren't exactly easy but you'll be fine if the TA is good. Final project at end of semester that you work on individually, everything else is just lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is reflective of the TA and class itself since it's a lab, and I never saw Dr. Perera. This was harder than it needed to be. The instructions for the labs were unclear, and my TA confused my group even more. My TA was also a bit petty with grading. I think if you're lucky and get a good TA, you'll probably have a better experience.

Definitely pay attention to the examples he does during lectures, and do the extra practice he posts before midterms. But I wouldn't recommend him if you haven't taken physics before; the class is kind of like a flipped classroom, and he's hard to approach. He can be condescending if you ask questions.

The homework is very similar to the tests, and the reading's super important to understanding the concepts, not just the math. Dr. Perera's lectures focus on examples because he expects you to read the textbook. As for the midterms, each is two days, with one day being a more difficult section that you do with 1-2 others, like a group project.

Worst class I've ever taken. He overcomplicates topics which makes them seem harder than they actually are. Doesn't give partial credit back despite some past reviews saying he does. Use the homework to study, but expect to teach most of this class to yourself. I also never took physics before this which I think put me at a disadvantage
Literally so hard for a one credit hour lab. Would not recommend

as long as you do the hws and actually understand the math behind it as opposed to just memorizing the answers, the class should be fine. i really didn't think the final was comparatively harder than the prior midterms since a lot of the types of questions he went over in class or through hws.

Do NOT take this class. Some tests are fine and fair, but the final was much harder than any previous exam and he does not curve at all. I would recommend another professor if you care about your grade. He is not worth anybody's time.

Dr. Pereira was a strong and effective instructor. His homework aligned very well with the exams, and the lectures were reliable indicators of what material would be tested. If you stay on top of the homework and pay attention in lecture, you will be well prepared for exams. I personally did not need to use the textbook much.

I was able to do well in this class mainly because I had taken physics before. If I hadn't had prior physics experience I wouldn't have done well in his class at all. He explains topics like Torque in a more complicated method than necessary and genuinely seems like he wants students to fail during exams. Take a different professor if possible.

Perera's lectures, while great in quality and for conceptually understanding the topics, do not adequately prepare you for the difficult exams which all had very low averages and he "doesn't believe in curves." He's not a bad guy but you have to put a lot of practice hours in with HW and extra textbook problems if you want to do well on exams.
Dr. Perera is a solid professor in terms of his leture style. Speaking to him in person, I realized how condescending he is. Final very hard.
His lectures are honestly really good. He is not the most friendly person to talk to one on one and can be passive aggressive at times. Ultimately, good professor, below average personality.
Good lecturer, kinda condescending/standoffish if you ask him questions 1 on 1, generally fair exam and homework except for the final which was definitely much harder than any of the previous exams.

I was baffled that people have bad experiences with him. imo he puts a lot of care and thought into making his lectures engaging with tons of demos and connections to real life (which I'm realizing as I cram the recordings for finals), and he cares a lot about learning over just grades so he often gives bonus and extensions when needed. Great guy!

Perera is an decent lecturer but is very unhelpful during office hours. He always seems anxious and paranoid, even though he is willing to help he doesn't actually do it and is always very jittery. Parth (his TA) was amazing though

Dr. Perera pours so much into his students, he has more office hours than any of my other professors. His teaching style is easy to follow, he's fair with exams, and he genuinely cares about his students. I added a physics major because of how much I enjoyed this class. If you do the hw and go to lecture, you'll do well. Take him, he's the best.

He is truly a terrible professor. He never answers questions during class and is very inaccessible from email. I would not recommend taking this class. He tries to inflate his own ego by making simple concepts seem more complicated than they really are. I wouldn't recommend Perera.

Perera is a decent lecturer but the material he presents in lecture is completely insufficient for the course. He leaves out key details and is terrible about answering questions with certain students. He doesn't have favoritism, but he definitely shows some dislike towards particular students and that becomes very clear during the lectures.

Not exactly a reflection of the teacher, but of the class, because I never once saw Dr. Perera. 
Very much TA dependent. The only thing I learned was about statistics. Lab is done in groups, so choose good partners. Most of the labs were pretty straight-forward. You can leave once you're done (1-2 hrs). Spent maybe an hour a week on lab reports.
This lab is very poorly designed and the professor never shows up
He does a good job lecturing but needs to teach closer to the exams
Decent professor but poorly structured course. Just take it at community college

This class felt pointless, and labs were often confusing, vague, and long. 9 labs total, with a final project at the end of the semester. Don't expect to gain or retain relevant physics knowledge because it's basically just statistics. Doesn't supplement learning in physics lectures. Grade is TA-dependent.

Perera is an amazing lecturer, and his class is clearly structured and easy. The midterms are multiple choice and similar in difficulty to homework. If there are bad questions, Perera will drop them to ensure the exams result in grades that reflect the knowledge of the material.

I would not recommend taking this class. He doesn't believe in curves or extra credit even when most of the class fails the test. Lectures can be informative or you can spend an entire class going over a single problem that he doesn't even explain well instead of necessary material.However, not hard to pass because of the way the grade is weighted.
The class is fine, but this is mainly a statistics class. Extremely TA dependent.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a lab and the lab is one of the worst designed pieces of education conceived. Its all stats and uncertainty. the whole point of physics is that its not engineering, its ideal, but this class is 5% doing physics concepts and 95% propagating uncertainty. Doesn't make a lick of sense. Perera is great though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: His summer course is fast paced, but his lectures are great and he makes sure that students understand the content before moving on. There's a decent amount of hw, but it helps to solidify understanding and to prepare for the exams. Course organization is solid and the teaching team is active on Ed. This is likely the easiest UT physics gets.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I always struggled with physics but taking physics 2 with Dr.Perera was awesome. His lectures are very conceptually heavy, but they set you up well for the homework. Homework served as great practice for the midterm. TA's and Dr.Perera were quick to answer questions on Ed Discussion.

Dr. Perera obviously cared so much, offering at least three office hours a day between him and the TAs. Even split of HW and test weight. That being said, this is a lot of physics condensed into five weeks. Don't recommend unless you have previous experience. It's not impossible, but difficult problems can't be conveyed in the short lecture times

I took him for physics 2 lab, never saw him. Grade is dependent on whether you have a good TA or not. I  had Afsana, who was a very tough grader and took points off for everything. If you find out that you have her you gonna have to lock in.

Professor Perera is caring but also straightforward and to the point. He is extremely accessible outside of class. My only complaint is the test length. They typically range somewhere around 12 questions. Though he's very open to feedback and allowed test retakes after students made him aware that the test length was a problem.

Dr. Perera was amazing. He really cared about student success and gave plenty of resources and opportunities to do well. Tests were formatted like the homework problems and he gave us a chance to get half points back on our tests, which helped my grade a lot. Great professor, highly recommend!

Unfortunately, he does not explain concepts clearly, and his tests are significantly more difficult than the material covered in class. It may be beneficial for him to observe how other educators successfully teach physics in a more accessible and supportive manner.

The class is a basic introduction to engineering physics. The topics taught are the same as high school physics with a few changes. Dr. Perera wants his students to succeed and has designed his course so that most students will get A's. Homework will take a bit of time, but it isn't too hard; exams are just like the homework. Best UT Physics Prof!

Dr Perera truly is one of the best professors I've had at UT. If I could have him for physics 2 I would. Dr Perera gives lots and lots of resources to study between the textbook problems, quest homework, and several reviews and gives the opportunity for up to half credit back on exams. He's extremely generous and will always offer clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fall 2024. TA-led, I have never seen this professor once. All labs were done in pairs, and conceptually, this lab has almost no overlap with the corresponding lecture course. The entirety of this course was methods of statistical analysis such as t-scores, chi-square, etc. (given formulas). 1 lab/week, weekly reports, time-consuming.

His lectures only adequately covered 80% of the material on the test. He would derive useless formulas and the formulas he did give us were only the basic ones. The test was made up of questions you have never seen before with some being conceptional based. The good thing was that he offered remakes. Hes the best option for phys 1 tho.

His lectures do not cover what's going to be on the midterms as they are very abstract and barely contain practice problems. He would often go on tangents or go through unnecessary derivations of formulas that we would be given on formula sheets. Review Quest HW's and practice exams to succeed on the midterms. Lowest 3 Instapolls are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I had an extremely weak physics background, but it went fine. I took his in person class, and I think a lot of my success for the exams went to grinding for them via redoing hw and luck. Heads up, the 3rd midterm class avg was in the 60s (most ppl got 40-60s) and final class avg in 70s. TAs were extremely helpful

Offering retakes on tests will not solve the problem; it will only address the symptoms. If most students perform poorly on a test, the professor should pause, reflect, and adjust their teaching strategies.

Don't trust the positive reviews. He overcomplicates si.ple.topics, rarely replies to emails, and his exams are much harder than what he teaches. If you want to understand Physics, either take a different professor or be ready to self study. Worst class I've taken at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, MY FAVORITE, very passionate. However, hws are EXTREMELY long and the tests are VERY HARD. The only respite is that these r online classes, and the Instapolls and HW's do help bump my grade up from the hws. This class was the one I had to study for THE MOST this semester, and the content in class is much easier than the exams.

I really struggled with physics in high school, but taking this class changed my perspective about it. Dr. Perera cares about his students a lot and urges them to actively participate in their education. The grading policy is generous and you are graded by a lot of things so don't panic over a bad test grade.

Physics is hard but Perera's lectures are good and he really cares about making sure you understand the content. He lets you earn up to half credit back on each midterm (3 of them) which is super generous. One Quest homework each week which can be a little long but really good for test prep. Instapolls in class for attendance (4 are dropped).

Great professor overall. Interactive lectures. Good lectures that give you all you need for tests. Would definitely take in person, not online. Grading system is extremely helpful and he genuinely wants you to do good in the class. This class isn't a 100% breeze, but it will with no doubt be enjoyable to have in your schedule.

This professor was pretty average. I'm sure it would've been better if the class wasn't mostly online but he seemed to go through few examples pretty slowly. The grading makes the class very easy to get an A in as you can get half of your missed points back on exams, you get many tries on homework, and discussion and instapolls give free points.

First time ever taking physics, and I thought Dr. Perera was great. Mechanics is a lot of content to teach in a single semester, especially for someone like me who knew nothing, but Perera's lectures were excellent. The only thing I didn't like was that lectures were all online, but that might be a positive for some.

Literally the best physics professor ever. Does an amazing job conveying concepts and how things work. Very understanding. Daily instapoll problems for attendance throughout lecture. Lots of examples worked out during lectures.

Very generous with grading, if you try you can get an A bc all midterms you can earn half points back, 50% of grade comes from HW and attendance, so would 100% recommend taking him. Lectures were sometimes engaging and sometimes not, but he is very passionate about the subject!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera is passionate and caring with his lectures and content. He also gives half credit back for each exam and the final replaces the lowest midterm score. Most of the grade comes from hw, discussion, and instapoll (~50%) and each exam is only 10% with the final being 20%. I would recommend him but you will have to study for the tests.
great lecturer and genuinely cares about his field of study. cares about students, gives opportunity to improve midterm grade. final replaces lowest midterm. best prof for phy1

The prof is easy to understand and explains concepts well. The class has three midterms and a final which is a bit much but half ur grade is just homework and participation. The first unit is the easiest and the second is the hardest. Exams are medium difficult because of limited time and amount of content.
Pretty easy lab. It's mostly statistical analysis based so be prepared for that.

Physics lab really depends on your TA. I got lucky with mine and this class was really chill. Lab notes and a prelab every week (took maybe 3 hours total including doing the lab). Final project is a DIY experiment that you design.

I took this course over the summer and Perera was unreachable and not very helpful. The final was also completely different from anything we had learned all semester which caused me to end with a B+ instead of an A (the average for the final was a 60).

This guy cares so much about his students. He reminds me of Dr. Sparks (another amazing professor) because he always dedicates time in lecture to making sure students' questions are answered. He loves what the does and it shows. This guy made me love physics!
Very kind professor and cares a lot about his students, get ready to study a lot though

Certain lectures were more helpful than others, but I learned best through the homework. Exams are never harder than the homework given and there are usually a couple questions that he pulls straight from it. Only issue is that there aren't too many questions on the tests, so not much room for error especially since he doesn't usually curve.

He gives a lot of quest hw, and the exams are based on those problems. Aside from the amount of homework, the class itself is not super difficult, and his lectures are alright. It was mostly easy but I don't think I really learned the concepts too well. HW makes up a lot of the grade, and the final can replace your lowest midterm.

Great at lecture. He is really good at explaining concepts and showing how these equations come about and does a lot of practice problems during lecture. He shows a lot of space related engineering feats to support physics concepts and is really interesting.

Amazing, caring professor. Dr. Perera clearly enjoys teaching and is passionate about physics. He explains things clearly and holds many office hours (which you should attend) where he will walk you through a problem step by step if needed. Tests are hard but similar to homework and practice problems so if you know those inside and out you're set.

If you took AP Physics or Onramps Physics, this class is just a copy pasted version of that. And if you didn't take physics before, then thats fine, the concepts aren't complicated. If you take the time to actually solve the homework instead of searching on brainly, then the exams are an easy 90-100.

Prof Perera is one the best physics professors that I've heard about at UT. I had no prior physics learning, but I was able to get an A. My class was hybrid, so online lectures and in-person tests. Attend lectures cause instapolls (but works through them). Two homework per week. Free online textbook provided, but I didn't use it and still got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Twice weekly homework. Attendance not strictly required but is graded with Instapolls. Tests are just like homework. If you skim the textbook, make a good formula sheet, and actually do the homework, you will do well.

2 midterms, 1 final. One of the midterms gets dropped. His lectures are very conceptual and don't really go into any practice problems. A lot of your learning will be through the quest homeworks and reading the textbook. Honestly, it's very manageable.  As long as you do good on midterm 1 (easiest one) you'll have a solid grade in the class.

If I could go back and choose a professor to take for 303K, it would still be Professor Perera. With that being said, his class wasn't just a walk in the park. You need to stay on top of all homework assignments and understand what was going on fully to do well on the exams. Overall, an informative class and would reccomend.

The lectures were somewhat boring. Homework due every Monday and Thursday, which were manageable. Test were decent, and before lecture you had to read a piece of the text book. Overall decent class and made Physics enjoyable. Would recommend.

He is incredible, teaches material very well, very easy tests that are clear if you have an ounce of ability to apply the concepts in class and from the homework, if you study the quest, tests are a breeze, if he could teach my engineering courses I would only ever take him.

Dr. Perera made physics about as enjoyable as it could be. 50% of the grade is basically participation/completion, and you get a cheat sheet on every test. If you understand the topics conceptually you can easily get an A (a 93.5+) in the class. Lectures were very boring but the textbook gave you all the info you needed to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera is a great lecturer who incorporates entertaining demos. The grading is super generous, with lots of drops and 50% of the total grade of off hw and completion grades. Sometimes the quest is kinda tricky but it prepares you well for the tests since they are also from quest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took him in the fall and he was a great prof with interesting lectures. only 45% of the grade was tests and the rest was attendance, discussion posts, hw. super accessible outside of class and helpful. getting an A is very doable if you do the hw and practice problems.

Great guy, great demos, great class. If you can take him, do it. I wan't that great in physics in high school, but took Dr. Perera and was able to understand what was going on. Attendance and hw is a good part of the grade alone, so it's manageable with other STEM classes and set up for you to do well.

If you have any sort of background in physics, this course is a breeze. Extremely easy A, and homeworks are easy as well. Lectures are enjoyable and his demos are super helpful in explaining concepts. I would highly recommend him.

I think people fail to realize how much math is actually in physics. Dr. Perera is good, but he spends most of his lectures deriving equations rather than doing practice problems which didn't work too well for me. Other than that, his exams were manageable, and his course is set up to help you succeed.

Super nice professor! His lectures were ok and imo his homework/exams were easier than other physics profs. Grade cutoff is higher than normal (an A was a 94+) but because his exams were not bad, getting a good grade was manageable. His exams are similar to homeworks so study those. Also instapolls are graded for participation but you get drops.

Honestly, he is a great guy. I really enjoyed taking physics with him last semester. Lectures are mandatory because there are instapolls in class (you can not do them at home, DONT even try). HWs are on quest and exams are in the form of quest but in person. You do get to use a notes sheet during each of the exams. His lectures are engaging and fun

Fantastic professor. Material was conveyed very clearly, and in a way that closely aligned with the textbook provided as well as homework and tests. Was willing to provide the class with an opportunity to make up for a particularly rough test.

I'm so glad I took Dr. Perrera for Physics II! I'd heard horror stories about other Physics professors, but Dr. Perera was an amazing professor. I had health issues all throughout the semester, and Dr. Perera was accommodating to me and was understanding of my situation. His class is an easy A if you put in the work.

Great professor but didn't let me reschedule my final when i caught the flu lol. so i took the final sweating my ass off and dizzy af but i still got an A+ because he prepared me so well. so def take him if possible but don't get sick

One of the very best professors I've ever had, for any subject. Physics is tough, but his lectures make everything clear, with good demos, notes, and practice problems, all of which are saved and recorded on his canvas page. There were no surprises on tests, and they were very easy if you put in the work. He is the professor to take for PHY 303K.

Dr. Perera is one of the best professors I've had at UT! Lectures were super engaging and he is just an overall sweet professor!!! Go to class, ask questions, and make sure you understand the Quest homework, and I guarantee you'll get an A in the class.

9 AM class & instapolls were graded, so it was hard for ME to wake up that early. Tests were very similar to homework & both were not terribly difficult. Exam 3 was a curveball though; questions were not expected. He said he was experimenting, so it makes me think the class *may* be harder next sem. Lectures were a bit hard to follow. Good overall.

Amazing professor! He is so good at explaining physics in a way that makes it less intimidating and easy to understand. Interesting in-class demos and reading are assigned before every class. You can tell that he cares about the well-being of students and is always open to questions.

Perera is an incredible professor and very obviously an extremely gifted educator. Attendance is mandatory and my discussion section was really late for some reason, so that was annoying. Textbook is openstax. All the tests were very fair and a high A is extremely attainable.

Such a great professor for physics, if you get him you're a very lucky student because he's a great teacher. Attendance is mandatory, takes it through instapolls. Tests are fair but study and textbook is online. Homework once a week. Overall very fair class in comparison to other physics classes so take his!

Dr. Perera is a very caring professor. Attendance is mandatory, but he still records his lectures which helps a lot.  He explains most topics well and is very clear on what you are expected to learn. Tests are quest-based and are very similar to the homework. If you took high school physics and put some effort into this class it should be an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera just started teaching and is already a legend. 35% of the grade is completion/attendance, 2 short Quest hw per week, 3 midterms with decent class averages and lowest is dropped. Very engaging lectures and he is always approachable. I originally heard that Physics 1 at UT was impossible but he makes it a stress-free class and experience.

I took PHY303K with Dr. Perera.

So thankful I chose him this semester, he teaches very comprehensible and gives amazing & fun lectures with lots of interesting demonstrations throughout the lecture.

His tests are easy if you know how to solve his Quest problems (which some are almost HS physics level).

Make sure to know fundamentals and excel!

Took this class over the summer during session 2 and it was probably one of the best decisions I could have made. Physics 2 was way easier over the summer, even with the accelerated timeline as Dr. Perera was very accommodating with one exam drop and all exams mostly resembling the homework. Practice the HW/custom quest reviews and you will do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall good class. Some parts he could have taught better, but I was in his first semester at UT. Very lenient and dropped a test for our class.

Took this over the summer so things went by pretty fast. Exams can be difficult, there are not many exam questions so each one is worth a lot. The textbook is not that helpful, I would pay more attention to the homework and lectures because that is where test questions are pulled from. Overall it wasn't too bad, just don't fall behind.
W teacher 10/10
He is op. He is perfect
Awesome, teacher would take this college class again.
coool but like yeah
awesome cool nice teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: good nice preofeeseo
very good and nice
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is very good i would take him 1000 times.
he's amazing

Boring lectures to help prepare with the lab. Occasional quizzes and a short exam. Doesn't really help prep for lab. Overall, not super necessary or detrimental to doing well in the lab portion of the course.

Dr. Bahadur's lectures were very good. His exams are fair but comprise most of the grade. They are generally very similar to the samples he gives. Fall 2024 he provided extra credit to those that attended the final few lectures. He asks tough conceptual questions on his midterms, be prepared. Homework is generally much harder than any exam.

His class was very disorganized. He would quiz over material learned in class that day, giving us no time to study or ask questions, and the midterm was not a good representation of the class material. He also canceled office hours every week. Lectures were boring and low effort. Heat Transfer lab is also a lot of work in general so fair warning.

Good lecturer, great guy. He focuses on concepts during lectures and is always open to questions from the class during lectures. Sometimes his lectures would be a little bit hard to follow, but he always encouraged people to speak up if he needed to reiterate a topic. He generally also grades the exams pretty leniently.

Pretty decent lecturer, the lecture focuses mainly on concepts and doesn't do as many questions that apply the concepts to problems but the concepts are well explained. The tests are very straightforward and are not hard to do well in as far as fluids goes. Class is pretty test-heavy like many engineering classes but he curves fairly.

Professor VB is a good lecturer and you can tell he cares deeply about making great future engineers. The homeworks are easy, however, definitely study for the exams and work through his past exams as they are really good practice. His class is challenging, but an A is doable and you learn a lot! He also gives extra credit quizzes that are easy.

He focuses a ton on real world examples. It's one of the first classes I feel like I'm solving real world problems and bahadur teaches by example. He's a really generous grader on exams and posts previous exams to practice. He posts all his lectures notes online, so you don't have to read the boring book. Fluid mechanics is a tough subject tho

Doesn't teach anything in the class. No examples solved at all. The only thing he does during lectures is copies stuff from the summary section of the book. If u want to pass this class you must self study ftom the book and practice questions on your own.
i dont even know what to expect yet. but anything is better than Morgan Fong.

The programming assignments get increasingly hard through the semseter. There are many TA's but they have not been particulary active in helping students who have trouble with sessions being timed out in Gradescope. All assignments are graded with the auto-grader and no partial credit is given if you mess up the output of the code.

This class is not designed to be beginner friendly. It gets increasingly difficult fast and there are many assignments due each week as homework, some right after test days. The coding assignments are difficult with the autograder which is super finickly and often gives 0's for timed out sessions. Be prepared to suffer. A lot of AI is involved.
by far the worst teacher I have had. save your time and your GPA don't take this class. she's nice, but she has no clue on how to teach, just save take any other professor

This teacher makes people's lives harder. Content is not hard but she explains it in the most abysmal way possible. Can't understand why UT choose for her to teach a very important theory class like this!

Wow her tests were so easy, and she's actually like one of the nicest people ever. She is excited about the topics she talks about, but she isn't the best lecturer, and you sort of ending up learning the whole class with the TAs. Take her over Parikh if possible!

This class is poorly organized, it is very easy to get overwhelmed and confused by the homework and assignments especially at the beginning of the semester. Honestly, the reviews make it sound way worse than it actually is. Before you enroll, inform god that you will be sitting with the devil twice a week.

Lowkey just be ready to do the textbook problems, class isn't done completely yet so like if I do bad in the final it's on me lowkey and I deserve a bad grade. Take her over Parikh, easier tests. She isn't as bad as everyone else is saying. For the first unit, its ok because you can learn by yourself. Then, the next two units get ready to suffer.

Proper viewing of the amazing lectures is almost mandatory not only for the grade but also the process of learning. This is a very useful class for personal finance as well which helped interest me during the lectures. Additionally, the class is very clear cut and doing all the exercises and quizzes throughout the course helps a lot for the exams.

the TA's atleast for my semester were terrible compared to my other math classes ive had. you have chatter to ask questions about any of the assignments but they take days to reply or dont give you an answer at all...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is only two exams and a "final" if you need to replace a midterm. Overall the class is pretty self explanatory and self paced but boring. The assignments can be long and time consuming. Tests are not proctored and make up most of ur grade. Professor seems nice but I didnt need to interact with him ever.

Sweet sweet man. I loved this class and Verduzco so much. If you're like me and are typically really bad at math but enjoy it when you understand it, this class is for you. Prof. Verduzco was so funny and I loved him as a teacher. I would 100% take this again!

Weekly modules were very manageable and the videos he posts cover all information that you need. Kind of boring content but not difficult to get an A. Exams aren't difficult, but take awhile so make sure you pace yourself.

Nice guy, not very personal but to the point with lectures. Can go a bit too fast and lecture slides are not 100% available outside of class. Pay attention, don't be afraid to ask questions, and show up to class if doing in person. It is not that difficult if you do those.

Take this class if you want to take exams that are nothing like the class assignments or practice exams. The concepts are actually fairly simple and easy to understand but I just felt that the exams were full of trick questions worded oddly. Definitely difficult for the scope of this class. I studied for 5 days for the final and still struggled.

Dr. Verduzco was a lousy lecturer that didn't explain concepts and practice problems well, even when you took the time to email him about test problems. Forward through the lectures and do many many practice problems in order to prepare for the tests. He gives a curve at the end ranging from 0.5-1 points on your final grade.

This class was online and very fun to go through. 2 exams and 1 final optonal to drop lowest and drops in all copmontents. Class was self paced so it was up to you to learn. Super easy if you studied and did every assignment with notes. Note everything he says. Exams are not proctored. Practice the problems and it should be easy a.

For most of this class, I had no issues with this professor. Deadlines are absolute. The reason Im giving him such a low score is because of the absolute power trip this man goes on for the final. You cannot move your final unless you have a conflicting exam. No exceptions. Grandpa died? Medical issues? House burned down? This man does not care.

The async class was fine, especially with study partners. The concepts are simple, mainly involving reading tables and basic addition/subtraction. Exams are async, and you can skip the final if your grade is good enough. Overall, I didn't learn much from the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though the Professor was lively during the online lectures, he was so useless when it came to the exams and some assignments. The tests were completely different from reviews that we were given and overall the resources in this course were not helpful at all.

He was so rude and unprofessional. He is not very understanding at all, and lacks empathy for students. The exams were so difficult and most people I know as well as myself bombed them. Never turn in anything LATE because he will not take partial credit. I wish I hadn't taken this class. Would not recommend. Only take this class if u really need.

Professor Verduzco is AMAZING!!!! Seriously one of the best professors that I have had at UT. He truly cares about his students and will do anything to help them succeed. He does instapolls every class for participation and practice. Go to class!!! He makes lectures interesting and its easier to follow along in person than it is online!
Easy and straightforward class, lectures are good but need to be on 2x speed. Do the modules and use the same formulas on exams and you're chilling. Courseload is probably 2-3 hours every 1.5 weeks.

THIS CLASS IS HARD!!! Professor Verduzco is hard to reach, his lectures can get confusing real quick. The textbook is honeslty useless. The class isn't horrible but you have to work really hard for an A. He makes it too difficult, and if you bomb the Exam (which most people did) you're in trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Verduzco teaches the material well, but the class is challenging. The exams are tough and require detailed notes - using Unstuckstudy ai for practice problems helped me prepare. Stay on top of the work, form study groups, and you can get an A. Overall, a worthwhile class.

This class is for those who are non-business majors, but the professor taught it like it was for business majors. We would cover formulas in the online lecture and use the same process during the quizzes. However, he would not follow this during the exam. This slows down getting through the exam which is timed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was far more difficult than necessary due to poor explanations that required many students to rewatch lectures constantly. No need to buy the textbook, as it's overpriced and more confusing than the lectures. Slow to reply to emails, and repeatedly refused to add approved exam accommodations until I threatened to get the D&A office involved.

I took 17 hours, and 6 courses as a BCH major... and somehow this course caused me the most suffering. This professor isn't great in regards to how his lectures translate to graded assignments and exams. The lectures are boring. Also, the first exam comes as quite a shock seeing how easy all the practice was. Thankfully, he drops an exam.
Really nice professor who teaches the content very well. If you stay on top of the work, it's a pretty straight forward class.

I got C's on the Exam 1&2 b/c Idigitally write notes and it was a STRUGGLE scrolling. Exams are open-note 50%, TYPE all notes in a doc and write down EVERY thing he says (his lectures are good). I made a huge doc for the 3rd exam and control F for it got me a literal 99 on it. Lowest of 3 exams dropped. Exams much harder than practice problems.

The tests are 50% of the grade and they are a bit challenging. But, it is very doable to get an A if you stay diligent with the notes/practice. Start studying for tests min 4 days in advance, take very detailed notes (tests are open-note) and do all the practice he gives and you should be fine. The rest is quizzes and assignments which are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Verduzco is a nice guy and good professor, this class is just difficult. Practice exams were not comparable to the actual exams, actual exams were way harder. DEFINITELY take this class in-person if possible, probably would not have done well if I was taking it online.

Honestly, if you do the work it is a simple class. The exams aren't bad and he drops your lowest one. The assignments are open for a long time, and they're pretty self-explanatory. Its just grouping numbers with categories for a whole semester and doing some middle school math.

This class was challenging but doable. Highly suggest studying for test in groups, and working on the assignments with others. Tests were weighted very heavily (two tests, one optional final) and there's barely any extra credit. Tests asked about very niche things and require problem-solving, and the textbook wasn't that helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he seems like such a fun and sweet man, but his exams... do not be gaslit into taking a business minor for funsies

I SUCK at math! Class mandatory for business minor; (as a senior I had no choice) .Great teacher, but if not for the group me I would have failed. 50% & 43% on both exams (worth 50%); got help from classmates on assignments (got A's) = C- in course. A dub is a dub ! but pls ask for help if math isn't ur strong suit! He WON'T do favors so DONT ask!
This class is pretty easy but you actually have to watch the lecture videos online to do well. The tests are kind of difficult but can be done.
Videos were very entertaining and engaging. However, the exams were very difficult. The exams are way harder than the quizzes on the modules and assignments. Great professor but hard exams.

Yikes. I'm pre-med and this class is harder than either of my genchem courses as no matter how much you study, you will see questions on the exam that you've never seen before and that are honestly unfair. Exams are nothing like the practice problems he teaches. I was really excited about his liveliness and class at first - now I'm disappointed.

Class is very interesting and gives you a pretty solid accounting base. However, 50% percent of the grade is based on 2/3 exams that are way more difficult than anything covered in lectures. Even the practice problems provided include topics not covered in class. Take the class at ACC if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David Verduzco is a great professor, the video lectures in the online class are great and he explains the topics thoroughly. HOWEVER, the exams are much harder than the practice material, worth 50% for 2 tests. Be sure to study ahead of time, he provides practice exams, but they are easier than the real exam. Doable class, pay attention to details.

You will do well if you pay attention and take advantage of all the practice questions. What's frustrating is the assignments - I would get all of the answers correct on them but still lose points for reasons I'll never know because you don't get feedback. When I reached out for this I was given vague explanations so it was difficult to improve.
The only B I ever got at UT so far. His tests are ridiculously hard and does not prepare you for them whatsoever. Look for another prof

i think the online course is organized well. there is a module each week with 3 participation grades (u get 3 tries) and sometimes 1 assignment a module. the videos are clear and he gives good examples. the tests are weighted heavily (50%) but i feel like his exams arent as hard as everybody says they are. theres a lot of content but its easyish

1/2 your grade easy to do. HW + quizzes get multiple attempts, find a helpful group chat if you're stuck. However, the tests are pretty difficult. If you are a last-minute studier you will struggle. You NEED to find outside practice problems for the math. Take previous years' exams and practice exams and you will be okay. Can use notes on exams.

Prof. Verduzco's teaching content and approach is awesome. The lecture videos and demo problems are really helpful. However, I think his exams are unnecessarily difficult. A lot of students could have done better if the exams weren't weighted so high and if the questions were more suited to the time that is given. Also bad at answering emails.

I loved the format of Verduzco's online class. He made things very structured and easy to hone in on certain concepts. The tests were a little nerve-wracking but I think he really does everything he can to help you do well.  Need to study though to do well, so you have to do your due diligence on your part as well. Overall he's a great professor!

Verduzco's asynch layout was great. Typically had 1 module per week where there's 5ish videos on concepts with participation exercises and quizzes throughout w/ multiple attempts. He was a fantastic lecturer where his videos are concise. However, his EXAMS ARE HARD BUT DOABLE. You need to have a deep understanding of A LOT OF CONTENT. I rec. him

Verduzco is a very tough grader. There are essentially only practice quizzes and participation quizzes that count as grades, which were not bad at all, but when it came to the exam it's much harder. Essentially if someone in your family isn't dead and you have documentation to provide as proof, you won't be able to redo any assignment/test.

The way this class is structured kinda sucks. It's very organized but he does not set you up for success on the exams AT ALL. There are two practice exams for each exam that prob helped with 1/4 of the questions on the exam. Also ur grade completely depends on 3 exams. Like the participation quizzes/ modules due every week barely matter. STUDY HARD
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor. Tests do not match practice questions. You can study for hours and know the material and not do well, along with the added pressure of very limited time to complete the test. In addition to this, TA appeared to not even understand the material themselves during office hours and the prof. essentially told you to "figure it out."

I took his async class. Gave lots of practice examples in the lectures with similar problems on the quizzes/tests. 2 tests, 1 final, but he drops one. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS! they help a lot (he gives explanations for the answers) and can use on the tests as they're open note.
I never read the textbook and did fine with just the lecture material

Great professor! The class is challenging, but if you enjoy the material like I do, then you can easily make an A or B. Otherwise, you may not like this class. The professor was very nice and understanding especially regarding technical difficulties. Attendance and paying attention will help you succeed tremendously.

Daily work is pretty easy, just read a chapter and do the modules. You have one week to do the work, but it takes about maybe 2 hours. The tests are the hardest part, there is definitely not enough time to complete them so work fast. But he does replace one of the 2 tests if you score higher on the final exam.

This prof was super enthusiastic and made it interesting, even though I had no prior interest. It's pretty straight forward and easy to get through. Tests have a curve, but theres only 2 of them. Would definitely recommend enrolling with friends to study together.

Fully online so it's up to you to do good. Daily work is easy, you get multiple tries. Exams are extremely difficult and honestly you need more time than what is given. Overall better to take online that in person, but be ready to study and work hard.

Very light class with some introduction to accounting topics. Ideas flowed well and expectations built on each other in a reasonable way. Lectures were concise and generally engaging. If there's any big problem with the class, it's the lack of depth in topics discussed and general lack of open-ended questions and feedback throughout the course.

I HATED this course so much. I took this course because it was a beginners course for non-business majors but the professor expected a lot and moved fast. He never gave enough time on assignments because there were steps that needed to be done and if they were rushed you could get the whole question wrong. Also his questions were not clear.

His lectures were very straightforward, but the quizzes and exams were quite challenging regarding time management. He expects you to understand the concepts and be able to apply the calculations. Overall, his class is great! I enjoyed it even though I don't have any accounting/ finance background. He curves at the end also, which is great.

I had heard bad things about accounting, but Dr. Verduzco taught the material very well. He recommended we print out the notes at the start of the year and everything we covered was exactly what we needed for assignments and test. He dropped the lowest of the 2 midterms and final, so I didn't even need to take it. He's a great professor!

I took the summer Asynch version for my business credit and I would not recommend it. I have put countless hours into this course (readings, reviewing lectures, doing the practice problems, studying for the tests) and I still feel entirely lost. There is an overwhelming amount of course content shoved into ~3 months. This ate up my entire summer.

His lectures are pretty good. The exams and quizzes can be very cutthroat and fast paced. If you take notes seriously and don't just click through everything you can get a good grade in the class. Do all of the assignments and triple check everything

He is a very good lecturer and has a clear grading structure with drops in each category. The tests sometimes have confusing or subjective answer choices, but a lot of the questions are based off of examples done in class. Self-paced class meant I could watch lectures whenever I wanted, which made it flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his online section, and everything was pretty clear cut. If you watch the lectures, do the homeworks, and quizzes you will be fine. The exams are not very difficult, especially since they follow the same structure as the 2 practice exams he posts. Overall, class gives many opportunities to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Took for business minor. Not a blowoff but it's still pretty easy. I took the asynchronous version so I did not interact with the professor but he seemed like a nice guy. Lectures and notes are solid. Good communication/coordination from professor. No real complaints but also nothing super memorable. This was one of the classes of all time.

Verduzco is a great professor and really good at explaining concepts. The class itself is also pretty easy as long as you pay attention to the lecture, literally everything is either word for word of similar but with the numbers changed. Go to office hours if you're struggling with something. It's not a complete blow off but still pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't slack bc of the reviews-- u have to WORK in this class for that A. best advice i can give: FIND A STUDY GROUP! he's v clear during lectures but the tests/quizzes have tricky questions!! and ALWAYS do the practice exams before tests!! imo the quizzes are harder bc there's no practice quizzes for it so be prepared!!

Class was good, hard mainly because of the quizzes. A lot of tricky questions and even some that contradicted the textbook which was annoying. I enjoyed how he taught in the modules, but I sometimes struggles with quiz and test questions even after studying quite a bit. Still got an 89 which at least for this year counted as an A- which was nice!

super sweet and easy prof! doesn't make module vids too long and explains each topic in an easy and uncomplicated way. just make sure to rly understand the material in each module and you'll be fine for tests. always available on chatter and posts practice exams and quiz questions so you can be prepared!
A surprisingly tricky class as the assignments and especially the tests have some trick questions and very weirdly worded questions that can get points docked. Lectures quite well

He was a very nice person but the class is hard for no reason. The material is easy until the exam comes. There is not a lot of time given to do all the calculations. Also, the TAs never responded to any of my emails.

Great teacher. The asynchronous class is very organized. Each module is released with multiple lecture videos as well as participation problems. The quizzes and tests are a little more difficult than the example problems so be sure to deeply understand the concept and equations. Overall great teacher and very kind!

Don't let  bad reviews scare you if you're good at quantitative stuff or a stem major this class is super easy. His lectures are very well organized and he  drops a bunch of grades including the lowest exam. It is test heavy and the questions can be tricky but if you take good notes you'll be fine. assignments were a bit tedious which was annoying.

Very organized class, and he assigns 1 learning module/week, making the pace super manageable. The content is really easy, but it's easy to mess up because you do lots of calculations. He provides so much practice. Textbook is not necessary, but its helpful. A lot of people view this as a blowoff class and they end up doing poorly. Take it asynch!

Many people who hate on him have never taken a STEM class before, and it shows, lol. It really isn't that bad; I would say it is comparable to a stats class, maybe a little bit harder because, I will not lie, he does ask some tricky questions. That being said, I liked it, and his lectures were fun. EC of 2 points on grade at the end. TAKE ASYNC!

I was a bit hesitant going into this class, but Professor Verduzo is such a great professor. His class is very organized, and he teaches accounting concepts in a very clear way. The exams are worth a lot, but if you put in the effort, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Honestly this class was really difficult for me and I wouldn't recommend taking it if you don't have to. The quizzes, tests, and assignments are hard and will contain trick questions. Aside from that, professor Verduzco is insanely nice and the class is very organized. 1 exam is dropped and there are other drops in the class as well.

during class, there are small group and insta polls taken to count attendance and they are participation grade. there are a lot of assignments, around 6, that take quite some time to complete. there are three exams, but the lowest gets dropped so don't have to take the last! 7/10 really not that bad
This course is just generally hard. Verduzco is a good professor but I found the class unnecessarily hard, especially the first few modules. If you want an A, get ready to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy and a great lecturer. His lectures were easy to understand and explained well. However, the assignments were very tedious (if you mess up one part of an assignment you will likely miss most of the questions that follow). He does not give partial credit. The class is based on a few grades (mostly 3 exams), but you get to drop your lowest.
Good professor, all work is online

The questions he assigned were unclear about important aspects of the question that determined if the answer was correct. He also assigned long questions with multiple steps and didn't give enough time to complete the questions. He has attendance points and despite my doc note he REFUSED to give me attendance credit when I missed class for SURGERY.

He makes the questions hard by writing them without clarifying important things. He wouldn't take my doctors note to excuse my attendance when I literally had surgery.  He doesn't give enough time for the questions he asks.

Verduzco himself is a great guy & amazing lecturer. Definitely take asynchronously bc he talks slow and you can just speed the lectures up. Layout of the modules makes it easy to stay on track, but this is DEFINITELY not a class to brush off. Pay attention, study materials he gives you, and you'll do fine. Spent about 4 hrs/week on this class.

Took this class for the business minor, not as bad as I thought it would be, however you MUST pay attention to succeed. Really wish this class wasn't online but besides that professor verduzco is very funny, and explains concepts well. Most assignments are super easy, however he does not give enough time for Quizzes/ Exams, so be sure to work fast

Course was engaging, liked that he played music. Have the notes in front of you and work through problems as he goes through them, try to actually answer the instapolls. It will help you succeed! Between practice exams + reviewing assignments, participation exercises, and quizzes I felt more than prepared for the tests and thought I learned a lot!

Took the course asynchronously. Teaches the concepts he needs to teach and very easy to grasp knowledge. However, some exam questions are sort of ambiguous and can be tricky. Just prepare well and study with others.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Get a study group! Very low workload. Drops one exam, two quizzes, and one homework. Funny guy and entertaining lectures.

Verduzco was a great professor who taught well but it was difficult. One think I do recommend is to form a study group and do all the practice problems given. Extra help is necessary to do well in this course. Although the time situations with quizzes and exams really makes or break a grade. I believe you can do well. Be prepared for a challenge.

For awhile, I procrastinated on registering for this class because I was scared it was going to drop my GPA. Do not let these reviews scare you! Trust yourself and your abilities. Re-watch lecture videos if you need to and make sure you understand the practice problems. To prep for exams, just do the practice tests he puts up!

This was an asynchronous class so the lectures were pre-recorded videos. The class was very well organized from the start. Exams and quizzes were difficult because there is a time limit but as long as you do the practice exams and learn some basic excel, these can become simple. You get drops on every type of assignment so one bad test grade is ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really easy content and not much work (< 2 hours a week total). Tests sometimes have pretty dumb questions where multiple answers seem correct, but it's an easy A either way.

Tough class. Very test heavy (60%) and the margin for error is quite slim. The content isn't that difficult to grasp, but quiz and test questions are rarely similar to what he covers in class. Calculation questions are pretty easy, but mc is hard. You also get little time to do the assessments. Everything is open book, but you will need to study.

terrible class tbh. 310F was so difficult, VERY exam heavy. wouldve been better if this class was offered in person instead of online. professor barely explained content and if he did, it was difficult to understand. im no longer a business minor after this class

One of my favorite personas during my freshman year of UT. He's kind, funny, and really sounds like he loves his job. The class is VERY straightforward and he makes accounting concepts really easy to understand. I would be cautious of the strict grading policy and how some of the work may not feel as familiar. Also seems to love Chipotle a lot.
A great class to take overall.

He is a nice man, but a pretty harsh professor. His exams are really tough and he barely gives you any time, nor does he accommodate well for students with disabilities. This class is tough, but sadly he is the only one who teaches it, so good luck charlie. Rewatch the lectures as much as you can and pray.

Proffesor Verduzco was great! This class if definitily  not an easy A and you have to watch all the lectures and practice to do well. This class took up most of my time but he was a good professor and i actually feel like i learned alot.
This class made me drop the whole business minor lol good luck. Maybe you have better luck in joining the synchronous class, but do not do asynch! You will fall behind and do terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really randomly structured class. Tests are incredibly difficult and horribly timed (30 math heavy long questions in 75 mins). Quizzes horrible too and he springs them on u. The material itself isn't too tough but the class is just not structured well; if he changed the way the class was set up, it'd be much better
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The best accounting professor you will get tbh, sure his class is structured tough (exams are 60% of your grade), but his lectures are rlly good. Ig it helps that I kinda like accounting... but seriously don't know why his ratings are so low. You have to try ... if you expect to just have an A without studying then idk what to tell you.

His lectures are great he gives you notes that you fill out throughout the class but the 2 exams make up a big portion of your grade. The tests are open-note, but I wouldn't rely so much on your notes due to the time limit and the questions being more concept based. If you keep up with the work and pay attention to lectures you will do fine.

I really liked this professor. For the synchronous version of this class, attendance is mandatory. His lectures are straight-forward and only basic arithmetic is required to do well. Tests and quizzes are open-note, and, personally, the amount of time to complete them is doable. Taking the final is optional and grade cutoffs may be lowered.

The lectures are great and very clear. He even gives you notes to fill out along with him. However, the class was very test-heavy (60% exams). Other grades are made up of quizzes, participation exercises, and multi-question assignments. It's tough doing decent on the other assignments just to get a C on the tests and it severely affect your grade.

Really easy class and one of the best professors. We only covered 2 slide decks for the entirety of the semester. Most of the content is straightforward and only basic arithmetic is required for this course. Drops lots of different grades and lowered the cutoff grades for the spring 2022 semester.

Asynchronous. He is a really good lecturer, I would recommend. Pretty easy class, some of the quizzes and test questions would trip me up. A bit harder than it may seem at first, but still not toooo difficult. Basic math. I loved the asynchronous option of the class. I would finish the units quickly and not have to worry about it for a week!

Verduzco is a nice guy but a mid professor. His structure for the class SUCKS. 2 exams the entire semester is a lot of information to be tested over and theyre worth so much as well. There's no chance of recovery from a bad grade in this course however he lets you take the final optionally to better your grade. He's lucky hes the only acc prof here
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class moves too fast unnecessarily. Dr. Verduzco is a great lecturer and provides a lot of opportunities in class for practice. The class content is interesting and the lectures are helpful, however, all quizzes and exams give very, very little time which I found a bit excessive.

He is really great at teaching. He is clear and gives examples with you during class. You have to work and spend the take the time to ask questions and do the practice problems. He gives you everything you need to succeed. The grade you get is up to you. This is no easy class, it requires practice and studying a moderate amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had to write a review because I took this course Fall 2021, and I feel like the other reviews from this same semester give the wrong impression. All you have to do is watch the lectures, take notes, follow the tips given by David to do well in the course, and go to office hours when confused and you will do fine. Time on exams was adequate.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very clear lecture videos. Assignments are easy. Exams need you to be very familiar with all the concepts for accuracy and time. Recommend to make a summary for each module so that you can apply them in exams, otherwise you will feel that there are too many concepts that you can't organize them.

Lecture's and assignment's were great + easy to understand and apply knowledge. Tests were horrible. Very little time and ALWAYS much harder than anything else we've done. Tests are 60% of your grade and are near impossible. Not to mention, he's the type of teacher to have an assignment due on Thanksgiving. Not sure how he is rated so high on here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took asynchronous, and finishing lecture videos was quick and simple. Lecture videos? AMAZING to understand. Assignments that go w/ lectures? EASY, always got an A. Quizzes and Exams? Dead HORRIBLE. Ridiculous time limit that always screwed everyone over. I HIGHLY recommend using Quizlet to make a formula sheet/step-by-step guide during exams.
Prof Verduzco gives good lectures and explains concepts clearly, but the exams are difficult and the time limits don't help either. I'm glad I changed this class to pass/fail.

Professor Verduzco is very nice, has a good lecture pace, and his lectures are generally exhaustive enough to where you can probably get an A with no textbook. However it is the middle of finals week, and all the students are fighting tooth and nail with him to just to tell us what day our final exam is going to be lmao.

Absolutely the worst class Ive ever taken. Class grade is mainly off tests and they are ridiculously hard. Practice barely helps. He wins worst professor award. Even though he does teach decently, his tests are far harder than what we should be able to do. Time limit for the test is also an issue. He literally curves your average down. Dont take!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class asynchronously if you are not good at math. I have never struggled in school and I took this class and had so much trouble. I basically taught myself everything and all of it was new to me. I failed all the tests after studying. Verduzco was nice and I'm sure my experience would have been way better if I took this in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Accounting can be HARD, but Verdusco makes it easier to understand plus he is very engaging. Definetely take him, he is a nice man.

I took the asynchronous class. Dr. Verduzco is a great instructor! He is upbeat during lecture and gives good, clear examples of problems and what is expected. Weekly assignments needed only a couple hours' work. Exams had a bit more complex problems than the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Asynchronous Summer 2021. About 1 day's worth of work per week, multiple attempts for the practice quizzes so it was easy to get full points on those. He covered all topics and formulas needed for quizzes & tests. My only complaint is that 2 tests made up 60% of the grade and an A is 94%+. The tests had some curveballs too, which didn't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Participation matters

reviews.comment: i took the asynchronous version and liked how it was organized. the weekly modules were easy to understand and the embedded exercises were really good practice. the quizzes and exams could be tricky. math/calc questions were easy but concept questions were worded very specifically, so pay attention and be careful! no ec but a couple of drops.

I took this class online. It was very hard for me and caused me a lot of stress. I think the most stressful thing for me was the time limits, EVERYTHING IS TIMED. It is a very test heavy class. Wouldnt take again, but Im proud of myself for getting a A-. NO EXTRA CREDIT PERIOD dont even ask haha, however I did learn a lot. Expect to study a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Verduzco was always super friendly and generally lectured well, though some were a bit boring. The only negative thing about the class is the exams, as they make the large majority of your grade, so one bad one and you're already sunk. Just make sure to study and read the textbook.

Participation exercises and assignments are easy since he encourages collaboration. For quizzes and tests, the calculation type questions are easy and similar to questions done before, but the concept questions can be tricky especially the "how many of the following" questions. Open note tests. Lowest grade(s) in each category gets dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Despite some concerns about the exams, I think using the textbook really helped me in this class. Professor Verduzco encourages practicing in it quite a bit and you're going to need it. Easy recommendation

I took this class asynchronously for the spring semester, and I think Professor Verduzco is such a gem. He explains the concepts very patiently and clearly. 3 exams (1 is optional) take up 60% of your grade. If you take notes and review carefully, it's totally an easy A. Textbooks are not that helpful (they do sometimes though).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very relaxed course with very few assignments and interesting material; HOWEVER, this course is NOT an easy A. The exams/quizzes are tricky, and wording on conceptual questions CAN be ambiguous as it can be interpreted in different ways. The exams are hard due to this, so watch out for "How many of these are true" type questions on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: if youre taking this class as a GPA booster. dont. i aced all his quizzes and assignments but ended up doing bad on his exams because theyre worth 60% of your grade and getting an overall poor grade in the course. the quizzes and exams have super tricky questions and he barely gives you time to finish them.

Verduzco is such a sweet guy that cares about accounting and how you do in the course. He is enthusiastic and makes lectures bearable, he gives clear examples and his notes are well structured. Quizzes and tests are hard but if you study you should be successful.

Overall enjoyed the class and didn't think it was too difficult. Verduzco is always very enthusiastic and engaging during lecture and the course was very organized. As long as you take notes and pay attention, it isn't difficult to do well on the exams.

As a STEM major taking the business minor, this was an overall easy class and a great prof who explained examples in detail. Saying that though 60 percent of your grade comes from 2 midterms and there are a few conceptual questions that are tricky. Easy A- but hard A in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class asynchronously and enjoyed it overall. He is very good at explaining the concepts during lectures and I feel like I understood everything thoroughly. The online quizzes and exams are very fast, however. Make sure to pay attention to his lectures. While they were optional, they helped tremendously.

I was in the asynchronous version of the course, and I felt that Professor Verduzco's lectures and structure of the course was not very effective. I thought the quizzes and exams were difficult and had some tricky or confusing wording. I personally would not recommend the asynchronous version of the course-I'm not sure about the synchronous.

The class was pretty interesting and material was simple - on the surface. Verduzco's tests are full of tricks, so it is easy to mess up on the conceptual questions. He is really nice/accessible during office hours though and provides a lot of resources. The workload is not too bad, but make sure you study for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was okay overall. The quizzes were unnecessarily hard just because we weren't given enough time to complete them which didn't make sense because the point is to test us on how well we know the subject, not how quickly we can do math. Still, as long as you do well on everything else you should be fine.

Good lecturer. Tests and quizzes are tricky. Quizzes were only 20 minutes long to do a lot of calculations, and concept questions are harder than math ones. Could get by w/o a textbook, but you should find it online for free if you want an A. Stay on top of material. Tests account for almost whole grade, and one dropped exam among three.

Professor Verdusco is very smart in regards to accounting. He does a good job of explaining test material in class. However, there are a lot of complimentary assignments that don't account for much. 60% of your grade is determined by your two top test scores. Nevertheless I think he's good.

Professor gives tricky and specific questions when it comes to tests . Tests are worth more than half your grade. Yes there is a long break between tests but any silly mistakes like rounding wrong or not carefully reading will get you! Even if you know the concepts like the back of your hand the test will trick you and have you looking dumb
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Little to no feedback on assignments/quizzes, and when feedback is given the explanation is unhelpful. Questions are always vague with some confounding variable to 'trick' students. Most questions seem nonsensical/nit-picky, cannot pass from only the textbook. Prof literally uses diff formulas for certain calculations, you must do things his way.

His quizzes are ridiculous. I watched all the lectures, took note carefully, created charts for calculation, sometimes read the book as well. But I did badly on the tests/quizzes still and I don't know why. I got the calculation mostly right, but the concept questions are extremely tricky sometime and they are not even covered in class. DON'T TAKE!
I didn't take for credit cause it was during COVID and I gave up, but it's a super easy A. Legit don't show up and pass. Open note everything. Optional final. What a G
Pretty cool guy. Tests werent very great when it came to timing. This was mainly bc we had to fill in charts and do calculations. Tbh a bit harder than I had imagined, but doable.
I'd like to say I'm pretty good at math, but this class was awful. Concept questions trick you up more than some of the math.

Verduzco is a very mediocre professor and assigns A LOT of work. There is hw due before every class. Also, he will not round your grades no matter how close you are to an A (I was less than 0.7% away from an A, and he didnt round it).

This class is hard considering its for non-business majors. 2 test + optional finals, homework due before every class, 5 group assignments so make sure you make friends in class, and multiple quizzes. The quizzes were really hard especially conceptual(harder than exams). Exams are online open note. Nice guy but no room to negotiate grades ever
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good, organized lecturer, even when class transitioned online. Most assessments are done through canvas, except for about 6 "group projects" which are easy to get done during class. Quizzes and tests are timed, which was more of a problem for the quizzes than the tests. The A cutoff is a 94, so you have to be very careful to not lose any points.

You have participation quizzes every week but they're pretty easy. The exams and other quizzes are all on canvas. I found them to be a little challenging since they have a time limit. Overall, Professor Verduzco was great! He will help you on any questions you have.

Literally a game show host. Lectures are scenario questions he works through and then has you do your own, so if you don't go to lecture you'll have a blank ppt slide. Studied 3 days before exam, but GO TO CLASS! Def doable but not an "easy A." Don't buy the textbook. Exams are 30 mult-choice Canvas q's set up like the group assignments + quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Has fill-in-the-blank notes that are helpful during lectures. Quizzes and tests are hard because there's often not enough time and there are some questions that are from the textbook that he doesn't even discuss in class. PLUS sessions are extremely helpful, so go to those. Know how to do the math for problems and you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His answers are sometimes unhelpful. Pop Quizzes: 20-min limit stressful when doing quick calculations. 2 Online Exams: 30 Qs (fill-in/MC) & open-note like long quizzes. Concept questions are hard bc we mainly practice math. Group Assignments: Like class practice. Easy if you're in a good group. Attend PLUS. Optional final. Don't need textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes were the main issue I had with this class. They are timed and there was just no time to do the calculations necessary. It hurt my grade and it was so frustrating because I knew the material and did well on participation exercises, group assignments, and Tests. The timing on the quizzes were just off and i felt like i never had time to think
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy
