reviews.comment: Fine class. Lectures were very bland and he was boring to listen to but he got the information across moderately well. Tests were not too difficult and he lets you drop your lowest test score. Pop quizzes on information we did not fully understand yet hurt my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's been teaching this course for a while so he has the structure of the course down. He can go pretty fast sometimes but he posts the lecture slides ahead of time. Content is not too hard, annoying part is constant participation exercise before each class, online quizzes that don't have enough time and mandatory group projects.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I fully understood the course content but failed every quiz/exam and had to drop the class. Quizzes and exams are timed, and it is IMPOSSIBLE to finish in time and check your work. If you must take it (but DON'T), go to the PLUS sessions, the student leaders are far more helpful than he ever was and not condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good lectures but theres a lot of material. 3 exams, no final, one drop. HW every week and about 7 quizzes. Easier if you make friends in the class for group assignments. Everything else is online and open note. Took this class P/F. He sometimes words questions weirdly and exams/ quizzes are timed which can be stressful bc theres lots of math.

An amazing prof who genuinely cares about what he teaches and his students. Actually makes accounting fun to go to everyday. I would recommend going to class just because it makes life easier when it comes to testing, but you dont necessarily have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are very entertaining and he tells corny jokes which made me laugh. You get to use notes on online quizzes and exams. Optional final. Does not round :/ so 89.9 was a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I did not like the structure of the notes and examples. There was so much going on from the previous slides that is relevant to the current that it was difficult keeping up. Nice guy, fair with grading and exams, but sometimes it was really boring and practice problems were dull
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Okay class and okay professor. The quizzes and tests were frustrating in that they had weirdly specific word questions on things we'd never learned in class and weren't explained in the textbook either. So it's pretty difficult to do very well in class even putting in extra effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was the most frustrating class that I have taken in my academic career. I knew the material and how to work problems yet the pointless, tricky worded questions on the tests and quizzes seem designed for your demise. Highly recommend NOT taking this robotic professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The tests for this class are timed, and there is basically no time. You can manage an A in the class if you try really hard but you do have to work for it. Quizzes are harder than tests but the tests are still somewhat hard. Also you fill in notes when you go to class and he goes over a lot per class. Missing class means missing important concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I got a 93.1, and that's considered an A- in his class?? so annoying. But his lectures were engaging, and I recommend printing out his slides (2 per page, double-sided) bc it makes lectures easy to follow. He does not curve bc of the mccombs "rule". Textbook is not necessary if you take adequate notes & pay attention in class.

Verduzco's class is set up in a way that forces you to fail. Random pop quizzes in class with super specific information on it that you've barely learned destroy your grade. Tests are online and many students will hire tutors to take it with them which kills the curve. Do not take if you can get credit elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I thought this class was fine. nothing too hard, nothing too easy. It is known for being the easiest of all the accounting classes offered at Mccombs. As long as you go to class and follow along you should be fine. Not bad at all. Verduzco knows what hes talking about!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an easy A, but can manage it with some effort. Hw is easy, quizzes r harder than the tests in my opinion, and he recycles some questions from both on the tests. He also gives 2 practice exams for each test, with similar questions to what you will see on the test. Minimal use of the book, only needed it for a couple of questions on quizzes/tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class isn't a breeze, but it's still a watered-down accounting class. Pay attention, take notes, find a good group, and you'll be fine. The participation exercises (3 tries) and quizzes (2 drops) and notes are all formatted like the exams (1 drop), and everything is open-note. I'd suggest taking notes on the ppt template he provides.

Show up and pay attention! This prof is really bad at answering questions even in office hours. Take really good notes because it will be difficult to go back and do the homework without good lecture notes. There are quizzes (5-6), participation homeworks (over 20), group assignments in class (5-6) and 2 exams with an optional final (cumulative).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I never thought that Accounting would be difficult, but Verduzco made it so. *Most* concepts were easy enough to work through, but some were so far out there to the point of frustration. My accountant friend reviewed one of the quizzes I had taken and said, huh? I just shook my head. Find a good group EARLY or you WILL struggle. Good drop policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Verduzco gives so much opportunities to make a decent grade in accounting. He drops three group assignments, two quizzes, and one exam! Most of the quizzes and all of the exams are online! However beware, he is really big on concepts for quizzes and exams. Please try not to miss class because you would regret it! Also choose your group mates wisely
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never gotten below a B+ in any classes in my whole life. I got a C+ and tried very hard. Dont even bother asking Verduzco a question in class because he will be extremely condescending, look at you like youre an idiot and wont answer the question anyways. The questions on his quizzes and exams are impossible, even though theyre open not

Verduzco was a cool professor. Very clear and defined layout of the class. Lectures were nice and easy to follow. Although it is very easy, you definitely have to go to class because there are pop quizzes and he doesn't post the full notes online. But as long as you go to class and take good notes, this class is a breeze. Very chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He won't post filled in notes, so you have to go to class to learn. Refused to answer some of the questions I asked and when he did answer them he refused to explain them. Tests are okay, there are three including the final and he drops one. Quizzes can be rough but group assignments are easy if you just pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I honestly hated this class. It wasn't hard for me, it was just tricky. Don't bother emailing him because you will send a formal email and he will respond with 3-6 improper grammar messages. He is just a very annoying professor. I would have rather taken it online.

Most of the content is taught in class, you really don't need the textbook at all. Group assignments save your grade and tend to be pretty easy. Tests and Canvas quizzes are open note, which helps a lot.

Must show up to class or office hours for the notes. Textbook is not necessary at all. Everything tested or quizzed over comes from class notes. Most graded activities are completed using personal notes, so an A is absolutely obtainable. He is obviously passionate but lectures can drag sometimes. Random group assignments/quizzes in class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He added tests this semester, so quizzes (which I thought were harder) weigh less. Once you get used to the structure of questions on quizzes, the tests aren't too bad. Practice exams are life savers for the tests. His explanations are easy to follow but it's pretty easy to zone out. Find smart people to work group assignments with.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was much easier than I expected it to be, if you know how to add, subtract, multiply, and divide then you already have 50% of the class covered and learned. The hard part is mostly the conceptual stuff which can be confusing since its not that interesting. Group projects are mandatory so find a squad before its too late!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Funny guy, he recently added exams to the class but it was probably for the better since the quizzes felt way harder and it used to be your only grades. Daily participation exercises, easy & drops 3. Dropped 2 quizzes. If you truly pay attention in class, you will be just fine. He does a lot of examples that relate to the ones on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The exercises in this class are pretty easy, but the exams are SO much harder than what you've been doing. Practice exam is also easier than the real test. There are 2 midterms and a final. The midterms are 30 questions and you only have 1 hour to do them, which is not enough time. Take this class only if you have the time to dedicate to it!!!

I took the Foundations of Accounting Summer Online class, which was one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Since it is largely self-paced, if you stay on top of the deadlines every week, then you will do well. The problems come when waiting until the last day to get through all the materials. This class was taught by a team of instructors.

His class is huge and I have never made eye contact with him. His lectures seem dull but you learn well enough if you pay attention. You should get a decent grade if you're careful enough but overall not the most interesting class I've taken.

He's a pretty good lecturer, definitely find a smart group early to work on group assignments with. Quizzes are tricky at first but you learn what to expect. It's really not a hard class if you just go to class and for God's sake work through the questions in class so you have notes to reference.

I believe this professor has one of the easiest classes for the business minor. He was a pretty decent professor and was always able to give me the lecture notes when I missed class (8 times). Just now the concepts in the beginning and you'll be fine. Making some friends in class will also help a lot

Do not take this professor. He makes a lot of careless mistakes but refuses to admit that he made them. He is rude when you ask questions and is not helpful. I spent hundreds of dollars on a tutor for this class and will still not be making an A. I am typically an A student.

If you wanna make it out with a decent grade, you HAVE to find smart friends. Timed quizzes are tricky and generally hard, and in class assignments are fairly long. Your only easy A's are the CNOW assignments. Verduzco himself is an alright teacher, I could understand the concepts. Playing lemonade tycoon is also pretty fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Tough class, you definitely need to make friends in this to pass. Very vague and boring during lectures. One of the toughest classes I had to take for my minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not an enjoyable class, the timed quizzes at home are very stressful, and it's difficult to know what exactly is going to be on them cause he'll pick stuff from all around the unit. Class wasn't very helpful either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: the timed quizzes make up most of the grade and they can be pretty challenging
do NOT recommend taking this professor. tons of 10 question/20 minute online quizzes which are impossible to finish in time. I love math, but this class and teaching format is impossible. Easy C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It will be an easy A for you if you have a group of people in that class to help you understand what you don't understand. I enjoyed this class, and this is how I made my first few friends at UT despite my sophomore status.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Most of your grade is based off of around 17 quizzes that are timed and pretty stressful (since they require calculations on the spot). It's difficult, but doable to get an A in this class. Must go to class for participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. 60% of your grade is based off of 17-20 EXTREMELY DIFFICULT (& nearly impossible) timed quizzes. You get 20 minutes for 10 questions (and half of these questions require extensive thought/math). I have 100s for everything else, yet will get a B b/c of the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took this class expecting it to be a blow-off - it wasn't. There's so many timed quizzes to take and they were incredibly difficult. Study groups will be your savior in this class!  Just make sure you do all the assignments (surveys, assignments, quizzes), as he will drop a couple of each. The class isn't difficult, you just need to work for an A

Dr. Verduzco is a wonderful professor for non-accounting majors.  I have learned a lot through this course.  The class is made up of weekly quizzes and participation surveys, no tests.  Defiantly would recommend for anyone needing ACC310F

As a CNS major I completely underestimated this class. There are 20 difficult, timed quizzes that make up the bulk of your grade so try to do well on them from the beginning.  He sometimes breezed over material, but still quizzed us over more in depth concepts. Try not to take with rigorous courses needed for your degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Don't take this class expecting to get an A. His standard for an A is scoring 94+ with no rounding which is pretty hard to get.  The quizzes are open note and make up 60 percent of your grade and can be pretty challenging.  There's a TON of cheating that goes on as people collaborate to do quizzes and assignments so take with a friend or make some.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you think this is a blow off class, YOU'RE WRONG. The entire grade is basically based on these online quizzes which are freakin' hard. Make study groups to take them or like a Facebook group or something. He drops 3 quizzes and 1 assignment though so that kind of helps. Attendance isn't technically mandatory but you assigns surveys in class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a really funny teacher, which makes class more enjoyable. He explained the concepts well and had me excited to learn more.
Probably the best teacher to teach accounting. He makes it easy if you pay attention. No exams, just try your best and this class is a nice ride.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The quizzes are somehow impossible. I've made perfect scores of the assignments, but I have hardly passed any of the timed quizzes. I have my dad on the phone for help on quizzes(who has a Master's in business/accounting/finance) and I STILL can't pass them. Despite having perfect attendance/assignment grades, I'll be making a C because of quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class is much harder than it used to be. Quizzes are timed and can be quite tricky- if you miss one question, you're left with an 80 or 90. You need 94+ for an A. Expect homework after every class, twice a week. Most profs are much friendlier/less intimidating when you speak with them one on one. Verduzco is the opposite. NOT an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is essentially designed to be a weed out class. It's extremely fast paced and Verduzco does not give adequate time on his quizzes. Does not accommodate to students who have anxiety about timed quizzes. Just disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He does absolutely nothing to help students learn the content. He moves way too fast and expects you to understand everything. You teach yourself everything in this class. Quizzes are quite difficult. Not easy like everyone says it is. Don't care for teaching style. Don't take this professor if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's literally lectures like a game show host. Verduzco is adorable but doing well in his class can be a little tricky. The majority of the final grade comes from 18-20 quizzes which can be a little tricky and confusing at times. Makes LOTS of friends in the class and you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nice and funny, but not the best at teaching material. 15-20 quizzes make up bulk of your grade so if you keep up with material and have friends in the class its an easy A even if you get lost during lecture. Participation surveys are way of taking attendance, and often what determined students final grades as most had very similar quiz averages.
Great professor and great class if you put in the relatively light amount of work required.

Pretty easy class. He tries really hard to be funny and connect with the students, but overall it doesn't work. The quizzes were super easy, he basically gave all of the answers in class. If you show up to class and pay attention getting an A is super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There are no exams and the class is instead based on about 20 quizzes. Verduzco is not a very organized professor, but the topics covered are not too difficult. You kind of have to teach yourself the material.

Tries hard to be funny. Not good at explaining anything. My mom is an accountant and disagreed with multiple things he taught us throughout the semester. Expect a quiz as homework after  almost every class. No exams, but if there were exams I would fail because he is not good at teaching.
If you take the online class, it's poorly formatted and he really doesn't care if you even have legitimate excuses to not finish quizzes on time.

Verduzco is a very nice and funny guy. Although the class is huge, he makes you feel welcomed. The class wasn't a blow off course, but it wasn't extremely difficult either. The workload was an average amount, especially considering there being no exams (which he replaced with a higher number of quizzes). I enjoyed the class and would recommend.

Not a fan of the layout of this class, though it did make it easy to pull a good grade - 20 quizzes, most online and untimed. A 5-6 assignments also online and untimed, and 15% of your grade is just participation surveys. Made a good grade, and really like Verduzco as a person, but know nothing about Accounting still.

Classic "Easy A" class. Teaching style is not my preferred one so I honestly don't think I've learned much in this class. Better off just going to Accounting Coach if you want to learn about accounting. He's a nice guy though. Like most accounting classes, his lectures are pretty boring.
There are no exams in this course which is nice. Although, he uses Lemonade Tycoon to teach us accounting and it made things more confusing.

I didn't like this class. Only took it because it was required. It's easy if you already understand accounting, but he does not explain the information well. I didn't do poorly but I didn't do as well as I expected. No tests and no final, which is cool. He's not the worst professor but I don't like his teaching methods. Its not that much work.

By far my favorite class I've taken. Lectures are mandatory but interesting, and essential to passing. No tests, no final. All the grades were homework, quizzes, and in-class polling. If you understand the lecture then the textbook is not necessary, but is supplemental. If his section is open, TAKE IT.

I took this class to fulfill a BFP requirement. As long as you show up to lectures and take notes, you will have an A in this class. Although there are a lot of quizzes (both inside and outside of class) and homework, there are no tests! He teaches through Lemonade Tycoon and Marketplace which is a cool way to grasp the concepts.

He tried something knew and gave around twenty quizzes throughout the semester instead of exams. That requires you to be on top of your game more but they were easy quizzes over stuff he just lectured about. Best to attend each class for the best quiz grades (60% of final)!!  No final exam. A few assignments throughout the semester (7 tops).

Lectures are clear and engaging with very helpful notes provided by the teacher. Extremely helpful in office hours and very personable. Tests are very manageable. Highly recommend any optional software packages. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Overall takes a bit of work for the homework and two tests but nothing outrageous. No final exam.
tough class..............
tough class

The material is really boring, but he does his best to spice it up. The entire course revolves around two simulation games: LemonadeTycoon and Marketplace. iClicker participation grades in class every day, online quizzes twice a week, Cengage assignments every two weeks or so, two exams: midterm and final. Not too bad if you prepare.

Verduzco is a good professor. If anyone writes a really strong and scathing review about him, don't trust it. The class is simple and lecture is often boring. Quizzes always seem to get the best of me but the tests are easy if you study. He offers good study materials and does simulations of the concepts that are helpful. Good class, nice prof.
First class I have ever had to drop because I hated it that much. This class is not cool. Not interesting. Very boring and excruciatingly difficult.

I wasn't a fan of Verduzco, as his humor can get annoying really fast. There are 2 test, but he has a tendency to give out random quizzes, so make sure you go to class. Also clicker attendance is 10% of grade. Wasn't an easy class, but doable with some effort.
Very difficult tests. The other accounting teacher is easier

He is boring, and you have to come to class everyday for the clicker. Gives random pop quizzes. Also he gives certain sections 1 point on the overall grade if they win marketplace, but its not fair for the sections that don't win. If you are in the right section you can get a lot of extra credit.

Lectures were ridiculously pointless and made learning concepts way harder than it should've been. Mandatory clicker questions, and you have to do 95% of the learning on your own. I learned nothing from going to class other than how to daydream about Lemonade Tycoon.

Energetic professor, but the material is so dry and boring. His lectures were confusing at times and this class requires a lot of practicing problems. Tests are hard! Hated the class and the material, but Verduzco is a nice guy.

Dr. Verduzco was not a good professor in my opinion. He was overly animated and taught in a way that made things more difficult than they should have been. I attended every lecture, and the practice problems in class were ridiculously easy in comparison to his exams & there are only 2! I regret not taking this course from the other prof over summer
Took him for accounting, he talks like he's on a game show everyday which gets a little annoying after awhile. Hard to pay attention, doesn't teach very well but it's not too hard.

He is funny and makes accounting interesting. You spend the semester playing Lemonade Tycoon against over sections. You must be there 85% of time. He takes participation with clicker and those can be use as bonus in the end. 2 tests, he gives you practice tests almost identical to real test. Not difficult and easy to listen to.

I liked this class! He was funny and I enjoyed the interactive class with the lemonade game and the monopoly. It really put things into prospective. His tests can be a little difficult but other than that, you learn a lot from this guy.
He is in an okay professor. He is funny, but does not know how to teach.

Attendance not mandatory but you can build up your grade with participation points each class. He let's you decide how you want the class to break down between tests, quizzes, participation, and assignments in the first week of class.

I went to 75% of the classes stoned and still got an A. All you have to do is show up and click. Study the practice exams to do well on the real exams. People usually post the answers to the hw/quizzes on the online discussion chat room. Pretty fun class, VERY EASY

Funny in an accounting nerd kind of way.  Good lecturer.  Pretty helpful but is sometimes unnecessarily, and annoyingly, ambiguous.  All exams were online, which was nice, but I'd HIGHLY recommend doing the practice exams ahead of time.

When I had class with him, I actually went to class for a change and made an effort to learn. I used to look forward to his class. He is a very chill dude and probably one of the funniest professors at UT

Tests are tricky, I did better towards the end but I read more towards the end. Bit of advice try not to miss class most of the stuff on the test he covers in lecture. He's super funny, and he's pretty clear in his lectures. Get a smart group! Other people that know what they are doing will help a lot. TURN OFF UR CELL

funny guy which makes class more entertaining, but the tests are killer and the group activities seem easy enough but one mistake can ruin your grade on it. it is possible to make an A if you go to every class and get a good group. Bs are easy to get though

Interesting class. Not a bad professor. Study!! If you read the book and understand it (do the hws) then you should be fine! Exams aren't too bad, just make sure you understand everything from the book. He posts a pratice test online before exams, it helps!
omg, this is a tough class.  esp if you miss which i did.  so my advice, don't skip!  and don't let your cell ring - he's not kidding when he says he'll answer it :(
He's good and friendly.
No Comments
No Comments
Funny guy.  Good Prof.

She is very mom-coded and cares about mental well-being. The class is not too difficult; however, the tests sometimes throw a curveball, and you don't have much time. Her lectures can be difficult to follow, but she provides resources for all the cycles you learn, though her Canvas is a bit hard to navigate.

Cares a lot about student mental health, which I appreciated a lot. Her teaching style was very helpful for breaking down thermo concepts into something understandable, and grading is lenient. The course may have cut material though(?), so I worry a little about being adequately prepared for future classes

Best prof I have had so far at UT. She really cares for you, and the HW and the quizzes are not very hard if you actually go to class and pay attention. Ppl complain about the exams, but they're fine. I think its a genuine skill issue if you can't apply what we learned to determine more complex quantities. Ignore the negative ratings below.

The weekly homework and open-note quizzes were straightforward and graded leniently. The exams always asked for something that we had never been taught how to find before. The first exam was graded leniently, but the second exam and the final were not. I also had an emergency on the day of an attendance quiz and she would not excuse it.

Dr. Wang is very sweet and caring. Thermo is a very hard class and her exams were very difficult but she stressed mental health and the lectures were pretty informative but a little boring at times. She doesn't deserve all the negative reviews she's gotten this semester because I feel like any thermo class is going to have tough exams.

Dr. Wang was a very caring professor, but her exams were so much harder than expected. She gives exam review problems that are nothing like the exam, especially for Exam 2 and the Final. Exams have curveballs and require intuitive thinking. Homeworks are easy and can be resubmitted for full credit and quizzes are easy and open note.

She's a nice person, but her tests were nothing like her practice problems. They were way harder and sometimes she would give things on the test that we had never gone over in class or on any homeworks and expected us to know. She's always preaching about mental health but I think that's a lie because if she cared she would not give us these tests.

Dr. Wang is a lovely person and cares about her students. However, after repeatedly telling us that there was no way for her to "trick" us on the midterms she LIED. Midterm 2 and the final were difficult and required strategies we had never used in class. It felt like she set us up with way harder content than we expected and were prepared for.

She's a nice professor, but the only helpful thing she could provide were her deep-breathing exercises. She always manages to throw curveballs on the exams (especially test 2 and the final), so it was hard to keep a good grade. TAs carried the class, as they were very helpful with understanding the concepts and dealing with grades.

Dr. Wang is very sweet and cares about your mental health, she gives great free extra credit, and the midterms are graded lightly. The weekly homework/quizzes are free 100's, cheat sheets on tests. However, her lectures are incredibly boring and often feel directionless. The test review helped on MT1, but MT2 was a complete curveball. Tough class.

I found that this class was very smooth sailing if you do the 2-5 HW problems assigned each week and really ensure you understand them. All the quizzes and midterms were based off those. The final was a curve ball to everyone with new problems so I recommend keeping your average high (95+) for that. She's very kind and considerate though.

The lectures are mostly just a slideshow being read word for word. You also learn a lot of material that will never be presented again. As for the midterms, they were manageable if you did the practice tests and HWs beforehand. However, the final went over problems very different from the practice and had a failing average. Mid.

I may have different views on this class than most people. I enjoyed the lectures because they were clear; It just boiled down to her deriving stuff and then leading us to the final thing we needed to remember, which was easy to follow for me at least. The final was difficult, yes, but the midterms were similar to homework problems.

Homework and quizzes were simple and short, but you would have to teach the material yourself. She is very disorganized and did an awful job at teaching. She just expected us to know what she knows. Midterms were similar to example problems. She tricked us on the final and made it super hard with problems we had never seen before. Do not trust her.

Dr. Wang is sweet and cares a lot about mental health, but the course structure is a mess. We skipped huge fundamental ideas related to thermo and went straight into advanced concepts (cycles) with no real knowledge as to why they work the way they do. Overall, the course wasn't too difficult, but you don't really walk away with anything,

SO considerate! Sweetest prof ever. Cares tremendously about her students' mental health. Homework was easy & tests were predictable & graded very leniently. Was scared for thermo based on what engineering students say but Wang's course is very easy. Wants her students to succeed for sure. My only criticism is I wish she focused more on concepts.

She's a great lady, but her teaching style doesn't work. Said she's cut out material over the semesters to get to the "important stuff" but the class feels choppy and disorganized. Notes, homework and tests are ripped out of a textbook. Messy, incomplete notes. Material would be covered just to never be seen again on any test, homework or quiz.

Dr. Wang definitely changed the structure of this class as I have heard horror stories from the past. She broke down all the cycles in a way we would understand and the homework never felt useless (short enough to get to the point). Additionally, she would make us do breathing exercises, would calm us down before quizzes & was overall amazing.

Absolutely amazing; she changed her teaching style this semester and it definitely helped us understand the material better. She really wants to help you succeed. Thermo is hard, and her lectures can be a bit confusing at times, but that's when you go to the recitation sessions or office hours to clarify. I mean it- go to the recitation sessions!

She is an absolute treasure. Semester isn't over yet, but fairly confident I will get close to a 100 in this class. She cares so much about her students and every day she spends at least 10-15 minutes in class talking about mental health and her personal journey to find self actualization. Class is all open note, so easy, and instructor is AMAZING.

Dr. Wang is a great professor for heat transfer lab. I cannot help but feel the Spring 22 class ganged up on this woman with little justification. To be fair, the class could have been organized better, but the material on the final exam was reasonable, and she accommodated our requests on MC grading policy. Study, turn in labs, and you'll be fine.

Wang's class ranks among the classes I've ever taken. While she showed good intentions throughout the semester, often the lectures were hard to follow and not very useful, which was particularly bothersome because attendance was required. The material was achievable, but required studying materials outside of just the provided course materials.
Professor Wang is absolutely awful at teaching this class - most unorganized course I have ever taken. She makes heat transfer lab, and already terrible class, even worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thermo is a really hard class but Dr Wang makes it a bit easier. Her lectures are hard to follow but she always posts notes and videos if you need to go back to anything. She's very kind and very open to feedback so definitely let her know if she needs to change anything. She also gives out 2 free bonus points at the end for feedback which is nice

She is genuinely one of the most compassionate professors I've ever had. Thermo is just a class with a lot of content, so it's fast paced. Ask questions no matter how dumb, she will always respond kindly and clarify. Used the textbook a lot, very helpful. The tests were difficult, but if you do the practice problems, not too bad.

As hard as this class was, I did not deserve the grade I got based on my participation in the class. Dr. Wang is caring and lenient with her students and takes all things into consideration because she recognizes that this is one of the hardest courses available. I barely learned anything, but Wang's generosity made this course bareable.

Hard subject matter to learn; sometimes hard to follow during class, especially for completely new topics. But nice professor who is receptive to feedback from a large class - and the teaching/learning got better bc of it. Offers many resources - recitation sessions w/ TAs, hw exercises, notes in and out of class. Examples & visuals helped lots!

Dr. Wang is a very nice person but this class is poorly structured and it is extremely difficult to learn anything. Dr. Wang has very high expectations and some of those can be quite unreasonable. In general, if you are not a fan of self-learning, you are going to have a very tough time learning this material. Exams are very tough.

She is very nice professor and is knowledgeable in her field. However, she might as well have just read the textbook to us during lecture. Her slides, examples, and homework were all out of the textbook. Given that, definitely get the textbook and do the many many homework problems. Exams are very similar (& sometimes the same) as the homework.

By far the hardest class I've taken at UT. She doesn't do the best job at making it easier on her students either, but she does care about her students and is always available. Homework's are unnecessarily long and difficult. Lectures are hard to follow and not very organized. For how hard the material is she does a sub par job at teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly Wang was the worst professor Ive had at UT. She doesnt teach, all she does is read from slides with no explanation. The homework takes way longer than it should because you have to rewrite the problem, draw a picture, write what is given, assumptions, laws, solve, if it makes sense, then implications. Definitely avoid taking her class.

This class is not to bad, just read the textbooks and and listen to his lectures(really important). Tests require fast writing/thinking bc of the time limit. The professor is so entertaining. I enjoyed the class and felt like I actually learned something useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class just to fulfill your core requirement!! The grade is 80% exams that are 3 SAQs and an entire essay written in the 45 minute class period, and they will tank your grade if you struggle with timed writing. It is also very textbook heavy and I'm 90% sure Prof. Weyland is in love with David Held so keep that in mind

Professor Weyland is very passionate about what he teaches, so it is important that you show interest and effort in the course. He is very engaging and interactive with his lectures and strongly encourages you to speak up. The reading, which may be a lot, is necessary to do well in tests and quizzes but they do help. You really get what you put in.

I really enjoyed Dr. Weyland's class; his lectures are extremely interesting, and it's clear he cares about what he does. That being said, I'm pretty sure I'll end up with a B because your grade is based solely on exams. That would be fine if the tests weren't essays and the TAs were nicer graders, but alas, we can't all get what we want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you're wanting an A, the best grade you can receive is honestly a B. Graded on 3 quizzes and 3 exams (no final) and the TA has no clear grading criteria. I went to office hours because his grading was either really high or really low; couldn't explain to me why I got that grade. Doesnt post grades throughout the whole sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I've ever had in my life. Dr. Weyland has a superiority complex and will not give you any constructive feedback.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU'RE NOT WILLING TO READ OR AREN'T INTERESTED IN GOVERNMENT
Dr. Weyland is an amazing lecturer, but he also asks a lot from his students in terms of reading and grading. Only 3 quizzes and 3 exams throughout the semester, which are graded harshly by the TA
If you don't like reading and can't write, I suggest staying away
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's not worth it. I sold my soul to get an A in this course. The fear that you're going to fail the test/quiz because of a minor mistake really takes away from enjoying the class content. The readings are so long and you're expected to take the smallest details away from them. Don't take it if you're trying to check off your core requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Weyland was the best professor I've had. The class is hard, I won't lie. There are 3 textbooks, and the readings range from maybe 15- 50 pages a day. There are 2 major exams, 3 quizzes, and a paper. Weyland, however, is incredible, and taking this rigorous course is very rewarding. Super funny, smart, and passionate professor. 10/10 worth it

This class took years off my life. 100 pages of reading a week and the toughest grader known to man. Everything is ambiguous and there is no possible extra credit. I got a B for my participation grade even though I've attended every class and spoke in the discussion multiple times. I feel like he wanted to fail me on purpose. Don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Weyland has been my favorite social sciences professor at UT. His lectures are incredible. However, it is extremely reading-heavy and challenging, especially since there are only 3 quizzes and 3 exams throughout the semester. Only take this course if you are truly interested in the topics discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures and is very knowledgeable but your entire course grade consists of 6 exams and nothing else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His way of delivering feedback isn't very pedagogic.  The professor would fail me in every assingment providing feedback such as: "Things are not working out, Worrysome, I was Generous 5/30 score.  I went to office hours to see ways to improve where he told me he didn't think I was gonna pass the class because I couldn't criticaly thing.

Prof. Weyland is extremely knowledgeable about the subject and has very engaging lectures. The class  explores broad concepts that apply to current political events. You are graded on short answer questions. that is it. show up, pay attention, read and you will do great in the class. strongly recommend this class for your gov credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Weyland is an engaging lecturer and clearly is passionate about his field of study.  The readings are very heavy, but overall, it's a great opportunity to discuss contemporary matters in Latin America.  Tests are easy if you study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Any professor who makes it this difficult to pass his class does not deserve to teach. The grading criteria for the essay is completely ambiguous. You have to take hand written notes, you have to buy 4 textbooks which are not covered by the school so my scholarship didn't cover. Hard to understand and a HARSH grader. Also a prick about attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weyland is a good prof, but the format of this course is not. This course has no opportunity for dropping/replacing grades, EC, etc., so one bad exam and you're screwed. He also doesn't post any slides or allow you to take notes on laptop. Papers graded harshly by TA. Attendance not mandatory but you need to go to do well. Take 312L online or at CC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Weyland was fantastic. Had I taken this course earlier in my life, I might have picked a different career. One of the books he chose, Politics By Other Means was illuminating.

Kurt Weyland is the type of guy to make running sentences with big words to make a term sound more fancy and difficult than it really is. For example, his futile definition of a democracy doesn't fit every democracy around the world. He is hard to understand and mispronounces words and not helpful nor are the TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Weyland's lecture is fun but his short answer and essay exam make this class much more stressful. He provide a generous curve in every exam (8-20 points). I recommend go to SI session held by TA. Exams are based on lecture in textbooks. A LOT of reading. You will definitely get something from this class.

LOTS of studying, reading, writing. Lectures are dense but Prof. Weyland brings a lot of enthusiasm and is clearly very passionate about the content. Had to buy 4 textbooks but I was mostly able to get by by taking diligent notes during lecture. Only grades are 3 quizzes and 3 exams (all short essay questions). Hard but not impossible to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Weyland was in one word amazing. I loved his class, despite the class not relating to my major at all. He does make you read a lot and make sure to take good, handwritten notes--useful for tests. He shows a passion for the content that is infectious. I learned a lot and can confidently say I know a LOT about US-LA interventions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Weyland is amazing, easily one of the best lecturers I've ever had. He is a brilliant professor and knows the course material like the back of his hand. Very big emphasis on quizzes and tests, but they are all curved very generously (at least 10 points higher).

Professor Weyland is an extremely caring & passionate individual. I found his lectures well-organized & entertaining. Although the content is quite challenging, he provides ample support and is always available to his students to help. Tests are weighted heavily, but are also curved generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is sooo hard. The professor was very good and caring but the tests are really hard. Quizzes and Tests make up 100 % of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, super passionate, super smart. Grades are tough. The TA grades, and if you don't match Weyland's words exactly you get no points, even if your idea is right.

Weyland is honestly one of my favorite professor I have come across at UT. The lectures are really enjoyable and will help in the Exam/quizzes but you will have to read a lot as he will advise you to understand. Very well spoken just read and understand the lectures and you should succeed. He gives extra credit, so as long as you put in the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Weyland is a professor who cares, and he REALLY knows what he's talking about. There are only 6 grades in this class, which follow the lectures and readings pretty closely. I didn't do the readings well, and did poorly on the first 3 assignments. I took notes and got over 100 (+ 25 curve). Overall, the lectures are great. Read to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weyland's international politics of latin america was very enjoyable. He gives generous curves to most assignments and is dedicated to his students success. Very approachable in office hours. There is a lot of reading and the lectures are mandatory attendance, but they were extremely helpful and answered the quiz/test questions verbatim
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Weyland is super nice and funny, and the class was very straight forward! Just go to lectures and discussions, and figure out the key points from the readings. I think exams were graded fairly, and the questions were very direct. Dr. Weyland is super knowledgable and I really enjoyed the content. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can't recommend Dr. Weyland enough! I came out of this class a whole different person; it was EYE-OPENING. Incredible and engaging lectures; the prof is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. Lots of reading, but nothing too crazy and he breaks it all down very well! He's also always there for students + helps however he can! 10/10

This class is based off of 3 quiz grades and 3 test grades. The lectures are well structured and can be easily followed. The tests are short answer/essay, and in order to make a good grade you need to use wording very similar to Weyland's. Overall the class was very interesting, and as long as you go to lecture and pay attention you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His class was a lot of reading but it was totally worth it. I loved sitting in on his lectures because you could see how passionate he was about the subject. Sometimes he would tell jokes in class and it was really nice seeing him trying to make his lectures fun. However, we only had 3 quizzes and 3 tests and the tests are heavily weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Weyland's passion and enthusiasm are contagious and his lectures are easy to follow, make sense, and are enjoyable. There's a lot of readings that were great supplements but shouldn't have been required. Exams are 2 or 3 essays/short answer and grading started to be harder with time. HE does speak slow and tends to repeat a lot but an easier class.

Dr. Weyland is a very entertaining lecturer and a genuinely nice person. There is a LOT of reading in this class, but I didn't find it boring (surprising for me tbh). Overall, this was the best gov course I've taken at UT, but it definitely wasn't the easiest. If you actually do the reading, you'll make a grade you're happy with.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: ONLY 3 EXAMS AND 3 QUIZZES. HARD LECTURES.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved him as a professor! He was very and reviewed topics thoroughly. While he is lecture heavy and you read a lot, the subjects are interesting and you dont have much work: good/bad as your grade relies on 3 tests and quizzes. You can get over 100, and as long as you pay attention, you'll pass. (Accent may be difficult at first, but he's clear)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unclear grading criteria. No assignments. Entire grade is based on 3 written exams and 3 written quizzes. All grading left to TA's, graded harshly. I'm a government major and had to pass/fail this course. You have to hit the nail on the head with his exams. Don't, you won't pass. Questions typically complicated. Lots of outside studying required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found it so hard to stay focused in class, there's no graphics at all, just him talking the whole hour, and sometimes it's hard to understand his accent. only three exams and three quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Weyland!! He is so adorable and very passionate about the topics. He lectures for 50 min straight with no notes. Makes hilarious jokes in class and makes the info engaging. There is a ton of reading and you need to memorize the lectures to do well on exams and quizzes. A difficult class, but Dr. Weyland makes it worth it!

Weyland is a great professor and you will learn so much from this class. There's a lot of reading but if you go to every lecture and pay very close attention you can get by without reading every single thing. The only grades are 3 quizzes and 3 tests that are all essays/short answers so you really need to know the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The reading is demanding, and the essay exams annoying but doable. Weyland himself is just so enthusiastic that it is infectious. I don't know if this course will give me any material benefit, but I feel I have a greater understanding of my own political beliefs. Just be ready to read and write a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I like hard courses, but I don't like those that make you do a lot of studying and never pay it off. That is exactly how it is in this class. And by the way, the exam has nothing to do with the lectures, even though they can be interesting, it is not helpful AT ALLL.

Great lecturer! Took his latin american course and does a great job making the content interesting. There are only three exams and three quizzes and they're all based off the lectures AND readings. There is A LOT of reading and information that he covers in class. The exams and quizzes are all essay based. Loved him, but wouldn't take it again.

Fantastic Lecturer, funny guy, respected and knows his topic, but extremely difficult blue book exams. Exams are extremely content heavy, with no study guides, and way too little time given. Also, uneven grading. Great Teacher, but be prepared to work.

He's an incredibly interesting prof but a very very tough grader. The exams and quizzes are all short answer or essay and he want verbatim answers or you'll get graded harshly. That being said, you will learn a lot from this class as he's a very interesting lecturer but it most probably will kill your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Your grade is dependent on you writing down what he says in lecture verbatim. If it is not verbatim, then you don't get any credit. The average on his quizzes and tests are so low that even with a 20-30 point curve, it's in the low 70s. He just tells you to ask questions to the TAs and the TAs are unhelpful. Don't take him if you can help it.

Intnl Politics of US + LA: Weyland knows what he is talking about and genuinely wants students to participate. Get ready to read about 100 pages a week and DO NOT FALL BEHIND! THERE IS IS NO CATCHING UP! If you don't read, you won't pass. The content is interesting and Weyland is a good lecturer but is sometimes too comfortable with students...

Kurt is one of the most caring professors you can have. His lectures are amazing and he encourages student participation every class. However, his course is extremely reading heavy. His exams are hard to study for because there is no review sheet, but if you make a study group, it can be very enjoyable. You will learn A LOT in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor requires students to buy and read several textbooks and does not refer to them in class almost at all. His lectures consist of him talking quickly and expecting students to absorb all the information he presents (without notes provided). His exams require specific answers without asking specific questions. His exams/quizzes are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was definitely one of my favorites! He was super entertaining and overall the coursework wasn't hard (especially since he gives HUGE curves). I did about half of the readings and showed up to most of the lectures and paid attention and ended up with a 99 in the class. All the exams and quizzes are essays though.

You can read all of the required readings, attend all the lectures, and take detailed notes and you will still struggle on his quizzes and tests. He is a good lecturer, but don't expect to come away with a good grade in his class. His TA's are also super hard to impress with quizzes and tests. They never give higher than an B to anyone
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There are 3 quizzes and 3 exams. I never did any of the readings and still scored high on all of them. He also gives 8-15 extra points each exam or quiz. Lectures are pretty interesting, and I thought the topic was interesting as well.

Long readings, but relevant to lecture. Uses 4 books - read them all! No final, but exams and quizzes are difficult in that they are all free-response - no multiple choice. Three of each, and they are each done during one lecture. Very entertaining lecturer, very helpful, but difficult grades. Don't put off this class. He has clear expectations.

He is a very entertaining lecturer, one of the best. Extremely high amount of readings. His tests quizzes are challenging and made much more difficult by the time limits. His class requires/deserves a lot of attention.

Professor Weyland is a strong lecturer, and gives insightful points about the dense and numerous readings he assigns. The tests/quizzes however are incredibly difficult to study for, and tough to do well on.
He is really great and enthusiastic about the subject. The exams and quizzes are sometimes tricky, but I only went to class and never did any of the readings and managed to make a B.

Professor Weyland was an amazing teacher, enthusiastic, hilarious and German! Coming into the class with little knowledge about Latin American Politics, it became one of my favourite classes! There is a lot of reading, but it is useful for the essay. If you make notes during semester the quizzes/exams are super easy! DO IT.

He's absolutely amazing! He makes a potentially dull topic very interesting. His excitement makes it even more enjoyable. Tests and quizzes are all short answer/essay, but they aren't too hard if you go to class and read the assigned readings. Going to class is really key, especially because his lectures are very ordered and notes are easy to take.

Professor Weyland is an incredibly enthusiastic professor. He really makes the material interesting and his accent is pretty funny, but understandable. I recommend going to class every day, and it shouldn't be too hard if you do the readings. It can be a good amount of work. Only essays for tests and quizzes.

I highly recommend this class. There is a lot of reading if you want feel extra secure of the material, but I didn't read for the last half of the class, went to all the classes, and made an A. Go to classes! Not only will it make the tests and quizzes more manageable, Prof. Weyland is funny too. His accent is great!
His quizzes and tests are hard, but he's a really, really good teacher. He really knows his stuff and has a good sense of humor. It's one of the few classes I actually laugh in.
He is a great professor, extremely knowledgeable about his topic. Definitely take his class if you are interested in learning and working hard!
Is a tough grader but is very receptive and helpful to students.  Essay questions only.  Gotta love the German accent  and hyper mannerisms, all while teaching Latin American Politics.
No Comments

Weyland is awesome! He is one of the best lecturers at UT. There is a lot of reading but it all has a point. He is very funny and very intelligent. If you want to learn how to think critically about government take this class.
No Comments
Professor Weyland is the BEST!  He is extremely thorough and knowlegable...take his class!  Also, he is quite funny and his German accent is fun to listen to!
Good teacher and lectures, but hard & SUPER-HEAVY on the reading.  Must have love and deep understanding of gov.  If either descriptions don't sound like you pass!

Its very important that you listen to every word he says in class. He is really nice dude, meh prof, the class is probably doable if you have a very easy workload but working and taking this w, biochem and ochem lab was a lot. I think you have to eat, breathe, sleep his course to be able to truly master the content in the way he wants
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: lowkey wait and take with partridge. The class is doable, but beware.

Although Dr. Wilson gets some hate, I think he is genuinely a great professor. Yes his class takes work, however, it taught me how to actually engage in the material and learn that understanding/connection/asking why is key to success rather than memorization. I definitely recommend going to office hours if you're able to!

Tests are extremely hard and no matter how hard you study there will be something you don't know anything about. Tons of hypotheticals and need to know details of almost everything. He's funny and seems like he wants students to succeed until you get to the exams. Take someone else until he figures this out.

Tears have been flowing, and I've had enough of him. He's nice and all, but he doesn't seem to realize we lack the experience he has, so all his questions are insanely hard and don't reflect our mastery of the content. Having a 65 average on exams should be a huge red flag because there's no way this many students should be doing that badly.
where do i even begin...I study hours on hours for the test only to be met with 44 questions of pure nonsense. there is literally nothing you can do to be prepared because it is never enough.
he NEEDS to make exams easier and take some constructive criticism from theses reviews people on here ARENT lying

if everyone is doing bad on the exams that should be a sign to curve or make them easier. averages of 65-70 aren't normal and exams in this class don't reflect learning you can practically learn everything he gives and tells and still won't do good on exams wish he took these ratings into consideration for exams and the sake of his students

the exams are insanely difficult the material itself isn't bad but his question style is out to get students. he seems nice however seems to make the test with intentions of making the student struggle
you can practically memorize every word on the slides and still barley get a B in the class. harder than chem don't take it with him unless he curves or fixes the exams

EXTREMELY lecture heavy. he has not ever finished a lecture in class on time, always carriers over. exams are NOT reflective of what we go over in class. RARELY goes into depth when explaining topics. ZERO good practice for exam, everything outside of exams is MUCH easier than actual exam. i feel bad bc he's a nice guy, but professor? nah.
sooo much material, only gives 4 points back on exams at most, exams have the most tricky questions, no practice like the exams

Nice guy but SO MUCH MATERIAL - Definitely possible to do well in the class but don't expect it to be easy. NEED to review ALL material outside of class before tests to do well bc they can cover anything. If you have an A at end of semester don't have to take final. Go to review sessions bc EC can do big things for u at end of semester

Lectures are not detailed enough for tests. Go to study sessions. He is very kind and enthusiastic but does not understand that he knows the material much more than his students. Tests are difficult and have so much material so watch lecture videos before class and read the textbook.

Wilson is definitely a difficult prof. Tests are not hard in terms of concepts, but coverer lots of material. I usually had to study 20+ hours for each. Lectures are interesting despite the amount of content, and Wilson is approachable/welcoming in office hours. Don't be afraid to take over Partridge. One group project and EC pts, ended with an A

Class was harder than expected bc it was ALOT of content and he skimmed through it. Method is to watch his mini lectures, read ppts, and take notes BEFORE lecture & just listen/absorb info during actual lecture. GO TO STUDY SESSIONS. They help a lot and are extra credit. Exams are hard so study a lot. DO EVER IN-CLASS ASSIGNMENT, its on the exams.
The 5s are crazy. Theres a good/interesting course in here somewhere, its just buried under not needed details and busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are not working full time while you are in school, you have no reason to not pass this class. I struggled a lot because it was hard to manage my time carefully. Also, see Dr. Wilson personally if you can. Tests can be tricky, and it is important to review each exam right after taking it. Take another prof if you are looking for a perfect A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: a lot of content, can get overwhelming as expected for upper div bio class. I recommend going to all the TA discussions and classes as they all have extra credit. 1 group project that's easy and weekly take home quizzes, also easy. Hardest part is the exams: 45+ multiple choice and trickyyy wording. Read carefully.

Definitely not 2.5 bad, but this class will require a generational lock in. You can't get behind on material and have to be studying consistently each week. He's such a nice funny guy though and great to chat with

This class is VERY content heavy so I recommend only taking it with a lighter course load or just locking in. I recommend studying a week in advance for each exam since theres so much content. TA sessions are extra credit so definitely attend even though they're not the most helpful depending on which ones you attend. Carol is the goat!

Professor Wilson is a nice guy and clearly passionate about microbiology, however I felt his lectures were overly detailed and difficult to follow. He tends to skip over slides which you are expected to review at home, making it confusing to be sure what content is important for exams. There are study sessions and TopHat points for extra credit.

Very sweet guy but I feel that he lectures a level above what most people can digest. They can be very dense and feel like he is just talking at you but you can definitely be successful with lots of studying. This class covers a ton of material but you can do it!

Dr.Wilson is the most genuine professor ever!! He never fails to make me laugh. He truly cares for his students. Please dont be scared away from taking him. You would be missing out on an amazing professor and great lecturer. Yes.. you need to study and work hard to do good but its like that for any upper division class.
pretty hard class but i did alright i think

Dr. Wilson is a very kind professor and passionate about Microbio. Case studies and lectures are very interesting if you are interested in medicine. Exams are all multiple choice and reflective of content covered in class. The UGCAs and Grad TA were very helpful and responsive. For an upper level div bio course, this is very doable to get an A in.
TA's are straight baddies and class was dope

Lowkey if you can't do well in this class, you should just give up on the MCAT. So many whiners in the GroupMe about how Wilson won't move the test for Halloweekend. Just don't get blackout drunk and study XD. UwU
This class was taught very well, cool prof, easy exams, extra credit. Idk how anyone wouldnt get above a 97 in this class if you try.

The tests were honestly self-explanatory for the most part. If you take the time to study the learning objectives and slides, the questions themselves aren't that tricky. You definitely need to take time to study more so than other biology classes. The information was genuinely interesting and Michael Wilson actually has a genuine interest.

class isn't too bad. if you focus on the lectures and go to office hours (which are extra credit), you will do well in this class. using all your resources (textbook, office hours, wilson himself, etc.) will allow you to do the best. wilson (MY GOAT) is chill but he lowkey kept on talking about his butt and diarrhea.
Dr Wilson is the GOAT, tests are easy, case studies are interesting, and lectures are fun. Class went by fast every day cause its interesting.

Lectures can be long and wordy. The exams are very specific so you have to know absolutely everything there is to know about microbiology. Quizzes are weekly but online and open note at your own time. One partner project that was pretty simple. Just so much information to learn (NOT JUST MEMORIZE)

Nice teacher; hard class. I know it's a hard subject, but the lectures don't really improve your understanding of the material. He knows his stuff, but could structure the class better. I learn more from reading the textbooks than from his videos/lectures. And the test questions are so hard! You'll need to study a lot, both before and after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor is a nice guy. Unfortunately nice guy does not equal good professor. Tests are ridiculous and practice questions have nothing to do with exams. He expects students to teach themselves half the unit every unit, but then asks insanely difficult questions. I've never had a professor or class that makes me feel stupid and incapable until now.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilson genuinely cares about his students and adjusts exam grades based on difficulty. He's approachable and fun to talk to. Try to go to his office hours, I wish I had gone more. TAs are very helpful and great at clarifying questions. Tough class, exams require a lot of memorization, many students Q-drop too, but it's definitely doable.

Class is honestly nowhere as bad as people say it is. I found him to be a great lecturer that I could understand very well. He is also a great person outside of class. Most of the complaints are due to the heavy slide content on each test. But if you just study throughout the weeks and don't procrastinate, high A's on tests are very easily doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Wilson's class, he seemed to actually care about the content he was teaching and he was super accessible in and after class. His lectures can be a bit boring though...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lets be clear, he's a nice guy and seems well intentioned. The class is interesting for the most part. But the structure of the class needs work, content needs focus, and the timing/pace of things needs rethinking. Anyone giving 5 is crazy, as is anyone giving a 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took his class over the summer and I really enjoyed it. I was able to dedicate a lot of time to the course so my experience may be different from others, but I found Dr. Wilson was quite pleasant and helpful.

Took genetics and biochem and can you tell this class was not a “piece of cake”. He is not organized, he had two days of lecture material covered in one day and rather than move the test he chose the lecture before to cram it into one day and ran through it. When students asked if he could move it since it was halloweekend he laughed in their face.

Never in my college career have I met a professor who seems to enjoy his students' misery as much as Wilson enjoys ours. Lectures are unreasonably dense; rarely do I even grasp anything from attending. I only even go now to fill out mandatory TopHats. Exams are written to confuse- you really gotta be on top of the material to do even slightly well.

Please disregard all the bad comments. If you were able to make it through biochem and genetics, this class is a piece of cake. Just make sure to study the PowerPoints and case studies, and you will be fine. Dr. Wilson truly cares about his students doing well, so he adjusts exam grades to reflect their difficulty.
lots to do and little awareness of what i should know

Many people Q dropped out of this class but I decided to stay. Unfortunately the class never got better. Dr. Wilson is a great guy- super nice and funny. But the class is so difficult to study for and the material is hardly narrowed down. Test questions can be difficult and lectures are not helpful. There is Instapoll for a grade every class.

All the bad reviews are from his first semester after transferring here, but he took students' criticism and made it way more manageable. Overall well organized and enthusiastic. Class isn't easy but its no worse than any other upper div bio. If you want easy classes pick a different major.

He's funny and keeps class interesting, but the lectures can be hard to follow. There are a lot of assignments, and they don't really help with the exams. The tests are tough and require a lot of memorization. I mostly went to class for the participation points.

Big fan—I've learned more in this class than I have in any of the prerequisite biology courses. The course is still probably harder than Dr. Partridge's, but if you attend class (for TopHat) and study for the tests, you'll be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilson's great, he's def fixed Fall '24 issues. 60% of grade from 5 exams (including final) w/ 1 drop, pretty large amount of busywork. Very funny guy with a lot of interesting stories, although sometimes the sheer amount of content forced him to speed through slides. Exam Qs were pretty specific, but worst questions were often thrown out.

Genuinely one of the nicest and most fun professors I have had here. Exams can be tricky, but he gives practice and they are very doable. Get to know him in class and in office hours, he is incredibly welcoming and fun to chat with. Wish I spoke with him more over the semester tbh

Had to take this prof after I couldn't get into Partridge. Was scared from the ratings, but this man deserves better. Lectures can be a bit disorganized, but he's aware of that and gives plenty of extra credit and curves to adjust. He clearly cares about the topic and is very passionate. He takes feedback really well and makes a really fun class.

Dr. Wilson was one of my favorite professors here at UT he cares about his students and will answer any questions you have during the lectures. Topics for exams can be a bit blurry but he does try to emphasize what will be tested.

i loved his class! he has improved a lot since last semester. his lecturing is good and the exams are an accurate reflection of the class. there is a lot of content, so you cannot just half ass it and get an comfy A. put in the work, and you will be just fine. he throws out exam questions if he notices a trend of incorrect answers- so very fair imo

Honestly, super nice guy. Not the best lecturer, but got better over the semester. Tests were hard but got easier. Super accessible and accommodating - he's very passionate about what he teaches. If the class was less material, it would be great!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly a sweet man passionate about microbio. Exams were initially hard, but I went to every office hour and got As on exams because he emphasized important points in OH. If you review lecture slides in great detail and ATTEND OH (!) this class = very doable. Listens to student complains. More you see him in OH, you realize he's just a sweet guy.

Dr. Wilson was not a good lecturer, and I would not go to class if he did not make them mandatory. His exams were really difficult, and he assigned too much busy work. Take partridge or anyone else if you want to learn even a little bit of microbiology
Horrible class do not take!

Started out rough, but he was receptive to student feedback and improved the class. Lectures improved over time as well, and the inclusion of relevant case studies was cool. Lots of busywork but it helps to cushion your grade, as exams are only worth 46%. Somewhat stressful this semester, but I learned a lot. I have high hopes for future classes.

The first 2 exams were not at all representative of the material taught. However, he did address student concerns and made the last exam and final fair. Despite this, there was a lot of grade cushioning with hw and attendance.

You will have to put in a lot of work in order to do well. It's not impossible, but review the slides, attend office hours, review TopHat, and in-class work. The beginning of the semester was really rough for this professor, but it's getting better since he's getting more feedback and you do learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was on the tougher side, but doable. He was receptive to student's complaints about niche exams (first exam was unfair, but there was an overall improvement on following exams) and a nice guy in general. Grade is cushioned by lots of HW that are easy 100s, but its a bit time consuming and not helpful at all. Review his slides for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UT. His class was hard but honestly he listened to feedback and provided study guides for the exams. A difficult class but it's UT what do people expect. It's not impossible to do well. Go to OH, talk to TAs, & to him. He is very nice, approachable, and accommodating! you will be fine if you take his class :)

Hard transition for him into UT. Very difficult, and lecture-heavy first two exams, but eased up for the last midterm and final. He is a passionate microbio professor, but while he tries to figure out his lecturing here at UT, find someone else. A lot of busy-work that's not helpful. Perhaps his future classes will not be experimental like this one

Rough in the beginning; however, he eased up and the class got way easier around exam 2. I feel that most people were exaggerating about the difficulty given that we are at UT and wanting to go to med school...
