Absolutely horrible. Take someone else and save yourself. His exams are impossible and he doesn't care.

Dr. Wilson is a super nice guy and this was his first semester teaching at UT. However, his class was much more difficult than needed. I think he came into UT intending to make his class harder for a "smarter school" and it didn't go as planned. Exam averages were consistently high 60s-low 70s. I think he will improve as time passes. Good EC.

Dr. Wilson definitely has passion for teaching, but he made his class way too difficult. For the first two midterms, the question were very detailed and lecture based, so I would recommend watching the lectures again instead of reading the textbooks. It is doable, but you would have to dedicate a lot of time just to understand one lecture.
A million slides and tests were basically impossible to study for. If you are already not to great at biology, get ready to cry.
learned a lot at the expense of my sanity.

Insanely difficult professor. TAKE ANYONE ELSE. He doesn't lecture and makes exams so hard to the point where the TAs can't answer exam questions. He will tank your gpa and he will not care. Absolutely horrible and I wished I had dropped when I had the chance.

He's a good guy, but this class is genuinely worse than ochem, physics, or genetics combined. It is soooo lecture heavy, and when I read the material, I genuinely do not know what is important or not. His exams are extremely specific, and he does not let you see your exams afterwards, but the final is composed of past exam questions.

Wilson's first semester was rough. Exams were major examples of such. I would say such were unreasonable in their difficulty and that 326R under Wilson was 1 of the most busywork filled classes I've taken thus far. Said Busywork did not help on exams. Drop before exam 3 so he may have improved in the final stretch. Still, I do not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The beginning of the semester was a rough start as his exams were really difficult and didn't correlate at all with the homework, smartbooks, or quizzes we had to do (a LOT of busy work). He made good changes for exam 3 and did take our feedback, however, which is why he's getting a 3. Hopefully next semester will be a lot better for him.

From a senior, while Dr. Wilson may seem caring and kind, he expects too much from students with ALOT of unnecessary busy work and exams being too difficult. His lectures are dense and not helpful. He made some changes, but the changes were not drastic enough to give higher than a 2, trust me there are way better more structured professors at UT.

Professor Wilson's exams did not correlate at all with the lecture material. During lecture, he skips around slides and different powerpoints and makes it difficult for students to follow along with their notes. Busy work assigned in homework, smartbooks, and quizzes have no connection to exams.

Microbio is a difficult subject, but Dr. Wilson did a great job of highlighting how applicable it is. He is super accessible outside of class and always willing to answer questions. Seeing as it was his first semester at UT, there are certainly still some edits to be made to tests/assignments, however he was very receptive to feedback and curved.

His first semester at UT, but hes taught for years before this. The difficulty and misalignment of exams to what is covered in class is just not acceptable. Curving and extra credit is just slapped on top to try and makeup. My grade recovered slightly. My stress levels never will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The concepts are not hard to understand at all, but the sheer amount of content can be hard to memorize. Everything on the exams is found in the lecture slides (few exceptions, but he removed questions + curved). I've gotten >100 on all 3 exams. Prof and TAs are caring for students. He just needs to fix content distribution because unit 1 was hefty

Each exam has a lot of content, especially unit 1 (so much memorization) but it's not hard to get an A overall in the class because its only 10% of grade and there's a 10ish point curve each exam. Slides are directly pulled from textbook, so you don't really need to read textbook besides for completion assignments. End-of-semester project isn't bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Maybe he'll be better in the future, but this semester was NOT it.

Prof is nice, caring, and receptive to feedback. First unit was rough, it's his his first sem here after all. He listened to feedback and exams got easier. There's a lot of HW, but they are easy completion grades. A LOT of content slides, but sometimes he'll cut them if we don't get through them. Final project is easy enough, TA-graded. 1.6% EC

Units/exams were super content-dense and tested on tiny details. He tried to give us a group project to save our grades, but instructions were extremely vague and even he didn't know what he wanted when asked. He generally didn't seem to be sure what his expectations of students were except "high". He also made up curves/points recovery on the go.

While this class was difficult and I didn't do great in it, I did enjoy and have learned a lot. I would take it again with Dr. Wilson. He's a good professor and very caring. I would recommend reading the textbook if you can.

I really have enjoyed this class. Dr. Wilson is a good lecturer and he cares. The exams, which everyone has complained about, account for a very small portion of your semester grade (30%), and they actually weren't that hard. With or without the generous curve I've gotten an A on all three....
Dr. Wilson is a decent professor, but his class is a mixed bag. the first exams were really stressful, and there's a lot of busy work that doesn't feel helpful. It's not the worst class
Solid class, solid professor. Nothing to write home about, but certainly I have no complaints.

His first two exams were really difficult and stressful, but he was able to adjust his third exam so it was a normal difficulty. He assigns HW/smartbooks which don't help w/ the course at all, and are busy work. He also doesn't skip over slides as much as he used to. It's good to see that he's changed the way this course is based off our feedback.

With it being Dr. Wilson's first semester at UT, he was receptive to student feedback and implemented changes immediately. First exams were challenging, but he made changes, curved, and midterms are 30% of final grade. In addition, if you go to TA study sessions you get extra credit. Lectures and case studies are entertaining. He is a cool guy.

completely unrealistic expectations in my opinion. i attend class, do the homework, study on top of that, and still cant pass the exams. its very difficult to figure out what we're supposed to study or focus on because he wont tell you. tons of small assignments too that are time consuming and dont even really help your grade or learning
Avoid him if possible and take with Partridge. The exams are insanely difficult and the difficulty of the class is unfair compared to Partridge.

Dr. Wilson makes his exams extremely difficult. It is stressful and has ruined my interest for microbiology. Exam 2 average was a 58. He's a nice guy, but the main reason why his RMP is so low is because of the difficulty of his exams. Make exams easier and remove all the busy work (the smartbooks) and people will enjoy your class more.

Dr. Wilson is a very kind professor and he is super passionate about teaching and microbiology. He assigns readings due the day of lecture - If you do the readings, it makes lecture much more comprehensible. I find his lectures helpful, everything he lectures about will be on the exam so it gives me an idea of what topics to study more in-depth.

Dr. Wilson's microbio class will not be easy, but this is my favorite class I've taken at UT. The class is a lot of work, but the topic is super interesting and the homework is meant to cushion your grade. Pay attention to the case studies and go to office hours! Get to know Dr. Wilson, he's amazing!

Listen to everybody else and do not take this class. The tests are impossible and he is all over the place in his lectures and skips 3/4 of the material that shows up on the tests. There is no way to study everything and the TA's don't even know the answers to his test questions.

I took this class for one day and dropped it because he was the worst teacher I have ever seen. His expectations were absolutely unreasonable and his teaching style was terrible. I have never seen a professor that is more terrible and hated than him.

If the sheer amount of criticism you've read so far isn't enough, here's my take. This professor provides a plethora of information through lecture slides and busy-work that would seemingly be indicative of what would be on the tests. Wrong, there is no way to study for these exams and he doesn't respond to feedback nor keep TA's in loop. Beware…
Worst professor in all of UT austin and maybe the world tests are impossible WTF!!!

Dr. Wilson is the worst professor I have ever had at UT. Exams are nearly impossible, especially given that he skips lecture slides in class and assumes we will just magically know the material come exam day. It sucks, because he makes a bio elective feel worse than a weed out class - avoid him at all costs if you enjoy being mentally healthy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Why did most people at Texas State recommend him, and at UT he's uniformly hated? Did he come to Austin and decide he wants start torturing people?! Anyway, everything everyone is saying is true. Busywork- endless. Tests- impossible. Response to feedback- ambivalent. Path to a good grade- complete mystery. Hours out of class needed per week- 20??

The structure of the class is difficult to follow. You learn so much material, only for the exam to not represent what you studied & the wording is confusing. Other microbio professors have clearer class structures. The lecture slides are so dense & he skips over so many slides, saying that it should be review. He doesn't take criticism seriously.

Please beware this professor. The textbook assignments are entirely useless and his exams have questions irrelevant to the lectures and reviews he himself posts. I genuinely can't recommend this class to anyone. Study hard and memorize everything you possible can. I'm so sorry if you have to take this class you have my condolences.

This class makes learning stressful. I came into the class excited about the course, and now feel defeated, demotivated, and unheard, because nothing was changed based on our feedback and poor performance. I wish I could have liked this class and/or took a different microbiology class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His RMP at TXST gave me high hopes, but his first sem. at UT ends up being poorly planned, lectures are scattered, and tests are substantially more difficult compared to the content taught in lecture or in homework. He doesn't take students' criticism into account as much as he should, considering an unfair majority of the class probably struggles.

The WORST professor I've ever had. He makes micro incredibly difficult when it shouldn't be. The TAs have no idea how to answer questions because the exam content is so incredibly difficult. I have never struggled as much as I am now. Please take ANYONE else. I wish I waited another semester to take microbio instead. He will TANK your gpa

The lectures do not cover all of the material, so there is a lot of self-studying. There are quizzes, homework, readings, and random extra assignments assigned each week. Slides are ALWAYS skipped in lecture, and students are expected to learn everything on their own. Tests cover material outside of class and are unreasonably detailed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a kind person but the course is absolutely awful. The workload is ridiculous that it seems he forgets that we have other classes that also require our time and effort. It is impossible to do well; 4 exams with no drops, constant HW and in class assignments, quizzes, group projects. Very defeating class structure, its unbearable.

I honestly cannot describe how awful this professor is. I have taken some terrible professors while at UT but this man is honestly something else. He barely pretends to actually care about us and really just wants to keep lowering students' grades to make his average look decent as a new professor.

The lectures are not well organized and there is a bunch of information that you have to understand (He also skips slides, so it is hard to know what to focus on). Homework and quizzes do not reflect what will be tested on. Exams are extremely difficult and do not represent what you need to know in the learning objectives. Find another professor.

His exams are very difficult and cover materials that were only taught in his office hour. His homework and quizzes are not representative of his exams. He does very little curving. Exams cover a lot of content but he does not provide topics that should focus on when preparing for exam. Do not expect test grade to represent your level of knowledge.

Do not take this class with Dr. Wilson if you can help it. There are other professors at this school that are much better at teaching microbiology. He is a nice guy but he is so bad at lecturing and it is so unclear what is going to be on the test.
Nice guy but tests are impossible. Not clear on what is testable material and test questions are extremely complex. Would stay away from this class cause it will hurt your GPA

Teacher does not use learning objectives or listen to feedback. Expects us to know 250+ slides. HW and readings do not help with the exam. The slides are not well written. Introduces random class assignments we have not learned. TAs are confused by the class expectations. Exam average below passing and expect to memorize unnecessary details.

If you're taking micro bc it's required, wait another semester and take someone else. Only take if you wanna be a microbiologist, but even then expect a trial by fire with the hardest bio class you'll have taken so far. Tests cover "applications" but really cover obscure knowledge he didn't cover in lecture.

Possibly the worst professor I've had which sucks because he seems like a nice guy. The exams are extremely difficult and require so much knowledge that we aren't taught but are expected to know. Half the time the TAs don't even know what's going on and have apologized for how hard he makes the class. The other micro classes are nothing like this.
He is a bad lecturer and the exams are made up of everything we don't learn. I genuinely have no idea how to be successful in this class because everyone does bad and he barely curves or anything.

Ya'll are actually playing with these 5 star reviews...This class is extremely difficult and it stems from the fact that there is a lack of clarity in his expectations. Him dedicating a class to our complaints and saying, "Yeah idc sorry," is actually a real thing that happened and I really hope you do yourself a favor and take someone else.
This class is hard, but Dr. Wilson is super kind

I really like Dr. Wilson. He's by far my favorite professor this semester. He's a fantastic lecturer who is passionate and super knowledgeable about the material. He incorporates case studies into the class and other short stories which make the material feel more meaningful. He also includes tidbits of his own research and personal life.
just finished the second exam and it might have honestly been worse than the first. wilson actually doesn't listen to any feedback. 100% the wrong choice for microbio, don't take this man.
sigh... just obscure class with obscure expectations..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Had slides that were 60+ and went through about 10 of those slides but expected you to know everything else from the slides he didn't go through. Had terrible communication, would tell students to study one thing and another group of students to study another. Exams are impossible to pass unless you devote your entire time to the class itself.

he simply doesn't care about his students' success. way too much information is rambled to us during lecture, he goes on frequent tangents, talks about himself 90% of the time, and we have to read textbook for hw that is not relevant to the exams. I am just so confused about the unclear class structure and he makes micro much harder than need be.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had at UT. I have had a few bad professors, but at least they were open to feedback and could make their expectations known. After students emailed him for the first exam, Wilson spent an entire class (which could've been devoted to lecturing) defending himself. He incorporated none of the students'

An actual irresponsible professor. Skims over stuff in class and harps on random topics that don't show up on the exam. When asked if he ever mentioned a topic that is asked on the quizzes in class, he always says he said it to one of the three class periods or that it was prior knowledge.
He's awful. I am a senior and this is the worst professor I've had at UT.

makes microbio 10X harder than other professors. exams are extremely hard and dense. doesn't provide clear study materials and is vague when we ask him what to study. exam questions are written badly. does not reply to my emails. one of the worst professors at UT. talks about himself all the time and doesn't care about students at all.
If you take Dr. Wilson prepare to memorize 300+ slides for each exam. If you haven't taken biochem, good luck.
He is the shabbir of the ut bio department, his exams are unreasonable and do not directly align with lecture, tons of busy work with minute details that were barely covered in lecture

Take quite literally anyone else if possible. He is easily the worst professor I have taken at UT. He acts like he's teaching microbiology to graduate students and thinks everyone has an incredible amount of time to pick up on the minute details he mentions in lectures. I greatly regret taking this class and hope others don't get stuck with him lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE!! Wilson was the worst decision of the semester, as he overloads students with assignments irrelevant to his exams. After the first exam, he dismissed students' complaints and stated, "I hear you, but I'm not listening." All of the TAs are confused and can't help students because he makes the class unnecessarily challenging. AVOID HIM!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Please don't take his class if you're interested in microbiology!!! You will spend the whole semester stressing over the seemingly random pieces of information he mentions but doesn't teach that make up most of the exam. Industry veteran with some interesting stories, but he WILL ruin this course for you!
Content covered and tests given just don't correlate. TAs seem poorly prepared and unsupported. He's new to UT, so I suppose we can also blame the people who hired him for such a messy semester

On worksheets, quizzes, and exams, he often asks questions he didn't cover in class, aren't on the materials provided, and you were not told to seek info out on. No drops. Incompetent professor, thinks he's the first application-based course for THIRD YEAR stem students when in reality 50% of the application Q's are niche knowledge questions.

He  laughs at students' confusion and complaints about the structure. Is not clear cut about what to focus on for the exam. He doesn't care about his students and their inability to understand him. He is overly passionate about microbiology to the point he forgets he is teaching an undergraduate class. DO NOT TAKE HIM

When your TAs don't even know how to help you in the class, you know you're screwed. We get hit with tons of info with very little guidance on what to emphasize. His office hours are useless too. He doesn't communicate with the TA's either and even they don't seem to understand some of the concepts as their micro classes were way less challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Expectations are both high and unclear. Exam I was a bumpy start to what looks to be a poor planned semester.

Just finished the first exam, and it was rough. Lectures are so scattered, difficult to understand, and have NOTHING to do with the textbook/learning objectives. Dr. Wilson is infuriating as he laughs at students' confusion. He wants to emphasize "understanding" of the material with no effort to properly teach it. Take anyone else if possible.

Genuine, nice, wants to help students. Lectures aren't the most helpful. Lecture slides aren't fully accessible but have the most important info you need for exams. Exam reviews mirror exams closely. Great TAs for lab. HW is not overly difficult and tends to be more difficult than exam questions.

Professor Li is the nicest professor you can have in ECE. She only wants you to understand theory and do the labs which are very straightforward and easy. The exams are word for word directly from the powerpoints. You only have to just pay attention to 70% of lectures and you will get an A

Super fun class with lots of interesting topics covered. Prof. Li teaches the fab process and steps clearly, making sure you have an intuitive understanding of each step. Lab was fun, hands on experience in fab of devices in a cleanroom. For exams, attend lectures and know concepts, graded for specific key words and steps for design questions.

He makes simple concepts somehow impossible to understand. Lectures are difficult to follow. Despite being a neuro class, this course covers strictly math concepts. Exams are difficult since he thinks he explains concepts much better than he actually does while the entire class stays confused.

Took class after seeing previous reviews, but unfortunately prof has significantly changed class structure. Lectures difficult to navigate. Exams are no longer take-home writeups, now difficult. Quite lenient on grading is only good thing but still low exam scores due to hard concepts. Very hard class now, take another neuro class to fulfill degree

Professor is not good at explaining concepts. Even though this is technically a neuro class, it's a ton of math which he expects you to already know the fundamentals of. He password protects lectures and files, making it a pain to access them and download to write notes alongside lecture.

This class changed my life. Yes, it's very math heavy BUT he is so fair in grading, homework and exams. The exams were open note and I thought were a fair representation of the course material. OH and rvw sessions were beneficial too. You can tell he cares for his students, he's also knowledgable in the field. deff take it, not a hard class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had no computational/math background so there was much new (but useful) material about understanding computational modeling of neural systems but he explained very comprehensively! Dr.Wei and the TA sessions were clear on exam content and helpful for preparing. He took student feedback and made availability for students outside of OH if needed.

Dr. Wei is a great professor. Don't be afraid of taking Neural Computation with him because of the complex topics. Go to class, ask questions, take notes, and watch YT videos if you need more math help. This neuro math/cs is a great foundation for any further work in computer vision/neural networks type stuff.

A lot of assigned material (readings + film) outside of class, but they were all interesting, albeit the readings can get dense. Class is discussion heavy, so make sure you come prepared. Low-stakes weekly response essays to assigned material, group presentation, and final essay (focus on this). Overall super fun and informative class.

Yes it's a little intense for a lower-division class but I had fun and never thought that the assignments were too hard. Easy 2-page film reviews that once you get the formula down you can just repeat every week and she gave me 10/10 on almost every one. Just like watching films before you sign up for a film class (I saw that problem in my class).

The class consists of almost weekly 2 paged double-spaced papers that analyze assigned movies, but that's it. You WILL be paired up with a partner where you need to lead the discussion, but only once. Readings are practically unintelligible- and she knows this. The only bad thing was the strict attendance policy. 3 absences then letter grade drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took her film class to receive a flag I needed, she was very pretentious and condescending. The course isn't well structured and consists of watching several films repeatedly and discecting scenes in class. 70% of the course was taken up by group presentations. High work load and there is 1 paper worth 30% of your grade, the reading is nonsense

His lectures are very boring, and you won't learn anything. Quizzes became more about memorization of homework problems than actual learning. If you can self-study well or have some preexisting knowledge, you will be fine. Otherwise, try to take it with someone else. However, he does give lots of partial credit on the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty pointless. He teaches straight out the textbook. First two exams werent bad and he does a decent enough job of telling you general problems on tests. But, the final was awful. Had an entire problem that was never taught in class and genuinely no one knew how to do.

Terrible lecturer, excellent one-on-one. Go to office hours, read the textbook, and put in the effort of learning on your own, and you'll be ok. Despite the terrible lectures, he is a very kind person who is willing to explain the material and help you. Genuinely cares about the success of his students.

Bad lecturer. If you can stomach self-studying entirely, you will be fine. Quizzes are directly from textbook problems, and tests are similar to, but harder. The problem is, you don't learn much, if any, dynamics fundamentals/intuition, you just end up memorizing textbook problems. If you want to actually learn dynamics, look elsewhere.

Weekly homework with a quiz during discussion. The quiz was a homework problem with different numbers. There were 2 tests and a final. These questions were picked from the textbook, so it was pretty easy to practice for them. All things are graded with generous partial credit. He adapted his teaching to help the class. Very nice guy as well.

I hated this class. The only day Dr. Hamilton taught an informative class was the day she was observed by higher-ups. Your grade comes from teaching a PE lesson as well as weekly discussion posts and a midterm+final. Strict 0 absence policy or you fail. Don't waste your time in this class, you won't learn anything.

If you have the possibility to take a different professor for EDC 314, do it! Professor Hamilton not only was slow and repetitive during lectures, but constantly contradicted herself and treated the students like children instead of adults learning to become teachers. The TAs were the only saving grace for this class.

Absolutely awful. Just the worst in every way. Made statements such as:
1. "Students are either normal or disabled."
2. "If a student can't meet the PE Standards for any reason, they should be failed."
3. "Weigh yourself every day and don't eat if you don't need to."
Harassed multiple students after classes for their disabilities and identities.

She changed the project guidelines every week and treated students poorly. She also said things like "we should fail children with disabilities who don't meet standards" and "ladies weigh yourself every day and never gain weight." She was confusing, outdated, and none of the students respected her after 3 weeks. Choose the other professors!!

Very easy class. Do not buy the textbook, it is very useless and definitely not necessary. There are no tests besides the fitness ones you have to perform. You are given opportunities to revise all the writing assignments, essentially guaranteeing a 100.

Fitness For Life is such an easy class. You don't need to buy the textbook its basically useless. There is no exams. You just need to write for majority of the class and you have revisions to get a 100. Her lectures are pretty boring and will make you stand up and do stuff in class but just do homework or something else to keep yourself busy.
She was sweet, but lectures were very long and pointless. She had a habit of rambling about topics that were not even related to what we were studying. TA did all the work. Easy class though.

I took the Fitness for Life class and it is a solid, easy choice! The class is about improving and setting your own goals for physical activity, so it's a great 2-in-1: getting in exercise and an easy class for your GPA. My TA was also really nice. There's a textbook for the class but I didn't use it, honestly. Would totally recommend for a UGS!

Fitness for Life was an easy fun way to get your UGS credit. You do have paper assignments but they are extremely easy as long as you follow the requirements. The TA is the person who led our class zooms, but my TA, Toby, was great. The class is really fun and encourages you to stay in shape. This is an easy A if you get your work done on time.

I took Fitness For Life, and it was the easiest class I took this semester! No exams, just a few papers, and revisions are allowed. But the TAs grade pretty easily, so you probably won't need to. For this class you either use an Apple Watch or Fitbit (provided by TA) and track your fitness data throughout the semester. Weekly discussions are easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fitness for Life is the easiest class you will ever take at UT. There was zero interaction with Keating, and class structure consisted of a one hour weekly discussion section with a TA (mandatory), short discussion posts, an oral presentation, and a handful of writing assignments. Grading was an easy 100 on nearly all assignments. Take this UGS!
This class is an easy A, and online there is no interaction with the professor. But the readings and the papers were super easy so I recommend this class and this professor.

I took her for Fitness For Life and it was by far one of the best decisions I made. You show up to class and get an A basically. She was not a hard grader and the papers and readings assigned were minimal and/or easy, so you'll be fine.

Dr. Keating is an amazing professor! I took her "personal physical activity" class and she and her TA Xiaolu are the greatest! They explain all the assignments very clearly and are not tough graders. Attendance is mandatory, attend class and get the A. Easiest class I took all semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took her personal physical activity class in the Spring, but she teaches a similar class in the Fall called fitness for life. The teacher and her TA were helpful and nice. We got to go play outdoors on Fridays. This was a fun class and I really enjoyed it. One thing to watch out for is that the attendance is mandatory and effect your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: The Fitness for Life class was relatively easy. You just show up and do some simple assignments and you get an A. You have to show up though and cant be late more than twice or she starts docking your grade. In terms of UGS classes, this is by far one of the easiest ones on calls, definitely recommend. Oh and each Friday you play a sport.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The contents for this class are difficult as is, and although the professor is very nice, keeping up with her lectures was hard. There is quite a lot of information for the class and the lectures covered a lot of material per class. The exams are weighted the most and can be challenging if you don't study thoroughly.

Super nice but soft spoken. Was hard to pay attention during lectures and usually never finished her lectures. She did have the high A distribution though so maybe she gives a nice curve. I think she's also retiring so wont be teaching again not sure though.

One of the worst classes I've taken. Xiaolan's nice, but she gives you the same randomly assigned group for all of the cases throughout the semester, and you don't get to switch groups at all, regardless of how many people complain about issues they've had with their groups. Other profs let you pick groups/switch. Would not take again.

FIN 367 kind of sucks, but I think she's better than she gets credit for, because she has the highest averages and makes the midterms seem easy. Connect homework is a complete nightmare and nothing like the exams, so don't waste your time. Most of the TAs have no idea what's going on and are quite rude. I'd say she's your best bet for the class.

Very hard to learn from lectures. Entire semester consisted of me teaching myself through the textbook because her lectures felt redundant. She provides midterm and exam practice problems but none contain explanations and only solutions so it's basically impossible to learn concepts you don't understand if you're unable to attend office hours. GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mindy is absolutely fantastic: her knowledge, passion, and intellect for FIN 367 are actually so inspiring. FIN367 is just inherently a difficult class (regardless of prof), but she does a very thorough job of explaining concepts in class and during office hours. She appreciates questions and will honestly break down difficult concepts. Love her!

FIN 367 is just an incredibly hard class, but professor Xiaolan does a pretty good job explaining concepts and making sure to answer any questions students have. Our class averages were significantly higher than other classes. Overall solid option for 367.

FIN 367 is hard with anybody. She is a researcher, so she simply isn't good at transmitting information to people who don't have a PhD. Fast paced class with two chapters each week. Smartbook and HW are excessively long and useless. Lectures for 75 minutes straight. If you want an A in the class, study outside of class.
Take metrics with Brendan Kline.

Sad to see the lack of engagement from the class- his humor is underrated! This class was very content packed which made it hard to process and remember everything for the tests. Good news is that they were not cumulative! Lab component isn't something to stress out about. I did every assignment the night it was due and got a 97+ on all of them.

Course is graded 65% lecture, 35% lab. Lectures are long but he tells you what specific concepts will be on midterms and quizzes (makes for easy studying). His accent really isn't that bad, just pay attention. Lab section consists of a couple papers, nothing crazy difficult just time-consuming. Be sure to get assignments in on time.

Professor Xu has a very heavy accent that is difficult to understand, and the course is very very lecture heavy. As a result, I don't feel like I learned anything. I paid a lot of money to hire a private tutor, and I feel like that was the only reason I didn't flunk the class. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are decent. The practice exams are very useful. The exam isn't too difficult. The writing section might take some time to find data.

Surprised by this rating. I thought he was fantastic. Lectures are fine. His accent is over blown imo however could just be me. Super nice guy very accommodating. I thought this class was fairly easy math was lite and essays were fine. Would be surprised if he's isn't the easiest metric teacher. 10/10

Nice prof. Clear slides and materials. Chill HWs. 2 exams. No final.
One of the best choices of Econometrics.
My lab (paper) TA sucks. Thanks Dr. Xu's curve.

Language/accent barrier made things hard to understand sometimes (not his fault). If you have a strong AP Stats background, it's really easy at the beginning of the semester. Homeworks are completion, and the entire course (minus the two exams) are all doable online, including the quizzes. Last exam cumulative before Thanksgiving with no final.

Professor Xu's heavy accent makes his lectures difficult to understand at times. Additionally, lectures are very unengaging and content is presented sporadically.  Although the class has a light workload (2 exams, a lab paper, and weekly completion-only homework), I would recommend taking another professor in order to truly learn the content.
His lectures are not helpful at all. The things that will save your grade are the papers, the first exam (NOT the second), and doing good on the quizzes.

Takes a while to understand his accent and lectures can be a little weird: it's hard to know what's relevant and what's not. Personally, the 'casual' way he lectures and his tangents help me pay attention since content is boring. Exams are fine and the class isn't hard. Homeworks are completion. I just struggled on the weekly quizzes a bit.

He is very kind and wants to help his students, however his accent makes it difficult to comprehend what he is teaching. Often goes on tangents about AI and data science which may not be relevant to many students. He was helpful on quizzes though and the lab portion was mangeable.

Very sweet man but just not a good teacher honestly. Stands and points at slides, and then rambles about how data science is the only useful skill. over a month in and I have NO idea what we are actually supposed to be learning. Also very difficult to understand. Honestly feel robbed paying for this class when all his material is from other profs

Professor was caring, but accent is thick and sometimes he wouldn't come with a mic. Lectures were iffy to go to and pay attention. Material covered is fair, with exams being short T/F exams with FRQ. Can honestly just study slides and reviews and get an easy B. Lab portion was half the grade and was easy, just don't procrastinate. Fair class.

Dr. Xu is very kind and is passionate about economics. He does really try to help you learn and is understanding. His lectures are rather long and can be kind of boring at times, but he is a good professor and teaches the material well. There is only one homework assignment a week for the class and two tests, so it is not bad workload wise.

could not understand his very thick accent, and suffered as a result. I went to his office hours and asked how I could improve in my studies and see what resources might help me (maybe some extra problems, videos, etc). He accused me of not attending his class, and claimed that's why I was doing poorly. I attended every lecture.
Seems like a very nice guy. I just have no clue what he's saying due to his thick accent.

If I could rate him zero I would.
The topics themselves aren't difficult - but he makes everything overcomplicated. I self-taught using the textbook
His accent is rlly difficult to understand and he does a lot of (unnecessary) work that's not on the slides
Doesn't really care about students and scheduled the final way before the examination period
very difficult to understand his accent. makes it hard to know what's going on, when he cant even pronounce the terminology of the math he's doing.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Xu cares about his students! This course is intimidating but he wants you to do good & is honest about what is expected of you. Course load is reasonable & rigor is usual for an upper division eco class. I highly recommend this prof, he is approachable & open to explaining topics further if needed. I appreciate Xu's enthusiasm for the material
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He teaches the course very well and makes econometrics much easier to understand. The lecture and lab were really helpful overall, and the professor breaks down complex topics into simple, real world applicable examples. He has a thick accent that at times is difficult to understand but his presentations are filled will great info.

He curves really well and the homework is great to pad your grade. I just had a hard time understanding his accent in class. Whenever I asked questions after class his explanations didn't help and he just repeated what he had said earlier and couldn't explain the concepts in a different way. Good guy but thick accent

Prof. Xus class is useful and the course is not so hard if you try to do the web assign hw and prepare well. Learned a lot and application to the paper session as well. He gives a lot of curve for exams. If you put time into the class, its not hard to get an A.

This class was a lot more time consuming than expected, but the grading was very fair and the tests were curved. Though Dr. Xu has a thick accent, he really tries his best to convey relevant information and really clearly knows his material well. The papers are long but teach a lot about practical application of econometrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is pretty easy. She reviews the same content multiple times so you really understand it. The exams are pretty similar to the practice ones she gives. It's sometimes difficult to understand her lectures and follow her notes, but it's not difficult to self-study, especially if you took statistics in high school.

Prof Zhang taught the class very well, and attending the lecture helped out a lot when preparing for the midterms. She used a strategy where we would make the equation sheet during class time and write down the more important formulas, which really helped a lot. Tests are kinda tough, but I usually use practice to study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 2 midterms, one gets dropped. Get equation sheet for each exam and always has practice test. There are participation quizzes but they're pretty much for extra credit. She goes fast, but not bad. Notes are posted.

CE 311S is easy if you go to class and lab. Homework sometimes gets tough but no big deal. Random quizzes to make sure people are coming to class. You get to bring a formula sheet to tests. Tests are pretty much exactly the practice tests. She's also very willing to bring in students who want to do research with her.

She went over a practice midterm the class before the exam day which made it super useful to study for her exams. She had random quizzes during class that weren't bad. Her lectures were useful and if you go to class and go over the practice midterm you should get an A.

For the most part, the homework was straightforward, as were the labs. Her lectures cover everything relevant to the assignments, but she usually moves too quickly to take notes. This is made worse by the fact that the annotated lectures are not posted. Still, as long as you follow the material and read the textbook, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not lecture well and made everything complicated. Annotated notes are not posted. Labs were every week which were more helpful than the actual lectures. Gave practice exams and didn't post the key for them. Have to attend class to obtain the answers. Attendance pop quizzes are determined with a coin flip. Good luck.
NA

Prof Zhang is not good at teaching. She makes everything super complicated when in reality you need to know a few simple formulas. Her exams are just like the practice exams, you can bring a 1 pg sheet from home, and she has pop quizzes by flipping a coin in class. I really don't like how she teaches but the content is fine if you look it up.

If you have to take an upper-division psych course, take his! The majority of his bad ratings are from old classes, but he's a good professor. Lectures were pretty interesting and funny. There are weekly assignments on Persuall, but it's just annotating, and there are a couple of group assignments, but it's such a chill class. Easy A for sure.

I would never recommend this class to anybody. He assigns so much unnecessary homework and readings that have nothing to do with what we are doing. Half the time he doesn't know what he's talking about, and makes the TA's do everything. The midterm project has literally no guidance and is graded extremely harsh. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I finished with a 98.7%. If you do the work and talk to the TAs, you'll be fine. The workload is tedious and often feels unnecessary. Ironically, he assigns a book on concise writing while requiring multiple 30-page readings each class. There was no syllabus until the second month, and it was just a flow chart with topics, not dates or assignments.

WHATEVER U DO PLS DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS the worse class i've taken in my 4 years of education. It is not worth ur mental health, 10/10 would not recommend this class, the grading criteria was so unclear, and the course is so unorganized and the professor is all about mentoring but is a terrible mentor.. pls listen to the reviews and save ur sanity

most of the assignments were making ~2-3 comments on readings which wasn't bad. what frustrated me most about this class was how unclear the expectations are for projects. you have to ask them for additional instructions or expectations that aren't explained in the rubric files. not a terrible experience but i wouldn't recommend to someone else
Prof is in class half the time, he doesn't even grade anything or give us feedback. For someone who preaches about the mentor mindset he's a pretty ineffective mentor

I have never been this stressed out in my life. I had to take this class for UD credits in PSY, if you don't have to, don't take this class please. From horrible structure to having little to no urgency about the projects. They worry so much about attendance/ daily assignments, it is honestly so annoying. I feel the TAs could do wayy better.

2 group projs, & filler hw that waste your time. Expect your grade to drop a letter b/c of a final proj. with a class avg of 60%, but don't worry you can revise it during finals week! Oh and mid-sem email sent after missing 2 classes, suggesting to drop the course if you "can't commit fully." Good content, horrendous waste of time, confidence lost

If I could sell my soul to the Devil to get back the time I wasted in this class, I would. The professor goes on tirades and likes to name-drop people you'll never look up. The lectures are so unstructured, and he has one "head" TA do all of the grading and work for him. If it weren't for my group projects (you have to do them) I would have dropped
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was interesting, and the lectures were great. The TAs were always willing to help. There are 2 presentations, and it just depends on who your partners are. You can always ask for a group change. Workload is tedious, but not difficult.  Dr. Yeager is an amazing professor. By far my favorite psych course!

I LOVED this course. Its tough, requires a lot of participation and time, & group projects were hit or miss.. but I found the TAs to be super helpful and always received great feedback. Dr. Yeager is super knowledgable and engaging. If you're passionate about this subject, TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is very interesting and engaging, however, a lot of the course is lead by the TAs. The rubrics for many assignments vary depending on the TA grading it so there isn't a definitive way to do the projs. There's a lot of readings but if you stay on top of the work you should be good. Def a class for ppl who are passionate about the subject.

The class relies mostly on your relationship to the TAs. Yeager himself is fine, but communication with the team is insufferable. There are quite a few TAs yet none of them seem to be on the same page about rubric/expectations. My grade felt like a complete gamble and their feedback was tough/unpredictable. Wouldn't recommend…

This class was riddled with so many unneeded assignments, which just felt like busy work. Dr Yeager is an Ok person but the TAs are what really ruined it for me. There seems to be a disconnect between how they grade (some grade leniently and others grade as if their lives depend on it.) 

I don't recommend

THE TAs ARE SO BAD!!!! Professor Yeager himself wasn't bad and I actually enjoyed learning/meeting him however the TAs are so rude and tough and that's where your grade comes from. Also why was there SO MUCH WORK wow. The only plus side is that the extra credit brought me up 6+ points.

SOOOO many assignments, seemed there was so much to turn in every week and the Canvas modules were constantly being updated and disorganized. This class had more work for me to turn in than my 6-hour credit course. Lectures are rushed. TAs say different things for expectations and they are tough graders. They grade you on class chats 4 attendance

group things, grades are tough itll be like good job but the actual grade wont reflect that so its like ?? u have to depend a lot on ur group mates, sometimes good or bad. a lot of pre discussion with chapters and long videos to watch, its really his book and data nothing else outside of the class. 4/10 wouldnt really do it again unless i have to
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Yeager does seem to teach this class based mainly on his research or that of colleagues he's worked with. I will say that group projects for an online class is quite difficult to navigate. The grading for the final project is also way more difficult than the other group project early in the semester. This class had little to no impact on me.

Dr. Yeager is so self-absorbed. I had a genuinely horrible learning experience because he talks about himself and his work ad nauseum. The TAs seem nice but no one seems to fully know exactly what's going on or how to answer questions- the class itself and rubrics are confusing and misleading. Save yourself the stress and do not take this class.

I found Dr. Yeager personable and I can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, but unfortunately I felt like this enthusiasm didn't fully translate into the class. TAs are rude, disorganized, and grading standards are vague.

By far the worst class I have taken at UT. Listen to everyone else. Grading is awful and unclear. Professor talks about himself and his accomplishments basically the entire lecture, I gained no knowledge from this class. 2 group projects which again awful because the rubric is unclear and they tend to grade pretty heavily. Honestly STAY AWAY!

I felt Dr. Yeager was very self-absorbed and just talked about himself/his own work basically the entire lecture always. I didn't think any of his work was very profound, but he still managed to be extremely condescending to students. Just being present in the lecture felt like such a bother because of his attitude and lack of organization.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: They can't even give you a clear description of what the class is about. They never have clear grading agendas. They grade harshly and give bad instructions. I hate this class and I can't wait for it to end.

Dr.Yeager is a great professor and a I really enjoyed this class. There was homework for pretty much every class which I wasn't used to with my other college courses, but none of it was that hard so it was pretty manageable. He definitely cared about his students leaning and not just proving how smart he was... He was also very funny.

I like behavioral science less now- from a values misalignment place. I do not think that spending valuable time, resources, and money on getting people to change their minds about inequality, rather than changing the inequality itself, is an approach I want to invest in. Also, TAs were disorganized, far too many tiny assignments.

There are so many participation assignments. 2 weekly readings. Prof and TAs were all over the place telling ppl different things. Very disorganized. 2 group projects (which were hard bc instructions and rubric were not clear and class was fully online which made it hard to contact group). Content was interesting, class was not good. ethics flag

The course isn't challenging, and as long as you participate, you'll do fine. 

However, I get the sense teaching this class is a low priority for him. I enjoyed the content, but felt he didn't care about building relationships with his students (went to his office hours; he was always pre-occupied, never remembered me, interrupted me a lot).

Dr. Yeager is a great professor who is clearly very smart and accomplished and also wants his students to succeed. He encourages an engaging and interactive classroom environment, even though the course I took was online. There is a lot of reading and assignments, but he makes sure students have the support and resources to do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Yeager was condescending and rude. He's a well regarded researcher and acts like he's a celebrity. Did not enjoy this class or interactions with him

Dr Yeager is super nice and values your input. The readings are manageable and relatively condensed compared to other classes. Quizzes are based on readings so no surprises. Group projects can be really enjoyable if you have a good group. All in all one of the best psychology classes I've taken at UT!!

I went into this class with a bad mindset, but I grew to really like it. I think Dr. Yeager is very passionate about the content of the class and I liked the way the class is set up. There are a lot of readings, but I usually just skimmed them and was able to follow along in lectures. There's no tests and a lot of opportunities to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Yeager really knows what he's talking about and is really passionate about the subject. This class has taught me so much. There is a lot of material, but it makes up for not having to do any tests, midterms, or final exams. As long as you put in the effort and use the resources they provide for you, the class enjoyable and an easy A.

Way too much busy work, super boring lectures, group work every day, quizzes over material learned weeks ago, 4 TA's but the class was very disorganized. Group project worth 30% of grade at end of sem. I'm disappointed that I have to leave this review bc Dr. Yeager himself seems really nice and passionate, it just doesn't translate into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He does not care about his students. His methods of grading are confusing and disorganized. Quizzes aren't even up to date with what he's lecturing, and it's 4 questions yet is weighted so much, so a few mistakes can tank your grade. I do not recommend it. TA doesn't care either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The material in his Ado Dev was super interesting, and in contrast with some of the comments below, he provided plenty of feedback and he showed he cared about his students not only by having office hours, but also by saying things such as: "as future leaders in your field..." or "I will always be a resource to my students".

I don't know why he was rated so low by some people. This was my favorite Psy class. Interesting, relevant, funny, never boring. He cares deeply about this subject and is very flexible with your needs and thoughts. Would recommend to anyone.

His class is  disorganized and he doesn't give any  feedback.  Very inconsiderate  - he once rescheduled class to 9:30 pm because the normal time didn't fit his schedule.  It's pretty clear he doesn't care about his students or about teaching.

Worst class I've taken at UT. Tons of work, but doesn't give you the guidance to complete it. Lecture style is SO confusing and rambling .... I went to his office hours once and he was generally unhelpful, condescending, disrespectful, etc. Never went back after that.  Also he made several insensitive jokes about Asians... My advice? STAY AWAY!

Best prof for 306 w/o a doubt, considering both lectures and grading. He explains in such a meticulous manner that anyone can understand. The programs are hard, homework are often lengthy, quizzes are take home, and exams are 100% fair. He understands everyone's background when lecturing and is truly the GOAT! He also does yoga and is a chill guy:)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Y is incredibly understanding of his students both in and out of the classroom, and he grades generously. I came into the class with zero coding/computing background, and I never felt behind in any way. Lectures are clear and well-structured, homework is simple and follows lecture material. Labs aren't too hard but can be time-consuming.

Was my absolute favorite!! Probably the best professor at answering questions in office hours. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He is so patient and you will not leave there confused. Class not impossible but coding exam 2 can kill your grade as its either 0, 50, 100 on exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Y is amazing at explaining concepts to beginners. He has office hours twice a week and is willing to explain everything as long as you are willing to learn. He is clearly passionate about this subject (somehow lol). He chooses great TAs and tells them to grade fairly, so tests are graded easily. He also gives out a lot of free food!

Super nice prof! Dr. Y is a fun lecturer and does a really good job of explaining programming from the ground up so that it becomes much more intuitive. His grading criteria is clear (programming assignments have an autograder) so it's not too hard to do well on homework. The TAs are also easy to reach and SUPER generous with test credit.

Dr. Y is a really nice guy. He wants everyone to succeed and clearly cares. His lectures are always chill, and I feel that he does a really good job of taking difficult topics and breaking them down. This class was pretty easy. The autograder on programming assignments came in clutch. Lots of instructional material and past exams to study with.

Very reasonable compared to the other ECE306 Sections. He's always very patient and accessible for office hours. Tests are similar to prior years so exams (3) usually do not get curved because they aren't very difficult. Although sometimes his lectures make you a bit sleepy, take him over other 306 professors.

He is a great guy, very chill and always ready to help. However, his lectures, at times, feel a bit scattered, though most of the content is essential for the future. I learned more from figuring out the homework than from sitting in his lectures. He often notes things about the industry, which makes his lectures interesting to listen to.

100% the best professor to take for 306. He explain everything so well from a beginner's viewpoint. The Midterms and Finals were also very fair as long as you have some idea of what you are doing. The programs do take a while in the end, but are still manageable. He is the GOAT. Can't wait to take him for ECE 319H next semester!
I am really grateful that ECE306 was my first programming class I took in college. Dr. Yerraballi is extremely knowledgeable and a great lecturer.

literally the goat, he teaches so calmly and you can understand everything he is talking about clearly. even with no prior knowledge, he understands everyones skill level and provides thorough explanations for everyone. homework is chill - once a week and not very long. attendance is non mandatory but definitely recommended!

Great class. Dr. Y is the GOAT and your TA's will help you tremendously. I took this class with 460N and made it through just fine. Labs take time but you should never be stressed if you start them early. All we had was 4 labs and weekly quizzes which helped with the work load. Apparently exams are coming back next semester though.

Dr. Y is amazing. The concepts will all be relatively foreign in this class but Dr. Y makes sure everything is digestable. The exams are more than fair and similar to previous years. The programming assignments are difficult but not impossible. Dr. Y also really cares and wants you to succeed. The grading curve is generous and I enjoyed this class.

Amazing professor, he is the GOAT. I love attending his lectures, and his office hours are extremely helpful. He cares a lot about his students and his class. He is a funny person, and so helpful if we go to him for help. Great at teaching! Definitely try taking his class!

Amazing professor: will explain topics in easily understandable terms and ASK. Code work is simple if you know archaic coders (LC3) except the final two. Go to office hours, he will answer questions—though verbose at times. The recitations are a nice way to reinforce previously covered topics. 2 paper exams are kind of difficult without coder.

Dr. Y is amazing!!! He's probably one of the best lecturers you'll ever have (explains pretty hard concepts in very graspable ways / layman's terms). He also understands students' situations and is just a really good person, too.
Amazing lecturer, genuinely a great person outside of class as well. If you do the homeworks and go to recitation/OH, you'll be fine for the exams.

Dr. Y is amazing! I wish I wasn't procrastinating as much and put in the effort from the beginning. His lectures and office hours are very helpful, and he makes sure we have a good understanding of the concept. We don't have extra credits but I think the exams are fair, especially if you are able to solve all of the homework problems successfully.

Yerraballi is the GOAT. Taught concepts very well, very kind and had many office hours available. Lectures were recorded and posted, so many people did fine without attending class or recitation, though I would still recommend going. Unintentionally hilarious, and he cares a lot about his students and their input.

Excellent lecturer, excellent person. Dr. Yerraballi broke down the most difficult concepts into basics where everyone was able to understand. He is respectful to students; he makes us feel comfortable asking questions. ECE319K was a fun class, and he was always happy to help.
Yerraballi makes the giant mess that is 319K slightly easier than other professors thanks to his lectures.
He's the GOAT. Best 319K professor and by far the best lecturer out of all the choices. Only problem is how everyone else joins his lectures and there are not enough seats.

I adore Dr. Y! He truly wants you to do well in his class. If you ever need help, he is there! His lectures are awesome too. 319K can be difficult at times but the profs and TAs are all there to help you. Please make sure to understand the reasoning behind why you do things in this class. It will really help your understanding of the material.

One of my favorite professors, super knowledgeable about everything. The weekly labs can catch up with you if you don't manage your time correctly, and make sure you pick a good lab partner so you don't end up doing all the labs yourself. If you study well for the exams and do the practice tests you will do well.
Dr. Yerraballi is an amazing lecturer. He explained everything clearly and deeply and conveyed it in an fun way. He was nice and considerate during office hours or before/after class. Good professor.

He is by far my favorite prof I have had so far, very helpful, teaches extremely well, theres a reason his lectures are packed when courses are standardized. I only got a B+ due to my lack of effort, he wants you to succeed and very obviously loves teaching.
Yerraballi posts all of his lectures & assignments online. His online lectures are high quality and enable you to do the class completely virtually. The assignments and tests were fair.

Dr. Y is one of the best instructors and lectures I've ever had. His teaching makes even the most obscure concepts simpler and easier to understand. Class is structured so that no single program/exam hurts you, but make sure to stay on top of all your work. Take him for 306 if you can!!!

Dr. Y is the absolute BEST choice for 306! He really cares and knows the key to our hearts is free cookies. Tests   (15%Midterm + 15%Final) could be prepared for with TA sessions and past exams. Programs (30%) should be started ahead of time and tested thoroughly. HW(20%) is very important so do well on the beginning ones. Overall great professor.

I thought that this class was fairly interesting even for someone like me who HATES LC3. Make sure that you think of EVERY possible test case on your programming assignments. It's very common for students to not prepare for extreme test cases and then get Bs on their programs. You'll definitely understand what I mean when you're in the class.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer. He draws out visuals and uses diagrams to complement his teaching. His OH are very helpful if you need help. Programs and homeworks carry a lot of weight, so make sure to do them ahead of time. Attending class is important as he will cover a lot of material and topics within one or two lectures. Best prof for 306 imo.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer, and all recordings are made available. Take detailed notes in class, because he goes extremely in depth. Quizzes are taken online asynchronously, and the grade is mostly determined by HW and programs. Make sure to start HW early, or you won't finish, many are extremely long and in depth.

Dr. Y has won awards for his teaching and it shows in 306. Yerraballi is a god, but beware of the programming assignments especially the last few. Go to office hours for homework questions and programming questions, he is very willing to help you learn.

Instructions can be unclear on homework and programs (programs are 30%, so a small instruction-caused mistake can damage your grade pretty heavily), but otherwise a fantastic professor. Lectures are informative, beginner-friendly, and always recorded. OH are helpful. This is the prof you want for 306.

Dr. Y was an impeccable prof, who went above and beyond in teaching the low-level aspect of computers in EE 306. His lectures were intriguing, and his teaching style was unequivocally the best of any teacher I have had in my life. Although homework and programs did take some time, the end knowledge gained was fulfilling. Yerraballer is the goat.

Dr. Y is a fantastic 306 professor! Great lectures, very accessible (both him and his TAs) to help outside of class.
He teaches very well, and if you put in the work, you'll have a solid understanding of 306 topics.

Highly recommend!

Professor Yerraballi is an excellent knowledgeable teacher. He presents his lectures as if he's writing down notes with us on a program he created. He remembers the faces of the students in his class and is a humorous individual that is also respected by his students and the university. Definitely recommend taking his class. Programs are difficult.

Dr. Y is absolutely amazing, take him for every class he teaches. His lectures are paced well and in-depth and his OH are amazing. He postponed homework for midterms, makes lectures enjoyable and fun, and is honestly just a great person. He teaches 306 as if you have no base in coding at all, exactly as it should be taught.

1. Brought us cookies upon receiving Outstanding Teaching Recognition

2. Dressed up for Halloween

3. Postponed homework because other ECE classes had midterms/tons of work

4. Drippy

5. Cracks jokes

Legend. I'd give him a 10/5 rating if I could. Take him for every class he offers. 

Yerraballer = godsend.

I love Dr. Yerraballi! 

His approachability and thorough explanations make 306 digestible. Although the programs and homework are challenging, he reviews critical concepts in lectures/OH. His pace in lectures makes them followable; consequently, catching up is less stressful. 

He dressed up for Halloween and once brought us cookies! GOAT
Won Teacher of the Year, Gave Us Cookies. W Professor
Amazing Prof, I would take him for every class he offers. Plus he gave us cookies when he won teacher of the year. Go to office hours he's so amazing.
Gave us cookies for winning teacher of the year, automatic 5

EE319K is a difficult class because it bridges hardware and software on a rudimentary level. Dr Y approaches the material in a straightforward and organized manner that attempts to convey the significant material. Unfortunately, the quizzes/labs are often outside the scope of lecture material; regardless, Dr Y is a solid choice. Beware the final.
EE319K is a very difficult class, so best option is to come to Dr. Yerraballi. He is the best at teaching. Period.

Just beware that they will constantly change the syllabus since they use a website. They don't update canvas to accurately represent you grade so beware of that. You may go into the final thinking you have a 97 but that isn't the case. Made the final in person because of "too many A's" so that was rude in my opinion. Had him for 306 and he was nice

319K wasnt a difficult class, it was just time consuming and there was a lot of non-complex material covered. 80% of the class is just basic programming and the rest is basic circuitry, data, logic, etc. The midterms are easy 100s if you have the programming side down and the quizzes are open everything. The labs are tedious and time consuming too
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yerraballi is one of my favorite professors at UT. The class focuses heavily on labs, but Dr. Yerraballi does a great job at making them approachable, and explains the concepts behind it well. During class, he's not the best with questions, but is very approachable outside of class if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the best choice when it comes to 306 professors. His grading is easy and straightforward and the exam at the end is very simple.

Yerraballi means well but his lectures are a bit dry. OS is valuable mainly in the context of systems programming (concurrency,atomicity, etc), but most time is spent on labs. While not difficult conceptually, these labs are a bit excessive (30+ hours avg) but will definitely improve your programming skills. Just invest in a good lab partner :)

Dr. Y is an amazing professor, really engaged in what he teaches and obviously enjoys it. The class is very nicely paced and no prior programming experience is neccesary, just the logical mindset needed for it. They don't call him Yerraballer for nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Y is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. I came into UT with no programming background or anything and he taught in a way that even those with no experience can learn quickly and do well in his class. His office hours were incredibly helpful and he will work with you one on one and don't be afraid to send him an email or the TAs !
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Yerraballi was a great professor for EE 319K. He explained things thoroughly for students in lectures, as well as being generally nicer on grading. However, this may have just been because the class was online.

Took class in Fall 2020. Great at making sure his students understand the concepts. Class had good structure, lectures were very organized. and always available for office hours. Heavy on the WEEKLY QUIZZES, HOMEWORK, AND LAB ASSIGNMENTS. Always study and prepare by reviewing lectures & textbooks. Lab assignments ARE ESSENTIAL TO UNDERSTANDING.

I've taken 3 of his classes (306, 319k, 461s) and every time I took one of them they were my favorite class that semester. His lectures are very relevant and easy to follow, and he is very easy-going and nice. In 319k and 461s make sure you pick a good partner though, because that matters a lot. He is very helpful if you need help on any projects.
He was great at making sure his students understand the concepts. Class had good structure. Was always available for office hours, he never leaves more confused after leaving office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor for 306, his lectures were very good and explained content well. He adapted his class to COVID by making easier weekly quizzes than larger tests. The only problem is that sometimes the HWs are ambiguous and the TA's aren't great, but he is very willing to fix stuff and clear doubts in office hours. Start programs early! Solid choice

Tough class if no previous experience but amazing lecturer. Also really cares about his students. Homeworks were pretty demanding and were assigned each week however they were usually directly over the lecture material. The notes from each class are saved as a pdf after each lecture, which helps to review for tests.

This guy is a yoga extraordinaire, an EE wizard, and a big-time Yeraballer. Oh yeah, he also literally built his own house by himself from scratch. Besides being a cool dude, he's a very good lecturer and focuses on making all concepts extremely clear. Take him if you can, I would definitely recommend it.

Professor Yerraballi does an amazing job at explaining concepts from a ground-up perspective. If you go to his office hours, he will clear up any confusion you have on material or the lab so GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. He's also a good guy in general and cares for his students, understanding how difficult this class is.

Good lecturer, even more amazing person. Going to office hours will guarantee you leaving with a deep understanding of whatever your question may have been. He truly cares about every single student. If you find yourself doing bad in the class, shoot him an email, schedule a meeting, or go to OH and find out for yourself!

Get. The. Book. The homework will not be related to the lectures, until after the homework is due. One of the major problems I've had with this class is the ambiguity of the problems. So if you are good at self learning, Yerraballi is a great professor. He's nice and explains what he does explain in a calm and concise manner

This class is hard, but you learn alot. Dr. Yerraballi is very fair with grading and the TA's work hard to help you understand. Lectures follow the book so read the book before exams to study. Make sure to choose a hardworking partner for the PINTOS projects, start early, and utilize office hours. I got  a 74 and that was a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I personally really like him as a person but his lectures are really unorganized. He doesn't understand that there are people who have little to no program experience prior to taking his course. His office hours are helpful and I would strongly recommend going to the drop in tutoring at the EER. You don't have much time to complete homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Caring teacher but goes off on tangents. Can be rude to some students sometime. Crowded office hours but that is because he really knows his stuff.

I honestly don't get the hype. His lectures are disorganized. Tests are unfair (near failing averages with no curve). Labs have unexpected test cases. If you look at grade distributions, make sure to only look at recent years, bc he clearly made the class much harder. Tough way to start college with his 306 Nice guy though, and will help you in OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture professor but doesn't reply to student emails. 20 people in office hours at any given time Exams inconsistent with the practice tests Syllabus says no programming experience expected, but that is definitely not the case. Other profs are worse though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Cares about students and wants them to succeed. Available for many office hours but don't wait for the last minute before a programming assignment.

His lectures could be hard to follow at times due to his teaching style, but he is generally a good professor. Nice and encourages people to ask questions. His tests aren't quite as easy as they used to be but are still pretty fair, and there are a couple of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Grading on the programs could be harsh.
He's literally the GOAT. I love this man. Class is so easy to follow. He teaches amazingly clearly. The assignments are straight forward. Always available. GOAT
His lectures are really unorganized but his tests are easy. He is also very rude to his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very rude and very mean to his students. His lectures are unorganized but tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Y is an awesome lecturer. He explains very clearly and clearly cares about his students understanding of the topics. The lectures relate directly to lab which I really liked. Labs do take a long time (probably averaged 10+ hrs per lab) but this is standard for this class regardless of the professor. Ebook and youtube vids offer help a lot too.
Loved this guy. He obviously cares about his students and clearly explains everything in lectures. Its definitely worth it to show up to class. My one piece of advice is to pick a good lab partner

He has a well-earned award for Nicest EE Faculty. He is very helpful during office hours and his lectures go over everything you need to know for the labs. The tests are standardized across professors, but his lectures teach you enough to do well in them.
