A god. He cares so much about students. His lectures are so clear, the labs he gives are so helpful, and the exams are challenging yet fair. He is the best 319K prof in my opinion, and overall I learned more in this class than I have in any other class this semester. Labs take forever though. Expect 6-20 hours to work on lab, depending on the week

Dr. Yerraballi is a pretty solid professor. His lectures can be a bit boring, but they're straightforward and easy to follow. He's available outside of class and is helpful in office hours. I would recommend him for EE319K for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: LC-3 programs are difficult sometimes. I read the book to understand the concepts, but for me it was hard to piece it all together. Taking Dr. Y again for 319k ready to work harder than I ever have before. Hopefully ARM and C with resonate with me more than LC-3. Very caring and courageous professor. Read the book before lecture it helps.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer who teaches in a way to make material understandable. Although I have had prior knowledge for a lot of topics in class, the pace is set at a speed viable for new learners as long as you put the time to understanding. Make sure to show up to class as his lectures go over everything you need to know.

This class is very dangerous. It is easy to pick a partner who will do all the work, but you will fall behind and suffer. Y makes note of that throughout the semester, and he is absolutely correct. He generally does a good job of explaining things clearly and effectively, though he is not the most helpful guy in office hours bc he's always swamped.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The best lecturer I've had in college, he does a very good job of teaching concepts and using visuals to help explain everything. This course is lab-heavy and you will need to be very knowledgeable in coding to do well on exams! DO NOT pick a partner that does all the work, you will cheat yourself out of the learning process.

Dr. Yerraballi is a great explainer. I took both him and Dr. Telang and I can say that he explains the material much more clearly. His labs are also easier in my opinion. Will definitely take him for EE319K

Great professor that cares about his students. Dr. Y teaches in a natural way where he introduces material when you need to know it and writes down his own notes and visuals as he goes. The only possible negative is he is soft-spoken so some of my friends had trouble staying awake. I enjoyed his class so much I'm taking him again for 319K.
Great teacher, very helpful and clear presentation of information. Super helpful during office hours, but they get really crowded

Yerraballi is a wonderful professor! His lectures are clear and straightforward, his tests aren't very difficult, and he's very nice. He genuinely cares about his students. I liked him a lot and I'm taking him again for 319K! Definitely my favorite professor of the semester.

Dr. Y was great for 306. I think he is probably the best professor I have ever had at UT my first two years here. He teaches clearly and drills concepts well into your head. I think the experience overall was great-- he didn't count our final exam if it hurt our grade. He is a really nice guy and is always willing to help you.

Although Professor Yerraballi is a great teacher, he wasn't in charge of the EE319K course as of Spring 2016 (that responsibility fell to Dr. John Valvano, a very intelligent but scattered and disorganized man). Due to this, the quality of the course suffered - it was difficult to parse what was actually important to do in order to learn.

He's a great professor who cares about his students. Attending lectures is not mandatory but important for success. The labs were time-consuming but interesting and rewarding. I found the tests to be difficult, but coding isn't my strong suit. Yerraballi and the TAs were super helpful.

This class was not hard, but just took a lot of time with the labs. It's been standardized now, so everyone takes the same tests. Yerraballi overall is just an awesome guy. I had him for EE 306 as well, and he  knows me by name. I always visited his office every week, and people are out the door waiting for him. Take him.

Yerraballi is great at explaining things, if you can follow his messy notes. However, the class is mainly lab-based, and most of the time what you cover in class isn't helpful to complete them until the day before, and the textbook takes several hours of deciphering. Going to your TA's office hours is your best bet, but go early!

Dr. Y's a great professor and willing to help. This class is a lot of work. Get ready for many late-night codings. The tests are doable, but make sure you know the material well. It's very easy to fall behind.

Dr. Yerraballi (Yerraballer) is probably the best of my professors so far at UT. He's clear about his explanations in lecture, and won't hesitate to help you out with your problemquestions in office hours. He graciously made the final optional if your midterm scores were good enough to make your desired grade.  1010 would take again.
Yerraballi is great, and the class really isn't very difficult. Just keep up with your assignments and read the textbook (it's extremely helpful in understanding the material).

Dr. Y is an okay lecturer. This semester however he rushed through most of the material. The only people who understood the stuff in class were people with previous programming experience and who already knew the bulk of the material before taking the class.  He's willing to help in office hours but there's always 15+ people in line ahead of you.

Dr. Y was a decent lecturer; he got off to a slow start, then sped it up way too fast bc he was behind schedule. I stopped going to lectures after midterms, and I got a solid A in the class. Just read the book, do your programming assignments, and do your best. He even made final optional for us, so he's a nice guy. Office hours always too full.

This semester he and valvano traded off lectures in our class, which was a little distracting. Yerraballi is a great lecturer, and is fairly organized in his presentations. 319K is a swift moving course, and the labs take around 10-15 hours a week at the end of the semester.Prepare to pull all nighters debugging and ripping your hair out, cheers!

Professor Delville is extremely passionate and funny. He quickly responds to emails, and is very helpful during office hours. This class is test heavy, but if you listen to his lectures (which are recorded) and understand the concepts, you will do well. Questions are pulled directly from them and article readings he assigns. Highly recommend.

Professor Delville is amazing with enticing lectures and extremely funny stories. However, this was the hardest course I've ever taken. I expected it to be a psych course, but it was full on a neuroendocrinology course and had the hardest exams that I've ever taken. I had to change to pass/fail

LOVED him. he is so bubbly and animated. loves his job and psychology. easy ugs to take and he is sm fun. only thing we really did was a presentation on a research paper we got to choose. and a written research paper on the paper we chose (had to rewrite how we would do it) easy A! super helpful and great in office hours! take him!!

Was accommodating to students (sometimes pushed back deadlines). Learned a lot about stress from the class. Not many "lectures" either. Only 1 paper and 1 presentation for the class, which were both graded leniently. Also, easily accessible outside of class for feedback. Overall, great choice for a UGS credit.

This course was nice because Dr. Delville's office hours are very flexible. He didn't always give the most specific feedback and half the time I had no idea what was going on in the course. Nice man, but class feels a little unorganized. The work load is manageable, but it comes in waves.

Dr. Delville doesn't break things down at all. I'm pre-med and this class was hard for me. His exams are TRICKY. The major percentage for the class comes from 2 midterms (25% each) and comprehensive final (30%). Test reviews are NOT helpful. Be prepared to WORK HARD for each test to score well. This was my least favorite class all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super hard to understand, class consists of 5 easy quizzes and 5 easy assignments but the majority of your grade is 3 tests including a comprehensive final and the tests are HARD. I am a science major and still did not do well on his exams (C on the first one and a B on the 2nd and I'm taking the final tomorrow).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Delville is a very knowledgeable professor, but this class is difficult. Expect reading a LOT of research papers, and memorizing much more than you'd think you would for a psychology class. This is the hardest "psychology" class I've taken, and the only one with a (hard) cumulative final. In other words: this is a biology class, not psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He was always available for office hours and once spent over two hours having a conversation about class material and explaining things in depth to me. The material he teaches is not easy, but going to office hours pays off. Ask intelligent questions during office hours that show you are  invested in the material (which is very interesting)

In class, he may seem to genuinely care about students but this was not what I experienced in office hours at all. He wasn't paying attention to my questions, made me feel really dumb and test material only comes from lectures. Textbook optional. Also I had a 89.75 and he wouldn't round me up to an A. Pls choose another profclass if possible.

I had him for upper division neuroscience class - and I loved him. He doesn't use a textbook, so his lectures are simplified, without too much focus on the technical and the structural. He really wants you to know what is going on in the brain, rather than what does what function/structure wise. You have to attend lecture. Funny and down-to-earth!

If you aren't a bio major, his neuro classes can be difficult to understand. he is a very sweet and understanding teacher and will always help you if you can. He loves to talk about rat sex and hyenas and can be very funny at times. It isn't fair that people rate him poorly because his subject is difficult to grasp.

I really didn't like him. I felt he was arrogant and he thinks too highly of himself. You had to fill in a lot of the lectures (but the problem we don't use a book so finding sources are ridiculous). I didn't like him.

Okay if you took him for some intro to Psych class I could see easy, but I had him for a neuroscience psych class and this is definitely not the case. He is a nice guy, but prepared to fill in all the gaps yourself because he can not answer a question clearly, leaving you confused and frustrated. I am not the only one who has these sentiments. Kind
This guy has it! I mean, if you really just have to pass intro to psych with a C or better, then you need to go to him! Oh yea, and he's a nice teacher!

Delville is a pretty nice teacher that gives you all the notes you need for the test. No need to buy the book because it is worthless. As long as you listen to his lectures and review those notes for the test, you'll do fine in the class.
He likes to talk about sex.  Funny guy.

Dr. Yao is pretty good at explaining physics concepts and has helped me reinforce what I learned prior to his class. Make sure to read the textbook and DO THE HOMEWORK. It is just like the exams and for physics, practice makes perfect. Also you can skip the discussion, but have more weighted exams.

There's weekly homework, including exam weeks. There were 4 midterms, with 1 drop. He changed the final to a midterm retake, so I ended up not having to take a "final." Tests are similar to the homework and pay attention to practice questions in class. He uses Instapoll, so attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Got saved with the final exam being dropped. With a midterm avg of 82, didnt need to take the last midterm either but solid lectures, difficult material compared to phy 1. took perry for phy 1 and yao was slightly worse at explaining but way nicer and easier exams.

Physics will make you say YAOUCH but Dr. Yao is the absolute best. Physics 2 is a really uncomfortable class to be in and its constantly breaking your brain but Yao made it great. He had great lecture slides that made it clear how to do the homework and his tests were very fair if you study properly. Sorry for your loss Yao and thanks so much.

There is a weekly homework on Quest that is more challenging than lecture examples, but doable. The tests are similar to the HW, so if you can do HW, you can do tests. I took him for calc based physics 1 and 2 and learned so much. Can miss a few classes, but he has instapoll for attendance. Tests are NOT curved, but are not a huge portion of grade.

Dr. Yao is among the better physics professors at UT. Yao expects you to read the textbook, but he does cover everything you need to know in class with dense lectures. He gives 4 midterms (two being in the same month), but he drops one, and a 90 is an A in his class. Yao also replaced our final with a replacement exam. Plenty of potential for an A.

Dr. Yao himself isn't the best lecturer; however, if you have questions about the HW, he is good at explaining the question in office hours, and will ensure you understand it for future times. This is good because the HW is exactly the exams. He made the final optional my semester. To get the content down, I did the Youtube channel Chad's prep.

A chill guy, had him for 317K, class structure exact same, except he made final optional this sem. Definitely harder than 317K but not impossible. Exams very similar to HW and lectures. Practice the HW and actually understand the concepts behind the equations to do well. Use his OH and discussion, his TA and him explain very well. Overall not bad!

Dr.Yao is the nicest guy, he really is. This class always isn't, but the grading scheme is forgiving, midterms and final add up to 50% of your grade while the rest is HW, discussion, instapoll. Lectures didn't help me very much but genuinely do every HW question because exams are same format. Just put some work in and you'll get An A- minimum.

Exams are fair, very similar to HWs and practice exams. Midterms + Final = only 50% of grade. 90+ is A. Dr. Yao is passionate and knowledgeable, and made the final optional for this semester. Getting an A is extremely doable, even with other difficult courses. Definitely recommend Dr. Yao. He makes physics very manageable.

Genuine professor who is excited about physics, always eager to show you the demos. If you put in the work outside of class, you will be fine. You can tell Yao is passionate about physics, and he doesn't take offense to people being confused or disengaged. The TA you have also makes a huge difference. Mine was great.

Nice person, but a mediocre lecturer. Lectures mainly cover basic concepts, Quest HW expands on them and has you apply these concepts. Exams are fair and closely resemble the homework, so make sure you understand those problems. Grade breakdown benefits students and the class is precurved (A is a 90). For UT physics, he is a good option.

Lectures were boring, but 15% of your grade is showing up, so use that to your advantage. I self-taught the class though. Grading scheme is so nice! Exams are fine. You get a handwritten cheat sheet. The exam questions are sometimes similar to HW, but some of those questions came from thin air. I used the HW to teach myself the class.

He seems like such a sweet professor and was very lenient on his grading scheme even allowing us to opt out of some stuff (percentage just moved to a diff category). I didn't do as good as I had hopped, but I just suck at physics, but a lot of test questions seemed very similar to the HW questions.

This class was so hard for me. The professor was funny and had cool demos and he makes the grading scheme very generous. Reading every page of the textbook and doing all the homework problems 3 times over was not enough for good exam grades. I'd say get unique with study methods.

Yao is so nice and helpful, his lectures are dense and hard b/c he goes so fast, not his fault as he has a lot to cover in a short amnt of time. Go to discussion and OH to get full explanations. Tests are VERY similar to HW, so understand the HOW and WHY behind the HW Qs to prep for tests. Spend time outside of class, practice and u will be fine :)
Lectures were okay and homework was definitely where a lot of the material was expanded on. Discussion and lecture attendance were both optional and exams are exactly like the homeworks

The professor seemed nice, and his demos were entertaining. However, I really didn't find the content of his lectures helpful, since they covered things on a very basic level when compared with homework and exams. Averages on exams were consistently in the 60s, and he did not curve or offer credit back. Discussion sessions useless too.

Amazing person, great professor, horrible class. Its just simply unfair how hard the exams are. Sure the exams are similar to the homeworks, but not a single person gets the homeworks right on the first try or without outside aid. Just an extremely unfair class that focuses too much on hard exams which penalize you heavily.

Dr. Yao was a great professor. Although his class was hard, he was always very helpful in office hours and was very understanding of the struggle of this difficult course. The exams are very similar to the homeworks that he assigns so I recommend studying by using those.
Goated physics prof. Listened to student feedback and made exams less weight. Exams are doable as long as you practice old hw problems

Took him for PHY 1 + 2 and he is such a caring teacher. His lectures were difficult, but good OH. His exam is just like hw. No EC for PHY 2 like last year but he changed the grading to each midterm is 15% of grade, 1 drop. Attendance mandatory with Instapolls (4 drops) and 2 HW drops. Weekly discussion, super chill with good TA.

I took physics in high school and had a terrible time, but I took it again with Prof. Yao and learned a lot! He has good slides and explains things well, with a good mix of math-based and theoretical problems. There's a lot of extra credit built in and you only need a 90 for an A+. Go to his office hours, he's really nice and will explain problems

Yao is one of the best profs I've had! Super caring, and truly loves to teach. Exams are difficult and very time restrained, but you get a sheet of notes! He has a lot of super interesting demonstrations, and always takes the time to answer any questions you may have. Physics overall is tough, but he makes it fun! If you have the option, take him!!

Professor Yao is truly a nice person, however his grading is very difficult. Homeworks, exams, and a final are essentially what make up most of your grade. The homeworks are incredibly difficult since the lecture questions are way simpler. The exams are similar to the homeworks somewhat so if you do not understand them, the exam will not go well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yao is an experienced and patient lecturer, his lecture slides usually do a good job of covering everything on the quests and exams. Tests are tricky, but only an 85 is needed for an A which makes it very attainable. Quest HW weekly reading quizzes buffer your overall grade too. Overall solid option for Physics 2!

I took Yao for 1 & 2, and I personally think he makes college physics super doable. Some beg to differ. Way easier than ochem 1 & 2. Additionally, if you are taking pchem simultaneously during physics 2, you will find physics 2 super easy, as all it takes is applying algebra appropriately. Love Yao's demos, comments,  and passion for physics!

I took Yao for 1 & 2, and I personally think he makes college physics super doable. Some beg to differ. Way easier than ochem 1 & 2. Additionally, if you are taking pchem simultaneously, you will find physics super easy, as all it takes is applying algebra appropriately. Love Yao's demos, comments,  and passion for physics! Take Yao for physics!

Dr. Yao is really sweet, and an engaging lecturer! Homework problems require a significant time commitment, but if you can do them, the exams are pretty similar. The class takes effort, but the grade boundaries are also lowered/going to class adds around 5% extra credit.

Physics is difficult but you only need a 90 for an A and you get 5 bonus point for showing up to class. This basically makes it so you can get an 80 on every exam and still get an A. HW is similar to exams as well.

Physics is HARD, specially bc the class was graded mainly on exams (+ homework). Prof Yao explains things very fast, but he's nice when answering questions (def go to OH!!). Prepare for the exams with a week in advance (min.), and start the HW early. Be aware that this class will need most of your time when signing up for other classes.

Yao was a good professor. But this class is challenging,I don't recommend taking this with other math or chemistry courses. The HW needs to be started at least a week in advance. Exams were very challenging. Much of the work falls on you to learn the material prior to class since lecture is intended to be review and practice questions. Take at CC.

I Q dropped this class but it's not on the professor. He's fine, it's an intro physics class so don't expect something super engaging. Graded on 10 HW assignments and 4 exams (1 drop), everything from Quest.

Yao is a very run-of-the-mill professor. Don't be scared to take his class because it's honestly not too bad. He tries to keep it pretty simple, but it is physics 2. And he's genuinely a nice man who cares about his students and what he's teaching. Don't take the class for fun but if you need a physics credit he's a solid choice.

Lectures hardly ever matched up with hw/tests. Example problems were wayyyy too rudimentary and essentially useless for hw/tests, which is what the course grade consists of. You basically have to self-learn physics if you take this prof. If you could solve the hw you're set, but solving hw is incredibly difficult. Just self-learn while taking yao.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get the hate for Yao here. Physics is hard, shocker. He explains concepts well in lecture with good practice problems. The tests are hard but fair as they resemble the  HW, and your first attempt doesn't take off points on the HW. Cool demos too and lectures are recorded. Also, the grading scheme takes off pressure as you need an 85 for A-.
Implied a curve all semester until it came time to curve. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS.

Cannot recommend enough to not take him- test averages were quite low (48, 68, 71) and final average was 68%, but somehow he is convinced "the class average is pretty high" really hard to understand-especially in lecture. Only time i understood things was a few days before the exam the TA niral is amazing tho
I would give him a 0, but that's not possible, so I give him.... a 1.

Save yourself from a lot of stress & avoid.I worked my butt off for the grade I earned while I saw everyone around me struggling to pass. Exam averages were always low (1st was a 43). All he did was give us 1/4 credit back (what a joke tbh), if we redid test and got it right. I'm sorry but if the average is that low, the prof is obv the problem.

He helped me understand physics, and his lectures are easy to understand. Only physics class in which I understood what was happening. His exams are challenging, though, so make sure to prepare very well for those too, and go to office hours if you're confused. Dr. Yao is overall really caring and fair. Just be prepared to put HOURS for this class.

I really felt like Dr. Yao had a lot of empathy for his students and listened to our feedback. When the first exam average was really bad, he gave us an extra credit opportunity to fix our mistakes and the exam averages went up after that. Graded by weekly homeworks (a little over 20 problems on quest) + 3 exams (lowest dropped).

This class has honestly destroyed me and my mental health. I've done everything - master the homework problems and classroom problems/dedicate 30+ hours a week to this class, but for some reason, he always makes the exam questions WAY harder than anything we've done in class. I'd recommend to stay as far away from taking this class as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really wouldn't recommend taking this professor. His lectures are very dry and often were difficult to actually apply to the course material. When asking questions about how to improve and better understand the problems, he had little advice.

This class is very difficult. The first midterm average was a 45 and there were no curves for that midterm (or any midterm). The workload isn't a lot, but the concepts are super tough and I was left to fend for myself. Yao isn't the greatest lecturer and his slides are so dense it's hard to understand. Textbook needed for pre-class quizzes.

This was a very hard course. 3 midterms with 1 drop and a final make 60% of grade so do well on the hw and other assignments to create a buffer. 1st test avg 45, 2nd 65, 3rd 66. Weekly hw 24 questions is a lot and can't be done in one night if you wanna actually understand it. Take lots of notes in class and write his explanations for problems.

Had to work extremely hard for an A-. Got a 53 on the first test, which became my drop test. Mandatory final was like the 3 midterms. If you truly understand how to solve homework problems, the exams won't be too bad. Test averages around 66. Get 97-100 on homework, instapoll, and pre-class quizzes and you'll be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the class and the exams were quite tough. i learned more from the TA than yao. yaos lectures are kind of boring and he completely disregards the students who attended via zoom. he is also a little intimidating, which is also why i pref'd the TA. the first exam average was like a 40/45 and he didnt do much to change his exams or lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is hard, getting an A is a grind. Test averages floated around high 50s or so. Grading scheme already has 5% curve built in. Yao is very nice, but writes hard exams and is a mediocre lecturer at best.

I failed my first 317K class with a different professor, but Dr. Yao was great for my second round in physics! Attend lectures, ask questions, do the homework and the practice midterms. The TA's and him were helpful and approachable. Exams are MC but you get multiple tries on the homework. Overall, the content is hard but Yao makes it more bearable

Dr. Yao is AMAZING!! He gives great lectures and is so helpful during office hours. His class is very straightforward and working the homework prepares you well for exams! The TA's are also very helpful and caring towards the students. I originally was really intimidated about taking physics at UT but Dr. Yao made it very approachable!

I came in never have taken a physics course before and the prof and TAs made me feel like it. Yao constantly interrupted students when they were asking questions and would even laugh at some of them. He's ok as a person but generally unhelpful as a professor. However, the tests are easy and the hw isn't bad. You could get an A if you put in work.

Good professor if you do not know physics. If already familiar with the subject and need to take this class for credit it will feel a little tedious. Pre-class and in-class quizzes are a little silly for an intro-level online class. Tests are multiple choice with no partial credit despite better possible formats. Yao explains concepts clearly.

I've never understood Physics before. Dr. Yao has been the only person who has been able to make concepts clear for me and provides plentiful practice for each subject. He is very understanding with questions and never makes you feel stupid for asking one. I would highly recommend him as a professor to take!

Keep up with the reading! He breaks down the formulas and where they came from, but it is really up to you to understand the concepts. I would recommend reading before class, take light notes during class, and watch some Khan Academy or other YouTube videos to solidify your knowledge of the material. Exams are multiple choice and review homeworks!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took him over the summer. His lectures aren't mandatory, but they are recorded and I would recommend watching since he does a good job of explaining everything and does example problems actually relevant to the test and HW with you, hard to find in a physics prof. Extra credit was offered and the final was optional depending on grade.

I took this class for Summer 1 and it was great. Lectures were recorded so i could rewatch. 3 midterms and the optional final made it less stressful esp. during the pandemic. He is very passionate during the lectures and keeps it straight forward so you can learn well. HW heavy but tests are based off the HW so its understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Yao is a good teacher. His tests can be tough but if you do the homeworks and understand the concepts you will get an A. Yao is the boy.

This class is super hard if you didn't take AP physics in high school. Yao does as good of a job as one could with the amount of content he has to teach in one semester. However, he writes on the chalkboard instead of on the slides and doesn't provide answers to in-class slides which sucks. Not the biggest fan of this class, but overall it was fine

His lectures are very straight forward, with a lot of examples to help you. I'm super bad at physics but having to read in order to do the pre-quizzes (which aren't hard), makes sure you understand lecture a little better. Always has demos to help understand the concept and to keep students engaged. Doable amount HW and tests are same format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Best choice for 317L. Class is much harder than 317K, so unlike 317K, DON'T skip class: you want the answers to ppt questions. Lectures dry and dull, but stay awake bc he explains well. Tests resemble HW, so study them! Tests are pretty fair, but theory questions can suck. Study hard! Also, his demos are all cool witchcraft stuff, man's a wizard
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yao was a good professor. I would recommend his 317L class to anyone who needs a physics 2 class. My favorite part of the course was how fair it was; because the course is Quest-based, there is a clear path to success - do the homework and practice test, and you will do well on the exam. I also like Quest because none of the questions are ambiguous
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is curved from an average of around a 50 each semester. In my opinion, that much failure almost shames students for even trying rather than helping them grow. Yao is super kind and really wants his students to learn, but moves very fast and the tests are nearly impossible. My advice for passing them is to do a million practice problems.

Dr. Yao is a great professor. He really tries his best to make sure everyone understands the concepts. Though he can be fast and dry at times, this isn't his fault. Physics is just a difficult subject. Regardless, he tries to make the lectures interesting with the use of cool demos. In general, he's a very nice guy and an awesome professor.
I have studied the material all by myself, lectures do not offer anything more interesting than learning oneself.

Yao is a very nice man who really cares about his students. The class is weighted on tests and homework. The tests are similar to hw probs or lecture slide questions just with slight changes. Honestly did better when I didn't read the textbook because I had more time to understand the lecture material. Highly recommend ClutchPrep as a supplement.

Loved his teaching style. Very caring, he would stay well after his office hours helping  students. Doesn't bs you on tests and would even clarify a question if it was confusing. Reading the book and doing the HW's are a must, his lectures really clear up misconceptions. Pretty funny guy too. Open to questions about grades too. Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Zhen Yao is an amazing teacher. I love his teaching style - It is entertaining, and at the same time very informative.
He's an amazing teacher. I love his teaching style - it's funny, and very informative.

Yao was a great person, however it was hard to stay engaged in lecture. The test were fair, however easy to do bad cause questions were worth a lot. There was a one drop test and a final. One Quest assignment a week, and the test were somewhat similar to the homework. I hate physics so much, Yao really tried to make it interesting. I did learn.
frendly

Let me start off by saying I suck at Physics but the way the class was set up was nice because homework (quest) is only due once a week other physics classes have homework due twice a week. This caused me not to stay too behind. Attendace is kinda mandatory to take clicker quizes and at the end of the semester Yao curved, I passed bless you yao

Hard to understand at times, but is knowledgeable about course, you need to pay attention to his writing or you will get lost. However, you do learn alot by paying attention. Tests aren't that hard, just quest.
Professor Zoe is an incredibly kind and knowledgeable professor and is always willing to make accommodations. Grading is very easy as long as you do the yoga lectures. Overall very fun and engaging!

Beginning yoga is honestly not for pure beginners. She does NOT really explain or demonstrate the poses and the proper way to do them, which can be really confusing and even dangerous if you have actual zero prior yoga experience. Also kind of patronizing and self-serving sometimes with how she talked about herself and her accomplishments/training.

I did the web-based class so I did 2 45-minute lessons a week and recorded myself. Some weeks have a "meditation challenge" or other challenge. Midterm and final are not hard, and you can create something not just a written submission. She has flexibility with due dates. There are some extra credit options at the end or come in person for a makeup.

You could opt to go in-person or stay online to do the coursework. If you ever turned in something late or never submitted your assignment, just go to the in-person classes to get your credit back. She's kind of strict about the nature of yoga, so make sure to memorize all of the written portion of the limbs of yoga, niyamas, and yamas of a yogi.

Took intermediate yoga with her as someone that has prior experience of learning and teaching yoga. She doesn't do a very good job of explaining complicated poses and how to do them CAREFULLY. We had a class of 50 students kicking into headstands against a wall, which can be so so dangerous. She rarely provides modifications for harder poses too.
okay prof, she could be quite condescending at times. the projects in class are easy 100s. worst thing is attendance. not lenient at all considering it makes up a majority of your grade.

idk Zoe has gone off the rails this sem. she has absolutely no critical thinking skills, which doesn't seem to be a new development, but she's on this new quest to “be more assertive” and in doing so has decided that accountability and empathy are not in line with her new goals. really strict on attendance, but will claim her policy is “generous”

Zoe cares a lot about yoga and is perceptive to student feedback. Coming to class never really felt like a class, more so just a fun free yoga lesson. Attendance is mandatory (she's pretty strict about it, only 2 allowed absences for an A, you get 2 makeups though) so make sure you register if you'll show up. She's great, I do yoga every day now!
the class teaches you a lot about all the different aspects of yoga. professor is typically nice and attendance is mandatory.

There is no attendance lenience.  For every absence you get she takes 5 points off your grade. "You have two free absences" what she really means is you can miss class twice and still get an A (90%). This is an impossible standard with COVID still being a thing. She does allow for makeups but they are hour long yoga videos.

Super fun class! Nothing is due until two checkpoints so if you don't have time to do the yoga or small lesson videos it's super flexible. The "final" is really easy and she has some in person opportunities outside of class that count for extra credit! Loved it so much I'm taking the intermediate class next semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is awesome. I highly recommend taking yoga if you are a Kinesiology major who needs PED classes. Zoe is amazing and if you go to class you will get a 100. She offers makeup classes too if you are unable to attend!
Zoe is the sweetest lady ever. This class is a great way to relieve stress, improve your balance and flexibility, and get a PE credit. Highly recommend!

I love this prof and this class! You learn the philosophy and movements of yoga. This class is awesome and you will earn an A just by showing up and paying attention. I absolutely recommend this class and I will definitely take the next level yoga class! Prof is very understanding and caring, don't underestimate how cool the philosophy of yoga is.
Zoe's class is cool because it's more than just yoga poses for a workout, but it's also yoga philosophy. Most of the grade is attendance with an easy project at the end of the semester.

Amazing! She is the sweetest professor and is an amazing yoga instructor. She did not give a lot of assignments, just midterm and final exam. Easy A! If you're looking for a stress relieving class with a bit of workout involved, this is the class you should take. 10/10 would take again

professor himself is kind and pretty lenient. has a huge curve at the end of the semester. BUT, due to the fact that attendance is not mandatory and coding isnt a strong suit at all for me, class was  difficult, especially the tests. studying takes a LOT of time after the first midterm as you cover a LOT of content the rest of the sem.
do not take this guy

I love this man with my whole being. He is so understanding of whatever situation you're in and always believes anyone can code. I have an A right now because of how much practice he offers. He is so underrated and will walk you through the hw in office hours.

I think most of the frustration comes from the volume of assignments and the difficulty of the tests, but Professor Young curves this class so high you can't not pass with at least a B. TA's are largely unreliable but instructed to be lenient. Exams are tricky at worst, manageable at best. You will be fine if you put the work in.

Online Lectures and SI are pretty useful for actually learning Python, but when it comes to the tests it's a lot of memorization and not how well you can code. Make sure you do practice worksheets in the class doc and really study before the tests or you will struggle. Curve is extremely generous went from 85 to an A.
Lectures didn't add anything and weren't helpful. The exams are extremely easy, but there's a decent amount of busywork. Ends the class with a very generous curve (about a full letter grade).

Lecture videos aren't super helpful sometimes, he doesn't go into great detail. I watched each one at least twice because it was easy to miss stuff. HW is 1/week along with projects and quizzes, and tests are hard. Test 1 (100%), test 2 (64%) test 3 (74%), but I ended up with an A because he's generous with curves and drops lowest HW/quizzes,

Exams are cumulative and very hard, they ask questions on obscure python topics. You also have to write programs by hand on the exams which is unrealistic to real programming where you debug. Because of this exam scores are low and he blamed AI for them. The class isn't conceptually hard though.

I would avoid at all costs. I came in thinking it wouldn't be too bad but insane amount of assignments, and the exams get you. You could know a lot, but it's a 45 min long exam with trick questions. It messed me up a ton and honestly had me worried most of the semester. Don't expect to learn very much. He's also lowkey passive aggressive and strict
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Young tried his best to make the class as easy and seamless as possible. The material was difficult at times and there was a lot of work to be doing in the background between watching lectures, doing homework, projects, etc. However, the class is very doable if you stay on top of your work and give genuine effort.

Homework assignments and quizzes are not bad, try to do all of them because it pays off extra credit wise. If you actually watch the lectures and take notes you will know everything you need to know for tests. The tests are very doable if you are tedious and read and write carefully. Dr young is super caring and a very good professor.

The content of the class is fairly easy to grasp, and weekly homeworks weren't difficult, just time consuming. Honestly the only thing students should worry about is the exams. They are very tedious, and mcq portion reads more like trivia, mostly the reason I kept failing the exams. However, Bill Young is super nice, and generous!!

Definitely need to use resources given (optional weekly worksheets/practice problems, SI sessions). Since it's hybrid it's a lot different than most classes but I thought the professor did a good job organizing the weekly lecture videos and weekly homework assignments. The in-person session is just going over examples and attending is extra credit.

Class was flipped with video recordings. As someone with coding experience, the class is structured decently and his videos were okay. The homework, projects, and practice problems all def improve skill in Python. His tests were much too difficult imo. They were very tricky, tested small details and the 1-page cheat sheet wasn't super helpful.

Practical and interesting class. As a first-time coder it was approachable if you watched lecture videos and took notes. In-person lectures weren't very useful. Weekly homework is short (under 1 hr). Test prep is manageable with lots of practice problems (harder than exams). Plenty of extra credit. Hybrid format works well if you stay on track.

He gives great comprehensive lectures, although I have heard that referencing the textbook is more helpful. Having a Python background is pretty beneficial, but not necessary. Exams are much easier than the practice problems. This was not the hardest class I've taken at UT, but it was still fairly difficult. Overall, I learned a lot!

This class is only good if you have the time for it. A lot of people tend to claim that Young grades harshly, but if you attend his office hours and participate in Ed Discussion, he tends to be more generous. The tests are hard and worth 20% each, so you'll definitely have to prepare for those. He's generous with grading, and hw % can go over 100%.

If you have prior experience in coding just even a bit you should be fine, Quiz are pretty easy and sometimes even repeat from the slides. I didn't go to many of the friday sections because he mainly just goes offer programs similar to that weeks homework. Tests are a bit difficult but easier than the practice tests and hackerrank practice.

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU HAVE NEVER CODED BEFORE! So many homework assignments, projects, and quizzes that are time consuming. Exams are difficult and test niche python facts. Exams are graded with scrutiny and he refuses to curve despite low scores.

Dr. Young is a nice professor and can be helpful. However, he tests on niche Python facts that don't actually have anything to do with practical coding. The exams are therefore pretty hard to study for. The TA that I had was not very helpful at all and took two months to grade one of my projects.

Dr. Young puts in effort, but the course structure is flawed. Weekly in-person classes feel like a waste, they are just practice problems better done alone. Worksheets and mock exams are labeled optional but are essential. Exams test formatting quirks and niche Python facts, not real coding skill. Unrealistic expectations for practical coding.

Material taught very effectively. You LEARN in this class, which I appreciated. Projects and homeworks are respectably difficult. He and the TAs are very good about answering questions. Do not use AI cause they WILL find you. The class is incredibly well organized. Very glad I took it with him.

He's a decent professor but you can see his age seep into some of his lessons. Most lecture videos were too boring so I would always go over the presentation slides. Make sure to practice. His tests were pretty hard as there were some super specific problems regarding Python. Has a ton of hw, projects, and quizes. He does give extra credit tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bill knows his stuff and structures the course in an organized way, but towards the second half things really pick up and it gets rly hard. The online videos can get a little monotonous. Exams are actually pretty hard if you never done any computer theory and coding before, lowk got an A cuz there was a curve on the final. Him & TAs accessible tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He isn't a bad professor but underestimates the computer skills of students. I am a slow programmer, so the timed quizzes were not super fun but they aren't super hard either. Weekly homeworks, 4 quizzes, 3 projects, 2 exams, and 1 final. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on python as he packs a lot into the semester. There are drops/extra credit.

The only reason I passed this class was because my friend helped me understand the concepts and stuff when no one else would 💔

There were times I felt so overwhelmed with the workload. Lots of extra credit at the end, but stay on top of your stuff and don't rely solely on the extra credit.

The class itself should not be this hard but since it's mostly asynchronous (in person lecture once a week but doesn't really help) it's important to keep in track and do all the homeworks/projects beforehand. Tests are hard but he will give you extra credit at the end of the semester somehow since everyone bombed tests. Take if only if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Young is a sweet person and I believe he did his best to teach the material. I recommend using the textbook over his lectures, as he cannot compress all of the material via video and the textbook offers so much more. Overall, this was my hardest class I've taken yet, but I do believe I learned a lot as someone who had never coded before.

First time in life I thought I did SO GOOD on my 1st exam but was HUMBLED. Everything is difficult in this class, you will not get any time to actually learn stuff because you will be busy doing all the HWs and Projects due every week. No cheat sheet allowed in exams except the final exam. final replaces the lowest midterm. DON'T TAKE

Lectures and online videos are useless; the textbook prepares you for the exams better (and teaches Python better) than the in-course materials do. Mock exams and "optional" practice assignments are also pretty much required to review to succeed. Will give extra credit though. Annoying and confusing exams where you have to write programs by hand.

Overall this class was pretty terrible and made my life very hard, especially for a beginner CS class. If you have no coding experience DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! The class was hybrid but the lectures nor the slide were very helpful for the homework's or the tests. It seemed like he was teaching this class for people who already familiar with CS.

Mandatory attendance for a useless in-person lecture (for the hybrid version) and so many assignments. Doable for a freshman comp sci major but if you have other things to do this class becomes extremely annoying. If you're biochem, you don't need to actually take this class for 339N btw- watch a video on for loops and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of quizzes and homework and the course just becomes a time sink. You can learn Python. but you're not tested on ACTUALLY USING IT. If you're a biochem major taking this for BCH339N- they don't enforce the pre-req and use R in that class, so don't bother taking this one. Maybe it's good for CS students, but a waste of time for anyone else.

If u haven't coded before save yourself. Extremely TA dependent so if you get a bad one, ur basically screwed. Dr. young barely interacts with students. head TA was the only reason i didn't rate this class a 1. some weeks were so busy w/ HW+quiz+project and exam the next monday. tests are nothing like HW/practice. save ur GPA, don't take this class

So. Ignore all the good ratings. Went in knowing zero python. Leaving knowing zero python. Currently studying for the final. I'm going over the review worksheets and low and behold! Not a single thing on the review worksheet was actually mentioned in the lecture! After the first exam tests and hws became actually undoable. Run AWAY.

This class is terrible Don't even think about taking it. The test averages were around the 50s, and we get no curve. The professor doesn't teach anything, and if you score low, say goodbye to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was taught as a hybrid class, so avoid his class if you don't like asynchronous learning. Young is OK but the class can definitely be challenging w/o prior coding experience. I find some of the quizzes to be very difficult. He does provide a lot of practice resources for exams, so make sure to complete ALL of them.
he is genuinely the worst professor ive taken. he only have you learn off of videos and blames the student for scoring low. DO NOT TAKE
Take this class and be depressed for the semester.
Worst professor I have had at UT. Do not take. His lectures are terrible, and the exams are challenging.

Awful and frustrating class. I'm constantly drowning in assignments. HW after HW... His teaching style is awful - lecture slides are pretty much useless and exams test on a lot more than what is covered in his lecture videos. He stopped allowing cheat sheets on exams which is now making this class unbearable. And his attitude is condescending.

He seems like a good person, but he's not a great prof. I have absolutely no coding experience, and I've been struggling for a while. Oh and he stopped allowing cheat sheets for exams so that's that. I felt like I was getting a hold of the content at the beginning and then boom, everything got so hard for no reason. Lots of homework and projects.

difficult professor teaching a difficult subject. time consuming with homeworks and projects. slides are confusing and video explanations dont help. also ... vocal about his frustration/confusion with students scoring low (ed posts about students scoring low) or using AI/cheating ("i dont care if you get deported" in his syllabus). really bad vibes

Why is he allowed to teach? he is so worried about students cheating that he will talk about it more than the material. SO old fashioned in his teaching style and grading. If you make one mistake on a test, you are docked several points. He teaches computer science but couldnt figure out how to use instapoll. RUN AWAY literally take anybody else.

Does a decent job teaching material, but the class tests you on stuff so rigidly because the professor is terrified someone might cheat with ai that it really limits the scope of what your doing. HW and quizzes are very difficult sometimes, not because of content, but because you have to figure out how to format something "the right way".

Ignore past ratings. He stopped allowing cheat sheet on test. I have zero coding experience and I'm learning a lot, but I wish he stressed the importance of doing the "optional" practice problems/worksheets. They shouldn't be considered optional (questions show up on tests and quizzes). I think he can make discouraging remarks too w/o realizing.

God ... why ? RUN don't walk , as far away as you can from this guy. Teaches the "absolute bare minimum needed to move on to 313e" yet I promise you your semester will be consumed by his class. SO MANY hw assignment , hw ,projects AND/OR quiz or test in the same week. Does not teach at all. Avoid at all cost and ignore the "good ratings".

Great person but teaching style is awful. Not a beginner course in the slightest and does not pair well with other difficult classes. Slides were no use at all and it's true that the grading takes forever. Being a good person does not equate to being a good teacher.

Young is a sweetheart who is well-knowledged and willing to help. However, it's true those without prior coding experience, like myself, are disadvantaged in this course. Certain TAs also graded more harshly than others. Tests are the hardest part because of niche questions, but with studying and practice you can succeed. An A is very achievable.

Had limited programming knowledge before coming in so first half of semester was ok. Found the class to be annoying with sporadic due dates. After exam 1, the class started to get very time consuming with multiple assignments due within the same week. Grading is super slow and feedback is scarce. Do the weekly worksheets to prepare for exams.

The class is very straightforward. I had very little experience with coding so the only thing I had problem with was the timed quizzes. However, he drop 4 assignments (quizzes included) and there's only 5 quizzes. His exams are pretty doable if you use the cheat sheet well and do the weekly worksheets

His recorded lectures don't go into much detail compared to the level we are expected to code at on homework, quizzes, and projects. His grading system is pretty generous though, just be sure to submit all assignments to get a boost in your grade. Wouldn't recommend if you really need to understand coding for future classes (I only needed this one)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Having almost no knowledge of python or coding in general, this class was extremely easy. There was only single assignment that took me more than 45 minutes, all you have to do is watch a lecture a week and do the corresponing homework and or quiz plus a couple projects. On each test you get a large cheat sheet and there is tons of extra credit.

I thought the class was difficult if you have no previous knowledge of coding. I did think the optional textbook was really useful - I didn't watch the lectures because they were too long. There were weekly homework assignments and some of them were really hard, I got really annoyed at one point because he started mixing up assignment due dates.

This class was alright but the first test trips people up. It's more general coding facts than actual code, do the weekly problems since he takes some of the questions from there. Grading takes like a month, but Prof. Young and the TAs answer questions on Ed Discussion. I didn't watch his lectures because they were boring but I read the slides.

This class has a lot of moving parts - homework, quizzes, and projects all due within tight timeframes. However, the TA support and unstuck AI tools can make it more manageable. Just stay on top of the workload and you'll do well.

Not a great class if you really want to learn. Lots of opportunity to get a good grade by doing all the assignments and quizzes but will leave you slightly unprepared for 313e. Go to SI, TA office hours, or youtube if you really want to learn it. Never watched lectures with him, only reviewed the slides. Test aren't too hard.

Online lectures and slides are helpful. Homeworks are very doable, just use logic and keep pace with the class. The 3 projects take longer but can be fun to work out. Handwritten Midterm and Final test you on more detailed and specific intricacies of code rather than just making another program, which hit my grade worse. You get cheat sheets though

To succeed in the class, do your homework in a timely fashion. There are moments in the semester where there will be a quiz, homework, and project due in the same week. The class is straightforward and not too complicated. Homeworks are weekly and quizzes are every few weeks, projects are every once in a while.

Fairly generic computer science course. Somewhat dry slides, but they can be skimmed fairly easily. Two things. #1: Proceed with caution if you have ADHD like me. It's gonna be 100% self-motivated since it's online. #2: Do ALL of your homework. There's a LOT of extra credit to be held if you do all of your homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lots of work. Hw due on M, quiz on W, but you have a project due on Fr, but then next hw due on T. The TA's were very kind and gave points to what they could. Tests are tedious trivia questions- not the best to assess if you know how to code. Only two tests - Would not have passed if he didn't give a very very generous curve at the end there.

If you keep up with the homework and don't wait until the last day to start it's not too bad. If you learn/understand every part of your code for the homework you are set, so don't copy if you want to succeed. I didn't do too good on exams, but his grading policy worked in my favor and everything turned out well.

Outside coding experince is needed for class or else you have to put in hours of work each week. Go to office hours but some TA's are not helpful because they don't understand that people don't know how to code. Exams are very difficult and are on paper. 
13 homeworks, 5 quizzes, 3 projects, 1 midterm, and 1 final.

no teaching is done in this class other than what seems like decade old videos he posts online, and those videos barely even cover anything despite being 1-2 hours. learned nothing in this class, and way to much homework/papers assigned. do not take this professor

I was told this was a beginner Python course and did not require outside knowledge. The only people who really succeeded were students who already had experience coding. The teacher did not teach; he had online videos recorded from 3 years ago, yet they only covered the basics. I only passed this class because of Dewayne Benson. He actually taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For someone who has never coded, this class was hard. There were many assignments: Quizzes, hw, projects, and exams. Sometimes there were 2 hws due in a week. Lecture videos lightly covered the concepts but applying them was difficult. Quizzes were the hardest because of the 1 hr limit. Exams require a lot of studying, but he allows cheat sheets.

Homework and quizzes aren't too bad, and that's about all the good I can say. The grading is very nitpicky and takes off a lot for minor oversights. The 1 exam and 1 final are very hard for people who aren't already familiar with the lingo, T/F and MC questions are very annoying. The online format makes it hard to learn when you are stuck.

Oh boy where do I start. His lectures were pretty boring, but at least he went over all the material. He assigned a ton of work and grading was always super behind. The tests were ridiculously hard and you had to write out code on paper. TAs were pretty hit or miss. Only reason I did well was because I would put in 10+ hours of studying per test.

Average class, easy if you have coded before. TA's are very helpful, USE THEM!! Exams can get a bit tedious but you're allowed a cheat sheet which is helpful. I don't know why people complain, just study brah

He wasnt a bad professor just a bit scatter brained and all over the place. It was a little hard getting help outside of OH since they sometimes take a long time to respond and are super picky on homework like if you forgot a space or a period thats points off. All in all not terrible but a little annoying.
super easy class and great professor, very nice but serious about academic dishonesty
Python. Disgusting

Good professor who wants you to succeed. Didn't like that homework deadlines weren't consistent. Check Canvas daily to stay on top of deadlines. Prof and TAs were quick to answer Ed Discussion questions and gave great responses. Do the worksheets, go to office hours, do the extra practice, and watch lecture videos. Plenty of resources to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take the time to learn the content and PRACTICE. His recorded lectures were good and I liked the flexibility of his online course.

The material isn't difficult, but the workload can be. If your considering taking this course, please PLEASE have the time to do so. I'm taking 16 hours as an engineering major + extracurriculars and I'm struggling to keep up. Tests are hard, homework and quizzes are doable with practice.

He is no help to a beginner CS class. How do you expect to learn coding only by looking through PPT and then doing homework by yourself? (The TAs are super helpful and kind though). How do you manage to do three assignments(one hw, one quiz, one project) in seven days for this single class since you are taking multiple classes? It is a nightmare.

His lectures are great and he does his best to be available for students through an online platform where you can submit any questions regarding materials in class. He also drops a few assignments to help with your grade. I didn't have any coding experience but managed to get an A. But you need to be willing to learn, if not, don't take this class.
Online environment makes learning code difficult. You are pretty much on your own. Do all the homeworks and quizzes and read the lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were boring but they made sense. TA's take forever to grade and are super nitpicky. My main issue with this class were the tests they're very hard to prepare for and are nothing like the rest of the class. I bombed the first one then did good on the final. He is generous with dropping HWs and curving which saved a lot of ppl.

There is nothing positive to say about this class or this professor... I love coding and will continue to enjoy doing it and learn about it, but I am a beginner, and this class is not very beginner friendly. Lectures are boring and the exam is relatively hard since you need to write your code on a piece of paper, making it hard to test your code :P
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bill Young is a tough grader with boring lectures, making for a stressful and unengaging learning experience. Students should proceed with caution when considering taking a course with them.

He is a great professor and teaches very well. The course requires a lot of work, but It's normal as all other cs courses. There will be a curve after the final exam. I spent about 8-10 hours watching lectures and finishing the assignment every week, sometimes more because of projects.

He is a great guy but CS (esp at such a high lvl uni) should not be taught online in my opinion. This class is taught for beginners but goes really fast and if you don't understand a concept it's hard to ask because it is online. Don't take it if you are relatively new to coding find another professor. And the class was hard for an intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: OK professor when it comes to lectures. The class is only hard because the exams are on paper and test over obscure python trivia. Even with a 104 HW/quiz average and a 100 project average, I finished with an A- as the tests were near impossible to prepare for. From debugging code by hand to memorizing the ASCII table, the test wanted you to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The homework assignments and quizzes were very manageable and correlated to the lectures. However, the tests were difficult. There were questions over random python trivia and obscure facts. The recorded lectures were fine, but it's helpful to do the practice problems on HackerRank to understand the concepts better.

Exams have tricky questions with a few random python trivia that you'll never need to use practically. For the handwritten code portions, small typos will still lead to points off (e.g missing a closing parentheses). Gives ample time for exams. Quizzes move at a fast pace. A lot of wiggle room when it comes to quiz and HW grades.

Not a huge fan of Bill Young. He can be pretty mean and unhelpful. Anytime I tried to go to office hours I could not get in due to a system where people could only be seen one at a time in a class where everyone had questions. If you are new to coding, take this class in person! If you have some experience, an A is easily attainable online.

CS 303E was very doable with Young, I appreciated the fact that all of the lectures were concise. All of the projects/homeworks weren't to bad. I found the tests to be fairly difficult, he tended to test on a lot of obscure python trivia that wasn't gone over extensively, but as long as you keep up with the HW and Projects, an A is very doable.

Young is pretty good, although his lectures can be a little boring or unclear if you have no prior coding experience. He is very accessible outside of class though and if you're planning on taking this class online, just be prepared to take initiative and do a lot of work on your own
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO HACKERRANK and WATCH YT VIDEOS! these saved me for the exams. does a poor job explaining concepts and homework/projects are difficult to do with just the information he teaches you. I encourage anyone taking this class to utilize outside resources to build a stronger foundation in coding. DON'T CHEAT! dozens of students got caught for cheating

Dr. Young gives very good lectures and explains the content very thoroughly. I had 0 experience with CS before this class, and I scored a 60 on the first test. I did well on homework, quizzes, and the final and ended up getting an A in the class. It is definitely feasible, just keep up with all the work. SI sessions and office hours are helpful.

Quizzes are very important to succeed in this class, where you only get an hour to solve two coding problems. Exams consist of very niche Python questions, where you have to memorize some very random terms and scenarios in order to be able to answer, some code tracing, and T/F questions; only have two actual coding problems. Do practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I have ever taken. I had no coding experience prior and I felt lost the entire time. The test were very difficult and getting help was hard to do as there was always a super long line to ask the TA's something. If you do take this class, DO THE WEEKLY PRACTICE PROBLEMS and good luck!!

I've been coding python for 5+ yrs and would've been lost without experience before this class. I scored perfect on all quizzes and HWs (except 1) and found the exams...interesting. A majority of the points came from conceptual MC, True/False, tracing, or remembering to add random vocab words to your note sheet. Only 2-3 coding problems on exams.

I had a little coding experience in high school, and I'd say the prof makes some of the hws unnecessarily complicated. The lecture slides were way more basic than what we had to actually do on the hws, so they're not super helpful. The class grading also depends a lot on which TA you have; they grade wayyy too slowly and really inconsistently.

My biggest advice is DO THE EXTRA WEEKLY PRACTICES! Exams are SO easy if you can figure all of them out, but not everyone does it. In fact, I saw that only 12 people attempted one of the more recent ones even though hundreds of students are in this course, which says a lot. If you can figure them all out, you will be more than ready for the course.

I don't recommend taking this class without prior coding experience. Lectures are not great but the homework, quizzes, and projects aren't too hard most of the time (combined they're about 60% of your grade). Tests make up the other 40% and feel more like random trivia than questions that test for your understanding of python. Grading is also slow.

Pros:
If you have coding experience, the class is very easy. 1 assignment per week. If you know the content, the quizzes/tests are a joke.

Cons:
People who didn't have prior coding experience struggled a LOT. Young isn't a great lecturer, and the class goes fast. If you don't have prior experience or aren't strong with logic, it's gonna be hard.

Very sweet guy in person, good at explaining (although this is an intro course), and would definitely take other courses by him if the school made it possible. One thing to note though is that lectures are all online likely due to the large amount of people taking this class, which is a bummer since he's so cool when you get to meet him in person.

Young's class can be a rude awakening for people who think the CS certificate is easy. I'm not a first-time coder and can still see how the course is challenging. But the syllabus was transparent to me. The assignments, recordings, and lectures were always posted ahead of time so I would do everything in one day every week. Your mileage may vary.
There are two homeworks every week and a quiz every other week. There are also 3 projects. The content is pretty difficult.

Horrific organization of the course. Syllabus wasn't reliable, randomly scheduled in-person midterm for a web-based course, TAs constantly cancelling their office hours, everything felt 'subject to change', grading took forever. Content wasn't too hard, though. Take the class with someone else, as Dr. Young and co. don't respect their students much
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are useless and exams are not even like the HWs or quizzes. HWs once per week, quizzes every other week, and 3 projects with 2 exams. This is a very hard class not designed for beginners and requires previous coding knowledge. You will get behind bc the assignments are HARD and TEDIOUS. You will have to self-study!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into this class without any previous coding experience, but Dr. Young includes a lot of helpful tips throughout all of the homework assignments and lectures. Exam questions could be very specific so be sure to study the slides. Practice Problems were extremely helpful for quizzes since you knew what to expect.

Genuinely worst professor of my life and made me want to quit computer science altogether. You will only succeed in this course if you have previous Python experience. His exams were on paper, like you have to write out code on paper bruh. Take literally any other professor and you will learn Python without having to do so much.

I give 5 star ratings like stickers bc I'm easy to please. But when I say if you don't NEED to take this, don't. I went in w/ no CS experience bc my advisor recommended it. IT'S HARD! and not due to a lack of effort. You'll have to teach urself everything and he jumps right in with no consideration to ur foundation even though it's lower division.

I had zero coding experience and this class was HARD. I went to office hours for help on nearly every homework. TAs only see you one at a time, so if you wait until the last day to get help, you will likely not be seen cause there's 1-2 dozen other students ahead of you in line. Because of this, DO THE HW AND PROJECTS AHEAD OF TIME.

I ended up doing fine in this class but I would definitely recommend watching videos on YouTube regarding topics learned in class. I did not find Dr. Young to be too engaging, and sometimes when questions were asked he could be condescending in his answers. Office hours were too busy and grading could take two months.

Dr. Young provides a lot of practice problems and support with prompt Piazza responses. Only complaint is that assignments took a long time to grade so it was hard to gauge how I was doing in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He catches every cheaters in his class, and I extremely like it. He's a nice professor who gives useful feedbacks and advices when you personally reach him. However, this course could be very hard especially for first coding experience. Class materials get exponentially harder after the first half. Get prepared with lots of given practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had no coding experience before this class and it was HARD. Honestly his lectures are fine, and he'll put some examples and command you can use on the slides. His quizzes and exams are challenging with the limited time he gives you. TAs are really really helpful. They can't give you answers directly but they'll help you and give you directions.

There are two people in this class: those who have a little bit of experience and easily get A's and those who go into the course with no experience. The latter often struggle because they understandably try to learn from the lectures and slides, which are both awful. My suggestion is to watch youtube videos on the topics instead of the lectures.

As an engineering major with a coding background this class was harder than it needed to be. Grading is not clear and test cases are out to fail you. Tests are tricky, even after knowing the material. Honestly wouldn't recommend this class for any reason.  I took this to learn and would've been better off without it just using resources to learn.
The tests are so much harder than the material presented in the lecture. Like we are tested on stuff we don't know and aren't even taught. Unless you are experienced in CS this class is not for you.

Do not recommend. Very difficult if you have no prior coding experience. Not a lot of resources to get help - office hours are hard to get into and oftentimes the TAs don't provide adequate help. Took 7 weeks to enter grades, including a major project grade. Young is a poor lecturer and not engaging. Take a different prof or learn outside the Univ
I'm a senior. I've taken other upper div math and coding classes. This is the most difficult class I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The content was pretty easy from the beginning until the middle of the semester. afterward, we were thrown a lot of new content in a short period of time. Make sure you do ALL the weekly practice problems if you want a chance at doing decent on quizzes that barely give you enough time. hard to get one-on-one help. also, don't cheat

Get ready to teach yourself Python because he is reading off the slides and not really good at teaching. The grading is super behind and TAs office hours are impossible to get answered. Not a class for science credit or someone with no coding experience.
I hate him

People were not joking when they said this class was HARD (I'm an RTF major with no coding experience). Prof Young was not a bad professor, but he assumes that you have the foundation for this class. I took this after not dealing with math in over two years and it was HARD but very rewarding. You will need to spend lots of time studying to do well!

Most negative reviews are left by students who were not able to keep up with the class. It requires A LOT of time dedication/consistency, which is made very clear. I had no prior experience and did fine. That being said, TAs are sometimes not available, & prof is aggressive w his answers at times. If you are used to leniency, you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Young's class is not an intro class, he does not teach in a way beginners can understand while also not giving any support. Office hours were impossible to get into and some of the TAs were mean and slow graders (5 weeks behind). Please take the other prof class I heard they give lots of extra credit and have easier assignments!

This is my 2nd time taking this class. I got caught for cheating the 1st time and dropped it. Anyway, the class is still just as difficult as everyone says (Homework, Projects, Quizzes, Tests). Probably gonna get a C. Office hours are impossible to get help in. Take a diff prof. Pros: asynchronous & prompt replies on private piazza posts
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you can't stay on top of an asynchronous class, don't take this. Homework and projects are basically impossible with no help if you have no prior experience, and he is very strict with testing code for similarities. Join TA help when they start or they won't get to you. Unrealistic for an intro course. Grades really tough with no extra credit.

even if he knows his stuff, he doesnt know how to teach

i was excited for the class and it was my first time learning python, but he made the experience really bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not cheat in this class. He will catch you and you will be miserable. His plagiarism tools catch people frequently. It's better to get a bad grade than get your future dirtied. Young is a respectable guy and while there is a lot of work for someone with no prior knowledge, you will learn the basics of programming and logic even. I recommend it.
doesnt know how to teach
