Honestly, he is one of my favorite professors Ive had. He keeps his classroom entertaining and engaging. Concepts are explained well, and he likes to add in personal stories for connections. I would recommend him as a professor to any of my friends.
He can come of as egotistical especially considering his unfunny jokes and personality. Obviously lacks compassion towards students. Do not take this class unless you attend every single session.

Professor is not very understanding to students situations based on my observations. Sometimes he's chill, but majority of the time I felt uncomfortable. He has a strong personality which students have mixed opinions/feelings on. I wish he had more compassion for his students. He's one of the only professors I have had that have lacked empathy.

Do not take this class unless you plan on attending every single class. If you miss more than one, make sure to study for that final exam. He comes off as a nice guy, but he actually lacks compassion/understanding when it comes to situations. Every science/math professor I've had are much more empathetic and this a ugs. The TAs are much nicer.

he makes jokes that make some people uncomfortable. he does not seem very understanding in my opinion. his class is interesting but it would be better if he would tone it a bit down with his jokes and show more compassion towards his students.
take bc its an easy A, but god this guy is so full of himself and thinks he's is the funniest man alive. lowkey passive aggressive at times.

Best UGS out there! Class 1 day a week and you watch a movie for most of it. Super interesting concept for a class and I looked forward to going every time. He can seem tough but is very straightforward with assignments and grading, easy to get an A. Theres a few big projects but they were easy and fun to do. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Rochlen does a pretty good job at teaching content. You will learn. Along the way, however, you will be subject to his painfully unfunny jokes and passive aggressive tone. This dude thinks he's the funniest person on earth and gets annoyed when you don't laugh at his jokes. Also incredibly pretentious, the definition of sitting on a high horse.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Movies and Mental Health is an amazing class. Both Dr. Rochlen and the TAs were amazing and super helpful. About 4 1 page papers, a final 2 page paper and presentation is ur main hw for the semester. They are super easy. It is hard to stay awake at 9am watching a movie so bring caffeine. Can only miss 1 class though but they only meet once a week.
very easy class as long as you show up and pay attention

Easiest UGS I've heard of by far. Class is actually fun and interesting, literally just watch actually good movies (not documentaries) and analyze psych disorders of the characters. Essays were one page max, very easy. Only got one class miss though. Downside is class is 3 hours long, but just because you're watching a movie. Love him, so funny.

Rochlen's Movies and Mental Health class wasn't all that bad. There was more writing than you might expect and the grading criteria could be a little weird, but this class is manageable if you show up and put in effort. The topics were interesting enough to be able to stay engaged. It can be hard to stay awake if you take it in the morning.

I personally enjoyed Movies and Mental Health with Dr Rochlen, but I do understand the complaints about him. You basically just watch movies and evaluate them in a psychological context. The assignments consist of 5 one page essays, and a project. Beware there is a final quiz that is very annoying so if you don't like tests it may not be for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I did not respect this guy. He thinks he is the funniest man on earth and god's gift to the universe but this class (movies and mental health) felt very dumbed down and elementary. The grading is also randomly hard for a class this unserious. But, as long as you show up and turn in your work it is a pretty easy A. Very basic material.

Loved movies and mental health so much. Often left the class feeling inspired. Do be prepared to share your opinions and analysis to the class after each film. Have a big individual presentation at the end of the year for a final exam that was a little nerve wracking. Overall, I would recommend this ugs.

Dr.Rochlen is very knowledgeable and dedicated to his teaching! This class was so fun (who doesn't want to watch movies as a college class) but you do have to be very engaged when it comes to analyzing what you're watching and having complex opinions about the films. Just make sure to show up on time and never fall asleep!

Dr. Rochlen's class was basically a guaranteed A if you watch the movies in class and write a few comprehensive papers. The class is cool and I really enjoyed it, it was like a mix of a psychology and film class but just the basics of both. However, be careful bc he's on a power trip. He'll yell at you for random things and is a prick.

Fun teacher that actually gives good insight into the topic. I liked how the class was structured around student discussion and participation, it allowed for a lot of insight into first hand accounts of topics discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rochlen is a man child. He loves to hear himself talk. Even though the class is easy, he is so hard to respect. He grades incredibly hard on the few assignments he gives. He is full of himself and it is three brutal hours of his lectures. I do not recommend taking this class.

One of my favorite classes! While I thought purchasing the required coursebook was a pain, I actually learned a lot and had so much fun in this class. 10/10 would take again best UGS ever!! Oh also, Dr. Rochlen is very nice and accommodating, just don't be late to his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Movies and Mental health is SUCH a good class to take. Be ready to write when it comes to this class, you'll have a 1-1.5 paper due weekly/bi-weekly. While he IS a semi-tough grader he always gives clear and concise feedback. Overall really chill and funny professor, just make sure you're respectful of his time(don't be late to class)!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: EDP 352D*** I sat through every 3 hr lecture of this counseling theories class cringing and irritated. Honest to god I think I understand human nature better than Dr. Rochlen. His lectures were super unorganized, inarticulate, and surface level. If you want to learn anything you couldn't learn from a 5 minute youtube video, I'd steer clear.

I enjoyed the class. He's straightforward and I was interested every lecture. The only time there was a lack of direction were the labs, which could get awkward and confusing. Tests are long but fair for the most part, except those few questions designed to test whether you were awake in class and not if you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall pleased with my experience in this class. Clear directions about what he expects, and the lectures are actually engaging and interesting. I would say hes a little hard on people occasionally in class, and I dont love the psych skits or labs, but its not bad. Responds to emails and questions super quick which is nice, and the TA is great

Many students have mixed feelings regarding Dr. Rochlen. Personally, I enjoy his personality but his lack of clarity in class lectures and grading are major issues. His directions for assignments are often unclear.  His hatred towards rubrics only makes issues more complicated for his students.  In the end, I got an "A' in his course, so I'm happy!

Loved it! straightforward about what he expected in class. Answered questions pretty well.Of course he couldn't answer all of them because some questions, there is just no way to know or there has not been very much research. taught class well..would always lecture some and then have some activities so we wouldn't be super bored. I recommend him!
No Comments
The only reason I didn't hate Ant301. He went slow and made it easy to understand the topic!

[UGS: History of Friend VS Foe] I had Dr. Sandel for my UGS and I loved the class! It was so chill, we just had in class discussions on what love or friendship is, etc. Dr. Sandel seems really passionate about his studying of chimpanzees and it was rlly interesting to hear about his work in Africa. If you want a light + fun UGS, take this class!

Least scientific science course I have ever taken--Dr. Sandel is a joke. I genuinely didn't learn a thing all semester, I just listened to classmates debate about nothing in particular. Easy enough class I suppose, I didn't do anything besides free writes and making sticky note maps. There was no structure and even less learning. Waste of time.
Literally didn't learn a single thing all semester. Exams were easy enough and essays just required a few readings. Not exactly sure what the prof did - I only talked to TAs
If you aren't a science major and don't care to learn anything, get science credit, and want to get an A+ to take this class for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a really great online class to get a science core out of the way; definitely need to read and take good notes if you want to get an A.

Goofy ahh class. It was okay though. Online, asynch, pretty relaxed. It's one of those classes that's initially intimidating and then you realize you can just like... look up the answers to stuff. Wierd exams-- not hard, but there were oddly worded questions and answers throughout. Essays are extremely easy. Never met the prof, seems nice though.

This is for UGS Origins of Friend and Foe, the class was super boring but an easy UGS to get an A in and just get it over with. Attendance is necessary as this is a small seminar type class, but we spent so long learning about chimp aggression which I thought was very funny but not useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very easy-A science credit. Tests are pretty straightforward and it's not hard to get full points on essays. Most weeks we did not even have assignments to do. There are also no lectures, so you learn from the textbook and canvas notes. Overall, an easy class but not the best if you are really interested in learning something.

this professor and his Teays were the worst. Not only did they ghost us for the entire semester, they only post a lecture twice once in September, and once in November. Only take this class if you have to it was the absolute worst.

I absolutely love Dr. Sandel! Primate conservation is the best class I have ever taken! Participation matters, but he makes class time so much fun while learning about important concepts. Community gardening with him was the highlight of this course and taught all of us so much about conservation! Highly recommend!!!

This professor is very easy but he is extremely disorganized. We go very long stretches of time with no assignments or instruction, do not receive grades in any reasonable amount of time, and do not receive any feedback. TAs do all the work for this class and then are not allowed to do anything without approval that takes way too long.

If you need a science credit and aren't a science major this is a great class! Easy and the professor cares a lot about what he's teaching. Super interesting too. 110% recommended. 3 online exams, 2 essays, and some modules with no due dates. I took the asynchronous ANT 301
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr.Sandel for my ugs, and nothing can explain how much I enjoyed his class. He cares for his work, so it was easy for me to care too. I didn't fully understand the timeline, but he was always ready to give an explanation. Great prof.  ATTENDANCE MATTERS! I missed class but he let us make it up!!

This was the best class I took last semester. All you really need to do is show up to class and participate a bit, and you will get an A. The professor was very interesting and a bit socially awkward, but it made the class funny. The only con would be that his assignment instructions are a bit unclear sometimes.

OO OOH EE AH AH!!! These are the sounds of the Ngogo chimps that we studied in Professor Sandel's UGS 302 class. In this class, I made so many lasting social bonds. This class is my fav class I've taken so far in college, and Dr. Sandel was super nice & caring. This class changed my life. Would definitely take again. Attendance is mandatory.

(This review is for his UGS 302 class, there was just no way to select that on RMP)

Dr. Sandel is super kind and caring! His class was very easy, and basically, a guaranteed A if you attended the classes (attendance matters a lot). The actual subject, how chimpanzees make friends and enemies, was pretty interesting, although a little confusing.

I was in his UGS "friendship and foe". He is very nice and understanding. Not much if any work and it was a writing flag. Also, the subject is interesting-- understanding relationships among humans through chimpanzees. Can be awkward in class at times and never a clear goal but really easy and fun. Great guy!

Very nice guy, kinda odd. Studied chimps for 10 years and is super sensitive about them. Nice guy but he has 0 expectations for what the class goals are. The UGS is a joke, and a waste of my tuition money. He makes us learn about chimps and memorize their names while sidetracking for maybe 5 classes. Guy is nice but hes super weird dont takehis UGS
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sandel is a really nice person! He does not always have clear expectations for assignments, but he grades easy and will give you an A if you show up and participate in class. Really cool class, he wants to see his students do well and is very understanding if you miss an assignment or need anything. You will regret not taking him!

Dr. Sandel is a great guy and is enthusiastic about his field. Unfortunately it seems that he has little to no teaching experience, and it is truly reflective in his class. While the topics we learned were interesting, the expectations for the students were unclear. Tests seemed a bit off topic and there were no concrete lesson plans.

i'm sick of the aaron hate he is so awesome! he's so funny and incredibly smart and adapted what is usually very convoluted and complex material into a really interesting and easy format. i thought i was going to HATE this class--i could not have been more wrong! i loved the readings and the material and prof tugendhaft made it so much fun!

He's a very genuine guy, cares about each student and their academic pursuits as well as who they are as people. Very reading heavy outside of class and you must be prepared to participate in lecture. Would take again, he is a stud.
Reading and thoroughly understanding the material prior to class and for essays had no connection to final grade.

Dr. Tugendhaft expects students to actually do the reading and come to class prepared to discuss and analyze. He took the time to meet with each student during the essay writing process, and helped me improve as a writer and thinker. The writing tutor for the course (who was a quasi-TA) was also very helpful when I scheduled a meeting.

I enjoyed the class but I do think the grading of essays and the final essays were arbitrary. I suspect that perhaps they were trying to fit a grade distribution and some students just got what they did to fill out that distribution. All students in this class were top notch, so distribution was not needed. If all deserve an A, they should get it.

Slow to grade, but quick to take  points off because of inability to take the time to actually read essays thoroughly. Also, followed prof directions on essays and had points taken off by TA that were in direct conflict with guidance given by prof.
This was not an english composition class, yet the TA graded it as such. Content took a back seat.

End the semester positive you have a high A and get blindsided by a much lower grade. Grades not posted until it is too late to contest them. Unless you are a genius writer or a grad student taking this UNDERGRAD course, you are in trouble. I had other professors look at my essays and the final essays and they said they were A's. Odd...
Grading is subjective and isn't transparent. I felt as if factors other than my work affected my grade.

Essays are graded by the TA (who gave great feedback for improvement after I scheduled a meeting), but Dr. Tugendhaft requires a meeting prior to the submission of your essay. Ultimately, you get in what you put out—he expects you to read and come to class prepared, and he can often tell if students haven't been engaging with the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
While knowledgeable during essay feedback sessions… he's not the most tactful. I didn't have the worst experience, but there were a few jokes that annoyed me. Go in with a thick skin.

Beware: he will not be grading your essays! There were many instances where corrections made according to the prof's advice resulted in point deductions from the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This guy's awesome
Aaron made this course incredibly engaging, and his passion for the subject shows. In-person essay reviews with him are extremely impactful on your writing.

Aaron is the best professor I've ever had at UT. He is an extremely talented, engaging lecturer and the first I've ever had who I feel legitimately cares about his students' academic progress. I'm taking another class with him next semester!

Professor Tugendhaft was frequently available to students and was engaging in every single class. Each day was an insightful discussion with peers that garnered a deeper understanding of the material. I absolutely recommend taking any class by Professor Tugendhaft, you will not be disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Aaron structures his class for the sole purpose of you actually learning something. His class is not designed to put you under immense stress or anxiety about grades, its really all absorbing the subject matter. Even if you are struggling for whatever reason, related to the class or not, he will help you out. His lectures are very enjoyable.

Professor Moses is an incredible lecturer and is clearly passionate about the material. He made me genuinely interested in art history. However, the exams are brutal and both took me at least 4 hours (2 exams, 15% each of your grade). They're open note but 9 essay questions can be taxing. There are 5-6 other writing assignments besides the exam.

He's super passionate and it was interesting, but man, those exams were brutal. You have a long period to complete them (like all day) but they take like 4-5 hours and they're not easy. At some point, writing essays (something I'm very good at!) became physically difficult because I'd been at it for so long. Some other assignments, but not many.

Prof. Moses is a very passionate lecturer and cares a lot about his subject. There aren't a lot of assignments, however the exams are lengthy and challenging (the exams ARE open note). We had a 7 hour period to take the midterm and it took me 6 hours. The midterm has 9 essay questions, and the exams require a pretty good grasp of the content.

Professor Moses is an incredibly sweet person who knows a lot and cares about this subject. If you take detailed notes you should be fine but  be warned the tests take around 5-6 hours. They are open note but the questions can be quite hard, also have 9 essay questions. if you don't like art history then this class is def not the vapa for you.

Professor Moses' ARH 303 was very interesting and an easy VAPA. We had two tests that were open note and a few short writing assignments. The tests were easy if you paid attention to the lectures and took notes on the starred topics on the powerpoint slides. There is a textbook, but the lectures are so in-depth you don't have to read it or buy it.

For juggling a PhD AND a teaching job, Professor Moses was incredible. I took his class for a VAPA because I was interested in art history and it was a rewarding experience. He put clear effort into lectures, writing assignments were easy, and tests were completely open note. Just show up for in-class lectures and skim the textbook every so often!

Exams are 30% each for a total of 90%. Difficult but fair tests similar to practice probs and HW. His lectures tended to be a panic-y period where I frantically wrote what he wrote to keep up. Tests weren't too bad as it only included a few topics from lecture -- most of what you learn won't be tested over, but you cant know that before-hand.
His exams are very hard and the averages for those are usually between 65 to 70%, but he gives a really good curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Transport is a difficult subject, but Dr Baker really takes the time to explain concepts that people have questions about, and he seems to have a lot of empathy for his students. The exams are fair, and the homework and in-class questions are adequate to prepare you for them. Definitely attend lectures; there is new content covered every day.

This class is A LOT of work, especially if you don't start with any Persian. Very homework-heavy, flipped-classroom, so you work through the textbook on your own, class is for practice and tests. However, this professor really cares about student outcomes and tries her best to help. You could also see the class improving throughout the semester.

Great class and will really teach you Farsi if you commit to it. Simply doing the homework and making sure to get it right will basically get you literate. It is a time commitment, 2hrs three times a week and it takes about 2hrs to do homework every night too, upside is all the other assignments also take 2hrs so nothing is killer. She is also nice

The class is a mess. First time teaching and she's just as lost as us. Two papers and a presentation account for 80% of your final grade. She doesn't know how to use a computer or any kind of technology. The class organization is absent. Due dates are listed on the syllabus and make sure to remember them cuz no one will remind you. DON'T TAKE THIS!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You do not need to read anything!!! he spends all of lecture going through the summary of that happened over the "assigned reading" and gets really off track, but ALL of the assignemnts are super easy and the prompts are so broad that you can just research and write instead of reading the dense material. HE GRADES ON GRAMMAR OVER CONTENT!!!

Enthusiastic, fun, and interesting, but a lot of the content covered in class is unnecessary to do well. Once you understand how he grades papers will be easy A's, he is not tech savvy but genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching

Dr. Afolabi is a very enthusiastic professor! His class is interesting and straightforward but can be pretty disorganized at times. Many papers are assigned, but the class does carry a writing flag. He grades mainly based on grammar instead of the essays' actual content. Once you understand his writing style, getting A's on the papers is very easy

afolabi is passionate, caring, and super funny! class had lots of papers but that comes with any writing flag. papers were graded mostly on grammar and less on content, so it was very easy to get above a 95. you can get by with skimming the books he assigns (no need to buy since he has pdfs) or listening in lecture. loved this prof and the class

Much of this class is saved by the interesting topic and the professor who presents the information. His regular enthusiasm and willingness to describe a culture which, at least to me, was novel proved to be highly valuable. However, his critiques of writing are at best technical and the stylistic and argumentative feedback was distinctly limited.

Professor Afolabi is passionate about what he teaches, and I highly recommend his UGS class. There is usually a 2-3 page paper due every week. However, he grades very fairly and the vast majority of students in his class receive an A. The class is actually really interesting, and I have a new found appreciation for Brazilian culture. Solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Afolabi is an amazing professor, he certainly does not do things the "standard" way you might imagine. He is articulate, passionate, and hilarious. The course consists of incredibly unique and interesting topics that are important to learn. He may come off as harsh sometimes, but his criticisms are honest and in the best interest of the student

Professor Afolabi is such an interesting, funny, charismatic, and enthusiastic professor! He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and comes to each class full of energy. There are quite a few essays to write in this class, but Dr. Afolabi grades really leniently and gives great constructive criticism.

His enthusiasm can be a lot for some students, but it makes the class more interesting! He gives out a lot of writing assignments but it is a writing class but they are pretty easy and he is very flexible on grading (especially on the midterm). We have one midterm (annotated bibliography) and a final paper. Overall, this class is very interesting!

Whatever class you take with afolabi will be really interesting. He's super outgoing and funny, and he's really flexible with grading. I took Intro to Brazilian Studies and had a great time, and you can tell he's really passionate about what he does.

Professor Afolabi is an interesting professor. I learned a lot from his UGS302 Brazilian Studies class, and the small class format made it more engaging and fun. He can be hard to understand with his accent and his comments on papers dont always make sense, but he is very knowledgable about Brazil. One of the best classes I've taken at UT.

Dr. Shaikh is a caring and compassionate professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and assigns relevant and thoughtful assignments. With fair effort, this class is very doable and enjoyable. She is wonderful!

Dr. Shaikh made her expectations for the class very clear and graded content fairly. She truly cares about each one of her students and is always open to talk about any concerns. This class did not require a ton of effort, but you should still put an honest effort into the assignments.

I took the EDP Career Planning course over the summer and enjoyed it! We learned so much—I especially loved our textbook since it was actually fun to read. There were reading/content quizzes, assignments graded on effort because they were focused on your personal career planning, and an interview of someone in your field of interest for the final.

This is the third class I've taken with Afsar. He's a great professor. The subject material is always very interesting, and he doesn't shy away from controversial or 'awkward' topics. He always brings humor to the discussion as well. He is very interested in students' progress and is always willing to meet to discuss papers,etc.

Presently, I'm in Prof. Afsar's "Modern India and Literature" class. I'm so lucky to get into the class which has a long wait list. And,Prof. Afsar never disappointed until now. He is passionate, fun and clarity of thought. Wonderful insights into the materials.

Taking Prof. Afsar's new class "Pilgrimage in South Asia." Heard a lot about Prof. Afsar before, but this is my first class with him. Really enjoyable! Extremely fascinating/ real research experiences! Accessible Professor, loves to spend more time with the students. Values the student voice and he has a great smile!
Great Professor!

Afsar is passionate about his subject and enjoys sharing the materials. Focuses a lot on the progress of his students and meets even outside the class to have conversations and discussions about the subject.

Really cares for the progress of the student. Makes every class a memorable experience with lot of stories. I've been taking his courses continuosly. Specifically his course on South Asian Novel is my favorite.
Afsar is very particular about attendance and pushes you to participate in the class discussions. Always thought-provoking and worth pursuing materials.
GREAT PASSION FOR TEACHING AND VERY ACCESSIBLE PROFESSOR!

He is a great professor with lots of passion for his subject! I enjoyed every minute of his class. If you keep up with the work and go to class then you should have no problem getting the grade you want. How much you get out of the class depends on how much you put in!Make sure you meet him outside of class because he is a great person to get to kn

hes alright. he always tells you the basics of what you need to do but doesnt offer further help. he doesnt give feedback which is pretty annoying especially since he acts like the class is an internship. shouldn't there be more feedback in that case?? anyways do the reading bc he takes pop quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Taking Aarons can result in a love-hate experience. He promotes treating class like an internship but offers little feedback. While he has a sense of humor, he is extremely rude and dismissive of student ideas. It's best to avoid him, as his class may be challenging and not worth the effort. Overall, he's a really narcissistic and egotistical man.

This professor structures his class like an internship. Overall he's the best professor I had in my time at UT, would recommend him even if you are not a marketing major due to how much this class opens your eyes to how the world works. Be ready for random pop quizzes off required reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Digital marketing is an interesting topic but this class was unenjoyable. Students were shot down often. Was told to treat the class like an internship which was strange bc he didn't act like a supervisor OR mentor. The semester long group project was graded without ANY feedback and a lot of the time his comments were vague and/or discouraging.

I looked forward to Professor Aaron's Digital Marketing class, but his discouraging attitude stifled participation. Overall he had a narrow mindset, failed to provide any feedback on exams, and left our biggest assignment (our group campaign) completely ungraded. In-person requests for feedback felt vague, as though he hadn't even read my work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was amazing!! Absolutely loved everything I learned. I appreciate how he kept the class interesting and engaging. Aarons is a very caring and understanding person who is great to have as a professor. I look forward to taking more classes with him in the future. Highly recommend!!!

Digital MKT was great. I learned practical skills and how to build a campaign. Great (high profile) guest speakers. Chris is also extremely dedicated and will make himself available (even nights/weekends) to help his students with jobs/internships. He also is a marketing consultant himself so can speak to his experience.

Grade spread is very tight in this class, essentially he keeps everyone at a B/B+ and if you excel than you can get an A. I would recommend just doing well on the homework assignments and communicate with him A Lot on the final project. Otherwise he is a fantastic teacher who makes marketing fun and educational. Just dissapointed with my grade.

Very caring prof who is very knowledgeable in the subject. His lectures were great and very engaging. Very well versed in marketing and uses his past experiences to teach. Can be a bit condescending and intimidating when you ask for help. Only complaint is his grading criteria is vague and unclear, makes you work for anything higher than a B/B+

Chris is passionate and enthusiastic about digital marketing and gives many great case examples to help the learning process. However, his exams and grading criteria on all assignments are vague and poorly explained. Not too much homework, and definitely a worthwhile class to take. I would recommend it to all marketing majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Aarons is one of the best professors I've ever had. He incorporates his real world experience into his lectures, which helps the information to stick. He is very personable, so it is easy to participate and stay engaged during his lectures. He teaches only what is actually useful. Take him if you can!

This is my favorite professor EVER. No need to take notes, very little amounts of HW but so much learning. He is charismatic and makes you laugh while teaching and telling real life experiences. His class is so interesting and he is always there to help with any situation (school/non school related). Take his class if possible!

Would not recommend anyone take this class unless you don't care about your grades. There's no feedback about grades and you get a b no matter what. Tests are easy though. Even if you do above average on everything will still get a b. Take a different professor if possible.

It is NOT worth waking up in the AM for. Take someone else and get more sleep. If you are looking for a class with fair grading on assignments or tests, do not pick Aarons. He grades on a scale with no feedback and gives B's on every assignment. He has a lot of marketing knowledge, but he is way too harsh for no reason when it comes to grading.

Grading criteria is vague. No direction given ever. One of the worst classes I have ever taken at McCombs. You will get a B no matter what. Please take anyone else for marketing. Idk where the good reviews are coming from. Maybe he's just becoming a grinch in his old age. Very full of himself.

Grades are all subjective to how often you talk to professor outside of class. Extremely subjective grading, leaves the assignments very vague. Gives everyone in the class a B on all assignments, no matter the effort. I would not take this class again. Don't advise taking this class if you aren't a consistent office hour attending student.

The assignment instructions are extremely vague and his TA grades tough. We took a midterm (I studied multiple days for) and because he did not handle canvas correctly, he threw out the midterm grades and weighted every other assignment heavily in its place. Overall an extremely discouraging class. Interesting yes; but not good for the GPA.

If you're a marketing major, you will LOVE his class, and if you aren't a marketing major, I think you'd still love his class and learn so much from him. He is SO easy to reach outside of class, cares a lot about preparing his students to be better marketers, and gives GREAT lectures. Definitely one of my favorite classes and professors at UT ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Aarons is an awesome teacher. I would highly recommend taking his Digital Marketing class. His lectures are entertaining, and the concepts learned in this class are very applicable to the "real world." He also is very accessible outside of class and gives his personal phone number to students to schedule office hours, or to just chat.

People saying hes horrible, either hate marketing or they didnt care about the class. Prof Aaron is the best professor Ive had in McCombs! He cares more about us LEARNING than grades. And idk why people complain about the tests. THEYRE SO EASY and he tells us what will be on it. Also, if you ask him anything, he will be straight up.

Professor Aarons has been my favorite professor that I have had at UT so far. His lectures are extremely interesting and genuinely cares about each of his students and wants them to be successful outside of the classroom as well. If you have any interest in marketing, I can't recommend Professor Aarons enough.

Professor Aarons is extremely accessible outside out of class and very passionate about his students. I really appreciated the opportunity to have a hands-on group project experience. The group project has taught me a lot about dealing with unpredicted challenges and working with teams virtually.

Professor Aarons is one of the best teachers I have had at UT. He made me fall in love with marketing. We did a group project to help small business struggling during COVID. He was always available even if it was late at night. Aarons made the class fun and had great energy. He taught me a lot and I highly recommend this class! Tests weren't bad!

Professor Aarons was my favorite instructor at UT. I have never enjoyed lectures as much as his - from his humor to the relatable content, I have gained so much valuable knowledge from his class. He is willing to get on a call with his students at virtually any time in order to ensure our success. He is kind, empathetic, and incredibly smart.

Chris was the best professor I had at McCombs BY FAR. He is so caring & wise & willing to do anything to help his students & better their learning experience. I'll carry what I learned in his class with me for the rest of my professional life. He will also casually and humbly drop things like how he met Travis Scott or Amazon is one of his clients.

His exams were extremely hard. Even you studied for them, you wouldn't be able to finish them in time. A lot of the questions that he didn't cover in class. Basically, you have to write an essay plus 10 short answers questions for the exams. You won't have enough time. He doesn't provide study guide/reviews for the exams.

If you want an A, don't take his class, because the way he grades the exams and homework, is just basically giving anyone an average grade -- 85%. That way he meets UT's requirement to keep a 3.2 of the class average. He doesn't care how hard you work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The most honest answer is "One of the worst professors I have taken. He doesn't really teach anything useful during class but expects so much on assignments and exams. He doesn't give clear instructions ever and then grades so hard on them. For the exam its all short answer and he admits we can't do but laughs and still gives it."

Professor Aarons is a wonderful instructor and one of the most valuable people you can meet at UT. He always bends over backwards to help his students out in any way possible and puts immense effort into making sure students succeed. I learned more about marketing in his Digital Marketing class than any other class I've taken at McCombs!

Chris Aarons is an incredible professor and my favorite I've had at UT. He cares so much about his students and makes himself available through several channels outside of the classroom, more than any other professor I've known. He even gives out his personal phone number and responds to texts or calls immediately! You should definitely take him.

Professor Aarons has been my favorite professor at UT Austin so far. All of his lectures showcase information that is actually helpful for real-world situations. The class is fast-paced and fun, and professor Aarons has a great sense of humor. He's always there for his students and is very approachable. Definitely take this class.

Chris is without a doubt the best professor I ever had & a huge reason I am doing marketing. He makes time for all his students, makes lectures engaging and fun, gives thorough feedback, and tells great jokes & anyone who thinks otherwise is confused. He even cancelled our final class presentations bc he could tell we were all stressed. He's a gem.

professor aarons is amazing. i have never seen a teacher so genuinely eager to help students succeed. he was always available outside of class to help me figure out where i went wrong on the midterm and final and he even recommended me to companies for job opportunities. he believed in me constantly even when i didn't. take his digital mkt class!

- THOUSANDS of dollars worth of AMAZING guest lecturers? Check. - Learning real-world skills that you can apply immediately? Check. - This class alone is worth an entire semester's tuition alone? CHECK. AND. MATE. You are doing yourself a disservice if you aren't going to take this class. Put your heart into this class and you will thrive.

Chris was arguably the best professor I've had at UT. His class is hyper relevant and I feel so much more prepared for a career in marketing after taking his class. He is also extremely accessible and helpful outside of class. You will spend much of the semester working on a digital marketing plan for a real client, which I really enjoyed.

Honestly I'm not gonna lie, it is a lot of work BUT I have never learned more than I have in Chris's class. He's very engaging and fun to learn from and ALWAYS open to talk or give advice on what he's looking for.

Chris funniest, most laid back, knowledgeable prof I had at UT. Fun class vibe for such an important topic. If youre a marketing major or just biz major & dont take digital w/ Chris, youre simply not preparing yourself to be the best you can be in todays digital world  I learned more about marketing here than all other courses. Fav prof ever!

Chris is the best EVER. He's kind, funny, and extremely knowledgeable. For his digital marketing class: he brings in AMAZING guest speakers, every lecture is relevant to current events, and his teaching dynamic really allows you to learn while having fun, as well as bond with your classmates. Take him for any class, you won't regret it. 10/10!

Chris is easily one of the best professors I've had in my 4 years at UT. His class is tough since it's a ton of content mainly from lectures, but I learned more in one semester in his class than I have in all my other marketing classes. Phenomenal guy that's always willing to help out where needed, it's a heavy class but couldn't recommend it more

Chris is AWESOME, and his class helped me realize that marketing is definitely for me. All class assignments are to benefit his students and help them develop a digital marketing mindset! Class discussions are also super insightful and dive into real world topics. IF YOU ARE SERIOUS ABOUT MARKETING, TAKE THIS CLASS. It will change your life!

Aarons is hilarious, & the best professor ever!! It may seem like his instructions are vague, but it is all to help you think for yourself & unlock your full potential. He is always available to chat in office hours or even over the phone if u are confused, & his main priority is to make sure his students succeed! Lectures are also super engaging!

Prof Aarons is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. Taking Digital MKT with him impacted me in many ways - landing an internship, growing in knowledge, and being challenged to do my best work. He is an inspiring lecturer, hilarious, and gives priority to help his students even on weekends. His class will change your life! TAKE!

Prof Aarons class isnt necessarily an easy A but its very very doable if you just try. And some projects/ assignments can be vague, but if you simply ask him questions he is more than happy to help. In this class you will have a blast (he is hilarious) and learn so many real life useful things. And amazing guest lectures. Best class ever!!

Professor Aarons is hands down the best professor I ever had, any negative reviews on here are quite frankly wrong. He truly cares about all his students, actually teaches useful information you WILL use in your career, gives incredible feedback, and his class is FUN. Take his class, trust me.

Do not take this guy. He is one of the worst professors I have taken. He doesn't really teach anything useful during class but expects so much on assignments and exams. He doesn't give clear instructions ever and then grades so hard on them. For the exam its all short answer and he admits we can't do but laughs and still gives it. Do not take, run.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Aarons is a pretty nice person, it's just that his class is extremely hard. The instructions for all of the assignments are so vague, it is hard to figure out what he expects from us. His grading is also really harsh, with minimal feedback. There are also a lot of long assignments to do during the week.

He is one of the worst professors and you should definitely avoid him. The instructions for all of his assignments were very vague and he didn't have any office hours. He wouldn't do Zoom meeting with you. He didn't offer exam reviews and the exams were very difficult. Basically, 1 PPT and 1 paper every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's alright. There was originally a lot of work, but he eventually scaled it back. Tests were kind of difficult in my opinion. The group project revolved around working with an actual client, but there weren't many guidelines. Instructions are vague at best with most of his assignments.

Professor Aarons is very smart and personable. He has great industry knowledge, and his lectures are often interactive and involve real-world marketing examples. I will say that he probably expected too much from students in an introductory marketing class. Solid professor, but not the easiest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Aarons is hands down the best professor I've ever had in college. I have never learned more in any other class than I have in this class. His lectures are fun & really interesting. He sends out surveys to his students and really takes feedback & caters to what you need throughout the semester. If you have the chance to take him, DO IT!

Chris is an incredible prof. Def one of the most memorable, impactful classes i've ever taken. He teaches things that are extremely relevant and he really cares about his students. I would take any other class with him as prof again!! Highly recommend!

Professor Aarons is one of the most impactful professors I've worked with. His class is insightful, interesting, and engaging. We gained hands-on, real-world experiences for digital marketing. This was the most useful class I took at UT. Highly recommend Chris as a professor and a resource for career interests!

Taking Digital Marketing with Chris was hands down the BEST class I've ever taken at UT. Not only is the information extremely useful, he delivers it with humor and you can tell that he genuinely cares about all of his students. He uses real world examples and brings in amazing guest lecturers. This class was a ray of sunshine every week !!

Professor Aarons' Digital Marketing class was one of my favorite electives. The class is a good amount of work but worth it. We got certified in digital marketing tools we could add to our resume, the lectures were engaging, and you could tell he really cares about his students.

Learned a lot of useful, tangible skills that are really relevant in for a career in marketing. Big group proj working with a small co to revamp their digital marketing strategy. Aarons is so caring & invested in all his students & makes it a priority to be available for lots of office hrs- one of my favorite professors @ UT! Pls take this class

Prof. Aarons is honestly one of the best teachers I've had at UT. He's super funny and genuinely cares about his students, his lectures are interesting and always relevant to the real world, and he's had tons of experience in the field that makes him a great resource. You NEED to take this class!

Chris is an amazing professor! Hands down, he's the best professor I've ever had. His class (Digital Marketing) has been the most helpful and impactful class outside of school. We learned and executed real-life examples and tactics that have been extremely helpful in the marketing workplace. He is funny and really cares about his students! 10/10!

Took Digital Marketing his first semester teaching. He is such an engaging lecturer and wants to make connections with all his students. The class covers such a broad topic, but he breaks it down so well and gives such a good foundation for these topics. Participation helps you enjoy the class, and real world examples are always included.

Great professor, extremely knowledgeable, and a lot of fun if you have conversations with him. Is very straightforward with feedback and is always going to try to push you if he sees potential so dont be sensitive and realize his intentions are good. Also a great lecturer; youll never be bored in class. Group project is in depth but worth it.

Best professor I have had at UT & digital marketing is the most useful class I have taken. The group projects are fun - a digital marketing consulting project where you work with a real company, google ads simulation competition, etc. His lectures are entertaining and prof Aarons really goes out of his way to get to know you & help you. TAKE THIS

Aarons is a great professor and my favorite one I've had at UT. He is extremely personable, he gets to know his students really well and works closely with each of them to ensure they're successful if they want to be.

Because he was leaving this semester, it felt as if his class was sloppily composed due to his lack of passion for UT. He's great at what he does, but he put the bare minimum into this class's structure. However, he is great at explaining Bangla for non-native speakers and was such a kind and hilarious professor. Smart man, just very disorganized!

Professor Shamim is adaptable in his teaching methods. If a student is struggling with a particular part of the Bangla language, he will make sure that the student will eventually understand it. This ranges from the alphabet, general grammar, vocabulary, to even dialects. Not only that, he is available outside class if you ask him. Adore this guy!
Dr. Shamim is a great teacher. He is fun, caring, and laid back. The workload is also very reasonable and slow-paced as he wants everyone to learn on the same page. Take him!
He is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are clear and beneficial to the class. He engages his students with understandable materials. Would recommend everyone to take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best ever
Take his class. Gives a heavy curve and material isn't complicated

Like another reviewer said, Shaz's lectures lack any sense of cohesion. She jumps around in topics, time periods and regions frequently. Judging by the lack of attendance everyday, I would say most people agree with me when I say that this class was a waste of time. Shaz is very smart, but a bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Liked her approach but lectures can be quite hard to follow. Tends to assume everyone is on the same page based on a few vocal students. However it was still pretty easy to make an A in the class, and I felt I didn't need to show up to make the grade. Essay assignments are the majority of the grade and can be done largely independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures were highly informative and she encourages independent reading when writing papers. Shaherzad is extremely knowledgable and will guide you in the right direction. If you like the course title and topic, she's the person to take it with!
Pretty easy grader, I feel like if you put in the effort you'll make an A. "Shaz" knows her stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I did not think she was great at all. Her lectures were very sporadic and they did not follow a clear progression. She had way too many assignments and expectations for a lower division history course (over 20 pages worth of papers for the semester). She was available outside of class but she had clear favorites.

He's a great professor, and the class was a lot of fun. I'm a huge history nerd, and I really learned a lot and gained new insight into politics and philosophy. The reading and the class discussions were great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great guy, great professor. Class is clear-cut & minimalist: do the daily readings, come ready to discuss/debate, and complete the two assigned papers. Final grade comprised of few assignments, w/ each paper weighted HEAVILY. Can be a tough grader w/ sorta unrealistic standards, but final is easy. Very intellectual, pensive guy - great to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is really good at leading discussion based courses and helps keep class discussions from getting too tangential.  I didn't do a lot of the readings near the end because I was swamped and got recked by the final.  I liked him though, wish I could take again and try harder.   Really cool to talk with during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Siddiqi is very thorough. His class is difficult for a lower division government class, but I found it enjoyable. If you don't like philosophy, you may want to steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This course is an introductory survey of the political philosophy of several philosophers throughout the western world. Those who are uninterested in reading antiquated texts pertaining to political philosophy should not take this course. This course contains substantial reading. This course was incredibly thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: an amazing professor, i would highly recommend to take this class. he is a very patience person and a very fair grader. show up to class and you'll do well. because of the material of the class and how it is taught dont take this class as a freshman which is the mistake i made. would retake this class still.

Professor Aguayo is extremely understanding. He is also a student, so he understands the stress of finals season. Attendance in his class is for extra credit. His assignments are clear, and I literally ended with a 100 by turning all the assignments in. Definitely take this class if you need the credit!

This class was easy, but I  learned a lot. There's some freedom in how you complete the assignments. He doesn't post any information for each lecture until like an hour before class, so there's not much time to review things before class. Great class for people unsure of their career path or who want to learn how to prepare to enter the workforce.

Professor Aghaie was the opposite of helpful and supporting. His lectures consisted of him going off on tangents about whatever he felt like discussing that given day so most of the learning was up to you as the student. It often felt like he was making the class structure up as he went along and he never responds to emails. I q dropped.

Lectures were really random and didn't relate to the assigned readings often, had to mostly self learn/ study with the textbook. Primarily about history of the middle east, not gov, which was still interesting, but the random lectures and quite difficult timed essay mt/ finals were still difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think getting an A is pretty manageable if you do the readings and go to all the lectures. However, I didn't really feel that his lectures were very organized, and having to take notes on literally everything he says because it'll end up on the test becomes annoying when, on the test, you're having to remember his jumbled trail of thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. The class had no structure and the lectures were whatever he came up with that day. The only way to do well in the class is to write to what his preconceived opinions are about the given subject. You wont learn anything from him only on your own.

I cannot begin to describe how awful this man is in class. He loves to talk about how he is a “historian” and loves to interrupt you. I was 0.1% away from a A, had great attendance and built a teacher student relationship but that didn't matter because when I reached out about my grade he rudely ignored me and just said happy holidays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was just weekly readings and build up to a final research paper. Readings were long and often went undiscussed in class because Dr. Aghaie would go off on long tangents (he is clearly VERY intelligent on this subject, and makes that known). He was approachable, but was often unhelpful with feedback. Course was unorganized. TA was useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aghaie is a great professor, he truly knows his stuff and I really enjoyed the research project. He is very liberal which made some classes awkward for me as a conservative but he is in no way intimidating. The course is essentially a research course so pick a topic that interests you and you will have no issues !

I had a great experience in Modern Middle East. It is not an easy A, do the readings and take notes. Lectures are very hard to follow, but it encourages you to lock in and pay attention during class. He cares about his students and is willing to work with the class to direct learning to what people are interested in. Great guest lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

Kamran is rude and arrogant,  no more fascinating than any other person you see in the classroom.  I was rather disappointed as he lacks teaching methods and is extremely unapproachable. Good prof. Expects you to work very hard and produce excellent work, but is encouraging and helpful. If you do the work you will get a good grade.
is he for real! Arrogant and not that well read, I took more than one class with him and he teaches the same things in all of them!!
He delivered information in class, but doesn't really know how to teach.  He was not helpful.  Not someone you could call a mentor.  Did not find him approachable at all.

I took four different classes with him. He is old school in all the right ways. His lectures are the most organized I have ever experienced, he does not waste time and babble. His class is easy if you work hard, meaning keep up with the reading and go to every class. I would take any class he ever teaches.

The way he lectures is just confusing...he lists names on the overhead rather than outlining what he's talking about.  So if you don't get everything the first time, you're stuck with just a bunch of obscure arabic names. twenty essay questions for the final??? TONS of reading but the quizzes often involve only one book??? This guy is totally lame...this is an INTRO course!!!!!!
What kind of ass puts the same two questions on the final that were on the midterm? An named Aghaie. I could have spent the last half of the semester not learning anything...

I read a lot and even I think this guy assigned WAY too much reading.  He has hardly any humor/charisma to keep your attention and tends to drone about the subject. No Comments

good class presentation very open to questions, willing to help

professor agarwal is a great professor. The concepts covered in the class and inherently difficult and directly apply to real world scenarios. Go to class and actually listen to lectures/discussion. he is great.

Professor Agarwal is great. The course itself is definitely hard, and very self-paced with a lot of self-learning. But it's doable if you have good time management and collaborate with TAs and friends. Overall good professor for a hard class!

reviews.comment: Ashish is a very cool guy, is willing to extend deadlines on projects and assignments. Assignments are long and tedious, but you learn a lot. Not as hard as its reputation.

People says that MIS301H will be a hard class, but they're wrong. Dr. Agarwal is super knowledgeable and cares for his students.

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There's no way to get around it; this class is hard. Homework will consume a lot of your time (8+ hours per assignment). But the workload does get lighter through the semester. Dr. Agarwal is nice and cares about his students; lectures could be more engaging though. Read the cases to participate in class, and study well in advance for the tests.

MIS301H will consume all of your time and if you don't study three times as much as you think you need to, you won't do well. While he is nice and generally decent at presenting the info., understanding the material falls solely on you. Do not take this class if you don't want to read thirty pages a night or spend less than 30 hours on assignments.
He's hilarious and adorable. A ton of work though.
guys i love her

Her lectures are dense and can be hard to follow, especially if you lack background knowledge. Attendance is mandatory, so if you'll miss more than three classes, this course may not be for you. Exams are application-focused with more points allocated to the FRQ. Overall, I wouldn't take this course again.
Guys she is amazing. I literally loved this professor and her lectures were phenomenal. Like seriously do not listen to anyone that says anything bad about her.

Neuro development is an amazing class that absolutely improved how I read and write academic papers. This class is completely worth it if you are ready to put a substantial amount of effort in. She does cold call and her quizzes are hard, but you only need a 90+ to get an A and something like an 86+ to get an A-.

Dr. Agarwala is so knowledgeable and her lectures are very concise without fluffing up any information. The discussion sections led by her TAs were also incredibly helpful and everyone involved in the team ensures that you're ready for the exams. The exams and analyses of research papers ensures success in and out of her class. Take her!

This is a very tough class, but it's doable. The exams are open note and aren't that difficult as long as you understand what was covered in lecture. The pop quizzes are hard, you NEED to study for them. Overall, very interesting material, but expect to spend a good amount of time outside of class working.

reviews.comment: Tough at the start, it's not an easy class and she cold calls, but it forces you to build good revision habits and learn to study. Can be a little nitpicky on grammar and vocab.

I genuinely don't know how this person teaches at UT. She's a terrible human who lacks empathy for students and is anti-accessibility. She's very patronizing, making it seem like she enjoys student failure. She lacks interest in the subject and is obviously just teaching to collect her paycheck. I took BIO 320 btw. She lacks basic tech skills too

Dr. Argawala is incredibly impatient with her students and creates a hostile learning environment. She gets frustrated when students ask questions and is overall condescending. She does not promote a safe place whatsoever and will mock and embarrass you for saying the wrong thing in class.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwala is not an easy professor, she does not take shit from the students, but she's a great lecturer and is incredibly engaging in class. Dr. Gheith is an exceptional CS professor!

Gheith is an incredible lecturer, and I learned so much from his class. But the projects are brutal. Expect honors-level difficulty in an already very tough course. If you take this course you should probably clear out some other commitments and be prepared to spend 30-40 hours per week on it.
very good prof

Prof. Gheith is a great lecturer, and is willing to explain topics further for interested students (his lectures are more freeform). However, assignments are often tougher than they seem, so get started EARLY!! Also, quizzes are no joke, so try to do some learning about topics on your own. Experience is definitely summed up by the 5.0/5.0 rate.

One of those classes where you come out with a profound jump in mastery even if you only got a C-. The lectures are an absolute delight, he has immense understanding of the material. Likely the hardest programming projects you will do during your time at UT, but also thoroughly instructive and insightful. May have to no-life this class to do well.

Dr. Gheith is the best professor I have ever had! His lectures are truly amazing, and while the class is incredibly intensive project-wise, this finished product (a good chunk of an OS) is incredible and extremely rewarding. Having a small community with amazing TAs made the class experience even better. 10/10 would recommend!

For context, he teaches normal OS in Spring, honors in the Fall. Professor Gheith is one of the smartest professors I have taken and honestly, my favorite. No slides, just him, you, class, and whiteboard. Would I recommend over Norman? Yes, if you want a challenge. I also learned an incredible amount, but did I also spend 35+ hours per week? Yes.

Honestly, he's the best professor I've ever had in my entire life. While expectations are high, it is so rewarding, and Dr. Gheith and the TAs do their best to help you. Projects take a long time to complete, but are genuinely so awesome since you get to build your own operating system. I would strongly recommend taking Gheith over anyone else.

This was undoubtedly the hardest CS class i've taken here; however it's also been my favorite. Expect atleast 25 hours a week on projects with 0 days off. Our TAs were so goated and we had a great little community going making it that much more enjoyable. Gheith is also insanely well versed in OS and is genuinely always willing to help. 10/10

As an average CS student: CS439 is the hardest class you'll ever take, 30+ hrs/week is real. I couldn't take Norman and was terrified, but Gheith is amazing. Insanely rigorous, but his passion is mesmerizing. Office hours became group therapy. I now feel emotionally bonded to my TAs and peers. Might be Stockholm Syndrome. 10/10

He just knows

You will get docked big on participation unless you go to TA OH i think
Do you like operating systems? You better like operating systems. If you don't like operating systems, you are in for a whole lot of pain.
I did not sleep for more than 5 hours per day because of this guy. I lost 60 pounds because I was glued to vscode every minute of the day that i didn't even have time to eat.
This was the most eye-opening course in my career. I strongly recommend students take Dr. Gheith's OS courses!

Gheith is an incredible lecturer and is filled with knowledge. But the pace of this class and the fact that TAs (other undergrads) are in charge of all things grading makes it extremely difficult. There are 9 projects and quizzes every other week. Projects are intense and quizzes are hard with unclear grading at times. Don't get behind.

Dr. Gheith is defo one of the best people I've had as a professor-- you can't not like him. But, this might've been the most disorganized course I've ever taken. The TAs (mostly undergrads) handle everything including grading. Sometimes it felt like they weren't sympathetic, and their quizzes were nightmare fuel. The projects were hard but doable.

reviews.comment: Lectures will trick you into thinking this is a simple class, and the projects will quickly make you realize how many details the lecture missed. Very challenging and unfair class, and one of the worst experiences of my life. I learned a lot, but I would recommend taking Norman.

Gheith is a kind professor and obviously very smart. However, his class structure is very disorganized. There is little to no support for students who are struggling. The TAs are honestly the worst part of this course. They have no empathy for the students and struggle to explain concepts coherently.
Normies take Norman, GOATs take Gheith
good luck !

Gheith is one of the best lecturers at UTCS. Projects are difficult and require a network of friends to succeed. Take Gheith if you want a challenge, GL.

don't take it if you aren't super interested about os. you would probably be better off with norman.

reviews.comment: This is sink or swim class and there is no support for those sinking. The teacher is unavailable outside class, OH lines are long, and there are few resources unlike Norman's. Gheith is a good lecturer, but lectures are unorganized which can make it hard to figure out what exactly you're supposed to be following. Projects also have NO instructions.
No materials for the class. TAs don't exist until the last week. Your Grade depends strictly on the quizzes. Servers WILL be down when you're trying to submit. Take Norman
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I took Norman

Super unstructured class w/ minimal resources. Waste hours waiting in office hours for TAs who are clueless on how to help half the time. Lectures aren't recorded & get insanely long + difficult to follow. Only take if you actually like OS... Otherwise take Norman, easier content w/ more resources available and partner projects.

Gheith gave some of the best lectures I've experienced at UT - super engaging, with nothing but a marker. He extended project deadlines to help our struggling class. Yes, this class is HARD, individual projects and bi-weekly quizzes are VERY challenging. Still, this class is so rewarding. If you have the chance to take him, do it.

Dr. Gheith is not the god of lectures, but he's exceptionally kind and understanding. Graded by projects, difficult quizzes (that will only be easier if students write quiz questions for participation points), and participation. I wish he would record the lectures himself instead of someone from the student body being responsible for it.
bro cooked us
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yet another 5.0 Gheith rating!

The only bad thing about Dr Gheith is that there's only one of him. I wish we could clone him and have him teach every class. He's at least a standard deviation above every other professor I've had in lecturing/communication ability, clarity and fairness of assignments and grading, classroom management, pacing, and motivation of the subject matter.
Still the goat

Projects are insane and take at least 40 hours/week - get ready to sell your soul to this class. Lectures are outstanding, going to class and paying attention is a must. Gheith is utterly inaccessible outside of class. Biweekly quizzes are hard but projects help study for them. You will not know your grade until the last week of semester.

Weekly projects take 50+ hours, no exams, biweekly hard quizzes (study for them!). This will undoubtedly be the hardest class you will ever take, but Gheith's lectures will make it ALL worth it. The second half of semester was much easier based off of feedback. This class is a rite-of-passage, and one of the most life-changing classes I've taken.

Gheith is so smart that I can't understand half of the content for the life of me. Great if you want to learn systems, not so great if you want to do well in the class because TAs dictate all grading. He does his best to accommodate individual circumstances if you just talk to him about them. Nevertheless, he is invaluable to the UTCS department.
Incredible lecturer. Homework can be very time consuming and quizzes can be quite difficult, but overall great class.

i love prof. gheith. he's very patient and an exciting lecturer. the class is hard though, projects take lots of time but gheith and the TAs are pretty understanding. grade will be rough but you will learn a lot.

Amazing lecturer, but does not communicate with TAs at all/enforce any restrictions on them. The TAs were free to provide difficult quizzes without Gheith's approval and did not grade assignments until several months after they were due. The professor is impossible to reach via email.

Best professor I've ever had. Very knowledgeable and he explained extremely complicated topics from the ground up in a digestible way. Lectures were entertaining and he explained why we built things the way we did and other alternatives. 10000/10 would take again.

Best lecturer ever, loves computer architechture and knows everything about everything. Amazing projects where you learn so much, but they can be challenging. Weekly quizzes that were really hard but not impossible.

Get ready to spend all your time on this class. Some weeks I was easily in the GDC past 12am. It kinda got fun after a while tho. It is extremely hard, don't be afraid to ask the TAs questions as well as those around you. Also I thought I was gonna fail until the last week and ended up with a B if that gives you any hope. Utilize office hours!

Amazing professor, hard ass class. But that's OS for you so don't be scared to take him. Somehow this genius man could show up to class with nothing necessarily prepared, and give a whole lecture off the top of his head. He is very engaging and helpful, but outside of class you have to rely on TAs/others to help understand.

Great professor but insanely inaccessible outside of class. TAs do 100% of the grading and like others have mentioned some can show favoritism, so it can be difficult to get help during office hours. When it comes to deciding between Gheith or Norman for 439, expect amazing lectures and difficult, rewarding assignments but delayed/no communication.

I agree with others on Gheith's knowledge and kindness, but sometimes I felt an over-reliance on office hours and friend networks to complete projects. This course pushes those interested in systems to their limits for the better, but the culture of the class can feel strangely intense and cliquey (both TAs and classmates) when trying to seek help

Super interesting course. Dr. Gheith is an amazing, kind, and approachable lecturer. However, projects cannot be competed without OH. Make friends. Get to know the TAs. Dr. Gheith is not easily accessible outside class. Great lectures, but projects require TA assistance and a network of friends to get info, and are borderline unfair.

I really liked having Dr. Gheith. He is an AMAZING lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory in this class but going to class helps. Weekly quizzes (no tests) - fairly difficult. The assignments are fairly challenging too. The class is hard but make friends in the class, and talk to the TAs and Dr. Gheith himself. Also, the final project is fun to do.

OS will be hard no matter what. Gheith is an amazing lecturer, I enjoyed going to class for once. Gheith himself is a bit disorganized. However, the coding assignments and quizzes are very hard and the TAs had an intense disconnect from what's happening in class. Make friends, go to OHs (including Gheith's), and introduce yourself to the TAs early.

OS is one of the hardest classes in UTCS, no doubt. But taking it with Gheith makes it easy to get through. He doesn't use slides but is able to teach such complex ideas in easy to grasp chunks on the whiteboard. Going to OH is a must for the assignments. No tests, weekly quizzes are pretty difficult, final project is fun.

Gheith is great if you're interested in systems. However, that's really not my strong suit, so the class takes a lot of time for what feels like very little payoff. Make sure to study for the quizzes (altho usually depends on TAs) since they're not curved and worth 40% of your grade. Also, final project is graded much harsher than in arch.

In many ways this class felt like 429 part 2. It was almost like Dr. Gheith picked up right where he left off at the end of the previous semester. The style of the class was basically the same with all the signature Gheith specialties. I personally think this class was harder than Arch but some will disagree. There are fewer quizzes than Arch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Papa Gheith never ceases to bless the UT Austin Computer Science Department. Never leave papa, never leave...
I love professor Gheiht!

Weekly assignments and quizzes can be pretty challenging (quizzes more dependent on TAs who write them, but questions are at the upper end of Bloom's taxonomy expecting creation, evaluation, and analysis of topics from class). Because it's every week, the schedule can be tough with little breathing room. Start early, do not fall behind.

Amazing professor. This class is worth the hassle of getting an honors petition. Taught difficult concepts in easy to understand chunks and very good at answering questions. Amazing lecturer. The assignments are very hard but worthwhile. Going to office hours is essential, there's just so much material. No tests, but weekly quizzes.

Probably the best professor I've had at UT. He comes to class and just lectures without slides which were easy to keep up with most of the time. Class is HArd. But going to help hours and piazza helped a ton. Structure of the class was weekly quizzes/assignments, participation, and one final assignment they are lenient on.

Dr. Gheith explains concepts well. The TAs are nice and knowledgeable. His lectures are a little disorganized sometimes. We only had 8 quizzes. If you misunderstand some questions, you may lose many points from the final grade. There are no practice quizzes, so sometimes I know my understanding is wrong in the quizzes. Learn a lot from the course.
Thank you professor Gheith! This class is my favorite class in UT. Professor Gheith is not only a wonderful teacher but also a great person. I learned a lot in this class!

Dr.Gheith is a great lecturer, really just came to class with a dry erase marker and started lecturing from the dome. The class is 50% coding assignments that vary in difficulty but be prepared for at least 15 a week and up to 30 for the harder assignments. Would definitely recommend for OS.

Dr Gheith continues to be a great OS professor. Honors and nonhonors versions were pretty much the same. The honors version had CSB and Turing. Regardless while the projects expectedly take time, you learn a lot of interesting content.
