I suggest having a friends to study with to get through projects, or someone to discuss with if you're stuck.

I am thrilled that I took OS with professor Gheith. He knows and understands the material so well, literally walks in and starts speaking, and the content makes sense. The only problem is that the projects are VERY time-consuming. This class sucked my soul away for a semester, but Gheith and the TAs made the class doable.

The class is lecture-heavy, there are weekly projects and quizzes that cover that week's topics. The projects are HARD, period. Tough graders, it's somewhat ridiculous. The quizzes are alright if you attend lecture except for one question each week that barely anyone gets right. Participation is 10% of your grade. Getting an A seems very difficult.

Dr. Gheith's Arch class this semester had 9 individual projects, each a week long. They are pretty time consuming and you may lose some sleep. There is a huge learning curve in this class. I learned a lot more than expected, very satisfying. The class heavily uses Piazza. Quizzes every week, pay attention. Dr Gheith loves memes, jokes, and convos.

Dr. Gheith is a true gem of a teacher. Like an emerald (or platinum, etc.). He TEACHES like an ideal lecturer: always introducing concepts from the basic, trivial cases and gradually explaining the next natural step to take. Some parts of an OS are ugly, per se, but Gheith explains the theory + code for EACH component you build. Terrific.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Gheith's 439 class online during COVID, and I can say I was pleasantly surprised that the class was not as terrible as made out to be. Lot of work, but mostly in the beginning. The last 5 or so weeks, the workload was pretty light. No tests, and quizzes are graded easily. Participation counts. Biggest advice: get started on projects early.

Yasss!!!! Absolutely amazing teacher that teaches, cares for, and helps you. Weekly quizzes ensure you're on top of the material and programming assignments are interesting AF! Piazza discussions are engaging. He makes boring material super interesting. Take his course and it will be the one of your best decisions.

Probably one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Thoroughly answers questions in lecture and explains concepts very clearly. Projects are very time-consuming; start early. Weekly quizzes can be annoying, but if you paid attention in class you should be fine. Very flexible and listens to feedback from his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tied for best professor at UT (along with Mike Scott). Taking OS with Gheith is a real learning experience. I would highly recommend taking OS with Gheith instead of Norman, for all the reasons outlined on this page (I did both).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The hardest CS class could not have been taught by a more caring professor. He genuinely wants you to succeed and will stay late to help students with projects. It's hard to fail the class, but at the same time it's as tough as advertised. Attend the lectures and office hours, and you'll be ok.

OS is going to be difficult with whoever you take. That being said, Gheith's class was not overwhelmingly difficult. He makes you work for your grade but so long as you work, you will pass. Lectures are not mandatory, but if you miss one you will be very far behind. He is extremely knowledgeable, lectures from memory. He cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: First things first, anyone saying that they got an A+ in this class or that attendance is mandatory is lying. Keep that in mind when you see all these positive reviews. Lectures still aren't interesting but are more related to the projects. Projects are more designy than Arch. Quizzes were hit or miss. Tests are open book but way too fast paced.

Best teacher I've ever had in my life. Gheith is a treasure of the UT CS department, and explains OS concepts in an approachable easy to understand format entirely from memory. Projects are hard, but Gheith and the TAs are more than willing to help you through them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was hard but rewarding at the same time. Gheith is a great lecturer and I actually wanted to go to lectures because of how good of an educator he is (BAMF lectures completely from memory). Assignments are rough but capped at around 40-50 hours for a given assignment. Going to office hours saved me a bunch of time on the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Walks in with nothing but a whiteboard marker, and delivers amazing lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy sucks. Nothing against him personally, just really didn't enjoy his class. Lectures are super slow and go around in circles. Projects are time-consuming and not related to class material. Quizzes are random. Tests are open-book so questions ended up being either super easy or super hard. I did learn a lot but not due to his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gheith is one of the most amazing professors I've had at UT. His lectures are easy to follow and he manages to make complex subjects very easy to understand. Projects were difficult and time consuming but easily doable if you started early. My only complaint would be that it isn't really possible to study for his tests except by coming to class

Dr. Gheith is probably the best undergraduate professor in UTCS. OS is usually seen as the hardest class of undergrad, but Dr. Gheith's amazing lectures made it a much better experience. He's always available at office hours too. The class is hard but grading is fair and you will come out of it with so much more knowledge than when you went in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Gheith's OS is very project based, and you'll know it. Assignments are weekly, and take anywhere from 20 to 60 hours of work. However, he's a great lecturer, is very helpful during office hours, and is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. But with all the late nights in the lab, I never want to take that class again. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gheith is an amazing teacher who knows the material cold (lectures with no notes) and is very nice in office hours. That said, the class is extremely tough, and of the 14 projects, I and most people I know put in 40+ hours of effort on 4 of them. Find a solid group to work with and plan carefully before writing any code, and you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an excellent professor, but OS is genuinely one of the hardest classes you can take. It will be really difficult for you. Yes, even you. I'd take it again, but only because of the friends I made in it. I literally lost 15lbs because I was working so much on it. Really. It's 50-60 hrs/week. If you do take it, don't take anything else hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Legendary. He's the person who made OS, the most infamous course on the CS degree list, my favorite class at UT. Projects were very time consuming (spent 30+ hours/week) but that's where most of the learning happened. His tests were tough but if you do well on project/quiz it'll be fine. Most importantly he's very approachable so go to office hour!

Gheith was one of the best teachers that I've ever had. He knows his stuff and encourages interesting conversation and lecture. The class is objectively very difficult however. He pushes you hard and enables the student to perform well. As long as you can put in the effort it should be wonderfully challenging.

Gheith is honestly one of the best professors at UT, and has such a different method of teaching. He's really aware if you're not doing well and will do everything he can to make sure you understand the material given you at least put in some effort. I really wish he taught more classes other than Operating Systems
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very, very hard

Absolute best lecturer at UT. He could make a phone book sound exciting, and he explains complicated things really well. But he doesn't expect you to have a life outside his class, and he experiments with the curriculum, often with painful results. Generally 40-60 hours a week on projects. Insane. Exams and weekly quizzes are also pretty tough.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best lectures I've ever attended. He is an amazing teacher and truly cares that his students understand the material. I took 429H and 439H both with Dr. Gheith. Operating Systems (439H) was a lot of work but I learned so much it was totally worth it! 10/10 my favorite professor and would take any class taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! He's very knowledgable and obviously very passionate about what he teaches. LECTURES ARE BASICALLY MANDATORY because lectures & projects are where the majority of learning is done, and you won't know how to do the projects if you don't go to class. His quizzes and tests are very hard so beware because he doesn't curve.
Amazing teacher!
Helpful professor and knows the material inside & out. However, his CS 429 Summer class was insanely challenging. The assignments and quizzes were brutal. I think half the class ended up dropping.

Professor Gheith actually cares about teaching, and is very good at it. There are projects every week, ranging from fairly easy (3 hrs) to very hard (25hrs). I've taken 3 classes with Gheith so far, and if he taught any more, I'd take them too.

Gheith was hands down the best professor I've had so far. His lectures were clear and he took his time to make sure everyone understood what was going on. The projects were challenging, but nothing not doable. If you get the chance to take this or any other course by him, do it.

Great guy and lecturer. He is one of the nicest professors I've met and truly cares for the students. Class was hard though. Tests were intended to fail you and were far too long for anyone to finish (which he said was his intention.) These tests, however, were curved to compensate. Grading: 40% Projects, 20% Midterm, 20% Final, 20% Quizzes

The best professor I have had at UT. Take any classes that he is offering. Incredibly clear, coherent lecture that goes out of his way to ensure that you actually understand the material. On top of that, he is funny guy that is not a hard ass and understands that grades aren't the be all to life. Tests were open book/notes. Highly recommend

Dr. Adams for BME 344 was pretty good; she got the job done and was funny. She also brings her dogs often to class. Weekly homework took a while but it was reasonable. Final exam is optional. You can miss 6 class instapolls which is generous. Weekly quiz over the previous hw, and occasional pop quizzes just to add as bonus (fine if you miss).

She cares more about instapoll than attendance/learning. The content for this class is learnable but not through her lectures. If you do understand the material (outside sources), the hw and tests are pretty easy. Lots of partial credit.

The class structure is very consistent, and it is always obvious what is expected of you. Show up to class and understand concepts and you'll be fine. Grading is generous and allows you chances to learn through your mistakes. Overall, would recommend!

I went back here to say that I am so glad Im taking other BME professors rn that are genuinely qualified to teach at this level and material. After going through several of her classes, I almost lost faith in pursuing BME. She dropped my grade by a letter grade for not taking an instapoll during an exam I literally took and directly handed to her.
every day i drove to this class without wearing my seatbelt in hope of going to the hospital instead of class. genuinely one of the worst professors ever!!! made me switch to mech e.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Instructor is condescending in Office Hours. TA never shows up to Office hours. LA was very helpful tho so go to them for help. Heat transfer is pretty difficult and instructor struggles with teaching it because of staffing issues so be prepared. 1 exam is dropped so try to do well for them and don't take final exam unless you have to.

She was good for fluids but not heat transfer at all. That unit was an absolute nightmare. Be sure to go to every class because she has pop quizzes. She goes through instapoll later in the semester and cross checks to ensure proper attendance.

Professor has a very disorganized style of teaching. Very difficult to follow. Never solved problems fully in class, claiming that she would mess up on the math (which ig she did anyways). Never paid attention to her in class because its frankly a waste of time. I recommend watching Dr. John Biddle's lectures on youtube.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She cares way more about Instapolls (which she takes even during exam days), than showing your mastery of the material. Wish she just had a sign-in sheet. Lecturing style is monotone with slow pacing; shows no enthusiasm in the material. You'll learn way more from watching CPPMechEngTutorials, who saved me during the heat transfer unit.

Lectures didn't make sense to me, but watching a YouTube video would always suffice. Exams are super easy. Attendance is mandatory, and if you miss more than 6 lectures, you receive a 10% grade deduction.
She emphasizes showing your work and gives most of the credit for the process, which makes it easier to get a good grade

Even when I was physically in class and completed Instapoll, I was marked “absent” because I had not taken the optional bonus quiz. No clear communication, policies that were not detailed in the syllabus were suddenly enforced later. One additional absence results in a 10% drop from your overall grade. Grade dropped from A to B.
Instructor cares more about instapoll than actual learning - even when there was proof that you were jn class.
Just be ready for her to single handily ruin your entire life and any future prospects of you enjoying your major. I hope to never set foot in her class again. Please avoid at all costs.
Dr. Adams spends most of the lecture giving a poor explanation of concepts and limited or incorrect application to the field of BME.
I loved the consistent structure of Adams' classes. She is very fair and has a fun personality. You get a lot of credit for just showing your work on homework, quizzes, and exams.

Hands down my favorite BME professor at UT! She's incredibly caring, energetic, and funny. Her ability to simplify complex concepts makes them easy to grasp, and she teaches consistent problem-solving strategies that work no matter the difficulty. The extra credit practice problems are a huge help for exams!

No idea why she is teaching so many classes for being new here. It's very apparent how stretched thin she is with her basically learning as she reads the slides, so be warned bc the bme department does not gaf at all. Good luck getting through a single lecture, you'll be learning outside 100% of the time.

Professor Adams was nice but didn't really know how to teach biomechanics. She wouldn't really go over what was going to be covered each day--she would just start doing an example and you had to figure out what was going on. Homework sometimes took an incredibly long time, and the grading system was pretty harsh on tiny mistakes.

I liked Dr. Adams approach to the class(ie: cheat sheets on exams, weekly quizzes, ect), but a lot of the class was teach yourself to do well. The weekly quizzes were often difficult, and covered stuff in the lab, which means you were cooked if you had lab after the quiz. Overall, would take Dr. Adams again, shes a sweet professor.

Dr. Adams is a caring professor. It was her first time teaching BME313L so she didn't always know what was going on, but I thought she was pretty good for BME344. Quizzes and homework were tough but manageable if you put in the time and effort. Opportunities for extra credit if you are willing to put in the work. I enjoyed being in her class.

Strict on attendance with no leniency w those instapolls. Tests are only doable if you get outside help from anyone else. Difficult experience with her methods of teaching, which include reading off of slides and struggling to get through a single problem. Wish she was more understanding

You will have better luck taking anyone else. She doesn't understand the material, or care, so her lack of understanding will rub off of you. She is not accommodating at all; she won't come to any sort of understanding with you about attendance or any other concern. Probably THE most difficult professor I had to deal with and you will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, I never hated this professor until it came to how unmoving and disingenuous she is. No matter the situation you are in she does not care, dog died? too bad. Mental health crisis? good luck! You relay on teaching yourself and TAs, steer clear of her if you can especially for numerical methods. (i've taken 3 of her classes)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Adams clearly did not want to teach Numerical. Not her fault due to lack of BME staff, but she could have put more effort into understanding the material herself. Quizzes were difficult w/avgs around 14/20 but exams were easy. Labs were difficult as they would occur BEFORE we learned the material. It seemed like Adams was learning WITH us.

I love Adams! (as a person) while her circuits class was amazing, she's not that well suited for biomechanics nor numerical methods. She's sometimes as confused as we are, while this is no way her fault (due to the little amount of bme professors). Honestly, teach yourself before lecture, stay on top of your work and it should be a breeze.

I had three of her classes and I wish I was with another professor. Everyone I talk to also agrees that she is not good at teaching; she sounds just as confused reading the slides as I am. Weekly quizzes and attendance is graded.
She is a great professor and is very kind and welcoming when students have trouble understanding the content.

This was her first time teaching the class so it was a bit unorganized at times. However, she is very nice and helpful when you are confused in class. Always tries to make class more engaging when the content may be boring at times. Lots of homework so try to stay on top of the work. The midterms and final are graded pretty fairly.

Dr. Adams is new, so she's developing her teaching style. She grades very generously and uses the GUESS method to give points, so follow it and you'll be fine. Exams are similar to exam reviews and homeworks are much harder than the exams so don't worry. Weekly quizzes and potential extra credit makes going in person worth it. I enjoyed her class.

As a STEM major, I really enjoyed this class. No tests, engaging lectures, and weekly quizzes every Friday. The annotations/readings due before every class can be difficult to stay consistent with, but you only need to write a few sentences. Write your notes during lecture and review by re-listening to recorded lectures on 2x speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is a great lecturer, but it's the lengthy daily readings that made me dread going to this class, as well as the weekly quizzes.  You truly will learn a lot, but unless you like learning out of an online textbook and then going and being talked at about it, I don't recommend.  If you're looking for an easy a though, take her Rome class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I fell ill and had to drop.  The nature of the course is fast paced but I love the way she has the course structured and once I understood the flow it got so much easier.  It takes time to learn another language but the way she teaches does make it really fun. I plan to take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT I'm a classics minor but I feel like even if you don't know anything about classics it's very accessible. Dr. Adams pairs the readings and movies so well and it is just such an interesting class. I'm also not a big horror movie person but still loved it, definitely recommend. Also not too much work!

Overall decent and lenient professor. I definitely recommend taking one of her classes for a VAPA. I took her in Fall 2024, and we had no tests, just daily annotations, weekly quizzes, and one final project. The final project is also very vague and you get to be pretty creative with it.

This class is a simple but engaging VAPA that Dr. Adams structured to be easy. The class is beyond manageable and has little to no workload as long as you pay attention to the lectures, do the readings, and study a bit for the weekly quizzes. There were no exams in the class, and instead of a final, there is a fun final project. Highly Recommended!

I'd die for Lizzy. If you didnt like her you probably thought you could get away with doing nothing, which is just plain lazy and you only have yourself to blame. Loved her lectures, she's so funny. Have to buy tophat for attendance. No tests, just weekly quizzes with 2 drops and a final project. Loved this class so much, it was really interesting.

Every day I woke up for MWF, I hoped for a lime scooter to bulldoze through me on speedway for the sole reason of not attending this class. I dreaded even opening my eyes and having to walk to this class. Tears.. straight tears... this professor drove me to insanity. Take her if you want permanent migraines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory and even though I was in the hospital I wasn't able to exempt the weekly quizzes or attendance making this drop my GPA. Teacher did not care and was told some quizzes were mandatory even though I could not make it because of my medical condition.

Dr. Adam's is a lively and compassionate professor, who clearly understands her class is a VAPA that's not meant to be hard or time consuming. Graded mainly by participation in class and 2-ish weekly reading assignments that are chill. Quizzes every Friday that are specific, but no tricks and are pulled straight from lecture. Super chill class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for my VAPA, but she doesn't include a lot of content about art, so if you aren't an art person this class is for you. Dr. Adams is super understanding, kind, and funny. The quizzes are nitpicky, but you get used to it. She is a very entertaining lecturer and I learned so much!

The professor includes small details on the quiz so If you're not really interested in Ancient Rome, it's hard to get good grades on them unless you put in a lot of effort. The lectures can be interesting at times but as mentioned if you're not passionate about the subject, it's just not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures. Have to pay to use tophat. She records lectures but doesn't upload slides. Didn't study and still did fine. Towards the end turned on location tracking bc people were skipping. overall not bad and interesting, just thought she was a bit too upset about attendance things that weren't a big deal as that happens in every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Every Thursday night I'd stare at my ceiling fan wondering if I could launch into another universe—one where Rome had never been founded. I studied, cried, studied more, and still got obliterated. Took this for an art credit and found less art than on tax forms. I'd rather eat cement than take this class again. Emotionally shattered. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams's lectures are always engaging and interesting, and the content of the course is intriguing. There are daily readings that are a bit tedious but can be completed in 15 min or less. There are no exams, just weekly quizzes that take questions directly from the lectures and a final project. Overall a very easy and fun vapa.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams and the TA Lane are super knowledgable! i took this class for my CEHET and the material was pretty interesting imo. attendance is graded, but i never talked ehe. quiz due every day of class (therefore a bit of reading) but its calm. there r no exams, only projects! super lit and easy and fun take her if u can!

Loves to talk and elaborate on topics, especially if you engage. Weekly quizzes with no exams (experimental, 1st class to do so), readings to annotate, and a creative final project. If you love reading and/or Ancient Roman history, you will excel in this class. Attendance is also a must; they are recorded based on effort (quizzes are code-locked).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: EASY VAPA! Her lectures were interesting and she knows what she's talking about. The grade was based on homework readings (persuall) + quizzes (every Friday based on lectures) + participation (tophat questions). Take her if you can!!

Horror in Classics and Film was a LOT of fun, and this was my favorite course of the semester. Dr. Adams is a very fun lecturer, and I enjoyed all of the readings and movies that she selected for this class. There is a good amount of reading, but if you like mythology, you will enjoy them all (I did!).

Dr. Adams is a great prof and made the content pretty engaging. I took for GC credit and think its pretty easy A if you just do the work. Grade made up of annotations (2/week), weekly quiz, in-class participation (not accuracy), and final proj. Fun times I love Ancient Rome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was a blast. As a STEM major, I took this class as my VAPA, and I honestly could not have asked for anything better. Lectures were engaging, the material was interesting, and it really wasn't that difficult. There were a lot of readings, but they didn't take too long. As long as you show up to class and do the hw, you're guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't particularly love history, but Professor Adams made the content really interesting. Her lectures were really funny and informative. Grade was made up of annotations (2-3 times a week), quizzes (once a week), and participation (during class). Quizzes were fair and relatively easy if you took good notes and studied a little beforehand.

Heavy on reading between classes, though the annotations that were required were graded very easily. Weekly quizzes on Friday, but they were pretty easy to do well on if you just studied for half an hour. Relatively entertaining lectures, definitely tries to accommodate well for her students.

Professor Adams was superb! Her lectures were so engaging and interesting, she is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about this course. Homework readings consist of a few annotations. Mandatory quizzes every Friday with questions from lectures and hmwrk readings. No final. Participation is recommended. Easy A for a VAPA. Take her!!!!

Professor Adams is an engaging lecturer and makes it easy to get an A if you do the work. Grading was based on attendance questions during lectures, assigned readings, and an in-class quiz at the end of the week with the final being an open-ended project on the course subject. If you follow the readings and attend class, you'll be fine.

Lectures were good but there was homework after every lecture, which could sometimes be long. We had weekly quizzes, which were fairly easy as long as you did the homework and paid attention in the lecture.

Dr. Adams is great! She is very clear with how she describes topics during lecture, and the homework is not too hard. The class is very easy as long as you pay attention to lectures and show up to class. Grade is based off of attendance, participation, homework (one is due before each class), and quizzes. The quizzes are fair; take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Very fascinating lectures, found myself very interested. Participation polls during class. Weekly quizzes covering lecture material, pretty easy. Tests are also relatively light.

Professor is very down to earth and easy to approach. Gives material to read outside of class - sometimes a lot, but rarely boring.

Overall, very enjoyable class.

I agree that this class is not an easy A for VAPA. Her weekly quizzes are hard, especially the select-all questions. Midterm is not cumulative. The first midterm is hard but the rest are much easier. I enjoy her lecture and have fun learning about Ancient Roman. Pay attention in the lecture, review nots before the exam. All answers are on the slide

I had Dr. Adams for Intro to Ancient Rome (VAPA and Global Cultures Flag). An A in this course requires some effort but is not overwhelming. Attend class, take notes, do the assigned readings, and study for the quizzes and midterms, and you will be fine. Dr. Adams wants students to succeed in her class and is there to help you. No complaints.

Dr. Adams is a really thoughtful professor. I took her Ancient Rome class for my VAPA, and in the beginning it was QUITE intimidating, however, as the semester progressed I did better in the class. This class isn't an "easy VAPA" but it's doable. Beware of weekly quizzes, they have tricky questions. The tests are reasonable, and I did well on them.

Dr. Adams is chill and tries to make her lectures entertaining; however, she provides so much material that it can feel like you are drowning in it. Grade is made up of 3 exams, which you should definitely study for if you want to pass because she makes oddly specific questions, weekly quizzes, in class participation, and a few discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Adams is very passionate about what she teaches, and as a result assumes that students have a foundational knowledge of Classical Myth, and starts teaching harder material from day 1. Attendance is taken through TopHat and the worst part of this class by FAR are the mandatory Friday quizzes which are unnecessary and oddly specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is a cool, hilarious, and compassionate professor. Her lectures were so funny, and she made mythology so interesting and fun to learn about. There are weekly quizzes on Friday, and one exam before the final. They're all very easy so long as you keep up with the material. I really liked her for mythology. Take Dr. Adams!

Dr. Adams is so much fun to have as a professor. Her lectures are engaging and funny and made even the boring parts of the class fun to learn! Super lenient grader, just had to do a handful of discussion posts, weekly quizzes, and the midterm + final. The exams & quizzes are easy and straight forward if you do the reading and pay attention in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There's assignments due every Thursday and Sunday and aren't too bad. Quizzes aren't hard just make sure you're familiar with some of the material. ID assignments aren't graded hard, they only take points if the information is incorrect or if you did the same topic as someone else. Overall, a good class especially if you want to learn about Rome

I took this as an online course for my vapa, so I didn't interact with Dr. Adams. But I emailed a few times with the teaching team and they responded quick! Assignments were due weekly on Thursdays and Sundays. 3 quizzes and a small discussion post per week, so not terrible. Just make sure to prioritize time for the course and don't blow it off!

I really love professor Adams. Her class is very engaging and she is super accommodating. She makes the course as fair and easy as possible. While there is still a lot of reading and effort in the final project, the material itself is not difficult. My only critique is that she does not answer her email. But she is still understanding/accommodating

I took Intro to Ancient Rome online with Dr. Adams. Since the class was online, I never interacted with her but she seemed very sweet from her recordings. Don't be fooled by the fact that this class is online, there is still a lot of work that you have to put in. However, if you do your assignments (they're not hard at all), it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It was a lot of work to go through all the modules and the exams weren't easy, but I really enjoyed the class, and it was nice that I could do it on my own time.

Professor Adams is a great lecturer. She makes the class very interesting and involves the students too. But, the class requires loads of reading and she isn't someone who will just give you an A. You have to work hard and be very good at writing to get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Lizzy for Intro to Classical Mythology and it was definitely my favorite class I have taken at UT. Lizzy is hilarious and I genuinely enjoyed her class. Best professor by far! Her lectures are also amazing. There is a lot of reading required for the class but they are super easy and enjoyable for the most part. Take this class if you can!

Took Introduction to Classical Mythology. Lizzy is an amazing professor. She is young, super cool, and hilarious. The lectures are super interesting and very helpful in understanding the material. She is easy to reach through email and highly responsive. Exams aren't bad - just study. Go to SI! One downside - lots of reading, like, every night.
Lizzie's great--- always answers questions, super chill
Overall Lizzie was a great TA and definitely helped clarify issues I had within the class. She was always very helpful and timely with her answers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy, you just have to keep up with your work, but you can definitely put it off until the last minute if you really want to lol. The module quizzes were pretty sucky because the questions vary in difficulty and sometimes you get stuck with a whole bunch of hard ones, but other than that it was a pretty awesome class.

Dr. Bush's class was pretty enjoyable and easy enough to get an A in. Projects are a large part of your grade, which have really confusing directions but at least are graded easily. Essentially no homework (completion, really short even if you do it) and only 2 exams if you do well on both. You gotta go to class though for your hw/participation.

Lectures were posted online & 50% of the grade was essentially participation (20% attendance, 30% projects which were graded very leniently). I feel he has gotten a bad rep. I came into this class honestly expecting the worst but he has improved immensely as compared to previous semesters. Optional final & exams were very similar (easier) than HW.

Prof Bush was good at explaining the concepts during lecture, and his tests were very fair. Optional final if you do good enough on the midterms, and the homeworks are all optional too. Light amount of coursework and overall easy class. Only complaint is that there weren't enough instructions given on the projects, and there was little time given.

Dr. Bush integrated his research in a way that made the class so much more interesting than your typical circuits class. Seeing as it was a BME class, he integrated physiological circuits and imaging from his lab so that we had cool projects like analyzing our own vasculature. He also had super neat demos and plenty of extra credit opportunities.

"if at first you don't succeed, try, try again." And that's exactly what Proff Bush is doing - he's enrolled to teach the class again in Fall 2023. So, I'm here to give you a fair warning: If you're looking for a professor who will teach this class take 311 in the Spring.

Dr. Bush was new to teaching. He had never taken a circuits class before having to teach it, and many students did poorly on the first test; however, he gave his students several chances to raise their grades. Students who failed the first exam ended the class with A's. Also, there were plenty of optional extra credit opportunities.

It was his first year teaching, so it was a little rocky (esp the first exam), but he corrected it with tons of extra credit, which was nice. The exams generally reflected the concepts from the homework, which was optional. The final project involved imaging our own arteries with ultrasound, which is the coolest project I've done for any class.

I thought Dr. Bush did well for his first time teaching the class. I don't think he deserves as many bad reviews as he has. The homeworks were completion and were always harder than the exams, so if you do the homework the exams are pretty straightforward.
He's a really nice person, but not so great as a professor. He gave a lot of extra credit, though.

This was Dr. Bush's first time teaching, and he really seemed to struggle in figuring out a consistent teaching method. He used the whiteboard and wasn't sure of himself in the material he was teaching. He does accommodate by providing a lot of extra credit opportunity and dropping a lot grades. He does integrates his own research into the class.

Dr.Bush is helpful in OH. Reading the textbook helps, build your foundation. He doesn't record lectures and uses the whiteboard, so going to class is how you learn. DO THE HWs bc they do help. He is a new professor, so still learning the ropes. This class will probably get better with time. If there is extra credit, DO IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yes, it was Dr. Bush's first semester teaching, and yes that did affect the class. However, he cares about his students' understanding of the material and made lots of effort to be available to answer questions and concerns. The end of semester project was really interesting and will be hammered out in the future. This class takes effort,dont slack

Proffesor Bush was just not meant to be a teacher. He was unorganized, chaotic, and passive aggressive. He made content mistakes daily, and didn't care if we were stressed/confused. He used our project to data mine us for his own research, the project was a waste of a month. Grading system was very lenient, but this class was an awful experience.

I would not recommend taking a class with Professor Adam Bush. He lacks clear expectations and seems more focused on his own research than teaching. He gives a lot of extra credit, but the exams are hard Professor Bush also undermines his own abilities which makes students feel worried about their success in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is super lecture heavy and unfortunately Dr. Bush is a horrible lecturer. Everything feels planned so last minute and it was like he started pulling topics out fo thin air. You can't get a clear explanation out of him and he makes so many unnecessary passive aggressive comments!! I can't stress this enough, avoid this man at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is a nice and respected person but he lacks the academic initiative to teach sophomores a class he recently learned in the summer. He used a whiteboard for a classroom that fits 100+ students which was inefficient. His tests were a lot more difficult than the homework, & you had to heavily rely on external sources to do good in class.

This class heavily relies on the lectures, but he is a terrible lecturer that makes many mistakes and is very unclear. He is bad at convey information and uses a whiteboard. His office hours are unhelpful and he was rude/condescending in office hours and during class. The tests are an inaccurate assessment of your knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Dr. Bush's first semester teaching. You could tell. Additionally, he had no prior experience with circuits. The combo produced a mismanaged, disorganized, and overall unfruitful learning environment. If you want to succeed in this class, you must teach yourself. First midterm average was a 50, and he told the class we had to figure it out.

He expected class participation yet was rude to students who didn't answer exactly correctly. He was also weird about using computers and will give you a very hard time if you are even slightly late to class. There are only 4 assignments and they're graded very strictly. The material is interesting but do not take his class if you can help it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very harsh grader. Extremely short tempered, often rude, and does not give students space to learn. Grades on the assumption that every student knows the same amount of knowledge as him. Often talks over students as well. This is very unfortunate as the course material was extremely interesting.

The topics discussed in this class were interesting, and I even enjoyed some of the assignments. However, Dr. Cobb is the most disrespectful and condescending professor I've had at UT. A good part of the grade is participation, but he makes it almost impossible to participate as he belittles you and your opinions.

Took it last fall, and thermo is a pretty harsh class, but Prof Rodriguez teaches the concepts very well, and his TAs were pretty approachable. The grading wasn't too punishing, and I was able to reach a B despite thinking I was barely gonna pass. Oh, also, he likes to bring snacks to every lecture, so that was pretty cool of him to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: It was Rodriguez's first time teaching this course, and I really appreciated his willingness to work with students to make the class a smoother ride. Thermo is a difficult class, but he provided many opportunities for extra credit and always asked for feedback. His lectures were engaging, and I enjoyed his class.

Dr. Rodriguez is great, and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Thermo is naturally a difficult class, but he definitely made it easier through his effort and availability. Weekly quizzes are based on one hw problem from the additional set, and make sure to use the ASME test bank to study for tests, as problems are often recycled.

It's Thermo; it will be difficult. However, Rodriguez is caring and communicative enough to lighten the mental load. We used an online textbook (ZyBooks) with participation (watch a few animations) and challenge (homework problems) activities built in. Study for weekly quizzes, cram for tests, and rest assured Rodriguez is there to help out.
Dr. Rodriguez had the most organized Canvas page I have ever seen, and he makes expectations very clear. Super kind and approachable- would highly recommend for 318M

Nice professor, and it is helpful that he is an editor for the textbook being taught. Weekly assignments are super easy, and the lab quizzes can be challenging. Tests were not bad and the final was take-home (he might get rid of this though). I did not like the class material, but it was easy enough to get good grades and lectures were recorded.

Dr. Rodriguez is a phenomenal professor! Was always there to help out if you needed, lectures are straightforward and helpful, first exam and final were online. Textbook is $90 and all "homeworks" are through it, but this class was a de-stresser
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Ok class. He's a really nice professor. You need to pay 90 usd for his online textbook to do homework. Super tough but fair grader. DO NOT let your guard down for the numerical methods parts. And don't turn in your stuff late cos he will take heavy heavy points off. He's one of those prof that let your nerves relax but relentlessly unforgiving.

explains matlab well but an extremely boring imo; class is easy with 20% of grade being easy zybook assignments; lab quizzes aren't bad if you get code from others; take-home midterm and in-person midterm - both easy to do well on. final take home and easy if you just pay attention to lectures. would recommend bc hes an easy A with little effort.

really nice guy and an amazing professor! it is super easy to get a good grade in this class while also learning the course material. we had weekly quizzes but they were really easy to study for and the weekly homework was super quick and easy (and actually helped me learn). he also brings snacks to class (coffee, cookies, candy, etc.) LOVE HIM!!

Rodriguez cares a lot about his students, and he's great at providing resources and is a lenient grader. 2023 was his first year teaching as a professor, so there were some issues with class pacing and materials covered during lecture. That didn't detract from how helpful he is, and I learned a lot from his class :)

His extra credit carried a lot of people to an A. Midterms weren't always graded the same across TAs, which sucks. He does give you food and is very available outside class. But lectures do NOT engage at all and he will be too nice to the point that he doesn't cover the content he needs to cover because he's answering questions. Overall, maybe 6/10
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly he would get a 1 if he wasn't so nice and didn't offer extra credit. Lectures were dull and not engaging, he would take an hour to get through a single problem. Homework was short but very hard. This class didn't teach me anything new, I'd recommend taking someone else. I would've gotten a B without the extra credit.

I would highly recommend! As long as you do the readings and homework, Dr. Rodriguez does his best to keep his students on track and cares very strongly for his students. Overall the positivity of his class helps your motivation as a student strongly. There is also extra credit available, but again his course is super easy to stay on track in!

Professor Rodriguez has got to be the most understanding and caring professor at UT. Not only that, but he is also a great lecturer and told us he likes to teach the way he wished he had been taught, and it shows. He is a very fair and understanding professor and tries to give as much partial credit as possible on exams and quizzes.

Dr. Rodriguez was a great professor. His lectures are taught in a modern way that helps you understand the topic. He grades the exams and quizzes based on the procedure rather than getting the correct solution, so you can get a lot of credit. He also provides a decent amount of extra credit. Overall, he deeply cares for his students. Take him!

Adriana is a wonderful teacher. It's impressive to see someone so young balance dual majors while demonstrating such maturity and intuition when working with children. She brings both professionalism and warmth to her teaching, creating a positive and engaging environment for her students. For the kids classroom felt like a room full of friends.

I had the opportunity to take private lessons with Adriana, and she is an incredibly patient, organized, and thoughtful teacher. She approaches each lesson with creativity and is able to adapt her teaching to meet students where they are, which makes the learning process both comfortable and motivating.

Adriana's enthusiasm for teaching truly stands out. She sets high expectations in a way that is encouraging rather than forceful, creating an environment where students feel motivated to grow. She allows young students to discover music for themselves, helping them develop discipline and autonomy at such a young age. Thank you for this experience!

Dr. Adut is kind, approachable, and a very skilled lecturer. Attendance isn't mandatory BUT coming to class helps a ton, especially if you do not do the readings. Three tests count for 100% of your grade but they are straightforward.This class is a breeze as long as you pay attention, take notes, and go to the review sessions.

This class was probably the easiest class I have taken in university, although it can be boring at times. Dr. Adut is a very kind person, so the class felt very relaxed. I would definitely take again.
This was a really engaging course! You do not have to buy the book, I just showed up to class and the review session and was good to go for the tests:)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You don't really have to go to class. You can show up to the review, memorize it, and still do well. I went to class because I like his lecture style. He is entertaining, funny, and actually makes the lecture material very interesting. Would definitely take another class with him.

Dr. Adut was a great professor and lecturer, wanting his students to constantly participate. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you skip class you will miss all of the information on the exams. Don't bother buying the books, I never needed to read them because Dr. Adut was so good at explaining the information. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Adut is very knowledgable/passionate about what he teaches. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you show up and take good notes then you will do quite well on his tests. The course was made up of 3 written exams, no final.

Dr. Adut was wonderful. Very knowledgeable and made the lectures really interesting. Just make sure you go to class, pay attention to the lectures, and take good notes. And also go to the reviews: they'll help you know what to focus on for exams. If you do these things, you'll be fine. 10/10 would take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Adut was good. Class lectures were interesting and fairly well organized. Go to the reviews before each of the exams, which the TA goes over exactly what will be on them. Your grade depends on your TA so its important to know what they want. Go to class, take notes and you should pass no problem.

Honestly, I don't advocate skipping class but if you were to only show up to the review and memorized it, you'd pass with a B. No joke. Don't bother buying the book, NEVER miss review day, but don't buy the book.

Solid professor. No PowerPoints, class is all discussion. 3 tests, short-answer. Reviews really help you prepare for the tests. Tests are not tricky, if you know the material you will do well. Overall interesting class and he makes good points. He encourages student participation in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall this is a good professor. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow, but the reviews before the exams help a whole lot. Not a bad class or professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clulow is an excellent lecturer and professor. This course is graded by quite a few components which can pile up fast if you're not prepared. You have 3 free absences throughout the semester, and Dr. Clulow is readily available to work with students on extensions, extra credit, etc. Highly recommend for an overview of Japanese martial history.

Professor Clulow is an amazing professor who obviously cares a lot about the material he teaches. His lectures are engaging, funny, and in-depth. Most readings he makes accessible through Canvas. The course is thought-provoking and interesting, and Prof Clulow makes every effort to make sure his students understand the material.

Loved this class! An exciting approach to a history class with many clear connections drawn between the events of the distant past and present. I swear I think about something I learned in this class at least once a week. Just remember to stay on top of your independent research project because the due dates will sneak up on you.
Dr. Clulow is very knowledgeable in his field and passionate about the topics he teaches, which makes his lectures very interesting. He was also very personable and easy to reach outside of class.
He is an awesome person and an amazing lecturer. He really cares about his students and will almost always give you an extension. The class is super interesting and the projects are fun to do.

Clulow is a great teacher and you can tell he loves what he teaches, he's super kind and almost always gives an extension if you reach out to him. Assignments were not too hard as long as you show effort you should get 80s and above. You only really need the lectures for the mid-term, everything else is accessible via online information. Cool Class

I took Age of the Samurai, and it's my favorite class I've taken so far. Professor Clulow was really nice and had really engaging lectures. There weren't a lot of assignments, but there were enough that one bad grade wouldn't ruin your average.

Clulow is my favorite professor ever. He's engaging, passionate, articulate, considerate etc. I never felt bored during his lectures. The class does require some work but he's very nice; don't slack off, but don't over-stress either. He ties current events to history to invite critical thinking, and I left a changed man. Seriously.

I really enjoyed Dr. Clulow's class, he is very engaging and kind. The Tests are reasonable and essay response. He also has quizzes that are pretty easy. He gives you the questions that will be on the test so just study and you should be fine.

Dr. Clulow was one of my favorite professors ever. He is super knowledgable, passionate and engaging. His lectures are fun and easy to get engaged with via watching clips, listening to songs, and tying in pop-culture. He responds to emails super quickly and if you can't make office hours he will work with you. A lot of readings, but not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clulow is such a funny, intelligent man! The class itself is very interesting. He combines a lot of modern culture and integrates it with his class. For example, when discussing samurai, he will pull up a modern day video game and compare. It's really funny and super interesting. He is also a really nice man! I highly recommend him.
Disappointing how ineffective his lectures are for an online class. He is clearly very knowledgeable and smart, but poorly communicates ideas in an easy to understand manner.

Regarding the Master's class for Machine Learning, he does not even reply to my direct emails and instead I get a reply weeks later from the Staff. Would avoid taking his class, I didn't feel like he cared about my learning outcomes.

The lectures are all pre-recorded and are pretty dense, but you can watch them on your own time. Homeworks (4 total) are interesting/difficult-ish but easily graded, midterm was easy to get 100 if you take good notes. I learned a lot, but the final was way harder than anything else in the class. Brought my grade down from a 100 to a B.

Using the old-school blackboard approach for online lectures is a little ineffective and sometimes becomes downright painful with multi-step derivations and such. But I'll put that to being new to a medium that is also very new. He's a pretty solid lecturer otherwise.
I liked Kivans' humor and I loved his hair even more. His tests are often easier than the homework and the TA's do their best to get you to understand the material.

He literally read Captain Underpants in class. His humor is either you love it or hate it, and I definitely found it one of the best aspects of the course. Tests were open notes, and for his discrete math class, it's similar to a high school physics course in that you are given the formulas/proofs and all you had to do is know which one to use.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Klivans was the most unorganized professor I ever took. His Quest modules don't fully fit his class material. Tests are hard. His notes are unclear. Whole semester you'd think you are getting a good grade in Canvas but the final grade would be completely different. I would never take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Flipped Classroom. His online videos were actually really good, but his practice problems in class were generally too difficult. First two exams were really easy, but the 3rd was much more difficult to balance it. He isn't great at answering questions. Also, not much feedback on tests/quizzes. Overall, solid class and I feel like I learned a lot.

During the lecture he does practice problems for you but they are often more complicated than the videos you watch before. Homeworks are graded really leniently but each TA grades different so it's a coin flip on midterms. All tests and pop quizzes are open notes which gives him the excuse to give more difficult problems. Class is curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Klivans! He focuses on the big picture, so tests and homework are about learning to think. It's an easy class, but don't slack! Show up and pay attention! Two tips: if you have a question, ask the person next to you first. Dr. Klivans can be brutal, and you don't want to ask a stupid question. Tip two: extra credit!

Grades weren't weighted correctly on canvas, so you never know truly where you stand in the class. 3 midterms no final for us. Grading is very arbitrary on the midterms and each TA/Klivans grade very differently. Expects you to be very smart & felt like he was constantly disappointed in our classes.

Klivans uses flipped classroom so you will have to walk into class having watched his videos. However, the videos are old and go over the bare minimum of the concept and in no way prepare you for the depth that he goes into. As for exams, the exams can oscillate between hellish and stupidly simple; its just luck of the draw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is okay, tests are manageable, homeworks are graded easily, makes us buy quest, kinda funny sometimes and he reminds me of a divorced dad. Explanations are 50/50.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: CS391L - Machine Learning class for online MSCS. His lectures are disorganized; skips over fundamentals; uses non-standard terminology and notation; fails to explain concepts discretely. Gave us review questions for the first exam, but none really related. Felt like a waste of time and did poorly cause the exam was nothing like hmk or review.

I should have just said this to Klivans during class, but if you're going to have a linear algebra/probability heavy lecture, you should give the students a heads-up. Also, instead of saying ""You're not gonna learn this anywhere else better," it would be more helpful to point us to other resources (b/c he's very bad at explaining stuff).

I don't have much love discrete math but Klivans himself is a pretty interesting individual. Lectures are ok. There are 3 pop quizzes. You can use your notes on all quizzes and tests. Sometimes he/TAs will explain concepts really quickly, so you'll just have to keep asking questions until you get it. Curve is based on the class- we didn't get one.

CS311 with Klivans is a flipped course, meaning you watch lectures via videos on your own time before class. In class, he goes over some interesting practice problems. His class doesn't have a lot of direction, and the tests don't represent an breakdown of the material given in class, mostly whatever Klivans felt like testing us on.
Smart research professor, but hates teaching 311, and it shows. Go to your TA office hours, and you'll do fine.
Pretty cool dude, lectures are pretty lively and interesting. Homeworks are a million times harder than the tests, but the solutions are usually online, and they prepare you to do well on tests.

Great professor. His lectures are not required, but he does have occasional pop quizzes in them so beware. If you do show up to lecture, he goes over some interesting proofs and techniques that you should know for the exams. His HW is much harder than the exams so don't stress about exams. Both HW and exams graded by TA's who are fair graders.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good professor overall. Will assign very interesting work, and it is graded reasonably. The class is also slightly curved, so it isn't too hard. He is quite sarcastic when people ask questions, so that might throw off a few students.

Prof Klivans is an excellent teacher. Material is learned online by videos he made, then problems are done in class. What made the class tricky is that HW and tests are graded by TA's, who were pretty strict with their grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: There are at least 6 or so TAs and it still takes around 2-3 weeks for a grade to be submitted. Grading in this class is harsh as hell.

I do not recommend this class. The grading is really tough and it is sorta difficult to ask questions and get a good response. Most of the material on homeworks and exams were never touched on in class. For a class that was supposed to not be so bad, it was my hardest class

Klivans was a great professor who  knew what he was doing, even though he sometimes got confused by his own material in lectures - I think this is somewhat cause of a lack of preparedness tot each at times. Class wasn't too hard or too easy, and he curved it a bit at the end which took me from A- to A. Overall, great experience, learned a lot

I don't get what the other people in the comments are saying. If you take this class with him YOU ARE GOING TO LEARN A LOT. The class is also curved so you can definitely get "A" if you work. It's not a class you can pass by skipping classes, but I had a fun semester.

Klivans is brilliant and he knows his stuff, but he's not the best at explaining concepts. He records lectures and assigns them as hw before every class. In class, you do absurdly challenging practice problems. Tests and homeworks are VERY difficult. The greatest thing about this class though: he's a very lenient grader and it's curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Klivans is probably one of the best 311 professors. His field is theory and it shows. The classroom is flipped and you watch quest videos before class. If you don't come to lecture expect to fail the test. He's smart and knows what he's talking about. The homeworks can be hard but the tests are usually nothing like that. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's pretty awesome!
Terrible, don't take him.

Klivans is definitely one of the more difficult 313 professors although he curves the grades at the end. He will be sarcastic if you ask a question, although he does try to make sure you understand. It is a flipped class so lectures are online, problems worked in class. Also gives pop quizzes in class.

Tons of proofs in class.  He follows very logical presentations (it's LOGIC Sets and Functions, after all) and wants them to be clear to people.  Isn't always great about restating/rephrasing if you don't get it the first time, but is helpful and wants the students to learn.  Very interesting class and easy-going guy.
so unorganized that the department had to transfer her to intro anthropology for the fall.

I had her for a different class than the one I had listed here. But the points still remains that she is not really capable of teaching and has a huge ego and I guess the department is making her teach some other classes for the fall.
Beware any class she teaches, she's not good at this and it isnt worth the stress i'm enduring with her. She's teaching other classes this fall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very slow to grade things with very minimal feedback
The reviews check out, unfortunately I didn't check before taking her.

had her for INB-337. All she does is read off the slides, no emotion, no care, nothing interesting in teaching style. She's showed up late to her own class so many times. As of right now she's been late more than on time. Class is boring and she's intentionally vague on assignments.
literally marked me absent EVEN THOUGH I WAS IN CLASS. man she for the love of god can't do her job
Very hard to follow.

NEVER take this class or anything with this teacher. She does not know what she's doing and will make you stress over the class until the last-minute. Not sure why there are random positive reviews here.

This was definitely one of the harder anthropology classes, especially bc I had no genetics background. She lectures very quickly, & I got points off for unimportant stuff, but she's knowledgeable. You can tell she cares more about her research than teaching. Admirable professor but not an easy class - check prior syllabi before registering.
I hated Anthropology after her
Teaching is clearly farrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr from her strong suit.

I liked anthropology.... until her....
I really did try to like her class but she made it downright awful. Now I dislike her class and the topic altogether. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: no, just no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: There's better options for sure
Normally I don't write reviews but she was so bad that I had to let others know that if she's teaching then you should stay away.

Lots of reading (~2 scientific papers by the start of each class). Lectures were often too fast to make time for class discussion and student lectures which were unproductive in my opinion. Very disorganized, most assignments had no rubric or clear guidelines and instructions would be changed at the last minute. Was hard to discern what she wanted.
She doesn't know how to teach or really what she's doing
She doesn't do much and doesn't give much information. This class, in her words, is supposed to be easy but she intentionally makes it more difficult.
She doesn't give any rubric, just throws you into the water and expects you to figure it out. Avoid this class if you can
Prof Childebayeva wants you to succeed, just show up to lectures and work with the TA.

The courseload was very heavy, office hours were often cancelled. Had to read 2 scientific research papers and a textbook chapter by every class, had a 5,000-word research paper due at end of the semester and 2 exams worth 30% of the grade. Found it hard to keep up with slides in lecture due to the speed of her lectures and lack of explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unorganized schedule that we were behind on Homework. Overall, she posted assignments late as well as exams her format did not help in studying. READ the textbook and take good notes on her class. Late on grading as well, and quizzes every day so try not to miss her class as much as possible cause those points will save you. Choose Wisely

One of my favorite teachers. She is super sweet and makes class fun. Homework and quizzes every day, but it's manageable. She forgets to upload things sometimes, but nothing that can't be found on the JOSHU website. She's good at getting you to practice speaking and repetition in class, so you retain quite a lot. Really good for starting Japanese.

Aida-sensei is a very sweet professor who is kind and caring and puts a lot of thought and effort into her lectures and assignments. There are quizzes and homework essentially everyday, so beware of skipping multiple classes. That being said, there are dropped quizzes, extra credit opportunities, and a fairly lenient grading system.

I can see why she has so many good reviews because at heart, she is such a nice and caring person. However, I found her lecture pacing incredibly slow, especially in the first half of the semester. At times it felt like "Okay let's move on, but we'd spend too much time on the SAME thing. She also tends to keep class over the allotted time.

Aida-sensei has a genuine passion for teaching, & it's evident. Her lectures are very informative, & she's very open to questions/discussions over content. Quizzes & HW every day, but that's with every JPN class. Super kind person as well; she gave me the courage to pursue a Japanese double major. Can't recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Extremely kind and genuinely wants to help you learn Japanese. The course load is what you expect for any language learning class; lots of homework, quizzes, and exams. Still, this was one of the funnest classes I've ever taken and that was due to how great Aida-sensei is as a person and a lecturer.
awesome professor in all ways, always avaiable for help either at her office hour or by emails.

Aida-sensei genuinely cares about her students, and their learning. Additionally, she presents material in a clear, easy to understand manner, and encourages active participation to learn the language. An added bonus: she is incredibly energetic and her class is fun to attend.
Really nice teacher. A lot of homework and daily quizzes, but the class was still great. I would definitely take a class with her again.
She was one of the best language professors I have ever had. Awesome teacher!!
Great prof. fun and easy!
You will LOVE her. I have nothing bad to say whatsoever. The Best!
seriously the best japanese teacher at UT

Professor Hosemann is an excellent teacher, and is the type of person who values each and every one of her students and their ideas. The class is very interesting and is not difficult. There is a lot of reading, but you can get by with doing about half of it, in all honesty. All in all, amazing professor and a truly great experience in her class!

The class is super easy and interesting. No final, just a book report, so a lot of people stopped going to class after the midterm. I went to every lecture though because they were honestly fun. Discussions were kind of a waste of time but attendance is mandatory. No text book but a few cool, short books are assigned, as well as journal readings.

I'm a business major, but I really enjoyed this class! One in class test, one take home test, and one essay. 2-3 readings per every 2/3 weeks, so a very manageable amount of work. The lectures are super interesting and it's an easy A if you do the readings, go to class, and look over your notes before the tests. Hosemann rocks! Highly recommend.

There is a lot of reading, but you review everything in class so you can get by without reading.  There is only one test and it's easy. The class is very interesting and thought provoking. The professor is very friendly, open, and humorous. It's a fun class. Discussion group attendance is mandatory, but class attendance is not.

Extremely easy class. She is a very engaging professor. You really don't need to show up for lecture after the midterm. Discussion sections: go to them. If you go to lecture, no attendance, it'll be a very interesting discussion, but I didn't find them extremely helpful after the midterm. No final exam! Only a book report, so as long as you read...

Her lectures are engaging and interesting. Required reading passages are short, easy reads. She goes over all of them in detail and expects three "I statement" journals throughout the semester which she leaves feedback on. Also, one semi-short essay over a book about Walmart. NO harsh grading. Very kind and values all opinons. Easy A!

She is DEF one of the best professors at UT! I loved her class, if I wasn't a Sr., I'd probably switch to Anthro. She really cares about what students think and assignments are "discussions" with her on paper, which she responds to via Canvas! Not to mention EVERY lecture is interesting. Even if you wouldn't normally think its an interesting topic.

It was a summer course, so it was a little more compacted, but still great. There were only 3 "journal entries" which are written in third person. She wants to hear what you think ALWAYS. In lecture and on paper. She was a seriously great lecturer and sincerely cares about her students. I could tell she LOVES her job. I am so glad I took the class.

Professor Hosemann is a pro! She is a super smart, well cultured professor. Everything is fair game in lectures, this course is really entertaining because you get to explore so many things that are otherwise taboo. Really glad I took this class, it almost makes me want to be an anthropology major.

Easiest class I've ever taken, I have a 98. It's a really interesting class, but she is a really easy grader. I definitely recommended as the social and behavioral science. It's a great gpa booster, she lets you take the quizzes over again until you get an A. Her midterm is easy if you go to class the week before and the final is take-home.
Professor Hosemann is a great professor to have. She's very interested and knowledgable about anthropology and does not grade harshly.

Professor Mana was an excellent teacher and is clearly knowledgeable and cares about the things she teaches. I took her class about the BG with her and learned a lot. Grading was easy as long as you actually take the time to read the instructions and meet the clear requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly such a sweet and informative professor. There's a lot of reading, but you could get away by just skimming through them. She's also very accommodating as long as you communicate with her! I had no real knowledge about Hinduism, but it's very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (I took ANS379 Translating Asia. I'm not sure why there isn't an option.) Mana is truly a student-centered teacher, always willing to help, really cares about her students, and listens to their concerns. One thing to be aware of is that her course requires a significant amount of reading. Her grading is very nice, rarely loses points.

Pretty easy class, however for a non-hindu may be confusing. professor is very friendly and always willing to help. Her understanding of Hinduism and its philosophies/beliefs is a little off. So if you are a hindu you may be confused or even heavily disagree with her approach to some gods. Overall she is very kind and I enjoyed this course
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Mana for South Asian gods and goddesses....her class is an easy A. I never even did the readings when I was taking this class (I was born and raised Hindu) but for someone who wasn't it may be more difficult...she assigns bunch of readings in class. She often also rambles on during class as well but overall this class was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed taking this class. Mana always made an effort to allow students to take control of their learning, and made the environment very comfortable for her students. I really enjoyed coming to lectures and always looked forward to hearing our in class discussions. She is a professor, I truly recommend to take if you have the chance.

Professor Mana is very kind and is passionate about Hinduism. However, if you were born and raised Hindu and have a good grasp of the teachings, you may not want to take this class- unless you're interested in fundamentals. Professor Mana does not seem to have a proper grasp of the meaning behind Hindu texts, and her opinions can be incorrect.

She's lowk rude sometimes and I swear she goes over the easiest examples in class and then the exams/homeworks are way, way harder. She confronted the class after the MEDIAN on MT2 was a 57 and told us to study harder… lol just admit you're not a good prof it's fine. It's fine tho, she gave us 0.5% extra credit at the end of the semester, how kind

Idek if she could get a A on her own tests. Other professors make midterms more conceptual but she spams math questions. puts questions on the test that she hasn't taught the class how to work. We're supposed to learn to solve the questions thru the HW –> the crazy hard test questions aren't covered there. dont take her if you value your gpa/time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's slow. During tests she has the most ludicrous method of passing out the exams. Wastes 20 minutes just doing this. She'll get annoyed for anything. A student accidentally shifted some tests while grabbing his and got called out. Her accent makes it hard to hear some words she says + she has no patience for people who mess up her instructions.

tests gets successively more difficult. Test averages are in the 50s, and she blames the students and says “physics is difficult”. Some of the test material, besides problems recycled from HW, were NEVER covered. Covering a simple concept doesn't mean students actually learn well. she's nice but lecture doesn't help at all…
