I loved the energy she brought to each lecture and the way she simplified concepts while making it more interesting than a normal lecture. She could organize her course better. Quest questions are very hard compared to what she teaches. If she gave resources on how to relate calc to physics, more EC, or easier exam questions, she'd be the goat.

MIGHT be the worst class I've taken at UT. I've heard other physics professors give way more leeway and extra credit. She also doesn't curve any exams even though they hav below failing averages. Provides not many resources to understand how to solve problems. There's discussion but obviously you won't get help on every question. buns prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst physics professor at UT. Doesn't matter how nice or passionate she is if she can't teach the course at the level she expects students to perform. Showed exam scores for MT2 during one lecture and blamed STUDENTS for how poor the scores were. If Some students do bad it's their fault, but if the whole class does bad it's the PROFESSORS fault.

If you took physics in high school, you'll probably be ok, but Torabi's teaching style is too simplistic for the difficulty level of the homework and exam questions, especially if you are learning from "scratch." Exam averages were failing 2/3 midterms and there is no curve. Torabi herself is very sweet, but avoid this class if possible.

Tests 2 and 3 are very difficult and do not get curved. She is a nice person, but her lectures do not help at all. Just by word of mouth, Torabi seems more difficult than other physics classes (because of no curve)

Dr. Torabi is very sweet, but you won't learn much from the lectures. The way she explains problems is nothing like how Quest explains it, so you often end up confused on how to get from point A to point B. Exams are super application-heavy and have “zombie questions” that are pretty tough. Her grading scale is super good though.

Her lectures are simple, but the homework feels like it's from a completely different class. I could never solve half of it because she never teaches at that difficulty. The exams are even harder than the homework and tougher than any other physics prof. She also randomly yells or drops things in class, which is more scary than helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Calc-based physics is a hard class and torabi does a good job of breaking down concepts to be more simple. However, she makes them TOO simple. Tests and HW questions surrounding said concepts become much more complex. students who can't learn from a textbook will need extra help and put it extra time. She needs to curve tests or give more EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she's so obviously passionate about physics and would help every single student if she could, and that makes this class bearable. she really does try to make lectures engaging, which is nice. physics is hard and it feels like her lecture examples don't get as complex as they should, focus on quest questions for exams and go to office hours often.

Good reviews on here will just say she's nice –> she is but she's a terrible lecturer. Shows simple applications of concepts in lecture but on exams and HWs tests on very complex applications of concepts. 1% EC but that's if you show up to all lectures and do 12 extra HW assignments (all with over 15 questions). No curves on exams w/ an avg of 60!

Dr. Torabi is a very respectable figure and a fantastic lecturer. She's very knowledgeable about the subject and is ready to help with any questions. She takes the course at a steady pace and is very understanding of concerns regarding the course. As someone who has never enjoyed physics that much, she made physics very enjoyable.

The only way to succeed is by reading the textbook and drilling practice problems. Torabi is a bad lecturer and goes over simple applications of the content, but u're expected to do much harder questions on exams. Only good thing is that she weighs HW heavily and provides EC 1.5%. I wish I stopped attending class earlier. She tries though

She's very nice and funny and tries to make lectures engaging and interesting. Lectures were much simpler than homeworks/exams, and I often felt lost because the class notes didn't help me much. Her grading scale is lenient and there is extra credit, but the disconnect between class content and exams made it challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is very nice but gives little to no guidance on how to solve problems. She tells you to read the textbook and do HW but if you get stuck ur lowk cooked. In lecture she'll put up problems and just pop up the solution without much context. Test avgs are 50 and she doesn't curve (kinda insane). EC is 1%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Midway through the semester, I stopped going to lectures and began reading the assigned textbook chapter and making sure I understood every single quest problem (I was at sangers drop in for hours every week). Exam averages are low, and the exams are not like the homework.

Dr. Torabi is a very nice person. She cares about the students and is funny. Homeworks were kinda hard, but helpful to understand for exams. I went to drop in tutoring and that really helped me get through the semester. Regardless, she is a good option for this class. Put in effort outside of class, and an A is not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Torabi is really sweet and patient with the whole class. She really tries to make physics fun, even if it's 8 in the morning lol. If you go to lectures and try on the HW, you should be fine! She has REALLY late discussions... like 9-10 pm. If you're nervous about walking at night, make sure to plan ahead or choose another class!!!

I took AP Physics in hs so I really enjoyed this class. However, without any background it is pretty challenging because lecture material tends to be simpler than HW and exams. Class averages are usually in the 60s but if you figure out the HW you should be ok. There are drops and extra credit which is very helpful and overall a very doable class.

torabi needs to realize that pre-med students are not passionate about physics and can't spend hours a day studying for her class. homeworks and exams become increasingly harder; extra credit is helpful but not enough. a nightmare if u didnt take ap physics. class avg was failing for 2/3 midterms and final avg was a 56. take this as a warning

If you took AP physics and did well, you will likely excel in this class. However, if you did not, this class might be very challenging for the exams. Torabi is great at nailing the general idea but you have to thoroughly understand it to apply to exam questions. Learn the most common Quest question types and study the 'zombie' questions

Dr. Torabi is a very nice person and wants you to succeed however she did not teach in necessary detail to understand concepts fully and do well on exams. Exams were very hard and only through homeworks and extra credit I was able to get an A. Go to her office hours if possible. Take another professor if possible!

She is not very kind, and does not seem to want to really help her students. Rather she is upset for asking qs, and lectures you on otherwise. Every exam was easy, however the final exam was significantly more difficult than any homework or exam that was provided. Take someone else if you can, it's quite hard to keep up with her method of teaching.

Physics is hard but Dr. Torabi is very caring and her lectures are sometimes interesting. The midterms are NOT similar to the hw questions, you really have to understand the materials to do well. HWs and 3 midterms are both worth 35% (1 drop) 3% of EC. 90 and above is A. My average for 2 midterms was a 75 and ended with A-.
You really gotta work hard!

Lectures often engaging, but most importantly are optional/extra credit. Very manageable class with forgiving policies. As with both engineering physics, be prepared for painfully scheduled discussion sections that do not provide meaningful value -- even when the TA tries to be engaged
If the majority of her class fails on exams perhaps the issue is not the students.

Let me just preface this by saying that as a professor, Dr. Torabi is pretty nice. However the biggest problem with her class is that the exams are designed for you to fail because they are completely different from all the HW problems we get and are significantly harder. Honestly just take someone else if you can.
Very hard!!!  I literally got a like a 58 on first test

Dr. Torabi was the best physics professor I have ever had! Although the content was really tough for a summer class, reaching out to her helped me a lot. Dr. Torabi is a little intimidating at first, but is extremely kind and wants you to succeed. Don't be afraid to go up to her and ask her questions! Exams are most similar to lecture slides
The best professor I've had. She is super caring. Put the work in an you'll get an A

She's nice and definitely cares for your learning, gave 4% extra credit which helped a lot; exams could be kind of tricky and included topics she barely went over in class (heavy emphasis on conceptual); 3 Midterms worth 35% (1 drop), 10 HWs 35% (3 drop), and Final 30%; helpful in OHs and responds to emails; study lecture and HW questions for exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very generous with extra credit opportunities and "zombie" questions. Getting an A in this class is definitely achievable, but you really need to be on top of your game with hwks - it is very easy to fall behind. Taking physics II over the summer is not easy, and the class is extremely accelerated, so prepare yourself.

Don't procrastinate her hw!! I did and it cost me a lot of time. When studying, stick to the hw, there are a lot of questions from it on the test. If you maintain a high average on your hws you can afford to fail a test or two because your hw and exams are weighted the same. Take advantage of the extra credit AND go to ur discussions!

Dr. Torabi is a great professor to take, if you're able to take her, definitely do. All exams will have zombie problems from the previous exams which should be free points. Homeworks are every week, don't procrastinate them, they take a very long time to do. Exams and homework are weighted about the same so make sure to do them.

Torabi is an amazing professor! HWs were given every week/two weeks, but they were mostly easy. Tests were very similar to the HW and they contained zombie problems. She was also very generous with the extra credit. All in all it was a really easy class! Only downside were the extremely late discussion sections.

so many extra credit opportunities!! tests are very similar to homework (quest) and there are a few zombie questions. discussions are mandatory but pointless. one of three midterms is dropped, and final is very easy- broken down into the units and where the questions were coming from. she's very passionate about physics and wants you to do well!

She is an amazing professor, one of the best, TAKE HER!! Her discussion sessions are mandatory. She gives so much extra credit and opportunities to succeed. She uses questions from homework and zombie questions on the exams. She is caring and loves what she does. I was terrified to take physics but she made it an easy transition.

PHY 302L over the summer was great with Torabi. She is very kind and has a clear structure. As long as you do the homeworks and practices, you'll be good for the exams. She also takes 3 questions from the previous exams & puts them on the following ones so you're guaranteed to get those right. Final was also mainly questions from past exams & HWs.

One of the nicest professors I have ever had! Clear grading policy and lots of extra credit. Always had a smile on her face and you can tell she is passionate about physics and wants you to understand what is expected. If you can understand the homework problems and pay attention to the examples in lecture, exams will be a piece of cake.

Calculus-based physics is hard, but Dr. Torabi made it approachable and gave so many real-life examples to make it easier to understand. She gave extra credit opportunities and worked through many homework problems and examples in class along with extensively reviewing concepts. Her exams were reasonable, and she did reviews in class. TAKE HER!
Easy class. Only need a 90 for an A, 85 for an A-, et cetera. Can bring handwritten notes to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best prof I have had at UT! She is super knowledgeable and enjoys what she does. She also listened to our feedback and made the class doable for sure. She gives interesting lectures and the exams are like the homework. Definitely take the time to take this class and get to know the professor! :)

Exams in this class are based off her homework and her Quest homework's are worth 30% of your grade. As long as you understand the homework and attend discussion sections, you should do fine in this class. Her final exam was pretty difficult though and makes up 30% of your grade
Dr. Torabi is very understanding of students. I had no physics background from high school but she made it possible to still succeed in the class. I would highly recommend taking her.
She designed the course so that the students would succeed. There is honestly no reason anyone should get below a 90 in this course!

Torabi is little difficult to pay attention to, so I recommend going in person. Biggest recommendation is to the read and take notes on the textbook section before the lectures! Overall, she's really nice and very accommodating. Would recommend if you can also dedicate some time to the textbook.

Aida is probably the best professor in physics at UT. The class is very clear and was a breeze. She cares about her students and her youthfulness makes physics fun. I would recommended signing up for her if you have the option.

By far my favorite class I've taken. Half the grade is participation and the tests are heavily curved. If you show up and participate you are almost guaranteed an A. He's extremely smart and has great real world experiences, and he really cares about his students. No better class to learn about what is going on in markets AND how to talk about them

Professor Kanojia is an excellent lecturer. His capital markets course is one of the most useful that I have taken at McCombs in terms of real-world relevance. I highly recommend taking this class for an elective.

Great professor and lectures, sensible content to address markets from different perspective (and each week has a market lecture too). Exams aren't too hard, it's like 2/3 general understanding from lectures and readings and then 1/3 hard/nitpicky questions "to make a curve." If you listen in class, a day's studying probably enough.

Great class to learn about markets and keep up to date. There are 2 exams that are pretty difficult but the class gets curved to a 3.6 anyways so it doesn't matter as long as you get within the average (~65). His class emphasizes participation so show up and try to contribute as much as possible its worth 30% of your grade. Overall, great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Akash is an excellent professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter. If you really want to learn about markets, you'll absolutely love this course. The tests are tough, but the class is heavily curved. He's one of my favorite professors I've had at McCombs. Just show up, participate, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN
Great Professor. Test are very difficult, but if you attend you will receive a good grade. Honestly, this was the best class I had while at UT.

This is a fantastic class to get an in-depth understanding of markets. This is completely an open discussion class, but Akash does a great job of explaining everything in a fun and detailed way. There are two exams which are difficult, but the class gets curved anyways. Highly recommend taking this class and getting to know Akash!

Phenomenal professor who cares for students. You really need to participate but he makes it fun. Basically nobody does the readings but exams (all MC) ask questions about it. Very open to meeting students. My favorite class at UT and it's not close.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite class and professor at UT. Class is discussion based and just feels like a casual conversation about the market. Only two exams.

Exams are long MC with references to specific readings and lectures, so you have to attend class. I found each lecture pretty interesting, but it's a hit or miss if it correlates with the exam. He's passionate about markets and has a high-level background. Wants you to actually learn the material. Overall, be sure to participate early and read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Direct and likes to talk about markets a lot (interested in interest rates, MBS, and regulations). However, the rigor of the class does not match the rigor of exams. 75 T/F with specific answers on readings and concepts. Average exam = 65 and apathetic to it. Only take if course appeals, but A unlikely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard tests but curved to 3.6. If you want to learn about capital markets Akash is the best professor on campus. Mondays are market discussions and Wednesdays are lectures about various capital market topics ranging from "What is Money?" to "Shadow Banking" and everything in between. Absolutely amazing course. I wish I could be in it longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never written a review on this site but Akash is deserving of one. He one of the best professors I have had at UT Austin, and gave me helpful advice during a difficult time in my life. He is passionate about finance, and is dedicated to making sure his students actually understand the material. He is also very down to Earth, and relatable.

Honestly he seemed like a nice guy who wanted us to succeed, I just disliked the finance class itself. For each test I memorized all the terms during the week beforehand and made sure I could do the practice test. Luckily since its McCombs, there was a curve
Great professor who cares a lot about the material and the success of his students. His lectures are entertaining and engaging, and he is more than willing to answer questions.

chill professor, good at teaching and connecting to more broadly applicable/personal concepts. class is a lot of self-learning though so be prepared for that vs. another more established/seasoned professor in the FIN department, such as Toprac or Chhajawani.

Great guy. Lectures are kind of iffy though since there isn't really PowerPoints he does them in excel. He knows his stuff so his discussions in class time is good to reinforce concepts. His cases also wasn't bad as he would give the answers you just need to solve it yourself. Super caring to actually help you learn so definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very witty. Definitely related to him and he inspired me bc I have imposter syndrome at this school, and he told us the first day that he got a D/F in finance and accounting. He really drills into the content and makes sure we get it. I liked him.

Fantastic professor who is clearly limited by the fact that FIN357 has a standardized curriculum across all courses. If this curriculum was set by him and he was teaching the stuff he wanted to, easily one of the best classes at McCombs. However, lectures at the moment are not the most effective, but the homework/required readings make up for that

My favorite professor at UT. The classroom is flipped, which is good in case you miss class. You can watch the real lecture whenever. His in-person lectures are more review and discussion. He makes them super engaging and applicable to our lives. Made the class enjoyable. I can't recommend him enough. Gives great career advice—very impressive guy.

Reverse classroom style. He posts videos ahead of class that vary in length. He is a very accommodating professor that cares about students success. Overall he makes a class that is meant to be difficult accessible to the average student. Would recommend him for sure.

I really like this professor! He was a UT student so he just gets it. Class is for discussion, he uses a flipped classroom system so you should watch lectures before class. Finance in itself is hard, but he really cares about students and is so flexible with office hours. Take him if you can! 100 percent recommend.

Hard class, but really nice professor! Very caring and goes out of his way to answer our questions and meet with us in his free time. His current real world experience makes this class all the more interesting. Go to class and watch his Youtube videos.

One of the best professors in the department!
If you get 100 on the final exam, you will automatically get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The exams are multiple choice but not much partial credit is awarded if you select the wrong answer for whatever reason. Lectures didn't feel that helpful either, so I would recommend reading the textbook and/or watching the relevant Razavi Electronics I and II lectures on YouTube and doing the assigned practice problems to succeed in this course.
I have had such an awesome semester with him. Definitely recommend, I wish I could take another class taught by him!

I loved Deji's lectures, he made funny anecdotes about his life and somehow strung it back to transistors and circuits haha. The exams were very chill, but since they're mcq, its a bit unforgiving if you make small mistakes. He does pull questions  from the textbook though, so theoretically you can just do all the book problems. Labs are good too.

Dr. Akiwande was an amazing professor! He cracks funny jokes and tells his life stories sometimes during lectures. I learned a lot about how transistors work in his class. Although it's a lab class, the tests still make up 60% of your grades. But they are all MCs and very doable! This was an excellent class, and he was an amazing guy to talk to!
Relatively difficult circuit concepts but Dr. Akinwande structures the class well. Do a lot of extra practice to understand how to solve problems, and then the tests come easily.

Prof does amazing with helping you understand all of the concepts. Does plenty of practice problems. He expects a lot because the course lies heavily on your understanding of the material and performance in the labs, which will help you in the exams. READ THE TEXTBOOK. It is your best friend! Exams & homework can get challenging. Labs can be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He explains concepts very well, both during lectures and during office hours. For students struggling in the class, he offered extra office hours, which were very helpful. The tests came directly from the textbook questions. Even though this is a lab class, the majority of the grade comes from 4 exams (no final). Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Erin gives amazing feedback & understands most students are not english majors. She makes class inclusive, fun & engaging, one I always woke up to go to. Her feedback is super helpful, drops quizzes, and grades super leniently, while also wanting you to stretch your understanding. 4 books to read, and 3 papers, only hw is reading. AMAZING PROF
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took Banned Books with Erin and she is probably one of the best professors i've had. By far my favorite class of the semester and I'm sure everyone else in my class would agree. She takes the books to new levels and is phenomenal at explaining she may act like she's all over the place but she knows what she's doing. Cant wait to read her books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Class was Rhetoric of Apology and it was very interesting & doable! Akins is currently a grad student, and the only issue was the slow grading and limited feedback as the course progressed. There is no TA so that's why grading multiple essays took a long time. Rewrites for points back are available and its overall a great class for a writing flag!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Daily Quiz at the start of the class( at the start of your day too) won't spend time on Kanji, force everyone to shut their mic, go over things too fast but again and again, daily homework is also a pain
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved Katayama-sensei when I took her for 601 and 610. She's a little strict at times but it shapes you into a good Japanese speaker. Show her you care and that you like Japanese and she'll love you. Read the book before class, study your kanji, participate in class, and you'll do great, especially for 610D
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Katayama may seem a little intimidating at times but she overall cares for her students very much and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. Pay attention in class and be ready to participate. Reading the textbook before class really gets you a head start on lessons in class. 601D is easy but 610D is a little more difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sensei is a great teacher but you do have to put effort into the class. As one of the previous comments said, she doesn't care for slackers. But she does care that you get an education and really immerse yourself in Japanese, so try in class and take the time to talk with her in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's nice and helpful in her office hours, but very hard on transfer students. She does take an interest in every student though.

Nice but plain. I had her for and 8 am class and she was not the most exciting person to take up to. She does't care much for slackers but she's very helpful if you go to her office. It's a pretty easy class with a lot of quiz and homework grades. If you show up everyday, you also get +2 points on your overall grade.
I liked Katayama-sensei a lot. I had her for JPN 506 and then again for 507, and had very high A's both times.
Just read off her slides the entire time. I only went because of the clicker questions. If you do the readings, you can pass her class. Honestly, I was really bored in class. Not engaging at all.

Lectures are mandatory due to partial iClicker grade but are not very helpful. She just lectures off of slides It is better to just take notes from the book while going through the slides at home. Her tests are very unpredictable, no reviews, only a chat session the night before the test. Generally 25 MC, T/F, and about 5-8 free response.

A very disorganized class. would rather take another professor. Was very nonchalant regarding helping students study for exams. R Great at explaining but you could NEVER know what to expect on exams. Just hope your T.A. prepares you well..

Despite the monotone voice, his lectures explain concepts very well and learning from him was not difficult.  Weekly quizzes based on the homework, and the homework is from the textbook. Exams are a mix of free response solving conceptual short answer/multiple choice, and are pretty fair. Very helpful office hours if you have questions.
He is a great guy!

Great professor. Lectures are good, help with high-level understanding and intuition. Quizzes are from homework, fairly easy. The only downside is that tests are meant to challenge you, so some of the questions, you have to work out intuitionally, memorizing text book questions won't always help. Otherwise, great guy, fun class.

Weekly homework that is graded for completion. Weekly quizzes that are identical to a homework problem. Good and interesting lectures. Tests consist of open-ended computational questions as well as conceptual questions at the end. Nice professor and offers opportunities for extra credit :)

the only bad thing about this professor is that he sounds like he hates his life when he lectures, but if you stuggle with insomnia this class will definitely cure you! weekly homework is a bit challenging, but super super helpful for exams. quizzes are regurgitated hw questions. he also curves amazingly and genuinely wants students to succeed.

Very nice and understanding professor. I learned a lot from his class, and I enjoyed his personality. He gave tons of extra credit and allowed us to replace our worst exam. No required reading quizzes, and I honestly didn't need them for most of the class. Would take him again!
Goated professor, makes the lectures really easy to follow, and the exams are a guaranteed 70 or up if you just use the formula sheet or pay attention, awesome dude 10/10 would take again.

he doesn't post lecture recordings or previous exams, and there's a lecture quiz for every single lecture (twice a week) that makes it so that you had to go to lectures, and in lectures he goes on random tangents very often. he also hardly taught verilog at all and we had to learn it off labs. overally an interesting person but not very good prof

Cuevas will appeal to people who love knowledge, technical history, and real-world practical skills in Digital Logic. Take him if you want to become an expert. If you are looking for a definite A, better choose another professor. I don't agree with the hate he gets; he is a good, rigorous old-school lecturer/tester, and he's there for his students.
Extensive assignments, but rewarding in the long run

As a girl this class is hell only like 4 other girls were in the class and I lost soo much hair. the guy that prayed every night for some kind of B wasn't wrong, it took all my effort to barely avoid a C. He gives exam questions ahead of time to help you prepare but then throws all kinds of little tricks in to mess you up. HW is online so not bad.

At least for 411, I think the reviews are a little exaggerated, but he's not the worst professor. His lectures are unorganized, but the exams aren't bad, just weighted too heavily, so if you mess up one really badly, you might as well drop. You should definitely still go to the lectures, if only to get the past exam questions he puts on the board.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cuevas isn't a horrible guy, so I almost feel bad writing a bad review, but the truth is he is a bad teacher. He is super knowledgeable but horrible at conveying it. While I think people exaggerate on how hard exams are (they arent bad + he's nice with partial), he doesnt teach well enough to prepare you for them, and he can be very condescending
Avoid taking with Cuevas

Taking a class with Cuevas is like hiking up a mountain with a man on your back who smashes your knees with a hammer every 1000 steps and then blames you for having your knees in front of his hammer. He accused a large portion of the class of cheating because they used a technique for convolution that Cuevas couldn't do. He grades very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer and he made the content easy to understand. He's also very accessible outside of class and always willing to help. Overall chill guy. My only problem is that his test procedures are ruthless. Homeworks do not prepare you in any way whatsoever, does not give any type of practice tests or problems, and grades very harsh.

My brain could not tell the difference between  getting chased by a bear, or being in this class. I prayed to God (I'm an atheist) every night to give me at least some form of B in this class. The exams weren't that bad, but if you mess up ONE exam, don't expect to get a good grade in this class.

His lectures are OK and cover the material well. It is just hard to prepare for the exams since he does not release any practice exams. The only homework that tests the concepts was infrequent Matlab HW. The tests are graded very difficultly and there is a huge emphasis on complex algebra. Take another professor to actually learn conceptually.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: $120 textbook and exam averages hovered around 75 (Cs). Chill and helpful guy in class, but my grade got cooked.

He's a good lecturer and a nice guy. Passionate about what he's teaching. He responded to emails quickly and was happy to answer any questions in class. It's a tough class (labs were harder, tests weren't too bad but weren't curved, 2 lecture quizzes + hw + readings every week), but it never felt unfair or impossible to do well. Learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: hes def passionate abt the subject, but lectures feel disorganized. the textbook is super helpful, labs, hw and lecture quizzes r chill, pretty easy to do well on them but the tests feel like getting the rug pulled from under u. no matter how much i redid problems, explained to others, etc it felt impossible to get an a. idk killed my confidence 😞

Even though the grades are harsh I like that this professor doesn't curve. Students are not meant to compete against each other. However I don't like how some students have access to their friends past finals while others don't and suffer for it with bad grades.

His labs compared to other 411 professors are significantly longer. But he is a really nice person, loved his lectures, however he does go on tangents although interesting, combined with a missed school day due to weather caused us to go very behind missing an entire topic. Underrated and not a bad teacher as others make him seem.
Honesty this professor isn't bad at explaining things, it's just that his tests are impossible. Feels like he doesn't want students to get an A or B, test avg was 65 and he is not curving.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were a little disorganized and they didn't adequately prepare students for labs and exams. Too much emphasis was placed on easy/minor things, and not enough time was spent teaching students how to use Verilog and other important concepts. The lectures themselves were okay, although I wish they were a bit more focused.

His lectures are good as long as you are REALLY that interested in the syllabus. From my perspective, and from what I've heard from my classmates, his lectures are very boring. Exams are hard, you could loose half of the points for a minor mistake in a big question.

Do not take this professor if you can. He intentionally gives bad grades so there aren't as many A's. Our TA told us he graded our labs harshly as our professor didn't like how many people got 100s on them in a previous semester. The lecture quizzes are lazily written and error-filled. Finally, he yaps too much and we don't learn that much in class

was rude when i asked for help on a problem and dismissed me. proceeded to help a student on same problem right after. TAs grade harsh on lab reports, had to chase them down for feedback. does not post lectures & thinks that benefits students in their learning.seems like i got the short end of the stick with him but he made 411 wayy too complicated

His lectures are fine, but tbh his lecture quizzes (MCQ/short answer) and homeworks (graded fairly late and leniently) don't really prepare you for how strict the tests are. It keeps the class chill, but he also doesn't provide past practice tests for Exam 2 and the Final, so it's really hard to know what nitpicky grading to expect on an Exam.

Do not take his course. You learn nothing. There is no curve for all his courses. Lecture is a mess. There is quiz after every lecture. The quiz is not relevant to what he said. He is happy to see students make mistakes in exam and then he would say "I made a trick on that question and many of you were wrong." The worst professor I have ever seen.
take with other professors if you can. cuevas is a harsh grader, does not give partial credit, and will not curve.

Lectures are not recorded. Template for the exam given beforehand only if you are in class. 
No solutions are given for any exams. Sometimes the "expected solution" is not correct. But doesnt entertain any feedback. Seems unreasonable to me. Had a hard time.

Doesn't like curving or recording lectures, even in summer courses. Releases lecture notes, but they often differ from what he says and can be lengthy. Lectures are unstructured, and quizzes are held before releasing notes, penalizing those who miss class. Quizzes may cover material not discussed. Advises students to read the textbook to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dull, but informative, but daily lecture quizzes are given based on examples he does briefly on the whiteboard. If you zone out for 5 minutes you get a 60 on a quiz. He also doesn't post previous year's exams, or solutions for the earlier exams in the semester before the final. He makes an easy course artificially difficult.

To be honest, the man just does not give partial credit.  If you do perfect, you are fine.  But if you make one mistake, you lose most of the points, even if it is just a minor error. And it does not help that he has cutoffs be 94 for an A, and doesn't curve, despite when the averages for his midterms are 72.5 and 68. Love the guy, hate the class.

Spring 23 was Dr. Cuevas' first time teaching Analog Electronics after it was resurrected after 6 years, so he may improve it more. Lectures had a lot of info not always relevant to HWs and tests. HWs were written by the TA and often needed clarification due to confustion or unclear info. You'll learn a good deal about filtering topologies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do NOT take Prof. Cuevas for 411. Lectures are extremely rushed. It's easy to get lost and confused. This class is very time-consuming and you will have to dedicate a lot of hours to studying. There were two exams and a final, and there were lecture quizzes every other day, as well as homework assignments every week. he does not record his lectures

Took the class over summer, it was really hard. Take the class with any other professor if you have the option to. Lecture quizzes are really difficult and there are no homework drops. Homeworks are Matlab assignments and take forever. Very strict grade cutoffs, very less likely to curve the class. I failed at 59.82 where the cutoff was 60

Dr. Cuevas is a great professor. He would often relate the material with personal anecdotes regarding their implementation which made the class engaging. He skips the math and derivations and focuses on the intuition of the concepts which helps to understand what is actually going on. Lab and lab reports were very exhausting but I learned a lot.

I enjoyed the course. He discussed the mathematical fundamentals which made the concepts intuitive. He had a quiz after each lecture which helped to check my understanding. You need to put effort to understand the class. Numerous students struggled because they were uncomfortable with complex numbers, especially those who took 411 with Swartz.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His teaching style is just lecture, lecture, lecture, hard midterm. Concepts were rushed right before the final. Convolution was practically impossible to understand with his teaching.

I really wanted to like Dr. Cuevas, he seems like a nice guy. But his class is extremely frustrating and disorganized. He barely releases exam prep material and when he does it's without an answer key. He rushes important concepts before the final. Has a quiz after every lecture. Expects a lot of prior knowledge. You can do well, but it's not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Would you be ok with a prof not curving a C class avg when another Prof 411 class avg is around a B+? Would you be ok with a prof who lectures only off the textbook but gives exams that are much harder? Would you like a prof who makes lab much harder than it needs to be? If your answer to the above questions is yes, then take him. Otherwise, don't.

The class isn't too horrible, the tests are pretty straightforward once you get a good grasp of the basics. He unfortunately does a poor job of lecturing as about ~75% of what he says is irrelevant or very long derivations or proofs that will not at all be on the test.

I enjoyed taking 411 with Dr.Cuevas. He kept the lectures lively by sharing anecdotes and funny incidents. The lab assignments were a bit lengthy but they helped you understand the material better. The lectures might sometimes feel a little dense but he is always available outside class and is eager to help.

Great professor, for 411 - attend class and take notes, do problems. Each exam only has 4-5 questions so crucial you understand the content well. He tells you what chapter-type problems he will put on the test so few surprises. Having a graphing calculator that can do systems of complex equations can help. Put in work but it's do-able!

He will tell you question by question what will be on the exam. You can do fine on the tests if you only attend the review day the week of the exam to learn what problems will be on there. Not so great if you're actually trying to learn though.

Very structured/organized class and lectures. There are lots of complaints on here about teaching out of the text, but I'm not sure what else you'd expect from courses like EE411 and EE313. If you attend lectures and pay attention, he does sprinkle in extra little snippets of knowledge from industry/his business.

Dr. Cuevas does a good job of getting what he expects us to know across, but not the actual concepts themselves. I took him for two classes, and personally did not really learn much in lecture other than what to expect on the exams. Then, I would go home and learn on my own time. His tests were usually fair and he curves his classes a good bit.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His lectures are kinda terrible and his slides are wordy and confusing and not useful to refer back to at all. I spent a lot of this class confused about what I was actually learning. But, he's really cool and his tests are pretty easy. The material isn't super hard either. Just do the readings before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are word for word from the text book. The TA writes the HW and some of the exams and Dr. Cuevas sometimes doesnt even know whats going on. Basically, expect to teach yourself the entire course and be ready for the somewhat tough exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures were the textbook verbatim. His tests were way too easy too, except the final. Just do the textbook reading chapters, and hard problems at the end of each chapter and you should make an easy A in the class. Honestly, I feel like he didn't cover the whole course. No exam questions over Three-Phase, Magnetic Coupling, or two-port network
Not a bad professor. His class is easy, but his lectures can be dry. He's also not very organized which shows during class. Overall, he's a pretty nice guy, but not a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If your learning style is lectures based on the prof writing on the board, then I'd take him. Gives plenty of examples and explains the material well & ties concepts back together. His HWs are very helpful and the tests are pretty good since he teaches everything you need to know. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED FOR 411/any circuits class, he knows his stuff.

Dr. Cuevas is very respectable as an engineer. However, his teaching is not the best.   He relies heavily on the textbook, fails to clearly explain examples, and has exams that are much more difficult than they need to be. Often, it is better to just read the textbook rather than attend lecture. Too bad there's pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Cuevas taught by the textbook, which usually meant explaining example problems given and showing us techniques. His lectures were great until op-amps, where he repeated the book almost verbatim. That was zero help and is my reasoning for marking down. Read the book before class and show lots of work on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She teaches so well! She always makes sure you understand the material and truly sets you up for success. She puts exactly what she says will be on the exam, on the exam!
Amazing professor, THE most kindest and caring professor I've had at UT, super helpful and detailed lectures, she is also super understanding when you make mistakes, just a fantastic human being.
She is very kind, and understanding with all situations. She is willing to work with her students to make sure they succeed and actually know that material.

I would say the only downside of this class is the grade distribution, but I really love her resources like her practice sets. I re-took CH301 after taking Laude last semester. She is SO incredible and straightforward and the way that she teaches makes perfect sense to me. We learn exactly what we need to do well on the exam, no fluff!

If you have to take any sort of Chemistry at UT, TAKE HER. This is probably the most caring and thoughtful professor I have ever had. Her lectures are actual fun and she goes out of her way to make sure students understand. Uploads all here lectures online and offers so many resources for studying. Occasional extra credit during class
This is the best professor EVER. Love her. She makes my day. Records all the lectures and posts them online with so many resources

I took chem last semester and I didn't too well because I felt I did not understand it too well but Dr Eman makes me feel very good and confident in chem as a subject. She is so amazing and sweet you can tell she deeply cares about her students!!!!

Prof Eman is such an incredible professor, really gives you all the information you need to get an A in the class. There was no homework but instead self-paced quizzes that were a completion grade and review material for the exams. Take her if you can!!

Truly an outstanding professor. She goes above and beyond to support her students and provides an exceptional amount of resources to help you succeed. She is deeply invested in making sure students actually understand the material and is always willing to spend extra time explaining concepts. PChem could use slightly more rigor, but she's great

I LOVE Professor Eman, she is so knowledgeable, respected, inspirational, and just overall an amazing professor. I learned so much from her class and was actually able to retain what I learned. She offers lots of extra credit which is also a plus. I recommend that everyone whether you are a science major or not take a class with her!

Professor Eman was the best chemistry professor ever!! She is super sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She offered 2 makeup exams at the end of the semester that will replace your lowest two exams. She is hilarious and lectures were always engaging. You do have to study and put in some time/work, but all the material is accessible and organized.
Best professor ever, she sets the standards for how a professor should be, will for sure miss her class and the way she taught!

Even if you've had bad experiences with chemistry, I totally recommend taking Dr.Eman. If you reach out, watch her YouTube videos, do the modules and practice quizzes/exams, you are sure to get an A in this course. She is extremely dedicated and respectful to students. Take her if you have the chance.

She is the best professor I have EVER taken at UT. I think she deserves a 6/5 tbh. She teaches so sincerely, her exams are very representative of the content, and she prepares you very well and gives you everything you need to succeed.
Dr. Alasadi is one of the best professors you will take. She provides summarizing annotated lectures, YouTube videos, and extra credit. You will not fail her, and she will not fail you!

Professor Eman is THE GOAT. I don't enjoy chemistry at all, but his class actually made it bearable for me. The class is extremely well structured, has tons of resources, extra credit, but most importantly, the professor truly cares about each and every one of her students. If you have the chance to take a class with her, you should 100% do it.

Dr. Eman is an awesome person and great at explaining difficult topics. If you attend most classes, complete the extra credit homework and you put in the effort, you'll be fine.  She gives you a TON of resources but once you find what works for you, just stick to it. (But the practice exam with explanations are a lot of help.)

The best professor I've ever had. She gives out: extra credit, participation quizzes, practice questions, multiple practice exams for each unit, cheat sheets, FAQ's, annotated lectures, her YT channel and transcripts, a STUDY SCHEDULE, and keys to go with everything I just mentioned. Hilarious, laid back but caring. Exam grading is clear. TAKE HER.

The definition of her class is literally "you're not cooked, you will cook." If you can take her class, PLEASE DO! Professor Alasadi is absolutely magnificent with great lectures, annotated notes, and exam resources. I wish I had to take OChem so I could have another semester with her. The only way to fail is not to do the bare minimum to pass.

Genuinely the best professor I had at UT. She goes out of her way to provide help with ample resources and explains content well. Exams are like the practice ones. This course is an easier version of normal PChem, so while she's a great professor, I'd probably go with PChem I (CH 353) if it's a pre-req for another class.

My goat #eman i genuinely could not say enough about professor alasadi she not only is sweet and caring but she provides so much amazing resources for exam and understanding content.Additionally she pays well attention to her students that attend class and I have so much respect for her and the way she runs the class would always take her again.

LOVE DR. EMAN!! She is an outstanding professor who makes chem an enjoyable subject. Her youtube vids and other resources are phenomenal and will guarantee to prepare you well for exams. many extra credit opportunities too, my overall grade rounded up 4 whole points!!
If you can take this class, take it. There is no better chem professor at UT Austin. She's amazing, and so kind and caring about her students. Love her and her class!

Very passionate and kind professor. Lots of resources to help you succeed (YouTube videos and practice exams were very helpful). Easy exams with medians in the high As and homework sets graded on completion are the only grades. Great for an easy pchem credit, but I might avoid if you need a stronger pchem foundation for future courses.

Had a 100 in the class with extra credit. She gives so many useful resources. I was so close to accepting my AP Chem credit and taking Ochem, but I am honestly glad I didn't because this class is a really good GPA booster. Pay attention and use the resources she provides. Not only is she an amazing lecturer, but also a super kind professor.

Took her class for both CH 301 and 302. love love love. She is very caring and teaches everything so clearly. Her youtube channel also explains the topics which is a helpful resource if you miss lecture (which I was in the 8am so you can imagine). Would take her class again if she taught ochem next semester, but she's teaching 301 again

One of the BEST profs I've had. Caring, funny, smart. Exams were never unfair, always on what she taught. She inspired me to take Pchem 2. She would give us donuts on exam day, extra credit galore, and optional finals. She made P-chem such a fun class and I genuinely found myself enjoying what I was learning. If she is teaching, TAKE HER!!

If you get the chance to take Professor Eman, consider yourself blessed. She is so passionate about teaching and truly wants every student to succeed. She has an educational YouTube and TikTok account aimed at helping students understand chemistry and biology. Take her!!!!!!

I absolutely loved this class her teaching style is so easy to understand, and her youtube channel is the most helpful. She provides lecture notes which helped feel more comfortable and prepared for lectures. She's full of humor and she actually cares about her students.

She writes the lectures, and they cover everything on the exams. I just took the class early, so I slept through a lot of them. Fun teacher that gives very helpful resources like her own videos and her exam study sessions. Very good extra credit added like 3.5% onto my total grade.

Prof Eman was by-far the best professor I've had this semester (and probably at UT as well). She made P-chem so digestible with all the resources she provided without sacrificing on rigor. I feel that I have actually learned physical chemistry without wanting to die. If only she could teach all my classes

Very good professor. 80% of your grade is dependent on 4 midterms, but that's standard for most UT Austin gen chem 1 & 2. There's no homework, but you have 4-6 quizzes to complete asynchronously (+ unlimited attempts) before tests that make up the remaining 20%. Tests are easy to cram for if you remember AP chem.

Professor. Eman is hands down the best professor you could ever ask for, she is such an angel. She effortlessly made a course deemed challenging so enjoyable. The amount of ORIGINAL resources (Annotated notes, YouTube videos, Recorded lectures, Quizlet flashcards, etc.) provided are beyond me. love her

Professor Eman is easily the best professor I had this semester. She genuinely cares so much about her students and makes great effort to make chem as simple and accessible as it should be. She has such a talent with communicating ideas, the tests are all extremely easy if you just attend lecture and listen. So much study material. She is the GOAT

I dont usually write reviews on here so that just goes to show how great of a professor she is. I used to hate chemistry before her class but she helped me really come to love the subject because her teaching style and the effort she puts into her classes is unmatched. Yall should defo take her best professor ever!

Professor Eman loves her job and her students, and it shows. Her lectures are fun, and she provides so many resources. She has a YouTube channel where she goes over content, and it is all so detailed. Went to her office hours just to chat, and she's so sweet. She wants everyone to succeed; I couldn't recommend anyone better
Prof. Eman is literally the Michael Jordan of teaching chemistry. Hands down the best Professor I've had thus far at UT. If you have the opportunity to take her, TAKE HER!

Professor Eman is one of the best teachers here at UT. She truly cares about each student in her class and makes a difficult subject easy to understand. She also makes youtube videos, practice problems, and flashcard decks. If I could take her for any chemistry related class I would. 100% recommend her.
Hands down the best professor you will ever have. Nothing more needs to be said.

I don't really like Chemistry, so I did not like studying Chemistry at all. However, she encouraged all the students and gave a lot of extra credit opportunities. 100% I would take her class again if I need to learn more about Chemistry. 100%.

Uploads all lectures and so much more (annotated lecture, practice questions, additional learning modules) to the Canvas you could go through the course and only show up for exam days. Lectures are easy to grasp. No quizzes, just exams. Finals are optional if you get the 4 midterms down. Sometimes fell asleep during lecture though (8am)

Love how many resources Professor Eman gives for her students, from online lectures to problem sets to practice exams. She really cares about her students and even tries to learn all of our names. Lectures are very easy to follow thanks to her digital notes. Would recommend to anyone, one of the best chem professors.

Professor Alasadi is a unicorn. I am not a STEM major, but I took this class after taking CH301 many years ago. The resources that she provides are IMMENSELY helpful, and they mirror exactly what will be on the tests, if not harder than the tests. She is also kind, caring, and understanding of her students. If you need any chemistry, take her.

Professor Eman is the GOAT! I mean it, she is so awesome, so caring, and so thoughtful of her students. She wants you to succeed and wants to get to know her students. If you get the chance to take her, please do. She is a blessing and truly wonderful. THANK YOU EMAN!!

Prof Eman's chem class was very easy. She provided a bunch of practice questions for you to study for the exams. And as along as you understand those questions, you'll be fine on the exams. She didn't curve but the questions were all mcq.

CH302, Amazing professor provides so many resources and worksheets that reflect exactly what's on exam. Don't need to attend lecture if you keep up with her videos. Only graded on practice sets which she provides key for and 25 MC test that she gives tons of useful material for. No final unless you want to retake 2 lowest test grades.

I took CH 302. If a student did poorly, it's because they didn't put effort into their studying. We're given all the tools needed to do good in class. She may be the best professor I've ever had. I appreciated her energy through the course, especially during our 8 am lectures. I would hope to have more professors like her as I keep taking courses.

She is such an angel, I have never had such an amazing teacher. She provides many resources over every single question type you can think of, and extra credit is given randomly, but just a simple participation is what gets you it. Nothing hard. I can go on and on about how much I love her, she is the goat.

She has the best possible resources with youtube videos, practice quizzes, anything you need for no matter your learning style. It was her first semester teaching and she was literally the best professor I ever had and I learned so much.

You really couldn't ask for a better professor on a subject deemed "difficult". She is incredibly resourceful and so helpful. Her lectures aren't mandatory but they are the most enjoyable, she explains clearly, always open to questions, and makes you feel heard. The class is exam heavy but there are makeups and sooo many good preparatory resources.

THATS WHY SHE IS THE GOAT, THE GOAT. 
Professor mean is super good she is supper attentive and her class is basically based on exams which are 80% of grade but you get to retake two at the end of the semester. she has YouTube videos explaining everything we see in lass and also she posts a review before every exam. Best professor ever take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eman is AWESOME!! She's easy to reach out to, super funny, and extremely caring to her students. She provides a ton of resources to stay on top of the class, including her very own YouTube channel!?!? It's insane how much work she puts into supporting her class, and she makes chemistry feel so easy. I never had to struggle in her class, 10/10 rec.

CH 301 with Professor Eman was amazing, I really like her teaching style. You can tell she cares for her students and wants them to succeed. She has her own youtube channel where she explain her lectured throughly again (not just a recorded lecture). You can tell she really passionate about teaching!

Lemme tell you, absolutely goated. She is extremely professional, patient, and respectful. Lectures are a bit slow, but it really helps if you need the material at a slower pace. (All of the TAs are helpful) I'll be biased here, but I have taken other chemistry professors, and Professor Eman has made it by far the easiest to understand.

Professor Alasadi is truly a blessing. Her lectures were always very thorough and thoughtful. She has a YouTube channel with amazing videos to help with test reviews and complicated topics. She also gave multiple opportunities for extra credit and wanted everyone in the class to succeed. If you get the chance to have Professor Alasadi TAKE IT!!

prof eman is so kind, and she teaches extremely well! i had her for chem 1, and lots of kids in my class including myself emailed the hiring department asking them to hire her to teach chem 2. she dumbs down complicated topics, and you know exactly what to expect on her exams if you just do her reviews and watch her videos!

I said no textbook, but she offers links to resources online, she has a YT channel, her lectures are relevant and soo helpful, and she makes notes to help you know what to study for tests. She's amazing for chem!! Communicate with her and she is very understanding. Make sure to do practice questions she offers, show up, and you'll be set!!!

If you read any reviews, read this one. Professor Eman was easily one of the best professors I've had at UT. I dropped Chem 301 first semester of freshmen year because I could not learn with either Caudill, the older guy or Viviani. I enrolled in Eman's class and passed with an A+. She offers so much extra credit and makes her own yt videos!! GOAT!

im a senior that retook it for a better grade, and she's like SO much better than the other gen chem profs at UT (idk why she taught in the off semester...). she dumbs chemistry down for you from the START, which is pretty rare for any PHD level/highly qualified prof. Her TA's were all rlly nice and taught j like her (s/o abdullah). take her trust

Even though she was new, she went ABOVE AND BEYOND to help her students. She reads EVERY SINGLE student's feedback and take it into account for the next topic of CH301 (extra practice problems, exam review class time, extra credit, etc.) She teaches well and is really funny too!! Would love it if she taught CH302 next year

I LOVE Eman. I hated CH301 last semester (I had to end up doing course switch) but I loved chem. Class is mostly based on exam grades but possible by attending lectures and doing all the practice problems (ample posted and all very representative of what is on test). Eman is a great lecturer and explains big concepts in an understanding way.

The. Best. Professor. Ever. 

Her lectures were not boring at all considering it was at 8 am. If you can PLEASE TAKE HER. I need her to teach Ch302 and o-chem because that's just how good she was. She cares about her students and has many resources and a YT channel that thoroughly explains everything.

If you have the availability in your schedule, PLEASE TAKE HER. I hate chemistry, and I dreaded taking it this semester, but Professor Eman was so amazing and super sweet. She had YouTube videos, study guides, and multiple review sessions available to us to help with the exams. Just study and use the materials provided, and you'll be fine.

SHES GOATED! She is such an amazing professor and lecturer! She is so easy to talk to and will never make you feel dumb. She has a YouTube channel called “Professor Eman” and you can just see there how great she is. She truly provides you with all the resources you need to succeed. TAKE HER!!!

TAKE HER! She a new professor at UT but she explains content thoroughly and cares ab her students. I took her ch 301 class n never got bored. Because shes young, shes relatable and funny. 4 exams worth 80% but u can retake at end of sem and a "5th exam" that's just 200 participation points you get from in-class aissgnments or learning modules.

Professor Mrazek was an amazing professor who clearly cares about her students and the topic. The class was easy but really engaging and helpful. However, you should only take it if you genuinely care about learning. There are two journal entries a week and attendance is really important to get a good grade.

Professor Mrazek is super nice and gives ample opportunities to build a relationship with students outside of class. Grade is based on attendance, daily quizzes, projects, and 2 exams. Daily quizzes are based off of the previous class lecture and homework which is a good refresher.Class starts with meditating and has a movement break in the middle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Mrazek is one of the best professors at UT! The course is genuinely life changing and the professor is approachable and helpful!! LOVED this class!! Highly recommend. Workload is not bad and doable!!
One of the best professors I've had, truly such an amazing and caring professor. Really preaches what she teaches and is so kind to students. Cannot recommend this class and Dr. Mrazek enough!!

Dr. Mrazek was the best professor I have ever had. She was so engaging, kind, and the content of the class changed my life. She does have a bit of a strict assignment deadline policy, but you have multiple drops and she gives you plenty of time for the bigger assignments. If I could take her class again I would do it in a heartbeat.

Dr. Mrazek has been one of my favorite professors at UT. This class has taught me multiple strategies to better my own mental health that I will continue to utilize for years to come. I felt such a sense of belonging in the class, and Dr. Mrazek makes sure there are opportunities for each student to connect with her personally.
Dr. Mrazek is so intelligent and an awesome professor. This was by far the best class I've taken at UT! HIGHLY recommend, absolutely no qualms.

I must admit I did think this class was going to be gimmicky at first, but I was very wrong. Dr. Mrazek teaches some genuinely helpful skills that can and will improve your life. The class was not difficult, and was very relaxing and overall a positive experience. If you can get in, I'd highly recommend this class.

She is the most interesting and caring professor I've ever taken classes from! I had 4 back to back classes the day I have her class, and her class was always a breath of fresh air from my day of stress. Her lectures are interesting and well organized, assignments are reflective and fun, and the material was so helpful to my own life.
Very interesting class, always very captivating and Dr. Mrazek is a great lecturer.
This class is life-changing. It should be a required course for every student at UT! JUST TAKE IT!!!! I promise you will be so happy you did.

I leave Dr. Mrazek's class feeling positive and motivated to do the best I can. This has been the least stressful class throughout my time at UT. There is one final cumulative exam (open-note), a midterm-interview project, and class quizzes consisted of 3 questions each. I can't stress how amazing Dr. Mrazek is and if you can take this class, do it

This class is basically you experiencing firsthand the benefits of psychology. Class is truly therapeutic, as others have said. There are exams and quite a bit of homework, but nothing too hard or time-consuming (mostly journals+1 group project).
I'd recommend this class to anyone, especially those who need a boost of positivity and good guidance!

I just love this professor. she is one of my favorites at UT.  Her class was very therapeutic and she is very understanding. You will not regret taking her course. The fact that you are learning how to better yourself in this class makes the material super easy.

She's an incredible professor and lecturer! She's kind, funny, and is really passionate about positive psych. This is a great class for learning how to live a happier life! Workload is pretty light, and all the readings are usually short and very interesting. If you can, take this class!

Dr. Mrazeks positive psychology was not only educational, but it was LIFE-CHANGING! This class should be a requirement to graduate, that is how POWERFUL IT IS. The work is easy & reflective, which helps you get the most out of the class. Dr. Mrazek is also very organized & cares about her students. If she taught more classes, I would take them!

The material in this class is genuinely beneficial and Prof Mrazek does a fantastic job of relaying the information. Not only does she encourage you to apply what you learn in class and keep you engaged during lectures, but it's clear that she truly cares about her students as well.

In Positive Psych with Dr. Mrazek, you can tell that she really cares about the content shes teaching you! Not only does she teach you what it is, but how to use these methods in your everyday life too. Shes a great prof and I couldnt recommend her more. Take Positive Psych!! You wont regret it!!

Dr. Mrazek is an amazing professor! This class is about learning how to be happy and even utilizing some of the techniques for yourself. There was a journal entry for every class day, which at first was a bit easy to forget about but she drops a couple! She is so kind, honestly one of the best profs I've ever had! Only a final and a midterm paper
The lectures honestly make the material kinda interesting and fun. Basically PSY 317 but I had a much easier time.

This class is easy, just make sure you attend the weekly labs and do the labs, case studies and prepare for the quizzes. Mona is an amazing TA, I'm not really good at coding and she helped a lot to understand the concepts and formulas. If you are able to take the class with her, take it.

This class is all based on the TA you get. The only time you'll use the lectures are for the quizzes throughout the semester. Lab was easy as long as you followed along with the TA and I felt it was an overall easy A if you get a good TA.

The class content is taught by 3 professors: Cormack, Etz, and Josephs. Some of the lectures were a bit boring, but it's significantly easier than 317L as there is almost no RStudio involved, it's just about the formulas and theories. Just make sure to go to the labs and follow along with the TA, and to work on the semester paper.

How well you do in this class depends on your TA. The instructions for the final project components are not very clear, so I would go to office hours to ask for feedback before each part is due. If you make every correction your TA gives on the components, you will get a 100 on the final project. The labs are easy, just follow along with the TA.

Lab participation is mandatory but they're pretty easy labs. If you follow their timeline for the final project of the semester, you'll do fine. Make sure you at least listen to the lectures because the quizzes are based on them, and you can't always figure out the answers from online, you actually gotta know the material.

Etz is a nice guy. I only gave him 4/5 because sometimes when I asked questions his answers were not very clear. But for the class, as long as you pay attention to the lectures you should be fine. The textbook is written by the old professor, Curly, who also does the lectures and I usually just did Command F during the weekly quizzes for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Etz was great, very kind in office hrs. Class was asynchronous (1 2hr lab a week (never took full 2 hrs)). Labs due weekly, final paper broken up into parts through the sem (very clear rubric). 5 (1 optional) 30pt quizzes based on videos, hard but go to office hrs. TAs graded dif (some harsher than others). Independent Inquiry and writing flag

One research paper with no finals. Only about 3-4 quizzes which are 30% of the final grade. Weekly Labs that are done in class and attendance is mandatory but Labs are not hard. In person class taught by TA.
Just 4 quizzes, labs during class with TA, and a final project (just lab report). Nothing terrible, just listen to TA and it'll be chill.

Loved Professor Etz! Hands-down best person to approach! Shoutout to TA Monkia (if you get her, you'll be in good hands) The class includes weekly lab reports, 5 quizzes (one is optional), and a semester-long project. The class is also very straightforward, study the practice problems and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All lectures were Dr. Curley's vids, but Etz is a good online prof -- quick to address technical issues/answer student questions in forums. Though his syllabus doesn't permit extensions since the course is self-paced, he's willing to provide them if you have a good enough reason. Just don't do assignments last-minute.

Overall, really enjoyed this class. The one major complaint I have is the time sink some modules were, as it could take me (personally) up to 10 hrs+ to do the videos+notes+ quiz on Friday. nonetheless, I found I really enjoyed the subject and will be taking psy 420M with etz as well this next fall. Very much looking forward to it!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class if you put in the work. Grade is made up of weekly modules based on lecture videos. You work at your own pace and modules are due every Friday at 5pm. The videos were very slow but I downloaded a chrome extension to speed up the videos. Highly recommend this class for an easy A!
Take PSY 317 with Etz!!! Althought he doesn't give the lectures, whenever you have issues regarding modules. REACH HIM OUT! he is very understanding and genuinely cares for his students!

As much as I dislike stats, I loved this class taught by Etz and the other stats professors! There is a lab every week led by a TA, which are very easy and the TAs are always helpful. There is a research paper, which was pretty easy. The lectures are posted online and there are quizzes every 2 weeks. Make sure to study for them.

Professor Etz is the best statistics professor I have ever had. PSY420M is the most dreaded course for psychology majors, but if you take Etz you will be happy! His TAs are very helpful and knowledgeable. The course can be overwhelming but if you attend office hours and voice your concerns to your TA, you'll be okay! 
TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I had professor Etz for both of my stats classes and he is very helpful. Received the most help from TA in lab, but Dr. Etz's online lectures really explained the content in the simplest ways. This course consists of weekly labs, four tests, and a research paper.

Dr. Etz is truly beyond amazing! He responded to emails quickly & always had interactive ways to explain complicated concepts. This class starts "easy," but the rhythm picks up quickly w difficult statistic+programming lessons. Def watch the lectures at the recommended pace! There were EC opportunities to help w points missed in harder modules.

TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Professor Etz and his TAs were absolutely amazing. They responded quickly to emails and any questions you had and there was an online discussion board where he answered even more questions.  There were just weekly lectures and quizzes that weren't even timed so you could do the questions as you watched the lecture.

Great professor for PSY317L and relatively easy class but I also had him as a TA this semester for PSY420M! He lectures slowly and clearly but graded a bit harshly. He'll probably be great as just a lecturer next semester while his TAs grade the papers, though!

This class was asynchronous completely and at your own pace! There were a few lecture videos a week, a practice quiz, and a module quiz due on Friday by 5 PM. Additionally to the videos, there was a very in-depth textbook available to reference. Professor Etz and his TAs were very available and responded immediately to your questions and concerns.

Professor Etz was very chill and understanding! He always gave us lots of opportunities to improve our grade! Offered many office hours, and overall was a great professor! Would definitely recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took PSY317L this course is asynchronous so the content is recorded you will watch it and then take the quiz. There is a quiz every week so it makes it easier to good in the class compared to other classes where there are 2 tests worth 50%. I recommend Professor Etz!

Took Dr. Dan at ACC for Chem 2 Lab. He's very kind, wants you to succeed. Thick accent and speaks fast, so his lab lectures are a little hard to understand, but he is a generous grader. He will try his best to help direct you to the correct answer and even lets you redo work. Be cautious taking him for lecture, might be hard to understand content.

They removed my rating before, but I stand by what I said. This was the worst science professor I have ever had in 3 separate countries. He was rude, homophobic, spoke constantly and handed out papers during active exams, and treated his students as less than. 
This man shouldn't teach.
He is really caring and great. Take the class if you are already good at math, I think the material was pretty difficult on its own but just attend lessons and do all the practice problems.

I went to every class. I aced every online quiz due to 2 attempts, and I aced every homework assignment. I stayed for 1:1s. I went to tutoring. I did group work nothing worked. I found the professor to be really hard to understand with his thick accent, but equally hard to understand his concepts when he broke it down and that becomes your problem.

I wish professor Dan used the board more. He is super chill and understanding but just goes through the course contents on the presentation. At the end of the semester, the presentation wasn't working and when he taught on the board, it was so much more informative. Great professor overall. Easy to get As if you invest enough time.
