He cares about his students, offers flexible schedules, and inspires us to do our best. He shares his experiences, gives helpful advice and encourages questions if we don't understand. He's available during office hours and is passionate about learning. I'm glad I took chemistry with him. Amazing professor!

Professor Dan is a good teacher as well as person, he helped guide me through the labs and answered my questions any time of day. Beware of the pop quizzes after every lab because these will replace your final exam.

Dr. Dan is one of the best proffessors Ive had at UT. The only reason you would not get an A is because you did not try hard enough( learned from experience). He is very motivational, he loves what hes doing and really cares about his students. Such an inspirational teacher and I 100% recommend you taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is a nice teacher and seems to really like this subject. This class isn't what I expected and the lab portion is very intensive for only 25% of the grade, but I definitely learned a lot. He talks a lot about participation and that wastes time, but if people answer questions he moves on. I liked him overall, but didn't like ACHEM in general.

This is a boring subject, but it is difficult enough that you have to pay attention-this is a tricky combination. However, this professor cares about his class and will spend as much time as necessary during office hours to make sure you have it down. People are mean; he is not a bad teacher. Read the textbook, ask questions, participate and try.

He really loves chemistry but he is an awful lecturer. He is very difficult to follow and gives quizzes on stuff he goes over that same day. The labs take more than half the time you spend on the class but aren't worth enough to be worth it. I have been getting above the average on every assignment and my grade is a very low B. do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic about teaching, but doesn't teach well. Pulls random info from lecture slides to put on exam. Go to reviews (helpful bc of TAs). Also bc he ran out of time to cover the material, he had an extra 3hr class on a Friday. Avoid CH455 altogether if you can - exams are worth more than labs even though you spend more time on lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVED Apfeld! He really wants his students to do well. It's 25% midterm & 25% final (both curved), 25% a paper (he'll give you 100 if you check all the boxes he's looking for), and 25% a series of community engagement things (5 for 5% each). I was nervous about it but I was really glad he made us do them. He's a great guy and a good teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awesome Professor. Chill, young dude. Does not grade hard. If you actually do the assignments then you can expect an easy A in this class. There are 2 multi choice tests and a paper at the end of the semester. The paper is only 4 pages tho! I got a 90 and an 80 on the tests with only a few hours of studying for each. And a 95 on the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was the best professor I had this semester. I attended his every lecture. He is really passionate about his subject, and cares a lot about his students. I approached him during office hours a couple of times, and it was always fun conversing with him. Attend his lectures, follow the guidelines of all the assignments, and do all the readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: LOVE Dr. Apfeld! This was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken at UT; as long as you do the work you'll get an A. He doesn't take attendance, but I would recommend going to lecture because it's really interesting and helps a lot for the tests. A lot of the test questions are basically word for word from the readings as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Apfeld is great! Definitely got me waayy more into politics and how important they are. Only one midterm which was a little rough bc I didn't study as much as I should have, but he gave a very generous curve! He's teaching again next semester and even though attendance isn't required, I would go to every class bc he notices students who do!

Apfeld's class is pretty easy, but his grading is strict. He doesn't accept any late work so make sure you never mix up deadlines or forget an assignment. I never really showed up to class and only did the readings once he told us what was on the test. Wouldn't take him again though.

Apfeld is such a great teacher. He really cares about government and has very clear lectures. There is a textbook, but you can basically get away without reading it. He's super nice too our first exam had like a 15 point curve because he felt bad that everyone did poorly. Overall I'd def recommend him!

Took a risk taking a first-time teacher and it paid off. Very fair exams, fun assignments and great teacher. Glad I took him. Only con is the textbook sucks, but he said he hates it and won't use it again. The exams are fairly lectured based, but he puts the powerpoints online so its not life or death if you miss some classes!

Apfeld's class is fairly easy, though the tests are more difficult than you might expect. He makes occasional jokes and his videos that he plays during lectures are generally very entertaining, though the lectures themselves are sometimes boring. Attendance is not mandatory though your alternative is the most boring set of books put to print.

I took a chance on Professor Apfeld. This was his first time teaching a college class so he had no reviews or anything. That said, this is a very talented young dude and a great teacher. Readings are long, but study (memorize) the lecture slides HARD for every quiz and test and you can get fairly easy 100's. It's April and I have a 99.3 average.
Great solid young teacher. Tests are very fair, assignments fairly reasonable, good at teaching. Nothing to worry about.
Horrible, deeply boring professor. They should give her a mop instead because she shouldn't be teaching.

PROS: This class is a very interesting class. You basically sit there for an hour and listen to Professor Aprile tell you stories.  The tests are pretty straightforward CONS:  The class is a lot of work and is lecture based. If you miss a lecture, you will be left behind

She does read off a paper but that's because she is telling you the stories of mythology. If you think she is rambling then you aren't paying attention. It's not too much, but you have to write down EVERYTHING! Then reguritate it on the test and you will get an A. Sometimes I would have to read the book for discussion post but it was easy enough.

Very boring lectures. She literally just reads off a paper in class. Very sarcastic at times when asked a question. Tests are too long for the time given. I recommend to not take that class. I did great in all my classes this semester except in hers, because she doesn't really teach, all reading in class.
Very boring lecturer.
Poor teacher. Easy material but not given enough time to finish test in class. I think she is new though.

Best elective class I've taken! It was kinda easy because I love mythology, but if you are not a fan of reading 30pg chapters and memorizing names, events, & theories do not take it. Tests are basically over lecture and book. If you study hard you'll pass. I ALWAYS finished the tests (ppl complained about the test being too long for an hr class)

I have taken classes in McCombs as well as the school of natural sciences and this, an arts class, is the hardest class I've taken at UT. She expect you to memorize 270+ different pictures of artifacts that all look the same. And it isn't simple fact either. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. it isn't worth the effort.

Completely unrealistic expectations! This is an Intro course and half or more of the students are non-majors and she expects everyone to memorize the what, where, when and significance of EVERY SINGLE artifact, building, and sculpture we have EVER SEEN in class or in the book. Absolutely ridiculous! This is like an UD Art History class! Do not take

I liked her class a lot, probably since I liked Mythology. I didn't like how the final was 40% of my grade, and the final had so much writing. So. Much. Writing. There was a 4 page essay, 4 short answers (each at least a page), and a bunch of multiple choice and defining. If you feel like stressing at the end of the semester, take it.

Very poor teacher. Reads off a sheet for the entire 50 min and mumbles her sentences. Worst of all, when I had her she designed her tests so that no one could finish (not even on purpose). She's new and I think she got flustered and didn't know how to conduct the class during those 4 days we missed because of the weather. AVOID

She talks really fast, but if you write down everything she says and know the information well before tests, you will have no problems! If you are not a fast note taker, read the book, but I never opened the book and had no problems!

She was a really good professor. After a few classes though, the class (which comprised of 9 students) figured that we have to ask questions because she literally can talk non-stop for an hour straight. She used power points for her slide so there is at least some visual aids in the class. There will be a lot of reading though.

She is ridiculously passionate. Honestly, it really is a TON of information in only THREE tests, so there's a ton of studying needed for each test. That being said, people grumble about it being super hard, BUT it really isn't If you take decent lecture notes a ton of those too!) and read the SUMMARIES online, NOT the book. Study SMART. Easy A.

Avoid this class as much as you can. Way too much required reading. Too much material to even attempt to learn. She's annoying. She has this annoying 2 second cough every few minutes that she has from the first day of class. The tests are impossible. STAY AWAY

Only take this class if you're already interested in Greece and mythology! If you are then you will LOVE it, tests can be long but are all multiple choice. If you pay attention and look at the book you'll do fine. It's really not hard but you will have to study a little, but she's amazing. If you don't have an interest you probably won't like it.

Mythology is very easy if you go to lecture and read the textbook.  The tests reflected what was taught in class and usually didn't have bad questions.  The final was very long, but not difficult.  I would take another class by this professor

The tests are too heavily weighted and are tested over too much information. There's three tests and they are 90% of your total grade. She enjoys the subject a lot and teaches with enthusiasm but the workload is way too much. I somewhat enjoy mythology, but a lot of the material covered is very boring. I don't recommend taking the class at all.

I had no interest in Mythology before taking her intro course, but I enjoyed her as a professor. Her passion for what she teaches made it hard not to enjoy the class, despite no interest in the topic. Also, I did not find it to be an overly difficult class.

HARD professor. Rambled on during lecture. Way too  much reading expected. Tests were DIFFICULT! Thought this may be an interesting class that would make it easier to comprehend...the joke was on me. Would never take a class from her again.
lectures were interesting but be prepared to STUDY!!! and READ!!, test were also difficult. This class demands a lot of work.

Worst professor i have ever had. She reads off a paper the entire semester in a monotone voice and expects students to read close to 50 pages a night. I could not stay awake during class. The test covered way too much material and there was about 4 one-paged essays per test. The material was interesting, but not worth all the work.

As a junior classics major, I expected this class to be a joke. Hardest class I have taken, ever. The professor reads off a paper during lecture and then expects you to read for an hour and a half a night. She doesn't respond to emails, and in office hours she is condescending.

Worst professor I have ever had. Rambles from one thing to another. Expects you to know way too much material necessary for a non major course. Extreme amounts of reading. Lectures are boring since she just talks non-stop. Do not take her if you plan on maintaining a good GPA. I usually do not rate, but I had to which shows how bad this professoris

The class was a little on the hard side and I wasn't expecting the amount of work for an introductory course. But the class isn't boring in the lectures and she knows what she's talking about. If you are the least bit interested in greek society at all i would take the course and do the readings as you get them because the class isn't that hard

Very hard professor! There was a ridiculous amount of material covered on tests and she had them planned by the minute.  no time to stop for a sec and think if you want to finish.  expect lots of reading. If you do go to class you will learn a lot and she is interesting to listen to but I don't recommend her for anyone who is not that major

I really really liked this professor. She always knew exactly what she was talking about, was very well prepared for lectures and never wasted time or bored you in lecture. However, this class was SOOOO much work. It was impossible to keep up, and the tests are all really difficult. It requires alot of time and intense studying. Be forewarned.
She's a good professor and has absolute understanding of what she's teaching. You will read A LOT!! so be prepared. Test tend to be difficult.

Overall I would say she is a good teacher, but be prepared to read a lot!  She definitely knows her stuff but expects us to know too much stuff.  If you keep up the readings, you will learn a lot, but it takes some quite a bit of effort to do well in the class. Kinda sucks to do that much work if if the class has nothing to do with your major.

I can't say enough great things. Very caring and gives wonderful feedback. By far the most supportive and invested professor I have had. Her students are lucky to have her. Expect a well-structured class that you will really learn from.

Took for Rhetoric of City Streets. You get to choose a topic related to Austin that interests you to research for the whole semester. Most smaller assignments are completion pass/fail, with two large essays, and one final multimedia project. Definitely recommend!

I loved taking Rhetoric of City Streets with Professor Taylor so much that now every time a new course schedule comes out, I check for her name specifically to see if she's teaching a new class that I could take. There is writing, obviously, but she gives you plenty of class time to work on the projects and offers great, constructive feedback.

a true hidden gem for a writing flag. tookrhetoric of city streets with her and do not regret it. super flexible and caring and the class is actually very interesting. papers do tend to be on the heavier side, but taylor is always willing to help and grades leniantly. you also have a lot of opportunities for extra credit!
Lectures were very helpful and offers a lot of extra credit.

Assignment instructions can be ambiguous. Adds a lot of unnecessary assignments to the course that do not help enhance our knowledge or performance in lab. It seems like their purpose is to waste our time. The professor is very nice, and when she lectures, it is helpful. However, she only lectures for 10-15 minutes once a week.

This class is well-organized and an easy A, but the workload for a 2 hr credit is considerable. Weekly reflection essays & PyMOL activities often took hours, plus there are weekly lab quizzes to study for and pre-lab assignments due. Labs are helpful but incredibly long. She offers lots of extra credit and drops your lowest quiz though.

W Prof Seminars always introduced to us new things for research/ECs. Lab quizzes were tricky as they tested on some random specific details in the protocol. My TAs were THE BEST (shout out to Janice and Tu-Quyen), always super helpful. Labs were longish, a lot of EC, PyMol project was fun, practical was light, a lot of busy work (my only complaint)

Dr. Garrett is genuinely the most kind and caring professor I've had at UT. The course can have a heavy-ish workload if you leave everything to the last minute but the TAs are so understanding. So accessible outside of class if you have any questions about the major, career plans, etc!!

Dr. Garrett makes it very easy to succeed in this class, if you're willing to put in the effort. Certain weeks can be very assignment heavy (never more than 3-4hrs outside lab), but you always know what to expect and there's never any surprises. Canvas is organized very well, and Dr. Garrett/TAs are very kind/receptive w/ questions and feedback! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Garrett is incredibly kind and compassionate. The Lab quizzes are pretty tricky, but they don't count for that much of your grade. The Reflection Essays (Lab Reports + PyMol work) are incredibly - and unnecisarily - long (5-6 hours / week). End of Semester PyMol project was enriching and fun!

Dr. Garrett is really sweet. Seminars were a bit boring but very interactive. I was in the FRI lab, so we did have a shorter lab and less labs to attend to so that was nice. I absolutely loved my TA's (Emma and Caitlin y'all rock). They were really sweet and for someone that doesn't get things on the first try, they were really patient with me!

Dr. Garrett is awesome! The course is very organized and expectations are clear. The seminars were helpful for preparing for each week's lab, as well as for learning about college and career resources. She's very friendly and is generous with grading and extra credit points. She also makes the lab practical as unintimidating as possible.

very sweet professor! labs were fun and informative, but long ofc. beginning of class was pretty bad with TAs not knowing what is needed on lab notebooks. notebooks were SO long as well. mid-semester survey was a turning point: expectations were more clear and lab notebooks weren't as time consuming. take notes on a doc during lab and rewrite after

Very sweet professor! The class has a lot of cool labs that teaches you basic lab techniques. There's a lot of busy work each week, make sure to study for quizzes using the material provided focusing on the topics she tells you to. Some of the assignments are vague or not taught well which can be frustrating if you don't have time for office hours.

Organized course with plenty of resources laid out for you. Some experiments are cool, but there is a lot of busywork that goes with them. PyMol project at the end of the semester can be fun and plenty of guidance is given. Just do the work and you'll be good; everything is graded very leniently and getting an A is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: An insane amount of busy work that felt overwhelming and useless sometimes, but the grading was extremely lenient. Prof. Garret is also extremely caring and understanding and is always asking for feedback on how to improve the course to be more accommodating. You'll be fine as long as you keep your head up and turn everything in on time.

I loved this lab and seminar! I learned a lot more about biochemistry careers and skills and am much more prepared for my degree. I appreciated how she tried to keep things fun and was always available for office hours. Plus, my TAs were PHENOMENAL! There are a lot of assignments but it isn't bad, I just asked TAs when I was lost :) Honestly fun!

Be prepared for an insane amount of busy work. Every week is something to dread with the sheer amount of work you're expected to put into an intro-level biochem lab, so expect that you will receive the most useless and longest assignments that you will encounter at UT. I'd advise not taking this course, but it's unfortunately required for biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attending seminar is mandatory weekly (2 drops), a quiz for each lab session (+ a lab notebook and a reflection essay for each), a 3-week-long PyMOL project + presentation, and a lab practical (pass/fail). Overall, I enjoyed having Dr. Garrett for this course but there were lots of unnecessary (IMO) assignments even if they were graded easily.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, she really does care about everyone. Very helpful for learning about the bch major and different lab techniques. There are quite a few assignments between the weekly essays and lab notebooks, and they feel very unnecessary but grading is very chill. My UGCA was super helpful and accessible outside of class!

Dr. Koltz and Dr. Wolf were great lecturers! The content was mostly memorization and the exams were not too difficult. The exams did take a long time to be graded and there are outside projects that are easy but you do have to still do them. Very interesting class and content overall and both professors were kind and understanding.

Dr. Koltz and Wolf, along with the teaching team were nice and knowledgeable. The class itself wasn't bad, it's mainly memorization-based and exams are heavily graded. However, the class was harder than what I had expected it to be. There are a few projects that the TAs grade strictly on, and exams are a mix of MC and FRQ. Content is interesting!

The content of this class is not TOO difficult, but the course structure is set up a lot harder than it needs to be. Grades are almost completely based on exams, and each exam is graded atleast a month after it's taken. Grades aren't posted until LAST minute. They mentioned a curve, didn't apply it. So stressful not knowing how you're doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Koltz was a great lecturer, and she and Dr. Wolf made sure to cover everything needed for each exam! It's mostly memorization, but as long as you stay on top of the content it's manageable. The discussion projects are also a good grade boost, just make sure to actually try on them.

would definitely recommend for ecology! grade is based off of exams, a few writing assignments, and discussion section participation. i felt that everything was explained very well and exams were very fair. as a bio major this class was really interesting to me.

I personally did not enjoy this class, I felt that the lectures weren't that intriguing. The grades are hidden throughout the semester so you can't see how you stand in the class, and assignments can take 2-3 weeks to return to you. At least there's no final. If you really like ecology then this class might be for you, but it wasn't for me.

Easiest UGS ever, the only negative thing was at 8am. Attendance is not mandatory, but quizzes are based on lectures which are not accessible outside of class so...you miss out a lot if you don't attend. My TA Meiying Xu was the sweetest person ever and I got 100s on all essays that I personally thought were very mid when I wrote them.

Great UGS to take! The topic of the course was interesting and engaging. Dr. Liu is very kind and a good lecturer. The weekly quizzes are exactly what is covered in lecture, so if you take notes they will be very easy. There are multiple in-class essays, but they are pretty straightforward to prepare for and write. Gave extra points at the end.

Professor Liu is great! Her class is super engaging and the course itself is interesting. Your grade mostly depends on the TA and some of them are harsh graders. There are projects, quizzes every Friday, and 4 essays, and a debate. No extra credit, but she does drop 2 quizzes. Overall really easy UGS, highly reccomend!

Dr. Liu is an amazing professor! I took this class for the credit, but the content she covers is honestly really interesting. Write down what she says WORD FOR WORD during the lectures, because the quizzes are fully based on what she says. My TA graded a bit hard on the first essay, but after that you'll figure out her expectations for the essays.

Great UGS! Lectures and class content were extremely interesting, and weekly quizzes were almost rote what was taught in class.  Dr. Liu is also wonderful. She brought us breakfast burritos and pineapple bread to sweeten the 8 AM once! You will need to write 4 essays in class, but follow the rubric and you will be fine. No quiz makeups, but drops.

I loved Professor Liu so much, all you have to do is show up to class to do well on the weekly quizzes. There are 3 timed writes, but they are easy and you get to revise them after. She is very accessible outside of lecture, and my TA Gillian Sun was amazing, but I heard the other TA isn't as great. Overall, this class was awesome!

Strong and clear lectures. Friday quizzes were heavily tailored to class content, almost verbatim. I was worrying through the semester but she granted a bit of extra credit at the end of the course. If you put your best foot forward (and show up to lecture!!!) you don't need to worry about getting a good grade.
Easy class with free flags.  Take the bare minimum notes required (basically exactly what she writes down) and expect that material verbatim on the quizzes.

Dr. Liu was a great professor to take for UGS. did not take much of my time, just pay attention during lecture and you will be fine for the weekly quizzes. Communicate with your TA, they are beyond helpful!! I would def recommend to anyone looking for a UGS on the easier side.
she's awesome in what she does. i don't have much to say but you'll learn a lot from her ugs class! not too hard of a grader but make sure you adhere to the rubric!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Amy Liu was a very good lecturer that kept her students entertained and intrigued throughout classes. The weekly discussion sections were also a great time to go over lecture materials and the quizzes often got content directly from the lectures so if you paid attention you were fine. She was very generous with her grading and often gave 100s.

Not the easiest UGS, but it has flags. The weekly quizzes could be a bit challenging, but they are straight from the notes. We wrote 3 short essays and a final paper that built off of the three essays. The TAs were very helpful. The lecture content itself was interesting and Professor Liu outlined the lesson on the blackboard very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is clearly passionate about what she is teaching and her lectures reflect this. She was very accessible outside of class and is helpful with stuff not related to class as well. She is currently my advisor for my research and is helping along my journey to Fulbright. She has an amazing educational background.

Prof. Liu was great for UGS303. Very lecture heavy, you have to go to lecture if you want a good grade on the quizzes. The writing was not bad, an essay each week but the last major essay is just a combination of all three essays. Quizzes every week but if you go to lecture they are exactly from the lecture.

Easy class as long as you pay attention in class. Essays are straightforward, and you can get feedback from TAs. Although I took this class to fulfill a non-major degree requirement, I still enjoyed the class.

Dr. Liu is really passionate about Eastern European Politics and her lectures definitely reflect this. This class is very manageable and easy to get a good grade if you do the assignments. Quizzes can be pop quizzes but she usually lets you know before. Papers are not bad, just require a little bit of research. Overall great class and professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is a great professor. She is funny, caring, and easygoing. Lectures were interesting and recorded for reference. Dr. Liu writes notes on the board during each lecture, and quizzes are easy, covering the lectures' topics. There are no midterms or finals, just weekly quizzes & 4 papers which are easy. Keith was an amazing and friendly TA.

Dr. Liu is THE BEST professor I have ever had at UT. She cares about the success of her students and does an amazing job organizing the course. She gives amazing lectures and has very interesting insights into Eastern Europe with her vast experiences in the region. Often she gives you time to ask questions and the class is graded on many things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An amazing professor to have. Genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I had the opportunity to take part in her summer research internship course as well and learned a lot. Wish every gov class I took was taught by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked this UGS. It was way more interesting than I expected. Professor Liu is a great lecturer. Weekly quizzes are pretty easy if you go to class, and five are dropped. The essays are easy, and the TA's are very helpful. Final essay is basically the first three essays combined. I learned a lot more than I expected to in this class.

This is a pretty good UGS! There's a weekly quiz during discussion sections and if u attend the lectures (or watch the recorded lectures) and discussion sections and pay attention they should be easy As. There's a few papers throughout the semester that are graded pretty easily and you can ask the TAs for feedback. They also drop a few quizzes.

Professor Liu is a very organized professor. Her grading criteria are straightforward and detailed in the rubrics of writing assignments. There are fifteen quizzes but she drops the lowest five. There are no makeups for quizzes because she drops 1/3. The lectures are interesting and she is a more than fair professor. Show up to class & you'll be ok

I really liked lang, politics and culture for my ugs. not that much work and the grading is easy if you put in effort and listen in lectures. never did the required readings, just copied notes in lecture and thats all the short quizzes were over, wrote each of the papers in like 1 hour each, TA was so sweet and very helpful

Professor Liu is very nice and she is very passionate. If you choose to attend lectures, it is well worth the time. However, this class is an easy A even without doing so. Projects that could be done without attending any lectures made up most of the grade and tests were not too difficult if you do some reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu's lectures were informative and interesting. Although the quizzes were difficult, she announced them beforehand and kept only the top 10, For essays, grading was firm yet fair, and the TA provideed good feedback. If you read the assigned articles and do not fall behind, you will succeed in this class. I am glad that I took it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Considering this was just a UGS it took way more of my time than it should have. The quizzes were worded terribly the way they were graded was awful. Her lectures were super boring and always made me want to go to sleep. The class seemed like just a bunch of information no one needs or cares about and was just a waste.

TAKE HER IF YOU CAN. My class was quiz and paper focused, but for the most part, it was easy. After the sh00tings around campus, I reached out to her because I was unable to make it to class that morning. She checked back in with me a few days later and I think that shows her character. Also, Lang, Politics, and Culture (UGS303) is SO interesting.

I took Prof. Liu for lang, politics, and culture and it was an AMAZING UGS course. I highly recommend taking it; it was an easy A, she writes the notes on the board, 3 short essays and 1 final essay, and straightforward quizzes. The TA, Katy, was also PHENOMENAL so 100% take it with her! Loved this class <333 Take it if ur looking for an easy UGS !
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I feel like Language, Politics, and Culture with Dr. Liu was a pretty good choice for my UGS. The quizzes can be hard but they're not worth that much and 4 get dropped. The heart of the course is 3 short, easy to write papers, and the final paper is essentially just copying and pasting those 3 essays together with transitions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer, and the material is interesting. The multiple choice were difficult and the cheat sheet she allows,if she allows one,will help only marginally. If you have the option between multiple choice and written assignment,choose the written assignment . Do all assignments and you'll get a least a B.
Professor Liu has a real passion for what she does. She is very kind and willing to work with you. However, her grading and guidelines is often unclear, particulary in her writing assignments.
Prof Liu is one of the best proffesors at UT. I love the way she lectores and writes notes on the board. Her teaching format is perfect and lectores are always interesting.
Class was called Politics of Eastern Europe but more history than politics. She gives good lectures and writes excellent notes on the board. Pretty easy but also interesting class.

Dr. Liu really enjoy teaching student, she's more interested in you learning than to grade your works. Lecture is more like high school history class, you basically listen to GER stories and copy down the notes from the board. Her notes are very clear. No need for reading because she teaches you everything in lecture. Quizzes are easy.
Miss Liu has a cool background and likes to relate the class to her experiences. Her lectures are extremely clear. Class is not mandatory. Some quizzes, two essays, a project, and no final.

Easy class with clear grading expectations. Make sure to put effort into the weekly discussion posts, show up to section meetings, and go to most lectures because attendance is taken randomly. I wasn't super interested in this class but Professor Thompson did a good job teaching and I would definitely recommend her if you need to take this class.

One of the best classes I've taken. Only thing you have to worry about is your participation grade in the discussion sections since they weigh heavy. Most of the class work is made up weekly DBs over the topic of the week. Exams (2 total) are easy if you follow the review provided.  Keep track of deadlines, attend class and you should be fine.
Great class, tons of extra credit, not too much homework, and the exams are incredibly easy if you follow the review. Attendance is taken randomly, so make sure to show up to lectures.

Sweetest prof and truly cares about what she teaches + she's pretty quick to respond outside of class. There are short participation assignments at the end of lecture once in a while and the exams are really easy if you prepare (class Avg. ~90). Around 10 EC opportunities, each worth 0.5 pts for a max of 2.5 pts on your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is a great lecturer, and the class is pretty easy. Not a lot of homework, just reading and discussions. The worst part is that she takes attendance on random dates, so you really want to go to every lecture, and the discussion sections feel a bit useless to me. Overall, though, really good professor and class, 8.5/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet, engaging lectures, comprehensive, kind. Reasonable with grading and assignments. This was a very good intro GRG class.

I love Dr. Thompson! We had short lectures and the labs are 60% of your grade. Class is usually outside and it's amazing to be able to learn how to do geographical measurements in the real world. She's a fair grader, and I would recommend to never miss class. Labs are during class time unless your group doesn't finish. She's very flexible and kind!

She is super sweet and kind, as well as funny and relatable!! Class consists of 3 exams, the final one being cumulative; it's a lot of information given to you in lectures, so study well because the exams are the majority of the grade. There will be extra credit, I suggest doing all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has been one of the kindest professors I've had. While the material can be challenging, if you pay attention and study, you will be fine. You can tell that she cares a lot about each student and wants to see everyone succeed, so utilize office hours if you need! She is also funny and very relatable, which makes class enjoyable.

She's very caring! There are three exams (40%) that are fill-in-the-blank. The rest of the class is composed of daily discussion boards at the end of lectures, a few in-class assignments, and a few outside-of-class papers. They are great buffers to the hard exams. If you put in the work, you will succeed (don't rely on the study guide, though).
Dr. Meeks is a very good intro teacher; the class is very lecture-heavy, and you have to pay attention to succeed on the tests. She offers a lot of extra credit, but there is a lot of McGraw-Hill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's an incredibly fair professor. I think due to the pandemic, her class wasn't exactly how she would have taught it in person, so it was a bit of a disappointment after all the good things I'd read about her lectures. It was mostly just reading from the textbook. Regardless, she wanted students to do well and was very available and caring.

She's a great professor. Lectures were very interesting and informative, and the tests were pretty easy. There is a textbook, but you don't really need to read it unless you want to. There's basically a weekly extra credit assignment, with extra credit also given for attendance. It's an easy A, and lot's of fun!

She was a  nice lady. The book is not necessary as the exams are mainly based off her PowerPoints. They're very straight-forward, so as long as you pay attention and read your notes a couple of times, you should EASILY get an A. Only issue about her is that her lectures usually ended late. She gives extra credit for papers and perfect attendance.
Had plenty of time to take notes by hand. She's adorable, and grades fairly. Show up, take notes, and you'll be sure to get an A+. Ended up with a 100 in the class.  Loved her.

I love all things psychology and I couldn't handle this class, it was so boring. You just went to class and filled in powerpoint slides she would give you, you also have to use a laptop because she goes way to quickly to take by hand. Her lectures go along with the book so if you don't go to class you can use that. She gives a lot of extra credit.

Seemed to be pressed for time every lecture and discouraged class discussion by not calling on students very often. All material was not covered in class so the book is a must. Attendance isn't mandatory but gives extra credit if you attend or write journals which are only a page long each. Seemed to be unavailable outside of class through email.

Dr. Meek is the sweetest lady ever! She treats her students like they're her children in a way. Anyways...she is very EASY! Tests are basically just like her powerpoints so reading the book is not really necessary but it does help. It was an easy A for me. I would reccomend her!

Dr. Meeks is sweet and well...meek. She makes her own PowerPoints and basically lectures about the exams and shows videos in class. She's approachable and has 4 exams with no drops, but overall the class is easy so there's no need. She has a few extra credit opportunities but nothing that can save your grade.

4 tests without any drops. There is no extra credit other than the stuff given on the exam which is only 3-4 points extra. Her cutoff for an A second semester was a 94 which is pretty steep. Take anthropology instead of psychology.
Very easy. Tests very similar to lectures

Dr. Weems is truly passionate about cell biology! He is super funny, and will answer any question you have. Exams are open note. Discussion sections are extra credit, BUT they are super helpful if the TA continues to be AJ. There is a lot of material and readings, but I have truly learned a lot! He is super strict on deadlines so keep up.

Dr. Weems is a super funny and engaging lecturer. I can tell that he cares about the learning of his students. He really values teamwork in class so make sure you find good groupmates at the beginning of the year. The only criticism I have is that this class is a LOT. It has all the same coursework as advanced cell biology except with exams added.

Really funny guy, lectures were always interesting and easy to understand. A lot of the content was reading dependent, but it isn't anything super difficult to grasp. Great professor, take him for MBS 320 if you don't mind reading and writing every week.
He's a pretty solid prof with funny lectures. The tests are tricky but they're open note. Attendance is part of your grade

Amazing prof. Her lectures are super engaging and she is obviously very knowledgable about what she is teaching. There is so much extra credit and the exams are very easy if you read the textbook and use the study guides she posts.
Dr. Angulo is my queen and I love her. She is hilarious, her lectures are amazing, and her passion for the job and the students is so abundantly clear.

I LOVED this class! I looked forward to it each week, and Professor Angulo is so caring! The assignments and exams were straightforward, and our papers were always about interesting topics. I highly recommend this class! I love my small group in the class, and Isabella was an amazing TA this semester! Also, I loved the extra credit opportunities.

Take her if you can! Dr. Angulo genuinely cares about you and your success. She tailors course content to make it more relevant for students— her lectures are SO interesting. I didn't know anyone in this class but they all feel like family now. Exams are super fair if you attend lectures and read the textbook. Isabella was also the sweetest TA.

Dr. A made this class so enjoyable! And even though I had already learned a lot of the concepts, the class never felt boring to me. Lectures are team-based: the professor goes over the slides, and we break into teams to discuss them. Dr. A is so kind and knowledgeable, and I would highly recommend taking this class!

Dr. Angulo is such a sweet and amazing professor. I would take a class with her again 100%. The assignments consist of two-page writing assignments. The exams are very understandable if you go to lecture and read the book. She is extremely good at explaining things and very easy to talk to.
Dr. Angulo is by far the best professor I had at UT. She is simply an amazing person! She makes coming to class worthwhile and loves interacting with her students. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Angulo was one of the best professors I've had at UT. She really cares about her students and is willing to help, not only with class but with other career goals. She has very straightforward lectures that relate well to the tests. The workload is very manageable, interesting, and relates back to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the asynchronous online version during first-session summer which was taught by the lecture videos led by Sam and Paige during the semesters, grade based on 27 RAS (5 dropped), 2 writing assignments, and 5 benchmarks (1 dropped), all very easy and open-note, just keep up with the lectures and readings by taking notes and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were very fun and engaging! The only downside was that she didn't record the lectures or post lecture notes because she wanted us to make friends with other students. I reached out to her recently for some help getting an internship, she was super helpful and I wish I could retake her class!

Dr. Angulo is an amazing educator. Her lectures were incredibly interesting, and she is personally a very kind and caring individual. She does not post her slides so I would highly recommend attending every class, but honestly it's worth it because her content is very interesting. Overall one of my favorite professors at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: OMG!!! seriously best professor I have ever had. She is so caring, and her lectures are really engaging. If you need help she will definitely work with you!!! Attend the lectures and do the written reflections on time and you will be fine! Tests are straight from study guides. If I could take her again I would!!!!

dr. angulo is the most amazing professor i've ever had! she genuinely cares about all of her students and really wants you to succeed. she provided us with a ton of resources for the future and even brought snacks for us! she's big on making sure her students engage with the topics so she likes to give group discussions. can't recommend her enough!

I took the asynchronous online summer class version of PSY301, with the lectures coming from Dr. Gosling and Dr. Harden. I never really interacted with Dr. Angulo, but the class was structured well with engaging on-demand lecture videos. Graded from 2 writing assignments, 22 RAS, and 4 Benchmarks. All open-note. Favorite online class I've taken!

Dr A was one of the best professors I've ever had at UT. You can tell she really cares about her students and what she teaches. Her lectures were super interesting and I seriously looked forward going to her class. She gives a comprehensive study guide before each exam that, if you study it, you will easily get an A. Such a kind woman!!

One of my favorite profs! Dr A is so clearly caring about her students in and out of class, and gives really interesting lectures. Very easy A -- honestly, almost too easy of a course. Textbook is a little expensive, but super interesting, and correlates well with the course/test material.

Loved this class!! Prof Angulo was always very kind and engaging. Grade based on weekly reflections and 4 easy tests. Attendence is not for a grade but she does not post lecture slides. Regardless, I always looked forward to lecture because it was super interesting! Easy A!

Dr. Angulo is an amazing professor and always made lectures very engaging and interesting. She genuinely cares for the well-being of her students and offered extra support for students pursuing graduate school. She made study guides for each exam, so exams were straight-forward and easy to study for.

Outright amazing class/professor. Dr. Angulo is probably one of the best lecturers at UT; she applies her expertise in psychology to teaching very well. Content and instruction genuinely broadened my knowledge, and exams were not difficult if prepared for adequately. Written assignments were engaging and presented new opportunities for learning.

There's a 2 page reflection due every week, but they're not too difficult. Dr. Angulo is really knowledgeable about the subject, and she goes at just the right pace in her lectures. My only complaint is that she doesn't upload lectures after class anywhere, so make sure you know someone in class who can share notes if you miss a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Took her social psychology class last semester and loved it! She was super helpful and engaging, and you can tell that she really cares about her students. There were many easy in-class opportunities for extra credit, and her lectures were super interesting. 3 noncumulative tests, I missed one because of the flu and was able to easily retake it.

Professor Angulo easily became my favorite professor at UT. She is so passionate whenever she teachers and cares a lot about her students. She very interactive and does her best to answer any questions you may have during lecture and always allows her students to make comments on the material she lectures on. I definitely recommend her class!

One of my favorite classes. I enjoyed going to lecture even if it was cross campus. I would recommend making friends with the people next to you since we have a lot of in-class "talk to the person next to you" application based questions (not for credit). Tests were scenarios based on material covered that module. Very interesting class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was easily the most fascinating and fun class I took this semester. Dr. Angulo makes the content extremely fascinating and encourages a lot of in-class discussion so the lecture doesn't feel boring. There are only 3 exams (no drops) and weekly reflections that are very easy to manage. Exams are pretty easy and class is very fun to take

Love love love Dr. A, she's an amazing professor! If you're looking for an extra elective/psych requirement to fulfil definitely take this class, the material is insightful and interesting. Exams are easy, weekly essays that are not as bad as they sound. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Take this class!

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS CLASS!!
 Dr. Angulo has been my favorite professor at UT. All of her lectures and interesting and interactive I never left class without learning something new that I could apply to my life. As long as you go to class, pay attention and take notes the tests are fairly easy.

Dr. Angulo is amazing. I always looked forward to going to her class and genuinely enjoyed the lectures. She is so kind and intelligent. Her class also genuinely improved my life-- in studying, relationships, mindset, etc. The tests are not too difficult as long as you go to class and take notes. She also offers plenty of extra credit.

Such an amazing professor and an interesting class. Make sure to attend lectures and take notes! Tests were very easy as long as you put in some effort. She also gives out study guides for the exams which are very helpful! There are weekly writing reflections but are not graded harshly. The homework is often enjoyable and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: BEST CLASS EVER!!!! So many interesting topics discussed, and Dr. Angulo is by far the most intelligent and caring professor I have EVER had. There are weekly essays (completion) and exams make up all of your grade, but the exams are very simple if u pay attention in lecture. Many of her test questions are direct quotes from her slides.

Dr.A is amazing! Shes very kind and definitely loves her job!!! Her tests have detailed study guides and tell you what to look for!! Attendance wasnt mandatory but 70% of the tests are based of the lectures!!

I absolutely adore Dr. A! Her lectures are very engaging and interesting (given you are interested in psych). Her tests are super easy because her study guides tell you everything you need to know. There is also plenty of extra credit opportunities! Overall, I can't recommend her enough! She is the best!

The lectures were very engaging and explored a plethora of interesting topics. However, the majority of your grade depends on these 8-question benchmarks that consist of these questions where the answers can often be very ambiguous.

Although I took this class 100% online and Dr. Angulo wasn't in the lecture videos, she is an awesome professor. The grade breakdown is very clear cut. We had no midterms, just weekly benchmarks. The content is actually very engaging and interesting. Note: If you are taking PSY301, look into the PSY301 research requirement before takingthis course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor. Really cares about her students and explains material very well. 100% recommend.

Dr. A was an amazing professor. I took Intro to Psych Honors, so the class was relatively small, but still very engaging. Her lectures are detailed and she makes it very interactive so that you're never bored. There's only 3 tests which are easy if you study, and she gives plenty of extra credit. She's a very caring professor.

You don't really see much of Dr. Angulo as this class is asynchronous and uses the regular lectures from Dr. Gosling and Dr. Harding. However, the class is well structured with weekly tests and lectures that bring the material in an interesting way. Definitely take in the summer, it is way better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was amazing!! I took this class in the summer of COVID - I really hope this pandemic ends soon :(... - The lectures were from Gosling and Harden, but she was always available if you had questions! Some complain, but I think this class is rlly straightforward. Just keep up with the lectures and readings, and you'll do great. Weekly benchmarks!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Angulo is straightforward when it comes to what to expect on tests. She provides detailed study guides and many of the questions come straight from lecture. PowerPoint slides aren't published online so I would recommend attending class regularly. She's approachable and very kind to her students. Would highly suggest taking her class!
I really enjoyed this class. All exams are online and she gives study guides that are helpful. Her lectures follow her power points, but she doesn't post the power points so take good notes.

She was a great professor and I got a lot out of this class just from attending. There were a lot of class discussions. She was funny and really wanted to make sure students understood the material. Easy A. Visit her outside of class if you have any interest in grad school. She was so, so helpful with application information.
