She's a very fair grader, doesn't try to trick you, but must EARN an A

She honestly writes her own reviews. The class should defiantly not be a 5.0 in any category. This class is really really boring. She is also very annoying and very repetitive during the lecture. One of the worst professors on this campus. Not worth my tuition. By the way I'm an ADV major.

She was funny and made lectures interesting and entertaining! Tests were all multiple choice and pretty much all based off her lectures - you don't really have to read the textbooks. She doesn't round up, but there are extra credit opportunities.

I loved this class and i loved her as a professor. She makes the class fun and easy to understand. Also the tests were easy as long as you read your notes and sometimes textbook. Attendance not mandatory but the bonus questions were based on class lectures. it was an easy A.
She's enthusiastic!
Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand. She is engaging and gives you bonus questions that are super easy if you came to class!
Pretty easy class. Grade based on exams and in-class assignments (which are basically tests). Lectures are definitely worthwhile.
She's so funny and easy-going!
This man is the worst. Avoid at all costs. He does not know how to teach besides reading from a PowerPoint and is not helpful when asked questions.

You can definitely get used to his accent, but not his teaching style. Just reads directly off slides that could be posted later and achieve same effect. Lots of homework, but manageable since there's an answer key.

Once you get past his accent he's actually pretty funny, but it took me a while to start understanding him and honestly I still don't sometimes. Classes are him reading off of slides with handouts that are fill in the blank. 2 exams, some cases, and homework from the textbook and the course packet. I don't find the textbook useful.

Prof Atiase may not be my favorite professor ever, but he definitely is not as bad as the other reviews here make him out to be. There is a lot of written homework due before each class, but it is completion and he just wants you to attempt it before actually seeing the solutions in class. Tests are very similar to the review problems which is nice

Homework structure supports memorization, not learning. Lectures are worthless fill-in-the-blank notes that he reads from. He either assigns busy work or problems that he has not prepared you to complete. Hard to understand due to accent. Only reason I did okay was bc his test was near identical to the review. Lots of wasted time in class. ACC 312H

Don't do it! Claims that he doesn't give us busy work, but that is all he gives us. Teaches too fast, and has the audacity to call exams "parties". He is a very smart guy, as he's worked at some very high up companies in the world, but teaching just isn't his thing. Avoid him at all costs please, unless you are feeling like a risk-taker.

Prof. Atiase is by far my least favorite professor I have ever taken. His sarcastic attempts at humor seem to demean students more often than encourage or amuse them. You come to class to copy down verbal notes which could be posted online instead. Homework is explained, in a confusing, hard to understand manner, leaving you to learn on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class consists of you doing a ton of reading and written homework/handouts before class (at least 2 hrs for each "lecture"), coming to class to copy notes verbatim that he won't post online, and then getting called on to answer the questions you did before class without a good explanation. You have to teach yourself--just avoid altogether
Her class was very difficult but she did a great job of making difficult material more easy to understand.
challenging, but she is fair
The class itself is pretty tough and not just because of the subject matter. It's how she grades. I really wish I took this class with a different professor! Avoid, if you can.
A very good professor, helpful, good explanations.
Sometimes hard to understand and hard to follow in lectures. Also, very uninteresting to listen to because of the way she teaches
No Comments

I took his beginner level (6week long) Spanish course and was forced to pay 62$ for a program to do work that wasn't even graded. Yet he expected everyone to finish (literally) 12 assignments every day. His lectures were unfocused, and I spent most of my time in breakout rooms w peers. Despite him saying he cared it was abundantly clear he didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The quizzes were a little tricky but he really offers a lot of content to study for both exams and quizzes, and makes class really fun to go to. He engages with each student and genuinely cares for each person's wellbeing. Most fun I've had taking a class in college for a long time, and I will miss this prof

I took SPN 314 with Prof Aviles in summer 2021, and I really enjoyed it. He is super enthusiastic and helpful, and he really cares about the students' learning. There was a lot of homework because it was a summer class, but it wasn't too challenging. Overall, it was a great course and I highly recommend taking it with Prof Aviles!

I took her arabian nights class, and really loved it. the class is interesting, and Noy is very knowledgeable. she is a hard grader, however, and sometimes frustratingly so -- a few times i thought about throwing my computer out the window. LOTS of reading. too much. not burdensome, though. overall, id recommend for people interested.

Took Arabic Lit. Highly difficult class yet rewarding -- you learn a lot! Readings are super difficult. Noy's lectures are amazing and she is easy to reach outside of class and understanding. PLEASE CONTRIBUTE IN THIS CLASS. It's small and discussion based, don't take it if you're not ready to talk. DO THE READINGS, she likes to see effort!

Honestly one of the best professors I've had. The content was phenomenal and she is such a kind professor. It is reading heavy and discussion based so make sure to read or at least skim. No tests however there are 4 written assignments and weekly journals, but so far they have not given me any issue and 2 of the papers are only 2 pages long.

Uses Socratic method to a fault, basically to have students teach for him. Grades are completely arbitrary and he provides no feedback. I received high A's on all homework papers (no feedback provided), and this was completely inconsistent with the final grade. He spent half a class arguing he should be allowed to buy votes. Not approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Avraham is really sweet and loves torts.  He explains a lot of things at a level even a 5 year old could understand. Some other readings were hard to understand.  Overall, highly recommended.
Avraham is funny and makes class enjoyable.  I had him for Torts. He really covers everything he wants you to know during class, so don't miss class!

She TRULY cares about whether or not her students understand the material. She checks in to make sure we understand what she is saying throughout the lecture and advocates for lots of practice tests. Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had, you should definitely take her class!

Best math teacher I've ever had. I took her for calc one and for lectures you would read the textbook before class and then complete a really short online assignment. The weekly homework load was very manageable. subject was explained very well and always answered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a new professor at UT but friendly. Lectures are straightforward. Homeworks are short. She offers plenty of support if you're confused. Participation work is required on Mondays, but she gives makeups for it. Exams closely follow the practice materials and HW, though they can get tricky—especially the final. Highly recommend!

The course content itself is incredibly easy. If you get stuck, she is very helpful over email/office hours. I did very well on the HWs and midterms, but I just barely got an A bc of the final, which is weighted 30%. In-class activities once a week for a participation grade. Handwriting is a bit difficult to read at times.

Really great experience taking her for Probability 1. Explains everything very clearly and tests are pretty easy as long as you are familiar with the material. Gives a lot of really good prep material for the tests too.
Really great and caring professor. Good lecturer as well, although attendance wasn't mandatory — take if you can.

Really sweet guy, but like other reviews said he kind of struggles with lecturing in a clear, easy-to-understand way if you don't already know the subject material. It's clear he knows a lot about what he's teaching, but you'll definitely need to study outside of class. Overall a pretty average class experience.

He does seem very sweet, and I can tell he's trying, but for the portion I was there for (electrochemistry) I genuinely never had any clue what was going on during class. I felt like he was just saying things, but I could never follow the lecture. I did manage to do well on the first exam somehow, but honestly try for another professor if possible.
I found it kind of hard to be engaged with his lectures, but it's clear he knows what he's talking about. It was a pretty normal class I'd have to say, and he is very friendly and approachable.

For his materials chemistry course his test reviews did not actually prepare us for what would be on the tests. Topics would be on there we hadn't even really covered. He seems like he knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgeable, just not the best at preparing us for exams and thus our grades kind of took a hit because of this.

Dr. Aubrey class wasn't the best but it was manageable. He gives you two attempts on the reading and lecture quizes which is pretty nice. The problem is that if you dont do the reading before lecture you will be lost in his lectures. He's a great professor to talk to about research and he will try his best to help you out. He's very approachable.

Dr. Aubrey seems like such a sweet, knowledgeable professor, but he can't teach. His lectures are quite scattered and he struggles to simplify things for the intro-level course this is. The lecture quizzes are also absurdly difficult. It's his second year, so hopefully he'll figure it out soon. But for now, brace yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: very disorganized; posted the study guide the day before the test; hated lectures; I liked the material I was learning but boring lectures and intense readings make it hard to engage with the class; it is an especially hard transition from laude to aubrey... good luck :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he is trying his best, as he has just started teaching. however, exams do not resemble quizzes and reviews are not at the level of the exams, so studying is difficult. feels like the level is way too high for a gen chem class. i am biased since i did not take ap chem, so i do have to put in extra effort since this material is completely new.

I would definitely avoid Dr. Aubrey for CH302C if possible. It was his first time teaching the course, he wasn't clear on how grading worked and didn't attempt to explain concepts in class whatsoever. I pray that Laude goes back to teaching it because he is not good with underclassmen. Harsher ratings were suspiciously removed...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Aubrey is knowledgeable about the topics he taught, but it was his first time teaching this course, so his lectures were confusing even after reading the textbook pages that were assigned. This was often due to his wanting to talk about real-life applications of these topics. He also taught us inorg chem instead of prepping us for ochem.

As everyone said, he's a brilliant man. He clearly knows what he's teaching but doesn't yet know how to deliver it (at least not to freshmen). He records his lectures, so I would advise skipping class and watching them on your own time. The books are difficult to understand, but the lectures contain relevant information that is tested on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is a very kind and smart man, but he probably shouldn't be teaching first-year students. I am sure his upper division and graduate courses are amazing, he just expects a bit too much for gen chem. That being said, the class is extremely doable if you work hard to understand the concepts and you will be better off because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is an incredibly smart and kind man, but his class is difficult and he doesn't seem to have much experience teaching freshman. Textbook is hard to understand, and the course is almost entirely self-taught. There's hardly any homework to cushion your grade (5%), and quiz questions are made from scratch which makes them hard to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is a brilliant professor, he doesn't have experience teaching a freshman, general chemistry audience though. I'm genuinely confused why he was picked to teach this class, but it was clear he tried his best to deliver factual, relevant information. Tips to succeed: Housecroft will not help you, but study groups and ChemLibre will.

Lectures are hard to follow and are frequently focused on interesting but ultimately irrelevant applications or details of course content, making tests and quizzes very difficult. The textbooks are the best way to learn the test/quiz relevant material. He's kind and clearly very knowledgeable about the content, but doesn't convey it well.

Prof. Aubrey makes Gen Chem 2 pretty challenging because he chooses to cover very complex topics other professors don't, but it's still a very doable course. No homework outside of class besides readings, and the quizzes over lectures. Exams are fair game, but definitely have to take good lecture notes and put work in to grasp concepts

I don't think Dr. Aubrey should be teaching Gen Chem 2. His quizzes are hard and you can't study for them because he puts a harder version of the example that you have never seen, he makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. He doesn't explain things during lecture and expects us to know a lot (we are 2nd semester first-year students).

Prof. Aubrey is new at teaching this class and pretty bad at it so far. His quizzes are inconsistent, difficult, and have had lots of mistakes. He does not explain things at all and assumes we should know everything. This is Gen Chem 2 for chem majors and makes me want to change my major. :(

This class is recommended for the chemistry major/honors track and so most of us thought we had to take it, but you do not have to! Dr. Aubrey is one of those guys that are just way too smart to be teaching intro to gen chem. Because he is so smart he does not explain nor teach very well. He is not a good teacher, but he is nice, I don't recommend.

The semester started rough with difficult quizzes that tanked grades, but slowly the structure of the class got better and more organized. Lectures are sometimes pretty boring, but you can tell Dr. Aubrey puts effort into his class and is always willing to help if needed. Dr. Aubrey is very nice, but I don't know if I would recommend his class yet.
The best faculty I've ever met.

He's definitely knowledgeable and speaks with coherence and confidence, but I found that I had to do a lot of learning after lectures to comprehend the concepts. Granted, that could be an issue on my part. Workload was manageable, but there would be 0 feedback left on assignments, which was odd. Advice: watch Coding With John and Bro Code!!

Definitely take Nando over him
-Next to no review material for exams, only one previous exam. Actual exam was way harder, ~70 avg no curve
-Tests and projects are much harder than other profs
-No in class test review or exam prep guidance
-Useless lectures, don't help with projects, just end up self studying 
Overall way harder than it should be

While Shi's lectures can sometimes be dry, he always tries to encourage class participation. He is a very talented developer and there is a lot to learn from him. The recitations and TA's were very useful for keeping up in the course. No final, but make sure to leave plenty of time for the final project.
Enjoyed his teaching style. Went through many examples when teaching new concepts.

This Prof has useless lectures and is not understanding at all. He doesn't have practice exams and doesn't send out announcements that are crucial to passing assignments/the class.The lack of coordination among the professor and their TAs has negative consequences on students' grades. Take a different professor if you can.

Useless lectures, self-taught course/no guidance, unclear project requirements, no announcements on canvas, expected to check Piazza to do well/pass, harder projects than other profs, unreasonable expectations, not understanding/flexible, no Test reviews, unorganized exams, doesn't use IDE, unlear answers to questions, taught like a grad course.

She is such an amazing teacher and lecturer. She breaks down every concept completely from scratch so that everything is very digestible and easy to understand, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students understanding the material by the quality of her explanations and slides.

She is SOOO nice. Got super lucky with registering for her class for Fall 2024. Individual exams are 45% with the rest of the grade being group exams, group work, and instapoll. IMO the groups were big enough so that at least a few ppl could be on top of things, and even though the exams were hard, they weren't weighed heavily + small curves!
Honestly the best professor I had at UT—go to office hours and study using HER lecture slides and iClickers and you will come out fine.

Dr. Austin was awesome. She encouraged us to truly understand physiology by forming connections rather than simply memorizing facts. Most of our grade was derived from group assignments (weekly homework, iClicker, group exams). As much as I dreaded physiology entering the class, I left with a love of the subject and a deeper understanding as well.
Great professor, simplifies physio as much as she can. Class is doable. Many EC opportunities. Go to office hours for HWs. Austin clearly wants the best for students.

Dr. Austin is THE BEST. Study for exams by using HER lecture and exam review slides, explaining the concepts to yourself, as well as doing the practice problems for math-related topics/questions. She has learning objectives from another prof which you can do for extra practice but you should mostly focus on her slides and you'll be fine.

I LOVED Dr. Austin. Grade is based on group assignments every week, group exams, individual exams, iClicker participation and peer evaluation. Physiology is hard enough but she does a great job to give enough extra credit as a buffer. Don't slack off on group work from the get go. If you have the chance to take her, don't hesitate to do so!

goated professor. only downside is having to be put into random groups and doing all of you're assignments together so it sucks if you have a bad group. nevertheless, Dr.Austin is awesome and wants you to succeed.

Really enjoyed this class. The pre-lectures were helpful. Attendance is mandatory, because of the iClicker questions, but they help keep you paying attention. Homework assignments are done in groups. Exams with your group too if you want. Reading the textbook helps. Go to Dr. Austin's office hours!! She helps break down concepts

Dr. Austin is amazing! All of the homework, iClicker and exams are group work, which forces you to actually pay attention and help out your group. The material is a bit difficult if you are not interested, but her lectures are great and interactive. Attendance is mandatory because of iClicker questions given during lecture. Amazing overall!

Dr Austin is so kind and a great lecturer. She's so smart and passionate about physiology and teaching. She makes it attainable to know the material and understand it. The way she did group homework assignments was helpful and group exams were extremely helpful as well. She's so accessible outside of class as well as her TA's and they're so helpful

I loved Austin as a professor and she made the class more intriguing and forced you to be involved. Charismatic and light personality and brough positive vibes into every lecture. Take her for any class that you can because if you mess up, she is very generous and tells you exactly where you went wrong. Avg/easy HW and Exam difficulty, long HW's.

Dr. Austin is really nice and creates an environment where you can focus on learning without worrying about your grade. Her guidance is great, and she is a must take professor to enjoy your intro to proofs class. Overall 100% recommend taking her.

A very nice professor. The homeworks are insanely difficult, but she has tons of documents available to help with the homework. The tests are exactly like the test reviews and she is very helpful in getting people prepared for the tests. She doesn't explain some of the in depth concepts the best, but you at least understand how to do the problems.

One of the few amazing teachers at the ut math department, She breaks down complex proof topics into easy to understand lectures and practice problems. Tests were not too bad if you studied for them, and did the review problems. A lot of extra credit was given if you participated in class problems and presentation problems, definitely a must take.
Let us work with others in the class during the final minutes of the test. Often wouldn't explain concepts fully or in depth.

This review is for M 175T, Being You in Mathematics. It is indeed rather boring. However, I cannot deny that it is applicable to math majors, even pure math majors. Take this class to get your ethics flag done and perhaps learn a bit more about the major in the process.

This class is an introduction to the upper-level proof classes, and it has a reputation for being difficult since it is so different than all previous math courses. However, she is very good at teaching, is not too harsh on grading, and gives more than enough opportunities for success given you are willing to try.
She is one of the best (math) Professor in UT. Discrete math is typically easy, but she made it much easier. Exam reviews are very useful. Study homework, exam review and in-class examples!

Dr. Austin is probably the best math professor I've had at UT. Exams are pretty easy as long as you study. Showing up to class is important. Attendance isn't required, but you get engagement points for answering questions and she notices when you're not there. Dr. Austin is an amazing professor and a great person to have a connection with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BEST MATH TEACHER/PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!! Dr. Austin is amazing! I have sucked at math since I can remember and this is truly the first time I have understood it to the full extent. Her lectures are amazing, tests are easy with a independent portion and a collaborative portion, with maximum two-three assignments each week! Take this math!!!

I took M175T, Being You in Mathematics (there was no option for this). This class is crucial to any STEM major (mainly math majors) and teaches fundamental ethics and different job perspectives mathematicians can pursue with their degrees. Dr. Austin was very encouraging, and the course has really impacted my future.

If you need math credit, and are trying to find a good professor...Dr.Austin is the one!!!!! Please trust me on this one you guys!!! Her lectures are very easy and very understandable. Shes such a funny person as well, and she is very caring!!!! Best professor I have ever had!!!

Tests were pretty easy. None of the concepts were difficult, she mostly focused on teaching how to write proofs and basic logical reasoning. Only complaint is that towards the end she started letting students do the examples but the class then became just jotting stuff down and I wasn't sure if I was learning how to do the proofs correctly.

Dr. Austin made math easy!! pay attention in lecture & you'll get an easy A. At first it was hard to think about math from a logic perspective, but it gets so much easier - don't drop the course after the first lecture! Dr. Austin was quick to answer questions & she cares about her students. Exam questions came directly from content in review pptx.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE! Dr. Austin.  She made a seemingly boring class very relateable and applied real-life concepts.  I would say the only thing is that she does call on people in class, whether you raise your hand or not, but I would not let that be the reason you don't take her.  She's extremely sweet, and her exams were very fair and manageable.  Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT LISTEN!!! Guys this class lowk kicked my butt it was kinda difficult, the homework was graded harshly and I found myself LOST in like all the lectures. BUT there are lots of extra credit opportunities! I'm trying to keep my A rn. Apart from that, exams are kinda easy, and if you put in the work- you can pass

Dr. Austin is great and this class was literally the easiest class I have ever taken. Even if you think you're awful at math, you can definitely take this class. She walks you through everything and the exams are super easy.

this review is for m325, Dr. Austin is easily the best professor to take for proof writing. I highly enjoyed the content in this class, and there's tons of opportunities for extra credit. I found her class super engaging and inspiring, she truly helps you find your mathematical voice :-) also, easiest writing flag.

I would take every single class with Professor Austin. She is the most caring and kind professor I'll probably ever have. Tons of extra credit, you can literally ask her how to solve the homework, engaging lecturers, and straightforward tests. 1000/10 math class, take it if you can.

Dr. Austin is easily one of the best professors I have had at UT. I have taken two classes with her, and both were phenomenal. Her lectures are easy to follow (and to review later on). Her grading criteria is clear, and she has lots of opportunities to improve your grade.

PLEASE take this course if you need math credit. Collaborative exams, homework is gone over in class, fun and easy projects! Dr. Austin is so sweet and wants to make sure everyone does well plus she has lots of office hours! TONS of opportunities for extra credit and making up missed group projects during class!
Professor Austin is by far the best math teacher I have had. She is very clear about the material she teaches, and she makes lectures interesting, fun, and inspiring. I would take this class again!
This review is actually for M 329F. Great professor. Tests were split into take-home and in-person components. Medium amount of homework. Lots of chances for extra credit.

This was an amazing introduction class. Tests are collaborative, meaning the whole class can work on it together, and you can use any material provided through the course. Tests are take home for a 3 day period. Usually there are homework due every Friday, but she doesn't mind if you miss a deadline-- so long as you do turn it in. HIGHLY RECCOMMEND

Media and Technology. Very interesting class! Learned so much about level design and the art that goes into making 2-d games in Unity. Definitely great for beginners such as myself. It was a lot of work but! It was fun work and not agonizing work, very simple and got a 100 in the class, very easy grading too.

I don't want to be biased, but honestly professor Augustin is the best teacher that I have had in my entire life. He goes above and beyond not only for his work and projects, but also for his students. He is always watching out for you and may come off as having high expectations, but genuinely its because he cares.

Design&Interactivity is focused on creating a character, an environment, and then making a game based off of that in Unity. I never attended the in person sessions (class was held once a week online) and despite taking that blow to my grade, still ended with an A. As long as you try you'll do great. Prof Augustin himself is super cool and laidback!

Love Professor Augustin! He makes it clear that you will get a good grade as long as you try your best, and he is super understanding when you have other things going on. He's also generally very cool and funny. I'm taking another one of his classes next semester because he was so nice to be around.

*This rating is for PSY 332S*
 I was very optimistic about taking Neuroscience of Sleep; however, Professor Duarte was extremely condescending when I asked for feedback. She had daily quizzes over readings, and you had only 5 minutes to answer the question in full paragraph form, which had to have extremely proper grammar that made sense to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I did really well in Psychopharmacology with Duarte but not because of any help she provided. Her lectures are really interesting and the topic is fascinating, but Duarte doesn't provide ANY resources to study except for in class slide shows. I  passed with an A+ by making hundreds of flashcards for each test covering every sentence on every slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found her class harder than expected- it definitely requires studying to do well. There were 2 lectures a week (which were fairly dense), but she was very willing to help out outside of class hours with more than just the class, which i appreciated. She's a good professor and knows what she's doing- just make sure you put the time in the class.

This is the first time I've gotten below an A and I've taken both OChems, biochem, and physics. Exams are impossible, you basically have to memorize every word she says and even if you do you still probably won't do too well. No extra resources to study beyond lecture and lectures aren't recorded. Save your GPA and avoid this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is really smart but just doesn't know how to teach a class. The only assignments in the class was a paper and a few in class quizzes with one question. The tests are like trying to win trivia. No emphasis on what you need to know, and she tests very randomly. It is a strange combination of neuroscience, history, etymology, and geography.

Grade is based primarily on 4 exams. While you can drop one exam from your final grade, her exams are very difficult. She is very lecture heavy and so you need to be prepared to be a good note taker as her slides aren't sufficient and she doesn't record her lectures. Took a huge chunk of study time and effort. I wouldn't take her again.

Don't take her. Take another psych class. Lectures seem simple, but tests are impossible. Must memorize every word she says. No textbook and ppt slides have very few words, so don't miss a class or you'll be totally lost. My advice would be to record every lecture, make Anki decks, and memorize them word for word.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever met. She doesn't like helping anyone with extra questions after class. Also, theres no textbook so you will find this class difficult to study for. The quizzes are much harder than what she teaches in lecture. If you signed up for this class next semester drop before its too late. You will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSY308- Her class is HARD. She is intelligent and passionate about what she teaches. She will quiz you on exam content if you ask. She tells you point blank what you need to know, but it is your responsibility to study. Make an ANKI deck and you'll be fine! Wish I could take her class again, this was easily the most interesting class I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She complained for a month on low attendance, and even wrote an email saying that those that attend lecture make higher scores in class. I attended every lecture, studied, and still did only subpar for this course. Tests were insanely awful and down to the detail, and overall she seems unconcerned about student success. avoid her if possible.

Audrey made me fall in love with printmaking. Truly the perfect professor for intro to print. Jumping between four types of printmaking in one semester seemed overwhelming in my head, but audrey and our TA noah made it so doable and fun. She is so knowledgeable about processes, concepts, and history of print. You must take print if she's teaching!

I love Audrey. She is incredibly well prepared always and organized. Is knowledgeable about almost all printmaking but especially Intaglio and papermaking. She gives fantastic support, feedback, and suggestions (artists, films, books, poems, research, etc.) Her class discussions were so insightful and fun. Such a wonderfully kind educator as well.
Loved this class!! Audrey is so nice and is so helpful. She definitely helped me with my drawing skills. I would recommend any art class given by her.

Dr. Shaffer is very kind, and is a very good professor. She gives very specific feedback, and provides extra credit. She's also willing to work with every student. Attendance is mandatory, but it makes up a big chunk of your grade and is easy points. She's amazing, I love her. My speaking has improved a lot because of this class.

I wish I could stay in this class forever. I loved Prof Shaffer so much. She cares for her students like no other professor I've had, and her feedback was always helpful. This is an amazing class that I think everyone should take (and definitely try to take it with Audrey Shaffer)!

This class helped me (mostly) get over my fear of public speaking! Prof Shaffer was very kind and encouraging to all of her students and allowed us to give speeches based on our actual interests instead of just boring assigned topics. If you're going to take this class, make sure you get Prof Shaffer as your instructor.

Prof Shaffer is a professor that really only wants to see you do good. Understands all the pop culture references and is really respectful to all her students. Amazing professor. I went from never life drawing to being amazing at it all because she knew exactly what she was talking about. Highly recommend.

Nicole is one of the most understanding and caring teachers I've ever had. She tries to make you a better artist even if you cant see it in the beginning you understand at the end of the semester. If you have any concerns about your progress she'll sit down and talk with you even if shes busy. She's really amazing I would take her again in a second

Dr. Awad is extremely down to earth and understanding. She is very knowledgable on both subjects of the psychology of women and psychology of race/racism. During COVID, she encouraged cameras to be on and attendence is graded. Assignments were critique papers, journals, and tests. I really loved Dr. Awad and feel like I genuinely learned a lot.

she ROCKS really funny if youre not a liberal just be warned but she is really funny and is a fair grader. she wants her students to do well. PARTICIPATE it shows her you care and she will fight for you more if she sees that

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Awad is funny, caring, passionate, and respectful of all students opinions. 3 exams (half multiple choice, half short-answer) that are somewhat tricky. 3 journals, 2 critique papers, one final paper, and pop quizzes. Dr. Awad's "Psychology of Women" course was amazing and informative. The topics we went over were really interesting and relevant. There are 3 exams, several pop quizzes throughout the semester (if you pay attention in class, these are easy). Most info for tests comes from lecture, with some material from textbook. Also she's a really cool person.

reviews.comment: Smart. Knows her stuff. Fantastic choices in readings & a diverse array of them, and very up-to-date on the subjects (unlike some profs who reuse old material to the point of absurdity). Very liberal and will expand your (even if already open) mind.

Awapara was a great professor and gave really great lectures. The tests are fairly doable if you pay attention in class and read the assigned readings. You'll also need to do an essay, but it is not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Omar is a really great guy, and you can tell he cares about his subject a lot. reviews.comment: Really kind professor!!! Make sure to go to most classes because there are pop quizzes sometimes and they are pretty easy so you don't want to miss them. reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I really liked the class content and you could tell the professor was really fond of the topic. The exams were chill if you read and attend the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Omar is a really nice guy. He uses powerpoints for his lectures, which unless you do the assigned readings, won't make much sense. Exams are easy if you do the readings, its a make it or break it class.

reviews.comment: He uses a powerpoint for all his lectures, which he uploads so it isn't crucial to go to class. However, there are pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's a very likeable guy; he will engage you if you engage him.

reviews.comment: Amazing UGS Professor!!!!! So passionate on what he does and explains the material so easy! Genuinely a great UGS for those need one. The material is super easy and the TA's were super helpful. Light readings but you can lowkey get away with not reading them. But overall and amazing class!!

A few straightforward quizzes + discussion attendance = your grade. He started making the quizzes open note halfway through the semester which made them even easier. You don't really have to pay attention in class or discussion either, and a lot of people just skipped class. Probably the easiest UGS at UT.

Professor Auyero is so sweet and funny during his lectures. He made every topic we went over very engaging. Literally one of the first courses I was able to pay attention to. There is lots of reading, but the material is usually interesting and easy to read. The quizzes answers are given a lot in lecture, but questions can be worded weird. 10/10

He is such an amazing professor! He's funny and even though they're readings, they're not long and most are pretty interesting. There's not a lot of homework which motivated me to further understand rather than stress out, and he usually gives out hints of what's going to be on the quizzes, and the quizzes are simple. Take him for your UGS!

Super funny guy, easy class, lectures are pretty interesting, and the readings are not too bad since he basically gives the quiz answers right before. However there's only like 5 quizzes that make up your grade. Solid UGS choice though.

Easy UGS, Professor Auyero is clearly knowledgable and passionate! Getting the books is annoying but honestly optional, you don't even have to read, he literally summarizes everything in lectures before quizzes. No graded writing assignments! Mandatory discussions weren't too bad. Genuinely interesting class, got me interested in sociology :)

Highly recommend taking Javier. Had an early class with him but his lectures were still able to keep me engaged half awake. Very lenient with grading and TAs were chill too. You can tell that he is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and wants students to leave class with an understanding of the content instead of emphasizing grades.

i love him sm. hes pretty humorous and full of energy that its kinda hard to fall asleep in his class. the class is just do readings, review reading in class, then quiz over reading. theres like 6 and hell drop one. u lit dont have to do the readings tho like js ai a summary and listen in class for someone else to summarize it. very easy ugs

- Caring, wants to get to know your name, personable
- Stimulating lectures, learned a lot
- TA-led discussion mandatory, shoutout Francisco
- Class attendance not mandatory but you're maybe cooked if you miss a quiz or some details. Just go! It's worth it!
- Just going to lectures and discussion helps a lot with quizzes, can get 100 just like that

Professor Auyero is an awesome professor! Attendance isn't mandatory, but your grades come from pop quizzes which Professor Auyero will hint at in lecture. Discussion sessions are mandatory, but useful (TAs are great!). You will have readings and they can be somewhat long, but it is all interesting stuff. Quizzes are easy if you read the chapters.

This professor is good and makes his lectures very enjoyable. He makes the material of what will be on the quiz well-known before you take it. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures, but it is for discussions. It is still very important to attend the lectures so you know when the surprise quizzes will be.

reviews.comment: GOAT ugs teacher

Javier always had engaging lectures and even remembered our names. Very interesting (albeit boring) class and the prof was great. Attendance during main lecture isn't mandatory, TA sessions (required, but chill). Quizzes were light (gives answers in class usually), reading was so long and boring but you can get away w/ not reading (goes over in class),and essays were long but light. better than other ugs - easy A.

Javier is an amazing professor and lecturer. It is incredibly easy to get an A as long as you pay attention in class (he gives most quiz answers out before the test if you listen) and complete your readings!

Grades are based on 4 multiple choice quizzes and 2 essays (1000 words each) about readings and personal connections.

He is amazing, I will always recommend. You have 2 papers and like 4/5 quizzes, lowest one is dropped. He gives you all the answers before the quiz. Show up to every lecture and you will be fine. He is so amazing and funny. The best class I had all semester. TA meetings seem a bit useless but it was nice getting to know them. Overall, take Javier.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the easiest ugs classes; all my friends were stressing while i was there with a free A in this class. TAKE IT.

Attendance is only mandatory for discussion sections. Very generous and understanding to students. I didn't actually read because he would always go over the answers and readings for the quizzes (he was discussing maybe changing that, but he may not). Very easy and interesting UGS. More controversial topics but if you're into sociology I say do it!

The best UGS! Javier is a great professor and his class is an easy A. Your grade is based off of 4-5 “pop” quizzes (he tells you when they will be) that he gives you the answers to + 2 written assignments that are an easy 100. If you do the readings and attend lectures you'll be fine. 100% recommend

Javier was the most intriguing and kind professor I have had. His lectures were extremely eye opening and he is super funny. His officer hours are very welcoming and he is always willing to talk with you. There is a lot of reading but the books are magnificent. Highly recommend for UGS.

reviews.comment: Lots of reading but very doable. Would Highly recommend this UGS option since it is very eye opening.

Javier is seriously the best to take this UGS it's not hard at all there is a lot of reading but it is definite stuff you can skim and there are no tests but 'pop quizzes' (Javier tells you multiple times and gives you 1/2 the answers in his lectures) which I never got below a 100 on! The TA's are also awesome overall a great class

I LOVE JAVIER!! This class was amazing and opened my eyes to so many things. Not many assignments and quizzes, and they are easy. Lots of readings, but very interesting material. Javier is funny and lenient when it comes to grades.

This class was an extremely easy A and very enjoyable! The professor is very kind and funny, and keeps lectures engaging. The class is reading heavy, but I was able to get by just paying attention in lecture without doing most of the readings. Not too many writing assignments and a few easy quizzes. Would highly recommend this UGS!
The easiest class you could ever take. He wants his students to succeed, TA's are great, and he makes his lectures engaging. 0% chance you won't get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Javier is incredibly funny and makes attending class enjoyable! He offers 3 "pop-up" quizzes that he tells you about weeks in advance. The books you'll read in this class are interesting as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Javier is an angel among men. Social Scientific Imagination is interesting and so easy. The few quizzes he does give were open notes. There were two writing assignments that you had years to do and they were not very long at all.

I'd highly recommend this course for your UGS credit! Javier is incredibly funny and makes the class interesting and stress-free. He even learned almost all of our names. Grades mainly came from "pop" quizzes, multiple choice, and he literally tells you what's going to be on them. You do have to read some books, but it's nothing too difficult.

Javier knows how to make a class bearable--even if you have no interest in this subject, you will enjoy the class! There was quite a reading load at the beginning of the semester, but it died down and the last third of the semester is very chill. TAs were very kind. 

Take this UGS for an easy A and interesting content!

Javier is such an understanding professor and a great person to learn from. He does such a great job engaging with his students and made me feel eager to learn what he was teaching us. Grades were very forgiving, easy to get an A as long as you go to class and do the occasional reading, which was actually very eye opening content that I enjoyed.

Great professor overall, he's genuinely a reason I'm minoring in sociology now. His grading criteria is much clearer now and his lectures are super interesting. If you can sit and pay attention in lecture then it's an easy A and a great way to get an introduction into sociology.

Honestly, Professor Auyero made my first semester in college so fun. He's so chill, and explains concepts very well. He will literally tell you what will directly be on the quiz, so pay attention in class. TAs are very kind and easy grading on writing assignments (which can be long sometimes). Sometimes a lot of reading, so be prepared.

His class is very interesting. There are pop quizzes, but during class, he basically tells you what will be on the quiz. Most of the readings are really interesting. The writing assignments are really nice and are honestly better than what I had to do in high school. He's very funny and passionate about what he teaches. Highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great class with a hilarious professor! The majority of your grade is participation and attendance, as well as five "pop quizzes." Most of the quizzes are open book and pretty easy. TAs are nice and the discussion sessions are fun.

I recommend him a million times over! His UGS is really interesting and he is a funny guy. There are 4 essays, not long at all, and the TAs give good feedback. There are some readings and quizzes over them but they are not bad.

love prof auyero, his UGS is so interesting and very easy. no tests, 1 quiz a week, TA's are so helpful and their discussion is easy. take this UGS!!! he's really funny too. big class but if you participate and make an effort, it'll be fun and easy.

Prof Auyero was hilarious and his class is incredibly laid back. If you do the readings, which is normal fro UGS courses, then you will get an A. HE IS VERY PASSIONATE ABOUT SOCIOLOGY! I learned so so much in his class. I highly suggest you take his UGS. It is a lot of reading, but the pop quizzes and essay are easy.

I found Javier to be very funny and his lectures are never boring. His writing assignments were an easy A and he quizzes you on topics said in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Fav class, Javier is so much fun while also getting into some really interesting material. Good amount of reading, writing, and participation but very doable and he walks you through everything. Some "pop" quizzes that he warns you about a million times and long readings he goes over in depth if you don't manage to finish them. Easy A and a blast

Amazing professor. He's passionate and it spreads to his students. He's very understanding and grading is quite open-ended so there's freedom to write what you care about, love that for this type of class (social scientific imagination). Very easy writing assignments and quizzes that he warns you about. Take his class!!!

Great teacher who really cares about what he teaches. just pay attention in class, he practically gives answers for quizzes. he usually tells u if there will be a quiz. some readings, but nothing bad. 10/10 recommend

He's really funny and passionate about what he teaches. He clearly cares about his students. He assigns a lot of readings but they're all really interesting. He uploads all the pdfs you'll need so you don't really need to buy anything. The essays and quizzes were easy. It's an easy A. Would definitely take another class with him.

Javier is my favorite professor I have had at UT. He is so genuine and his class was very interesting (especially during the pandemic)!!! He worked well with us via Zoom and made class so enjoyable! The TAs were amazing and I really looked forward to going to class! 10/10 recommend!

Sit in the front two rows!

Javier was a hilarious dude and really passionate about his subject. Pay attention to his lectures because all the quiz info comes from there - he makes it really clear what certain questions will be asked and warns about the "pop" quizzes in advance. He just wants students to show up and participate - boring class but a nice guy and easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

The class itself can be boring but him and his amazing TAs keep it fresh.

Javier was so funny and made his class so interesting. He would tell us when pop quizzes were so there was no surprise. The entire grade is really based off the quizzes and the final paper. The final paper is so easy and I literally got a 100 on it. Show up to the discussions and you'll get an A

listen to the lectures and you'll be fine.

Auyero is an amazing person and his class is super easy. No tests, just quizzes about readings and one gets dropped! Easy final paper also.

Enlightening, significant, and meaningful are only a few words I can use to describe this course. Professor Auyero is an influential lecturer, and I feel incredibly blessed to have had the privilege to take his UGS303 course. The course was structured around reading, quizzes, and one final essay -- which were very manageable and easy.
