reviews.comment: Really good guy. My only complaint about his class was that his TA got on my nerves. He enforces attendance by having quizzes which you don't know when they will happen. Required attendance in TA sessions too. Easy A as long as you do the required readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Javier is HILARIOUS and so knowledgable. He explains things incredibly elegantly in a way that's super easy to understand. Pop quizzes can sneak up on you, but if you listen, he usually gives the answers in lecture. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by just using his explanations. Definitely one of the coolest professors ever.

Javier is an amazing professor. I'm not even into sociology and he made the class interesting. He gives you the quiz questions and also basically the answers before you take the quiz. The TAs also go over them in the discussion sections so go to those as well. Yes, there's reading but they're minimal and you could probably skim them before class.

Awesome professor, super easy class. Just do the readings and show up to class and you will get an A. He's extremely passionate, and probably the only prof you will have that actually wants to learn your name. You only have 7 quizzes and a paper, and he drops a quiz as well as basically gives you the answers to the quiz. Super great class.

Went on a lot of tangents, but they were one of the most entertaining parts of the class.  A fair amount of reading, but most of the material is interesting and relevant.  Overall, a really good teacher who was passionate and knowledgeable about his subject.

Javier Auyero is probably one of the hidden gems in the Liberal Arts Department. He has this way of engaging students and making them see real world issues in a broader scope that encompasses both sides of the argument. The lectures in this class are top notch, and most of the time you will feel time fly away. The coursework is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you just want an easy A for your UGS, he's a good guy to take. If you want to learn anything meaningful, take something else. Everything learned in the class is heavily liberally biased and your grade in the class is dependent on your agreement with their opinions. Auyero's ALWAYS lies about when the quizzes are going to be. Beware of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: No exams, a couple "pop" quizzes you usually get warned about in the prior lecture. He's an amazing prof that's passionate about sociology, I absolutely loved his class & learned a lot. Readings are far less than other UGS. 1 paper graded by TA's so go to the TA sessions!!! If u put in the effort you'll get extra cred. I got a B+ with little effort

I absolutely loved this class. I considered changing my major after taking his social scientific imagination course. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and he is hillarious. He is hands down one of the best professors I have had. Class is an easy A if you pay attention to lecture and know the gist of the books. DEFINITELY recommend!

His class can seem fairly dry if you're not interested in sociology. There's a good amount of reading, but you can get away with skimming it. The most important advice I can give you is to attend lectures and discussion sessions. I had a hard time getting myself to sit through his lectures, but it pays off. His quizzes cover material from lecture.

Javier is very passionate in his UGS 303 course, and isn't afraid to confront and address a lot of deep racial issues in American society. The quizzes aren't that bad either, and he drops obvious hints as to when they'll be and what will be on them. The readings are important!

This was a very easy UGS 303 class: there are no 'tests', only 6 or 7 ten-question 'quizzes' that he will RANDOMLY do in class. The questions are simple and quite obvious most of the time. Discussion is mandatory, but not very helpful in my opinion. The key to doing well is showing up, and paying attention to what he says. Lots of reading!!
Auyero is my favorite professor at UT. His lectures are exciting and get everyone involved. I was completely out of my comfort zone at times, and it was really fun. Great class and great teacher.

He's a great lecturer, very passionate and entertaining. His power points are posted on canvas and he always tells you what will be on the quizzes. If you study and keep up on reading an A is achievable. He can be kind of scatterbrained though, and the TAs often had to push him to keep us on schedule and give the quizzes on time.
Great and nice professor. Very passionate about the subject and an interesting teacher. A lot of reading. Worth while UGS class.

This class is super easy, one open note quiz every week and a couple of other assignments here and there. Definitely go to class because there are random attendance checks, and missing too many can add up. Overall really easy class but the professor can be really boring.

Amazing teacher. Very approachable and caring. Open note quizzes and several projects using the UT Library resources. Interesting digital topics during the course. Gives extra credit for early submission in assignments. They can become heavy, starting early is a must.

Genuinely such a nice person, she's one of the kindest professors at UT! Her class is super easy, and even though there are some group projects, it's really doable. You learn pretty useful things when it comes to the digital world too. She really accommodating to students, and is accessible even when it's not class time.

Professor Gursoy was extremely kind and understanding. She will be lenient with you as long as you talk to her in advance. Extremely easy class. A quiz every week, open note. Two projects. As long as you do your work on time, you will pass.
Very very smart and an amazing lecturer but you are graded on so few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a great prof who genuinely cares about his students. He is absolutely brilliant and I love his lectures. However, you are graded on very few assignments and if you don't test well, I would avoid this class. He always dresses really nice. He's kinda fine ngl.

Was not familiar with Islam at all coming in but this class is interesting and well structured. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit and easy assignments. Professor Ayoub made it clear that he cared for his students.

Great Professor. He is very knowledgeable. If you are pre-law, take his classes. I got into many programs because of his rec letters. He teaches at UT Law. Attendance is mandatory. Two tests: midterm and final. He gives exam reviews for both. Take this class!
Professor Ayoub is a great mentor and passionate professor. He is inspiring and I find him very handsome. One of my best professors at UT.

He jumped around a lot and was horribly hard to follow. Instructions for assignments are unclear and graded harshly. He doesn't make any sense if you don't know the subject then you won't have any idea what he is talking about. I NEVER DO RMP RATINGS, but this class and professor is not worth it.

I hated this class. Lectures were boring, teacher was hard to follow at times. VERY few assignments and one missed point is hard to recover from. I still did well, but assignments are not graded lightly and most any missed points on quizzes/exams were basically trick questions that were offhandily mentioned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is extremely difficult, so please beware. That being said, Professor Ayoub is fantastic and incredibly engaging. His lectures are packed with information, but you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, and you should be okay as long as you pay close attention. Be ready to read a lot, however, and it ain't easy to make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel like he is a professor for the type A person. He lectures quite fast and there are no laptops allowed in class so it can be difficult to keep up with written notes. Very knowledgeable and will teach you a lot though. I don't feel comfortable speaking up in class. Beware pop quizzes worth 20% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is one of the best professors I have had during my time at UT. His lectures might be a bit boring but the majority of the exams and quizzes will be based on the lectures.

I really enjoyed Professor Ayoub's Government and Islam - it opened me up to a whole new field of thought. He is obviously very knowledgeable about the area and passionate for it as well. Just be aware that there is a huge amount of reading for this course, though much of it is reviewed in the following class.

I took intro to Islam. It was an easy class, you can get away without reading the readings as long as you can bs an answer bc he loves to randomly call on people. I wish it was more of a collaborative class but he mostly just picked on ppl all class. He makes good points during lectures and tests/quizzes aren't too bad. Just go to class and easy A.

I took ISL310, Introduction to Islam; it wasn't one of his provided courses for some reason on rmp. Overall the class is pretty straight forward. Sometimes he might ask an oddly specific question on an exam or quiz, but honestly if you show up to class and read the slides you can definitely get an A. I think the class was pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ayoub was lovely but firm, Id just recommend to always go to class (hardly any leniency), do your readings, and make sure you take note of PowerPoint lectures. He gave us 4 journal entries, 2 exams (a midterm and cumulative final), attendance grade, and 2 quiz grades. Its open note but doesnt mean its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Interesting class for sure, but he was insanely passive aggressive if he didn't like you and almost never responds to emails. Very infuriating, especially in the middle of the quizzes/exams... TA was also confused most of the time.

All I'm going to say is I was in the hospital and the man still refused to give me an extension for a quiz we were given a 24 hour window to take, so I took the quiz on 3 different pain medications. Do with that information what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is a great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Ayoub is a great guy, well dressed and a knowledgeable teacher. The class left me a little disappointed because it didn't require students to think critically.

One of the easiest and most interesting classes I've taken at UT. Weekly readings help you participate in class discussions but honestly are not necessary. Attendance is part of your grade. One midterm and mandatory final. He gives exam reviews for both and the tests are verbatim the reviews. Take this class!
I loved Dr. Ayoubs lectures and discussions. He is clearly invested in his students. He challenged us to grow intellectually. I strongly recommend his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is very passionate and knowledgeable. He is approachable and he likes participation in class. I would highly recommend to take his classes, if you can get in. It took me a semester to be able to enroll in one of his courses.
I took two classes with Dr. Ayoub. I enjoyed every single minute of them. He is very knowledgeable and accessible outside of classroom. I would definitely recommend his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one the best teachers I had during my education at UT. I greatly enjoyed his lectures, especially the discussion part.

He's a very smart guy and cares a lot about the content. I was able to find the book online for like $10, and while the reading was helpful, it wasn't completely mandatory to do well on the test. He gives a study guide a week prior and there are no curve balls on the test. I'm not even a gov major and pulled an A with an average work input.

Professor Ayoub seems extremely passionate and knowledgeable about his subject but appears to have a difficult time diffusing that knowledge and passion to his students. His class structure was a little hazy and no one seemed to fully understand how things worked in terms of grading or participation. Pretty easy A, though, if you put in any work.

The book cost a lot first of all and there is a lot of reading from the chapters and a lot of supplemental reading that consists of 20 pages per reading that he gives. The test had items that were not talked about in class. Little small detailed things. Just get ready to read a lot if you want an A and show up to class.

She's a really interesting teacher with great lectures. She made reading classic texts a lot more fun and she introduced many themes and elements of the stories that I never realized were present. Lots of reading, but you do get to read Game of Thrones a lot in Classics and Modern Fantasy. Essays were rough but debates and discussions were fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: For a course with a writing flag, it is, in my opinion, a surprisingly small amount of writing overall. There is fair bit of reading though, but nothing awful. Participation is graded for the class, but if you're quiet she understands that and just wants to hear your thoughts every once in a while during discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors out there. She is there for her students and provides helpful feedback. If you make an effort to show her that you care about the class, she will reciprocate. She is also extremely easy to talk to, and overall an amazing person. I enjoyed her humor & enthusiasm very much.

Dr. Ayvaci was a nice guy, but his teaching style is bizarre. He's very boring in his lectures and we were never on syllabus, so nothing was clear. Granted it was his first semester teaching at UT when I took the course, but he kept changing things as he went. His iClicker quizzes were ridiculously difficult. Avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He should learn that teaching doesnt consist of preparing and showing slides. As a teacher his value should be more than that. Your learning will be mostly limited with your capacity in his class.

He's a nice guy, but not so great of a teacher. I stopped going to class because I couldn't understand his style of teaching and the test was straight from the book anyways. Right before the test I would memorize the powerpoint slides and textbook chapters, and would do ok. Aside from that, the homework assignments and quizzes are really easy!

Professor Ayvaci was a nice guy to say the least, but he had trouble keeping the lectures interesting. Luckily the material is fairly easy and he provides all the slides you need, so if you just read/memorize the slides before the tests and quizzes, you should do fairly well. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but has trouble clarifying.

I really didn't vibe with this guy's teaching style at all. Every example is taken directly from the book, and he rarely, if ever, leads the class step-by-step on a block of code, and this is nominally a CODING class. By far the worst MIS professor I've taken thus far at UT. He's just not an effective teacher when the goal is programming knowledge.

Professor Ayvaci is a nice guy but his exams are very difficult and he has some very backwards policies. This is a SQL coding class and exams are all multiple choice, so they are not a good measure of what you know. No chance to actually write code in exams. He doesn't let you even see graded quizzes, so it's impossible to know what you got wrong.

Ayvaci is a really good guy and he seemed to care a lot about his students. That given, he typically summarizes the readings during his lectures but his tests had questions over small details that were from the textbook or case readings, so be sure to read everything and take good notes. He usually has a quiz at the end of each class so don't skip.

Ayvaci is a nice guy, but his lectures are boring and hard to pay attention to. Participation is mandatory as he takes attendance, the online textbook is dense and his lectures are just him re-telling the material in the most boring and long way possible. There's also SO MANY layers to this class so being on top of everything can be overwhelming

His lectures are extremely boring, and the material you are being tested over is very hard to pick out. He simply talks about different businesses and generalizes everything where when you're studying for the test you don't know what to study. There is a lot of reading and you're quizzed on it but its impossible to know it all. Excel assignments...

I was one of the lucky ones in his class and scored an A but most of my class failed. He was so confusing if he was going to take the original paper/test or the retake one for the final grades. You were one pins and needles waiting for your report card. He really shouldn't be teaching Intro to Shakespeare, expects far too much.

I took this professor in the mid 1990s, and from these reviews, it sounds like he hasn't changed much.  Terrible instruction.  Abusive to students.  Loves to give Fs.  He certainly knows Shakespeare, it's just a shame he can't teach it.
just awful.  soul crushing.  i changed departments because i thought this was what all english profs were like. took years to realize it was just him.

Took this professor many years back. Shakespeare at Winedale made a significant change in my life, for the better. Still not sure how much is Doc's teaching and how much is the experience, itself. Winedale was like bootcamp and this had both it's positive and negative sides. If I had it all to do over, I still would have taken the course, anyday.

He failed my entire class on the majority of our papers.  But EVERYONE failed on the first essay.  He gives at least 35 pages of reading per night, and then a quiz over the readings the next morning.   I dropped his class along w/ 19 other students and we are working on a petition to have him removed from our college.  DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!
No Comments

Wow. This jerk taught my first UT course in 1989 & I'm dismayed to see he's still up to the same sadistic garbage. He knows Shakespeare but wd rather bully than teach. On the 1st paper, he failed every student in the class (all had placed out of fresh comp) except 1, whom he gave a prize for a C.  I dropped (along w 1/2 the class) & took Prof Velz.
extremely unclear as to what he wants from you, somehwat rude email...:|

took his class one semester and found shakespeare completely innacessible, failed it. took it with another prof the next semester and she presented it and breathed a life into it  in such a way that I understood it and enjoy it to this day. made a B.
No Comments

He likes to hand out "F" grades and watch his students squirm. I'll agree that he's interesting but damaged.  He keeps a former Charlie's angel's poorly written term paper in his office as a souvenir.
You can get a lot from him, but expect to take a LOT of abuse. Interesting, but damaged, teacher.

Lectures were often hard to stay engaged with, and exams were difficult to prepare for. The professor taught this as a second job, so office hours and communication were limited. He was lenient on some assignments and seemed to care about students when approached. I'd recommend relying on the slides to study for the exams and note every detail.

Probably the most boring lecturer I have ever had. No reason to go to class as the course material is very easy and can be self-taught through the homework, and he uploads the lecture slides. This guy should not teach and just stick to txdot. 75% of the grade is through exams.

As others have mentioned, Dr. Azambuja works full-time at TxDOT and teaches on the side... but he should probably just stick with TxDOT. He's a pretty unengaging lecturer and is very monotone. The project management material is pretty easy, but his engineering economics lectures are almost unbearable. Exams were straightforward and fair, though.

I went to maybe 6 classes over the course of the semester because it genuinely pained me to listen to this man speak for more than an hour. The content is relatively easy and can be self-taught. I recommend going to the classes before exams because he will talk about what will be tested. Study for tests with hw problems and examples from slides.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had, he will not work with you and clearly does not care about the class whatsoever. There's no practice tests so you only have 2 MAYBE 3 homeworks to actually use to study, most of which don't really correlate to the test whatsoever. The most nothingburger class that shouldn't have been difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want a professor that cant teach and will lie to your face and say that he will curve the class but doesn't, Azambuja is the one! All jokes aside, worst teacher I've ever had. All he does is read off the slides with the most monotone voice ever. Doesn't upload slides before class so a lot of ppl skip. All exam avgs were under 75. Good luck.
Bro should just stick to txdot.

He doesn't accept late submissions for homeworks and doesn't understand the students circumstance at times. Submission also through gradescope so always have to stay on your toes for it. Exams are hard even though he tells you whats gonna be in it and you have to self study because he just reads off the slides. Great dude but poor lecturer.
worst lecturer ever, doesn't upload slides and just reads off the slides all class. his exam averages are very low and your entire grade is just exams

Worst professor ive ever taken at UT. Nice guy but this man cant teach to save his life. The course itself is easy and the material is light but his exam averages r also very low compared to other PM classes. Doesnt upload slides before class so a lot of people dont go. All he does is read off pwpt slides. Wouldnt take him bc hes a bad teacher.

Marcelo is a great guy, his class is chill and its very easy to get an A. Beginning of the semester was project mgmt which was easy. Second half is engineering economics which is a bit trickier but still easy to get an A on the exams. His lectures are boring, takes ages to grade exams, but being a prof is his side job bc he works at TXDOT full time

Overall an OK prof. He spends most of lectures going over proof of theorems and lectures are very theory heavy in general with little to no examples. I wouldn't recommend taking him unless you've already taken real analysis. He is a nice guy and always willing to help out, class material and teaching style is just very difficult. Read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the exams were hard, you can get a good grade as long as you do the homeworks and work hard on the project. Drops the lowest grade and has lots of office work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I found the subject matter incredibly difficult to grasp at first, Dr. Turnquist was a great professor. The grading scheme made getting an A possible if you put in some work: 50% from homework + a project and 2 exams, dropping the lowest score . Homework was harder than exams, but he had many office hours available for getting help.

Numerical Analysis is hard, so the content for this class is harder than other math classes. It consists of both computational and theory. 50% HW, 25% project, 25% midterm, and 25% final. He drops the lowest 25% from any of the following. HW and the project weren't too bad, but the exams were hard. Read textbook. Overall, very caring professor.

Dr. Turnquist gets an unnecessary amount of hate. For one, his teaching style is unique from other professors. Rather than just give you the answer or just give you a definition, he makes you think about that definition and why it matters. Homework isn't bad. Beware of tests however since he really wants you to think. Overall, good professor.

Brutally hard class. Very different from other Diff EQ classes. Super theory based and very difficult to understand. If you're a math major, this class is for you. If you need to do anything applicational, find something else. I wouldn't take this class. It isn't worth the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are theory/proof heavy, and lecture notes (hand-written) are horrible. Self-study enough to do all the HW, and you will be more than able to do well on the exams (easier than HW). Coding project took about 2h and accounted for 25% of the grade. Just self-studying and being confident in linear algebra can probably honestly get you an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very hard class. Go to office hours as much as you can to check your homework answers and Project, and read the textbook after every class to get the material down and you'll be fine. I got a 60 on my final but the curve brought me to an A-.

Absolute joke of a class. He is a very conceptually heavy teacher who spends all of his time deriving and proving the theorems and leaves no time for examples. Class is a drag. The homework is impossible. And even if you end up doing the homework, they don't correlate to the exams. Don't take. Bottom of the totem pole for M427J professors.

Professor Turnquist is very smart and definitely enjoys math, but his lectures are theory heavy and difficult to understand with almost 0 practice problems. Homework is nitpicked, and the 1 exam and the final are all theory (avgs were around 50-60). Very difficult class, especially considering every other professor teaching 427j give most kids As.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man is a threat to society.

Obviously, the class is "unique". Don't expect to do too well on homework, as that is very arbitrary (unless you go to office hours, which I didn't). The exams were way easier than HW, and  tested what he taught/ was in the book. Interesting teacher, but you have to understand and not memorize. Or just bring a textbook (Open note exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought I was always good at math. I easily surpassed the A grade in every class I took, until I got to this class. This class was a pain. Very theory heavy, and if you don't like that, do NOT take him. His exams are not for people who like applying math, and solving equations.

Regardless of what other reviews say, his grading is NOT lenient. His tests will not match the material and if you want a chance at passing you must read the textbook (which again, is almost as bad as his lectures). 
My grade is wildly different from my peers who took other professors. This seriously needs to be addressed by the Math Department

Turnquist is clearly insanely smart, but he is not fit for teaching or lecturing. During lectures, he basically writes his notes onto the board with no numbers and poor examples. It's essentially a self-taught class since lectures aren't at all helpful. Tests/homework are also insanely difficult. 2 stars since he's funny and nice in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. He rants about concepts that won't be on the homework or exams for the entirety of class and then grades everything like it's a dissertation. If you think you can teach yourself an upperclass math go ahead - but it will not be fun. He isn't mean, just a terrible professor. UT please fire him.

I sincerely believe a higher power sent Axel Turnquist to punish me for any wrong doing I have ever committed. While Axel is a jolly fellow with clear passion for mathematics, the very last thing he should be doing is teaching. With a current RMP score of 1.9 and difficulty of 4.6, UT should find another use for him immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you have to take this class with this professor, do yourself a favor and just change your major or dropout. no degree is worth taking this class with this professor. dean of CNS, if you're reading this, I think I speak on behalf of all of us when I say we deserve some type of compensation for what we were put through in this class.

This professor is a RED FLAG!!! Avoid this professor at all cost. He lack the ability to teach at all, he does not explain concepts, nor does he actually provide resources. Unless you are trying to drop out of college, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Genuinely might be the worst professor at UT Austin
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Personally I loved him and thought his explanations and lectures were great. His style of lecturing may not be for everyone though, which is understandable. While the class is test-heavy, I believe there were curves, and doing well on the project is a huge grade-booster. He was accessible outside class and hosted extra office hours prior to exams.
worst professor I have ever taken. class made me question my sanity. stay away.

The professor is very good at explaining concepts (albeit he teaches more than other professors for this class), but if you fall behind on lecture notes, it can hard to catch up. He's lenient with grading the homework, and your midterm is dropped or your final is only counted for half credit, there's also a final project to help boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So about a month into the course, I can safely say this guy is not a good professor. His lectures are annoying for the same reason a lot of other professor's lectures suck. He simply is not a good communicator. Also, the homework assignments so far have been exceptionally difficult. Probably should take someone else.

I would have changed the professors if I had the chance. At first, I thought I was the one not understanding the material but my classmates felt the same way. Lectures have too much theory with few to no examples of how to apply the theory. I saw how content was taught for other differential equations classes and it was easier to digest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: bad

Please do not take this professor if you are taking M 427J. He was not able to teach the class at a level his students would understand. I had a notebook and a half of lecture notes, yet I was lucky if I understood a third of it. He was also not receptive to student feedback throughout the semester. Find ANY way to take another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor if you can avoid him! He is the literal worst at teaching. There was only one midterm and the average was a 50 even thought it was open note. His lectures are super confusing and he only talks about theory and rarely ever taught us how to apply the theory to examples claiming we would "learn how to in our homework."

Silly guy and very intelligent however a very bad professor. Lectures are very confusing and theory-based. He did not do many examples even when we begged him! Asking him questions just makes things more confusing; he cannot explain this class to non-mathematicians. Mentions of extra credit but (as of after the final) we have no clue if we got any.

I went to therapy because of this man. Whatever you do, DO NOT take him. He is actually the worst professor I have ever had in my entire life. He knows his material but does not explain it well at all and his lectures are heavy on theorems. If you do take him, drop his class and take Differential Equations next semester unless you want to fail.

Diff eq is already a heavily theory-based course, and combining it with a theory-based teaching style was not efficient. He mentioned in the first day that there would be a heavy curve at the end of the course but has yet to inform us what it would be, and it is the day before the final. The midterm average was a 55.4%. I have an A or F right now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture was difficult & very concept heavy. Midterm was 3 conceptual questions that barely covered the material & avg is 50. Curve is unaddressed. Homework is graded harshly and mostly material you would have to independently learn. Final could be 50% of your grade. Prof is intelligent and responsive but difficult to understand. Take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives a pretty good curve on the class, but the average on the only midterm was a 50%. Its very easy to fall behind and his lectures can be very confusing.

do not take this professor if you can help it. his lectures are impossible to understand if you are not a math major or heavily invested in math. discussions are pretty helpful, but depends on the TA. only one exam + final + project. he is also a tough grader when it comes to homework.

Although he isn't particularly a tough teacher, his lectures are hard to follow. If you miss class there's no good way of seeing what he presented that day since his recording are terrible. The class is test heavy with the final being half of your grade.

He's nice, but he's a really bad lecturer. I stopped going to class and self-studied after a point in the semester. The average for the final was 50% but he didn't curve it. I would not recommend taking him.

His lectures are not beginner friendly at all and unclear. He unnecessarily covers topics beyond the scope of the class. The final, where the mean was a 50, is worth 50% if your grade. You don't get feedback on your project and the grading turnaround time is awful. M340L is not supposed to be a hard class literally take any other professor.

The professor is a nice person, but not a great lecturer. Many people skipped class and read the textbook instead. If I didn't do the reading before it would be very hard to follow. He curved the course grade, but the change in exam styles was drastic from the mean being 74 on the first test to 54 on the final. I kept a high A until the final.

Dr. Turnquist is very smart, but he's too smart. It was difficult to retain things during his lectures and the textbook problems didn't prepare us well for the hard exams. Also, he's really slow at uploading grades. This class is meant for non math or cs majors but felt too difficult. Maybe he'll be better in the future. The TA was great tho!

You can tell he is incredibly smart, but he struggles to teach it well. Nearing the end of the semester, grading homework and projects was extremely slow. I was only able to see the grade on a project worth 25% after taking the final exam. He is very kind though and hosts office hours and review sessions when asked, so I believe he will get better!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, and a chill dude overall. I took his matrices class, and though the material isn't easy, I always just referred to the textbook if I was lost. Office hours are super helpful too, just make sure you don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the bad reviews, she's a really kind professor and wants all of her students to pass the class. She is lenient with assignments and understands that we all have busy schedules. This class improved my presentation skills and was also a lot of fun.
She didn't grade any of our assignments until the very end of the semester. I had thought I was doing well in the class b
It's an easy class, but she is a horrible professor. She is unorganized and unprofessional
She is not a good professor at all. She is completely unorganized, has absolutely no reason for giving the grades that she does, and she does not seem to care about her students

She's a great and well-intentioned person, but I felt like her lack of organization put me at a disadvantage at times, which I didn't feel was made up for with extra credit. We were given details of the assignments much later than we should've been, and we waited months for grades.

Professor Dewi has been one of my favorite professors on campus. This is a presentation-based class where you will give speeches, typically 1-2 per month. Exams are in person, she provides study guides, and allows us a page of handwritten notes. Assignments are very easy and straightforward. Highly recommend if you want an easy class.

Dr. Azevedo is brilliant and you will learn a lot from him. He doesn't really care about grades (it is not really that hard to make an A if you do the right things) but you will care about doing well in his class because you will be inspired to really learn it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Flavio is a great professor! He really knows his stuff and cares for his students! There were even times he brought cake for all of us! The class isn't difficult! Yes, there is long readings but those can bring you get. 2 drops for it! The midterm isn't that bad since there is a review. You will get to know your classmates! Participate/enjoy it

This grad class is by nature difficult, as a review of cognitive research. Flavio is cool, very laid back. His style is not for everyone (looking at you, A-types), but he makes sure you get what you need out of the class. You are treated as a colleague and beginner researcher, with respect and also support. Your head will explode, but worry not!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Flavio is awesome; genuinely cares about students. Class itself consists of readings which can be long and pretty dense. During lecture, there is A LOT of group discussion. Not hard as long as you do the readings and put in some effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: - Only his view is valid - When you ask for help his answers are vague - Rude, criticizes students in class in front of everyone (very unprofessional)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's an okay professor, he kind of acts like an desi uncle. There is a quiz, a paper, midterm and the final and everything is essay/short answer. Randomly does attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is amazing. fundamentals of acting was the best class

Barbara is a gem. She cares tremendously about ALL of her students. She takes the time to learn about each student & celebrates their accomplishments. Really cultivates a comfortable & safe learning environment. You do not have to be an amazing actor to do well in this class. Show a willingness to participate & learn & you will succeed. LOVE her!

Chisholm is very friendly and makes an effort to connect to each of her students. The class (T D 303) is easyyyy to the point of almost being boring. I'd recommend it if you're in need of a GPA booster. If you're looking for a useful class that will teach you advanced acting techniques and challenge you to become a better actor- do not take this.
Cared about each one of her students as individuals and really cares about what she teaches.
This specific class is basically create digital media and you get maximum credit. It's really cool to be able to create things as an elective without any strict rules, would definitely recommend!

Professor Bays is probably one of the most caring professors here at UT. Comics & Cartoons was such a fun and relaxing VAPA, and he often brought snacks for us and comic books to look at. His point system is super easy, so many people finished most of the class pretty early on. I loved coming to his lectures even if I was completed with my points!

Took him for comics and cartoons as my VAPA and it was beyond easy. All assignments are fun little drawings and are not graded on quality. Ben is a SUPER caring guy and loves what he does and who he teaches. I will miss this class every day.

I took RTF 347C: Business of Video Games, and I gotta say, this was the most fun RTF class I've ever taken at UT. He does post a lot of different class assignments, but you don't necessarily need to do all of them since the grading scale for this class is points-based. A score of 95 points is all that you need to earn an A in this class.

Awesome Professor! Plenty of extra credit, super easy class for upper division credit. Take his class, you won't regret it. He is very kind and supportive. He patiently reviews almost all of the assignments.
Quite literally the easiest class ever. i did not show up past week 2 and got an 100 in the course. LMAO

I took this class for an elective, and this class didn't even feel like school work to me. I had so much fun creating each assignment. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit throughout the semester too!

Ben is just a great teacher. A lot of professors should aspire to be like him. He knows how to work with students and is very creative and enjoyable to learn from! Whether you procrastinate or not, this class is structured for you. One big deadline at the end of the semester to turn everything in, so work at your own pace.

This class was one of the most interesting courses I've taken at UT. You really get free-range for what type of digital content you want to try making in the course. If you're worried about little or no knowledge in certain aspects, Ben includes great tutorials in the assignment page and you can always redo assignments to improve.

Ben Bays is a great instructor. Very fair grading. Projects can be completed at the student's pace. There were a wide variety of assignments to choose from that covered different aspects of Digital Art and Media.

I love Professor Bays! He is so kind and personable even thru a fully online class. This class is fully self paced and self taught thru using various resources. Its points based so super easy to get an A+. easy A and also really fun!

Prof. Bays was a great professor. He was easily accessible for any questions, and the class model was very flexible. As someone who has never used Photoshop and has no editing/animation experience, I was able to complete a ton of assignments on powerpoint and using scratch. It was an easy class and I'd love to take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very fun dude. No hard deadlines except to turn in assignments by the end of the semester.

I absolutely loved this class. I would recommend anyone from any background enroll. Bays was funny, caring, and showed genuine interest in his students growth. The assignments really allowed students to explore their relationship with creativity and I wish I could take it again!

Ben Bays is the sweetest professor I have taken, I this is my second class taken with Ben Bays. I'm not much of a CGI person, but I had so much fun taking this class. Ben is passionate about what he does and is super caring and will go out of his way to help anyone struggling to get points in his class! I highly suggest anyone to take his classes!

Ben Bays was honestly one the sweetest professors I have ever met. He's extremely passionate about what he teaches and absolutely loves getting to know his students. The class itself is set up so you determine your path of learning, and are able to focus on certain aspects of digital/graphic design. You do it at your own pace so use your time well.

Easy A+ online asynchronus class. I waited until the last 3 weeks of school to do the work for this class and all I had to do was 6 easy video projects and ended with a 100 in the class. Your work doesn't even have to be that good and Ben will still give you a 100. EASY A CLASS ONLINE asynchronous!!!

Class projects were pretty straight to the point. You only have to complete enough assignments to add up to the point equivalent of the letter grade you desire. The professor and TA's feedback was always super positive and encouraging. The only way to fail is if you don't do the assignments, so just pick out the ones you like/are interested in.

Genuinely, there are few professors who care more then Ben Bays at UT. Took this class for UD credit, but had so much fun taking it. The assignments can look really scary, but the amount of effort he puts into ensuring that you know what you're doing is crazy. Amazing feedback and extremely caring and accommodating, please take him if you can.

Ben was such an amazing professor and he clearly loves what he does! The course is online and the projects are spread out. The only real due date was at the end of the semester so you had time to finish all of them but they were really fun to work on and he hosts online office hours to help with anything. Took 2 of his classes and both were amazing

Ben Bays is such cool guy! I took his online DMP class, and you get what you put in. It's solely project-based, so the class naturally takes up a lot of time, but if you plan ahead, it's very manageable. He and his TAs give feedback on all of your project submissions. Pretty straightforward class. Easy A as long as you don't fall behind schedule.

Excellent professor. Clearly explains complex topics. Great office hours though not overly accessible. HW is nothing too extreme and prepares ok for exams. Exams are hard but curved to the moon (including final exam and final grade). Previous review stating class is based off reading textbook and coming in with questions is incorrect.
Good course and very doable if you attend class.
Tough class but he does a great job answer questions and making the content interesting.

Prof gives pretty fair exams, but they're graded very hard. Lectures are pretty bad, but textbook and hw are good to teach all the necessary contents for the 2 exams. Probably your best bet for solid state given the grade distribution for the other profs are not good
If you dont want your gpa to be lower than hell, dont take this class

Overall a great and caring prof. His lectures are pretty dense and goes quickly through the material, but if you go to OH he is willing to help clear up any misunderstandings you have. THE TEXTBOOK IS KEY, read and go through EOC problems and you'll do well on the exams as they are similar in style. Tough test grader but lenient on grading (75~A).

Class is structured where you take notes on the lengthy textbook sections, then come to lecture to ask Qs about them. Can't survive on lectures alone, which are fast & not well-organized. Homework problems are difficult & always required clarification with the TA due to confusion. Tests are weighted very high. Wouldn't take again (error in header).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Banerjee was a great professor. He makes it clear that he is not looking to fail any students, despite how difficult the content is. As long as you put a clear effort into understanding the material, you will get the grade that you deserve. :)

His lectures can be a drag sometimes, so the textbook will be your best friend for this course.

I enjoyed the course. The lectures are very dense, but prof. is available outside class and is happy to help. The course was difficult but the workload was manageable and hw usually had only 2-5 questions. I wouldn't worry about grades since a 70 will get you an A. I learned a lot and encourage everyone to take 339 to learn about semiconductors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Banerjee is a nice guy but not with lectures. Majority of discussion is not relevant to the scope of the class. Class content was heavily centered on formulas which he explains in detail during lecture. Tests are based around using these formulas to solve problems. Solid state concepts are pretty cool but wasn't personally very beneficial.

Poor lecturer- writes messy, poor explanations, and does not go over the tested material. Requires you to buy his personal written expensive textbook. He taught this class like a graduate math class with an EE application.

He makes solid state a doable class. He explains concepts clearly and answers questions well. Attending class is important because he does tell you what concepts will and will not be tested on. Tests are somewhat similar to home works. Conceptually this is a difficult class. However, Banerjee is a liberal grader. 45 is B, 65 A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an incredible lecturer -- he explains clearly and answers questions. But the amount of information he gives is just too much to handle, even for some of the best students. Blink and you've missed an important derivation. Miss a lecture, and you'll be hopelessly behind. Thankfully he is very kind and patient in explaining outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good prof, knows his stuff.  Requires some definite study time, but not unreasonable

Lectures are hard to understand- but the exercises that she provides for the exams are extremely helpful- and I don't see how anyone wouldn't get an A in this class. Use your resources and you'll be fine. She likes open discussion, so will try to get you to talk during classes. She is sweet, and cares a lot about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately I didn't have a great time in this class, mostly due to the lectures. The powerpoints were somehow both overly complex and vague at the same time, and I ended up using the textbook to understand many of the topics we had to cover. Exams were fine though, but I wouldn't be surprised if she changes things up in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Santos disappointing. The course lacked clear guidance and structure, making it difficult for students to understand expectations or succeed. Opportunities for meaningful feedback and support were minimal, and most times, the instructor's tone felt discouraging rather than constructive. Avoid if possible.

Truly cares to make class engaging. Kind and excited about French! Fantastic lecturer and fun exercises to really make you practice. The work is not too bad. Her outfits are always fun and attitude happy. Sometimes she can not pay attention to the time during class, so we get out late or rush a quiz. However its a great class and I recommend her.

An excellent, caring, and loving professor. She just wants the best for her students & truly loves the French language and culture. Most meetings consisted of us talking to our peers in French and then working as a class to learn something new. Lots of extra credit if you go to OH, exams are pretty easy. Pretty lenient grading, just do your work.
The format of this class really ensures that you have lots of participation time -- my french speaking skills improved so much. Liz is funny and made this class a blast!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think the last person who left the review put a 1 for quality on accident. Great professor who cares about her students, fun class tbh.

Dr. Beach was an incredible professor. I thought the lectures followed the textbook too much, so there was no reason to take notes on the lectures and the textbook, just follow one. I found the lectures to be informative, sometimes I got bored, that's not on the professor, though. What is taught in lecture will be on the exam so focus!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a nice professor, but there are LOTS of readings give to you every week. You have to read these textbooks and readings for the short answer/essay questions on the exams. Unless you already have a good knowledge in this field, I would not recommend you taking her class as this class takes too much of your time.

Professor Beach is a fine professor and seems very passionate about research in her field. This class is easily approachable if you have taken some other stats classes but is probably not worth it if not. Lectures are pretty boring but she is forgiving, lenient, and overall a nice person. Labs are pretty easy but exams were a little too dense also.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Slow, boring, intro level course. The final was too long and like only one person in the room finished it in the time allotted. She's really kind and seems very approachable, but honestly if you can help it, don't take this class at all. 
She's allegedly very passionate about water quality, but I didn't see any passion in this course.

I liked Beach just fine, but the lectures are quite boring, and I relied much more on the textbook for the tests than anything in lecture. I read the book and did just fine, and I found some of the content interesting, but the class itself could be extremely dull. Overall, I think it was worth to take for the credit I needed. My TA was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor did not follow her own attendance policies written in her syllabus. If you're looking for a class for your natural science credit, this one isn't it. Extremely boring, not worth it.

Not only are the lectures unbearably boring, but they often skim information in a way that doesn't even match up with what's on the exam. Certain exam questions are purposely made to be confusing, like using interchangeable words for a process as options with a definition that doesn't even match the terms used in book. Doesn't care about you at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are extremely hard and you have to learn lots of information. Do not take this class. The TA's do not really know the content and a lot of the work is by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Did not care about the students. Grades a test based and hard and lab depend on your TAs and they aren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor. Does not care and is the most boring lecturer. Seems to be unprepared to class. The class average on the first exam was 76. TAs are not helpful. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR AN EASY SCIENCE CREDIT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Beach. Her lectures were a little dry, but she knew what she was talking about. 60% of the grade is based on three exams, all multiple choice. They're difficult, but not too bad. A lot of textbook reading. Getting an A is tough, getting a B is easily attainable as long as you do the stuff. The lab & TA section was pretty chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Process Geomorphology w/ Dr. Beach. She is very passionate about her research and what she teaches. 75% of course grade is based off 2 exams and a paper. Exams are over very dense material and can be hard to study for due to format of some questions. Easy grader on non-exam assignments. Also is nice and cares about your learning and wellbeing.

very boring lectures but unfortunately, that's where majority of the exam content comes from. textbook can also be used in place of lecture. Labs are easy and online, can be done very independently if needed. tests are worth a lot towards overall grade, labs are a good amount of grade, quizzes are small part of overall grade

Dr. Luzzader-Beach is passionate about geography and is welcoming and kind to all students. I loved all of the content and spent a few hours outside of class reading and taking notes over the textbook before filling in the rest of my notes during lecture, which made me successful in the course, but it was hard to stay awake in class sometimes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is really nice. However the tests are extremely hard and you have to learn lots of information. Do not take this class, tests are 60% of your grade. The TA's do not really know the content and a lot of the work is by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures might have put me to sleep at one point, but the content is great and she gets the message out really well. She's caring and will work with you if any issues arise. Her labs weren't too tough, but be aware that some time may be needed outside of class to get a good grade on a lab. Reading the book and going over slides will help tons.

She's so cool! She's retiring, so this review probably won't be used by anyone, but I still want to let everyone know what a great professor she is. Very interesting lectures, and knows her stuff about Shakespeare. She's very straightforward and can be a bit surprising, but it's endearing.

Prof. Cullingford is by far my favorite professor! She truly cares about her students and is passionate about the subject material. There is a fair amount of reading, but that's almost the only homework and you do not have to be thorough to participate in class. Her essays are short with revisions and there are lots of completion grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Our class time was discussion-based and we were graded solely on writing. Professor Cullingford gives a lot of feedback, and tends to be pretty blunt, but she improved my writing immensely. Take time to get to know her, and go to office hours- she is so interesting and will openly offer advice. She is the kind of professor who wants you to succeed!

Dr. Cullingford has a vast array of knowledge that is admirable & interesting to listen to.  Sometimes, her behavior acted like that of a Shakespeare purist (unable to receive criticism against Shakespeare that addressed his sexism, racism, etc).  Very difficult grader whose numerous vague comments for feedback could almost be perceived as rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elizabeth was enthusiastic and invested. As long as you did the reading, usually a few acts of a play per week, and formed opinions you'd be all set in class. She's not great at using computers. Her feedback always made my day, because if you do well she is very sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a reason for Prof Cullingford's 5/5. She is so caring and funny to her students. She was very understanding during covid and made sure to make us feel comfortable. Very detailed feedback on essays. She gave us a chance to revise both essays and recorded the average of our revision and the original. Hard to get a high A on essays.

I hadn't taken a poetry class before, and this ended up being a GREAT choice. Although Cullingford does have high expectations for your essays, I promise that getting a good grade in the class is attainable (she gave us lots of cushion). Her commentary is extremely thorough on all of your work and her lectures are highly informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are plenty of reading and writing assignments; if you put in the effort, you can learn a lot. Dr. Cullingford communicates expectations clearly. She's a hard grader, as well as a helpful, insightful professor who wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: No Comments

She is such a wonderful professor. She is genuinely interested in teaching so you actually learn something. She is one of those professors who when you leave her class you feellike you've actually learned something, and enjoyed it!
Wonderful professor.  Intelligent, friendly, seems to actually like teaching.  Great voice and accent.

Honestly, she has been great to have this semester. She is so understanding, caring, and engages with her students. She does give a lot of homework, but that's normal for a language course since it's worth a lot of credits. She is strict on grammar, but I really love that because it helps improve a lot. There is no required textbook. Recommend 100%

Ok to be fair I took this class when writing flags were mandatory so idk how the material will change, but I loved Mme Schleppe, she's witty and caring, and really wants you to just learn the language. This class really helped me deepen my understanding of the french language and encourage me to continue learning french.
An excellent, caring, and loving professor. She just wants the best for her students & truly loves the French language and culture.

I love Madame Schleppe! She is a great professor and so funny. The class is pretty fast-paced. However, that is expected from an advanced language class. She sets up all the assignments with detailed instructions, is very thorough with grading, and gives excellent feedback. There are a few oral and written exams and a final project.

Mme. Schleppe is great! The class is 3 essays, 3 written exams, 4 oral exams (15-30mins), and a final project. The workload is manageable, but you do have some videos to watch/things to read before every class and a few smaller, easier assignments mixed in. The content is great if you're interested in French culture, politics, and social issues!

Dr. Schleppe is the best professor in the French department at UT and undoubtedly one of the best professors I have had overall. This class was focused on music in the Francophone world, and while there was consistent homework, the topics were usually fun and interesting, especially if you're a music lover. She's super engaging and accessible too.

The film topics help you learn french and she goes over grammar from FR 320E so that you establish a better foundation. The movies are fantastic and give you a good basis in french cinema and the importance of storytelling. This has got to be my favorite french class with the best french professor. She is a stickler for grammar, so keep that up!

Madame Schleppe is one of the best professors I've had at UT! She's definitely one of the best French instructors I've ever had. She makes learning French practical and fun. What makes her class so enjoyable is her unique personality that shines through her teaching. If I could give you any advice, stay on top of the homework and review often.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Madame Schleppe is wonderful! There's daily homework which can sometimes be tedious, but it's always very helpful and key to success in this course. She never cancels her classes or office hours and is consistently available to support you. I will definitely be taking French classes with her in the future as she's kind and very engaging.

I love Bea! She made my mornings so much better with her ever-present enthusiasm. She'd show us all these hilarious French music videos for us to learn vocab or grammar. As long as you take the time to do the homeworks in the packet and actually talk to your partner in French in class, you'll be sure to succeed.

I ADORE Mme Schleppe! She is a fair grader and homework is EVERYTHING for a decent class environment. She is always on top of things and helps you if you reach out. The course uses French and integrates it with current issues in France. Relative to big chapters, the assigned readings aren't long as long and keep up with the grammar!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I LOVE Madame Schleppe. She makes you want to work hard. She is very accessible via email and rarely cancels office hours. The subject material is challenging and interesting! Get ready for grammar quizzes.
She is so helpful and funny. The class as every language class in UT is very demanding but still as long as you put effort you will be fine. I would definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mme Schleppe was an amazing French professor and really knew how to connect learning advanced French concepts with talking about current issues going on in society. Nonetheless, the class is extremely grammar-intensive and if you should definitely brush up on grammar topics if you need before taking the class with any professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Mme Schleppe is one of the best professors I've ever had. She wants you to succeed and is very easy to talk to. She will explain what you got wrong on tests and is a pretty fair grader. It was a difficult class but I did well in it because of her

Mme Schleppe is an amazing French professor! She is really easy to talk to and definitely always there for you if you need anything. She does give a good amount of homework which is expected to get better at the language and will call on you in class so be prepared to speak. As long as you prepare and do your work you will love the class
Very sweet woman who knows her stuff. I found she was a very fair grader, the tests were hard and the homework was plenty, but I got through this class with a decent grade.

Best french professor I've had by far. This was supposed to be my most difficult french semester, but I ended up making a higher grade in her class than any of my past french classes. She's a really easy grader, but she does follow the strict no-absence policy.

VERY fair teacher. She genuinely cares for her students!! She was extremely flexible and accommodating when I got sick and had to miss an exam. I did let her know ahead of time and provided a doctor's note, though. One of the best teacher's I've had!

Overall, she is a great professor, however she WILL NOT break from the syllabus. I missed a test and went over my limit on absences due to family issues and the death of a close friend, and she would not budge on the "no make-ups" and  "too many absences = loss of points" rules. I ended up failing because of this. Other than that, she is great.
Best teacher in the French department.
No Comments
No Comments
Great prof, as Polish was already a language I spoke, (with many errors) she made sure to correct me and taught me a lot I previously did not know.
You have to pay attention, she is very nice and sweet.
Very passive aggressive.

Pani Kaminska was truly one of the best professors I have had in my life. She was incredibly fun and I loved how we also learned about Poland's culture. The small class size allowed us to get individual help and do lots of group work. Definitely take her class!

Dr. Barchas is unclear on what is expected from students and gives contradictory information on assignments. She is good at lecture, but cannot communicate assignments. She also didn't tell us we had to come up with a UNIQUE object for the final assignment until the day we were allowed to choose objects, so start thinking now if you have her.

Not a bad class, definitely can be fun if you like close reading and Jane Austen. Relied mostly on TA, I had Emma and she was super nice and accessible. Lots of reading and writing super early though. Midterm annd quizzes isn't that bad if you just pay attention to lectures though. Tons of extra credit opportunities, total 5% extra possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Not as bad as others say it is. Lots of reading but you can get by skimming it.
As long as you write according to the professor's style in class, you'll do fine on the three writing assignments. Quite a unique class. Mandatory discussion attendance but you get 3 skips. Amazing and helpful TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Barchas has a psycho-sexual relationship with Jane Austen. She obsesses over her to the point of sucking out all the fun of her novels. When first signing up, I read the warnings of this class, and ignored them. I thought I would be the exception - I love to read, write, and I'm well versed in Austen. Listen to me now: you are NEVER the exception.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You will enjoy this class if you enjoy reading and literature. It is VERY ready heavy, so be prepared to annotate and keep track of details, but lectures were super helpful when it came to essay writing and quizzes. If you can write well, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting, but the class is so difficult for no reason. The TAs do all the grading, and they are both really different in terms of grading, as one is really harsh while the other one lets bs slide. Don't take this class if you have a choice, find something else in the first week, because I promise you ITS NOT WORTH IT.
this prof is ruder than a b and is a cheeky nancy just flat out annoying to be in class

This class was HARD, don't get me wrong. The reading/paper-writing was overwhelming at times, but honestly, it was worth it as someone who genuinely loves Jane Austen and was okay with committing a lot of time to learn more about her books. Just DO NOT take this class unless you also love Jane Austen!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of writing, with no writing flag. Quizzes are heavily based off of what is said during lecture. Grades are also based on what TA is grading, so if you have a harsh TA, then you might not score as high in the class as others.Lots of reading in short periods of time as well (4 novels). Honestly, I only read and wrote about the first 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class as a UGS was VERY challenging. It was a lot for me to balance with other classes that were much more important. I ended up getting an A but it was a lot of trial and error which I struggled with. Be ready to put in more effort than expected but you will be fine if you're in this class! Professor Barchas is very fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you are taking this UGS beware. It's so difficult for no reason that everything is graded very hard. It is possible to get an A but only if you put in a lot of effort which was a real struggle for me since I had a lot of other classes to juggle. DO NOT TAKE THIS IF YOU HAVE A CHOICE. It was honestly awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: GET READY TO READ FR. there are three books you have to read. there are no clear rubrics for any assignments, so you have no idea where your grade is coming from. She's honestly an icon, so I can't be mad at her. Also, if you max out on extra credit, an 89 is an A (because you can get up to 5 points on your average added).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For an UGS, this course was unreasonably difficult. Dr. Barchas is a harsh grader and it is almost impossible to an A on an assignment. The only thing that saved me was my TA. The lectures are interesting and Dr. Barchas is passionate about Austen. This UGS is not for the weak. Beware and good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas is somewhat unapproachable and has very strict views when it comes to grading. Students never get access to the rubric and expectations for all assignments are not made clear whatsoever. Lectures are somewhat useful as they serve as material for the quizzes, research papers, and midterm. Attendance is mandatory for discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Do not listen to most of the negative reviews on this. This is not a blow-off class, but I think it's worth it. Barchas doesn't take BS, and it made me a better writer. I got an A+ in the class and I didn't read every book all the way through. If you aren't completely incompetent, you will be totally fine. Interesting content, smart professor!

Barchas is harsh but she is very knowledgeable and teaches a lot of information well. This course was definitely challenging for a UGS but our class became a community. Grading is determined mainly by your TA and there are no rubrics which made essay writing hard. The canvas is a bit outdated and confusing but office hours will be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nearly impossible to receive a grade higher than a B+. Considering this is a UGS, that's unreasonable and laughable. Barchas' main statement was, "We do not read for plot." Course should not be titled "Jane Austen on page & screen" if we are just looking at the historical context + significance/meaning of specific words/objects during the time.

Dr. Barchas is super funny and I can tell she wants the best for her students. A lot of the class is trial and error which can be frustrating. If you are looking for a blow-off UGS, this is not the one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of fun extra credit. So much reading. Prof is a tiny bit unapproachable but not in a bad way. The essay topics are interesting and make you think, but are totally doable. She's also a good lecturer and knows so much about Austen. I will say it was a bit much for a simple UGS class and was kind of more of a pain (at times) but overall was nice
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory on Fridays for discussion with the TAs. Hard graders and doesn't provide a lot of information for each assignments which are only 3 mini essays, oral presentation and weird museum scavenger hunt. Lecture at 8am on Tuesday and Thursdays are so pointless and boring, fell asleep almost every time I attended. Hard & weird class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. B is difficult to please. The course content is interesting, but the pace of reading 4 novels in a semester is grueling. The learning curve is high and Barchas can be condescending at times if your ideas don't match her own. Overall, there are easier UGS classes. My saving grace is that my TA was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was my third class with Prof. B, and I  have so much respect for her. She can undoubtedly be intimidating, and her grading is a bit harsh, especially on your first assignments. However, her main goal is always to make you better and she is very good at doing so! This class was a great course to cover the inquiry flag and learn about research.

This class is grueling, but I honestly think Prof B made me a better writer. The feedback on research papers is extremely constructive, but 4 difficult novels was a LOT of reading for one semester. The TA was incredible, but unless you have a passion for literature that feels unbreakable, there are easier UGS courses. Know what you're getting into.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Barchas will make you wish you never knew how to read. She's extremely rude, and will make you feel ashamed if you have reach out and ask for help. Expects her students to be obsessed with Jane Austen, even though we are taking the class to earn a mere credit. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas has high expectations and can be a tough grader. However, her lectures are some of the best I've had, and her curriculum improved my essay-writing skills immensely. She is extremely knowledgeable and well-respected in the Jane Austen community.

I never cried over assignments before taking this professor. My problem with this course is, as a UGS, the pacing can be very overwhelming. She is a tough grader, and the assignments require a lot of brainpower to conceptualize. She can also be very condescending in feedback. Amazing lecturer but there are much less stressful UGS' you could take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked Jane Austen until I took this class. Hard grader, claims that we don't read for plot but for vague pass by references you would never get. I thought I was a good writer until this class. When I asked for help, I felt looked down on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. B is very challenging but so worth it! She's a harsh grader, and you'll probably have a bit of a learning curve at the start of the semester, but as you understand her expectations and grading style you'll improve. Her critiques are harsh but are genuinely meant to make you better. She rewards improvement and wants to see you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a class for the faint of heart when it comes to reading/writing. Although perhaps Professor Barchas took a different outlook on classes this semester because she was totally awesome. Super witty, perhaps a bit condescending at times. Regardless, her class was great, and I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: If you're not willing to devote some serious time to this class, I wouldn't take it.
