Professor Barchas can come across as scary or intimidating but she really does root for your success. The workload was definitely a little bit heavy, but she was extremely open to suggestions from students. We were all at least a little sad when we said bye to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Burchas was my UGS professor and it was rough. It felt like no matter what I did, I could not be successful. Especially when writing papers. I ended up dropping the class because I refused to let a UGS drop my GPA as much as it was going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I must admit my writing, in general, has improved since taking her class. However, she is challenging and is very vague on how she grades essays. She will make you question everything you write in an essay. She can be condescending sometimes to. I would not recommend her class if you don't like Jane Austin and if you are an ok writer.

The grading criteria for essays is unclear and vague. The professors and TAs are stubborn and slightly condescending. The only good thing about this class is that the quizzes are easy. I wouldn't recommend this class for anyone. Even you like Jane Austen, I'm sure this class would kill whatever passion you had for her works.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Barchas' "Jane Austen on Page and Screen" is an obsessive and impossible course that is headed by someone whose passion for Jane Austen has turned them into a pretentious scholar who cannot relate to nor teach their students. If you were a good writer in High School, you will find that none of your skills will be good enough for her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the class because I love Jane Austen novels, but that love is gone now. The class is based off of 3 papers, I believe 10 quizzes, and a midterm, but her grading criteria is EXTREMELY unclear, and her critiques are blatantly mean instead of any kind of constructive criticism. Avoid her at quite literally all costs, I regret taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm a Sophomore now and this is easily the worst professor I've had in my three semesters. Had her for my UGS. I attended all the lectures, went to office hours often, and did all the homework and still did poorly. If i could do it again, I would definitely have Q dropped the class. Avoid at all costs.

Her grading system is very unclear. You could turn in an essay she calls "full of merit"and yet she'll give you a B. She had a lecture on writing well but spent the whole time making fun of examples of our peers' papers. She's a great lecturer, I'll give you that. It was a very stressful class though, and I wouldn't ever ever ever take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Slightly intimidating, personally made me feel kind of dumb sometimes, but she does genuinely care about your success and knows how to engage everyone. Grades consisted of three papers (one of which you discuss with her and revise), one test, and one in-class essay. The class was really interesting, but make sure to keep up with the reading.

If you don't love Jane Austen, DON'T take this class. Barchas is passionate about what she does, but there is just too much work for a UGS course. Essay projects that aren't really explained very well, hour discussions every week, oral presentations, plus reading 4 novels. The tests are very long, so you must have a good understanding of the novels
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took her Jane Austen UGS: Too much work!! You have to read 4novels, write essays, oral presentations etc. The expectations for assignments are unclear and grading is very tough. Even the extra credit requires too much work. Although the professor is SUPER passionate about her subject (and take it if you are too) but otherwise there are easier UGSs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: When you enter this class you think its going to be an easy UGS compared to the other UGSs UT provides. Well your wrong get ready to be forced to dive hella deep into Jane Austen your expected to basically become her. Grading is harsh but assignments wont be hard if you work on it early. Most activities/assignments are irrelevant extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Being in this class is a little like being in a cult: do not take it if you're not obsessed with Austen, you will not enjoy being called a Janeite or being around others who are obsessed. Barchas is not the nicest, I would recommend asking the TAs questions instead of asking her because she will accuse you of being illiterate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Friendly, qualified and passionate about the subject material, but sometimes got carried away discussing her own accomplishments. 3 research projects count for most of the final grade and introduce students to resources/databases which was a huge help in other classes. Avoid if you're looking for an easy UGS or hate writing essays/doing research.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The Jane Austen film and literature class is incredibly interesting but also incredibly difficult. The amount of reading you do is A LOT, and once you get behind it's very hard to catch up. The three essays are difficult, but graded fairly. Just make sure to utilize the TAs and ask lots of questions. Dr. Barchas is very knowledgeable and exciting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading and the three essays given are graded really tough. The essay prompts are also pretty stupid so don't take this class unless you are confident in your BSing skills. Otherwise, there was some interesting things learned in this course, and Dr. Barchas and the TAs were okay.

I took this class because I needed to have a UGS, thinking it would be interesting because it is covering Jane Austen. I have to admit the material was interesting, but the way papers are graded ultimately hurt my score in the class. Papers are graded heavily on views that you're supposed to have on specific topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had her for a Jane Austen class. I absolutely hated the class and the TA but Barchas herself was pretty cool. Funny, and passionate about what she teaches. Class itself was dreadful but she was sweet and taught me a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas is hit or miss, you either love or hate her. Do not sign up for this class unless you are a good reader and writer, truly it is not for the faint of heart. But you learn so much and get exposed to so many amazing things. This is not an easy A course, but is the kind of course you will be thankful for later in your college career

Pros: she is so entertaining and funny, lectures are amazing, she improves your writing and research skills exponentially, tons of extra credit, interesting content. Cons: VERY unclear grading, does not accept any opinion but her own as right, can be harsh and judgmental Overall, I would definitely recommend her- its painful but worth it!!

Barchas is obnoxious, over-the-top and thinks she's really funny. She knows a lot about the material she teaches (Jane Austen) but looks for very specific answers and expects near impossible creativity and originality in assignments and tests. It's important to go to lecture, though attendance isn't counted (only for section). Frustrating at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you're a Jane Austen fanatic, and are ready to join a cult dedicated to her excellency, I still wouldn't recommend this class. Grades are based upon essays to do with "research" where the expectations are very unclear + 2 exams. Professor and TA's can be arrogant and VERY particular to their own point of view, and VERY condescending otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Knowledgable about what she is teaching but is very difficult. You are asked to write 3 papers about in detail things about the novels and have 2 in class exams about things she has mentioned in class. She is unclear about expectations. This class is way too difficult to be a UGS. I do not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very hard to please professor and TA's in the Jane Austen class. If your papers don't really reflect what they have in their minds then you won't do great (difficult to truly figure out what they want). Unreasonable amount of reading. To me the class is just ran by people overly obsessed with Jane Austen. Waste of money and no purpose to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's animated and obviously loves what she's teaching. I'm a film major and have read very little 19th century novels before this and only for class. You get what you put into the class - don't ever read the books (and only look them up on sparknotes) and never attend class? - of course you're going to do poorly.  High expectations and great class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever met in my life. She knows nothing about teaching. She just grades your paper whatever she wants and she ruins many students' GPA. If you want to take her class, please prepare for a C or D for this class.l

Ridiculous standards for what she wants from her essays (not difficult, she just has her own ideas for what SHE thinks your writing should look like, and will crucify you if you don't give her what she wants to see). I found her obsession with Jane Austen and constant patting herself on the back obnoxious enough that I wouldn't take her again.

Prof. Barchas was hard.  I'm a music major and I don't particularly like english, but I thought learning about Jane Austen would be fun. Boy was I wrong.  The TAs do your grading, but they are just as hard to please as Prof. Barchas. If you're looking for a fun UGS, this is not it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: It's definitely a tough class, but I learned a lot - not only about Jane Austen/the regency era, but also about how to conduct research and write effectively. She is very passionate about her work, and her passion is contagious.  Don't take this class if you can't commit to reading 5 Jane Austen novels and writing 3 papers.

Shes a good professor for helping you tune up your writing, but is insanely into Jane Austen and expects the moon from your essays. All the reading sucks and only discussions are mandatory. Lecture is a joke that is naptime for half the class.
Prof. Barchas is with out a doubt an amazing  professor. She's very thorough. But if you don't like English courses, or have trouble keeping up with readings, this class probably isn't for you.

Grading is harsh. It's her way or the highway. For papers you practically have to invent the moon. I love Jane Austen and overall I found enjoyment in the class but if you value grades or free time I would not recommend this UGS.

I love Dr. Barchas' lectures because  she's very animated. You have to read A LOT and take a lot of notes during her lectures. Your grades depend entirely upon your TA and participate in sections as much as you can. There are only two tests in the class and it is a lot of writing. If you are looking to take an easy UGS, don't take this.
Very long papers and very hard grading. Tests are near impossible to study for because of multitude of materials. Lots and lots of reading.

Prof. Barchas knows her stuff when it comes to Jane Austen. She presents interesting and engaging lectures, but you'll have to read the 4 books she assigns to remain interested and do well. My TA was really helpful when it comes to writing the 3 papers, and Prof. Barchas always gives examples in lecture. Challenging class, but definitely worth it!

Dr. Barchas knows her stuff when it comes to Jane Austen. Most of the people in the class were Jane Fanatics and Barchas is as well; if you don't have much interest in this genre I would not take her. Barchas is funny and witty and likeable, but sometimes can be moody and not the most helpful. I made an A- in the class mostly because ofessay grades

I never took the course. He seems like a chill guy, though. I spoke to him a couple of times in person, and he is very knowledgeable about the subject matter he is teaching. I didn't fully follow everything because the class was not related to my major :( I would highly recommend taking any class that he teaches!

He's a great guy I really enjoyed going to class and learning about asphalt lol :). He always listens to the class in terms of making open notes or group quizzes. You can work on homework's in groups and the final exam was open notes. The final was pretty similar to the in person quizzes we took in class. Overall great guy and interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took him for design of Bituminous Materials. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gave great lectures where you really do learn a lot. Quizzes are very fair.

Perhaps my favorite professor at UT, knowledgable, approachable, caring and well-prepared. The project can be a lot of work but is also fun, you learn so much. I would definitely take another class with him.

Amazing professor! Ask questions, you'll get answers. Class centers around the main project which is a fantastic approach, everything you see during lecture gets to be tested/applied on semi-real project scenarios. I recommend this class and this professor.

A fantastic professor, who genuinely cares about the well-being of his students. In his lectures he gives you important background knowledge and information about the assignments. In every class he promotes curiosity and critical thinking. Although the course load is very heavy with multiple research papers, this course will allow you to grow.

This is a hard class in general, but I would say he is the best professor to take it with. The homework are 10% midterm is 40% and final is 50% of the grade but his curve is the only reason I passed. As long as you show up and take good notes you should have an easier time on the exams. Try to find people to do homework with to help you understand.

The class is very interesting and the problems are fun.... when you are given effective material to work with. Homeworks do not prepare us for exam questions and often take multiple hours to do. I got myself sick once because of how much time it took to do one homework. The material is very interesting, just study as much as you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: High stakes exams (Midterm 40% and Final 50%). No recorded lectures, but lecture notes are posted. Homeworks (10 total, 2 drop) are good practice for the exams. Midterm and Final are curved for fairness for those unable to attend midterm (Final 90%). I would recommend staying on top of the course material as falling behind can easily overwhelm you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bhaskar is a smart man which is why it's so easy to get confused when he explains. Watch videos for clarity and DO additional practice problems. There is one midterm worth 40% (avg ~60) and one final worth 50% (avg ~68). I got below average for both exams and got a B so he curves good. DO NOT WAIT LAST MINUTE FOR STUDYING. Keep practicing activley.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Best!! This class was easy. Homework was a big part of your grade, but they are easy if you read the textbook. Tests were taken at home and open note. Lectures were also interesting and Dr. Best tries to make them as interactive as possible.
Dr. Best is genuinely amazing and if he taught more astronomy classes I would take every single one. I truly enjoy his lectures and the homework and tests are not bad at all.

Prof. Best is an amazing lecturer, and he knows why most students are taking his class, so he makes it as fun and engaging as he can. I would recommend this as a science credit for sure, one of the best classes I've taken here at UT.
Amazing professor! Loved his lectures. Very manageable for a student not in stem. Take this class!!
good teacher, not much else to say

Dr. Best is great! Assignments are very very manageable, lectures are genuinely interesting, tests are take-home, and there is ample extra credit. If you're considering taking this course for science credit, do it!

Best is an amazing professor who is passionate about what he is teaching and genuinely wants to get to know and interact with his students. If you have to join a waitlist for this class, DO IT! I would take this class 1000x over
I love Dr. Best. This class was great, interesting but not unnecessarily difficult for a science credit. Highly highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Best is great. Knows students are there for credit, you are still able to get something out of his class if you go every week. There are instapolls in class not for credit and questions for EC every single class so attendance helps your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! He knows how to keep students engaged, even though most of us are only taking it for the credit. In his lectures, he makes complicated concepts easy to understand. If you take his class, please participate and ask questions. He is genuinely so kind, funny, and nerdy in a good way.

He knows most people taking this class are not majoring in anything related to astronomy. Still genuinely one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I've ever met. My only regret with this class is not paying attention more during the lecture and choosing to do other class work instead. Every lecture was extremely interesting and engaging.
He's my queen.

100% recommend this class for science credit. Lectures were extra credit points and tests were take home. You can tell Professor Best truly has passion for what he teaches and fosters a great learning environment.
Best professor at UT. Attendance is EXTRA CREDIT. His exams are at home as well. Easy Science credit so please take it.

Best is a very good lecturer and is very knowledgeable. There is HW before every lecture and they are due before class. They're also a big part of your grade. Tests are open-note and timed, gives us like 3 days to do it. An easy A as long as you do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best is an excellent professor who gives good lectures and makes the class super accessible. Attendance is not mandatory but gives extra credit. Tests are open-note, online, and not hard. Homework makes up most of the final grade, and getting a good grade on it is easy.

LOVE PROFESSOR BEST! Such an amazing professor, probably one of the best I have had so far! Definitely recommend taking his class if you need an easy science credit. He is very approachable and loves answering questions. He's passionate about astronomy and you can tell! He is so kind and cares for his students. This man must be protected
Take this class if you need an easy science credit. Attendance is for extra credit and the tests are all online! The homework is doable and the tests are easily done as they are online and open note.

AMAZING TEACHER/CLASS! Lectures are interesting, but not mandatory since attendance is extra credit. Teacher is so nice and engaging! Homework is light and there's time in many class periods to start it. Tests are online, at home, open note, and for you to take whenever in 2 day period. I would recommend this class to anyone needing science credit.

Very straightforward class. Just gotta do the homework. Then 2 exams a week. Teacher kinda sucks at giving lectures. But hey, classes aren't mandatory. My friend was in the class with one of the other professors and she had tons more work, so I'd still recommend Best over the other teachers, for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class and adored his teaching style. His lectures do an excellent job of explaining everything in the reading in a very easy-to-digest way. I did all the reading and went to all the lectures, but you don't really need to do both. I'd recommend just going to the lectures and maybe reviewing the reading if you're having trouble.

Dr. Best is a quirky and wonderfully enthusiastic professor. My major is in no way related to Astronomy, but I found myself considering taking additional classes or even taking on a minor if CNS allowed them... All-in-all, a very great professor who clearly loves his profession!

This class was super easy because everything was online and open note. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you can get a lot of extra credit just for showing up. The professor was super nice as well and clearly very passionate about astronomy. Highly recommend to get your science credit through this course.
Interesting class that is not difficult. I took his class for a science credit and don't regret it at all, his lectures are interesting an he offers extra credit every class period.

Professor Best is actually the best. His class is by far one of the easiest classes I've taken so far. I recommend him so much. His lectures were also very interesting, you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches.
Professor Best is the best professor. Class is pretty simple. 10/10 recommend him if you need to get a science credit out of the way.

I took this class for an easy science credit. As someone who struggles with science, this was one of the easiest classes I took this semester. The professor himself is extremely passionate about the topic, was super funny, and was a lot of fun and interesting to listen to. I would 100% take this class again and highly recommend!

EASIEST CLASS EVER. Attendance not mandatory so I stopped going. Mastering Astronomy HW due Mon, Wed, Fri, each week, all on quizlet and its 70% of your grade. Three tests, all take home, also all on quizlet! Not protocored and its 10% each of your grade. TAKE FOR EASY SCIENCE CREDIT!

Dr. Best is amazing. His lectures are super interesting and you can tell he genuinely cares about his research. There are pre-readings for every class and homework after every class, but the homework is easy and lectures cover the readings. Theres also 3 easy exams and he provides opportunities for extra credit.
Love having Dr. Best. There's a decent amount of reading technically assigned, but the lectures are simple, fun, and easy to understand, so you could probably get by without reading.
Fun easy science class. 5 homework grades = 1 test grade. Interesting lectures, lots of reading assigned but the tests are open note and homework-based so I didn't read much. Tiny bit of math.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bhat is a pretty good professor. His exams are fair, but he underestimates the time it takes to do them which led to a failing class average on the 1st exam. The class only has 2 exams, mid-term is 30%, final is 40% of your grade, homework is 25%, & participation is 5%. He covers how to do the HW well in class and is an understanding prof

He is a great prof! Super nice, cares about students, explains concepts well. However, there is breakdown in grading with the student grader being SUPER harsh and Dr. Bhat did not accept any feedback on that. Material can get confusing, homeworks are easy but the exams are incredibly hard
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students. There's are one midterm (30%) and final (40%). He pretty much gave us all the answers to the homework (25%) in class so it is important to attended them all (they are not recorded). He made the exams open notes which helped tremendously. If you understand how to do the homework and you go to class you'll be fine.

Dr. Bhat is a passionate lecturer who cares about his students. He always wears a lumbar support attachment strapped to his back which brings me joy. This was my easiest class this semester because the homework is easy, and the exams are cake with the curve. W
Super great professor, he wants you to really learn and understand the material. He loved to get to know students which makes me want to go to class.
Brilliant lecturer, explains difficult concepts in an easy and clear way; also a tough grader.

Dr. Bhat is an inspiring and caring prof. The course isn't too difficult but there is only one midterm and one final (40%) so you have to do well. I wish he went over more examples before the first test because I wasn't ready. Weekly homework isn't bad. Lectures are actually enjoyable and he keeps things interesting.

I left started and ended the course completely confused. No notes except from lecture. The only practice you have are homework problems where he explains half of it and expects you to know the concepts he never went over. Little communication between graders. No TA. He seems like a nice guy but not a great professor at all :/ sooo many tangents

The material itself was super interesting, but Bhat wasn't the best lecturer. His handwriting was sloppy and he went on many different roundabouts that didn't pertain to the content. Any time I contacted him for help on hwk or clarifying grading he would spew off some philosophical nonsense and wouldn't answer my questions
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loved him ,made me want to be a transportation engineer (which I now am). Really enlightened me on daily transportation things I had never thought about before.

Good instructor, worst professor in my life. After class, I asked a calculation question cz I was confused on the concept. He raged because I didn't get the concept. He kept saying "I don't know how you can't get this" over and over. He didn't try to listen to me. I was asking different one first time learning transportation system in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he is honestly not a bad professor but sometimes lectures are boring. the exams are very fair and are similar to the practice ones that he uploads but they definitely felt very rushed. the case studies and hw take forever to complete though. overall not as bad as what these reviews are making him seem like.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bickel was a mixed bag. He gave great lectures explaining finance in a way that applies to real life, but the assignments felt like busy work because they weren't hard, just many problems to solve. The material was really easy, but you had to rush through the exams and there wasn't enough time to check your work. Going to lecture made it an easy A

This was by far the worst ME course I have ever taken at UT. Bickel has no empathy for the students with his low exam averages, and his condescending attitude makes it difficult to ask him questions. The exams are filled with niche concepts from the textbook and excel cell knowledge. My TA couldn't even explain concepts from Test 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Studied the material he gave us + textbook for weeks in preparation for the final. Did not matter he decided to test us over software formulas and stuff that was not on the textbook or any class work. There was no way to study for that final. A lot of people failed even with his “holiday bonus”. Condescending when you ask questions. Bad teacher.
Out of all the MechE courses I've taken, by far the worst experience thanks to Professor Bickel. I hope he gets in trouble for the way he graded students

Absolute worst professor I have ever had in my life. Failed the class my senior year and now I will have to be behind a semester. Test questions were nothing like the homework's and quizzes and instead were completely random and never really taught. He should be fired

Worst professor I've ever had. Homework didn't match exams, quizzes were useless, and he referenced group projects on exams without notice. Final required Excel formulas for paid software we barely used. Curve was 6 percentage points, leaving half the class failing or with a C-. Unhelpful, arrogant, and spiteful—avoid at all costs.
Poorly written final exam that included content NOT mentioned would be on the final.

The homeworks and case studies are fine if you put in the effort, but some of the exams felt more like trivia rather than Engineering Finance. Students were tested over content not covered in homework or TA sessions, making them artificially difficult. Overall, this was my least-favorite class at UT.

Bickel has the biggest ego I have ever seen in college. He is condescending when you ask him questions, wastes everyone's time in an 8am clicking through slides, and makes ridiculous exams. Bickel must think I'm Alex Trebek the way his exams felt more like playing obscure jeopardy completely unprepared than actually testing over a class I took.

The homework isn't the worst and sure the cases are long but the exams are just ridiculous. On the second exam and on the final, he heavily weighted questions that were not covered by ANY homework problem or TA session, but rather briefly mentioned in class. It seems he is actively punishing students and this is not acceptable. Avoid if possible.

Bickel fails to create an environment where students feel their effort to learn the course content is rewarded.

Reading the textbook and completing supporting material, like the homework, will not help you succeed on tests. Test content tends to be artificially difficult, with questions requiring methods we never used or random @risk knowledge.
Tests should be to test learning but he decides to make it about very niche topics. Do not take.

The exams are significantly more challenging than the material covered in class or the homework. He does not test students over relevant topics and does not want students to succeed. As a mechanical engineer, finance with Bickel is the hardest class I have ever taken.

This professor strives to create tests that are malicious towards students, with convoluted prompts for questions, to testing students on methods that are never used in the real world such as the Pool Method. His lectures were very hard to follow and the cases took a long time, avoid this malicious teacher at all costs.
hardest class in meche degree for no reason, pulls most of his exam questions over things he glazes over in 5 seconds in a class that nobody goes to cuz he's so boring and its at 8 am
Bro has nothing better to do so he on a power trip teaching mechanical engineering students finance.

If you want to fail and hate yourself take this class. I don't even think he knows what he's writing in these exams. He made this semester so much more rigorous than he did last semester. He took away a test drop and designed his exams for 60 averages. I used a grade calculator at least 3 times just for this class. Students are scraping by for C's
FIRE BICKEL!
Bickel wants engineers to take a 5th year so we can continue to give him terrible course evaluations and RMP's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He intentionally misdirects students on the content that will be on the test and throws pointless curveballs that have no objective other than crushing the grades. My TA literally didn't know how to solve a question worth 25% of Exam 2, which he then repeated on the final. If you take this professor, don't bother studying because it doesn't help.

I wish this thing didn't have a word count. Just came of his final confident in none of my answers. I have put in more work in this class then an actual upper level division engineering course. This guy must hate himself and wants his students to hate him too. If I have to retake this class, absolutely nothing will make me retake it with Bickel.
No aura. Don't take Bickel

He writes his exams to fail his students. He does not test on your understanding of finance he wants you to attend his classes so you can remember what a button does on @RISK. TA's treat the exam setting like a highly guarded prison facility. Cheat sheets are unhelpful bc you cannot prep for his exams. Condescending attitude during office hours.

Avoid this guy if you can. His exams are hard, w/ concepts that are barely touched on in class. Grading feels almost vindictive. The class doesn't feel like an educational experience—it feels like a punishment for not deciphering his convoluted teaching style. Case studies are lengthly, discussions mandatory, 8am, no exam drops, steer clear of him.

I wouldn't wish 8ams w/ Bickel upon my worse enemy . His exams are intentionally designed to trick students, often covering obscure material barely mentioned. His grading is incredibly unfair, with little room for partial credit. This class is an unnecessarily stressful experience,he is trying to punish us for not remembering made up techniques.

4th years are failing eng finance. Exams are known for being unrealistically difficult. They frequently include obscure topics that were glossed over in class, making studying impossible. This course demands alot amount of time and effort, and the disconnect between the workload, instruction, and evaluation makes it feel unnecessarily grueling.

This class is supposed to be about finance not if you can remember excel and rick cell formulas. The workload is heavy, with case studies that require time and effort. The exams are designed to be difficult,bc lecture attendance is low, and the tests often center around abstract, poorly explained concepts to punish students for not attending class

Professor Bickel's exams are unrealistically difficult, often covering topics barely mentioned in lectures. He provides minimal resources to prepare, leaving students to teach themselves most of the material. The disconnect between lectures and assessments makes the class unnecessarily frustrating and stressful. Extremely heavy workload with cases.
Hardest exams, made up methods to trick his students. He wants his students to fail.

He is very knowledgeable and cares about the subject matter on a level different from his students. He is difficult to follow through the course and the tests and case studies often came from nowhere. Many engineering students do not want to devote the work and knowledge he requires for finance, because it does not feel relavent.

Took this class as a requisite, it has been heavier than most labs and project-based courses. Exams are purposely made more difficult due to the low attendance in lecture with abstract concepts being a majority of the exams. TA's also grade very harshly on exams. Lectures consist of him talking about himself and very little on content.

Exams are a lot harder than content covered and HW. He often throws an unreasonable curveball on the exams, doesn't care about students' understanding of the topic, and gives trick questions to punish students for not reading every small topic in the book.

Exams consist of topics not practiced on the homework and rarely mentioned in class. Doesn't prioritize making sure students actually understand the material and are able to practice it. Alongside this, there is a heavy workload with tests, case studies and homework, along with weekly quizzes.

Professor seems intent on using his class as some sort of "filter". While his first priority should be ensuring students understand the material, he is more interested in using his position for his own interests. Exams seem to be deliberately convoluted. You'd think some people would have better things to do in life but maybe he doesn't.

Uses a very strange scoring metric that could end up giving you a negative grade. There is homework and quiz every week, two exams, and four case studies. Probably the most workload I had out of all courses I took so far.
Good luck in this class. It will take up all of your waking and sleeping hours
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Get ready to work in this class. The topic he teaches is difficult, but he makes the content even more complicated. Very strict and has no compassion for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is probably the hardest classes that I have taken at UT. The subject itself is very difficult, but Professor Bisetti is extremely knowledgeable on the topic. He is extremely helpful at office hours and I feel that I truly have a good grasp on this difficult subject because of the classes rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bisetti is a fantastic professor. His understanding of and enthusiasm for the topic are unmatched, and he is extremely helpful if you seek guidance outside of class. The course is very difficult, but this is the nature of the subject. I think Bisetti does a good job of making it manageable without losing rigor.

Great professor, made CFD interesting for me and I had no previous interest in it. Really cares about the subject and is really good at teaching it and is great at answering and clearing up any and all questions. Some attendance pop quizzes.

CFD is an extremely hard subject but Prof. Bisetti is obviously an expert and is amazing at teaching it. This class was very hard at the start as sometimes the homework focus on material he hasn't taught yet, but lecture slides are posted before hand. Group project heavy but plenty of guidance is given. Overall, hard class but amazing teacher.

Awesome prof, super fun and great music taste. 610D is the heaviest homework load in the Spanish sequence, but Prof Luke makes it worth it with great, engaging lectures. He's clearly passionate about Spanish and I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Awesome professor and taught the content really well. Just a super nice guy as well. He gives great feedback and is very approachable. There's homework every day, but if you do it there's no way you won't do well. I really enjoyed being in the class.

This Spanish class was time-consuming, but very doable. Doing the homework/online work really helps to understand the grammar and vocabulary. Class was enjoyable because we were able to practice talking and applying what we learn from the workbook. Also, Professor Bishop is very patient and helpful when learning new concepts. Really recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although the textbook did awful job at explaining the grammar, Luke was great at helping you understand. If you didn't get it he would rephrase his explanations until one stuck. Very helpful office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class, as with the Spanish classes at UT, comes with a lot of outside work due to it being a 6 hour credit! He gives great feedback on homework and as long as you put in the effort you will do well in the course! I recommend making quizlets for vocab and using the chapter reviews in the textbook to study for the exams! Participation is vital!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got a 91 in the class and he gave me a B+ because of his grading system that is not fair

OK professor. Easy quizzes and exam. Complete all possible extra credit because he will try to give you the lowest final grade possible. I ended this class with a 91 and received a B freaking plus as a letter grade.. because of his unfair grading policy. The final presentation policy is a nightmare.

Nice guy w an unfortunate grading policy. His class material is engaging, but competitive nature of the final project makes caring about material>grade difficult. Wants you to read his mind and doesn't go by rubrics well. Said he would curve us down. Also asked for good CES survey scores. If the final wasn't a competition he wouldn't have to ask.
Horrible grading scale

While this class is interesting and Professor Bisett clearly knows a lot about marketing, the grading scale of this class is one of the worst at UT. He curves the class down and 30% of your grade is dependent on a group project, where he shows clear favoritism and the grading scale is unclear. He also frequently used AI for slides.

While the lectures can be interesting at times, the grading sucks. He wants his students to compete in order to get a good grade in the class. The final project is worth 30% of the grade, and if you are not a finalist, you can only get an 80%!! He also cleary has favorite students!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bisett is definitely passionate about marketing and cares for students. But he has inconsistent grading, curves down, and often doesnt follow his own rubric. Tests are easy but the curve down really messes with your grade. He uses AI for slides and tests which make the class feel less personal and is frustrating imo. Wouldnt take again unforch

Pits students against each other because he's curving us down. Wants us to stroke his ego. Uses AI to make all his slides and test questions. Tests are not too challenging but everything else is. Has a problem with almost everything. Don't take him if you don't absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Questions on exams and quizzes are pretty easy. The project is very important; it determines 30% of your grade and is graded more toughly than the other assignments. 30 minute podcasts paired with each chapter. He is lively and tries to encourage participation in class, fun professor. Easily accessible and understanding of student situations.

Professor Bisett is genuinely a very caring person and is a great professor! The class is structured very fairly with exams and a group project. Do the reading and participate in class, and you will be fine in the class.

MKT 357 was easily one of my favorite classes this semester. Prof Bisett genuinely seems to care about his students, and is very flexible regarding deadlines. Grading on projects was initially a little arbitrary. However, this improves a lot if you seek to understand expectations. Overall would recommend.

Great professor and even better person. He is knowledgeable about the subject and engages the class in nuanced discussions. I was consistently surprised at how well he was able to engage the class and encourage participation. He was a bit disorganized, but it was his first semester. He truly cares about each student and it shows.
He is wonderful! He loves what he teaches and is very knowledgeable about all kinds of film.

The content is easy and enjoyable, no exams, but the class is formatted HORRIBLY, and the professor is very confused by his own syllabus. Doesn't know how to use Canvas, not clear about due dates at all. TA mentioned he was about to retire, but I saw he's teaching English classes this summer and fall. Don't take him, just unnecessary stress.

The professor's lectures were very engaging, covering a wide range of topics, and the class exposed me to many films that I wouldn't have otherwise watched, many of which were exceptional and now among my all-time favorites. There are no exams but there are essays, but you can choose the topic of each essay and which film it's about.

Biow is really kind and understanding. He was very lenient with papers and often made accommodations/pushed back deadlines for us. Trips to the Blanton Museum were lots of fun! Only thing is that lectures seemed to be a little self-explanatory at times, but still engaging.

All you have to do is watch the movies, attend the lectures, and write thought pieces/ essays on them. Dr. Biow is passionate about film and the history of Italy, which made his lectures so enjoyable. Discussion sections were unenjoyable because people didn't talk much, though.

Dr. Biow is a great guy, and I enjoyed his lectures for Films and Filmmakers of Italy. All you have to do is watch the movie and be able to write about it. He will give you great feedback and extensions if needed. Mandatory discussion sections with TAs sucked, though, and were not very helpful since nobody would speak or show up. Good UGS choice!
Professor Biow is knowledgeable about the subject matter. Italian Films and Filmmakers was eye-opening and allowed me to gain a lot of cultural understanding.

Professor Biow was amazing. I hate writing, but I actually really enjoyed it. It's not a difficult class as long as you watch the films and can explain a film. Prof Biow gave extensions if students just asked and was all around a nice person to be taught by. I definitely recommend taking his class as a UGS, really easy way to get your credit.

This professor is hands down the type every student should encounter. He is very passionate about the discourse of his subject and encourages students to critically think and relate varying topics to the subject film. 5 Essays, first isn't graded. Quizzes every week about the film. Extra credit is given and they're lenient. Enjoyable and easy.

Very apparent that Biow cares about the subject and class. Biggest recommendation is to go to office hours and get his help he is very clear and helps so much. I don't love writing or analysis and it is one of my biggest weak points however Biow is so understanding and gives extensions if you need. Incredible professor one of the best for sure.
Biow is one of the nicest professors I have ever encountered. He always gave extensions, and always wants to see his students write their absolute best.

Took him for Italian Films and Filmmakers. Lectures were really interesting, even if I had no idea what I just watched in the movies. Definitely a guy who loves to hear himself talk ngl lol. Grade consists of 5 papers, and he grades one of them, rest are by the TAs. Biow himself is a harsh grader, but it's really easy to pull an A in this class.

Although I wasn't very interested in the content (not his fault at all), I really liked this professor. He was super understanding about deadlines, and made the workload very easy. Quizzes at the beginning of each class and 5 papers, with the first one being diagnostic. He gave great feedback and was very easily accessible!

I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would recommend it to everyone. While he is a tough grader, he is willing to help and he gives great feedback. He goes in-depth with his constructive criticism and it helps you improve your writing a lot! Super understanding guy and would give us lots of extensions and extra credit opportunities.

Biow gave C averages on papers despite needing a B to pass. You spend hours outside class watching movies to write 5 papers with prompts released days before the due date. The little feedback you may receive comes 6 weeks after turning the papers in. He did offer an extra credit assignment but it didn't help really anyone. Just take another UGS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Liked Biow, hated the class itself. The good: I rarely attended class and still managed to get an A & the lectures were enjoyable if interested in the subject. The bad: the required films were boring and excessive, and the papers were graded SO HARSHLY. You need to like writing and be somewhat interested in the subject to do well in this class.

Look, I've had ups and downs with this class, but Dr. Biow is a great professor and person despite the strict grading by him and the TAs. However, he became more lenient towards the end of my semester and allowed us to be more creative with our writing. He is willing to help and the classes are comprised of daily quizzes on the movies and 5 essays

Overall, the class wasn't bad. An A and even an A+ is definitely manageable. Especially if you really take the time to go into office hours to discuss your essays with the TAs and Professor Biow. I heard a lot of complaints about this class being too hard for a UGS course but TBH, most people were overreacting and got butt hurt over their essays.

Professor Biow is a great person but his class and these ratings were so deceiving. Most people often found themselves feeling worthless after getting grades back from their papers since they grade them so harshly. The mean for the papers is usually in the 70's range and for a UGS class, it should not be that hard. The films are also so boring.

(Fall 2020) Great class, great guy, watched a lot of movies I rly enjoyed. 4-5 papers to write but the analysis is fun. You won't learn much about cinematic techniques but the way he breaks movies down is interesting. Papers are graded kind of strictly (either by the TA/himself) but he's a really nice guy.

I love Prof Biow. He's so passionate about the films he talks about, and he's an interesting guy. Biow is very willing to work with you on your paper so ask him for help!!!! I had a love hate relationship with this class, but in the end I'm so glad I took Italian film.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biow is the best! He is fun, caring and passionate. You will learn a lot, but you are never graded over it. The info is useful, but not mandatory for your essays. He will help you work through your essays, so PLS TAKE HIS HELP! And you have weekly quizzes but they are easy if you watch the movies. Cherish your time in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Biow is an absolute dream! Although he is a very direct grader for papers, he cares about his students and takes time to help them outside of class on how to improve their writing. Hes passionate about what he does, and it shows. funny guy, kinda like danny devito

Prof Biow is really passionate about what he teaches, which makes it easy to be interested in the course material. There's a lot of papers, so be prepared for that. Don't volunteer yourself to have him grade your paper (as opposed to the TA) unless you're an extremely strong writer because his feedback is intense and brutal (albeit spot-on).

Biow loves what he teaches, which for me, was Italian cinema. He knows how to keep students engaged and has a great sense of humor. He even paid for some of us to see a film off campus. Be ready to write essays 1/2 times a month & a quiz over the movies every class day. Quizzes are easy to get an A on, as they are over basic things. Learned a lot!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Biow's lectures were super interesting and fun. He is a tough grader, but he only grades one essay and he is more than willing to work with you outside of class to improve your essay. Go see him if you want to ensure an A on your paper! There were some really good movies, but a lot of the postmodernism unit movies were disturbing and confusing.

The movies we watched were often depressing but the lectures were very interesting. This class is a writing flag but the amount of writing you have to do is far from outrageous, the final (longest) paper is only 4-5 pages.

I adored this UGS and am so glad I was able to learn from Professor Biow. He is a fantastic lecturer and incredibly passionate about Italian history/cinema. I learned so much, and I actually enjoyed writing the papers! If you like film analysis, this is the class for you. You don't even have to watch all the movies to get an A (though you should).

He is a really friendly professor and definitely has interesting lectures. His expectations of papers are a little confusing and he is a really tough grader. Overall it is an interesting class but the movies are time-consuming.

Dr. Biow's UGS over Italian Cinema was overall a good experience. He is an engaging lecturer and the class was an easy A. He didn't put in grades till the end of the semester but due to weekly quizzes about the films (which were easy as long as you watched), your grade should be fine. Super caring guy and would definitely recommend this class

His lectures are fun. There's a decent amount of homework (watch a 2-hour film for each class period) and 5 papers over the course of the semester. Dr. Biow is a tough grader but he only grades one of the papers (I made a B- on the one he graded and As on the rest). Papers are on a sliding scale so have him grade your first one.

Great lecturer, but very harsh grader - luckily, he only grades one of your papers and the TA does the rest. Take good notes during his lectures to help you write your papers. There are easy quizzes every class. Grade consists of attendance, quizzes, and 4 essays. Dont underestimate this class, but take it if youre interested in film!

I have taken many classes at UT and I would take Italian Cinema again in a heartbeat. Dr. Biow is so incredibly good at lecturing, I was intrigued every day I went. I even still watch the movies for fun. Writing will be heavy, but he is very willing to help!

I loved this class! Be prepared to write quite a bit, but the films you watch and the lectures about them are well worth it. The subject matter is interesting and unique, and honestly, I learned more about film from Dr. Biow than from the actual  RTF class for my major. If you need a UGS, you should take this class!

Quizzes every week, but they were super easy. Even if you don't know anything about cinema, TAKE THIS CLASS. I loved it more than I expected to. It's a writing flag, so get ready to write. Good GPA booster if you write well. You won't regret taking this class.

Italian Cinema (or Films and Filmmakers of Italy) was, hands down, the best course I enrolled in this semester. Dr. Biow is an incredible lecturer who understands, and delights in sharing, the history and significance of writers, directors, and movements that shaped Italian cinema. Most importantly, he and his TA's are incredibly helpful. Sign up!

Originally, this class wasn't my first choice UGS, however by the end of the semester I ended up absolutely loving it. Dr. Biow is a great lecturer and he always gives his insight on the movies. Although there were essays, the movies were amazing and there was so much to talk about that they were not hard. Take this class, you won't regret it!

His course, carrying a writing flag, requires lots of writing for a 1st-year class. However, you'll definitely learn a lot about writing film analytic paper and to look at films differently in general. You can 'work' with him, meaning he'll personally give you feedback and grade the assignment. Super attentive and friendly. Not ez-A for foreigners.

Considering my lack of writing skills and knowledge of Italian culture and film in general, this class turned out to be really fun. We were required to watch an Italian movie almost every week and they were, for the most part, entertaining. I believe we had 5 papers to do, and they weren't too long. Biow provided awesome insight into the films!

Did not want to take this Films and Filmmakers of Italy class. However, I ended up absolutely loving the class. Biow's lectures are incredibly interesting. Also, you get to watch one old Italian movie every week, pretty much, which is a great time. Learned a lot of valuable life lessons in this class.

I was completely uninterested in Italian Film before taking this class. I only took it because all other options were full. Biow is a captivating lecturer. He speaks passionately, and he makes just about any boring old Italian movie mega entertaining and philosophical in ways that I never imagined a movie could be. Attendance is mandatory.
Really entertaining lectures, he's very interested in his material and excited to be teaching it and talking about it. He's great at generating discussion and answering questions. Awesome class!

I had Professor Oyvind for Planet Word and he was extremely passionate about what he teaches. The class itself is an easy A, there's weekly hw quizzes that take about 3 min max, only one essay, and a short presentation for grades. Attendance is mandatory but the class is a super easy A if you spend even a little time on the assignments.
Great class, great professor, great TA! By far my favorite of the year!!

Best professor ever. I took his Planet Word course, and it was so good that it almost made me switch my major to Linguistics. Very little work and amazing lectures. There's one midterm essay (which you condense and revise for the final) and a short 4-minute presentation, both easy and fun. Lukas Rudzinski, the TA, was also great and very caring.
He's great! Very kind and understanding. I took his UGS course planet word and it was so fun! Very easy with no tests and only one essay. World recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had. He actually cares about what he teaches. You will have a lot of fun in his class!

If you need a language credit TAKE NORWEGIAN!! Prof Øyvind is genuinely one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He is incredibly patient, kind, and empathetic and wants you to succeed. He will work with you if you need help and is understanding and flexible with illness/absences. This class is a gpa BOOSTER and the timing MWF 11-1 is ideal.

Prof Øyvind is the best! If you need a lang credit, take Norwegian! He is so thoughtful & patient and just wants you to have a positive experience. Attendance is mandatory, but he is forgiving about sickness. Exams are online/at-home & there are only a few in class quizzes. It's one of the easiest languages for English speakers.

90+ college hours and this is the first prof worth a review. If you need a foreign language, take Norwegian. Even if you have no clue what's going on, you'll get an A. The professor is incredible super smart, tells amazing stories, and makes the class feel low-pressure and fun.

Oyvind is probably the best professor I've had at UT. He's incredibly understanding and cares about his students, but he's also an amazing lecturer. I didn't care about the noir genre, but understanding all the intricacies now has given me a newfound appreciation. I'm taking Norwegian because I just wanna have him as a professor again.

Norskprofessor is the best professor I've ever had. He is caring and supports all his students. His lessons were fun, engaging, and fairly simple. If you attend class and participate, you'll get an A. He encourages all his students to embrace Norwegian culture and doesn't focus too much on the technicalities. Vi elsker Norskprofessor!

Nicest prof I've ever had (too nice sometimes, people be taking advantage 👎) and likes to make class fun and content understandable. Norwegian is prob the easiest language you can take and he is not a tough grader. Put effort in and show up and you can't not get an A. Vi ❤️ Oyvind!

Professor Bjoru is extremely well-versed in everything related to Scandinavian literature, history, and culture. I learned so much in his class and would highly recommend it. On a personal note, he is genuine, kind, and helpful. He always makes time for students, answers questions patiently, and knows the material backward and forward.

I've taken Oyvind for both Nordic Noir and Viking Lit, both very different classes. Oyvind does a great job of creating a community feeling within the class and caring about his students. He also does an excellent job of making sure you gain an in depth understanding of the topic while making sure you aren't overwhelmed with coursework. Great class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! So funny, genuinely kind, and very lenient. He has a swath a knowledge that makes lectures so interesting every time. The workload was average, but he's an easy grader so long as you just do the work. If I wasn't graduating this semester I'd sign up for another one of his courses in a heartbeat.

As long as you get your work done, you will be fine. Ever since I met Professor Bjoru I have recommended him to any and every body. He genuinely creates a connection with each student in the classroom that makes the overall learning environment welcoming and comfortable.
One of the best professors I ever had. Truly outstanding

One of the most caring and best professors I have ever met. He always had a smile on his face at the beginning of the class. Geniuely will look out for you and make sure you are on the right track. Also I met a lot of awesome people through this class.

I genuinely looked forward to this class every day, and I can't recommend Professor Bjoru enough. He's so kind and truly wants to help us learn. If you need a language class, take Norwegian, it's the best decision I ever made. I'm really going to miss this class. Oh, and squirrel in Norwegian is "ekorn".

Very down to earth guy and is open to feedback on all issues and only asks that you memorize a list of words and grammar each week related various topics in Norwegian culture. I cannot recommend his class enough for those needing to get their language credits without going mad in the process.
LOVE this class and LOVE this professor! Literally so wonderful. Class is fun and engaging, easy workload, and easy language to learn/pick up! TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! :)
One of UT's best kept secrets.

Nicest guy ever. I wish I could take more classes with him. He is so funny and genuinely cares about his students. He is very knowledgeable about any subject that he teaches. He does assign a lot of reading, but it's not hard stuff. So kind, definitely recommend!!

Prof. Bjoru is one of the best professors at UT and has been my favorite thus far. He goes to extreme lengths to make learning Norwegian fun and culturally based. Homework is on the light side, with a focus on in-class participation. Quizzes and exams are through Canvas, mostly with some in-class. You won't find a better professor or language.

If you need a language credit take this class! He's super caring and understanding about life as a college student. He also is more focused on giving a good impression of the language and culture rather than getting stuck on making sure small details like your pronunciation are perfect. One of the kindest most helpful professors at UT!

This class and professor are my favorite at UT! He's super understanding to first time language learners. He's always happy to answer questions! There's very little homework for the class, and the midterm and final are online and open note. He also doesn't just lecture about grammar and vocab but also talks a lot about the culture! Take this class!

Lovely professor, favorite class of my whole semester. Easy and fun language class with hilarious lectures and a lot of good feedback. Very understanding for first time language learners and shares a lot of fun cultural tidbits in our vocab and lectures.

Very engaging and super funny, knows a ton about what he's teaching and really also cares about what he teaches. He's super willing to let you take more time on projects and stuff if you need more time, also super loose with what you have to do with big assignments. Quizzes were 2 attempts and were basically a free 100. So funny and kind
Nice guy, I missed half the semester but was willing to do all the makeup work and he was very understanding

Prof. Bjoru is one of those guys who's incredibly smart yet is so kind at the same time. Super fun to talk with and very knowledgeable of what he teaches. If you see a class and he is the teacher, know you'll be in for a good time and that you'll learn a lot. As long as you do assigned readings and participate in class discussions, you'll be fine.

Absolutely fantastic. Prof. Bjoeru was so incredibly kind, funny, and interesting to listen to. He cares about the material and wants everyone to succeed. He is also understanding if you simply talk to him. There is quite a lot of reading, but it is over interesting material. Weekly discussion posts/quizzes but they're both really easy to do! TAKE!

Professor Bjoeru is a great man and a greater teacher. He was kind, respectful, and most of all genuine. He handled his first iteration of Nordic Noir to just about perfection, bringing a majority of his students into a new world of genre. His flexibility and responsiveness are what sets him apart, he is understanding of college life and strife.

Best professor ever. Take his class no matter what it is. I was easily the worst student ever--turned in papers and homework a week late almost religiously (pun intended). Never was a problem, he was always super understanding. Great person, super passionate, super understanding. Will not be a waste of time, whether you like the class or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors I have ver had. He really cares about what he is teaching and his students and will work with you to make sure you get the most out of the class. deadlines are very flexible and he's hilarious! take him if you can, he's amazing.

Professor Bjoru was one of the best professors I have had at UT. He really cares about students and wants you to succeed. There's a decent amount of reading but nothing too crazy or difficult. The lectures were entertaining and there were various fun activities spread throughout the semester.

Professor Bjoru was an amazing and very kind Professor. This class was fun and very manageable and it is a really great introduction class to the Ancient Middle East even if this has nothing to do with your major. Professor Bjoru definitely sparks students interests in his class and I highly recommend taking him.

Amazing professor! 
Extremely caring and considerate towards students. The work we studied (films, reading excerpts and tv shows) was interesting and the class is filled with lots of group interactions. I have taken two of his classes and would definitely take a third! Really glad to have had them as my professor.

Lectures are mandatory (square caps during class), but they don't prepare you for the homework or exams. Only 1 exam throughout the entire semester (15% of grade) and 1 cumulative final exam (25% of grade). Professor's explanations are hard to follow, so attend TA office hours for more helpful and better explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If youre not religious, pick a religion and start praying

Lectures have nothing to do with the content in the HW or Exams, but you have to go because he gives attendance questions. He is not accessible to students outside of class, and rarely answers emails. This class has caused me a world of anxiety and stress- take anywhere else.

Dr. Hegelich is very approachable outside of classroom. He responds to emails and questions very quickly. His lecture is mid, but sometimes it is fun too. The class is heavy on attendance, so prepared to show up to get the attendance points. Overall, it is a great class.

Lectures are extremely unhelpful, but you have to go because he gives clicker questions. The tests and homework have nothing to do with the lectures; get ready to teach yourself physics. Take this class anywhere else if you can.
Decent lectures, tests are not too hard if you know the material. I suggest looking at the online lectures which he will post. Overall, you can succeed if you do your work.
Do your work, you'll do fine.
Hard class, take anyone else if you can.
what he teaches is not on the test
Does not use class time effectively. Does not explain the material well. Doesn't even teach whats on the exams.
All he does is stand at the front a derive equations. He does not help at all in the way of actually learning the concepts of physics which is what this course is supposed to be about.
Definitely the least caring professor at UT. The averages on the tests are a 55. Good luck my friends.
Does not teach, test are extremely hard
Would not recommend
unhelpful

She clearly has read students' surveys because during the course of the semester, she didn't just read off from PowerPoint slides, and she explained things in detail.  She is very responsive to questions.  If you need clarification, ask her and she will explain in more detail.

She is not an  awful professor by any means but does lack the ability to make the lectures engaging and it's common to even find her looking at the clock. Her pauses  between statements give the appearance that she doesn't even know what she's talking about; but that isn't the case because she does in her own capacity. Paying attention is hard.

Though some people are opposed to papers, I enjoyed her class. She's pretty confusing, so I had to do some minimal outside research on the topics she mentioned. All in all, adorable and will help you if you are ever confused. Which you will be.

It's like Einstein said: "if you can't explain it to a 6 year old, you don't fully understand it". She answers questions in a convoluted, round about way and often mixes up her terminology. The book is no help either; nothing is explained in an introductory way, not in lecture or from the book. HW problems are out of the book so its essential

I thought I would take this class because I was interested in learning philosophy. The only thing I left  this class with was a dent in my GPA. The professor was hard to understand and read slides that were even harder to follow. This class was absolutely useless, I should have dropped it.

Don't let her casual demeanor lure you into thinking the midterm and final will be simple. Expect to put some effort into understanding the concepts bc they aren't always explained well in class. Students asked questions as if the views she was suggesting were her own. They'd debate her, she wouldn't be able to get on track, and we'd get nowhere.

She follows the slides and explains things pretty well until someone asks a question. Then I stop taking notes until she goes back to talking about the slides because any response to a question seems to make her uncomfortable. She pauses a lot while thinking how to respond. She really is a nice woman and very intelligent, though. I'd say, take her.

Human Nature: The teacher is amazingly lenient and super nice. The problem is that she reads DIRECTLY from her slide shows and the class was at 8 in the morning MWF. Her TA was VERY nice and lenient also. There is a midterm (essay answers) and a final (essay) and there are two Response papers and about 10 in class assignments. Hard to pay attention

I liked this prof. He was very helpful to students, and worked lots of examples in class. Also, I took this class over the summer, so we were moving pretty fast, but I nevers struggled with his pacing. As mentioned by someone else, he does mess up a lot in examples. This can be annoying, because he writes very fast and taking notes is hard enough.

It might have been the class material was easy (math 408M is suppose to be inbetween 408D and 427L) But when I took his class back in spring I remember it being very easy. His lectures were nice in that he'd work examples in class, he sympathized with students and graded very leniently. I'd recommend this professor and I hope I can take him again
I don't attend class at all. but there's really no need to. Just rework all the homework questions before every exam and you'll get an A!
Constantly messes up while giving examples. His lectures are boring and the only reason you will get a decent grade is  because everybody else does poorly.

He's a good math professor, willing to work with students, accepts questions immediately and tries very hard to reconcile misunderstandings. Has good lectures, organizes very well. Grades haven't come out yet but for the midterms there appears to be quite generous partial credits awarded, not really any curve though.
Teacher is good and all midterms are reasonable if studied. However, the final is brutal and class average was a 60. No curves are given.

Dr. V is the GOAT!!!! She is so amazing and super helpful. Whenever I had trouble, I would go to her OH, and she would guide me through the questions/concepts, making it so much easier to understand. She would also check your HW answers during OH, which helped boost my grade sm, and she rounded our grades up at the end. LOVE HERRRRRRRR

Professor is really great at explaining concepts so go to class & OHs. There is extra credit for going to class. Homeworks can be a little difficult, going to OHs def helps. Exam 1 was the hardest because of counting. Exam 2 and 3 are straight forward. Exam 3 is cumulative. Do practice problems and redo homeworks before exams. Go to OH to check hw.

Lectures are a bit boring but she is very passionate about what she teaches. Expectations are clear and formatting is consistent. Rely on practice problems she provides for questions and go to office hours because she is very helpful and easy to talk to.

Dr. V is very sweet, but the class itself is boring. Homeworks are not terrible and going to office hours helps. For exams, Exam 1 is the hardest because it has counting. Just do all the practice problems she gives. You can also see what you get wrong on tests and dispute it if you think you were right. Exam 2 and Final were both straightforward.

The lectures were good, but definitely boring at times. Office hours were very helpful, Dr. Viswanathan was happy to go through our exams with us and regrade them/give points back on the spot when the TA made grading errors. You're given sufficient resources to prepare for all the exams, but the final was surprisingly way harder than the 2 midterms

Very boring lectures, but not her fault (material is boring). Her class is very well organized, limited/delayed feedback on hw, hw every week but easy. 3 midterms, make sure to study and you'll be fine. Posts lecture slides, along with plenty of practice problems/worksheets (do them). Very doable class, work hard and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. V was great! Lectures were engaging, and any and all questions were answered. Biggest tip would be to prioritize the tests (especially the first one). Definitely a great class to get introduced to statistics!

The class is challenging due to the material, but Prof. V genuinely cares about her students and is very accessible during OH. After each exam, she asks for feedback and adjusts based on our input (e.g., removing topics from the final). Extra credit + bumps ur grade if ur on the edge. Go to OH to get ur HW answers checked as HWs are 25% of ur grade

Dr. V is one of the best professors I had. She cares a lot about the class overall. The content gets challenging through the semester, but she is always willing to help you when you reach out to her by email or at office hours. As long as you use the resources she gives (notes, practice worksheets, textbook), it is easy to get at least an A-.

Lectures and tests were tough but that's more a result of the material than the professor. Always very helpful in office hours and gave plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely the better of the two SDS 431 teachers.

Dr. V was super accessible outside of class, very approachable and super nice. Lectures at times can seem boring, but it is statstics and I think she made it as engaging as she could. Overall great course and great professor.

Dr. V is a wonderful person. She's super empathetic about grades and will make sure you succeed if you put in the effort. She is not the most accessible outside class---her office hours are very limited, but she is more than willing to help you if you ask. She provides sufficient practice problems

Lectures weren't bad and homeworks were fair. Exams were okay; however, the final was exceedingly difficult. The questions contradicted what we learned throughout the semester. The final did not reflect concepts from practice problems at all. There's no curve but some bonus points during class. Honestly, the final exam (weighted 25%) was brutal.

Lectures can get very boring and hard to sit through but she is very kind and willing to help. I found myself confused during lecture and then was easily able to grasps concepts outside of class through either videos or outside of class resources. She doesn't explain concepts well but she really does try and stops to help if needed.
Clear, detailed explanation that's easy to follow during class. Very accessible. Tests are similar to homework problems. Lecture slides with answers to problems provided are very helpful.

I really enjoyed her lectures most of the time. At times it can get a little boring but overall they were pretty digestable. Exams are very fair and reflective of the content covered in class and the study guide. HWs are a bit harder than the exams so don't worry too much if it can get a bit difficult at times. Offers extra credit for attendance.

She's a good professor and lecturer. An A is very attainable in this class if you review the material before exams. She is very generous with partial credit on exams. Lectures can feel a little slow at times, and I feel like the material could've been covered in 1 hour instead of 1.5 sometimes. Homework can be hard sometimes, 2-4h/week

Dr. V is super nice and a lovely woman. Her lecture style is great and she loves teaching the subject. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's the only way to learn the material since she doesn't record the blackboard. If you put in one extra hour per week to understand the material, you will have a really easy A. Enjoy!

She's one of the best math professors I've had. Will answer every question that you have during lecture and will make sure you understand before moving on. She's always accessible during office hours and very caring. Exams aren't that hard, and homeworks aren't that bad.

Each class was conducive to learning the content, and the professor often considered students' suggestions in terms of exam content. Attending every class provides 10 extra credit points. Each homework was the right amount of difficulty, with the professor and her TAs available in-person or over Zoom to assist. Even held Office Hours during break.
