When I asked Bonevac, he described it as an "old school humanities course" that combines both. 2 papers. 2 short essays. 2 tests. Weekly quizzes. If take & study quizzes then tests are manageable. Med-low grades occur to slackers. Failing is rare.

My favorite first semester professor. You need to like philosophy, reading, history, thinking about thinking. If you don't, you'll be miserable. I found every lecture interesting and enlightening. Only a few grades, though. Justin is the best T.A., he just catches you off guard at first. Prof. loves this stuff, and lecture feels like a documentary.

Dr. Bonevac is really adorable and is really passionate about what he teaches. I wouldn't recommend for people who do not care about philosophy. Take an easier UGS class bc this one is really test heavy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: UGS Ideas was an interesting change of class for me as an engineering student. Bonevac has really interesting lectures and knows his stuff. At the same time, his exam is really specific. You'll have to read two books and write two essays which aren't terribly hard but can be stressful with the time constraint.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Posts slides online so you don't have to go to class. Papers only kind of relate to the course material. Only two tests, a midterm and final, that are 50% of your grade. The rest is made up of papers and quizzes. The quizzes are 25 questions in 5 minutes which sucks. A tough class if you don't care all that much for philosophy

Dr. Bonevac is awesome. He's a very interesting lecturer and is hilarious. He can go very quickly through difficult concepts but he records his lectures every class and then posts them online after. If you're looking for an easy UGS this is not the class for you but if you have any interest in philosophy take it.
Bonevac is fantastic! This class was fun because of him. This class was actually pretty hard, but he's a great professor.

Dr. Bonevac is an okay professor. He's very knowledgable on his topics and all but can also be hard to understand. His lectures are sorta like rambles of sorts > hard to follow. Not the best if you're detail oriented.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bonevac is a nice guy, but he talks too fast and often loses his train of thought. It's hard to keep up with what he is lecturing on because he goes off tangent very often. Philosophy should be taught by someone more concise.

This class was pretty good, and the workload was very manageable. There are quizzes due at the end of every week, and there are 4 papers written over lectures and books. The final exam can maybe destroy you if you have been googling all of the answers for the quizzes, because then you won't know the information. Start studying for that early!
He is a genius but pay attention because he talks extremely fast. Applies philosophy to the Simpsons which is always entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: he gave out a lot of info in his lectures so going to class is a good idea. reading the assigned texts really helps you understand what is going on in class. hes a really cool dude and makes so many Simpson references. easy to talk to and get advise for papers. the only thing is theres no tests just a final with all the info from the whole year.

Great prof with interesting lectures, nice and approachable. Attendance wasn't a grade. Class was mostly essays that were graded by a TA so mostly depended on them. The final was pretty difficult though, had a high A heading in to it, studied a lot, but it still knocked me down to barely an A- , a lot of people did badly on the final.
Great professor, but the class was pretty hard. It was a philosophy course. I am a chemistry major, so philosophy is not my forte.

The class itself was easy... up until the final. The final exam was VERY specific, and covered very minute details that seemed unimportant to the main idea of lectures. Making your own study guides for people and ideas, as well as reviewing/memorizing past quizzes helps tremendously. MY TA (Ben) was great, too. Find another UGS -- NOT AN EASY A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Deep existential crises may ensue... Hilarious, brilliant professor. Use of Simpsons/Rick and Morty clips to explain concepts. Pay attention in lecture and the textbook is only supplementary. Quizzes are easy A's. Keep track of the material, though, because you have to know the content to pass the final. He doesn't take attendance, but show up!!

Cool dude. I loved his lectures, some people did fall asleep though. The class is basically powerpoints he posts online, but I still took notes. There's a quick quiz every week, but this is a large portion of your grades. Paper grades are important too, only about 5 papers, 1-2 pages long. Only those who skipped had trouble

This is by far not the easiest UGS credit, but it's not that bad. My TA was amazing which helped because they grade. Bonevac has great lectures and others that make you want to fall asleep. THE FINAL IS AWFUL, so keep up with the work and make sure you have a lot of slack going into it. Also find a group to take quizzes with, they will save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Free 25% online quizzes, 5% discussion attendance (1/wk, can miss 2) rest is all written, so know your TA and make sure they know you, by name. You do not need to go to class, but bonevac is passionate and the stuff is interesting. 25% final, hard (72 avg but doable, use quizlets) Dont buy the history book!!! difficult A, find another UGS

Good teacher and can be scattered but is passionate about the material. However, your grade relies mostly on your TA and some TAs grade really tough while others are lenient. Reading will prepare you for the discussion class and papers. Enjoyed the material even though I'm in STEM. Do not take this UGS if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about, and if you reach out to him he will listen. He's respectful and respectable, class isn't difficult especially if you're into philosophy. Keep up with the quiz questions to do well.

I had a 96 in the class. After the final, my grade dropped to an 87. Don't underestimate the final. The quote part was easy. The MC after the quotes was the hard part. out of the 45 MC I knew maybe 10 of them. It was straight up guessing after that. Quizzes every week. 3 papers. Not to mention a lot of the stuff you learn is boring.

Bonevac is an awesome lecturer and he tries his hardest to use every day examples to make difficult concepts easier to understand. He is VERY understanding that you have other classes and a life, so he moves due dates to give extra time due to holidays or other inconveniences. He also records his lectures and puts them on YouTube. TAKE HIM!

Loved Dr. Bonevac and this class! Made confusing concepts much easier to understand. Very fair grader and takes TA toughness into account. Crazy intelligent but approachable. He used Simpsons clips as examples. Always happy to talk with students, gives advice, welcomes student feedback. Loves what he does. Endearing, engaging. TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Make sure you don't skip classes from the beginning (it is so hard since attendance isn't mandatory and he uploads lectures on youtube). Keep up with the lectures, take good notes and enjoy the class! It definitely teaches you a lot of stuff and he tries to make it interesting with personal anecdotes and corny jokes.

Weekly quizzes, four essays, and one final so do well. Philosophy isn't my thing so it was hard for me. Bonevac is really cool though and tries his best to make it easy. His jokes are corny and awkward which makes them funny. Always wants to take about his 20 cats. Go to discussion!!! Read read read!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Bonevac is an amazing professor! He truly cares about his students actually learning the material instead of focusing on grades as some professors like to do. Lectures are not mandatory, but it's a great disservice to yourself not to go, as his lectures are very intresting and often hilarious. I would definitely recommend Dr. Bonevac!

The smartest man I've ever spoken to. So much so, it's hard to have a convo with him. Anyways, attendance isn't mandatory but if you start skipping early on you'll fail the final like I'm going to this Friday. You'll have a 99 in the class like I do right now because of the easy online quizzes, but it won't matter in the end. *DONT SKIP!*
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bonevac loves to talk (and fast). Lots of information is covered and it's hard to see how it connects. The tests are ridiculous - questions over minute details. It's impossible to read everything, but you need to read a lot. Most of your interaction and grading is with a TA. It was nice the lectures were also available online but I never used them.

He records all of his lectures and puts them on YouTube, so if you want to see what this class is like go watch a lecture. 1 midterm, 4 essays over 3 assigned books, and one lecture paper. This class is pretty hard for a UGS especially if you aren't into history and philosophy. There are a lot of daily readings as well that are lengthy.
100% recommend.

I'm glad Prof. Bonevac was one of my last philosophy professors. He always made the content interesting (his impressions are hilarious) and is interested in his students' success. Don't skip as attendance is one of the only grades in this glass besides a long paper due as your final. Probably my favorite philosophy professor at UT. Take his class!

Professor Bonevac is my favorite professor at UT in the time I have been here. His lectures are interesting and he always uses good examples to illustrate the ideas he's trying to convey. He's a pretty funny guy and an overall great person. I would take this class again in a heartbeat.

He's a great lecturer who really loves what he's doing. He does a really good job at giving general overviews of different philosophers' ideas and how they relate with other philosophers' ideas. He really knows how to engage the class, often showing the Simpsons in class. He's a big part of the reason why I'm now double majoring in Philosophy.

Love him as a professor! He's super personable and he made lectures fun to listen to. Grades are determined by TAs who will be grading essays (some are a LOT easier than others). Tests are decent, just pay attention and make sure you get the key points. I made.

Super nice Professor. Some concepts are confusing, but he tries his best to explain it and is very lenient with grading. He genuinely wants you to understand the material and tries to make the boring parts as interesting as possible . Encourages discussion, and never puts down an answer, but rather tries to incorporate it into the lesson.

Bonevac is seriously the most interesting man in the world. I took Ideas of the 20th Century, and it was pretty enjoyable. There is a bit of reading, and a couple of papers but he really listens to his students feedback--go to him if your TA is grading weird.  I went to his office hours and he is really helpful and let me take my final early!

Great professor. Passionate and funny. Five short papers, graded by TA. If you want to skip discussion, make sure your TA is chill. A midterm and a non-comprehensive final, both of which are multiple choice and just memorization of key quotes and concepts. Generous grader, tries to make sure everyone who tries passes.

Bonevac's  a great teacher. There was a midterm and final, but they're only quotations from the readings and ppts. If you show up to class, then you'll have nothing to worry about. His lectures are fun, because he's super passionate. TAs can determine your grade because of papers, but if you have an issue, Bonevac WILL work with you.
Lectures are sporadic, not very organized. Professor is very resourceful, interested and knowledgeable about the class. Standard A, B, C system, no plus minus.

I HATE PHIL but he was a great Prof! Only 2 midterms and a Final with 8 reflection papers on confusing material. Not much wiggle room for grades. I rarely went to class and walked out with an A but because I POURED over PP and readings night before exam.  Avg. final grade was 77. Tests are hard. Don't take as blow off course cuz it could back fire.

Bonevac is an amazing professor.  The lectures were really interesting and kept you listening, however, his TAs are awful.  I got stuck with the hardest one and would make 75s on papers while friends would make 100s.  I loved the professor and the course, but I would never take another class from him again if he has the same TAs.

Honestly, Bonevac was a really cool professor, but the assignments of his class were just graded more difficultly than I had imagined. Bonevac is an awesome guy, but the grade of the class relies solely on your TA. I had a lazy TA with unconventional grading and it lead to a lot of stress. For his tests, study the powerpoints, the practice exams.

I was disappointed with this class. Bonevac, in Ideas of the 20th Century, spread ideas so thinly that just as you were grabbing on to one concept, it was ripped away and a new one was introduced. Get ready to study art, photography, philosophy (!!!), history, literature, ethics, politics, etc. Too broad of a subject to really engage in.

The Ideas of the 20th Century was a fun class. The tests are kind of hard so beware, but not too bad. There's a lot of essays in this class and the TA discussions are weird and unhelpful. However, Bonevac is awesome and very helpful and understanding. He let us take a class vote on dropping on of our essays, super nice guy and smart.

He is an amazing lecturer! you never get bored in class while he talks. He loves it when students participate. There is never a wrong answer because well its philosophy. He incorporates the Simpsons a lot in his lectures as examples. I love the class. However, the tests are a bit difficult. If you go to the office hours, he will help you.
His lectures are at the same time simplified, summarized, dense, lively, stimulating. He's a good actor. Sometimes his conservative opinions shine through.
He's funny, easy-going, and his class isn't very demanding, but he's sort of all over the place and unclear.

Dr. B is pretty much one of the best teachers you can have! He's one of those adorable funny old guys you just want to sit and have tea with :) also word of advice: you can get by with just studying the power point notes, some of the philosophers are incredibly mind-numbingly boring. tests are mult. choice, & just 5 essay assignments.

pretty good class. i wasn't in his philosophy class this was a general studies class called ideas of the twentieth century but the class was well put together and interesting. you write a few short 1 page reaction papers and a couple tests for your grade.
I am in love with Dr. Bonevac!!! He is the best professor I have ever had. If you are thinking of taking a philosophy class I definitely recommend taking one of Dr. Bonevac's classes.
Awesome
His midterm and final were EASY! Both have extra credit questions on them, and the test itself is pretty easy if you've paid attention and done the assignments for his class. Very funny.

Take him if you can. Great teacher!! You wont know what the heck he is talking about sometimes, but them he explains it in easy terms(relates philosophy to football, baseball, the simpsons, ect.). Funny guy too.

Amazing professor.  Makes philosophy interesting with simpson's clips and personal stories.  Must go to class and do the readings or you'll be lost.  He's a great lecturer.  His class is lots of fun.  The tests can be difficult if you don't do the practice test first.  Bottom line: great prof.  Take his class before leaving UT.
Fun Professor, His lectures are very interesting and will keep you awake. Multiple choice Tests, 3 HW Essays, Attendance Optional, Must do Readings!
Bonevac is an entertaining professor & a good guy. His tests can be a little challenging, but as long as you read the text you should be fine.
he's the best, hands down, if you are going to take philosophy, take it with him.
the best professor i have had in college.  he is an awesome professor.
this is the class you'll be dying to go to everytime.  lol ok maybe not but he's simpson clips always kept me entertained and related it all to philosophy.  good guy but his tests can be a challenge.
No Comments
He is incredible, his ability to be awesome is amazing.  He really listens to the students and he is fun to watch.  It was a class I actually enjoyed going to.
fun guy
awesome, and helpful in class! simpsons clips are always welcome!

won't take in class questions, you have to wait for the discussion sections. the class is mostly OK but he presents a biased version of the philosophy surrounding abortion, and he showed a video from right to life.
awesome guy. fun class. hard tests.
Awsome teacher, the best of my freshman year.
Very fun, laid back class.  He uses Simpsons clips to make his points! Major plus.  Tests are moderate with a little bit of studying.
No Comments
Clear, logical, humorous, and always ready to help students both in and outside of class.  One of the best professors of my freshman year.

Tests are the only thing making up your grade and they are long. Preparing for them is very time consuming (I did about 8 hours per test), but it pays off and I did really well. It is not any easy class but it is doable if you apply yourself when it comes to the test. LOTS of readings but aim for big picture understanding not little stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most off putting professor I've ever had Im pretty sure you'll get sick sitting through her talk for 50 mins. Trust.

This is a very easy course to take during the summer. To be honest, the lectures were taken from Dr. Crosnoe so he is really the one who should be getting this great review. The paper assignments were easy and the discussion boards were not time consuming, I always had time to do all the assignments. The TA I had was not harsh either, great class!

Professor McCaslin is a very nice professor, but this class is so much work. That's expected for a course like this, but the assignments felt endless. It took forever to get feedback for assignments that were necessary for the final grade. I had the same grade for 90% of the semester with no real idea of how I was doing until the final week.

The exams are hard, and the readings are very long. The other professor for this course uses projects rather than tests, and I think that is the better route to go when learning these research concepts. If you can take the other professor, you should and save yourself the trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I've taken Dr. McCaslin twice now and I really don't think she is that bad. The biggest issue she has is slow grading times and rather excessive readings. However, I really do think she cares about her students and she's always available and is helpful when you need it. She definitely isn't out to get you, just be prepared to read.

Very condescending; before every class you have to read 30 page articles, and she forces you to talk to your neighbor even for the most basic concepts. If you can take this class with a different prof, you definitely should. She will put you on the spot if she feels like you're not paying attention and is extremely snarky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Essays are not bad but are graded so late it's impossible to know what your final grade will be. 2 reflection essays, 3 reading responses, and a midterm and final. Expects you to read 20+ pages of readings before every class. Exams are short response and fill in the blank, never multiple choice. Manageable to get a B, don't expect to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor ive ever had. dont take

McCaslin was good and her TA's were excellent. The course material itself was pretty easy and interesting. Her personality isn't for everyone and I don't love that her lectures are mostly her personal reading off the slides. That being said, she's a reasonable prof and your experience will be good if your are communicative with her and her TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a stem major I expected my ugs to be pretty easy, I took this class as my ugs and the amount of writing for this class to have is extremely unnecessary for it to not even have a writing flag. The content was interesting but the quantity of outside work we had to do was unmotivating and pointless. Avoid this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor McCalsin gave great lectures, we'd go over assigned readings in class. She is open to different perspectives and discussions. I would say exams weren't too hard and she doesn't grade harshly on them. You also learn a lot of new things in The Family
McCaslin encouraged conversations during lectures and really wanted us to understand concepts. Assignments and exams are fairly easy and graded pretty easy. Overall great professor.

Professor McCaslin is great, and she really cares about her students. She encourages discussion among her students and gets them involved with the lecture through group activities. Only a couple of assignments are graded throughout the semester, so if you do well on them, you should be okay. Grading takes a long time, but not a big deal.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't let these ratings scare you, she is a good professor overall, and has good spirit. The only thing is that this class is graded on 2 reading responses, 3 reflection papers, and 2 exams. She does provided many opportunities to complete the reading responses. If you read the articles and attend the lectures you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has us discuss during class and it is 1/3 of the lecture. She keeps saying that she doesn't have things in her head and needs to look it up if someone asks something but never get back to us about it. She has midterm and final, but there are also five different papers to write. Overall, I would NOT RECOMMEND this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She took a really long time to grade things, and I didn't get full participation pts for a blanket reason she gave to everyone in the back. In fact it would have been better if I had never said anything bc ik someone who did, and they got a better grade than I did for that. The lectures are really boring, but most of the test was over readings.

This course is very interesting and the professor is always interested in what she is talking about, but it is very writing heavy for a course that doesn't have a writing flag and is usually graded relatively harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you're thinking about taking this for an easy UGS credit, don't. Overall the information is decently interesting and it is not that difficult of a class, but when there are big assignments due they are very time-consuming and graded harshly.

This professor is very passive aggressive and tends to make comments that are completely unnecessary. Her lectures consist of her reading off of her slides and its all pretty much basic common sense. The class is made up of completely attendance and four essays which aren't bad except three of them were assigned and due within the same two weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE. If you are looking to take a UGS DO NOT TAKE HERS! She is extremely passive aggressive, and makes snarky comments that are insensitive. I get the impression that the TA's are scared of her. Theres not that much homework but the papers are extensive and this class doesn't even suffice a writing flag. DO NOT TAKE IT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McCaslin was so awesome and she even wrote me a rec letter!! Her lectures were super enjoyable. She and her TA gave awesome constructive criticism. I wish this course had a writing flag though because the papers were extensive!! Participation also mattered in lectures and discussion sections. Overall recommend her, she is amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. McCaslin's UGS was very enjoyable. If you are interested in the topic and don't mind writing lots of papers, this can fulfill your credit easily. There are a few books to read, but nothing too crazy.

Dr. McCaslin was difficult to work with, the class was boring, and group projects/papers were EXTENSIVE for a 303 UGS. I would take literally any other UGS than this one. Expect to be researching for hours on topics like hooking up where there are no credible sources, and to get a bad grade in return. Hated this class.

I took her for UGS 303. Professor McCaslin is a great lecturer. She is so engaging and the content was interesting. However, assignments took an incredibly long time to grade, so we had no understanding of what our grades would be until the very last week of the semester. Writing-heavy with multiple essays often due in the same week.

I took her UGS 303 Sex, Love, and Relationships. She was really nice and participation matters. The class is actually really interesting. Lots of assigned readings and essays, with a big research project that takes a while. If you like reading and writing, and find sexuality interesting then take it. You have to put effort into this class to get A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very condescending, I would receive catty remarks back on my papers that didn't feel very constructive and were just outright mean. Her lectures were boring and we had upwards of 3 assignments due each week. Definitely overkill :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took her UGS bc it had no writing flag and I hate writing essays. We had to write 4 essays, which wouldn't be so bad if 3 of them were not all assigned and due in the same week, and a big final project that ended up being 16+ pages. We had to read 4 books and lectures were mandatory and boring. I wish I could go back and take any other UGS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor McCaslin is a great professor and you can tell she truly love what she does, BUT I would not recommend this course. The topics are interesting but the work is extensive for a SIG course. We had to write four papers throughout the semester which i thought was a waste of time I could have used studying for my other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: !! I actually took her for UGS 303 Sex, Love, and Relationships. These other ratings are so confusing I wondered if I was reading the right professor! The class was super easy, the lectures were cool and McCaslin was cool. If you just go to class, you don't even have to thoroughly read the books. The class was perfect for a UGS, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took her for UGS303 Sex, Love, and Relationships. At the beginning I would do all the reading on time until I realized she essentially just spits back the reading to you in class, so you can totally do fine just attending class and not doing the reading, or vice versa. Not super hard since it's just a UGS, and she's nice enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McCaslin was one of the worst professors I've had at UT. She's passive-aggressive in class and over email. Her lectures and boring and the readings and assignments are utterly useless. The content is repetitive and I dreaded having to go to class. Only take this class if it's a requirement, and try not to take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor McCaslin was one of the worst professors I've had at UT. She's passive-aggressive in class and over email. Do not pass up Dr. Bryan!! He is an amazing lecturer and cares deeply about applying class concepts to the real world. This class was super easy, workload was average the only thing is participation matters heavily. Professor and TA are so helpful.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bsumek was a nice professor and you can tell she cared about her job. TAs can be annoying, but group projects are ultimately what matter in the class. Groups are randomly assigned but if you get lucky then the class is an easy A. There are discussion boards and quizzes sprinkled throughout the course and attendance is via a QR code each class.

Professor Bsumek is so nice and gives so much individual attention in her UGS class. I found it very moving and I loved discussing the readings, but for the final timeline project her expectations were often very unclear and when it came time to peek over the rubric there were lots of requirements that she hadn't previously specified.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was truly enlightening, learning about the history of a group of people that have often been overlooked. The lectures were interesting and the class overall was a great experience. However, there are two group projects, and you can't choose your own group.

The lectures for this class become difficult to attend very quickly, between the emotionally charged material and the slow pace of this class. As far as the papers, the rubric is fairly ambiguous and arbitrary. However, Dr. Bsumek is clearly knowledgeable and very open to feedback. If you have an interest in History, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class but the material was a lot, and I wish it was more organized for this semester. And if you don't like reading there is a lot of it, because it is very important in order to succeed in this class. Interesting class, but I would try to look for another history credit.

Native American Histories was a bit tough, but that's the nature of history courses (memorizing). Really broadens your understanding of such an important topic and gives you knowledge you'll carry with you long after the course. Lots of textbook reading, midterm that is okay but you gotta study hard for. Easy online final. A few group projects.

Dr. Bsumek is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, her lectures are very insightful. You can get by without reading too much of the textbooks, though they do help. The group timeline projects were cool, though they can become a bit redundant. The one midterm exam was difficult and has heavy weight, but her online final exam was easy.

Professor Bsumek is nice and the class felt comprehensive even with such expansive subject material, but I really wasn't a fan of the emphasis on group work and Cliovis. Aside from that, this class is very solid for an intro course.

Dr. Bsumek is great at helping, answering questions, and being available outside of class. This class was very easy because she made it very clear what was expected. You are given the terms and questions for the midterm/final in advance, so you will be well-prepared for both tests. Dr. Bsumek does use ClioVis often, assigned 2 group timelines.

Dr. Bsumek is very knowledgeable and passionate. She understands that many people take her Native American history class for a GC flag and core requirement, and as a result doesn't assign much work. There are weekly discussion posts (1-3 sentences) and a few group projects, one individual project. Overall great, would reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am not joking when I tell you this class changed my life. It was very eye opening and Professor Bsumek approached the subject of Native American History with so much grace. The lectures were always interesting and informative, if a little heartbreaking for obvious reasons, and even though I'm not great at history, I would take this class again.

Interesting UGS. Initially had a lot of readings. Need to purchase 2 books that we didn't really even read the whole thing. She really cares about what she's teaching and wants to interact with her students. Provides good feedback and help if needed. The final project is a lot of work, but she gives you time to work on it. Easy to get a good grade.
super kind and understanding, great lecturer too. her projects are resonable and the readings are interesting

Prof. Bsumek was an amazing professor, with a very easy class and manageable workload. Only complaint would be the group projects and individual project as they are alot of work but manageable with a group. Easy quizzes and discussions. She tries to make her class as engaging as possible and mostly does so. Highly recommend for STEM majors.

You can tell that she is passionate about American history in her lectures. The ClioVis app she uses for a lot of assignments is very janky, but the tests are pretty easy with weekly short answer discussion posts and in-class padlets. I barely attended the class and got an A.

Dr Bsumek was great! Her lectures were very engaging and she was very passionate about the subject matter. The workload for the class was very manageable as well. The group projects in the class were mildly annoying, especially given the group I had, but they weren't too difficult.

Dr Bsumek's class was great! Her lectures were very engaging and the workload from the course was very manageable. There were a couple group projects throughout the class which was somewhat annoying since I didn't have the best group, but they weren't that difficult..

Dr.Bsumek was very caring about her students and truly wanted everyone to succeed. I read the textbook for the first two weeks and then stopped since there were never any quizzes given. As long as you know the terms that she gives before the exams, you should be able to ace the exams easily.

Class is manageable and I was never extremely stressed about it, and she took a couple assignments of the syllabus so that was slay of her. Lectures can be really long though, and she goes fast so its a good class to improve typing skills. I stopped reading the textbook after the midterm and was fine so don't let that deter you. Solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her Native American Histories course was an extremely rewarding experience. The group projects I wasn't crazy about but they weren't bad. The midterm and final weigh heavy on the final grade. I suffered a personal loss outside of class and she was very accommodating when that happened. I cannot recommend her enough.

She is great with her rubrics and grading, she's very clear on what is expected so the work is very straightforward. there were 2 group assignments but they were timelines and easy. She does offer extra credit and gives study guides for all test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this class just to get the cultural diversity flag. Prof. Bsumek is aware that many students that take her class do so in order to knock out a core class/flag requirement, so she has made efforts not to make the class too demanding and time-consuming. This was an easy class, and getting an A should be easily done if one attends the lectures.

Dr. Bsumek is very reasonable, kind, and intelligent. She takes her students' feedback into account and overall I respect her a lot! If you have trouble keeping up with reading I definitely recommend going to the study groups she makes available (not mandatory)--I have a hard time reading and those helped out a TON!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be on top of your readings and you should be fine. This isn't a class you'd want to procrastinate on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class & the material a lot, and the prof was really nice. However, I wish it was more organized for this semester. Make sure to do your reading because it is very important in order to succeed in this class. The midterm and final both consisted of 2 essays (one long and one short). The two books & textbook we read are very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is very understanding and easy to talk to. The class is very discussion led, so there's not many lectures. Most of the class is discussing readings or whatever activity we do in class, and every once in a while there's a paper. There's also an easy project at the end. As long as you follow the rubric and participate you should have an A.
Great teacher! Really passionate and great to talk to. Not too many assignments, which is good and bad. You need to make sure you keep up on your own.

Go to lectures. She sends out slides, but they're bullet points and what she says is more important. Essays can be prepared beforehand, so it is advisable that you write out exactly what you want, otherwise you may be pressed for time. Lots of readings, but I stopped after the 2nd week. Group projects aren't that bad if you put a little effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very easy class for a history credit, definitely take it! Dr. Bsumek was very nice and interested in her subject matter. However, attendance is counted.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was unnecessarily hard! There is 3 group projects which you have to present, a 3-4 page paper, and2 exams. If you can pick someone else please do!! When we switched to online she did not try to accommodate her students at all! She expected to do the same and more work not understanding at all!

love love love this class and this prof, I learned so much. Bsumek is really great approaching complex topics with objectivity and sensitivity, and is clearly very knowledgable about the subject matter. Couldn't have asked for a better professor or a more interesting class.
This class is great and so is Bsumek. Very interesting stuff. Only graded on 2 tests which both have an essay component, a couple of quizzes, and some papers. Not too hard though if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bsumek is very transparent and kind. She makes the class engaging and not too hard to keep up with, although it is a lot of content. Exams aren't easy but she gives clear study sheets/lists of what to know. A very well-organized class on a really important topic! Sit in the front to see her cool shoes ;-)

Dr. Bsumek actually takes the time to learn everyone's name and is super sweet! This is one of the best classes I have taken at UT! Pay attention during lecture and make sure to read because they are super helpful for the essays and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bsumek is probably one of the most caring professors you will find at UT. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is genuinely concerned her students. Her grading criteria is usually clear, there isn't a lot of work but she does focus on class participation. Overall, I enjoyed my time in her class and would take again.

The professor is very caring and kind. The class is kind of hard because there are is lot of papers and readings. You have to do discussion posts, 3 short papers, and a research paper at the end. The class is interesting, but boring at the same time. A lot of work and time, but if you do the work, you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You can tell that her heart is in the right place. The only thing that I somewhat disliked is the fact that her syllabus is not consistent through out the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her lectures are interesting but not always easy to follow.  For American Indian History, there was a lot of information that was difficult to organize.  However, Dr. Bsumek listens to her students' concerns and is willing to make reasonable changes based on our feedback.  If you take her, and have a problem, don't hesitate to bring it up.

You'll learn a ton in this class! There are group projects which can be annoying, but it's not too bad. There's a lot of reading but no one ever reads it. She really cares about her students, she even hosted a competition for the best group project and she even gave out prizes!  This class takes a bit of work, but it's worth it!
She is a nice lady. The midterms come with study which are pretty straight forward. It is a easy A if you attend to class.
Do yourself a favor and take her class. She's fantastic.

This may not apply to everyone, but Prof. Bsumek's teaching style does not really suit me.  She relies too heavily on the textbook; her tests cover many details that aren't even mentioned in her lectures.  She also has a tendency to get behind in lectures and skip sections to stay on schedule, then wait a couple weeks before posting the slides.
More writing then both of my writing intensive classes. 12-20pg takehome midterm + final. 4 books - choose one to write another 6pg paper. Would not take the class again.
cool class, her t.a.s are very helpful.
The TAs do most of the grading and discussions were required, but the class was very straightforward and stress free.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures! You can tell he truly cares about the content and is incredibly knowledgeable about it. He has a great enthusiasm toward baseball which makes it that much more interesting to learn about. Would love to take another course from him in the future.

LOVED this UGS. Do not understand the low ratings he gets on here. First off, he is a super nice, funny, well-rounded guy. He is so passionate about baseball which made me want to show up to lectures (which were not required). ONLY complaint was the TAs.

I almost never leave reviews, but this class deserves a warning. class material not hard but grading is harsh. Discussion average in the 65-73, papers land in the same range, no curve or extra credit. I maintain straight As in tougher STEM courses, but I only pull a C here. The evaluation standards feel excessive for an otherwise reasonable class.

This professor is one of those professors that will give you more work just because he knows people will not care about his class. He is a harsh grader, and in my opinion does not follow the grading criteria and just grades depending on his opinions of the paper, and I feel like the TAs do not even know half of the stuff we are talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is determined to make sure his class is not known as a blowoff so he ruined everyone's GPA instead this semester. Group project is awful because it's graded as a whole, not individually so your group mates will drag your grade down. TA's know nothing about the class and use chatGPT to grade assignments if they don't understand it.

I took this class because I heard it was an easy A and I needed a course that wouldn't require too much work, as I have a job. While attendance at lectures isn't mandatory, participation in discussion groups is. Tests are on paper within your small group. The professor does not offer extra credit, and the TAs are tough graders…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE THIS!! You get a different grade based on different TAs. Your grade COMPLETELY out of control. Even if you do well, some TAs will give you the right grade and others won't. Prof MB also backs up their grading, making it impossible to get points back or even understand what it takes to get an A. Don't trust them and don't take this class.
really hard to do well, no reason to take this UGS. Would rather push back taking one for a semester and make sure I get one that is reasonable

Overall, such a disappointing class. Was super excited to learn more about baseball but ended up being a stress fest. Every assignment had unclear grading and even if you met the requirements for a 100 they still found ways to knock it down for arbitrary reasons. Just sad that both TAs and professor feel the need to hurt students grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is the epitome of, "I teach a joke subject so I am going to grade way too harshly". About halfway through the semester, the students complained about the ridiculous grading and MB responded with, "a C is the grade you get for following the instruction. Don't complain about a C". There are so many more easy UGSs DO NOT TAKE THIS ONE.

I loved lectures. Dr. Butterworth was very engaging and entertaining to listen to! I highly recommend attending lectures, even though attendance isn't taken, but discussions are mandatory. Group project at the end of the semester.
I was told for the first exam that there would be not dates being asked yet about 1/3 of the exam was about dates and I was only given a “I apologize” after borderline failing. It seems t

After taking this class, I now understand that producing well-written and maximum effort papers/final projects is never enough to get an A. I would receive comments on the writing assignments that started with "I would like it better...", and feedback that a great paper is worth of a B. Most will agree, don't take this class, for your own sake.
Super tough grader for no reason. This is a UGS not a math class.

I thought he was cool at first, but during the final half of the semester, he said, “Guys, a B isn't a bad grade. A C means you met expectations, a B means you exceeded expectations, and an A means you went above and beyond.” For a baseball class and a UGS requirement, it's not that deep.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Butterworth himself is a cool guy, the TA's are terrible and grade extremely hard when the rubrics are very unspecific. There are very little assignments so if you do bad on one thing, you are screwed. I will say that Dr. Butterworth does not easily give points back and it was annoying when he did nothing to help us students with our grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do NOT take Butterworth. I took him because I heard it was an easy UGS and it's graded so harshly for absolutely no reason and the TAs and Butterworth himself are so unhelpful and very unclear about what the expectations are. They also agreed that a C should be the average grade for the class??? I regret taking this class so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is very interesting and was supposed to be a fun UGS class, but the grading in this class is so terrible. For a UGS class the grading here is so bad the TA's and the professor have decided that a C should be the average grade in the class. They are very very VERY picky when grading assignments. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is easy, but the TA's are very picky graders when it comes to the papers. Group project is not too bad but again grade too harshly unless work is perfect.

Used to be really easy, but TAs and Professor decided that getting a C is a good thing. 3 tests, 1 group project and a few short papers. The class itself is actually pretty interesting, but the grading policy is terrible. Would not recommend.

A lot of people have different opinions on this course. The lectures are not mandatory but the discussion sections are. Test are taken in discussion sections and are not too hard. As long as you look at the rubrics/try hard on the assignments it really isnt hard. The only downfall was the TAs are not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAs collectively decided a C is the average. the class used to be really easy but now it is insanely unrealistic for a UGS. there are way better UGS courses. dont take this if you just need a credit. my TA was awful just made us come and asked if we had questions because she has no plan and we all sat in silence for an hour.

The professor is very nice but the TA's SUCK. The lectures are not mandatory, however, the discussion groups are. They collectively think that a C is a good grade and they want to make their grade point average lower. Be really careful taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Butterworth had interesting lectures. The tests were easy and the lab section was not bad. This class was as easy A and I highly recommend for a UGS.

After a year at UT, Prof Butterworth is the best professor I have had. As a baseball fan, his lectures were so engaging and interesting and he's such a good orator. Assignments were manageable and I often enjoyed doing them. My TA for discussion was great and discussions themselves weren't too bad. I wish I could take this class again! GO O'S!

By far the best professor I've had at UT. Really good lecturer and entertaining guy and though they're not required, he still makes you want to come. Facilitates discussion really well and assignments are relatively easy and all exams are take home. If you're looking for an easy A but still an entertaining class, he's the man for you.

His baseball UGS is so easy. Attendance is only mandatory for discussion. There are a few papers, but they can all be completed in an hour max and are a page long usually. There is a group project, which is annoying. But it is a super easy UGS. 3 tests, all open note as well.

Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't to strict, but look at the lectures tho since the tests were very lecture heavy. Overall graded on like 5 things so if you mess up one you mess up half of your grade. Test were open note and taken at home do they weren't terrible, takes some work to get an A tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Butterworth's lectures were extremely engaging and his passion was evident with every lecture. As a result, his class was highly accessible even for someone unfamiliar with the subject matter. I'd recommend largely studying your notes from his lecture to study for the tests, but the readings are a good frame of reference to understand larger themes

Probably my fav professor here! His lectures are pretty engaging even if you aren't familiar at all with the topic. Attendance is mandatory but definitely come to the lectures and take notes because he has easy open-note exams that are straight from the lecture slides. TAs are generally chill and all other assignments are easy.

Dr. Butterworth is the most passionate and knowledgable professor I have had. As someone who knew nothing about baseball, I learned a ton, and found myself very interested in the course. If you aren't a strong writer, the essay grades may hurt a little. Weekly readings provided in canvas, so no textbook. Everything on the tests is in the lectures.

I took UGS303 America Through Baseball in Spring 2022, and it was harder than all of my engineering classes combined. The exams are so specific and questions aren't covered in lecture or the readings; it's basically like trivia exams. Essays and projects he takes points off for dumb reasons. He is a decent lecturer though and he gives extra credit

Was a great guy and was helpful during office hours. It was way too much work for a UGS class and the test material was very knit picky. The essays were also challenging but he is willing to help you out with them. You need to put in a decent amount of work in this class to get an A but Dr. Butterworth is a great guy.

Professor Butterworth is one of the best professors I've ever had. He gives AMAZING lectures and the class is very well-organized. He is so kind and loves talking to students outside of class! Your grade is based on 3 exams, 2 papers, a timeline project, a final group project, and attendance in discussion sections (which are very helpful, so go!)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took UGS303 America Through Baseball spring'20. Told the history/foundation of the sport, not necessarily the game itself. Relevant topics like race, sexism, immigration, etc., & I was pleased to see he didn't sugarcoat any of these. I dislike sports, but Butterworth made this class worthwhile. Understanding of personal issues, loved his course!!

I really love Professor Butterworth! His personality is awesome and lectures are engaging. He is also very knowledgeable on this topic of communications and sports. He offers extra credit, and exams are not too hard if you study and pay attention in class.

Dr. Butterworth is a great guy and very understanding. Super nice, and his lectures are engaging and easy to follow. Class was Tuesday/Thursday, and we probably had a short pop quiz over the reading once every 3-4 classes. The readings were easy to read and interesting. Exams are essay format. I would definitely take a class from him again.
Save your sanity, your tuition money, and your GPA: Avoid this person at all costs.
She isn't on your side.  Not clear with directions.
By far the worst professor I have ever experienced during my time at UT. If you value your GPA or your mental health, stay as far away from this class as possible.

Your grade depends heavily on your group, be prepared to pick up the slack for other just to pass. Reporting it does nothing. Study guides are disorganized and include unnecessary material, while giving no clear direction on what to study. Assignments have extremely poor instructions. Overall, one of the most unhelpful and frustrating instructors

Do NOT take this class. I thought it wasnt going to be that bad but it is. The lectures are so boring and there is SO much work. The tests are hard and she is not the nicest. Seriously take any other class. Especially if you know you already have a busy semester!
Rudest professor I've ever had. How do you teach a communications class but lack all communication and leadership skills?

Do not take her if you have any other option. To say the least, the assignments were odd, with poor instructions, and poor explanations when you asked for clarification.  The only thing you could do for a test was pray, most of the topics on the tests we never covered. And the group project, all I can say is good luck.

The most impressive part of this class is how simple material was turned into an unnecessarily harsh and mind-numbing course. Feedback didn't improve grades, studying didn't help exams, and missing class meant penalties with no leniency. 

The course could have been more manageable and engaging. Frustrating and poorly handled, I hope she eases up.

The material was easy to learn, and although the assignments did not have the clearest instructions, they were also pretty straightforward. When asking questions for help, she wasn't the most helpful or nicest, but she did her job I guess.
This class was a complete joke.

He's not too open to criticisms of his research work, but I have to give it to him, he's a great professor. Assigned textbooks are very helpful. Attendance not mandatory, but you should just go and experience his lectures. Very interesting course, but don't get caught up in the narrow social framework of Evo Psych. Always stay skeptical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors here at UT hands down. You'll definitely need to read the textbook to pass the exams but the readings are manageable. He loves to interact with his students and he is a very funny guy. One of my favorite courses I have taken.

The lectures had a lot of interesting and valuable material! This course was only graded on 4 exams, but they were all very easy to pass as long as you did the readings. The lecture slides also give an overview of material you needed to focus on knowing for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Buss is back to teaching evolutionary psych! I'd highly recommend the class. The only grades are 4 exams, which are fair and the info is largely covered in the lectures. (But reading will help a lot). Very interesting topic and lectures -- no attendance taken but you'll want to go. Dr. Buss and the TA are truly experts in this topic.
Super interesting and fun class, it's definitely a lot of reading but it is manageable. Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston were both great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took his class with Dr. Meston and he was pretty alright. In the lectures, it is separated by Dr. Buss and Dr.Meston I felt that Dr. Meston's lectures were better than Dr. Buss's lectures. He's a caring professor, and I would recommend his class with Dr. Meston. This class is very lecture-heavy and you have to read the book to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Buss is a great educator and gives very concise lectures. This course is lecture heavy and you need to read the textbook in order to pass the exams. The content itself is pretty easy to digest. Overall this was one of my favorite courses I took.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good professor, explains things very thoroughly, and provides a relatively unbiased and distinctly knowledgable perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is good at explaining things and is respectful as he approaches certain topics. I like that both Meston and Buss teach this class as they each bring their own expertise and knowledge. I'm glad that someone like him is working in this field.
Ask "have these results been replicated" about any study they talk about and both professors will get so mad. Very well respected professor in a field that demands way more respect than it deserves.

Exceptional lecturer. He is very interested in what he says and very open to different theories and ideas than his own. Make sure to attend lectures for 10 bonus points to your grade, read the books, and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you read, attend the lectures, and study for the exams you will do great in this class. I believe if I made more time to study I would have gotten an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSY306 was one class I always looked forward to attending throughout my week, I was always engaged and it never felt like a chore. Buss is a highly knowledgeable man and is ranked one of the top living psychologists in the world so it was an honor to take the class. The tests are highly specific though and require a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures and readings were super interesting. Grade is based on 5 tests, but one gets dropped. The tests are very specific, but if you do all the readings and pay attention in lecture you'll do fine. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were very interesting! Lectures are recorded so you can go back and watch them if you miss them. The tests are pretty specific and are the only assignments, so definitely take notes on the lectures and readings. That said, they drop your lowest grade and have in-class quizzes for extra credit, so you'll be fine if you put in the work.

Great class with interesting lectures. Be prepared to read the books included in class materials. A lot of the info from the books is in the tests. Both teachers for this class were really great and had done a lot of research on the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed these lectures so much. Attendance is not required but it was honestly so interesting you just wanna stay. exam based but offer extra credit question every lecture so incentive to go to class. hes a great teacher and his research is really neat.

Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston's class was definitely tedious and required a lot more work outside of class than I was anticipating. It took me the first two exams to realize that you really do need to read and take very good notes. Basically, if you read for this class you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class def takes a lot of time outside of class. There's no attendance and I personally didn't know one person who actually attended during live lecture. I loved the material & Cindy and David are very fun professors. If human sexuality/human psychology is interesting to you, TAKE IT!! Don't expect this to be a blow off though.

Don't waste your time with Buss.  The class was poorly developed using outdated materials. Buss presented as fact many things that clearly weren't. Overall, the class had a chauvinistic tone that was hard to ignore.

There's nothing I can't say about the professors (Buss & Meston) that hasn't been said. They're by far the most interesting professors I've listened to. From witty jokes to stories about their friends to recalling documentaries. The lectures are engaging & fun. The tests are simple but really specific... make sure you listen to everything.

I can't thank Dr. Buss & Meston enough for such a great course; they're both hilarious & excellent professors. The lectures couldn't be any more fascinating. You do have to pay close attention to the lectures & READ THE BOOKS to pass the class. You are graded on 4 out of 5 exams (1 dropped). I highly recommend this course to everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the course content is interesting, Dr. Buss and Meston are simply not good professors. They use research from the early 2000's and their lectures are *at least* four semesters old. They are definitely the most unaccommodating professors I have ever had and use their " one free exam drop" as an excuse for missing an exam due to poor health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful class. The lectures are prerecorded from like 2 years ago too. I don't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Buss has been named one of the top 50 psychologists in the world and UT is genuinely so lucky to have him. He really knows what he is talking about and I still remember and tell people about what I learned in that class!
Dr. Buss is a gem of a professor - insightful, well-respected, and brilliant.
Dr. Buss is such an impressive and respectable professor. I wish I couldve seen him lecture in-person.

Buss and Meston are funny but you have to pay attention during lectures and do the readings since the exam questions are VERY specific. Speed up lectures/videos to save time. 5 exams (1 is dropped) based on lectures, textbook, articles, and videos- lots of work but it's an interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Meston and Dr. Buss are phenomenal professors. Their lectures are very engaging, and they are clearly very knowledgeable. It's not extremely easy, but definitely doable. I got a 91.5 in this class which is barely an A, by just watching all the lectures and taking notes. You take 5 exams, and your whole grade is made up of the 4 highest grades.
Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston did an incredible job lecturing. I was in the asynchronous class and the only thing I have to say is stay on top of the lectures and make sure to read the textbook.

I took the asynchronous version of PSY306 and absolutely enjoyed it. The material was actually very interesting, it's just that the tests were extremely specific (so be prepared for that). Dr. Buss (and Dr. Meston) are great professors and I absolutely recommend taking PSY306 with them.

This class taught by both Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston was very fun and interesting. However, you can not slack in this class at all. Your grade relies heavily on taking very structured notes and doing the readings precisely. If you do not study hard or watch all the lectures you will not do well in the class. But it is worth putting in the work.

The most interesting class I've taken at UT! I took it over the summer session, so my experience was a bit different but the class was still amazing. Grade was just based on exams every week. Some test questions were tricky, but if you watch the lectures and do the readings, it should be an easy A. Really changed how I think about sex >:)

Dr Buss and Dr Meston taught a super interesting class together. There were a lot of lectures and it seemed like we had tests every other week but as long as you take detailed notes the tests are not too hard. I learned so much and am actually going to miss their class! They are both very knowledgable and fun to listen to.

Your grade is going to be made up of 6 exams but as long as you take detailed notes and keep up with the lectures you'll do fine. He co-taught with Dr. Meston and his sections are a little more dull but him and Meston have a good dynamic so it's not too bad. The lectures are really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Buss & Dr. Meston's talk show style of recording lectures made it difficult to know what was important for the exams, but were easy enough to follow and understand the material. Also take this class with a friend so you can split the work because it's insane how much they expect you to read and watch per section.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you watch all the leactures and extra material assigned, the tests shouldn't be hard. Two books are also needed and should be skimmed b4 the tests. Watch the videos on x2 and they will go by quicker. Course covers a lot of interesting topics, and the Buss-Meston dynamic is very enjoyable to watch during the lectures.

Make sure to watch all the module lectures, read the book chapters assigned, and watch the additional videos because it's all going to come up on the test. Take your time on your notes and make them as detailed as possible. Really enjoyed the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston's different specialties compliment each other well to make great lectures. I loved this class- it was one of my favorites bc the "awkward" material is discussed so casually and is super interesting. However, there are a lot of assigned readings and a LOT of test q's over them. DON'T blow these off! Take this class! Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Buss was an interesting professor. I did actually enjoy the class, but was not expecting to work as hard as I did for an A. There's a lot of reading involved and quizzes almost every class. There was no curve, but they did drop one of our lowest exams (out of five) and two quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took this class thinking it was easy but it turned out way harder than it seemed to be. A lot of reading and taking notes is a MUST, I cannot stress that enough! The class was pretty interesting but definitely took more work than I thought. The online version had many glitches and was not always fair so would recommend to take it in person
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Would definitely take any class with him again. He's very informative and is constantly making references and jokes that make class more fun. His tests are challenging but not harder than you would expect.
Honestly, Dr. Buss is the man. He's funny enough to make human sexuality a little less serious than it sounds, and knows so much about his subject matter.
I took this class online, very enjoyable. Dr. Buss is hilarious and him and Dr. Meston make a great team. Don't hesitate to take this class! I'm really, really going to miss it

Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston taught this class together. The subject matter was very interesting, tests were not too difficult if you watched lectures and read/watched the assigned material. There is a quiz for almost every lecture, so don't miss those. 5 exams and one is dropped.
Buss and Meston are hilarious and make this class so much fun. Dr. Buss knows so much about his respective field. I was sad that this class ended.
As long as you actually are logged on to canvas and paying some attention you should be fine! Dr. Buss is pretty cool and they play videos and there is no homework
As long as you actually are logged on to canvas and paying some attention you should be fine! Dr. Buss is pretty cool and they play videos and stuff to keep you interested
Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston co-taught online live lecture course. Talk show style, hard to decipher important info from tangents. Tend to associate correlation with causation. Tests are ambiguous.

He made the class very interesting and I could say that I learned a lot in the class. There are four exams and each one is 25% of your grade. Don't think just because the stuff seems common sense that you don't have to study. Make sure you read the material and question your self. Being terrible at multiple choice style exams I did okay.

Wonderful professor. Very fair, very fun. Makes class entertaining and easy to relate to. He likes class participation, and his TA was very awesome. I would definitely take more courses with Buss in the future if presented with the opportunity.
Great prof!! Funny, helpful, smart, makes the subject matter interesting and relevant.
No Comments
No Comments
0 leniency for difficult situations. Has an odd stuck up attitude. Do not reccomend, save your grade from stress.
This class was really interesting. Burke did a great job making it interactive and engaging. The exam is difficult but doable.

Dr. Burke is amazing! If you can take him, DO. His lectures are engaging and make OM an easy to understand concepts. If you attend class weekly, you won't need to study outside of class. The homework is easy and take less than 30 mins weekly. You absolutely should attend class (no tech allowed) to succeed on the exams, but it's very doable.

I enjoyed Professor Burke's class. He's an engaging lecturer who explains material clearly, is approachable during office hours, and is always willing to help. He's also very understanding and accommodating. The weekly homework is manageable, and while the exams can be challenging, staying on top of the material and studying makes them very doable
His lectures are extremely boring and he just flies through material without being engaging. Also if you turn an assignment in even a minute late it is an automatic 0.

This professor does not care about his students one bit. If I were given the option to take another course taught by him or drop out of UT, I would start packing my bags and go. I have never met a professor who grades so harshly on exams and then looks at his students as if it is our fault. This guy will laugh at you for failing and not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Burke is super nice and always replies fast. The midterm and final are moderately hard, but homework is easy and helps your grade. Class is pretty boring, but you can learn everything from his slides. As long as you stay on top of it, you'll be fine.

OM should be easy but this man makes it so difficult. Do not take his class unless you hate yourself. It's graded based off the fact that his students get C- on exams and he still doesn't curve, you get counted off on HWs all the time and he can be boring. Taking OM with him is a GPA NO: anyone who tells you otherwise is a supply chain major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Listen...OM 235 as a class in my honest opinion, easy money—honestly pretty interesting.

OM 235 with Burke? Now that's a different story.

Don't take him if you care about your GPA, don't take him unless you don't mind no partial credit on FRQ based exams and no curves despite a C- average on exams.

Just...don't take him. Trust, take ANYONE else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is one of those classes where you would be fine if you only came to the review class before the exam. Unfortunately, attendance is mandatory, and electronics are banned, so I was in class every week. Burke is a great professor, but there is just not enough content to warrant a two-hour mandatory class.

For OM he knows his stuff. His lectures are really good and he post his slides after. He made us take notes with only paper and not laptops which is a little strange. Class isnt too bad, theres just no practice material which makes it somewhat iffy.

As someone without a 4.0, this course is not hard at ALL if you pay attention. Burke is engaging, and walks through example exam questions in every class; especially with the allowed cheat sheet, you're golden if you pay attention. Personally, I enjoyed his lectures greatly (other than the mention of food around lunchtime). Take him if you can!

He is genuinely very rude for not curving the exams that have no practice exam. You go in blind to the exams which are worth all your grade. There is no grace and the “extra credit” favors only a few people. Take anyone but him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nothing about this class is hard but Burke is the only prof that doesn't curve and u NEED a curve for the exams. Exams and hw aren't hard but getting a few (2-3) mistakes/not understanding a problem on both exams will get u an A-/B. If u don't care abt GPA this prof is fine and the class is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. This guy does not care about students. Unreachable and unhelpful. He is the only professor who doesn't curve the grade which is insane. I would at least have A- if it wasn't for that. Unless you're a beast at supply chain, don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Burke's lectures are too long and conceptual; more in-class practice would help. A 35%-weighted final without a practice exam is unreasonable, especially with limited resources for tough topics like project crashing. There's also no curve, on either the exam or final grade, despite all the other OM professors doing otherwise.

DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR BURKE. He fosters an environment of fear, and a simple mistake on an assignment can get you in huge trouble. Not welcoming and doesn't care about his students. He uses his platform to make himself look superior and belittles students. Really discouraging and is extremely strict overall.

I truly don't get what people in here are saying because Burke is by far the best OM professor. He's super understanding but stern. He's always there for you and he's a pretty good lecturer. 100% recommend. If you don't like OM in general, every prof will be challenging. Just work a bit hard ig

The way he teaches the class itself is pretty good. I am giving him a low rating because of how he is as a person. I personally feel that he is rude and does hold racial biases. Overall as far as workload the class is pretty doable. We only had to refer to the textbook like twice the whole semester

Based on what I've heard from my friends who took other professors for MIS 301, Burke is by far the best professor to take for MIS 301. Although this class is memorization heavy, the class is structured in a way that will set up up for success on the exams. Burke also has a great sense of humor and keeps the class engaged. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Burke for MIS301 and OM235 and would recommend taking his class for either. Does a good job explaining what to do for each kind of problem. Before each test, redo all of the homeworks up until that point and create a good notes sheet (you can bring one to the test) with all the required formulas and you will do well in the class.

Burke is a pretty humorous guy who always begins his class talking about the weekly UT sports scene. Classes are slides based on readings, and assignments are simple excel worksheets and interactive textbook questions. He makes a review slide for the midterms and if you study those you will do well. Class is usually released 30 minutes early.

Honestly not that bad of a class. Incredibly passionate professor who will work with you if you have any issues. He is very no BS, and does not allow screens in class and will call you out. Memorize how to do the HW problems for the exam and you will get a B/A.

Going into MIS I was fearful of the course work because other people said it was bad, but Burke breaks it down into VERY manageable chunks and is a funny guy!
