The tests are pretty memorization heavy, but if you pay attention in class and review the notes and supplementals it provides you with everything you need.

I understand how some people can find him strict, but I absolutely loved this class. MIS was boring for me but Burke really made the lectures interesting. To pass the exams you need to memorize ALL of the VOCAB on the slides. Learn the Vocab and you'll do great. All of the other mini-assignments throughout the class are pretty easy.
He's a more no BS type of professor. MIS301 is a memorization of key term class. His lectures don't really help for the exams you need to self study by yourself. Not bad but not great professor.

Professor Burke lectures entirely from textbook slides, which is a total repetition of content that you're already required to read. It is impossible to stay engaged during class. Additionally, Professor Burke exercises his power to pick favorite students, scrutinize students on their honesty, and make inappropriate jokes for a college classroom.

Burke was a pretty decent Professor and was willing to help students with concepts outside of office hours. 50% of your grade is based on assignments that aren't terribly difficult. However, the other 50% of your grade is based on tests that require you to memorize the textbook and slides. Tests are not cumulative.

Was this class hard? Yes. Did I have to memorize literally everything? Also yes. But did he curve my grade to an A at the end? Yes. So, at the end of the day, he gives you the resources to succeed you just really have to memorize every detail in the powerpoints and do the textbook practice quizzes. Nice guy too, decently understanding.
The lecture is boring and everything he talked about is directly from the book. Text is 100 question multiple choice, T/F and fill in the blank
I would recommend taking Burke for MIS, he seems to have made the class better than some people I know with different professors. If you study and understand the terms you will make an A.

Professor Burke is amazing! He keeps lectures engaging to his best ability. The OM 235 material can be dense, so please take advantage of his OHs if you're struggling. Attendance is "mandatory" but participation is based on completing pop quizzes. He advocates for YOU. Exams are tougher, but that's not his fault.

Worst prof I've had at UT. Lectures consisted of him talking about sports and using only 20-30 minutes to read directly off of slides from the textbook when we already had to read the chapter before. Prides himself on making tests as difficult as possible without any actual teaching. By far my easiest course content wise, but brought down GPA.

I took Professor Burke for MIS and OM. Not my favorite classes but Professor Burke made them both easy to understand and was always available to answer question over email or zoom. Would take any class given by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are extremely boring, especially since they're straight from the textbook when you have to read it ahead anyway. You have to know the book and vocab by heart for the tests; make sure to start studying ahead with quizlets and practices. Gives difficult pop-quizzes that are harder than the other profs' so look through your vocab before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy and I like how he explained topics like it was a conversation. Participation pop quizzes can be harder than other profs who just do completion instapolls (Finney). Tests are same for all profs: 100 randomized Qs so you need to know the textbook well especially vocab. Strict on no extra credit, only curves if class avg is

Quizzes are unnecessarily difficult and much harder than other professors. Tests ability to answer fill-in-the-blank under time constraints. Tests are challenging but not impossible if you study and are standardized. He's is funny and a good lecturer but the lectures do not help with anything. The class is entirely based on reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is so freaking annoying and hard. They are testing you over memorization of the textbook and by memorizing I mean MEMORIZING LINES to the dot. The lectures do not do a good job of reiterating the information and he even tells you in class that we won't talk about everything that could show up on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were very difficult--100 questions, no word bank, and weirdly written too. You have to study in advance and pretty much memorize the textbook. Lectures were mundane and there are pop quizzes that are graded so do some light reading before class. You learn Excel outside of class but the lessons were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class follows very, very closely to the textbook, to the point where the lecture slides are taken straight from the book. I found this really good, as it kind of standardized the information and made it so the topics that we were tested/quizzed on were directly in line and could be found in the textbook.
misogynistic. talks over you. narcissist. brags about himself the entire time. don't even pay attention, he reads the textbook out to you like you didn't pay money for it
I don't even know what to say. The grading is so unclear, and you cannot even see the average score of your assignments, leading you to believe that you are doing worse than you currently are.

Not only is the class confusing , but while other professors curved according to the McCombs guidelines, he didn't despite grades not being great. Weekly homeworks don't line up with exams and lectures don't have anything to do with exams. Take it with someone else.

This might be one the worst classes I have ever taken. I took Burke for MIS301 and enjoyed it. The assignments were fair and the tests correlated directly to what he taught. OM is a whole different story. I have never learned less in a course. The homework has NOTHING to do with lectures and the tests don't correlate to the homework either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took MIS with him and thought he would be just as good as a professor for OM. I think that the tests are very hard and your grade depends on whether the TAs hold review sessions. Class is not helpful and practicing emphasizes the concepts the most.

Burke is the worst. His lectures are so boring and you don't learan much and it is very dumbed down but then his homeworks which are supposed to be based on the lecture are extremely difficult and quite frankly you must teach yourself how to do. If there is another option, take a different professor

Dr. Burke's MIS class focuses on the business side of technology, which is why he does not test on the homework that involves coding. The tests do require you to understand a good amount of information, but if you study ahead of time and use the slides as a guide they are very fair. His grading is fair, and his lectures were always entertaining.

The tests are relatively easy if you study the material and the projects teach you things that are actually useful. That being said, lectures can be a little dry and instructions for projects/assignments can be pretty limited. If you study well, this class can be an easy A and its an easier alternative to other MIS301 options.

This class is just you teaching yourself the lectures are pretty vague for how much he test you on. All the assignments are self taught he doesn't give any information of all of the projects and assignments that are due and they barely count for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are easy if you attend lectures, review slides, and read the textbook. Although his lectures seem dry, they have a way of sticking in your memory. He did not curve my class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke is really funny and kind. Exams are tough- they have very specific questions from the textbook. Essentially, they test your memorization of the textbook. If you start studying early, an A is doable. Group work is not too bad, and you can always ask the TA questions. Overall, the class requires effort, but is well structured.
Tough, but fair. Attend lecture and do some studying before the exam and you're solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke has interesting lectures that he pairs with his sense of humor. He lectures directly from the slides with some videos and experiences in between. Exam questions were pulled from the practice quizzes, so you know what to expect on the exam. Ask your TA for help with group projects and cases. No final!!

This class was has completely changed from one semester to the other. was recommended to take him from others but they had a different syllabus. The class is super test heavy that one grade can mess you up. He skims slides during lectures and doesn't highlight on any of the important topics that you will be tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was miss informed by past students that this would be a pretty easy class with online exams but he has changed the format of test. They are no longer online and open note so be ready to study a lot for the exams. The test make up most of your grade while the other assignments require you to learn it yourself and barely count towards your average

Do not take burke his lectures seem fun when it comes to test they have hard multiple choices. All of the assignments given to you are never even talked about so you have to learn them all on your own.

MIS 301 with Dr. Burke was alright. TBH, I could've made an A- in the class, but I was lazy to actually study and crammed the day of tests. There's three exams, but not final. Recommend buying the textbook, it has practice quizzes which he bases the exams off of. Honestly, if you put some effort into this class you'll get an A- or A.
Professor Burke is a great, funny, and knowledgable professor. Take the group work seriously and pay attention in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a fairly easy class for MIS. If I studied a little harder I believe an A would have been achievable, as the grade is based 57% on 3 tests. As long as you read through his slides and know how to apply the concepts you will be fine. The case assignments are annoying and the TA grades harsh but overall not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are okay, the way the course is graded is kind of weird since there are only three things that matter. The exams and cores and cases. The cores are not too bad. The cases are depending on how your TA is feeling that day. Exams are okay too. Not lenient with grading and is not the nicest professor. He's just okay.

Honestly dont take him if your care about your gpa. Took him because everyone said how good he was but he has changed the layout of the class. No more open note test like the last several semesters and they make up 60% of the grade and are hard. Most of the assignments given in the class you are never taught how to do.

Took him during COVID. Class was scheduled to be hybrid, but we only met in-person once. His class is definitely the easiest for MIS 301, but don't expect to actually learn anything. One time he didn't even show up to class and never offered an explanation of why. Regularly curves final grades down and isn't transparent with grading criteria.

Say goodbye to open-note tests. Tests are majority memorization (not much application, just memorization) and make up almost 60% of our final grade. Get ready to read! Burke is a cool guy, but the tests can really affect your grade, even if you prepare extensively for them and do great on all the other assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I definitely would not recommend this prof. I based off my selection on his RMP but he has in fact changed the lay out of the class. The test are no longer open note like previous semester which makes the test super hard to do good because its test heavy. There is no extra credit nor curve and he a pretty bad lecturer.

I had MIS w Burke online in Fall 2021, and enjoyed him and the class a lot. He breaks down the textbook into concise slides, so all you need is the slides, and the exams are open note, making them pretty easy if you are at least somewhat prepared. Actually engage in class and apply yourself a little, and you can get an A pretty easily. Great Prof

overall, meh. He does the bare minimum but then grades rly hard. I did well in the class, but see how easy he made it for others to struggle. He was more concerned abt telling us to attend the next football game (bc apparently he was paid to do so) and just read off slides that are STRAIGHT from the book. if he likes u, he grades u better too

Professor Burkes is a class i would definitely take again. SAM assignments are frustrating but very do -able, the TA guides you through the help if you need it. Lectures are interesting and there is 5 assessments, 4 case assignments, 4 partner core assignments. watch the lectures/take notes and you will do well.
Only 2 exams and homework for this course and no extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Burke is nice, funny, and has good intentions. I have heard he is a really great MIS professor. However, he went through topics much too quickly and the exams were overly difficult. You did get to use notes on exam though, but they were still so hard. Too much info too fast. Not sure if there is a better option though tbh...

I really like Prof Burke and the lessons he gave. Although reading the textbook wasn't necessary it helped me a lot. People were saying you need a high at (95/96) but personally getting a 94 or above got me an A. Burke made MIS pretty interesting even though some of the assignments were annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Burke is a great professor. He gives you powerpoints that concise the textbook so that as long as you take notes during lecture, the textbook is optional (he says it's a supplemental resource). However, because of the high cutoff for an A in this class, you do really need to work it (like above 95/96). But it is doable if you put in the effort.
Class is mostly him reading off lecture slides. He makes jokes sometimes.
Overall good experience, interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Burke is an amazing professor. The class itself has a lot of elements to it, but very doable. I thought it was a pretty easy class to do well in and a better choice in comparison to other MIS 301 professors. The only thing is that with the curve, you need to have a high A to actually get an A in the class. Tests online are open note!!

Took Fall 2020. DON'T want to major in MIS or have Rock? Take Burke. Easy A if you thoroughly read the textbook. I had Sam (TA) and she was very understanding with grading and explanations. MUST read textbook for assessments. Keep in mind Burke does not follow the UT grading scale. He often curves up for what counts as an A (Ex: 93+A).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His classes are lecture heavy and there are required readings, but as long as you read and digest the PPTs that Burke posts on Canvas you would be fine. The assessments can be tricky at first because they are specific terms and concepts that he looks for in a response, but once you get a hang of it you can do well on them.

Burke is a nice and amazing person but lectures are boring. The grade is composed of too many things you need to put effort into during the whole semester. The average score for this class is extremely high so be aware of the curve.

The class is you having to do a lot of work yourself, but it's not too hard and actually useful to learn. There are assessments where he looks for specific answers that are all outlined in the notes. Once you get used to him, not a hard class. He also knows what he's talking about as a professor. Lectures don't really help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The daily iclicker quizzes gave me anxiety. I did not enjoy this class. He seems nice but he just reads off the slides. I felt like I didn't really learn anything. The tests are so long(consist of MC,short&long free-response questions). It was so hard trying to stay awake in this class at 9:30am. The test reviews are just him reusing lecture slides

If you have to take MIS and get the chance, take Burke! He tests based on class slides that are posted on canvas. There are fewer projects than other MIS classes and you get multiple attempts and/or a partner to work with. If you complete the assignments and study slides you can get an A. Daily iClicker quizzes to take attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he is super monotone so his lectures are unbelievably boring. he treated the tests like a guessing game by making our review material a shortened version of the powerpoint (lots of information to know). his tests have free response. never knew what was going to be on the test. couldn't ask him for help on SAM. canvas assignments were really hard

Burke is a nice guy and tries to connect with his students. I would give him a 5 if I was rating him as a person, but as a professor he is pretty average. Pretty much just re-lectures the textbook in class and doesn't add much insight. Take him if you do not want to major in MIS, take Rock if you do. Put in the work, and you can easily get an A.

Lengthy Canvas assignments (not necessarily hard, just long). Weekly SAM assignments easy, but annoying. Daily quizzes over the readings using clickers. Kind of hard to make an A because of the curve. Exams are literally definitions from the textbook and pretty easy short answer questions. I would take again. Reading is long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor, often cracks jokes. Very straightforward class. SAM assignments are easy but can get annoying. Class PowerPoints are long (50 slides) but can easily be summarized. Definitely one of the easier 301 classes. Only annoying thing is the excel assignments that come up later (not too bad w/ a good TA). Skim read for daily iClicker q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures were very interesting and kept me awake at the ungodly hour of 8. The class was a lot of work in my opinion. He also ghosted me when I sent him an email regarding my grade. Other than that, he's very knowledgable. Do the readings, prepare for the daily quizzes, or you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love the guy, used a lot of slides and sometimes assigned projects that neither he or him TA fully understood, but he would grade easier because of it. I honestly enjoyed the class but was a chore having to go at 8AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Just show up for daily quizzes and make sure you actually read the textbook and other materials. Really textbook heavy, but its easy enough. The only problem is that the curve is whack; the A cutoff was like 96 for my class, so you have to really work to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Burke has a supply chain/operations management background. His MIS knowledge is lacking. Lectures consist of him reading off of lecture slides provided by the textbook. He answers questions by re-reading the slides. Projects are poorly organized and explained. Not a bad guy but not equipped at all to teach MIS
In class quizzes are worth 25% of your grade so you have to prepare for every class, but the tests are much easier than the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I looked forward to professor Butters's classes every week! I learned so much about journalism from the stories he told of his experiences as a journalist. We wrote 3 stories throughout the semester and he offered much guidance and good feedback. Attendance is definitely important!

Professor Butters was so kind and passionate about journalism. I looked forward to the lab every week. Professor Butters was very accessible and always willing to help and share experiences from his past that were humorous and inspiring. I wish I was a journalism major so I could take more classes with Butters, his lectures were very engaging.

So disorganized. 50% of grade is HW (formatted in Latex). Considering the time commitment, he should bother to grade our work. 10 out of 13 HWs graded 1-2 weeks before finals, solutions posted a week before exams/final, midterm graded the day of q-drop deadline. It's impossible to consistently check your understanding unless you can make it to OH.

I would rate Professor B-dawg a 7 if I could, PLEASE TAKE HIM. 

Advice for those who will eventually read this letter. The homework is rough, It took ALOT of time to complete (If you're quick on Latex you're fine).

If you can jump that hurdle, the B-dawg lectures are the best Physics lectures known to the human race.

VERY MATHEMATICAL. Really steep learning curve. The class is a LOT more bearable if you can make it to office hours. I never read the textbook. Exams are slightly adjusted HW probs, and he tells you exactly which problems to study, no lies. Gives up to 6% extra credit w/ attendance and course eval. He's very caring if you just reach out.

His class definitely felt different than my other physics classes, but in a good way. This class is really mathematical, and I think there is a lot to learn from his way of thinking. Also, it is really easy to get an A since the midterm is literally the homework, and he tells you which questions to look at beforehand. Also 5% EC for attendance.

Dr. Burby is a very kind professor, but his mechanics class is very much geared towards physics majors and understanding mechanics concepts deeply. However, he was very helpful, and with the extra credit and attending office hours, it is definitely feasible to do well. If you are a physics, math, or astro major, I highly recommend taking his class!

Burby is a likeable and insightful professor. Lectures are rigorous and geared toward physics majors with an interest in theory; not everyone will appreciate his style. There is disconnect between the difficulty of getting a good grade (not too hard), and what he actually teaches (hard). His class has issues likely due to him being a new professor.

I'll be honest, this class was not an easy A and as a new professor he is still figuring out teaching. Still, he clearly wants his students to do well and is always happy to help you with any questions you have when he is available. If you take his class, I recommend going to office hours if you can and don't be scared to talk to him.
If you want actually to learn physics, take it! If you want an easy time, don't. Those who have a problem with this class just don't want to put in effort.

His lecture and homework got more difficult over the semester. However, if you understand the homework questions well with the help of OH/TA/friends, you are more than set to get an A. So overall, it is not hard to do well in this class even without fully understanding the content as long as you know the methodology for solving the HW.

A good calculus background would help for this class. An 8x12 “cheat sheet” was allowed on the midterm/final. Dr. Burby is very passionate about physics and strives to teach derivation and the why behind the principles of mechanics. It was significantly more difficult FOR ME to do well in this class if not for the EC offered/Curve.

He was a tough teacher, although I don't understand most of his lecture but his exams are fair with the similarity to homework. Also with 65% of homework grade and 3% of discussion attendance, getting a fair grade is relatively easy.  Also, his final is similar to homework and past exams. Overall he is a nice person. TAs are nice too!

Horrible professor. Lecture is no help at all, explaining problems that are WAY beyond intro undergrad level. These same problems (that sometimes the TA's cannot solve) are on the homework and tests. It is the day before our final and we have no idea what our grade is in the class because he has not decided grade cutoffs.

Dr. Burby writes his own homework and test questions except they are extremely hard to solve. In addition, his explanations are confusing and he basically skips all of the work and just restates the answer which is not helpful at all.

Joshua Burby makes a difficult class so much more harder than it needs to be. It does not help that his course is disorganized. It is one week before class ends and I have no idea what my grade in the class is.
I srsly cant do any problem that this man puts out. I feel so unmotivated and confused and sad in this class.

Dr. Burby's class is the most difficult course I've taken. Every day in class he has a problem and solves it the most complicated way. Doesn't give you formulas you just have to know. He makes his own homework questions and they are ungodly difficult. The TA's are stuck sometimes, and extra credit was just 2 more exams. GG WP 0/10 NO RE

His class is really good for those who want to understand physics at a fundamental level. However, this class might not be for those who want an easy "A." He is clearly a genius, and his brain could probably power the entire North American continent. There is a lot you can learn, that is if you put in the effort. However, this is NOT an easy class.

he a cool dude, its obvious he really love physics and teaching it in general which i think is awesome but he's trying to teach us at a much higher level than the class should be, n it just confuses everyone. he just be goin through 2 page long proofs every class and god damn i'm lost as hell. exams r 13% and hws are like 50% so its chill doe.
He must be stopped. His physics problems are beyond undergrad level. This is some NASA level wizardry.

Second midterm stats:
Mean: 39.7
Median: 42.86
HIGH Score: 78.57

Do not take him it's not worth it.

Nice guy, but overcomplicates too much for an intro course. 1st test was like hw, but everything got worse. Homework problems had concepts not covered in class and 2nd test tried to apply hw "concepts", except we never fully learned them. Asked for feedback but didnt follow it. TAs are a godsend, but even they + other grads cant solve some problems

He is bad at explaining things and cannot find a way to teach his class. Most of the students do not show up for lecture. Homework problems are extremely difficult. TAs carry this class but even they can't solve some of his problems.

He is not a very good professor. His lectures go beyond classical mechanics and he ends up lecturing about derivations and proofs. You end up having to teach yourself most of the material in order to do the HWs. The test and HWs are very hard. The test and HWs always have some hard questions that he wrote himself. The TAs carry this class.

Interesting teacher, although it is an entry level physics course but the prof always uses mathematical way to teacher. Lecture class is problem sessions actual content is in the recorded pre lec. Actually I don't understand a word…… although I took ap physics 1 and c. Although the grade is relatively nice but it is more like a linear algebra class

He was great, he was really funny and he made you want to come to lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but it earns you slip days for homework. He makes the subject really accessible and a really good lecturer.

Dr.Bulko is an awesome lecturer and his class is fairly easy (10 HW assignments - small iOS apps; 1 semester project App). His lectures mostly consist of him doing Swift/xCode demos and the assignments are pretty enjoyable. My TA was great and most people get A's on the HW, but the instructions are picky. Start the project early!

Great professor and easy class, but the TAs are extremely nit-picky and borderline annoying. They take off for the smallest things and will refuse to give points back. Be sure you do everything the assignment asks to a T.

The professor IS GREAT. Let me repeat BULKO IS AMAZING. 

However the TA grades everything and they are so unreasonable and is on a power trip. Genuinely worst coding experience of my life.  Please stay away it is not worth it.ONCE AGAIN: STAY AWAY

I really want to enjoy this class! I love the lectures, the homework, and I thought I'd like the group assignment. The absolutely disrespectful way he is treating our group though when we try to tell him issues we're having with a troublesome groupmate that has literally cussed us out and done such little work though makes me dread this class.

Bulko is an amazing professor. His teaching style is straightforward, and everything he teaches in lectures relates to the HW. Attendance is "required" only in name, and it's not tracked.  The group project is well outlined and the expectations are clear. The grading is straightforward without strict "gotchas" for stuff like syntax or style.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with prof Bulko, hands down go for it. He is such a kind man, he cares for his students and loves to teach. If you ever want to ask him about anything CS-related, he is happy to provide resources and make time for you. Simply just a great man, I wish I could take another class with him
one of the best instructors I've ever had.

Class attendance is "Mandatory" but nothing is done to track it, and all lectures are shared online. Assignment guidelines are clear and specific. This is the first course I've *ever* received a perfect 100 in. If you follow the assignments to the *letter* you'll get an A every time. Plenty of time given for tests. Homework is annoyingly frequent.

Really great prof, very witty which makes lectures interesting. First 3/4 of the class is demos, followed by group presentations. HWs are really light, just copy paste code from demos. Easy A as long as you put in reasonable work on your group's app and don't procrastinate too much. Most groups get 97+ on alpha/beta even if app is kinda broken.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: What an amazing course. What an amazing lecturer. The homeworks are all VERY doable. He is also extremely funny and caring especially with the semester long group project. I highly reccommend this course. Made me love CS all over again!

Very smart professor with a good sense of humor. He makes lectures fun and explains the subject matter thoroughly. The grading system is fair and there are plenty of opportunities for help from him or other TAs. He can be very blunt/sarcastic at times.

I LOVE PROF BULKO!! If you ever get the opportunity to take one of his classes and are interested in CS, he will do anything to help you learn and understand. The man is very very smart but knows exactly how to dumb it down. I told him I wanted to go into SWE and he set up a meeting with me to give me good resources and connections. LOVE!

phenomenal lecturer - everything i wanted from a non-cs major professor. he was careful to not throw you in the dark about new concepts and was good at dumbing down concepts to develop them into more complex concepts later. class goes through a lot of material - but hw are doable. so are tests

Bulko's Mobile Computing class was the best CS class I've taken at UT. His lectures are entertaining and very in-depth. His assignments are the perfect balance of challenging enough to learn, and easy enough to be enjoyable. As long as you do all the homeworks and don't procrastinate on the group project, an A is guaranteed.

I really enjoyed the class, but get ready for a lot of work (though a normal amount for a CS class). About 2 homework assignments a week (17 total), 3 exams, and one group project. I literally couldn't wake up in time for any of the lectures, but he gives a lot of resources on his website so I was still able to keep up and understand assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: REFUSED to share lecture recordings when I missed a week due to medical emergencies. He asked me: "So if you had gotten ill in 2019, before anyone was even considering recording classes, what would you have done?" He should ask himself how he could better provide us the resources we need in order to succeed given these difficult times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prob my favorite CS course. Bulko kinda makes a big deal of the proposal & design doc which was kinda dumb but whatever. Class is structured very well and the HWs are fairly easy and the instructions are helpful. Group project is up to you and I found it fun. Bulko is a little dated on some of the new iOS stuff but his lectures were still good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Bulko is an amazing professor. I took him for Web Programming and he taught very well. The class assigns 1-2 homework assignments per week on top of 3 tests and a semester-long group project, so the work is pretty heavy. However, if you pay attention and go to office hours, you'll do fine.

Mobile Computing (iOS): Practical skills. Can learn on your own, but class gets you hands-on experience. Easy A if you do the work. 10 HW assignments - all have helpful instructions, and are well-documented online - not too hard. Meat of class is group project. Lots of steps. Very generous grading. Great feedback too. Don't forget journal entries!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class is structured pretty well; 10 homeworks, a group project, and journal entries that accompany the group project. The homeworks were all straightforward and fair, and he grades the projects fairly as well. Getting an A isn't difficult, but this class might be more work than you'd expect because of the project, so keep that in mind!

Currently taking him for Web Programming, and its been super fun! Not a big fan of programming server-side in PHP instead of inside an IDE like when I took his 303E Python course, but he's been very amazing in the transition. He assigns A LOT of homework (1-2 weekly) but its only to get you involved in the programming. He's really helpful and nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had Bulko for CS303E and am taking his Web Programming course. He is a great teacher as well as a good person who cares about his students. He makes all concepts easy to understand. 10/10 Definitely recommend taking a class with him! His exams are very fair and similar to the homework he assigns.

Awesome person! His lectures are super interesting and very informative, and he is incredibly accessible outside of class, always answering questions outside of class on piazza. One of my favorite class experiences! Side note: he is hilarious and a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This Professor is amazing. REALLY emphasizes breaking a situation down to its core so you understand how your program or code truly functions. He's an extremely knowledgeable guy with a lot of years in the industry. If you go to lecture and do the programming assignments you're getting the A.

Attend all the classes and you don't have to read the textbook. Dr. Bulko explains all the concepts very thoroughly. He and the TAs are very helpful and responsive on Piazza. There are 15 HW assignments but not that hard, he always go over them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bulko is a fantastic teacher. I never found myself zoning out during lectures, and attending those are definitely required if you're looking to get a decent grade. I didn't buy the book, but Google works well for any questions that you have. Written exams were difficult.

Bulko is the BEST, take him!!! He's funny, kind and is very clear in explaining any concept, which is good even if you have no background in the subject. HW are fair, exams might be a little hard but fair. Hes the best professor you could take though and is very accessible outside of class with office hours everyday and quick email/Piazza replies
He is funny, good sense of humor. But he makes the class very hard. The TAs point out the smallest of things and you will lose 10 points. Too many homework that take forever to figure out
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bulko is awesome. Funny dad humour aside, he is succinct in teaching an intro class to a bunch of people who know little to nothing about coding. Homeworks are just challenging enough to figure out but learn from, and exams are just slightly harder (but fair). I got a B because I was lazy and didnt do the last HW. I would have an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: IOS was a really fun class and the grading was all reasonable. Bulko takes the time to comment on all of the journals and is really caring. The grading criteria is clear. The amount of homework is a bit heavy, but anything less and you wouldn't learn the material. Make sure to find a good group and you'll do well in the class.

Dr. Bulko was fantastic! His lectures were always clear and easy to follow. The homework assignments were never too difficult and he would provide help on those in office hours. His tests were a little tricky but overall not too bad because you're allowed a cheat sheet. He's overall an amazing professor and you should definitely take his class.

Great professor. He really knew how to explain concepts clearly and concisely. Most of your grade (55%) comes from homework assignments, and he always went over the solution to them in class using other examples (so attend class if you can!!). The tests can be tricky just because he asks you to write programs, but they were doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Imma keep it real. Class was not difficult if you attended class. However, Bulko expects you memorize something he said once in class. And God forbid you ask a question - he will answer you with an air of condescension. TAs grade pretty harshly on homework, and the exams test the minutae, a lot of which I've never needed to use outside the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly why would you choose anyone else? Take his class.

Lectures were clear and well explained. He acknowledges that the content is really boring and does dad jokes. Your experience in this class will be defined by how good your TA is. Ours was godly. Good amount of homework and tests were straightforward. Cheatsheets are allowed on tests. A good counterbalance to Mike's 314.

Bill's lectures can seem slow sometimes, but that's just because he's thorough in his explanation. In my opinion, that's better than a professor breezing through difficult concepts. For the class itself, 10 weekly HWs, no exams or final, 1 semester-long project to build whatever app you want. Easy upperdiv CS class.

Bulko has interesting lectures. He understands the class isn't CS majors so he explains things thoroughly. Exams can be challenging but do-able if you study. Homework assignments every week but are not that hard. He is caring and understanding and is always available during office hours, although you should get there early- lots of students go.

I learned a decent amount without the class being difficult. Easy A, but don't completely blow it off or it may sneak up on you. Also, I had already taken Statistics. We spent some time on set theory and such, which is great for when you get to stats but, if you have already taken it, feels a whole lot like going to lecture is pointless for a bit.
Bulko explains everything at least ten times in class and provides plenty of examples. Go to class, do the homework in the discussion sections and you have an A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Somewhat mediocre jokes in class, seems like an alright guy, until you get to his office hours. Explains answers with almost a level of contempt, overall not very nice or helpful. TA's were good and helpful though.
I'm not a CS major (anymore), but I did think he was a good professor. The class was very difficult, but I think he was somewhat of an easy grader (relative to how crappy a student I was).

IThis class is really boring but Bulko knows that and tries to keep the lectures semi-interesting, but still if you're not careful you'll fall asleep. The TA's were not very helpful but if you form a study group for the homework you should get good grades. Make a good cheatsheet for the test and you'll be solid, they're not as hard as the hw.
A really easy course, he allows cheat sheet in the tests and that is really helpful.
Great class and great professor.

He lets you bring a cheat sheet on the test, which is great. The tests should be easy if you put the right things on your cheat sheets, unless you're great at memorization. Homework is helpful in preparing you from exams. Good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really funny, smart and nice professor. He goes over everything thoroughly and tries to help you get good grades on the exam. The only downside this semester was our TA, who took forever to grade stuff and was pretty ruthless in the grading technique

I found Bulko's CS311 class easy and manageable in terms of concept and workload, and a good counterpart to Mike Scott's difficult CS 314 class. His lectures are understanding and entertaining (enhanced by his amusing/dry jokes (depending on the person)). HW can be unnecessarily difficult, but tests are a lot easier. Just watch out for your TA.

Sometimes he wasn't prepared, and because the course is a boring topic to many, it was really hard to focus during class. There's one assignment per week. The TAs were my favorite part of the class. He mentions things in class that are essential to the exam. They take time to grade to give proper feedback. Some tests were more difficult than others
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bulko is an incredibly reasonable professor. He doesn't ask you to buy the textbook because he understands that college kids already have to pay for so much! He also gets that Discrete Math isn't the most exciting topic, so he jokes and does his best to keep lecures entertaining, which I really appreciated. All in all he's a great, caring prof!

Bulko's class was pretty easy, and for the most part he was engaging in his lectures. Sometimes the lectures felt a little drawn out, but I think that's just due to the topics we went over. Be sure not to forget to turn in a homework, homework was about 40% of the grade, so if you do them the class should be a pretty easy A since tests were easy.
An amusing professor who will try to engage the class. Very nice and tries to explain further if needed. Work was doable for slackers and slow people like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: great professor who makes discrete math easy. if you need help then just go to his office hours, he's super helpful and tries to remember your name if you go.

He's a very sweet and logical professor in that he won't make you do unreasonable work. Weekly homeworks are worth a portion of your average but are super easy, so be sure to keep up with them. Provides most information in lecture so studying isn't hard or long at all. Tests are easy and he provides help if needed. Would definitely take him again!

Prof. Bulko is an amazing human being but can be a bit confusing while explaining stuff. The exams and hw were super easy and he helps out a lot if you go to his office hours. The class was a bit unorganized in my opinion and could be improved upon. He does make the occasional joke to keep the class interesting though. Take if you want an easy A.

Professor Henry explains concepts clearly and demonstrates genuine concern for student success. However, lectures tend to lack engagement, with lengthy, difficult-to-follow slides and a presentation style thats really boring. Exams are challenging, but the grading policy reduces the weight of the lowest test score.

Professor Henry is fantastic. Topics in lectures are clearly conveyed to students using approachable language and class assignments. He takes an individual interest into each students success both in and out of the classroom as well. His classes are tough mainly because of the McCombs standardization of accounting classes however.

He is a caring and knowledgeable professor. I really enjoyed his lectures because he encouraged participation and explained concepts in depth. He engaged us quite well with the content, allowing a fundamental and intuitive understanding of the course. He was also generous with grading and attendance. 10/10!

Awesome instructor! the class itself is very small and intimate. The variety of reading and film materials makes the class interesting and I had fun. You get 3 unexcused absences for this class - make sure you don't skip more than that and you should be fine. Overall, the class requires minimal work and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: shes a great professor. she really cares about her students and has a fun class. the book and movie choices are so interesting and she lets you revise your essays for another grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great lecturer! Interesting topics, books and movies. Since the class is small, it was mainly discussion about the book/movie. She gives great feedback on essays and is really willing to help you out. Weekly reading or movie watching. Part of your grade is participating in discussion and divided up between three essays and pop quizzes

I had professor bybee in the spring semester and really enjoyed his class. He took the time to meet with students before the semester began and was passionate about the subject matter. Only drawback was that it was a lot of writing that can pile up if you are not careful. Would recommend!

There are far better professors at UT teaching this course. The only thing you get from Bybee is a regurgitated version of the researchers on campus who are critically engaging with these topics. The class is incredibly easy though and, honestly, pretty painless if you don't mind dealing with a grad student who likes to hear himself talk.

Easy class. terrible design. Vague direction from professor, unnecessarily long and pointless assignments.  Grad student on an ego trip.  Does not inspire college level interaction from class. Treats students as tho they are  still in kindergarten.  If u have the option and don't want to shoot urself mid-semester,choose another prof.

LOTS of reading u have to buy all of them, 7 books ranging from 70 to 10. Don't read, you'll be lost. He has difficulty explaining the reading in simple terms for the class to understand and tends to go very slowly through the material. We were constantly behind. cold calls but most of the time the class just stared back at him in silence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Defrinitely do the readings and attend class and you're in for an easy A. The classes and readings are foundational for succeeding in the papers, but he does a good job explaining what he wants to see and what he expects in the papers. Great lectures, I learned a lot and he really made me think over problems with a new perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: These other reviews are crazy, this prof will have u praying a frat bro drunk driving home at 9AM hits you JUST so you don't have to listen to his French, smoke latent, disengaged demeanor. this is not an easy A class, prepare to grovel, prepare to read 1 book per week. Doesn't sound like a lot but it catches up to you. oh and he cold calls :)

Tough but fair. Once you realize what he wants from your essays, it gets a lot easier. Attendance is required, and participate in class for full credit. Ask questions in class. Definitely read the books, you'll learn something new and you can't write a good essay without them. This class was super difficult, but also a great learning experience.

Lecture heavy (you'll fail after enough absences), be prepared to take notes, and do try to read the books for a chance at extra credit during discussion. Sometimes gave us emails on extra notes and thoughts on lectures. Once had a turn-in issue and he was very gracious and allowed me to turn it in even after the close date. 3 papers 1 final.

Genuinely one of the funniest professors I have ever had. While the content can be boring at some points, she is very engaging and fun to listen to. As long as you show up to lectures, loosely pay attention, and review before the exam, you will get a good grade in this class. The exams are intuitive if you listen in class.

Easily one of the BEST professors I've met. If you have the chance to take one of her courses, I'd highly recommend it. The course content was new, interesting, & particularly relevant. She's very down to earth, open to feedback, and offers great advice. Super knowledgeable with engaging lectures. If you commit to this class, you'll be rewarded.

If you need an upper level gov I would highly suggest this one. The content of the course was about the politics of critical minerals which not a lot of people really know much about but she made it interesting. Dr. Evans was such an amazing and understanding professor. I went through a tough year and she helped me through it & gave the best advice

Professor was great at lecturing but course content was dense. There was so much material and it was tough to navigate and contextualize it. She provides everything needed in lectures, I barely read. My issue was more it was heavy in content and didn't leave room to understand things in depth. She is a caring person and takes feedback into account.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is a great person and good for life advice (she sets aside time for this in class, but I mean one-on-one). The class itself was more unorganized than I hoped, that might just be that semester. Many assignments were restructured or canceled with course material seemingly too much with too little depth. Great remote/online accessibility!
Dr. Evans was a great professor who seemed like she cared except I am not sure she always did. She is very anti-law school so be prepared for that. But she does make the lectures semi-relatable.

Dr. Evans human rights class lacked real-life examples and modern events, hindering relevance. Poorly explained measurement unit and tough TA grading added to frustration. Peers felt the same. Assignments were too spaced out, leading to cramming. Cancelled final was a relief, but overall learning experience felt lacking. Nice person though.

Rhonda is my favorite professor at UT. She is an incredible resource to gov students and really cares about you. GO TO CLASS AND TALK! She remembers who participates and makes class really entertaining if she knows your name. She gives great advice about law/grad school and is a great class to see how you would do in law school. Rhonda is the GOAT

Loved Dr. Evans' lectures. Negatives are that we are graded by like 3 assignments and 2 exams. The writing assignments weren't that bad. Exams were generally poorly worded and my classmates and I shared the same sentiment that it was unnecessarily tricky. The true and false format was atrocious and a poor way to test us. And no extra credit? Boo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her UGS course, Australia, US, and the Rise of China was very interesting and engaging.  Grading can be strict sometimes and attendance does matter, though when I took it (Spring 2022), we were allowed 5 absences w/ no penalties. Do the external readings and the major assignments at reasonable times and you will do just fine. Don't procrastinate!

Dr. Evans is a great professor. Her UGS, Australia, US and the Rise of China, was extremely interesting with a number of engaging guest lecturers, and the lectures are very conversational. Definitely ask questions, have a conversation and she's kind and caring.

Dr. Evans helped me decide my future major. When it comes to the class, it is writing intensive because it carries a writing flag. It was all online, so we only had to watch lectures and read about 5-10 readings a week. Dr. Evans was available by appointment outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Evans is the most lovely, most hilarious professor on UT's campus. She's super accessible in just about every way, she knows her material incredibly well, and she can make even the most boring content fun and interesting to learn about. She's an angel and I pity anyone who goes to UT without meeting her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is an outstanding professor that clearly cares about her students and her subject. There is a lot of reading in this course, but it is usually very interesting and important for the tests. She encourages lots of class participation and provides you with plenty of support if you need it. She clearly wants to see her students succeed!

It was a great class and I learned a lot about it. She talks a decent amount about law school so if youre interested in that shell try her best to persuade you out of it lol. The lectures were always interesting but you better write everything down because the ppts are not useful. even if you didnt read she goes over them in class so dont worry
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher,  and cares about students but lectures are all oral with no power point. Covers a lot of information and test on a lot of it. Gives out a ton of readings that can be tough to read

Such a helpful professor! There are an insane amount of readings, but she gives you a reading guide for every single one so you know what you need to for the exams. She also allots time before each exam for class time review. Professor Evans truly wants her students to succeed, go to her if you need help! Overall a really great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: if you are not into law/debate/policy/govt you will absolutely suffer through this class because the tests and reading materials are relentlessly  difficult and ridiculously time-consuming. She is def an amazing prof--her lectures are interesting and her intelligence is engaging. but i would never take her again due to the massive workload

She is really interesting. You need to go to class to understand the information. There are readings for every class with discussion questions but she pulls the exam questions straight from the discussion questions

Carley, by far, is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. You can tell she loves what she teaches, and she teaches it well. I was never stressed by her class and the assignments she gives out. Very understanding of your time! As for the other and much lower ratings for her, I think she has improved her teaching methods and syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Carley is an amazing professor. She is so passionate about what she does & you can tell she wants to connect w/ her students. We haven't received grades yet, but she offers PLENTY of opportunity to raise your grade by attending design events. I'm not sure why she has bad ratings? She's genuinely such an inspiration. It's not a hard class at all.

Carley was a lot of fun, she's very down to earth and understanding if things that arise outside of class. some of the projects seemed like they were just expansions of des304, they were still great to work on and complete. Grading happens at the end of the course so i found it best to chat with her throughout about things that I was unsure of.

You only receive grades back at the very end of the semester. Even when she likes something in class, you may receive a poor grade on it and there's no way to know. She's extremely nit picky in her grading. When her TA told me they liked something, she would disagree but I would not know this until grades came out. The grading feels subjective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If there's another professor for the class you need, take the other one. Her grading depends heavily on your relationship with her, plus you won't know your grade until the end of the semester when it is too late to do any changes or do better in the next projects. Very passive-aggressive with her emails if you even get one from her back.
Terrible professional. Does not provide ruberics for grading and it feels very arbitrary or personal. If you do not try very hard she will fail you. Don't use ai she will fail you.

Honestly kind and caring professor when it comes to critique and individual feedback. Though, does not hold herself to the same standards she puts onto her students. Pushed back deadlines, last minute project changes, passive-aggressive when it comes to discussing grades, and does not grade anything until the last minute. Sweet but unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely love having Carley as a professor. I feel like she generally is a very kind person and always wants the best for their students. She's understanding of mental health, and very understanding of absences. I felt like I always gained something from her crit and never felt beat down by her like I have from other professors. Def take her

When I signed up for this class, the instructor was not determined yet, and I'm grateful that it was Carley. She gave really interesting projects, and I love the way she conducts feedback in class; she cares a lot about creating a kind and supportive environment. I've definitely grown, not only as a designer but also as a person in her class.

Carley is an amazing educator, designer, and human being. She cares so much about her students and leads all of her interactions with empathy. She is incredibly knowledgeable about typography and letterpress printing, assigns really interesting and engaging projects, and gives wonderful feedback. One of my favorite classes!

She is a very tough grader and is very disrespectful. She does not care about the wellbeing of her students. She is very unclear about her projects and assignments and gets mad when students don't understand. She will embarrass you in front of the whole class and is very unencouraging.

Carley is an amazing professor who does everything in her power to help all her students succeed. I took her Images in Communication class and though it was project heavy, she explained in detail all of the concepts the projects would entail and she also clarified anything when the students needed it. I'm excited to take her classes in the future!

Carley is an amazing professor! She is always helpful and is really good at advising and guiding her students. If you work hard, communicate, and create something that you are proud of, Carley will see that and gives fair grades! She's also very easy to talk to outside of class and is an amazing and supportive person during stressful times

We didn't get grades until our section with her ended. She was vague about assignments until it came to grading, when she would grade harshly for criteria she never explained. I approached her about this and she said I "didnt listen in class or to critique" which is not the truth. She is unwilling to explain or correct you until after submission.

Pretty much the same style as 311C. Her grading leaves very little room for error if you want an A. She's definitely she best bio prof. She does mini field trips for 311D so try to go if you can. If you can keep your grade in the A and A- range before the final then youre fine.

She's a good lecturer but you need to have previous bio knowledge. I came in with no bio knowledge whatsoever and I didn't do great in the class. I studied hard and it was still hard to understand. Three exams and a final, she averages your lowest exam with your final or something like that.

Very kind and caring professor, and excellent engaging lectures. However, her tests are very strangely worded and if you are not naturally good at test taking and answering confusing questions then you will have a hard time earning a high grade.

Buskirk is super sweet and funny, not many quizzes and attendance isn't mandatory but there are instapolls u can just do from home. Just study the learning outcomes, she gives so many resources and great lecterer!

Dr. Buskirk is really sweet and knowledgeable in her field. Going to office hours helped clear up a lot of my confusion, but I feel like some of the questions her tests are really weirdly worded and lack proper context, and understanding the concepts is not enough. Overall, she's a lot better than the other professors but the tests need work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you fully understand biology already, do not take this professor. She is very nice, but she skips slides and expects you to already know everything and never really dives deep into material. Tests are extremely hard and very specific with no exact outline of what is on them.

Tricky wording on tests, read it carefully or you'll end up missing questions. There is content tested that is not included in reviews. However she explains topics really well and assignments are easy. Memorize Instapolls and HW for test and final because they show up. No need to get textbook.

A lot of the chemistry stuff is covered pretty quickly, and if you haven't taken AP chem or AP bio, it's important that you review it before the tests. You only need to study the LO's, instapolls, and hw's that she gives out. There are a lot of repeat questions and certain LO's will be heavily tested!!!

Dr. Buskirk is extremely knowledgeable and kind. She offers many office hours and is always willing to help. However, the exams are extremely difficult and unfair due to tricky wording, content not covered in class, and limited questions, leaving very little room for error. The course is heavily exam-based, with no drops or extra credit.

Great professor and deeply engaging lectures, however, exams are quite difficult and worded strangely. The final was more difficult than the midterm exams, causing some to lose the letter grades they held all semester.

Thoroughly explains all the content you need for exams in her lectures; only exam prep you need is to just take notes on what she says in lecture in relation to LOs. Textbook is ‘required' but I never used it / readings overcomplicate things that would not be tested on. Lots of exam questions are just repeat instapoll / homework questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures feel pointless because the slides are only unanswered learning objectives, leaving students to learn everything on their own outside class. Little of the lecture content appears on exams, and many test questions are poorly worded “select all that apply,” making assessments confusing and frustrating. No point in attending lecture tbh.

I haven't taken biology since 9th grade and I couldn't have asked for a better professor to ease me into college coursework. Dr. Buskirk is maybe the most fair intro bio professor in terms of what she expects you to know and she's super accessible with office hours. Many exam questions are essentially variations of homework / Instapoll questions.
Test heavy

Dr. Buskirk is an incredibly sweet lady! As someone who didn't take AP Biology in high school, this class felt straightforward. Instapolls, Homeworks, and Apply Extend assignments were all fairly easy and she never assigned too much reading. Her exams are sometimes worded poorly, but are similar to lecture questions. If you can, take 311C with her!
Very tangential lectures with no clear objectives
Do not take, she shamelessly adds random scenarios into the tests that she doesn't go over and expects you to have lottery-winning luck to guess them. Nice lady though.
Buskirk lectures are known for being pointless yet required while her tests simply have nothing to do with what she discusses

Dr. Buskirk is an amazing professor! Her lectures are very engaging and helped me understand bio well. She provides many practice problems both in & outside class, which help prep for exams. Be sure to pay attention and study well for exams, as they are worth 80% of the course grade (and can be tricky if you don't understand concepts well enough)!
loved this class!

Amazing lecturer! Many practice questions throughout the lecture + canvas assignments throughout the week similar to exam questions. Pay attention during lectures then take notes after class. For exams, do the exam practice on canvas and answer learning outcomes. Textbook is unnecessary. Easy to follow along, JUST DON'T PROCRASTINATE!

BUSKIRK IS THE GOATTT literally the best bio prof at UT Austin, she cares so much about her students and is super approachable and friendly. she wore a mustache to class once. personally i didn't find her tests overly challenging, just show up to class and do your homework on time and you're set. actually the sweetest woman ever and best prof 10/10

Her lectures are amazing, definitely try to attend every class if you can. Exams are difficult but manageable. She doesn't really do extra credit, so exams are weighted heavy. She's also really sweet to talk to, I wish I went to her office hours more often. She has so many drop-ins if you need help and her TAs are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think she's a good lecturer, but the way her tests were spread out made it that our last exam covered over a month of content. This made this exam very difficult. Her content and slides are great, but they are not enough to get an A on her tests. I found her tests to be confusing, detailed, and hard.

Dr. Buskirk is an incredible professor and a gem of UT. She is incredibly inspirational and respected in her field, but made her class very approachable and doable even for "not the best" bio students. I went into her class with no AP bio but have kept a high A all semester. She wants you to succeed and it shows. Take her class if you can!

Great professor and genuinely cares for your learning, and her lectures were very fun to attend. Instapol's carry hard on the tests and make sure you review discussions. Though the test will have random curve balls that truly test your ability to "apply knowledge", and there isn't a lot of room for error to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She lectures well, and class was interesting. Exams were extremely challenging, though, and seemed irrelevant to what was taught in lecture (questions were worded weird too). I rewatched all lectures, took detailed notes, and went to some of her office hours, yet her exams were still tricky. A very confusing course to say the least!

Spring 2025, She is truly a caring and inspirational professor! She offers many extra credit opportunities and takes advantage of office hours and mini field trips that are planned. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Tests are kind of difficult, but can be easy if you just study and focus on the topics you are struggling with.

This is my second semester taking Buskirk, but I personally enjoyed 311C more than 311D. She is an amazing lecturer (you don't really need the textbook), but some of her test questions were quite confusing! However, her grading system is pretty nice, and she offers many resources to learn the content! Make sure to study the LOs and her slides!
Dr. Buskirk is an amazing professor. Her lectures are engaging and well-organized. Additionally, the grading system is very forgiving.

good lecturer + passionate about biology but grade is almost fully dependent on exam scores and her cutoff for an A is higher than most other professors. offers no extra credit and tests were often difficult + oddly worded
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buskirk is a good lecturer & a nice person in general; her tests are just weird. Tests rely on more of you figuring out how to answer her odd questions compared to you applying the material that you learned from her slides & the class. No extra credit at all either.

Professor Buskirk is extremely passionate and sweet about this topic. She really tries to make you succeed and offers many practice questions to recall information actively. There are 3 midterms and one cumulative final. Tests are MCQ and FRQ and use similar or/same questions from Instapoll and discussions.

Her lectures can be a bit hard to follow at times but she is super approachable for any questions that arise. Also does mini field trips throughout semester that are fun. Tests are pretty hard but she gives a ton of resources so they are manageable. Get ready to read and study!

She is such a nice woman, but grading is so strict. Her tests would have questions that you would only know if you attended lecture. Basically your whole grade is the tests, with no bonus or curve. I would do the learning outcomes and make sure to go to her office hours. You can tell she cares, but she is so set in her ways with grading.
Tests are everything. if u can't test take well don't bother taking her. the A cutoff is a 94 and she doesn't round at all. if u bomb even one test there's no way to recover.

I enjoyed taking intro bio w Dr. Buskirk. She made clear what she wanted us to learn and taught us well. There is a textbook, which I read from before lectures, but it is not really needed to do well in the class. Instapolls keep u engaged and grading is clear. TA's were also very chill. She has office hours in her office and is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Buskirk is sweet but her grading scale is strict. Her exams test exactly what she says in lecture. I used to study hw's, AE's, instapolls and wrote the learning outcomes with AI (basing it on the slides) but I kept scoring 80–90. Don't chat the LOs. Rewatch lectures and use only those to fill out learning outcomes. Know her exact wording. Trust me

Not much leeway with getting an A, but very doable as long as you are a good test taker. Review everything she gives you, LO, HW, AE, Practice Quizzes, Instapol, etc. Lots of test will be pulled from those, and also applying the knowledge you learn. There will be a few tricky questions, but overall Buskirk really cares for you and is so sweet.

I had Dr. Buskirk for BIO 311C and D (i'm a bio major). She is a great lecturer and cares about the success of her students. Go to lecture, do the instapolls, and study and success is possible. Grading scale is a little strict but very consistent. Test can be hard to get used to but all follow a similar format. Go to discussion and ask questions.

There is so much I could say about how amazing this course was! All I will say is take this course and treasure every second. This class extended my love for biology, the world, and being in college overall.
Dr. Buskirk is angel, and if I could have her every semester for the rest of my degree I would!

TEST ARE HEAVILY WEIGHTED. Utilize lectures online, lots of test questions come from things she says out loud. Use learning outcomes and AE/HW questions. Dr. Buskirk is very kind and obviously passionate about Biology. About to take my final, I have 100% on every section except for tests with 94.1 in the class. Need a 92 on the final to keep my A.

BUSKIRK IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! I love this woman more than anything! Such an interesting lecturer, work is doable, and she genuinely cares about student success and understanding! Her jokes are funny and tests are easy if you attend/review lecture content. Fair grader with limited out of class assignments. Favorite prof at UT!
sweet angel. So kind and caring and lovely. Reminds me of my mom. Passionate about the material and wants everyone to succeed :)

Dr. Buskirk is such a kind human being who loves teaching and cares so much for her students. She is so knowledgeable and a source of information about anything biology. You can come up to her to ask about anything and she will remember you and even remember to ask you about your personal life. Best biology teacher ever!

screwed the whole class over with the final-- "reviewed" stuff that would be on the final, only for her to test content she didnt go over/ said wouldn't be on final. It takes a special type of person to make a final significantly more difficult than the midtemrs exams, knowing students will lose their letter grades they're upkept all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a sweet lady and a nice professor. Really attentive about student feedback and enjoyed her field trips.
The best professor I ever had.

I love her so much she is so adorable but she kind of expected you to already be a bio nerd and I hadn't touched it since freshman hs. Exams were very very hard. Don't just memorize go inside of a cell or something learn every little detail.

I loved Dr Buskirk and she made her class very manageable. She teaches bio well and her tests consist largely of MCQ and some fill in the blank/short answers. She wants everyone to succeed and structures the class as so. Definitely take her if you can she makes life so much easier than other professors in the Bio department.

BEST PROF EVER! Such a sweet lady with a lot of care for her students and their success! Homeworks are super easy and clear and lectures are well organized and well explained. Exams are super easy if you review lectures and pay attention in class. Genuinely such an easy class if you put in the slightest effort.
Overall, Dr. Buskirk was a good professor. Her exams were a little hard, but as long as you do practice questions, focus on the learning outcomes, and GO TO class, you'll do fine in her class!
Overall, Dr. Buskirk was a good professor. Her exams were a little hard, but as long as you do practice questions, focus on the learning outcomes, and GO TO class, you'll do fine in her class.

I LOVE BUSKIRK SO MUCH!! if you want to do well in this class it's important to study, form a list of questions, and then go to her office hours. She genuinely wants you to succeed and find happiness in helping students do well. I formed a very positive relationship with her and I couldn't have asked for a better bio teacher.

Dr. Buskirk is such a sweet lady that truly cares about all of her students! Most lectures were well explained, but the tests do tend to go very in-depth so make sure to read the textbook and learning outcomes if you need help! She doesn't offer any extra credit, and the cutoff for an A is a 94, but tests are only 46%, which helps as a buffer!

Buskirk is an amazing lecturer if you have an interest in biology! Her tests are difficult because of the sheer amount of content, but if you start studying early (and I mean eaaarrllyy) you'll be fine! Wording on tests is tricky but if you know the base idea you'll figure it out. Lots of other activities to cushion your grade.

For her test, she gives u 80 learning outcomes & only puts 20 on the test so u study useless stuff, overwhelming u with info you don't even need (She used to highlight important ones & now she doesn't) They're formatted as 24 MCQ's 6 FRQ's in 50 min, doesn't give extra credit or curve & her cutoff is a 94. so if you didn't take Bio AP, good luck

Lectures were boring & her tests questions were worded weirdly & made to trick you. She's changed up so much this year, especially her final (which was EXTREMELY difficult). Doesn't believe in extra credit or curves, only thing that saved me was that her grading is 'cushioned' by other assignments. If you can, save your GPA & do partridge for 311C

Such a sweet individual, but DOES NOT give extra credit. I found tests to be challenging and hard to study for. The best tip I can give is study the lecture slides and LEARNING OUTCOMES over and over till you can regurgitate them. The tests are fair, but worded strangely which is why they are hard. Lectures can be boring, but overall a good class.

Such a sweet lady, but just wasn't my preferred teaching style. She would often say random things in class that "weren't on the exam" but would be. In her lecture slides, she would often write questions that were important but never answer them. The exams are pretty difficult and the questions asked are always worded very hard to understand.
My appreciation for baddie buskirk has gone up SOO much since i took genetics; i miss her lecture style and just her whole format of the class so much. truly one of the best professors at UT.
Dr. Buskirk was an amazing professor who provided me with an immense amount of insight into biology and science as a whole. Definitely take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class
