Holmes is such a sweet professor! He makes class so wholesome to be in, and he is super super understanding. The assignments are definitely on the fewer side, and he takes literally the last week of the semester to grade, so that can be annoying. There is a lot of group work, so be prepared.

Professor Holmes is my favorite business professor! He's caring, funny, and super supportive. His assignments aren't hard, but can be time-consuming. He shares amazing stories (and LOVES DIET COKE). If you need help, he's always there for you. His class is fun, engaging, and worth it—definitely TAKE HIM!
He is a super nice and funny guy that shares cool stories. The only thing is that he takes FOREVER to grade assignments.

Such a sweet and funny professor. BA324 is all about presentations but he gives the least amount of presentations compared to other profs. He does has 2 exams but they are EXTREMELY easy. He takes WAY too long to grade but helps students when they ask for it. He goes off topic most of the time and talks a lot but is so funny.

This is probably one of the easier BA324 classes. That being said, he doesn't grade assignments until the very last day, so you have no idea what your grade is. Most of the grade is based on group assignments so if you have a bad group, you're screwed. Professor Holmes is a really nice guy but the class was very disorganized and boring.

Still have not received a grade on any of my presentations and some of my assignments. Or the semester long capstone project. Never was clear on grading criteria and the TA was such a harsh grader for no reason. Easy tests though. Very frustrating to never know your grade for the entire semester. Sweet old guy, but does not have it together.

Super easy prof imo. I took 324H btw. If you start early on group projects, there is nothing hard about this class. Grading rubric is clear and the only thing that requires work is the final report (however could be harder if you have a bad team). Test are easy. Super nice guy as well.
His instructions are unclear and you will receive a bad grade for unreasonable things. I recommend taking other professors for this class. this brought my GPA down for silly reasons.
Not a big fan of this professor. Very slow to respond to emails and this often caused a lot of trouble. Would not recommend.

Listen to me guys, this professor right here, is the best professor in McCombs. Always regraded my assignment if I asked him to, ofc with a valid reason. But trust me, I don't see him disagreeing to anything I would request him to do. I failed in 2 quizzes, and he gave me more chances to work on them. Best classes and he's super nice. Go for him!

Loved Professor Holmes! He genuinely cares about his students & is passionate on the subject. Easy grader, the TA is annoying about grading but if you get stuff checked by her in advance you'll do well. Holmes' workload is also the lightest for BA 324 based on comparison with friends with other BA professors

Professor Holmes is a fun, relaxed professor who loves to lecture. Exams are easy after looking over the slides/notes. A few presentations that are not graded quickly so you do not have a gauge as to how you are doing in the class. However, it is a class to look forward to going too.

Professor Reed was a phenomenal lecturer. I can seriously say I wasn't ever bored at one of his lectures he made 400 year old book seem interesting. His class is homework heavy tho. Theres an assignment every week and multiple readings throughout out the week as well. His class is manageable as long as you stay on top of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He understands that students are busy and he makes the course structure forgiving. He repeats important concepts multiple times so you're familiar with them by the exam. If you go to class, do the assigned readings, and make an effort, the class is rewarding. He's friendly and passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Reed is a great teacher. He is extremely passionate about this subject. He is a very lenient grader, and he changed the syllabus several times, including take home exams, more allowed absences, extensions, and an opt-out option for the last exam to make it easier on students. I would take his course again, in a heartbeat.
This class is not worth it! There is more work than any of my other classes and lots of reading and writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's passionate about the material, making him a fantastic lecturer. You can miss three classes, so attendance is crucial. Goes over required reading in class which is extremely helpful. Majority of homework can be completed in class and he's very accessible for office hours. The exams are take-home. It's a pretty easy A if you don't half-ass it.

Dr.Reed is a PRO. I loved this UGS, and if you're worried about it being hard, don't be. He was an amazing lecturer, and as long as you pay attention in class you don't HAVE to read the book. It was a very interesting UGS that didn't feel like a throw away class, and I enjoyed the discussions. It is writing heavy tho, so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably one of my favorite classes I've taken at UT, just because the content is so interesting and rich. If you attend the lectures in person, you'll have a very smooth time; Prof. Reed gives great explanations of the poems and ballads read in class, and breaks it down into ways that are much easier to understand than what's seen at face value.

Professor Reed is very passionate about the course subject, and you can definitely tell through his lectures. The course consists of a term paper, two exams, and discussion sheets. You have around two months for the term paper, it is easy to get feedback. Office hours for both Reed and the TAs are very helpful. You need to put in work for an A.

Prof. Reed is incredibly passionate about Don Quixote and the course content, and is seen as a 'God' (TA's words) in the Don Quixote community. He is very willing to accommodate for his students but you have to be the one to reach out first. Do not be afraid to go into office hours and take notes for every lecture. Lots of work, but a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Reed is extremely passionate about his subject and is a fantastic lecturer. I originally registered for the class because of the flags, but I ended up falling in love with the course content. For anyone looking to take the class, please keep in mind that you need to take it seriously. This isn't an easy A, but it's so worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Be warned: if you are looking for an easy UGS to get some flags, you'd probably be better off with any other class. Otherwise, Prof. Reed is adept at what he does, and it is reflected in his teaching style. Lectures were informative and the information was highly relevant to tests, so take comprehensive notes in class and keep up with the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
For UGS 303, Road Movies and Quixotic Journeys, Prof. Reed is so passionate about the course content he appears to want us to just learn and apply the content more than purely grading us on our knowledge.

It's a lot of reading, but if you get into Don Quixote you'll find it as interesting as he does. He is very approachable and accommodates well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Reed was great. However, I only recommend you take this class if you actually enjoy reading and analyzing old literature. If you attend all the classes, take decent notes, and read all the stories/books in class you will 100% get an A.

As long as you take decent notes and pay attention, You'll be fine. Was very accommodating, and willing to offer assistance when I asked. The majority of your grade came from 2 exams, but there was plenty of extra in-class points to boost your grade if need be.

AMAZING. Prof Reed is an great lecturer and very helpful. Attendance is mandatory but you need it. He goes through question sheets in class and answers them for you so you have something for the exams. The discussion hws are basically answered in class and the tests are take home/open note. The material was so fun. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN, easy A.

I loved Dr. Reed's class. He was passionate and knowledgeable about what he taught. There was a lot of reading and writing, but he was very helpful during office hours. As long as I stayed on top of readings, the class wasn't too stressful and Iknow I became a much better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this UGS class. Professor Reed and the TAs are tough graders, but are passionate about what they teach. There are film worksheets, two tests, two exam. All of these assignments give you a ton of freedom in your writing. If you pay attention and take good notes, you will be fine. You will have to put in the work to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Reed was a great lecturer. You don't have to read if you pay attention in class. Attending class helps a lot. There were a lot of assignments for this class (weekly film worksheets, two essays, multiple mini assignments) but if you pay attention or reach out to the TAs, you can get them done. You will have to work hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is out of touch with what students need to understand his lectures. Does not come prepared to class, and does not utilize slides for student accessibility.

Professor Reed is one of the best professors I have had at UT so far. He has a really good teaching style of repeating concepts in a way that makes you remember them really well. He also is really knowledgeable and passionate about the material. If you like learning about history or the spread of culture from this time period, he is a great prof.

Professor Reed is honestly is one of the best teachers that I have had at UT. As a non-native speaker, his lectures were highly engaging and very easy to understand. He is more than willing to slow down or go back over things if you need it and is incredibly understanding of the fact that everyone is at different levels of proficiency.

I took Road Movies: Quixotic Journeys with Prof Reed. The grades were weekly film worksheets, a few papers, and 2 tests. The grading of the papers was vague- those are what brought my grade down. I didn't read the book, but if you pay attention in lecture and take good notes, you'll be fine. There are easier undergraduate courses available.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolute G. Took him for Spanish literature, and I think most bad reviews came from UGS. To see someone who is this smart about everything Spanish was inspiring. Literally, this man is one of the most knowledgeable professors on his course I've had at UT, but the best part is that he is also super approachable and willing to slow down and explain.

Professor Reed is a G. One of the best classes I've taken in college (and without a doubt the best of the six Spanish courses I completed). Highly recommend this class, especially for non-native speakers, as he is very patient and willing to slow down to make sure you understand.

A great class that really makes you work for it. While I didn't receive the grade that I ultimately desired, taking the course was, nonetheless, extremely beneficial to me as it improved my writing skills drastically. Prof Reed is great at what he does so his lectures are very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lost points on a paper for not properly using MLA citation. I COPIED AND PASTED the citation DIRECTLY FROM THE SOURCE. He is claiming that the MLA citation provided from the source itself is incorrect. I am so lost in this class. This UGS is the hardest class out of any that I am taking. Do NOT take this class if you want to maintain a 4.0 gpa.

I regret signing up for this class. I have more work in the class than all my other classes combined. Expect weekly writing assignments that take forever, endless amounts of reading, and tests that are way too lecture specific. I spent over 10 hours on our midterm and am constantly bogged down by the excessive writing assignments for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not take this class, worst decision of my life.

He'll make you work for a good grade, but if you just complete the readings and do the homework you're bound to get an A. He's enjoyable to work with, so brilliant, and really respects your academic abilities. Always available, he's very open and honest about giving and receiving feedback. If it wasn't my last year, I'd take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Although he was a tough grader on essays, he made his expectations clear and was very knowledgeable on the subject. He's literally a genius when it comes to this stuff so it was cool to just listen to him talk about it. Yeah you have to work for a good grade and read the assigned books, but totally worth it IMO.

Professor Coles gives very clear lectures. You learn all of your content through lectures, but there is a textbook if you want extra clarification. Assignments and tests were reasonable. I feel that I have a strong grasp of the content and never struggled unnecessarily.
My only complaint about him was that he moved fast during lectures. Everything else was fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very chill guy. however, lectures can be pretty monotonous and he teaches straight from the textbook. attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures but one quiz in discussion weekly which was pretty manageable. my advice is skip the lectures and learn from the textbook in your own time. tests are easier than hw and have a bonus question.

Since it was my first semester, I assumed all math professors were THIS good. I was wrong. I can now see how goated Professor Coles was. Make sure you take his class, he explains really well, gives relevant ONLINE homework, and gives extremely useful exam reviews. W Professor Coles

Amazing Calc Professor. Homework and quizzes are similar to tests. Tests aren't hard if you truly know the material. Lectures move fast but are insightful. He knows SO much about the field and is genuinely interested. 65% of grade based on tests. Quizzes in discussion. DO THE HOMEWORK! He really emphasizes it for good reason. Amazing professor!

As a math major, Desmond is literally my role model. Everything about him is AMAZING. His lecture are simple, yet inspiring. If you get a chance to take him (even if you aren't a STEM major), please do!!!!!!!!!

Tests are similar to the hw, albeit a little bit longer and more difficult. He was a great lecturer as well, and  even though I find calc 2 to be incredibly boring, he did an awesome job of teaching it. The multivar section was the highlight of the class, so if you're scared of calc 3, take him! He's great at explaining calc in 3D.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor during Fall '25. He really knows his subject and can teach it well. He answers questions thoughtfully and explains concepts thoroughly (how particular formulas are derived) so that we understand better. Gave useful homework problems, practice exams, straightforward quizzes/exams, and had a bonus question on exams. 10/10 prof.

Chill guy, good teacher. Hw typically takes anywhere between 0.5-3 hrs per week, don't procrastinate. Show up to lectures even if you took AP, b/c theres content not taught in AP thats taught here.(I'm not talking about multivariable). 65% of your grade comes from the exams. Feel free to ask questions, although he can ramble on a bit when answering

Desmond Coles is an excellent professor with lots of knowledge about his course. It's not absolutely necessary to read the textbook before the lecture, because he will explain EVERYTHING in the lecture. 
However, it is crucial to not skip classes. Also just a chill guy, he's always wearing hats.

TLDR: don't skip class, do half the homework before

Good lectures, though sometimes he can ramble on about something y'all don't need. One question quiz every Tuesday and homework due every Thursday (20-30 questions). Quizzes aren't too hard and help you stay on top of material. 3 exams and a final, mix of mcq and frq. They're not too hard if you actually study and practice. Would take him again!
DESMOND!!! He's a great prof, knows what he's talking about and easy to love. He assigns a good amount of homework and quizzes but he tests pretty easy. Would def recommend!!
Overall very good professor and not a very hard class as long as you show up to lectures
I love Professor Coles so much. The tests aren't too hard, and the workload is manageable. I'd definitely take another math class with him.

Great professor, super passionate abt what she teaches. Grade heavily depends on how you do on the exams (worth 60% of overall grade) and also what TA you get assigned. Def don't take if you want an easy blow-off UGS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved Dr. Coleman! She's very passionate and funny. This class is very interesting and in my opinion pretty chill. Class is TA heavy, and your grade depends heavily on your TA. Shout out to my TA Carlos Byrd! He was the best, and made me enjoy the class and subject more. Would 100% take again.

Professor is very familiar and passionate about the subject, which makes lessons interesting. The exams make up 60%, but most questions are common sense aside from some hyper-specific examples, which test reviews from professor and TA's mention. Not an extremely easy UGS and had to spend hours studying/doing homework. TA's grade the 6 essays hard.

Do not take this course if you want an easy UGS!!! Dr. Coleman was nice and cared about the subject and her students, but there was a lot of homework and you really have to work for an A. Depends very heavily on your TA. Lectures were boring at times, but overall an interesting course.

She's incredibly passionate, and her lectures are pretty interesting. The exams are unbelievably easy and require little to no studying, especially if you go to class, just read the cheat sheet they give you beforehand. The only thing is some TAs grade essays harsher than others, but as long as you do well on the exams, they don't really matter.

Dr. Coleman gives clear expectations and a weekly outline, and the class is easy if you read and pay attention since she gives the test answers in lecture. My TA gave great feedback and review sessions. Overall, a well-organized and enjoyable UGS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was really easy, most of your grade comes from 3 tests that were all super easy if you went to the discussion test reviews. There were also six one page papers throughout the semester, but were honestly all fun to write (also two got dropped so you only have to do 4). The lectures were probably fun if you are interested in pop culture
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate about what she teaches! Exams are worth 60% of overall grade. Pretty easy to study for as long as you read and follow through all of the material given. This class was definitely heavy on the workload for a UGS. Also, your grade may depend on the TA you are assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who is super passionate. Lectures were interesting and relevant! Had a great TA-sheila lawani who constantly encouraged us as first-year students. Did not read the book once and still got 90's on exams. There is weekly papers but they are very straightforward. Take this UGS!

Part III. It is a very commonsensical and easy class, but the tests are dependent on lectures and chapters. However, the 2 things this class has rewarded me is my TA, Sheila Lalwani, who gave tremendous personal and academic advice, and the growth of my critical thinking through the reflection papers.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Part II.  She has the ability to be both passionate and monotone simultaneously that it makes the class boring and a bit useless compared to countless UGS that could do some good to someone like me, who's already cultured and caught up on these topics.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Part I. First of all, I hated this class. As a pop culture enthusiast who was raised into this field and developed my identity though it, the curriculum satisfied me and accurately portrayed every single pop culture event which filled me with nostalgia but boredom. Professor Coleman is well-spoken but often stutters and loses her train of thought.

Coleman tries her best to set you up for success - she gives you all the materials you need to do well. Who your TA is matters alot - they are the ones giving you reviews before the tests and grading your discussion papers. There are definitely other better UGS courses than this one - don't make this your first choice.

Professor Coleman is really nice and lectures are really interesting! The class is quite difficult though. Getting good grades is pretty difficult on tests; I studied for almost 10 hours for the first one and received a B. There's a lot of content to memorize, but the content is interesting.

If you are an engineering major, please don't take this class. You will get burnt out from the amount of things you need to memorize for exams. 

But the professor is nice. It's just the class that's hard. I took UGS 303 POP CULTURE AND MEDIA.

DO NOT TAKE THIS UGS. I switched my UGS because I was interested in pop culture. However, this class was the most difficult class in my freshman year. The grade depended a lot on the TA. They held the review sessions for exams. MY TA WAS NOT HELPFUL AT ALL. She barely showed up to the discussion on time and deducted points if we were late.

Professor Coleman is great. Her lectures and screenings were interesting. Her tests are pretty easy if you study, all multiple choice. Your TA makes or breaks your grade though, hopefully you get a better TA than mine because she was a harsh grader and didn't know what to do during discussion labs so we basically just sat there.
lit! wish i studied more for first test. reviews are exactly like tests so do them! shes fun too. lots of energy.

NOT an easy "A". This course depends on your TA. Lab Paper were due every week, and tests came around quickly. The tests were so hard to get an A on, to even get a 100, you had to be in Coleman's head. Lectures were also unbelievably boring. No point in even going. Even though lab is mandatory. This course was a waste, seriously take another UGS.

This is NOT an "easy A" as it stole my 4.0 from me. You have to pray to God that you get the better of the TA's as they are the ones that make the study guide for you, grade your papers, and some are more willing to help out on test prep than others. First assg of the year "I know y'all were prob not expecting this, but the average grade was a 68."

I love this woman so much, she genuinely makes her class so interesting!! So many cool topics every class and keeps you engaged. There are 5 one-page papers to write and 3 exams; be careful with the exams because they can get tricky and weight a lot on your grade. Otherwise SUCH a cool class please take it

Professor Coleman is a great professor! She makes lectures fun and engaging so the material is pretty easy to learn. You can also join class on Zoom if in-person isn't really your thing. There are weekly one-page papers and attendance questions which are relatively simple as long as you're paying attention and writing your own opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly do not take this as an "easy A" UGS. Studying for the tests were a pain but if you put in enough effort you will be fine. Pray you get an amazing TA because they make their own study guides and some are far worse than others. Wording on tests was kind of confusing and the lectures alone aren't enough to do well on tests.

not gonna lie i went to like 5 classes. i had an awesome TA (the turkish one) that always gave study guides for the tests the day before. he usually gives this guide to other TAs as well. i would just study that before the test and do fine. just be sure to read the entire thing thoroughly. it is pretty exam heavy though

The lectures and course content is interesting and very relevant, however the tests are very hard to study for, but the group project was easy. There are weekly lab papers that don't have a clear rubric, and my TA was rough on grading at first but then got easier over time. Overall, not the worst UGS you could take, but not the easiest for sure.

don't take this as an easy UGS, no clear study guide, could do good on everything but if you dont get a 90+ on every test an A is impossible, doesn't drop any attendance if you get an attendance question wrong

Dr. Coleman has been an amazing instructor. Her lectures are fun and easy to follow, and the class itself is very interesting. At first, the structure of the one-page essays is slightly confusing, but you quickly adjust. Dr. Coleman usually let us out of class early, which is another thing I appreciated. Overall, is a nice and compassionate person

This class was easy. Just be sure to focus on the lectures and stay on top with attendence questions. Showing up to lab is sometimes mandatory but she will zoom record the lectures. I loved the lectures because pop culture is engaging to me. The lab papers get easier. I suggest taking this class if you want a fun and somewhat easy UGS.
Prof Coleman makes the class super easy to understand, all you really needed to do for studying was understand basic concepts and you were set. Genuinely such a sweet person!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Renita was easily one of my favorite professors. She is super captivating and always explains clearly what you need to know for the test. There are lecture/reading reflection papers due every week, but they are only one page double spaced and don't take long to do. Tests are easy if you study and read the book. Overall a great class and professor!

Excellent professor with very interesting lectures. Tests were generally straight from lectures and no final. Weekly one page papers which are easy to write but can be graded differently based on TA that you have. As long as you attend lectures, either in person or Zoom, you'll do well in the class. Definitely a fun UGS!

There are weekly papers, but they get easier as you progress. The content is very interesting, and Dr. Coleman replies to emails pretty quickly. However, in my opinion, this class was a bit too time-consuming for a UGS (granted I'm a STEM major), but it was doable. This course is definitely one of the more interesting UGS classes.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my favorite course of the semester. There were 6 one/two pagers we had to do but they get easy as time goes on. Dr. Coleman's lectures were my favorite. Overall, I enjoyed this class and would 11/10 recommend it.

Great pick for UGS. The weekly papers become easier the more you do them. The lecture content is very engaging and fun. Dr. Coleman is a journalist and that topic bleeds heavily into the lecture content (if that interests you) but there are also a lot of intersections with advertising among other areas. Take good notes to study for the exam.

Her lectures were very interesting, and I always liked going to her class. We had a paper due each week, but it was only one page and you had a lot of freedom over the topic. There are test questions about the textbook, but you could definitely pass the class without it. She also gave the option to watch the lectures on zoom.

I really enjoy Professor Coleman's class. There are a few essays, but they are only a page and easy to complete. She makes her lectures very interesting, and I enjoy coming to her class. The tests are also very easy and she gives you a study guide which also helps you succeed. I recommend this class for your UGS.

Her class is very organized, and all resources are posted on Canvas. Lectures were somewhat engaging, but they're also recorded in case you miss something in class. There is some reading, and almost every week you are required to write a 1 page response paper to talk about during lab. Class is not hard though if you utilize the resources for tests.
Renita is amazing, she's funny, the class is pretty easy, and I genuinely enjoyed going to her class every day

Renita was the absolute sweetest and you could tell that she genuinely cared about her students. The coursework was pretty light and very manageable. There were 3 tests, a group research paper, and weekly reflection papers. I would recommend taking this course as your UGS!

She is a great lecturer and I almost invested and interested in what she has to say. Such an interesting class. Weekly one-page papers but once you understand what they are expecting, super easy to complete. Soojeong is an awesome T.A!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was amazing! The prof really cares about her students and is very accommodating. There are very few assignments that are easy to do. I really enjoyed the lectures because she gave a lot of different points of views on things I had never really thought about. Def recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Prof Coleman!! She was so sweet and definitely cares a lot about her students. Your grade is based on 3 tests and weekly 1-page reflection papers, which are not difficult. Going to the lecture is not mandatory, you have up to a week to watch the lectures online and take a 1 question attendance quiz. I recommend taking this class!

I took Prof. Coleman's Pop Culture and the Media class last semester and thoroughly enjoyed it. She is such a kind and sweet person who cares tremendously about her students. She also has a ton of experience in the industry and knows what she is talking about. Going to Prof. Coleman's class always put a smile on my face!

Let me tell y'all, this is THE best class I've ever had. She the most awesome person ever and understanding as well. If you miss a lecture, you can always just watch the recorded lectures (she gives you a week to prove you've watched it for attendance purposes). You write a 1 pager every week, but they're straight forward & simple I promise.

Professor Coleman is a real gem of a professor. Her class is very interesting and she gives really entertaining lectures. There's lab papers every week but they're really easy. Textbook is required but is not relied on heavily, and the exams are easy if you touch base on the major concepts taught during lecture. TA was also really cool.

I took her for her UGS Popular Culture and Media course and I absolutely loved it! She is very knowledgable and her lectures are really fun and entertaining. She cares a lot about her students. This class was very easy and I would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very nice with entertaining lectures. There is a textbook used through the course but only to read a few chapters. I never read and did fine on the test. There is a lab paper due almost every week but its easy, quick, and graded fairly. Attendance is mandatory but she allows a few absences.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Clear grading criteria--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There's a textbook that we used more often in the beginning of the semester so there was more readings at first. You write a 1 page paper every week and after a couple you start to get the hang of it and do a little better on them. This was her first time teaching this class and so the exams in the beginning were harder & then the class got easier.

reviews.comment: Super easy class if you need a science credit as non-science major!

reviews.comment: Taking this class online was the best thing I can do. I can easily replay his lectures to fill out the given outlines and then do quizzes. Instapolls with every video but easy to complete. Extra credit lab is the best, boosted my grade by 5%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great! Took it online for summer science credit - very easy class, very organized, do the work and youre fine.
Great! Took it online over the summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: easiest class if you need to fulfill some credit and this is a class you can take i would def take it. all online, labs can be difficult but not horrible. gives opportunity for extra credit up to 5% added to final grade and syllabus was lenient with some due dates

I took this class my first semester at UT, easy A class, he is very kind and approachable, his lecture is fun and informative, a lot reading but assignments are graded based on completion, one group presentation and final paper

Covey is potentially one of the sweetest teachers at UT. Took this class solely for some needed flags and learned a lot about anthro. TA Blaire was unfortunately unhelpful and graded papers at the last second and harshly. A lot of assigned reading for Monte Carlo quizzes but most readings are short and you're able to use notes on them

I generally found this class to be extremely boring, if you're into ancient history and how humans domesticated animals and plants across the world, this class is for you (it sounds a lot more interesting than it is). There are weekly inQuizitive's which didn't help me at all. The labs did a lot of heavy lifting for my grade.

Covey is a kind professor and very knowledgeable about the topic. Although, he did go overtime every day. Tests are semi-difficult with MCQ & a writing portion. In the end, take a different culture class if you can...

I am so glad I took this class. I wish I took it in a regular semester because the summer session is only 1 month. There was a lot of reading and lectures but they were all so very interesting. The professor was passionate about this subject, patient, understanding, and always available for questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I highly recommend this course to non-science ppl to get your science credit! Cov wants you to do well, so if you study for the exams and show up to lab you can get an A. All exam material provided in lectures, and Cov provides bank of possible multpl choice and short answ questions on exam. He kind of rambles in lectures, but is a super sweet guy.

Professor Covey wants you to succeed in his class. He realizes there is a lot of information, therefore, gives many resources to help you secure an A if you're willing to put a little work in. Easy science credit!

I had Dr. Covey for two online classes in the fall and he was so flexible and understanding with his students. He is also one of the sweetest professors I've ever had! There was a good amount of homework every week, but he offers extra credit, good feedback on your writing, and a chance to make your voice heard in his small discussion groups.

Covey is a very respected archaeologist and professor. It is clear that he is very knowledgable about this subject. His lectures seem very long as he has a very monotone voice that can be easy to fall asleep to. His grading policy is a bit iffy, as he does not round up any of the final grades, but sets labs to a 95-grade (exceptional for a 100).

Covey is a great guy! He wants you to get an A and gives many opportunities to bring your grade up (open note quizzes). This class wasn't super interesting to me, but I do feel like I got something out of it.

I really liked his UGS! His lectures are kinda boring, but then he's really sweet and cares a lot about his students! This class is an easy A-I would just do the questions that he gave us w/ each reading(since the Monte Carlo quizzes are based on that, and you can access your notes). He WANTS you to get an A.

Dr. Covey is an excellent professor and is obviously very enthusiastic about Archaeology. His lectures are very engaging to someone interested in the subject but may be seen as dull by people who aren't that into archaeology and history. Tests aren't difficult if you go to lecture. Labs are a large part of your grade and are pretty fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Covey is a great, underappreciated professor. His class is interesting, but a little too dull for me as someone who isn't into science. This is a lecture heavy class, there is a book but I never used is and still managed. He gives a GREAT review making the exam easy as expected. This is a class with a lab, helping towards overall grade.

I had Dr. Covey for Cultures in Contact. Good professor, VERY knowledgeable on the topics at hand, and he'll very readily answer any extra questions you may have. But it's a flipped class. It's too easy to just skim through the outside work and zone out in class (attendance measured with Squarecap). Lectures not on test, homeworks only.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: This class is structured extremely strangely. He gives you ALL of the material to learn outside of class without talking about it much during his lectures. The material from the homework is on the exam, but he will not confirm or deny if you had the right answer to the question. You're pretty much on your own if you take this class. Unhelpful Prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class was quite boring, plus the professor was not very enthusiastic. Your quiz grade is reliant upon a dice roll everyday. The professor also does not tell you that on most your averages, you cannot get higher than a 95. This is typical of some professors, except for the fact that someone in this class got a 100. Not recommended at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It can be a really dry lecture for people not interested in archaeology. Grading could be more clearly explained throughout the class as a 2.5 out of 2.5 is a 95 instead of a 100. He does show clear knowledge of the material, but can come across as standoff-ish. As long as you take the quizzes seriously, it's not too difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class itself can be boring to those not interested in archaeology. He gives reading questions and then quizzes straight from them during class. If you do those reading questions, the class is relatively easy- just boring. The final (essays) is tough though becuase its very content and vocab heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There is a quiz every single day and it's a roll of the die whether or not it counts. These quizzes are the majority of your grade so you MUST go. The majority of this class you learn about domestication of different plants in different regions-so if that's your thing-then you'll love this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: there are 2 sets of reading questions a week from the txtbook and & a possible quiz, determined by rolling a die. u get to use the reading notes but the answers are rly hard to find in the text. no tests, just the quizzes, attendance, labs, & a final. the final is 5 one page essays for 5 questions out of the 15 that are given beforehand, that was:(

Professor Covey's lectures are interesting. I recommend focusing on the answers to the questions he puts on a slide at the beginning of each lecture, because they will later be test essay questions. Textbook reading is unnecessary if you can memorize the answers to the chapter quizzes, because the exact same questions are on the tests.

This class is pretty simple if you can dedicate time to read and do the quizzes each week. A background knowledge of world history helps as well. The lectures can be pretty dry, but he does post the slides right before class. Study groups are useful. Labs were kinda cool. Overall I enjoyed it a lot.

Professor Covey's class was not my favorite of the semester by any means. I found that, despite attending all lectures and studying for every test, I never made better than a 73 on a test. I usually make As. The reading is extensive and unhelpful, in my opinion. About halfway through the semester I stopped reading because it wasted my time.

The reviews for each test are about 35 pages of multiple choice that cover 11 chapters and he gives 18 essay questions however only 3 will be on the test. The TA's grade the essays super harshly too. The final is cumulative of  70 pages of multiple choice questions of all the quizzes taken online plus 18 essay but he only chooses 3 again. Lab30%.
Very disappointed in Dr Connolly. Final was graded unfairly, and didn't even explain what I did wrong after 3 months of asking. Otherwise, he is a nice individual. Exams are pretty easy

Difficult but caring professor. He is very sweet but I found it hard to take what I learnt in the lecture to an exam. I often had to look for other practice problems apart from his own to feel prepared. His extra credit is ~1 % added to your final grade (5 pts bonus for course evals) so dont be counting on it for anything.
He's very caring. Lectures were irrelevant, but attendance was mandatory...bummer. If you get stuck with an unproductive TA, then you won't learn much in this class. It's easy, just not meaningful.

Great and honest guy with lots of advice for incoming engineering students. Lectures and labs are completely different, where lectures are just general engineering student advice and content and labs are actually working on the semester project. TAs were most influential of grading because grades were based on lab work.
As long as you attend lectures and complete the group project, the class is an easy A.

A great professor who genuinely cares about students' success. He really takes the time to get to know students and is really trying to make sure we succeed, not only as engineers but as people and professionals. As a freshman taking the class, it is fantastic. However, as an upperclassman, it is somewhat repetitive and basic.
Dont take dynamics at UT with this guy. Take it online somewhere else

95 for an A. The 'curve' you get is 4-8 bonus points added to your lowest exam (which all weigh the same) meaning a 1-2% grade boost. Kind Professor, but avoid. Stopped uploading solutions to his work after a few weeks in. Never have felt so unprepared going into exams, which the worst is NOT dropped despite the 95+ for an A. Non-cumulative final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gonna have to watch external videos if this is your first exposure to Dynamics. All you do in class is scratch your head at problems he hardly gives solutions to. First few weeks he is active with posting his "in class examples" solutions on Canvas but as the semester progresses, good luck seeing anything. Not enough exam prep either. 95+ for A...
Knowledgeable and understanding.

Lectures were very boring to sit through, and the teaching style involved making the class do in-class exercises, which was much worse to follow than normal lectures in other classes. The cutoff for A is extremely high despite the entire grade being based on quizzes and tests.
Personally was not a fan of his lecture style - mostly in-class exercises; the exams seemed to expect us to connect a lot of concepts that we were never really given the guidance or *how* to connect.

Solidworks tutorials were easy but really busy work. Lectures taught you how to be a better engineer sort of. The class itself was kind of disorganized. Overall, fairly easy grading criteria and class if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class content is not hard, especially if you have a good physics background. Lectures are extremely boring, as the prof ends up spending most of class working through (and messing up) in-class exercises. 95 for an A is hefty, and the TAs were sometimes equally as lost as me. End of sem extra credit saved me as it gave +8 on lowest test

He is a solid professor. 80% of the class is SolidWorks tutorials that you do each week Lecture was mandatory, but boring as it was basically a seminar on how to be a successful college engineering student. Very easy to do well however.

His lecturing style is one of the worst out there. He does not explain things well & relies on his students learning from "in-class exercises." The TAs were also so unhelpful. Most questions were answered as "I don't know, to be honest." The exams were nothing like what we had during quizzes, and they were super late at 8-10 pm on Thursday nights.
Tests are ridiculously hard, averages on the tests were always 50 or 60. His lectures and discussion sections are basically useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are ridiculously hard. Class averages were always around 50 or 60. What he teaches in lectures are pretty much useless for labs and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great person and professor. The class is easy but you learn everything on your own through tutorials. The assignments are doable but the TA took points off for no reason. Lots of extra credit offered and teaches things beyond CAD.

The class was just tutorials which really wasn't too great but necessary to learn how to CAD because you can't really lecture over that. He cares about the students learning which is why he added short pre-lab assignments. I loved his lectures even though they weren't content heavy. Wish I had him for another class because he seemed great

TA ran the Lab, which was entirely SOLIDWORKS tutorials or projects. Pre-labs every week. You have plenty of time to work on assignments, but my TA wasn't very helpful and you only see the Prof. during lecture. Lectures were mandatory, but had nothing to do with the labs; mostly tips for college; was OK, but felt like time could be better spent.

Dr. Connolly is not good at teaching. His lectures consist of "in class exercises" where you needed to work out the problem before you know how to do it. I learned the most from the TA, which was the only saving grace. Exams are graded tough, and are late from 8-10 PM. Thankfully, i managed to pass but if you have the choice do not take this prof.

Dr. Connelly is a bad teacher, full stop. He is a super nice person, but has not ability to rephrase or explain concepts. He also has no time management - projects that were meant to take 2 hours took 4 or 5 because he did not work them out he didn't know how long to give us, and we were so behind we missed a full 3-week unit.

The lab isn't too bad. I had no experience with CAD, and pretty much the whole semester you will be doing SolidWorks tutorials. The tutorials can take some time, but if you get ahead it makes it a lot easier.  The labs are run by the TA's, and the actual lecture was him giving talks about professional development.

Had for both dynamics and SW class; TAs carry both, doesn't matter for SW class if you have him or not cause he's irrelevant to it. For dynamics lectures suck, midterms were 8-10pm, does have 1 extra credit thing but it relies on matlab. I didn't have a choice taking his class but I hope UT changes that. He is very nice though 🤷
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Connolly wastes lectures to talk about whatever he or the university feels is important that day, which is rarely relevant. The lab is where all the grades come from, and it's extremely easy. 4 hours are allocated allowing for you to finish all assigned work and still leave early. Boring, required, and easy about sums up the course.

If you have ADHD prepare to self teach. All he does for lecture is give in class exercises with minimal instruction, let us work on it, then explain the solution. Least engaging lecture I've ever had. Tests (2 mid 1 final) are 25% each, no curve, took over a month to return 1st midterm. +1 to the other recent reviews; don't trust the positive ones

He is a very laid-back professor. He consistently changed quizzes into ALE's (open note quizzes). The first exam was easy, but the next two were not so easy. Overall I think he's a great choice for dynamics just make sure to lock in since day 1. Homework is not graded but used for practice for the weekly quizzes. The crash assignment is trivial.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lecture is the prof's yap session. There is a SolidWorks assignment every week that can be finished in the 4-hour lab, sometimes less but sometimes longer. You're just following tutorials the whole time but it can get so tedious and time-consuming. My TA was chill af but I heard some others aren't.

He does not even teach during class!! Lecture is wasted doing problems with partners but they can't even be accomplished because he didn't even teach how to do the problems. Exams are super hard and he does not curve at all. The only way we were given grace was because the TA's fought for us.

Who gave this guy a job? Maybe if he laid off the Girl Scout cookies and focused on giving good lectures the class would actually be bearable. Lecture is a waste of time. Instead of him teaching the material, you spend half the time teaching yourself how to do practice problems during group work. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The SOLIDWORKS sections seemed a little bit like busy work, but my TA was always available and helpful if I had an issue. The lectures were thought-provoking and a nice break from harder classes. It was clear that Dr. Connolly and the TA's cared about what they were teaching and tried to prepare students for success in engineering.

Class is mostly a lecture about his life. Unfortunately, you can not go to him for clarification for the lab's Solidworks assignments. I honestly couldn't tell you who is in charge of this class. I am mostly convinced it is a TA in the shadows.

Beware of trolls rating this professor; he is not that great. For a Dynamics Physics course, a 95 and above is an A! (For reference, his test average was a 68, and no curve was given). In other words, it's extremely difficult to earn an A in the class. A 90 is a B+! He doesn't even teach well and will not post any notes (so you're on your own).

Took this fall of 21'. One of the easiest gen-engineering classes there is. Dr. Connolly goes through material very slowly and thoroughly. The only crappy part is that the discussion section is mandatory, but I don't know if that's different with any other profs. Overall you cannot go wrong with Dr. Connolly. I remember this class fondly.

the lecture is 1 hour a week and very easy, it requires not work but attendance is required; the lab session is a 4 hour class one time a week where you go over the week's work using solidworks; it is easy to get a head of the work and also easy to fall behind on the work; use youtube to help

Lectures themselves were just professional development and at times pointless for me. Assignments are time consuming especially if you have no SOLIDWORKS experience, but pace yourself & you'll be fine. We had lots of changes to the syllabus but if you monitor Canvas it's all doable. My TA was also very approachable and helpful.

Dr. Connolly changed the syllabus so that lectures were about professional development instead of engineering topics. For this class, that was okay, since the content was self explanatory and my TA was very good, but lectures felt irrelevant and boring. Had attendance been optional, I wouldn't have gone. With a good TA, this class is super easy.

The most challenging aspect of this course was forcing myself to show up to class for the attendance grades. The lab sections were completely worthless, especially when the TA shows up ten minutes late then dismisses us after five minutes of ranting. He also reworked the entire syllabus halfway through the year to include worthless career advising.

Dr. Connolly is a great guy and I'm looking forward to having him in dynamics. Only problem I had with this class was the fact that solidworks tutorials felt like busy work. He changed the structure of the course because other students felt this way but he didn't change the syllabus to account for it. Disorganized but a useful and fun course.
Super chill dude and a very straightforward class. Just give yourself plenty of time to do the SolidWorks tutorials.

lectures were for engineering readiness, recitation was actual learning for future engineering classes. solidworks was a pain but TAs were helpful. class was a bit disorganized; a is easy to get but you will actually have to try in the assignments

Dr. Connolly is a sweet guy and really understanding. His engineering readiness stuff was cool but wasn't super useful aside from just awareness. The Solidworks aspect was okay, just too much work for what the class is worth. Extremely heavy assignments with not enough time and just felt useless in actual content to talk about. Overall, not great.

Connolly's lectures are about student resources/advice, and his projects are simple and very easy. The majority of homework is through SW (SolidWorks) during recitation with the TA. With SW, tiny details can delay your progress, and Dr. Connolly doesn't know SW very well, so take advantage of time with your TA. I had to ask TA for help very often.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
He often just... messes up problems. Makes lectures somewhat confusing.
Requires his $100 online textbook that provides no real value assides from a few concept quizzes, around 20 pages of content in the book total.

Professor Connolly is a super nice and chill guy. His class was pretty easy, the lecture sections are completely different from the lab sections. Lectures IMO were a little boring but really easy. The lab sections involve actual engineering projects and are taught by the TAs, so that can depend on your TA but were not too hard.

Material is pretty simple and his lectures cover it well. Textbook situation is weird, he draws heavily from a different textbook than the one you are required to purchase so watch that. Very nice person but lectures can be slow. Gave us a few breaks on grading throughout the semester.

He seems to be a very nice guy and he is a great professor. Anyway, I like lecture because he would let us struggle with practice problems but then explained the concept, he never finished a problem, tho. He would post the solution after class. He can be slow and the grading criteria was not clear enough imo

Pretty difficult class. Our class average on the last exam was in the high 60's and the class is fully comprised of engineering students. Don't skip class or recitations and you'll do alright. A is set at a 95 and is pretty much unattainable given the TA's grading but a high B is certainly manageable with a lot of work (1.5 hours a day).

Nice guy, cares about student success and understanding of dynamics. Can be unprofessional at times; lots of mistakes in exams and homework. Very unlikely you get an A, but a decent grade is easily attainable. Most frustrating aspect is you have to purchase his textbook, which is a 90 dollar 10 page pdf file.

Dr. Connolly is a very nice guy who does care about his students. However, dynamics itself is a very difficult subject that requires a LOT of time commitment. The material takes a lot of time and effort to understand. Exams can be extremely difficult. Don't expect an an A in the class, but if you're looking to learn, this is a good class to take.

Dr. Connolly has a great teaching philosophy. He is always open for questions and is willing to help anyone. There are weekly quizzes is discussion section and three tests and a final. Sometimes he makes the tests too hard but he will curve.

He's good professor who wants his students to learn. Although the course did become slightly more difficult as time went on, he was always ready to answer any questions you had. The grade scale was a bit high but the course was relatively easy and didn't require too much effort if you knew what you were doing. His tests are more application based.

Really cares about his students. Lectures are clear and he makes you work out problems. The first two tests were not terrible but the third test and the final were difficult. However, he'll curve the grades. Overall he's a great professor for dynamics.

Every lecture he has a clear example of what you just learned. The grading was easy for the tests. He gave us a great test review with plenty of examples and solutions, if you knew how to do them you were fine for the test. very fair

Professor Tuttle is my favorite professor at UT. he is so caring about his students and its clear his passion for SQL. The one thing that really stood out is genuinely his ability to make a difficult subject so easy and clear for students. I thought learning SQL would be super tough especially having no background knowledge but he made it so easy

Tuttle cares about teaching and talks about his own experiences here and there. Class is not open note anymore. Course is also very content heavy and the semester I took it, it felt disorganized so that combination together didn't mix well. Textbook mandatory. Labs are meant to be helpful but felt like busy work. He's passionate for sure tho!
Take Professor Tuttle.

Best professor I've had at UT. Has the privilege to learn from him as a student and support him as a TA. Truly changed my understanding of data and how its become the new gold for businesses. If you have the chance please take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fun and cool professor, but the classes are flipped style so you have to be ready to read and prepare before class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Tuttle makes a dry topic engaging. Lectures are clear, and he cares about student success. Open-note exams and Unstuck ai make studying a breeze.

Class requires pre class reading. Good amount of HW and studying required but def doable. I would rate difficulty a 3.5/5. He really is a great and caring prof tho. Test are online and remote but very fast paced so you have to move quickly. Take it with him if you actually want to learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Incredible class and prof. You can tell he's put a lot of thought into the structure of the class - it's clear and reasonable. Lectures are engaging and effective. Non-mandatory attendance (except quiz days) was a lifesaver. Very receptive to questions/participation. Exams are open internet so it's an easy A if you get the work done.

Literally the GOAT. I've never learned more in a class in my life or been set up for my future. This class has directly been responsible for helping me land an internship. Professor Tuttle is the most caring professor who will help you in your grades BUT REALLY focus on helping you succeed in LIFE.
tuttle is a genuine and good guy who wants to help you succeed and provides the necessary resources to do so. however, grading can be arbitrary at times depending on your TA
great class, tuttle is a genuine and good guy who wants to help you succeed and provides the necessary resources to do so.

Professor Tuttle is the best professor I have had. He genuinely cares for his students and wants everyone to gain a deep level of understanding. His wit makes classes enjoyable. He allows for lots of practice time in class while he assists those who need help. Reading the textbook before makes the material easier to grasp. Open note exams.

Great guy! Made learning about databases interesting and explained concepts really well. Tests are open note and were not too difficult if you were familiar with the course content. Homework was tough but not impossible. Middle part of the course requires effort outside of class by reading the textbook and watching videos before in class practice.

This course could be renamed "Corporate Bloat" 374. Agile certainly has its place in software development, but this course prioritizes work unrelated to it. A friend of mine said only 20% of their work for the ending project was directly for the client. This should be flipped, but Clint would rather sacrifice quality software for micromanagement

Professor Tuttle is extremely knowledgeable over the subject and offers a lot of insight, even about things not directly tied to class. The class guidelines are rigid, but he cares and will offer as much help as he can for mostly everything.
He is really funny and makes his lectures fun and engaging. The homework assignments are kind of hard but the tests and quizzes are a lot easier.

Don't get the Tuttle hype. Heard great things about him, but I found him to be extremely condescending. He always praised asking questions, but would oftentimes respond in a snarky/rude manner. Pulled through at the end with a curve though, so grade-wise it's chill. Found the "reverse-lecture" format annoying since you have to teach yourself.

I honestly dont know what the point of the prof is if it's just going to be self taught. You learn from the readings that u have to do before class. He barely lectures in class and has u just do in class practice. He never gives enough time for the quizzes and it rude in office hours. On the test he barely gives u enough time to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class has an insane amount of information that you are expected to keep track of in a canvas page that is very oversaturated and the professor is not the most understanding about mistakes that are made or things that are done non traditionally. The grading is mostly done by the TA's and is fine.

This class is pretty much self taught. you have to read and learn from the book because his class is just practice problems and the amount of pre class assignment he gives out is insane. He also gives you quizzes where he doesn't even give you the time he promise he would give. His instructions are also very confusing on HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He will preach that he's a "helper" type enneagram but ask him for help and be prepared to be met with the most passive aggressive comment. He will also make a lot of jokes about how much work he does to prepare for the class and interview potential clients, and yet his lectures have been reused possibly since his first year teaching the course.

Tuttle has got to be one of my favorite professors at UT. The class was hard and required a lot of effort from the student, but Tuttle makes his expectations clear in order to succeed. His philosophy for teaching really matched my personal learning style but I can see how that might not apply to all students. He makes being an MIS major fun!

Reverse classroom format. Read textbook before class. Exams are open note. Make sure to review slides, demos, and homeworks for in-class quizzes + exams. Attend office hours. Overall, Clint is a wonderful professor and he cares about you. His textbook readings and demos are REALLY helpful for homeworks. He sang for us on the last day of class.

Although it was a hard class for me, he does an amazing job breaking down what you have to do in order to succeed. Make sure you get ready to read and participate in class. Gives amazing feedback. Exams are slightly tricky with wording, read the textbook and you'll be good.

Clint is okay, but he's very overrated. Homework instructions, installation directions, and test questions are very confusing because he doesn't use punctuation when he types. He can also be a little bit stubborn when "answering" questions. The SQL part of the class is good, but the rest is a bit of a drag. The last day lecture is very inspiring.

The textbook was really relevant and easy to understand. The material gradually grew in difficulty, but skills grew quicker. He's really involved and in-class practices are helpful but rarely graded. 

The class is easier with a buddy to discuss things with, but 10/10 would recommend.
One of the best professors at UT. Period. Class is not hard and he makes learning interesting. Go to the Huddle with Tuttles!

I am not a fan of coding, but he made it more manageable. There is a lot of reading/homework, so be prepared for that. the quizzes are pretty difficult imo bc they ask very specific questions. the exams aren't too bad bc they are open note. tuttle is very accessible outside of class and truly wants his students to succeed in his class and onwards!!
Tuttles class is interesting but he does get easily irritated so be extra prepared before class and only ask thought out questions. Overall would take this class again because it is so organized!

Listen this man is clearly passionate about databases and I really appreciate that. But never in my life have I had to spend so much time outside of class just to learn the material. Recorded 45 min lecture + textbook + lecture in class + lab + weekly homework that takes hours on end. If you have that kind of time great, if you don’t- be warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tuttle was just awesome, he made learning about databases fun and engaging and the in-class activities and labs are extremely helpful for doing the homeworks. His tests are not bad if you have a general overview of the material and do the homeworks as thats where the material actually starts to make sense. Overall, great class!

I had professor Tuttle as a professor two years ago and all I can say is, absolute king. Hes very engaged and cares about the success of his students with out regards to their career choices. Hes knowledgable and someone who encourages you to think and do better

Tuttle is my favorite professor after this semester. Test questions are sometimes tricky, but nothing that they don't go over in the reading. Class mostly consisted of independent reading, going to class for him to answer questions, and doing a coding lab with a group. He made the class fun. Read everything before class and do all labs to get an A

He's an awesome professor. Doesn't take the course too seriously and basically wants you to learn. He is funny too and will randomly bring up stories of his past and will bust out his guitar and start singing on the last day of class so make sure to attend. His Excel game is off the charts btw, I really recommend taking notes.

I took MIS302F over the summer and it was super chill. He released all the modules at the beginning of the session and finish the course in 3 weeks if you wanted. Wasn't too difficult, most of the time as long as you paid attention to his videos you can do great on the quizzes. Final wasn't hard either, started studying a day before and got an A.

Databases with Tuttle was great. He was very conscious of how students felt in his class and really did everything he could to make sure we were comfortable. A lot of hands on during class, so watch the pre-class recordings and at least glance at the book before you go. Overall great choice for MIS 325.

Take Clint for Databases! I took him online for Fall 2020 (COVID) and loved it. Attend office hours to get to know him, he's so cool and friendly. Homeworks aren't too bad, use the book, tests are open note, content is easy to grasp, but don't fall behind or you will be lost! Class is less lecture and more hands on, so you really learn a lot.

I really didn't like this class, but that's not on Tuttle. I enjoyed his enthusiasm, but I did find his lectures quite draining. I struggled with his tests/quizzes for sure. His slides are super helpful, and you won't pass without paying attention to his lectures.

I was so glad to have gotten off the waitlist for Tuttle's class. Definitely worth it. If I had any doubts about switching to an MIS major, this class diminished them all. Tuttle is super passionate and it is so obvious. It's amazing to learn from someone like him. Definitely a class that requires you to put in the work, but you will learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor! Make sure to do all the readings before class so you understand the lectures. This class is highly dependent on what group your in so make sure you know people in the class so you can have a good group. His grading is tough and will leave you frustrated since it is very tedious, but he is fair with final grades.

Honestly, I had to learn most of the material on my own outside of class. The class setup was that we would read the textbook and then come to class where we would ask 5 mins of questions and then do "in-class practice"... on material that he hadn't actually taught to us yet. If you want to learn anything at all in this class, read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clint is an amazing professor. When he isn't singing songs about Excel, you can find him in his office helping students with their course work or talking about life. He spends a lot of time preparing his course and truly cares about his students success.

This course was overall not to bad, but you do have to put in the work if you want an A. The final exam was worth 40% of the grade so even if you get 100s on everything the final can tank your grade and the required grade for an A was a 94. The writing assignments and excels werent too hard, and tuttle and the TA give feedback if messaged.

Good guy but it was his first semester teaching MIS325 and it showed. Class was kind of unorganized but TAs are helpful. He does random pop quizzes so try to go to class. I generally did better on homeworks than exams and quizzes just because homeworks use SQL while you code by hand on exams and quizzes.
Very passionate about MIS. Might get a little irritated in class but overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took his first semester teaching MIS 325, and it was not good. He is one of those professors who thinks his class is the only class you take. No organization to the class whatsoever. Unreasonable when it comes to grading. Exams, quizzes and homework are difficult and will take you a lot of time.

Tuttle is fantastic. I highly recommend for everyone to take at least one course taught by him because he is inspiring, always there for the students, and pushes knowledge over grades. Hard work pays off. I learned a lot about what I wanted to do as a career from him! SAM hw are simple, read the txtbk, & always go to class. Tests are tricky!

Prof. Tuttle gives great lectures. His online class is not hard at all except for the final. 60% of the grades are weekly assignments and the other 40% is the final exam. Questions in the final are all new questions, so you need to review everything not only just old quiz questions. He gives two extra credits and curves the entire class in the end.

Amazing professor who truly cares about his students. He's always trying to give extra help on Excel assignments and the assignments were either graded by a computer system (with 3 attempts allowed) or peer reviewed. He also gives chances to argue your grade on the peer reviews. Test material was not word for word from class, so studying will help.

HIGHLY recommend taking this class online. You have 2 assignments (usually a quiz and an excel or a paper and a n interactive quiz) due every sunday, but that is it. There is also a final at the end. Took up basically none of my time and I did not mind it at all. For sure the best way to take MIS

It was a pretty straightforward class. A few assignments due every week that make up about 60% of your grade and one big proctured final at the end that makes up the other 40%. Contrary to other reveiws, the final was not old quiz questions so make sure you do go back and review the chapters before you take it.
Tuttle is a great teacher. Took his class even though I didn't need it. Was worth it. Not a difficult class.

I've had the honor of taking some fantastics professors at UT, but Tuttle is hands down the best one BY FAR. He's very inspirational and clearly cares about his students. Although this class requires a lot of work, I would one million percent recommend it.

Professor Tuttle is the best professor I've ever had at UT and one of the greatest people I've had the chance to meet. I think that he is one of the nicest and down to Earth person and is very passionate about what he teaches. The class is also very informative but he makes it very understandable in lectures and notes. Loved every minute of MIS302F

Incredible prof! Tests are super challenging if you don't fully understand the material so utilize office hours. Would sometimes do in-class surveys so basically pop-quiz for attendance. Tons of hw thru excel spreadsheets so if you aren't familiar with it you have to learn how to work it. Everything in his class can be applied in the real world!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tuttles online MIS 302F class is one of the easiest As at UT. The class is pretty straightforward, though it does require time, but not a lot.

Clint is a good person, motivational coach and mentor, but not necessarily the best lecturer. His lectures are unclear most days, and he wasn't able to build a clear lecture style at all during the semester. He knows what he's talking about in terms of MIS content, but he isn't great at communicating it at a easy-to-understand level.

Overall, the online class was pretty straightforward. It was clearly outlined and had all of the information available. Requires a little bit of reading, but not anywhere close to the average amount of reading in other classes. Lecture videos really help more than the extra readings. Study with friends and definitely do the extra credit!

Professor Tuttle was one of the best professors whether or not you do business his class is very interesting and the projects quiz and discussions are doable. The final is easy if you did well on the quizzes and studied the questions. The class is taken for those trying to get a business certificate but I would recommend it anyone overall.

MIS 302F was such an awesome and informative class! Tuttle is an amazing professor and explains everything very well during lecture and makes sure that we fully understand everything. Textboom is online and you just have simple readings. However, Tests are pretty tricky and hard but study guides are provided! DEFINITELY WOULD TAKE AGAIN!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pretty doable overall. The class is super interesting. Quizzes at the end of each unit that are open note. No midterms. ProctorU final is all old quiz questions.

Clint Tuttle is one of the greatest professors I have had so far at UT. His lectures are clear and helpful. The material is useful for your future as a business professional, and if you pay attention you will come away with tons of interesting IT information. Be prepared though, the material is very dense. Take time and understand every concept
Clint is one of the best professors I had at UT he taught me way more beyond class material. He is truly interested in helping students.

Answers to unit quizzes are online, only pain is the interactive quizzes. Excel assignments get harder, but if you spend time on them, you'll eventually figure it out. Self paced class, so it's easy to get ahead and vice versa. Don't bother watching the videos and reading the articles tbh. Final is recycled quiz questions.
Super cool professor, seems to really enjoy his job.
Outstanding professor, large work load though just a heads up!

One of the best teachers I've had at UT. Lots of components such as quizzes, assignments, group projects, participation surveys and tests. If you stay on top of everything it's pretty easy to get an A but also requires you to not procrastinate due to assignments every week. EC opps at the end of the semester. You'll learn so much in this class.
So entertaining. Best teacher ever.
You will do alot of work, but I have learned alot. It is worth it.
Dr. Turtle is a STRONG atheist and he lets you know it. not a day went by when .he didnt let you know that he had not gone to church. where has our countries moral compass gone. Not with this man

Professor Tuttle is great, and the online modules were very thorough. Though many people have recommended that you work with others, I found it completely manageable to do on my own. Work load is as expected, and as long as you put some effort into it, you'll do just fine and will likely learn a great deal.

AMAZING  AMAZING AMAZING.

Guys, y'all have to take MIS302F with Prof. Tuttle. First of all, he is an AMAZING lecturer. This wasn't even a class for my major or minor, but it's been the best class I've taken at UT. So many useful skills that we learn and he does a great job teaching them in a fun way.

You could tell straight off the bat that Tuttle cared about his students and cared about the information. He cares more about learning than the grading & most importantly... He preaches "everything is going to be ok"
