By far my favorite professor at UT. I would hands down recommend him to any student who wants to sit in an awesome lecture and learn useful skills for the future. Let's just say my boss is happy that I know excel :) Thanks to Tuttle that is!!! Clint is an outstanding professor! He's really hilarious and just an all around cool guy. Clint Tuttle is a UT LEGEND!!! This guy is freaking awesome and if you don't take him, you're missing out on one of the best classes UT has to offer. Tuttle is an awesome and funny guy. He is there for his students!! Take him! If you're having trouble understanding the material, ask in office hours. He's really helpful! EXCEL HELL. Tries really hard to be cool in person then DUMPS you a metric ton of homework. Does a guitar performance in the very end. Have you ever watched a Kia or Hyundai commercial and think to yourself "Oh Wow amazing car!" Then after owning it for a few weeks realize a few things? Let me save you some time. Really, would not take again.
Hands down the best teacher i have ever had. 12/10 would reccomend. You will actually WANT to go to class!

One of my favorite professors ever. Really, the assignments are lengthy but they are not hard. He gives detailed instructions for EVERYTHING. Great lectures. Easy quizzes. Easy group grades in class. Brilliant Entertaining lectures. Horrible, infuriating assignments. 5-mile treadmill-boring articles.

Would not take again. Get ready to devote huge part of your night extremely long, boring articles. HTML was infuriating and Excel assignments are pull-out your hair horrific. Entertaining lectures but the class does a 180 turn on assignments. Will drop you off a cliff on assignments - you have been warned.

Took his online class but wished I took it in person. He's a really nice professor with clear criteria. Excel heavy- but for BFP students, Excel is a pretty useful skill to have. Easy to make an A but a good amount of work (none of it too hard, though).

Great professor, I actually went to every single one of his classes, even though they weren't mandatory. His test are alright, they're easy as long as you keep up with the readings. He sings for you at the end of the semester, and he's hot af.

Tuttle is awesome. The class is not hard but you must participate. The tests are easy if you study his ppts. Its the HW that is more time consuming (SAM excel assignments). He is very inspirational and teaches life concepts along w his course material. Very fun and a really interesting lecturer.

I hesitate to recommend this professor. Take another electives class. The reviews were too good to be true. Way too much reading like 30 page assignments. wtf. Excel was a nightmare. HTML wanted me to pull my hair out. Not what I was expecting at all.
Class is not mandatory, but you will want to go! I learned so much about top dog businesses and HTML coding. And you really dive into excel, which is a must to know these days! amazing class!

This class is really interesting and the stuff you learn in here will be very beneficial for your career.  Not too difficult to get an A or A-, but there is a lot of work you will have to do. TUTTLE ROCKS. If you put in the work, you'll make an A. I learned so much in this class that will make me competitive when I am trying to get a job, highly recommend this class for anyone and everyone.
Clint is fantastic, but this is actually a class that you need to be on top of- mainly B's on tests (averages of classes).
Amazing professor! His last lecture of the semester is the best one! Really inspirational

He's a good professor who cares about helping students. However, there is soooo much unnecessary work. Way to many readings and so many assignments. Also there's group work so be prepared. Tuttle is one of those professors you'll still remember when you're 50 years old. He's just hilarious and smart and really, truly cares about his students. Tuttle's class was better than I thought it would be. The topic is not the most interesting, but I feel like he did a good job making it as fun as possible. So many assignments about Excel; that was the worst part.
Basically only came to this class every time because Clint if hot af and he is also hilarious. Super worth it

Class is fairly easy, and Tuttle is a nice guy and tries to keep class interesting. I didn't really find excel or HTML assignments useful.
awesome dude. really will do everything to help his students understand, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND GOING TO OFFICE HOURS. fun class, extremely interesting and useful just for life
Great Prof! He is dedicated to all of his students and keeps you entertained! I'm about to finish this course and am sad to leave it. I love how encouraging he was to all of his students!

Great professor. Entertaining, smart, connected, and loves to teach. Go to class and take good notes, and go to office hours for help on assignments. This guy is dedicated to teaching this class and really wants students to do well. Great introduction to business technology and a motivational teacher. Would definitely recommend this class.

absurdly overhyped. Lectures are easy (just sit there). During lectures... it's best to let him talk.. trust me. Do not comment or be noticed. Excel HW sucks so bad. Such a good professor. He's interesting and he's funny without even trying to be. Before every test he has his class do Texas Fight. Best Professor I've had at UT so far. Presented the information in an interesting way and made me want to learn it. (I even considered switching majors.) Tuttle is awesome. He's a younger guy and you can tell he loves what he does. His tests aren't too bad, but there are some tricky questions. Homeworks are easy (since you get five attempts at them) and the readings are simple. TAKE THIS CLASS! You'll learn more than just business-stuff from Tuttle.
Great professor. He's fun, interesting, and seems to really be there because he wants to. Highly recommend any course that he teaches!
By far the best professor. His lectures are interesting and engaging. Don't miss out in a great professor, highly recommend this class!

Professor Tuttle won the 2012 Texas Exes Teaching Award (nominated by students) AND it's only his FIRST year teaching. That pretty much says it all. Go to class & you'll definitely learn and laugh. Clint really cares about you learning the material & he makes class entertaining.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. He makes class really enjoyable so you want to attend lecture. Read the book + look over the power points = A. Earning an A isn't super easy, but it's definitely manageable with Clint.
Aww I'm gonna miss this class :( I recommend taking it cuz the instructor is AMAZING! He is very helpful, and did I mention awesome!? Take it! I highly recommend it. He is the man!

CLINT TUTTLE WAS AMAZINGGG! Keeps class fresh and fun. Homework is consistent but not overwhelming. Fair amount of reading. Reviews help focus notes for test. Highly recommend going to his classes. Great class and instructor. The lectures are interesting because they are based on actual companies.
Great class! The lectures are interesting as the examples the instructor uses are already occurring in the real world. Take this class, I highly recommend it.
The man.com

Funny interesting Lectures; if you read the chapters and read the powerpoints he uses in class i'm sure you'll get an A. Its easy to follow along in class because the examples he uses is stuff we know, like facebook, netflix. take it!
Funny guy, just seems to get off topic most of the time during lecture as he rambles on about his personal life like we care. But overall he provides good examples of the material.
Fun lectures.

Great guy, great teacher. Keeps his class of 300+ interested and involved in his lectures. Gets really good discussion out of his class and is always willing to talk. Reads all his emails and students constantly email him information relative to the class. Take it, it is fun.

DONT take if u have another option. kirkpatrick was ok but exams r niche + only 1 exam was curved. linders section is frustrating bc lectures are awk, quizzes are strict, & the exam curve only helped low scores more & did nothing for higher scores. disc grading is bs since participation doesn't seem to count unless u directly answered a question
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DONT take if u have another option. kirkpatrick was ok but exams r niche + only 1 exam was curved. linders section is frustrating bc lectures are awk, quizzes are strict, & the exam curve only helped lower scores more & did nothing for higher scores. disc grading is bs since participation doesn't seem to count unless u directly answered a question
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader but willing to round up my grade that's off by 0.003 to an A. His exams are quite hefty and it is so important to keep up in his class by being readily prepared with lectures he post afterwards. Love that he rounded my grade up so I have to give him a 5, but prolly won't take him again 😭

Don't listen to the ratings on here. Just go to class and actually pay attention. I recommend rewatching the lectures and paying attention to the examples. The learning objectives are super helpful and the exams are basically written from them. It is a lot but things make sense if you actually try to understand. He is super nice and I LOVED him.

Was scared bc of reviews but I've learned a lot. Super lecture heavy - its easy to see the pattern of his tests. He often asks questions about the examples he puts on the slides. My grades so far Exam 1: 82 raw, 87 curved. Exam 2: raw + curved 89. He's nice + I think the people that complain don't actually come to class. Disc attendance mandatory.

Professor Linder's lectures are very boring, his slides are all words and advanced evolutionary terms that he does not define. His exams are all free response and he grades answers harshly without providing explanations. On top of all that, he never responds to his emails. He changed the final the week before and didn't respond to anyone's emails.

MANY advised against him, but he really isn't bad. To be honest, I dont think I've ever learned more, (objectives are key for exam), but still his grading is hard. Exams: 1: 83, 2: 84, 3: 81, 4: 84. So in all you can get an A- with 80s, just do every homework (not that many), do every journal entry (easy points), quiz average was about 13/15.

Incredibly strict grading on FRQ only tests. Lectures were fine but exams genuinely felt unfair at times as credit is often awarded very arbitrarily and the TAs are prone to making mistakes when grading so get ready to request regrades

Grading scheme on exams felt genuinely malicious. No mercy for getting it mostly right. I felt like I fully understood everything from the lectures inside and out and I barelyy scraped an A, mostly due to having Kirkpatrick first half. No A- or B+. One thing I liked was all lectures are recorded and you don't miss info if you miss class.

Extremely unaccommodating. Missed one of the quizzes due to a medical emergency, which I had multiple doctor's notes and billing receipts from. Linder refused to let me take the quiz 1 day late, so I received a 0. Exam questions are graded on a specific phrases that the questions do not prompt. Does not want his students to succeed.

He's a nice guy and I feel bad writing a bad review for him. His grading on exams and quizzes is insanely strict and points will be taken off for no good reason. The quizzes are difficult and are meant to trip you up. Overall, the class is almost entirely graded by quizzes and tests. I was genuinely so relieved to get at least a B...

Linder's half was more challenging than I expected. The all-frq exams expect very specific answers, so receiving full credit for a question is difficult (but you can get partial credit). The weekly quizzes were also tricky. I had to watch each lecture 2-3 times before each exam in order to understand what I needed to. This class was a lot of work.
If he were a Jolly Rancher, he would be the grape flavor

Dr. Linder is an average lecturer, nothing special there. My big grievance is the questions he writes, particularly the MCQ on the quizzes have horrendous wording and nobody knows what he's asking. Exams are all FRQ but at least the FRQs better say what they're asking for and aren't trick questions as much. You'll need to study *everything* though

If you can take a different professor, do it. This class was incredibly nit-picky and unfair. The exam and quiz keys were ridiculously specific AND he changed our scores for a previous exam 2 days before the final because people dropping the class meant he needed to give a smaller curve. I liked his lectures sometimes, but not worth the effort.

Dr. Kirkpatrick? A literal king—clear, caring, and makes lectures enjoyable. Then there's Linder: rushed, confusing, and painfully boring. His 30-question free-response tests feel like essays, and regrades? Don't bother. The vibe switch is wild. If this class were all Kirkpatrick, it'd be elite.

This class was hard for absolutely no reason. Linder is wayy worse than Kirkpatrick. Linder's tests were too specific and you had to memorize literally everything he said. Both the tests and quizzes were worded very weirdly. Linder is also very rude. Imagine sending regrade requests and he refused to grade them because he saw them as "fishing".

Absolutely DO NOT take. I put way more hours into studying for this class than ochem. Got an A in ochem and a C in this class. It was co-taught by kirkpatrick and he wasn't any better. Exams and quizzes are worded very vaguely and grading is very harsh. FRQ on exams are just a test to see if you can recite verbatim something he mentioned for 1 sec.

This class seemed just intentionally unnecessarily difficult. Weekly quizzes are open note but difficult because of weird wording or answer choices that are made just to throw you off rather than to check your understanding of the content. Tests are all FR and require very specific and thorough answers for full credit.

Don't let the fun disposition fool you- he really want to make his class more difficult than it needs to be and most of the tests/quizzes are all about memorizing specific examples instead of learning real evolutionary concepts. Take the other evolution course.

Not an interesting lecturer by any metric. Terribly designed exams and overly strict answer keys. No MC or TF on exams. Essentially, if you want any amount of credit for an answer, be prepared to repeat verbatim what was said in lecture to very nuanced subjects. Also, get ready to be ignored and/or berated if you question his grading or keys.

Dr. Linder is a cool guy but his class is NOT. I understand that he wants everyone to truly learn the material but the quizzes and exams are unnecessarily difficult. There is simply not enough time to complete 35 short answer/paragraph questions in 55 minutes. Grading is annoyingly consistent in being provocative. Just be prepared to do alright.

Awful. I got MULTIPLE points off on a test for spelling long terms wrong though it was clear I was trying to spell those words. Quizzes are awful I got in multiple arguments with TAs about grades back because the rubric was so random and specific. Tests are so specific to random parts of the lecture so you basically have to memorize everything. Gl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Linder means well and cares, and I his lectures are interesting. An A is more possible than people believe, but it doesn't feel that way, as tests have you regurgitate information essentially verbatim for full marks. He seems to take suggestions on teaching, but not grading. I studied by making transcripts of his lectures 2x each on 2x speed.

Lowkey wouldn't recommend. Grading system makes no sense, and your answers have to be really specific with majority of grade being FRQ. Doesn't post lecture slides before class either which hurts students learning. It has been unlike any other science class I've had at UT.

Lectures are clear and interesting. He's also nice if you ask him questions 1-on-1. However, quizzes and tests (88.4% of course grade) are difficult and are often graded based on an arbitrary (but specific) rubric. He seems to mean well, but the almost unfair grading scheme makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Cool class, but very stressful.

Has not responded to any messages all semester and the grading system is extremely faulty. Exams are tedious FRQs that require you to regurgitate every detail from boring lectures. Get ready to request for regrades for everything because the TAs always mess up and take off points they shouldn't. Weekly quizzes are set up to trick you. Terrible.

Honestly, avoid taking this professor. This class was dual-taught, with the first half with KirkPatrick who was doable. Quizzes can be difficult at times; they're open-note, but some questions are still tough to answer. I emailed Linder multiple times throughout the semester and not once did I ever get a response. Exams are very detail-oriented.

Please do not take this class for your own sanity. The actual class content seemed to be a review of AP Bio in high school, but yet it was the most demoralizing class I have taken at UT so far. Simply unfair grading. Would be writing an answer, word for word as Dr. Linder stated in class, for it to be counted wrong on the already messed up tests!

Funny how the syllabus says you won't be tested on "rote memorization" when that's completely false. The quizzes were very hard and the exam rubrics were very arbitrary/specific. Just an overall unnecessarily complicated class. If you're someone striving for an A, be prepared to lose your sanity when you take this class.

He is horrible and incredibly narrow in terms of what he considers the right answer. He's not like other professors where he's smart but struggles to communicate, he's genuinely just not intelligent. The TA is completely useless, and he never updates the grades on canvas. Do not expect to get an A in this class, especially with the insane quizzes.

Had him with Kirkpatrick. Felt like Linder's lectures were more interesting (maybe it was just the information) because everything made more sense. Aside from that, beware that he's very specific on quizzes and exams so I recommend watching the lectures and taking great notes to understand the concepts. Tests are frq, most qs are from memorization.

I thought that he gave good lectures but has quizzes that are difficult and have a lot of trick questions. He posts all lectures online and discussion attendance is not required but there is an extra project in discussion. The tests are all frq's and are difficult to study for because he does not provide a study guide.

Curves for exams are ridiculous. Instead of a curve that would help the average, they multiply your raw score by 1.xx amount (for example, 1.15), so if you get a 100, you'd get a 115, but if you get a 60, you'd get a 69. Grading on exams are also crazy specific and you basically have to memorize word for word what he says in lecture or on slides

The worst class I've ever taken. Not impossible to get an A if you put in consistent and lots of effort, but VERY hard to get an A. Inaccessible professor. Feels like we are being graded on an imaginary, arbitrary rubric and that is preventing me people from doing well. Really hard quizzes, even harder exams. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Mentions things briefly and expects you to get it. Type fast and get EVERYTHING he says. I had to rewatch lectures 2/3 times each. Grade is mostly based on quizzes but they are very particular. Use learning objectives for exams (which seem easy until you get your grade back). The highs on exams are usually low A's and there's no curve, mean ~ 70.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is really one of the worst professors I have encountered. I work so hard and still never manage to break the mean and get up to an A. Every test has a B or C average. Tests are so convoluted and consist of 30 FRQ in 45 minutes, which he grades so meticulously and nit picks everything. This class seems like it is set up for students to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've actually never struggled in a way like I have for this course. Quizzes (the majority of the grade) are based ON lectures, however, some of the questions are extremely specific. Tests themselves don't seem bad at a glance, but after he grades, you'll find that he expects specific, explicit answers. Scheduling office hours with him was difficult

i tried to enjoy this class and the lectures were interesting.however, quiz questions often felt like they were made to trick you and i barely finished with enough time to spare.the exams are extremely detailed and open response,forcing you to rewatch the lectures a bunch to memorize everything that was said in class.learning objectives were useful

The problem with this class is that there's a huge gap between what is taught and what is assessed. The best way I can describe an exam is it feels like being asked to satisfy a set of criteria, but the criteria isn't defined. Since it isn't defined, relying on your understanding/intuition isn't enough because the exams are subjective.

Tests and quizzes are all based on word for word his lectures. Even if you understand an underlying concept,  you will likely get many points off just because you miss a few phrases or words (that are way too specific to his lectures). Dr. Linder cares about you knowing the material in HIS way.

Dr. Linder was definitely enthusiastic about the topic, but he did not clearly articulate important things and key concepts well. Our weekly quiz average dropped 2 points (9/10 to 7/10) when he became the professor and his tests were impossibly long with only short answer and specific regurgitation of really specific topics.

Dr. Linder is clearly very passionate about evolution, but his lectures tend to get boring and he won't give a clear definition of a concept, he'll just beat around the bush by giving some example for awhile then elude to the definition and move on, leaving me confused about whether or not I understood what he was saying correctly.

I felt like the exams and quizzes got a lot harder when we switched to Dr. Linder. His lectures were a little harder to understand and some of his explanations of difficult concepts didn't quite break them down in an easy to understand way. Overall not bad but def tough.

Dr. Linder does not upload the slides on canvas, give any practice tests, and will not give back points whatsoever. All of his tests are essay based, and are more deceptive than thought-provoking. He prioritizes adherence to HIS own guidelines and constantly fails to consider the perspective of other students.
Not accomodating in the slightest bit, even for things out of your control. Do NOT pick him unless you want an entitled, stuck-in-his-own-ways lecturer.

Dr. Linder is passionate about evolution, but his lectures were extremely dense and hard to follow. The lectures are loaded with too much information and the exams were very lecture heavy. The textbook didn't help me but rewatching/retaking notes on the lectures (they're recorded) helped retain information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Linder has strict teaching methods that he stands by because of his previous years of teaching. All of the exams are based on lecture information and things he talks about in class. He uploads ppts and zoom recordings. His quizzes are harder than his exams, and he will throw in questions that require you to read very carefully during the quiz.

The exams are straightfoward and heavily detail oriented. Quizzes felt more challenging and costed a lot more of my points. Definitely recommend studying days or even a week before the exam. I found the posted lectures and LOs to be the most helpful. Linder is kind and clearly knowledgeable in the topics he discusses, but it definitely gets dull.
Really picky about grading and makes the questions extremely hard. Almost like he's trying to trick you smh.

Please do not waist your time with Dr Linder. Not only did he fail to teach any genetics content that you would expect from an honors genetics class, he doesn't respond to email, assesses over semantic details, and is really boring.

Linder is kind, but his lectures are boring, dense, and you lose focus very easily. Both his quizzes and exams are difficult. Quizzes are open note, open internet, but exams are not. Exams are all free response, so memorization is key to doing well. Plan on studying a lot for the exams. Lecture is not mandatory, he posts slides and Zoom recordings.

I think Dr. Linder is a really sweet man. He's nice and humorous, but he doesn't really care about his students success. Don't ask questions after class, he'll say you should've just listened to the lecture. Also, he lectures slow and doesn't adjust his weekly quizzes based on what we have and haven't gone over. No leniency whatsoever. Good luck!

I really enjoyed Dr. Linder's portion of Bio 370. It was lecture based, so we didn't have to read any textbook. But to do good, you'll need to know how to apply concepts to scenarios. His exams are mainly essay based and reward you for understanding content at a deeper level. Luckily, Dr. Linder's office hours and study session  help a lot.

Had him for BIO325H and BIO370. Very vague/ambiguous wording on quizzes so easy to lose lots of points even if you know the material. Have to pay attention to every single word he says - you never know what little side thing will be tested. Won't provide ppt slides before class to follow along with and not accommodating.

I would not recommend this professor as you need to learn any and everything in his lectures in order to make a descent grade. Beware of the curve as it is really unfair. For example, if i made 84 and if my friend make 62 on exam then mine will still be 84 after curve while her's will go above 75 which is very unfair to me.

Dr. Linder made really content-heavy powerpoints and could go over things too quickly, but my best tip would be to note important concepts and take notes from lecture recordings for anything you missed. Linder is passionate about what he teaches and is clear about what students need to know for exams.

This course had co-instructor system, one professor for each half. Anyway, his style was harder, and he gave less opportunities for exam practice. To get ready for his exams, I recommend attending his office hours and ask for extra real world cases that are related to class materials. He is kind and respectful overall.

Dr. Linder's quizzes/exams are open note and all of the material comes directly from lecture videos. Not too tough of a grader, second half of the semester content is just a little harder. Overall, evolution is an easy class and doesn't require too much other than a weekly quiz and four midterms. Great class, great professor.
Dr. Linder is very nice and is helpful during office hours. I was not a fan of his weekly quizzes but the rest of the class was fine. His tests were all open note and take home.

Dr. Linder is an awesome guy, very smart, nice, and helpful. The class itself is, as other reviews have said, very particular. The tests are open ended and really require you to know what you are talking about. It is possible to write 2+ paragraphs to answer a question and miss a few key words and you lose points. While tough, Dr. Linder is Fair.

Linder's class changed ALOT for spring 2021 so beware of old comments! Tests are solely lecture based and practicaly the learning objectives. No textbook use at all. Very knowledgable prof, will take time to explain in as much detail as possible if need be. GO TO OFFICE HOURS to ask questions. Much less work than other profs, less work than BIO315H
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Linder is awesome. He gives amazing lectures and he has clear expectations of what he expects you to know for every quiz and test. Some of the quizzes were pretty hard, but nothing excessive. You do need to study for them, but he gives clear learning objectives which basically define what is on everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Linder is awesome and he makes his lectures really dynamic and interesting like a story. He got me interested in evolutionary biology. Make sure you show up to class and take notes on the lectures.

Dr. Linder is a good professor, very knowledgeable, and also very kind. Those who are complaining on here have forgotten to mention how genial he is. His grading can be VERY specific, so if you do not know the material perfectly, you're going to be in trouble. However, rewatching the lectures is pretty much all you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Did not like this class at all. I reached out to the professor via email for help and he never replied. I even went to his office hours once and they were not useful at all. To do well you have to literally memorize every word he says in class. Powerpoints were completely useless and the test format was mainly short answer.
Going to office hours helped me out a lot for the exams. Prof linder has a great understanding of the topic and is willing to teach you if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Co-taught the harder 2nd half of evo. Nice guy, clearly knows a lot about the subject. It's just inherently difficult material. His tests were SO hard and came directly from lectures. I recorded the lectures and had to re-listen over and over to really get the material. Discussion readings were tough and grading scheme made it hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I wish I would have listened to the reviews on here. Tests are extremely long, open-ended, and graded harshly. You don't know your grade until the end of the class, which is super stressful. Save yourself!!!

Whoever says Dr. Linder's class is easy is a big fat liar. This was the hardest class I've ever taken in my entire life, and this is coming from a straight A, 4.0 student. I busted my ass off studying for his exams, which are ridiculously long and convoluted. His lectures are monotonous, his final was a complete joke, and my GPA is now ruined.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't really understand how he structured his exams or what rubric he went off on grading. The quizzes were pretty hard, and I really had to put in tons of effort for his class. Lectures were very monotonous and hard to listen to; nice professor, but I would take the other honors genetics class tbh. Not worth tanking your GPA like I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall was a great professor. Tests were based off class lectures only, so no need to read the textbook much. Very helpful in office hours. Understanding his "learning objectives" for each lecture important for getting As on the tests. Keep up with the material for pop quizzes (short and easy) & understand all the objectives and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SAVE YOURSELF. NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is like any other in BIO-go to lecture, memorize, and take a test worth 30% of your grade. The first co-teacher, new professor, Justin Havird, was fine, but Linder tended to talk to himself most of the time. Lectures were convoluted, confusing at times, and exams were hard. Class curve centered around C, no real curve. I regretted this.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Discussion section was worth 14% of the course grade,but we had to read at least 2 scientific articles each week that were above our level and did not exactly relate to what we were learning in class. This course was also co-taught with another professor and they changed the test style halfway through the course.

Dr. Linder is a great lecturer and clearly loves what he does. He is willing to take questions from students and makes himself available. I would take him again. As long as you attend lecture, study, and ask questions, you'll be fine.

Tests are solely taken from lectures. Luckily, hes is a really chill professor to listen to, and he clearly explains correlations between different concepts, so this means that the class is completely passable. An 86 is also an A . Some others thought he was condescending, but I think he truly means well and he always makes himself available.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. class is completely disorganized and TAs have no idea how to grade. with one of the TAs you can barely understand what she's saying and is always making mistakes when grading or doesn't know how to explain assignments so you end up confused. don't waste your time taking this class.

this class is ruining my life. the professor doesn't know what's going on, the TAs don't know, nobody knows. this class has one of the worst TAs i have ever encountered, which is who grades the assignments. big mistake, bigger regret. do NOT take this class.

Good grief, I'm so glad this course is over. 
Interesting material, and Dr. K is super caring and helpful... but this course was a disorganized wreck. If you didn't go to office hours frequently you'd be stressed out of your gourd. Unclear, constantly changing deadlines, assignments not published until the due date.. But it did all work out fine...

Honestly, nobody even knows what this class is about. Easiest A ever, but everything is super disorganized, and I feel like most of the things that are taught are extremely elementary level and are odd to be taught in a college class (venn diagrams, flowcharts, mind maps, etc). No words to describe what a confusing experience this was..

Took this class bc the rmp reviews said easy A but very tedious and disorganized. I thought "Why are y'all ranking her so low if you got an easy A?", I now understand the ratings and truly do regret taking this class. Half-way through the semester people stopped showing up bc of how boring the lectures were. 2 hour class full of nothing.

Professor Crews' lectures feel disorganized and uninspiring, making the already dull course even harder to engage with. Her grading, especially on participation, seems inconsistent and unclear. While the class is an easy A, her condescending tone and unpredictable expectations make it frustrating to sit through.

This professor was extremely unorganized. She did not follow the syllabus and I ended up learning nothing. I dreaded going to this class but it was the easiest A you will ever get. Take a fun UGS with a good prof instead of this.

This professor was extremely unorganized with the opposite of clear grading criteria. I hated going to this class even though it was the easiest class imaginable. Take a fun UGS with a good prof instead of this.

DO NOT TAKE HER. Can't believe an upper level course could be this disorganized. She gives us assignment deadlines but never posts the instruction until the due date and brings so much anxiety. The assignment is meaningless. I still have no idea what I am learning even if it's already 5 weeks. FYI we spent a whole class to make a name tag.

This class was extremely disorganized and I learned little to nothing after its completion. It is an extremely light workload with many unclear assignments. She clearly cares about what she is teaching but I don't know what she is teaching. Take a different ugs that is fun and easy and not just easy.

I gave her a 2 because it was easy to get a high A. However, I didn't learn a single thing and I don't even know what the class was supposed to be about. Very disorganized, doesn't follow the syllabus, and even TAs didn't know what was going on. Instructions never made sense and assignments were pointless. Lectures were boring, but she is caring.

Dreaded going to every class because the class was highly disorganized. The assignments were confusing and the TAs didn't know how to help most of the time. It's clear Professor Crews is passionate about teaching, but it was hard to enjoy her class when it's so chaotic. In the end it was an easy A, but caused a lot of unnecessary stress.

Honestly only giving a 3 because she seems passionate about what she teaches. Other than that, lectures are optional and hardly useful for assignments. Assignments are sometimes tedious (especially the last few) but still pretty easy to get an A. I just felt like the content was uninteresting, so mostly better to take a different professor for UGS.
uhh wtf is this class. take it for the flags and dip. More useless class ever lmao. also its a free A. Take it for the flags + free gpa boost. attendance is not required
Unorganized. I don't know what's happening in the class, and the lectures don't make a ton of sense, but at least it's an easy A.

The course is very disorganized. Everyone in this class does not know what's happening in the class. Homework assignments are very boring. Although the class is an easy A, it was a pain to attend the lectures.
Dr. Crews's lectures are all over the place. They often have no clear message. They usually don't focus on the course topics.  The work is really easy.

Crews is nice, but her lectures are all over the place. No topics are connected to each other, few are connected to "our global backyard," and content is either something covered in middle school or just completely irrelevant to college. Workload is light, but the instructions for assignments are usually unclear.
I took her for our global backyard and the course was organized horribly with no clear criteria but its an easy A if you just complete every assignment. Attendance is taken r

Super disorganized, lectures are all over the place, didn't really learn anything. Assignments especially IE's (take home long assignments in place of exams) don't make a ton of sense and take forever but its an easy grade. Only reason why I gave a 3 is because its almost impossible to get lower than an A if you turn everything in. Tons of ec

Easiest class ever. Idk why people complain about this class, it is literally an easy A. She cancelled half of the classes throughout the semester. The assignments in class are extremely easy and braindead. Take this for your UGS, there are no exams and not really any readings.

I took this UGS because I thought it would be interesting but I literally haven't learned anything. Just a pain in my butt at this point and I just want to get it over with. Attendance isn't mandatory but she gives out in-class exercises almost every class day, so if you are not in class you miss out on the grade.

dont take this class for an easy class. 
i did after reading previous years' reviews, but i guess the prof increased the difficulty now; graded very harsh, assignments are stressful and meaningless to me, and disorganized.

Pros: 
- Extra credit is offered frequently
- Class assignments, such as watching Social Dilemma, really make you think about society.

Cons:
- Unorganized, unpredictable class
- Seemingly easy assignments are graded roughly
- Busy work
- Huge busy work exam due during spring break
- Watch out when she says "Hint hint" - its not a good thing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Take classes that are meaningful to you, not to complete flags

lecture attendance not mandatory , discussion sections once a week in-person and is technically mandatory but u can just take a picture of the QR code. Grading heavily based on your TAs (mine was hella lazy and didnt even grade my extra credit). Lecture are useless, theres only one assignment per week and theyre always short about 15-30 mins to do

Crews is purposefully vague so that you learn to be "creative" but is looking for something specific. So frustrating AVOID. You will get a B no matter what but may lose all your hair from frustration. The syllabus gets practically thrown out the window after day 1 and is so unstructured. There is a fair bit of extra credit. Just don't do it
AVIOD THIS PROFESSOR. While

prof likes her job but does not follow the syllabus at all tbh. we've covered maybe 50% of the material that was on the syllabus. the TAs are what really affect the class bc they give instructions for assignments but honestly don't make a lot of sense. the class always has surprise assignments due randomly and the instructions aren't very helpful

Don't take this class. Dr. Crews does not follow the syllabus whatsoever and did not cover more than 60% of the content included in the syllabus. Descriptions of assignments are incredibly unclear and you will get 9/10 assignments every time unless it is considered "above and beyond". TA's not helpful. Extreme lack of communication from prof and TA
I learned absolutely nothing but we watched District 9 in class so yay!

Easiest UGS! Guaranteed B by contract if you show up, very easy to get an A (especially through tons of extra credit). Required to buy Packback for $60 to write weekly 300-word assignments. No tests, only in-class pop assignments, and weekly writing discussions. The class moved online/was canceled very frequently. Very receptive to feedback.

Dr. K was very caring and understanding for this UGS. Super easy class as long as you went. Felt like some students were quite disrespectful to her which was sad to see. Would recommend taking this UGS if you want an easy class.

She is so sweet and loves her students. The course will have a weekly written assignment 300 words on an AI tool called Packback that we had to purchase for $60. She is really unorganized. Lots of extra credit. Lectures are confusing and assignments are random. If you complete everything she guarantees a B+, but this class is an easy A if you try.

Kelley has such a kind heart. She is really passionate about what she's teaching and cares about her students a lot. However, she's very disorganized and all over the place. She kinda just rambles in class then gives random assignments. That being said it's very easy to get an A in this class if you do everything and there's lots of extra credit.

GRG 440L, "Landuse/landcover change". The lectures are sometimes redundant (which may be a good thing) and boring. There were only a few quizzes for the lecture, and they can be easy if you try. The labs with the TA were pretty tough. We used Google Earth engine, with coding involved. Pay attention and participate to pass.

Due to the flew, class was canceled a lot. We watched over 5 movies/documentaries in class. Your TA will grade your assignments and the rubrics are not followed. If you want an A you will have to be active about going to office hours and asking for things to be clarified. Pop quizzes are held to check attendance. She really wants you to participate
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 10% Discussion Participation, 30% Discussion Assignments , 60% Quizzes. You take the 4 quizzes at home. 1 of our quizzes got dropped because the teacher was sick for 2 weeks. You get 3 extra pts. on your FINAL GRADE for 20 hours of volunteer service!! 90+ is an A. This class is still not easy tho! Most ppl would have gotten a B if no dropped quiz.

The material in this class is very relevant and the work load and assignments weren't tough, but this class was EXTREMELY unorganized with inconsistent grading from the TA's. 100-150 word assignments due every week, four short answer quizzes, random extra credit attendance checks, and no +/- system. Still not worth the stress. Take a different UGS

she missed 2 weeks which made the course very unorganized. your grade literally depends on your TA's grading and its very inconsistent. you never get feedback so you never know what you did wrong. quizzes(4) were short confusing. she dropped the lowest quiz for us but honestly take another class. it wasnt worth it. we watched like 10 movies overall

This class really just frustrates me. Never give a rubric for our quizzes and don't really know what to expect for them. TAs and professor is really unclear and claim for it to be super easy but the tests get really specific things gone over in lecture.

do NOT take this class. the assignments are super easy but they are graded incredibly hard by the professor and the TAs. The professor is super judgemental and tries to justify the horrible grades for the easy assignments and also does not have neutral political views, which even if you agree with you still get a bad vibe about her attitude.

This class was an EXTREMELY easy A. You just have to show up for the super random attendance checks and write one essay a week (500 words) which is graded so easily I would write the morning they were due and get a 100. However, Dr. Crews is very zany and scatterbrained. She goes off on massive tangents and class can be exhausting to sit through.

She is nice and class is very fun! Very easy UGS class. You should get an easy A unless you don't do homework. 500 words paper every week. Extra credit is doable. Fun topics and we see 3 movies during the semester.

The class as a whole was the easiest thing ever. You have to go to class for the random attendance checks and the only other grades are weekly 500 word essays that take like 10 minutes to write. Overall, super easy A. However, I hated Professor Crews with a passion. She is condescending and impresses her beliefs upon students which IS NOT okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy A class I showed up and did my other classes homework in there every single lecture and probably didnt learn a thing, she cares about attendance with random attendance sign ins,  but still very easy UGS class and if you go to TA office hours you can lowkey fix your mistakes on essays and they'll give you a 100
Best possible UGS class

This is the BEST UGS you could take. She only assigns weekly 500 word essays that are graded super leniently. No tests or final- just an easy final exercise. Some in class participation grades, but not many. She is super interesting even though I'm only taking this class for credit. Super fun class I recommend for any Freshman.

She's very entertaining and experienced in environmental studies having traveled extensively to research. She's very clear in her lectures and although her tests are super detailed she's a very good professor and if anyone can make 8am class fun it's her

Love love love her! Thoroughly nows what she's talking about, has street smarts about economics and the environment, and really cares about how students do in her class. Easy to approach with questions. Not too difficult of tests, just have to know the material and specific facts, and short lab writeups outside of class. GREAT PROFESSOR!!

Professor Michelle was great for an entry-level class. I had her 4-6 pm, and for being such a late and long class, she kept us actively engaged. She taught us a lot of dialectical differences and has a lot of experience teaching languages. I struggle a lot in school and she helped me feel more confident.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Michelle cares for her students and goes above and beyond to ensure everyone is understanding the content. She answers questions without condescension and enthusiastically. If you have never taken Spanish before, the content will be difficult with any professor, but I wholeheartedly recommend Michelle.

Prof Crabtree does very well at managing her personal life with her graduate studies and the classes she teaches! She goes above and beyond teaching wise and offers some immersion experiences (ie brought gazpacho to class)! I hate the Spanish dept at UT, but she made this class more than tolerable and goes the extra mile to make up for its faults.

This class is not that hard but is still harder than most other UGS classes. I don't think it's worth it to take this class. Dr. Crowhurst is nice but unclear with her grading scale and lectures are interesting at times (and on zoom) but not enough to outweigh the negatives. If you end up taking the class, make sure you talk in class to get an A.

This class was pretty interesting, Dr. Crowhurst is really passionate about what she is teaching. You do have a term paper and a group presentation, but they aren't really all that bad, you do have a lot of time for them. Overall this class wasn't all that difficult.

Typically, each week consists of Powerpoint lectures in class and 1-3 readings outside. Some of the readings were a bit long and boring, but if you find at least 1 thing to discuss, you will get participation credit, worth 10%. For the W flag, there are 3 journal entries to connect to other experiences, as well as a major research paper.

If you can take LIN372K with the other prof who teaches it, skip her section. Grading criteria is unclear and it's impossible to meet her standards. You could have everything right on an assignment and lose points because it wasn't worded how she wanted it. The class experience was stressful.

Prof Crowhurst knows a lot and is really interesting to listen to. Some of the readings are a bit lengthy and seem a bit unnecessary. My biggest complaint would be the lack of structure in the course. The lectures can also get a bit monotonous with her just reading off powerpoints. She was nice and pretty accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had a lot of trouble in her class trying to meet her high standards. A lot of the material was difficult to immerse myself in and I felt that half the time she expected us to understand concepts that are near impossible to grasp with the way she explained them. I also found her a little abrasive in her individual critiques on hmw. Not a fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had her for two classes, did not enjoy either. She thinks you know more than you actually do. No matter how much you contribute, it's never good enough for her. I have accommodations because of a disability, but I rarely ever felt accommodated in her class. It feels like none of my work resulted in anything to her standards
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very likable and intelligent prof. The material itself is quite difficult IMO but she tries her best to help the class: moving hw due dates, EC, giving points back. Weekly hw and only 2 exams so make sure you go to class and put effort in. She is from Canada so one of the best things is hearing the way she pronounces certain words like "schedule."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Took Language, Cognition and Rhythm with her and was really disappointed in how little she actually knew about music and the brain. She even said during one class that she doesn't know much about music and even though she had us discuss neurosciencey papers in class, she was hardly able to answer any questions about the technical aspects.

Sounds Patterns was difficult class, even for Linguistics majors. I really had trouble concentrating. There are some concepts you'll really get, and some that make 0 sense. Homeworks helped a little. I felt like she thought we understood more than we really did
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Drops lowest HW grade, offers HW replacement assignment at end of the semester and offered extra credit to participate in her study at the end of the semester. Go to class, she will round your grade up at the end. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

This prof isn't the worst but complicated. At first she is nice, but then I realized she uses rhetorical devices to single out people she didn't like. It made it tough to learn anything, trying to constantly sift through her maze of points to figure out what was important or not. Her grading reflects a corporate agenda not correctness. I'd avoid.
She's pretty nice, but honestly, I was bored in the lectures. It's kind of a tedious course, but the material is fairly easy to master. Homework was imo much harder than tests.

Dr. Crowhurst understands her knowledge. I enjoyed every lecture because the complexity of the material meters well with the explanation. The class consists of cutting edge research so come prepared to have your mind blown. The writing assignments will leave you tired but not exhausted. Plus, if you find new research she will try to incorporate it.

She really knew her stuff about everything that she taught, didn't use notes at all. Super interested in the topic, and had a clear and effective learning plan for the class. It was definitely worth the time.

funny and overall sweet professor but can be disorganized at times. that issue sort of goes away once you enter the simulation. TAs can be nitpicky with grading but that is usually offset by EC points offered during the simulation; go for a leadership position!

Lectures first half of semester and then attendance matters for second half (the simulation). Lectures are common sense, and she just rambles, so not really necessary to show up. Simulation is fun and attendance goes toward your participation grade for these days. Extra credit offered. If you don't end this class with an A+, that's your fault.

Dr Craig is a GEM. The mock senate simulation may seem daunting but it is actually easy to earn participation points. I had a health crisis and she was very understanding and worked out a way for me to get more credit to make up for what I missed. Okay so she may not be the most organized person lol but she's so funny and fantastic. Take her class!

Dr. Craig is awesome! Her class is taught as a senate simulation, but she takes from her immense knowledge to support students in the class. There are 6 total assignments, one of which is an exam that's based on her lectures - which are funny and helpful. You'll want to attend class, especially in the simulation, but the classes are lots of fun!

Took US Congress with Prof. Craig. Class is largely based off of a senate simulation, where participation is important. She gives lectures that are funny but also can seem somewhat unorganized. There are 6 assignments including 1 exam, all of which are easy to do well on if you pay attention in class. Overall a fun and easy class and professor.

The class I took isn't on the list here. Dr. Campbell is one of my favorite professors. He cares deeply about the students and the course material. The class was more-discussion based, and he gave really insightful input. There are a lot of readings, but they're manageable, interesting, and very helpful to the big final project. Really cool class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: the professor would also always talk in circles and the pop quizzes were torture because even though I did all the required reading, the questions were always the most obscure random quote from page 3 line 4 from some book about some white guy studying people of color and then going and publishing a book about it for more white people to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was so boring. Easy, yet boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly, I found his lectures to be boring. He would read material straight from the textbook. The videos that he played were cool, though. Attendance was mandatory due to the in-person quizzes. The discussion section was the only interesting part of the class, and my TA was more engaging than this professor.

Professor Campbell's ANT302 class was not difficult. He is super chill and a really cool professor, but his lectures are very wordy and theoretical. Someone said the same thing below but if you're not on the same wavelength as him, lectures are a bit hard to follow sometimes. Interesting class

I took this class online, and I really enjoyed it. The lectures were really dense and I had a hard time understanding some of them, but as long as you do the readings and go to discussion youll be fine. The assignments are fairly simple. I learned a lot, and Dr. Campbell is a really cool guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Craig's class may seem daunting at first, but if you can get through the first 2-3 weeks, you will get the hang of things and as long the classes seemed, the content is pretty relevant. Honestly, if you can skim through the required readings and get the gist of them, it's not bad at all; the projects are straightforward and flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Craig's low rating is undeserved. He is a sweetheart and our class got very close because it was so small. He cares a lot about each student and their projects. But you have to be someone who likes reading about anthropological theory, discussing it, taking photos, and artistic critique. I absolutely loved it, but YMMV. Craig rocks, though!

Professor Campbell is really passionate about photography and is very knowledgeable, however his lectures are very theoretical and dense. He is not good at explaining. It is difficult to be on his wave-length unless you have an expansive understanding of anthropological history and theory. It was an interesting class but I wouldn't take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought ANT 305 was a really interesting class, and I found Professor Campbell's lectures really enjoyable. I didn't do as well as I wanted, but it was mostly due to outside circumstances. The assignments are fairly straightforward, the hardest part were the quizzes which were often weirdly worded/structured and specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Campbell is a nice guy, but I dreaded going to his lectures every week. He basically goes over the chapters we have to read (which are really long), or we watch videos. His grades are based on quizzes(50%), papers(30%), and attendance(20%). Unfortunately, I found the class really slow and unorganized. However, if you work hard, an A is possible
His lectures just seem to drag on. Boring and very theoretical. Assignments are boring, however, not difficult at all. Easy A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, but the class is a bit disorganized. Project topics are not exciting. Equal grading emphasis on photos and writing. You'll enjoy it if you like really abstract philosophical lectures, but I thought it was kind of frustrating and boring to talk in circles about theoretical anthro and photography for 2 full hours twice a week.

A lecture heavy proffesor who's lectures kind of drag on, the course was kind of difficult to get immersed in to and Campbell really couldn't win over the class. If you write the 5 essays carefully you can totally get an A, there's no room for slack you have to read the material assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Campbell is a wonderful and smart professor.  His lectures are pretty fun, he likes using technology.  Be prepared to talk a lot, he encourages students to be active talkers.  Be prepared to spent around $100 in his "the photographic image class" you will need to print a lot.  Grades are based on 2 presentations, 7 projects, participation

Dr. Crabbe is an excellent professor, she explains things in such a clear way and makes you feel like your opinion matters. This isn't a blow off UGS, but still light work. It was genuinely one of my favorite courses this year because the content you learn and talk about matters. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVE DR. CRABBE!!! Yes, there is some reading and weekly reflections. However, Dr. Crabbe does her best to make it accesible and there's plenty of time to complete. She is genuinely so knowledgeable, and you'll leave with such a rich understanding and curiosity of marketing. TAKE THIS CLASS- you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, she is extremely thorough with lectures and truly cares about the subject. HOWEVER, I would not recommend this as a UGS course simply because it requires SO MUCH WORK and you are better off in an easier one. We had reflections due weekly, all requiring a ton of reading (mainly academic articles that were hard to understand).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Crabbe's Influence of Marketing in Society course was one of the most thought-provoking, enlightening, and engaging classes I've taken at UT. Each lecture functions as a time to discuss readings, and participation is a big part of your grade, but Dr. Crabbe makes it easy to do so! The amount of reading also lightens up throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Crabbe was the best professor I could've asked for. Her assignments were challenging but impactful, especially with the amount of time to submit each paper. It may feel like a lot of writing and reading at times, but her care and knowledge for what it's like to be a student makes her 1 of 1. Would definitely recommend, just be ready to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Crabbe will probably be my all time favorite professor at UT. Although the class did require a lot of reading at the beginning of the semester, she genuinely wants you to succeed in her course. I do believe I have become a better writer after taking her class, and I highly recommend her UGS course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Crabbe's Influence of Marketing on Society class the first time she taught it (Fall 2022). Dr. Crabbe is very willing to work with you and assignments are manageable. Not much of a lecturer, she is mostly focused on our discussions as a class.
Amazing professor! Lots of open discussions but overall not a hard class, definitely manageable!

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Legare is a very nice person and she's very highly educated in her field, however attendance was mandatory so if you took one day off your grade would go down, she threw random assignments at us then later told us it was for extra credit, and the TA grades the exams harshly. Very insightful class but not the best I'd say.
I really enjoyed this class. I looked forward to attending Dr. Legare's lectures. The class discussions were engaging (and entertaining!)

Do not take this class. 6 exams, and you will literally never get comments on your exams or how to improve on your essays.  You wont even get your last exam grade back until you are already taking the next exam.  TA is a horrible and harsh grader for no reason.  You are never told what they are expecting for the exams so it is impossible to do well

Dr. Legare is a wonderful teacher and person. I took her CSR class Fall 2025 and can easily say it was my favorite. She talked during the whole class but was interesting and engaging. She expects you to read the textbook and come to class with understanding. She then connects dots and helps synthesize. Tests are written but questions posted before.

The best class I've taken at UT. Amazing lectures, cool projects, and all of the exam questions are posted in advance so you can prepare. It is a writing flag class so (obviously) expect to write. Not an easy A but you will learn a lot.

Very disappointed for how this class turned out. Don't get me wrong the lectures are engaging (somewhat lol), but the exams being fully based on the textbook AND we don't even discuss it at all is crazy work. Waste of time, so save yourself from learning common sense stuff about religion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can take another professor DO SO! She is an amazing lecturer and a god in her field but her class is made up of 6 exams that revolve around a textbook she DOES NOT USE IN CLASS.Her TA was a very harsh grader. There was also random projects not included in the syllabus but they were worth the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This isn't an easy A but I learned so much in this class. I enjoyed the course content so much I decided to do research in her lab. Highly recommend.
This was my favorite class this semester. Loved her lectures and the class discussions. Attendance is part of your grade, but if you attend, this works in your favor.

She was incredibly vague about how attendance would be graded. If you take this class, GO, it will make or break your grade. The class sounds way more interesting than it actually is, and was extremely boring in my opinion. The TA grades too harshly and is extremely unhelpful. This class is boring and, honestly, kind of difficult. Don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best class I have ever taken. Legare is my favorite professor at UT hands down.

Dr. Legare is really funny. When she did show up to class, she was hilarious and the best lecturer I've ever had. She's just a really harsh grader, and the questions to the test were so unique that feedback for one couldn't apply to the next test. I seriously considered dropping the class because my grades were so bad.

Loved this class so much I applied to be a research assistant in Professor Legare's lab. Class material is very interesting. I really enjoyed the group projects. There are lots of exams, but you get the questions in advance to prepare.

There are 6 exams 3-4 questions each: 1 pg essay per. Questions release 2-3 days before. Exam time was shortened from 90 to 75 mins 
This class killed any interest in the subject. The textbook is disorganized, the professor doesn't lecture, and exams are impossible to write to the prof's standards for all 4 questions in the given time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures are very engaging and interesting. Prof gives all of the essay exam questions in advance so you can prepare.

The lectures are an open discussion with the class; there are no lecture slides. The lectures did not have relevance to the exam, we had to learn everything on our own. There are a total of 6 essay exams and a final essay exam all in person without notes. There would randomly be group projects that were not on the syllabus. Class was not organized.
Cognitive science of religion is the best class I've taken at UT. Renewed my interest in psychology. Fascinating topic, amazing professor.

Dr. Legare is very accommodating and gave us many opportunities for feedback on our writing assignment. We were always allowed to reschedule exams we missed, and she gave us all of the exam questions in advance so we could prepare.
Loved this class, and this professor.I learned so much, and really enjoyed class discussions.

This was my favorite class at UT. The lectures were fascinating and I really enjoyed the course discussions. Dr. Legare is never flexible, she extended the due date for the final exam, and even had a pizza party for us during a peer review writing activity. I learned so much in this course. Highly, highly recommend.

Lectures are almost completely unrelated to exams, but attendance is mandatory. She never gave a rubric for essay exams, and for our 15-page term paper, the format requirements (changed margins and we all lost 1-2 pages) were changed a week before the due date. Nice woman and seemed to care about the course topic, just a little lazy unfortunately.

changed paper formatting a WEEK before our 15 page paper was due. she doesn't have powerpoints or notes or ANYTHING. she doesn't even talk about what we're being tested over in the in class essays. i left class 20 minutes early for PERSONAL REASONS and was penalized for it. that's never happened to me before. do not take this class

This has been my favorite class at UT. The professor is engaging and passionate about CSR; her lectures reflect this. She cares about her students, and her course is designed to help equip and prepare you for graduate-level coursework. This is an excellent course regardless of whether you are a Psych Major. I can not recommend this class enough!
Very interesting course. Caring and accommodating prof who gives multiple opportunities for feedback. Highly recommend this class.
The cognitive science of religion is a fascinating course. The lectures are inspiring and group projects are engaging. Highly recommend taking this course.

She is one of my favorite professors at the university. Dr. Legare is immensely inspiring and overflowing with passion. The class was rigorous with a lot of content pored through but all was worth it. This is a class to take if you want to learn and progress your critical thinking, not to take just for credit. If you take this class, lean into it.
Awesome class. Professor is inspiring. Very interesting class discussions
Course discussions were really interesting. Loved the group projects. Would recommend!

This is a writing flag class, so obviously you should expect to get lots of practice writing. Professor Legare invited staff from the UT library to help us with literature searches which was very helpful. Very caring prof, very interesting class.
CSR was a challenging class but I learned a lot.
I really enjoyed Dr. Legare's class. I learned a lot about religion, cognition, and culture. Her class provided great preparation for grad school in psychology.
HORRIBLE CLASS AND SO BORING
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This has been the worst class I have ever taken at UT. The TA is an extremely hard grader. The professor just talks for most of the class and doesn't really give material we can engage with.
Hardest class at UT. So many papers. Tough graders. Almost the end of the semester and have not learned a thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I thought this class was gonna be fun but instead it's been the class I've hated the most this semester. I feel like Dr. Legare kind of stalls and asks open ended questions during class instead of actually teaching us something. The readings are so long and the ta is a horrible grader. We usually end up in breakout rooms for most of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is very passionate and I love listening to what she has to say but we just make papers based on the textbook which is weird. Plus, the TA is such a hard grader. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Legare is a cool person, the psych of religion was interesting, but I only learned from our assigned readings. Legare just asked open-ended questions in class you dont know the answer to. Reading quizzes are easy but only 5 questions, so getting one wrong lands you a B

of course, spanish at UT is going to be a heavy course load. maymi makes it to where you feel supported throughout the course. took her over summer and during that my father passed away. she made it to where she was flexible with not only my work during that time but always checked in to make sure my mental was good as well. take her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I cannot express enough gratitude for Señora Maymí. I took SPN 610 last semester (not listed here), and her class was super engaging. Thanks to her support and recommendation letter, I got to study abroad in Spain and traveled around Europe. She's an amazing professor who continues to support her students even after the semester ends.

She's literally the sweetest professor ever! She genuinely wants you to learn Spanish, not just pass. Yeah, the class is a LOT of work, but she's incredibly supportive, and by the end, you'll actually know Spanish. I had a tough time toward the end of the semester, but was able to pull through and pass. We seriously need more profs like her. 10/10.

This professor was kind and you could tell really wanted to see her students succeed. She was flexible with late assignments and very understanding. This class was hard, but she made it easy because she's an amazing professor. This course load is heavy, but again, she was so helpful.

The content was interesting, but the lectures did seem to drag on, and the TA is not very nice. The grading was a bit harsh, depending on whether you got the TA or the professor as your grader. I would recommend taking this class if you have a genuine interest in the material rather than just for the credit.
Boring lecture, harsh grading, bad treatment. Do not recommend

Material and readings 4 me were very interesting so long as u care about the topics. At times lectures felt somewhat contrived, but overall they were engaging and interesting. Essays are graded somewhat harshly but the feedback provided is helpful. I wouldn't say the class is an "free" A, but if u have a passion for LGBTQ+ issues it's a great class

i was really excited to take this class at the beginning, but now i wouldn't recommend it. the professor and ta weren't very nice and the lectures were not interesting. there's definitely better ugs options out there.

She wasn't a very good lecturer, so the class would just be her talking nonstop about random things, and it was super boring. She was very rude and got mad easily. Don't even try emailing her, she NEVER answers. Her TA Gabriel was very harsh in grading. It seemed like they both didn't like each other & didn't want to be there. Syllabus unclear.

Dr. Cvetkovich is very passionate about her class but it doesn't necessarily translate into having an interesting class. The graduate TA, Gabriel, is a very harsh grader with vague rubrics so it's slightly hard to make an A. The field trips are interesting but a little irrelevant to the class. The readings are long & slightly boring & repetitive.

Dr. Ann is an excellent professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable in her field and provides great feedback on assignments. Many experiential learning opportunities, which is very enjoyable. She appreciates honest participation and encourages questions. Course load is easy to manage, would recommend for UGS!

Pretty easy and something you can put on the side. Discussion post every week and a short quiz over the lecture (3-5 questions that can range from 5-15minutes). A couple of papers, but the lectures are enjoyable to watch, and you can find them very relatable in your day-to-day life.
This class was genuinely so easy. Very light in terms of work. I didn't read the textbook once and I had an A+. No exams either, definitely take it if you need Sociology.

Professor was super nice and knowledgable. Was easy to follow lectures, and subject was super interesting! Only complaint is the TA, very tough grader, very vague feedback on writing assignments. YOU NEED TO READ THE TEXTBOOK OR YOU WILL NOT PASS THE QUIZZES. (I learned the hard way, so don't be like me)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Crosnoe is a nice guy and I enjoyed talking to him one-on-one. My only issue is that I found it pretty difficult for me to focus in class during the lectures (which were live streamed). There is quite a bit of reading as well as quizzes and discussions for almost every class, but nothing too hard. Not a bad class overall :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy. Lectures are very interesting, and the professor tells stories about his life and it added to the class. Although there's a textbook, you can get by without heavily reading it. Your grade is basically just quizzes(every class but they're short), 3 papers, and attendance.

Crosnoe is the GOAT. Super sweet, pretty funny, and actually wants to get to know his students despite being online. Essays are so light. Quizzes get a little challenging at times, but it's nothing crazy. Biggest advice: go to his office hours! We talked about Hobbes for like 10 minutes and it was great! + he'll help you out w/ your grade if you go

Although I never met with Crosnoe personally, he is obviously caring and kind. The papers were actually enjoyable to write (hot take?) and the quizzes are easy as long as you actually pay attention and take notes on the lecture.

The class itself is completely online, there are quizzes and participation discussions every class but very easy. He also gives instapolls during class, but not for a grade, just to see if you are paying attention. There are three main assignments during the curriculum, but he grades them very easily. Overall, the guy cares about your well-being.

Professor Crosnoe is a pretty chill and relaxed professor, and his lectures are interesting. Overall, the class was fairly easy. There are three papers and daily quizzes. The quizzes can be annoying, but the lowest three are dropped. The best way to score well is to pay attention to the lectures.

Sweet guy. 3 big papers due throughout the semester plus quizzes at the beginning of every class, instapolls, and chats for participation. The papers are pretty easy honestly you don't really need to pay attention to be able to do them and they don't grade super hard. You have to go in person once for participation credit. Didn't need the textbook.

There were daily quizzes based on the lecture so attendance is super important. When it comes to the papers, make sure to talk to the TAs and go to the office hours. Answering the prompt gets you most of the points but you have to go above and beyond to get an A. Overall, Dr. Crosnoe was a great lecturer and very thorough!

This is an easy UGS to take! Daily quizzes in class via UT instapoll are worth 45% of the grade with the lowest two quizzes dropped.
