Quizzes are straight from the reading and lectures and will be difficult if you don't go to class. The rest of the grade is from two papers and a group project. Crosnoe is really nice and his lectures are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The hardest about this class was the daily quizzes, but those come straight from the reading and the lectures so as long as you are attending class and keeping up from the readings then you will be fine. The lectures and readings were actually super interesting and changed my view on adolescence. He is also just so nice and great to chat with.

Prof. Crosnoe was amazing! His lectures were went prepared and executed. The short papers (3) not only enforced class topics, but really helped me to see society more clearly. (i.e. intersectionality) Loved this class.

Rob is an amazing & caring professor and I wish I would of met him because hes truly awesome! I was afraid to fail the class, but I  passed the class with an A-. He truly does care for his students and his TAs are really good at their job. Theyre there for you if u dont understand the prompt to the essays.

His lectures were super engaging and I really enjoyed the class. The papers were not hard and the daily quizzes were pretty easy if you paid attention in class. The two TAs are great. Overall, don't be afraid to take this class.

I'm a biochem major, and I needed an extra class to take. The professor is super engaging, introspective, and entertaining at times. However, the grade is based on daily quizzes, and you have to get 100's on a majority of them to get a good grade, the TA's were super helpful .

Most of the grade comes from showing up. There were easy, 5 question weekly quizzes and 3 papers. The papers were graded very fairly and its very possible to get an A+ on them. His lectures were VERY engaging and funny. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Crosnoe is funny + knowledgeable but has very unclear grading criteria and does a crap job of communicating them to TAs AND students  TAs all grade differently. A frustrating class, no reason why I had to try so hard to get a 4.0 in an intro class. No tests which is great but quizzes slowly crush you. I did get the 4.0 but def had to work for it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is great! TA's ruin this class because they grade the essays so hard. All three of them grade differently and are unclear about what they want. They expect you to write at such a high level.

Lectures are fine, quizzes aren't difficult. My problem is with the essays - TA"s act like there is an obvious way to write the papers that somehow everyone conveniently misses out on (no way that this could be the fault of the prompts!). Very little forgiveness with grading for an intro level class. AVOID!

He's a good professor and the class is very interesting. Quizzes before every class but they're pretty easy if you write good notes. Three essays that aren't clear on instructions. TA's grade the essays and they expect you to write with their level of knowledge in sociology. The class would be better if the essays were clear.

Professor Crosnoe is a great instructor and gives very interesting and relevant lectures. The bulk of your grade depends on the daily quizzes and participation which make up 55% of the final grade. So attend class! There are 2 essays and a group presentation that make up the rest of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Crosnoe is an awesome professor! Really knowledgeable guy and interesting lectures. In American Teens UGS, easy daily quizzes were 45% of the grade, which made it easy to do well!

Very interesting teacher and not too much homework, just skim the bold in the book and the readings. However, the tests are overly difficult and I struggled to get a good grade. Do well on the three essays and you'll be in A-B range. SEE HIM AT OFFICE HOURS. he keeps track and will raise your grade at the end if you go

Professor Cushing is difficult to work with and creates a stressful classroom environment. He is quick to raise academic integrity concerns and refer you to SCAI without clearly communicating reasoning or providing sufficient context. If you take this class, be extremely cautious, and keep detailed records of everything you submit.

He's ridiculously smart and very knowledgeable on like everything history related. He's big on participation and discussions for his smaller classes. My course had a lot of readings and writing but check the syllabus cuz that not true for all of his classes. A good professor but his lectures are very wordy.

Dr. Cushing is very enthusiastic about this course and cares a lot about students- he makes lots of fun extra-credit opportunities through the semester. His lectures move quickly and cover a lot so take notes and do the heading ahead of time to not get lost. Tests are open note and the study guides are really helpful.
Your TA grades your work and mine graded very harshly based on her standards as an art student. The class itself has a lot of work for a VAPA but it is fairly easy to get an A.

Dr. Cushing is a fantastic lecturer and the assignments for this course actually added depth to the materials being discussed in lectures and discussion sections. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Attendance was not mandatory and study guides made it possible to prepare for exams without perfect attendance.

Not many assignments, but the ones that we had were not too easy, and not graded too easily either. 2 exams. Weekly HW "quizzes", but aren't bad. Lectures are really long, and he does not stop talking throughout. Meet once a week w/ TA, which was nice to get to talk to people about the class. Overall, not super hard, but it is a lot of content.

This professor is so nice and he gives amazing and interesting lectures. I got a 100 in this class and it is not hard if you do the work on time. He gives exam reviews and everything on the review is basically on the exam. He is very patient and gives good feedback when I go to his office hours. Overall a very good professor.

If you have to take a VAPA, let it be this one. Class is a very easy A, just be sure you prepare for the weekly mandatory discussion sections. There are a few writing assignments and two exams, and there's plenty of extra credit to make up for anything. I genuinely love Dr. Cushing.
He was a great professor. He made lecture super interesting and fun, and the material was quite fun as well. The TAs were decent, but not bad.

Professor Cushing is great! Easy class if you want to knock out your VAPA. The class itself consists of various writing assignments, exams, quizzes, and extra credit. Lectures are online so I literally attend it in bed. Discussions are mandatory and we are only excused 3 absences, but it is not hard at all and the TAs who run it are super chill.

There are weekly quizzes that are online and open note, like three or four writing assignments, and two exams that are also online and open note. Basically everything is from the textbook, discussion section attendance is mandatory but lecture attendance isn't.

From a person not pursuing a field in art history, this was a tough VAPA and very demanding. I do think that Dr. Cushing would be great if you are attempting to pursue a career in art history. His grading is tough, and often backloads a lot of grades, making myself predict what my final grade for the class will be. Funny Instapoll answer choices.

Easiest A/A+ ever. So many redos and EC. Online lectures (boring) + (instapolls), not in-person :) . Annoying writing assignments every 2-3 weeks, but not bad. No Honorlock, exams taken online anywhere (subject to change in the future). Take it as your VAPA.

Dr. Cushing is such an amazing professor! He's very caring and moves essay deadlines when he feels that students need longer to work. There's 3 research-ish assignments and 2 exams- no final. Lectures are recorded and not required, but discussion sections are required. He's super sweet and makes great cookies. As an economics major, take his class!

This course is extremely easy and Dr. Cushing provides every opportunity to raise your grade through revisions and extra credit. Despite how easy the course is, Dr. Cushing doesn't sacrifice the educational value of the course. The lectures are genuinely interesting and  you will walk away from this course learning something.
lots of essays and quizzes to do but pretty easy

Decent VAPA. Yes, some assignments can be annoying if you're just looking to get your VAPA out of the way and don't care for art history, but quizzes/tests are easy—this class is a GPA booster (not honor-locked as of this semester). He's a genuine and knowledgeable professor, and TAs are understanding. Fast-paced lectures, not required though.
Doctor Cushing is the nicest professor ever. His class is super engaging and his tests are very easy if you just do the study guide.

Dr Cushing is genuinely a great person who brings a lot of knowledge and insight into his teaching. Overall the class is very doable even if you're taking a heavy course load. Class section meetings often require some reading but the discussions are usually very engaging. I would highly recommend this class for the VAPA requirement!

If you need your VAPA, take this class! Attendance isn't mandatory for lectures, but discussion sections take attendance. Exams are take-home and open-note, and he gives you essay prompts before the exam. There are 3 writing assignments, but they're super easy. He truly cares about all of his students and is beyond passionate about art history. :)

Dr. Cushing is an amazing professor! There are 3 writing assignments and 2 exams (no final). Exams are open-note and virtual. He often extends the deadline for the writing assignments and has soft deadlines for them anyway. Lectures can be a bit boring, but it's clear he is very passionate about what he is teaching. Please take him!

Took this class for my VAPA and can say for sure that this class is easy. He makes it near impossible to fail his class, especially with so many extra credit opportunities. Is talking more about potentially making exams on paper to avoid using AI, but even then he creates study guides and is very willing to help and answer any of your questions.

Goated professor. The class is super chill; there are two online lectures a week and one in person discussion with small group and a TA. The discussions are pretty much useless, but attendance is mandatory. There is some writing assignments, but its pretty easy. Never once listened to the online lectures, and still got a over a 100 in the class.

Super nice prof who wants best for students. Online open note tests and weekly quizzes. 3 kind of heavy writing assignments but he gives enough time to complete and grades pretty lightly. 3 extra credit opportunities. lectures can be a little boring but not mandatory to attend, however weekly discussion is mandatory.

Take this class. Not only was it easy, but it was interesting. Lectures aren't insanely boring and quizzes are easy if you pay attention. Exam is open note, open book. There are only two exams but there is not reason you shouldn't get an A. There is not a lot of work outside of class. Take it.

best class ever ! if i could take it again i would. he is very caring but his class is also really easy. he record lectures but for discussions attendance is mandatory and for a grade. just take this class you wont regret it

Dr. Cushing is an amazing professor! Though he goes fast in lectures, they are all recorded, and to be honest, you won't need to know every word he says, just the overall concepts. Tests + quizzes are incredibly simple, and writing assignments can be tedious, but not difficult. TAs aren't that important for your success! Take the class!

Loved this class! I took it as a VAPA, and he was such a passionate teacher! I loved listening and learning (even though I am an engineering major), and quizzes were very easy. He got us cookies once, all his discussions were very participatory and exploration-based, and we even went on tours during discussions to learn about our art's history.

I took this class as my VAPA and it was pretty easy but that doesn't mean you should put no effort into the class. Prof Cushing crams a lot of information into the class but is super fair on letting you know what you need to know for the exam beforehand. Him and his TAs are super helpful and easy to reach out to as well!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr CUSHING IS AMAZING!! lots of work (4 papers) for a VAPA but tests are online and open note. hes genuinely such a kind man and cares about you doing well.

Super Easy VAPA- Take it. The only annoying part was there was a lot of writing, but they weren't graded too harshly and you could do re-writes for full credit I believe. Tests were super easy, open note and essay prompts before hand. Weekly quizzes - easy and you can drop some. Didn't listen to a single lecture and ended with 100+.
There are definitely easier vapas to take but this isn't the worst one. lectures are boring and you have to write a lot of papers

If you're thinking about taking a class with Dr. Cushing this is your sign to do it. In addition to being extremely knowledgeable in the field and teaching me more about art history in one semester than any other class combined, he's also just a really funny guy that loves baking and a good cat meme.
The best literally the best. Lots of papers and readings but he is literally the best so it doesn't matter
Professor Cushing is very approachable and knowledgeable. Definitely recommend for VAPA.

professor cushing is the sweetest and most caring professor. as a freshman trying to get their vapa credit, i was rlly worried abt taking a higher level art history class but this class was great! his powerpoints and lectures are supppper helpful for the weekly quizzes (abt 8 questions, pretty easy if u pay attention).

Dr. Cushing seriously made my semester so much better with his chill, interesting lectures and relaxing voice! He is very well-versed in the material and passionate about it. Weekly online quizzes were easy, the essays were graded fairly, and the tests were open-note and online, with many extra credit opportunities. Take this low-stress prof!!

I took ARH 301 for my VAPA, and I'd recommend it. All exams are taken at home and are pretty easy, and all the papers aren't graded too harshly. There are a lot of long assigned readings, but you can get away with skimming them. The lectures are really fast paced, too. The professor is a super nice guy, and the TAs are chill.

All homeworks and tests are easy if you watch lectures beforehand. He gives you the essay prompts to tests in advance to prepare. Writing assignments are not lengthy at all and don't take up more than an hour or two. Grading criteria is very simple and easy to understand. He wants everyone to get an A in the class so it is an easy VAPA.

I took Dr. Cushing for my VAPA, if you still need a VAPA credit I highly recommend taking this course or his ARH 301 class. In this class, there is a lot of writing but as long as you follow the grading rubric you are guaranteed at least a 90 on those assignments. My Ta was Erin and she was incredibly helpful so I highly recommend her as a Ta.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took for my VAPA, ended up really enjoying the class and discovering an interest in art history. If you enjoy history/anthro or poli sci you'll enjoy this class and the prof a lot. He really engaged in discussions and genuinely wanted to know how we felt/what we thought. Really passionate and kind. Only downside is lecture attendance was mandatory.

I absolutely loved this class. I needed a VAPA and chose this one just because it was the only one that was open but I ended up loving the material. Professor Cushing is very dedicated to his work and you can tell when he does his lectures. The lectures were very interesting and he is a very kind man. I would definitely recommend him.

I usually don't take time to write reviews, but Dr. Cushing was fantastic! He was a sweetheart and enthusiastic about art. He also responds very quickly to emails and has office hours. The class textbooks aren't mandatory to read, and just his slides/video lectures alone help me through the class. He also gives extra credit opportunities.

Professor Cushing is such a sweetheart. He 100% cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is very quick about responding to emails and gives good feedback. He also offers extra credit assignments along with extra credit questions on the test. Tests and quizzes are also online and open note. Just take good notes and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: prof cushing is a really cool dude. his lectures are dense and sometimes difficult to follow, but for someone who has a genuine interest in the subject you will do just fine. assignments and essays are not extensive and easy to understand, but he also opens up class for questions and provides time in office hours. just a chill guy talking about art

Although Cushing has good lectures and seems very passionate about the topic, be prepared for vague instructions on assignments and not super constructive feedback. He does seem to want all students to succeed and is very engaging but writing assignments are confusing and vague.

TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He genuinely wants YOU to pass! he gives out forms with literally what going to be EXACTLY in his tests, He gives out extensive and detailed guides to each of his assignments. He is SUPER understanding and genuinely wants you to learn!

Professor Cushing is an amazing instructor. He wants you to understand what he's teaching and will take those extra steps to insure that you succeed in his class. I cannot say enough good things about him. I highly recommend that anyone who has the ability to take his course do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cushing's love for art history is very clear in his lectures. The course content isn't my favorite but I still managed to enjoy and learn from his lectures. There is A LOT of readings but you can manage without it. The tests aren't too difficult, and he gives lots of material beforehand to prepare. He is very kind and accessible as well!

I used this class as my VAPA credit and let me tell you: even if you don't have a background in art history, this class is still manageable. As long as you show up to lectures and take notes, the A+ is solid.  Try not to fall behind on lectures; Dr. Cushing takes most of his weekly quiz & test material from the lectures. Also, TA sections were fun.

Super interesting lectures! I didn't do reading and still did fine. There are a few essays but they are manageable, and the tests are super manageable if you study the key works! I loved how they introduced different perspectives and cultures. Great VAPA class especially with flags!

Great class, great professor. This was for sure my most difficult class, mainly because I have no background in art history and used it as my VAPA credit, but the content was explained well and Dr. Cushing is very understanding and provided us with multiple extra credit opportunities. The lectures were engaging and very beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clearly very passionate about the subject with a good sense of humor. Very eager to help students learn, incredibly helpful. Lectures are interesting with lots of information (but not overwhelming).

Do not take this class for your VAPA requirement, unless you have a prior understanding and love for the history of art. This professor is very passionate about the subject and it is clear in class. If you are an art-related major, highly recommend him. The courses is almost exclusively lectures and there are multiple exams/ essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curley was wonderful! Highly recommend going to OH; he gives full explanations if you get stuck. It's all quizzes, but they're untimed & pretty straightforward. I personally found the material super easy, but there's usually replacement grades if needed. Textbook isn't needed but a good resource with Ctrl+F. Overall, a lowkey class & simple A!

Loved Dr. Curley! Anyone who says otherwise is lying to you!! He's super helpful + his TAs, and even though the class is online, he is very helpful when it comes to asking him questions. His class was pretty chill, basically just a quiz every week & no tests!! Loved his class, just familiarize yourself with R & R Studio! Lots of resources too!
Easy class to take! Complete the weekly quizzes, and you'll be good to go! The TA's are also very helpful.

Professor Curley is such a sweet guy! As long as you keep up with your weekly quizzes, it's easy to succeed in this course. There are no trick questions and everything you need is covered in the weekly videos and textbook readings. You can easily go into this course knowing nothing about statistics or programming and be fine.

This class is asynchronous so I didn't get to meet the professor, but he seems pretty kind from his online lectures. The course is solely based on weekly quizzes with about 15 questions each. All the information is provided on canvas sorted into weekly modules. Overall, not a difficult course, but you do need to learn to use R studio!

This class started off pretty hard, but if you stay consistent with the work (since it is asynchronous), you will do fine. I honestly didn't think I'd end with an A since I had a B all semester long up until the end. USE YOUR RESOURCES, the TAs are SO helpful!!!!!!!!!!!

grade is entirely based on weekly quizzes that are open-book open-internet, just use the search function in the textbook or google lol. I did watch the vids to get a better understanding but they drag at times so just skim if you got it. if you don't office hours were frequent or you can ask on chatter. I ran into prof Curley once, he's chill lol
Not bad. He was very active and available during office hours. He also has cool birds behind his desk and is pretty funny.
Such an easy, fun class. Prof Curley is such a sweet and helpful person and the content is well taught. Easy to get an A and a good introduction to R Studio.
The one downside of this class is that it is too easy. No midterm or final, everything is online and open book. Probably won't prepare you for Psych 420M unless you have great personal discipline.

Each week you have multiple videos to help you with an open book untimed quiz to do. This class will only take up 1 day in your week. He gives out tons of extra credit for small things. I thought learning statistics would be hard, but this class made is so manageable. Great class, very organized, and great professor and lecture videos.

this class will take up about one full day of your week for lecture content and test. only one test a week typically 15-20 questions open notes. Curley is definitely a s sweet guy and would recommend. he went out of his way to make sure we were set up for the class extra credit was also given throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curley's videos are easy to follow, just don't put them off until the last minute. Use office hours and talk to the TAs to do well in this class. Learning R was harder than I thought, but with all the resources they provide, it's completely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: open note/book quizzes each week. lectures are kinda long, but his accent made up for it. never met him, but he seems like a nice guy! he offers 3? redo quizzes and lots of extra credit. the tas and dr. curley himself have a lot of office hours, and offer help on chatter.

Although the lectures cumulatively are quite long and drag at times, he thoroughly explains each concept to ensure comprehension. Ive never had such a thorough professor tbh. I had no background in stats/coding, yet I didn't find the material too difficult due to the profundity with which he explained it. He's also super likable, imo.

Dr. Curley had many time consuming lectures that ultimately wouldn't help much when it came down to it. The practice quizzes were often contrary to the actual quiz in difficulty. Even someone who was aptly familiar with stats (me), found the course to be taught in a way that overcomplicated it. Sweet guy, but I ended up in office hrs each week.

Although I don't have a background in stats, I really appreciated Dr. Curley and his class. He was very kind, friendly, and understanding. Weekly modules with a quiz (lectures can be a bit long, just speed them up or read the textbook) and 2 redos and multiple extra credit surveys. Lots of office hours, very possible to get an A in this class!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! This class is extremely hard and me personally, I'm not the best at math and this class did not go easy on me. There were several concepts you had to learn in a week and there was a quiz every Friday which is just evil! This class was too fast paced and a hard class shouldn't be, therefore I do not recommend this class.
He is so sweet but lectures are long and can drag. Go to office hours, TAs are so helpful! If you put in the work, an A is extremely achievable.

definitely not a blow-off class but as long as you put in the work to watch the video lectures and read the textbook (its free), you'll get an A. and go to in person office hours! the TAs will help you so much with the weekly quizzes. Never actually met Dr.Curley but his recorded lectures are pretty easy to understand. Lots of easy extra credit too

This course is incredibly difficult. It is very lecture heavy and incredibly time-consuming. It also takes some time to fully understand the material, and you will have to take time to practice before you attempt the weekly quizzes. Professor Curley himself is a great guy and very caring. If you are struggling go to office hours!

Professor Curley explains the topics in the weekly videos very thoroughly and makes them easy to understand. The weekly quizzes can take a long time to complete and are a bit tedious, but they are open book without a time limit. The professor and TAs are super active and helpful on chatter and offer lots of EC. I highly recommend this class.

This class was set up to have one quiz a week over the lecture videos Curley uploaded every week. It was a fairly simple class. As long as you actually try to learn the concepts, you'll do fine. The textbook was free and online. The only difficulty was learning how R studio worked, but the textbook shows step by step how to do it.

AP Stats in high school set me up really well. Regardless, he gives you all the information you need to succeed and offers so many chances to bring your grade up. One 15-question quiz every week paired with lecture videos (that I did not ever watch--I preferred textbook). Super manageable class even though content can be a bit overwhelming.

This prof is amazing. Gives you points back if you go to office hours and have already submitted the quiz (there's only one per week, no tests, no homework, and it's all open note and not timed). If you go to office hours before submitting, he'll also help you thru it. Online lecture heavy, so start early. Make sure to ask questions when confused

He was honestly a great teacher! If you pay attention to the lectures or follow along, then you will understand what is going on. The quizzes are open note and have no time limit. Even though coding can be grueling, I followed along the videos and learned so much! He was also lowkey funny because he is British so he uses British slang.

The goat if I'm being honest. Quizzes are open note and don't have a time limit. If you're stuck on a question just go to office hours and ask a TA. Pretty hard to get a bad grade with the amount of extra credit surveys/quiz redoes he gives you.
Great professor! He has a lot of TAs and office hours. As long as you watch all the lectures and keep up you will do fine.

I dislike coding, so I naturally found the class boring and taking the quizzes were kinda hard. He is a forgiving grader in the way that we get two drops and extra credit opportunities. The quizzes are also open note. If I payed more attention to the recorded lectures, I think it would have been much easier.

Dr. Curley is a very friendly professor that offers SO MANY extra credit opportunities that it would be difficult to get a bad grade in his class. I enjoyed learning from him because he's very clear in his lectures and has many office hours opened to students in need of help. His lectures can be tiring to listen to but he was very enjoyable.

Lots of extra credit provided. Quizzes sometimes had errors and needed to be edited throughout the week. Lectures were boring and dragged. Tons of opportunities to go to office hours and professor always made sure to respond to emails/chatter when he could. Very caring professor.
His resources are plentiful, but his recorded lectures are so boring and outdated. Speeding up the videos doesn't even help either. Was a light class, just was very hard to get through the lectures.

I found Curley to be very sweet and accommodating. His lectures do run quite long, and I personally found his oversimplification of concepts to be redundant, but he explains things extremely well and makes it easy to understand. Quizzes are difficult, but the class an easy A. If I would've attended office hours I would've gotten a better grade.

Curley is a good professor, but his lectures can be unreasonably long as they are all pre-recorded and can span upwards of 25-30 minutes per module with around 4-7 videos a week. He simplifies statistical concepts really well, but does so in ways I think are sometimes redundant. Overall, definitely an easy A if you apply yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof. Curley was so so so helpful with all of the questions I had over the material. He clearly wants his students to succeed and works very hard to make sure that everyone is able to understand the material.

Dr. Curley is an amazing professor who cares about his students and is always accessible. The class consists of weekly quizzes which are slightly on the harder side, but you can go to the TAs office hours anytime during the week to ask for help. Definitely take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Curley is such a sweet guy, he cares about you, and even though this class is a bit hard and a lot of work per week he has so many resources to help you succeed! He also gives out a ton of extra credit that makes an A attainable even if you didn't do amazing on the quizzes :)

Outstanding professor who excels in both teaching and empathy. Challenges students with thought-provoking questions and supports them with humor and understanding. Highly competitive during office hours, but you have to GO. Creates an engaging learning climate. Highly knowledgeable; with that said, R is not always easy and does require patience.

This man does not like his job. He gives very minimal help during his office hours. The class overall is difficult but you can get a good grade if you go to TA hours for help. This class is the most stressful psychology weed out class ever and will make you so stressed out your neck will be strained.

I'm NOT a stats person, so this wasn't the most fun class for me, but Dr Curley was amazing. Very caring and went above and beyond when I had a personal emergency in the middle of term. TAs are kind of useless, but Curley is great at responding to questions. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Provides the online textbook for free!

Prof. Curley is very knowledgable about what he teaches but the concepts can be very confusing if you do not pay attention 100% of the time or have some sort of preexisting knowledge in stats. Grades are weekly quizzes over the lectures and can take a lot of time to complete. Lecture modules are also very long

I had background stats knowledge so the coursework wasn't that hard, but for any occasional issue or confusion, Professor Curley was incredible. Most of the TAs are kinda clueless, but if you email him with a question, he'll always get back to you, and there have been multiple times when he gave me back points for things I didn't even ask for.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Curley is so funny and amazing. Him and the TAs are always so helpful. Honestly, if you put in the work to watch the lectures you will do just fine. Sometimes, quizzes can be a little tough but again, Chatter is utilized to receive help. No exams so that was amazing too.

The best stats class I could've taken. Very clear explanations in the videos, goes through example problems that are very similar to the quizzes, just a really nice guy. Always accessible on chatter and answers questions very quickly. The class is only based on a quiz every week. NO EXAMS :D I was actually able to learn without stressing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice prof!! class is also a breeze if you just keep up with the lectures and the modules!

Professor Curley was a great professor-this class is entirely online-content can be a bit hard to grasp from lectures (just abstract concepts, not because of his lack of any explanation) but it is overall very doable if you put dedicated time into to watching lecutres; TAs are helpful and will guide you on how to complete the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course is not stressful but will become stressful if you do not keep up with the weekly videos and quizzes. He is direct when teaching and is always helping students with questions and any problems they may face. If you struggle, reach out to the TAs who are always available on Zoom and make friends in this course to help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a completely online course. No tests, no papers, just quizzes. If you watch all the videos and read the assigned chapters for the week, you can pass. The videos are old but it's all the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof. Curley is an AMAZING professor and makes the content very engaging. he is a very interactive professor despite the class being online. His TAs are very good and they provide great feedback as to how you can approach problems or if you need help with anything. Great class.

I took this course entirely online, so I have nothing to say about the professor. However, his class structure is fantastic. You are given one open note quiz every single week. He drops your lowest grade and offers two replacement grades for your quizzes. Follow along with the textbook and ask questions on chatter if needed and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great professor, but a slightly difficult course if taken online and you struggle with math.

Prof Curley's a lovely guy. He outlines everything in the syllabus, and his TAs are super helpful. Your grade is determined by a weekly quiz, the answers being found in the textbook or vids provided. if u start on time and utilize the resources available, and A is super achievable.

Such an easy class, would definitely take again! The course is solely quizzes, but they are extremely easy if you watch his lectures and look through his textbook (which he wrote!). He is extremely helpful to those who ask questions on chatter. His TA's are also really cool and will provide you with any help you need! An A is extremely achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curley's class was one of the easiest ever. It is graded solely on weekly quizzes; however, there are multiple TA sessions where TAs will basically "check" your quizzes for you. Additionally, there are many extra credit opportunities. As long as you utilize the TA office hours and do the extra credit, you are guaranteed an A.

modules with videos and quiz every week. the module quizzes determine your whole grade, but are untimed and u can go back to the videos if needed. if ur stuck, theres plenty office hours where u can ask for help. i usually did each weekly module in one day, and didn't find myself struggling. decently easy class. ec also given thru class surveys
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Curley is great! The class is asynchronous, so you can watch lectures at your pace. It's fairly easy to understand, and the textbook is a very helpful reference. Prof. Curley was great in office hours and answered questions in a timely manner on Chatter. The quizzes weren't difficult for the most part, and there was plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Somewhat of an easy class. Grade based on quizzes that are not timed and are open-note. However, it is still math and coding so it is still hard if you can't find a good example of the problem you're working on. Watch the lectures and read the textbook and you'll be good. TAs and Dr. Curley are very accessible and there's a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curleys class is strictly an online course but he and his TAs are always willing to answer a question or help during their office hours or on Chatter. The weekly videos he posts can sometimes get a bit lengthy but it's important to watch them to prepare for your quiz. The module quiz every week is the only thing your grade is based upon.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Curley is very engaging and entertaining in his lectures, and pretty clear about the content considering its complexity. The class definitely takes time and attention, but Professor Curley does offer practice quizzes and makeup quizzes.
Great professor! Listen to lectures for statistics concepts and consult textbook for any Rstudio related questions on quizzes and you should have an easy A!

Professor Curley's class was pretty good, as someone who isn't very good at any kind of math he made the material easy to understand with both lecture videos and a textbook. I would strongly recommend.

Professor Curley is great! This class was very informative and good for learning the basics of R. It's pretty easy if you already know intro stats concepts, but even if you don't it wouldn't be bad. Textbooks are free online and would be really useful if you don't have previous stats knowledge.
Weekly modules, some are more difficult but pretty easy in difficulty for the most part, google and the textbook with be useful for quizzes

Dr. Curley is an amazing professor. So caring and the lectures can be long, but they are helpful for R studio and sometimes funny. The TA's are very helpful and he has a lot of office hours. It's just one quiz a week and no final. He is very generous and even offers two quiz retakes. Fun fact: he does international scrabble and loves lego birds.
There is only one quiz every week, no other assignments. He is accessible via email and very nice and overall the class was pretty easy

This was an easy and simple class. He assigns between 4-7 videos a week to watch that are not more than 25 minutes, and your only grade is quizzes, but he gives you the whole week to do it, and it is open everything.

Since it is a prereq to 420M, it does have a lot of content to work with and takes a bit of time. Quiz once a week with 15 questions that go with the lectures. Very lenient on assignments and such a nice guy! He's amazing and is so helpful if you go to his office hours. His lectures are very insightful but you can choose to read his digital textbk

Professor Curley is a very nice professor and he wants his students to succeed. There are weekly quizzes, but you can go to office hours and get help or you can submit the questions anonymously and the TA's or professor Curley himself will comment to help you answer it. There are also 2 makeup quizzes to improve your grade.

Professor Curley really cares about his students and wants you to succeed in his class. There are weekly quizzes which are open note, and you can ask questions about the quizzes in office hours (definitely recommend going to office hours!). An A is very achievable in this class if you do the work. Extra credit surveys can really help your grade!

There are weekly quizzes with lectures to watch but by using the online textbook and office hours it is easy to get an A. He also gives out surveys for extra points, 2 redo quizzes, and the chance to drop the two lowest. He is also so very understanding I once got an extension on a quiz for mental health reasons. An amazing and knowledgeable person

Grade based on weekly module quizzes- can sometimes be frustrating but overall not too bad- can have textbook, lectures, and powerpoint slides open so just look through material during instead of before to save time. 2 "redo quizzes" for extra credit. Prof and TA's answer questions quickly on Chatter and are very helpful during office hours.
didnt ever watch the lecture videos and still did fine-- v clear and fair grading criteria. also, going to office hours is v helpful

Professor Curley is an amazing stats professor! He understands when life becomes overwhelming and always does his best to help his students when needed. In addition to this, he is a great lecturer and makes learning coding nearly a breeze. The actual content can be a little difficult at times, but if you watch the lectures you'll be fine!

Prof Curley definitely cares about his students! Before taking this class, I had no idea how to code or anything about the program R, but this class really takes everything step by step. Your grade is made up entirely of weekly quizzes, which are open-note and not timed; if you watch the weekly lecture videos you will be totally fine!

Professor Curley is by far the kindest and most respectful person Ive ever met. His class is made up of 15 modules(quizzes) and theyre very easy if you watch his lecture videos and read the textbook(which he provides). GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! TAs are amazing and are there to help. He offers extra credit and only wants the best for his students!

Professor Curley's absolutely amazing/caring ! There are 15 quizzes overall, all due Fridays at 5 pm with unlimited time in between the start and due date (one attempt). ATTEND OFFICE HOURS. He helps so much and clarifies any questions there! He helps with quizzes too and gives AMAZING LECTURES. Also gives EC for doing surveys+going to office hours

Professor Curley has been my absolute favorite this semester. The class consists of 15 module quizzes (open note), and he provides many extra credit opportunities. Office hours are extremely helpful, since you are allowed to ask questions about the quizzes. I couldnt recommend this course enough, Prof. Curley genuinely cares about his students.

I took the course asynchronously, and though there were a lot of videos to watch, Dr. Curley makes it easy to get a good grade in this course. He drops your two lowest grades and lets you replace two other grades with a redo quiz, and there are no cumulative tests. He's a sweet professor and there's plenty of office hours from him & the TA's.

Prof. Curley is the BEST! Would 100% recommend taking his intro stats for psychology course. Grade only made up of 15 weekly quizzes and gives plenty of extra credit opportunities. Really cares about students and his class. Gives a free (optional use) online textbook that he published w/ a grad student (that's super rare - appreciate him for it!).

Okay, so I am non-math major that took this class for a QR flag, & man was it difficult for me. I took this class during the summer, so it was condensed, but PLEASE be warned that you have to take amazing/thorough notes to get an A, and you'll be spending hours on this class a day. Prof Curley is SO NICE, but the material is super hard in general.
Best professor Ive had so far. Hes so nice and understanding. He also gives good feedback in piazza and provides a lot of extra help. I definitely recommend taking him

Professor Curley is incredibly sweet and genuinely a nice person. It is clear that he wants everyone to succeed. He is patient and clear with his feedback I wish the best for Professor Curley because this felt like the only bearable class during covid and isolation. The course was asynchronous and well formatted but grades are directly from quizzes

Prof Curley is the best intro to stats teacher you can get. Weekly quizzes are easy if you watch the lectures. Super accessible outside of class. Curley wrote his own guidebook to R that you use for free in class. Would take again!

Professor Curley is absolutely amazing. You will not regret taking him. He is incredibly accessible throughout the week, and his recorded lectures are clear and easy to follow. I'm no math whiz, so I really appreciated that Prof Curley never assumed you obtained prior topics to the t; he always reiterates past points. Cheers!

You're only graded on quizzes but they aren't that hard and they're open note, as long as you learn the lesson you should be good. If you don't understand something the TA's and Prof Curley are soooo helpful.

Great professor! He's very considerate of student's needs, helpful, and great at teaching. I've never done coding or stats, but he made it very manageable and easier to learn. Highly recommend taking his class (and he has a british accent)! The material was difficult for me, but you won't have any trouble if you practice a lot & go to office hours

I appreciated his grading criteria of only weekly quizzes during this uncertain time. I did not feel the need to worry about this class since his lectures were straightforward and the workload was easily manageable. He gave multiple opportunities to help your grade with dropping the two lowest grades and having optional quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: So kind and caring, he really wants his students to succeed. Quizzes every Sunday that are easy if you watch the lectures and reference the free textbook. If you have trouble on a question, join office hours he is VERY helpful. Also answers super fast and detailed in Piazza. Such a great prof, I'd take another course of his in a heartbeat.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Make sure to pay attention to lectures and then scan over the readings to get 15/15 on all your weekly (open-note) quizzes. Gives extra credit!! The lectures are very helpful and he answers questions super quick via Piazza/Office Hours/Email. He cares about you. Cannot recommend enough.

Professor Curley is a super nice professor! Each week you have videos to watch and then a 15 question quiz. He will answer whatever questions you have about the quizzes during office hours, so definitely go to them! He also adjusts the quiz grades if people didn't do well and he adds surveys for extra credit. It's a challenging class but worth it!

He was super caring and wonderful. It was very easy to get in touch with him through email or office hours. He was very caring and understanding about grades and quizzes often giving back points if he made a mistake or if the distribution of grades for a particular quiz didnt match up to past quizzes. I would love to take him again if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He might be great in person, but his class is fully online now. Last week I had 3.7 hours of videos where he drones on and on about things that are not on the weekly quizzes. The quizzes also have questions where you can select as many or none of the answer choices, making it super difficult to get questions right. Make sure to read online reviews.

One of my favorite professors, made me actually like statistics. He has a lovely British accent and explains the material clearly and thoroughly. Go to his office hours, he's super caring and will help you understand the material. Would definitely take another class with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Defiantly one of my favorite professors so far at UT, super caring and understanding. If you show you understand the content, he gives lots of slack on the tests. Highly recommend!!
Curley is my favorite professor so far! He is so funny and grades super easy. There is a lab and the attendance is mandatory but the lecture is optional.

Professor Curley is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He truly cares about how well his students do and is willing to help no matter what. He is very accessible and is willing to work things through one on one. He is by far the best teacher for this class, so take him if you can.

Professor Curley genuinely cares about his students performing well in his class. He was very helpful in giving in class examples that were very similar to exam material. He also gave practice exams that were very similar to the exams. Lab is required with an individual project presentation. I would take this class again.

Professor Curley was incredible. He was extremely patient and great at explaining how to solve problems. For the last two exams, he gave practice exams that were extremely similar to the test. The first exam was just definitions. 4 exams, final is an optional exam. You have to go to lab, though. Once a week. Lab isnt bad.

This class is very interesting if you are interested in thinking about how certain political/social problems in today's world work and how different ethical theories can be applied to them. There are about 3 weekly readings. There are 3 tests and they aren't too difficult as long as you understand the readings and attend lectures.

I honestly think for his first time teaching it really wasn't too bad. He was kind of rude and sassy at times and the course is strictly based off of tests. The tests were worded weirdly, and though he says that attendance was required, he took it ONCE. He would go off into tangents and I would get lost, so this course is pretty much self taught.

I really enjoyed having Henry as a professor. His lectures were very funny, and his office hours were quite helpful. There was a decent amount of reading, but it was never impossible to manage. Our grade was made up of 3 exams and participation, which causes some pressure, but if you attend every lecture and do the readings you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory but never taken except on TXOU weekend. Lectures were dull, off topic, and he often sat on his phone during group work. Exams had bad multiple-choice but okay short answers. He tries to make an intro class harder than it needs to be and said, "philosophy is as hard as chemical engineering". Overall a childish professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely chill, accessible outside of class, very accommodating and did a fairly decent job at explaining readings. Lectures could get a little dry. He never actually took attendance tho and it was often difficult to participate because he sometimes goes off on tangents. Do the readings, sit front row and go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, great professor. Everything is open notes, and the course project isn't hard at all.

Cutbirth is a caring professor with decent lectures. Exams are open-note, open-textbook, so they're generally easy. The class project consists of interviewing someone about their experience with deception and isn't too demanding with very manageable deadlines. If you're looking for something that's not too hard on your schedule, take this class.

Really fun class! Definitely take it with Prof. Cutbirth if you're looking for an interesting elective. Project is tedious but graded fairly. Exams are very textbook centric but open note so pretty easy. Lectures are fun and overall Prof. Cutbirth is an amazing lecturer!

Professor Cutbirth is great. There are 3 exams and 1 cumulative final (the final can replace one of your exams). The course project is long and tedious but as long as you follow instructions, it should be a high grade. Many answers to the open note exams are found in the textbook, so make sure to get it. Overall, the material was super interesting.
This class was very interesting and I would highly recommend taking any of his classes if you get the chance!

Buy the online textbook, Quizzes (3 of them) can be taken anywhere (normal classroom made available too). Very, very easy class. 
MAIN THING: Interview Project (alone or with group up to 4 people). Interview someone unrelated to you, about their experience with lying and deception. Interview is an hour long or so. Paper made with it. Graded softly.

I took this class my first year at UT, this class was one of my favorites. Most of the assignments are in class and you work in a group. This class has readings and videos to watch before class for content. However, most videos are shorter and really interesting to watch, many of them are music. Dr. Cutbirth is fun to talk to and willing to help.

Dr. Cutbirth is an exceptional professor! I took CMS 338 and CMS 367, both of which made me a stronger writer, a better researcher, and more informed about the modern news media. His classes are engaging and insightful. He genuinely cares about student growth and hearing their perspectives. Highly recommend if you're interested in media studies!

No value. Uses class as a way to talk about himself and likes to hear himself talk so a lot of him talking AT you. Also has mentioned his political affiliation multiple times even though he tries to act casual about it. Does not take feedback well gets feelings hurt then gets defensive and aggressive. Should not be teaching at any university

Prof. Cutbirth is very caring and accessible! I took this class during the summer: only 5 quizzes (1 dropped), choose 2 out of 5 discussion posts and a final exam. Everything's open note and material, so while you do have to buy/rent a textbook, it's really helpful for quizzes and exams. Definitely recommend this course and professor!

This class was very fun and engaging. Professor Cutbirth is very passionate about honest journalism, and I learned a lot from him while still enjoying lectures. I want to say he pushes his political beliefs pretty heavily, so if you don't like liberals, maybe stray away lol. But, at the same time, he is accepting of literally all ideas. Fun class!

I recommend any course Professor Cutbirth teaches. He values attendance and participation. Show up, participate and you will learn a lot and make an A. Professor Cutbirth focuses on leaders' contested narratives and examines them in depth. You'll leave with a better understanding of what true leaders are.

Easy class. 
Professor uses lectures as a soapbox for his life & beliefs. 
No real substance in the course. 
Can't say I learned a lot, as basically nothing is required besides two papers.  
Repeats the same points about racism & society constantly. 
Slightly denigrated religious beliefs/stories once in class.
But hey, you get 2 flags out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not too hard but just frustrating at times

Professor Cutbirth is a pretty laidback professor. I barely went to class but he uploads all his lectures and material so you can still get an A as long as you keep up with the work by yourself. Only 4 exams and he drops your worst grade. The main project is also pretty simple. its a 7 page paper but not overwhelming at all.

I had Professor Cutbirth for Leadership Stories and Lying and Deception this past Spring semester. He is strict on APA formatting and grade rounding, but other than that,the way he taught the class was very engaging/clear and he cares A LOT for his students. Just do the work, and you'll get an A/A-! He is an amazing professor, definitely take him!

A great class. Cutbirth deserves a lot of credit for focusing Leadership Stories on stuff we are all dealing with at UT. He gave us a chance to research it then separately to reflect on our own roles in it. He is passionate about his work and how much he loves the school even if he does expect you to write like a college senior. ;/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took lying and deception with him and it was great. Great professor, reasonable guy. However, do not take Leadership Stories. It's super paper heavy (no it's not a writing flag) and you get graded more for formatting and technicalities than understanding of the material. I'm teaching myself more about APA than I'm learning about leadership
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Well-read, passionate, and woke king! If you don't like writing reconsider taking this class as he is a tough grader and the essays really push you. I felt the readings he pulled were inspiring and relevant which I appreciated. You won't finish this class w/o feeling proud of yourself, but it's gonna take work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Cutbirth is passionate, smart, direct, and creates classes where people learn the most interesting things that can be learned around communication. He is honest, gives great directions, pushes people to really understand material, and become better students. If you try, you should get an A and find a mentor along the way.
Professor Cutbirth is an incredible professor. He really cares about his students, he is very fair, he is clear about what is required to do well in his class, and he is an engaging lecturer.

I absolutely loved Prof. Cutbirth! He genuinely cares about his students and wants us to walk away from his class having learned something. A few writing assignments, a few in- class assignments to boost your grade, and one final paper at the end. Quite a bit of reading, but overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I think this class is too strict on writing requirements. Doesn't give you the chance to analyze and he doesn't want your opinion on the papers, just wants facts and will grade HARD. Also summer students beware! The readings will take you a long time and the two main papers are long and tedious! Cutbirth is really cool, but this class isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking this class if you get the chance. Material is fascinating, and Dr. Cutbirth is an awesome and very reasonable professor. He is clear about his expectations, and the reviews for exams are very helpful in helping you prep for the exams. He tells you exactly what to study, and does not try to trick you.
Super nice guy. High standards (but in the end your grade will be ok). Good BS detector.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I LOVE Cutbirth! Fake News is such a fun an interesting class, and he keeps you thinking and on your toes during class. Openly encourages discussion for different opinions on things happening. the essays are a little hard to get right, but he leaves good feedback to help you improve. One of the best professors at Moody hands down.

He's got my vote for best professor on campus! I've taken him twice, once for his small lecture and once for the big lecture. There's typically a lot to read and you need to go to class, but engage with him (he has tons of office hours) and you're A ready!! He also writes great recommendations and is a great friend to have in the building.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Lying and Deception is straight forward, slides up and available, regular quizzes with key that ties the questions straight to the book. The interview assignments are a little work, but after I finished I realized why he assigns them. In all, a good solid class.

He has unclear grading criteria, and is sometimes condescending when you ask him a question that you seriously don't know the answer to. Then he answers with an answer to a question he would have WANTED you to ask instead, and it's not very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not really give 100's. He wouldn't answer emails. Assignment instructions were not clear. He said it would few short readings but they were actually long. He seems really nice at first but he just was not helpful at all and he has high expectations of students, but with little guidance.
Passionate professor who really puts himself out there in class. Can be a little rough around the edges. Super nice one-on-one. Very available and helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took both Fake News and Lying & Deception with him and I can't recommend him enough. Fake News was arguably the best class I ever took at UT. L&D was definitely fun, but Fake News was phenomenal. He forces you to think about important issues in our society and what they mean for our future. I felt so inspired finishing that course. 10/10 prof.
My favorite professor so far at UT. Very nice, has high standards that can be a little surprising sometimes, but he bends over backwards to be fair. Take advantage of his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took both classes. Pretty informal but his standards are high. Quizzes  mini-exams with stuff from books but not lectures. He posts slides BEFORE the lectures, lets you drop two quiz grades and gives a good midterm and final review. Go to his office hours, but beware he can be a little chatty. Fake News was my favorite course yet at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at this University. He makes the weekly quizzes very deceptive and tricky. Lectures are vague. Honestly I didn't know how to win and make a good grade in this class. I did all the readings and went to all the classes and couldn't make a good grade.

A lot of writing (no exams) and a group project at the end. Not hard and a lot of flexibility with the "hybrid." The professor went out of his way to take some unconventional approaches with readings and "leaders," and that was cool. He's good to meet up with in office hours, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super nice guy very straight forward. Take him literally when he tells you how things are done. He isn't very flexible on make-ups and excused absences. Has a great career with a lot of practical experience. See him in his office. He likes knowing who you are and what your interests are. And he will go out of his way to help if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Cutbirth is an awesome instructor who really takes the time to invest in his students. His lectures are interesting, and he knows his stuff. Eventhough it was a large class, it was very failry taught and graded.

Really enjoyed lying and deception with Cutbirth. Class consists of weekly quizzes over the reading and 3 easy interview projects. Material itself is really interesting and Cutbirth allows for a lot of discussion (though not required). Attendance isn't tracked but he is a knowledgeable guy with a lot of cool experience so it's worth going.
Lectures were hard to follow, homework was really difficult, projects took a while, and exams were hard to prepare for. Still, she is the sweetest person on the planet.

One of the nicest professors that I've ever taken. Super nice with everyone and helpful beyond measure,extremely conciderative as well. The class context is very difficult though If you really want to understand the class as she sort of expects you to have a general understanding beforehand, but getting a high grade isn't hard
Perhaps the sweetest person in the world. However, lectures and homework are ridiculously onerous and notation heavy. She makes up for it with pretty straightforward exams.

The class covered some good content, and the majority of our grade was made up of the 3 midterms and optional final. She provides practice tests that give you a clear indication of what to expect for the actual exams..being able to solve those is a good indicator for how well you will do on the actual exams. The homework is challenging however.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The absolute GOAT. Lectures were a bit slow, but she is very friendly and encouraging. Exams were similar to HWs. Take if you can.

There were 5 group projects, which was kind of annoying to have to meet up, but they were a grade booster because she gave you the opportunity to send her your work beforehand. The exams were very similar to the practice tests and there was weekly homework. She's a great lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her for M 378K and M 362K, but same rating for both. Very caring and friendly professor! M 362K is good Exam P prep, too. But do note that you will need to put a lot more time into the homework assignments. Not a free A, but you learn a lot even if you walk out with an A-. P.S. Free fruit snacks at her office hours :3

Lectures were a bit dense and went over people's heads, but Professor Cudina was very helpful during office hours and always gave good feedback on group projects. Exams were a good reflection of what was done in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you put in the work, you will do more than fine. If you don't go to class, of course you you'll have a difficult time especially since it is upper-division. Her lecture material accurately reflects exams (not exact same questions but same concepts).She is very generous with partial credit given that you try. Probably my favorite class so far.
She was an okay presenter and used a really old probability textbook which made it really hard to understand. Only the undergraduate LA was useful when learning this material.

Predictive Analytics: Lectures are a bit fast-paced if you don't have exposure to ML, but Cudina is more than happy to clarify if you ask questions. HWs/projects are graded leniently, OH is very helpful for projects. Cudina genuinely wants students to do well, she even reduced the final project when seeing students stressed with other finals.

Dr. Cudina is an amazing professor! She is very caring for her students and her lectures are very comprehensive. Her notes are also very easy to read and are posted after each lecture on her website. Her tests can be a bit tricky but very doable. She also offered extra credit this semester and the assignment was very interesting. Would take again!

The professor is very clear, lectures well, and her assignments are pretty relevant to the exams. There are lots of places to earn extra credit, and exams aren't weighted heavily. The exams are open note, are similar to practice problems, and you get some good experience with R. Overall, pretty easy class and nice professor.

One of the nicest professors you will ever have. She cares about her students and will help you with anything, as long as you ask. She really is there for you. The problem is that there is no textbook and it is taught as though you know everything when you walk in on day one, making you feel clueless throughout the whole semester.

I learned a lot from the class. Dr. Cudina lectures at a good pace and records her lectures. She dropped our lowest three homeworks, offered lots of extra credit on the midterms, let our final exam replace our lowest midterm, and gave us a formula sheet for the final exam.  My only complaint is that 49% of the grade comes from R group projects.

Dr. Cudina is a good teacher, but the content was so light that I stopped getting anything out of her lectures. If you go everyday and participate, she will know your name and face which is pretty cool. Homeworks and group projects were easy, but I did come into this class already knowing R. Great teacher, wish I could take her for harder classes.

Dr. Cudina was great! Fun, exciting little tasks! Solid course material covering some of the basics of probability and statistics. From here the actuary career path is very viable so she adds a ton of value to our department and the students.
2 quizzes and 1 homework every week. All her lecture notes were online and she gave enough practice problems to prepare for the 3 open book exams.
She is very caring and explains the stuff very well. Her notes are great!

Dr. Cudina relies heavily on RStudio. 3 group projects, 3 proctorio exams, 1 individual project. You can submit projects early for feedback which is nice! My only issue was the amount of extra work (quizzes, hw, practice problem sets, etc.) It was excessive and hard to keep up with. She does offer extra credit. Tests were tricky and go by quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her lectures are great as Cudina is a great lecturer so that the lectures are engaging and easy to follow. She's also really nice and helpful in office hours as well and gives pretty good feedback on your assignments if you let her check them before the due date. Assignments aren't too bad at all. Definitely (one of) my most favorite class at UT.
Just a great professor all around. Clearly cares and knows about what she is teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable on everything actuarial and does a great job at explaining the subject matter. She does LOTS of examples in class which is beneficial. The homeworks, quizzes, and tests can be difficult but she is very helpful in office hours. Additionally, she makes an effort to get to know her students by name. I do recommend taking her.
Dr. Cudina is very caring and helpful during office hours. Her lecture slides and reviews really help prepare for the tests. I would take her again for any class!

Really great lectures. Spends most of class going over examples, which is very helpful. Recommend getting and reading the textbook, as I think it gives a better general overview of the diff topics that what she gives in class. Her tests/HW/quizes are difficult but doable.
Great at explaining stuff. Reasonable amount of homework. Fair tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The only time I've ever said that the workload felt too light. We had about 8 take-home quizzes and 6 homeworks. They weren't hard, but the majority of them came at the second half of the semester. Teaches well, and her notes are posted online. Utilizing coaching actuaries on the side was very beneficial for this class.
Prepares well for the Actuarial Exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cudina is a very caring professor, however her lectures can be a little boring. Tests are hard and there is no textbook which leaves you only with class notes to study from, so take good notes and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Cudina is a great professor. Her lectures are easy to follow and she really cares about her students learning. The tests are a bit tricky...I ran out of time each test so definitely move quickly! Going to her office hours are helpful! She posts about 1 homework a week and theres 1 pre req exam, 2 midterms and a final (exempt if you have an A)

Cudina is the only professor choice for multiple upper level math classes. She is flowery in her rhetoric of math, but is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject. Keep up and ask questions, even if they seem silly. You will fall behind if you don't.
Pretty lenient teacher, very helpful in and out class, final exam is optional. Want to take an upper-div math, take this one, easy A.

She is kind of relaxed in teaching this course in that she doesn't seem to really care.  I mean, it's pass/fail, so the students don't seem to care either.  Most people do not have trouble with this course.

Great Probability instructor, but her exams can be pretty tricky.  The practice exams don't seem to help much on the actual exams.  She'll help you if you ask questions, but her exams can have questions on there where you can't even figure out how to start solving the problem.

Discussion section attendance mandatory (otherwise, lectures are optional). Botero and Cummings were both great lecturers, although only Botero provided study guides for the exams. The TA, Brittany, was very helpful throughout the course. Tests comprise ~80% of final grade. Exams mostly short-answer and fill-in-the-blank, class avg mid- to high-B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not usually review, but she was the rudest person ever for no reason. This class was SO MUCH HARDER than it had to be. Attendance was optional but not rlly. Maybe people would come in person if she wasnt so mean and passive aggressive about it and cold calling on students who look confused. She didn't accept my accommodations?? Is that legal?
Calls randomly on students during lectures. Tests are difficult.
Truly made this class more difficult than it needs to be.

I love animal behavior but Dr. Hutchins/Dr.Cummings made it extremely difficult. their tests were way too broad and detail-heavy with some of the things never even mentioned in lecture. They don't even provide practice problems or even a study guide. Also complains about people not attending lecture when they are so uninteractive. Do better.
Do not listen to the good reviews on here. She is not a great professor and does not seem to highlight the main points of her exams on the lectures.
I would not recommend taking this class at all.
So disorganized and lectures are barely covered on the exams. TAs are also very unhelpful and their exam reviews have nothing to do with the exam.
Does not provide practice exams or problems or even a study guide for her extremely difficult tests.
She is extremely unaccommodating and her exams are way too hard. She barely touched on half of the topics for the exam. Does provide extra credit though.
Exams are way too hard.
PLEASE listen to us!! Do not take her for this class. She does not teach properly and her exams are way too hard.
Awful professor.
awful professor

literally one of the worst professors at ut austin. her exams are not indicative of what is taught in lectures and focuses on the most high yield questions that were barely discussed in class. the class is also taught with dr. hutchins who is equally as bad. would NOT recommend.

She seems to be a well-respected expert in the fish behavior world. Her lectures aren't confusing but they are dense with content, which can be hard for non-neuro majors. The content she emphasized the most in lecture was not tested on the exam, rather it was on minor/less-focused details. She does not provide practice problems nor practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor ever. My biggest piece of advice is to show up to class and sit near the front. She explores the topic by having us contemplate the subject and encourages discussion, so you are missing a lot by watching online. I found this really useful during exams, as I could remember something based on my memories of talking it through.

When Dr. Cummings starts teaching in BIO 359K, the class ramps up and gets much harder. It also gets way more interesting. If you're interested in animal behavior, you won't want to miss out on her lectures.
Dr. Cummings is very big on participation. I found her test to be graded easier than Dr. Muth's, but they were harder. She also assigns readings. She is a very engaging professor!

Loved Professor Cummings. She is so passionate about animal behavior which is reflected in her lectures. She was always enthusiastic and made learning animal behavior interesting and fun. She taught the 2nd half of the class but overall 4 easy exams and one paper write up. Take her if you can!

Switched from another prof in the middle of the semester and had us take exams in person on paper instead of with notes online like we were used to. Very energetic and learned names, but overall not an exciting class. The reports took FOREVER to be graded along with the tests, and they were often graded harshly.

I took Dr. Cummings for Animal Behavior (although she only taught the second half of the class), and I loved her teaching style and enthusiasm. It definitely helps that this is my area of interest, but I always found lectures very engaging and enjoyed this class thoroughly.

While I wasn't the biggest fan of the course, Dr. Cummings is a good professor who genuinely cares for her students. Very helpful during office hours and added extra credit to the last exam. Beware of the TAs though as they grade unnecessarily harshly and provide little to no feedback on lab reports/exams.

This was by far the worst class I have taken at UT. Tests are random and difficult and papers are graded incredibly harshly with absolutely no feedback. She tries to keep the class engaged during lectures but everything is graded so hard that it doesn't even matter.

I loved Dr. Cummings and this class! Her tests are straight from lecture, so as long as you participate in her discussions during class and have a general grasp of the concepts you should be fine!
