The class doesn't have a lot of grades, which is unfortunate, but my test scores improved with each test, and she offers extra credit at the end to help!

Dr. Cummings was great! She made lecture very enjoyable and engaging, and gave very fair exams. Animal Behavior is also just a very fun class and I definitely recommend it to anyone who is a Bio nerd as well. I did not read the textbook and was completely fine, although she does recommend it. Make sure you do any mandatory readings!

Dr. Cummings is one of the best professors I have had at UT. The class is super interesting, but she is also just a great lecturer. Super understanding and cares about her students. Cannot possibly recommend her enough.

Dr. Cummings is so nice and always in good spirits. I took the class online bc covid so it may have been easier than normal. Tests were open note so I barely studied and did well. 1/4 of grade is a group research project where we were not given a rubric. There was a presentation and then a paper. I despise both research and writing but was fine
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a good professor! One thing is that she doesn't give you many resources outside of the lecture slides. no practice questions, no reviews, and the project at the end of the semester had unclear grading criteria. but she gives good lectures, the tests are straight forward & the class is generally easy if you put forth a lil bit of effort.

Makes the group project about her data from her research lab. The issue is that she doesn't give the master list and you'll be forced to score more than you need to(10 hrs of video). Asks for ALL of the data you scored at the end of year. No instructions on how the final paper/group presentation should be done and the TA is constantly in the dark.
Easy

Is overall a very skilled and caring teacher. I'm not a fan of sculpture, but I enjoyed learning new techniques and hearing her opinions in crit. Her class requires participation, but has a chill atmosphere and she'll check in on you to see if she can help with anything. Would definitely recommend.

Erin is the best! I took her Sculpture for Nonmajors class. There were 3 projects (found-object, wood, and metal), and Erin really wanted to help us make pieces that we liked. Overall, a very fun, engaging, and informative class. I would recommend it to anyone.

Core class taken for studio art major, no way around it, but I appreciate Erin. She's pretty chill and even when I thought a student was being very disrespectful towards her she just laughed and went along with it. I personally don't like sculpture too much but I still found enjoyment in the projects and her critique for everyone thoughtful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Penwell is ok. You will have weekly reflections due on Sundays, which you can begin writing only at the end of the week because you need the entire week's lectures to complete it. Rubrics aren't always clear. Shes definitely knowledgeable in her field, but just beware of the many writing assignments youll do compared to other professors.

Great prof with field experience, but totally disorganized. Extensive weekly papers and a ton of readings she never touches on during lectures. She does mix students up A LOT and does not seem to know who is who. Besides that, she is an OG who also works in the field while teaching and is a brutally honest person, which is rare, and I appreciate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Long weekly papers with no rubric and harsh grading. Only 2 allowed absences. She is not understanding yet is literally a SW professor. She mixes up students' names of the same race. She is so hard to work with. By far my most time consuming, repetitive class. DISORGANIZED! You will have to suffer for an A. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THE HIGH RATING!

She's very respected and knows what she's talking about because she is so experienced in the social work field. She's very funny and kind. She is willing to work with those who have personal issues, and the class is mostly based on papers and a group project as well as attendance. LOVED her! One of the best professors I've had.

Penwell is incredibly passionate! I appreciated her insights on SW. There are a lot of weekly papers, and the grading criteria can be unclear. Despite this, I really enjoyed the class! There's a group project 1/4 of your grade, which includes a roleplay aspect. I personally found it fun though! She cares a lot and is very accommodating, just ask!

Penwell is a great, very caring, compassionate professor. I recommend taking her, she is truly interested in her students. Class does have a lot of tedious assignments, though, but I do learn a lot. Weekly papers, service learning requirement, and a big dyad project, which was interesting and you learn a lot, but you roleplay in front of the class.
Professor Penwell is super passionate about the work she does. She is divisive only because she is so herself. Be open and honest with any concerns, she is responsive and will understand.

I really enjoyed this professor and the class, really makes you want to keep learning about social work. There was a big group project that was very interesting to do, weekly essays, and a final research paper. The professor is very nice, gives feedback, and is accommodating. We had very insightful discussions in class. Recommend prof and class!

Professor Penwell is extremely left-wing in a way that makes you feel isolated or like you're wrong about your beliefs if you have conservative ideals. Dropped the class because of this, but if you're looking for an easy A this class would be great as the only assignments are reflection papers based on the readings(probs write "liberally" though).
Great class, interesting topics! There is a bit of writing but its really not difficult, mostly reflections. The 'vibe' of the class is great and you learn a lot!
This professor was sooo cool and caring. She kept it real and the assignments were just a weekly reflection and one presentation at the end of the semester.

Can't recommend Penwell enough. Took her for 312, easily has become my favorite class I've taken at UT. She's incredibly insightful, passionate, and inclusive in her teaching methods. Clear communication, clear grading criteria, and flexible based on needs of the class. 10/10 recommend Open Door Preschool for service learning

I can't wait to take another one of Penwell's classes. Her way of lecturing is captivating and made me wake up for this class, even though it was early. It's a groups class so of course you're going to do group work, but Penwell keeps the divide equitable and makes the projects fun.

Professor Penwell was super nice and very adaptable! Each class we'd discuss a new topic/watch videos and I learned a lot. Easy grader too. There is a 2 page reflection every week but it was super easy to do

Loved taking groups with Penwell! She clearly cares about her students and is extremely open to feedback. Not sure if it was mostly because of the pandemic, but she was an incredibly lenient grader, I made a 99! Very approachable and understanding. Definitely recommend!

This professor is amazing! She'll make you work, but more importantly she'll challenge you to think. She really knows her stuff, cares, and is actually pretty funny too. I would take another class from her in a heart-beat. Highly recommend
This class was interesting, no assignments were hard BUT she did grade hard.....

The professor is highly critical of students. While she gives feedback on all presentations (there are multiple), she always finds things to deduct points for. Her critique is subjective, even if you argue your points, she is unlikely to give you your points back. You will not receive a 100 on any presentation. Just take it online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Marentes for Professional Comm. Studies in the spring semester of 2024 and she was amazing! There are quizzes after each chapter that are open notes, lots of presentations, and class participations. This class definitely helped me improve my presentation and communication skills. I thoroughly enjoyed her class and would take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Dr. LaBrake in Spring 2023. Rather than lecture, she posted videos online. Every Tuesday was an optional office hours, and every Thursday consisted of either two quizzes or an exam. The exams, which were multiple-choice, resembled the homeworks and the practice exams. She offered 1.5 percentage points of extra credit. The TAs were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: honestly, my fault i didnt put much effort into the class. requires memorization of a bunch of stuff fr, but helps with the mcat if you care about that. group quizzes

Dr. Labrake's class consisted of anywhere from 2-5 hours of online lectures from 2020-2021 a week, and you have to know exactly what she says in lecture for the exams. She was completely uninvolved in the class, and Ana and the other TAs were the only reason I was able to pass. If you have ADHD, get medicated (lol) or this class will be even worse.

I think I saw her in person a total of 8 times the entire semester. Pretty bad lecture videos from 2020. As a BME I didn't have much time to study for it, but the class requires a lot of studying to do well. Final replaces your lowest grade, but the tests are pretty hard (miss 3 questions you're already at a B). Weekly quizzes weren't too bad.

The exams for this class are difficult, but if you study a lot and put in the work you can still do well. Watch the lectures, watch the TA recordings, treat the HW like an exam, and study every week for the quizzes. It's a lot of studying, but if you put in the work it's pretty easy to do well.

Personally, I did not mind watching recorded lectures on my own time outside of class time. With that said, it is a pretty big time commitment. There is a significant amount of content every week, and although you have the materials, the learning and memorizing is completely in your hands. It's doable, and you'll truly get out what you put into it.

Mostly asynchronous class tested on lectures from COVID era. Mandatory attendance for in-person quizzes (individual, group). 1.5% extra credit on final grade, made grade cutoffs -0.5 what they were supposed to be on syllabus. My advice: pay attention to the lectures and take extensive notes over them. Lecture vids are boring, just take good notes.

Labrake records most of her lecture videos between 1 am to 5 am and as you can imagine she is not the most alert at this time. I know this is a hybrid class but it might as well have been online. I can hands down say she is one of the most uninvolved professors ever. The TA (Ana) carried the class more than the actual professor.

be ready to teach yourself. class structure is as follows: watch her lecture videos, at least 4/week of length between 20-60 minutes EACH & a weekly homework (3 attempts, sort of similar to exams), done before thursday (quiz day) then take a weekly quiz (an ind. MC 4 question part & FR group part). exams = hard & objectives are unclear sometimes

Dr. LaBrake's class follows a flipped style (learning at home and taking tests/quizzes in class). Take it if you have the motivation to study by yourself. It worked for me. Reading the provided notes helped. TAs and professor available during optional Tuesday classes. Optional activities, homeworks, and practice exams will help during tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Flipped class; some like it, some don't. Very consistent structure and you always had 1 week dedicated to exam studying. Teaching team (UGCAs + Ana) was amazing. Dr. Labrake and co. were always happy to help on Tuesday office hours (highly recommend going; their worksheet is usually similar to the quiz). Piazza was also great for asking questions!

Dr. Labrake provides online lecture vidoes that you can watch at own pace. In-class quizzes on one day, and other day is office hours. GO TO OFFICE HOURS.  Teaching team is great and they want to see you do well. Have to study for tests but it is straight memorization. Not much application. Lots of EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had a super fun time with this class. Me and my buds would have late night parties watching the lecture videos. I enjoyed that they took several hours because it helped pass the time. She was hilarious in them and super funny irl. Only complaint is that the class was a bit on the easier side. Would have enjoyed a greater challenge.

Class was so easy. I got bored at several times. I didn't watch the videos and I just looked at the student notes a couple minutes before the quizzes and did fine. But the videos were still high quality. Tests I just didn't even study, they were so easy. Labrake was always present and active, you can tell she's super passionate about what she does.

Overall, super easy class. Dr. Labrake is very caring, compassionate, and really wants to see her students succeed not only in this class, but in life as well. Tests were too easy. Quizzes were a joke, and part of it is done with a group. Overall, great experience and great MCAT prep.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was super easy. Just watch videos and study for 1 hr max extra for quizzes. Quizzes are a joke. Tests are super easy as well. Basic information don't really need to know the details. Dr. Labrake is awesome and will answer any questions you have about the material. TA Ana is awesome as well. Overall, easy class with easy tests. Lots of EC.

This class is a sad remnant of COVID. TAs did everything. Several hours a week of pre-recorded "lecture" videos from years ago, very disorganized and chaotic. Student notes taught the course better. You just cram those videos then take a quiz/test on Thursday. Felt like an assembly line being pushed through the content with minimal professor input.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Labrake is by far the worst professor. She doesn't teach a single lecture all semester and made the Tuesday class office hours. All of her "lectures" are prerecorded from 2020. Anything I   learned was just from TA Ana. Every Thursday is a test or a quiz. I would rather drop pre-med then take this class again.
TA Ana carried this class. Her office hours are the only thing that prepared me for the quizzes and exams. The actual lectures were very content-heavy and often confusing.

LaBrake's class is very difficult to keep up with. You basically never get a break, and I felt like she made it much harder than needed. 
- 3-6 hours of recorded lectures for hw weekly
- hw weekly 
- quiz every thursday
- exams every 3-4 weeks
It felt like a struggle throughout and quizzes/exams were much harder than the content viewed in class.

Why are we doing a flipped classroom in 2023? Thursdays are quiz and test days Tuesdays are literally just office hours or do ur own thing. my god this class has at least 4 lecture videos that are at least 30 minutes long per week. Say goodbye to ur social life when taking this class. I recommend going to Ana's OH and prey that u some how pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No lectures, only recorded videos. "Tuesday lectures" are office hours, "Thursday lectures" are MC and FRQ quiz (the same every week). Basically self-taught so you need to be attentive to the videos, study with friends! Frequently do active-recall when studying, exams are HARD! TA's and Labrake are super helpful and want to help you pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom. Labrake's lectures were hard to digest, so watch Andrey K or Pearson. Exams were not too difficult. Be careful on quizzes. Ana is the best TA! Lots of extra credit given & sometimes tests are curved.

The class material itself is fine, biochemistry is a heavy class by nature. I personally don't like the fact that she never lectured and just gave us pre-recorded lectures to watch. When she did try to teach she talks a lot and ends up convoluting it more. Get ready to teach yourself everything. The TA's help a ton.

Professor Labrake uses a flipped classroom, so you basically watch old pre-recorded videos on the topics being tested. Weekly quizzes were okay if you reviewed the TA notes the day before, and exams had a few tricky questions, but overall fine if you know the information well. Tuesdays were optional so learning is mostly independent.

Dr. Labrake's flipped classroom model emphasizes watching asynchronous lectures which can sometimes be dense. Grades consist mostly of exams and in-person group quizzes which are pretty easy to score well on, while exams are a bit tougher but fair as long as you pay attention to small details from lectures. Overall a straightforward class

Good class, but you have to learn everything yourself (flipped classroom). Choose what works for you - book, prof videos (very long), or external videos, keeping in mind the main goal is to MEMORIZE. Lots of little details and facts that WILL show up on exams even if not emphasized. With extra credit, easy A. Easy weekly quizzes, harder exams.

Dr. Labrake uses a flipped classroom model which frankly found extremely cumbersome. However, the class is very doable. There are plenty of resources and opportunities to build your grade. The material is quite difficult but read the textbook, watch the lectures, and show up for office hours and you will do fine in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Labrake really cares about students. Her flipped class is accommodating. Weekly quizzes are straightforward, exams consistently curved. Labrake does not actually teach though, as almost all content is from recorded videos. Take Labrake for an easy time. Don't expect to be inspired with biochemistry or fall in love with the material.

I learned quite a bit from Labrake through her pre-recorded lecture videos, but I do agree that sometimes I needed outside resources for clarification. Getting a high A is easily achievable if one put enough work to study, as most of the concepts are memorization based. Her course structure is designed to help students getting a good grade.

The class was mostly self taught where you watch videos each week on your own time and then come to class to participate in a group quiz and individual quiz. Personally I didn't like watching videos from 2020 and the exams were alright I guess. Class consists of weekly group quizzes, individual quizzes, clutchprep HW, and discussion hw, + 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class had a flipped setting and so it was up to us to learn via recorded videos, and then we would come to class to take weekly quizzes and tests.The quizzes were easy and part of the quizzes was group quizzes. The exams were difficult, but she gave so much extra credit and sometimes let us use cheats sheets which helped greatly.

Great class, but requires a lot of self-learning. Take the time to really understand, rather than memorize, Dr. Labrake's lecture videos along with the supplemental videos she provides as she lets you bring a notes sheet to the exams. She also offers enough extra credit to bump your letter grade up by 2 (e.g. B to A).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was way more work than it was worth done mostly outside of class. The tests were extremely specific and hard to study for, but I failed all three and will pass the class. Labrake herself is really nice and organized and teaches really well, but the tests were just too hard to do well on even after hours of note-taking and studying.

Overall, I really enjoyed Dr. Labrake's class. She organizes the content super clearly so you understand what is expected each week and what the quiz will be like. Group quizzes are manageable and tests are okay. Sometimes, learning the material was difficult though, since a lot of it is individual study, so it requires a lot of self-management.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend this class. Schedule is erratic, making it difficult for students who have jobs. She expects students to attend in person for our hybrid class outside of times listed originally listed on the syllabus. Obviously very out of touch with her students, she literally sends emails detailing her relaxing weekends and vacations.

It is so evident that Dr. Labrake would literally rather do anything else than teach. Old videos filmed at 2am in the morning that havent been updated since 2020 arent how we should be learning a subject that is so heavy on the MCAT. She should seriously consider how she can actually be a help to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The online, self taught format was not it. The videos were super old and not really helpful in actually learning the content. I did not feel prepared for the weekly quizzes since the videos were overwhelming being like 3-6 hours worth of content on top of homework and other assignments. I would avoid this prof :/

Labrake is kinda hit or miss for most... actually liked the whole flipped-classroom format since it gave more flexibility. I will say lecture videos can be improved quite a bit. She gives a weekly study schedule in each of her modules and I recommend adhering to it as much as possible bc it helps you stay on top of the content. Lots of EC!

a flipped classroom doesnt make sense for a complex course like biochem. recorded lectures were messy and outdated with no clear flow and i literally relied on some guy on youtube to do well on the last exam. office hours were meh and the TA's were not the most helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Loved this class! It's pretty much completely self directed, and you only have to show up for one period a week for a quiz and group quiz. She emails and tells you exactly what is going to be on quizzes and exams. She really made biochemistry really easy to learn and I highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs. This class was a tiring and a mess. EVERYTHING was self-taught with videos for you to learn within each week which was stressful. There was one TA in the class who would grade pretty difficult on the frq of tests. Would def not recommend this class if you don't want daily mental breakdowns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: her old recorded lectures glossed over the material too quickly and did not prepare students for the application based questions on exams. she emphasized "self-directed" learning and that was annoying considering how difficult the concepts are. this class was pointless bc i learned better from AK lectures & other videos. she's a nice person tho

this class was the absolute disaster. Very boring, confusing, and not clear videos posted to watch every week, and most of the time we were referenced to watch another videos because she knew that she did not teach enough at all as she should. I am really speechless and shock with very low rate of science professors at UT.

To even call her a professor I've had is a bit much since she used videos over a year old full of errors recorded at odd hours and videos she liked from youtube that replaced her lectures. I feel she tries to claim this is part of 'self-directed learning', but I feel there's a difference between encouraging learning and not teaching.

Probably the worst professor I have taken. She basically wasn't even a professor because she made her class a "self-taught" class. She left a bunch of undergrads to teach themselves biochemistry which is the worst possible thing anyone could do. Her videos are terrible! I learned by reading the textbook and watching a guy on AK LECTURES.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think anyone hates being a professor more. She wanted us all to be 'self-directed learners' which essentially means that we teach ourselves all of the course content and she does no work as a professor. She posts videos recorded over a year ago at 2 in the morning that are riddled with errors and expects the students to pick up minutia.

Dr. LaBrake is very nice, however, oftentimes I felt that she didn't enjoy teaching. At the beginning of the semester, we had 9+ hours of ClutchPrep a week (+ 3 hours of lecture videos pre-recorded). The exams weren't terrible (follow her Heads Up as a guide, but not your only study material), quizzes were easy & got 2 pts. of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her class was really structured. Weekly quizzes made studying for exams much easier and I felt like I left with a good understanding of biochemistry. She offered many opportunities for extra credit which helped a lot.

There is 3 exams + optional final. Weekly quizzes + homework that are fairly tough but help you learn. Test can be hard but fair but you have to study but she provides lots of resources like free clutch prep videos, extra hmwk etc. Dr labrake is very knowledgable and wanted us to succeed the TA's are very good also.

Although I was scared of this class, it ended up being manageable. I am not the type of person to attend every office hour, do every homework assignment, and invest all of my time into studying, but I still got an A. It was not difficult to get good grades on Sapling and quizzes, and I got a low B on every exam. Extra credit bumped my final grade!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is not as bad as these reviews makes her out to be. She emailed us every week detailing what we were going to be tested/quizzed on, and the questions being asked were over basic details. As long as you take good notes from her lectures and read the textbook, you'll be more than fine. The average grade for my class ended up being like a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Labrake made us have an exam on Election day 2020... She gives you topics to study for quizzes & exams but they get progressively more vague & inaccurate as the weeks went on. I felt like I would fully study her "Head's Up" email and still miss things because she didn't mention to study it or did not emphasize it in lecture.

Dr. LaBrake's class does not show clemency. The content is difficult (no matter what professor you have), the recorded lectures are dense and confusing, the homework is peripheral, and the tests are merciless. Ideas and topics were incohesive. If you have a solid 18 hours a week, you will probably be fine. Props for the extra credit though! Huge.

I am currently taking her online course because of COVID, so I don't know if it would be this bad in person. She posts almost 3 hours of lecture videos but still expects us to log in on Tuesdays for 1.5 hours to take a quiz. She expects more than 3 hours of our time a week for lecture and then assigns us a lot of homework on top of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Spring 2018. Class learning through modules, with comprehension checks and easy homework checks along the way. The exams are easy if you learn the modules, and the class overall is one where an A can easily be achieved if you work for it. Amazing lectures by the teacher, and extra credit through pop quizzes by attendance is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. Weekly quizzes to keep you accountable, but this makes studying for tests much easier. Labrake really cares about you learning the material and is very understanding/ constantly working to make the class the best possible environment to learn the material. Tests are straightforward. Take her for bch 369!!

this class is pretty easy but the amt of sapling she gives makes me literally want to kms. tuesday, thursday, and sunday. sometimes you have 2 due each day. each one takes like an hour, sometimes 2. that's literally 8 hrs per week dedicated to something worth 5% of the grade. such a waste of time

I was very disappointed with the content of BCH 369 (Spring 2019). She did not add anything to the lectures that the text book did not already cover. EVERY test and quiz had mistakes. The final was incorrectly graded due to the answer key being wrong. I do not feel that the tests were hard but she did add additional answers to throw you off.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you read the textbook and show up to class and ACTIVELY pay attention, this class is so doable. I also recommend going to her office hours as she makes it very clear of what she expects on the midterms. The final was fairly easy because she had prepared us so well all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is honestly an awful teacher. She would just scroll through her pwerpoints and never really explain the information in depth. She mostly just told us to read the textbook to learn more. I went to class every day but it was a waste of my time. I studied very hard (5+ hours) and still did awful on every test. Would NOT recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lot's of work, but it is doable. She gives you a heads up for the quiz and tests, and the test reviews are somewhat similar to the exam. HW and Quiz each week. I was not a fan of her lecturing style, since it's fast paced and not that organized. I did minimum work (studying the heads up, quiz, hw and reviews) and got a B.

Labrake was really fun for biochemistry. Her class is really easy and straightforward and you learn a lot. She gives a bit of extra credit and clearly defines exactly what information you need for the quizzes and tests.

I loved Dr. LaBrake's Biochemistry class (she started teaching it Fall 2018) and recommend taking her! The tests are straightforward, she makes the lectures interesting, and is always available for questions outside of class. I put in the work for the A, and got some extra credit, but the class was not unbearable. Would take again for fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't even go to class. Just do the reef stuff somewhere else and do other stuff. There are 4 tests with one drop test. I studied the night before each test by watching Albert and Jimmy's reviews for each week and doing the EP on canvas and got a 99.04. The final isn't all that bad. People hype chem to be super difficult but it honestly isn't bad.

Labrake is best described as "intense." My best advice is to make sure that you understand as you go because 302, unlike 301, heavily builds on each concept. But Labrake, while a little scatterbrained, really knows her stuff and is accessible outside class. She convinced me not to Q drop and I'm glad I didn't. Would take again.

Be wary that the lectures aren't there to teach you content, they exist to review it. I'll be the first to admit I skipped more than my fair share of lectures, but I do believe if you put in the effort of learning the modules before class, then show up to solidify what you've learned, you'll do fine with Labrake.

LaBrake is awesome! She is so quirky and funny, and she keeps your attention the whole time during lecture. She uses reef A LOT, so be sure to attend lecture. The learning exercises are effective at helping you learn the material, so make sure that you pay attention when you're doing those. She's super approachable/kind, so take advantage of that!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: LaBrake is one of the best chem professors in the department. Her lectures are super engaging and she knows what she's talking about. She goes a little fast so you really have to do the homework ahead of time, otherwise you won't understand what's going on. She has a few options for bonus points on tests, so look out for those opportunities.

She may seem a little scatterbrained at times but she does everything in her power to not only make sure we pass, but to make sure we understand everything she is teaching. Lots of good TA's and PLA's. Good reviews before exams!

Labrake was one of my favorite professors during the semester. While the class is challenging, if you do the Learning Exercises, ask questions, do the homework, and go to the TA's review sessions every Friday, you'll be good. Don't expect to go to class though and learn the material like high school. Do the work prior and ask q's while there.

If you are coming into this class with AP chemistry background, it will be a lot easier. However, do not slack off, because there is a lot of material to absorb. There were 8 tests throughout the semester (if you take a MWF class) & you have 30 minutes to take a 10-14 questions test. Honestly, it is enough time for most people, just dont cheat.

I learn by seeing the problem done step by step and explained why things are a certain way, but she does the problem on her own and I never know what I am doing. The textbook to me was not helpful at all. Goes too fast on the powerpoint and barley goes on a topic when all of a sudden she's on another.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Did not take AP Chem in high school, but had an easy time in this class. I actually learned from lectures, unlike previous reviews. Having the 8 tests makes it easier by having less material to study for. Many assignments get dropped at the end to help your grade. And the LE modules at home were a good way to learn IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: The structure of the course was changed this year to 8 exams, which causes you to spend more time studying throughout the entire semester. There is work for essentially every class. Labrake herself is quite scattered, requiring you to learn outside of class. However, her and especially Albert's reviews are worth going to and will help you on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is self taught, but you still have to go to lectures because she uses reef polling as a way of taking attendance that gets taken for a grade at the end of the term. The class is both homework and test heavy, which allows a lot of room for error as you can make up for any bad grades, although it is very time consuming.

Completely average professor. Easy if you took AP/Ib chem in high school. I honestly learned next to nothing from the lectures but had to attend for REEF points. Most of the learning is from the online modules that all the chem profs use. There are certainly worse professors but she is not one to inspire
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had no idea what to expect going into CH301 as a freshman, but I could tell from the first day that this class wouldnt be enjoyable. 8 tests and a final, REEF polling in class that makes attendance vital, and repetitive lectures that would be made useless by completing the LE's online. If youre taking this class, study on your own.

Dr. Labrake teaches kinda like a high school teacher, and does a lot of cool demonstrations in class. Don't skip class because she does a lot of reef polling. There's a lot of opportunities for reviews but be warned there's a lot of tests in this class.
She teaches almost like a high school teacher. Love her! So funny!

Everything is expected to be learned at home by yourself. Class is mandatory because of online polling. They make you buy their student handout which is just questions they want you to do in class, but the packet doesn't teach anything. Chem is so far the hardest class I have taken at UT (CH301 and CH302) because everything is self learn.
Cool professor. Tests count for alot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Completely average professor. I took for both CH301 and CH302, if I could have taken a different one if I would have. I honestly learned next to nothing from the lectures but had to attend for REEF points. Most of the learning is from the online modules that all the chem profs use. There are certainly worse professors but she is not one to inspire

It's not mandatory to go to class, but it's helpful. She makes us do in class clicker questions with REEF that's worth a grade, but one could do it from one's room. As far as material, we teach ourselves and she goes over and clarifies anything we have questions on or thinks we need extra practice in, during class. She's a little scatter brained.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. LaBrake cares a lot about her students and wants you to do well. In office hours she is really helpful and always happy to answer questions! The tests are all reasonable with enough preparation, and the course pack is a great help with that. Some people found her a little annoying, but I genuinely liked her and found her really funny and a joy

Assignments are due frequently, but they are not too time demanding or time consuming (although some can be). Although LaBrake was a good professor who cared about class understanding, you have to meet her halfway with effort. To study for exams I only did the supplemental worksheets she supplies us with and got an A on every exam. I recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. LaBrake runs her class very well, and has a quirky personality. An A in this class is very manageable, and she rewards participation. She seemed a little condescending at times by asking students what their major was if they said something intelligent, but overall good professor.

Not the best Chem professor, I probably wouldn't take her again and instead have another professor, as the others seem like they're much more interested in the subject material and go over it. I'd recommend to just find another professor, but if you're stuck with this one it's also okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I spent the entire semester having to teach myself just about everything for this class, as Labrake doesn't help during class and will only do "experiments" involving mixing water with something, instead of actually teaching you. This class was a nightmare, so many hours put into this compared to others. I couldn't stand it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hated this class, she didn't teach us a single thing and you're forced to learn it on your own. Believe me, she's not a good teacher, and it feels as if she hardly cares about her students.
Not as bad as everyone else says. She isn't the greatest but not the terrible teacher some make her out as. Although, her attitude rubbed me the wrong way sometimes.

It's a flipped classroom so technically the learning is done online. Lectures aren't necessary to attend except for REEF quiz points but you can sometimes get extra credit for participating. You could honestly learn an entire unit during the week of the test. I recommend going to her review sessions - she will tell you exactly what to study!

Don't take her for this class, you basically have to do everything yourself as she doesn't explain a single thing in class. All she does is give clicker questions and speeds through them for attendance so that's the only reason to show up.  Otherwise, all the work you have to do is at home and it's long and grueling. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I wasn't pleased with how the course was thrown at us. It's a learn by yourself and get quizzed in class everyday. She is insanely boring, and wow they need to work on getting interested curriculum. Also, she has office hours in a room that can sit no more than 4 or 5 people max and she teaches hundreds off students in each class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She doesn't teach. All she does is does in class is online polling and "experiments" that are suppose to reinforce what you are learning. THERE ARE BETTER TEACHERS. Avoid the hassle that is LaBrake.

Literally worst teacher ever. Does not teach anything all she does in class is mix salt in water every day or some other demonstration. Has never taught any topic or had us take notes on anything. In the process of dropping or switching teachers.

Not a bad teacher, and I suck at chemistry. However, is a flipped classroom, so be expected to read a LOT. If you memorize everything and regurgitate everything you're good. TA review sessions are really really helpful and probably the reason why I did well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Labrake often goes off on a tangent and gets distracted easily. It is hard to follow along and she does not make sure the class understands what she is teaching before moving on.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class wasn't bad at all, but there are better chem teachers. The tests aren't hard at all, you just have to look for old ones before you take them and go to reviews. You have to put in some effort in the class to get an A and actually show up as there are grades for attendance. Flipped classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed taking Dr. Labrake's chemistry course this semester, considering my horrible experience in high school. I held a strong prejudice towards chemistry until I took her class, and am happy I did. We learned some really cool things and look forward to next semester with her. With that said, I had to work really hard for my grade.

Flipped classroom was nice because it meant that I didn't have to go to class except for the polling. I would slack off until the week before the exam and then learn everything online through Clutch or the learning exercises. Hard material but if you put in enough work its manageable. I also wish tests were curved because its easy to mess up.

Basically, if you do homework on Canvas and go to class, this class isn't that hard. There is online polling that happens during class, but you can do that at home if you need to. Because of this, technically you don't need to go to class but I would suggest it. She's a pretty good teacher, even with the 200+ students class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is very straightforward. Do the learning exercises and homeworks then go to class to review over what you learned outside of class and ask any questions you have. Attendance is not mandatory but you do have to answer questions through an app that are posted at random times during the class that are easy to miss if you're not present.

As a Chem major, I saw this class as being a solid introduction to Chem and thought that the Prof did a good job. While the class is very crowded, the lectures a bit less helpful than I would've liked, and a bit of a heavier workload, I thought she was a funny and engaging teacher.
Flipped class and lecture were awful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A funny professor, but she is not clear in class and often rushes over things. Her tests are hard and there is no curve or forgiveness in them. A good TA and asking TA's/PLA's questions during class is essential. There's also a lot of homework and learning modules to do on your own outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very nice person, if that matters to you when looking at a professor, but lectures run off topic very easily and it is hard to understand what the professor is trying to say. Tests are fairly easy, but you do have to study many days in advance if you want an A.
Awful class. You won't learn anything during class time, but attendance is still taken via an online app every day and its a huge waste of time. The only way to learn is if you have a good TA

She literally spends more time trying to figure out her computer than teaching. Don't learn anything in class. Homework and learning modules all online. The only way to learn is from TA lecture hours. Will not do anything in class.
cool
This class was definitely a flipped classroom. Laude/Labrake was a very good combo. Class was interesting and tests were easy-medium if you looked at review videos and attended office hours.

This class is really taught by three professors, which is an interesting set up. It's a flipped classroom, so you learn the material and quiz over it and then review in class that week. They all really care about the students understanding the material and doing well in the course, and test expectations are made crystal clear. Highly recommend.

Ch 301 is easy because she is only the secondary professor (either vandenbout or laude as primary), and thank god for them. She gets distracted very easily, and it's questionable whether she even knows the information. Not to mention she is extremely rude in a "trying to be funny" kind of way. You cant really avoid her, but just be prepared.

Make sure to pay attention because she tends to ramble and you'll want to follow her train of thought. She is also a little disorganized. However, she is very approachable and you feel comfortable speaking up in that class even though it is a 500 person lecture.

Cynthia is a good professor, however her lectures can be extremely boring. They drag on for what seems like forever! Some of the material is really dense too and she doesn't do a great job of explaining. Be prepared to have to read the book and go to ALL of the TA's review sessions (they really help).

Very good professor. Ch 302 was a bit harder than 301, but it is doable with the grading they have in place. They use a "blended" classroom style instead of completely flipping it, so some learning is done at home but they still lecture over it to reinforce it during class. I found this helpful since all of the materials were online.
Fairly easy and simple class, I'd recommend her.
Easy Class, Easy Tests, I enjoyed going to class. Good professor

Expect to pay attention in class or be very lost! Clear lecturer when she's on a roll, but loses her train of thought often. There's in-class worksheets for most lectures which are good if you like working in a group. Quest HW is challenging but similar to the tests. There's also a free response portion to the test similar to the worksheets.
Make sure to keep up with everything. If you do, you'll be fine. 4 Exams(60%)(One Gets Dropped), Participation Points(15%) (iclikers,hws,learning modules), Final(25%).
Excellent prof, makes the material very engaging.
she really cares about her students learning the material, this is a flipped class so there is an expectation to do the assigned homework in order to do well

Always excited to teach chemistry. Gives out candy to students that participate. Pretty straight forward on the material, though most you learn through modules. Homework is on Quest and tests are Quest-based.
4 tests and a final, but drops the lowest grade
She is a great Professor and makes lecture worth going to!
Labrake is a really great teacher. I highly recommend her. Her lectures are fun and she covers material really well.

LaBrake is awesome! Her lectures are very fun and interesting and she keeps the material very concise as to not overwhelm you much. She is a very fair grader as she offers times for extra credit points.  Above all, she is very funny/smart and really cares about the progress of her students! I highly recommend her.  She rocks!

labrake is an awesome teacher who cares about her students. the notes are online and are powerpoints. if you ever have any questions, she is readily available to help you. the class is pretty easy and the final exam was not heavily weighted. i recommend her as a chem prof. and plus... at the end of the semester, we made ice cream. =)
No Comments

The lectures don't help preparing for the exams. The exam depends on the textbook and I think it's silly you have to study so many terms but only like 15 terms show up. The tophat is everything because it's hella extra credit. It'll boost you up by a whole letter grade. Go to every class!! The lectures don't help but it's extra credit.

Took this class as a Kinesiology major, super textbook heavy. He gives up to 10pts extra credit for showing up to class and doing the attendance. Pretty interesting guy and he likes to yap but lectures are pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the textbook is your holy grail, and i NEVER read textbooks. if you study and pay attention, it is relatively easy to get an A, bc 90+ counts as an A. 10 extra credit pts possible if you attend the class. it's heavy as any course w this prof but worth it imo. all memorization, but no cumulative exam. i'd recommend for pre health students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: he's easy to reach outside of class and the lectures are usually interesting. however, take something else if your schedule is already heavy. i'm stem and it was practically more material than my cores. he gives 5 pts of extra credit but you need to start that project YESTERDAY. i got away w/o reading much but you will need that textbook :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny professor, you can tell he cares. Always happy to help you. However, the class is extremely heavy on readings and weekly homeworks. Attendance and participation throughout lectures are part of your grade through TopHat. If you like learning about Greek Mythology, absolutely take his class, but look elsewhere for an easy low effort VAPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis made an already fun class even more interesting and engaging. In CC303 (Intro to Classical Mythology), you learn about many Ancient Greek/Roman gods, heroes, and background. Such an interesting topic was made even more fun with Dr. Curtis. He was hilarious, chill, and engaging with his students in the class. I never once felt bored.

The fact that he counts 90 and up to be an A, not A-, makes sense with how heavy the work is. I had more work and was more fatigued with this class than calculus 1. That being said, if you are (also) a nerd and come in with foundational Greek/Roman mythology knowledge, you will be fine. Just don't miss lectures and FILL IN THOSE WORKSHEETS PROMPTLY
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: dr curtis rocks, just prep for a lot of reading. he's lenient on grading, is very knowledgeable about his lectures, and has fantastic TAs that provide great feedback. i found his class really enjoyable to be in!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis's class is great in terms of quality, but the workload is pretty excessive for an intro VAPA class. There are MANY readings that must be done, and lectures are necessary for grades and test prep. Extra credit is generous, so you can get a high grade if you put the work in. Tests require a decent memory but aren't difficult in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Coming into this class I was naive thinking it'd be a low effort, easy class there are in class quizzes and bi-daily HW. However, Curtis lectures in an engaging and fun style that helps you learn and stay engaged. Test include essays but are graded lightly ( I came into the class with no knowledge of mythology) and they are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor and funny guy. Lots of outside of class work though

Dr. Curtis is very kind and funny! The course can be a lot of work, especially for a VAPA, but the topic is interesting. Assigned readings before every lecture and sometimes online textbook work as well. The tests are open note and straightforward, but preparing the worksheets for them does take a sizable amount of time

This class is harder than it needs to be, I shouldn't be worried about getting an A in a VAPA. Funny lecturer but expects a lot, study lots for the exams.

Dr. Curtis is a extremely kind man! He keeps everything light hearted which always makes me always look forward to his lectures. Super interesting class---you get to learn about a lot of enlightening language material. Just put the time in and study on quizlet and you'll be fine.

Amazing professor! One exam gets dropped, and attendance is extra credit! I would highly recommend taking this professor. Lots of memorization, but that is what you sign up for when taking med term.

Only downsides are too much assigned reading (but you can skip most of it) and lectures are boring if you don't care for mythology.

Dr. Curtis is a good professor and his grading policy is amazing, this class is just unnecessarily time consuming and difficult.

Dr. Curtis's lectures were interesting and engaging. Attendance isn't mandatory but leads to extra credit and easier test prep. Make sure to read and comprehend his assigned readings. The example tests and review sheets are helpful for exam preparation and he usual pulls a test question or two directly from those materials.

Dr. Curtis cares for his students and wants them to succeed, however, the class can be difficult at times. You are expected to learn 200 terms as well as understanding Latin grammar per test, usually every two weeks. We had 7 tests (lowest was dropped), no final, and up to 10 points extra credit by going to class and answering questions correctly.
The course is easy, lectures are interesting, and homework is light.

The class starts off difficult but gets easier as you go on. Dr. Curtis is very straightforward with what he expects on tests, even if they are frequent. Find good quizlets for the tests (1 of which is dropped) and you'll have no problem making an A in the class. If you're struggling, go to class and take advantage of the extra credit (up to 10%)!

This is a HARD CLASS. Id say minimum 300 terms per biweekly test. However, Prof Curtis drops the lowest grade and offers up to 10 POINTS of extra credit. EC is earned through in-class questions that are typically super easy.  Feel free to use my quizlets, look up Ben_RO2 and I should have a folder labeled med terms. READ THE CHAPTERS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is genuinely an enjoyable teacher to have. His lectures and participation are crucial for this course but he makes it very engaging, so I thoroughly enjoyed the course. This course is based on textbook readings, participation, and tests. Progressively it becomes an easy course, just show up to class and engage as much as possible.

Class starts pretty hard, but it gets better. I'm neutral about Dr. Curtis himself - he is a bit type A but certainly not evil, he tries to be friendly. Very generous extra credit if you go to class. You will need to make flashcards and memorize tables right from the beginning if you want a good grade. TopHat homework is basically free 20% of grade

A lot of the reviews on here will scare you from this class but I honestly loved it and it deserves a lot of credit. I got a 34 on our first exam but BELIEVE me it gets easier. This class is very vocab and study heavy but if you have the study skills to do it, this will be the easiest class ever. Dr Curtis is very kind but very strict on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: grade is from hw and tests, all graded objectively. ec every lecture but had to be present to answer right, theres a ton and can get up to 10% ec. tests are memorizing terms w a little history. ended the class w 97.8 he doesnt round or curve. there are 7 tests one is dropped no final. tests are only 50 qs but there are 400 terms to know for each

This class was unnecessarily difficult. There's a lot of readings and constant in-class quizzes. There's also one extra credit assignment- do it. The way the class is set up, you'll definitely need to do the extra credit if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Found the content super interesting and fun. Basically reading/learning about Greek and Roman mythology. Straightforward tests and essays/ID were directly from the reviews. Up to 5 points EC. However, exorbitant workload with 3 different textbooks and up to 15 pages of reading every 2-3 days. TLDR: fun but a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly did like the content of this class, but the structure of it really made me struggle. It was easy to find what readings you needed for class, but Dr. Curtis would post so many assignments only on tophat, and I wouldn't see them until it was too late. I was able to do fine on the tests while hardly doing the readings though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't have to take this class, DON'T. He talks more about how great he is and weird, unnecessary historical trivia than medical terminology which the class is literally titled. I also don't understand why this was basically a language course... he's seriously the most un-understanding humans I've ever met.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't understand how he has such a high rating. He's a bad lecturer and an annoying professor. His jokes are crappy, his lectures are borderline useless and his tests are weird. The homework readings are interesting are doable but that's the best part of the class. Wouldn't recommend.

If you want an easy VAPA, don't take this one. Yes, it's interesting. No, it's not impossible to do well, but this class is super annoying; thankfully the tests were easy. Dr. Curtis is nice and a cool professor but not a good lecturer. He speaks in run on sentences and I can never tell what his point is during the lectures. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is by far one of my favorite classes at UT! Dr. Curtis is a phenomenal lecturer, so attending class, while optional is your best bet to scoring well on the exams. Class is structured very well where you have an exam every other week, and in class Extra Credit via tophat. The first two exams are tough, but after that it's quite intuitive.

Honestly, I think this class was easy, but I took it as a freshman when I didn't have much going on. Sophomores and juniors said it was easy but hard to balance with ochem, physics, etc. I would take it when you don't have much going on because you will have to dedicate time to it, but after a while it is very repetitive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory, but highly recommend attending (gives extra credit). The only thing about this class is that it is a lot of memorization. Each quizlet I made had at least 200 terms.  Practice tests have questions that are on the exam so look over it.

Don't be scared of the ratings, everyone who did bad procrastinated. Readings & worksheets are doable WHEN DONE ON TIME! Open note tests, impossible to fail with good worksheets. Test essays are graded easily. In-class tophat questions are weighted heavily. If you like Gr. myth or Percy Jackson, you'll like this. Dr. Curtis is very knowledgeable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is SO unnecessarily hard. It's an intro class, sir. We are not trying to be greek mythology majors. I was expecting to read greek mythology stories, but you have to read his confusing textbook. Every class textbook homework, and worksheets on the readings. He tries to trick you with his questions, which is stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was the highlight of my semester. He was so funny and kind. I took CS303 as my VAPA so it wasn't my priority but I had a lot of fun. This class requires the time to read and take notes but if you put in the work, you will do well. Going to office hours to get to know him is highly recommended - he really cares about his students!
Best prof on campus, so nice and funny. Definitely get to know him if you can because he's so interesting and wants to get to know his students!!

I only took this course for 3 days before I decided to drop it. The grade distrib seemed so good but upon joining the class, I saw that the amount of work is INSANE for a VAPA. 60 pages of dense text to read per night and the exams are all essay heavy/graded harshly. Absolutely not. Dr Curtis seems nice though. Pick an easier VAPA. This is a TRAP!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: His Lecture Slides were a mess, It was like a dictionary without definitions, you will be facing a bunch of Latin word roots or pre/suffixes which you will have no place to google and the only way to get explanations is from his mouth. Honestly the Lectures are great and interesting. If you Take it, Don't Miss a Single Class!! YOU SKIP YOU FAIL.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved the information I learned in the class but Dr. Curtis can be rude. I asked for help a couple of times through email and at one point, I got a response so condescending that I began looking for ways to drop the course. Bewwwaarreeee
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class needs a lot of work outside of class due to the amount of terms you have to memorize. Even so, I thought Dr. Curtis was hilarious and I feel like I learned a lot! That said, your grade depends a lot on your test average, but there are 10 points of extra credit so it's easy to get a good grade (if you attend class, that is).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tests were difficult because they are all memorization of hundreds of words and terms. Homework is long but half of the grade is participation. Extra credit is extremely helpful and without it, it would be very difficult to make an A.

He is a nice professor but the class itself is very rigorous and requires a lot of memorization skills, especially with the course being test-heavy. Attendance in the class is not mandatory but it is helpful to go in person. Most of the PowerPoints used are not detailed. Otherwise, this class is interesting and he is an easy professor to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis as a person irritated me greatly. Every two weeks, you must memorize approximately 350 flashcards, and the course is unquestionably difficult. He is more concerned with learning Latin and strange history than medical terms, which was frustrating.  Despite the fact that this class offers up to ten extra credit points, it is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is fine. His biggest flaw is that he simply moves too quickly during lecture and spends too much time on unnecessary information. While the lecture is tough to keep up with, quizlet and the extra credit can help earn a grade. Exams are fairly straightforward, but he includes some questions that are destined to irritate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He seems passionate about what he's teaching. I see so many people complain about him and his policies but IDK what they expected from a college course. He gives you strict deadlines & everything you need to pass (lots of memorization!). You test every other Friday & no final (tests  lecture-heavy) + extra credit opportunities in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Curtis is a neat guy, seems to know what hes talking about but definitely do not recommend taking his course unless you already have a general understanding of latin and greek terms and declensions. Very hard to study for his class because theres just so much to remember! Not to mention he doesnt curve or allow extra credit. Cool dude but beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not accommodating at all. Truly has very little empathy for his students and gets shocked when his test averages are in the 60s and 70s. Would not take again. Only good things is that he's passionate about his content but overall he's not supportive outside the classroom.

He is one of the most condescending professors I've ever had. I had an emergency and couldn't submit an assignment and he was so dismissive he just did not care. He doesn't care about his students and the lectures require a lot of notes and a lot of hours goes into studying the vocab. If you're not pursuing medicine then don't even bother with him.

med term was very doable! your grade is made up of 80% exams (there are 7, one is dropped), and 20% hw. the hw is time consuming, but it's easy and very helpful practice for the exams. the exams are very straightforward; quizlet is your best friend. the first two exams are the foundation, so know them well. also, LOTS of EC is built in!

I absolutely loved Intro to Classical Mythology! Dr. Curtis was so funny and knowledgeable on the various myths and culture we explored throughout the course. The lectures were always so fascinating and I wish I could take this class again because the course material was so interesting! The coursework and tests were easy if you did the worksheets.

Professor Curtis was a great teacher for CC 303. He offered many chances of extra credit, totally to 13 points added to the final average. The homework would sometimes be tedious, with copious amounts of reading and writing. For tests, he outlines what the test will cover, with exact same questions and essays on the test.

Curtis is a gem! This class involves A LOT of memorization, but he gives so much EC so it's honestly really easy to get an A. Just put in the work. Work hard on the first two units, and the last exams become much easier. Highly recommend for anyone planning on going into health professions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor is so condescending its not even funny. Everytime I asked him a question he is very rude and dismissive.

I highly recommend Dr. Curtis's class, especially if you're pursuing a career in medicine. He is a serious professor, but is incredibly knowledgeable and might you give credit for missed HW/quiz questions if you email him. Lectures are very straightforward and interesting. Test heavy - 7 exams, but they are fair and he offers LOTS of extra credit.

Dont underestimate this class. It can be pretty tedious when you have to remember a bunch of words, rules, and history. Ofc, if you study and put in the work then it should be slight, especially with the EC and HW. The first two exams/modules are pretty much the foundation to the other tests so remember your declension and vocab.

dr. curtis is awesome, has a odd sense of humor in lectures which make them interesting. this class requires a lot of effort to get an A in but as long as you study, watch the lectures, and take notes, the tests are a breeze. he offers a lot of extra credit and drops one test out of like 7, lots of memorizing but you will learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mr. Curtis class was great! I had some prior knowledge to medical terminology, but his class really taught me many more things I didnt know! He offers a good amount of extra credit, and his lectures were always interesting to view, pretty test heavy- 7 tests, but lets you drop one & are pretty fair, he doesnt give you anything not in lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot of mythology to memorize but I took the course because I wanted to learn all about it so I didn't mind. Maybe not the easiest VAPA but honestly super rewarding and if you like mythology it makes studying so much easier

Like any other class, the TAs can make or break you. However, if you're interested in mythology, you'll enjoy the work you put in. Dr. Curtis may seem intimidating but he's a really caring and funny person that wants you to succeed. It's not that hard to get an A, but that doesn't mean you can sit back and do nothing and still expect high marks.

Idk why there are so many bad reviews. Dr. Curtis is very engaging and sometimes tells mythology like a story with different voices and it's just very fun to witness and learn in his class. He gives you worksheets that verbatim make up the test and the answers to the worksheet questions are given through lecture. Take good notes and you'll be fine.

Not bad of a class, it's very structured and very predictable since the tests and homework are very similar to each other. Once you get into the rhythm of the class, you'll be good. Do ALL of the extra credit, gives you up to 10% bump on your grade. It'll be tough in the beginning since it's almost learning a new language because of the grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: boring lectures. Wanted to learn medical terminology, not latin history
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy A. Bi weekly exams based on lecture. First 2 were harder, then they got easier. Just exams and homework assignments due every other week. Overall good class, although kind of boring. But what would you expect ya know. It was annoying always having an exam to think about though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Todd Curtis is the goat. Although you take exams every other week, the material isn't intimidating and the grading is very fair. There are great extra credit opportunities and lectures are the most important thing. Not bad at all.

The class offers up to ten points extra credit and 90+ is an A. The grading criteria makes the course manageable, yet there is a lot of memorization. Student-created Quizlets are very, very helpful for test preparation.

Curtis is a gem! He is so passionate about what he teaches. The homework quizzes are due every MWF for extra credit and the textbook exercises are due the week of the test. Tests aren't bad if you study the review sheets. Make Quizlets and study the terms from the lecture. The lectures don't have subtitles so you have to pay close attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis incorporates a lot of history into his lectures and personally I wasn't a big fan of it. The tests are usually made from his lectures, so study your lecture notes. There is also TopHat assignments that are 20% of our grade. There is a TON of extra credit and he drops our lowest test grade. No final! Get ready to memorize a lot of stuff!

Dr. Curtis is really passionate about what he teaches. I am not a huge history nerd, but I actually thought this class was really interesting and am glad I took it. This is not a super easy A and you will have to put in a decent amount of time (extra credit available though!), but I think it is definitely worth taking.

Really really hard class. I'm a biochem pre-med major that came into Freshman college with 60 credit hours and this class was the hardest I've ever taken so far. Really hard and specific tests that have questions out of nowhere. Did give 10% extra credit ontop of 80%test and 20% book work though. Would not recommend for flag class or easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a slow talker in his lectures but they are helpful for the tests. Tests are every other week, so prepare to spend a lot of time studying very frequently. The amount of terms is daunting but if you stick with it you can get an A. He offers up to 10 extra credit percentage points on your final grade.

Dr. Curtis is in my top 3 favorite professors. He is one of those people whose mannerisms and somewhat corny remarks make him hilarious. He is always authentic yet professional during his lectures and its sad I have not had more professors like this. If you are amused by innocent unintentional humor, he is the walking embodiment of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grades way too specific. Boring and monotone
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is the most boring and monotonous person I have ever come across in my life. I have to watch all the lectures at twice the speed to cancel out that awful aspect. On grading- if you don't have every answer exactly the way he wants you too (which he often doesn't tell you) then he will give you zero credit for that answer. It stacks up

Wow this class is information overload. Basically there are 7 tests that count for the majority of your grade and you have to memorize all of the vocab to have a chance at passing the class. You definitely have to put effort into but the professor is cool and its obvious he knows his stuff. Not an easy elective at all but theres is extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a great professor. He genuinely cares about his students and provides a bunch of help to allow us to get a high grade. All my friends in the class also loved him! The only people who disliked him were the ones not willing to put in effort for the class and expected to still get an A. Interesting material, fairly easy, and fun class!

only take this class if youre premed/prehealth! Everyone else will suffer.   U have a test every other week. It can be a lot of work but hes a good lecturer and an A is attainable if u actually do the work. I got As on all the tests but ended up with a B in the course bc I forgot to do a couple top hat activities (20% of your grade)

NO FINAL! Had a test every two weeks (7 total, 1 dropped), assignments on tophat are 50% participation, and he offers up to 10% EC on top of your final grade. You can tell he loves what he is teaching, and he makes lectures as fun as possible. it was required to buy the textbook (i think) but I honestly never used it. Take this class for GPA boost!

This class killed me. Take an easy VAPA and this is really not it. This class was easy at times but Dr. Curtis was not at all understanding of outside circumstances and the TA's graded like we were getting our doctorates in mythology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst that UT has to offer. The grade distribution paints a deceiving picture, b/c even though about 50% make an A, about a quarter of the class drops this class, so really, not that many people make an A. He's really one of the most inconsiderate professors I've had, he's made this class so difficult, and ruined my entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No final! Test every two weeks, but all multiple choice and mostly vocab. Lot of memorizing, but the practice tests are really helpful. Pretty easy A if you try because he gives a lot of extra credit. Up to 10 points on the final grade by attending class and answering questions on the online classroom page. Pretty good class overall.

Dr. Curtis really cares about his students and offers them many resources to succeed. The textbook by Nath is honestly super helpful in studying and has a lot of practice opportunities. He assigns tophat homework, but doing that homework is pretty much studying at the same time. Offers extra credit for attending lecture; great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis's lectures were interesting and enjoyable to attend. Tests were totally doable if you went to lecture and did the homework (not difficult, just do it). Easiest A at UT so far, and I feel like I learned a lot too.

He's a fine professor, but don't take his class if you have misophonia. Constantly clears his throat extremely loudly, straight into the microphone. I could barely sit through his lectures it was so bad. Luckily, his tests are almost all vocabulary, so you don't actually need to go to class.

Professor Curtis is an amazing professor if mythology is your thing. However; if you are just taking this class to gain a VAPA credit I would highly not recommend this class because of the many hours you will spend reading and studying for an honest grade. I do not regret taking this class because of the work ethic I gained from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't be fooled by the grade distribution on the chrome extension. This class is A LOT OF WORK and if writing and analyzing is not your strength, then this is NOT your class to take. Be wary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.
