reviews.comment: dr curtis is a super cool guy! hes awkward but in a funny way. med term was pretty hard at first, but once i got the hang of it i did fine. attendance is optional but the tests have specific questions only covered in the lectures and the extra credit offered during lectures is helpful. i skipped a lot of lectures and still ended up doing fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got an A on every single test. This is the only class where all nighters worked for me because I waited the last day to study. Take his practice tests, they are almost the same as the exams. Know every single term in his lectures!! All of the terminology is from his lectures. Use the book if you missed what the term was during lecture.

Overall the class is very easy if you grind and put in the effort. You always have the chance to make an A. Made two C-'s and an F on the first 3 tests, but managed to get an A in the class. Homework is difficult and you will most likely make lots of mistakes and get demoralized if you don't get help. Dr. Curtis is a funny guy and I enjoyed class.

This class is basically a vocab class . Lots to memorize but pretty interesting class. He had lots of extra credit ( up to 10%) and his tests are fair. Homework is a little hard because its so specific so I would recommend doing it with a friend . NO FINAL :)

Dr. Curtis gives a lot of opportunities to improve your grade throughout the semester, the hardest part of the class is probably figuring out the latin grammar, other than that its just memorizing terms and historical facts. His tests are very very similar to the practice tests he provides.
Really funny professor and easy class. I always studied the night before the exam and got an A. Pure memorization and a grade above 90 is considered A+!

He posts all of his slides and material on Canvas so you can easily go back and access anything, but most of the information you get from the lectures so I strongly advise going to class if only for the 3-5 extra credit questions at the beginning of class every day (which are only over the last lecture so get ready to use that Ctrl-F)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is so difficult simply because the test are every two weeks on Friday morning and you have to know about 200-300 terms per test. Lots of the words are extremely similar and the lectures aren't always very clear. Yes, in class participation is extra credit, but he makes the test so hard that if you don't go to class you will do very bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved taking medical terminology! Professor Curtis really makes an effort to make his lectures interesting and engaging. This is definitely one of the most useful classes I have ever taken. You're essentially learning Latin and thus, can easily apply what you learn to figure out medical jargon. It's a lot of memorization but worth it in the end!
I hate taking med term. It is a hard class and it is very unclear what I have to study for the test. Material is very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I have no idea what is going on. Studying for this garbage is so hard, since you just try twice until you get it wrong and have to wait to the next day to see the answers.

Dr. Curtis is hilarious. He is a genius in his own right, and he is super engaging. I loved taking medical terminology with him. Plus he's a super cool guy to just chat with -- Go to his office hours! If you need help with anything whether its TopHat or life advice, he's always available and willing to chat.

This class has interesting lectures and the professor seems alright. However, the TAs grade hard and count of points for basically anything. He even gives you the questions beforehand but you don't get to know the correct answer for the short answers. Lots of readings and the TAs are really awful.

Super funny guy! Get ready to read and a whole bunch of dad jokes. One of the easier As at UT but that doesnt mean you dont have to study. He gives you worksheets and basically the answers through lecture and those worksheet questions are the exact ones on the test so just study those.
Amazing professor!!!!!!!! Great lecturer and great human. HIGH KEY RECOMMEND!!!

This is the second class I've taken with Curtis and he's still in my top two profs. Grades are simple: There is SO MUCH to read for almost every class and an accompanying quiz. There is a attendance poll but other than that no checking for att. and The Exams are straight forward essay and SA. Expected difficulty for a Upper-Div class but he's fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: SO if you are new to the subject of mythology DON'T take this class. You have questions that will be on the exam beforehand, but there is no guaranteeing your answers are right. Keep up with the readings. Lectures were okay but there's so much information you have to remember for the exams. If you are taking this class form a small study group!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this was the hardest class I have ever taken! The lectures were confusing and the textbook even worse. The TA's grade over every little thing, including spelling. The tests are super long and you only have 50 minutes to finish everything, and you needed to know so much information for just one test. For your own sanity, don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The textbook was available online in PDF so you don't need to buy it! Attendance wasn't mandatory but extra credit is given during lecture using TopHat and it was a lifesaver to get that A at the end of the semester. You should do well if you do all your TopHat exercises, extra credit, and get at least a B on your tests.

He gives up to 10% extra credit in the class based on attendance and top hats!! He's absolutely amazing and this was legit my favorite class last semester! His lectures are fun to listen to, and normally you can study for the tests the day before and still do decently well on it. One of the easiest classes at UT by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is awesome! He truly cares for his students and is interested in the subject matter he is teaching. Take medical terminology! It is an easy A!! Every class there are opportunities to make extra credit on your final grade - up to 10 possible points added to your final grade (a whole letter grade!!) For tests just do the practice tests.

This professor wrote a book that is full of grammar errors, and expecting everyone to pay around 40 dollars for this middle-school writing style book. Also, at the same time he agreed with the TAs that our essays should get harsh grading while we only have around 30 minutes or less to write one. This should give you a idea what kind of class it is.

Awful class, take something else. Piles of reading every single day, study guides that are 20 pages long, and TA's that take points off your essay for misspelling a super confusing Greek name. This class was insane. Biggest mistake of my college career and now I need to make up for it. Don't roll your dice, take literally anything else - please.

This lecturer taught the class badly, because he never provided one definite answer of the worksheet he created. There was never a guideline about what answer is determined correctly on the test, which made our studying extremely difficult. Please avoid this class!!!

He makes this class way more difficult than it could have been. The TAs expect you to write perfect essays when you only have 50 mins for 10 ID questions, 5 short answers, and an essay. They take points off for very EVERY little things, so it makes it very challenging to get an A. Even without the harsh grading, the class was too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor did not know how to lecture at all. He constantly talked out of topic and never provided editable answer for the worksheets. Just a horrible class structure, and 20% of people drop out of this course.

This professor is very passionate about his class. If you've taken some type of physiology or medical terminology in the past, this should be a breeze. If not, just ask old students for old tests and learn everything on there. He likes to recycle. His grading system is very fair. His lectures get boring but doable. Would take this class again!

Extreme amount of work for a VAPA. Attendance questions for accuracy every day, 4 exams, every exam you must memorize 200 short answer, 10 essays, and 50 identification questions. TAs graded very harshly on exams so the class as a whole was under a lot of stress the entire semester. He does give extra credit, this course was insanely stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DIdn't care for his personality or backhanded comments about students. Lectures were pretty bad and test questions didn't always make a lot of sense with him never fully elaborating on them during class. That being said, you know exactly what is expected of you for an A and with an unnecessary amount of effort (especially for a VAPA) it is doable.

This class is too much work for an intro VAPA!! 4 exams, tophat quizzes almost every class, and a lot of textbook readings. It might sound nice that he picks questions from worksheets that he gives you before hand, but you have to prepare 200+ short answer questions, and outline for 10 essays ahead of the exam, and memorize all of them for exams.

One of the worst in the university! He normally talks random stuff throughout the entire lecture, never providing any sample response for the student!! Also, he disdains students quite often during his office hour.

The lectures, readings, and his online textbook were all interesting. There's a lot of reading, but be strategic about it. His tests involve short answer and essay, but you have all of the questions and prompts which he will address in his lectures. If you can fully answer around 60-75% of your compiled study guide, odds say you'll ace the test.

I had Dr. Curtis for Ancient Greek Medicine. He's hilarious and straight to the point, and is definitely fair with grades. He tells you what is expected and as long as you hold up your end, he'll hold up his. He is super approachable and easy to talk to and office hours are a great place to get help for class but also just to get to know him. 10/10

Easy A with flash cards and lecture. Only used textbook for exam 1. Gives practice exams as well. Have to learn Latin and the second exam was the most difficult. (Afterwards only 5 Latin on future exams. Simple if you do top hat). Make sure youre comfortable (20% of grade is Latin exercises). Also offers upto 10% EC. Can possibly skip last test
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a very good professor, do not let my rating that the class is hard fool you, but this intro to mythology class was the most stressful class I had this semester. Even when I had other tests for other classes I stayed up studying for Myth. An A in this class is a 90 but in order to get that you have to keep up with the reviews and study

This was my hardest class my freshman year, please dont take it! Curtis is alright, but the TAs grade so harshly. I studied for these tests and I could never make an A bc with time constraints I couldnt conclude my essays. He does give extra credit, but this is about the only way you can make an A. He defends the TAs nitpickiness. Save yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Recent reviews are bothering me because they're (probably) all from the people who complained all semester long in the groupme rather than put in any effort. I've never had a more helpful professor (huge extra credit), he curves and is SO straightforward about what he expects on his tests. Yeah these TAs were pretty awful but that's not his fault!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the worst professor's at UT. His lectures are interesting and keep you entertained, but wow.. The TA's grade the tests and they are the worst. They take off points for EVERY LITTLE THING. It does not matter how much you study or how well you did, they will take off points. Zoe is a horrible TA. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis my favorite professor I have taken. Nobody beats his lectures. I agree with about 15 hours of study for the test. it's not bad because you know what to study. He is a very understanding man and has helped me through many tough situations (dyslexia diagnosis). Yes, the class is hard but if you put forth the effort you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is by far the worst and most stressful class I have taken. Lectures are really boring and not well-structured. There are like a lot of readings and they are sometimes difficult to understand. Tests are incredibly hard and TAs take points off for unreasonable reasons. There are many better VAPAs; it is not worth your time to take this one.

I was so excited for this class, and it ended up being my least favorite not just this semester, but out of my entire UT career. The TA's grade obnoxiously hard for no reason. The tests have fill in the blank picture IDs, 5 short answers, and an essay in 50 minutes. Points off for spelling. I love mythology but I struggled so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr, Curtis is an incredible lecturer and professor however you should only take this class if you are 1) a history buff and 2) an excellent timed writer. The tests are incredibly hard. The TA's grade the test like this class is your career and you will not pass if you don't make it your career. Plan on studying 15 + hours for each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Everything is based on the lectures, so if you don't go you're going to fail regardless of whether you read the textbook or not. The TA was beyond obnoxious and rude - thought she knew everything. I had high hopes for Curtis, but he wasn't very responsive nor did he seem to care about his students grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is one of THE WORST classes I've taken at UT. Curtis's lectures make no sense and this year's TAs grade OBNOXIOUSLY hard. Like it's seriously ridiculous what they take off points for. Save yourself the heartache and take a different VAPA!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading, very hard to stay on top of it. TAs grade pretty harshly. Memorization is also very important. However, this class was absolutely FASCINATING and I learned more than in any other class this semester! Thoroughly enjoyed it even though my grade wasn't great. Definitely recommend if you're willing to put in the work.

Prof. Curtis rushes, goes off topic, and rambles throughout his lecturesmaking it unclear what the primary take-always of each class is. Youre assigned 4-5 very dense readings every week that youll have to understand like the back of your hand come the testas the questions could be based on anything in those many readings. VERY boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class got so much harder this semester. Long tophat homeworks, insane amount of reading, lectures are rushed, and exams worth 70% of your grade that are graded extremely harshly by TA's. Way too much work and stress for a VAPA. Very hard to get an A.

This class was really difficult for me. I took it as a VAPA expecting a fun/engaging class on mythology (which I love). The lectures were rushed & crammed in so much material that every class was stressful for me. The tests (50 minutes for 4 short answers, 1 essay, and fill in the blank) are graded so harshly by the TA's, who nitpick every detail
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitley possible to get an A! just study for the tests using the review a few days in advance. Do the extra credit !! and stay on top of tophat!! with those three its a relatively easy A!! and mythology is semi interesting. Chill class, decent workload. If you stay on top of it its totallly an A. it was my fault i got a B. theres no plus minus.

Unlike others may say, NO! this class is not an easy A! After missing the deadline for some of the grammar HW (20%), I had to haul my ass to class EVERY day to get the extra credit points (10%+ extra credit) and spend time studying/making quizlets for the exams (80%). Small margin for error, you may end up with an B+ if you think it'll be easy.

This class was super easy. I just found a quizlet set the night before, memorized the entire set until my exam in the morning and made high Bs. I made like 3 A's on tests. I went to class like half the time and just racked up a 50% in class participation (thats equal to 5 points added to my final avg) Do the HW with friends. made an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Curtis for CC303 (classical mythology). Really fun class, he provides lots of good feedback (just email, he responds SO fast). He's super invested in the material and it shows! The work is lots of reading & analysis, and the amount of work is around where it should be for the course.
Dr. Curtis was AWESOME and so likable! Super cool subject matter, I still use the material I learned everyday. 10/10 would recommend.

I think I showed up to class a total of 7 times and managed to get an A. No final, just 7 MC midterm exams and he drops one (most people don't even show up to the last one). Attendance is extra credit and a 90 is an A. Purely based on memorization, you can learn everything the night before and still do fine. Beware the 2nd exam though

Dr. Curtis makes his lectures interesting for his students. However, he assigns alot of reading and his tests are entirely short -answer/essay-based. The good news is that the TAs grade the tests easily so it's not hard to get an A without reading or paying attention to lecture. Make sure to study the worksheets, which contain all the test prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: BEWARE: The first two tests, ESPECIALLY the second unit (shudders) were nothing like the remaining 5/7 of the course. I remember screaming doing the homework on the second unit because I just didn't get the material (latin grammar, its is odd). But I loved attending class. This was the only 8am I made sure to never miss! Real sweet teacher.

Lots of details, lots of reading. Go to lecture, a lot of the text can be hard to decipher without. Not an easy A, but fun. Very nice professor, the kind of guy you would be comfortable leaving your kids with. He knows his stuff, so you need to as well for the all fill-in blanks tests. Very good choice for a VAPA credit if you like reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I agree that Dr. Curtis is very knowledgeable about mythology but the readings are just a killing. I stopped reading all together and just took detailed notes of his lectures, I mean word for word of what he was saying. He gives assignments with all possible questions and I would just memorize the answers and my essays. Too much work for LAC credit
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a fun professor who clearly knows medical terminology very well. There are 7 total exams and one is dropped. Materials for the class were expensive (textbook and TopHat). He offers extra credit in class quizzes. Overall I learned a lot in this course and would recommend it for pre-health students.

Do not need to buy the textbook, I bought it and never opened it. Getting an A in the course still. He offers extra credit just for showing up to class and answering easy pop quiz questions. Literally is turning my 85% into a 93% it's THAT much extra credit. Plus an A in the class is a 90%.

Really funny guy. You will want to do good in the class because he is genuinely just a good professor. I see him more as a funny friend than a professor which is great because it shows he's not crazy intimidating.

Dr. Curtis is an amazing professor. He's very passionate about what he's teaching and always has funny jokes. The first two test are hard but don't let that discourage you from not taken the class. It is worth is and is one of the most easiest vapa class you can take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a cool guy but there are 7 tests in one semester. you have one every other week so if you have a busy schedule are a crammer I wouldn't recommend. It's not a hard class it just requires a lot of memorization. He posts lecture slides but does not post the meanings of words or important history information thats on tests. does give extra credit

Lectures are fast paced, but focused. He likes to throw in stories now and then about Latin and Greek history. 7 midterms, 1 drop, no final. Be prepared to memorize a lot , but also know that this class is based on literal translations of terms, not the "common definition" we usually think of. You will learn Latin anatomical grammar too.

says "okay" way too much and it gets annoying. tophat quizzes are extra credit. textbook you can find for free online but really don't need it. Top hat textbook you'll need for sure though for homework. tests are every two weeks. quizlet helps a lot because it's mainly memorization.

Really liked him. Took his class 2 yrs for my VAPA and it was my most intensive class at the time, but not unreasonably so. The homeworks were all questions that would show up on the test, so my friends and I made a study group to go over the answers before exams, which really helped! Reading is intensive but he'll explain the myths in lecture too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Todd is an interesting character. The class was an easy A if you just took 20 minutes every day to study and work on the homework. The test reviews were basically the test. We were given an extra credit opportunities every class.

There is a separate HW site for medterm! I had no idea until midway thru the semester (don't make the same mistake)! The class has a lot of tests/one drop/no final. HW is nothing like the tests, the tests are more based on lecture/quizlet material.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was a great professor. His class was really interesting, but don't be fooled it was a lot of reading. Don't procrastinate his class until the night before the exam, because you will be beyond stressed (trust me). He is a really nice guy and will round up. Overall, interesting class but LOT of reading. (Also a 90A)

Dr. Curtis is the best professor I had this semester. He's fun, witty, and makes a lot of Dad jokes. There is a TON of reading, long Tophat assignments, and minimum 2 pages of DECENT notes per class. It makes the time go by faster, but still fries a brain. He gives you an exact outline of the exam and expects a fifth grade level essay. Helpful.

wow this class was actually so much work and so hard for a VAPA. I cried because of this class and was doing well in my science classes, Im pre-med. In the end he gave extra credit which bumped to a 90.8 and a 90+ is an A in his class. So it saved me. This class requires a lot of reading and a lot of memorization but boy if i can do it so can you b

Curtis is a cool funny dad like dude. You'll easily make an A if you commit the terms to memory via quizlet/his powerpoint slides. Extra credit is offered for showing up and correctly answering questions. I skipped about a month of class and made an A (barely)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are 7 tests, the lowest of which is dropped, and then the online top hat textbook and the online extra credit (which is worth an extra 10 points). Dr. Curtis was very passionate and knowledgeable about the information he was teaching, and that made the course material very interesting to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is extremely passionate about Greek medicine, has very lively lectures, and is really good about answering your questions. Be prepared to do a lot of reading and to take good notes. For this class, tests are worth 80% of average, and the tests are mainly essay based. DO NOT COUNT ON MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS TO SAVE YOU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dont take this class if youre looking for an easy A. youve been warned.

He has changed up his style of tests but his syllabus did not reflect such. There are no longer multiple choice on his exams and is now all free response. He did give extra credit, but it was a competition for who got to turn in the paper first. His lectures are okay and the readings can be a lot. The tophat readings were rife with spelling errors.

This was such an awesome class! Dr. Curtis makes the class enjoyable and the topics were interesting. This class is an easy A if you do the reading and actually try on the quizzes. If I could I would take it again!

Dr. Curtis is an awesome guy! He really has a passion for medicine as well as history. That being said, this class is insanely easy! I had over a 100 going into the last couple weeks because of the extra credit and ended up with a 98 because I skipped the last 2 weeks of class and dropped the last test grade. JUST USE QUIZLET!!

Absolutely amazing professor. Really funny (dad jokes mostly) and offers views from all sides the material. Has a very in-depth and comprehensive knowledge of classical mythology. For CC303 you have to work hard for an A as the tests are a lot of material, but it's doable. Readings aren't completely necessary, but good to do. Worksheets  tests

Dr. Curtis is funny and this class is very easy. 7 tests, no final, one test gets dropped. Extra credit quizzes at the beginning of each class period (up to 10 points of EC are possible.) A 90 is an A which makes it even easier. Definitely take if you're interested.

Go to class, do the online hw (yeah you have to pay for access to top hat as well as the online hw) but i only used the textbook for the 1st test. 7 tests, 1 every 2 weeks and he drops the lowest so i didnt even take the last test. no final. extra credit worth up to 10 points added to ur final score.

Dr. Curtis was one of the few professors I have actually enjoyed having. His class is so much fun and he makes his lectures very interesting. There is reading to do every night but I found that just listening to the lectures would get you the same information. There are four exams and no final, and reading questions due every day but those are easy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love him so much he was my favorite prof from this semester. The class is interesting, if you pay attention to lectures you'll have all the info you need to get an A, and attendance is only mandatory bc he's so awesome.

A pretty average class in terms of difficulty, lots of reading (don't get behind like I did!), and the tests can be stressful but very doable. The tests consist of 20% multiple choice, 30% short answer, and 50% essay. All the questions on the test are given to you before hand, and he just picks out of the list. Very fun lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There are bi-weekly HWKs you can check the answers and easily get 100s, exams are basically class lecture, just pay 100% in lecture, glance over the textbook, and study the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was the best professor I've had at UT so far. I had him for medical terminology and honestly didn't use the book once. I took notes over the lecture in class and looked over those along with the practice tests the night before the tests and got an A on most. Show up to class to do the extra credit. A A is definitely do-able. A's are 90+

Had Dr. Curtis for med term and mythology! Just be warned mythology is way harder than med term. Also, there is tophat hw due every day of class. Although there is a lot to memorize, it's an easy A because he essentially gives you the entire test. The best thing to do is have a google doc with the class and help each other! He's really funny!!!!!

This class will be one of the easiest classes I'll take at UT by far. If you look at his grade distribution on UT catalyst, the large majority of people get an A. There is no final and he doesn't give A-'s so an A is 90+. Make a group chat with as many people in the class as possible to split the worksheets for the tests and they are a breeze.

Professor Curtis is a funny caring teacher, however, this class requires a lot of reading and is definitely not a blow off class. There is a worksheet that goes a long with each lecture and tests questions come from the worksheets as well as the top hat questions. This class is only easy if you truly put in the work.

A lot of extra credit, but this isn't a blowoff class. 200+ terms per test, which are every other week. You have to master the terms to not get tricked on tests. Homework is quite time consuming, but you have all the resources to get them done correctly. I wouldn't buy the textbook since terms are all over quizlet. No A- is given; a 90 is an A.

Do not get me wrong, he is an awesome professor/very engaging in lectures. All memorization. Tests are 20 mult choice, 6 short answer, and 1 essay. Mult choice is slightly altered from TopHat. The free response is chosen from the docs he posts on canvas. This class is doable but there are so many easier VAPAs out there. Reading is not required.

This class isn't a blowoff. You have to go to class and pay attention and study for tests. Tests usually cover around 100+ terms and are every two weeks so it can be a bit overwhelming. The hw is tedious and takes a long time to do. However, he is an engaging lecturer and a very nice guy. Gives plenty of extra credit, put in the work, get an A.

Dr. Curtis has been one of the best professors that I've had at UT. The lectures were engaging and I wanted to go to class, despite it being held at 8 a.m. In addition to the amazing lectures and interesting material, Dr. Curtis gives SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT. Seriously, you can earn up to 10 points extra credit added to your final grade. TAKE HIM!!!

He recently changed the format of the class. You will have to memorize 200-300 words for each exam. Exams are every other Monday, so your Sundays will have to be dedicated to studying. There's so much homework that is lengthy and difficult, and his powerpoints are useless. I have a 3.9 GPA and this is the hardest, worst class I have taken at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He gives engaging and entertaining lectures. I highly recommend taking this class!

This class can be very time consuming. The professor is a nice guy, however tends to go off topic. There are a lot of readings and quizzes due every other day before class starts. You only get less than 50 min to complete your test (includes essay). Only take this class if you are very if you are very interested in mythology. It is NOT an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is probably my favorite professor so far. He is very passionate and knowledgable. Lectures are actually interesting, and exams include mainly lecture content. Extra credit quizzes in class, so you should attend. He is funny and keeps you engaged. It is good to have the textbook and he uses TopHat textbook a lot, too. GREAT EXPERIENCE
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had so far at UT. Professor Curtis has the most interesting lectures, you actually want to come to class just to listen. He gives you plenty of opportunities for extra credit, plus you get examples of each test to study with. What more could you ask for? He's a great guy who really loves what hes teaching and is super great.
(Clear + caring + funny + engaging + great teaching style + profound knowledge of the subject)  x  fairest grading system  awesome professor! Overall - amazing learning experience!

DR. CURTIS IS THE BEST! He's hilarious. Lectures are super interesting. Top Hat quizzes at the beginning of every class for extra credit help out a lot. Lowest test score gets dropped. The second exam is pretty hard but other than that EASY A. There is also a lot of memorization(making flashcards helped)

His lectures are mandatory, but awesome. He is a funny character. You'll have to study information from both the textbook and lectures in order to pass tests. He also gives out a lot of extra credit so it is pretty easy to get an A in the class.

Good class to meet a flag if you need one! 4 tests for 80% and cumulative tophat for 80% of the final grade. Tests (which were directly from worksheets he posts for every lecture) consist of MC (20%), short answer (30%), and one essay (50%). Attendance isn't mandatory but he goes into detail in the lecture that you wouldn't get if you skipped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: NO FINAL

Curtis is a great guy. Made lectures interesting. 7 Tests, one every other week, lowest dropped. Test 2 is the worst one so study hard for that. Top hat extra credit allowed me to easily get an A. This class is really useful for any health care major. Don't hesitate to take his class!

Curtis is a great guy overall. Easy if you keep up with the readings and take good notes in lecture. There are 4 exams and no final. All you have to do is review your reading quizzes ( which are open book), and answer 5-6 optional short answer questions he posts for every lecture. The reading quiz questions and the short answers make up the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a great professor. His lectures were always interesting and I enjoyed going to class. I was able to make an A easily (test grades were: 94,68,98,94,90,0) because of the TOPHAT quizzes, and didn't need to take exam 7. Go to class, memorize what he tells you to, and study for a few hours the night before each exam and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a cool prof that makes many jokes. You can use your notes or talk to a friend in TOPHAT extra credit quizzes. I got 25/33.25 pts for the end of the semester. The quizzes are pretty easy. I recommend studying everyday for this class to get an A on the 7 test! They're not hard but don't overthink them. He is a smart, nice prof! Enjoy it

Some pointers are don't complain about you grade even if it's a 269.5. You need a 270 for a A. He won't round. You should be happy he doesn't have plus or minus for A's as well as having lots of extra credit. What other profs do you know at this campus do what he does? Use google docs with people from your class! It helps so much. He is a cool guy!
He is amazing. Took his class and got As on all of the tests by memorizing the study guide. This class is pure memorization and tophat questions are easy to find.

If you are a reader, good at history, and know a lot about ancient Greece, I'm sure you can easily get an A. He is a GREAT professor. However, I knew nothing about ancient Greece, hate to read, and had to work extremely hard for this A. It is primarily about sociocultural factors (directed towards my fellow science-wired premeds), you have to read!

grading: seven tests, drops lowest - first two tests are super hard but IT GETS BETTER; extra credit quiz every day at beginning of lecture over the lecture before (4 questions worth 1 point total)- I think I ended up with 20 points of extra credit Dr. Curtis is really engaging, fun to listen to, super knowledgeable, and lots of dad jokes... easy A
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was great!! Took this class as an elective and i really loved it. He gives extra credit at the beginning of every class. You only have to get a 90 to get a 4.0. There are tests every other week all MC. If you just study all the words from the lectures and practice tests you'll do fine. There are a lot of words but its doable. Loved him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a super smart and interesting guy. You MUST go to lecture to pass this class. He posts slides but he only includes half of the information that you need on them, he also talks really fast. The tests are pretty easy, I made a quizlet and studied it the night before and have a solid A+ in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was one of my favorite professors at UT so far. I took his Medical Terminology course and he did an amazing job going over all of knowledge we needed. His tests are based on vocabulary of the terms, and every class he gives a pop quiz that can boost your grade by 1 pt. I think I had over 20 pts at the end. He made my 8 am so enjoyable!

I honestly don't know why so many people see this class as an easy A. Sure,  it's a little better to be taking tests over mythological figures than something like psychology. But there is SO much reading for this class and SO many names and stories to keep track of. He wasn't a horrible lecturer, but it wasn't super interesting either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class. Dr. Curtis tries to make his lectures funny and entertaining while he speaks. He goes a little fast but reviewing the ppt if needed is easy. He drops your lowest test grade and there's so much extra credit. I would take his class again!

Professor Curtis is just an amazing guy. He cares so much about his students. As long as you do and keep up with the worksheets the tests will be fine. He gives 4 exams, no final. The test questions come directly from the worksheet.

This class is definitely a gpa booster. As long as you do and keep up with the worksheets the tests will be easy. He gives 4 exams, no final. The test questions come directly from the worksheet. His lectures are just a powepoint presentation but make sure to take notes. Great class!

This class is definitely a gpa booster and will count towards your global cultures flag if you need it. 7 tests over the course of the semester with one every two weeks. Drops the lowest one. At the beginning of each class has a 4 question extra credit quiz, each question worth .25 points. No penalty for getting it wrong. Easy tests if you study.

Take him! Provides a bit of extra credit everyday through the form of Tophat. Test every 2 weeks, but if you score well enough on the first 6, you do not have to take the 7th. Easy A, take his class! Cool guy, too.

Dr. Curtis makes a lot of jokes in class and sometimes they're funny and sometimes they're not but his class was very manageable. Goes off of a point system where when converted to percent a 90 will get you an A which is really nice. Give 7 exams, one every 2 week where he drops the lowest. Tells you everything you need to know in lectures.

4 exams, no final, every test question comes from pre-assigned worksheets from each lecture. Pure memorization and easy to find quizlets of the answers. Boring class if you're not interested in mythology but easy A for core curriculum credits.
Such an easy class and just pure memorization. Test are straight forward and super easy. He also uses tophat to give so much extra credit. I had 19 points in extra credit for my final grade.

Highest degree of professionalism I have seen in education. His lectures were outstanding. His knowledge was profound. Medical terminology isn't the most bright subject but he made it very interesting. Clear cut professor, we need more professors like him in upper level education.

The class is an easy A if you study. it's a lot of memorization. He goes over powerpoint's but make sure to take notes because some of the words are not in the textbook. Go to class everyday because the extra credit helps you a lot in the end.
Great guy, great class. Good amount of reading, but very manageable and enjoyable.
the class was easy, but boring as hell. I wish it was more engaging, but it was literally a powerpoint presentation that he walked back and forth on the stage explaining.

Dr. Curtis's lectures are pretty funny and engaging. He gives TopHat quizzes, but they are all for extra credit. There are 7 tests (one dropped) and the first two are the hardest. Just study his lecture slides and take notes during lecture and the tests will be easy. Also he does not apply the +/- system for A's. B's an lower he will use the +/-.

Dr. Curtis is the bomb!!! His Medical Terminology class is all memorization. he gives practice tests that are basically the same as the regular test. NO FINAL. tons of extra credit enough to raise you a whole letter grade. drops the lowest test grade. is a lot of studying. USE QUIZLET!!!  Don't be worried, take CURTIS.

Lectures are 80% from the textbook and posted online. His tests are straight from the textbook and lecture, so if you study, you'll be fine. The class is basically memorizing copious amounts of vocab words! He also offers extra credit which has a substantial l impact on your grade if you choose to participate. His lectures are really boring.

I absolutely love his lectures. Does daily quizzes (heavily affects your grades actually) about the previous lectures, but as long as you pay attention and take notes (MUST), you'll be fine. Exam questions are the quiz questions. 4 exams, no final, each exam has multiple choice, short answer, and an essay.
Great class and great professor! Learned so much and he made the class very interesting!

He is extremely interesting and makes you interested in the lecture topic. Although medical terminology can get confusing and boring, his 8 am lecture kept me interested and engaged either way. He's super sweet and is always willing to help and answer questions.

Dr. Curtis's class is really interesting and he is very knowledgeable on every topic he discusses. Highly recommend taking it, not hard to make an A. Attend lectures to get info thats not in the book. Study the practice tests and go over in class powerpoints. Extra credits helps a lot. Out of 7 exams, he drops one!

Dr. Curtis is a great professor! His lectures keep you engaged and he often tells funny stories about his experiences. He always has a great attitude and is passionate about what he is teaching. He provides extra credit opportunities every class and does a great job of teaching a memorization class. I would definitely take this class.

Dr. Curtis is a great professor. He's very passionate about what he teaches, and the material is always interesting. He keeps you very engaged. The class is an easy B or very doable A if you diligently study his PowerPoints and attend lecture for his extra credit TopHat questions. He's very helpful in his office hours, too.  Highly recommended!
super easy if you read the required texts and strictly memorize given vocabulary for tests

Dr. Curtis is such a great professor! He is so passionate about what he teaches! The material is usually very interesting, save for a few lectures on declensions. He gives extra credit, so go to class! He is also very funny, and really wants everyone to learn.  I honestly wish I had gotten to know him better. I loved him!
must memorize a lot to get an A

Class is an easy A if you study. I only studied the night before each test and got an A. Class is basic memorization of medical terms. There are 7 tests, but no final. You are also allowed to drop your lowest test grade. Beginning of class everyday is a tophat quiz. This is extra-credit. Extra credit could bring up an entire letter grade.

AMAZING! Loved this class!! Todd is a good lecturer and incredibly helpful outside of class. Must go to class to obtain material that might be not test. Easy test if you study. Great course for pre-med. Test every other Friday. Easy A ONLY if you study. Excellent EC opportunity. Can raise your grade an entire letter. Funny guy. Highly Recommend!!!!

Med Term was an amazing class! There were extra credit quizzes every lecture and he gave away a bunch of information on the tests, so you don't want to skip very often. There are 7 tests, but he drops one (even if it's a 0) and there isn't a final. A LOT of memorization, but it's interesting and not too difficult. It was a very useful class.

Even though a lot of people get A's in this class it is NOT an easy A.  Straightforward class: 7 tests, 1 gets dropped, a test every 2 weeks.  Extra credit every class but you HAVE to go to class to get it.  Barely made an A (by one point lol) because I skipped class most of the time.  Tests can be quite tough but there are old ones online.

Dr. Curtis is hilarious and extremely knowledgeable. It is necessary to write down every word, prefix, suffix, and definition he says during lecture and then simply memorize it all for the test. There are opportunities for 5 extra credit points per test out of 7 and he drops the lowest test grade. Very easy to make an A.

At the time i was taking the class, i didn't love it. But looking back, i strongly recommend taking this class especially if you are Pre-Med! Very useful and interesting. He is funny and kind and finds a way to TEACH a memorization based class. Studied all night the night before all the tests and made A's!

took him for medical terminology as an elective. Half way through the course was when I decided to look at careers in the medicine and health science field. He is a knowledgeable prof and cool guy. Curtis makes the topics interesting and adds humor to the lectures. Just go to class and participate in the pop quizzes. Bam! Easy A!
This guy is THE MAN! This is by far the MOST USEFUL CLASS I've ever taken. I learned so much everyday and it was all interesting. He's such a great professor.

Dr. Curtis is great. He is a funny guy and always can crack a joke. He is also really willing to help if you need him. Also, his class was really easy (for me anyway). There are 7 tests and bi-weekly quizzes which count to your total points. If, by the time you reach the last two weeks of school, you have an A, you don't have to take the last test.
Write down every single thing he says and memorize.
HE IS SIZZLING HOT, Y'ALL! ;) Go to class, pay attention, study the terms shown in lecture and in the book = guaranteed A. Great class for pre-med students.
He was amazing! Very funny, cute, and friendly. If you go to the lectures, you can ace the tests no problem!

Awesome Teacher. Pretty Laid back explains everything clearly.The textbook helps a lot, I don't see why anybody would fail this class if their is a lot of resources to use.Great course to take even if it is not required for your degree plan!
Kind.
Sooo hott!

I thought the class was really hard. There are no grades except the tests, and there are only 3 so if you bomb one your in trouble. There is just a lot of information to know, if you are good a memorizing you would do fine.

He is a great professor and I highly recommend his class. The class is beyond easy if you can memorize terms and history. The material is dry but is a good class to take if you need an A. 7 bi-weekly exams (he drops one) and they are 50 multiple choice exams. The classes are always early (8 and 9 AM) classes but really it is so worth it.

A great professor. You can't miss class because he does not post his powerpoints online. But maybe thats why you pay your tuition? Just a thought. He keeps the class interesting and interactive. The tests are all multiple choice. Homeworks count as extra credit on exams. Easy to boost your test score up a letter grade. Recommend him.
Very easy class. Grade is based off of 7 quizzes (1 dropped) and no final.  Don't really need to attend class to do well.

Blow off class. Don't really need to go to lectures unless you want to hear history stuff which only contribute to 3 extra credit questions on the quiz, and he sometimes pulls a few questions not in the book, but still really easy tog et an A. 7 quizzes (1 drop), no final. Nice and pretty funny/corny guy.

This class is completely useless. He doesn't post his slides online so you have to go to class to get all the random historical information. His quizzes are all pure memorization from the book. All you do is cram the words, but not really learn anything. Total waste of time but an easy A for those who can just memorize everything.

One of the easiest classes offered at this university. It's essentially a cram course. Grade is based entirely on 7 quizzes (lowest grade is dropped and there's no final). Go to class because he gives info on the extra credit questions he puts on the quizzes.

Dr. Talbot is a very good professor, the history course of the premodern world is very interesting, tests are in essay form, and both the professor and TA give good feedback. But reading, attending class, and paying attention to class and test preparation are very useful and important. Overall, very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Talbot is a terrible teacher. Graded one of my assignments without her laid out rubric and instead by how much she liked the paper. The tests and quizzes have no relation to what you learn in class and requires extra prep for tests. If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't it. Too many assignments . She was often unsure on her history info

Dr. Talbot is kind, intelligent, and she really cares about her students. She posts readings that will help you better understand, in-class review sessions before exams, extra office hours around exams, and she always helps out the best she can. Very fair. Great professor. I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: sweetest professor ever! I look forward to her classes every week. Easy to get in contact with, inclusive with all students, explains material in a way that's easy to understand. Love going to office hours and just chatting with her! Would definitely take any and all of her classes again.

Great option to take as a science core class, even if you aren't an SLH major. Dr. Czimskey is funny, engaging, and is truly passionate about her field. Make sure to take notes in class as the slides don't cover everything you need to know. Very helpful in office hours if any guidance is needed.

I LOVED taking Dr.Czimskey's class. She also has the "Longhorn Friday" where, if ALL class wears burnt orange on Friday, she will bring either treats next class or add extra points. She will also allow you to give burnt orange items to classmates before class. She is very funny during lecture and you have access to all ppt. on Canva.WILL take again
She's my favorite professor ever and I love her forever. Even though attendence wasn't mandatory, I still always went and feel like I got a lot out of this class. She's great 10/10!
Very kind person and her TA was great too
Very kind !

Professor Czimskey is truly a kind person. Every day, she would walk into class ready to start the day. Class is very low maintenance, which is helpful for a UGS. IN the discussion portion of the class, there is a lot of writing. TAs aren't horrible, just communicate with them when necessary.

She is amazing as always, phonetics content is very overwhelming at first but makes sure her students fully grasp the info. Her and her TA are very easy to reach outside of class and will help you in anyways they can. She makes sure we get the printed out version of the lectures and I think it helps a lot more than typing it out on a computer!
Chill class. Chill professor. Chill TAs. Take her!
Super amazing professor! Her lectures are super interesting, and she is super energetic, engaging, and caring. Tests are not too difficult, and homework is very doable.

Professor Czimskey is super nice and obviously very passionate about the subject matter. The lectures are very engaging and all homework is completed in groups. She responds fast to emails and is very caring/accommodating to her students. If you need a science credit definitely take this class.

Dr. Czimskey is such an inspiring and amazing professor! Overall, class was not to difficult. Only 3 homework assignments, all of which are group work. Only 3 test and 2 papers. Class was good and I HIGHLY recommend taking a class by Dr. Czimskey!
Dr.C has a lot of energy. I had her class at 10 am and it gave me a boost to start my day.

Truly, such a wonderful and caring professor. She's very engaging in her class and makes her lectures very interesting and understandable. I recommend her to anyone who still needs to take a UGS and wants an easy course.
Czimskey is extremely energetic, and for my UGS at 10 in the morning, she gave off so much energy that it made me pick up on it! I absolutely loved her class and totally recommend taking her UGS.

EXTREMELY caring and accessible prof. Attendance isn't mandatory. All tests are online and not monitored (she respects our privacy and trusts students not to cheat). I am not an SLHS major, but she made the class fun. Also, an optional final to replace the lowest test grade. Only con is that there's very few assignments outside of the tests.
Good course
The best! Genuinely cares about making difficult content accessible to all.
THE BEST!!!! Dr. C makes every lecture interesting and actually cares for all her students. Class is pretty easy, all the tests are online

This is the BEST professor on this entire campus. Dr. Czimskey genuinely cares about every single one of her students and wants us to succeed. Her lectures are very entertaining and engaging! Love her so much and highly recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Czimskey has the best lectures, inspirational with anecdotes to keep us engaged. Very little homework. Tests are online and reviewed for in class. She is always willing to help students. She took time out of her weekend to personally help me catch up on weeks of content when I was sick. No other professor cares for students the way she does.

If I could have her for every class I would. Phonetics is NOT easy but she took so much time and effort into teaching us it that she made it bearable. Had her for both intro and phonetics and she was great. Super passionate and understanding.

Doc C is among the best professors out there, she is truly talented at teaching and you can see how much she cares for her students and wants them to understand. Attendance isn't required but you'd be missing out, she always makes class so interesting! Not a lot of homework, tests are multiple choice and  very reasonable. highly recommend!
SHE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER.
She is literally the best professor on this planet.
She was very engaging and knowledgeable, and the subject matter was amazing to learn about.

literally best ugs professor ever. All assignments are weekly reflections and the final is a project you work with a group of ppl in your discussion section. Only thing that could make this hard is if you have a terrible group. W lectures, W professor, W ugs. take this if you can.
love her she is awesome and very inspirational and real

Absolutely amazing professor!! I highly recommend taking Dr. Czimskey if you get the chance, learning from her was incredibly easy bc of house she keeps the students engaged and is so passionate about the topics.
Wonderful professor and makes the class so interesting. Super understanding and loves to hear from the students during lectures. She is a 10/10 and I would take her class again.

Not an SLHS student but took her for my UGS. Class was split into lecture and discussion, where you would work on a group project. Lecture was engaging. Grades and discussion completely depend on your TA. Mine was fine and graded easy, but I heard the other TA was more fun. If you need to take your UGS, I recommend this one!
Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had the privilege to learn from. Wouldn't wake up for a non-mandatory 8am for any other class or professor. Just outstanding
Dr. Czimskey is the best. She has a funny and engaging energy. I've taken SLH306 and SLH311 with her and both classes were phenomenal. You won't regret taking her.

I could seriously write a book about how amazing Czimskey is, but I will spare you. She is incredibly caring and so willing to help if you reach out. Additionally, her compassionate teaching methods and trust in us as students 100% made me a more active learner and honest student.

Dr. Czimskey is LITERALLY THE BEST 1000/10. She's so kind and a fantastic lecturer. Her passion for the material is contagious! The class is a lot tougher than I anticipated, but she does such a wonderful job explaining everything. If you show up, take good notes, and pay attention you'll be fine. I cannot stress how awesome this class is.
Great class and wonderful explanations
She is such a kind soul and wonderful teacher.

I absolutely love Dr. Czimskey!! She is a fabulous professor, however, this class is difficult. She takes a lot of the stress away from the material with her great lectures, but be prepared to do lots of studying and homework. It is worth it to take such a hard class with her because she is the best and is so great at what she does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is incredible!! I absolutely loved this class and I would recommend 100% taking it. She is very passionate about what she does and you can truly tell she loves teaching. This class was super insightful and makes me really excited to become a future SLP. Even if you are not an SLH major, you should totally take this class!

Czimskey was absolutely amazing! She is very passionate about SLH and it really shows in how much effort she puts into us understanding the material. Everything is presented in a understandable way with outstanding examples. I really could go on forever. Take her class!

100/10 professor. I took three classes with her and she is literally who I want to be. Boss lady who is extremely knowledgeable, caring, respected by students and faculty, kind, and hilarious too! She makes her lectures fun by adding personal anecdotes every once in a while. Her tests are not hard and the homework helps a lot! Take czimskey!
I LOVE Dr. Czimskey. She's very patient, caring, and funny. That phonetics class, however, was rough.

Dr. Czim is such a sweet and honest person who truly cares about what she is teaching. She is a pleasure to be around and cares about you as a student as well. This class is graded on about 10 things the whole semester, so everything has a lot of weight. Take this even if you don't need it, this class is super interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Listen to all of the reviews and take her classes. Shes not an easy grader my any means, but shes absolutely amazing and inspiring. Her humanity and kindness make her an amazing professor. Adore her.

Dr. Czimskey is the best professor I will ever have. She makes even a hard and boring class worth it. If you can ever take any of her classes, do it. I've never met someone who cares so much for their students success and wellbeing. So understanding and a great role model. Grading from TAs felt harsh sometimes, but overall not a crazy hard course.
Doc Czimskey is the absolute sweetest professor you will ever encounter. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students. I would 100% take her class again!

I love Dr. Czimskey! She is super caring. Taking phonetics online was definitely a bit odd (simply because it's the sort of class that is probably a bit easier to understand in person). However, Dr. Czimskey did an amazing job keeping the class engaging and was very caring, as well as flexible.

I would give my life for Dr. Czimskey. She is the reason I knew SLH was the right major for me. She is so accommodating and goes above and beyond for her students. Her lectures are informative and never too long or boring. She knows exactly how to teach you what you need to know to be successful. If youre thinking about taking her class, DO IT.
Amazing. Take this class!!

She was so supportive when we switched to online classes and you could really tell she cared about all of her students & how they were adjusting. I've never had a more caring professor! She genuinely wanted us to enjoy the class and do well in it without making us stress about it with everything else that was going on.

Dr. Czimskey is the best! She's really passionate about CSD and makes you want to be, too! She always makes it clear what's going to be on the exam, and the HWs are really helpful when studying. She made an 8 AM lecture feel like no big deal because she was always so lively and made the material interesting. You'll learn so much with her!
I LOVE DR. CZIMSKEY!!! A real gem in CSD. I stan.

Dr. Czim is by far the most passionate professor i've ever come across. She's really chill to converse with and is always open to answering questions. My tip: at the end of the week, make time to fill out your lecture notes on the HW. This will save you lots of time before the due date (the HW is very long, do NOT wait until the last min).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Czimskey is honestly the best professor I have ever taken at UT thus far. The class was very easy, and the material you learn is practical and very interesting. If you're interested in speech/hearing/language sciences or if you just need an elective class, then I highly recommend this class!
Amazing class. Shes awesome. Please take this class!

She is extremely passionate about what she is teaching to the point it rubs off onto you. You will do great in the class as long as you take notes in the lecture and skim textbook chapters. She makes the material understandable and takes the time to engage with the students. Any question you have she will answer it.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm not even in Moody and took this class to fill my schedule up. The best professor I've had thus far and will remember her as the most caring prof at UT. The tests are easy if you show up to class and take good notes. There are "pop quizzes" that are based on attendance. Homework and study guides are basically the test. Love this class.

Amazing professor. First test is very hard. Homework due before every test that is mainly a study guide. She also makes a study guide. Attendance is counted as a quiz grade and is randomly a couple times. You don't really need the book unless you feel like reading helps you. She is one of the best professors I've ever had.

I took this class to see if I could envision myself doing CSD in the future, and while I don't it's for me, Dr. Czimskey is definitely an amazing prof and this was a class that was valuable while not being overbearing in courseload, etc. I did skip a few classes, but it didn't hurt me at all, though there are pop attendance "quizzes."

Dr. Czimskey is a very inspirational professor that clearly cares about her students and the course she teaches. She helped solidify my decision to pursue a CSD major. She is very funny, uses lots of examples to help communicate various challenging topics, and is caring overall. Lectures, ppts, and homeworks all prepare you adequately for tests.

an incredibly inspirational professor. I took it as a 9am and never wanted to miss. This course explored comm. disorders from hearing loss, autism, stroke, dementia, etc., but also teaches other courses. I'm not a comm. major, but she made me want to convert. The best thing is that she has real experience and always shares. Grading is fair. loved!

Czimskey is one of the hands-down best people I know, on top of being an incredible teacher. She is so passionate about her career and really encourages her students to be passionate as well. I am grateful that I had her this year and her enthusiasm about speech path made me excited to pursue the career myself... I wanna be her when I grow up :')
I can't stress enough on the awesomeness of this professor. Take her class!

prof. czimskey has a special kind of conviction for her students ... she is unchallenged the most caring professor i've had at ut thus far. 3 exams, 4th optional (i didn't take it; you won't need to so long as you study). attend lectures for material, exams easy if you put in the time. i implore you to take this class - you will not regret it.

Professor Czimskey was the first professor I have ever had at UT and a tough one to compete with! She is not only a knowledgable and great professor but (as cheesy as this sounds) inspires her students to be better people and love hard. One of the most caring and passionate PEOPLE (out of everyone, not just professors) I have ever met!

If you think this is an easy A you are wrong as was I when I took this class. I thought it would be my blow off class but it ended up being one of the more challenging if you are not a CSD or SLP major. Czimskey is the sweetest professor I have ever had and should be given an award or something

I took Natalies Intro to CSD class and loved it. her lectures are really great but most importantly shes the kindest, most caring prof Ive ever had. this semester was the hardest of my life and she was so understanding and accommodating. shes so funny and really cares about her students. 100% recommend her. get to know her in office hours!

Prof. Czimskey is by far the most caring professor I've had. She has 3 midterms, 3 homework, 3 pop quizzes that are attendance dependent, & an optional final (to drop your lowest exam grade). She's funny, makes lectures interesting, and she genuinely cares and wants the best for her students. While her class is not a super easy A, it's doable!

Prof. Czimskey is a fantastic professor and reaffirmed my love for CSD. She is extremely passionate about her field, and this translates clearly in her lectures. The homework assignments are the reviews for the exams, so it is not a waste of time to do it. Pop quizzes are a thing, but they are super easy and used for attendance. Highly recommend her!

Professor Czimskey made this class extremely enjoyable. The course gave a grand overview of the field, and I feel more secure in the fact that I want to pursue it. She is funny, personable, and genuinely wants you to do well! There was extra credit and the few assignments may as well have been called study guides. WOULD RECOMMEND!!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An amazing, passionate, caring professor. She knows so much and is so excited to share it with her students. She cried multiple times during class because she cared so much about the material. She makes sure you're prepared for all of her tests, giving you a list of topics that the (multiple choice) questions will be on.

She is the best professor I have ever had, hands down. She cares so much about her students and the field. I cannot recommend her enough and I am sad to see my seamster with her end. I 10/10 recommend.

Be prepared to buy lots of books and read before every single class. The readings were a little hard on their own but with the lectures, they became a little fun! Prof. Stauffer was an amazing lecturer and tried to make it easy to understand. Consisted of 2 papers and pop quizzes. Also offered a lot of extra credit which was super appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stauffer is one of the best political theory professors here. He explains complex topics simply & provides many opportunities for grade improvement like quizzes, optional papers & SI sessions (much appreciated as political theory classes are tough). Even with large class sizes, he tries to learn everyone's names. I cannot recommend him enough!

he's so funny and super cool. just very lecture heavy, just make sure to read. he gives pop quizzes but he lets you know when the quizzes will be before he gives them. he doesnt ask for participation because a lot of people always talk. take him, hes cool
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stauffer is an ICON. He's rly funny and super knowledgeable. He encourages participation and makes an effort to learn names. This is my favorite class that I've ever taken, ever. I never had the desire to skip class (except on my birthday!) and I'm a chronic skipper. Take his class! And then take him again! You will learn so much, and laugh a lot.

Professor Stauffer is amazing and engages with the class, which makes class much easier and more fun. He gives out random (easy) pop quizzes to make sure everyone is staying on top of their reading. No phone usage allowed in class so that people arent distracted. I would definitely recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Any class you take with Professor Stauffer will not be one you regret. His teaching style is to the point and engaging. A fair amount of reading that is required because he gives out (easy) pop quizzes to make sure you've been reading. He doesn't grade too hard, and offers plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Engaging and great lecturer. Very reading heavy, but you can skim. Graded on two exams and one optional paper. You were given exam prompts ahead of time. Easy to do well in this class if you put in the time (also talk to the TA, they will do all the grading).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute genius. What a class act. Devin Stauffer is the greatest professor I have had the honor of taking a class for. He genuinely cares that you learn and understand the material, and is immensely passionate about what he does. However, if you aren't prepared to put in the effort, don't take his class. But he will inspire you to do your best.

Professor Stauffer is an incredible teacher and very wise man. I adored his lectures and was consistently surprised and entertained by his insights. He loves to hear what all of his students have to say and is always fair in his responses. I like that he encourages participation and it's clear he wants his students to enjoy the texts and class.

Stauffer was a great professor but I got tired of all the readings by the end of the semester. There is an optional paper offered at multiple points throughout the semester. All blue book exams. The TA was a tough grader so I wish I had spoken with him about my grade since he basically determined it. Pop quizzes but allowed to use reading notebook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Stauffer is the best gov professor I have ever had. His lectures are interesting, the books he assigns are all good, and he gives extra credit simply for turning in a book of notes at the end of the semester. He also allows you to write extra credit essays. Overall, a super caring professor that will actually teach you and try to make you succeed.

Great lecturer, class was always interesting. pop quizzes over readings, they're easy if you read. Tests are essays, gives you prompts ahead of time. TA sometimes had different interpretations for the readings than stauffer, so if your test doesn't look right you may want to take it to the prof. do the reading journal, it really helps in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Coming to class is super important but the discussions are interesting enough that you will actually want to go. I really enjoyed the class and you leave feeling like you learned something. I would definitely take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he really cares about the subject. the textbooks seem scary but he explains them in an easy to understand way. hes interesting and gives you every opportunity to pass. love this class

Fairly simple class, very enthusiastic and thorough prof. Exams never ask something that hasn't been covered, so take good notes on what he says and you'll be thankful come exam time. Grade: attendance, pop quizzes, essay exams, extra credit. No ppt used, lecture not recorded, laptop allowed only with permission.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stauffer is an amazing professor. I'd recommend him if you are interested in political theory. He gives pop quizzes from time to time, but if you've done the reading, they are super easy. The exams aren't difficult either. Midterm is an essay. The review sessions are super helpful.

He teaches about political theorists, and his style of teaching allows for those theorists to be more accessible for an average government student. The tests are in-class essays and he will usually offer two prompts. One that is reciting the stances of the writers and then an opportunity to outline an interpretation of the text.

Dr. Stauffer gives really awesome lectures and makes it easy to incorporate comments from students in the class.  Makes it a hybrid discussion and lecture course.  Blue book tests are graded ridiculously easily if you write what he says.

Professor Stauffer is a brilliant lecturer, and manages to break down dense material. He has pop quizzes every couple of weeks. Participation is attendance based. He offers extra credit for a reading journal. He gives three chances in the semester to write the term paper. Two in-class essay exams. Repeat what he says in lectures and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lecture class with blue book tests. As long as you go to lecture you will be fine. Knows his stuff and is funny conveying it to the class. Encourages discussion which makes it interesting. Pop reading quizzes
Amazing Prof!
Stauffer Kicks ASS

OK, so Dr. Stauffer is a really interesting, fun, intelligent professor. He is a fair grader, expects a lot of his students, but provides ample opportunities to make a good grade. He does stutter a bit, which can be annoying at times. Side note: If Mr. Weasley and Chandler Bing had a love-child, that child would look just like Dr. Stauffer.
Stauffer is extremely knowledgable, personable, and helpful. He has very high standards, but provides a lot of feedback.
An excellent, personable, hilarious professor. He has an incredible grasp on the material, and teaches is in a very accessable way. You can really tell he cares about the students. TAKE HIS CLASSES!
Read the textbook. Her lectures are copy and paste off the respective chapters. She's sort of mean to students but I think she means well

Cares very deeply for all her students. Lectures can get boring, but it is the material that's dense. Practice as many problems as you can, especially harder proofs. Weekly quizzes are not too hard, but not reflective of exam difficulty. There is a lack of exam prep material, so the textbooks/online resources are your best bet. Costudy is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't really too hard, but the homework and quizzes were pretty confusing at the beginning of the semester, getting worse as the semester went on. The professor might seem intimidating, but is very nice and understanding when you actually talk to her. However, lectures are very boring and NO PRACTICE TESTS.

Dr. Parikh is a great lecturer for CS311 -- take her! She is incredibly busy (hence a procrastinator), but she is kind. Ask her good questions in lecture -- save simpler ones for the TAs, who have the time. This course requires a lot of practice outside of class to succeed, so use office hours, co-study and the textbook. And start homework early!!

She arrives to class late and posts test locations late. She answers too many students' questions. She jokes around, for which people hate her, but without the humor the material would be very boring. She offers many examples of proofs and conjectures in the practice sets with plenty of office hours. Practice set solutions are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although this subject is difficult, she doesn't make it any easier with her teaching. She was really irresponsible, openly admitting to making the exams the morning of the test day. For the final exam, she didn't release seating charts until 3 hours before the scheduled time, and the first time she released it she got it wrong and had to fix it!

The subject itself is already difficult, and it's worse because of the teacher. To a certain extent it is the material, but Parikh fails to prepare the class for the difficulty in the exams because she barely goes over hard proofs during lecture and only includes them in problem sets. Material available to prep for exams are also hard to come by.

Odds are you will be forced to take Parikh so just know that this class starts out pretty easy for the first 3-4 weeks then there is a massive difficulty spike once you get to proofs. Also, always make sure to do the problem set before the quiz as the content is heavily based on either the material in discussion or the material on the problem set.
Weekly quizzes on material learned, watch the prelecture videos fully for participation grade. No practice exams for midterms but problem sets are good practice. Attendance taken at lecture.
