She wasn't really a good teacher. Lectures were drab and boring, and she wasn't very accepting of student questions. Section TAs were decent, but not great. I did like the format of the class as it was well-organized.
take anyone else

Parikh is genuinely a sweet professor if you know her fr. She seems scary but she's actually chill. Long lectures, lots of material, make sure to lock in. Participation grade based on videos and attendance. Study A LOT every day and prep for dreadful weekly quizzes. TAs are goated they lowkenuinely carried my grade.
Loved Dr. Parikh she was very nice and accessible. However, I thought the class focused way too much on format rather than mathematical correctness. I wish she would focus more on the math
Was actually a good professor just annoying exams and section.

This is kind of a weed-out class, so be prepared and be prepared for it to be confusing. Still, I think Dr.Parikh does a good job explaining, but make sure to be engaged, because while she doesn't mind "bad questions," if she thinks you're not engaged, she will call you out, also, don't be on your phone or AirPods; she'll call you out there, too.
The class teaches very little. The effort given by the instructional staff no where near matches the effort asked from the students. The class is lazy, unorganized, and uninteresting.

she was the worst professor i had so far in college. she genuinely wants you to fail get ready for YouTube university because she explains the concepts in the most complicated way she can. whole class basically bombed the second exam (avg 65) because she failed to go over any complicated questions CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSEHIM

It's a difficult class made exponentially harder by the fact that the professor is just genuinely mean. Instructor is unapproachable and actively shames students for asking questions in class. Does not provide adequate resources to prepare for exams.

The worst part of this class was the weekly quizzes worth 23% of your grade. I studied for these quizzes and had LOTS of points lost for tiny mistakes. I'm not sure what the averages were but me and my friends consistently got 70s despite doing great on exams and understanding and participating completely during section. inconsistent between TAs

Difficult class, especially if its your first proof class, but you will survive if you work hard. Lectures are boring but very helpful. Quizzes and hw every week, 3 exams but not weighted horribly. Worst part is lack of practice materials, but plenty of TA's and study sessions to help. Overall, difficult and boring but not a bad class.

This class did prepare me well for other courses. Remember that the participation grade is measured through pre-class videos and attendance. The pre-class videos are timed. My grade would have been like a B ~ B+, but it dropped to C- after getting nearly a 0 for participation.

Parikh's class is tough, but using resources like Unstuck ai alongside the textbook can make it manageable. Attendance is a must, and exam feedback is hit-or-miss, but the content itself is reasonable.

Class is hard but Parikh is a good professor. Lectures, and understanding of the homework are very important to success. Exams are unpredictable but you will be fine if you engage in lecture, and she does a good job of answering questions so make sure you ask.

As a professor, I'd say Parikh is overall fine. The lectures are very boring. I honestly had a hard time with the class because much of it had me relying on intuition so I felt extremely stupid. A huge issue was that the exam was more difficult than the material we went over in class. I'd suggest trying to get the other 311 professor instead.

Make sure you watch the pre-lectures the whole semester. Since there isn't a lot of study material for tests, I would recommend the textbook, specifically the questions at the end of each chapter (one of the midterm questions was pretty much exactly repeated).

She doesn't really come off as wanting her students to succeed. She's not particularly approachable and can be demeaning when you ask questions. The study materials are gatekept (unlike 314). The quizzes and tests will have some questions that are significantly harder than what is gone over in class. Test grading is nitpicky and harsh.

Switch to Fraij if you can. Parikh is a bad a lecturer. Her lectures are pretty boring and honestly she doesn't even teach effectively. Even at the beginning, my pod mentor said that most absorption comes from outside. Also, she is a HEAVY procrastinator. She is somewhat caring which is nice, but I could not grasp any topic she covered in lecture.

Pretty good class overall, Parikh is a decent lecturer and the concepts are understandable. Homework sets are difficult but solutions are provided, weekly quizzes are much easier. The first exam is relatively simple, but the 2nd and final are much more difficult and there aren't many practice problems provided unless you go to co-study.

Dr. Parikh is a great professor. She makes her lectures engaging and makes discrete math as much fun as it can be (which isn't a ton). The quizzes are easy, but the WPPs are hard. The exam will probably be somewhere in the middle of the two, but a bit closer to the WPPs. For the exams, you get a cheat sheet and they give good partial credit.

Her lectures are incredibly boring and she provides such little study material. It's genuinely one of those classes that you just have to "get" no matter how hard you work for it. From what I know, her exams are incredibly difficult in comparison to Fraij. Also, the amount of points taken off for such little mistakes is insane to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Parikh is a great professor and explains concepts super well and will hold your hand while doing proofs in the class. 

Many people complain about the Exams, but you can bring cheat sheets so it makes them much easier, fill those up. DO THE WPPS!!! The questions are never harder than that.

Only complaint is there was no practice exam material.

Her teaching is decent though class is boring. The homeworks, while difficult, have answer keys that usually explain well. The weekly quizzes are usually fine. Exams are the hardest part. The final exam was much more difficult than previous exams, and the lack of study materials didn't make exams any easier. I'd recommend taking Fraij if possible.

Terrible professor. Gave so many tough problems on quizzes and tests that she did not teach at all. These problems were very complex and made for you to get bad grade. Just wants you to get a bad gpa and doesn't care about anyone but herself. Always talked how people gave her bad reviews all the time and did nothing at all to help me.

Her quizzes are easy but are exams are way too complicated. She doesn't teach the harder problems nor does she provide previous exam papers for you to practice. She expects everyone to perform well on her exams without any practice problems or previous papers and complains when she receives poor feedback.

She was fine, but I had to work to earn my grade in class. She's a caring professor, but her lectures were kind of boring. The exams are slightly hard because there's very little practice material and she nitpicks your proof formats. However, you do get a cheat sheet for the exam. No textbook is required, but the Rosen textbook is a lifesaver.

Bad lecturer and exams were tough.

Format of class is awful, exams don't really seem to test the content learned but simply problem solving skills and the exam prep and format is stress inducing.

For reference, I got an A in Mike's 314 by studying around 5 exams each exam, but in Parikh's there are simply no good study techniques, just pray

Lectures could get a little boring sometimes but the content was pretty fun. Homeworks being completion is nice. Exams were pretty close to the homework so not too bad. Having to watch prerecorded videos was annoying though, as she would just teach the same content during class.

Dr. Parikh is a pretty good lecturer, but she didn't provide many accessible resources to practice the material. Aside from the required problem set, only one set of extra practice problems are available per week, and they may only be accessed through a TA or an organized help hour session (co-studies).

terrible professor please try to get a different professor if possible just awfully structured class with below mediocre teaching

EDIT: final was terrible 0 resources to help prepare
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class wasn't the best or worst. I thought I didn't get an A but I did. Exams are somewhat tricky but honestly for me it was just the exam environment that made me panic. Calm down and read the problems carefully and the problems actually aren't too bad. Lectures are really useful to review afterward. Other than that it just felt like a mid-class.

The class touches on a little of proving algorithms and really emphasizes how to optimize matrix multiplication. Beyond the 5-loops lab, the exam, projects, and homework are really not that difficult. Dr. Parikh is a bit of a procrastinator, so keep that in mind when expecting grades and feedback.
Quite possibly the worst professor I've ever had at UT. Stay away from her and her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is incredibly nice and friendly and covers her course content in a fairly organized manner. She did get off of her schedule after exam 1 which made her pre-lecture videos not align with her lectures. She allowed us to have cheat sheet(s) on the exams which was helpful. Like many other posts suggest, exam 2 feedback was handled poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content of the class isn't very hard; it's the professor that makes it that way. The professor makes you feel as if she doesn't want you to succeed. Feedback on exams is not the best. She even purposely regraded Exam 2 as she felt the TA's were "being too nice." Final exam grades aren't even released.

Parikh is nice enough once you get to know her. Her main problem is expecting students to care more about her class than data structures and grades subjectively at times. Her class was mostly organized besides exam weeks and she's decent at explaining earlier unit concepts. Pay attention to pre-lecture and section problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but CS 378 was a disorganized disappointment. Unclear expectations, scattered lectures despite required attendance. Unclear exam content. Weird grading scheme. Very disorganized compared to her solid Discrete Math course. Use Robert van de Geijn's edX version to actually learn. Texts are way more helpful than lectures.

This course is good in the sense that she is very approachable outside of class and she knows what shes teaching. The course material is dense and the projects are very time consuming and hard. Class gets better as the semster progresses but I would consider this a pretty heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam 2 feedback was handled poorly and made a lot of people dislike her, which has led to a lot of bad reviews this semester. Apart from that, she gives the HW solutions so that students have more examples of how to accurately answer questions, but if you just copy given answers it makes studying for exams a lot harder. Lectures were not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. When new symbols are being introduced, you should not handwrite your notes. She does. Very difficult to understand what is being written and what is a part of the problem/given or the solution. She blatantly regraded a test to be scored lower. UT really needs to add a new CS prof for Discrete Math. Disappointing, disheartening. I'm sorry.

bad lecturer and very boring lectures. when you ask questions outside of class she can be passive aggressive with responses. also she went back and regraded a test just to take away points because the tas were too lenient.

I don't think she understands that some of the topics in this class are very difficult to conceptualize, especially because proofs require some sort of creativity or ingenuity. She should give more practice because of this, but she always claims that she gives enough (I think most people would disagree).

Not really sure what to make of this class. Parikh is a good professor in the sense that she's personable and cares, but the way she ran the class gave something to be desired. We didn't understood what she was teaching until we had projects and could actually piece her lectures together. Overall, wouldn't recommend. I got nothing out of this class

She doesn't really prepare you for the tests, she puts topics barely covered in the class and expects students to magically be able to answer the questions, And starts whining in class when students do bad on a test she didn't prepare us for
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On Midterm 2, she curved down our scores because the "TA's gave us too many points." I had an A which dropped me to a B on the test. Her lectures are not that bad, she is just very passive aggressive. Because of this, I do not show up to office hours and sometimes not even class and just learn the material on my own.
pretty bad at lecturing...

Extremely lacks clarity and assumes we comprehend short abstract explanations, then speeds through hard examples. For midterm 2, many people did horrible, and instead of trying to help the students, she said she was going to go back and take away more points. The prestige of UTCS feels tarnished by such disregard for student learning and success.
She does not care about students understanding of the material
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: extremely boring lectures, this class made me want to switch majors
Although I cooked and got an A, this class was the worst experience of my life, unfortunately you have to take this class for your degree so pucker up and enjoy the ride

This teacher is the worst teacher in the history of UT computer science. Because this class is commonly taken at the same time as CS314, the day of one of the CS314 midterms, very few students (I think 3) showed up to lecture that day, causing her to visibly whine the entire lecture and explicitly say that she was going to make her exams harder.
Great lecturer but the course content is just really hard and the projects are also really difficult. I would reccommend taking her but read the textbook. One exam 3 projects 2 homeworks.

She's too smart for her own good, explains concepts abstractly then speeds through the 1-2 examples done in lecture as if we should know it already. Have to master content in 1-3 days for the weekly quizzes. "Practice test" is useless and homework includes untaught material. While grading is lenient and she's nice, the course has its flaws.

Parikh does not present the material in a way that is understandable. She does not explain things well and does not answer questions well. She also gives us important content in the lecture before the test, provides no practice problems/ practice exams before and then asks us a difficult question about a concept just taught. Would not take again.

Dr. Parikh is a very good professor. Her course is very well laid out and her teaching style is great. The only thing that I felt was lacking was that there was not enough examples of certain topics so finding helpful resources was tricky. Other than that, you will have a good time with her, but I am also happy that it is over.

Parikh is a good teacher and cares for her students but it may still be difficult to learn from her. Her lectures can be a little hard to follow and will require work outside class to learn the content. If someone is confused, her explanations don't really make sense to lessen the confusion and just repeats what she said before.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Parikh's lectures favor direct instruction and are structured around notetaking, corresponding with my learning style. She delivers material well, but pre-class videos were a chore. HW solutions provided and weekly quizzes were easy. Exam grading is lenient but hard to prep for. Final exam score not revealed, but curve implied. Study induction.

Really good lecturer with engaging presentations, always ready to help even outside of class. Grading isn't too harsh & all the assignments/quizzes are basically completion grades. There are 3 major tests, all of them honestly aren't too bad but you don't get much practice material. Content is pretty interesting, math-wise it's just basic algebra.
I love Dr. Parikh. Notes are very helpful and she cares a lot about her students. like a lot. she is also really funny and really relatable too. parikh is the goat

Pretty good professor, no major complaints. Lectures can feel long, but attendance isn't mandatory. The course material feels gimmicky at times, as you can completely fail an exam problem / quiz if you don't know some specific trick that the problem is designed around. Also a little tough grading on formatting. I still feel I learned a lot though.

Dr. Parikh is approachable, funny, and knowledgable. She is animated at times, which some saw as mean or sassy but I found it light hearted and entertaining.
There are weekly homeworks, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. 
Homeworks were hard but graded for completion, quizzes were easy, especially with two attempts, and exams were forgiving and doable.

This professor seems nice but she is very, very mean. She picks and chooses who gets to get a round in the grade, she chooses who gets to reschedule an exam or quiz. Everything is up to her discretion, if it's something serious like missing a quiz because of a death, she states the syllabus is the final say, but gives someone w a cold a reschedule.
Towards the end of the year the topics get convoluted and kinda difficult to understand. The lectures are mid. Not terrible, but not great.
worst prof I have had in my 4 years at utcs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't think I'd end up with an A but I did. Just need to put in a lot of work and study the practice problems she gives diligently. She's a very caring and good lecturer. One of my favorite teachers from last semester. Overall, great class and great professor.

She is a very good lecturer but the topics after induction are really difficult. Make sure you take the time to properly learn the content on your own, and do practice. Exams were not bad at all, but the final was difficult and confusing. Weekly quizzes are also pretty easy if you pay attention in class.

Her lectures consisted of a lot of practice- which was good because exams reflected exactly what was on the homework, quizzes, and lecture practice. Her pre-class videos were incredibly useful, you should take notes on them before class and amend during class- this will make the class SO much easier for you (i wish i did this).

Lectures were about as interesting as you can make discrete math; with jokes here and there. Quizzes and exams were usually lightly graded (depending on who graded yours). Not extremely difficult to pass, but material is a bit confusing (have to do a lot of practice & lots of looking at the solution) but makes up with light grading. No bump/curve

Dr. Parikh does a good job of teaching a very hard subject. Practice is hard to come by outside of the section and TA runs study sessions since proof formatting is so stringent. Keep up with the content and PRACTICE!

Professor Parikh is super knowledgeable and Discrete Math was interesting. However, it's easy to fall behind if you don't practice and do the homework while you're learning content, so make sure to study as you go and not the night before an exam. Practice in-class activities, homework, and past quizzes to prep for exams, which are all open-ended.

Parikh is a nice professor however she can feel dismissive at times when answering questions. Exams make up a majority of the grade and curves almost never happen (if at all). The TAs in this class are also very hit or miss, especially my TAs who evidently did not prepare for sections because of how many mistakes they would make in example problems
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CS378 Programming for Performance and Correctness was a bit disorganized, but Parikh really cares about the material and teaching it to others. I think the class will be even better in the future now that the projects are set up and won't need to be delayed as Parikh finishes making them. Not a ton of work and easy to balance with other classes.

Discrete math itself could be interesting, but the professor's execution in teaching it is bleh. I would recommend paying attention during discussion meetings, as it offers some challenging content. The test prep material is subpar, so prepping for the exam is hard with the lack of questions on par with the difficulty of the exam. Easy grading, tho

Content is pretty straight forward if you keep up with the practice problems and homework. Exams are pretty difficult if you don't understand the exact proof formatting but she gives a LOT of partial credit. Quizzes can be confusing at times but TA's go over similar problems before you get a redo at the end of discussion and HW solutions are given.

chill teacher and cares about students personal lives. just take opportunities such as costudy sessions and practice problems and review them for mastery before exams. Dr. Parikh is very down to earth and is ver accessible in office hours.

The material in CS311 can be difficult to grasp but going to TA study sessions and Dr. Parikh's office hours are very helpful. Tests are difficult, but they are graded in a way that allows you to do well.

Formatting for proofs is emphasized way too much. None of the upper division math classes you'll take after this will be so adamant about proof formatting. The lectures are decent but the pacing seems pretty slow. Lots of examples are provided in class and the material is pretty straightforward.

Dr. Parikh was a fantastic professor. She was very accessible during office hours, and she was very down to earth. She is the smartest teacher that I've ever had, and she knows a lot about the subject she's teaching. Even though I'm not a math person, she explained concepts in an understandable way.

While this class can be tough, I feel that she does a good job at explaining things. It's really important in this class to ask questions and go to office hours for extra help/practice. On that note, there isn't a lot of practice for those who don't go to office hours or study sessions, so utilize those.
Very friendly teacher, wants students to succeed at her class. Lectures weren't always easy to comprehend. Exams were challenging but graders are lenient and it isn't to hard to keep an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had I known there were prerecorded lectures I would have used them much more than sitting in 1.5 hour ambiguous lectures. This is a mindset heavy class as it's full of things such as logical proofs. Professor is competent it's just the class itself is hard. Quizzes were much easier than exams and easy in general. Exams increased in difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is a nice, caring teacher that genuinely cares about her students. She makes a genuine attempt at fostering personal connections everyone. However, her lectures can be boring and drawn out. There are times where she cannot answer basic questions, and she can be cryptic with class logistics.

I struggled to understand Discrete, but that's more on me than the professor. Dr. Parikh explained concepts well, but flew through material due to the large amounts covered. Go through EVERYTHING when studying for exams, questions from help hours and homeworks are recycled.
Also, no curve for difficult exams means she graded very leniently.

Class covers a lot of material fast, especially in the graphs unit, so to gain a deeper understanding and for an easier time, definitely self-study some mathematical logic before hand. Learning To Reason by Nancy Rogers helped a lot. Learned lots of interesting things. NOTE: 5% participation earned by watching videos without skipping BEFORE class.

Although discrete math can be highly technical, the regularity of conventions and clear presentation of expectation makes most of the class revolve around understanding the logic puzzle rather than fighting for what the professor wants you to say. That said, falling behind on understanding technical concepts will make catching up nearly impossible.

Overall a hard class. I find discrete math to be interesting, but the lectures are long and boring. Lectures consisted of providing long, text-heavy definitions without examples. Professor is unwilling to answer RELEVANT questions during lectures. only during office hours. everything is graded HARSHLY, she did not release final exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ASK QUESTIONS. Lectures/videos are almost always confusing, especially after the first unit, but Dr. Parikh gives amazing answers if you just ask her a question. Tests are worth a lot and an A is 94+ but if you do all the work you will do good.

Once you pick up the pattern of questions from class and quizzes/tests, it gets very manageable. You learn a bunch of structured proofs. Professor was very sweet and down-to-earth. Lectures sometimes had ambiguity, but they were usually minor and the professor is actively open to questions.

She sometimes defers to asking students to come to her office hours to discuss questions rather than answering them in class, but for the most part she provides a lot of material to study for quizzes and exams, but both are pretty tricky
She will sometimes get confused by her own notes in lectures. Nevertheless, her lectures are mostly interesting and I think the tests are fair enough in terms of difficulty and time given.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Parikh is super knowledgeable about her subject, but her teaching comes off as heavy-handed, and she sort of dumps all the vocab and info all at once. Note-taking is important. Quizzes every week, but the TAs go over similar problems right before. Tests are 5-6 questions each, and they're similar to problems on past homework or in study sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: lectures are very long. she covers the content but struggles to answer student's questions sometimes. tests are only around 5 questions, so if you struggle with a topic and it shows up on the test, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
She is not the best professor but definitely not the worst. 

If you do not show up to class, ignore the quizzes, or just copy the solutions from the homework you should expect to do poorly. However, it is possible to get an A in the class if you just go through everything provided and stay on top of your topics. Material is dense but not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh was a pretty caring teacher. That being said, the course is not very easy to grasp at times. Lots of the material is pretty dreadful to try and figure out, but Parikh will do her best to help you out if you go to her office hours.

Parikh as a professor makes the subject alright, however, Discrete Math in general is an absolutely abismal subject to take no matter who's teaching. Make sure to watch the pre-lecture videos, they have very useful information. She lets you write down some notes to take to exams as well which helps.

Dr. Parikh was very accomodating and a great lecturer. In 311 you have to watch pre videos before coming to class which really cements the knowledge in your head which she then expands on in class. Great professor and great class.

You have to work outside of class by watching pre lecture videos and having weekly homework, discussion problems, and quizzes. But the answers are made available to you, so there's no reason to get stuff wrong. Hard class to get through if you don't like proofs. She herself is a nice person and she's passionate, just not a fun subject

Pay attention in discussion section, the TA's are helpful and the problems sometimes end up on exams word for word. Her reviews also have questions that are similar format to those on the actual exam.

Homework assignments were sometimes time consuming and a bit difficult to complete since we often learned the material covered on the homework the day before it was due. Tests were similar to the homework assignments and practice tests, and they were not too difficult if you paid attention during class and really understood all of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely important to understand the material, as are all of the practice problems Dr. Parikh provides. Although the material being covered is pretty dense and challenging, Dr. Parikh does a great job of making it manageable and understanding the kinds of problems she will have on her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are really dry, puts most people to sleep. Attendance is taken every class - try not to be late. Latter part of course appeared rushed. Some of the content here is hand-waved through. Expectations were clearly outlined and tests are a fair assessment of the content. Book is not required. Homework and discussions were graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is an awesome professor. Sometimes teaches in flipped classroom style, which is very convenient. Videos are concise and helpful. Homework solutions are posted ahead of time so you can check your work. I learned a lot from this class and it was very fun. Lectures can be slow if you have worked ahead because she gives people time to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is a good lecturer, but sometimes she can get confused by her own notes. However, for the most part she is very helpful, especially her pre-lecture videos. Class is very easy to get an A in, just pay attention in class and do the homeworks.

Professor Parikh seems to struggle teaching in an online format. Participation went from 100 students to 60 students in each lecture by end of semester. 1-3 hours of required pre-lecture videos, sometimes posted late the night before lecture. 50+% of lectures is her mumbling/making mistakes to the point where it can get difficult to follow her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Programming for Correctness and Performance alongside OS this semester. Was doable since my other two classes were easy. Class is taught through an edX made by van de Geijn, and the TAs are good at explaining the concepts. Tests would have been harder closed-note. Utilizes basic linear algebra (doable), ask for help if you had bad linalg prof.

Overall decent, lectures are pretty dry though. If you show up to the beginning of class and then later on you dip I think you still get credit. I often went back to the recorded lectures and put them on 2x speed. Easy enough class if you can pay attention long enough.

Dr. Parikh cares about students and gives good lectures. The only thing is she does not tell us what style we need to follow in the exams sometimes. I feel it's important to make sure your answer styles in the exams are the same as the answer styles in the homework. Or you may lose style points in the exams. She did not post final grades on Canvas.

Dr. Parikh is a very good lecturer with a lacking curriculum. She does her very best to take questions and answer everything, but she seems disorganized at times, with many students asking for clarification on homework and her responding that actually the homework was wrong and she'll update it for next time. Teacher: 9/10, Class: 6/10.

Dr. Parikh is an awesome lecturer. She has a clear agenda and itinerary decided for each day of the lecture and provides concrete examples about the material being covered in class. The homework and quizzes are fair and within the scope of the material learned. Tests are slightly more challenging than homework. She does rush to finish sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is a wonderful instructor! She explains everything very clearly and takes time to make sure we understand, even in the virtual setting. The homework is very fair, nothing outside of course content, and the exams are only slightly harder than the homework. Don't skip class though, you can quickly fall behind!

Parikh was a very good professor. She always tried her best to keep the lecture entertaining. But still, lectures can be quite boring and dry at some points. Homeworks are just a completion grade, weekly quizzes, and discussion sections as usual. Exams are quite doable and not hard at all, just be punctual. The final exam was a take-home exam.

I actually enjoyed this class! I've actually been more interested in the theoretical side of computer science because of Dr. Parikh too. Dr. Parikh is incredibly nice and she really tries to engage with her students. Homeworks are difficult, but quizzes and exams are much easier. Overall, great class!

Parikh is a pretty good professor for discrete math! Content is sometimes confusing and dry but it's just bc it's discrete math. Doing pre-lecture readings / videos can take a bit of time, but tests are very fair with good review in discussions / practice tests. Course is well organized & they respond well to questions. Don't buy the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is super nice, I don't know what some people are on about. I see that some people say she is boring, which is NOT true. The COURSE MATERIAL is boring, not the professor. It's not her fault that discrete math puts even the nerdiest kids to sleep. The material sucks, but its required. Great professor. Tests are fair. Directions clear. 9/10.

She is a very nice professor and she is willing to answer all questions even if it takes up some of the lecture time. For tests, they are pretty easy and similar to homework and discussion problems. There is only one homework per week and some recorded videos to watch before each lecture so the class is not too difficult.

Dr. Parikh is a really good professsor if you make an effort! If you have questions do not hesitate to ask her during office hours she will explain it as many times and in different ways till you understand it. Work out all the practice problems from class and discussion because the test questions are really similar to those
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh cares about you learning the material, and is really helpful when you go to office hours/ask questions. She can be intimidating at times though, and sometimes gets frustrated. The grading in the class itself is extremely lenient and the workload is low.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do all the posted homework and go to class. Tests are pretty easy and there will be no surprises if you do everything. It would be nice if she learned how to be less frank when she talks to her students. Sometimes she comes off as intimidating, but overall a pretty nice teacher.

Explained content very clearly in class. Effective use of examples to illustrate concepts. Was incredibly well organised for a new professor. Loved the problem-solving ethos Parikh inspired; her in-class activities, discussion and homework questions provided ample opportunities to develop problem-solving skills. An enjoyable and fulfilling course.

Extremely long & boring lectures. Typos in quizzes/exams. Course was decent in-person but terrible online. Workload increased; she started taking attendance for lecture/discussion & assigning an hour+ of pre-lecture videos. Actual lecture didn't cover any new content anymore. Responses on Piazza are useless & she gets irritated at questions asked.

This class level of difficulty isn't the issue w the class. After online schooling began we had to watch around 2 hours of videos before a 1.5-hour class, the amount of work dramatically increased. she is very honest; however, she can get very irritated when people ask questions & skip steps while introducing new content because they are "implied".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is pretty easy, but the lectures are VERY dry and usually word for word from the textbook (You'll fall asleep). The course work is pretty light, with a HW, discussion, and quiz every week. Tests are also easy and like the sample exams. After moving online, the amount of work and assignments due were 10X what they were pre-corona.

Not the best professor in my opinion bc she gets annoyed at people asking questions sometimes. But overall she is nice and has decent lectures. Tests are very similar to class work so shes a pretty fair grader. Not the best, not the worst.

Coursework was relatively light for the class, tests were pretty easy too and she's a pretty lenient grader. If you show up to class (she had quizzes that were basically attendance, but she was talking about switching it up in the future) and put some effort into the online edX course (which was our homework) it's an easy A.

Her lectures help a ton to learn the concepts with a ton of slides, but you won't do well on the exams without completing the weekly Quest homework. I thought that Professor Thomas was very well-versed on the content and explained concepts very well. Checked understanding with instapolls so that you could see if you knew the concept. Overhated tbh

Very nice person but lectures are so so so disorganized. TAs never knew how to solve the homework or practice problems and they were always way too hard because her lectures never prepared you well enough. I studied extremely hard, went to tutoring, read the textbook, did the HW, and do not know what I could have done differently
Lectures were required but useless, had to self study using the homeworks, no curves on the exams even though the class average was in the 50s and 60s. Try not take

Lectures and discussions were required but completely useless. She was really charismatic, but really did not help with actual graded things. Exams were 2/3 hw, 1/3 new stuff and the new stuff was always too hard. Failing averages on 2/3 midterms + the final with only multiple choice tests that offer no partial credit. She is a strict no curver.

Dr thomas was great. Her exams are literally HW problems + 1 or 2 conceptual questions, not hard if you study. She's nice and idk why people are complaining, I didn't have prior knowledge of physics and did fine. Practice hws and pay attention during her test review session. Discussion is useless but you only need to participate once. Great class.

DO NOT TAKE HER!!! Her accent is so strong and I would go to class and I literally could not understand a single thing she was saying. There are instapolls in class but she kind of stopped doing them because no one shows up to class. She often gets confused when working out problems in class. I tried teaching myself, but still makes no sense.

This professor is not clear at all on what is going to be on the exam. Attendance is mandatory but lectures seem to have no use, and the textbook is confusing. Tried to self teach but even that wasn't super helpful.
Do not take this professor for PHY 317K unless you have previous prior physics knowledge

Lectures fast. Oftentimes gets confused about the problems on her slides and cannot solve them herself. Homework is extremely difficult, exams are more fair but you will still find yourself unprepared because it will be unclear what/how to prepare for exams. Does not curve even if exam averages are abyssal.

Super nice and respectable. Couldn't teach a  rock to sit still. Just reads what's on the slides and expects everyone to get it. Maybe just not my style, but I found it very difficult to learn from her.

Lecture is not always the easiest to follow. If you are lost, I would recommend reading the textbook, she posts a free pdf version of it, it is easy to follow & has good example problems with detailed break down.  Exams are similar to homeworks. I know there are better profs, but if this is the only class that works for you, you are not doomed.
Truly terrible. Exams are hard and not reflective. She does not explain topics well and moves very fast. Avoid taking.
Honestly she is kind of hard compared to the other prof i would not take her since the other ones are a lot more lax. she also doesn't curve and her exams are hard.

Lectures moved so fast, but she's very willing to explain topics outside of class until you fully understand it. Fascinating class content, the Python simulations are really helpful if you're a visual learner

The class itself is pretty easy. She essentially just goes over the notes that are given to the entire class, so class is pretty much optional. Homework would consist of finding what you needed in the notes, and exams were open note, open book. I didn't really learn much, and lectures were kind of dull.
avoid taking her if possible, lectures are incredibly boring and just reads off from the files. Had a problem about a grade and wasn't understanding nor helpful.

reads off of the screen, not engaging, switch syllabus towards the end from exam being online to in person without much of a warning. not understanding about creating a clear announcement on canvas about her test switch policy and she not engaging at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures consist of her scrolling and reading through a Jupyter Notebook file. She also posted these online, and they were actually very good study material. She speaks very softly so it's very hard to understand, and even harder not to fall asleep. Attendance was not mandatory so I stopped showing up. Weekly homework and exams were pretty easy.

Class was not very difficult, but Dr. Thomas' lectures were basically her reading off of her Jupyter Notebooks. I stopped showing up after a few weeks, just did the weekly problem sets on my own and exams were all online. Her TA this sem, Jonathan, was very helpful and quick to answer questions through email. Didn't feel like I learned much though.

Didn't buy the textbook for this course and I was fine.  The lectures consisted of the prof reading from a note page so I never went.  Exams are online, taken at home, and open everything (notes, class materials, internet) so it wasn't too challenging but I don't think I got a good grasp of some content as a result of Dr. Thomas' teaching style.

This class was an easy A, but I didn't really learn much. She gave one homework a week, and the exams and final were take home. Lectures consisted of her scrolling through a google colab pretty quickly, so it was hard to keep up with the derivations. However, those google colabs were incredible study resources. Pretty generous grading scale.

Amazing professor, easily the best I have had so far! His lectures are very engaging and you will feel motivated to learn and retain the content of his class! He also does Kahoots every lecture with a chance to win prizes.

Amazing professor, his lectures feel like movies and he really knows how to keep 300 students engaged! He also does Kahoots every lecture with a chance to win prizes!! Truly the best professor I have had so far.

Truly the best professor I have had. He is funny, passionate, and helpful. This class is very easy if you attend the class, do the practice tests, and do the homework. Anyone who takes him is truly lucky.
Amazing. More than amazing. Love his class.

Yeah this guy is the goat. If you show up to class and review the practice questions before exams I genuinely don't see how you'd get below an A. If you get a B or below in the class, it speaks volumes to you more than anything(coming from a 3.4 STEM major). Best lecturer I've had so far.
The actual GOAT please take this man's class if you have to take Econ. There's extra credit opportunities and the lectures are very engaging and fun.
Best professor ever

He makes his lectures fun and engaging, really made learning economics enjoyable. This is not an easy A you definitely have to put in the effort and study a lot to do well on exams. He provides practice questions for each chapter that are very similar to the ones on the tests, which helps a lot. Just study the practice questions and you will pass.

So fun and easily manageable while taking calc 1. There are lectures 2 a week, and they're really interesting. You read 1 chapter a week and do in-Quizitive every Tuesday by 8 pm. He does do in-class Kahoot's and Think-Pair-Shares for participation points, but we have 3 weeks left of classes, and almost everyone already has enough points.
Amazing lecturer.
Love Prof. Mateer, he's very funny and keeps his lecture engaging. If you are thinking about taking this class, I highly suggest you do. (Winners of his kahoots win $10-$20 btw)

My fav class this sem!!! He gives super amazing lectures, makes all the concepts very easy to understand and always cares about making students engaged during class. Very kind, funny and knowledgeable man who cares about his students' success. Take his class, you'll never regret it!!!

I was dreading taking an economics class—I was a mostly straight A student in high school, but nearly failed macro. I took micro with Dr. Mateer, and honestly, it was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He makes lectures fun and engaging with games and activities that demonstrate key economics concepts. I highly recommend! Take this class!

Dirk has easily been my favorite professor so far. He wants you to care about Econ as much as he does. Every day, he made class entertaining with fun class demonstrations, and he would offer prizes for participation. The class itself is not that difficult; read the textbook, go to lectures, and you'll be fine.
Very light class! Tests essentially mirrored practice exams in Canvas. Weekly discussions were boring but will boost your grade. Professor Mateer himself is amazing
good teacher and really easy to get an A, i just got busy halfway through the semester

Dirk is the best professor I've had. Fantastic lecturer and a super forgiving grading system (everyone should get A's as long as they show up and try). Don't need to study too much for tests and very engaging in class as he gives out candy for participation & money for kahoot wins. Only downside to this glorious man is his nephew Mateer (OU's QB).

Love Prof. Mateer! He's such a kind and funny guy. Engaging class, lots of extra credit to help out your grade. Love him for making the final optional. InQuizitives are easy and helpful, tests are straightforward, textbook is interesting to read. I grew to love econ through this class. Take Mateer, you won't regret it.

if you're looking for an easy, non-time consuming, and somewhat engaging ugs, take economics and ethics. Mateer doesn't just do a great job of teaching the material, he really tries to get everybody engaged with it. If you're not an econ major, please consider taking this class. If you are, consider it less, you won't learn much.

Dirk is the GOAT. King made everything easy and he was just so real. Nothing about the course was hard and exams were similar to the Kahoots and the homework. He's funny and always gave out prizes for first in the Kahoots or for participating when he needed volunteers. He bought me a frosty from Wendy's one time and also brought donuts to class.

Dirk is probably one of the best professors here on campus. He makes all the concepts easy to understand and genuinely cares that his students learn them. So much opportunity for extra credit and the exams are not hard to prepare for (a lot of questions are pretty much what you see in class). He also bought me a Frosty from Wendy's 🐐.

In-class demos are fun and helpful, attendance is greatly encouraged. He's kind, funny, and understanding. Notes are easy to follow. Tests are very straightforward; he posts a topic list, as well as the number of questions per topic. The extra credit saved me from taking the final. Grade is based off cumulative points earned throughout the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made learning Microeconomics interesting with lectures and interactive examples. While attendance is technically not required, the more you show up, the more points you will get due to the Kahoot/TPS, and the extra credit you can gain from that. He also goes over example questions that are similar to what is on our test.

Dr. Mateer is an amazing professor. The class is relatively easy, and it's not difficult to earn an A if you put in some study time. Class participation is part of the grade. He offers extra credit. The InQuizitives are an easy 100 too. He's super engaging and gives out money and candy each class.

amazing professor, go to lectures! the way he explains things in person makes it 100x easier to understand. Gives more skips on tests than other econ professors and he wrote the textbook they all use! super easy class to pass and he genuinely wants to get to know his students

Dirk was genuinely so funny and caring. I would say some of the demonstrations didn't necessarily help with economic concepts, but they were very fun. I attended every lecture and stuff from in-person lectures were brought back at tests so definitely attend even though it's not mandatory. The tests were easy if you just study.
Dr. Mateer is amazing. Super engaging, and makes sure the material sticks with you. If you put in effort and show up to most of the lectures, you'll have no problem getting a good score. Take him!!

Dirk is friendly and passionate about teaching, but lectures are often inefficient/irrelevant. The textbook has the important content for exams, while in-class “activities” meant to be engaging are a waste of time (ex: donut eating contests). Exams are fair but get harder through the semester. Class attendance is needed for participation points.

Prof Mateer is the best! He has so many fun lectures throughout the semester and we do kahoots pretty much every day, so the class never feels too boring. As long as you read the textbook, do the Inquizitives, and pay attention in class, this class is overall not too challenging  and very light on homework.

Professor Mateer made this UGS super fun and interactive! He gives out free candy and treats throughout the year and has 1-2 kahoots pretty much every class, so the class feels like a break from other classes. If you study the practice exam questions he gives you, you're pretty much guaranteed an A. He's also super approachable and down to earth.
Easiest Micro professor, attending lectures is not required but extremely beneficial. Exam questions might be ripped straight from kahoots or class discussions

BEST ECON TEACHER EVER!! He makes economics so interesting and makes you want to come to class even though it isn't technically mandatory... (you should go since he has in-class participation). Exams are relatively easy if you study and look back at past Kahoots, TPS, and InQuizitives. He gives out $10-$20 if you get 1st place in Kahoots! TAKE HIM!

Dirk is an amazing professor who makes a big class feel small and is genuinely funny. He uses hands-on activities and even hands out about $10 every class. His three test skips are generous, and his exams are fair. He also wrote the textbook. I couldn't recommend him more.

Dirk is amazing. Most of your grade is Kahoot and TPS, which is so free. He gives money to the winners of the Kahoot, ranging from $10-20. Dirk makes every lecture easy, understandable, a good time, and worth it. Kahoot and TPS are used for your attendance, which earns you points. The exams are exactly what you learn during class.

Dirk is amazing. Most of your grade is Kahoot and TPS, which is so free. He gives money to the winners of the Kahoot, ranging from $10-20. Dirk makes every lecture easy, understandable, a good time, and worth it. The Kahoot and TPS are what are used for your attendance, which gives you points. The exams are exactly what you learn during class.

Dirk is a super fun teacher who wants all of his students to succeed, there is extra credit and three tests in this class, but they are all easy tests where you can get three skips on each test that if you skip it gets counted as correct. I would 100% take this class again.

Mateer makes econ engaging every step of the way. He makes me want to come to a traditionally unpopular subject and learn. His text book is fun to read and his weekly assignments are easy and take about an hour. Overall, best class I've taken my freshman year.
its econ, its hard. but dr mateer makes his lectures fun and engaging. he also cares about us a lot (he bought be a frosty hehehe) and he gives out money in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mateer is awesome. Would highly recommend this class. Professor Mateer is a great lecturer and makes a huge class still feel personal. Exams are not too hard, and many questions are pulled directly from the practice problem he gives so study and you will do great.
Professor Mateer is the absolute goat
Most engaging professor I have ever had. Also deeply knows what he is talking about and is able to explain it in a way that anyone could understand.

Professor Dirk is very kind and tries to make lectures engaging, but the Kahoots and TPS (Google Forms) are stressful, tricky, and timed, making the class high-pressure. The point-based grading is confusing, and it's hard to know your actual grade. If you prefer traditional lectures, this class is not for you. Lots of reading, high stress envirnmnt

Mateer makes lectures fun and interesting and will use videos, interactive activities, and Kahoots to teach. I recommend going to class, as 20% of your grade is in class stuff, and once you hit 100% in class points, it becomes extra credit. If you do the chapter problems and Inquisitives, you will do well on the test. You get cash for a Kahoot win.
Dr. Mateer tried to make lectures engaging with demos. Super generous since he gives out cash and food for winning kahoots and going up on stage. Very manageable to get an A
He is just awesome. Such a great professor; really cares about making the class feel fun and not boring; tests are quite easy and is very conversational. Sticks to his values which I respect heavily.

I love this professor so much. He clearly loves what he does, participation and extra credit is kahoots and surveys in class. He is so fun, interactive, and his lectures are incredible. Honestly, best class I've taken, I'm not even an econ major or anything related, but loved this class so much. Take this class very very highly recommended.
Very easy class, we are given everything we need to do well. Mateer is very engaging and has been one of my favorite professors here at UT. Take him.

I took him for micro, not having much prior knowledge. His lectures were engaging and he seems very excited what he is teaching. Lots of resources given for tests making it easy to do well. Attendance is important to get the points (200 based off of kahoot). Inquizitive HW could take a while but very helpful. You get 3 skips on exams too!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is one of my favorite professors so far. His lectures are awesome and engaging. He clearly outlines what is going to be on the exams (you have seen all of the questions prior) and gives tons of extra credit. He cares about his students and is a great guy overall

A truly excellent economics professor—just attend class and you'll do well. I'm not an Econ major, and I still really enjoyed his course. The exams aren't too difficult since he clearly outlines exactly what to study. He's not only a great professor but an even better person. His final lecture was incredibly inspiring!
He's a dog. Class was always super entertaining and plenty of extra credit/outside of class materials to help with grade.

Good professor. Engaging class with lot's of interactive activities throughout and working with others is encouraged. Easiest testing style I've seen. Every question was already on a Kahoot, in class, or on InQuizitive. Realistically could be more difficult but you get out what you put in. Dirk is great.

Aside from academics, Dirk is just a great man. He is very level-headed and even tempered. He loves his job. He runs from one end of the class to the other engaging with people. Good luck on the kahoots, winner gets 10 bucks and their are plenty of prizes 2nd and 3rd. There are even prizes for participation. Thanks so much Dirk. All love homie.

I took “Economics and Ethics” with Professor Mateer, and he was fantastic! He's a passionate and engaging lecturer who makes the material interesting. The class is easy, with in-class Kahoots and Google Forms for participation grades. Weekly Inquisitive assignments are straightforward, and the sample exams on Canvas closely match the actual tests.

He's SO NICE and very approachable.  This class felt fun going to and he PAYS you to participate (candy for activities and $10 for winning Kahoots).  The exams have 3 skips and are relatively easy (some questions from random class examples though).  Discussions are redundant and boring, but everything counts for points.  Lectures are engaging!

This was an amazing ugs that wasn't very time consuming. It is definitely easy to get an A with the loads of resources provided. The test are also pretty easy as long as you paid attention and there's a lot of room for mistakes in the grading criteria.

This was an ok ugs that I took because it seemed easy since I took econ in my senior year. However it is extremely boring if you dont like econ. Super forgiving grading and it is very easy to get a good grade. the professor is very nice and good at teaching. Doesn't fulfill any flags so pretty much useless unless you are a business/econ major.

Mateer's lectures have plenty of examples and tries to keep things funny. Unfortunately he speaks very quickly and can be hard to follow. KHAN ACADEMY SAVED ME IN THIS CLASS. I would recommend that plus re-reading the textbook to make sure you have an understanding of the list of concepts he publishes before exams.
Comically bad at teaching and comically unorganized. Avoid at all costs.

Her lectures were most of the time very interesting. Started out as a great course but soon realized tests are nothing like the homeworks. Also, your grades on tests/assignments depended on your rank in the class compared to your classmate's grades. Doesn't curve grades. Weekly homework. Tests are hard & don't align with homework.
The lectures are easy to understand but the tests are tough so studying is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her powerpoints look easy to understand, but the tests are incredibly difficult. You have to self-teach complex concepts by reading the book and constantly review material outside of class to make sure you at least pass. Graded on a rank curve, which is her excuse to make her tests even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Shamoun for ECO304K, the class itself was not bad, but the grading policy and tests were very unclear and difficult to follow. Her lectures were fine- but I learned everything from the textbook or an online resource, not from her.

Do yourself a favor and avoid this class at all costs! coming from someone that cares about school and grades this class has quite literally ruined my GPA. The tests make up pretty much all the grades and are pretty much set up to fail you. The Homeworks are Difficult and the TA's are NOT willing to help and are completely different to the lectures

Please avoid this class at ALL COSTS. Coming from someone who cares about school and grades, I still found this class EXTREMELY difficult. If you have the option to take another professor use that to your advantage!!. This class very test heavy and the test have open ended questions which affects your grade immensely, and its set up to fail you.

The exams cover a lot of material and the questions tend to be a lot more difficult then those on the homework. Even if you don't think the questions are difficult, it will be hard to complete all of the questions in the time frame since you aren't allowed to use a calculator. She does realize it's a difficult class so she grades on a rank scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This professor assigns a lot of homeworks, does not explain the material well and doesnt provide extra examples when students arent getting the concepts. Her tests are extremely difficult, and youre not allowed to use a calculator. So for the first exam youll find yourself having to calculate the midpoint formula BY HAND. Avoid at all costs.

The professor lacked the professionalism and composure I would hope for in the way discussions were led. I feel like the lectures were helpful to understanding the material at the beginning of the course, but slowly moved away from meaningful discussion over time.

Very interesting class to take. Class discussions were very engaging and it is a class I looked forward to attending every week. You will need to read, but it is manageable. For the final project, you have a lot of freedom, which is nice. My only comment is that you need to study a lot for the midterm because grading can be harsh. Totally recommend
Great professor, and I signed up for another one of his courses!

daniel was a great professor! the class itself, full transparency, it doesn't entirely fall in line with my belief system, however, he was very inviting, and it is truly a safe space to have a voice. as long as you did all that was required, i find it harder to fail than pass; i genuinely never stressed. be respectful, enjoy, and get a good giggle!

The class was fantastic! The lectures were super interesting and I really appreciated the way Dr dillon approached topics and he was funny. But the midterm was graded really harsh everything else is graded on completion so that's good.

The best SOC class I've taken! Prof. dillon is funny, engaging, caring, and taught me so much. Readings were amazing. Midterm is a test + essay (you get a day to do it), relatively easy. He makes it so you don't have to do the final but it's a creative project so I enjoyed it. I'll miss this class and I hope to take another with him in the future!

This is not a very good professor. He does not have any industry experience and his background is just physics and water. I don't get why UT Austin keeps hiring inexperienced professors being so close to Houston. His lecture notes and writing are a mess. He makes us show memes every class, because of how boring it gets!
Best class I've ever taken. People say it's hard, but it's so light if you just lock in. 10/10 would take again, all thanks to Professor DiCarlo
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Is it fun? No, its thermo. DiCarlo makes it as enjoyable as thermo could possibly be though, and makes an effort to know all the students. Topics are not digestible just through lectures, and required lots of reviewing notes, textbooks, and office hours (always very approachable). Test heavy, but if you understand concepts, they aren't that bad.

He is very disorganized and sloppy. He makes many mistakes. He is very hard to understand. No one understood what he was saying. The only thing good about him is that he had a good sense of humor, other than that, he is a terrible prof. I wouldn't recommend anyone taking a class with him.

Genuinely an amazing professor that really cares and makes you want to come to class. Great lectures make it super easy to pay attention, and the smaller class size helps you feel more comfortable asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor DiCarlo makes coming to class fun he stops the lectures halfway through class so students can stand up and tell dad jokes, a much needed break from a 1.5 hour lecture of heavy material. He cares about each student and makes an effort to learn everyones name and interests. Thermo is a hard subject but he keeps you invested and tests easy.

Class is so unnecessarily difficult. There are almost no pre-worked homework problems, so there is almost no way to practice. Unorganaized. He'll forget to add crucial info, or it will be unclear where it is. Prof is funny, but that doesn't mean much when you have no idea how you're performing. Unfortunately, this class is required for PGE.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Dicarlo is not the best lecturer as he goes through material very quickly and does not explain concepts deeply enough. For most of the homeworks, you will have little idea on how to do a majority of the problems and so going to office hours is highly recommended. Tests aren't that bad if you get the general concepts and homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awesome guy. Class is super hard but he's an awesome professor. He is super funny, has really good understanding of the material, and will help students out. His class is super test heavy (85%), so try and do well on exams.
Class is hard in nature. Exams can be very difficult. However, he really does try and look after the students.

Professor Ditmire is clearly a very talented physicist, but he falls short when it comes to actually teaching students. He moves VERY quickly through his notes. His notes are terribly organized which makes it even harder to keep up with him. He does not give enough time on instapolls and closes them abruptly. You will have to learn on your own.

DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. should retire atp, no one would miss him here. don't ask questions because he'll look at you like you're challenged. also changed tests from take home to in class, tests are 26 questions long, final is 45% of the grade. just evil work all throughout. also he's from prague (he'll make sure you know this)

Awful subject and even worse professor. His lectures are terrible since he writes on the blackboard very quickly and messily. Lectures are not recorded and there are no online materials for you to go back and review. Only upside of this course is that the exams are open note and online from home.

Lectures are hard to follow and not helpful for homework's or exams. Had to self teach myself. He's a chill, nice, and easy going person. Tests were online and take home. Haven't taken final, but believe final is as well. Tests are formatted like exams.

There are no lecture slides or recordings - he derives equations on a chalkboard the whole time. If you fall behind in this class, it is almost impossible to catch up because you don't even know what topics are being covered (again, no slides). All assignments and tests are online, un-proctored, but still very difficult. Final is 45% of your grade.

he's so nice and so knowledgeable and so passionate about lasers! unfortunately he's just a terrible teacher, his lectures are extremely difficult to follow & are mostly about deriving equations rather than applications. the exam time is way too short for the # of questions (esp w calculations). he's very easy to reach outside of class at least

Todd is such a genuine professor. His love of lasers and physics really shine through in his excitement in lecture. He loves to play rock and metal before class. He is very accesible outside of class and loves to answer questions during class. Honestly one of the best professors at UT. Will buy everyone beers after tests.
had this class at 8am, never went, read the textbook, 10/10 would recommend, todd always down to get drinks with students, wish i wouldve went
His lectures are a bit difficult to follow at times but he is a very chill and nice person. He takes the class out during the semester and has a fusion start-up that sounds super interesting!

Lectures were initially hard to grasp because of his teaching style, but they're still good to attend to know the expected topics and get extra credit (instapolls). He makes up for it in office hours--he walks you through the problems step by step. Exams similar to hw. Super chill--once gave the class a free 100 on an exam since Quest was down.

Overall, Physics 2 is a very dense course. Although his lectures may be tough to follow (as mentioned by others), he makes up for it by formatting his exams closely with the HW. Outside of classwork, he is a very chill dude and takes the class out for beers.

He only derives equations in class, with no practice problems given as an example of how to use these derived equations. You'll need to teach yourself, especially since the homework and exam problems are incredibly hard. I would not recommend anyone take him for this course, as he has been one of the worst teaching professors I've had.

he doesn't teach at all, he just scribbles ! his exams are difficult (57 class avg on the first one). he promises a curve but doesn't curve in the end. he also doesn't factor in instapolls which he says are EC. he's the one who assigns grade cutoffs so you'll never know what your actual grade is until the end. one of the worst profs @ UT

(302L) You learn more by teaching yourself than by attending his lectures where he just derives formulas. It's still good to attend as he's an interesting guy and Instapolls provide a little extra credit. HW/exams all online on Quest. Caution: the curve he talked about all semester was not as big as we were expecting. You can still do well, though!

Super sweet professor, encourages students to ask questions and participate in class. Physics is hard but he tries to make it fun by playing music and taking the class out for beers occasionally. Open book exams that are given online along with weekly hw. Overall great prof would take again.

Prof. Ditmire is a great guy to talk to, but not so much as a teacher. He gets so excited about a concept and talks so fast that he fails to clarify a concept. The office hours didn't help that much, and I ended up teaching myself (also bc of corona). The tests are very hard, though he loves to talk about his lasers!

Great guy, less so of a professor, but if having a professor interested in his work pulls you in as well you'd do perfect. Caution though as final is worth 50% of grade and guessing on his exams is next to impossible.
Tough but fair
Ditmire is an awesome prof, though physics blows. He loves to talk about his lasers, which are a lot more interesting than gauss's law
One of the best professors I have had.  I expected to sleep through physics but this guy kept it interesting (well as interesting as physics at 9:30 in the morning can be)

I don't think he is hard, or maybe engineer physics isn't hard. however I think he did terrible job on explaining stuffs. Also, every time I went to his office to ask question, he seemed annoyed like I owe him 200 bucks or something, but he seems pretty happy to help other students. Well, I still made an A even though he doesn't like me. hahahaha
Well, I thought his jokes were funny.  I guess I just have the humor of a freshman.  Yes, the exams were hard but I did learn a lot.
He is hard and irresponsible, he likes to say a few jokes during class that can only make freshmen laugh. You probably will have a fun time but you won't learn much and your grade will suffer.
Super professor!  Very energetic and fun.  I learned a lot in what is a really hard class.

One of the worst professor in UT, he did a terrible job to explain the material and the tests are hard. Final exam take 50% of the whole grade. I won't take him if I have to retake engineer physics one more time.

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER... not only will you not leardn ANYTHING from him but you will also FAIL every single test. he derives equations and then moves on, leaving everyone confused. seems like a smart good guy, but when it comes to teaching, horrible! his tests are very hard(20-24 questions) 1.5 hours. if you dont care about your education and gr
No Comments

We had weekly quizzes instead of psets and they can't put problems which require lots of thinking on the quizzes, unfortunately making the class very mechanical. Dr. Dillig goes very fast in lecture, but she's willing to stop and explain if needed (and she brings candy!). Curve is also very generous; I wouldn't stress over exam grades.

Dr. Dillig is not a good professor. She lectures way too quickly, is barely accessible outside of class, and mostly dismisses student questions. She also assigns HW due the day before the test, even though the material is assessed on a later exam. Despite the generous curve, wouldn't recommend taking her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are dense and move very quickly. Knowledge is tested through weekly quizzes, so even though homework is optional, completing it is essential to understand the topics. Tests are quite difficult and make up a large portion of the grade, but the final grade is generously curved. Dr. Dillig is nice, understanding, and very open to feedback.

Isil is an exceptional lecturer and person. Her course might pose a challenge if you're new to this level of mathematical rigor, but both she and the TAs are readily available to support. Grading is prompt and precise.  While the exams are very hard, the class is curved, offering a fair assessment. Btw, chocolates are distributed during lectures!

This class is no joke, but Isil is a fantastic professor. She knows her stuff extremely well and is very helpful during office hours. Lectures are fast-paced and challenging, yet they are clear and organized. Accessible online as well. Collaboration isn't allowed, but you can always consult the (optional) textbook for extra help. Highly recommend.

I really enjoyed Isil's lectures and the material in the course. I've both taken this class with her and TA'd, and I think she presents the material in a very accessible way. As long as you are able to put in some work outside of class (going to OHs, etc.) if you don't understand something, then you will get a good grade in the course.

Very knowledgeable and amazing lecturer. She does go very fast, so you need to continuously remind her to slow down and re-explain, which she is happy to do so. Problem sets are difficult, but through office hours, they are doable. Tests are very challenging. Beware of the 1st exam (much more hard than expected). Class is nicely curved at the end.

Exams are very difficult but the class is curved. Homework is very similar to lectures, but often goes more in depth/ties 2 concepts together. She always welcomes questions in lecture (which is on Zoom) and usually does a good job at explaining things. The slides are all on her class webpage and are helpful to reference later on.

Isil cares a lot about her students and has a great understanding of discrete math. Homework is difficult and tests are really hard but the class is curved so if you're above average on everything you'll probably end up with a good grade. Grading is 50% homework and 50% tests. Lectures are on Zoom. Try really hard cause content is very difficult.

Absolutely wonderful professor who knows discrete math very well. Open to questions and participation in class. Homeworks became more doable/got used to them toward the end. Exams are challenging but classed is curved. Do textbook problems, discussion problems, and redo homework to succeed on exams. Office hours are useful. sometimes fast-paced
GOAT professor. Really cares about her students. Exams are difficult but graded generously and there's a nice curve at the end.

Isil is a great person and always wants to help students succeed. She is very smart and course material sometimes flew over my head but she is very open to questions. Homeworks and exams are hard but help you learn. Looking online and at the textbook can help you with the HW.

Isil is amazing. First of all, her lecture slides are very thorough. She works through problems, is very interactive, and also got us in groups to work through stuff ourselves too. Drops the lowest homework assignment. Tests were pretty hard, but its a curved class. Your understanding of Discrete Math will be far better after you take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great instructor, reasonable workload, and very interesting topic. Lectures were easy to follow and well organized. I definitely recommend her courses!

Isil is a great teacher. Her course is well-organized, and she explains the topics crystal clear. She also cares about the students. Don't hesitate to ask questions.  Course workload is medium. There are some assignments and exams, but no project. If you do the assignments, the exam won't be hard.

The class is very well prepared, it has very good slides. The presentation is extremely clear. If you ever read Isil's paper, you will know why. Even if there are things unclear, if someone asks, Isil would like to explain in more detail.  No project at all. Light homework, but there are exams. Workload OK.  BTW, I took the class three years back.

Isil is one of the best professors that Ive ever met at UT Austin. She can explain the course material clearly and make everything easy to understand. The course is well-designed and slides are well-organized. It is fantastic overall.

Isil's a terribly professor overall, but she's great as a person. She also gives out candies in class. Well, honestly, her lectures and TAs were both pretty terribly when I took the course, so I hope you at least get decent TAs.
