The key to doing well in the class is to get the textbook (pdf available), read it, practice the problems before lecture.
Very hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There's a lot of material. Though Isil explains it well, it's covered too quickly during class. I recommend going to class, reviewing notes afterwards, doing the homework, and looking in the textbook for extra problems to practice for the challenging tests. Just doing what's required may not be enough if you want to excel. Practice is key to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bro thinks he's Ray Delahanty and I'm here for it

Your grade is basically dependent on your group project! He is very passionate about what he does and encourages students to find their area of interest as well. He is always open to criticism and has a few assignments asking us for our opinions on the class and civil engineering as a whole.

He is a very engaged professor and you can tell he cares about both his students and what he's teaching as he lectures. He really helped me become interested in the different disciplines of civil engineering and sets you up for success!

Very caring professor that knows what is talking about and wants his students to succeed. Projects were sometimes a bit stressful but they exposed me to new aspects of civil engineering I probably would've not otherwise. Great introductory course!

Dr. Dick is a very nice guy. Helped students learn about different disciplines in civil engineering and brought in other profs for guest lectures. There is a lab, but it is not hard as long as you work with your group and listen to the TA's and Dr. Dick's instructions. Emphasis on nice guy, he was probably one of the chillest profs ive had.

I enjoyed the class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it will count towards your final grade. He was very good at ensuring all students could determine the civil engineering sub-discipline that best fit their interests throughout the class. He is very patient and has a nice personality. I enjoyed the guest lectures thoroughly and the class was easy.
Great professor, class is very lab heavy. He was so nice and understanding when I had to miss class for a family emergency, gave me full points back on the in-class assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gives engaging, fun lectures and is super friendly to talk to! The semester design project we did was really fun and lightly touched on an array of civil engineering disciplines and he brought in some really good guest lecturers. Overall amazing class and amazing professor!

Attendance isnt mandatory but he does in-class assignments every class day that counts towards final grade. The labs are easy but the TA's are kind of tough graders for the lab reports. I highly recommend you take ARE217 before this class because you will need to know basics of AutoCAD for some of the projects.

An excellent lecturer who consistently provides valuable feedback to students on projects and helps them develop software skills in MicroStation. Course materials are slides. He is incredibly patient, guiding students through step-by-step calculations in class. If you stay engaged and follow along, you'll definitely succeed.

Had 327/334 w/her. Cons: Often shows disregard for students that aren't liberal, made evident by political commentary. At times, passive aggressive in response. Little to no feedback. Pros: Accessible by email and after class. Accepted late work and gave a few xtra credit opportunities.

I took two courses with Professor Rhodes this semester, SW334 and SW327, and she was amazing in both. She is very caring and flexible, which I appreciate. I enjoyed her insight and hearing about her experiences as a social worker. She is also crazy funny. Wish I could take more courses with her because I feel she has so much wisdom to share.

Rhodes was a decent professor but the classes were boring and not engaging. The asynchronous setting was not helpful for this, but all we did was watch videos and go over slides that were already posted in canvas. The assignments weren't very helpful for learning the material and weren't related to the lectures. Paper was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about Social Work and relatable. Interesting assignments that force you to think outside the box. I genuinely enjoyed her course and was excited to learn every week.

TAKE THIS CLASS. because it's asynchronous and doesn't have mandatory due dates it's a huge relief/ easier to get through (for me at least). Prof is very passionate about her subject, the workload isn't bad at all, and easy grading.

I typically hate asynchronous classes but I LOVED SW312 with Rhodes. Her lectures are thorough and easy to comprehend. I spent around 1-2 hours total on the class per week (with the exception of the final paper). Each week covers a different social justice topic and usually has one easy assignment to go with it. Everyone should take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took a class with Dr. Rhodes for my BDP. She is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. She is incredibly understanding and makes activities that allow you to think critically about social justice. I would recommend everyone to take her class. While her class is not at all hard, it requires introspection and willingness to engage.

She is amazing! If you think your eyes are open to how the social world works, think again. She challenges you to think outside the box, and to challenge your own beliefs. She does very out-of-the-box style. No tests in this class.

I took Rhodes for Generalist SW Practice, Communities & Organizations, and HBSE. She's probably my favorite professor at UT. So smart, hilarious, wise, and caring. She's understanding, flexible, and wants every student to succeed, but she still pushes you and helps improve your writing and analysis skills.

One of my favorite professors at UT. I've taken 3 of her classes and each one has been amazing. She is a super interesting and extremely intelligent person, and gives great advice on Social Work related issues. As for this particular class, its been a great learning experience with assignments that help give hands on experience.

Dr. Rhodes is amazing, she is so charismatic and funny and honest. Classes with her are really fun and full of really great discussion. She is very laid back and understanding. I'm taking Foundations of Social Justice with her; 3 papers and a take home final. A lot of reading but it's all very interesting. Super kind and accessible. Adore her!!!

She wants to invest in your personal career growth and will help you achieve your goals. Her readings were relevant to my academic and professional interests. Class flew by and she makes it very interactive.

One of my favorite professors I've had. She's passionate about her work and is very open to listening to her students talk about any subject and will keep it going. She makes sure we participate but doesn't make us feel pressured to. Easy grader and easy going. Make sure to read so that you can participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Every week we had to read about 30-50 pages of the textbook and take a quiz. There were two exams which covered very knit-picky details from the textbook so you had to take very good notes and study well to do okay. Professor was available. Wasn't prepared to have to do so much work for a class outside of my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor wanted students to recite textbook info through quizzes rather than learn course concepts and hardly provided genuine engagement. For this online course, he didn't provide video lectures or assignments outside of what came with the book ($135 and required). The course covered basic computer concepts and was not what was advertised.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great course & fantastic professor! He cares and is truly invested. All students should take his class because data privacy is becoming so important. Recommend getting txtbk online, hw is easy if you go to lab, and tests are tricky if you don't do optional quizzes. ATTENDANCE MANDATORY and can help push your grade if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment:
Professor Djurdjanovic makes this class very accessible to someone with no background in programming. The class starts out quite slow, but about halfway through the semester difficulty skyrockets and you'll need to put in 10 hours of homework/labs a week.

It isn't hard, though—and extra credit makes the class an easy A.

Lectures really only explained the theory of what you do, not actually coding it, which made the homework tedious and reliant on self-teaching. The homework/lab assignments are fine, just long in the middle units of the course. Take-home tests are a blessing, though, so keep up with the class, and an A is very possible.
He likes to go on about his own research, but you can tell he loves the subject. He cares a lot about his students, especially if you go to office hours. Take him if you can

Phenomenal professor with some of the best lectures I've ever seen at UT. He is truly passionate about numerical methods and isn't afraid to show that. It's a shame that his TAs are among the harshest graders I have ever witnessed. One of his TAs reeked of sanctimony whenever she graded my assignments (ex. losing 5+ pts for wrong plot color/marker)

Dr. Djurdjanovic was incredibly helpful in and out of class. He answered questions well, and provided a lot of assistance understanding the material. He also offered a ton of extra credit. The material isn't very difficult, and all formulas are outlined clearly in the lecture notes posted to canvas. If you're stuck, go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who is extremely passionate about what he teaches. Explains topics well and is clear with his expectations.

Really passionate about MATLAB. Cares about your success and available outside of class during exams. You can ask him questions about the exam and he will answer. The last 3 weeks of class are time-consuming but doable. You can ace every assignment as long as you try a little. Extra credit went crazy: 20 points on exams and 25 points on homeworks.

This course is easy if you know other programming languages. The workload was fine until the last 3 weeks. Assignments were time-consuming but not hard. Make sure to have a good grade before the last 3 weeks.
Dr. Dragan is a phenomenal professor. He explains the material well and really cares about the subject. He is always available to help and answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I found this class super difficult compared to a lot of my other M E courses, but Dragan's office hours are a great tool. Homeworks and projects are long but not necessarily difficult, but the exams I found to be of great difficulty. Overall good professor though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dragan is a great lecturer and really makes it a point that all his students understand the material. The content is relatively straightforward, but the workload can be a bit much some weeks. GO TO THE RECITATION SECTIONS, the labs will usually walk through all content covered that week.

Very tough professor. Lots of tough homework and projects and even harder take-home tests that span 5 days. He comes off as strict but going to office hours and talking with him one-on-one was helpful. Tough grader.

Prof. Dobbs was probably my favorite professor that I've had in the Neuro department so far. She makes lectures super interesting and the material easy to understand! Exams are challenging, but not unreasonably so, and she always includes extra credit points at the end of each exam. Highly recommend taking her class.
Loved it, made me love neuro more
I loved this class
I LOVED DOBBS!! The course is fantastic, but there is a ton of content. I thought the tests were pretty fair, but I'd highly recommend reading through the textbook and paying attention in lecture!

Class was easy as long as you didn't cram. What helped me ace every exam was going through lectures and reading the book to help answer the study guides she gave us. The study guides were pretty straight-forward and similar to the information she tests on. I made the info into anki flashcards and that's what worked best. An A is very doable.

Really sweet lady, but the extremely dense lectures are not recorded. Difficult exams. Study wiith friends to prepare for exams because you might miss some information (since lectures are not recorded) that may be tested on the exam. TA's grade a bit harshly on homeworks, so make sure you really understand the papers. Do NOT cram for the final.
Love her! Read the textbook. She encourages a genuine love of the subject. Her reviews are long, but they prepare you for the exams. A real gem that UT is lucky to have.

Dr. Dobbs is amazing as a professor. She's extremely friendly, explains concepts well, and has really helpful TAs. Her HW, quiz, and test questions seek comprehension over memorization, and urges you to learn. Her lectures are enough to understand, but reading the textbook def solidifies it. You can't go wrong with her, highly recommend.

I loved Dr. Dobbs class so much. She is such a wonderful lecturer and her class is so interesting. Sometimes the material can be a little dense but it helps to rewatch the lectures before the exams. I would recommend her class to anyone please take it!
I LOVE DR. DOBBS! I was scared to take her bc there were not any reviews about her but she is such a good professor and really knows her stuff. Honestly pay attention and lecture and you'll be golden
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Y'all this woman is my goat. I had her for LAH 350: Best Pictures (which wasn't an option on RMP oops) and it was my favorite class I've ever taken. She knows everything about film formalism and I respect her so much. Just do the assignments and stay engaged in class and she'll love you. I can't hype her up enough I loveeeee her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a fun class! We just talked about animated films the whole time, wrote a couple of very easy papers, and did a lot of joking around! Love love love her!

Took E 344S. Really liked it, and I learned a lot about film analysis! Professor Kornhaber is very nice, and takes a pretty laid-back approach to work that emphasizes class discussion - which definitely made the course even more enjoyable.
I took this class for my additional english requirement. The class somehow made me want to fall asleep but was interesting overall. There are lots of papers you have to write and exams are open notes

She's really nice, but doesn't give very good feedback. On my first short paper assignment I was given a 100, but no feedback. Then on the second an "A-" with no real grade and no feedback, and then on my final 8 page paper I received no grade back, and then once grades were reported I found I got an "A-" for the class. Recommended, but be careful.

Easy class for your VAPA. You don't even really have to read all of the assigned literature because she goes over what you need to know during lecture. The assigned movies are good, so you should definitely watch those anyway! Writing-heavy exams and assignments, but open-note. TA's grade easy. Lecture style can get boring, but it's not that bad
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber is one of the best professors I've had so far at UT. I'm a math major but her film and lit class was so much fun!! I always anticipated going to lecture because I knew she would have something interesting to teach. We got to watch classic films in this class and she made me appreciate stylistic techniques of filmmaking.

Loved taking this class! Graded assignments were exclusively essays, but they werent very difficult if you paid attention to the lectures. Dr. Kornhaber is a delight and she truly sparked my interest in film.

Dr. Kornhaber is incredible! I've never been so glad to have taken a class. She's incredibly brilliant and engaging. Everything she says is worthwhile and I always left her lectures in awe. She's very accessible and genuinely cares about her students and their insight. Her course truly enhanced the way I view film; I can't recommend her enough.

I took Dr. Kornhaber's class as my VAPA. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting, but she did change the way that the class is done from being essay based to literary/film analysis during your discussion section. But even then, it wasn't a bad class. Dr. Kornhaber is incredibly talented in film, but she makes it approachable for new learners.

Dr. Kornhaber is THE most chill professor. It's honestly hard to not get an A in this class unless you just never show up. You also learn so much about analyzing films, and honestly, the films that we watched were a lot more interesting than I thought they would be. Definitely my favorite class this year. Dr. Kornhaber is super sweet, def recommend

I would recommend this class for anyone who needs a VAPA. Dr. Kornhaber is very knowledgeable and it is fun to listen to her lectures. Exams are open note so you do need to be in class to take notes. I wasn't sure what to expect going into the class but the class had us watch really good movies and now I can't watch a film without analyzing it!

The class is about analyzing films and novels, which I took as a VAPA. We had two in-section exams (20% each) and a final (40%). There are 3 outside-of-class papers that just contribute to the 20% section participation grade. Dr. Kornhaber was passionate and knowledgeable, and I really enjoyed her class! Get ready to take lots of notes though.

I took a film noir class professor Kornhaber taught. The class was enriching, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I encourage anyone considering taking her class to do so. Both she and her husband David are English professors. I loved every course I took with each of them.
has great credentials and encourages student participation, but her lecture style could get boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As an RTF student, this was the best possible VaPA credit I could've taken. Her lectures took you step by step through the cinematography and mise en scène choices made in important films, so by taking the class you learn about the visual hints filmmakers have been giving you all along. It was cool hearing an Academy Film Scholar's perspective!

Kornhaber is a great professor and cares about her class. She's really passionate about film and helping her students understand the concepts. If you're taking this for your VAPA don't expect an easy A. She makes you work for it, but it's a fun class to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber's class is interesting and teaches you a lot about film. The course load seems daunting with all of the books and films you are assigned, but you can get away with just writing about films. I would recommend watching the films (which are all classics anyway) and just spark-noting the readings. The discussions are boring but required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention during lecture. I think that the discussion sections are a waste of time but you have to go to them for attendance. You can sparknote all of the novels and still get all of the questions right. Definitely, watch the movies because you can analyze those instead of the books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is kind, funny, and overall made me want to attend lecture every time. If you read the novels and watch the films, you should have no problem. Quizzes in discussion are multiple choice and matching with a word bank. Easy 100 and you learn a LOT.
Dr. Kornhaber is very educated in her field of film study and makes it easy for people new to film to understand and follow along. TAKE HER CLASS... she is awesome.

This class will seem like a lot of work but you can get by without doing all the reading and still easily make an A. If you're already a proficient writer, you will ace this class. She is so nice and genuinely cares about all of the students thoughts. Plus she's so smart and knowledgable and cool, definitely take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber is amazing!! She is the most kind and flexible professor I've ever had. Every opinion, insight, or thought is welcome in her classroom and she never makes a student feel stupid. The content is amazing and has changed how I watch movies for the better. Highly recommend to take her, she is beyond great!

As an RTF student and an avid cinephile, this class was a real treat for me. Dr. Kornhaber is so knowledgable and passionate about films and literature, and is always so bubbly during every lecture. HIGHLY recommend.

My favorite professor! She's so nice, loves what she does, and makes it easy to succeed. The quizzes are super easy, the essays are graded fairly, and there are no tests - just in class essays (called mini exams). The movies and books we looked at were super interesting and I learned a ton.

This class was very interesting, and the professor made the material very accessible. The concepts were easy to understand and the content overall was engaging. Level of feed back will vary depending on the TA but the expectations are pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: You can tell Prof Kornhaber really cares not only about film, but also about the students in her class. The books and movies we get to read/watch were super awesome and fun, but if that isn't your thing, you can totally get by with just watching the movies and Spark-noting the books. There are a few short essays and super easy vocab quizzes.

Very fun class! Watching movies as homework was great. Except when you watch movies in class you might fall asleep. She is very flexible with watching the movies and reading the books because she understands we have other classes. Grading depends mostly on TAs however, but still an easy A.

I got A's on my papers and very little feedback, so don't know what that was all about. But she really knows her stuff, there was basically no reading in the class because it was based off of music videos. Participation does help, but I don't know how much she takes off for not. More than three absences your grade lowers dramatically.

The class can be very interesting or boring but shes very nice and really wants you to learn the material. You do not have to do too much work on the essays and she gives you plenty of options to write on so you aren't limited.  The class was fun and very interesting. Make sure to use the university writing center. It helps a ton in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's extremely knowledgeable about the material. You can get away with not doing the readings because it's mostly focused on the films. If you don't show up and take good lecture notes, you won't have much to work with for the essays. I don't recommend the class if you're not genuinely interested in film analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kornhaber is an excellent lecturer. She really shows her knowledge in a way that is interesting and easy to follow. There are 4 essays- two short essays (20% each), a midterm(25%), and a final (35%). The TAs grade the essays. The grading was fair. As long as you watch the films/read the books the writing should come easily.

I am currently taking Kornhaber's Literature/Film/Other Arts class. Lectures can get very boring, but the bad part is your notes are vital to your grade. Only grades are  2 short papers, midterm & final, ALL essays. Exams are take home. She has 3 TAs, some grade harder than others so an A can be nearly impossible, but a high B-A is very possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: very funny and pretty nice! sometimes he can be blunt but i think its more of his sense of humor ... dont take him too seriously lol

Dr. Sackey lectures, TA's grade. His lectures are very interesting, random, and engaging. Just engage with him during lecture to make him feel a little more love. He is a great source of advice when doing the actual assignments for the class, but make sure to give him time to respond. He also had a great dynamic with Dr. Laude in joint lectures.

Dr. Sackey is the best! I've taken him for a few classes and he is a very understanding professor who likes to push his students to perform WITHOUT hurting their grade. I wish all my professors were like him.

Topic: Rhetoric & Data Visualization | Excellent (and hilarious) professor! I'd recommend this to any STEM major. You'll not just learn to write but make great PowerPoints. Btw, don't be scared by "98 = A". Like 75% of the grade is participation *and* there's enough extra credit opportunities to bring that down to a de facto 94.

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I had at UT so far. He always gives extensive feedback, makes lectures super interesting, and has a lot of office hours outside of class. He's kind, caring, helpful, and hilarious. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches! Would love to take a class with him again.

Professor Sackey is literally the best. He is funny, engaging, and cares about each one of his students. His grading isn't too harsh, and he wants to see each student succeed and put in effort. He is readily available via office hours/email. In-class discussion is thoughtful and fun. Reading isn't too extensive.

Regarding UGS 303 (Originality in the Arts & Sciences) Sackey provides engaging lectures, some of which really random, but he does get his point across. In this class you get three projects: a humanities inquiry, a science inquiry, and a group project that incorporates a little of both. If you ask him for help, he'll happily assist you.

Took him as one of two professors for UGS 302: Originality in the Arts and Sciences. We were graded by only 3 projects but the TAs who graded us did not follow the rubric at all and the expectations for our projects were never clear. I liked his lectures though and he's a really cool speaker to listen to (even if you aren't paying attention).

Took UGS: Originality in Arts and Sciences. Lectures were mandatory to attend but were often dry and boring. No tests over content but humanities project assigned was a pain. TAs did not grade this project to the given rubric and would not explain why they gave a certain grade. Dr. Sackey seemed like a nice guy but I did not like the lectures.

Dr. Sackey is a great professor. I took his Info. Design course, and he is very accommodating and really wants the best for all of his students. He assigned a lot of readings, but you could skim them and be fine in time for class. Overall, this was an easy class, and Dr. Sackey made it enjoyable.
I definitely recommend taking him for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sackey was very accomodating during the pandemic. The assignments were good and career-focused. While he occasionally had opaque grading requirements, the assignments were useful (I was able to get a job in technical writing after taking this class). Most of the readings were short but useful. The projects help you to build a good portfolio.

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I've had. The class was online and asynchronous. Sackey gives really great feedback and allowed for corrections on some assignments. He's super accessible if you have any questions, and clearly cares about his students, and he wants you to pass.

I took the digital rhetoric class when COVID shut the university down and we switched to online. Before, Professor Sackey was super easy to follow, not boring at all, and the class was so interesting! Post-COVID, he was super accomodating and always gave helpful feedback on the assignments I turned in without being demeaning in any degree.

Great digital rhetoric class with an amazing professor. Dr. Sackey allows you choose what you want to write about, so long as it relates to the course content. Reading responses were easy and meant to boost your grade. We made video documentaries for our final project and Dr. Sackey was very helpful and understanding throughout the process.

Attend lectures and take detailed notes, and you will succeed in this class. Exams are doable if you study, and Professor Donald provides past exams. Homeworks are doable and done with Stata. One of the best professors in the department. Funny, kind, understanding, and intelligent.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lots of hw but class was doable if you understand it. the hw is kinda confusing at first but it gets better. prof is nice and understanding.

There is lecture and lab which are graded separately. Prof Donald is very funny and always willing to talk to students. There are quizzes on some days but 2 or so are dropped & weekly homework which are graded on completion. Only 1 midterm and then final. Just study and you'll do fine for them. You will not pass if you do not do good in the lab.

He's a pretty fun and chill guy. Lectures are lowkey boring and slow but its also the nature of the course. Class is def not hard to get a good grade in (hw is on completion, some quizzes, and exams are curved). lots of practice for exams too. He's really funny without realizing it.
Professor Donald makes Econometrics interesting. The grading is more than fair as he grades on a curve and the exams are straightforward.
Easy class with easy to understand lectures. I highly recommend Professor Donald.

Two, sometimes 3 homework assignments a week that are pretty hard if you dont watch the lectures. Don't get behind either even though the content is boring. He has a sick australian accent, and is very responsive in the class groupme. He will change due dates if you just ask him, overall not a bad class just boring Stats OLS/regression modeling
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: nice guy, but the homework assigned often penalizes you for trying.
Funny guy. While attendance was mandatory through clicker questions, the lectures felt helpful. His test reviews were also informative. One of my favorite classes I've ever taken.

This is the first semester they added the extra hour lab component, and it adds a whole lot of work to the class because you have to write two extensive papers. Schneider (the lab instructor) was amazing, and she knew her stuff. Donald's lectures were engaging and fun. Be prepared to commit a lot of time to this class if you want an A.

Lectures were very difficult to understand and not very helpful for studying. Lecture notes are just random screenshots from textbooks without any explanation. 85% of your grade is from tests. Did not explain concepts very well but was a generally reasonable grader. would try to find another professor if you want to learn controls though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were detailed and example heavy. Very nice person who truly cares about students' learning and well-being. DSC is hard, but she makes it reasonable.
Very difficult class.  Definitely need to take a controls class prior to this class.  Nice teacher, hard to understand material.  Was pushed hard and learned a lot.

I took Drumsta for ARA 611C, which wasn't an option on RMP.
She is an amazing professor! Class is always fun engaging. Other Arabic professors are just as kind and friendly, but Drumsta's class feels more interactive. Less rote memorization, more conversational learning. Her grading for ARA is not tough. Do the work, go to class, and you'll learn!

I really wouldn't recommend taking this professor. A UGS shouldn't be as difficult as a STEM class, yet somehow it was (coming from a person who has only had A's and A-'s.) There was no reason at all to assign so many readings, and she isn't flexible at all. Avoid if you can.

I took this class for my UGS, and I should have just waited another semester.  She did not keep students engaged or interested. Although I received an A-, I had to attend multiple extra office hours, which you shouldn't have to do to earn an A- in your UGS. Four in-class essays make up your entire course grade, with zero room for error or makeup.

Prof Drumsta claimed to be there for us and help with grades but us the toughest grader I've ever had. Consistently gave out C's on essays that take the entirety of your grade. A C is a 55 for this class which means it should not be possible to get a consistent C on every exam while changing how I'm approaching them. DO NOT TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: :/ take this as a last resort but also lowkey don't
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Truly one of my hardest classes for all the wrong reasons. Just avoid this class and prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Avoid this class! Prof is disorganized, unreliable, and tough. Expect daily readings, 2-hour movies, lots of essays, and pop quizzes that increasingly get more frequent. She procrastinates on grades that drop your grade significantly EOY. Mandatory attendance, and you're graded on how much you talk and take notes. If possible, steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Drumsta provides no real instruction, teaches in a manner that dismisses any interpretation of the course readings and screenings that deviate from the norm as "simply incorrect," and provides no useful feedback as to how to improve your papers. If you try to dispute a grade, she'll knock your grade down an entire letter. Watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extremely strict and a tough grader. Class seems manageable but she changes the grades very last minute causing significant grade drops. Participation worth 20% and no remorse shown for students that show up late. Rarely gives out 100s even when deserved. Takes points off for "grade-grubbing" leaving students hopeless. Save yourself the headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's funny but what's not funny is the exam over acids and bases that you'll probably fail. With extra credit and good scores on everything else you'll be fine and still get an A without retaking.
Truly cares, great personality, excellent professor overall

His lectures are hard to understand and heavy. Quiz every single lecture that are HARD. Lots of outside of class studying and reviewing. Test are grade heavy but he gives lots of resources and direct help. Its a more difficult course for chemistry than other teachers.

Dr. Laude's great. His lectures can be a little confusing, but he makes up for it with his demonstrations. If you show up to class, the majority of your grade is going to depend on your 2 tests which he lets you retake at the end of the semester. It is very possible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Laude is an amazing professor. He provides lots of resources for success.
The GOAT of chem

Easy class - There is no shortage of resources provided and he will spend time to make sure you understand the content. Plus, he makes it interesting with his real world applications and stories of his personal life / academic history.

I'd 100% take this class again. He was interesting. While I mainly went to the lectures for the quiz at the end, they were entertaining. The quizzes and exams were EXACTLY like the material given. He gives learning modules are review notes. I'd recommend mainly studying the question types on the review notes and going to AC, amazing TAs

Dr. Laude is a great human- caring, relatable, and just hilarious. His class is so well done it might be the easiest way to digest chemistry out there. Lectures are all over the place, but there are SO many resources for whatever type of learner you are (Canvas modules, online discussion forums, office hours, group office hours, extra practice).
Dr. Laude is a fantastic professor. He drops quiz grades and lets you do test retakes at the end of the semester.

Dr Laude isn't doing the grading, he just lectures. They are pretty interesting and funny. You get to learn about him (Go Nuclear!). TAs grade the group projects and Dr Laude is just there to yap and outline the work. Don't go to him for advice though. Loved his and Dr. Sackey's dynamic. He says attendance is mandatory but he doesn't check.

I haven't done chem in 4 years. Dr Laude's class was the best. 
Clear expectations. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there's a quiz at the end of every class. Just do the review notes, and go to specifcally HIS office hours. 
Lecture's are mid because of his speed, but his outside resources and help aren't. He's funny and deserves the glaze.

Dr. Laude's lectures are either really fun or really boring, no in between. However, his exams are so straightforward that getting a good grade in the class isn't difficult. There are daily quizzes without a calculator, but once you get used to them, they help you learn the content more than anything. He now allows calculators on exams

I absolutely love the chemistry department at UT. Everything's organized and set up for you to succeed in this course. More specifically, Laude has amazing lectures that teach you the concepts in a visual manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude's lectures sometimes feel off topic and unhelpful, but his demonstrations are fun and educational. He lets you retest 2 tests at the end of the semester and it actually brought me from a B+ to an A, so he's definitely very forgiving when it comes to grades. I'm terrible at chemistry and still managed to pull an A.

Honestly the best chem prof for CH301. His practice exams are SUPER similar to his actual exams which is why everyone scores so high. Extra credit offered for going to office hours which I recommend because his UGCA's are really helpful if you have difficulty with a certain question.

Chem is not an easy subject, but the structuring of this class makes it less stressful. GO TO THE ACADEMIC COMMUNITIES. I learned the most at them and wish I hadn't waited until nearly halfway through the semester to go, take advantage of all of the resources there are to help you. Prof Laude is the goat as we all know, be grateful and try hard.
Gen chem is honestly easy, the content you do have to learn by yourself and there is a quiz EVERY class day. Straightforward class though and Laudes funny!

Dr. Laude's class was very doable because the grading criteria and exams/quizzes were predictable. There is a lot of practice that goes over every question type that will appear on the quizzes and exams. The teaching team is helpful and always available. In class, Dr. Laude is funny and pops a lot of balloons :D

Lectures were very unhelpful because he treats everything like its common sense. Just do the modules and study on your own. It's set up easy to teach yourself. If you need help, go see his TAs NOT HIM. There are quizzes at the end of each class. Several opportunities for extra credit if you need it. He's funny when he's not teaching.

Dr. Laude is a great professor, as long as you put in some effort to study outside of class. He gives review notes for each concept, drops your lowest quiz grades, gives you extra credit for attending office hours, and has practice tests for each exam that are wonderful resources to study. He makes chem interesting and easy so definitely take him!

Dr. Laude is funny/nice. SO MUCH practice made available. If you just do the practice provided its an easy A+. Tests are predictable and easy. Attendance is mandatory as he gives out quizzes each lecture which is a con however the quizzes are super easy. Gives 30 pts extra credit if you go to office hours which is 3% added to final grade. Easy A+

dr laude is the goat! the flipped learning classroom was a little strange bc i didn't like having to learn the material before taking a daily quiz in class. however, his notes are very clear and he elucidated each question type. tbh i slacked a little towards the end BUT his generous extra credit from going to office hours raised my low A- to an A!
TAKE HIM. THe lectures arent helpful but you have quizzes every class. Easy A, just put in work outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: there was a girl in our class that asked laude for extra credit and laude said no because he would have to do it for everyone. she said I don't see anyone else asking. laude told her you are embarrassing yourself in front of 500 people. I had my shirt covering my mouth out of embarrassment. she dropped the course btw lol no letter of rec for her.

Strange teaching style where you have to learn the content mostly by yourself before class (which takes a longgg time), but Dr.Laude gives LOTS of great advice on self-studying and provides the best chem materials ever! So A's are easy to get as long as you follow his suggestions. 
Take this class if you wanna learn how to study and get an A.

I was scared for this class since I had not taken AP Chem, but this class is very much do-able if you put in effort. Also, if you mess up an exam, he allows retakes for up to 100%. And there is a group project as well.

Dr. Laude is a good professor, but his lecture style is very, very disorganized - he goes on tangents for most of class. He does "flipped" class, so he tends to just ramble in class, but his grading is very fair and an A is easy to get. Same course content as AP chemistry, more or less.
Love this guy, best prof ever

Dr. Laude teaches through easy learning modules and lectures. He makes it very easy to understand exactly what will be asked on each test of the exams. His lectures are very engaging- TAs act out the chemistry principles, Dr. Laude reads poetry somewhat regularly, and at least one hydrogen balloon is blown up every week.

I went in without AP chem so I was stressing about making it in this class. And it was difficult, and there was a learning curve, but he provides SO many materials for you so that you can learn the information so it's not awful! You just have to put in the work. There's a lot of work that you need to put in outside of class though. Lots of quizzes

Every day that I come into my OnRamps class, I question why the 18 ibuprofen I took didn't do its job during the summer. I know less about chemistry now than when I started this class. Everything is online for homework, which would be fine if he actually taught in the learning modules and let us use calculators. No one in my class is passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Only take if your ready to teach yourself everything online before coming to lecture to simply review, the professor is funny and entertaining but only reviews in class, does not teach as if it is the first time you are seeing it. Don't hate the course but don't enjoy it either, two quizzes every week, extra credit offered.

Do not take the OnRamps course! It's made so it is hard to pass because they don't want too many high school students to get college credit, I got a A- in Lab and C in Lecture. The modules make sense but when you take the test they don't align. The only students who got higher than a C in my class used AI.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had at UT. He's a bit older now and his gripes with not going to med school shows, but regardless one of the most interesting (and fun) times I've had in a class. Oh and he also makes ice cream for y'all at the end of the year. Take him as fast as you can. He's amazing.

SO easy to pass. Lectures are very good + easily understandable if you do the learning mods before. Cool demos and good jokes. He's clear with what's on quizzes/exams. He can get a bit snarky with students which is annoying and discouraging. He's not above calling people out for eating in class or being late. Treats us like we're high schoolers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is great, his class is so easy its funny, but for the future he is not the best because he only stresses to review certain things for the tests so you don't know all the material half the time. Not the best class for actually learning, but nobody cares about that anyway so take this class and get another easy chemistry credit. =)

Don't take this class in the summer. It's temping but get ready to have no life because it will take up all of your time. Great class, Laude is very clear with what he wants for exams, so you'll never be surprised by what's on the test. labs are fun and reports arent bad, but the summer session is so fast paced. Take during the normal school year
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, best chem professor. Had to drop my grade for my own fault, so I'm writing to make sure you don't have to do the same! I didn't do so well towards the end of 301, and immediately fell behind on 302! It's difficult, so stay on top of the work, OR YOU WILL FAIL! Use all the resources provided to you, stay on track, STUDY!!!

Dr. Laude is a great professor! The class is taught as a flipped classroom, so the modules are done beforehand and Dr. Laude uses lecture to refine knowledge and provide clarification. Although the course is "exam heavy" as they make up 80% of the grade, optional finals provided. He gives lots of extra credit (through office hours).

Dr. Laude's class is easy to succeed in, but I found the lectures to be extremely irrelevant to the course. There is a quiz every class (during the last 15 minutes of lecture) that goes over content from the previous day's lecture. Overall, there's not much learning in class but the content and assessments are quite manageable.

Look, Laude is a great guy, very funny lectures and a lot of jokes... but the lectures as a whole were not useful. People DID NOT pay attention at all, they were just there to take the quiz then go. If it weren't for the fact that the chem dept made 301 and 302 VERY EASY opinions would be very diff. John is the BEST TA, go to his OH for help and Qs

Best prof I'll ever have probably. Super clear learning objectives with 1:1 test correlated review notes. His TA's are spectacular. Chemistry conceptually is hard, but this class makes it seem so easy to study for. I acc kinda like chemistry now which is something I didn't think I'd say

Dr. Laude is truly the goat of the chemistry department at UT. Receiving an A in his class is very, very achievable with him giving review notes which quite literally cover every question type on the exam, and two replacement exams in place of a final at the end of the semester.

Easiest A of freshman year. Lecture heavy but they can get boring/repetitive VERY quickly. Daily quizzes (mostly easy). His exam preparation notes are the best resources. Friends w/ other classes used to ask for them from me. If u can self study from exam prep notes u don't have to pay attention in class. He's entertaining + easy tests.
Pretty easy A. Horrible lecturer and you will teach yourself all the content. GO TO JOHN'S OFFICE HOURS he is the best UGCA.

I cannot express how grateful I am to have had Laude as a professor for 301/302, the way the course is designed makes receiving the grade you want VERY accessible. Review slides for exams and quizzes lay out exactly what questions/content you will see, there is never a 'surprise'. Even in a class of 500 you can tell he cares about his students!!

TAKE LAUDE!! By far the best prof I have had since coming to UT. He provides plenty of EC and is very clear about what is on the exam. There is daily quizzes at the end of class, but they are fairly easy. Laude is such a joyous hilarious person, but with that said his lectures aren't great. A lot of the information will be self taught/ TA taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bro is the goat. Even if you aren't a chem major or specifically in his class his learning modules are available to everyone so they can all get the same experience of being in his class. Bro saved my gpa with his videos, even if you had a mid teacher like caudill. Love that man, he's like a hidden npc celeberty outside the class setting.

I had Dr. Laude for CH 301C and CH 302C, and I loved having him as a professor. Aside from being a hilarious lecturer with many witty comments, he truly cares for the success of his students and offers many extra credit opportunities to receive an A. He also provides review notes before each quiz and exam that are very helpful- read them! :)

GOATT LAUDE. Took him for advanced achem and since this is one of the last class we chem major taken at UT, Laude wants us all to enjoy the course as much as possible. No tests, just straight up fun assignments. Lab portion was taught by another prof but it was fun as hell.

Good prof. Didn't find his lectures very helpful but did appreciate clear grading criteria, MCQ tests, plethora of resources, and modules. He also gave 10 points EC. He wants all his students to get an A in the class, even offering test retakes for the students who don't make an A at first. Very important to keep up with all the content though.

LAUDE IS THE BESTT so sad this is my last semester taking him, his lectures are so fun and engaging! There are weekly modules due and quizzes per lecture but it's always on the last lecture. They're really helpful in studying, and the exams are all multiple choice. Despite not allowing calculators he makes his exams simple math, just go to OHs! :)
Best professor to ever exist.

DA GOAT!!!!!!!!!!!! how to get an A is beautifully outlined and gives ample extra credit opportunities. 5 Q quizzes every class but he gives an instapoll with basically the same questions. tests are VERY similar to practice exams. free 250 pts at end of sem from a EZ group presentation

Such an awesome professor, his test prep material is unbeatable. You're given exactly what you'll be asked and exactly how to solve it. I thought I was bad at chemistry in high school, but Dr. Laude made it easy and possible for everyone to succeed.

Laude is easily the best professor I've ever had. His lecture demos are fun and he offers a good amount of extra credit. There are quizzes almost every day in class, but he gives you the question types before hand and amazing review notes to study. I loved coming to class, TAKE HIM!

I love Dr. Laude's lectures! I think he breaks down chemistry in a very clear way and he goes over each topic with care. He is very clear on what will be tested on exams and the TA's also were amazing in helping me wrap my head around some of the harder concepts in chem.

Dr.Laude is an amazing professor, very caring and understanding. He does not care about grades and wants everyone in the class to get an A. If you go to his office hours, a lot of the time he would tell you what's on the quizzes. He had so many resources to be successful on the tests, which he gave a very clear outline on what is tested. No final

TAKE LAUDE!!!!! Laude is the best professor I have taken at UT. I am sitting in his class rn writing this review because he is such a great professor. Any review that says not to take him is trying to trick you so there is more availability in the class. I am telling you, if you can take his class, TAKE IT IMMEDIATELY :)
Terrible would not take again

studying for my exam and just want to say i loveeeeeeeeee laude!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! hes the best. had him for chem 301 and now 302. he provides so many resources and genuinely wants all his students to succeed. hes a very genuine, funny, and engaging professor. makes the material understandable. doesnt get any better than laude.

His class was excellent. It focused a lot on the lectures, and was very quick-paced. The group project at the end was pretty easy. He's a very funny professor, and I enjoyed attending his lectures. I really only got a B because my study habits were not as good when I took this class, and I think getting an A is very achievable.

You're practically learning by yourself through online canvas modules. Lectures dont really explain the content at all but its mandatory cuz of the daily quizzes. You have to study alot for this class so be prepared and you absolutely cannot get behind. He and the TA's host amazing office hours and academic communities for extra credit so PLEASE GO

I hated chem my sophomore year of high school but now I am thinking of majoring in chem cos of Laude. He is so funny and gives SO much sources to help you study. Never learned in class but daily quizzes so you have to go, def forced me to study so I was fully prepared for upcoming exams. You have 2 exam retakes yayy!

Funny professor and seemed like a good dude, but learning style was definitely not for me. First lecture seemed very unorganized. Decided to switch to different prof after first lecture. Take him if you like flipped classroom, otherwise dont.

Ok, here's the deal. HE IS THE GPA BOOST YOU CAN GET. But, don't underestimate his class. He gives daily quizzes w/ clear study guides. The quizzes are exactly what is on the study guide. He tells the question types for the exams. Stay on top of your work, and don't play catch up at the end of the sem, with re-exams. That doesn't always go well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a super good professor and genuinely cares about his students doing well in his class. The only thing I didn't really like about his class were the daily quizzes. Other than that he makes getting an A in his class super attainable.

His syllabus outlines everything, and his lectures are super engaging, he's always up to one experiment or another. While I didn't love his teaching style, Robin's question-type guides saved me. Study them and you're set. There are learning modules and quizzes due in nearly every class, so don't slack off and stay prepared, or you'll fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor, other professors should take note. Being able to have each question type was a game changer. He made chemistry fun and his class structure is unbeatable. Definitely take him if you get a chance.

College chemistry is so difficult, but Dr. Laude makes everything so digestible and easy. The exam preparation slides made by Robin contain everything you need for every quiz and exam. His lectures are engaging and sometimes he throws in cool experiments to keep you engaged.
i didnt even have him for class but dr. caudill had many of his vids as a resource. just wanted to say that he is a great guy and an incredible help with general chemistry.

There is a reason why Dr. Laude is revered by many: he's the best. He clearly cares about his students. The TAs are great as well. There are quizzes done and learning modules due before nearly every lecture, but the work is manageable and there are so many ways to get a good grade. Don't sweat it.

Dr. Laude has structured this course extraordinarily well and his lectures are hilarious and fun to attend. He is very fair in what he expects you to know and has optimized this course to accommodate you as much as possible. Definitely take him!

Amazingly structured course. Although the lectures are a little too long winded and abstract for my liking, the course provides you with all the resources you need to succeed in a succinct and to the point manner. Academic discussions are very useful, and LMs, exam and quiz prep material give you everything you need to know.

100% take this!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prepares you for exactly what each test and quiz will ask. There are quizzes every lecture, but he has GREAT quiz reviews online. 80% is review of AP Chem, but you definitely do NOT need AP experience to do well. Modules/Reviews prepare you well enough, but his office hours are helpful AND he awards extra credit for going. Very funny and respected.

Extremely overrated professor. Does not actually teach during lectures and has occasional interactive parts about his "lecture". Only good thing about his class were the review notes that listed what we needed to know for quizzes and test. Overall, if you put in the work you will make an A, so don't slack off.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is truly a character in the best way possible, very engaging lecturer who evidently has his student's success in mind. TAs make review slides for assessments that VERY clearly define to you each topic/question you need to know. Daily quizzes and 4 exams, but 4 lowest quizzes are dropped and 2 replacement exams at the end of the semester!

He's an alright professor, but overrated. Extra credit and TA's is what rlly makes his class, so GO TO OFFICE HOURS & ACADEMIC COMMUNITY TO GET THE E.C AND MEET THE TA'S! If you don't do well on his tests, he allows 2 test retakes. Modules are useless, but do them bc they're worth 50 points, BUT go over the review notes til u memorize everything.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is an amazing chemistry professor. I was so nervous for this class since chem wasn't my strongest point, but he made class super enjoyable with his lectures and easy to understand. There are so many resources available in this class to make sure you're successful

Dr. Laude makes all of his lectures SO engaging and makes chemistry fun! Although the actual content isn't the easiest, he provides so many resources for review and extra help, so everyone feels like they can succeed. There are quizzes each class, TA reviews, and lots of extra credit and retest opportunities. He is so funny and is the best!

Laude is amazing. His lectures are fun and enjoyable, and he makes the content easy to understand. For the most part, the actual content is pretty easy. He gives lots of resources to help you learn the material and goes through exam/quiz questions in class.
He is probably one of the best professors at UT. He cares about his students, and his lectures are really fun and engaging. Be ready to start enjoying coming to class! Truly enjoyed this class!
nice and funny teacher. course was hard though so make sure you stay on top of the learning modules and work hard because it can be easy to fall behind.
One of the best chem professors at UT!

There are many exam prep resources available, and he is VERY clear about what will be on the test. The course content is naturally somewhat difficult, but Dr. Laude makes it very easy, and an A is very very very achievable.

Laude is an amazing teacher, he has years of experince behind him and it shows. He himself is extremely entertaining and fun to be in class with. The content can be tough but he provides tons of practice to get you ready for the tests. All in all this class is extremely doable.

I love Dr. Laude! His lectures are as funny as they are helpful. He shows every concept visually with the help of his TAs (who act as electrons, molecules, etc.). I'm dyslexic so I really value his teaching skills. His canvas is exceptionally organized and full of study materials to help you succeed. He makes it clear what will be on the tests.

I LOVE LAUDE!!!!!!!!!! i really have nothing else to say but that he's the best. I am sad about finishing chem bc I truly don't think I will have another professor that here that even compares to him. he is the best!!!! wants students to succeed, is very funny and entertaining in lecture, and overall knows what he's doing and how to teach.
laude is the goat
truly the goat
SUper easy class and nice prof.

I'm so obsessed and thankful for Dr. Laude. He makes lectures so engaging which is huge for chemistry, the review notes are so helpful and he gives you everything you need to get an A in the class. TAKE HIM.

Chem in high school was a train wreck but with Laude I actually love it so much! Before I took his class I hated chem but now I'm thinking about adding it on as a major. Incredible lecturer and just all-around GOAT. Even if you aren't pre-med or STEM, you should consider taking his class just because of how fun and interesting it is!!

Professor Laude makes this challenging course manageable. Frequent quizzes and the ability to retake exams provide ample opportunities to succeed. I found unstuckstudy ai an invaluable tool alongside the robust course resources. Overall, a rewarding experience with an engaging instructor.

TAKE LAUDE!!! Best chem professor. I took CH301 and CH302 with him and got A's on both. I was very scared to take chemistry at UT because I did not have a strong background in chemistry at all, didn't take any advanced chemistry course in high school, and I was able to do good. Dr. Laude gives so many resourses to help you succeed in the course.

Great professor & perspective on learning is so inspiring. Lectures weren't very helpful and didn't like flipped classroom approach, but class structure/canvas were soo organized for prep. Learning modules were not helpful. He is THE most accessible professor, from many office hours to 10pm zooms, he really wants students to succeed which I admire!

Dr. Laude is THE best chem prof! He teaches you how to THINK, which will prepare you for the MCAT and other difficult tests. He makes you do your work without a calculator, which trains your brain. He is very caring and clearly wants everyone to succeed. Always available to answer questions and opened extra office hours when we were confused. 10/10

Overrated and easily worse than other Chem teachers. Modules aren't clear, class is dumbed down to the point of confusion, and chooses to teach "Laude math" where you memorize a bunch of specific values rather than just normal math with a calculator.

Dr. Laude is truly an angel! A chem GOAT! He knows how to teach this course like no one else!! I had a full time job & couldn't prepare as much for exams, but if I had the time, I know I would've succeeded because he gives you ALL the tools you need and more! Super caring, funny, and passionate about students' success! Wish I could take him again!

I only had Laude for a UGS that I rarely went to (sorry Laude) before taking him for chem this semester and wow I understand the 5.0 rating. I had Anderson fall semester who was a great lecturer but his tests literally killed me. With Laude, I know exactly what to expect on the tests and quizzes. The study resources are great and he's also  funny.

Take this class! Every class there is a quiz so make sure to attend lectures. Chemistry is hard but Professor Laude makes it easy to understand given multiple resources and unique techniques. Best part about this class is that you can take up to two exams again!

Dr. Laude puts in lots of effort for the class to be this great. His canvas page is awesome & I wish all other professors had canvas like his. He spoon feeds you the course and has fun demos. My only note is I wish he'd not joke on topics that might upset students of certain beliefs. Other than that, a caring, dedicated professor.

This lab was a bit all over the place sometimes just bc we were the pilot but overall I thought the workload was manageable however it was a bit difficult to understand what we needed to do in the lab it was pretty hard but the TAs r awesome!
Its Laude. Really one of the best professors to take at UT. TA's are awesome and have so many office hours throughout the week.

Took this class as a pilot course to receive both credits in one semester. Highly recommend taking this course, tasks and assignments were very easy and doable with a good group. TA's were nice although there was some discrepancy with grading (fixed later) but that may be b/c it's the pilot course. No work outside of class, super easy!

Such a good prof and class! Genuinely enjoyed going to class. I struggled towards the start of the semester, but Laude and Robin really helped me out. They both care about the students, and I really appreciate everything they do for the students. AMAZING CLASS!!!!! Take it if you can!

Dr. Laude is very caring and funny, and makes his expectations for your learning very clear. The TAs are awesome and their office hours are tremendously helpful, more than the lectures IMO. Lots of quiz drops and can retake up to 2 exams, although many people do well enough not to need to. Extra credit given to those who attend office hours.

Easiest chem lab ever. We had no lab write-ups and no real assignments. Every grade was participation based, not accuracy based. We never had any homework, every grade in the gradebook was taken in class based on in-class activities. 
Easiest chem lab ever, but none of us learned anything about chemistry. 
Guaranteed 100 if you go to every lab.

Laude is a caring professor with a great sense of humor. The class is dependent on tests that make up 80% of your grade, but it's manageable as long as you study his exam reviews. He also allows you to redo two exams instead of a final. There is a quiz every day in class but the content is reviewed beforehand and you have drops.

Dr. Laude truly cares about each and every one of his students and wants to see everyone succeed. So many resources, office hours, and opportunities to bring your grade up if you screw up. Easy A and a really great professor.
Easy A... makes gen chem understandable. Don't fall behind on weekly assignments and you'll be fine.

Amazing teacher! Entertaining lectures! If you go to office hours once a week (which are insanely helpful for quizzes) you get an extra 3% on your grade. He is very clear on how exams will be and genuinely cares about his students. If you take his class, my biggest advice is DO NOT STUDY THE MODULES when it comes to exams. Study the quiz reviews.
I love Dr.Laude's style of teaching, super easy and fun class, and very easy exams.
Super easy class and very easy to get an A. Would take again!

Dr. Laude is a phenomenal professor. He is easily one of the most funny and interesting professors I've ever met, and he really does care about all of his students. Making an A is not very hard as long as you stay on top of the material. Take him if you get the chance, just know that most learning will be done studying for tests and quizzes.

Dr. Laude is the best chem professor out there. He tries to make chemistry understandable and interesting for everyone. He gives you every possible resource to succeed from flipped classroom modules to pages and pages of exam review materials. If you study what he tells you to, you will get an A in the class. Take him, you will not regret it!

I took him for UGS 303: Originality in Arts and Sciences. Overall, he was  solid. It is a SUPER easy class to get an A; however, the TA's were unbearable. Their grading is super wacky, but only the final papers matter, so don't worry about how they grade your assignments. They say the attendance is mandatory, but I was able to skip many classes.

Dr. Laude is dedicated to ensuring all of his students succeed in his course, taking extra steps to ensure students get an A on the exams: He gives extra credit, has many office hours (including a 10pm Zoom the night before a test) and releases practice exams. He is also hilarious and charismatic, so it's never uncomfortable when speaking with him!

Dr. Laude truly cares about his students and provides many resources to help them succeed, including office hours daily. He is understanding but the reviews on here may be misleading, suggesting his class is a blow-off class. Everyone can make an A but you must learn the material since your grade is mostly based on the tests. Live Laugh Laude!

Dr.Laude is amazing! He has a flipped classroom: you complete modules and then come to class where he is king of his circus. You can expect explosions, poetry, chemical theatre, out-of-pocket humor, relevant chemical demonstrations, and a little bit of math. The class is set up to ensure your success if you are willing to put in the effort.

VERY EASY class. Just do the review pages he sends out and attend office hours, then you are perfectly fine. He will outline everything that you need to know in the review pages and then tell you word for word whats on the test and quizzes in office hours. Plus, you get to retake 2 test for maximum credit at the end of semester instead of a final.
This professor is an amazing lecturer!

LOVED him!! Coming in, I knew it would be an "easy A," so I didn't put much effort in. However, if you want an A, you do have to put a bit of effort in (obviously). It's not a complete blowoff. Laude is the best and his lectures + TAs made chemistry easy.

I loved this class. Dr. Laude was super funny and down to earth during lectures. While having quizzes pretty much every class was a little annoying, the academic communities, exam prep page on canvas, and office hours were super specific about what the quizzes & exams covered. I would highly recommend going to most academic communities!!!

Laude wants his students to succeed in his class. He's clear about what question types are on the exams and how to study for his class. There are daily quizzes during lecture time and 4 exams, and you can retake up to 2 exams. The TAs are helpful, go to office hours or academic communities. The downside is that it's easy to forget what you learn

I love this class. The TAs (especially his assistant Robin) make the class though. His lectures are very boring and not super worthwhile, but going to office hours and reviews help IMMENSELY. This class is an achievable A compared to other science classes. Word of advice--don't leave his office hours or anything early because HE WILL call you out.

Took him for UGS: Originality in Arts and Sciences. Great guy and had no tests over lecture content. The 3 projects throughout the year were sometimes a pain. TAs would grade inconsistently and required office hour visits to get fixed. Never knew what my grade was until they were posted at the end of the year, but most people got As.

Dr. Laude is such a kind and hilarious professor. He is very understanding and gives lots of opportunity to make up lost points (extra credit from office hours, 2 make up exams, etc). He makes the content really easy to understand and his quizzes and exams are extremely straightforward. It's really easy to do well in his class.

Let's just say, attendance for lectures was optional, yet everyone showed up. We really loved Laude and almost everyone showed up to his office hours every day. He had wonderful lectures and interesting demonstrations with the TAs. He genuinely cared about everyone and offered to write letters of rec! He made the material easy to understand.

Definitely, lots of homework that piles up, but nothing too difficult if you pay attention. He genuinely wants everyone to get A's and he is such a great lecturer. He focuses on your understanding the fundamental concepts, which I really like. He also reserves seats for his chem 1 students to take his chem 2 class :)

Great professor, wants every student to succeed. Check out his TEDx talk "Everyone can get an A," he def provides resources to be able to. The TA team is amazing and offers so many OH to reach out and get help, and gives extra credit for attending office hours weekly. His tests are extremely fair and similar to the practice tests, gives 2 retakes.

Laude made it easy to study for quizzes/exams with his review notes that outlined exactly what would be tested. There are daily quizzes at the end of each lecture to keep people coming to class. Go to office hours to help prepare for them and also get the extra credit for going. His lectures are a mix of fun/random musings and actual material.

Best professor ever!! If you have the opportunity to take his class DO IT. He wants every single student to succeed and his lectures are amazing. He is very clear about what we need to know to be successful in his class and provides us with ample resources to achieve a stress-free A.

Dr. Laude is a great professor and his class is insanely easy! There are daily quizzes after each class that "make" attendance mandatory. Dr. Laude provides a review set before each unit that essentially outlines EXACTLY what'll be on the exam and quizzes. You'll know what to study before the unit even starts. Extra cred and replacement exams.

Dr. Laude is an amazing professor. The way his class is structured makes getting an A very easy. The lectures are sometimes hard to keep up with, but they're very entertaining and if you don't understand the content, the exam prep notes and office hours will help 100%. There's also multiple extra credit opportunities. Long story short, TAKE HIM!!

Dr. Laude is so kind and hilarious when it comes to lectures and office hours, he really wants his students to succeed and do well in his class. However, his lectures are quite chaotic and I found it hard to follow along with what exactly he was trying to get across. Even without lectures though you should do perfectly fine in this class. So easy!!

Dr Laude and all of his TAs are the best, they all truly want you to succeed and make what is supposed to be a complicated subject straightforward to understand. Don't listen to the reviews that say you don't learn because while you could memorize what is on the exams it is tough to answer his theoretical questions without understanding. TAKE HIM!
legit just saw him in a tik tok but he seemed like the coolest professor ever I wish he was at my school

Dr. Laude is a great professor who provides many resources to help you succeed in class. His TA staff is awesome, and are really helpful in their office hours! His quizzes every class sound intense, but are very manageable and help you grasp the material.
So great! Tests are very easy and he gives a lot of resources for you to succeed in the class.

Literally the best professor you could possibly have for chemistry. He put in a lot of effort to make the course feasible and the exams and quizzes were super easy. You literally can't fail the class because of the way Dr. Laude formats the course.

Dr. Laude helped me transition very smoothly from high school chemistry to college. As long as effort is put into the class you will receive an A. He is a great professor and the only downside is that he is not teaching CH 302C.

laude is a great professor, put a solid amount of effort into his class and you will get an A every time. he does a lot of extra credit and his lectures dont really make sense sometimes, but the canvas materials and modules are so good where you should never be lost in this class. learn how to study for the daily quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are very straightforward so just go to class and enjoy his lectures don't stress out too much!!

Dr. Laude is the best chemistry professor at UT. He is very caring and funny and has incredible resources on canvas that make learning the material on your own easy. The way he structures the material makes the exams extremely manageable and it is more than likely you will get an A if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Laude makes chemistry easy to understand, and I genuinely have enjoyed his class. The majority of the grade comes from 4 exams, which you can retake later if need be. There are also extra points (modules, quizzes, etc).  I highly recommend him, even if the material can be difficult to get (which the exam resources help with greatly).

if you want an A, take him. if you actually want to learn chem, dont. he only preps you for his tests which are watered down chem. if youre the type to need to understand every aspect of a topic and WHY things happen like me, you will struggle a lot since he tells you, "it doesnt matter. just memorize this and youll get an A on my exam."

Dr. Laude is awesome. He does everything he can to assist his students and is very understanding in regards to lecture attendance and faulty/unfair test questions. He's happy to answer any questions. The material isn't easy, but all resources are on canvas. Probably the best AChem professor, and the class is way better than PChem. Take him.

I know everyone loved Dr. Laude, but his lectures were scattered and didn't make much sense to me. The only major plus of the course was retaking exams, and the exams were just like the practice exams. If you need lots of instruction on material, don't take Laude

Live, laugh, Laude. I'm the minority who honestly doesn't care for Laude's lectures since I feel I didn't learn much from them. They were more like entertainment. However, Laude has so many Canvas resources like his exam prep notes, so it's easy to teach yourself. His TAs are also amazing where there's always an office hour occurring.

every high school has that professor everyone seems to love but is known to not really teach, Laude is a college version. taking his class can really backfire and if you like structured learning I would recommend taking a different professor. not a huge deal but he is also the only gen chem professor who doesnt allow calculators on exams.

I had Dr. Laude for CH 301 and 302 and while 302 was much more challenging, Dr. Laude was accommodating and set out clear expectations for what students needed to know to succeed. 2 opportunities to retake exams instead of a final.
