Though I took AP Chem in HS, I felt like I finally understood chem after this course. Amazing intro chem professor.

Had Laude for both 301 & 302; I think his teaching style doesn't work for me personally (somewhat flipped classroom and I need thorough explanations lol), so if this is you as well I highly recommend going to TA's ACs/OHs before quizzes/tests - I went to Robin's and she was so helpful and great at explaining the material a bit more methodically!

I am seeing a lot of reviews that talk a bit down on Dr. Laude with most of them saying that he is an easy A and he does not actually teach anything, which is because he runs a reverse classroom. Many of the people writing these reviews are privileged to have a professor like Dr. Laude as he really helps students transition to college chemistry.

Laude is a very caring professor with a very easy class. However, his whole class could be taught in 1/2 the time with better retention. His lectures are off topic all the time with half the class being dazed. The man is great; however, his teaching style is not optimum to actually learn the content. If you want an easy A, take him.

If you want an "easy A" but not learn anything, take laude. He just has you memorize random facts and ways to calculate things his way. I say "easy A" in quotes because you have to be able to tech yourself a majority of the content and be able to understand his version of chemistry so no other youtubers or online searches can help you study either.

Dr. Laude is probably the best professor a first-year can have. He understands that we just came out of high school and genuinely wants his students to succeed. You can get a good grade just by memorizing the facts and calculations, but you won't learn much chemistry unless you really understand the concepts.
You want an A, take him. you wont learn chem, its just a bunch of memorization for the sake of getting your good grade.

Took him for professionalism in healthcare. There are UGS courses with a lighter workload however this has flags in it. Attendance is somewhat mandatory. The UGCA's are slow graders but its easy to do well and the assignments are easy and you have multiple chances to redo it. Lecture's are boring but the class is easy.

The most student-friendly professor of the Intro Chem professors. 4 exams, with the opportunity to retake 2 at the end of the semester, with plenty of extra credit too. TAs are super approachable and friendly. His lectures are hilarious, and the demos intriguing as well. Has clear guidelines on what to learn for exams - know those and get an easy A

One of the most well-respected professors at UT. 301C is the majors/honors course, and it moves at a quicker pace than the regular class, so be prepared to work a bit harder. As long as you keep up with the modules, you're good. Quizzes are given at the end of every lecture. I will say some the way he teaches some things aren't super transferrable.
has to be the most annoying man ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is hands-down the best CH301 professor, you are lucky if you have him! He only teaches you exactly what you need to know for his tests.They're all multiple choice and 2 can be replaced! There are graded quizzes every lecture but they make you keep up with the material. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! They truly help so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Daily in class quizzes kinda suck ngl. His lectures are kinda all over the place but he gives a lot of other resources and notes to help prepare for tests. He gives you each question type that will be on the exam and a practice test before exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude loves his students and sets them up for success. He and the TAs provide excellent exam prep materials and as long as you study that, you're going to pass/get an A on all exams. He is wildly entertaining and I found myself not wanting to miss class. He also lets you retake any 2/4 exams for a better grade up to 100. He's awesome!

Professor Laude helped me understand chemistry so much better than I thought I would be able to. Really cares about his students and makes it very easy to understand his expectations for assessments. Practice exams were super useful. Don't worry about the quizzes at the end of every lecture because he gives you practice and many get dropped. Easy A

Dr. Laude is an amazing professor and is very well respected among students and faculty. However, his course is quite fast paced. Studying is very important, make sure you study his practice exams, quizzes, and go to office hours. There is a quiz every class day. Try to get good grades on his exams the first time- retakes are more difficult.

Took him for the Professionalism in Healthcare UGS class, TAKE IT! All you are graded on is a completion grade on the papers and your attendance. Lectures are extremely boring but turn in your work and you will get an A. No exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Laude is the type of teacher you want for chem. He is funny, caring, wanting his students to succeed, and is an excellent professor. He is the type of guy that will change the course up if he sees enough students struggling with a certain section. There is hw due almost every class but it prepares you for the dozens of quizzes that keep you up.

This class was time consuming as it involved many big projects one after the other. This course involves a lot of writing so be prepared. Guest speakers and lectures were great. As long as you complete projects and writing assignments properly then you will get an A. If you don't then you'll be able to make corrections and submit again to get an A.

Dr Laude is the best. Take advantage of the syllabus because it tells you exactly what you need to know on every single assignment. His office hours are helpful especially right before exams. The practice exams are pretty much the same stuff as the midterms. Take it seriously and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Average lectures but amazing resources. Personally, I never cared for Laude's lectures but his Learning Modules and Exam Prep pages on Canvas give you all the material to succeed. His grading policy is also very generous since you can retake 2 out of the 4 midterms if you want to score higher. TA office hours are extremely accessible as well.

Had a flipped classroom style, with learning modules. Tests were mostly straightforward, and there's a final group project (very easy). He has a philosophy about everyone who wants an A can get one, and I would say it's true. His study guides are amazing, use that to guide your studying. He's also a fun guy.
Amazing professor. An A is easily achievable if you study  the 25-question annotated notes for the midterms. No Final. easy homework and daily quizzes, and some get dropped.

This class will be rough if you haven't taken AP Chem; Laude's pacing is fast. It wasn't a complete repeat of AP Chem, but the new concepts introduced were fairly easy to comprehend, and he basically taught to the test. If you're in an honors program, felt like 301C was easy, and you have a choice, consider taking something else instead of 302C.

AMAZING professor, and likely one of the best that I will have for a while. He does his best to maintain student engagement in his lectures, often doing demos and blowing up hydrogen balloons. His grading criteria is very clearly outlined and he is VERY effective at communicating what will be on exams. He also has extra credits and retakes.

He is funny + kind, which gets you a long way as a prof. His teaching style is not for everyone. Try ur hardest to pass the exams the first time you take them because the retakes are the worst thing known to man fr. No calculators but the laude math style is easy until the numbers are close together which he says he doesn't do but sometimes does.
Laude is great, his passion is chemistry and he truly wants students to succeed. If you have the opportunity to take him, you should because his philosophy makes the class easy if you work.

Dr. Laude is a great professor who wants all of his students to succeed. However, I am not a big fan of his flipped classroom method, so make sure to go to his TA's office hours as they will teach you majority of the material. Quiz almost every class and 4 tests which aren't too bad. However DO good on them. His retake exams were inherently harder.

Dr. Laude is awesome. There was a quiz almost every single lecture but, he clearly outlines beforehand what you need to know for each question. As long as you read the posted exam study materials, you should be able to get an A on every quiz and exam. Lots of homework and studying throughout the week though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Laude is the best chem professor at UT. 4 midterms with NO FINAL, very easy to follow grading criteria and opportunities for extra credit and lots of breathing room for your grade. Lots of study resources for tests; there are quizzes almost every class but lowest 4 get dropped, lectures were boring at times but they can be enjoyable.

Laude is a cool and funny guy. He cares about his students and even reads poetry sometimes. Quizzes can be difficult, you have one in almost every lecture. Tests can be hard but he makes it easy to get a good grade with practice exams and there are a lot of TA office hours. Laudster is the best chem prof on campus, and if you can take him, do it.

Amasing and makes the class very fun to learn in

Dr. Laude is literally amazing! Do take him if you can!
i love dr.laude so much. he's so funny and his lectures are so engaging and he's truly the best chemistry teacher on campus.

Dr. Laude is one of the most caring professors I have ever had wanting all his students to succeed while providing the resources to do so. Laude is the best chem prof at UT!! He really cares about his students, and encourages them to do well. Dr. Laude is such a great professor and person in general. Hilarious af, even the syllabus. Puts care into everything he does and made chemistry bearable for me.

Dr.Laude was the best professor I have had at UT. I hated chemistry before I took his class, but Dr.Laude made it bearable. reviews.comment: TAKE HIM FOR CH 301. I did really well in the beginning and started to slack off whihc affected my grade in the end. Be on top of your game. Test are super easy fi you study for them the way he tells you to. To do good in the daily quizzes, attend TA/Laude office hours the day before and they will teach exactly what you need to know.

I got a 2 on my AP chem test and ended with an A in this class! Laude doesn't necessarily make chemistry easy but he tells us what to study for his exams/quizzes. These happen to be really important topics so I do feel like I learned a lot:-) he's also very helpful and wants you to succeed so don't be afraid to go to office hours!

I struggled with chemistry in high school, but Dr. Laude's class did an excellent job in establishing the foundation I needed. Before ANYTHING ELSE, study the 20 question-types for exams, and then move onto other content (Friday videos are helpful!). He's really caring, and unlike many other professors, actually makes chemistry understandable.

Laude is a Cool professor. His tests are very easy and the daily quizzes kinda force you to learn all the information. His TAs are super approachable and there is extra credit available. Although learning modules are not that helpful , his lectures are if you pay attention !

Dr. Laude has a very specific teaching style, he provides resources outside of class that make it very easy to learn topics on your own. If you do not utilize the resources before class that he provides his lectures will be confusing. His TAs are very helpful. There are daily in class quizzes but if you're keeping up with the work you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is amazing!! Go to his office hours. His notecard method really helped me. He is hard but wants the best for his students

Dr. Laude is THE best chem 301 professor. The class is easy as long as you do the modules, study for quizzes(which he gives reviews for) and the tests(which also come with reviews) are manageable since he teaches the material well. Go to office hours and academic communities. They help immensely! You are luck if you get Dr. Laude

What can I say- great professor! He's a great teacher and he gives you TONS of resources to do well. 3% added onto your average for teaching a friend about chemistry and for joining a club. Most people get A's and if you put in a little bit of time/effort, you'll get one for sure

Absolutely love Dr. Laude! He's the funniest professor and such a great professor! His lectures are very engaging and I love being in class. Material is very straight forward and the class structure is very clear from the start. Highly recommend!

Easy A. You dont even have to write down any notes to pass his online class. Just use his review notes that give you a hint on what to expect on the test/quizzes. Hes one of those professors that makes the answers straightforward, sometimes the answer is in front of your own eyes or even in the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dang, what a great Professor. Nothing makes we want to graduate more than Laude telling me that oxygen is diatomic. The Principles of Chemistry are forever engraved on the insides of my brain thanks to this class.

350/500 students get an A about, but he isn't the best teacher. He's a great guy and very intelligent, but the class is so easy that I feel that I didn't really takeaway as much as I could have from other professors that make you do more work. His TA's are really good though and theres a ton of office hours which is where I did most of my learning.

If you're looking to get an A in General Chemistry and not put in really any effort, Laude is the professor for you. Laude teaches to his tests and does not teach the fundamentals for you to really understand chemistry. Of course, this sounds beautiful to a Pre-Med, but in reality this class will not prepare you for future chemistry courses beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is one of the easiest professors to have for chemistry. He practically tells you whats coming for the tests and quizzes. I wasn't a big fan of his flipped classroom method, and he practically has his lectures in the form of learning modules.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very engaging and passionate professor, who keeps his chem lectures interesting. However, lectures may seem redundant if you're good at learning from the online modules. Furthermore, I don't feel as if this class has prepared me for the MCAT, due to the structure of the class being an "easy A" with minimal studying, understanding, and work required

Dr. Laude is amazing. I loved the layout of his class, and I used to HATE chemistry, but he honestly made me appreciate and love it so much more. I was at an A- and took the final to get an A in the class! I really liked how you just need to ace the final to ace the class! Would definitely recommend this class; plus, his TAs are always pretty solid

Dr. Laude is a great professor. He really strives to give every student a fair chance at college. He's great to get an A with, and if you go to his amazing TA's for office hours you can learn too! His lectures aren't the greatest but by just doing the exam prep material you can land an A. You can figure out chem for the MCAT later I guess!

Laude is amazing mainly because of his grading criteria. Watch out for the acid base chemistry unit... If you have like a C or a B in his class before the final and you make an A on the final, then you get an A for the entire course and honestly, that was what saved me. I would def recommend. Study his exam prep material! Not the learning modules.
Does not reply to emails, not a good lecturer at all, but easy to get exempt.

Want a professor who's going to prepare you for the future and at the same time practically guarantee a good grade? Laude is your guy. Extremely understanding, inspirational, and organized. Great class and definitely should take by all means.

I have never met a teacher that understands grade stress as much as Dr. Laude. This class is super easy, and you can learn a lot if you engage with the big picture concepts. I'll really miss having him as a professor; I can't recommend him enough!

Dr. Laude is a sincere guy who genuinely wants everyone to succeed. However, he is not very good at teaching chemistry. His lectures are meandering and boring and oftentimes very confusing because he oversimplifies everything. He tells you exactly what is on each test, which makes this class a very easy A.

Dr. Laude is the best professor at UT by a long shot. As long as you do well on the quizzes and memorize his review notes there's no reason to not get an A in the course. He has a dry sense of humor, in the best way. His lectures can be confusing, but he gives an overwhelming amount of review material to do well on the exams. Highly recommend. :)

Really easy A and hilarious guy if you have a decent sense of humor. Lots of office hours and TA help is available if you need it. Being able to exempt the final is also a nice plus. Only downside is you might be a bit lacking in standard chemistry math because there's no calculators but that's not really a big issue. You'll be fine.

Easiest chem professor!! An A is easy as long as you really learn the 20 question types that he provides for every exam! The quizzes in almost every class period really count a lot towards your grade so they will help a lot if you do good on them, which is manageable because he gives quiz reviews for each one.

Dr. Laude is no doubt an intelligent man and dedicated professor. You can exempt the final if you do moderatley well on his tests, complete the modules, AND DO WELL ON QUIZZES. You're essentially guaranteed an A if you can get into his class. He emphasizes big picture topics and leaves you to learn the rest but provides so many TA and office hours.

Dr. Laude is one of the easiest professors to have in UT. He makes the class in a way that you have to try really hard to fail. He may not be the best lecturer but he makes sure you understand the material. He basically tells you whats coming for the tests. There are quizzes almost every class day, so attendance is mandatory.

Laude makes class interesting and hes a real character. However, this class was insanely difficult. If youre not familiar with chem already you basically have to teach yourself everything bc Laude expects you to already know the basic concepts. The TAs honestly taught me more than the professor but theres tons of study sessions to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There's a quiz almost every class. The quizzes are weighted VERY heavy. Each quiz question counts as much as an exam question. The study guides tell you exactly what kind of questions will be on the test. The things I struggled with a lot was "Laude math" aka his type of rounding, and small things like confusing low to high for high to low etc.
lectures included participation activities to make it more interesting. gives you everything you need to know before a quiz/exam. lots of extra credit.

The chem prof you want to have! Despite having to GRIND for this class, Laude was awesome and made lectures interesting. TAs are very helpful & give great insight during test review sessions. Had in class quizzes nearly every day, but they can help your grade if you study the material. I struggled a lot at first, but still managed to get an A
BEST PROFESSOR!!! Hands down, everything is straightforward just let him guide you to victory.

Dr. Laude is the best chemistry prof and one of the best profs at UT. He wants all his students to succeed and goes out of his way to help every students. He clearly lays out his expectations. All the necessary materials and resources are provided. Go to office hours for help and hints on quizzes and tests. Course packet is not necessary.

While the material is fairly challenging, Dr. Laude breaks it down very easily and makes it possible to achieve an A. His office hours, TAs, and materials are very helpful. I also appreciated the consistent schedule for quizzes, exams, TA discussions, and office hours that made it even easier to get prepared and take advantage of resources.

Dr. Laude is one of my favorite professors of all time! He genuinely cares about his students. He offers a lot of opportunities in order for his students to get the grade they want. Hes a good lecturer and knows how to keep students engaged. Do the homework and study for quizzes and exams! If you try, you will do well!

I'm very bad at chemistry, and this class made my life a lot easier! That is because Dr. Laude WANTS you to do well! He's straightforward, tells you what he expects of you, and there are no tricks/surprises on quizzes/exams. I even ended up enjoying chemistry to some extent, with the fear removed. Solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A solid professor especially in a course as pivotal as CHEM301. However, if you're actually looking to really learn, Laude may not always be the best option. He's a pretty good teacher, but most of his course is teaching to his tests. Easy A, but you may still leave not fundamentally understanding the material you made an A on. You decide!

He has tons of quizzes (nearly on every class day), but he drops 7 of them. His class is flipped, so you have to do modules outside of class. He explains things really well, tells you what's on the test, and he actively works to get you an A. He's hilarious, and he has tons of office hours. Super nice professor; I cannot recommend his class more!!!

Dr. Laude is the best chemistry professor you will ever have. I've never had a professor care more about his students, Dr. Laude truly wants everybody to succeed. Do the homework and study for the tests and quizzes and you will get an A. He provides SO much study material, and SO much help preparing for each exam. Definitely take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKING CHEM 1 RIGHT NOW! DR. LAUDE IS THE BEST CHEM PROFESSOR!

This class is an easy A if you listen to Dr. Laude. He gives very clear instructions on exactly what he wants. He is very entertaining, but also very knowledgeable. He provides so many resources and help sessions, too, and answers emails really quickly. If you don't pass this class, then you probably aren't trying very hard.

Attendance is not mandatory but there is a quiz given at the end of every class & said quizzes contribute to a large portion of your grade. He very clearly tells you what is going to be on the exam but often throws curve balls during said exam. Very willing to meet with students either individually or in a group setting.

Dr. Laude is a great teacher. He provides tons of outside help by means of TAs, who are all usually pretty helpful. My only qualm is that sometimes he teaches by means of shortcuts, so you may not retain info as well in a meaningful and longterm way. Overall a fantastic teacher, just make sure you are actually working to learn and retain info.

Laudes class is structured to make you pass. However, most of his TAs do the work and the flipped classroom requires a lot of studying outside of class. Laude can also be condescending and cocky at times, especially since he has a position in Provosts office and doesnt need to teach. Take him to pass chemistry, but not to actually learn.

I love this guy! I thought I hated chemistry before I took this class, but it's not so bad with Laude. He really drills the important stuff into you, so if you pay attention in class and study his review notes an A is super easy to attain. Learned a lot and highly recommend

If you want an A take Laude, if you want to learn consider another prof. Laude is a great prof who provides all the opportunities to learn, but it is up to you to spend extra effort to learn which you'll find is hard to do. Most people end up memorizing the review guides where he lays out what is on exams and the forget the material after the exam.

Amazing professor! Love his style of teaching and splitting up each topic objective by objective. Would take it again if I could. Learned a lot about how to study for other classes from this class. The quiz questions are actually worth the same points as test questions so definitely pay attention to those quizzes and enjoy Chemistry!

Really quirky professor but his tests are very straightforward since he literally tells you what types of questions he is gonna put on the test. Easiest chem teacher BY FAR if you just wnat to get rid of the science credit. Good guy and class was somewhat interesting (i dont like chemistry lol). Also exemptions for the final is nice!

Really funny. Lectures on stage, but didn't take questions. There's like 6 different office hours to meet with TAs or Laude EVERY day to clear everything up. He tells you what is going to be on the exams, but that doesn't mean that they're easy. Learning modules instead of homework. Final grade replaces class grade and no final with an A

Dr. Laude deeply cares for his students. He is especially great for freshman chemistry because one bad test grade will not cause you to completely destroy your final grade. He adequately prepares you for tests and quizzes. His TA's and his own office hours are extremely helpful.

Dr. Laude is the best professor I have had so far. His test are easy because he gives reviews, even though you have a quiz everytime you go to class, there are not hard at all. he gives 4 test and if you pass all of them, you dont take the final. Honestly, take him, he will make your life so much easier.
Im only voting in order to raise Laude's overall rating. This guy deserves a 5.0! By far, the easiest science class you will ever take.
Dr. Laude is the best! The class is honestly not that difficult if you put in work. He's pretty funny sometimes too.
He really cares and is a great professor. I would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor, but don't let the other reviews fool you that it is easy. You get an A by working harder than you do in any other class. It takes work, but it totally pays off when you are exempt from the final! Go to as many office hours as you can! I love them, and they were so helpful! Daily quizzes help you keep up with the material!

Laude is an amazing professor, he definitely cares about his students and gives them many opportunities to do well. He provides question types and detailed notes about how to do well on each type of question for the exams. One thing to note is there are in class quizzes almost every class, so you cannot skip.

Dave Laude is a good man and an even better professor. Hands down the best chem professor at UT. He basically tells you every question on the tests, which obviously helps immensely, and half of the class ends the semester with an A.

This is an easy A, don't miss your chance. He makes chemistry fun and enjoyable. His test are easy and he has lots of accessible office hours and his TA are helpful. Take him and you won't regret it. I PROMISE YOU. I am stuck at Chemistry but I still passed his class with an A

THIS PROFESSOR IS AMAZING. 10/10 recommend. He teaches you how to take a college class and he truly cares about helping you achieve your goals. Make sure to go to office hours and don't slack off in the beginning because it's awesome when you can exempt the final while people in other classes still have to take finals.

Just do his 20p packet before every exam and youll get an A in the class and wont have to take his final. He gives up to 20points ec. and theres a daily quiz at the end of each class. its really not that hard and this is coming from someone who basically failed regular chem soph year of hs and hasnt looked at chem ever since

I did not take AP Chemistry in high school, so I probably think this course is tougher than someone who did. Dr. Laude gives tons of resources to help you succeed and genuinely cares/wants you to do well. His TA's are the best and his office hours are extremely useful. The tests are usually extremely fair and he gives you what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is by far the best professor of this class. There is a lot of homework and quizzes but they make the tests so much less stressful so its worth it. He is great at test prep and if you have an A at the end of the year, and a lot of people do, you can exempt his final which is great. Definitely requires lots of studying but an A is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Laude is the best professor I have had at UT so far. He is very patient and is good at explaining difficult concepts. There is extra credit given and he makes it very easy to get an A in the class.
Take this man. You probably won't get him unless you're in a FIG, but at least try. Chemistry is a difficult subject but he gives you everything you need to succeed and to get an A. Take this man.
Awesome Chem professor. He's funny during lectures and has an awesome class structure in which there are at least 2 ways you can make an A.
Great professor, would recommend 110%
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: He's the best lecturer, period. I have a weak chem background and expected to struggle but he truly does help to get the A. Study from his comprehensive review guides, and you're guaranteed an A . Is very helpful, and just to give an idea, it's expected that at least 300 out of 500 students will exempt the final bc their final grades will be A's.

If you have to take chem, try to get Laude. He is always clear on what he is testing and makes sure students have access to materials to help them succeed. It is pretty easy to get an A as long as you study what he tells you to. He is also a funny guy who has a lot of weird stories, so buckle up.

Laude is by far my favorite professor at this university. You can tell that he truly cares about how well his students perform in his class and really wants you to know the material. An A is definitely accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Laude is the best professor that I've had at UT so far. He has amazing lectures and his class is structured for the student to be successful. He hands out review packets before each test, and if you know how to do everything on the packet you will make an A on the test. Weekly homework and quizzes

This is a flipped classroom setting, but he is very personal and is willing to help anyone out who feels they are struggling. Gives lots of test prep materials and offers many opportunities to gain extra credit, or to fix your grade. If you make an A in the class you don't even need to take the final!
AMAZING

Dr. Laude is one of the few professors I've met who actually cares about his students' success. He's willing to work with you as long as you are learning and willing to put in the effort. Exams are generally very easy as long as you go to the TA's office hours. Extra credit is available, as well as exception for the final!

Going to class isn't mandatory, but he does do interesting presentations to get the students involved. There are weekly homeworks, 4 quizzes, 4 exams, and a final that you can be exempt from if you have an A. He gives you a practice exam and notes a week before the exam, and if you memorize all the info then you can get a pretty easy A.

Laude's lectures can be confusing sometimes so I recommend going to TA sessions with specific questions. He really cares about his students, which was clear after Monday's events. Solid choice, if you're looking to learn chemistry and have a teacher who cares.

Laude provides resources galore for any and every student to make an A. From extra credit to worksheets and practice exams, he desires that every student succeeds and offers the opportunities to back up that claim.
just go to class and make sure you understand what they are talking about and be able to know how to solve problems.

Showing up to class isn't mandatory because it is a flipped classroom. Dr. Laude outlines exactly what you need to know for the exams. He gives you a practice exam, and a copy of last years exam for you to know what to expect. If you put in effort, he definitely wants you to make an A.

Since it's a flipped classroom, you do most of your learning through the modules on canvas. He goes over the topics in class but not in that much depth. However, the amount of resources that are readily available is tremendous. Office hours (TA's and Dr. Laude's) are available every week day, with the addition of piazza! Overall, I would recommend!

He is an average teacher in my opinion. He has his TA's do everything for him and doesn't seem to care about any student. Also he makes you watch instructional videos before class, but in class he says the exact same information ( sometimes nearly word for word). However, his class is really easy and I would recommend taking if you just want an A.

One of my favorite professors at UT. You can tell he's very passionate about the subject and really wants you to succeed. The class is a VERY EASY A because he basically tells you exactly what you have to know for every single question on his exams. Be diligent with your online modules and you'll have no trouble in this class.

Dr. Laude is an amazing professor. He is very funny, and he makes his lectures entertaining. Your grade is dependent on exams, quizzes, and homework assignments. It is very hard to do bad on exams and quizzes, for he tells you exactly what you need to know to get an A. In addition, he practically gives away extra credit. This was an easy class.
Great guy, class is really well structured.

Hands down one of the best professors at UT. He truly cares about all of his students getting an A in his class. I used to suck in chemistry in high school but Laude really taught the class well and made chemistry easy! Definetly take him!

CONGRATS IF YOU HAVE HIM, BECAUSE YOU JUST WON THE UT EQUIVALENT OF THE LOTTERY. This man is one of a kind. He truly cares about his students and helps them all while making sure they genuinely understand the material. His lectures are fantastic and are easy to keep up with. His office hours and pre-test review sessions are highly recommended!!

Amazing professor! He really wants his students to do well, so he makes the grading criteria very clear. He offers extra credit towards the end of the semester. He posts a video with everything you need to know for tests and quizzes. He also had great TAs and was constantly available for office hours. He is very funny and sarcastic as well.

Modules done online cover the material lectured on in class. However, going to class is a good idea because he often gives hints to problems that will be on the test. Tests are always very doable gives very specific outlines and practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best teachers I have ever had! His only desire is to see students succeed. His class is flipped, so the students 100% determine their grade. If you work, you will get an A; he gives the resources to do so. Also has the best TAs. Would definitely take again.

Dr. Laude is awesome! He really wants his students to get A's and offers may opportunities to do so. If you've taken AP Chem you'll be fine and there are many office hours and videos outside of class to supplement the lectures.  Dr. Laude is very funny and a little intimidating but just go to office hours. You can also exempt the final.

Laude is love or hate, he really does try to make every student do well in the class- he's more about please pass this course rather than understanding everything in depth. He's a little chatty for lecture but it is a flipped course so you are supposed to learn more online. Solid guy- hard to talk to. BIG course

Highly recommend this professor if you want to have the option to exempt the final. I earned an A on all the exams and quizzes with the help of clutch prep (they offer great concept videos n exam reviews). It was SOLID and helped me get the A for the course. I ended up w/ more time to study for my other finals bc of the exemption!

Would undoubtedly take him again. It's a co-teach class.  Plenty of extra credit opportunities. There is also a possibility to test out of taking the final. Lectures were very helpful and so were the online resources. There are always quizzes to complete prior to classes, but you have three chances to get your best grade. Easy to ace the quizzes

Dr. Laude's classes are not "easy" - they require work because chemistry itself is just a difficult subject. Dr. Laude tries to help the best he can and has a clear-cut way for you to study. If you work hard enough and have some luck on your side, you can get an A. Go to office hours and try to really understand concepts. A's are very possible
Love this man. Great chem class!

I enjoyed his class. He is one of the more "famous" professors on campus, and seems to be relatively polarizing. My opinion toward him is pretty neutral, as you can tell he wants students to do well and works hard to be engaging. Tons of opportunity to get help before an exam, wish that attendance wasn't graded or I would've studied independently.

I believe Dr. Laude is a good person and seems to enjoy teaching this course; however, the way he teaches can be improved. He doesn't allow calculators in exams so instead of learning the concepts, I ended up spending more time on practicing the math. He doesn't have power points either. If you're good with doing freehand math, this is your prof.
He literally tells you the exact question types for each test. Material can be difficult but the resources are abundant. Really knows his stuff.

He was an amazing professor in my opinion. His in class lectures aren't that great but because the way he's structured the course, there is so many great learning materials outside of the classroom. From online lectures, the well written online textbook, and his office hours, you can make an A. Plus, he tells you exactly what you'll be tested on.

Dr. Laude's CH 301 course is a good introduction to general chemistry. I took it solely based on how highly I had heard him spoken about from other students during orientation. I liked the course, but did not get the grade I thought I deserved.

Dr. Laude is my favorite professor. I came to college with very little chemistry knowledge, and, because of his class, got As in both intro chem classes. He is engaging and exciting to listen to and makes himself available to students at all times. The class does require work, but is certainly worth it.

Everyone will tell you that Laude is a great professor and that he'll be an easy A, but that is completely false. He'll teach you shortcuts instead of explaining the concepts in full and expect you to think that chemistry is the easiest thing ever. If you're naturally good at chemistry, go ahead but otherwise, be ready to teach yourself chemistry.

Everyone thinks Dr. Laude is great, and he is. Funny, engaging, and clear, he puts all his expectations for all his students to follow. However,  I find it hard to see the main idea in his lectures because he doesn't really go into the concept, but rather focus on the big picture. Since it's a flipped classroom, teaching yourself is a must.

So everyone really loves this class. Mine was shared with another professor. It's okay, but it's not meant for people who don't like teaching themselves. He is really helpful if you go to his office, and there are tons of resources if you have questions - but it's a flipped classroom and you must learn how to teach yourself the concepts.

I adore Dr. Laude. Education is his passion. He understands how students operate and is really there for you if you need help (he gave individual pep talks to all who failed his first test). Not an easy class, but easy to get a good grade if you take his study advice and put in effort. I learned a lot and enjoyed him as a person and an educator.

Laude's class made me like Chemistry. If you're willing to work and study all the material he gives you before the exams, he gives you so many chances to get an A in the course. If you have the opportunity, take Chem with him!!

Dr. Laude goes above and beyond to help his students. He has a substantial amount of TA and office hours M-Th. He also genuinely wants all his students to get an A and provides more than enough resources to do so.
He gave all the resources needed to do well in the class. He is a very interesting lecturer, and a lot of the information will definitely stick with you.
Great professor and a great class. Only problem is that class sizes are gigantic and it makes it hard to get questions answered sometimes.

Dr. Laude is one of the best professors at UT. He is helpful, works hard to make sure the information is relayed in a relatable and engaging manner, provides copious amounts of study tools and resources and outlines each exam by question type. If you are willing to work hard, Dr. Laude's class will be rewarding. Thoroughly enjoyable experience.

Came in scared, quickly realized chemistry is doable with Laude. He goes over every question type on the exams so you know exactly what to expect. He has helpful review sessions and post review videos. 10/10 would take again - he is a FANTASTIC teacher. If you get an A/A- in the class you are exempt from final! Get him if you can! He is the best.

Dr. Laude is a great man however, you must study and self-learn the material he provides online since his class is flipped if you want to pass his class. He provides a lot of office hours and overall help if you need it. It is a bit hard learning by yourself so study a lot and also he provides hints and question types for his tests.

Awesome professor. Tests are very difficult because every misconception is an answer choice, so you can leave a test thinking you knew how to do every problem and get a failing grade, but as long as you study with a TA/group to clarify misconceptions you're fine. Also makes grade on final replace grade in class if its higher. Stay away from TA Jeff

Tough class and a bit archaic in grading and course work; no calculators are allowed which can make the tests and homework really tough. Lectures were never really much use. Don't skip class cause your iclicker score will tank (won't screw up your grade too much but enough to notice). Personally not a huge fan but I see what people like about him.

Loved Laude.  Take him if you are not into chemistry and struggled in 301.  He goes out of his way to make sure his students understand the material.  He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed.  I hate chemistry and made an A in his class because he helped me get there.

Great teacher. Wants you to get an A. Does everything in his power to do so. Content is tough, but that's chemistry. So many oppourtunities to redeem grade. Passionate and lectures are funny. Take him!!!!!!
He's the man with the plan. 1010 would take again.

Gives you about 3 opportunities for extra credit and gives you "question types" for tests so you know what you need to study specifically. If you go to his office hours, he will tell you what he is going to ask. TA discussion sections are SUPER helpful.

Most of your learning comes from the TA's, so go to office hours. He expects you to learn most of the material from his online modules, and he'll mention a few topics in class. You'd probably do better never going to class and just going to TA sessions. Office hours aren't scary at all, so many people go.

Dr. Laude is a great man. He loves helping his students. But when it comes to chemistry... If you don't already know it, you wont learn it through his class, well unless you self-study and teach the entire course to yourself. He provides A LOT of resources to ace the course, but he really does a great job at confusing his students during lecture.

There are LOTS of ways to make an A in this class. His grading scheme is pretty easy, but as a teacher, I don't think he's that great. His lectures can be very confusing and the tests are difficult. If you took AP Chem in HS and did well, I recommend his class, but otherwise (if you have little chem background), I would find a different teacher.

Great teacher that knows his stuff. Goes off on tangent sometimes. Lectures aren't vital. Most of your studying and learning comes from his four TA's. Uses iClickers at the beginning as a daily grade. Four quizzes w the lowest of the four dropped and then three major tests. If you have an A or A- in the, you can exempt the final with that grade.

In my opinion, if you're a good self studier, then you'll ace his class. Basically for me, I learned the lectures for the next class through the learning modules, showed up for class, attended TA sessions before tests and I aced his class and didn't take the final. A bit of advice, you put the work in early, you don't have to work hard at the end.

Laude is an amazing professor! Easy tests and quizzes, plus he gives you all of the question types beforehand. He loves to see his students pass and will really work with you one-on-one if you need it. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he has iClicker quizzes every lecture. He lets you exempt the final if you make an A. I would definitely recommend.

I LOVED Dr. Laude!!! He always wants his students to be exempt for the final. If you have an A before the final, you get an A in the class. If not, the final is your final grade. If a test grade is below passing, he will curve. He often voids questions that the majority of students miss. He has office hours every day. His TA's are AMAZING!!!!!

Great chemistry professor!!! He's very funny and does many in-class demonstrations to keep things interesting. Only mandatory attendance is a quick two question iClicker at the beginning of each class. If you get a better grade on the final exam than you did in the class, he automatically uses your exam grade as your class grade.

Laude's only goal is for his students' grades to be high. For him, this means teaching his students shortcuts,  preparing them for his tests (half of his lecture was him teaching us the format of his tests), and having an easy grading scale. Did not learn anything in this class. His class is especially difficult if you didn't have him for 301.
This class was very hard especially if you do not have a background of AP chemistry from high school. Would not recommend if you are not strong in chem. He also gets off subject a lot when lecturing.

The TA's are great, but rely on them to teach you the material.  Laude shows lots of  tricks in class, but doesn't teach much. I went to his OH after a test (C+) and he told me he wouldn't speak with me because my grade showed him I hadn't studied, he wouldn't even hear my questions.  Poor teacher, would not recommend.

Dr. Laude is awesome! He does a good job of keeping us engaged during class. In all honesty I did not really learn much in his lectures, but they we're super entertaining! His TAs are AMAZING. I went to 2 TA review sessions a week religiously and made an A in a class I thought I was doomed to fail. Definitely a highlight of my semester!

Before Laude's class I had zero background in chemistry and pretty much zero interest. He not only made the material easy to understand but enthused his students about actually learning it. Laude has a deep and genuine love for the course that is contagious. Take him if you have the chance.

Really cool guy. Had him for 301 and 302. By CH302 though, you realize that really his lectures are useless, and class attendance is only important to get iClicker points. Very very (like 5) flexible grading systems. Tests are still challenging though, you will have to work hard. However, TA sessions are THE BEST. Will help you get an A!!!!

Just make sure you watch the learning module videos and take good notes! The course notes he gives you is straight from the learning module slides. If you pay attention to the videos, attend exam reviews, and do all the practice tests and quizzes, you should make an A! Plus he gives extra credit opportunities!

Dr. Laude was the greatest professor I ever had. His class was not easy but he is so smart and makes you want to learn. One down side is that he teaches as if the students got A's in high school chem! Most people did not get A's in high school so some kids have a hard time. He really cares and will do anything to help you. Such a funny & great guy!

Dr. Laude is definitely a genius in the Chemistry world and will help you understand a lot. It's not hard to get an A in his class. However, that doesn't mean it's a blow-off class... Attend lectures, watch his videos, and you may still get a C. The key is to go to the review sessions and do extra practice - take each problem seriously.

Dr Laude is an incredible teacher and goes to great lengths to ensure student success. Every week there are countless TA sessions you can go to if you're confused. There are always review sessions for quizzes/tests a few days before. Grading scheme makes it very to get an A. Lectures were very interesting and Laude likes to explode things.

Very passionate about his students' success. Attend office hours and academic communities if anything is unclear and you'll be fine. I personally had no interest in chemistry before this class, and now I'm considering majoring in it. I would recommend this to anybody semi interested in science.

I had no background of chem before taking this class and in result struggled, but the teacher is a very helpful man. He truly wants students to succeed, you just have to put some effort into things as well. I recommend him!

Dr. Laude's class is awesome! it is really hard as well, he is the most approachable professor i have. The 4 TAs he has are helpful as well, there is no mandatory attendance but he has iclicker quizes at the beginning of lecture about the lecture that was due before class. i would really recommend this class to any incoming freshman, it is fun!

Laude is a great lecturer. However, he tends to tell more jokes than helpful information for the exams. If you think you can make an A by just attending his lectures and not discussion groups, you're wrong! I learned this the hard way! He is also very broad when informing the class of which problems are on the exams.

Laude is a great lecturer. However, he tends to tell more jokes than helpful information the for exams. If you think you can make an A by just attending his lectures and not discussion groups, you're wrong! I learned this the hard way! He is also very broad when informing the class of which problems are on the exams.

In my freshmen year, Laude was by far my favorite professor. He was hilarious, intelligent, and greatly cared about his students. Don't be afraid to suck up to him- He is a powerful figure in science and if you plan on entering medical school make sure you know him so you can get a letter of recommendation from him. Take him if you can!

His class is hard because it isn't structured very well. You really have to put in A LOT of extra time to learn the material and personally, I believe that he offers too many methods of learning the material. If you don't have any background in chemistry, I wouldn't suggest Laude, but if you do, he might be a great professor for you.

He has so may resources, that if you apply yourself you will be fine. He is very clear about what will be on the test and what not to waste time on. Entertaining classes with lots of examples. He also helps you learn how to study.

I have all good things to say about Laude. So entertaining in class making the lectures anything but boring then his TAs and resources are SO HELPFUL! I made an A in his class so I was exempt from the final. I watch his video clips online pretty much every quiz/test and I nail them. best class ever. Chemistry is hard but Laude is BEST.

Dr. Laude is very entertaining in class and does great demonstrations, however I learned nothing from his lectures. To make an easy A, do all the practice quizzes and tests and go to the TA office hours. TA's for this class were amazing. Learned everything from them and made an A.

Laude is a cool guy, but his class is very hard in my opinion and i don't think his lectures are very clear. He does give practice quizzes & tests though which help a lot. He also has the best TAs around. If you like chem TAKE HIS CLASS. if not stay away.

His teaching style is all over the place, and nothing in his lectures corresponds to whats on the tests. But he has the best  TAs. Practice quizzes and tests are helpful in learning what he actually wants you to be able to do. You could get through this class without going to lecture as long as you look at the question types and practice questions

His practice quizzes, class notes, and practice tests have errors in them so it is hard to learn.  He is also kind of cocky .  Many people like his style of teaching, but I find it unorganized and misleading.  His test reviews and TA test reviews are amazing though as they tell you how to do each question on the test.

Posts previous tests, worksheets, and quizzes, and will post practice documents that will basically reveal what is on the test or the quiz. He gives some extra credit, and tends to lower grade cutoffs at the end of the year. Lectures are good, at least entertaining, and the organized TA discussion sections can also be very helpful.

DO NOT TAKE LAUDE UNLESS YOU HAVE BACKGROUND IN CHEM! His course is tough and yes he gives out answers (sometimes there wrong) to test questions, but his teaching is not structured at all, and you may get lost. if you need to work hard in chem to get a good grade, don't take him. Dissc sessions with Travis (TA) are more clear then his lecture.

After his first lecture I was completely lost, but after that I learned a lot. His lectures tell you everything you need to know for the quizzes and tests, just pay attention to them. His TAs are extremely helpful, and make sure to attend their test review the night before! You can make at least a B with little effort, and As are very manageable.

Laude pretends that he cares about you, but he doesn't. You need a substantial amount of high school chemistry to keep up with the class. Drop it if you've never taken AP chem, you won't survive. He's vastly overrated. He doesn't teach you the material rather he jokes. He does however have the best TA's. People,stop hyping him up; his ego is huge!!

This professor did not teach much. Laude is a great therapist and comedian but as far as being a professor  he leaves much to the imagination. I hope that people start realizing to stop hyping him up and to take a prof that will actually teach. Only take this guy if you have taken AP chem in H.S. otherwise you are better off with someone else.

Excellent professor!  He wants you to do well in the class. If you are struggling in the class, make an appointment to see him- he can really give you some good, actually applicable advice about how to study and learn more effectively in his class. Good and gracious man.

He is SUCH an awesome teacher.  super nice guy with a great attitude. if you're at ut, you HAVE to take his course.  he is absolutely amazing.  although the material can be difficult, a little is all that it takes
BEST CHEMISTRY PROFESSOR EVER!  HIS EXPERIMENTS ARE AWESOME.  YOU SHOULD MAKE AN A IF YOU STUDY. DON'T HAVE TO REALLY USE THE BOOK.  GO TO OFFICE HOURS... HIS OR HIS TA'S... VERY HELPFUL!
EXCELLENT AND NICE PROFESSOR.  HIS OFFICE HOURS ARE VERY HELPFUL. HE MAKES CHEMISTRY FUN!  IT WAS MY FAVORITE CLASS AT UT.  HAVE TO STUDY THOUGH, BUT YOU SHOULD MAKE AN A.
My favorite class! =]

so i'm a science major and i loved his class, but his notes didn't really help me in anyway i learned more from the book. his final was supposed to be really easy, but it wasn't. one AWESOME pro about his class was that he dropped the avg for an A to an 83. really funny guy, just go to class,go to his officehours!

Dr. Laude's irreverent humor and explosive (literally) experiments make you want to attend class.  Provides a book of notes and old quizzes/tests that you can buy, which is very helpful.  You do need to actually read the chapters, but he and the TA's are very helpful, and there are lots of office hours you can go to for help.
Very good professor.  He tells you exactly what to do to get an A, it just takes a bit of work.
I absolutely LOVE this class. Laude is hilarious and gives optimal resources to succeed in his class.
No Comments
he's very funny and entertaining but the material is hard
Eccentric, fun, and involved.  He really makes analytical chemistry a class you never want to miss.
No Comments
Extremely helpful.  Fun class to participate in.  Highest recommendation.
greaaaaaaaaat teach

This professor will give you the most intense design semester of your life. I would say Andrew or Andy was too intense with his students and expected unobtainable perfection from every student. Somehow our year made him proud, but a lot of the students are mentally burnt out after the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: At front the workload is not insane it is the way its presented and worded that makes it unbearable, repeating the same terms over and over and over as if we would just understand if repeated once more. Incredibly confusing, burn out before midreview season, never had in-studio reviews, 1st time I gen considered dropping out, must stay locked in

Absolutely terrible. Hands down, Bako is the worst professor I have had at UT! He is so incompetent! Who hired him? Shame on UT Austin. All the reviews are accurate. He gave bizarre, unclear assignments and asked for a stupid load of work. He was rude and unsupportive. I am pretty sure this class ruined my GPA and chances of getting internship.

Take a class taught by him if you like wasting your time and money and enjoy being perpetually confused. He doesn't make sense when he talks and expected an unreasonable amount of work. Don't take any class taught by him, one of the worst architecture profs ever. How does he keep getting hired, do schools check student reviews ever? Waste of time!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't pay attention in a single lecture (attendance is mandatory & apart of your grade) and got an A. Essays are pretty hefty and he's a very picky grader. Overall easy but the essays sneak up on you if you don't start soon enough. Wouldn't do if you hate writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very particular on grading for essays but provides clear and insightful feedback. Interest in music and/or politics helps in being engaged by lectures but Drott is a great lecturer. Big assignments can sneak up but overall an interesting and worthwhile course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good UGS if you put the effort in, helps to have an interest in music. Sort of a picky grader, so ask for feedback before turning in papers. Three 2-3 pg papers, 2 quizzes w/ 4 open-ended questions on concepts (only 1 quiz counted!), final project. Minimal participation required, attendance is graded (although they do not care if you are late)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has a few essays, but I feel like they are all doable if you go to office hours/ask the TA/Dr. Drott questions! You should take advantage of their feedback, as Dr. Drott is very particular about his grading (esp for essays). However, it is very doable to get an A on essays and FRQ quizzes. Dr. Drott overall just wants you to succeed!

I've been genuinely interested in music since I've played instruments for most of my life, but the class really wasn't what I was expecting in aligning with my interests. It was a lot more conceptual. The grading I felt was pretty harsh, but very clear feedback, though, so you can fix it for the next assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Drott cares about what he teaches, and his lectures are genuinely enjoyable. Note that attendance is taken as a percentage, so you have to attend every class to get a 100. The papers weren't too bad, progressively got harder but they have rubrics. There may be a quiz over music theory which requires studying. Not as easy as people said.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class (Music, Protest, and Social Movements) was very interesting lecture-wise. There were 4 papers, on average 5 pages in length, so not as much writing as a UGS with a writing flag, but a lot more than most. Felt harder and graded harder than most UGS classes, but easy class overall. The main stressor was the writing. otherwise very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's nice, but the lectures were boring and didn't relate to the class assignments. The quiz was harshly graded. After doing poorly on the first paper, I spent hours perfecting them to what he liked. Go to office hours for help, and the TA Lauren was very helpful! The class felt unnecessarily difficult and the papers needed a lot of research.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting - more of a realistic historical take on Music, Protest, and Social Movement. You have a good bit of liberty in the things you choose to write about so you can make it as hard/easy or interesting as you like with the assignments and research. He can be a bit of a picky grader but always with good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was not difficult and easy to get an A, just do the work (3 short writing assignments and 1 final paper). 1 quiz, no final exam. Dr. Drott is very understanding, but his lectures can get very boring. There is a discussion every Friday, and TA Issa was amazing; discussions were never stressful. Overall, not a bad UGS pick at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drott is an extremely thorough and caring professor. His grading and philosophy are more based on showing clear effort put into your assignments (i.e. may not get all 100s, but 90+ is fairly easy to get), with there being 4 assignments (3 papers, and 1 quiz). Otherwise, great guy, the lectures can get boring/verbose sometimes but he's super chill!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're not interested in the subject, his powerpoint lectures can be dull. Most of the class grade is writing, but thorough feedback is given on assignments. Both Dr. Drott and TA Issa care about you doing well; they respond quickly to e-mail and are willing to set up additional office hours to provide one-on-one assistance. Solid UGS to take.
Professor Drott was funny and kind! I came in knowing nothing about protests and was pleasantly surprised. I really enjoyed this class content as well as the final paper, which is rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Drott is passionate about his work and is very caring; however his lectures are very dry and dull and just hard to stay awake through. He is very helpful with assignments and good at answering questions. Course consisted of a quiz, 3 papers, and a larger final paper. Attendance is mandatory, he passes a paper around and you initial your name.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Drott is very nice and funny! The content of the class can be boring but attendance during lecture isn't mandatory. He tells you to read materials before lecture but I never did and I was fine. They grade the papers easily. Attend discussion section and turn in the assignments and you will do well. There are 3 papers and 1 final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class this semester!! I came in knowing nothing and I learned so much! It was pretty easy (just essays) and you don't need to do the readings at all. Lectures are really interesting and Drott has a dry, but fun humor. Great professor, would def recommend this class.

Professor Drott is passionate and a nice guy!! The lectures can be boring but he really does try. 3 essays (1-2 pg), 1 final paper, 1 final project. No traditional "final". Discussions at the end of the week discuss assigned reading and topics in lecture. This class allows creativity and expression - no music background required. Simple UGS credit

Solid choice. There were only a couple short answer assignments that we had to do (2-3 pages) and one paper at the end of the course. Lectures were mandatory and kind of boring at some points, but some of the material can be interesting. The TA was super helpful for all the writing assignments and Prof. Drott was passionate. I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The content can be a little stale but the professor does his best to deliver it. He holds some respect in the ethnomusicology field.

Pretty interesting UGS to take and lectures consist of him going over different topics through powerpoint. He is very informative, and the class is mainly graded over four short papers and a final paper that he gives ample time for. Papers are mainly graded by his TA which is somewhat harsh but at least he gives great feedback on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class depends entirely on your TA. Most of them graded pretty harshly, and lab groups rarely, if ever, got full points on notes. Some experiments would take the entire three-hour lab. The lab practical is weighted very heavily, so you need to understand how to perform the experiments and do the calculations we did during lab.

Chill guy, passionate about physics. Physics is just hard in general but he really cares about students. However his lectures were sometimes difficult to understand so you definitely have to teach yourself. Corrections allowed for half points back on midterms and a video project to replace one exam. Exams similar to HW but hard.

Completely TA dependent, got lucky and mine was pretty ok in terms of grading. Also got with a good group, lots of writing, definitely more statistics than physics focused. Really focus on studying the statistical formulas for the practical and your writing. Overall pretty ok. You do get some extra credit opportunities though and points back.

TA dependent. My TA was Frances and she was amazing. Kind, walked us through the labs, great at answering questions (she sent me a hand-drawn diagram once when I emailed her for help), very fair grader. Be ready for the practical to bomb your grade, although (other than time) I thought it was fair. Average was a 57%. Too much work for 1 hour imo
It is very TA dependent. My TA was Frances, and she was awesome. Grading isn't easy necessarily, but she is fair with her grading.
Lab is TA dependent and group-dependent. I was not lucky...the reports were graded as if I had committed a crime against them

Great prof who make thermo and stat mech seem approachable and almost easy. This is the last physics class I had to take for my physics degree and am so happy I took it with him. Half credit back on exams for corrections is really nice and having class participation helps with a good grade. Exams are similar to practice exams. Best PHY prof at UT

No hate to this professor, but his lab is TA dependent, and my TA was awful. I failed the practical (as did most of my class) because my TA (for every lab) went off course and made a lab for us (which was harder) instead of letting us lead it ourselves. We ended up not learning anything from labs because we relied on OH all the time. 0/10 TA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Physics 1 lab is probably the easiest stem class I've taken. Experiments and reports are simple, I guess it depends in you TA but mine was fantastic. Lab practical isn't bad as long as you study. It's a good amount of work for 1 credit but it is what it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just don't take Physics at UT.

Loveridge is genuinely just an outstanding professor. Ignore the other reviews for the lab sections. Those are TA dependent. When talking about Loveridge himself, his lectures are excellent, he cares about his students, and he goes to extra lengths to ensure we succeed. Thermodynamics can be difficult but he made it approachable! Highly recommend.

Dr. Loveridge is a good professor who has a very fair system when it comes to testing. He doesn't give extra credit, but gives half credit back on exams with corrections. The tests are usually the easy problems from the homework; there usually aren't curveballs on the tests, but they are weighted relatively heavily if you include the final.

I took intro physics 1 lab taught only by a TA. I never saw dr loveridge but I will say the structure of this class is pretty easy. The type of statistical analysis done every lab is very routine, so once you get used to it it can be very easy.

This guy clearly does not care about this students at all. I sincerely doubt he's spent even a second preparing this course. Genuinely the worst lab I've ever taken in my life. Disgusting to me that this is allowed.The labs are horribly designed, the TA can just ruin you. Grade boundaries are determined at the end of semester. Even the canvas sucks

Never met the guy he j oversees the course but all the TAs r useless; NEVER RESPOND TO ED DISCUSSION OR EMAILS when students bring up many issues; lack of communication is crazy and is the most disorganized course I have ever taken at UT with the most indifferent TAs; lab notes r annoying

I had Dr. Loveridge for his first time teaching Modern Lab, in the summer. He is very caring and respectful, and clearly wants students to succeed. This is a difficult course but Dr. Loveridge made it manageable. Note that this was a very unique class for several reasons so my comments might not reflect him as a professor in a more regular class.

Entirely TA dependent. Useless prelabs and then TAs have no clear guideline on grading. TA (Aryan) was over 30-45 minutes late to lab 3 different times and still graded reports extremely harshly. The class itself isn't hard, the labs are relatively quick and you're out early most times. Practical is hard but doable.

This class is kind of a nightmare especially depending on your lab group. Everyone receives the same grade, so make sure you get good group mates. Depending on your TA, lab reports take forever to finish and the practical is an unrealistic time constraint. Too much of your grade depends on the practical, and its not easy.

Prof. Loveridge is very nice, but can make you feel dumb if incorrect. I can tell it is not intentional, but it was off-putting in lecture. Wants you to learn and makes it relatively easy to get a decent grade through test corrections (half credit back). Tests are mostly recycled HW questions, and tests questions are pulled from previous tests.

This is really just a coin flip on whether your TA is good or not, and I lost. She was super picky about the format of your submissions and took lots of small points off, which added up. Got an A- for what I felt was A effort. Shame

Prelabs were pointless. Pray you get a good TA. I did not. He was actually dumb, and he was so unhelpful. For the practical, it's all paper & pen, so make sure you know how to use those formulas without excel. Find a group you like, and try to stick with them the whole semester if your TA is nice. Reports were tedious and graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never saw the professor ONCE throughout the semester, but his TA for us was HORRIBLE. Graded so hard and wasn't even understanding of our needs. "Curve" applied at the end but there wasn't a curve man. Horrible experience overall. Pray you get one of the lazy TAs

Very Nice, Won't obliterate you with insane exams. Just wants to create a positive learning environment.
:thumbs_up:

IF YOU ARE TAKING 105M DONT TAKE IT PLEASE.IF DAKSHATA IS YOUR TA...QDROP! She grades all the labs on the last week of finals, poor at communication, and has no syallbus about the grading scale. Basically going into finals without knowing what your grade is. Class itself is a joke and the the final can be learned in 15 min review equation sheet

Depends on the TA, and I was lucky mine was really easy. I honestly just used Chat to review the lab reports based on the rubric and manual and got a perfect rating each time. Lab practical was hardest part because of the limited time and the amount of calculations for it, so you need to know your lab reports and the formulas well.

Realistic course for 1 credit hour compared to other labs. TA-based, 8 labs/prelabs, practical is pretty stressful, but making sure you know how to do every part of your reports will set you up well for the practical.

Everything that you learn in this course (uncertainty calculations and come basic statistical tools) could be taught in a single lecture. Only a few assignments but there's often some issue with them. A profoundly useless course that's sadly required for so many majors. Your own lab experience will depend on your TA. The practical is not too bad.

Entirely based on your TA. I had a more difficult TA, so I spent more time on this class than some of my friends with different TAs, but getting an A is manageable regardless. The practical can be challenging, so definitely review all your analysis strategies before taking it.

Never meet the professor, but my TA was great & graded pretty easily. Doesn't take too much time out of class if you keep track of the experiment data while you're doing it in class. The practical is easy as long as you know how to do the calculations they tell you of beforehand, and go over the labs. All of my group members did pretty well on it.

Great professor with a forgiving and fair grading set up (half back on tests). The lectures were a little helpful but physics is just annoying although loveridge is great. I excelled when I started reading the textbook (the class is very closely structured around it except for fluid mechanics) and trying to understand the material before homeworks.

loveridge is a nice guy but terrible at teaching intro physics. lectures are extremely disorganized and exams are unpredictable with only 50 mins to do 11 questions. can make up exams for 1/2 credit back but exams are unforgiving since they are online and there isnt a way to show your work for partial credit. rip my gpa, gave it all i had.....

exams are online and he does not grade work so you have very very little room for error. yes you can make up the exams for 1/2 credit, but the exams themselves are poorly designed. has not graded assignments from 7-10 weeks ago. is lazy and formats exams to benefit his grading efficiency and not student understanding. also not good at lecturing lol

never met the professor but this class is EXTREMELY dependent on your ta. my ta was super lenient about grades and still its pretty hard to get a perfect score on a lab report. make sure to have a good lab group and learn how to do the calculations because the lab practical is primarily dependent on it

This review is about my TA and not my professor because I have never met or seen Dr. Loveridge. My TA grades horrible, is hard to understand, and takes off points for writing the uncertainty of ONE individual number is 0.5 instead of 1 (yes he actually took off 5 points for this alone). I would recommend just doing it online over summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for the TA not the actual prof. Your grade in physics lab will depend ENTIRELY on your TA. Mine is awful. Genuinely finds the one place in our paper we used the wrong decimal and takes an entire point off. She is hard to understand and not helpful at all. Be prepared for way more work and stress than you signed up for.

This rating is for my lab's TA, not Dr. Loveridge. It's not the best rating because it was difficult to communicate with or even understand our TA, sadly. Our TA also seemed to not know what was going on, but, at the same time, found it no trouble to grade us harshly. Best recommendation is to create a template for the lab report!

I loved his course and even though his lectures wasnt the best help to solve hw problems the lectured are really interesting and he was enthusiastic to teach. Visited him for office hours and he turned out to be a really chill and funny guy. He cares about his students and tells us his story back in college often. Absolutely goated, 10/10
The concepts will always be hard but he doesn't make them harder than they should be. For only a semester, you learn a lot but there are a lot of opportunities to make back points.
Loveridge was a GOAT. Thought the lecture style was unique and I enjoyed it. Half credit back on tests for corrections is amazing.

I felt that Professor Loveridge did a good job in his first year teaching 303K. A major bonus is that you can correct for half credit on exams. However, lectures are usually inefficient and unrelated to the homeworks, and the "participation point" system is confusing - you will not know your true grade until the very end of the semester.

As head instructor, this course is honestly a disgrace to what UT represents. The lab instructions are vague, and one's grade is dependent on the TA.
