The lab practical is an absolute joke, with such limited time to do 3 experiments in 75 minutes- with the amount of calculations you need to do. While I got an A, this class nearly gave me a stroke.

ta & group dependent. never saw the prof. labs are time consuming & reports are annoying. final practical is meant to trip you up & was the hardest part. timing was a problem & too much data analysis/collection for the practical.
The "G" in Loveridge stands for GOAT. Great Professor who believes in his students and their ability to improve.

His lectures are actually enjoyable and you will get an A if you try for a little bit
He gives you exam corrections credit for half credit back and final replaces your lowest exam grade and the final is basically 9 exact same questions you already had in the past exams and 6 really easy questions from the last unit, take loveridge 303k if you can

Class structure was terrible. Final is meant to trick you and rubric is written in such a way to lose points. Never met the professor, TA and groups were great, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that the design of the curriculum for this course is actively trying to fail you. Labs aren't hard, but deal more with statistics than physics.
Never met Loveridge. Everything depends on your TA and lab partners. Very hit or miss

I have never met the actual professor but my TA was very great. He would give us written examples that truly did help everyone in the lab. However, this class heavily depends on what partner you have for the lab and how much of the material you know since this WILL be a difficult class if you don't know anything or have a bad partner.

Redos for half points back on exams, which have similar questions to the HWs. Optional video group project to replace lowest exam. The HWs were challenging at times but Loveridge always helped me out during OHs, and I felt that he genuinely cared about students. Even if you bomb an exam, it's possible to get an A! One of my fave classes and profs!

rating of the course rather than the prof bc 0 interaction. idk i disliked this lab. so so tedious + vague, but u can and should finish the lab notes in the lab sesh and avoid dealing with them later. TA dependent- mine was v sweet but difficult to communicate w. practical was so so hard imo but i have no calc bckgrnd and vv weak physics knowledge.

Phys 1 lab wasn't too bad. TA gave us written guides for our experiments, so we'd just follow those and leave within 1.5 hours. Some labs are a headache, but you'll get pretty quick at typing up the weekly lab notes since they all follow the same format. Practical isn't too stressful as long as you know the analysis tools that we use in every lab.

Like everyone says, it's TA dependent. They do curve at the end to makeup for differences in TA grading, so don't worry too much if your TA grades a little harder than others. I thought Labs were significantly easier and faster than the Physics I labs. Try to get a good group, it helps A LOT, but you will have to change partners eventually.

Very heavily dependent on who you get for your TA. The rubrics are vague, you will get counted off for the smallest things depending on TA. This class is very "notes" heavy, and is a TON of work outside of class. The practical was very random in my opinion, and not representative of the course. Be ready for a very calculation heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Physics 2 w/ Dr. Loveridge last semester and he has been my favorite professor so far at UT. He is very understanding and genuinely cares about his students. Test were very fair, but they were also reasonably challenging so I felt like I learned a lot. Super helpful office hours and some extra credit. An A is very attainable!

Given little instruction- u design your experiments, do a write up, and then submit those notes to be graded on technique and accuracy. It was hard and very confusing tbh. I NEVER knew what i was doing but my TA was chill and graded easy. You recreate 3 of the labs for the practical so try and understand the all the math and methods you use! trust.

It can be difficult to understand what your TA wants so communicate with them to determine how to do your lab reports. Difficult at first but okay when you get the hang of it, but the practical was stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is unnecessarily hard. Lab notes are graded very subjectively - even after asking the TA to check my work, I would get points off. Asking for help is difficult bc they don't answer questions on Chatter or provide clear instruction. Lab practical was stressful.
Pray you get a TA that you can understand. Class is easy, but if you get a bad TA it makes it an unnecessary headache.

Worst class I've taken at UT. Ridiculous amount of work for 1 credit hour. Labs instructions are vague and it was hard to know what we needed to do to not only set up the experiment, but also analyze it on the reports. Grading is TA dependent. Some people breeze by this class with a chill TA, but mine made this class an absolute nightmare.

The lab reports are 70% of the grade. The labs honestly aren't that hard, it's just that the lab instructions are very vague and it's up to the students to design their own experiments and collect data (which gets annoying). You're all set if you have a good group. Follow the rubric make sure ur group submits a detailed report. Not a hard class

the class is ok, as long as you do the homeworks and understand the underlying concepts - the tests will be easy for you. didn't really attend lectures because i found just watching yt videos to be more helpful - but not a bad class to take. of the better physics classes out there

Physics Lab II is much like Physics Lab I. The lab manuals are often quite dense and hard to read at times. But ultimately, the class depends on your TA. The final project was not too difficult as well. If in doubt, ask your TA on how they will grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading consists of prelabs (completion), lab "notes" (reports), and practical. No lab structure, you basically design your own experiments and type your methods, data, and conclusions in your lab notes. Grading is super TA-dependent. Way too much work for a 1 hour class but not hard at all. Practical is not hard unlike what some people say.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is entirely TA-run, so it rly depends on how strict your TA is.Labs were simple but calculations were tedious.Weekly lab reports around 7-8 pg long. All labs are in groups of two that are randomly assigned, so you just have to hope you get a partner that is willing to contribute. Practical is a time crunch but rly similar to practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Grading is very TA dependent, make sure to follow the lab report rubric word by word even if it's frustrating. Call me naive, but the thing I awe about is that you have to reproduce the EXACT results that matches the theory or you get points off. Why spend the time to refine the data when you can fake the data? It's totally a bureaucracy thing.

did not see dr. loveridge once. however, the lab was very easy. calculations are difficult at first but then very simple after a few mins of struggling. only spent about 2 hours outside of class per week on this class so it is very doable.

I never saw the professor. The class felt like a bunch of busy work/math for basic physics concepts that were taught in high school. Incredibly tedious but relatively easy. Grading is probably reliant on your TA.

Your grade is determined by your TA. The class wasn't too bad but if you're used to having some form of structure in your labs, this class lacks any of it. The practical wasn't as difficult as most people make it out to be. Just study your past labs and know how to do the calculations you've learned all semester.

I never saw the professor once but the class was laid out from the start. Labs are very vague in order to get you to be creative. They are graded based on your TA so ask them why you lost points to make sure you get them on the next report. Lab practical was difficult due to the time limit but a long as you know how the analysis tools work it's ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Never interacted with Loveridge but he answers questions quickly and seems nice. Your grades will depend on your TA. Lab and lab reports are annoying because the rubric and instructions are extremely vague. Pray you have a good TA and lab partner. 
Practical wasn't bad as long as you know all the analysis methods and work fast.

I never met the professor as the labs are graded and taught entirely by TAs; however, I enjoyed the class. The labs are generally manageable within the three hours. My only gripe with the class is the Lab Practical. This time-dependent exam puts you against the clock, which is difficult since there is no practice during class at all for this exam.

Start lab reports early, communicate with your partner, and hope you have an understanding TA. Your grade partially relies on how hard they grade, but I believe the course is normalized so the TA grading doesn't affect final scores too much. Took both 105 M + N here at UT. Just don't procrastinate.

You almost never see this professor. The class however was fine. Your grade depends on your TA, but I thought that the grading criteria were well thought out and assignments were graded adequately. Most of the work is group work so get ready to work with others and keep clear communication.
Class was good. If you really want to get on his good side though, make sure you mention Missouri during office hours. He loves that place.

never interacted with him -- only the TA so consider this a class review. It's doable to get an A but you have to work hard, and it's overly stressful imo. If you have a bad lab partner or a bad TA... good luck

I took Dr. Loveridge for 105M & N and he was the kindest professor I have met. For 105N, my TA did not know what was going on so my lab partners and I attended his office hours everyday after lab for further explanation. He was kind, understanding, and clear with his explanations. He helped us learn the material very well. Dr. Loveridge is the BEST

Never met prof. Grade fully TA dependent. Never expect a perfect score on anything but put in the effort and you can get an A. Weekly lab reports are long, DO NOT procrastinate or it will be very tedious to finish. The final exam was challenging but doable. Be ready to learn a lot of stats. Even the final tests this more than physics knowledge.

Relative to what past reviews have said, this class has gotten so much better. I never personally met Dr Loveridge, but the lab was definitely doable this semester, and the final project was a scientific poster. The class is still a lot of work for only 1 credit hour (the reports take forever), but I liked this lab!

I had a much better experience in Physics 2 Lab compared to 1, I felt like the reports were less difficult and thank goodness for no practical. Loveridge makes himself really inaccessible though, besides a few OH per week. Class is entirely TA dependent. I got lucky with a really nice and helpful TA Jatin. Make sure you get good lab partners too!!

Your TA will grade each lab according to how they see fit. My TA averaged grading around an 80/85 per lab (9 in total). Lab practical at the end of the semester is a bit difficult; however, the class does get curved and an 86ish gets made an A. Never met the professor in person or online. Lab coursework is very doable and not overwhelmingly heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So dependent on your TA. I was lucky to have gotten patient TAs who explained everything to me constantly (instructions for each lab and details for analysis were usually somehow... vague?) and weren't overly harsh graders. I have never seen Dr. Loveridge in my life. Communicate a lot with your TA about assignments and each lab to do well.

This is a lab run by TAs. Mine was good but it was mutually agreed that the labs were unnecessarily tedious and annoying. TA refers to Prof as "Angry Andrew" for some reason. He's super hands off and can only be reached if you go out of your way to find him. Just hope your TA is cool like mine. And lab partners, I had a few that tanked my grade.

was surprised to see such low reviews but I guess this class is super dependent on your TA. you don't interact w loveridge really but all content and instructions is very clearly laid out and he's available to help if you need it. my TA was super helpful and gave pretty good grades as long as you followed the guidelines

Everything is based on your TA, and most of them have no idea what they're doing.  HOWEVER, Loveridge is very helpful if you go into his office hours. I recommend going in if you're having any trouble. Worst part about the class is bad lab partners. Lab reports are pretty extensive, so make sure you pick good partners if you can.

you won't ever meet Loveridge so the class is highly TA-dependent. The instructions for each lab are so vague so the TA has to tell you everything to do which is frustrating. Each week there are "lab notes" due but they are really long lab reports that take HOURS to do. The labs are fun and the assignments aren't hard just time-consuming.

Everything about this lab is ridiculous. 1) you never see the professor (grade is very TA dependent) he isn't even approachable 2) they call them "lab notes" when it's 100% a lab report. Don't let them fool you. They will grade you hard and will count off for things they ask u for 3) lab practical average is failing and they don't care :)

Grade entirely dependent on your TA. The lab manuals have too much ambiguity in my opinion and need more details regarding what is expected from students on the lab report. The pre-lab quiz could be formatted better to help prep for the lab. You get a lab partner for the semester. The lab practical was ridiculous and the class avg. was failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I never saw Loveridge, only my TA, who did not grade fairly in my opinion. I never got full credit for an assignment, no matter what I did and believe me, I put great effort in. This is the second time I've been in one of Loveridge's labs and it was just as bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 1 hour lab but takes 4 hours a week outside of class. TAs grade RIDICULOUSLY hard. This is probably a required course for you, but if its not, for the love of god, TAKE SOMETHING ELSE.

Worst class ever. You have to take it as a pre-med. The grade depends on the TA. The instructions are super vague, and you get points taken off for criteria you didn't know existed. Least favorite class I've taken at UT by far.

Took his lab course over the summer, so I expected it to be very time-consuming and demanding. We are a week away and they still have not figured out when we are taking it, how we are taking it, and how long we will have. The level of disorganization in this class is astounding. Lab protocols are confusing and you HAVE to go to OH's to get answers

No matter what you do, do not take this lab with Loveridge, not like you will have him as a teacher anyway, because your teaching quality and grading is SOLELY determined by the TA's. They are not required to grade off of any rubric or anything. In other words, you are screwed no matter how hard you work. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is only worth 1 credit hour, but I spent at least six hours a week on labs. You always have a lab partner, but if you wanna do well, you'll probably end up doing most or all of each lab on your own. Also, your experience in this class is very dependent on your TA. Some TAs explain the labs well, while others don't explain them at all.

2nd time taking physics lab (not really something we can get out of), but the course really depends on TA. The first semester TA was awfully tough, 2nd semester TA wasn't AS nit-picky but it seems like Loveridge wants the TAs to take points off for tiny mistakes to keep some average letter grade in the course. Totally tedious course for no reason

Even though the class counts for 1 hour, I worked about 10 hours each week to perfect my lab reports. You work with a partner for each report, and you have to be incredibly tedious to do well. It's possible to do well, just get ready to study lots of statistics and work hard.

TBH, no one in this course will own up to their mistakes or apologize for issues. TA's do not grade clearly or consistently. Many TA's do not work hard to answer your questions during office hours. The final exam was accidentally posted on canvas, it took hours for an instructor to address the issue, and I do not believe it was handled fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do u want to spend 5+ hrs a week on lab reports just to get 10-15 points off bc u did smth wrong according to a nonexistent rubric? This class is perfect! The TINIEST "mistake" will cost u 3-10 points instantly. Lab practical had a failing average btw. Grading experience depends on TA. FOR THE LOVE OF GOD DON'T GET CHENYANG AS UR TA.

This class sucks so bad LIKE SO UNBELIEVABLY BAD. I would say don't take it but like ik most of the ppl taking this are forced to bc i mean who tf wants to take physics lab voluntarily! All I can say is if you have chenyang as ur TA, try to switch after the first class or it's just gonna be a terrible semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This rating is more for the idea of this class. It all depends on your TA. The final was horrible and there were little to no details provided about it until the very last minute not to mention it got leaked for later sections- a mess overall. The lab itself does not even really cover physics, a lot of statistics. Horrible experience.

Prof pretty much had 0 contact with students outside piazza. Online labs were always vague and grading came down to your TA, so if you get a nit-picky one you're kind of screwed. Lab itself isn't too difficult but there's barely any physics involved, it's just statistics. The final was ridiculous (3 experiments in less than 2 hrs how is that fair?)

I've never even had any contact with Loveridge himself, only the awful TAs. Lab reports are graded hard and very difficult, in addition to a lack of clear instructions from the TAs. No TA to my knowledge gave out a 30/30 no matter how good the lab report. In addition, the final is unbelievably difficult and you will not have enough time to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It all depends on your TA for physics lab. Some are really bad, and some are really good. Hope you get lucky, or learn to adapt to your TA's grading style.

The physics online labs are awful. The lab reports are written so poorly it takes me so long and multiple TA office hours to figure out what they mean. The TAs in the class don't seem to know exactly what they're doing either. This lab is more like a statistics class than a physics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loveridge is very clear, concise lecturer and grader. It is very easy to understand him, and sometimes he does cool demonstrations to supplement the lecture. His hw was fair, a bit long, so don't do it last second. Exams are very very fair and relatively easy. Overall great physics professor

The material was more interesting than the first section during the summer, and my LI for this section was great! The final project was to make a lab which was somewhat difficult, so ask for help from your LI or Dr. Loveridge if it comes to that. The lab partners were easygoing, and be sure to get emails or phone numbers to communicate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class itself was interesting, and my LI was very nitpicky. Be sure to ask for example lab reports and how exactly the LI will be grading them. ASK FOR HELP with the statistical methods if it isn't clear to you. Read through the instructions carefully and ask if certain parts should go on the lab report. Lab partners were all great for me.

I took Physics 2 Lab Online during the 2nd semester summer session. Two lab reports due every week, 8 in total PLUS a final where you have to design your own lab. I probably devoted 15 hours a week to this course. The workload does not match the 1 hour of credit, but there's not much you can do about that. :/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took during Covid Mess and Loveridge it doable. I didnt do too well in PHY 317K, but Loveridge made the topics easy to understand in 317L. His homeworks are tough, but there are discussions to help, and if you can figure them out, the test is very similar to the homeworks. 3 midterms and 1 cumulative final, all quest based, I midterm drop.

This man is the king of physics. I hated physics 1 but enjoyed physics 2. He really will help his students if they are not getting the materials. He offers test corrections. This man is great if you have an option to take him I suggest you do.

I think these reviews are a bit harsh. Database is an easy and manageable course if you just studied and tried on the exams (I would barely attend class and study a few days before the test). However, the course can be ambiguous and disorganized, which is why I think ppl are frustrated. It's not a "free" A, but with minimal effort you will do well.

STA301 is a hard class, and Drakou was just okay. I wouldn't recommend taking her if you want transparency for what's on the exam/what to prepare for. You will need to do a lot of studying for the exams, especially the final.

Zena Drakous is genuinely the worst professors I've had at UT. Her course is incredibly disorganized, exams weigh so much but only consist of few questions with incredibly vague instruction, but are graded extremely harshly. This is the worst classes I've taken--it's making me question the quality of the MIS/ BAX program here at UT. DON'T TAKE ZENA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its difficult to understand her.

The other reviews are pretty clear. She's kind, but the class has no structure. Slides don't match the textbook, which doesn't match the activities or homework. Expectation is that you know how to code, because time isn't given in class for it. Exams are cumulative and coding heavy. Be prepared to spend time outside of class studying and coding.

Zena is nice but I didn't find her lectures helpful. Vague "headcount" attendance?? Tests are tricky, read test questions carefully & know the code from the KCs + HW. This class is basically self taught from the textbook so actually read it and take notes yourself. If you want an A, take textbook notes each week instead of cramming like me lol

Although Zena is kind, it's clear she doesn't know how to lecture properly. She repeats what the textbook says rather than mentioning new information that can help make the topics more digestible. Exams are weighed heavily, and it's hard to decide if you're doing well in the class when the last midterm is one week before the final.

Shes really nice and chill professor, not strict, and we didn't have any pop quizzes at all. Her lectures did not really teach us the important parts of the coding and concepts, making understanding conceots on exams harder. Stats is really hard and particular in its wording so make sure to read all of the textbook and take notes off that.

A lot of the reviews are a little too hard. She is very nice and knows what she is teaching.  She is not great lecturer though, a lot of your learning is going to be by yourself. She also does not have the clearest grading, didn't tell us how she is taking attendance all semester. You will be fine if you are just willing to put in the effort.

Her lectures are very unclear and the class is coding heavy. There second midterm is a week before the final. The final was very, very difficult and had a class average of 62% without a curve and was worth 28% of the grade. Insanely hard class for no reason and a poorly instructed class across the board.
Waits til the end to grade anything and doesn't explain anything in the class. Barely goes over coding examples even though the class is 90% coding, avoid if you know what's good for you.

This class was hard. I think Zena is getting more hate than she deserves, because the class was hard regardless of the professor. Like most people taking this class, I did not actually try on hws and just coasted through the semester using gpt. When it comes time to take the test, you'll regret that I promise. Just read the textbook! Lectures suck

Hardest class I've taken, Zena is a nice person but her lectures are no help. The grading is a mess and unclear. Lectures were not engaging and did not focus on actual coding at all, which is the basis of exams. This class will be hard regardless of prof, GPAFactory is extremely helpful for homework and test review but is expensive for most.

Tbh I think a lot of the reviews are overly harsh. Zena is super nice and cares about her students. Although during class she focused on conceptuals rather than code (which is the bulk of the exams), it wasn't hard to get an A. Just take good notes on the textbook & actually put an effort into understanding the KC's & homeworks and you'll do well

Professor Drakou is great. She genuinely cares about the students in her class - every interaction I had with her was extremely helpful. Most of the other reviews on this page focus on the class itself, not on her. She actively works to improve the course and is an excellent teacher.
GPA factory saved my grade in this class. her lectures don't relate to the content and she is not engaging in the slightest. super sweet lady but I probably did not learn a single thing from her.
HORRIBLE! It's like she makes all the TAs do the work, she doesn't seem to know much about the course! Hilarious because it's hilariously bad!

Do yourself a favor and do not take Zena! This class is terribly hard as it is and half of the time Zena doesn't know what she is doing. Expectations are unclear making it difficult to know what is needed. Only reason why I am doing half-well is because of the online TAs and the book. Do NOT TAKE!

I know you see the comments flaming her. Mind you I took AP stats in high school and got a 5 on the exam. That is the reason why I am not crashing out right now. This class is HARD. Like she is monotone and does not make it fun or engaging. Her style of teaching is perfect when you don't have 3 exams dangling on ur neck like a knife. I crashed out

I would NOT take this teacher again ever. She is nice as a person but honestly her teaching is so so bad. GPA factory is the only reason I am not going to completely fail this course. Most of the tests are coding and I genuinely think we have gone over coding during a single lecture at the very beginning of the semester. DONT TAKE HER.

The class itself is hard across all professors, but I will say she does not go over coding very much. If you ask questions, she is very helpful. I would recommend reading the chapter before class. The besy help was to use GPA factory and go/watch to R-coding session.

Do NOT take Zena no matter what. Absolutely horrible professor who had no idea how to teach stats. Lectures are useless but she takes attendance based on headcount. A CUMULATIVE 2nd midterm with a final the next week and she barely goes over the exam material in class. GPA Factory was the only way to prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a person she's sweet, but not a great professor. The lectures are not very helpful as they go over zero coding when half of the exam is literally coding which is super stressful as the 2 midterms are heavily weighted. You will have to teach yourself the content for exams.

Terrible teacher; avoid her at all costs. Takes attendance based off headcount with no established way to determine who is actually there. if you're going to take her, MAKE SURE TO READ because her lectures are absolutely useless. I pulled pretty good grades on the tests just reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: PLEASE AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS IF YOU WANT TO SAVE YOUR GPA. Genuinely learned nothing, and then proceeded to tell us that she has been taking attendance the entire semester. Worst prof I have ever had at UT, she is sweet but holy she cannot teach.

Absolutely awful. Avoid her at all costs. She is just bad at teaching and doesn't even know the structure of her class. Asking questions just makes things more confusing. Be prepared to teach everything to yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buy GPA factory if your gonna take her class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sweet person, so nothing against her character but her teaching is NOT for me. TEST heavy, with three total, the final and exam 2 are cumulative?? does not make sense. She reads straight off the slides. STA301 is challenging, and I did not get the education I needed to excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We don't spend any time doing code we just learn "conceptual" that do not really tie in together. I practically self taught this whole class myself, spending too much money, time, and resources. Over 50% tests & we had our final less than a week after our second midterm with new content. Tests were harder than said, and expectations were unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cannot teach for the life of her. The homework and study guides don't match up with the exam at all. For reference, I've coded before but nothing lined up with the curriculum. Maybe half the questions were from the material we covered the other from next unit's material. She confused herself in her own class.
I get this class itself is hard but she doesn't teach very well to beginners and you will end up having to teach yourself a lot outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Although it is clear that she understand the course content, she is very disorganized. She skipped a large portion of content outlined in the syllabus and did not release any grades until 2 days before the final exam. However, the class is fairly straightforward and the slides alone are enough to understand the material and do well in the class.

Pretty easy class, especially for someone who has never coded in my life. Exam 1 was in-class but open note/internet. Exams 2 and 3 were take-home open internet. Not necessarily easy tests but if you have an understanding of the material you should be fine. Lots of other easy assignments and she even offered a bunch of extra credit at the end.

Zena is the sweetest human being!! You could learn all you need from the ppts, so whether she is an effective instructor seems irrelevant. 1st & 3rd exams are easy. 2nd one is challenging, so prepare. All are open note, open internet, etc & the last 2 were at home. The quizzes are tricky, so study the ppts.

I love Zena Drakou! Her teaching style is super chill and she is always ready to help! If you have never taken a coding class before DON'T STRESS! She starts everything from scratch and She also gives credit for comments on tests so If you can not code it all the way, dont stress! I love her so much and also she is super funny. TAKE THIS CLASS

I had Drakou for MIS 325, which was her first time teaching this course. The class was unorganized and there was no clear schedule for anything: assignment and test dates would be random and were always pushed back. Additionally, grades were released super late and there were few grades as a whole. However, Drakou is super nice and understanding.

Drakou is a kind and caring professor but sometimes she struggles to keep the class moving at a fast pace. My class finished two months behind where we were supposed to because of two canceled classes and the winter storm. While this is fine and made the class easier, it hurt my learning and made it difficult to learn essential Python. Hard Tests.

*Caveat: my first time learning Python* The class is paced well, and the homework assignments are easy. I would say that they are easy to the point that they are not indicative of the difficulty of the exams. For python newbies, you definitely need to practice outside of the course assignment material to really succeed.

Exams worth 65% of your grade. Exam I is easy. Exam II is harder. Exam III is comprehensive. Zena is nice, and teaches alright. If you do not have prior Python coding experience, you will need to put in more effort, especially for the second and third exam. Exams are open book. Study homeworks and practice notebooks. Attend office hours if needed.
